en: The Principality of Zubtsov was an appanage of the Tver grand princes, centered on the fortress town of Zubtsov at the meeting of the Volga and Vazuza rivers. First recorded in 1216, the town guarded a branch of the Varangian-to-Greek trade route and became the southern stronghold of Tver. In 1319 the sons of Mikhail of Tver divided his lands, and Aleksandr Mikhailovich received the southwestern districts, with Zubtsov, Gorodok, Kholm and Mikulin, making the town his capital. Aleksandr became grand prince of Tver but was executed at the Golden Horde in 1339 together with his son Fyodor; his widow and younger sons kept the appanage until the plague of 1364 to 1365 killed most of the line and Zubtsov reverted to the Tver grand princes. It was briefly regranted as an appanage between 1426 and about 1460, then reverted again, and in 1485 it passed to Moscow with the rest of Tver.
zh: 祖布佐夫公国是特维尔大公治下的封邑，中心在伏尔加河与瓦祖扎河交汇处的要塞城镇祖布佐夫。该城1216年始见记载，扼守瓦良格到希腊商路的一条支线，是特维尔南部的重镇。1319年特维尔王公米哈伊尔诸子瓜分领地，亚历山大·米哈伊洛维奇分得西南地区，包括祖布佐夫、戈罗多克、霍尔姆和米库林，并以祖布佐夫为治所。亚历山大后来成为特维尔大公，却于1339年在金帐汗国与长子费奥多尔一同被处死；他的遗孀和幼子们保留了这块封邑，直到1364至1365年的瘟疫使这一支几乎死绝，祖布佐夫重归特维尔大公直辖。1426年至约1460年，它曾再次被封给宗室王公，之后又被收回，1485年随特维尔其余领地一起并入莫斯科。

en: Zürich is a city state on the Limmat river at the northern tip of the Lake of Zürich, grown from the Roman customs station of Turicum. In the Middle Ages it held imperial immediacy, though until the fourteenth century its council was dominated by patrician families and its mayor appointed by the abbess of the Fraumünster. In June 1336 the guild leader Rudolf Brun overthrew that council, gave the thirteen guilds an equal share in government and made himself mayor for life; in 1337 he defeated his exiled aristocratic opponents at the Battle of Grynau, near Rapperswil. Under Brun the city joined the Swiss Confederacy in 1351 as its fifth member. It was expelled in 1440 after the Old Zürich War over the Toggenburg inheritance and readmitted in 1450, and from 1468 to 1519 it presided over the confederate Diet. In 1519 Huldrych Zwingli launched the Swiss Reformation from the Grossmünster, and the Zürich Bible was printed in 1531; the confessional clashes ended with the Catholic victory in the Wars of Kappel. The city built a new ring of fortifications in 1624 and declared itself a republic in 1648. An oligarchic council ruled until the Helvetic Revolution of 1798, and the city and its subject countryside were separated into a city and a canton in 1803.
zh: 苏黎世是位于苏黎世湖北端、利马特河畔的城市邦国，前身是罗马人的关税站图里库姆。中世纪时它享有帝国直辖地位，但14世纪以前市政会由贵族世家把持，市长由弗劳明斯特修道院的女院长任命。1336年6月，行会领袖鲁道夫·布伦推翻旧市政会，让十三座行会在政府中与旧贵族平分席位，并自任终身市长；1337年，他在拉珀斯维尔附近的格里瑙战役中击败流亡的贵族政敌。布伦治下的苏黎世于1351年加入瑞士同盟，成为第五个成员。1440年，因托根堡继承权引发旧苏黎世战争，苏黎世被同盟开除，1450年才重新加入；1468—1519年间它主持同盟议会。1519年，胡尔德莱斯·慈运理在格罗斯明斯特教堂发起瑞士宗教改革，苏黎世圣经于1531年印行；教派冲突最终在卡佩尔战争中以天主教一方获胜告终。1624年城市修建了新的环形城墙，1648年宣布成立共和国。寡头市政会一直统治到1798年海尔维第革命，1803年城市与其治下的乡村分立为城与州。

en: The County of Zutphen grew from the castle of Zutphen at the confluence of the Berkel and the IJssel, in the northern part of the old gau of Hamaland. In 1046 Emperor Henry III granted the district to the Bishop of Utrecht after deposing Duke Godfrey the Bearded of Lower Lorraine, and the fief was held by a line of counts whose heiress Ermengard married Gerard II of Wassenberg, Count of Guelders, around 1127; their son Henry I was the first to bear both titles, and from then on Zutphen followed Guelders in a personal union, becoming one of its four quarters. The town itself won self-governing rights between 1191 and 1196, minted coin for the counts and joined the Hanseatic League. In 1337 the county was held by Reginald II of Guelders, who from 1339 styled himself Duke of Guelders and Count of Zutphen. Zutphen shared Guelders' later fate, passing to Jülich in 1371, the House of Egmond in 1423 and the Habsburgs by the Treaty of Venlo in 1543. In 1579 the quarter joined the Union of Utrecht and the United Provinces; during the Eighty Years' War the Battle of Zutphen in 1586 left Sir Philip Sidney mortally wounded, and Maurice of Orange retook the town from Spain in 1591.
zh: 聚特芬伯国起源于贝克尔河注入艾瑟尔河处的聚特芬城堡，地处旧哈马兰高的北部。1046年，皇帝亨利三世废黜下洛林公爵大胡子戈特弗里德后，把这一地区封给乌得勒支主教，由一支伯爵家族作为封臣领有；其女继承人埃尔姆加德约在1127年嫁给海尔雷伯爵、瓦森贝格家族的格哈德二世，他们的儿子亨利一世成为首个身兼两衔的统治者，聚特芬从此与海尔雷形成君合，后来成为海尔雷四个区之一。聚特芬城在1191年至1196年间取得自治权，为伯爵铸造钱币并加入汉萨同盟。1337年，伯国由海尔雷的雷金纳德二世领有，他在1339年起自称海尔雷公爵兼聚特芬伯爵。聚特芬此后与海尔雷同命运：1371年转归于利希，1423年转入埃格蒙特家族，1543年依《芬洛条约》归哈布斯堡。1579年，该区加入乌得勒支同盟和联省共和国；八十年战争中，1586年的聚特芬战役使菲利普·锡德尼爵士受致命伤，奥兰治的莫里斯于1591年从西班牙手中夺回该城。

en:
The County of Zweibrücken was a western Palatinate lordship created between 1182 and 1190, when an inheritance division of the wealthy counts of Saarbrücken gave their lands around the Schwarzbach crossing to a younger son, Henry I. A water castle had been built at the ford around 1150, and the town that grew beneath it received city rights in 1352. Henry I also raised Lemberg Castle after 1198, and his descendants added scattered fiefs held from the Empire and the bishoprics of Metz and Verdun.

Joint rule by the brothers Eberhard I and Walram I ended in the partition of 1286, confirmed in 1333: Eberhard kept the eastern Lemberg lands, exchanged in 1297 for the lordship of Bitche as the Zweibrücken-Bitsch line, while Walram held Zweibrücken itself. His son Walram II, the count ruling in 1337, reigned until 1366. The last Walramide count, the childless and feud-bankrupted Eberhard II, pledged the county to the Wittelsbach counts palatine in 1385, and on his death in 1394 they inherited it, bringing the Palatinate line into the western Palatinate. Union with the County of Veldenz in 1444 produced the Principality of Palatinate-Zweibrücken, while the Bitsch line survived until 1570.
zh:
茨韦布吕肯伯国是普法尔茨西部的领地，形成于1182至1190年间：富有的萨尔布吕肯伯爵家族分割遗产，把施瓦茨巴赫渡口一带的土地分给幼子亨利一世。约1150年，渡口处已建起一座水堡，堡下发展出的城镇于1352年取得城市权。亨利一世还在1198年后修建了伦贝格城堡，他的后代又陆续取得从帝国及梅斯、凡尔登主教区封来的零散领地。

埃伯哈德一世与瓦尔拉姆一世兄弟的共治以1286年的分家告终，并于1333年最终确认：埃伯哈德保留东部的伦贝格土地，1297年又将其部分城镇换成比奇领地，开创茨韦布吕肯-比奇一支；瓦尔拉姆则占有茨韦布吕肯本土。他的儿子、1337年在位的瓦尔拉姆二世一直统治到1366年。末代瓦尔拉姆系伯爵埃伯哈德二世没有子嗣，又因频繁的家族仇斗而穷困，1385年把伯国抵押给维特尔斯巴赫家族的行宫伯爵，并在1394年去世后由对方继承，行宫伯爵一脉由此进入西普法尔茨。1444年与费尔登茨伯国合并，组成普法尔茨-茨韦布吕肯亲王国，而比奇一支延续到1570年。

en: Zhanyi lies at the source of the Nanpan River in eastern Yunnan, the gateway between Yunnan and the Guizhou plateau. Han China placed the area under Wei County, and from the fourth to the sixth centuries the local Cuan clan ruled it. In the later Nanzhao period it was the country of the Momi tribe, and under the Dali Kingdom it belonged to Shicheng Commandery. The Yuan created Zhanyi Department here in 1276 under the Qujing Route, with its seat at Shiliang, and the Ming kept an An clan Yi family as hereditary native department magistrates, linked by marriage and succession to the tusi house of Wusa across the border. During the great She-An rebellion the Wusa chieftain An Xiaoliang, himself a son of the Zhanyi magistrate An Shaoqing, rose in 1622 in answer to the Shuixi leader An Bangyan and captured Zhanyi along with Luoping and Bijie; Yunnan forces retook the city in 1625, when the department seat was moved to Jiaoshui, and An Xiaoliang was killed in battle in 1628. Under the Qing the old department was divided in 1727 into the two departments of Zhanyi and Xuanwei, and the border town grew into the present-day Zhanyi District of Qujing.
zh: 沾益位于云南东部南盘江上游，是珠江的发源地，也是云南通往贵州高原的门户。西汉时这里属益州郡味县，东晋至隋代由地方大族爨氏统治；南诏后期成为磨弥部的居地，大理国时隶属石城郡。1276年元朝置霑益州，属曲靖路，州治设在石梁；明朝以彝族安氏世袭沾益土知州，安家与邻境乌撒的土司家族世代联姻、承袭相连。明末奢安之乱中，乌撒土目安效良本是沾益土知州安绍庆之子，他于1622年起兵响应水西安邦彦，攻陷沾益，又攻破罗平、毕节；云南官军于1625年收复沾益，州治也在这一年迁到交水城，安效良则于1628年战败身亡。清朝时，旧地于1727年分设为霑益州和宣威州，这座边镇后来发展为今曲靖市的沾益区。

en: Zanzibar, on the island of Unguja off the East African coast, was settled by Bantu-speaking farmers and fishermen by the middle of the first millennium and ranked among the principal Swahili trading towns by the tenth century. Its merchants brokered gold and ivory from the African interior for Persian, Arab and Indian cloth and pottery, and settlements such as Unguja Ukuu, Tumbatu and Kizimkazi grew into stone-built city-states. In 1337 it was an autonomous Muslim sultanate, one of many rival Swahili cities along the coast. Vasco da Gama visited in 1498, and around 1503 the island became a Portuguese tributary, governed lightly through local rulers for nearly two centuries. Swahili elites then called in the Omanis, who took Zanzibar in 1698, and a revolt against Omani rule in 1784 was put down. In 1832 Said bin Sultan, Sultan of Muscat and Oman, moved his court to Stone Town, making Zanzibar the hub of an Indian Ocean commerce in cloves, ivory and slaves, until the Moresby Treaty of 1822 began British efforts to restrict that slave trade.
zh: 桑给巴尔位于东非近海的温古贾岛，公元一千纪中期已有说班图语的农耕和渔猎居民定居，到10世纪时已是主要的斯瓦希里贸易城镇之一。当地商人把非洲内陆的黄金和象牙转手，换取波斯、阿拉伯和印度的布匹与陶器，温古贾乌库、图姆巴图、基济姆卡齐等聚落发展为石建城邦。1337年时，它是一个自治的穆斯林苏丹国，与沿海众多斯瓦希里城邦并立争雄。瓦斯科·达伽马于1498年到访，约1503年桑给巴尔沦为葡萄牙的纳贡地，近两百年间葡萄牙人通过当地统治者实行松散治理。后来斯瓦希里上层请来阿曼人，后者于1698年夺取桑给巴尔，1784年的反阿曼起义被镇压。1832年，马斯喀特和阿曼苏丹赛义德·本·苏丹把宫廷迁到石头城，使桑给巴尔成为印度洋上丁香、象牙和奴隶贸易的中心；1822年的《莫尔斯比条约》开启了英国限制这一奴隶贸易的进程。

en: The Zerzari, also called the Zerzarok or Zarzariyya, were one of the oldest Kurdish tribes named in Arabic historiography and most likely a branch of the Hadhbani confederation of the Erbil region; their name is said to combine the Kurdish words for gold and child. Originally from the Erbil plain, by the fourteenth century they held a strategic mountain pocket between the Qandil range, Rawanduz, Lake Dukan and Ushnu, dominating the pass between Mongol-held Azerbaijan and the Jazira, and the geographer al-Umari, who died in 1349, described them as effectively independent of the great states. Zerzari horsemen served the Zengids, Artuqids and Ayyubids: the emir Shirkuh al-Zarzari commanded Ayyubid troops at the siege of Acre, while another chief, Nushirwan, pledged himself to al-Afdal after Saladin's death, and Imad al-Din al-Isfahani praised the tribe as cavalry who mocked the lion.
zh: 泽尔扎里人又称泽尔扎罗克或扎尔扎里耶，是阿拉伯史籍中最古老的库尔德部落之一，很可能是埃尔比勒地区哈兹班尼部落联盟的分支；据说其名称由库尔德语中“黄金”和“孩子”两个词组合而成。他们原居埃尔比勒平原，到14世纪时据守坎迪勒山、拉万杜兹、杜坎湖与乌什努之间的战略山谷，扼控蒙古人治下阿塞拜疆通往杰济拉的山口，卒于1349年的地理学家欧麦里记载他们实际上不受大国节制。泽尔扎里骑兵曾为赞吉王朝、阿尔图格王朝和阿尤布王朝效力：埃米尔谢尔库赫·扎尔扎里在阿卡围城战中统率阿尤布军队，另一位首领努希尔万在萨拉丁死后向阿夫达尔效忠，伊马德丁·伊斯法哈尼则称赞他们是敢于嘲弄雄狮的骑兵。

en: Zazzau, later called Zaria, was the southernmost of the seven true Hausa city-states, the Hausa Bakwai, whose ruling dynasties trace their origin to the legend of Bayajidda. Hausa tradition assigned it the part of sarkin bayi, king of slaves: its merchants raided and bought captives in the southern grasslands and traded them north, along with grain and leather, for Saharan salt and cloth, making the city a key junction of the caravan routes. Islam reached Zazzau only in the late 1450s, brought by clerics and traders from Kano and Katsina, and long sat alongside older Hausa spirit worship. The kingdom's great age came under the warrior queen Amina, who according to tradition reigned from 1576 to 1610, led her cavalry as far as the Niger-Benue confluence, forced Kano and Katsina to pay tribute, opened trade routes and left the earthen fortifications still remembered as Amina's walls. After her death the city weakened, passed under Jukun and Songhai influence and was renamed Zaria after the queen's sister, until the Fulani jihad swept over it in 1805 and replaced its old Hausa dynasty with an emirate.
zh: 扎造后称扎里亚，是豪萨七邦（七个“真正的”豪萨城邦）中位置最南的一个，其统治王朝按传说可追溯到巴亚吉达的故事。豪萨传统给它安排的角色是“奴隶之王”：商人从南方草原掳掠、收购人口，连同谷物和皮革一起北运，换回撒哈拉的盐和布匹，使这座城市成为驼队商路的关键枢纽。伊斯兰教迟至1450年代才随卡诺和卡齐纳的教士与商人传入，并且长期与豪萨本土的精灵崇拜并存。王国的鼎盛时代是在武人女王阿米娜治下：按传统说法她于1576至1610年在位，率骑兵远征至尼日尔河与贝努埃河交汇处，迫使卡诺和卡齐纳纳贡，开辟商路，留下后世所称的“阿米娜城墙”土方工事。她死后城邦转衰，先后受朱昆和桑海影响，并以女王之妹的名字改名扎里亚；1805年，富拉尼圣战席卷此地，以埃米尔国取代了旧豪萨王朝。

en: The Abau are a Papuan people of the upper Sepik country, living along the border between southern Sandaun Province in Papua New Guinea and Indonesian New Guinea. Their language belongs to the Sepik family and is noted for a whistled form of speech used alongside ordinary spoken Abau.
zh: 阿包人是塞皮克河上游的巴布亚族群，居住在巴布亚新几内亚桑道恩省南部与印度尼西亚新几内亚岛接壤的边境地带。他们的语言属塞皮克语族，除日常口语外还使用一套口哨语。

en: The Abazins, or Abaza, are a Northwest Caucasian people whose language is closest to Abkhaz and whose culture closely resembles that of the Circassians, with whom old maps often grouped their lands. Their earliest home lay in Abkhazia and along the coast around modern Sochi, where their ancestors made up the Abazg principality of the early centuries and the Abkhazian kingdom of the eighth century. From the seventh and eighth centuries small groups began crossing the main Caucasian range, and a large migration in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries carried them onto the northern slopes, into the valleys of the Kuban, Laba, Zelenchuk and Kuma; the early fifteenth-century chronicler of Timur even records a land called Abasa at the foot of Mount Elbrus. The migrants split into two main divisions, the Tapanta of the upper Kuban between the Besleney and Kabardian princes and the Ashkharua of the high mountains, each ruled by its own noble clans. They herded livestock and farmed the river valleys, and through contact with the Nogais and Muslim merchants from the sixteenth century onward they gradually adopted Sunni Islam. As the Russian Empire pushed beyond the Kuban in the early nineteenth century, the Abazins joined the Circassian and Abkhaz resistance in the Caucasian War, raiding Russian lines and suffering punitive expeditions, such as the one recorded by General Yermolov, while an Abazin-Circassian assault on Stavropol was reported in 1835.
zh: 阿巴扎人（又称阿巴扎）是西北高加索民族，语言与阿布哈兹语最接近，风俗则与切尔克斯人类似，旧时地图常把他们的土地一并划入切尔克西亚。他们最早的家园在阿布哈兹和今索契一带沿海，先民曾构成公元初几个世纪的阿巴兹格公国以及8世纪的阿布哈兹王国。7至8世纪起，小批阿巴扎人开始翻越大高加索山脉，13至14世纪的大规模迁徙更把他们带到北坡的库班河、拉巴河、泽连丘克河和库马河谷地；帖木儿的史官在15世纪初也记下了厄尔布鲁士山脚下一处叫阿巴萨的地方。迁徙者分成两大支：居于库班河上游、夹在别斯列涅伊与卡巴尔达王公之间的塔潘塔人，以及深山里的阿什哈鲁阿人，各由本族贵族氏族统辖。他们在河谷放牧耕种，16世纪起通过与诺盖人和穆斯林商人的接触逐渐改宗逊尼派伊斯兰教。19世纪初俄罗斯帝国越过库班河扩张，阿巴扎人加入切尔克斯人与阿布哈兹人的抵抗，投身高加索战争，不断袭击俄军防线并招致惩罚性远征，叶尔莫洛夫将军就记下过其中一次；1835年还有文献提到阿巴扎-切尔克斯联军攻打斯塔夫罗波尔。

en: The Abipones were a Guaicuruan-speaking people of the Gran Chaco, kin to the Toba and Mocoví, whose original home lay along the lower Bermejo River in present-day northern Argentina. Seasonally mobile hunters, fishers and gatherers with only limited farming, they took to the horse after contact: by 1641 they had abandoned agriculture for cattle and horse raiding, striking as far as Asunción and Corrientes and earning the name frentones for their half-shaven heads. Pressured by Spaniards and the Toba, they shifted south to the country between the Bermejo and Salado rivers. From 1710 Spanish campaigns gradually broke their power, and by 1750 Jesuit missions, notably those of Martin Dobrizhoffer, had settled and Christianized them. Disease had cut their numbers below five thousand by 1768, when the expulsion of the Jesuits left them without protectors; within half a century raids by the Toba and Mocoví and the loss of their lands ended the Abipones as an independent people, with the last speakers of their language dying out in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 阿比庞人是大查科的瓜伊库鲁语族群，与托巴人、莫科维人同源，最初住在今阿根廷北部的贝尔梅霍河下游。他们随季节迁徙，以狩猎、渔捞和采集为生，只兼营少量农业；接触欧洲人后迅速掌握马匹，到1641年已放弃农耕，转而劫掠牛群和马匹，兵锋远及亚松森和科连特斯，并因剃去前半头发的习俗被称为弗伦托内人。在西班牙人和托巴人的挤压下，他们南迁到贝尔梅霍河与萨拉多河之间。1710年起，西班牙人的军事行动逐步削弱他们的力量；到1750年，耶稣会传教站（尤以马丁·多布利茨霍费尔主持的为代表）已使他们定居并皈依基督教。到1768年，疫病使人口降至五千以下，同年耶稣会被驱逐，他们失去庇护；此后不到半个世纪，托巴人和莫科维人的袭扰加上土地沦丧，使阿比庞人作为独立族群消亡，其语言的最后使用者也在19世纪初离世。

en: The Abitibi are an Algonquian Anishinaabe people whose homeland centres on Lake Abitibi and the neighbouring Témiscamingue forests, on the present-day border of Ontario and Quebec. Families gathered on the lake shore in summer and scattered to their family hunting grounds in autumn, living by hunting, fishing and gathering; in later centuries they were known as the Abitibiwinni.
zh: 阿比蒂比人是说阿尔冈昆语的阿尼希纳贝族群，家园以阿比蒂比湖及邻近的泰米斯卡明森林为中心，地处今安大略与魁北克交界一带。各家族夏天在湖边聚会，入秋后分散到各自的家族猎场，以狩猎、渔捞和采集为生；在后来的几个世纪里他们被称为阿比蒂比温尼人。

en: The Abkhaz are a Northwest Caucasian people of the northeastern Black Sea coast, whose Abkhaz language is closest to Abaza and whose ancestors, known to Greek and Roman writers as the Heniochi and Abasgoi, traded with the Greek colonies of Dioskourias and Pitiunt. Under Byzantine influence Christianity became dominant in the sixth century, and in 780 their princes founded the Kingdom of Abkhazia, which in 978 passed by dynastic union to Bagrat III and became the nucleus of the unified Kingdom of Georgia. Abkhazia then formed the Duchy of Tskhumi, held from the twelfth century by the Sharvashidze house, while Genoese merchants briefly ran trading factories along its coast in the fourteenth. The collapse of Georgian unity in the 1450s and 1460s left the Sharvashidzes ruling an independent Principality of Abkhazia, only nominally subject to Imereti and Mingrelia. From the sixteenth century Ottoman suzerainty reached the coast, and over the 1500s and 1600s much of the population, including its ruling family, turned to Sunni Islam while keeping strong pre-Abrahamic customs. In 1810 Prince Sefer Ali-Bey accepted Russian protection, and during the 1810s to 1830s Abkhazia was drawn into the Caucasian War, with Russian garrisons, mountain resistance and the first waves of Muslim emigration to the Ottoman Empire shaping its society. Traditionally the Abkhaz lived by cattle breeding, beekeeping, viticulture and farming, and acquired a reputation for unusual longevity.
zh: 阿布哈兹人是黑海东北岸的西北高加索民族，所说的阿布哈兹语与阿巴扎语最接近。古希腊、罗马作家把他们的先民称作赫尼奥奇人和阿巴斯格伊人，他们曾与狄奥斯库里亚斯、皮季温图斯等希腊殖民地通商。6世纪时，在拜占庭影响下基督教成为主要信仰；780年，他们的王公建立阿布哈兹王国，978年该王国经王朝联合归于巴格拉特三世，成为统一的格鲁吉亚王国的核心。此后阿布哈兹成为茨胡米公国，12世纪起由沙尔瓦希泽家族统治，14世纪热那亚商人还曾在其沿海短暂设立商站。15世纪50至60年代格鲁吉亚统一瓦解，沙尔瓦希泽家族得以统治独立的阿布哈兹公国，仅在名义上臣属伊梅列季亚和明格列利亚。16世纪起，奥斯曼的宗主权伸到黑海沿岸，16至17世纪间，包括统治家族在内的大量居民改宗逊尼派伊斯兰教，同时仍保留浓厚的前亚伯拉罕信仰习俗。1810年，王公塞费尔·阿里-贝伊接受俄国保护，1810至1830年代阿布哈兹被卷入高加索战争，俄军驻防、山民抵抗以及穆斯林首批迁往奥斯曼帝国的浪潮共同重塑了当地社会。阿布哈兹人传统上以畜牧、养蜂、葡萄种植和农耕为生，并以长寿闻名。

en: The Abun are a coastal people of the northwestern Bird's Head Peninsula, occupying four villages around Sausapor in the Tambrauw country of present-day Indonesia's Southwest Papua region. Their own tradition remembers them as the Wen of the Tambrauw, or Ndokdar, Mountains; after groups moved down to the shore and mixed with Biak seafarers they were called Karon, meaning people from within, while the kin who stayed in the hills became known as Karondori. When that name acquired hostile overtones they took the word Abun, originally the name of their language and meaning tribal language. Linguists count Abun, with its four dialects and tone contrasts, as an isolate, its maritime vocabulary borrowed from Biak. The Abun are above all banana growers, recognising twenty-one kinds of banana, and their villages, called wis, are governed by a headman named Yekwesu with a deputy, the Yehos, whose authority rests on bravery, generosity and wealth in Timor cloth. Their Salara dance enacts the founding memory of ancestors who took snake form and led the people from the mountains to the beach. On this coast the Portuguese Jorge de Menezes landed in 1526, and from the sixteenth century Tidore's overlordship over the Bird's Head reached the Sausapor shore through Biak and Malukan middlemen.
zh: 阿本人是多贝拉伊半岛西北部的沿海族群，在今印度尼西亚西南巴布亚地区坦布劳一带的绍萨波尔附近占有四座村庄。按本族传说，他们原是坦布劳山（当地称恩多克达尔山）的温人；部分人下到海边、与比亚克航海者混居后，被称为卡龙，意为“来自内陆的人”，留在山里的亲族则称卡龙多里。后来这个称呼带上敌意，他们便改用“阿本”一词，它原是本族语言的名字，意为“部族之语”。阿本语有四种方言和声调对立，语言学家多视为孤立语言，其中的海洋词汇借自比亚克语。阿本人尤重种植香蕉，能分辨二十一种香蕉；他们的村庄称维斯，由名耶克韦苏的头人治理，副手名耶霍斯，头人的权威靠勇武、慷慨和积蓄帝汶布得来。他们的萨拉拉舞演绎着祖先化身为蛇、率族人从山中走向海滨的起源记忆。1526年，葡萄牙人豪尔赫·德·梅内塞斯就在这段海岸登陆，16世纪起，蒂多雷对多贝拉伊半岛的宗主权又经比亚克与摩鹿加中间商延伸到绍萨波尔沿岸。

en: The Acaxee were a Taracahitic-speaking people of the Uto-Aztecan family who held the rugged Sierra Madre Occidental of eastern Sinaloa and north-western Durango, the mountain country around Topia and Badiraguato. Before the Spanish came they numbered perhaps twenty thousand, living in dispersed extended-family farmsteads grouped into many small autonomous chiefdoms that accepted a common leader only in wartime; they farmed maize and beans where the steep land allowed and relied on hunting, fishing and gathering for the rest. A warlike people, they kept up constant feuds with their neighbours the Xixime, and Spanish chroniclers accused both groups of eating slain enemies. The conquest of Sinaloa in 1529 to 1531 opened their mountains to encomienda raids and Old World epidemics, and in December 1601 an elder named Perico led the Acaxee Rebellion, which was crushed; Jesuit missionaries then began their conversion in 1602, and over the colonial centuries the Acaxee merged into the mestizo society of Nueva Vizcaya.
zh: 阿卡塞人属犹他—阿兹特克语系的塔拉卡希特语支，盘踞在锡那罗亚东部和杜兰戈西北部的西马德雷山脉腹地，即托皮亚和巴迪拉瓜托一带的山区。西班牙人到来之前，他们约有两万人，以分散的大家庭农庄聚居，分成许多互不统属的小酋邦，只有战时才共推首领；他们在坡地允许的地方种植玉米和菜豆，其余食物靠狩猎、捕鱼和采集。阿卡塞人尚武，与邻族希希梅人长期仇杀，西班牙编年史家指控两族都食用战死的敌人。1529至1531年西班牙征服锡那罗亚后，监护征赋制的征掠和旧大陆传染病传入山区；1601年12月，一位名叫佩里科的长者领导阿卡塞起义，最终遭到镇压。1602年起耶稣会传教士开始让他们改宗；在整个殖民时代，阿卡塞人逐渐融入新比斯开的混血社会。

en: The Acciaioli were a Florentine noble and banking house whose line runs back to Gugliarello Acciaioli, said to have moved from Brescia to Florence in 1160 as a Guelph fleeing Frederick Barbarossa. In the thirteenth century they founded the Compagna di Ser Leone, a bank with branches from Greece to western Europe, which shared the great crash of 1345 when Edward III of England and other crowned borrowers defaulted; the family stayed at the centre of Florentine politics nonetheless, and Bishop Angiolo Acciaioli briefly governed the city after the fall of Gauthier de Brienne in 1343. Their wider fame came in the Levant, where Niccolò Acciaioli, soldier and statesman to the Angevin kings of Naples, built up estates in the Morea, and his kinsman Nerio I seized Athens from its Catalan rulers in 1388 to become the first Acciaioli duke. The family held the Duchy of Athens, with a Venetian interlude from 1395 to 1402, until the Ottoman Turks overwhelmed it in 1456 and 1458, Francesco II being the last duke. In Florence the Acciaioli then attached themselves to the Albizzi and the Medici, producing scholars such as Donato Acciaioli, while a branch settled on Madeira after 1512.
zh: 阿恰约利家族是佛罗伦萨的贵族与银行世家，世系可上溯至古利亚雷洛·阿恰约利：据说他身为圭尔夫派，为躲避腓特烈·巴巴罗萨，于1160年从布雷西亚迁居佛罗伦萨。13世纪他们创办了塞莱奥内合伙银行，分行从希腊一直开到西欧；1345年英格兰国王爱德华三世等头戴王冠的借款人违约，这家银行也在那场大崩溃中倒闭。但家族仍处于佛罗伦萨政治的中心，1343年戈蒂埃·德·布里耶纳倒台后，安焦洛·阿恰约利主教曾短暂主政该城。他们更大的名望来自黎凡特：军人兼政治家尼科洛·阿恰约利效力于那不勒斯安茹诸王，在摩里亚积累了大片地产；其族人内里奥一世于1388年从加泰罗尼亚统治者手中夺取雅典，成为第一位阿恰约利公爵。家族统治雅典公国，其间1395至1402年一度被威尼斯接管，直到1456至1458年被奥斯曼土耳其攻灭，弗朗切斯科二世是末代公爵。此后在佛罗伦萨，阿恰约利家族先后依附阿尔比齐家族和美第奇家族，还出了多纳托·阿恰约利这样的学者；另有一支在1512年后定居马德拉岛。

en: The Accawmacke, or Accomac, were an Algonquian-speaking people of the Eastern Shore of Virginia, the long peninsula between Chesapeake Bay and the Atlantic, whose name means the place on the other side of the water, for they lay across the bay from the Powhatan homeland of Tsenacomoco. Their main village, also called Accomac, stood near Cherrystone Inlet, and they were loosely linked to the Powhatan Confederacy while keeping their own paramount chiefs. English contact began in 1608, when the colonists found about eighty warriors under the chief Debedeavon, whom they called the Laughing King and took as an ally; epidemics reaching the shore as early as the Roanoke venture of 1585 had already thinned their numbers. Disease and colonial pressure cut their population by roughly ninety percent by 1700, and the English came to apply the name Accomac to every native group east of Chesapeake Bay. The remnant held communal lands in Accomack County until 1812, and the related Gingaskin band was driven out after Nat Turner's Rebellion of 1831.
zh: 阿卡瓦马基人（亦作阿科马克人）是弗吉尼亚东岸——切萨皮克湾与大西洋之间的长半岛——上的阿尔冈昆语民族；其名字意为“水对岸之地”，因为他们住在与波瓦坦故土切纳科莫科隔湾相望的地方。他们的主村也叫阿科马克，位于切里斯通湾附近；他们与波瓦坦联盟关系松散，但保留着自己的大酋长。1608年英国殖民者到来时，其首领德贝德冯被称为“欢笑之王”并与殖民者结盟，当时约有八十名战士；而早在1585年罗阿诺克殖民活动带来的疫病就已削减了他们的人口。到1700年，疾病和殖民者的压迫使其人口减少约九成，英国人进而把切萨皮克湾以东的所有原住民群体都称作阿科马克。残存者在阿科马克县保有公有土地直至1812年，与其亲缘的金加斯金群体则在1831年纳特·特纳起义后被逐走。

en: The Acehnese are an Austronesian people of the northern tip of Sumatra, whose forebears were Chamic speakers who crossed from the Southeast Asian mainland around the beginning of the Common Era and blended with older local populations and later Malay, Minangkabau, Indian and Arab settlers. Earlier Hindu and Buddhist influences gave way to Islam through Indian Ocean trade, and in 1267 the port kingdom of Samudera Pasai became one of the earliest Muslim states in the region; when Marco Polo passed through in 1292 the coast was divided among several small kingdoms. In 1337 Pasai and neighboring Peureulak were thriving commercial ports, and the Acehnese language, a Chamic tongue related to the languages of Champa, was spreading along the coast. Around 1496 Ali Mughayat Syah founded the Aceh Sultanate, which absorbed Pasai in 1524 and grew into a major power of the Strait of Malacca, rivaling Portuguese Malacca and Johor in the pepper trade and reaching its height under Sultan Iskandar Muda in the early seventeenth century, when its court was also a center of Islamic scholarship. Acehnese society was organized into villages called gampong grouped into mukim districts, with a tradition of communal life, wet-rice farming, metalwork and weaving.
zh: 亚齐人是居住在苏门答腊岛最北端的南岛语系民族，其先民是公元初年前后从东南亚大陆渡海而来的占语使用者，他们与当地更早的居民以及后来的马来人、米南加保人、印度人和阿拉伯移民相融合。早期的印度教和佛教影响随着印度洋贸易逐渐被伊斯兰教取代，1267年，港口王国苏木都剌–巴赛成为这一地区最早的穆斯林政权之一；1292年马可·波罗经过时，沿海仍分属若干小王国。1337年时，巴赛和邻近的佩雷拉克已是繁盛的商港，而与占婆诸语言同源的占语支亚齐语正沿沿海地带传播。约1496年，阿里·穆加亚特·沙建立亚齐苏丹国，1524年吞并巴赛，此后发展为马六甲海峡的强权，在胡椒贸易中与葡属马六甲和柔佛争雄，并在17世纪初苏丹伊斯坎达尔·穆达治下达到鼎盛，其宫廷同时也是伊斯兰学术中心。亚齐人的社会以名为“甘邦”的村落为基础，村落又组成“穆金”行政区，传统上盛行集体生活、水稻种植、金属加工和纺织。

en: The Achagua are an Arawakan, or Maipurean, people of the Orinoco llanos, whose territory at contact covered the basins of the Casanare, Meta and Apure rivers in eastern Colombia and western Venezuela. They were the most numerous people of those plains, perhaps more than thirty thousand strong, living in large villages where clans shared communal houses, farming bitter cassava and poisoning their arrow points with curare. Their towns formed a wide trading network that ran on its own currency, strings of quiripa shell beads. Many Achagua were later gathered into Jesuit missions, where they lived until the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767; afterward fresh waves of colonists seized their lands and successive epidemics greatly reduced their numbers. Small Achagua communities survive in the Colombian departments of Meta and Casanare.
zh: 阿查瓜人是奥里诺科平原的阿拉瓦克语（迈普雷语支）族群，欧洲人到来时，其领地覆盖今哥伦比亚东部和委内瑞拉西部的卡萨纳雷河、梅塔河与阿普雷河流域。他们是这片平原上人口最多的族群，可能超过三万人，居住在大型村落里，各氏族共住长屋，种植苦木薯，并用箭毒涂抹箭头。他们的村镇构成广阔的贸易网，还使用自己的货币——成串的基里帕贝壳珠。后来许多阿查瓜人被集中到耶稣会传教站，在那里生活到1767年耶稣会被驱逐；此后新的殖民浪潮夺走他们的土地，接连的瘟疫又使人口锐减。在哥伦比亚的梅塔省和卡萨纳雷省，一直有小型的阿查瓜社群存留。

en: The Aché, once called Guayakí by their Guaraní-speaking neighbours, are nomadic hunter-gatherers of the forests of eastern Paraguay. Stone axes like theirs have been dated to some nine thousand years ago, and around 500 CE the arrival of Guaraní horticulturists, who raided them and pushed them away from the rivers into wooded hills, may have confirmed their strictly foraging way of life: small roaming bands living on palm pith, roots, fruit and game, with the thunder spirit Berendy at the centre of their beliefs. Their language pairs a Tupí-Guaraní vocabulary with a grammar unlike its sister tongues. The earliest Jesuit archives mention them around 1620 under the name Caaygua, and in the 1630s several bands seized near the mouth of the Acaray River were forcibly settled in a Guaraní mission, where all died of disease within months. They eluded every later attempt at settlement, and after the Jesuit expulsion of 1768 they kept to a forest life beyond colonial observation for the rest of the period.
zh: 阿切人是巴拉圭东部森林中的游猎采集族群，邻近的瓜拉尼语族群曾称他们为瓜亚基人。与他们所用石斧相似的器物可追溯到约九千年前；约公元500年，从事园艺的瓜拉尼人迁入，袭击并把他们从河边赶入林木覆盖的丘陵，这或许促使他们走上纯粹的取食之路：以小群体游荡为生，靠棕榈髓、块根、野果和猎物过活，信仰中雷神贝伦迪居于核心地位。他们的语言有着图皮-瓜拉尼语的词汇，语法却与姊妹语言不同。约1620年，最早的耶稣会档案以卡伊瓜之名提到他们；17世纪30年代，在阿卡拉伊河口附近被掳走的若干群体被强行安置进一座瓜拉尼传教镇，数月内全部死于疾病。此后他们躲过了一切定居尝试，1768年耶稣会被驱逐后，仍在殖民视野之外的森林中生活。

en: The Achomawi, whose name means river people, are the nine northerly bands of the Pit River Indians of northeastern California, holding both banks of the Pit River from Goose Lake down to Montgomery Creek, with the closely related Atsugewi in the Hat Creek valley beside them. Their Palaihnihan language is grouped with Yana and the Shastan languages within the proposed Hokan phylum. Each band kept a central village with smaller satellite settlements, spending the summer in cone-shaped tule-mat lodges and wintering in semisubterranean houses of bark and earth; they took salmon and deer, gathered acorns and roots, and worked obsidian from Glass Mountain into arrowheads. The bow and arrow reached the valley around 200, and in later centuries horse-mounted Klamath raiders carried them off as slaves. Fur trappers began passing through from 1827, and epidemics in the 1830s thinned the Pit River villages before any settler had occupied their land.
zh: 阿乔马维人名字的意思是“河民”，是加利福尼亚东北部皮特河印第安人中北方九支的合称，占据从古斯湖到蒙哥马利溪的皮特河两岸，关系密切的阿楚格维人则住在旁边的哈特溪谷地。他们的帕莱尼汉语与亚纳语、沙斯塔诸语一起被归入拟议中的霍坎大语系。每个支派都有一个中心村落和若干卫星小村：夏天住香蒲席搭成的锥形棚屋，冬天搬进半地穴式的树皮土屋；他们捕鲑鱼、猎鹿、采橡子和根茎，并用格拉斯山的黑曜石打制箭头。弓箭约在200年前后传入这一河谷，较晚的世纪里，骑马的克拉马斯袭掠者常把他们掳为奴隶。1827年起毛皮猎人开始途经此地，19世纪30年代的传染病在移民占地之前就已使皮特河诸村人口大减。

en: The Achomi, who call themselves Khodmooni and are also known as Laris or Larestanis, are a Southwestern Iranian people of the arid southern Persian region of Irahistan, the present-day Larestan district of Fars, centred on towns such as Lar, Khonj and Bastak. Their Achomi tongue, also called Lari, descends from Middle Persian and is not mutually intelligible with standard Persian, and most are Sunni Muslims of the Shafi'i school with a smaller Shia minority. They have been linked to the Utians named by Herodotus and to the Persian tribe of Ira recorded in Sasanian sources, and from the early twelfth century Laristan was ruled by the local Miladian dynasty, whose lords made Lar a southern trade hub during the thirteenth century. Ibn Battuta passed through Khonj in 1333 and left an admiring account of its Shafi'i hermits. The local rulers kept their autonomy until the Safavids deposed them in 1610 under Shah Abbas I, and after the fall of Isfahan in 1722 the region passed through Afghan and Nader Shahi rule, with Bastak emerging as its leading town. As Persian Gulf traders many Achomi also settled on the Arab shore, where they became known as Ajam or Huwala.
zh: 阿乔姆人自称霍德穆尼，又称拉尔人或拉雷斯坦人，是西南伊朗语民族，居住在波斯南部干旱的伊拉希斯坦地区，即今法尔斯省的拉雷斯坦，以拉尔、洪季、巴斯塔克等城镇为中心。他们的阿乔姆语又称拉里语，由中古波斯语演变而来，与标准波斯语互不相通；居民多为沙斐仪派逊尼穆斯林，也有少数什叶派。他们被认为与希罗多德笔下的乌提亚人以及萨珊文献记载的波斯伊拉部落有关；12世纪初起，拉雷斯坦由本地的米拉丁王朝统治，其王公在13世纪把拉尔建成南方贸易重镇。1333年伊本·白图泰途经洪季，在游记中盛赞当地沙斐仪派隐修者的虔诚。本地统治者保持自治，直到1610年萨菲王朝的阿拔斯一世将他们废黜；1722年伊斯法罕陷落后，该地先后经历阿富汗人与纳迪尔沙的统治，巴斯塔克随之崛起为首要城镇。许多阿乔姆人作为波斯湾商人定居阿拉伯沿岸，在当地被称为阿贾姆或胡瓦拉。

en: The Acolapissa were a small Muskogean-speaking people of the Southeastern Woodlands who lived along the Pearl River, between present-day Louisiana and Mississippi, in at least six villages. Their language was close to Choctaw and Chickasaw, and their name is read in Choctaw as okla pisa, those who look out for people. In 1699 a band of Chickasaw led by two English slave traders raided their villages to carry off captives for sale in Charleston. Around 1702 the Acolapissa moved to a bayou north of Lake Pontchartrain and gave shelter to the Natchitoches, then in 1722 shifted west toward the future site of New Orleans. Weakened by French settlement and European diseases, they merged with the Bayogoula and by 1739 had been absorbed into the Houma, disappearing as a separate tribe.
zh: 阿科拉皮萨人是东南林地的一个小型穆斯科格语族群，住在今路易斯安那与密西西比之间的珀尔河沿岸，至少有六个村落。他们的语言与乔克托语、奇克索语相近，其族名在乔克托语中可解作 okla pisa，即“守护众人者”。1699年，一队由两名英国奴隶贩子带领的奇克索人袭击了他们的村庄，掳掠人口卖到查尔斯顿。约1702年，阿科拉皮萨人迁到庞恰特雷恩湖北岸的一条河口，并收留了纳基托什人；1722年又西迁到后来的新奥尔良一带。在法国殖民和欧洲疾病的打击下，他们与巴约古拉人合并，到1739年已被霍马人吸收，不再作为独立部落存在。

en: The Adamawa are the many peoples of the Adamawa Plateau and the upper Benue valley, a grassy upland spanning eastern Nigeria and northern Cameroon, whose eighty or so related languages Joseph Greenberg grouped in the Adamawa branch of the Niger-Congo family; the Mumuye, around the Benue headwaters, are the largest single group. In the Benue lowlands the multi-ethnic Kwararafa confederacy, whose capitals moved from Santolo to Pindiga and later Wukari, grew rich on the salt trade before 1500. Its cavalry raided the Hausa cities to the north and in 1680 even sacked Ngazargamu, the capital of Bornu, before decline set in during the eighteenth century. A Chamba invasion drove its last king into exile about 1810, and a Jukun dynasty at Wukari inherited the remnants. Meanwhile Fulbe pastoralists had settled among the plateau peoples, and in 1809 Modibo Adama, a lieutenant of Usman dan Fodio, carried the Fulani jihad into the region and founded the Adamawa Emirate, building its power on cavalry conquest and slave raiding among the hill societies through the 1830s.
zh: 阿达马瓦人是阿达马瓦高原和贝努埃河上游众多族群的统称，这片草原高地横跨尼日利亚东部与喀麦隆北部；约瑟夫·格林伯格把他们约八十种互有亲缘的语言归入尼日尔—刚果语系的阿达马瓦语支，其中聚居于贝努埃河源一带的穆穆耶人是最大的一支。在贝努埃低地，多族群的夸拉拉法联盟以盐业致富，1500年以前已经兴起，都城先后从桑托洛迁到平迪加、再迁武卡里。它的骑兵不断北侵豪萨诸城，1680年甚至攻掠博尔诺首都恩加扎尔加穆，18世纪才走向衰落。约1810年，昌巴人的入侵把末代国王逐走，武卡里的朱昆王朝接管了联盟残余。与此同时，富拉尼牧民早已定居在高原各族之间；1809年，奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥的部将莫迪博·阿达玛把富拉尼圣战带入此地，建立阿达马瓦酋长国，在19世纪30年代以骑兵征服和掠奴为手段，将山地诸族置于富拉尼人统治之下。

en: The Adharis are the Iranian-speaking population of northwestern Iran and the eastern Caucasus before Turkification, whose tongue, Old Azari or Adharic, was a Northwestern Iranian language akin to Talysh and Tati. Arab geographers recorded Adhari dialects across Azerbaijan and the Caspian coast, whose settled peasants, including the followers of Babak's ninth-century revolt, spoke them alongside standard Persian; poets such as Qatran of Tabriz and Nizami of Ganja grew out of this Iranian milieu. North of the Aras the same Persianate stock formed the Tats, partly descended from Sasanian garrisons planted under Khosrow I, who became the townsmen and farmers of Shirvan and Baku under the long-lived Shirvanshah dynasty. Oghuz Turkic spread after the Seljuk arrival in the eleventh century and accelerated under the Mongols, yet as late as the 1340s the chronicler Mostawfi still called the speech of Maragheh and Zanjan modified Pahlavi, and Tabriz remained Iranian-speaking through the fourteenth century. Adhari lost its majority status during the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, surviving only in mountain enclaves such as Harzand; the Shirvanshahs fell to the Safavids in 1538, and the Tats were gradually absorbed into the Azerbaijani Turkish identity, with small pockets near Baku and Dagestan keeping their language.
zh: 阿扎里人是突厥化之前伊朗西北部和高加索东部的伊朗语居民，其语言古阿扎里语属西北伊朗语，与塔雷什语和塔特语相近。阿拉伯地理学家记载，阿扎里方言通行于阿塞拜疆和里海沿岸，当地定居农民包括9世纪巴贝克起义的追随者在内，兼通标准波斯语；大不里士的卡特兰和甘贾的尼扎米等诗人便出自这一伊朗文化土壤。阿拉斯河以北，同源的波斯裔居民构成塔特人，其先民部分来自霍斯劳一世时期部署的萨珊戍军，在国祚绵长的希尔万沙王朝治下成为希尔万和巴库的市民与农夫。乌古斯突厥语自11世纪塞尔柱人到来后扩散，蒙古时期进一步加快，但直到1340年代史家穆斯陶菲仍称马拉盖和赞詹的语言为变化了的巴列维语，大不里士到14世纪仍讲伊朗语。阿扎里语在15至16世纪失去主体语言地位，只在哈尔赞德等山地飞地留存；希尔万沙王朝于1538年被萨法维王朝吞并，塔特人则慢慢融入阿塞拜疆突厥认同，仅巴库和达吉斯坦附近的小块地区保留其语言。

en: The Adzera are an Austronesian-speaking people of the upper Markham Valley in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea, whose villages reach into the mountainous Wantoat and Leron country. Their Markham language, unusual for an Oceanic tongue in being spoken well inland, falls into six dialects and bears heavy influence from the neighbouring Trans-New Guinea languages.
zh: 阿泽拉人是巴布亚新几内亚莫罗贝省马克姆河谷上游说南岛语的族群，村落一直延伸到万托阿特和莱龙的山地。他们的马卡姆语是少数深入内陆通行的大洋洲语言，内部分为六种方言，并深受邻近跨新几内亚语言的影响。

en: The Aekyom, also known as the Awin, are a Papuan people of northern Western Province in Papua New Guinea, centred on the Elevala River country around Kiunga near the Indonesian border. Their Aekyom language forms the Awin-Pa subgroup of the Kamula-Elevala family, itself part of the Awyu-Ok branch of the Trans-New Guinea languages.
zh: 埃克约姆人又称阿温人，是巴布亚新几内亚西部省北部的巴布亚族群，聚居于靠近印度尼西亚边境、基温加一带的埃莱瓦拉河流域。他们的埃克约姆语与帕尔语组成卡穆拉-埃莱瓦拉语系下的阿温-帕尔语支，该语系属于跨新几内亚语系的阿维尤-奥克分支。

en: The Aeta, also called Agta or Dumagat, are the Negrito peoples of Luzon and among the earliest inhabitants of the Philippines, reaching the islands tens of thousands of years ago across the land bridges of the Sunda shelf, long before the Austronesian expansion. They are small-statured, dark-skinned and curly-haired forest people, related to the Semang of Malaya and the Andamanese, and after the Austronesian arrival they absorbed both settlers and words, so that their recorded languages are Austronesian tongues rich in an older non-Austronesian vocabulary. Historically they lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers in mobile bands of a few families, moving through the Zambales and Sierra Madre ranges and the Cagayan hinterland with bow and arrow, trading wax, rattan and forest game for lowland rice and iron. Their name goes back to a proto-Malayo-Polynesian word for dark-skinned person. After the Spanish conquest of Luzon in 1571 the colonizers found them fierce and elusive: Miguel Lopez de Legazpi's men reported their proverbial marksmanship and iron weapons, but every attempt to settle them in reduccion villages failed, for the Aeta simply withdrew deeper into the mountains. They suffered heavily from slaving raids, particularly by Zambal raiders who sold captives on to Borneo and China, yet their scattered bands preserved a mobile forest life and an animist religion of mountain and ancestor spirits through the whole Spanish period.
zh: 阿埃塔人又称阿格塔人或杜马加特人，是吕宋的尼格利陀（矮黑人）族群，也是菲律宾最古老的居民之一：早在南岛语族扩张之前数万年前，他们便经巽他古陆的陆桥来到群岛。他们身材矮小、肤色深暗、头发卷曲，与马来半岛的塞芒人和安达曼人有亲缘关系；南岛语族到来后，他们与移民融合并借入大量词汇，因此其语言属于南岛语系，却保留着古老的非南岛语底层词。历史上他们是游猎采集者，以几户家庭为小队，持弓箭穿梭于三描礼士山、马德雷山脉和加牙因内地，用蜂蜡、藤条和猎物与低地人交换稻米和铁器。其族名可追溯至原始马来-波利尼西亚语中意为“深肤色的人”的词。1571年西班牙征服吕宋后，殖民者发现他们善战而难以捉摸：黎牙实比的部下曾记载他们神准的箭术和铁制武器，但每次试图把他们赶进“集村”定居都告失败，因为阿埃塔人径直退入更深的山林。他们还深受掳奴之害，尤其是三描礼士袭击者把俘虏转卖到婆罗洲和中国；尽管如此，这些分散的小队在整个西班牙时期仍保持着流动的山林生活和敬拜山灵与祖灵的万物有灵信仰。

en: The Afar, long called the Danakil, are East Cushitic-speaking pastoralists of the arid triangle between the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden and the Ethiopian highlands, where they herd camels, goats and sheep and mine the salt of the desert plains. The Andalusian writer Ibn Sa'id placed the Dankal along the coast from Suakin to Zeila in the thirteenth century, and Ethiopian chronicles of Amda Seyon's wars call their country Adal. Organized into more than a hundred and fifty clans under two ranked divisions, the noble Asaimara and the commoner Adoimara, they lived from the caravan and salt trades and were split among petty sultanates. In 1577 the Adal imam Muhammed Jasa moved his capital from Harar to Aussa among the Afar, but the local Mudaito clan destroyed that imamate in 1672 and in 1734, under Data Kadafo, founded the Sultanate of Aussa, the leading Afar monarchy, whose rulers held sway over the lower Awash. The Mudaito consolidated their power at the Battle of Darma in 1834 and kept the Danakil country independent through the mid-nineteenth century.
zh: 阿法尔人旧称达纳基勒人，是操东库希特语的游牧族群，活跃在红海、亚丁湾与埃塞俄比亚高原之间的干旱三角地带，放牧骆驼、山羊和绵羊，并开采荒漠平原上的盐。13世纪安达卢西亚作家伊本·赛义德记载，丹卡尔人分布在从萨瓦金到泽拉的沿海地带；阿姆达·塞约恩征战时期的埃塞俄比亚编年史把他们的家乡称为阿达尔。阿法尔社会分为贵族阿萨伊马拉和平民阿多伊马拉两个等级，下分一百五十多个氏族，靠商队和食盐贸易为生，并分裂为若干小苏丹国。1577年，阿达尔伊玛目穆罕默德·贾萨把首都从哈勒尔迁到阿法尔人中的奥萨，但当地的穆达伊托氏族于1672年攻灭该伊玛目政权，并于1734年在达塔·卡达夫领导下建立奥萨苏丹国，成为阿法尔人的首要王权，统治阿瓦什河下游。1834年穆达伊托人在达尔马战役中巩固了权力，并使达纳基勒地区在19世纪中叶保持独立。

en: The Afghans, known in later usage as the Pashtuns, are an Eastern Iranian people speaking Pashto, organized into a large confederation of tribes between the Sulayman Mountains and the Indus valley, where their earliest mention in a written source places them in 982. Afghan warriors marched with the armies of Mahmud of Ghazni into northern India, and Afghan dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate, the Khalji and then the Lodi, held Delhi until the Lodi sultan Ibrahim was defeated by Babur in 1526. Tribal life was governed by the jirga council and the Pashtunwali code of honour, celebrated in the seventeenth-century poetry of Khushal Khan Khattak and Rahman Baba. In 1722 the Hotak clan rose against Safavid rule and briefly held much of Persia, and in 1747 Ahmad Shah Durrani united the tribes from Kandahar into an empire stretching from Khorasan to the Punjab. After the Durrani decline, the Mohammadzai branch of the Barakzai took power around 1826.
zh: 阿富汗人即后世所称的普什图人，是讲普什图语的东伊朗语族群，以庞大的部落联盟形式生活在苏莱曼山脉与印度河流域之间；现存最早的文献记载在982年已把他们置于这一带。阿富汗战士曾随伽色尼的马哈茂德的大军攻入北印度，德里苏丹国的卡尔吉王朝和其后的洛迪王朝都由阿富汗人建立，洛迪苏丹易卜拉欣直到1526年才被巴布尔击败。部落事务由支尔格会议和名为普什图瓦里的荣誉准则支配，17世纪诗人胡沙尔·汗·哈塔克与拉赫曼·巴巴的诗作便歌颂这种生活。1722年，汉达基部族起兵反抗萨法维王朝，一度据有波斯大部；1747年，艾哈迈德·沙·杜兰尼在坎大哈统一各部落，建立起疆域从呼罗珊延伸到旁遮普的帝国。杜兰尼王朝衰落后，巴拉克宰的穆罕默德扎伊分支约在1826年掌权。

en: The Agai-deka, or Agaidika, are the Salmon Eaters of the Northern Shoshone, better known as the Lemhi Shoshone after the Lemhi River valley in Idaho where they made their main home, together with the upper Salmon River. Speaking Shoshone, a Numic language, they built their diet around salmon and trout runs, supplemented by camas root and gooseberries, and in the nineteenth century rode out on to the plains on buffalo hunts. Their bands were fluid and heavily intermarried with the Bannock. The most famous child of the band was Sacagawea, born into it around 1788, who guided the Lewis and Clark Expedition; the expedition met her people at the Three Forks of the Missouri in 1805. Through the early nineteenth century they rode with the Flathead as allies against the Blackfeet.
zh: 阿盖德卡人意为“食鲑鱼者”，是北肖肖尼人的一支，通常按其主要家园所在的爱达荷州莱姆哈伊河谷称为莱姆哈伊肖肖尼人，也活动于萨尔蒙河上游。他们说肖肖尼语（属努米克语），以洄游的鲑鱼和鳟鱼为主食，辅以卡马夏球根和醋栗，19世纪时还会骑马到大平原猎野牛。其群体边界松散，与班诺克人大量通婚。这支人最著名的后代是约1788年出生在该群的萨卡加维亚，她后来为刘易斯与克拉克远征担任向导；远征队于1805年在密苏里河三汊河口与她的族人相遇。19世纪前期，他们与弗拉特黑德人结盟，共同对抗黑脚人。

en: The Agaw are Cushitic highlanders who speak the Central Cushitic, or Agaw, languages and once held much of the northern Ethiopian plateau before the spread of Ethio-Semitic speech. They appear as the Athagaus in the third-century Monumentum Adulitanum and again on the fourth-century Ezana Stone of Axum, and the sixth-century traveller Cosmas Indicopleustes described a gold route through Agau west of the Tekezé River under a governor appointed by King Kaleb. From Lasta the Agaw built the Zagwe dynasty, which ruled Ethiopia from about 1137 to 1270 and whose most celebrated king, Gebre Mesqel Lalibela, ordered the rock-hewn churches of Roha, the town later renamed Lalibela after him. After Yekuno Amlak overthrew the Zagwe in 1270 and restored the Solomonic line, the deposed family kept the title Wagshum and governed Wag and Lasta. In the following centuries Agaw speech survived in scattered enclaves, the Bilen around Keren, the Qemant near Gondar and the Awi around Dangila, while many Agaw entered the Ethiopian church and others, notably in Semien, lived as Beta Israel.
zh: 阿高人是操中库希特语（亦称阿高语）的库希特语族高地居民，在埃塞俄比亚闪米特语扩散之前，曾占据埃塞俄比亚北部高原的大片土地。3世纪的《阿杜利斯纪念碑铭文》称他们为阿塔高人，4世纪阿克苏姆的埃扎纳石碑再次提到他们；6世纪旅行家科斯马斯·因迪科普卢斯特斯记载，一条黄金商路穿过特克泽河以西的阿高地区，当地由国王卡莱布任命的总督管辖。阿高人以拉斯塔为根基建立扎格维王朝，约在1137年至1270年间统治埃塞俄比亚，最著名的国王加布雷·梅斯克尔·拉利贝拉下令在罗哈开凿整岩教堂，这座城镇后来更名为拉利贝拉以纪念他。1270年叶库诺·阿姆拉克推翻扎格维王朝、恢复所罗门王统后，被废的家族保留瓦格舒姆头衔，继续管辖瓦格和拉斯塔。此后几个世纪里，阿高语只存于若干分散的飞地：凯伦一带的比伦人、贡德尔附近的克曼特人和丹吉拉周围的阿维人；许多阿高人加入埃塞俄比亚教会，而塞米恩等地的不少阿高人则以贝塔以色列人的身份生活。

en: The Agob are a Papuan people of eastern Morehead in Western Province, Papua New Guinea, south of the Fly River around the Pahoturi. Their speech comprises the Agöb, also called Dabu, Ende and Kawam varieties, which with neighboring Idi form a dialect chain within the small Pahoturi language family.
zh: 阿戈布人是巴布亚新几内亚西部省莫尔黑德东部、弗莱河以南帕霍图里河一带的巴布亚人。他们的语言包括阿戈布（又称达布）、恩德和卡瓦姆三种变体，与邻近的伊迪语共同构成一条方言链，同属帕霍图里语系。

en: The Agojuda were the little-documented Iroquoian people of the upper St. Lawrence and eastern Lake Ontario, around present Kingston and northern New York, remembered in Cartier-era accounts as the western enemies of the Stadaconans. Like the other St. Lawrence Iroquoians they farmed in palisaded villages and disappeared in the late sixteenth-century wars with the Mohawk and the Wendat.
zh: 阿古朱达人是记载稀少的易洛魁语族群，住在圣劳伦斯河上游与安大略湖东端，即今金斯顿和纽约州北部一带，在卡蒂埃时代的记述中是斯塔达科纳人西方的仇敌。与其他圣劳伦斯易洛魁群体一样，他们在设有栅栏的村落里务农，并在16世纪末与莫霍克人、温达特人的战争中消亡。

en: The Ahtna, or Copper River people, are an Alaska Native Athabaskan people whose homeland, Atna Nenn', covers the Copper River basin of southern Alaska from its Gulf of Alaska mouth up into the Wrangell and Alaska ranges. Their ancestors had lived in the upper Susitna country since about 5000 BC, and around the first century AD they moved into the Wrangell Mountains and the Chitina valley. Four dialect divisions and eight regional bands grew up along the river, the Lower, Middle and Upper Ahtna among them, living as Subarctic hunter-gatherers on salmon, caribou and mountain game. The Ahtna were formidable guardians of their valley: when Russian traders reached the Copper River mouth in 1781 they were repeatedly driven back, and a Russian post built at the Copper and Chitina confluence in 1819 was destroyed. Their neighbours included the Dena'ina to the west, the Eyak and Chugach Sugpiaq on the coast and the Tlingit to the southeast, with whom they traded river copper, furs and mountain products.
zh: 阿特纳人又称科珀河人，是阿拉斯加原住民中的阿萨巴斯卡族群，家园阿特纳嫩位于阿拉斯加南部的科珀河流域，从阿拉斯加湾的河口一直延伸到兰格尔山脉与阿拉斯加山脉深处。他们的祖先约自公元前5000年起便生活在苏西特纳河上游一带，到公元1世纪前后迁入兰格尔山脉和奇特诺河谷。沿河逐渐形成四个方言区、八个地区群体，包括下阿特纳、中阿特纳和上阿特纳，作为亚寒带采集狩猎者以鲑鱼、驯鹿和山地猎物为生。阿特纳人顽强守护着自己的河谷：1781年俄国商人到达科珀河口后屡次被击退，1819年俄国人在科珀河与奇特诺河交汇处设立的商站也被捣毁。他们的邻族包括西面的德纳伊纳人、沿海的埃雅克人与楚加奇苏皮阿克人，以及东南面的特林吉特人，阿特纳人用河产铜料、毛皮和山货同他们交易。

en: The Aikanã are an indigenous people of Rondônia in the western Brazilian Amazon, also known as Massacá, Tubarão or Corumbiara. Their tongue is a language isolate of the Guaporé region, spoken in the Tubarão-Latundê lands where they live alongside the unrelated Kwaza people. Their cosmology centers on Kiantô, a giant rainbow-colored serpent that rules over the waters.
zh: 艾卡纳人是巴西西亚马逊朗多尼亚州的原住民，又称马萨卡、图巴朗或科伦比亚拉。他们的艾卡纳语是瓜波雷地区的孤立语言，通行于图巴朗-拉屯德原住民地，与没有亲属关系的夸扎人比邻而居。他们的宇宙观以基安托为核心，那是一条身披彩虹之色、统御水域的巨蛇。

en: The Aymara are the indigenous people of the Andean altiplano, concentrated around Lake Titicaca in what is now Bolivia and Peru. Their ancestors shared the basin with the old city of Tiwanaku, founded around 110, though the Aymara whom the Spanish met no longer remembered who had built its ruins. By the fifteenth century they were divided into rival kingdoms and chiefdoms, among them the Colla, the Lupaca centred on Chucuito, Hatuncolla and Azángaro, farming potatoes and quinoa, freeze-drying chuño and herding llamas and alpacas. Inca conquest began after 1438 and was completed by 1500 under Pachacuti and his son Topa Yupanqui; repeated Aymara revolts, one lasting twelve years, were crushed, and mitma colonies and labour duty bound the region to Cusco, yet the Aymara language and clan life survived. Francisco Pizarro's Spaniards arrived in 1532-1534, and in 1542 the altiplano was incorporated into the Viceroyalty of Peru. Encomiendas, the Toledo reductions after 1569 and the Potosí mining mita took a heavy toll: eleven thousand native labourers worked at Potosí in 1573, but only 1,600 remained by 1673. The Jesuit Ludovico Bertonio documented the Aymara language in the early seventeenth century. Unrest ran from 1629 to the great Andean insurrection of 1779 to 1781, associated with Túpac Amaru II and the Aymara leader Túpac Katari, and after the wars of independence of 1810-1825 the Aymara became subjects of the new republics of Bolivia and Peru.
zh: 艾马拉人是安第斯高原的原住民，聚居在今玻利维亚和秘鲁交界处的的的喀喀湖周围。他们的先民与约110年兴起的古城蒂亚瓦纳科同处一个湖盆，但西班牙人见到的艾马拉人已经说不清废墟是谁所建。到15世纪，他们分裂为彼此争战的王国和酋邦，包括科利亚、以丘奎托为中心的卢帕卡以及哈通科利亚、阿桑加罗等；他们种植马铃薯和藜麦，制作冻干马铃薯“丘纽”，放牧羊驼。印加的征服始于1438年之后，到1500年在帕查库特克与其子图帕克·尤潘基治下完成；艾马拉人多次起义，其中一次坚持了十二年，均被镇压，米特马埃移民和劳役义务把该地区绑在库斯科身上，但艾马拉语和氏族生活仍然保存下来。1532至1534年弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗率领西班牙人到来，1542年高原被并入秘鲁总督区。委托监护制、1569年以后总督托莱多推行的归化村，以及波托西银矿的米塔劳役造成惨重损失：1573年波托西有一万一千名土著劳工，到1673年只剩一千六百人。耶稣会士卢多维科·贝托尼奥在17世纪初记录了艾马拉语。反抗从1629年绵延不断，最终汇成1779至1781年图帕克·阿马鲁二世与艾马拉领袖图帕克·卡塔里领导的安第斯大起义；1810至1825年独立战争后，艾马拉人成为玻利维亚和秘鲁两个新共和国的臣民。

en: The Ainu are the indigenous people of Hokkaido, southern Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands, whose ancestors also lived across northern Honshu, where Ainu place names still survive. Their culture emerged around the thirteenth century from the older Satsumon and Okhotsk traditions of the northern islands. They lived by hunting sika deer and brown bears, fishing salmon and catching seals, honouring the animals as spirits and carving the ritual wooden staffs called inau, while acting as middlemen in the trade between Honshu and the Amur. On Sakhalin the Ainu clashed with the Mongol-ruled Yuan dynasty, whose expeditions subdued them by 1308 and drew tribute from them, as did the later Ming and Qing courts. The Japanese frontier advanced under the Matsumae clan, enfeoffed at the southern tip of Ezo by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1590 and later granted a monopoly of trade with the Ainu. Resentment of forced exchange rates and overfishing led the chieftain Shakushain to rise in 1669, but his revolt was crushed by 1672. In the eighteenth century smallpox and exploitative trading thinned the Ainu villages; the shogunate took southern Hokkaido under direct rule from 1799 and claimed Sakhalin in 1807, drafting Ainu men into forced labour as Russian ships probed the coasts.
zh: 阿伊努人是北海道、库页岛南部和千岛群岛的原住民，其祖先也曾遍布本州北部，当地仍保留着阿伊努语地名。他们的文化约在13世纪由北方诸岛更古老的擦文文化和鄂霍次克文化融合而成。阿伊努人以猎虾夷鹿和棕熊、捕鲑鱼和海豹为生，把动物奉为神灵，雕刻称作“依纳乌”的祭祀木杖，并在本州与阿穆尔河流域之间充当贸易中介。在库页岛，阿伊努人与蒙古人建立的元朝发生冲突，元军远征后于1308年将其征服并征收贡赋，后来的明朝和清朝也延续了朝贡体制。日本方面的前沿扩张由松前氏主导：1590年丰臣秀吉把虾夷南端封给松前氏，后来幕府又授予其对阿伊努贸易的垄断权。强定交换比价、滥捕鲑鱼激起怨恨，酋长沙牟奢允于1669年举兵反抗，到1672年被镇压。18世纪，天花和盘剥性贸易使阿伊努村落人口锐减；幕府从1799年起直辖北海道南部，1807年又吞并库页岛，随着俄国船只出没沿海，阿伊努男子被征发苦役。

en: The Ais were a hunter-gatherer chiefdom of Florida's Atlantic coast, occupying the islands and lagoons from Cape Canaveral south along the waterway the Spanish called the River of Ais, the present-day Indian River. Several towns obeyed a paramount chief at Ais, and the people lived on fish, turtle, shellfish and gathered palm and cocoplum berries rather than farming. In 1605 the Spanish soldier Álvaro Mexía visited them on a diplomatic mission and, with their help, mapped the lagoon; the Ais agreed to rescue shipwrecked sailors for ransom. The Quaker merchant Jonathan Dickinson, shipwrecked among them in 1696, left a detailed journal of their customs at the town of Jece. Shortly after 1700, Carolinian raiders and their Native allies began seizing Ais captives for the slave market at Charles Town. The survivors merged into the Costas people after 1703, numbering only 137 by 1711, and disease had erased the remaining Ais by the mid-1740s; they vanish from the records after 1760.
zh: 艾斯人是佛罗里达大西洋沿岸的狩猎采集酋邦，占据从卡纳维拉尔角沿西班牙人所称的“艾斯之河”（今印第安河）向南的岛屿与潟湖。数个城镇臣服于以艾斯为首的最高首领，族人不事农耕，以鱼、龟、贝类以及采集的棕榈果和可可李为生。1605年，西班牙士兵阿尔瓦罗·梅西亚出使艾斯部，在他们帮助下测绘了潟湖，艾斯人也同意为赎金救助沉船水手。1696年，贵格会商人乔纳森·迪金森遇险流落他们中间，在杰塞镇留下了记述其习俗的详细日志。1700年后不久，卡罗来纳袭击者及其印第安盟友开始掳掠艾斯人，卖到查尔斯镇的奴隶市场。幸存者于1703年后并入科斯塔斯人，到1711年仅剩137人；到18世纪40年代中期，疫病又抹去了余下的艾斯人，1760年之后的记载中再无他们的名字。

en: The Ajan, commonly written Aja or Adja, are a Gbe-speaking people of the Kwa branch, native to the coast of south-western Benin and south-eastern Togo around the towns of Tado, Allada and Ouidah, and regarded by the Ewe and Fon as their mother tribe; their rites are among the roots of West African vodun. Their ancestors came from the Niger-Benue confluence before the 1000s and built the walled kingdom of Tado on the Mono River, which between the 1400s and 1600s led a loose confederacy stretching from the Volta to the Kouffo River under kings titled Anyigbãfio; the Jesuit Alonso de Sandoval described it in 1627 as a powerful inland kingdom with a safe coastal port. Around 1600 three princely brothers divided the Aja lands: Kokpon kept Great Ardra, or Allada, Do-Aklin founded Abomey, whose settlers blended with the Gedevi to become the Fon of Dahomey, and Te-Agbanlin set up Little Ardra, the future Porto-Novo. In 1724 Dahomey overran Allada and sold some eight thousand Aja captives across the Atlantic, among them forebears of Toussaint Louverture.
zh: 阿詹人（维基通译阿贾人，又称阿德贾）是贝宁西南和多哥东南沿海说克瓦语支格贝语族阿贾语的民族，聚居于塔多、阿拉达、维达等城镇，被埃维人和丰人视为母族，西非伏都信仰也渊源于他们的仪式。其祖先在11世纪以前从尼日尔河与贝努埃河汇流处西迁，在莫诺河畔建起筑有城墙的塔多王国；15至17世纪，塔多领导着一个从沃尔特河延伸到库福河的松散联盟，君主称阿尼格巴菲奥，耶稣会士阿隆索·德·桑多瓦尔1627年曾记述它是一个拥有安全海港的强大内陆王国。约1600年，三位王族兄弟瓜分阿贾之地：科克蓬保有大阿尔德拉（阿拉达），多-阿克兰兴建阿波美，其定居者与格德维人融合，成为达荷美的丰人；特-阿格兰林则建立小阿尔德拉，即后来的波多诺伏。1724年，达荷美攻陷阿拉达，将约八千名阿贾战俘卖过大西洋，图桑·卢维杜尔的先人便在其中。

en: The Ajie are the Kanak clans of the central east coast of Grande Terre in New Caledonia, whose Ajië language, also called Houailou, Wailu or Wai after its main district, is spoken around Houaïlou, Kouaoua and Poya. Ajië gives its name to the Wailic group of southern New Caledonian languages, all descended from the Austronesian speech Lapita navigators brought to the islands around 1100 BC. The Ajie valleys were dense with clan lands where taro irrigation, yam harvests and lagoon fishing sustained rival chiefdoms: warriors carried polished serpentinite axes, and villages gathered for pilou ceremonies of stamping bamboo and ancestor song beneath the carved rooftop spear of the chief's great house. The first European known to reach these waters was James Cook, who sighted Grande Terre in 1774, and French and British ships followed only fitfully after the Comte de Lapérouse vanished in the Pacific in 1788. As late as the 1830s the Ajie coast remained outside any colonial reach, its clans still governing themselves by custom and exchange.
zh: 阿杰人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛中东部沿海的卡纳克氏族群体，其阿杰语又称瓦伊卢语，得名于其主要地区，通行于瓦伊卢、夸瓦和波亚一带。阿杰语是新喀里多尼亚南部语群中瓦伊卢语组的代表，这些语言都源自约公元前1100年拉皮塔航海者带到岛上的南岛语。阿杰人的山谷里遍布氏族土地，芋头灌溉、山药收获和潟湖渔业供养着彼此竞争的酋邦：武士手持打磨的蛇纹石斧，村民聚集在酋长大屋的雕刻屋顶矛饰之下，跳起跺踩竹竿、吟唱祖先的皮卢仪式舞。已知最早抵达这片海域的欧洲人是詹姆斯·库克，他于1774年望见格朗德特尔岛；拉彼鲁兹伯爵于1788年在太平洋失踪后，英法船只也只是零星到访。直到19世纪30年代，阿杰沿海仍未落入任何殖民势力之手，各氏族依旧依照习俗和交换规则自治。

en: The Akinaa, better known as the Kainai or Blood, are one of the three Niitsitapi nations of the Blackfoot Confederacy, speaking a dialect of the Algonquian Blackfoot language. Their own name Akáínaa means many chiefs, while their Plains Cree neighbours called them the blood-stained people, from which the English label Blood comes. Like their Siksika and Piikani kin, the Kainai were nomadic bison hunters of the northern Great Plains, moving with dog travois before they adopted horses around 1730, after which they became among the most powerful mounted peoples of the plains. Summer gathered the bands for the Okan, or Sun Dance, and communal drives over buffalo jumps such as Head-Smashed-In; winter scattered them to wooded river valleys. With guns obtained through Cree and Assiniboine middlemen they pushed the Shoshone and Arapaho off the northwestern plains, and by the 1780s their confederacy's range ran from the North Saskatchewan to the Missouri. Their great rivals were the Iron Confederacy of Plains Cree, Assiniboine and Saulteaux, with whom they raided and counter-raided for horses and hunting grounds. The Hudson's Bay Company drew them into the fur trade at posts along the North Saskatchewan, but epidemic disease arrived with the traders: the smallpox outbreak of 1837, spread by an American Fur Company steamboat, killed some six thousand Niitsitapi and broke their unchallenged dominance on the plains.
zh: 阿基纳人更常见的名字是凯奈人或“血部落”，是黑脚联盟三大尼齐塔皮民族之一，说阿尔冈昆语系的黑脚语方言。他们的自称阿凯纳意为“众多首领”，而邻族平原克里人称他们为“染血之人”，英文俗称“血部落”即由此而来。与亲族西克西卡人和皮卡尼人一样，凯奈人是北部大平原上追逐野牛的游牧民族：约1730年获得马匹之前，他们靠狗拉的特拉沃伊雪橇搬运，此后则成为大草原上最强大的骑马民族之一。夏天各群体聚集举行奥坎仪式（太阳舞），并在“撞头崖”等野牛跳崖处集体围猎；冬天则分散到林木覆盖的河谷中。凭借经克里人和阿西尼博因人转手获得的火器，他们把肖肖尼人和阿拉帕霍人逐出西北部平原，到18世纪80年代，联盟的势力范围已从北萨斯喀彻温河延伸到密苏里河。他们的主要对手是由平原克里人、阿西尼博因人和索托人组成的“铁器联盟”，双方为马匹和猎场反复攻伐。哈德逊湾公司在北萨斯喀彻温河沿线设立商站，把他们拉入毛皮贸易，但疫病也随商人而至：1837年，美国毛皮公司一艘汽船带来天花，约六千名尼齐塔皮人丧生，他们在平原上无人能敌的优势就此终结。

en: The Akan are a cluster of Kwa-speaking, Tano-language peoples of the forest and coast of present-day Ghana and Ivory Coast, among them the Bono, Asante, Fante, Denkyira, Akwamu and Baoulé, who share matrilineal abusua clans and reckon chiefly authority through stools. Towns such as Asantemanso were occupied from the ninth century, and the early Bono state at Bono Manso sent gold and kola north through Begho to Wangara merchants of the Middle Niger. From the late 1400s Portuguese, then Dutch and English ships bought Akan gold on the coast, drawing the forest states into Atlantic trade, and after 1650 firearms reshaped inland politics as Denkyira, Akyem and Akwamu fought over the gold routes. Around 1695 Osei Tutu and the priest Okomfo Anokye united the Kumasi towns under the Golden Stool and in 1701 overthrew Denkyira, opening the Asante empire's way to the sea; Asante armies went on to take Bono in 1722 and 1723 and dominate the hinterland, while the Fante towns formed a coastal confederacy around Mankessim to hold them off. The Asante checked British expansion at Nsamankow in 1824, killing the governor MacCarthy, though they were beaten at Katamanso in 1826.
zh: 阿坎人是今加纳和科特迪瓦森林与沿海地带说克瓦语支塔诺诸语的族群总称，包括博诺、阿散蒂、芳蒂、登基拉、阿夸穆、鲍莱等支系，共同特点是按母系氏族组织社会、以凳子象征酋长权位。阿桑特曼索等城镇9世纪已有人居住，早期的博诺国以博诺曼索为都，把黄金和柯拉果经贝戈北运，卖给尼日尔河中游的旺加拉商人。15世纪末起，葡萄牙、随后荷兰和英国的商船到沿海收购阿坎黄金，把各森林政权卷入大西洋贸易；1650年后火器改变了内陆格局，登基拉、阿基姆和阿夸穆为争夺黄金商路连年交战。约1695年，奥塞·图图在祭司奥科姆福·阿诺基辅佐下，以金凳子为象征统一库马西诸城，1701年攻灭登基拉，为阿散蒂帝国打开出海通道；其后阿散蒂军队又于1722—1723年征服博诺、称霸内陆，芳蒂诸城则在曼克西姆一带结成沿海联盟与之抗衡。1824年，阿散蒂在恩萨曼科遏制英国扩张，击杀总督麦卡锡，但1826年在卡塔曼索战败。

en: The Akei are an Oceanic-speaking Melanesian people of the southwestern coast of Espiritu Santo in Vanuatu, centred on the village of Tasiriki, whose name means small water in their tongue. Their speech is known by a string of local names, among them Navaka, Marino, Pilipili and Wailapa, and neighbouring varieties shade into one another along a dialect chain whose ends are no longer mutually intelligible. The Akei share Santo's deep Lapita past, the island having been settled by Austronesian navigators some three thousand years ago. Europeans first reached Santo with Pedro Fernandes de Queirós's Spanish expedition of 1606; Louis Antoine de Bougainville followed in 1768 and James Cook in 1774, after which the islands appeared on European maps as the New Hebrides.
zh: 阿凯伊人是瓦努阿图圣埃斯皮里图岛西南沿海的美拉尼西亚人，以塔西里基村为中心；塔西里基在他们的话中意为“小水”。他们的语言有纳瓦卡、马里诺、皮利皮利、怀拉帕等一串地方别名，邻近各话沿一条方言链渐次过渡，链条两端的话已经不能互通。阿凯伊人与全岛居民一样承袭着深厚的拉皮塔文化渊源：约三千年前，南岛语系的航海者便已定居圣埃斯皮里图岛。1606年，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯的西班牙探险队首次让欧洲人来到该岛；路易·安托万·德·布干维尔于1768年、詹姆斯·库克于1774年先后来访，此后这片群岛在欧洲地图上被标作新赫布里底群岛。

en: The Xerente, who call themselves Akwê, “the people”, are a Central Jê people of the Brazilian interior, living on the right bank of the Tocantins river between the Tocantins and the Rio do Sono, in what is now the state of Tocantins. Their oral tradition tells of a distant home on the coast and a long migration through the dry north-eastern sertão; with the Xavante, Xakriabá and Krahô they form part of the Acuén cluster, split apart by warfare as each subgroup withdrew into its own stretch of country. Their villages were traditionally laid out in a semicircle, and society was divided into exogamous moieties named after the sun, Doí, and the moon, Wahirê, each grouping several clans. Jesuit missionaries and the inland expeditions known as bandeiras first reached them in the 1600s. After gold was found in the neighbouring captaincy of Goiás in the 1700s, the Portuguese crown gathered them into supervised native settlements, and the Capuchin mission of Teresa Cristina, founded in the 1800s, grew into the town of Tocantínia. The Xavante meanwhile broke away and migrated west to Mato Grosso, leaving the Xerente in possession of the Tocantins lands.
zh: 谢伦特人自称阿克韦，意为“人”，是巴西内陆的中部热语族族群，住在托坎廷斯河右岸、托坎廷斯河与索诺河之间，地当今托坎廷斯州。他们的口传历史称祖先远居海滨，后穿过东北部干旱的腹地长途迁徙至此；谢伦特人与沙万特人、沙克里亚巴人和克拉霍人同属阿昆族群，因连年征战而四分五裂，各支系退入各自的偏远乡野固守。他们的村庄传统上呈半圆形排列，社会分为族外婚的两大半偶族，分别以太阳多伊和月亮瓦伊雷命名，各统辖数个氏族。17世纪，耶稣会传教士和被称为“旗队”的内陆探险队最先抵达他们那里。18世纪邻近的戈亚斯都督辖区发现黄金后，葡萄牙王室把他们集中到受监管的原住民村落；19世纪嘉布遣会建立的特雷莎·克里斯蒂娜传教站，后来发展成托坎蒂尼亚镇。与此同时，沙万特人分道西迁马托格罗索，谢伦特人则留居托坎廷斯故土。

en: The Albaamo, better known as the Alabama or Alibamu, are a Muskogean people of the Southeastern Woodlands whose towns lay on the upper Alabama River within the Muscogee Creek Confederacy, and whose language is closest to Koasati. Hernando de Soto's expedition crossed their country in 1540, and in the eighteenth century the French built a fort on the Gulf coast at what became Mobile. Their towns followed the Creek division into red towns, which organized warfare, and white towns, which kept the peace and offered refuge. After the French ceded the Gulf coast to Britain following the Seven Years' War, British settlement and pressure from the Choctaw made the Alabama among the first Creek peoples to leave: they drifted west through Louisiana, and in 1805 nearly a thousand Alabama reached the Big Thicket of eastern Texas, where by 1820 they held three main towns beside their Coushatta allies. Their own origin tradition placed the birthplace of the people in the earth between the Alabama and Cahaba rivers.
zh: 阿拉巴莫人（又称阿拉巴马或阿里巴穆）是东南林地的马斯科吉语族族群，村镇分布在阿拉巴马河上游，属马斯科吉克里克联盟，语言与科阿萨蒂语最接近。1540年埃尔南多·德·索托的探险队经过其地，18世纪法国人来到墨西哥湾岸，在后来发展为莫比尔的地方修筑堡垒。他们的城镇沿用克里克人的红白之分：红镇负责征战，白镇维持和平、提供庇护。七年战争后法国把湾岸割让给英国，英国移民涌入，加上乔克托人的压力，阿拉巴莫人成为最早迁离的克里克族群之一：他们西走路易斯安那，1805年近千名阿拉巴莫人抵达东得克萨斯的大灌丛，到1820年已在盟友科阿萨蒂人的村镇旁建起三座主要城镇。按他们自己的起源传说，族人诞生于阿拉巴马河与卡霍巴河之间的土地。

en: The Alans were an Iranian-speaking Sarmatian people who dominated the Pontic-Caspian steppe from the first century, famed as mounted raiders and mercenaries. The Hunnic storms of the fourth century split them: one branch rode west with the Vandals through Gaul, Spain and on to North Africa, while the Caucasian Alans settled the northern foothills from the Kuban to the Darial Pass. In the late ninth century they threw off Khazar rule and built the Kingdom of Alania, with its capital at Maghas; Byzantine missionaries converted them to Eastern Orthodoxy in the early tenth century, and under King Durgulel in the eleventh century Alania grew rich on the Darial trade and sent its cavalry to serve the emperors and the kings of Georgia, whose Queen Tamar married the Alan prince David Soslan in 1187. By the early thirteenth century the kingdom had fragmented into feuding clans, and in 1239 to 1240 the Mongols stormed Maghas and carried off thousands of Alan horsemen as imperial guards as far as China, while another band found refuge in Hungary. In 1337 Alan communities still held the Caucasus foothills and stretches of the Pontic steppe, but Timur's invasion of 1395 broke their lowland power for good and drove the survivors into the mountain gorges, where they became the Ossetians; the western Digor took Islam through Kabardian contacts in the seventeenth century.
zh: 阿兰人是说伊朗语的萨尔马提亚族群，1世纪起称雄于黑海至里海的草原，以骑兵袭掠和充当雇佣兵闻名。4世纪匈人的冲击使他们分裂：一支随汪达尔人西迁，经高卢、西班牙远至北非；留在高加索的阿兰人则定居在从库班河到达里亚尔山口的北麓地带。9世纪末，他们摆脱可萨统治，建立以马加斯为都的阿兰王国；10世纪初，拜占庭传教士使他们皈依东正教。11世纪杜尔古列尔王在位时，阿兰王国凭借达里亚尔商路致富，并派骑兵为拜占庭皇帝和格鲁吉亚国王效力，格鲁吉亚塔玛尔女王还在1187年嫁给阿兰王子大卫·索斯兰。13世纪初王国已分裂为互相仇杀的氏族，1239至1240年蒙古人攻陷马加斯，把数千阿兰骑兵掳往中国充当皇帝侍卫，另有一支逃难到匈牙利。1337年，阿兰人的社群仍据有高加索山麓和黑海草原的部分地带，但1395年帖木儿的入侵彻底摧毁了他们在低地的力量，幸存者退入深山峡谷，后来演变为奥塞梯人；西部的迪戈尔人则在17世纪经卡巴尔达人接触而改宗伊斯兰教。

en: The Alawites, historically commonly called Nusayris, are an Arabic-speaking ethnoreligious community of the Syrian coastal mountains, centered on Latakia, Tartus, Jableh and Baniyas and also settled around Hama, Homs and Tripoli. Their creed grew from the ninth-century ghulat Shia teaching of Ibn Nusayr and was organized in Aleppo under Hamdanid rule after 947 by the missionary al-Khasibi, before spreading into the coastal highlands; it venerates Ali as a divine incarnation, teaches reincarnation and a trinity of Mana, Ism and Bab, and reserves its wine-centered rites to initiated men. Crusaders entering Syria in 1097 killed many Alawites but later tolerated and even recruited them, while Mamluk rulers of the fourteenth century pressed the mountain villages to accept Islam's outward observances. Ottoman conquest brought the massacre of the Telal at Aleppo in 1517, after which survivors withdrew deeper into the coast ranges, where repeated revolts kept their autonomy alive. In the eighteenth century some Alawite chiefs served as Ottoman tax farmers, and in 1834 and 1835 the community rose against the Egyptian occupation of Syria.
zh: 阿拉维人在历史上常被称为努赛里人，是讲阿拉伯语的宗教族群，聚居于叙利亚沿海山地，以拉塔基亚、塔尔图斯、贾布莱和巴尼亚斯为中心，在哈马、霍姆斯和的黎波里一带也有分布。其教义出自9世纪伊本·努赛尔的什叶派极端支派，947年后由传教士哈西比在哈姆丹王朝治下的阿勒颇整理成形，随后传入沿海高地；教义尊阿里为神的化身，相信灵魂转世和“玛纳、伊斯姆、巴布”三位一体，以酒为核心的仪式只对受戒男子开放。1097年十字军进入叙利亚时曾大量杀害阿拉维人，后来却加以容忍甚至招入军中；14世纪的马穆鲁克统治者则强迫山村接受伊斯兰教的外在仪轨。奥斯曼征服带来1517年阿勒颇的“特拉勒屠杀”，幸存者进一步退入沿海群山，凭一次次起义维系自治。18世纪一些阿拉维酋长出任包税人；1834至1835年，该族群又起兵反抗埃及对叙利亚的占领。

en: The Albanians are a Balkan people whose language forms its own branch of Indo-European and is widely held to descend from the speech of the ancient Illyrians; the name Albanoi was already recorded by Ptolemy in the second century, and Byzantine chroniclers place Albanians in the theme of Dyrrhachium around Krujë and Durrës by the eleventh century. The Shkumbin River divides them into northern Ghegs and southern Tosks, a split mirrored in religion, as the north leaned Catholic and the south Orthodox after the schism of 1054. In 1190 Progon founded the Principality of Arbanon at Krujë, the first recorded Albanian state, and the Angevins organized a Kingdom of Albania around Durrës in 1272. During the fourteenth century native families such as the Thopia, Muzaka, Balsha and Kastrioti ruled shifting principalities between Byzantine, Serbian and Venetian overlords, until Ottoman conquest began with the fall of Krujë in 1415. In 1444 the nobles united at Lezhë under Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg, whose armies held off the Ottomans until his death in 1468; Shkodra fell in 1479. Under Ottoman rule large numbers converted to Islam from the seventeenth century and Albanians rose to the highest offices of the empire, supplying more than forty grand viziers, while emigrant communities of Arvanites in Greece and Arbëreshë in southern Italy kept older Christian traditions alive. Around 1800 semi-independent pashaliks emerged at Shkodra, Berat and Ioannina, the last ruled by Ali Pasha until 1822.
zh: 阿尔巴尼亚人是巴尔干民族，其语言在印欧语系中自成一支，学界普遍认为源自古伊利里亚人的语言；“阿尔巴诺伊”之名2世纪已见于托勒密的记载，11世纪的拜占庭编年史则把阿尔巴尼亚人置于都拉齐翁军区的克鲁亚和都拉斯一带。什昆宾河把他们分为北部的盖格人和南部的托斯克人，宗教上也相应分化：1054年教会大分裂后，北方倾向天主教，南方倾向东正教。1190年，普罗贡在克鲁亚建立有记载的第一个阿尔巴尼亚政权阿尔巴农公国，1272年安茹家族又以都拉斯为中心组建阿尔巴尼亚王国。14世纪，托皮亚、穆扎卡、巴尔沙、卡斯特里奥蒂等本土家族在拜占庭、塞尔维亚和威尼斯的宗主权之间治理着不断易手的小邦，直到1415年克鲁亚陷落，奥斯曼征服开始。1444年，众贵族在莱什联合，拥戴斯坎德培（乔治·卡斯特里奥蒂）为首，他的军队抵抗奥斯曼人直至1468年去世；斯库台于1479年陷落。奥斯曼统治下，大量阿尔巴尼亚人从17世纪起改宗伊斯兰教，并在帝国出任高官，出任过大维齐尔者超过四十人；移居希腊的阿尔瓦尼特人和移居意大利南部的阿尔伯雷什人则保留了古老的基督教传统。1800年前后，斯库台、培拉特和约阿尼纳出现半独立的帕夏领地，其中约阿尼纳由阿里帕夏统治到1822年。

en: The Vakarel were an Evenki band of the Aldan, a long right tributary of the Lena, where they hunted elk and wild reindeer through the eastern Stanovoy taiga. In 1639 the Cossack Ivan Moskvitin ascended the Aldan on his way to the Sea of Okhotsk, opening the river to Russian fur traders and tribute collectors.
zh: 阿尔丹人是活动在阿尔丹河流域的鄂温克游猎群，在斯塔诺夫山脉东麓的林海中猎取驼鹿和野鹿；阿尔丹河是勒拿河的长大右支流。1639年，哥萨克伊万·莫斯克维京沿阿尔丹河而上前往鄂霍次克海，这条水道从此向俄国毛皮商和征税官敞开。

en: The Snchicu'umshcn, now commonly called the Coeur d'Alene or Skitswish, are an Interior Salish people of the lake district at the heart of the Idaho panhandle, whose villages stood along the Coeur d'Alene, St. Joe, Clark Fork and Spokane rivers and on the shores of lakes Coeur d'Alene and Pend Oreille. They lived by fishing, hunting and gathering camas on a seasonal round, wintering in clustered semi-subterranean earth lodges, and their language belongs to the Interior branch of Salishan. Their first recorded encounter with Europeans was in 1793, and the name Cœur d'Alêne, French for 'heart of an awl', was first written down by the Lewis and Clark expedition in 1805; from 1810 the North West Company traders Alexander Henry and David Thompson travelled and traded through their country.
zh: 斯尼奇乌姆什恩人通常称科达伦人，又名斯基特维什，是内陆萨利什人的一支，家园在爱达荷州狭地中心的湖区，村落分布在科达伦河、圣乔河、克拉克福克河、斯波坎河沿岸以及科达伦湖和庞多雷湖畔。他们按季节迁徙，以捕鱼、狩猎和采集卡马夏为生，冬季聚居在半地穴式土屋中，语言属萨利什语的内陆分支。他们与欧洲人有记载的首次接触是在1793年；法文名称科尔达伦意为‘锥子之心’，最早由1805年的刘易斯与克拉克探险队记录下来；1810年起，西北公司的商人亚历山大·亨利和戴维·汤普森进入他们的土地旅行和贸易。

en: The Algerian are the Arabic-speaking, largely Arabized people of the central Maghreb, settled in the cities and high plains around Constantine, Sétif and the Hodna. Islam and Arabic first came with the Umayyad conquests of the seventh and eighth centuries, but the countryside long kept its Amazigh speech until the Fatimids loosed the Bedouin Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym upon the Zirids; their rout of the Sanhaja cavalry at Haydaran in 1052 opened the interior to Bedouin camps and carried Hilalian Arabic across the plateau, fusing Arab tribesmen with Arabized Berbers. Rule passed through the Almoravids and Almohads to the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, founded in 1235, whose fourteenth-century court under Abu Hammu Musa II hosted Ibn Khaldun, until the Ottomans took Tlemcen in 1551. Spain had already seized Oran in 1509, and the Barbarossa brothers built Algiers into an Ottoman corsair regency from 1516; after the janissary coup of 1659 it became an elected military republic of deys, which recovered Oran in 1792 before the French invasion of 1830 ended the regency.
zh: 阿尔及尔人是中马格里布操阿拉伯语、以阿拉伯化居民为主体的族群，聚居于君士坦丁、塞提夫与霍德纳一带的城市和高原。7至8世纪倭马亚王朝的征服首次带来伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语，但乡间长期仍用阿马齐格语；后来法蒂玛王朝放贝都因的巴努希拉尔、巴努苏莱姆诸部东侵齐尔王朝，1052年他们在海达兰击溃桑哈贾骑兵，内陆由此向贝都因营帐敞开，希拉勒方言阿拉伯语传遍高原，阿拉伯部落与阿拉伯化的柏柏尔人逐渐融合。此后中马格里布先后历经穆拉比特、穆瓦希德王朝，1235年扎扬王朝建立特莱姆森王国；14世纪阿布·哈穆·穆萨二世在位时，伊本·赫勒敦曾寓居其宫廷，1551年特莱姆森落入奥斯曼之手。西班牙已于1509年夺取奥兰，巴巴罗萨兄弟则自1516年起把阿尔及尔建成奥斯曼的海盗摄政领；1659年禁卫军政变后，它成为由德伊选举掌权的军事共和国，并于1792年收回奥兰，直到1830年法国入侵终结了摄政政权。

en: The Alor are a Papuan people of the Alor Archipelago at the eastern end of the Lesser Sunda chain, occupying the rugged western coast of Alor Island, northern Pantar and the small island of Pura. They speak Papuan languages of the Alor–Pantar family and organize society into patrilineal clans called hieta, farming subsistence crops and cutting sandalwood for trade.
zh: 亚罗人是小巽他群岛东端阿洛群岛的巴布亚语族群，分布在阿洛岛崎岖的西海岸、潘塔尔岛北部和小岛普拉。他们操巴布亚语系阿洛—潘塔尔语族的语言，按名为希埃塔的父系氏族组织社会，种植自给作物并采伐檀香木贸易。

en: The Alsea are a Native American people of the central Oregon coast, whose villages lined the Alsea River and the shores of Alsea Bay; their closely related neighbours the Yaquina and Yachats shared their speech and, in Alsea origin tradition, belonged to one people. The name Alsea itself was given to them by their Tillamook and Coos neighbours. Their language, Alsea or Yakonan, was so close to Yaquina that the two may be dialects of one tongue, and it is usually placed in the Coast Oregon group of the Penutian languages, though some linguists treat it as an isolate. An ethnographic estimate put the whole Yakonan-speaking population at about six thousand in 1780. The Alsea hunted seals and sea lions, took salmon in the estuaries and dug camas roots; they wove baskets and grass raincoats, dressed in seal-skin robes, and shaped the foreheads of infants by gentle pressure in the cradleboard. Shamans worked to secure good salmon runs, and the dead were laid in canoes on points of land jutting into the estuaries.
zh: 阿尔西厄人是俄勒冈中部海岸的原住民，村庄沿阿尔西河和阿尔西湾两岸分布；与他们关系密切的邻族亚奎纳人和亚查茨人讲相近的语言，在阿尔西厄人的起源传说中本就属于同一个民族。“阿尔西厄”这个名字本身来自蒂拉穆克人和库斯人邻居对他们的称呼。他们的语言阿尔西语又称雅科南语，与亚奎纳语极为接近，二者可能只是同一语言的不同方言；学界通常把它归入佩努蒂语系的俄勒冈海岸语组，也有语言学家将其视为孤立语言。一项民族学估计认为，1780年时所有讲雅科南语的人口约有六千。阿尔西厄人捕猎海豹和海狮，在河口湾捕捞鲑鱼、挖掘卡马夏根；他们编织篮筐和草制雨衣，身披海豹皮袍，还在婴儿摇篮中轻压其头部以改变前额形状。萨满负责祈保鲑鱼丰收，死者则被安放在独木舟里，置于伸入河口湾的岬角上。

en: The Alyutor are a Chukotko-Kamchatkan people of the narrow neck of northeastern Kamchatka, the Olyutor and Karaga coasts facing the Bering Sea, in present-day northern Kamchatka Krai. Long counted as a branch of the Koryaks and speaking a tongue close to Koryak, they call themselves Alutal'u and built riverside villages on high ground with wide views, living from reindeer breeding, salmon fishing, seal hunting and trapping in octagonal earth houses shared by several families. Cossacks imposed the fur tribute on them in 1697, and armed resistance culminated in the uprising of 1751, after which their numbers fell sharply; they also lost herds to repeated Chukchi raids. Their isolation in the late eighteenth century let them escape the worst smallpox epidemics and keep their coastal way of life.
zh: 阿柳托尔人属楚科奇—堪察加语族，居住在堪察加东北部的狭窄地峡，即面向白令海的奥柳托尔与卡拉加海岸，在今堪察加边疆区北部。他们长期被算作科里亚克人的一支，说与科里亚克语相近的语言，自称阿卢塔卢；村落建在河边视野开阔的高地上，住几户人家合居的八角土屋，以养驯鹿、捕鲑鱼、猎海豹和设陷阱为生。1697年哥萨克向他们强征毛皮税，武装反抗最终酿成1751年的起义，起义被镇压后人口大减；楚科奇人又不断来袭，掠走他们的鹿群。18世纪末他们地处偏远、与外界隔绝，几乎未受天花大流行波及，沿海的传统生计也得以保存。

en: The Amaimon are a Papuan people of the hinterland behind Madang on the north coast of Papua New Guinea, centred on the village of Amaimon in the Transgogol country of Madang Province. They speak a language of the Madang branch of the Trans-New Guinea family.
zh: 阿迈蒙人是巴布亚新几内亚北海岸马当后方腹地的巴布亚族群，以马当省特兰斯戈戈尔地区的阿迈蒙村为中心。他们说跨新几内亚语系马当语支的一种语言。

en: The Amurdak, also written Amarak or Ngamarak, are an Indigenous Australian people of the Cobourg Peninsula in the Northern Territory, keepers of the coastal country and hinterland around the eastern shore of Van Diemen Gulf that now forms part of Garig Gunak Barlu. Their traditional lands ran over about 2,300 square kilometres, from Murgenella and Cooper creeks in the north to the East Alligator River in the south. Their language, also called Wardadjbak, belonged to the Iwaidja family and had two dialects, Urrik and Didjurra. In Cobourg Peninsula Dreamtime lore they descend from the children the founding woman Imberombera left at Mamul near Cooper Creek, whom she told to speak Amurdak and to gather the edible bulb murarowa.
zh: 阿马拉克人又拼作阿穆尔达克或恩加马拉克，是北领地科堡半岛的澳大利亚原住民，守护着范迪门湾东岸的沿海与内陆地带，即后来加里格古纳克巴卢国家公园所在的地方。他们的传统领地约2300平方公里，北起穆尔杰内拉溪与库珀溪，南抵东阿利盖特河。他们的语言又称瓦尔达贾克语，属伊瓦伊贾语系，有乌里克和迪朱拉两种方言。在科堡半岛的梦幻时代传说中，始祖女因贝龙贝拉在库珀溪附近的马穆尔留下子女，命他们说阿马拉克语、采食名叫穆拉罗瓦的可食球茎，阿马拉克人便是这些子女的后裔。

en: The Ambae are an Oceanic-speaking Melanesian people who garden the slopes of Ambae, Vanuatu's largest active volcano, a rugged basalt island in the north of the archipelago long known to Europeans as Aoba or Lepers' Island. The island has no permanent rivers and its only natural standing water lies in the inaccessible crater lakes near the summit, so villages draw on wells and stored rainwater while tending large gardens and managed forests above the coastal coconut groves. Their western language, also called Duidui, has its principal dialect at Nduindui with a further variety at Walaha, while kinfolk on the north, east and south of the island speak the distinct East Ambae tongue. The ships of Pedro Fernandes de Queirós's Spanish expedition first recorded a sighting of Ambae in the spring of 1606; Louis Antoine de Bougainville sailed through the group in 1768 and James Cook in 1774.
zh: 奥巴人是在奥巴岛坡地上耕作园圃的美拉尼西亚人，操大洋洲语。奥巴岛位于瓦努阿图北部，是瓦努阿图体积最大的活火山，海岸多嶙峋的黑色玄武岩，欧洲人旧称奥巴岛或麻风岛。岛上没有常年河流，唯一的天然积水是山顶难以抵达的火山口湖，村民便靠水井和蓄存雨水生活，在沿海椰林上方经营大片园圃和人工林木。他们的西部语言又称杜伊杜伊语，主方言在恩杜因杜伊，另有瓦拉哈方言；岛的北、东、南部同族则使用与之不同的东奥巴语。1606年春，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯的西班牙探险队首次有记载地望见奥巴岛；路易·安托万·德·布干维尔和詹姆斯·库克又分别于1768年和1774年航经这片群岛。

en: The Ambrym are an Oceanic-speaking Melanesian people of Ambrym, a triangular volcanic island near the centre of the Vanuatu archipelago, dominated by a vast desert-like caldera whose two craters hold some of the few persistent lava lakes in the world. Villages cling to the three forested corners of the island, and in the north the people speak North Ambrym, divided into a western dialect around Lonhali and a north-eastern one around Wowan, the survivors of an earlier five or six varieties that merged as communities moved down to the coast. Their island entered European records through James Cook, who sailed past in 1774 and is traditionally credited with naming it Ambrym, although his expedition never actually landed.
zh: 安布里姆人是安布里姆岛上的美拉尼西亚人，操大洋洲语。安布里姆是瓦努阿图群岛中部一座三角形火山岛，岛心是巨大而荒凉的破火山口，口内两个火山坑拥有世界上少见的常年熔岩湖，村落则散布在岛屿三个林木繁茂的角上。北部居民使用北安布里姆语，分为隆哈利一带的西部方言和沃万一带的东北部方言；随着居民向海岸迁移，早先的五六种方言合并成了这两种。该岛进入欧洲人的记载与詹姆斯·库克有关：他于1774年航经此地，相传岛名便出自库克，不过其探险队其实并未登陆。

en: The Ambundu, or Mbundu, are a matrilineal Bantu people of the high plateau north of the Kwanza River in present-day Angola, around Luanda, Ambaca and Malanje, whose ancestors arrived there chiefly between the thirteenth and sixteenth centuries. They speak Kimbundu, and their leading kingdom was Ndongo, whose ruler bore the title Ngola, the word from which the country Angola takes its name. When Ndongo tried to break the Kongo kingdom's monopoly on Portuguese trade, war ended in a Bakongo defeat in 1556 and Ndongo's independence; a later alliance with Matamba against Portugal was crushed in 1614. Queen Njinga, daughter of an Ngola, then withdrew to Matamba and built it into the strongest state of the region and a great exporter of slaves. Ambundu captives made up a large share of the Atlantic slave trade, and Mbundu taken in that trade were among the first Africans landed in Virginia in 1619. Portuguese armies subdued Matamba in 1836, though effective control of the Ambundu highlands remained weak for decades afterward.
zh: 安本杜人又称姆本杜人，是按母系传承的班图人，住在今安哥拉宽扎河以北的高原上，以罗安达、安巴卡和马兰热一带为中心，其先民主要在13至16世纪间迁来。他们讲金本杜语，主导的王国是恩东戈，君主称号为“恩戈拉”，安哥拉的国名即由此而来。恩东戈试图打破刚果王国对葡萄牙贸易的垄断，战争以1556年巴刚果人战败、恩东戈独立告终；后来它与马坦巴结盟对抗葡萄牙，又在1614年被击溃。恩戈拉之女恩津加女王退据马坦巴，把它经营成当地最强的国家和奴隶出口大国。安本杜俘虏在大西洋奴隶贸易中占很大份额，1619年运抵弗吉尼亚的第一批非洲人中就有被掳走的姆本杜人。1836年葡萄牙军队征服马坦巴，但此后数十年间，其对安本杜高原的实际控制仍然薄弱。

en: The Amdowas are the Tibetans of Amdo, the great northeastern reach of the Tibetan plateau between the Yellow River and the upper Yangtze, a wind-swept country of grassland, salt lakes and celebrated horse herds. Their valleys entered the Tibetan Empire in the seventh century, and after its fall the Tibetan kingdom of Tsongkha held the region from 997 to 1104 before the Mongol conquest of the 1240s opened the priest-patron bond between Mongol khans and Tibetan lamas. By 1337 Yuan garrisons were already crumbling: Mongol fiefs around Kokonor lacked leaders, Tibetan raids reached Liangzhou, and a general rising in 1347 shook eastern Tibet. The Ming afterwards held little beyond the Hezhou and Xining garrisons, leaving the grasslands to Tibetan chiefs and returning Mongol tribes, while Amdo-born Tsongkhapa, founder of the Gelug order, gave the region its lasting religious stamp: Kumbum monastery rose on his birthplace in 1583 and Labrang followed in 1709. After Güshi Khan's wars of the 1630s and 1640s the Kokonor country stayed under Mongol rule until the Qing drove out the Dzungars, and in the 1720s the Yongzheng Emperor folded Amdo into the new Xining administration, leaving Tibetan headmen and great monasteries to run local affairs under imperial commissions. Speaking a conservative, tone-free Tibetan of their own, the Amdowas long felt themselves a people apart from the Tibetans of Lhasa.
zh: 安多人是安多地区的藏人。安多地处青藏高原东北缘，黄河与金沙江上游之间，草原辽阔、盐湖散布，自古以良马闻名。其河谷在7世纪并入吐蕃帝国，帝国崩溃后，吐蕃裔的唃厮啰政权于997至1104年统治此地，13世纪40年代蒙古征服安多，开启了蒙古汗王与西藏喇嘛之间的供施关系。1337年时元朝的戍军已经摇摇欲坠：青海一带的蒙古封地无主，藏人的袭扰远及凉州，1347年东部藏地更有两百余处同时起事。此后明朝实际控制的不过河州、西宁等卫所，草原交给藏族头人和重返的蒙古部落；生于安多的格鲁派创始人宗喀巴为这里留下了深远的宗教印记，1583年其诞生地建起塔尔寺，1709年拉卜楞寺又告落成。固始汗在17世纪30至40年代的征战之后，青海地区仍由蒙古人统治，直到清朝逐走准噶尔；雍正皇帝在18世纪20年代把安多纳入新设的西宁府管辖，藏族头人和大寺院则凭朝廷敕命继续管理地方事务。安多人说保守而无声调的安多方言，长期以来自认与拉萨的藏人有别。

en: The Amhara are the Amharic-speaking Orthodox Christians of the central and northern Ethiopian highlands, whose historic homeland covers Bete Amhara, Gondar, Gojjam, Lasta and Shewa around Lake Tana. They took shape as Aksumite-descended Christian families settled southward into the highlands and absorbed the local Cushitic Agaw, and Amharic, a South Ethio-Semitic language, became the tongue of court and government for more than seven centuries. First named in twelfth-century records, the Amhara rose to imperial power when Yekuno Amlak overthrew the Zagwe dynasty in 1270 and founded the Solomonic line of emperors. In 1337 the warrior-emperor Amda Seyon I ruled from his mobile highland camps, extending Christian rule over the Muslim states of the eastern lowlands, and his successors built the first fixed imperial capital at Debre Birhan in 1456. The Adal invasion of 1529 to 1543, led by Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, devastated the Christian highlands until Emperor Galawdewos, with Portuguese help, won the war and rebuilt the Amhara state.
