From 1610 the Jesuits gathered them into the Paraguayan reductions, which at their height in 1732 held more than 140,000 converts in thirty towns, defended by their own drilled army against the Paulista slave raiders who had carried off tens of thousands in the 1620s and 1630s. The 1750 Treaty of Madrid, which handed seven mission towns to Portugal, triggered the Guaraní War of 1754 to 1756, and the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 began the collapse of the reductions: by the census of 1801 fewer than 45,000 mission Guaraní remained. The Bolivian groups around the Pilcomayo and Parapetí rivers kept their independence far longer, entering the nineteenth century as distinct Ava, Simba and Izoceño communities.
zh: 阿瓦人（更常见的名称是瓜拉尼人）是一群说图皮-瓜拉尼语的族群，家园从巴拉圭河与巴拉那河流域延伸到玻利维亚东部的安第斯山麓；其好战的奇里瓜诺分支曾长期同时抵拒印加人和西班牙人。他们自称阿巴或阿瓦，意思是“人”。接触时代之初，他们是定居农民，住在名为马洛卡的大型群居长屋里，种植木薯和玉米，各地总人口可能有40万左右。1610年起，耶稣会把他们集中迁入巴拉圭归化区；1732年鼎盛时，30座城镇里住有14万多名皈依者，并拥有自己训练有素的军队，抵御在17世纪20至30年代掳走数万人的圣保罗奴隶贩子。1750年的《马德里条约》把七座传教城镇割让给葡萄牙，引发1754至1756年的瓜拉尼战争；1767年耶稣会被驱逐，归化区随之瓦解，到1801年人口普查时，传教区里的瓜拉尼人已不足4.5万。皮科马约河和帕拉佩蒂河一带的玻利维亚分支保持独立的时间则长得多，进入19世纪时仍分为阿瓦、辛巴和伊佐塞尼奥等不同群体。

en: The Caucasian Avars, who call themselves Maarulal or mountaineers, are the largest people of mountain Dagestan, holding the high valleys and a cluster of fortress villages around Khunzakh, and they have no historical link with the Eurasian Avars of the early Middle Ages. Between the fifth and twelfth centuries Georgian missionaries brought Orthodox Christianity into their valleys, and the Christian kingdom of Sarir long dominated Dagestan under Arab and then Georgian protection, leaving the tenth-century Datuna church as its surviving monument. When Sarir collapsed in the early thirteenth century the Muslim Avar Khanate took its place, and Sunni Islam, arriving with Arab traders and preachers, became the prevailing faith from the fourteenth century. The khans grew rich through their alliance with the Golden Horde, though in the fifteenth century they were absorbed by the rival Shamkhalate of Kazi-Kumukh. Under loose Safavid suzerainty the Avar free communities kept much of their self-rule, and in the eighteenth century they routed an army of Nader Shah at Andalal; under Umma Khan, ruling from 1774 to 1801, Avar power levied tribute as far as Shirvan and Georgia. The khanate submitted to Russia in 1803, but Russian forts and taxes soon drove the highlanders to revolt under the imams Ghazi Mohammed and Hamzat Bek, opening the long Caucasian War of the mountain Dagestanis.
zh: 高加索阿瓦尔人自称马鲁拉尔，意为“山民”，是达吉斯坦山区最大的族群，据有高山谷地和以洪扎赫为中心的一批堡垒村庄，与中世纪早期那个横扫欧亚的阿瓦尔人并无历史渊源。5至12世纪，格鲁吉亚传教士把东正教带入他们的山谷；基督教的萨里尔王国在阿拉伯人及后来格鲁吉亚的庇护下长期统治达吉斯坦大部，10世纪的达图纳教堂是其留存的遗迹。13世纪初萨里尔覆灭后，穆斯林的阿瓦尔汗国取而代之，随阿拉伯商人和传道者而来的逊尼派伊斯兰教从14世纪起成为主要信仰。诸汗凭借与金帐汗国的结盟而致富，但在15世纪被对手卡济库穆赫沙姆哈拉特吞并。在萨法维王朝松散的宗主权下，阿瓦尔自由社群保留了大量自治权；18世纪，他们在安达拉尔击溃纳迪尔沙的一支军队，1774至1801年在位的乌玛汗更使阿瓦尔势力向希尔万和格鲁吉亚等地征收贡赋。1803年汗国向俄国臣服，但俄国的堡垒和赋税很快逼得山民在加齐·穆罕默德、哈姆扎特·贝克等伊玛目率领下起事，揭开了达吉斯坦山民漫长的高加索战争。

en: The Avoyel, also called the Flint People or People of the Rocks, were a small tribe of the lower Red River in Louisiana, with palisaded villages near modern Marksville and Alexandria and command of the waterway down to its junction with the Atchafalaya and the Mississippi. Their Tunican name Shi'xkaltī'ni means Stone-Arrow-Point people, and they grew prominent as middlemen carrying flint from the Caddoan peoples to their north to the stone-poor Atakapa and Chitimacha of the Gulf coast. French records put their population at only 280 in 1698, the year Iberville met them and misleadingly dubbed them the little Taensas, although they were distinct from the Natchez-speaking Taensa further east; their own lost language may have been related to Natchez. Epidemic disease steadily reduced them, and when Tunica, Ofo and Biloxi groups settled around them in the 1780s and 1790s the surviving Avoyel married into those villages. In 1805 the Indian agent John Sibley reported that only two or three Avoyel women remained, living along the Ouachita River.
zh: 阿沃耶尔人又称燧石人或岩石人，是路易斯安那红河下游的小部落，在今马克斯维尔和亚历山德里亚附近建有栅栏村落，并控制着红河直到它与阿查法拉亚河及密西西比河汇流处的水道。他们的图尼卡语名字意为石箭镞人，作为中间商把北方卡多语族群的燧石贩运到墨西哥湾沿岸缺石的阿塔卡帕人和奇蒂马查人那里，由此闻名。据法国档案，1698年他们的人口仅二百八十人；同年伊贝维尔与他们接触，误称他们为小坦萨人，但他们与更东边说纳奇兹语的坦萨人并非同族，而他们自己已经失传的语言可能与纳奇兹语有亲缘关系。瘟疫使人口持续减少，18世纪80至90年代图尼卡人、奥福人和比洛克西人迁居其地后，幸存的阿沃耶尔人通过通婚融入这些村落。1805年，印第安事务官约翰·西布利记载，整个族群只剩下两三名妇女，生活在沃希塔河畔。

en: The Guajá, who call themselves Awá, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the eastern Amazon, living between the Mearim, Tocantins and Araguaia river basins in the forests of Maranhão and Pará. They were once settled villagers, but from about 1800, as European settlers and slave raiders pushed into the region and cleared its forests, they abandoned fixed villages and became nomadic hunter-gatherers, moving in small bands of a few dozen people who lived entirely off the forest's game, fruit and honey. Through the nineteenth century the raids and the loss of woodland continued, and the Guajá responded by withdrawing deeper into the interior, with some groups avoiding all contact with outsiders.
zh: 瓜雅人自称阿瓦，是亚马孙东部的图皮-瓜拉尼族群，栖息在马拉尼昂和帕拉一带梅阿林河、托坎廷斯河与阿拉瓜亚河流域之间的森林里。他们原本是定居村民，但大约从1800年起，随着欧洲殖民者和奴隶贩子侵入这一地区、砍伐森林，他们放弃固定村落，转为游牧式的狩猎采集者，以几十人一群的小队活动，完全依靠林中的猎物、果实和蜂蜜为生。整个19世纪，劫掠和林地丧失持续不断，瓜雅人的应对是向内陆更深处撤退，其中一些群体回避与外界的一切接触。

en: The Ãwa, better known as the Avá-Canoeiro, are a small Tupi-Guarani people of the Goiás and Tocantins interior, also recorded under the names Canoeiro, Carijó and Cara-Preta. One tradition holds that they descend from Carijó Guaraní brought north from São Paulo between 1724 and 1726 with the gold-seeking bandeira of Bartolomeu Bueno, who used them as miners and auxiliaries before the group regained its freedom and settled along the upper Tocantins, though their language points to older northern Tupi-Guarani roots instead. They first appear in written records in the early nineteenth century, clashing with cattle ranchers and gold prospectors along the Tocantins, whose valley linked the mining town of Goiás with Porto Real, the present-day Porto Nacional. Pressed by the ranches and garimpos that occupied their lands through the 1800s, part of the people withdrew to the Araguaia and by the end of the century had reached Bananal Island.
zh: 卡诺埃罗人自称阿瓦，通称阿瓦-卡诺埃罗，是戈亚斯和托坎廷斯内陆的一个小型图皮-瓜拉尼族群，也被记作卡诺埃罗、卡里若或黑脸人等名字。一种说法认为，他们是1724至1726年间随巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺的淘金旗队从圣保罗带到北方的卡里若瓜拉尼人后裔，先被当作矿工和辅助人员使用，旗队结束后重获自由，定居在托坎廷斯河上游；但他们的语言反而指向更古老的北部图皮-瓜拉尼根源。19世纪初的文献首次提到他们，当时他们在托坎廷斯河沿岸与牧场主和淘金者发生冲突，因为这条河谷连接着矿业城镇戈亚斯和皇家港（即今纳雄奈尔港）。整个19世纪，随着牧场和淘金点占据其土地，一部分人撤往阿拉瓜亚河，到该世纪末已抵达巴纳纳尔岛。

en: The Awa, also called Cuaiquer or Kwaiker and historically linked to the Sindagua, are an indigenous people of the very wet forests on the western slope of the Andes, straddling the border of southern Colombia and northern Ecuador from the Telembí River in Nariño down to the provinces of Carchi, Imbabura, Sucumbíos and Esmeraldas. They speak Awa Pit, a language of the Barbacoan family. Their gold-bearing lands drew Spanish raids from the sixteenth century, and the conquistadors called them barbacoas after their raised stilt houses. In 1590 the governor of Popayán raised a force to subdue the Sindagua but his expedition was destroyed, and the survivors withdrew deeper into the mountain forests. Traditionally organized in small extended-family groups, the Awa farmed rotating plots without burning, grew maize, beans and plantains, and hunted and fished between the fields and the rivers.
zh: 阿瓦皮特人又称库艾凯尔人或奎凯尔人，在历史上与辛达瓜人渊源相连，是安第斯山脉西麓极湿润森林中的原住民，分布在哥伦比亚南部与厄瓜多尔北部边境两侧，北起纳里尼奥的特伦比河，南至卡尔奇、因巴布拉、苏昆比奥斯和埃斯梅拉达斯诸省。他们使用的阿瓦皮特语属于巴巴科安语系。他们的土地盛产黄金，从16世纪起就不断招来西班牙人的袭掠；征服者还因其高脚桩屋把他们叫作巴尔巴科阿人。1590年，波帕扬总督集结兵力试图征服辛达瓜人，却全军覆灭，幸存者撤入更深的山林。阿瓦皮特人传统上以小型扩大家庭群体为单位，实行不烧荒的轮垦，种植玉米、菜豆和芭蕉，并在田地与河流之间狩猎捕鱼。

en: The Awad Bing, also called Biliau after their main village, are a small Austronesian-speaking people of seven villages near Astrolabe Bay on the Rai Coast of Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Their language serves neighbouring groups too: some of the Ngaing learn it for trade along the coast.
zh: 阿瓦比恩人又称比利奥人，得名于他们的主要村庄，是巴布亚新几内亚马当省拉伊海岸阿斯特罗莱布湾附近七个村庄里说南岛语的小族群。他们的语言也供邻近群体使用，部分奈因人学会它以便在沿海贸易。

en: Awadhis are the Indo-Aryan people of Awadh, the Gangetic plain around Lucknow, Raebareli and Ayodhya that corresponds to the ancient kingdom of Kosala, whose name survives in the dialect's older label Kosali. From 1350 their country passed in turn through the Delhi Sultanate, the Sharqi Sultans of Jaunpur, who held it from 1394 to 1478, and then the Mughals, who incorporated it under Humayun around 1555 and made it the Subah of Awadh. In this age the Awadhi tongue, alongside Braj, was one of the great literary languages of north India: the sixteenth-century poet Tulsidas composed the Ramcharitmanas, the life of Rama sung in every Hindu household, in an Awadhi that carried the speech of Ayodhya across the subcontinent. As Mughal Delhi weakened, the Persian adventurer Saadat Khan became governor in 1722 and founded the line of the Nawabs of Awadh, ruling first from Faizabad and then from Lucknow; their court made the region a centre of poetry, music, architecture and Shi'a learning until the mid-nineteenth century, when standard Hindi began to displace Awadhi from formal writing.
zh: 阿瓦德人是阿瓦德地区的印度-雅利安民族，散居在勒克瑙、赖伯雷利和阿约提亚一带的恒河平原，这片土地即古代的憍萨罗王国，阿瓦德语较古的别称“憍萨利语”便由此而来。1350年起，他们的乡土相继历经德里苏丹国、1394至1478年统治这里的江布尔沙尔基苏丹国，随后在约1555年被胡马雍并入莫卧儿帝国，设为阿瓦德苏巴。这一时期，阿瓦德语与布拉杰语并列，是北印度最重要的文学语言之一：16世纪诗人图尔西达斯用阿瓦德语写成《罗摩功行录》，这部讲述罗摩生平的诗篇进入了印度教的千家万户，也把阿约提亚的言语传遍次大陆。随着莫卧儿德里衰微，波斯冒险家萨阿达特·汗于1722年出任总督，开创阿瓦德纳瓦卜世系，先以法扎巴德、后以勒克瑙为都；他们的宫廷使这一地区成为诗歌、音乐、建筑和什叶派学术的中心，直到19世纪中叶标准印地语开始把阿瓦德语挤出书面场合。

en: The Awaete, better known as the Parakanã, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Pará interior, holding the forests between the lower Tocantins and Pacajá rivers. They are slash-and-burn farmers whose staple is bitter manioc, combined with hunting large mammals, and they speak an Akwáwa dialect of the Tupi-Guarani branch.
zh: 帕拉卡纳人自称阿瓦埃特，通称帕拉坎昂人，是帕拉州内陆的图皮-瓜拉尼族群，占据托坎廷斯河下游与帕卡雅河之间的森林。他们从事刀耕火种农业，主粮为苦木薯，同时捕猎大型哺乳动物，所说的阿夸瓦方言属于图皮-瓜拉尼语支。

en: The Awyi are a Papuan people of Skanto District in Keerom Regency, in the far north-east of Indonesian New Guinea near the Papua New Guinea border. Their language, also called Awye or Nyao, belongs to the Border or Upper Tami family, which spans both sides of the international boundary and takes its name from the upper Tami River country.
zh: 阿维人是印度尼西亚新几内亚岛最东北部基罗姆县斯坎托区的巴布亚族群，邻近巴布亚新几内亚边境。他们的语言又称阿耶语或尼尧语，属边境语系，亦称上塔米语系，该语系横跨国际边界两侧，因塔米河上游一带而得名。

en: The Awyu, also called Auyu or Awya, are a Papuan people of the Digul River basin in the lowlands of South Papua, Indonesia, with communities along the Digul, Mappi and Gondu rivers; their neighbours include the Yaghai and, to the west, the Muyu. They comprise subgroups such as the Aghu, whose speech is also called Central Awyu, along with Nohon, Pisa, Jair and Shiaxa, all speaking Awyu languages of the Greater Awyu branch of Trans-New Guinea. Hunting, gathering and fishing supply their staples of sago, fish and river shrimp, and their traditions trace the people's origin to a cave from which ancestors migrated east along the rivers to settle at Yehundakai. Certain animals and trees are held sacred, with prayers and offerings before entering the forest; headhunting was once practised, while peaceful exchange relations were kept with neighbouring Jair, Muyu and Mandobo communities. They form part of the ancient Papuan-speaking population whose presence on the island long predates the Austronesian seafarers who reached New Guinea's coasts around 1500 BCE.
zh: 阿维尤人又称奥尤人或阿维亚人，是印度尼西亚南巴布亚低地迪古尔河流域的巴布亚族群，村落散布在迪古尔河、马皮河和贡杜河沿岸，邻族包括雅凯人和西边的木尤人。他们分为阿古（其语言又称中阿维尤语）、诺洪、皮萨、查伊尔、希亚克萨等支系，所说的阿维尤诸语属跨新几内亚语系的大阿维尤分支。狩猎、采集和捕鱼提供了西米、鱼和河虾等主食；他们的起源传说称先民出自一个洞穴，沿河东迁，在叶洪达凯定居。部分动物和树木被视为神圣，入林前要祈祷献祭；猎头习俗曾一度盛行，同时他们与邻近的查伊尔、木尤和曼多博社群保持和平交换关系。阿维尤人是古老巴布亚语族群的一支，远在约公元前1500年南岛语航海者抵达新几内亚沿海之前便已生息于此。

en: The Ayamanes, or Ayomanes, were the Indigenous people of the Carora region in what is now Lara state in western Venezuela, holding the valley of the Tocuyo River and bordering the Jirajara, Caquetío and Achagua peoples; their Ayomán tongue was one of the few documented languages of the Jirajaran family. Their first European encounter came on 9 September 1530, when the German conquistador Nicolaus Federmann of the Welser concession marched up the Tocuyo in search of the wealthy district of Carohana, reached its main village on 7 October 1530 and received gifts of gold from its cacique. A later smallpox epidemic left so few Ayamanes that the survivors intermarried with their Jirajara neighbours. When Bishop Mariano Martí visited Siquisique in 1776 he still found the village of San Miguel de los Ayamanes, one of the last communities to keep the old name alive.
zh: 阿亚曼斯人又称阿约曼人，是今委内瑞拉西部拉腊州卡罗拉地区的原住民，据有托库约河谷，与希拉哈拉人、卡克蒂奥人和阿查瓜人为邻；他们的阿约曼语是希拉哈拉语系中少数留有文献记录的语言之一。1530年9月9日，他们首次遇上欧洲人：受韦尔泽家族特许权派遣的德国征服者尼科劳斯·费德曼沿托库约河而上，寻找富庶的卡罗阿纳地区，并于10月7日抵达其主要村落，接受了当地酋长赠送的黄金。后来一场天花大疫使阿亚曼斯人所剩无几，幸存者只能与邻近的希拉哈拉人通婚。1776年马里亚诺·马蒂主教巡视锡基西克时，仍找到了圣米格尔-德洛斯阿亚曼斯村，那是延续这个旧族名的最后聚落之一。

en: The Ayan-Mai are Evenki-speaking Tungus groups of the northern Okhotsk coast, roaming the taiga and shoreline between the Ulya and Maya rivers in what is now Khabarovsk Krai. Unlike inland reindeer breeders, the coastal Tungus combined hunting and small reindeer herds with salmon fishing and sea-mammal hunting, moving between winter forest camps and summer fishing grounds on the coast. In 1639 the cossack party of Ivan Moskvitin reached the Sea of Okhotsk at the Ulya, and the ostrog of Okhotsk was built from 1647 after fighting with local tribes; the coastal clans were then registered for the fur tribute, or yasak. Through the eighteenth century Okhotsk served as Russia's main Pacific port, tying the shoreline Tungus closely to the fur trade.
zh: 阿扬迈人是鄂霍次克海北岸说鄂温克语的通古斯群体，在今哈巴罗夫斯克边疆区境内乌利亚河与马亚河之间的泰加林和海岸间游猎。与内陆的驯鹿牧民不同，滨海通古斯人把狩猎、小规模驯鹿牧养同捕鲑鱼、猎海兽结合起来，在冬季林地营地和夏季海岸渔场之间迁徙。1639年，伊万·莫斯克维京率领的哥萨克队伍在乌利亚河口抵达鄂霍次克海；1647年起，俄军在与当地部族激战后兴建鄂霍次克堡，滨海各氏族随后被登记缴纳毛皮贡赋牙萨克。整个18世纪，鄂霍次克都是俄罗斯在太平洋的主要港口，海岸通古斯人由此被深深卷入毛皮贸易。

en: The Ayoreo, whose name means “true people” in their own Zamucoan tongue, are a Gran Chaco people spread across the country between the Paraguay, Pilcomayo, Parapetí and Grande rivers, spanning both Bolivia and Paraguay. They were organized into more than fifty autonomous local groups, among them the Totobiegosode, each belonging to one of seven clans, and lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers, moving through the dry forest after peccaries, tortoises and anteaters and gathering wild honey, while planting small stands of corn, beans and squash in the rainy season. The first Europeans to reach them were the Jesuits, who founded the San Ignacio Zamuco mission in the 1720s. It was abandoned in the 1740s, after which the Ayoreo returned to their roaming life and remained almost entirely beyond colonial reach for the rest of the period.
zh: 阿约雷奥人是大查科的族群，分布在巴拉圭河、皮科马约河、帕拉佩蒂河和格兰德河之间、横跨玻利维亚与巴拉圭的地带；在他们所属的萨穆科语族语言里，阿约雷奥意为“真正的人”。他们分成五十多个自主的地方群体，其中以托托别戈索德人最为知名，各群体分属七个氏族。阿约雷奥人以游猎采集为生，在旱生林中追逐西貒、陆龟和食蚁兽、采集野蜜，雨季还小片种植玉米、豆类和南瓜。最早接触他们的欧洲人是耶稣会士，18世纪20年代建立了圣伊格纳西奥·萨穆科传教站；该站于18世纪40年代被放弃，阿约雷奥人此后重新过上游徙生活，在本时期余下的时间里几乎完全处在殖民势力范围之外。

en: The Azerbaijanis are a Shia Muslim Turkic people speaking an Oghuz language, centered on the cities of Tabriz and Ardabil in northwestern Persia and the Caucasian lowlands beyond the Aras River. The older inhabitants of this region, called Azaris, spoke the Iranian Old Azeri tongue; from the eleventh century Seljuk conquests brought Oghuz Turkoman tribes onto the Iranian plateau, and the Mongol invasions swelled their numbers. The newcomers Turkified the local population and gradually turned to Shia Islam, while their early heroic legends were preserved in the dastan of Dede Korkut. In 1337 the old Ilkhanid realm was fragmenting, and Azerbaijan soon passed under the Turkoman Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu confederations. The Safavid order, born at Ardabil, drew on these same Turkoman tribes as its Qizilbash warriors and seized power in Persia in 1501, making Shia Islam the faith of the land; under Shah Abbas the Great in the early seventeenth century Tabriz and the whole province formed one of the empire's richest cores. After the Safavid collapse the Afsharids and then the Qajars, themselves Turkic dynasties, ruled the Azerbaijanis, until the Russo-Persian wars ended in the treaties of Gulistan of 1813 and Turkmenchay of 1828, which split the Azerbaijani-speaking people between Persian and Russian rule.
zh: 阿塞拜疆人是信奉伊斯兰教什叶派的突厥民族，说乌古斯语支的语言，聚居在波斯西北部的大不里士、阿尔达比勒诸城和阿拉斯河以北的高加索低地。该地早先的居民称阿扎尔人，使用伊朗语族的古阿塞拜疆语；11世纪塞尔柱征服把乌古斯突厥蛮部落带上伊朗高原，蒙古入侵又使他们人数大增。新来者使当地居民突厥化，并逐渐改宗什叶派，他们早期的英雄传说保存在《德德·科尔库特之书》史诗中。1337年伊尔汗国旧土正趋于瓦解，阿塞拜疆不久落入突厥蛮的黑羊王朝和白羊王朝之手。兴起于阿尔达比勒的萨法维修道团以这些突厥蛮部落为其克孜勒巴什战士，于1501年夺取波斯政权，将什叶派立为国教；17世纪初阿拔斯大帝在位时，大不里士和整个阿塞拜疆行省是帝国最富庶的核心地区之一。萨法维王朝崩溃后，同属突厥王朝的阿夫沙尔王朝和卡扎尔王朝先后统治阿塞拜疆人，直到俄波战争以1813年《古利斯坦条约》和1828年《土库曼恰伊条约》告终，将说阿塞拜疆语的民族分割在波斯与俄国两版版图之内。

en: The Bacan are the Malay-speaking people of the Bacan Islands, a chain south of Halmahera that includes Bacan, Kasiruta, Mandioli, Kayoa and Obi. Their tongue, Bacan Malay, is an unusual Malayic language in the Moluccas, brought by migrants from Borneo centuries ago and close to Brunei Malay rather than to the Ternate and Ambonese trade Malay around it. Their rulers, titled Kolano ma-dehe, stood at the head of one of the four kingdoms of Maluku, alongside Ternate, Tidore and Jailolo; Dutch chronicles date the realm to 1322, and in 1465 Prince Bakar carried its influence to the Ceram coast and Hitu. The clove and forest-products trade drew Muslim merchants, the elite began accepting Islam in the late fifteenth century, and the first Muslim sultan, Zainal Abidin, reigned around 1512. After 1512 the Portuguese made Bacan an ally, and Sultan Hairun was baptized as Dom João, until Ternate's Sultan Babullah forced him back to Islam and had him poisoned in 1577. Early in the seventeenth century the court moved from Kasiruta to Amasing on Bacan Island, and after 1609 the sultanate fell under the Dutch East India Company and shrank to a minor role in Moluccan affairs.
zh: 巴占人是巴占群岛的马来语居民。巴占群岛位于哈马黑拉岛以南，包括巴占、卡西鲁塔、曼迪奥利、卡约阿和奥比等岛屿。他们的语言巴占马来语是摩鹿加地区少见的马来语族语言，由数百年前自婆罗洲迁来的移民带来，与文莱马来语相近，而不同于周边的特尔纳特马来语、安汶马来语等贸易用语。其君主号称“远端之主”科拉诺·马赫德，与特尔纳特、蒂多雷、贾伊洛洛并称马鲁古四大王国。据荷兰史家记载，巴占王国建于1322年；1465年，巴卡尔亲王将势力扩展到斯兰岛海岸和安汶的希图。丁香与林产品贸易引来穆斯林商人，精英阶层在15世纪末开始皈依伊斯兰教，第一位穆斯林苏丹扎因·阿比丁约于1512年在位。1512年后葡萄牙人与巴占结盟，苏丹哈伊伦受洗取名堂·若昂，但特尔纳特的巴布拉苏丹迫其重新归信伊斯兰教，并于1577年将他毒杀。17世纪初，王宫从卡西鲁塔迁至巴占岛的阿马辛；1609年后苏丹国落入荷兰东印度公司掌控，在马鲁古事务中沦为次要角色。

en: The Badimaya, also written Badimia, are an Aboriginal people of the Mid West region of Western Australia. Their traditional country covered roughly 29,000 square kilometres, from the later gold towns of Cue and Mount Magnet in the north to Paynes Find in the south and Yalgoo in the south-west, bordered by Western Desert peoples to the east, the Noongar to the south-west and the Watjarri to the north-west; the name Wardal recorded by early ethnographers was a Badimaya band name. Their language belongs to the Kartu branch of the Pama-Nyungan family, and like other peoples of the region they practised circumcision and subincision in initiation. When the Swan River Colony was founded on the coast in 1829, Badimaya country lay well beyond the settled districts, and pastoralists and gold miners only entered it in the later nineteenth century.
zh: 巴迪玛亚人（也拼巴迪米亚）是西澳大利亚中西部地区的原住民。他们的传统领地约2.9万平方公里，北起后来的金矿镇克尤和马格尼特山，南至佩恩斯芬德，西南到亚尔古；东接西部沙漠诸族，西南邻努恩加人，西北邻瓦贾里人。早期民族志学者记录的“沃达尔”一名，便是巴迪玛亚人的一个分支称呼。他们的语言属帕马-牛雅语系的卡尔图语支，和该地区其他族群一样在入族仪式中行割礼和下切礼。1829年天鹅河殖民地在沿海建立时，巴迪玛亚人的土地远在定居区之外，直到19世纪后期才有牧人和淘金者进入。

en: The Badtjala, more often called the Butchulla, are an Aboriginal Australian people of K'gari, the great sand island off the coast of south-eastern Queensland, and of the adjoining mainland around Hervey Bay and the lower Mary River. The island's rich fishing grounds supported one of the densest Aboriginal populations in Australia, organised into three units, the Ngulungbara of the north, the Butchulla of the centre and the Dulingbara of the south, divided into nineteen clan groups. They spoke Badjala, a dialect of Gubbi Gubbi within the Pama-Nyungan family, and their name has been read as meaning sea folk. In July 1802 Matthew Flinders became the first European to land on K'gari, meeting a Ngulungbara group at Sandy Cape. In 1836 survivors of the wrecked Stirling Castle came ashore, and the captain's widow, Eliza Fraser, lived among the islanders for several weeks.
zh: 巴特贾拉人常称布丘拉人，是昆士兰东南沿海大沙岛卡加里及附近大陆上的澳大利亚原住民，大陆部分包括赫维湾与玛丽河下游一带。岛上渔场丰饶，养育了澳大利亚人口最稠密的原住民群体之一；全岛分为北、中、南三个群体，即恩古兰巴拉、布丘拉和杜林巴拉，其下共有十九个氏族。他们使用巴贾拉语，是帕马—牛雅语系古比古比语的一种方言，其族名有一种解释是海上之民的意思。1802年7月，马修·弗林德斯成为第一个登上卡加里的欧洲人，在桑迪角遇到恩古兰巴拉人的一支。1836年，失事的斯特灵城堡号幸存者上岸，船长遗孀伊莱莎·弗雷泽在岛民中生活了数周。

en: The Baga are a West African people of the mangrove swamps along Guinea's Atlantic coast, divided into subgroups such as the Mandori, Sitemu, Pukur, Koba and Kalum. Their name comes from a Susu phrase meaning people of the seaside. Baga oral tradition says they came from the inland highlands and were pushed west by stronger neighbors; as first-comers on the Upper Guinea coast they held landlord rights over later settlers and lived in autonomous communities without kings. They speak Baga languages of the Atlantic branch, related to Temne, and many also use Susu as a trade language. Mangrove rice farming, kola cultivation and salt-making supported them, and their animist ritual sculpture became prized in distant museums. From the sixteenth century Portuguese traders, and the mixed Portuguese lançados who married chiefs' daughters, tied them into coastal commerce; the Gomez and Fernandez families founded ruling dynasties. In the eighteenth century the Fula jihad state of the Futa Jallon launched slave raids against them from the 1720s, Susu migrants took over the inland trade and a Futa tax official was stationed at Bara. Under Mandé missionary influence most Baga converted to Islam by the later eighteenth century.
zh: 巴加人是生活在几内亚大西洋沿岸红树林沼泽地带的西非族群，下分曼多里、西特穆、普库尔、科巴、卡卢姆等支系。他们的名字来自苏苏语，意为“海边的人”。巴加口传传统称，他们原住内陆高地，被强邻逐向西方；作为上几内亚海岸的“先来者”，他们对后来的定居者享有地主权利，社会则由没有国王的自治社群组成。他们讲大西洋语支的巴加诸语，与泰姆内语相近，许多人还把苏苏语当作贸易通用语。红树林种稻、科拉果种植和制盐是他们的生计，其泛灵信仰仪式雕塑后来被远方的博物馆珍藏。16世纪起，葡萄牙商人以及与酋长之女通婚的葡裔混血兰萨多人把他们卷入沿海贸易，戈麦斯和费尔南德斯家族还建立了统治王朝。18世纪，富塔贾隆的富拉人圣战政权从18世纪20年代起对他们发动猎奴袭击，苏苏移民接管了内陆贸易，富塔贾隆还在巴拉派驻税官。在曼德穆斯林传教者的影响下，多数巴加人到18世纪后期改信了伊斯兰教。

en: The Baganda are the Bantu people of Buganda, the fertile hill country on the northwestern shore of Lake Victoria, which they call Nalubaale. They speak Luganda, and every Muganda belongs to one of the exogamous clans, traditionally fifty-two in number; the seven oldest clans claim roots in local rulers going back to about the year 400. Their kingdom was unified around the thirteenth century under its first king, Kato Kintu, and a second wave of clans arrived with Kabaka Kimera in about 1370. Ruled by the Kabaka from a hilltop court and organized through chiefs who gathered tribute from their villages and passed it up to the throne, Buganda grew from a small lakeshore polity into one of the strongest states of the African Great Lakes during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. At the end of the eighteenth century it seized Kooki and Buddu from the fading kingdom of Bunyoro, and most of its neighboring rulers came to send it tribute.
zh: 巴干达人是布干达的班图人，布干达位于维多利亚湖（他们称纳卢巴莱湖）西北岸肥沃的丘陵地带。他们讲卢干达语，每个巴干达人都属于一个外婚制氏族，传统上共有五十二个；其中最古老的七个氏族自称源自约公元400年以来的本地统治者。布干达王国约在13世纪由第一代国王卡托·金图统一，约1370年又有一批氏族随卡巴卡·基梅拉迁入。国家由卡巴卡（国王）在山顶宫廷统辖，酋长们从各自村落征收贡赋再上缴王座，布干达借此从一个湖滨小邦成长为18至19世纪非洲大湖地区最强的国家之一。18世纪末，它从衰落的布尼奥罗王国手中夺取科基和布杜，周边大多数统治者也都向它纳贡。

en: Baghelis are the Eastern Hindi-speaking people of Baghelkhand, the wooded Vindhya country of Rewa, Satna, Nagod and Chitrakuta, known in earlier centuries as Dahala. Their speech, Bagheli with its Godwani, Kumhari and Rewa varieties, stands close to neighbouring Awadhi and shares the Gangetic literary world of the eastern Hindi lands. The region takes its name from the Baghel Rajputs, a Vaghela branch of the Solanki clan, whose chief Vyaghra Dev founded the kingdom of Bandhogarh around 1140 and ruled from the hill fort of Bandhavgarh. His successors kept an independent court amid the rise of the Delhi sultans and the Mughals: the boy Akbar found refuge in Rewa when Humayun fled India, and in the mid-sixteenth century Raja Ramachandra Singh sent the musicians Tansen and, later, Birbal to the emperor's court. In 1580 Akbar folded Bandhogarh into his new Subah of Ilahabad, and in 1617 Maharaja Vikramaditya Singh moved the capital to Rewa town, from which the Baghel rajas ruled until they accepted British protection in 1812.
zh: 巴哥里人是讲东印地语的民族，住在温迪亚山脉林木覆盖的巴格尔坎德，即雷瓦、萨特纳、纳戈德和奇特拉库特一带，这片地区更早的名字是达哈拉。他们的巴哥里语有戈德瓦尼、库姆哈里和雷瓦等变体，与邻近的阿瓦德语相近，同属恒河流域东印地语的文学世界。该地区得名于巴格尔拉杰普特人——索兰基族的瓦盖拉分支，其首领维亚格拉·德夫约于1140年建立班多加尔王国，以班达伽山堡为都。在德里苏丹和莫卧儿人崛起的年代，他的后继者维持着独立宫廷：胡马雍出逃印度时，年幼的阿克巴曾在雷瓦避难；16世纪中叶，罗摩昌德拉·辛格王公把乐师坦森以及后来的比尔巴尔送入皇帝朝廷。1580年阿克巴将班多加尔并入新设的安拉阿巴德苏巴，1617年维克拉马迪亚·辛格王公把首都迁到雷瓦城，巴格尔诸王在此统治，直到1812年接受英国保护。

en: The Bagri are the Indo-Aryan people of the Bagar, the dry sandy tract where the Thar Desert meets the Indo-Gangetic plain, straddling north-western Rajputana and the Bhattiana frontier around Bhatner, Suratgarh and Anupgarh. Formerly called Jangladesh, this semi-arid grassland was long the country of semi-nomadic cattle-herding Jat and Bhatti clans, who turned to settled farming in the later medieval centuries. Their language, Bagri, belongs to the Rajasthani group but shares features with Haryanvi and Punjabi, including three lexical tones. In 1398 Timur's army stormed Bhatner on its march through the region, and in 1488 Rao Bika, a Rathore prince and son of the founder of Jodhpur, conquered Jangladesh and founded Bikaner, which grew into the principal state of the area. The Bikaner Rathores entered Mughal service under Akbar: Raja Rai Singh became a leading imperial general under Akbar and Jahangir, and their desert kingdom prospered on the caravan trade between Central Asia and the Gujarat coast. In the eighteenth century Bikaner fought repeated wars with Jodhpur and local thakurs, until in 1818 it accepted British paramountcy as a princely state.
zh: 巴加尔人是巴加尔地带的印度-雅利安居民，这片干旱沙土地带处于塔尔沙漠与印度河和恒河平原的交接处，横跨拉吉普坦纳西北部与巴蒂亚纳边地，巴特奈尔、苏勒德格尔和阿努普加尔一带都在其中。该地古称贾恩格拉德什，长期是半游牧的贾特、巴蒂等畜牧氏族的家园，他们在中世纪后期逐渐转为定居农耕。巴加尔语属拉贾斯坦语支，但与哈里亚纳语和旁遮普语有不少共同特征，例如三个词汇声调。1398年帖木儿的军队在进军途中攻克巴特奈尔；1488年，焦特布尔建立者之子、拉托尔王公拉奥·比卡征服贾恩格拉德什并建立比卡内尔，后者逐渐成长为这一地区最主要的邦国。比卡内尔的拉托尔人在阿克巴时期投入莫卧儿麾下，拉伊·辛格王公成为阿克巴和贾汉吉尔两朝的重要将领，这个沙漠王国也凭借中亚与古吉拉特海岸之间的商队贸易繁荣起来。18世纪比卡内尔与焦特布尔及地方塔库尔首领连年内战，最终于1818年接受英国宗主权，成为土邦。

en: The Bagua were the people of the lower Marañón valley in what is now Peru's Amazonas region, a forested land brought into the Inca Empire under Huayna Cápac. Their language survives in only three words and cannot be classified; after the conquest the valley switched to Spanish and Aguaruna, and the town of Bagua was founded in 1561.
zh: 巴瓜人生活在今秘鲁亚马孙大区马拉尼翁河下游的林区，这片土地在瓦伊纳·卡帕克时期被并入印加帝国。他们的语言仅存三个有记录的词、无法确定语系，征服后谷地改用西班牙语和阿瓜鲁纳语，巴瓜镇于1561年建立。

en: The Baguirmi, who call themselves the Barma, are the people of the Chari-Baguirmi plain southeast of Lake Chad, farmers of sorghum and millet who also raise cattle and speak the Bagirmi language, though many also use Fula or Chadian Arabic. Their traditions claim a migration from the distant east, and their kingdom was founded at Massenya around 1522 by the first mbang, Birni Besse, after the expulsion of the earlier Bilala. Under Mbang Abdullah, who reigned from 1568 to 1608, the court converted to Islam and the realm became a sultanate, but ordinary Baguirmi long kept their old beliefs. The Bornu emperor Idris Alooma conquered the young state, and for generations it paid tribute in slaves raided from the pagan peoples to its south; it grew rich on the trans-Saharan trade, exporting ivory, skins, cotton and eunuchs as far as Tripoli. Under Burkumanda, between 1635 and 1665, its raiders pushed north to Lake Chad, and Muhammad al-Amin rewon independence from Bornu in 1751. In 1805 Wadai sacked Massenya, killed the mbang and carried off twenty thousand captives, reducing Baguirmi to a tributary.
zh: 巴吉尔米人自称巴尔马人，是乍得湖东南沙里—巴吉尔米平原上的居民，种植高粱和小米，兼营养牛，母语为巴吉尔米语，许多人也兼通富拉语或乍得阿拉伯语。按本民族传说，他们来自遥远的东方；约1522年，初代姆班比尔尼·贝塞在驱逐早先的比拉拉人后，定都马塞尼亚建立王国。1568至1608年在位的姆班阿卜杜拉率宫廷改宗伊斯兰教，国家成为苏丹国，但普通巴吉尔米人长期保留旧有信仰。博尔努皇帝伊德里斯·阿卢马征服了这个年轻国家，此后几代人它都以从南方异教族群掳来的奴隶纳贡；它靠跨撒哈拉贸易致富，把象牙、皮革、棉花和阉人远销到的黎波里。1635至1665年在位的布尔库曼达时期，劫掠队向北推进到乍得湖；1751年，穆罕默德·阿明又从博尔努手中赢得独立。1805年，瓦达伊攻陷马塞尼亚，杀死姆班，掳走两万人，巴吉尔米就此沦为附庸。

en: The Baham, or Mbaham, are a Papuan people of the western Bomberai Peninsula, living in the coastal districts of Fakfak Regency around the town of Fakfak. Together with the Iha language their tongue forms the Mbaham-Iha subgroup of the West Bomberai family, whose more distant relatives include the languages of Timor, Alor and Pantar.
zh: 姆巴哈姆人是邦贝拉伊半岛西部的巴布亚族群，聚居在法克法克县沿海各区，以法克法克镇为中心。他们的语言与伊哈语共同构成西邦贝拉伊语族的姆巴哈姆-伊哈语支，该语族的远亲还包括帝汶、阿洛和潘塔尔诸岛的语言。

en: The Bahau, also called Kayan Mekam, are a Kayanic Dayak people of the upper Mahakam River in East Kalimantan, counted among the Apo Kayan group and divided into the Modang, Busang and Saq branches. They speak a Kayan-Murik language, build riverside longhouses, stretch their earlobes with heavy earrings and perform the masked Hudoq dance.
zh: 巴豪人又称卡扬梅坎人，是东加里曼丹马哈坎河上游的卡扬语族达雅人，被归入阿保卡扬群体，分为莫当、布桑和萨克三支。他们使用卡扬-穆里克语族的语言，临河修建长屋，以重耳环拉长耳垂，并跳戴面具的胡多克舞。

en: The Bahnar, or Ba-Na, are an Austroasiatic people of the Central Highlands in present-day Vietnam, concentrated in the Gia Lai and Kon Tum plateaus with communities also in the coastal provinces of Binh Dinh and Phu Yen. Their Bahnar language belongs to the Bahnaric branch of the Mon-Khmer family, and the people comprise many local groups, among them the Jolong, Rongao, Tolo and Golar. Traditionally matrilineal swidden farmers, they honoured spirits with gong ensembles, buffalo sacrifice and recited epics such as Dam Noi. From about 1150 their highland valleys came under the Cham kingdom of Champa, whose power still ringed them in 1337. In 1471 the Vietnamese emperor Le Thanh Tong stormed the Cham capital of Vijaya, after which the Bahnar felt growing Vietnamese, Lao and Thai pressure. In 1771 the Tay Son rising began in the nearby coastal lowlands, pulling highland villages into the wars that ended with the establishment of the Nguyen dynasty in 1802.
zh: 巴拿人是南亚语系民族，居住在今天越南中部的中央高地，集中于嘉莱和昆嵩一带，在沿海的平定、富安等地也有分布。他们的巴拿语属于孟高棉语族的巴拿语支，内部又有约隆、罗敖、托洛、戈拉等众多按居地命名的支系。巴拿人传统上是母系社会，从事刀耕火种，以成套铜锣、宰牛献祭和《丹诺伊》等口传史诗侍奉神灵。约从1150年起，他们的高地山谷被占婆王国控制，1337年前后仍处在占婆势力的包围之中。1471年越南皇帝黎圣宗攻破占城都城佛逝，此后巴拿人日益受到越南、老挝和泰人势力的压力。1771年西山起义在邻近的沿海低地爆发，高地村落被卷入这场战乱，战争最终以1802年阮朝建立告终。

en: The Bahrani are the Shia Arab inhabitants of the historical Bahrain region, the islands and oases of the Gulf covering Bahrain, Qatif and Al-Ahsa, and they are commonly regarded as its original settled population, descended from Aramaic-speaking farmers, Nestorian Christian Arabs and Persian settlers before Islam. They entered Islam in 628, when the Prophet's envoy Al-Ala'a Al-Hadrami won over their ruler Munzir ibn Sawa, and their Bahrani Arabic still keeps Akkadian and Aramaic words for farming and daily life. Medieval dynasties from the Qarmatians to the Uyunids, Usfurids and Jarwanids ruled them, and the Shia scholar Maitham al-Bahrani, who died in 1299, made Bahrain a center of Shia learning. A Portuguese fleet under António Correia seized the islands in 1521, after which Safavid Persia shaped their Twelver faith. Omani and Persian invasions troubled the eighteenth century until 1783, when the Sunni Al Khalifa family of Najd conquered Bahrain, leaving the Bahrani as subjects in their own land; many then migrated to Kuwait, Basra and the Iranian ports, carrying their crafts of shipbuilding, pottery and palm weaving.
zh: 巴林人（又称巴哈纳人）是历史上巴林地区的什叶派阿拉伯居民，分布在海湾的岛屿与绿洲，包括巴林、盖提夫和哈萨一带，通常被视为当地最早的定居居民，祖先是伊斯兰化以前讲阿拉姆语的农民、信奉聂斯托利派的阿拉伯基督徒和波斯移民。628年，先知的使者阿拉·哈德拉米争取到其统治者蒙齐尔·本·萨瓦归信，他们随之皈依伊斯兰教；他们的巴林阿拉伯语仍保留着阿卡德语和阿拉姆语的农事与生活词汇。中世纪时，卡尔马特、乌尤尼德、乌斯富里德和贾尔万尼德等王朝先后统治他们，13世纪的什叶派学者迈萨姆·巴哈尼于1299年去世，曾使巴林成为什叶派学术中心。1521年，安东尼奥·科雷亚率领的葡萄牙舰队夺取群岛，此后萨法维波斯塑造了他们的十二伊玛目派信仰。18世纪阿曼与波斯的入侵接连不断，1783年来自内志的逊尼派哈利法家族征服巴林，巴林人沦为故土上的被统治者，许多人迁居科威特、巴士拉和伊朗港口，也带去了造船、制陶和棕榈编织等手艺。

en: The Bai are the people of the Erhai Lake basin in northwestern Yunnan, one of the oldest settled populations of the southwest and among the most deeply sinicized of China's minorities. Chinese texts knew them as the Bo or Bai people from the Tang, and from the fourteenth century called them Minjia, the civilian households. They formed the backbone of the Nanzhao kingdom of 649–902, supplying its ministers and townsmen, and in 937 the Bai chieftain Duan Siping founded the Dali kingdom, which gave the Erhai country three centuries of stable rule under a court steeped in Chinese letters and Buddhism. When the Mongols took Dali in 1253 the Yuan kept the Duan family as local governors, so that in 1337 the Bai valleys around Taihe, Heqing and Langqiong were still administered by their old ruling house under imperial supervision. The Ming conquest of 1381 ended that arrangement: the last Duan ruler was deposed, Dali became a prefecture, and Han soldiers and farmers poured into the basin, sharpening the Bai's long absorption of Chinese customs. Their Bai language, though heavy with Chinese loanwords, remains a Tibeto-Burman tongue, and Bai life kept its own marks in white dress, tie-dyed cloth, cormorant fishing on Erhai and the grey-brick courtyard houses of the old Dali towns.
zh: 白族是云南西北洱海盆地的居民，西南最古老的定居人群之一，也是中国汉化最深的少数民族之一。汉文文献从唐代起称他们为白（僰）人，14世纪以后又多称“民家”。他们曾是649至902年南诏国的中坚，出任大臣、营建城邑；937年，白族首领段思平建立大理国，使洱海地区在一个深受汉文化与佛教影响的王朝治下安享近三百年。1253年蒙古灭大理，元朝仍留段氏治理地方，因此1337年时，太和、鹤庆、浪穹一带的白族河谷仍由旧王室在朝廷监督下管理。1381年明军入滇终结了这一安排：末代段氏被废，大理设府，汉地军士和农户大量迁入屯垦，白族吸收汉俗的进程进一步加深。白语虽饱含汉语借词，仍是一种藏缅语；而白族生活也保留着鲜明的本族印记：尚白的衣着、扎染布匹、洱海的鱼鹰捕鱼，以及大理古城的青砖合院民居。

en: The Baima, whose name means White Horse, are a people of the forested mountains on the Sichuan and Gansu border, chiefly in Pingwu and Jiuzhaigou counties and in Wen County, where they call themselves Bai. They trace their descent from the Baima Di, one of the ancient Di tribes of western China who were linked with the Qiang. After Songtsen Gampo built the Tibetan Empire in the 600s, the Baima were drawn into the Tibetan world and gradually exchanged their old Di speech for an Amdo Tibetan tongue; their Baima language remains unwritten, with a symbol system used only in ritual. They kept an older religion of nature and totem worship, later coloured by Bon, honouring the Mountain God as their highest deity through dances such as the Caogai, and absorbed Buddhist and Daoist ideas without maintaining monasteries or lamas of their own.
zh: 白马人意为“白马之人”，是川甘边界山林地带的族群，主要聚居于平武、九寨沟和文县，自称“贝”。他们是白马氐的后裔，氐是中国西部与羌族关系密切的古老族群，古称氐羌。7世纪松赞干布建立吐蕃王朝后，白马人被纳入吐蕃世界，逐渐放弃古老的氐语而改操安多藏语；白马语没有文字，仅在宗教活动中使用一种符号体系。他们保留着古老的自然崇拜和图腾崇拜，后来又受到苯教影响，奉山神为最高神，以“曹盖”舞等仪式事神，同时吸收了佛教和道教的观念，却没有自己的寺院和喇嘛。

en: The Baining are the indigenous people of the Gazelle Peninsula in eastern New Britain, living mainly in the rugged Baining Mountains, from which they take their name. They are likely the peninsula's original inhabitants, on an island settled by Papuan peoples for tens of thousands of years; over the centuries they were pushed inland from the coast by migrating Tolai groups and by repeated volcanic activity around Rabaul, and they keep to semi-nomadic swidden gardening whose staple crop is taro. Their languages form a small family of their own, comprising Mali, Qaqet, Kairak, Simbali and Ura, each tied to a separate clan identity. Baining society is notably egalitarian, and its most famous ceremony is the night fire dance, in which dancers wearing large bark-cloth masks leap through the embers of a fire before the masks are destroyed after a single use. The outside world reached them only in 1700, when William Dampier became the first recorded European to visit New Britain and gave the island its name.
zh: 拜宁人是新不列颠岛东部加泽尔半岛的原住民，主要聚居在崎岖的拜宁山区，并因山得名。他们可能是半岛最早的居民，而该岛已有巴布亚人数万年的居住史；数百年来，迁至沿海的托拉伊人的挤压，加上拉包尔一带反复的火山活动，把他们从海岸逼进内陆。拜宁人过着半游耕的刀耕火种生活，主粮是芋头。他们的语言自成一个小语族，包括马利语、夸凯特语、凯拉克语、辛巴利语和乌拉语，每种语言对应不同的氏族身份。拜宁社会以平等著称，最有名的仪式是夜间火舞：舞者戴着树皮布制成的大面具跃过火堆余烬，而面具只用一次便被销毁。外部世界迟至1700年才到来：当年威廉·丹皮尔成为有记载以来首位登上新不列颠岛的欧洲人，并为该岛命名。

en: The Baiyungu are an Aboriginal people of the Gascoyne coast of Western Australia, holding about 4,000 square miles along the Lower Lyndon and Minilya Rivers and running south-west to Quobba. With the Yinggarda, Maia and Yinikutira they made up the Kakarakala grouping, the eastern fires known to the Mandi, and their Bayungu language was spoken along the Minilya.
zh: 白云古人是西澳大利亚加斯科因海岸的原住民，沿下林登河和米尼利亚河而居，领地约四千平方英里，向西南延伸到阔巴一带。他们与英加尔达人、马亚人、伊尼库提拉人同属曼迪人所称的“卡拉卡拉”群体，意为“东方之火”；其巴永古语通行于米尼利亚河沿岸。

en: The Baka are a forest hunter-gatherer people of the Mbenga, the western group of Central African foragers, roaming the rainforests of south-eastern Cameroon, northern Gabon and the adjacent Congo and Central African Republic lands in small camps of leaf huts. Their men hunt with poisoned arrows and spears while the women fish, gather wild plants and honey and tend small plantain groves, and each camp decides its affairs by consensus under the protection of Jengi, the forest spirit who mediates between the Baka and the supreme being Komba. They descend from the rainforest's ancient foraging populations, whom Ubangian and Central Sudanic farmers absorbed or displaced from about 3500 BCE and expanding Bantu villagers from about 1500 BCE. The Baka speak an Ubangian tongue close to that of the Ngbaka, although roughly a third of its words, mostly names of forest plants and honey, survive from an older forager language. Living beside Bantu farming clans such as the Bulu, they traded game and forest produce for iron and crops, a relationship that also exposed them to enslavement by their stronger neighbours.
zh: 巴卡人是中部非洲西部采集族群姆本加人的一支，是以森林狩猎采集为生的族群，在喀麦隆东南部、加蓬北部以及相邻的刚果和中非共和国土地上的热带雨林中活动，以树枝搭架、覆以大叶的临时小屋组成小营地。男子用毒箭和长矛狩猎，妇女捕鱼、采集野果和蜂蜜并照料小片芭蕉林；营地事务集体协商决定，他们信奉森林之灵詹吉，认为它是巴卡人与至高神昆巴之间的中介。巴卡人是雨林古老采集居民的后裔：约公元前3500年起，乌班吉和中苏丹语农民吸纳或驱走了他们，约公元前1500年起，扩张中的班图农民又接踵而至。巴卡人的母语已转为与恩格巴卡语相近的乌班吉语，但语言中约三分之一的词汇——多为森林植物和蜂蜜的名称——仍保留自更古老的采集者语言。他们与布鲁人等班图农业氏族为邻，用猎物和林产交换铁器和农作物，这种关系也使他们常遭较强邻邦掳掠为奴。

en: The Kele, who call themselves Ungom and are also known as Akele or Bakele, are a Bantu people of central Gabon. Oral traditions place their earliest settlements around Lopé on the middle Ogooué, from where their clans fragmented and spread through the Ogooué basin, probably during the 1600s and 1700s, some reaching the Estuaire coast and the upper Ngounié. Reputed as skilled hunters and river travellers, they became one of the main groups taking part in the slave trade with European ships on the coast, and their clans were bound together by initiation societies such as the Ndokwè. Their ethnonym is said to mean people of war, recalling the long era of migration and conflict behind their dispersal.
zh: 巴克勒人自称温贡人，亦称阿克勒人，是加蓬中部的班图族群。口传传统把他们最早的定居点追溯到奥果韦河中游的洛佩一带，后来各氏族在17至18世纪间分散迁徙，遍布奥果韦河流域，部分支系远达河口省沿海和恩古涅河上游。他们以善猎和擅长河上旅行著称，是在沿海参与欧洲商船奴隶贸易的主要族群之一，各氏族则靠恩多克韦等成年礼组织维系。据说其族名含义是“战争之民”，折射出他们分散迁徙过程中漫长的战乱岁月。

en: The Balanta, whose Mandinka name means those who resist, are a West Atlantic people of the coastal flats and mangrove channels of Guinea-Bissau, settled chiefly south of the Geba River, with communities in southern Senegal, Gambia and Guinea. Archaeological evidence suggests their ancestors arrived from the east in small migrant groups between the 900s and the 1300s, while their own oral traditions place their earliest home in the Sudan; they call the land between the Mansôa and Geba rivers their homeland of Nhacra. They never built kingship on the model of the empires around them, but lived in autonomous clan villages governed by councils of elders, where standing came from age-set initiations crowned by the Fanado ceremony held in the sacred woods every four years. Expert rice farmers, they devised irrigation works blending salt and fresh water to keep their paddies fertile and raised cattle for sacrifice at every stage of life. As the Kaabu kingdom expanded in the 1800s, Balanta groups spread further through the region rather than submit, the resistance that gave them their name.
zh: 巴兰塔人在曼丁哥语中的名字意为反抗者，是说西非大西洋语支语言的民族，居住在几内亚比绍的沿海低地与红树林水道之间，主要聚居于热巴河以南，在塞内加尔南部、冈比亚和几内亚也有社群。考古证据显示，他们的祖先在10至14世纪间分成小批移民自东方而来，其口述传统则把最早的家园指向苏丹地区；他们把曼索阿河与热巴河之间的土地称为故乡尼亚克拉。他们没有像周围的帝国那样建立王权，而是生活在自治的氏族村庄里，由长老会议治理，地位取决于年龄组的入会仪式，其中最高的是每隔四年在圣林中举行的法纳多礼。巴兰塔人是种稻能手，修建了混用咸水与淡水的灌溉工程以保持稻田肥力，并养牛用于人生各阶段的献祭。19世纪卡布王国扩张时，巴兰塔诸部不愿臣服，进一步向各地流散，这种反抗精神也正是他们名字的由来。

en: The Balinese are the Austronesian people of the island of Bali east of Java, distinguished in the archipelago by their Hindu faith, the holy-water religion of Agama Tirta layered over older local cults that the Bali Aga villages still keep. Indianised kings ruled from the ninth century, when the Warmadewa dynasty left the Belanjong pillar of 914, and in 1343 Gajah Mada's Majapahit armies conquered the island, ruling first from Samprangan and then Gelgel. Javanese arts came with the conquest: the Kawi script, wayang shadow theatre, temple architecture and gamelan. When Majapahit collapsed around 1500, Hindu nobles and priests fled to Bali, and the Gelgel kingdom kept the island independent; in the sixteenth century Dalem Baturenggong carried Balinese rule into East Java, Lombok and western Sumbawa, while the reformer Dang Hyang Nirartha founded the temple of Uluwatu and fixed the present form of Balinese Shiva worship. Portuguese ships reached the coast in 1512 and the Dutchman Cornelis de Houtman in 1597, but the Dutch East India Company found Bali unprofitable and left it to private traders. Only after 1816, when the Indies returned to Dutch rule, did the colonial government press treaties on the island's rival kingdoms.
zh: 巴厘人是爪哇以东巴厘岛的南岛语系民族，在群岛诸族中以信奉印度教著称；他们的阿加马·蒂尔塔“圣水教”叠加在更古老的本土信仰之上，巴厘阿加人的村落仍保留着旧俗。9世纪起，印度化的诸王在此立国，瓦尔马德瓦王朝留下了914年的贝兰宗石柱；1343年，加查·马达统率的满者伯夷军队征服巴厘，先后以桑普兰安和格格尔为治所。爪哇艺术随军传入：卡威文字、哇扬皮影戏、寺庙建筑和甘美兰音乐。1500年前后满者伯夷灭亡，印度教贵族与祭司逃来巴厘，格格尔王国维持了岛屿的独立；16世纪，达伦·巴图伦贡把巴厘的统治扩展到东爪哇、龙目岛和松巴哇岛西部，改革家当·延·尼拉尔塔则创建乌鲁瓦图神庙，奠定了巴厘湿婆崇拜的现存形态。1512年葡萄牙船只抵达海岸，1597年荷兰人科内利斯·德·霍特曼来访，但荷兰东印度公司觉得巴厘无利可图，把它留给私商经营。直到1816年荷属东印度归还荷兰后，殖民政府才开始向岛上相互争雄的诸王国强签条约。

en: The Balkars are a Kipchak Turkic people of the high central Caucasus, holding the gorges of the Cherek, Chegem, Baksan and Malka rivers on the eastern side of Mount Elbrus; they call themselves the alanla, or Alans, as well as the mountaineers. Their tongue, shared with the Karachays across the range, belongs to the Ponto-Caspian branch of Kipchak, and their ancestry joins native Caucasian highlanders to Bulgar and Khazar Turks, Iranian Alans and two waves of Kipchak migrants, the second driven into the mountains when Timur shattered Tokhtamysh's armies in 1395. Most Balkars accepted Islam only in the eighteenth century, under the influence of Kumyks, Circassians, Nogais and Crimean Tatars, and the Qadiri Sufi order grew strong in their auls. Their high valleys made them valued allies of the Kabardians in every rising against the Russian advance: they fought at the battle of the Chegem in 1804 and held the fortified gorges of the Cherek against General Bulgakov in 1810. In 1828 General Emanuel's expedition over the snow passes imposed Russian rule on the Karachay and Balkar highlands, yet in 1830 and 1831 the mountain communities swore a league of mutual aid with the Circassians and Abazins, choosing Sefer Bey Zanoko as their envoy, and kept up the fight into 1833.
zh: 巴尔卡尔人是高加索中部高山中的钦察突厥语民族，据有厄尔布鲁士山东侧切列克河、切格姆河、巴克桑河和马尔卡河的峡谷；他们自称“阿兰拉”，即阿兰人，也自称山民。他们与山那边的卡拉恰伊人共用属钦察语黑海—里海分支的语言，族源则融合了高加索本地山民、保加尔与可萨突厥人、伊朗语阿兰人以及两波钦察移民，其中第二波是1395年帖木儿击垮脱脱迷失大军后逃入深山的部众。大多数巴尔卡尔人迟至18世纪才在库梅克人、切尔克斯人、诺盖人和克里米亚鞑靼人影响下改奉伊斯兰教，卡迪里苏菲教团随后在山村中壮大。险峻的峡谷使他们成为卡巴尔达人历次反俄起义的得力盟友：1804年他们参加切格姆河之战，1810年又在切列克河的设防峡谷中阻击布尔加科夫将军。1828年，埃马努埃尔将军翻越积雪山口的远征把俄国统治强加给卡拉恰伊和巴尔卡尔山区；然而1830—1831年，这些山民社区仍与切尔克斯人、阿巴扎人缔结盟约、互相支援，并推举塞费尔·贝·扎诺科为使节，战事一直持续到1833年。

en: The Baloch are a Western Iranian people of the arid plateau and coast of Balochistan, speaking Balochi and long organized into nomadic pastoral tribes. Their linguistic homeland probably lay southeast of the Caspian, and from the late Sasanian period they drifted east over many centuries into Kerman, Makran and Sistan, where Arab geographers already described them as a numerous cattle-herding people by the ninth century. The Seljuk conquest of Kerman in the twelfth century pushed fresh waves eastward; tradition makes Jalal Khan the founder of the first Baloch confederacy in that age, and through the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries the tribes entered Sindh and the Sulaiman Mountains, the very country around Sibi and Kahan where they appear in 1337, before moving on into the Punjab in the fifteenth. Mir Chakar's Rind confederacy even briefly held Multan. Caught between the Safavids and the Mughals, the Baloch coalesced into the Khanate of Kalat from the seventeenth century, confirmed under Mir Ahmad Khan in 1666 and reaching its height under Nasir Khan I, while Baloch arms also served Nader Shah and the Talpur dynasty built its own rule over Sindh in the later eighteenth century.
zh: 俾路支人是西伊朗语族民族，生活在俾路支斯坦的干旱高原与海岸，讲俾路支语，长期以游牧部落为组织形式。其语言上的故地可能在里海东南，自萨珊晚期起历经数世纪东迁，进入克尔曼、莫克兰和锡斯坦，9世纪时阿拉伯地理学家已称他们为人数众多、从事畜牧的族群。12世纪塞尔柱人征服克尔曼，推动新的东迁浪潮；传说贾拉尔汗在这一时期建立第一个俾路支联盟，13至14世纪诸部落进入信德和苏莱曼山区，即1337年他们所在的锡比、卡汉一带，15世纪又进一步进入旁遮普。米尔·查卡尔的林德联盟还曾短暂占据木尔坦。在萨法维与莫卧儿两大势力之间，俾路支人于17世纪起凝聚为卡拉特汗国，1666年米尔·艾哈迈德汗正式确立统治，到纳西尔汗一世时臻于鼎盛；此外俾路支武人为纳迪尔沙效力，塔尔普尔王朝则在18世纪后期统治信德。

en: The Balotipone, known in the sources as the Umutina and once nicknamed the Barbados, or Bearded Ones, because their sparse beards were worn as a mark of manly pride, are a people of the right bank of the Paraguay River in Mato Grosso. Their Umotina language belonged to the Bororoan branch of the Macro-Ge family. They were farmers above all, growing maize and manioc in village gardens, fishing with bow and arrow, and rounding out their diet by hunting and by gathering honey, fruit, mushrooms and medicinal herbs. Their society was monogamous, parents arranged their daughters' marriages, and the wedding pair painted their whole bodies with red urucu dye for the ceremony. Through the 1800s they kept their riverine territory closed to outsiders by force, long after many neighboring peoples had been subdued.
zh: 巴洛蒂波内人在文献中称乌穆蒂纳人，又因把稀疏的胡须视为男子气概的象征而被外人叫作“大胡子”。他们住在马托格罗索的巴拉圭河右岸，所说的乌穆蒂纳语属大热语系下的博罗罗语支。他们以农耕为主，在村边园圃种植玉米和木薯，用弓箭捕鱼，并以狩猎和采集蜂蜜、果实、蘑菇、药草补充食物。社会实行一夫一妻制，女儿的婚事由父母安排，婚礼上新婚夫妇要用红色胭脂树染料涂满全身。整个19世纪，他们一直以武力阻止外人进入自己的河畔领地，比周边许多族群保持独立的时间都长。

en: The Balti are a Tibetic people of the high Indus valley in Baltistan, which they call Balti-yul and Persian writers named Little Tibet, centred on Skardu, Shigar and Khaplu with further communities in Kargil. They took shape from Tibetan Khampa settlers mingling with older Dardic tribes; the land lay in the Zhangzhung sphere before passing under the Tibetan Empire in 686, and its people followed Bön and then Tibetan Buddhism. Their speech remains an archaic Tibetic language, closer to Classical Tibetan than most of its relatives. Medieval Baltistan was a patchwork of valley kingdoms, chiefly Skardu, Shigar and Khaplu. The Maqpon dynasty of Skardu, traditionally founded in the twelfth century, ruled for some seven hundred years and reached its height under Ali Sher Khan Anchan around 1600, when Balti arms reached Gilgit, Chitral and Ladakh and the court opened ties with the Mughals, then masters of Kashmir. From the fourteenth century Sufi missionaries such as Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani carried Islam into the valleys, the Noorbakhshia order spread it widely, and by the end of the seventeenth century most Balti had converted, though many Bön and Buddhist customs survived.
zh: 巴尔蒂人是藏语支族群，聚居在印度河上游高海拔河谷巴尔蒂斯坦——他们自称巴尔蒂尤尔，波斯文献称之为“小西藏”，核心城市为斯卡都、希加尔和哈伯鲁，另有部众住在卡吉尔。他们由入藏的康巴移民与更古老的达尔迪部落融合而成；这一带原在象雄势力范围内，686年并入吐蕃帝国，居民先后信奉苯教与藏传佛教。巴尔蒂语是一种古老的藏语支语言，比多数亲属语言更接近古典藏语。中世纪的巴尔蒂斯坦分裂为若干河谷小邦，主要是斯卡都、希加尔和哈伯鲁；传统上认为12世纪兴起于斯卡都的玛格本王朝统治了约七百年，约1600年在阿里·谢尔·汗·安昌治下达到鼎盛，兵锋远及吉尔吉特、吉德拉尔和拉达克，并与已据有克什米尔的莫卧儿宫廷建立联系。14世纪起，哈马丹尼等苏非修士把伊斯兰传入山谷，努尔巴赫希亚教团广为宣教，到17世纪末多数巴尔蒂人已改宗，但许多苯教与佛教遗俗仍长期留存于民间。

en: The Bambara, or Bamana, are a Mandé people of the upper Niger basin, settled around Djenné, Macina and Ségou in what is now central Mali, and their language is mutually intelligible with Manding and Dyula. Originally a royal branch of the Mandinka, they emerged as a distinct power after the Songhai Empire dissolved around 1600, when Mandé farming communities along the river turned in on themselves. About 1640 Kaladian Coulibaly founded a small Bambara kingdom at Ségou, and in 1712 his descendant Bitòn Coulibaly turned a youth fraternity, the tòn, into a standing army and took the title faama, building the Bambara Empire of Ségou with war canoes on the Niger and cowrie-shell taxation. His armies took Macina, Djenné and Bamako, and in 1751 reduced the old Mali mansa to a vassal. After mid-century civil wars, the former slave Ngolo Diarra seized the throne in 1766 and ruled for nearly thirty years of prosperity. Unlike their Muslim neighbours the Bambara state upheld traditional polytheistic worship, and in 1818 Seku Amadu's Fulani jihad defeated it at Noukouma and tore away Djenné and Macina for the new Massina Empire. Its caste-based Mandé society placed nobles above griots, smiths and slave-descended fishing peoples such as the Bozo.
zh: 班巴拉人自称巴马纳，是尼日尔河上游流域的曼德人，聚居于今马里中部的杰内、马西纳和塞古一带，所讲的班巴拉语与曼丁语、朱拉语可以互通。他们本是曼丁卡人的一个王族分支，1600年前后桑海帝国瓦解后，沿河的曼德农耕社群转而自立，班巴拉人由此崛起。约1640年，卡拉迪安·库利巴利在塞古建立小班巴拉王国；1712年，其后人比顿·库利巴利把青年社团“托恩”改编为常备军，自称“法马”，建立塞古的班巴拉帝国，在尼日尔河上配备战船，并以贝币征税。他的军队攻取马西纳、杰内和巴马科，1751年又使古老的马里曼萨沦为附庸。18世纪中叶的内战后，出身奴隶的恩戈洛·迪亚拉于1766年夺取王位，带来近三十年的繁荣。与穆斯林邻邦不同，班巴拉政权坚持传统多神崇拜；1818年，塞库·阿马杜领导的富拉尼圣战在努库马击败班巴拉人，夺走杰内和马西纳，建立新的马西纳帝国。其曼德式种姓社会中，贵族居于格里奥吟游艺人、铁匠和源出奴隶的博佐渔户之上。

en: The Bamu are a Papuan people of the Bamu River country in southwestern Papua New Guinea. Their tongue, Bamu or Bamu Kiwai, is a member of the Kiwaian family alongside Kiwai, Kerewo and Waboda, and splits into the Gama, Lower Bamu, Sisiame, Upper Bamu and Nuhiro dialects, the Gama speakers reckoned within the Bamu group despite limited shared vocabulary.
zh: 巴穆人是巴布亚新几内亚西南部巴穆河流域的巴布亚人，所说的巴穆语又称巴穆基万语，与基万语、克雷沃语和瓦博达语同属基万语系。巴穆语分为加马、下巴穆、西西亚梅、上巴穆和努希罗等方言；加马人虽与巴穆本支词汇重合有限，仍被归入巴穆群体。

en: The Banaro are a Ramu-speaking Papuan people of northern Papua New Guinea. Their speech is the most lexically divergent member of the Ramu family, sharing remarkably few cognates with the family's other branches.
zh: 巴纳罗人是巴布亚新几内亚北部使用拉穆语族语言的巴布亚族群。他们的语言是拉穆语族中词汇分歧最大的一支，与语族内其他分支的同源词少得出奇。

en: The Banda are a Ubangian speaking people of the savannas north of the Congo basin, concentrated in the northeastern Central African Republic around the Ouaka and Gribingui rivers, with related groups spilling into the Congo, Cameroon and South Sudan. Their languages form a cluster of about nine geographically separated vernaculars within the Niger-Congo family. Banda society is patrilineal, organized in dispersed village groups under headmen rather than kings; in time of war the villages chose temporary war chiefs and stripped them of power once the danger passed. They lived by hunting, fishing and cultivation, and became known for carved wooden ritual objects and enormous animal-shaped slit drums that carried messages between settlements. Before the nineteenth century they led a largely unmolested life, but from the early 1800s slave raiders out of Wadai and Darfur swept down on their lands, carrying off captives for the markets of the Nile and Lake Chad and pushing Banda communities south and west along the Ubangi.
zh: 班达人是说乌班吉语的族群，住在刚果盆地以北的稀树草原，核心聚居区在中非共和国东北部的瓦卡河与格里宾吉河流域，另有支系散入刚果、喀麦隆和南苏丹。他们的语言在尼日尔-刚果语系内构成约九种地域方言组成的班达语群。班达社会按父系继嗣，以头人治理的分散村落为单位，没有国王；遇有战事，各村推举临时的战事酋长，危险过去后即收回其权力。他们以狩猎、捕鱼和农耕为生，并以木雕礼器和巨大的兽形裂口鼓闻名，这种鼓曾用于在聚落间传递信息。19世纪以前他们的生活大体安宁，但从19世纪初起，来自瓦达伊和达尔富尔的奴隶贩子不断南下洗劫，把掳来的人带往尼罗河和乍得湖市场，迫使班达社群沿乌班吉河向西、向南迁徙。

en: The Bandjabi, also spelled Banjabi or Bandzabi and better recorded as the Nzebi or Nzabi, are a Bantu people who trace their origin to the lands of the Congo basin and settled, by about 1800, in the great equatorial forest of the Chaillu massif, straddling what are now southern Gabon and the neighbouring Congo. Their clans built shifting villages around Mount Birougou and the iron-rich ridges of Lekeoumou near Mayoko, and they were already famous across the region as iron miners and smiths who forged their own tools and weapons, alongside pottery, hunting and the cultivation of bananas and groundnuts. Organized in mobile, markedly egalitarian clans rather than under kings, the Bandjabi took an active part in long-distance trade, carrying their varied produce through the forest to neighbouring peoples, and in the nineteenth century became prominent suppliers of rubber to the caravan networks. They speak Nzebi, also called Inzabi, a Bantu language with several local dialects. Sharing the forest with Pygmy groups and with neighbours such as the Kele to the north, they preserved their dispersed, village-based way of life through the period of growing commercial pressure before colonial conquest.
zh: 班贾比人又译班扎比、班扎比，资料中更常见的名称是恩泽比人或恩扎比人，是一个起源于刚果盆地的班图族群，约在1800年前后定居在沙尤山地的赤道大林区，地跨今加蓬南部与邻近的刚果一带。他们的氏族在比鲁古山和马约科附近富藏铁矿的莱库穆岭地周围建造游动村落，早已作为铁矿采掘者和锻造自家工具、武器的铁匠闻名遐迩，同时兼营制陶、狩猎以及香蕉和花生种植。班贾比社会没有王权，而是由流动且相当平等的氏族组成；他们积极参与长途贸易，把各色物产穿过森林贩运给邻族，并在19世纪成为商队网络中重要的橡胶供应者。他们讲恩泽比语，又称因扎比语，是一种带有多种地方方言的班图语言。他们与俾格米群体以及北邻凯莱人等族群共享这片森林，在殖民征服之前日益加剧的商业压力下，维持着分散的村落生活方式。

en: The Banggai are an Austronesian people of the Banggai Islands and the eastern coast of Central Sulawesi, heirs to the maritime Kingdom of Banggai centered on the island of Banggai. They fall into two branches: the coastal Banggai and the Sea-sea people of the mountainous interior, and their language and customs are close to those of the neighbouring Saluan and Balantak. The island of Banggai was already named as a Majapahit tributary in a Chinese document of 1304 and in the fourteenth-century Negarakertagama. In the sixteenth century the sultanate of Ternate conquered the four small local states, and its general Adi Cokro extended Banggai's rule onto the Sulawesi mainland in the 1580s; in 1564 the king had even sent his son to Ternate to weigh Christianity against Islam. After the Treaty of Bongaya in 1667 Ternate appointed Banggai's rulers and took annual tribute, while Bugis traders grew influential and the kingdom, a hub of the trepang trade, shifted its capital to Mendono in 1690 and Balantak in 1708 amid raids and noble conflict. Islam took root among the coastal Banggai, while inland communities kept their older beliefs.
zh: 邦盖人是生活在邦盖群岛和中苏拉威西东海岸的南岛语族群，也是以邦盖岛为中心的海上邦盖王国的继承者。他们分为沿海的邦盖人和内陆山区的西海人两支，语言习俗与邻近的萨卢安人、巴兰塔克人相近。1304年的一份中国文献和14世纪的《爪哇史颂》都已把邦盖岛记载为满者伯夷的属邦。16世纪，特尔纳特苏丹国征服了当地四个小邦，其将领阿迪·佐克罗在1580年代把邦盖的势力扩展到苏拉威西大陆；早在1564年，邦盖国王还曾派儿子前往特尔纳特，在基督教和伊斯兰教之间权衡取舍。1667年《邦阿亚条约》签订后，特尔纳特人掌握了邦盖统治者的任命权并收取年贡，与此同时布吉斯商人势力日增；作为海参贸易中心的邦盖因袭扰和贵族内讧，先后于1690年迁都门多诺、1708年迁都巴兰塔克。伊斯兰教在沿海邦盖人中扎根，内陆社群则长期保留着原有信仰。

en: The Banggarla, also recorded as Barngarla or Parnkalla, are an Aboriginal people of South Australia and the traditional owners of much of Eyre Peninsula, including the country around the later towns of Port Lincoln and Whyalla and the lands west of Port Augusta. They lived mainly along the coast, moving inland seasonally for food and ceremony, hunting kangaroo and emu in skin cloaks and relying above all on seafood; a ritual of singing from the cliffs was meant to enlist sharks and dolphins to drive fish toward the shore. Their Dreaming centres on the Seven Sisters story cycle, and their language belongs to the Thura-Yura branch of the Pama-Nyungan family. Groups known to early settlers as the Jadliaura, Kooapudna and Willeuroo were Banggarla hordes. Before European arrival the southward-moving Kokatha were already pressing on their northern borders. Matthew Flinders charted the coast in 1802, and after the colony of South Australia was proclaimed in 1836 settlement spread onto Eyre Peninsula, bringing decades of frontier conflict that oral tradition remembers in the Waterloo Bay massacre.
zh: 邦加拉人（也记作巴恩加拉或潘卡拉）是南澳大利亚的原住民，是艾尔半岛大部的传统主人，领地包括后来林肯港、怀阿拉一带以及奥古斯塔港以西的土地。他们主要沿海而居，随季节深入内陆觅食和举行仪式，身披袋鼠皮斗篷猎取袋鼠和鸸鹋，而以海产最为重要；族人还有在悬崖上歌唱的仪式，意在请鲨鱼和海豚把鱼群赶向岸边。他们的梦时信仰以“七姐妹”故事体系为核心，语言属于帕马-牛雅语系的图拉-尤拉语支。早期殖民者记载的贾德廖拉、库阿普德纳和维勒鲁等群体，都是邦加拉人的分支。欧洲人到来之前，向南迁徙的科科塔人已在挤压他们的北界。马修·弗林德斯于1802年测绘了这段海岸；1836年南澳大利亚殖民地宣告成立后，定居点扩展到艾尔半岛，随之而来的是数十年的边疆冲突，口述传统中的滑铁卢湾大屠杀便是其中一幕。

en: The Bangi are a cluster of Bantu peoples of the central Congo basin, among them the Nunu, Ntomba, Bolia and Sengele, who live around Lake Mai-Ndombe and along the Chuapa, Lukenie and other rivers of the Équateur forest in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, fishing, growing cassava and travelling by canoe. Their closely related Bangi-Ntomba tongues belong to the Bantu family, and Bobangi, a Bangi dialect, later supplied most of the vocabulary of the river trade language Lingala. Oral king lists recall that shortly after 1400 the BaNunu built up the riverine polity of Mwene Muji, which dominated the trade of the lower Kasai with a canoe fleet and exported fine woven cloth; an Italian writer first recorded reports of it in 1591. The polity's unity broke down in the early 1600s, when the Boma, Yaka and Bozanga chiefdoms split away, and the Nunu chiefdoms around the lake never regained their old power, though their canoemen remained prominent in Congo river commerce.
zh: 班吉人是刚果盆地中部的一组班图族群，包括努努人、恩通巴人、博利亚人和森格莱人等，聚居在马伊恩东贝湖周围，以及刚果（金）赤道省的楚阿帕河、卢凯尼河等河川地带，以捕鱼、种植木薯和独木舟航行为生。他们关系相近的班吉—恩通巴诸语属班图语族，其中博班吉方言后来为河上贸易通用语林加拉语提供了大部分词汇。据口传王表，1400年之后不久，巴努努人建立了河上政权姆韦内穆吉，凭借独木舟船队主宰下开赛河一带的贸易，输出精美的织物；1591年一位意大利作家最早记下了关于它的传闻。17世纪初该政权走向瓦解，博马、亚卡和博赞加等酋长国分裂出去，湖区的努努诸酋邦再未恢复昔日势力，但他们的独木舟水手仍是刚果河贸易中的重要角色。

en: The Banjar are the dominant Austronesian people of the riverine lowlands of southeastern Borneo, around the Barito delta and the port of Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan. They took shape from local Dayak tribes such as the Ma'anyan and Ngaju absorbing Malay and Javanese settlers. In the fourteenth century migrants from Java founded the Hindu kingdom of Negara Dipa on the Tapin River under Majapahit influence, succeeded in the fifteenth century by Negara Daha. When Prince Samudera fled a succession revolt, he won backing from Java's Demak Sultanate and in 1526 founded the Islamic Sultanate of Banjar, ruling as Sultan Suriansyah from Bandar Masih, the future Banjarmasin; the court chronicle Hikayat Banjar records these origins. English and Dutch traders established relations in 1602 and 1603, but Dutch expeditions aiming to conquer the sultanate in 1606 and 1612 both failed. The Banjar speak a Malayic language enriched with Dayak and Javanese words, which became the lingua franca of southern Borneo and splits into upstream Hulu and downstream Kuala dialects, matching the Pahuluan and Kuala sub-groups. After the scholar Sheikh Muhammad Arsyad al-Banjari returned from Mecca in 1774, the Banjar firmly adopted Shafi'i Sunni Islam, which thereafter shaped their law, learning and everyday customs.
zh: 班贾尔人是婆罗洲东南部河流低地的主要南岛语系族群，聚居于南加里曼丹巴里托三角洲与港口城市马辰一带。他们由当地的马安延、恩加朱等达雅部落吸收马来和爪哇移民融合而成。14世纪，来自爪哇的移民在塔平河畔建立了受满者伯夷影响的印度教王国内加拉迪帕，15世纪又由内加拉达哈王国继承。王子萨穆德拉在内乱中出逃后，借助爪哇淡目苏丹国的支持，于1526年建立伊斯兰化的班贾尔苏丹国，自称苏丹苏里安夏，定都班达尔马西，即后来的马辰；宫廷史书《班贾尔故事》记载了这段起源。1602年和1603年，英国与荷兰商人先后与苏丹国建交，但荷兰在1606年和1612年两度出兵征服均告失败。班贾尔人讲属马来语支的班贾尔语，其中吸收了大量达雅语和爪哇语词汇，是婆罗洲南部的通用语，并按上游帕胡兰与下游瓜拉两个支系分为胡卢与瓜拉两种方言。1774年，学者穆罕默德·阿尔沙德·班贾里从麦加归来，班贾尔人从此全面遵奉逊尼派伊斯兰教的沙斐仪学派，信仰深刻塑造了他们的法律、学术与日常风俗。

en: The Banjaras, also called Lambadas, are a traditionally nomadic trading and pastoral people scattered across India, whose caravans in 1337 already moved through the Deccan and Vidarbha, around Warangal and Basim. Their clans, possibly of mixed origin in north-central India, appear in Delhi Sultanate chronicles from the reign of Alauddin Khalji, and the name Banjara came into use from around the fourteenth century. Organized into great caravans called tandas under elected headmen, they moved grain, salt, cotton, cattle and forest produce with oxen, camels and donkeys, monopolizing the salt trade of Berar and the Deccan before the East India Company, and their trains also supplied armies on campaign, as Jahangir described in the early seventeenth century and as Arthur Wellesley found when he employed them against the Maratha confederacy in the 1790s. Their own tongue is Lambadi, a Western Indo-Aryan language without a script, written in Devanagari or the regional script, while most Banjaras also speak the languages of the peoples among whom they camp; the embroidered textiles and mirror-work of their women remain their best-known craft. As company rule closed down their salt monopoly and the long wars of the period ended, many lost their carrying trade, and by the 1830s some had taken to settled farming while others acquired a reputation for banditry on the Deccan roads.
zh: 班贾拉人又称兰巴达人，是散居印度各地、传统上以游牧贸易和畜牧为生的族群，1337年时他们的商队已经往来于德干和维达尔巴，活跃在瓦朗加尔和巴西姆一带。其各氏族可能源出印度中北部、族源混杂，早在德里苏丹国阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉时期就出现在宫廷史官的记载中，班贾拉这一名称约从14世纪开始通行。他们结成名为坦达的庞大商队，由选举产生的首领带领，用牛、骆驼和驴贩运粮食、盐、棉花、牲畜和林产品，在英国东印度公司到来之前垄断了贝拉尔和德干的食盐贸易；他们的驮队还随军供给给养，17世纪初贾汉吉尔曾记述其盛况，18世纪90年代韦尔斯利征讨马拉塔联盟时也征用过他们。班贾拉人的本族语是兰巴迪语，属西印度-雅利安语支，没有自己的文字，多用天城文或当地文字书写，同时普遍兼通旅居地的语言；班贾拉妇女的刺绣和镜饰织物是他们最有名的手工艺。随着公司统治挤压食盐专营、绵延的战事平息，许多人失去了驮运生计，到19世纪30年代，部分人转为定居务农，也有一些人在德干的道路上落草为盗。

en: The Banakwut are the Bannock, originally a Northern Paiute people whose speech belonged to the Western Numic branch but whose way of life drew them into the Northern Shoshone world across southern Idaho, northern Nevada, south-eastern Oregon and western Wyoming. Horses reached the northern trade networks by 1730, and in the middle of the eighteenth century several mounted bands broke away to form the Bannock, ranging along the Bannock Trail through Montana to hunt buffalo on the northern plains. In their Snake River homeland they fished for salmon, made tule-reed rafts, pottery and salmon-skin bags, and wintered in buffalo-hide tipis. Mounted and well armed, they grew dangerous to outsiders: in 1814 the chief called The Horse opened a long campaign of raids against fur traders on the Boise River that did not end until 1832.
zh: 巴纳库特人即班诺克人，源出北派尤特人，语言属西努米克语支，但其生活方式使他们融入了北肖肖尼人的世界，活动范围跨有爱达荷南部、内华达北部、俄勒冈东南和怀俄明西部。到1730年，马已经传入北方的贸易网络；18世纪中叶，若干获得马匹的群体分离出来，形成班诺克人，沿“班诺克小径”穿过蒙大拿，到北部大平原猎野牛。在斯内克河家园，他们捕捞鲑鱼，制作芦苇筏、陶器和鲑鱼皮袋，冬天住在野牛皮帐篷里。骑马善武的他们对外来者构成威胁：1814年，绰号“骏马”的酋长发起了对博伊西河一带毛皮商人的长期袭击，直到1832年才告平息。

en: The Banoni are the people of the swamp-fringed coast around Empress Augusta Bay in southwest Bougainville, in villages such as Mabes and Mariga. Their language, which they themselves call Tsunari, is an Austronesian tongue closely related to that of their neighbours the Piva, rather than a Papuan one.
zh: 班诺尼人居住在布干维尔岛西南部奥古斯塔皇后湾沿岸、沼泽环绕的海滨地带，村落包括马贝斯和马里加等。他们把自己的语言称作楚纳里语；这是一种南岛语系语言，与邻族皮瓦人的语言关系密切，并非巴布亚语言。

en: Bantoid here groups the peoples of the Cross River and the Cameroon borderland, a belt of forest and mangrove running from the Benue tributaries to the Gulf of Guinea. Its western end is Ejagham, or Ekoi, country around Ikom and Ogoja, whose civilization had produced the carved Ikom monoliths and the Nsibidi ideographic signs by about 200; the Ejagham also created the Ekpe leopard society, whose masks and grades spread to neighboring peoples. On the estuary the Efik built the trading towns of Old Calabar, including Duke Town and Creek Town, while the related Ibibio held the country around Eket. From the arrival of Portuguese ships in the fifteenth century these towns became middlemen in the Atlantic slave trade, with Ekpe serving as the supreme court and regulator of commerce, and after the British abolition of 1807 they switched to palm oil exports. Enslaved initiates carried Ekpe across the Atlantic, where it survives as the Abakua cult in Cuba. Inland, toward Katsina Ala and Kumba, related Tivoid and Grassfield communities shared the same Bantoid linguistic heritage.
zh: 这里的“班托伊”聚合了克罗斯河与喀麦隆边境地带的诸族，即从贝努埃河支流延伸到几内亚湾的森林与红树林地带。其西端是伊孔和奥戈贾一带的埃贾格姆人（又称埃科伊人）：约200年时，他们的文明已创造出雕刻的伊孔独石柱和恩西比迪表意符号，还创立了“埃克佩”豹会，其面具与会众等级传播到邻近各族。河口地带，埃菲克人建立了老卡拉巴尔诸商镇，包括杜克镇和克里克镇，与他们相近的伊比比奥人则占据埃克特一带。15世纪葡萄牙商船到来后，这些城镇成为大西洋奴隶贸易的中间商，埃克佩豹会充当最高法庭和商业监管者；1807年英国废除奴隶贸易后，它们转为出口棕榈油。被掳走的入会者把埃克佩信仰带过大西洋，演变为古巴的阿巴库阿教。内陆的卡齐纳阿拉和昆巴一带，与之同源的蒂夫语族和草原族群也共享这份类班图语言遗产。

en: The Bara are the largest of the zebu-herding peoples of Madagascar, roaming the dry southern part of the central plateau around their historic capital of Ihosy, in a land they call Ibara. They were split into five tribes, the Bara-Be, Bara-Imamono and Bara-Ianstsantsa and the smaller Vinda and Antivondro, living a semi-nomadic life in which young men proved their manhood by cattle rustling, and their society was strongly patriarchal, with nobles, commoners and slaves. Their earliest chieftaincies grew along the Ihosy River under noble lines claiming descent from the Maroserana dynasty of the Sakalava, and around 1640 a Mahafaly noble conquered the country and founded the Zafimanely dynasty, whose rule was firmly settled after 1653 amid decades of cattle raids and succession strife. About 1800 the Zafimanely king Raikitroka imposed new rules that brought a period of calm, but after his death the Bara fragmented again into a constellation of rival kingdoms. Even so, slave and cattle trading, together with raids on their neighbours, made them richer and stronger in the early nineteenth century: under Queen Ranavalona I the Merina planted a garrison at Ihosy, but they never wholly subdued the Bara, who kept their kings and their herds. Village life centred on the hazomanga, a tall wooden pillar of communal worship, on sacred tamarind trees and on the ombiasy seer, while alliances were sealed by the fatidra blood pact.
zh: 巴拉人是马达加斯加最大的牧牛族群，在中部高原南部干燥的草原上游牧，活动于他们称为伊巴拉的地方，以历史都城伊胡西为中心。他们分为五大部落：巴拉贝、巴拉伊马莫诺、巴拉扬粲察以及较小的文达和安蒂冯德罗，过着半游牧生活，青年要以盗牛证明勇气；社会父权色彩浓厚，分为贵族、平民和奴隶三个等级。他们最早的酋邦兴起于伊胡西河畔，贵族谱系自称源自萨卡拉瓦人的马鲁塞拉纳王朝；约1640年，一位马哈法利贵族征服此地，建立扎菲马内利王朝，1653年其统治稳固下来，其间伴随着数十年的盗牛和争位之乱。约1800年，扎菲马内利国王赖基特罗卡颁布新规，带来一段安定时期，但他死后巴拉人重新分裂为一群互相竞争的小王国。尽管如此，奴隶和牛只贸易加上对邻邦的劫掠，使他们在19世纪初更加富强：腊纳瓦洛娜一世时期梅里纳人虽在伊胡西驻军，却始终未能完全征服巴拉人，他们保住了自己的国王和牛群。村落生活围绕高大的木制公共祭柱、被视为圣物的罗望子树和占卜师展开，部族之间则以歃血为盟的血誓缔结盟约。

en: The Barababaraba, also written Barapa Barapa, are an Aboriginal people of the central Murray country straddling northern Victoria and southern New South Wales, sharing the lands around Deniliquin, Kow Swamp and the Perricoota and Koondrook forests with their close neighbours the Wemba-Wemba and Yorta Yorta. Their speech, recorded in an early grammar by R. H. Mathews, was a dialect of Wemba-Wemba within the Pama-Nyungan family, with another variety spoken on the Murray near Swan Hill. As one of the river Wongal-chewing peoples, they gathered wangul bulrushes for their starchy pith and worked the fibrous cortex into string for fishing nets and bags. For centuries before the Europeans came, the Murray and its swamps supplied fish, waterfowl, mussels and roots, and their society was bound by marriage and ceremony into the wider Wemba-Wemba world of the river plains. The first European known to reach these river reaches was Thomas Mitchell, who camped beside and named Swan Hill in 1836, on the edge of Barababaraba country.
zh: 巴拉巴人又译巴拉帕巴拉帕人，是墨累河中部地区的澳大利亚原住民，地跨维多利亚州北部与新南威尔士州南部，与关系密切的邻族温巴温巴人、约塔约塔人共享德尼利昆、考沼泽以及佩里库塔和孔德鲁克森林一带的土地。他们的语言由马修斯较早记下语法，是帕马-尼永加语系温巴温巴语的一种方言，另有一支通行于斯旺希尔附近的墨累河畔。作为沿河“嚼旺加尔”的族群之一，他们采集旺加尔芦苇取食富含淀粉的髓部，并把纤维质的外皮搓成绳子，用来编织渔网和口袋。在欧洲人到来之前的许多个世纪里，墨累河及其沼泽提供鱼、水禽、河蚌和根茎，他们的社会通过婚姻与仪式，与河原上更大的温巴温巴人群世界连为一体。已知最早抵达这一带河段的欧洲人是托马斯·米切尔，他于1836年在巴拉巴人领地边缘的天鹅山旁宿营，并为该地命名。

en: The Baradha are an Aboriginal Australian people of Central Queensland, whose lands of some 6,500 square kilometres ran along the Connors River from Killarney north to Nebo, between the coastal Koinjmal and the Barna to their west, with the Wiri on their northern border. Their alternative name Toolginburra comes from their word for a hill, tulkun, and the Thar-ar-ra-burra horde around Cardowan was one of their kin groups. Like other peoples of the Mackay district they were divided into two phratries, the Yangurru and the Wudhurru, classes that also ordered every part of the natural world. Their speech, the Baradha language, was a Maric tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family. In 1770 James Cook sailed up this coast in Endeavour, landing at Round Hill to the south-east and naming the Glass House Mountains, but the Baradha country itself was not settled by Europeans until the middle decades of the nineteenth century, when police patrols and introduced diseases swept away much of its population.
zh: 巴拉达人是澳大利亚昆士兰州中部的原住民族群，其约六千五百平方公里的领地沿康纳斯河分布，南起基拉尼、北至尼博，处在沿海的科因贾马尔人与西边的巴纳人之间，北邻维里人。他们的别名图尔金巴拉源自本族语言中意为山丘的“图尔昆”一词，聚居于卡多恩一带的萨拉拉布拉氏族是其亲族群体之一。与麦凯地区的其他族群一样，他们分为扬古鲁和武杜鲁两大胞族，这套分类也用来划分自然界的万事万物。他们的语言巴拉达语属帕马-牛雅语系下的马里克语支。1770年，詹姆斯·库克驾“奋进号”沿这段海岸北上，在东南方的圆山登陆，并命名了玻璃屋山脉，但巴拉达人的土地直到19世纪中叶才有欧洲人定居，随后警察的清剿和传入的疾病使当地人口大量消亡。

en: Barbakoan is the game's grouping for the peoples of the Pacific slopes and coast of southern Colombia and northern Ecuador who speak languages of the Barbacoan family, among them the Awa of the Telembí, the Pasto of the Nariño highlands and the Guambiano and Totoró near Popayán, together with the Cayapa and Tsáchila of coastal Ecuador.
zh: 巴巴科安是游戏按语系归并出的文化，涵盖哥伦比亚南部与厄瓜多尔北部太平洋坡地及沿海一带、使用巴巴科安语族语言的诸族群，包括特伦比河流域的阿瓦皮特人、纳里尼奥高地的帕斯托人、波帕扬附近的瓜姆比亚诺人与托托罗人，以及厄瓜多尔沿海的卡亚帕人和察奇拉人。

en: The Bardi were a Florentine merchant and banking house whose noble rank is documented from 1164, when the emperor Frederick Barbarossa enfeoffed their forebears with the county of Vernio near the Mugello. Staunch Guelphs, they fought at Campaldino in 1289 alongside Dante Alighieri, and their Compagnia dei Bardi grew into one of the greatest banks of medieval Europe, financing trade across the continent through bills of exchange. By 1338 it ran thirteen branches, from London, Bruges, Paris and Avignon to Barcelona, Seville, Constantinople, Rhodes, Cyprus and Jerusalem, and the family adorned the Franciscan basilica of Santa Croce with chapels frescoed by Giotto from about 1310. Their fortune was broken by royal credit: they had lent Edward III of England some 900,000 gold florins for the Hundred Years' War, and when he defaulted in 1345 the Bardi collapsed together with their partners the Peruzzi. The family survived the ruin, and around 1415 Contessina de' Bardi married Cosimo de' Medici, who restored their political rights after 1434; later Bardi merchants helped finance the Atlantic voyages of Christopher Columbus and John Cabot.
zh: 巴尔迪家族是佛罗伦萨的商人和银行世家，其贵族身份可考于1164年，当时皇帝腓特烈·巴巴罗萨将穆杰洛附近的韦尔尼奥伯国封给其先祖。作为坚定的圭尔夫派，他们于1289年与但丁·阿利吉耶里并肩参加坎帕尔迪诺之战；家族的巴尔迪公司凭借汇票为全欧贸易融资，成长为中世纪欧洲最大的银行之一。到1338年，它设有十三家分行，西起伦敦、布鲁日、巴黎和阿维尼翁，东抵巴塞罗那、塞维利亚、君士坦丁堡、罗得岛、塞浦路斯和耶路撒冷；家族还从1310年前后起请乔托在方济各会的圣十字圣殿绘制家族礼拜堂壁画。摧毁其财富的是王室信贷：他们向英格兰国王爱德华三世放贷约90万金弗罗林供百年战争之用，1345年爱德华三世违约，巴尔迪银行与伙伴佩鲁齐银行一同倒闭。家族挺过了这场破产，约1415年孔泰西娜·德·巴尔迪嫁给科西莫·德·美第奇，后者在1434年后恢复了巴尔迪家族的政治权利；后来的巴尔迪商人还曾资助克里斯托弗·哥伦布和约翰·卡博特的大西洋航行。

en: The Bardi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Dampier Peninsula in the Kimberley, whose traditional country of roughly 300 square miles covers the Cape Leveque tip from Cape Borda to Cygnet Bay. Their language is the northernmost member of the Nyulnyulan family and is mutually intelligible with the closely related Jawi of the neighbouring islands. Bardi life follows a calendar of six seasons, from the monsoonal mankal, when turtle eggs are gathered, to the cold southeasterly barrgan, the season for hunting dugong. On 5 January 1688 the English buccaneer William Dampier, sailing the Cygnet, described the low sandy coast off Cape Leveque, the first European account of Bardi waters; the French captain Nicolas Baudin later named the cape after his hydrographer Pierre Lévêque.
zh: 巴尔迪人是金伯利地区丹皮尔半岛北部的澳大利亚原住民，传统家园约300平方英里，覆盖勒韦克角顶端，从博尔达角延伸到西格尼特湾。他们的语言是纽尔纽尔语系最靠北的一支，与邻近岛屿上亲缘很近的贾维语可以互通。巴尔迪人的生活遵循六季历法：从季风多雨、可采海龟蛋的曼卡尔季，到刮寒冷东南风、最宜捕猎儒艮的巴尔甘季。1688年1月5日，英国海盗航海家威廉·丹皮尔乘“天鹅号”记述了勒韦克角外低矮多沙的海岸，这是欧洲人对巴尔迪海域的最早记录；后来法国船长尼古拉·博丹以他的水文师皮埃尔·勒韦克之名为该角命名。

en: The Baré, also called the Warekena, are an Arawakan people of the upper Rio Negro whose historical domain stretched from the site of Manaus upriver to the great rapids where São Gabriel da Cachoeira now stands, and across the border into the Guainía and Atabapo basins. Slash-and-burn manioc farmers, fishermen and hunters with blowpipes, they also made their own hammocks, baskets and pottery. Documentary mention of them begins in the early 1700s, and Jesuit records of the 1750s describe Baré villages on the Xié River already under pressure to relocate to the main waterways for settlement and conversion; by the later 1700s compulsory migration was resettling whole families as far as the Orinoco confluence. Many families chose instead a life of constant movement through the black-water rivers to evade slave raiders and debt traders, and under Carmelite influence they gradually gave up their own Arawakan tongue for Nheengatu, the riverine lingua franca, while keeping their clan organization and their territorial memory of the Rio Negro.
zh: 巴黑人又称瓦雷凯纳人，是内格罗河上游的阿拉瓦克语族群，历史领地从马瑙斯一带沿河上溯，直到圣加布里埃尔达卡绍埃拉附近的大瀑布，并越过边界延伸至瓜伊尼亚河与阿塔巴波河流域。他们从事刀耕火种的木薯农业，兼营捕鱼和用吹箭筒狩猎，也自制吊床、筐篮和陶器。文献中对他们的记载始于18世纪初，18世纪50年代的耶稣会记录写道，谢埃河畔的巴黑村落已面临强迫迁往干流、以便集中定居和传教的压力；到18世纪后期，强制移民政策更把整户整族远迁到奥里诺科河汇合处。许多家庭选择在黑水河网间不断迁徙，以躲避猎奴者和债务商人；在加尔默罗会的影响下，他们逐渐放弃本族的阿拉瓦克语，改用河运通用语嫩加图语，但仍保留着氏族组织和对内格罗河故土的记忆。

en: The Barem, also called Bunabun, are a Papuan people of the Sumgilbar area inland of the Madang coast, living in villages along the Dibor River. Their speech is a Madang-branch language of the Trans–New Guinea family, divided into local dialects such as Murukanam Barem and Asumbin.
zh: 巴雷姆人又称布纳本人，是马当沿海内陆松吉尔巴尔一带的巴布亚族群，聚居在迪博尔河沿岸的村落里。他们的语言属跨新几内亚语系马当语支，下分穆鲁卡纳姆巴雷姆、阿松宾等方言。

en: The Bariba, who call themselves Baatonu, are a Gur-speaking farming people of the Borgou grasslands in present-day northeast Benin and adjoining Nigeria, whose chief towns are Nikki and Kandi and whose language is Baatonum. Baatonu farming clans held the Nikki district from about 1350, when mounted Wasangari invaders from Bussa, heirs of the Kisra legend, imposed themselves as a ruling caste; Sounon Sero became the first king of Nikki, and his son Sime Dobidia founded its dynasties by marrying into the native Baatonu, Boko and Hausa clans. The Bariba weathered the assaults of the Songhai empire: they defeated Sunni Ali in the 1490s at Gwangwarake, though Askia Muhammad briefly held Bussa in 1505 and Askia Daoud raided it in 1558 and 1563. After Songhai fell in 1591 the Oyo Yoruba reduced Borgu to vassalage, from which it broke free in 1783 by winning the battle of Gberegburu. From the 1500s Wangara merchants made the country a link in the kola trade between Gonja and Hausaland, while the Wasangari elite kept their ancestral cults and left Islam to the trading quarters. In 1837 Siru Kpera, king of Nikki, fell in battle beside the Alaafin of Oyo against the Fulani jihadists.
zh: 巴里巴人自称巴阿通努，是今贝宁东北部博尔古草原及毗邻尼日利亚地区说古尔语支巴阿通努姆语的农耕民族，主要城镇为尼基和坎迪。巴阿通努农耕氏族约自1350年起据有尼基一带；其后，来自布萨、承继基斯拉传说的瓦桑加里骑手入主当地，成为统治种姓：索农·塞罗成为尼基第一代国王，其子西梅·多比迪亚通过与土著巴阿通努、博科和豪萨氏族联姻，开创了尼基的诸王朝。巴里巴人顶住了桑海帝国的连番进攻——1490年代在格万古瓦拉凯击败桑尼·阿里，但阿斯基亚·穆罕默德于1505年短暂占领布萨，阿斯基亚·达乌德又在1558年和1563年来袭。1591年桑海灭亡后，奥约的约鲁巴人把博尔古降为附庸，巴里巴人直到1783年在格贝雷格布鲁之战取胜才重获独立。16世纪起，旺加拉商人把这里变成贡贾到豪萨兰之间柯拉果贸易的一环，瓦桑加里贵族则固守祖先祭祀，把伊斯兰教留给商人区。1837年，尼基国王西鲁·克佩拉与奥约的阿拉芬并肩抗击富拉尼圣战者，战死沙场。

en: The Barna, also recorded as the Baranha or Barada Barna, were an Aboriginal Australian people of northern Queensland. Their traditional speech is believed to have belonged to the dialect cluster of Biri, and they were also entered on early ethnographic records under the name Parnabal.
zh: 巴尔纳人又记作巴拉纳人或巴拉达-巴尔纳人，是昆士兰北部的澳大利亚原住民。他们的传统语言被认为属于比里语的方言群，早期民族志记录中还以帕尔纳巴尔之名记载他们。

en: The Baruga are a Papuan people of Oro Province on the northeast coast of the Bird's Tail of New Guinea. Their speech, also called Bareji, belongs to the Binanderean family of the Trans–New Guinea phylum and, with Gaina and Korafe, forms its southeastern coastal branch. Baruga is split into four markedly divergent dialects, Tafota, Daghoro, Bareji and Mado, marking a string of distinct local communities along the Oro coast.
zh: 巴鲁加人是新几内亚“鸟尾”东北海岸奥罗省的巴布亚族群。他们的语言又称巴雷吉语，属跨新几内亚语系的比南德雷语族，与加伊纳语、科拉费语共同构成该语族的东南沿海分支。巴鲁加语分化为四个差异明显的方言——塔福塔、达戈罗、巴雷吉和马多，对应奥罗沿海一串各有特色的地方社群。

en: The Barunggam are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Western Downs of south-eastern Queensland, whose tribal lands covered some 20,000 square kilometres from the headwaters of the Condamine River near Jackson east to the neighbourhood of Dalby, taking in Tara, Chinchilla and Jandowae. Their south-eastern neighbours were the Jarowair, the Wakawaka lay beyond their north-eastern border, and the Mandandanji lived to their west; their alternative names included Gogai, Cogai and Kogai, words also applied to the languages of their western neighbours. Their own Barunggam speech was recorded in a wordlist taken down at Warkon Station on the Balonne River. The country they hunted was open, park-like grassland, and after the British founded the Moreton Bay penal settlement in 1824 it drew greedy eyes: little more than fifteen years later, well-connected Scots settlers, armed and accompanied by convict servants, drove in roughly a hundred thousand sheep and five thousand cattle, overwhelming the Barunggam and their neighbours in a campaign of occupation that lasted barely eighteen months.
zh: 巴伦加姆人是澳大利亚昆士兰州东南部西部唐斯地区的原住民族群，其部族领地约两万平方公里，西起杰克逊附近的康达迈恩河源头，东抵多尔比一带，包括塔拉、钦奇拉和詹多韦等地。他们东南与贾罗韦尔人为邻，东北边界之外是瓦卡瓦卡人，西边住着曼丹丹吉人；戈盖、科盖、科盖等也是他们的别名，这些名称也被用来称呼西邻诸族的语言。他们自己的巴伦加姆语曾有人在巴隆河畔的沃康牧场记录下一份词汇表。他们游猎的土地是开阔如园苑的草原，1824年英国建立莫顿湾流放殖民地后，这片沃土引来觊觎：仅仅十五年后，背景深厚的苏格兰移民携带着武器、由流放犯仆从随行，赶来约十万只羊和五千头牛，在仅持续一年半的占领行动中压垮了巴伦加姆人及其邻族。

en: The Shilele, better known as the Lele or Bashilele, are a Bantu people of the interior Congo basin, occupying the forest and savanna between the Kasai and Loange rivers around Ilebo in what is now Kasai province. By language and tradition they are close to the Kuba and Wongo, all three claiming descent from a common ancestor named Woto, but the Lele never joined the centralized Kuba kingdom built from about 1625 onward and kept to autonomous villages led by elders. Their society drew attention for its polyandrous marriages and for raffia cloth woven by men and used both as trade goods and as internal currency, alongside flattened masks and braided figurines. Hunting carried high prestige, and Lele villages maintained ritual cults centered on the pangolin long after the Kuba state reached its wealth and power in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
zh: 巴希莱莱人通常称为莱莱人，是刚果盆地腹地的班图族群，居住在今开赛省伊莱博一带、开赛河与洛安格河之间的森林和稀树草原。他们在语言和传统上与库巴人、翁戈人相近，三族都自称源自共同祖先沃托，但莱莱人从未加入约1625年起建立的集权式库巴王国，而是保持由长老主事的自治村落。其社会以一妻多夫婚姻，以及男子织造、兼作贸易品和内部货币的酒椰布闻名，另有扁平面具和长辫发式小像；狩猎享有崇高声望，村庄保留着以穿山甲为核心的仪式崇拜，直到17至18世纪库巴国家臻于鼎盛之时依然如此。

en: The Bashkirs are a Kipchak Turkic people of the southern Urals, pasturing cattle on both slopes of the mountains in a land their traditions call Badzhgard. Their ancestors were Turkic tribes who wandered the Aral and Syr Darya steppes before migrating to the Urals between the ninth and tenth centuries; the Baghdad envoy Ibn Fadlan met them there in 922 and described a warlike, independent people who still worshipped sky and nature spirits. Islam first reached them in the tenth century and took firm root in the 1320s and 1330s under the Golden Horde, which had ruled all their lands since the thirteenth century. When the Horde broke up, the Bashkirs were divided among the Nogai Horde and the khanates of Kazan and Sibir, and from the mid-sixteenth century they passed, clan by clan, under the Russian tsars. Nomadic pride made the bargain restless: they rose in the uprisings of 1662 to 1664, 1681 to 1684 and 1704 to 1711, and the building of Orenburg from 1735 provoked another six years of revolt. In 1774 Salavat Yulayev led them into Pugachev's rebellion. The crown then turned them into soldier-settlers, forming an irregular Bashkir army in 1798; Bashkir regiments rode as far as Paris in 1814, where German onlookers called them the Northern Amurs. Catherine the Great had already recognised their religious life by founding the Orenburg Mohammedan Spiritual Assembly at Ufa in 1788.
