zh: 巴什基尔人是南乌拉尔的钦察突厥语民族，在乌拉尔山两侧坡地放牧牛群，他们把自己的土地称作巴什古德。其先民是曾在咸海与锡尔河草原游徙的突厥部落，于9世纪至10世纪间迁入乌拉尔；922年巴格达使节伊本·法德兰在此见到他们，记载这是一个尚武而独立、仍崇拜天神与自然神灵的民族。伊斯兰教10世纪开始传入，在13世纪起统治此地的金帐汗国治下，于14世纪20至30年代最终扎根。金帐汗国解体后，巴什基尔人被诺盖汗国、喀山汗国和西伯利亚汗国分而治之；16世纪中叶起，他们逐部归附俄国沙皇。游牧者的骄傲使这份归属极不安稳：他们先后参加1662—1664年、1681—1684年和1704—1711年的起义，1735年奥伦堡动工筑城又引发长达六年的叛乱。1774年，萨拉瓦特·尤拉耶夫率他们加入普加乔夫起义。此后沙皇政府将他们改造为军屯牧民，1798年组建巴什基尔非正规军；巴什基尔骑兵团远征至1814年的巴黎，被德国旁观者称为“北方阿穆尔人”。叶卡捷琳娜大帝则早在1788年便于乌法设立奥伦堡穆罕默德宗教会议，承认其宗教生活。

en: The Basingui correspond to the Bobangi, also called Bangala, a Bantu river people of the middle Congo and the Ubangi, living in the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Skilled canoeists and fishermen, they were traders and warriors who controlled river traffic north of Pool Malebo before colonial rule, speaking Bobangi, related to Lingala.
zh: 巴辛吉人对应博班吉人（又称班加拉人），是活动于刚果河中游与乌班吉河一带的班图河上族群，分布在刚果（布）与刚果（金）两国。他们善操独木舟、以捕鱼为生，同时也是商人和战士，在殖民时代之前控制着马莱博湖以北的河上贸易；所说的博班吉语与林加拉语亲缘相近。

en: The Basques are the indigenous people of the western Pyrenees and the Bay of Biscay, in the seven historic provinces straddling Spain and France, distinguished by Euskara, a language isolate surviving from the pre-Indo-European tongues of ancient Europe; Roman authors knew their ancestors as the Vascones and Aquitanians. In the early Middle Ages their country between the Ebro and the Garonne was called Vasconia, and out of it arose the Kingdom of Pamplona, later Navarre, whose coast Castile seized in 1199 and which itself fell to Spanish armies between 1512 and 1524, while Lower Navarre north of the mountains became a province of France in 1620. The towns and valleys kept their own fueros, the customary laws that also enshrined inheritance by the eldest child, even as the War of the Bands set rival local lineages against each other. Basque entered print in 1545, when Bernard Etxepare of Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port published the first Basque book, and the Jesuit Manuel de Larramendi printed a grammar of the language in 1729; the French Revolution of 1790 swept away the self-governing institutions of the French Basque provinces.
zh: 巴斯克人是比利牛斯山西段和比斯开湾沿岸的原住民，分布在横跨西班牙与法国的七个历史省份；他们的巴斯克语是欧洲仅存的孤立语言，承自史前欧洲的前印欧语，罗马作家称其先民为瓦斯孔人和阿基坦人。中世纪早期，埃布罗河与加龙河之间的故土称瓦斯孔尼亚，后来从中兴起潘普洛纳王国，即纳瓦拉的前身；其海岸于1199年被卡斯蒂利亚夺取，纳瓦拉本土也在1512至1524年被西班牙军队征服，山北的下纳瓦拉则于1620年成为法国的一省。城镇和山谷长期保有自己的富埃罗斯习惯法，其中规定由最年长的子女继承家产；与此同时，帮派战争使地方望族世代仇杀。1545年，圣让皮耶德波尔的贝尔纳·埃切帕雷出版了第一本巴斯克语书籍，巴斯克语就此进入印刷时代；1729年，耶稣会士曼努埃尔·德·拉腊门迪出版了巴斯克语语法。1790年法国大革命废除了法国一侧巴斯克各省的自治机构。

en: The Bassa, who call themselves the children of Ngog Lituba, the pierced rock, are a Bantu people of the Cameroonian coast, speaking the Basaa language across the lower Sanaga and Nkam river basins. Their oral traditions tell of a long migration from the Logone valley and the Mandara Mountains in the Lake Chad region southward into the forest, where they settled at Ngog Lituba before spreading, on the eve of the fifteenth century, into clans such as the Eséka and Yabassi along the Sanaga and Wouri. Farmers and fishermen, they held the Wouri estuary until the Duala, another Bantu people, arrived and drove them inland, a displacement dated by tradition to the late seventeenth or early eighteenth century. The Duala had become the leading merchants of the Cameroon coast by the sixteenth century, and through the 1700s the Bassa supplied them from the interior with slaves and produce for the European ships, while keeping their own clan-based society in the forest country behind the coast.
zh: 巴萨人自称恩戈格利图巴，即‘穿孔之岩’的子孙，是喀麦隆沿海的班图族群，在萨纳加河下游与恩坎河流域操巴萨语。他们的口述传统讲述了一次漫长迁徙：从乍得湖地区的洛贡河谷和曼达拉山脉南下进入森林，先定居于恩戈格利图巴，又在15世纪前夕分成埃塞卡、雅巴西等氏族，散布到萨纳加河与武里河一带。他们务农捕鱼，原本据有武里河口，直到另一支班图人杜阿拉人到来，把他们赶往内陆；按口述传统，这次逼迁发生在17世纪末或18世纪初。杜阿拉人到16世纪已成为喀麦隆海岸的首要商人，整个18世纪，巴萨人从内陆向他们供应奴隶和物产，再由后者转卖给欧洲商船，而巴萨人自己仍在海岸后方的林地中保持着氏族社会。

en: Batak is the collective name for a family of closely related Austronesian peoples of the North Sumatran highlands, including the Toba, Karo, Simalungun, Pakpak-Dairi, Angkola and Mandailing, who settled around Lake Toba and the surrounding river valleys. Though long pictured as isolated inlanders, they were tied to maritime trade for over a thousand years, carrying camphor, benzoin and pepper on their backs to ports such as Barus, where a Tamil inscription of 1088 records a foreign merchant community, and Kota Cina near modern Medan. A Chinese work of the thirteenth century calls them a dependency of Srivijaya, and the Suma Oriental later describes a Bata kingdom lying between Pasai and Aru. In 1337 the Batak were still organized by exogamous marga clans under a syncretic religion blending ancestor worship with Hindu and Buddhist ideas, served by priest-healers who kept handwritten bark books called pustaha in the indigenous Surat Batak script. From the sixteenth century rice sales to the pepper-growing Aceh Sultanate drew them deeper into coastal commerce, while Mandailing and Angkola in the south came under Minangkabau influence and accepted Islam during the Padri War of 1821 to 1837; the Toba and Karo highlands kept their older customs far longer.
zh: 巴塔克是对苏门答腊北部高地一批亲缘南岛语系民族的统称，包括托巴、卡罗、西马隆贡、帕克帕克–戴里、安科拉和曼代林等支系，他们聚居在多巴湖及周边河谷。外界长期把他们看作封闭的内陆民族，但实际上他们参与海上贸易已逾千年，把樟脑、安息香和胡椒背到巴鲁斯等港口出售——1088年的一块泰米尔铭文记载了那里的外商社群，也在今棉兰附近的哥打支那形成了贸易集镇。13世纪的中国文献称他们为室利佛逝的属部，后来的《东方概要》则描述了一个夹在巴赛与阿鲁之间的巴塔王国。1337年时，巴塔克人仍按外婚制的“马尔加”氏族组织社会，信奉融合祖先崇拜与印度教、佛教观念的混合宗教，祭司兼医者使用本土的巴塔克字母，把药方和咒语写在树皮做成的“普斯塔哈”手册里。16世纪起，向种植胡椒的亚齐苏丹国出售稻米使他们更深地卷入沿海贸易；南部的曼代林人和安科拉人则受米南加保影响，在1821至1837年的帕德里战争期间皈依伊斯兰教，而托巴和卡罗高地将古老习俗保留了更久。

en: The Baure are an Arawakan people of the flooded savannas of the Beni, in what is now northern Bolivia, where their chief town, Baures, stands in the Iténez province. Their language, also called Baure, belongs to the Southern Arawakan branch and is closest to the Moxo tongues, with Carmelito and Joaquiniano as its local varieties. They were farming villagers of the Moxos lowlands when the Jesuit Cipriano Barace first contacted them around 1690. Nine reductions were built for their clans, beginning with the town of Baures, definitively founded on 8 December 1708 by Lorenzo Legarda; the missions introduced cattle, weaving and writing and grew to hold some sixteen thousand Baure by 1740. The Hungarian Jesuit Francisco Eder, who spent fifteen years at the San Martín reduction between 1720 and 1730 and published his account in 1770, left their fullest contemporary description. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 the reductions declined under disease and repeated Portuguese attacks, and many Baure withdrew into the forest.
zh: 巴乌雷人是贝尼泛滥稀树草原上的阿拉瓦克语族族群，住在今玻利维亚北部伊特内斯省，中心城镇为巴乌雷斯。他们的语言亦称巴乌雷语，属南阿拉瓦克语支，与莫霍诸语言最接近，另有卡梅利托、华金尼亚诺两种地方变体。耶稣会士西普里亚诺·巴拉塞约于1690年首次与他们接触时，他们已是莫霍斯低地的农耕村民。教会为其各氏族建了九座传教镇，首先是1708年12月8日由洛伦索·莱加尔达正式建立的巴乌雷斯镇；传教镇引入牛畜、纺织和文字，到1740年已容纳约一万六千名巴乌雷人。匈牙利耶稣会士弗朗西斯科·埃德1720至1730年间在圣马丁传教镇生活十五年，1770年出版的记述是对他们最详尽的同时代描写。1767年耶稣会被驱逐后，传教镇在疾病和葡萄牙人的接连袭击下衰落，许多巴乌雷人退回森林。

en: The Bauzi are a Papuan people of the forested hinterland behind the eastern shore of Geelvink Bay, or Cenderawasih Bay, in Indonesian New Guinea, with villages such as Danau Bira, Neao and Solom. Their language is the best-documented member of the East Geelvink Bay family and is reported to possess a whistled form of speech.
zh: 巴乌兹人是印度尼西亚新几内亚岛海尔芬克湾（今称极乐鸟湾）东岸后方森林腹地的巴布亚族群，村落包括达瑙比拉、尼奥和索洛姆等。他们的语言是东海尔芬克湾语系中记录最充分的语言，并有使用口哨语的记载。

en: The Baxoje, better known as the Iowa or Ioway, are a Chiwere-speaking Siouan people whose name for themselves means grey snow people; the label Iowa comes from a Dakota word, ayuxbe, meaning sleepy ones, which reached English through French explorers. Together with the Missouria and the Otoe, they once formed part of the Ho-Chunk nation before leaving southern Wisconsin and moving west across the Mississippi. From the fifteenth to the eighteenth century they lived around the Red Pipestone Quarry in present-day southwestern Minnesota, and by the early nineteenth century they had reached the Platte River, where Lewis and Clark visited their settlements in 1804. Semi-nomadic after adopting horses, they still grew maize and lived in bark lodges and earth lodges, using tipis on the hunt, and traded alum pipes and furs to the French. Between 1824 and 1836 they ceded their Missouri lands, and in 1837, led by Chief Mahaska, or White Cloud, they were removed to a reservation on the Kansas-Nebraska border.
zh: 巴荷杰人（常称艾奥瓦人或艾奥韦人）是说奇维雷语的苏语族群，自称意为“灰雪之人”；“艾奥瓦”一名来自达科他语中意为“瞌睡者”的词，经法国探险家传入英语。他们与密苏里人、奥托人曾同属霍查克群体，后来离开威斯康星南部，西渡密西西比河。15至18世纪，他们生活在今明尼苏达西南部的红色派普斯通采石场一带；到19世纪初已抵达普拉特河，刘易斯与克拉克于1804年访问过他们的村落。他们在采用马匹后趋于半游牧，但仍种植玉米，住树皮屋和土屋，狩猎时改用梯皮，并向法国人贩卖明矾烟斗和毛皮。1824至1836年间，他们割让了在密苏里的土地；1837年，在酋长马哈斯卡（意为白云）率领下，他们被迁往堪萨斯与内布拉斯加交界处的保留地。

en: The Bayagoula, whose name the ethnologist John Swanton translated as bayou people, were a small tribe of the lower Mississippi in Louisiana, with their main village near Bayou Goula in present-day Iberville Parish; their unrecorded language may have been a Southern Muskogean tongue akin to Choctaw and Houma. In 1699 they were among the first Louisiana peoples to meet the French explorer Iberville, sharing their village with the related Mugulasha. Early alliances shifted violently: the Houma raided them in the winter of 1699, and in the spring of 1700 the Bayagoula fell on their Mugulasha hosts and destroyed them. Disaster came in 1706, when first Taensa refugees and then the Tunica attacked them, the Tunica ambush nearly wiping out the tribe. Perhaps forty warriors remained by 1715, smallpox thinned the survivors further by 1721, and after drifting to Ascension Parish the last Bayagoula settled among the Houma and Acolapissa or married into the French, Spanish and German colonies, disappearing as a separate people before the mid-eighteenth century.
zh: 巴亚古拉人的名字被民族学家斯旺顿译为河湾人，是路易斯安那密西西比河下游的小部落，主村在今天伊贝维尔堂区的古古拉河湾附近；他们没有留下记录的语言可能属于南穆斯科格语支，与乔克托语和霍马语相近。1699年，他们是最早见到法国探险家伊贝维尔的路易斯安那族群之一，当时与同族的穆古拉沙人共居一村。早期的联盟关系变化剧烈：1699年冬霍马人来袭，1700年春巴亚古拉人反过来攻灭了收留他们的穆古拉沙人。1706年大难临头，先是坦萨难民、随后是图尼卡人进攻他们，图尼卡人的伏击几乎将该族斩尽杀绝。到1715年他们只剩约四十名战士，1721年天花又使幸存者进一步减少；最后的巴亚古拉人流徙到阿桑普申堂区，或定居于霍马人与阿科拉皮萨人中间，或与法国、西班牙和德国殖民者通婚，到18世纪中叶已不再是独立族群。

en: The Bayali are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Queensland coast, whose country lay south of the Darumbal along the shore from Keppel Bay to the Calliope River. They spoke the Bayali language, a little-recorded Kingkel tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family known from a single collected vocabulary.
zh: 巴亚利人是昆士兰中部沿海的澳大利亚原住民，其领地位于达伦巴尔人以南，沿海岸从凯珀尔湾延伸至卡利奥佩河。他们使用巴亚利语，这是帕马—牛雅语系金克尔语支中记录很少的语言，仅存一份采集到的词汇表。

en: The Bayono, also called Enamesi or Swesu, are a little-documented Papuan people of the mountainous Digul River headwaters in Papua Province, Indonesia, south of the Jayawijaya highlands. Their speech forms the Bayono-Awbono cluster, which most linguists place within or near the Greater Awyu branch of Trans-New Guinea.
zh: 巴约诺人又称埃纳梅西人或斯韦苏人，是印度尼西亚巴布亚省迪古尔河上游山区、查亚维查亚高地以南一个记载很少的巴布亚族群。他们的语言构成巴约诺-阿博诺语丛，多数学者将其置于跨新几内亚语系大阿维尤分支之内或近旁。

en: The Bazombo, or Zombo, are a Bakongo subgroup of the hilly borderlands between northern Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, around the towns of Damba and Maquela do Zombo in Uíge province. They speak Kizombo, a dialect of the Kikongo language cluster.
zh: 巴宗博人又称宗博人，是巴刚果人的一支，住在安哥拉北部与刚果民主共和国交界的丘陵地带，以威热省的丹巴和马凯拉杜宗博等城镇为中心。他们讲刚果语群中的基宗博方言。

en: The Bdewekhantunwan, or Mdewakanton, are the leading band of the Eastern Dakota, the Santee of the Sioux Seven Council Fires, and their name means Spirit Lake Village, after Mille Lacs Lake in central Minnesota. Tradition numbers them first among the seven council fires, and with the Wahpekute they formed the Santee Upper Council; originally the word Santee belonged to them alone. In 1687 the French explorer Greysolon du Lhut visited their great lakeside village of Izatys, recorded as the chief town of the Nadouessioux. Driven southwest like the other Santee by wars with the Ojibwe, by the early nineteenth century they held the lower Minnesota River under the head chief Wabasha, called The Leaf, who fought for the British in the War of 1812 and for the United States in the Black Hawk War of 1832 and signed the Prairie du Chien treaties of 1825 and 1830. In 1805 two of their chiefs, Little Crow I and Penichon, signed Pike's Purchase, ceding a hundred thousand acres at the mouth of the Minnesota River, and in the autumn of 1837 they sold all their lands east of the Mississippi.
zh: 布德韦坎通万人（即姆德瓦坎顿人）是东达科他四族之首，属苏族“七议团”中的桑蒂人，族名意为“灵湖村”，得名于明尼苏达中部的米尔拉克湖。按传统，他们在七议团中位列第一，并与瓦佩库特人组成桑蒂上议事会；“桑蒂”一词最初仅指他们。1687年，法国探险家格雷索隆·迪吕特造访他们在湖边的大村伊扎蒂斯，记载其为纳杜埃西乌人的首镇。与其他桑蒂人一样，他们在奥吉布瓦人的战争压力下向西南迁移；19世纪初，他们在大酋长瓦巴沙（人称“叶子”）率领下据有明尼苏达河下游。瓦巴沙在1812年战争中助英作战，1832年黑鹰战争中站在美国一边，并签署了1825和1830年的《普雷里德欣条约》。1805年，他们的两位酋长小克劳一世和佩尼雄签署《派克购地条约》，割让明尼苏达河河口的十万英亩土地；1837年秋，他们又出售了密西西比河以东的全部土地。

en: The Beami, also recorded as the Bedamini, are a Papuan people of the western Great Papuan Plateau in Papua New Guinea, living around Mount Sisa between the Strickland and Kikori basins. Their Beami language belongs to the Bosavi branch of Trans-New Guinea, and they traditionally dwelt in longhouses and lived by swidden farming centred on taro.
zh: 贝阿米人在文献中又称贝达米尼人，是巴布亚新几内亚大巴布亚高原西部的巴布亚族群，住在斯特里克兰河与基科里河两流域之间的萨山一带。他们的贝阿米语属跨新几内亚语系博萨维语支，传统上聚居长屋，经营以芋头为中心的轮垦农业。

en: The Beary, also called Byari, are a Muslim trading community of the Tulu Nadu coast, centred on Mangalore and the ports of Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, and count among the oldest Muslim settlements in India, with a documented history of more than 950 years. Their name is said to come from the Tulu word byara, meaning trade. Community tradition traces its faith to the Arab missionary Malik bin Deenar, who reached Malabar in the seventh century; his companion Habeeb bin Malik is credited with preaching in Tulu Nadu and building mosques at Kasaragod, Mangalore and Barkur. Their speech, Beary, is an outlying dialect of Malayalam shaped by Tulu phonology and enriched with Persian and Arabic merchant loanwords, and it is written in both the Malayalam and Kannada scripts.
zh: 比亚里人又称比亚里穆斯林，是图卢纳德沿海的穆斯林商贸社群，以门格洛尔及南卡纳达、乌杜皮一带的港口为中心，是印度最早的穆斯林定居群体之一，有明确记载的历史超过950年。其名称据说来自图卢语 byara，意为贸易。社群传说把信仰的传入追溯到7世纪抵达马拉巴尔的阿拉伯传教士马利克·本·迪纳尔；他的同伴哈比卜·本·马利克在图卢纳德传教，并在卡萨拉戈德、门格洛尔和巴尔库尔修建清真寺。他们的语言比亚里语是马拉雅拉姆语的边缘方言，语音深受图卢语影响，并因经商吸收了大量波斯语和阿拉伯语借词，书写时兼用马拉雅拉姆字母和卡纳达字母。

en: The Bedouin are the semi-nomadic Arab camel- and sheep-herding tribes of the Arabian, Syrian and North African deserts, known in Arabic as badw, desert-dwellers. Organized in clans tracing common ancestry, they lived by moving between wells and pastures, protecting caravans and raiding rival tribes in expeditions called ghazw; in the early Islamic centuries scholars of Arabic held their speech to be the purest model of Classical Arabic. As Islam spread, their tribes reached Sinai and the Negev, where their camps ringed Beersheba, Aqaba and the desert routes into Egypt. In 1326 ibn Battuta found an Egyptian customs post at Qatya on the north Sinai coast, its road guarded by Bedouin who hunted down travelers crossing without permission. Having sided with the Ottomans against the Mamluks at the conquest of 1517, the Sinai and Delta shaykhs soon fell foul of the new order, and Mamluk governors executed several of them in 1519. Under Ottoman rule the tribes kept their hold on the desert, and their raids on pilgrim caravans reached a peak in the eighteenth century, most bloodily in the great Hajj caravan massacre of 1757.
zh: 贝都因人是阿拉伯、叙利亚和北非沙漠中半游牧的阿拉伯部落，阿拉伯语称“巴杜”，意为沙漠居民，以牧养骆驼和绵羊为生。他们按共同血缘组成氏族，辗转于水井与牧场之间，以护送商队和对敌对部落发动“加兹武”劫掠为生；伊斯兰早期的阿拉伯语学者认为，他们的语言是古典阿拉伯语最纯正的范本。随着伊斯兰教传播，贝都因部落进入西奈和内盖夫，营地环绕着贝尔谢巴、亚喀巴和通往埃及的沙漠商道。1326年，伊本·白图泰在西奈北岸的加提雅见到埃及人的税卡，贝都因人受雇守卫道路、追捕未经许可越境的旅客。1517年奥斯曼征服埃及时，他们曾站在奥斯曼一边反对马穆鲁克，但西奈和三角洲的酋长很快与新秩序反目，1519年多名酋长被马穆鲁克总督处死。奥斯曼统治下，各部落保持着对沙漠的控制，他们对朝觐商队的劫掠在18世纪达到顶峰，最惨烈的一次是1757年的朝觐商队大屠杀。

en: The Beja are Cushitic-speaking camel nomads of the Eastern Desert between the Nile and the Red Sea, heirs of the Medjay and Blemmyes known to ancient Egyptian and Roman writers. The kings of Aksum made their hill country tributary in the third century, and the geographer al-Yaqubi counted five Muslim Beja kingdoms there in the ninth, though al-Maqdisi still found Christians among them a hundred years later. Their chief port, Suakin, had a Muslim sultan of mixed Meccan and Beja blood when Ibn Battuta visited in 1332; the Hedareb tribe made it their capital as Mamluk power waned, and after a spell under Adal the town fell to the Ottomans in the 1550s, becoming the seat of the Habesh pashalik in 1555. Inland, the migration of Arab tribes such as the Juhaynah and Rabi'a brought intermarriage and Islam, so that by the fifteenth century the Beja were Muslim, organized in the Ababda, Bisharin, Amarar, Hadendoa and Beni-Amer clans, some keeping their Cushitic tongue and others turning to Tigre or Arabic. By the eighteenth century the Hadendoa dominated much of eastern Sudan.
zh: 贝贾人是尼罗河与红海之间东部沙漠里讲库希特语的骆驼游牧民，是古埃及和罗马文献中梅德杰人与布莱米人的后裔。3世纪时阿克苏姆国王迫使他们的山地称臣纳贡，9世纪地理学家雅库比记载当地有五个穆斯林贝贾王国，而一个世纪后的马克迪西仍发现他们中间有基督徒。贝贾人的主要港口萨瓦金在1332年伊本·白图泰到访时，已有一位兼具麦加和贝贾血统的穆斯林苏丹；马穆鲁克势力衰落后，赫达雷布部落把萨瓦金定为都城，经过阿达尔的短暂统治，该城在16世纪50年代落入奥斯曼人之手，并于1555年成为哈贝什帕夏辖区的驻地。内陆方面，朱海纳、拉比阿等阿拉伯部落的迁入带来了联姻和伊斯兰教，到15世纪贝贾人已全部穆斯林化，分属阿巴卜达、比沙林、阿马拉尔、哈登多瓦和贝尼阿米尔等氏族：有的仍说库希特语，有的则改用提格雷语或阿拉伯语。到18世纪，哈登多瓦人已控制苏丹东部的大片地区。

en: The Belauan, or Palauans, are the indigenous people of the Belau (Palau) archipelago at the western edge of Micronesia, and speak Palauan, a Malayo-Polynesian language that stands outside the Oceanic group shared by most neighbouring peoples. Austronesian settlers from the Philippines or eastern Indonesia reached the islands between the third and second millennia BC, leaving terraced hillsides, stone paths and monoliths, and built a village society ordered by a strict matrilineal system that governed inheritance, marriage and the passing of titles. Ferdinand Magellan's surviving ship sighted outlying Sonsorol in 1521, but Palau long stayed beyond European reach: a map drawn after castaway Caroline islanders reached the Spanish Philippines in 1696 prompted Jesuit voyages of 1710 and 1711 that ended in the priests' deaths. Sustained contact began only when the British East India Company ship Antelope wrecked off Ulong in 1783; Captain Henry Wilson and his crew spent three months with the ruler of Koror, and took his son Lee Boo to London, where the young man died of smallpox in 1784. British traders then became regular visitors, yet in 1837 the Palauans still lived under their own matrilineal chiefs, with no foreign administration on the islands.
zh: 帕劳人是密克罗尼西亚西缘贝劳群岛（即帕劳）的原住民，使用的帕劳语属马来—波利尼西亚语族，与周边多数民族的大洋洲语不同。来自菲律宾或印尼东部的南岛语定居者在公元前第三至第二个千年间抵达群岛，留下梯田、石径和巨石遗迹，并发展出严格的母系社会：继承、婚姻和头衔传递都按母系进行。1521年麦哲伦船队残存的“特立尼达号”望见外围的松索罗尔岛，但帕劳长期处于欧洲人势力之外：1696年有加罗林水手漂流到西属菲律宾的萨马岛，欧洲人据此绘出第一幅帕劳地图，随后1710年和1711年的耶稣会航行均以传教士殒命告终。持续接触始于1783年英国东印度公司商船“羚羊号”在乌隆岛外海失事，亨利·威尔逊船长一行在科罗尔酋长那里生活了三个月，并把酋长之子李布带回伦敦，年轻人却于1784年死于天花。此后英国商人定期造访，但直到1837年，帕劳人仍生活在本族母系酋长治下，岛上没有任何外来政权。

en: The Beldet were an Evenki-speaking Tungus clan group of the Markha and upper Vilyuy taiga in central Yakutia, west of the Lena. Russian records of the 1630s show cossacks taking hostages and exacting fur tribute, or yasak, from the Vilyuy Tungus rods, who lived by hunting and small-scale reindeer herding.
zh: 贝尔代特人是说鄂温克语的通古斯氏族群体，活动在雅库特中部勒拿河以西的马尔哈河与维柳伊河上游泰加林。17世纪30年代的俄方记录显示，哥萨克以扣押人质的方式向维柳伊通古斯氏族征收毛皮贡赋牙萨克，后者以狩猎和小规模驯鹿牧养为生。

en: The Bemba, or AbaBemba, are a matrilineal Bantu people of the plateau between the Luapula, Chambeshi and Luangwa rivers in what is now northern Zambia. Their traditions trace them to the Luba country of the Upemba depression: a seventeenth-century revolt against the Luba king Mukulumpe, led by his sons Nkole and Chiti of the crocodile-totem Bena Ng'andu clan, sent their ancestors east across the Luapula, and before 1740 they had settled around the headwaters of the Chambeshi. The village of Ng'wena became the first capital of the Bemba kingdom under its paramount, the Chitimukulu. From the late 1700s the Chitimukulus turned expansionist, driving the Lungu and Mambwe west and north, and parceled out conquered lands to royal brothers, creating tributary kingdoms such as Mwamba, Mpanda and Kalundu; by the early nineteenth century more than fifteen chieftainships answered to the Chitimukulu. Bemba villagers practice slash-and-burn farming of finger millet and manioc, and their language, Ichibemba, is closely related to Luba and served as a lingua franca across the Sabi peoples of the region.
zh: 本巴人（自称阿本本巴人）是实行母系制的班图族群，居住在今赞比亚北部卢阿普拉河、谦比西河与卢安瓜河之间的高原上。他们的传统把源头追溯到乌彭巴洼地的卢巴故地：17世纪，卢巴国王穆库伦佩的儿子恩科莱和奇蒂率领鳄鱼图腾的贝纳·恩甘杜氏族起兵反叛，失败后族人向东渡过卢阿普拉河，到1740年以前已在谦比西河源头一带定居。恩圭纳村成为本巴王国第一个都城，最高统治者称“奇蒂穆库鲁”。18世纪末起，历任奇蒂穆库鲁热衷于扩张，把隆古人、曼布韦人赶往西方和北方，并把征服的土地分给王族兄弟，建立起姆万巴、姆潘达、卡伦杜等附庸王国；到19世纪初，已有十五个以上的酋长国向奇蒂穆库鲁称臣。本巴村民以轮耕方式种植穇子和木薯，他们的语言奇本巴语与卢巴语关系密切，曾是萨比诸族群之间的通用语。

en: The Bembe, plural Babembe, are a Bantu people of the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, settled mainly in the Fizi territory and the Itombwe highlands west of Lake Tanganyika, with communities also around Kalemie and across the lake in western Tanzania. Their oral genealogy names a common ancestor, Mbondo, and holds that the Bembe once lived beside the Lega in the northeast before the two peoples separated, the Lega turning back while the Bembe moved on toward the lake; a third brother, Bangu, is said to have founded the Bangubangu of Maniema. They grew into a fiercely independent mountain people, divided into lake and highland groups, where women worked the fields and men hunted, fished and traded from semi-nomadic forest villages. Their customs blend pre-Lega, Boyo-Kunda, Hemba and Bemba traditions, and oral history recalls that from 1820 the Babembe endured repeated wars that brought them close to extinction before the colonial conquest.
zh: 本贝人（复数称巴本贝）是刚果民主共和国东部的班图族群，主要住在坦噶尼喀湖以西的菲齐领地和伊通布韦高地，在卡莱米以及湖对岸的坦桑尼亚西部也有社群。他们的口传谱系尊奉共同始祖姆邦多，称本贝人曾与莱加人一起住在东北方，后来两族分离：莱加人折返，本贝人继续向湖区迁徙；另有兄弟班古，相传在马涅马开创了班古巴古人。他们后来成为以强悍独立著称的山地民族，分为湖区和高原两支，妇女耕作，男子在半游牧的森林村落里狩猎、捕鱼和经商。本贝人的习俗融汇了前莱加、博约—昆达、海姆巴和本巴诸传统；口传史还称，从1820年起巴本贝人连遭战乱，几近灭绝，而那时殖民征服尚未到来。

en: The Bena, or Wabena, are a Bantu people of the Njombe highlands in south-central Tanzania, within the basin of the Great Ruaha and Rufiji rivers, who speak the Bantu Bena language. An offshoot group, the Bena of Ulanga, settled further east down the Rufiji valley.
zh: 贝纳人（自称瓦贝纳）是坦桑尼亚中南部恩琼贝高地的班图人，居于大鲁阿哈河与鲁菲吉河流域，使用班图语支的贝纳语；另有一支沿鲁菲吉河谷东迁，称乌兰加贝纳人。

en: The Bena Lwalwa are a Luba-speaking cluster of clans in the Lwalwa country of the Kasai borderlands, in the same region as the Lwalwa and Lulua peoples. In Kiluba the prefix Bena means the people or descendants of a place or founder, the naming pattern borne by the stateless Luba farming groups living west of the Luba empire.
zh: 贝纳卢卢阿人是开赛边缘卢瓦鲁地区使用卢巴语的氏族群，与卢瓦鲁人、卢卢阿人同处一地。在卢巴语中，“贝纳”意为某地或某位始祖的人民、后裔，卢巴帝国以西那些没有王权的卢巴语农耕群体都用这种方式命名。

en: The Bengali people occupy the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, the fertile river plain of the Bengal region, and speak Bengali, an Eastern Indo-Aryan language written in its own Brahmic script. Bengali grew out of the eastern Magadhi Prakrit, also called Gaudi Prakrit, which passed through an Abahatta stage before taking distinct shape; a Sanskrit-Chinese dictionary of 782 already contains Bengali words, and the Charyapada, Buddhist mystic songs of the eighth to twelfth centuries, are the earliest surviving Bengali literature. It was the vernacular of the Buddhist Pala Empire and the Hindu Sena dynasty, whose rule ended when Bakhtiyar Khalji conquered Gauda in 1202 to 1204. Bengal became a province of the Delhi Sultanate in 1225, but by 1338 its three governors ruled separately, and Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah unified the country by 1352, founding the independent Bengal Sultanate with its capitals at Pandua, Gaur and Sonargaon. Under the sultans Bengali won court patronage, especially under Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah, and absorbed a large Persian and Arabic vocabulary; the poets Chandidas and Shah Muhammad Sagir and the Ramayana of Krittibas Ojha shaped its medieval literature. Mughal armies conquered the delta in the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, after which the Nawabs of Bengal ruled until the East India Company's victory at Plassey in 1757. A Roman-letter Bengali grammar was printed in Lisbon in 1743, and in the early nineteenth century a new literary standard formed around the west-central dialect of Nadia.
zh: 孟加拉人生活在恒河与布拉马普特拉河下游的肥沃三角洲，即孟加拉地区，使用东印度-雅利安语支的孟加拉语，文字为源自婆罗米文的孟加拉文。孟加拉语由东摩揭陀俗语（又称高达俗语）经阿巴哈塔阶段演变而成，782年的一部梵汉词典中已出现孟加拉语词汇，而8至12世纪佛教密宗的诗歌集《行句》是现存最早的孟加拉语文学。它曾是佛教波罗帝国和印度教犀那王朝的民间语言；1202至1204年，巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉攻占高达，犀那王朝灭亡。1225年孟加拉成为德里苏丹国的一个行省，但到1338年，三地总督各自为政，沙姆斯丁·伊利亚斯·沙阿于1352年统一全国，建立独立的孟加拉苏丹国，先后以潘杜阿、高尔和索纳尔冈为都。苏丹们、尤其是贾拉鲁丁·穆罕默德·沙阿在位时，孟加拉语获得宫廷扶持，并吸收了大量波斯语和阿拉伯语词汇；诗人昌迪达斯、沙阿·穆罕默德·萨吉尔以及克里蒂巴斯·奥贾的《罗摩衍那》译本塑造了它的中世纪文学。16世纪末至17世纪初，莫卧儿军队征服三角洲，此后孟加拉纳瓦卜割据一方，直到1757年英国东印度公司在普拉西战役中取胜。1743年，一部用拉丁字母拼写的孟加拉语语法在里斯本印行；19世纪初，以纳迪亚方言为基础的新书面标准逐渐形成。

en: This grouping covers the Benue valley and the adjacent plateaus, whose leading historical people were the Jukun. By about 1250 Jukun clans had settled along the Gongola, and their state of Kwararafa, or Kororofa, grew into a power centered on the Benue under a divine king, the Aku. The Kano Chronicle records Kano's forces reaching Kororofa in the fourteenth century, and Kwararafa later turned aggressor, sacking a gate of Kano in 1653 and raiding Katsina and even Bornu before its power peaked in the later seventeenth century, when it ranked among the great kingdoms of the Sudan. Its decline set in by the late eighteenth century, and Chamba and Fulani attacks in the early nineteenth century broke it up, leaving the Wukari Federation under the Aku Uka as the Jukun heartland; related splinters such as the Alago around Lafia had already broken away. Sharing this broad region were the plateau peoples, including the Berom around Jos with their own Benue-Congo speech, and the Mambila of the highlands around Nkambe, whose Mambiloid tongue belongs to the Northern Bantoid branch.
zh: 这一聚合文化涵盖贝努埃河谷及相邻高原，历史上的主导民族是朱昆人。约1250年，朱昆诸氏族已在贡戈拉河沿岸定居，他们的夸拉拉法（又称科罗罗法）国家在神王“阿库”统治下成长为贝努埃河畔的强国。《卡诺编年史》记载，14世纪卡诺军队曾打到科罗罗法；后来夸拉拉法转入攻势，1653年攻破卡诺的一座城门，还劫掠卡齐纳甚至博尔努，其势力在17世纪后期达到顶峰，跻身苏丹地区诸强之列。18世纪末它开始衰落，19世纪初在昌巴人和富拉尼人的打击下解体，只剩“阿库·乌卡”统治的武卡里联盟作为朱昆人的核心；包括拉菲亚一带的阿拉戈人在内的支系此前已陆续脱离。与他们同处这片广大区域的，还有乔斯一带讲贝努埃-刚果语的贝罗姆等高原族群，以及恩康贝附近高地的曼比拉人，后者的曼比拉语属于北类班图语支。

en: The Beothuk were the Indigenous people of the island of Newfoundland, where their distinctive culture took shape about AD 1500, the latest phase of a sequence going back to migrants from Labrador around AD 1. They lived in independent bands of thirty to fifty-five people, chiefly around Notre Dame and Bonavista bays, wintering in conical birch-bark houses called mamateeks and following caribou, salmon and seals with the seasons. Their spring custom of painting bodies, houses and canoes with red ochre led Europeans to call them Red Indians. Norse voyagers may have met their ancestors about AD 1000, and after John Cabot's voyage of 1497 the Beothuk increasingly avoided newcomers, retreating inland as fishing stations and traplines cut them off from coastal food sources. Expeditions such as George Cartwright's in 1768 and David Buchan's in 1811 failed to build peace, while starvation, smallpox and tuberculosis and clashes with settlers shrank their numbers. Demasduit, captured in 1819 after her husband Nonosabasut was killed, died of tuberculosis in 1820; her niece Shanawdithit, taken in 1823, died in St. John's in 1829, after which the Beothuk were declared extinct. Their poorly recorded language, known as Beothukan, is treated as an unclassified isolate.
zh: 贝奥图克人是纽芬兰岛的原住民，其独特文化约在公元1500年成形，是公元1年前后自拉布拉多迁徙而来的族群所经历的最晚一个文化阶段。他们以三十至五十五人组成的独立群队而居，主要活动于圣母湾和博纳维斯塔湾一带，冬季住在名为“马马蒂克”的桦树皮锥形屋中，随季节追逐驯鹿、鲑鱼和海豹。每到春天，他们用红赭石涂抹身体、房屋和独木舟，欧洲人因此称他们为“红印第安人”。诺斯航海者可能在公元1000年前后就遇见过他们的祖先；1497年约翰·卡博特航行之后，贝奥图克人日益回避新来者，随着渔场和诱捕路线切断他们的沿海食物来源，他们不断退入内陆。1768年乔治·卡特赖特和1811年戴维·巴肯的远征都未能建立和平，饥荒、天花、结核病以及与定居者的冲突使人口锐减。德马斯杜伊特于1819年被掳，丈夫诺诺萨巴苏特被杀，她本人也在1820年死于结核病；她的侄女莎娜瓦迪特1823年被带走，1829年死于圣约翰斯，此后贝奥图克人被宣告灭绝。他们记录稀少的语言称贝奥图克语，被视为归属不明的孤立语言。

en: Berrichon is the langue d'oïl of the old province of Berry in central France, descended from the Vulgar Latin of northern Gaul and very close to standard French. Its range also takes in the Bourbonnais around Bourbon and Montluçon, whose speech linguists now group with it as Berrichon-Bourbonnais, while its southern fringe forms part of the Croissant, the transition zone between the langues d'oïl and Occitan. The region takes its name from the Bituriges, the Gaulish tribe whose chief town became Bourges. In 1360 Berry was raised into a duchy, an appanage held by princes of the French royal house, and the court of the dukes at Bourges produced the illuminated Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry in the early fifteenth century. From the sixteenth century the local aristocracy and townspeople adopted standard French, leaving Berrichon as a peasant patois, and after the Revolution the schools of the Third Republic spread French further into the countryside. The old province was dissolved in 1790 and divided mainly between the departments of Cher and Indre.
zh: 贝里语是法国中部旧行省贝里的奥依语，源自高卢北部的通俗拉丁语，与标准法语十分接近。它的范围还包括波旁和蒙吕松一带的波旁奈，学者常把当地话与贝里话合称“贝里-波旁奈语”；其南缘属于奥依语与奥克语之间的过渡带“新月方言区”。贝里得名于高卢部落比图里吉人，他们的首府后来成为布尔日。1360年贝里被升格为公爵领，作为法国王室亲王的封邑，15世纪初公爵在布尔日的宫廷催生了泥金手抄本《贝里公爵的豪华时祷书》。从16世纪起，当地贵族和市民改说标准法语，贝里语沦为农民的土话；大革命之后，第三共和国的学校又把法语进一步推广到乡间。1790年旧行省被撤销，主要划入谢尔和安德尔两省。

en: The Berta, also called the Benishangul, are a Nilo-Saharan people of the Blue Nile borderlands, living in the hills between Sennar in Sudan and western Ethiopia, around Fazughli and Asosa. They trace their origins to the Funj sultanate of Sennar, where they are remembered as the largest Funj tribe, and in the 1500s or 1600s they crossed into the Ethiopian lowlands. Their old name Bela Shangul, later Arabicized into Benishangul, means rock of Shangul, after a sacred stone in the mountains where they first settled. Feuding communities and slave raids from Sudan drove them to build villages on rocky heights, with houses and granaries raised on stone pillars, and by the 1800s the country had broken into sheikhdoms such as Fadasi, Gizen and Asosa. Centuries of Sudanese influence made most Berta Muslims speaking Sudanese Arabic, while ritual specialists called neri still healed, divined and made rain, and farmers grew sorghum, kept bees and cultivated coffee.
zh: 贝尔塔人又称贝尼尚古尔人，是青尼罗河边境地带的尼罗-撒哈拉语系族群，散居在苏丹森纳尔与埃塞俄比亚西部之间、法祖格利和阿索萨一带的山区。他们把族源追溯到森纳尔的丰吉苏丹国，在当地被视为最大的丰吉部落；16至17世纪，他们迁入埃塞俄比亚低地。旧称贝拉尚古尔后来阿拉伯化为贝尼尚古尔，意为‘尚古尔之石’，得名于他们最早落脚的山中一块圣石。由于各社群相互仇杀，又要防范来自苏丹的奴隶劫掠，他们把村庄建在岩石高地上，房屋和谷仓用石柱撑起；到19世纪，这一地区分裂为法达西、吉曾、阿索萨等酋长国。数百年受苏丹影响后，多数贝尔塔人已是讲苏丹阿拉伯语的穆斯林，但称为内里的仪式专家仍负责治病、占卜和求雨；农人种植高粱、养蜂并栽种咖啡。

en: The Besermyan are a small Permian people of the forest country between the Vyatka and the Cheptsa, in present-day Udmurtia, whose self-name beserman descends, through Volga Bulgar, from the Arabic word for Muslim. In the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries Russian chronicles used it for the Muslim population of the Volga Bulgar lands and the Kazan khanate around Arsk, where Udmurts lived alongside them; the papal envoy Plano Carpini had already met people of that name under Mongol rule in the thirteenth century. As the Golden Horde tore itself apart and Timur campaigned through the Volga lands at the end of the fourteenth century, these Muslim settlers moved up the Vyatka into the lower Cheptsa, where they were gradually absorbed by the Udmurts while keeping a separate identity; after Moscow annexed the Vyatka land in 1489, the Karino Arsk princes granted the newcomers land and drew more of them from the Kazan khanate. The Besermyan speech is an Udmurt dialect marked by Tatar words and sounds, the linguistic trace of their mixed birth. Orthodox missionaries began their conversion in the middle of the eighteenth century, but their folk rites kept both Udmurt pagan spirits and Muslim-derived customs.
zh: 贝谢尔曼人是生活在维亚特卡河与切普察河之间林地里的小型彼尔姆族群，其自称“贝谢尔曼联”经伏尔加保加尔语中介，源自阿拉伯语“穆斯林”一词。14至15世纪的俄罗斯编年史用它称呼伏尔加保加尔故地和喀山汗国阿尔斯克一带的穆斯林人口，那里本就有乌德穆尔特人与他们比邻而居；而早在13世纪，教皇使节柏郎嘉宾就在蒙古治下见过同名的人群。14世纪末金帐汗国内讧不已、帖木儿大军横扫伏尔加之地，这些穆斯林移民遂沿维亚特卡河上溯，进入切普察河下游，在被乌德穆尔特人同化的同时保持了独立身份；1489年莫斯科吞并维亚特卡地区后，卡林诺阿尔斯克王公向新来者封授土地，并继续从喀山汗国招徕人口。贝谢尔曼人的语言是一种带鞑靼语词汇和语音痕迹的乌德穆尔特方言，正是其混合起源的语言印记。18世纪中叶，东正教传教士开始让他们改宗，但其民间仪式中既保留了乌德穆尔特的异教神灵，也留下了源自伊斯兰教的习俗。

en: The Betsileo are the third largest people of Madagascar, highlanders of the southern plateau between the Mania River and the Andringitra Massif, in a land of hill valleys centred on Fianarantsoa and divided into northern, central and southern parts. Their name means the many invincible ones, earned when King Besilau repelled an invasion by the Sakalava of Menabe in the 1670s. From the seventeenth century their country was split among independent little kingdoms such as Fandriana, Fisakana, Manandriana and Isandra, until the armies of Radama I of Imerina conquered them one by one in the 1810s and 1820s. Radama made Fianarantsoa the administrative seat of the central and southern Betsileo and attached the north to Antsirabe, so that the Betsileo began the century as an administrative division of the Merina state rather than a single kingdom; many of them were enslaved and sold either within the island or to European slave traders. Their society was ranked into andriana nobles, hova commoners and andevo slaves under the authority of village elders, and they became the island's most skilful rice farmers, carving elaborate terraces into the hillsides around Fianarantsoa. They honoured the creator Zanahary and their ancestors through the famadihana reburial ceremony, unwrapping the dead to dress them in fresh shrouds, and relied on diviners and astrologers to fix the dates of rites.
zh: 贝齐略人是马达加斯加第三大族群，世居南部高原，地盘北起马尼亚河，南抵安德林吉特拉山，是一片以菲亚纳兰楚阿为中心的丘陵谷地，分为北、中、南三部分。族名意为“众多不可战胜者”，得名于17世纪70年代贝西劳国王击退梅纳贝萨卡拉瓦人入侵的战绩。从17世纪起，他们的土地分裂为凡德里亚纳、菲萨卡纳、马南德里亚纳、伊桑德拉等各自独立的小王国，直到19世纪10至20年代被伊默里纳的拉达马一世逐个征服。拉达马把菲亚纳兰楚阿设为中南部贝齐略人的行政中心，北部则划归安齐拉贝，贝齐略由此作为梅里纳国家的行政区划而非统一王国进入19世纪；许多贝齐略人沦为奴隶，或在岛内转卖，或被卖给欧洲奴隶贩子。他们的社会分为贵族、平民和奴隶三个等级，由村落长老主持事务；他们也是岛上最出色的稻农，在菲亚纳兰楚阿周围的山坡上开出层层梯田。他们敬奉创世神扎纳哈里和祖先，举行翻尸重葬仪式，把先人遗骨取出换上新裹尸布，每逢典礼还要请占卜师和占星师择定吉日。

en: The Betsimisaraka, whose name means the many inseparables, are the second largest people of Madagascar and hold the long eastern coastal strip from Antalaha in the north to Mananjary in the south, where Tintingue and Toamasina became their chief ports. Before the eighteenth century they lived in scattered clans, each ruled by a filohany chief over a village or two. From the 1680s British and American pirates settled along their coasts and married chiefly daughters, producing a large mixed population called the zana-malata. One of them, Ratsimilaho, born around 1694 to a chief's daughter and the pirate Thomas Tew, led the northern clans against a southern invasion, took Fenerive in 1712 and was elected king at Foulpointe, giving his followers the name Betsimisaraka; allied with the Bezanozano and the Sakalava, he built one of the strongest kingdoms on the island, which held together until his death in 1754. His successors were weaker: Zanahary was assassinated in 1767, the French occupied Ile Sainte Marie and opened posts in every port, and Zakavolo was deposed in 1803, leaving the union in fragments. In 1817 Radama I of Imerina marched on Toamasina and garrisoned the coast; a revolt in 1825 failed, and Queen Ranavalona I destroyed the remnants of the old ruling line. The Betsimisaraka kept ancestor veneration, tromba spirit-possession rites, zebu sacrifice and the famadihana reburial ceremony, bound by many local fady taboos.
zh: 贝齐米萨拉卡人在马尔加什各族中人数仅次于梅里纳人，族名意为“密不可分的众人”，占据马达加斯加东部北起安塔拉哈、南至马南扎里的狭长海岸，廷廷格和图阿马西纳是他们的主要港口。18世纪以前，他们散居为众多氏族，每个酋长只管一两个村落。17世纪80年代起，英国和美洲的海盗在这一带海岸落脚，与酋长之女通婚，形成大批被称为扎纳马拉塔的混血后裔。约1694年，酋长之女与海盗托马斯·图生下的混血儿拉齐米拉霍率领北方诸氏族抵御南方入侵，1712年夺取费内里沃，在富尔普安特被推举为王，并为部下取名贝齐米萨拉卡；他与贝扎诺扎诺人和萨卡拉瓦人结盟，建成岛上最强盛的王国之一，统一局面维持到1754年他去世。后继诸王孱弱：扎纳哈里于1767年被臣民刺杀，法国人占领圣玛丽岛并在各港口设立商站，扎卡沃洛则在1803年被废，王国四分五裂。1817年，伊默里纳的拉达马一世进军图阿马西纳，在海岸驻扎军队；1825年的起义失败，腊纳瓦洛娜一世又清除了旧统治家族的残余。贝齐米萨拉卡人敬奉祖先，举行通灵附体仪式、祭牛和翻尸重葬，并受诸多本地禁忌约束。

en: The Beta Israel, whose name means house of Israel in Ge'ez and who were later called Falasha by their Christian neighbours, are the Jewish community of the Ethiopian highlands, centred on the Semien Mountains and the lands around Lake Tana. Long cut off from the rest of world Jewry, they kept Haymanot, a Judaism without the Talmud, and spoke Agaw dialects such as Kayla and Qwara. In the ninth century the traveller Eldad ha-Dani described an independent Jewish kingdom in these mountains, and in the mid-tenth century Queen Gudit of Semien overthrew the kings of Aksum, sacking the city and the monastery of Debre Damo before the Zagwe dynasty succeeded her. The restoration of the Solomonic line in 1270 under Yekuno Amlak opened long centuries of warfare: Emperor Amda Seyon I campaigned in Semien in 1329, the fifteenth-century emperor Yeshaq I gave the community the Falasha label, and Zara Yaqob married a daughter of its king Gideon in 1445. Under Susenyos in the early seventeenth century the Jesuits backed forced conversions and the conquest of the last Jewish strongholds, while Fasilides, who expelled the Jesuits in 1632, settled many of the community near his Gondar palace as weavers and smiths. From the mid-eighteenth century the era of the princes left them increasingly isolated.
zh: 贝塔以色列在吉兹语中意为“以色列之家”，后被基督教邻人称为法拉沙人，是埃塞俄比亚高原的犹太社群，以塞米恩山脉和塔纳湖周边为中心。他们长期与外界犹太人隔绝，保留着不依《塔木德》的海马诺特信仰，使用凯拉语、夸拉语等阿高语方言。9世纪时，旅人埃尔达德·哈-达尼曾记述这些山区里有一个独立犹太王国；10世纪中叶，塞米恩的古迪特女王推翻阿克苏姆诸王，洗劫阿克苏姆城和德布勒达莫修道院，其后由扎格维王朝接续统治。1270年叶库诺·阿姆拉克重建所罗门王朝，开启了数百年的战端：阿姆达·塞永一世于1329年进兵塞米恩，15世纪的伊沙克一世给该社群冠以法拉沙之名，扎拉·雅各布则在1445年迎娶其王吉迪昂之女。17世纪初苏斯尼约斯在位时，耶稣会推动强制改宗并攻灭犹太人最后的据点；1632年法西利德斯驱逐耶稣会，却把许多贝塔以色列人安置在贡德尔王宫附近，充任织工和铁匠。18世纪中叶起的“王公时代”更使他们日益与世隔绝。

en: The Bezanozano, also called the Antankay, were one of the earliest Malagasy peoples, holding the forested inland region of Ankay between the Betsimisaraka lowlands to the east and the Merina highlands to the west, around the towns of Moramanga and Ambatondrazaka. Tradition linked them with the Vazimba, the island's first inhabitants, whose ancient tombs in their territory served as places of pilgrimage and sacrifice, and their name means those of many small plaits, after a traditional hairstyle. They lived in fortified villages run by elders and guarded by eleven protective sampy idols said to have come from Sakalava country. In the eighteenth century they grew rich as middlemen in the slave and cattle trade between the highlands and the European and Arab ships on the east coast; Moramanga became the chief market, an alliance was struck with the Betsimisaraka Kingdom, a great slave revolt was put down in 1768 with European help, and Randrianjomoina emerged as their first and only king. Around the turn of the nineteenth century Andrianampoinimerina of Imerina reduced them to vassals, and in 1817 his son Radama I completed the conquest. Under Merina rule the Bezanozano were drafted into unpaid porterage between Antananarivo and the port of Toamasina, depopulating the Ankay until their very name became a byword for slave.
zh: 贝扎诺扎诺人又称安坦凯人，是最早定居马达加斯加的马尔加什族群之一，占据东部贝齐米萨拉卡低地与西部梅里纳高地之间林木茂密的安凯内陆地区，中心在穆拉曼加和安巴通德拉扎卡一带。传说他们与岛上最早的居民瓦津巴人同源，境内的瓦津巴古墓是朝圣和献祭之所；族名意为“梳许多小辫子的人”，取自传统发式。他们居住在长者议事的设防村落里，尊奉十一尊据说来自萨卡拉瓦之地的保护神像。18世纪，贝扎诺扎诺人充当高地与东岸欧洲及阿拉伯商船之间奴隶和牛只贸易的中间人，因而致富，穆拉曼加成为主要商埠；他们与贝齐米萨拉卡王国结盟，1768年还靠欧洲人帮助镇压了一场大规模奴隶起义，兰德里安祖穆伊纳则成为他们第一位也是唯一一位国王。19世纪初，伊默里纳的安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳将他们降为附庸，1817年其子拉达马一世彻底征服该地。在梅里纳人统治下，贝扎诺扎诺人被强征在塔那那利佛与图阿马西纳港之间无偿搬运货物，安凯人口因此锐减，他们的族名甚至成了奴隶的代名词。

en: The Bhils are the indigenous forest and hill people of western and central India, spread in 1337 across the Vindhya and Satpura country from Vagad in southern Rajasthan, where Dungarpur and Banswara stand, through Jhabua and Nimar in Malwa to the Dang hills of Baglana in Khandesh. Their name may derive from a Dravidian word for bow, and the bow and arrow remain their traditional mark; their speech, Bhili, is a Western Indo-Aryan language related to Gujarati and Rajasthani, split into many local dialects that shade into Marathi in the south-east. Divided into numerous territorial clans, the Bhils lived by shifting cultivation, hunting and forest produce, paying tribute to the Rajput and Muslim states around them, from the Farooqui sultans of Khandesh in the fourteenth century to the Mughals after Aurangzeb annexed Baglana for Shah Jahan in 1637. Yet they kept their value as soldiers, and four hundred Bhil archers under Rana Poonja fought beside Maharana Pratap at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576. As Mughal power crumbled and the Marathas pressed into Khandesh, Bhil risings troubled the region, and after the East India Company took Khandesh in 1818 the Bhils rose in a long series of revolts that continued through the 1820s and 1830s.
zh: 比尔人是印度西部和中部的山林原住民，1337年时散布在温迪亚与萨特普拉山区，从拉贾斯坦南部的瓦加德（栋格尔布尔和班斯瓦拉一带），经摩腊婆的贾布阿和尼马尔，直到坎德什巴格拉纳的丹格丘陵。他们的族名可能来自达罗毗荼语中意为弓的词，弓箭历来是其传统标志；比尔语属西印度-雅利安语支，与古吉拉特语和拉贾斯坦语相近，内部分成许多方言，东南方向逐渐与马拉地语交融。比尔人分为众多地域性氏族，以轮垦、狩猎和林产为生，向周边的拉杰普特和穆斯林政权纳贡：14世纪起是坎德什的法鲁基苏丹国，1637年奥朗则布为沙贾汗吞并巴格拉纳后又臣属莫卧儿。但他们始终是受重视的战士，1576年拉纳·蓬贾率领四百名比尔弓箭手在哈尔迪加蒂战役中随马哈拉纳·普拉塔普作战。莫卧儿权力瓦解、马拉塔人进逼坎德什后，比尔人的起事不断困扰该地区；1818年英国东印度公司取得坎德什，比尔人又发动了一系列延续到19世纪20至30年代的长期反抗。

en: The Bhojpuri people live in the Bhojpur and Purvanchal country of the middle Ganges, around Arrah, Buxar, Sasaram and Varanasi, where eastern Uttar Pradesh meets western Bihar. Their language, Bhojpuri, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan tongue of the Bihari group, descended from Magadhi Prakrit and written in both the Devanagari and Kaithi scripts; its folk epics, above all the Lorikayan, took shape between the eleventh and fourteenth centuries. The region takes its name from Bhojpur, the seat of the Ujjainiya Parmar Rajputs, who claim descent from King Bhoja of Ujjain and in the fourteenth century under Hunkar Singh drove the Chero rulers out of Shahabad towards Palamau. The Ujjainiyas then fought the Jaunpur Sultanate, founded in 1394, for more than a hundred years from their forest strongholds. Saints such as Kabir and Kina Ram preached in Bhojpuri between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries as Persian and Arabic words entered the language. Sher Shah Suri, founder of the Sur Empire in 1540, was born at Sasaram, and the Ujjainiya raja Gajpati helped him win the battle of Surajgarha. The word Bhojpuri itself is first recorded in 1789.
zh: 博杰普尔人生活在恒河中游的博杰普尔与普尔万查尔地区，即北方邦东部与比哈尔邦交界处，以阿拉、布克萨尔、萨萨拉姆和瓦拉纳西为中心。他们的博杰普尔语属东印度-雅利安语支比哈尔语组，由摩揭陀俗语演变而来，并用天城文和凯提文两种文字书写；11至14世纪间，以《洛里卡扬》为代表的民间史诗逐渐成形。地区之名源自博杰普尔，这里是乌贾因尼亚·帕玛尔拉杰普特人的据点；他们自称是乌贾因国王博杰的后裔，14世纪在洪卡尔·辛格率领下把切罗统治者逐出沙哈巴德，迫其退往巴拉穆。此后乌贾因尼亚人以山林为据点，与1394年建立的江布尔苏丹国缠斗了一百多年。15至17世纪，迦比尔、基纳·拉姆等圣徒用博杰普尔语传道，波斯语和阿拉伯语词汇也在这一时期进入该语言。1540年建立苏尔帝国的舍尔沙出生于萨萨拉姆，乌贾因尼亚首领加吉帕蒂曾助他赢得苏拉杰加尔哈之战。博杰普尔这一名称本身最早见于1789年的记载。

en: The Biak are an Austronesian people of the Schouten or Biak Islands, led by Biak itself, Supiori and Numfor, which guard the entrance of Cenderawasih Bay on the north coast of New Guinea, and speak Biak, also called Biak-Numfor, of the South Halmahera-West New Guinea subgroup. Born navigators, they built a far-flung maritime network across the bay: from the early eighteenth century they planted permanent settlements along the Bird's Head Peninsula, and such place names as Manokwari, meaning old village in their language, still mark their old routes. Legends of the war leader Gurabesi recall ties with the Sultanate of Tidore, to which Biak traders paid tribute in slaves and forest produce. The Portuguese navigator Jorge de Menezes first sighted the island in 1526, and by the early nineteenth century the Biak of Numfor were the leading middlemen of the New Guinea coast, bartering birds of paradise, massoi bark and slaves with Makassarese, Buginese, Chinese and European merchants.
zh: 比亚克人是南岛语族族群，聚居在新几内亚岛北岸极乐鸟湾口外的斯考滕群岛（又称比亚克群岛），以比亚克岛、苏皮奥里岛和农福尔岛为核心，操南岛语系东马来-波利尼西亚语支南哈马黑拉-西新几内亚语群的比亚克语（又称比亚克-农福尔语）。他们是天生的航海者，在极乐鸟湾一带建立了庞大的海上网络：18世纪初起，他们在鸟头半岛沿岸开辟永久定居点，马诺夸里等地名在比亚克语中意为“旧村”，处处标示着他们旧日的航路。关于战将古拉贝西的传说，记录了他们与蒂多雷苏丹国的联系，比亚克商人曾以奴隶和林产品向蒂多雷苏丹纳贡。1526年，葡萄牙航海家若热·德·梅内塞斯首次望见该岛；到19世纪初，农福尔岛的比亚克人已是新几内亚北岸最重要的贸易中间商，用极乐鸟、香料树皮和奴隶同望加锡人、布吉人、华人及欧洲商人交易。

en: The Bicolano people are an Austronesian ethnolinguistic group of the southeastern Luzon peninsula that bears their name, the Bicol region. Iron Age Austronesian settlers from Taiwan were their ancestors, and Neolithic burial jars and pottery show a long-settled farming society before Spanish contact. Their folk epic the Ibalong recalls that they were once called Ibalong, after Gat Ibal, who ruled Sawangan on the site of modern Legazpi; the later name Bikol derives from a word meaning meandering, after the region's principal river. They speak a dozen closely related Bikol dialects and grow rice, coconuts and abacá hemp in a typhoon-swept volcanic landscape. Augustinian and Franciscan missionaries brought Roman Catholicism, and in 1712 the seminarian Miguel Robles de Covarrubias introduced devotion to Our Lady of Peñafrancia, whose carved image became the centre of Naga's annual fluvial procession. Spanish prospectors also opened the gold mines of Paracale in Camarines Norte.
zh: 比科尔人是菲律宾吕宋岛东南部同名半岛——比科尔地区的南岛语系族群。其先民是铁器时代自台湾迁来的南岛移民，新石器时代的葬罐和陶器表明，在西班牙人到来之前这里已是定居已久的农耕社会。民间史诗《伊巴隆》追述他们曾称伊巴隆人，得名于统治萨旺岸（在今黎牙实比城一带）的加特·伊巴尔；后来的比科尔一名源自意为蜿蜒曲折的词，用来形容当地的主要河流。他们使用十几种彼此相近的比科尔语方言，在多台风的火山地带种植水稻、椰子和蕉麻。奥斯定会和方济各会传教士带来了罗马天主教；1712年，神学院学生米格尔·罗夫莱斯·德·科瓦鲁维亚斯引入了佩尼亚弗朗西亚圣母崇拜，其雕像成为那牙一年一度水上巡游的中心。西班牙探矿者还在北甘马粦的帕拉卡莱开采金矿。

en: The Bidayuh, or Land Dayaks, are related Dayak groups of the Sarawak River basin around Kuching and Serian and the neighbouring Sanggau district of West Kalimantan. They built hilltop longhouses for protection, farmed hill rice by rotation and honoured the rice spirits in animist rites, speaking many mutually unintelligible Land Dayak dialects.
zh: 比达友人又称陆地达雅人，是若干彼此相近的达雅群体，聚居于古晋、西连一带的沙捞越河流域及邻近的西加里曼丹上侯地区。他们在山丘上修建长屋以求自保，轮耕旱稻，以万物有灵仪式祭祀稻灵，所说的多种陆地达雅方言彼此不能互通。

en: The Bidjara, also spelt Pitjara or Bidyara, are an Aboriginal Australian people of inland eastern Queensland, distinct from the Bidjara of the Bulloo River and from the Badjiri further south. Norman Tindale reckoned their tribal lands at some 17,000 square kilometres around the headwaters of the Nogoa and Warrego rivers, running north of Augathella to Mantuan Downs, east towards Killarney and Chesterton, south to Caroline, and west as far as the Nive River. He also suggested that the Bidjara and the Badjiri had once been one people, splitting before European settlement under pressure from tribes pushing east. Their language, Bidjara, was a Maric tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family with several dialects, among them Gayiri, Gunggari and Gunya, and the nearby Wadjigu speech was closely related. James Cook had charted the distant Queensland coast in 1770, but the first Europeans did not enter this inland country until the pastoral expansion of the middle decades of the nineteenth century, when sheep and cattle stations spread along the Warrego.
zh: 比贾拉人（亦译皮贾拉、比迪亚拉）是澳大利亚昆士兰州东部内陆的原住民族群，与布卢河流域的比贾拉人以及更南边的巴吉里人并非同一群体。据诺曼·廷代尔估算，他们的部族领地约一万七千平方公里，位于诺戈阿河与沃里戈河源头一带，北起奥加塞拉以北直至曼丘恩当斯，东到基拉尼和切斯特顿附近，南抵卡罗琳，西达尼夫河。廷代尔还认为，比贾拉人与巴吉里人本是一族，在欧洲人定居之前因受东迁部族的挤压而分裂。他们的语言比贾拉语属帕马-牛雅语系的马里克语支，有加伊里、贡加里、贡亚等多种方言，邻近的瓦吉古语与之关系密切。詹姆斯·库克早在1770年就测绘了远方的昆士兰海岸，但欧洲人直到19世纪中叶的牧地扩张时期才初次进入这片内陆，牧羊场和牧牛场随之沿沃里戈河铺开。

en: The Bidwelli are the Bidawal, an Aboriginal people of East Gippsland whose hard country of sclerophyll woodland and rainforest, some seven thousand square kilometres, straddled the modern border of New South Wales and Victoria, running from Green Cape and Point Hicks inland to Delegate and the headwaters of the Cann River. Their name means “scrub dwellers” in the tongues of neighbouring peoples, and the ethnographer Alfred Howitt thought the tribe had grown from fugitives who had fled tribal justice among several neighbouring groups and found refuge in land most others shunned. In 1337 they lived in small bands on the few open tracts, hunting wallaby and gathering where they could, and brought boys to manhood through the Dyerrayal initiation. Their speech, called Muk-dhang, was close to the Kurnai dialects, though the Krauatungalung dubbed it “rough speech”.
zh: 比德维尔人即比达瓦尔人，是吉普斯兰东部的原住民族群。他们栖身的硬叶林地与雨林环境严酷，方圆约七千平方公里，横跨今天新南威尔士州与维多利亚州的边界，从格林角和希克斯角一直延伸到内陆的德利格特与坎恩河源头。在邻近族群的语言里，他们的名字意为“灌丛居民”。民族学家艾尔弗雷德·豪伊特认为，该部落是由从周边各族逃出来、躲避部族审判的难民汇聚而成，他们在别人避之不及的土地上找到了容身之处。1337年时，他们以小群体生活在为数不多的开阔地带，捕猎沙袋鼠、尽力采集，并通过名为“迪亚拉亚尔”的成年礼让男孩成为男人。他们的语言称穆克丹语，与库尔奈诸方言相近，而克劳阿通加伦人则把它叫作“粗话”。

en: The Bife are a Papuan people of the Morehead country in Western Province, Papua New Guinea, their villages lying along the eastern banks of the Bensbach River around Indorodoro in Kandarisa ward. Their speech, Blafe or Mblafe with its Ránmo dialect, forms the Mblafe-Ránmo chain of the Tonda branch of the Yam family.
zh: 比费人是巴布亚新几内亚西部省莫尔黑德地区的巴布亚人，村落分布在本斯巴赫河东岸、坎达里萨区的因多罗多罗一带。他们的语言称布拉费语或姆布拉费语，含兰莫方言，属亚姆语系通达分支下的姆布拉费-兰莫方言链。

en: The Bilala, who call themselves Balala, are a Muslim farming people of central Chad, settled around Lake Fitri in the Batha region with their traditional capital at Yao. They first appear in the fourteenth century as rivals of the Sayfawa dynasty of Kanem: allied with the Toubou, they defeated and killed the mai Dawud and seized Kanem itself, forcing the Sayfawa court to relocate to Bornu. Their rulers then took the title of sultan and built a kingdom so powerful that Egyptian chanceries treated them as equals of the Sayfawa, and Leo Africanus in the sixteenth century listed Gaoga, as he called the Bilala state, among the three great kingdoms of the Sudan. The Sayfawa retook Kanem only in the early sixteenth century under Idris Katagarmabe, who left the Bilala to govern it as a province, and their revolts ended only when Idris Alooma subdued them later in the century. Around 1630 the Wadai Sultanate drove them out altogether, and the Bilala migrated east to Lake Fitri, where they founded the Sultanate of Yao and grew cotton, millet and maize under a line of sultans.
zh: 比拉拉人自称巴拉拉，是乍得中部的穆斯林农耕民族，聚居于巴塔地区的菲特里湖周边，传统首都是雅奥。他们在14世纪首次见于记载，是加奈姆赛法瓦王朝的敌手：比拉拉人与图布人结盟，击败并杀死麦伊·达乌德，夺取加奈姆本土，迫使赛法瓦朝廷迁往博尔努。其首领随后自称苏丹，建立起强大王国，埃及官署把他们与赛法瓦人同等对待；16世纪的利奥·阿非利加努斯把比拉拉国家称作“加高”，列为苏丹地区三大王国之一。直到16世纪初，伊德里斯·卡塔加尔马贝才代表赛法瓦王朝收复加奈姆，但仍留比拉拉人作为行省治理；他们的反叛直到该世纪后期伊德里斯·阿卢马在位时才被平定。约1630年，瓦达伊苏丹国将他们彻底逐出，比拉拉人东迁菲特里湖，建立雅奥苏丹国，在历代苏丹治下种植棉花、小米和玉米。

en: The Bilinarra, also spelt Bilingara or Bilinara, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Victoria River District in the Northern Territory. Their language, whose name probably comes from bili, meaning rock or hill, is an eastern Ngumbin tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family, mutually intelligible with Gurindji and Ngarinyman and treated by linguists as a dialect of the latter. European explorers first entered their Victoria Downs country in the late 1830s, and later in the nineteenth century the Victoria River Downs station was laid out over Bilinarra and Karangpurru lands. Dispossession brought introduced disease, punitive massacres and forced station labour: at Gordon Creek captured people were shot and their bodies burned, while a strychnine-laced stew gave Poison Creek its name, and the survivors fled into Ngarinman country.
zh: 比林纳拉人（又拼比林加拉等）是北领地维多利亚河区的澳大利亚原住民。他们的语言名称可能来自意为岩石或山丘的“比利”，属帕马‑牛雅语系恩贡宾语支的东部语言，与古兰吉语、纳里宁曼语互通，语言学家把它看作纳里宁曼语的方言。19世纪30年代末，欧洲探险家首次进入他们的维多利亚当斯地区；19世纪后期，维多利亚河当斯牧场在比林纳拉人与卡朗普鲁人的土地上建立。被剥夺的过程带来了传入的疾病、惩罚性屠杀和强迫牧场劳役：在戈登溪，被俘者遭枪杀、遗体被焚；一道掺了士的宁的炖菜为毒溪留下名字，幸存者则逃入纳里宁曼人的地界。

en: The Bimanese, who call themselves Dou Mbojo, are an Austronesian people of eastern Sumbawa in the Lesser Sunda Islands, speaking a language closer to the tongues of Flores and Sumba than to the Sumbawanese of their own island's west. A Hindu-Buddhist kingdom of Bima, known in its own language as Mbojo, is traditionally dated to 709, and by the late fifteenth century it had grown into a crowded commercial centre and rice exporter; around 1515 the Portuguese apothecary Tome Pires noted its sales of cloth, horses, slaves and sappanwood, and its influence reached Manggarai on Flores and the islands of Sumba and Sawu. Makassarese expeditions of 1618, 1619 and 1626 opened the way to Islam: Prince La Kai converted in 1621 and ruled as Sultan Abdul Kahir, founding the Sultanate of Bima under Gowa's tutelage. When the Dutch East India Company broke Makassarese power in 1667-1669, Bima submitted to the Company in 1669 and kept wide autonomy under a Dutch resident, its elite intermarrying with Makassarese nobility. The highland Dou Donggo, fierce mountain warriors, retained their old folk beliefs and a semi-autonomous status within the sultanate, and in 1815 the eruption of Mount Tambora brought widespread ruin and famine to Bimanese lands.
zh: 比马人自称“杜姆博若”，是小巽他群岛松巴哇岛东部的南岛语族群，其语言与弗洛勒斯岛和松巴哇岛以东松巴岛诸语言的关系，反而比同岛西部的松巴哇语更近。印度教—佛教时期的比马王国在本地语言中称“姆博若”，传统上把建国时间追溯到709年；到15世纪末，它已成为商旅辐辏的商业中心和稻米输出地，约1515年葡萄牙药剂师托梅·皮莱士就记载过当地出售布匹、马匹、奴隶和苏木，其势力远及弗洛勒斯岛的芒加莱以及松巴岛、萨武岛。1618、1619和1626年望加锡人的三次远征为伊斯兰教打开了大门：王子拉·凯于1621年改宗，以苏丹阿卜杜勒·卡希尔之名统治，在戈瓦庇护下建立了比马苏丹国。1667至1669年荷兰东印度公司击垮望加锡霸权后，比马于1669年臣服于公司，在荷兰驻扎官监督下保留了很大自治权，贵族阶层仍与望加锡名门通婚。善战的高地居民“东东戈人”固守古老的民间信仰，在苏丹国内享有半自治地位；1815年坦博拉火山大喷发则给比马各地造成了普遍的破坏与饥荒。

en: The Binandere are a Papuan people of the northeast coast of the Bird's Tail of New Guinea and the namesake of the Binanderean, or Guhu–Oro, family of Trans–New Guinea languages. The family appears to have spread from the north along the Oro and Morobe coasts, and Binanderean-speaking inland communities gradually absorbed earlier Austronesian settlements on the shore; the contact was deep enough to give neighbouring Papuan Tip languages their Binanderean-style word order. Binandere speech stands at the centre of this network, close to the Orokaiva, Baruga and Suena languages around it.
zh: 比南德雷人是新几内亚“鸟尾”东北海岸的巴布亚族群，跨新几内亚语系的比南德雷语族（又称古胡—奥罗语族）便以它命名。该语族似乎从北方沿奥罗和莫罗贝海岸扩散，说比南德雷诸语的内陆社群逐渐同化了海岸上更早的南岛语聚落；这种接触之深，甚至使邻近的巴布亚尖端语言改用了比南德雷式的语序。比南德雷语本身处在这一网络的中心，与周围的奥罗凯瓦语、巴鲁加语和苏埃纳语关系密切。

en: The Bindali, also called Bendalgubber or North Murri, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the North Queensland coast, whose country of about a thousand square miles ran from the mouth of the Burdekin River north to Cape Cleveland and inland to the Leichhardt Range, taking in the Ayr district. Their extinct language, Bindal, belonged to the Pama-Nyungan family; linguists differ over whether it was a Maric tongue or one of the non-Maric Lower Burdekin languages, and only fragmentary, partly confused word lists survive to document it.
zh: 宾达尔人又称本达尔古贝尔人或北穆里人，是昆士兰北部沿海的澳大利亚原住民，领地约一千平方英里，南起伯德金河口、北至克利夫兰角、内陆抵达莱希哈特岭，艾尔一带也在其领地之内。他们已消亡的宾达尔语属于帕马-牛雅语系；语言学家对它的归属意见不一，有人认为它是马里克语支的语言，也有人把它归入非马里克语的下伯德金诸语言，存世的只有零碎且部分彼此混淆的词汇表。

en: The Bindji, also called Babindji or Mbagani, are a Luba-speaking Bantu people of the Kasai basin in the southern Congo, traditionally villagers of the Kazumba country west of the Luba heartland; related Bindji-Ngusu groups speak a Luban tongue close to Songye, and their carvers are known for wooden helmet masks.
zh: 宾吉人又称巴宾吉人或姆巴加尼人，是刚果南部开赛盆地讲卢巴语的班图族群，传统上居住在卢巴核心区以西的卡尊巴一带；亲缘的宾吉—恩古苏群体使用接近松耶语的卢班语，当地工匠以木雕头盔面具闻名。

en: The Birrbay, also spelt Birpai or Biripi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the New South Wales coast, their country centred on Port Macquarie and the Manning and Hastings river valleys, where the town of Taree now stands. Their language is Gathang, a tongue shared with the neighbouring Worimi and once used as a common speech when the tribes gathered. Contact was violent from the start: Birrbay oral history remembers the killing of many of their people at Blackmans Point around 1826, as convict settlements pushed up the coast. In 1831 the naval settler William Wynter took land at Taree and kept notably friendly relations, his son growing up among the Birrbay and learning their language, and by 1834 cedar cutters had laid camps along the Manning River.
zh: 比里皮人（又拼伯派）是澳大利亚新南威尔士州海岸的原住民，领地以麦觉理港以及曼宁河、黑斯廷斯河谷为中心，今塔里镇即位于其中。他们的语言加桑语与邻族沃里米人共用，各部族集会时也以它作为通用语。接触从一开始就充满暴力：比里皮人的口述史铭记着约1826年在布莱克曼斯角发生的屠杀，时值流放犯定居点沿海岸向北扩张。1831年，海军出身的移民威廉·温特在塔里取得土地，与比里皮人保持着罕见的友好关系，他的儿子在比里皮人中长大并学会了他们的语言；到1834年，伐木者已沿曼宁河扎下营地。

en: The Bitur are a Papuan people of Western Province, Papua New Guinea, living in the villages of Bisuaka, Kasimap, Petom, Tewara and Upiara in the Oriomo-Bituri area. Their language, also called Bituri, Paswam or Mutum, is one of the Tirio family, a Trans-New Guinea group whose members share about forty percent of their vocabulary.
zh: 比图尔人是巴布亚新几内亚西部省的巴布亚人，聚居于奥里莫-比图里地区的比苏阿卡、卡西马普、佩托姆、特瓦拉和乌皮亚拉等村。他们的语言又称比图里语、帕斯瓦姆语或穆图姆语，属蒂里奥语系，这是跨新几内亚语系的一支，各语言约有四成词汇相同。

en: The Bjarmians were the Finnic-speaking people of the White Sea shore and the Northern Dvina basin, the country the Norse called Bjarmaland, around the site of later Arkhangelsk. The Norwegian merchant Ohthere visited them around 890 and found a settled, populous farming people whose language resembled that of the Sami. Viking expeditions followed, including that of Tore Hund in 1026, which bought great quantities of squirrel, beaver and sable furs and then plundered a sanctuary of the god Jómali. Their trade routes ran down the Dvina and the Volga to the Bulgar market, where furs and walrus ivory were exchanged for silver. In the thirteenth century the Bjarmians became tributaries of the Novgorod Republic, and as Slavic settlers fleeing the Mongols moved north into the region, displaced Bjarmians sailed to Norway, where King Haakon IV in 1240 granted them land around the Malangen fjord. Norwegian raids in 1217 and 1222 had already broken their old trading centre, and the name Bjarmaland disappears from the Norse sources after the 1220s, though Finnic speech lived on in the place-names and loanwords of the Russian north.
zh: 比亚尔米亚人是白海沿岸和北德维纳河流域的芬兰语支居民，北欧人把他们的家乡称为比亚马兰，其地在后来的阿尔汉格尔斯克一带。约890年，挪威商人奥瑟尔航行到此，发现这是一个定居务农、人口稠密的富庶族群，语言与萨米语相近。此后维京人接踵而至，其中1026年托尔·胡德的远征最有名：他先收购了大量松鼠、河狸和紫貂毛皮，随后又盗掠了供奉尤马拉神的圣所。他们的商路沿北德维纳河和伏尔加河通达保加尔，以毛皮和海象牙换取银器。13世纪，比亚尔米亚人沦为诺夫哥罗德共和国的附庸；为躲避蒙古人而北逃的斯拉夫农民涌入这一地区，流离失所的比亚尔米亚人渡海前往挪威，挪威国王哈康四世于1240年把马兰根峡湾一带的土地授予他们。1217年和1222年的挪威袭掠已摧毁了他们旧日的贸易中心，1220年代以后比亚马兰之名便从北欧文献中消失，但其芬兰语在俄罗斯北部的地名和方言借词中留下了痕迹。

en: The Blaan are an Austronesian indigenous people of southern Mindanao in the Philippines, with settlements around Lake Sebu and Lake Buluan in Cotabato, in Sarangani and around General Santos, beside their Tboli neighbors. Their name may combine bla, meaning opponent, with the suffix an, meaning people. They speak their own Austronesian language of the same name and preserve an indigenous pantheon headed by Melu, a white-skinned creator with teeth of gold, alongside spirits of the trees, waters and rocks. Blaan women join abaca strands by hand without a spinning wheel and weave the tabih cloth using the ikat technique called mabal, while Blaan smiths work brass and copper into tiny bells and the ornate brass-handled long knives called fais. Their colorful costumes are covered in beadwork, and brass belts strung with small bells announce the wearer's approach. They live by farming the hills and plains of southern Mindanao, where Koronadal and the Marbel River both take their names from Blaan words describing grassy plains and murky waters. The Maitum burial jars unearthed on the Sarangani coast, dated to roughly 5 BC to AD 370, show that the Blaan country held settled communities and far-flung contacts in antiquity. In 1543 the Spanish explorer Ruy López de Villalobos sailed past Sarangani Island and named it Antonia, and the coast later passed into the orbit of the Sultanate of Maguindanao; the Blaan themselves kept to their inland hills and ancestral rites while the lowlands turned to Islam.
zh: 布兰人是菲律宾棉兰老岛南部的南岛语系原住民，聚落在哥打巴托的塞布湖与布卢安湖一带、萨兰加尼和桑托斯将军城周边，与特博利人为邻。其族名可能由意为“对手”的 bla 和意为“人”的后缀 an 组合而成。他们使用同名的南岛语言，保留着本土神灵体系：至高造物主梅卢肤色洁白、牙齿为黄金，此外还有司掌树木、水流与岩石的精灵。布兰妇女不用纺车，手工接续蕉麻纤维，以名为“马巴尔”的扎染技法织成“塔比”布；工匠还以黄铜和红铜铸造小铃，以及配华丽铜柄的“法伊斯”长刀。他们色彩鲜艳的服装缀满珠饰，妇女腰间系满小铜铃，行走时铃声远播。他们在棉兰老南部的山地与平原务农，科罗纳达尔和马贝尔河的名字都来自布兰语，分别意为草丛平原与浑浊之水。萨兰加尼沿海出土的梅图姆葬瓮年代约在公元前5年至公元370年之间，说明布兰人居住的这片土地在上古时代已有定居社群和远距离交流。1543年，西班牙探险家鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·维拉洛沃斯航经萨兰加尼岛，将其命名为安东尼娅；后来沿海地带被纳入马京达瑙苏丹国的势力范围，低地皈依伊斯兰教，而布兰人仍留居内陆山地，保留着祖灵仪式。

en: The Blang, who call themselves Plang or U and appear in Tang chronicles of 618 to 907 as the Puzi man and in Yuan, Ming and Qing records as the Puman, are an Austroasiatic people of southern Yunnan. Their largest settlements lie in the Bulang mountains of Menghai in Xishuangbanna, with further villages in Shuangjiang, Yongde and the Lancang river valley; Chinese ethnographers trace them to the ancient Pu, one of the Hundred Pu tribes of the southwest. They speak Blang, a Palaungic language of the Mon-Khmer family, without a native script, and many also use Dai or Chinese. Organized in small land-owning clans in bamboo stilt-house villages, they are among the oldest known tea cultivators, tending ancient tea forests on the hills rather than monoculture plantations, and grow rice and dry-land crops. In Xishuangbanna they profess Theravada Buddhism learned from their Dai neighbours, layered over ancestor worship and animist rites, and Bulangshan villages retain traces of matrilineal custom, linking a child's name to its mother's.
zh: 布朗人自称布朗、乌等，唐代（618—907年）史籍称扑子蛮，元明清三代称蒲蛮、蒲人或濮满，是滇南的南亚语系民族。他们最大的聚居地在西双版纳勐海的布朗山，双江、永德及澜沧江河谷也有村落；民族学家把他们追溯为古代濮人的一支，属于西南百濮系统。布朗语属孟高棉语族佤德昂语支，没有本民族文字，不少人兼用傣语或汉语。他们以拥有土地的小氏族为单位，住在干栏式竹楼里，是已知最古老的茶农之一，在山间照料古茶园而非开辟单一种植的茶园，同时种植水稻和旱地作物。西双版纳的布朗人信奉从傣族邻人那里接受的上座部佛教，同时保留祖先崇拜与万物有灵仪式；布朗山一带还留有母系氏族遗风，子女命名时要把母亲的名字连在自己名字之后。

en: The Bo were an ancient people of the mountain borderlands of southern Sichuan and Yunnan, remembered above all for their hanging coffins, and Chinese records class them with the Di and Qiang peoples. In the Zhou dynasty they were known as the Pu, one of the Hundred Pu tribes of the upper Yangtze who were subdued by the state of Ba and passed under Qin rule when Qin conquered Ba in 316 BC. Their language is thought to have belonged to the Kra group, and the cliff faces of their country still hold coffins hollowed from single logs together with bronze drums. The Bo fortress of Lingxiao on Bowang Mountain in Xingwen became the last redoubt of Song resistance to the Mongols, holding out until 1288, more than eleven years after the Song fell. In 1573 Ming armies besieged Lingxiao and Gong County, and the Bo were killed or absorbed into the surrounding population, vanishing from the written record thereafter.
zh: 僰是四川南部与云南交界山区的古老民族，汉文典籍将其归入氐羌一类，以悬棺葬闻名。周代他们被称为濮，属长江上游“百濮”族群之一，后被巴国征服；公元前316年秦灭巴，僰地随之归入秦的版图。一般认为他们的语言属仡央语支，故地崖壁上留有整木刳成的悬棺和青铜鼓。兴文县博望山上的凌霄城是南宋抗蒙的最后据点，在宋亡之后又坚守十余年，直到1288年才被蒙古军攻破。1573年，明军围攻凌霄城与珙县，僰人或遭杀戮，或被周边族群同化，此后便从文字记载中消失。

en: The Bobo, who call themselves Bobo Fing, are a Mandé farming people of the upper Volta basin, autochthonous clans long settled around Bobo-Dioulasso in what is now western Burkina Faso and across the border north to Koutiala in Mali; they are distinct from the neighbouring Bwa, who speak a Gur language. Their own Bobo tongue is close to Bambara, and they grow red sorghum, pearl millet, yams and cotton in clan-organised villages. Traditional religion centres on the creator god Wuro, who made the first man a blacksmith and gave him the first mask; blacksmiths lead the cult of Wuro's son Dwo, and masked rites restore the balance between village and bush. In about 1714 the Dyula leader Famagan Ouattara founded the Gwiriko kingdom with Bobo-Dioulasso as its chief city, ruling the Bobo clans through an alliance with Bobo-Juula merchants, and when Gwiriko collapsed in the late 1830s the Bobo towns regained their independence.
zh: 博博人自称博博-芬，是沃尔特河上游流域的曼德系农耕民族，由自古定居的氏族组成，分布在今布基纳法索西部的博博-迪乌拉索一带，北越边境直至马里的库佳拉；他们与邻近讲古尔语的布瓦人不同。博博语接近班巴拉语，村落按氏族组织，种植红高粱、珍珠粟、薯蓣和棉花。传统宗教以创世神武罗为中心：传说武罗把第一个人造为铁匠并赐予第一副面具，铁匠主持武罗之子德沃的崇拜，面具仪式则用来恢复村落与荒野之间的平衡。约1714年，朱拉人首领法马甘·瓦塔拉建立古里科王国，以博博-迪乌拉索为首城，通过与博博-朱拉商人结盟统治各博博氏族；19世纪30年代末古里科瓦解，博博诸城重获独立。

en: The Bodewadomik, better known to Europeans as the Potawatomi, are an Algonquian-speaking people of the western Great Lakes; Bodéwadmik, their own name for themselves, means keepers of the hearth fire of the Council of Three Fires, the long-standing alliance they formed with the Ojibwe and Odawa, in which they were the youngest brother. Early French records locate them in southwestern Michigan, around the lower end of Lake Michigan, before the Beaver Wars of the mid-seventeenth century drove them west to Green Bay. They returned east with the French fur trade, settling near Detroit and along the St. Joseph River, and fought alongside France in the Fox Wars. After Britain seized the region in 1763 they joined Pontiac's Rebellion, capturing every British garrison except Detroit. In the wars after the American Revolution they sided in turn with Britain and the young United States, and their warriors formed part of Tecumseh's confederacy, joining the 1812 Battle of Fort Dearborn. A series of treaties after the War of 1812, culminating in the Treaty of Chicago in 1833, ceded their Michigan and Indiana lands and opened the way for removal west of the Mississippi.
zh: 博德瓦多米克人即欧洲人所称的波塔瓦托米人，是五大湖西部的阿尔冈昆语民族；Bodéwadmik是他们的自称，意为三火议会的“守灶人”。三火议会是他们与奥吉布瓦人、奥达瓦人结成的古老同盟，波塔瓦托米人在其中位列“幼弟”。早期法国文献记载他们住在密歇根西南部、密歇根湖南端一带，17世纪中叶的海狸战争把他们逐往西边的格林贝。后来他们随法国毛皮贸易东返，定居底特律附近和圣约瑟夫河沿岸，并在福克斯战争中与法国并肩作战。1763年英国夺取该地区后，他们加入庞蒂亚克起义，攻下了底特律以外的所有英军据点。美国独立战争后的连年战事中，他们先后依附英国和新生的美国，其战士还加入特库姆塞联盟，参与了1812年的迪尔伯恩堡战役。1812年战争之后的一连串条约、尤以1833年的《芝加哥条约》为顶点，割让了他们在密歇根和印第安纳的土地，为被迁往密西西比河以西铺平了道路。

en: The Bodo, also called Boro, are a Tibeto-Burman people of the Brahmaputra valley in Assam and the largest group of the wider Bodo-Kachari family, whose forebears entered the valley from the north in prehistoric times; Tibeto-Burman river names across Assam, such as the Dibang and Dihing, preserve traces of that early settlement. After the break-up of the kingdom of Kamarupa in the twelfth century, Bodo-Kachari branches founded several medieval states, among them the Chutia, Dimasa (Kachari), Koch and Twipra kingdoms, with the Koch dynasty taking power in 1515, while the Bodo of western Assam remained village farmers, working irrigated shifting fields by collective labour and trading forest produce between hills and plains. They kept their old Bathou faith, centred on the high god Obonglaoree and the shijou tree, though many came under Hindu influence and some entered the Ekasarana dharma of the Assamese Vaishnavas. As Koch rule expanded and the Ahom kingdom tightened its hold on western Assam in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, Bodo communities withdrew toward the forested Himalayan foothills, staying mobile and outside state tax systems well into the 1700s.
zh: 博多（又称博罗）人是阿萨姆布拉马普特拉河谷的藏缅语族群，也是更大的博多-卡查里族群中人数最多的一支，其先民在史前时期自北方进入河谷；今阿萨姆各地的迪邦河、迪杭河等藏缅语河名，仍保留着他们早期定居的痕迹。12世纪迦摩缕波王国瓦解后，博多-卡查里诸支建立了楚蒂亚、迪马萨（卡查里）、科赫、特维普拉等多个中世纪政权，其中科赫王朝于1515年掌权，而阿萨姆西部的博多人仍以村落农耕为生，集体耕作带灌溉的轮歇地，并在山地与平原之间转卖山林物产。他们保留着古老的巴陶信仰，崇拜至高神奥邦拉奥里，以西久树为象征；不过也有许多人受到印度教影响，部分加入了阿萨姆毗湿奴派的埃卡沙拉纳信仰。随着科赫王朝的扩张，以及17至18世纪阿洪姆王国加强对阿萨姆西部的控制，博多社群退向林木茂密的喜马拉雅山麓，直到18世纪仍保持迁徙农耕的习惯，游离在国家赋税体系之外。

en: The Boe, better known as the Bororo, a name meaning village courtyard in their language, are a people of central Mato Grosso whose range once stretched into Goias and Bolivia; colonial records distinguish them under many local names, among them the Araes, Coxipone, Araripocone, Coroados and Porrudos. Their Boe Wadaru speech forms its own Bororoan branch within the Macro-Ge family. Jesuit missionaries made the first contacts in the 1600s, and for long afterwards Bororo war parties ranged far on raiding expeditions, with villages binding themselves into wartime alliances. The gold rush that struck Mato Grosso in the 1700s split them into an eastern group, the Coroados of the Sao Lourenco and Garcas rivers, and a western group on the Jauru and Cabacal, which never reunited. Bororo society is built around circular villages of clan houses facing a central court, divided into two exogamous halves of four clans each; descent and clan membership run through the mother, and a husband goes to live in his bride's house. Traditionally hunter-gatherers whose women kept maize and manioc gardens, they hold elaborate naming and initiation rites and funerals that can run for two months.
zh: 博埃人（游戏称博洛洛）即更为人熟知的博罗罗人，“博罗罗”在他们的语言中意为“村落庭院”。他们栖居在马托格罗索中部，活动范围一度延伸到戈亚斯和玻利维亚；殖民文献以阿赖斯、科希波内、阿拉里波科内、科罗阿多斯、普鲁多斯等许多地方名称呼他们的不同支系。他们的博埃瓦达鲁语在大热语系内自成博罗罗语族。17世纪耶稣会传教士最先与他们接触，在此后很长时间里，博罗罗人的战斗队四处远征劫掠，各村落还会结成战时同盟。18世纪马托格罗索掀起淘金热，淘金客的压迫把他们分裂成东支（圣洛伦索河与加尔萨斯河一带的科罗阿多斯人）和西支（雅乌鲁河与卡巴萨尔河一带），两支此后再未合一。博罗罗社会以环形村落为核心，各氏族的房屋面向中央庭院，全村分为两个外婚半族，各含四个氏族；血统和氏族归属随母系，婚后丈夫要住到妻子家中。他们传统上以狩猎采集为生，妇女经营玉米和木薯园圃，并举行繁复的命名礼、成年礼以及可长达两个月的丧葬仪式。

en: The Bohan, also called Bojanes or Mbohanes, were a small Indigenous nation of the eastern bank of the Uruguay River, holding the stretch from the Negro River to the Cuareim River, around the Salto Grande rapids on what became the border of Uruguay and Brazil; some groups crossed into Entre Ríos, where the tribe may have originated. Scholars disagree whether they belonged to the Yaro nucleus or were a branch of the Charrúa, and some link them to the Kaingang and the Jê language family. Before the Charrúa reached their lands they fought with slings, spears, darts and wooden clubs; after merging with the Charrúa they also took up the bow and the boleadoras. The Bohan backed the Charrúa in their wars against the Spaniards, and in 1715 a punitive column of fifteen hundred Guaraní from the Jesuit reduction of Yapeyú, led by Francisco García Piedrabuena, marched against the Charrúa, Bohan and Yaro as far as the Ñancay stream. After the founding of Montevideo the Charrúa advance northward overcame and absorbed them, and the Bohan ceased to be named as a separate people.
zh: 博汉人又称博哈内斯人或姆博汉人，是乌拉圭河东岸的一个小型原住民族群，占据从内格罗河到夸雷姆河的河段，中心在后来成为乌拉圭与巴西边界一带的萨尔托格兰德急流附近；也有一些群体渡水进入恩特雷里奥斯，有人认为那里才是他们的发源地。学者对他们的归属意见不一：或说属于亚鲁斯人的核心群体，或说是查鲁亚人的一支，也有人把他们同坎冈人和热语系联系起来。在查鲁亚人到来之前，他们以投石器、长矛、飞镖和木棍作战；与查鲁亚人融合后，又学会了弓箭和投石索。博汉人曾支持查鲁亚人对西班牙人作战。1715年，弗朗西斯科·加西亚·彼德拉武埃纳率领一千五百名来自耶稣会亚佩尤传教区的瓜拉尼人，对查鲁亚人、博汉人和亚鲁斯人发动惩罚性远征，一直推进到南凯溪。蒙得维的亚建立后，查鲁亚人向北扩张，征服并吸收了博汉人，博汉之名从此不再作为独立民族出现。

en: The Boholano people are the Visayan inhabitants of the island province of Bohol, speaking a distinctive dialect of Cebuano. Their ancestors were the pintados, the tattooed Visayans whose artifacts have been dug up at Mansasa, Dauis and Panglao, and the island takes its name from the pre-colonial polity of Bo-ol. On 16 March 1565 their chieftain Datu Sikatuna sealed a blood compact, the Sandugo, with Miguel López de Legazpi, the first treaty of friendship between Spaniards and Filipinos. Spanish rule and missionary Christianity nonetheless provoked fierce resistance: in 1621 the babaylan Tamblot roused the island's villages in the name of a native diwata before troops from Cebu crushed the rising, and in 1744 Francisco Dagohoy began a rebellion that held the Bohol interior until 1829, the longest revolt in Philippine colonial history. Most Boholanos later became Roman Catholic, while older animist customs persisted beneath the new faith.
zh: 保和人是保和岛省的米沙鄢居民，使用一种有特色的宿务语方言。他们的祖先是有文身习俗的米沙鄢“平塔多斯”，在曼萨萨、道伊斯和邦劳出土的器物可见其文化；岛名来自殖民时代之前的博奥尔政权。1565年3月16日，首领达图·西卡图纳与米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮歃血为盟，即“桑杜戈”血盟，这是西班牙人与菲律宾人之间第一个友好盟约。然而西班牙的统治和传教激起了激烈反抗：1621年，灵媒坦布洛特以本土神灵迪瓦塔的名义号召全岛村庄起事，最终被宿务调来的军队镇压；1744年，弗朗西斯科·达戈霍伊发动起义，据守保和内陆直至1829年，是菲律宾殖民史上持续最久的叛乱。多数保和人后来成为罗马天主教徒，而更古老的万物有灵习俗仍在新信仰之下延续。

en: The Boiken are one of the principal Ndu-speaking peoples of the Sepik basin, living around Boiken Creek in the Yangoru-Saussia District of East Sepik Province and on the small islands off the nearby north coast. Their word for the garamut slit drum, mie, also means tree.
zh: 博伊肯人是塞皮克盆地主要的恩杜语族群之一，住在东塞皮克省扬戈鲁-绍西亚区的博伊肯溪一带以及附近北海岸外的小岛上。他们把加拉穆特裂口鼓称作“米埃”，这个词同时也是“树”的意思。

en: The Bola, also called Bakovi, are an Oceanic-speaking people of West New Britain on the island of New Britain in the Bismarck Archipelago.
zh: 博拉人又称巴科维人，是俾斯麦群岛新不列颠岛西新不列颠省的大洋洲语族群。

en: The Bolghar are the Oghuric Turkic people of the middle Volga and Kama, heirs of the Volga Bulgar state. Their ancestors broke away from Old Great Bulgaria after its fall to the Khazars in 668 and, led by Kotrag, reached the Volga in the eighth century, uniting the region from the late ninth century with their capital at Bolghar. Ruler Almış made Islam the state religion in 922, when the caliph's envoy Ibn Fadlan visited his court, and the country grew rich commanding the Volga trade in furs and slaves between the Baltic, Baghdad and Constantinople; the cities of Bilär, Suar, Qaşan and Cükätaw rivalled the great towns of the Islamic world. Pressure from the princes of Vladimir forced the capital from Bolghar to Bilär, and in 1223 the Bulgars defeated a Mongol vanguard at the Battle of Samara Bend, but the Mongols returned in 1236 and subjugated the country within five years, destroying much of the urban elite. The survivors became subjects of the Golden Horde: their towns were rebuilt as Horde craft and caravan centres, masters were carried off to Sarai, and villagers resettled along the Sviyaga and Kazanka rivers. Through the fourteenth century they kept their Oghur tongue, recorded on Arabic-script gravestones, and by the 1430s their lands formed the core of the new Khanate of Kazan; their language lived on among the Chuvash, the last Oghuric people.
zh: 保加尔人是伏尔加河中游与卡马河流域的乌古尔突厥语民族，为伏尔加保加尔国家的继承者。668年旧大保加尔被可萨汗国攻灭后，其先人在科特拉格率领下西迁，8世纪抵达伏尔加河，9世纪末统一该地区，定都保加尔城。922年，统治者阿尔梅什将伊斯兰教定为国教，哈里发的使节伊本·法德兰当时正出使其宫廷；该国扼守伏尔加商路，经营波罗的海、巴格达与君士坦丁堡之间的毛皮和奴隶贸易，富庶一时，比拉尔、苏瓦尔、卡尚和朱克套等城堪与伊斯兰世界的大都会媲美。弗拉基米尔诸王公的压力迫使都城从保加尔城迁往比拉尔；1223年，保加尔人在萨马拉河曲之战击败蒙古前锋，但蒙古人1236年卷土重来，五年内征服全国，城市精英大半罹难。幸存者沦为金帐汗国属民：城镇被重建为汗国的手工业和商队中心，工匠被掳往撒莱，村民则被重新安置在斯维亚加河与卡赞卡河沿岸。整个14世纪，他们仍保留乌古尔语，留有阿拉伯字母的墓碑铭文；到15世纪30年代，其土地成为新兴喀山汗国的核心，而他们的语言在最后的乌古尔民族楚瓦什人那里延续下来。

en: The Bomassa, or Bamassa, are a Mbenga Pygmy people of the equatorial rainforest around the Sangha River on the Congo-Cameroon border, named after the village of Bomassa. They speak an Ubangian language close to that of the Baka, hunting and gathering and trading with neighboring farmers; like other Mbenga groups they enter the records only in the nineteenth century.
zh: 博马萨（又译巴马萨）是赤道雨林中的一支姆本加俾格米人，因刚果与喀麦隆边境桑加河畔的博马萨村而得名。他们说与巴卡语相近的乌班吉语，在林中狩猎采集并与邻近农人交易；和其他姆本加群体一样，直到19世纪才见于文字记载。

en: The Bonan are a small Mongolic Muslim people of the Hezhou country on the Gansu-Qinghai border, named after the Bao'an garrison built in their old homeland. Their ancestors were Mongol and Central Asian semu soldiers stationed to farm and guard around Tongren in Amdo during the Yuan and early Ming, who stayed when Mongol rule collapsed and intermarried with Hui, Tibetan, Han and Monguor neighbours. Originally Tibetan Buddhists, in 1585 the Ming founded the Bao'an town and garrison there under the Hezhou guard, giving the community its name; in the eighteenth century the Hui Sufi master Ma Laichi won many of them to Islam, and strife with their Tibetan neighbours pushed the Muslim Bonan north to Xunhua. They speak Bonan, an archaic Mongolic language without a script, and use local Mandarin for writing and trade. Farmers of wheat and rye who also raise livestock, they are famed above all as smiths, their folded-steel Bao'an waist knives prized across the northwest; veil colours mark married and unmarried women, while the Buddhist kin they left behind in Tongren kept the same Bonan speech.
zh: 保安人是甘肃、青海交界河州地区人口不多的蒙古语族穆斯林民族，族名得自故乡的保安营。他们的祖先是元代至明初在安多同仁一带驻屯垦守的蒙古人与中亚色目军人，元朝覆亡后留居当地，与回族、藏族、汉族和土族通婚融合。保安人本信藏传佛教，1585年明朝在其地设保安营、筑保安城，隶属河州卫，族名由此而来；18世纪回族苏菲大师马来迟使许多人改奉伊斯兰教，加上与信奉藏传佛教的藏族发生冲突，穆斯林保安人北迁循化。保安语属蒙古语族，保留着古老的蒙古语特征，没有本民族文字，书写和贸易通用当地汉语。他们种植小麦和黑麦、兼养牲畜，尤以锻刀闻名，折叠锻打的保安腰刀畅销西北；女子以头巾颜色区分婚否，而留在同仁仍信佛教的同族则继续使用相同的保安语。

en: The Bontoc are an Austronesian mountain people of the central Cordillera in northern Luzon, occupying the upper Chico River valley around Bontoc, Sadanga and Barlig in the Mountain Province; their name combines words for heap and top and means people of the mountains. They lived in compact village wards of fourteen to fifty houses, with separate dormitories for unmarried men and women, and were stratified into rich, middle and poor classes beneath a hereditary kadangyan elite. Wet-rice terraces, gold panning and headhunting shaped their life: a warrior marked each taken head with the chaklag chest tattoo, and they fought with pin-nang battleaxes and spears to the rhythm of gangsa bronze gongs. Their faith centered on the supreme god Intutungcho and his son Lumawig, the hero who came down from the sky, married a Bontoc girl and taught them irrigation and the crafts, while seers placated the anito spirits of the dead. Spanish expeditions sent against the Cordillera between 1566 and 1665 failed to subdue them, and the major campaign of 1785 left the Bontoc valleys unconquered; through the 1830s they kept their dormitories, peace pacts and rites without colonial rule.
zh: 邦都人是北吕宋中部科迪勒拉山区的南岛语系族群，聚居于高山省邦都、萨丹加和巴利格一带的奇科河上游河谷；族名由意为“堆积”和“顶端”的两个词素组成，即“山巅之民”。他们的村落由十四至五十座房屋组成紧凑村坊，未婚男女各有集体宿舍；社会分富、中、贫三层，之上还有世袭的卡迪安贵族。水稻梯田、淘金和猎头贯穿其生活：战士每取一颗首级，便在胸前刺下查克拉格纹身；他们手持平南战斧和长矛，伴着甘萨铜锣的节奏作战。信仰以至高神因图图乔及其子卢马维格为核心——卢马维格自天降下，娶邦都女子为妻，教会他们灌溉和百工；占卜师则负责安抚死者的阿尼托亡灵。1566年至1665年间，西班牙人多次远征科迪勒拉都未能征服他们，1785年的大规模讨伐也没能拿下邦都河谷；直到1830年代，他们仍在没有殖民统治的情况下保留着集体宿舍、和约与旧有仪式。

en: The Boon-Wurrungi are the Bunurong, a people of the Kulin nation whose coast and hinterland ran from the Werribee River around Port Phillip Bay to Wilsons Promontory, taking in the land where Melbourne now stands. Early settlers called them the Western Port or Port Philip tribe. Their speech is one of the Kulin languages within the Pama-Nyungan family, and their name joins words meaning “no” and “lip” or “speech”. Clans such as the Yalukit-willam moved seasonally between fresh-water camps, spearing eels, fishing and gathering murnong yam daisies, and paddled canoes to French Island to take seals and mutton birds; their dogs were buried with ceremony. They kept a long, bitter feud with the Gunai of Gippsland, whose raids in 1833 and 1834 may have killed sixty or seventy of them and nearly destroyed the Yowengerra clan. First European contact came in 1802, when Lieutenant John Murray’s Lady Nelson exchanged shots with them in Port Phillip Bay, followed weeks later by the peaceful French visit of the Baudin expedition at Western Port; a short-lived convict colony was planted at Sullivan Bay in 1803. In 1835 the elder Derrimut warned the new Melbourne settlers of a planned night attack, and the Boon-Wurrungi entered the colonial era already thinned by feud and disease.
zh: 布恩伍伦人即布努隆人，属库林族群联盟，其海岸与腹地从韦里比河环绕菲利普港湾一直延伸到威尔逊岬，包括今天墨尔本所在的土地，早期移民称他们为西港部落或菲利普港部落。他们的语言是帕马-牛雅语系下库林诸语之一，族名由意为“不”和“唇”或“言语”的两个词合成。亚卢基特-威拉姆等氏族按季节在淡水营地间迁徙，叉捕鳗鱼、捕鱼、采集名为穆尔农的菊芋，还划独木舟到弗伦奇岛猎海豹和鹱；他们的狗会得到仪式性的安葬。他们与吉普斯兰的古奈人长期结怨，1833至1834年古奈人的一次袭击可能杀死了六七十名布恩伍伦人，几乎灭掉约文格拉氏族。欧洲人最早于1802年与他们接触：约翰·默里中尉的“纳尔逊夫人号”在菲利普港湾与他们交火，几周后博丹率领的法国考察队在西港与他们和平会面；1803年英国又在沙利文湾建立了一处短命的流放犯殖民地。1835年，长老德里穆特向墨尔本新来的移民通报了一场计划中的夜袭，而此时的布恩伍伦人已在仇杀和疾病中人数大减，步入殖民时代。

en: The Boruca, also called the Brunca, are a Chibchan-speaking people of the southern Pacific coast of Costa Rica. Before the Spanish arrival their ancestors formed a cluster of chiefdoms that dominated the coast from Quepos to what is now the Panamanian border, including the Osa Peninsula, in the cultural zone between Mesoamerica and the Andes. The people who later carried the Boruca name were a composite group drawn from several neighboring communities, among them the Coto, Quepos and Abubaes. They lived from maize agriculture and were noted for crafts such as back-strap loom weaving and painted balsa-wood masks. Spanish expeditions reached the coast early in the sixteenth century, and in 1524 the territory was incorporated into the Captaincy General of Guatemala. In the colonial period the Danza de los Diablitos, a masked ceremony reenacting indigenous resistance to the conquistadors, became part of their annual life, while their Chibchan tongue gradually gave way to Spanish.
zh: 博鲁卡人又称布伦卡人，是哥斯达黎加南太平洋沿岸讲奇布查语的族群。西班牙人到来之前，他们的祖先组成若干酋长国，控制着从克波斯到今巴拿马边境、包括奥萨半岛在内的海岸地带，地处中美洲与安第斯两大文化区之间。后来以博鲁卡之名见称的人群融合了科托、克波斯、阿武韦斯等多个邻近社群。他们以玉米农业为生，擅长腰织机织布和彩绘轻木面具等工艺。16世纪初西班牙探险队抵达这里的海岸，1524年该地被并入危地马拉都督辖区。殖民时期，重现原住民反抗征服者场景的面具仪式“小魔鬼之舞”成为其每年的重要活动，而他们的奇布查语言则逐渐让位于西班牙语。
