en: The Bosnians are the South Slavic people of the mountainous middle Danube basin, settled from the sixth and seventh centuries when Slavic tribes moved into the former Roman provinces of Dalmatia and Pannonia and mixed with the remaining romanized population. In the twelfth century local lords built the Banate of Bosnia around the valley of the river Bosna, and under the Kotromanić dynasty it absorbed Soli, Usora, Donji Kraji and Zahumlje; Stephen II ruled from 1322 to 1353, and in 1377 Tvrtko I crowned himself king of a Bosnia that stretched to the Adriatic. Medieval Bosnian society was divided among Catholics, Eastern Orthodox and the followers of a native Bosnian Church, whose Krstjani were treated as heretics by both Rome and Constantinople. The Ottoman conquest of 1463 ended the kingdom, and over the following centuries large numbers of Bosnians converted to Islam, giving the region its distinctive mix of Muslim, Orthodox and Catholic communities sharing one Shtokavian speech.
zh: 波斯尼亚人是居住在多瑙河中游山区的南斯拉夫人，6至7世纪斯拉夫部落进入原罗马的达尔马提亚和潘诺尼亚行省，与残留的罗马化居民融合而形成。12世纪，当地王公在博斯纳河谷建立波斯尼亚巴纳特，科特罗马尼奇王朝治下又兼并了索利、乌索拉、下克拉伊和扎胡姆列；斯捷潘二世于1322至1353年在位，1377年特夫尔特科一世加冕为王，波斯尼亚版图一度延伸至亚得里亚海。中世纪波斯尼亚社会分为天主教徒、东正教徒和本土波斯尼亚教会的信徒，后者自称“基督徒”，被罗马和君士坦丁堡双双视为异端。1463年奥斯曼征服终结了王国，此后数个世纪里大量波斯尼亚人改宗伊斯兰教，使这一地区形成共用什托方言却分属穆斯林、东正教和天主教三大社群的独特格局。

en: The Botos, also called Votos and originally named Bocto, were the leading Indigenous people of northern Costa Rica at the time of the conquest, occupying the slopes of the Poas and Barva volcanoes and the plains of the San Carlos and Sarapiqui rivers down toward Lake Nicaragua, with their chief town at Cutris. The Tises and Katapas lived among them as subject groups, and the Guatuso, or Maleku, shared the same lowlands. Their first contact with Spaniards came in 1525, when Hernando de Soto reached a village on the Pocosol River, and in 1528 the scout Diego Mercado described the province of the Botos between the Sarapiqui and San Carlos. Politically fragmented and village-based, they were nonetheless skilled cacao growers who traded their crop along the San Juan, and they acknowledged the overlordship of the Huetar kings of the Central Valley, Garabito and El Guarco, in exchange for marriage ties and mutual defence against the Nahua Nicarao. Their speech may have been Rama, a Chibchan language, which the Huetar fugitives who joined them around 1640 had to learn. Conquest ended their autonomy: in 1569 Governor Perafan de Ribera granted the Botos in encomienda to the town of Aranjuez, and over the following century forced labour and resettlement dissolved their communities, leaving only the name of the Laguna Botos in the crater of Poas.
zh: 博托斯人又称沃托斯人，原名博克托，是征服时代哥斯达黎加北部最重要的原住民，据有波阿斯火山、巴尔瓦火山的山坡以及圣卡洛斯河、萨拉皮基河向尼加拉瓜湖延伸的平原，主城在库特里斯。蒂塞斯人和卡塔帕斯人作为从属群体与他们杂处，瓜图索人（马莱库人）也住在同一片低地。他们与西班牙人的第一次接触在1525年，埃尔南多·德·索托抵达波科索尔河畔的一座村庄；1528年，侦察员迭戈·梅尔卡多记述了萨拉皮基河与圣卡洛斯河之间的博托斯省。博托斯社会政治分散、以村落为单位，却是熟练的可可种植者，沿圣胡安河贩运可可；他们承认中央谷地韦塔尔诸王加拉维托和埃尔瓜尔科的宗主权，以换取联姻和共同抵御纳瓦语族尼卡拉奥人的同盟。他们的语言可能是奇布查语系的拉马语，约1640年投奔他们的韦塔尔难民还不得不学习这种语言。征服终结了他们的自治：1569年总督佩拉凡·德·里韦拉将博托斯人以委托监护制分配给阿兰胡埃斯城，此后一个世纪里，苦役和迁徙瓦解了他们的社群，只有波阿斯火山口的博托斯湖还留着这个名字。

en: The Brahui are a tribal, largely pastoral people of central Balochistan, concentrated in a belt running from the Bolan Pass near Quetta through Kalat down to the Arabian Sea coast, with smaller groups in Afghanistan and Iran. Their language, Brahui, is a northern Dravidian tongue isolated far from the other Dravidian-speaking regions of India; linguists note sound changes it shares with Kurukh and Malto, and most hold that the Brahui are either a relict population from a time when Dravidian speech was more widespread, or migrants who moved north from central India within the last thousand years. Brahui has no script of its own and is written in the Perso-Arabic alphabet. By the seventeenth century Brahui tribes were confederated around Kalat, and in the 1660s their chieftain Ahmad Khan I founded the Khanate of Kalat, ruled by his Ahmadzai line; the state reached its greatest power under Nasir Khan I in the late eighteenth century.
zh: 布拉灰人是以游牧为主的部落族群，主要分布在俾路支斯坦中部一条狭长地带：北起奎达附近的博兰山口，经卡拉特南抵阿拉伯海沿岸，在阿富汗和伊朗也有少量分布。他们使用的布拉灰语属于北达罗毗荼语，远离印度其他达罗毗荼语区；语言学家发现它与库鲁克语、马尔托语有共同的音变，多认为布拉灰人要么是达罗毗荼语分布更广时代留下的孑遗，要么是在近一千年内从印度中部北迁而来。布拉灰语没有本族文字，使用波斯-阿拉伯字母拼写。17世纪时，布拉灰诸部已在卡拉特一带结成联盟；17世纪60年代，首领艾哈迈德汗一世建立卡拉特汗国，由其艾哈迈德扎伊家族世袭，汗国在18世纪末纳西尔汗一世治下达到极盛。

en: The Braji are the people of Braj, the pastoral country on both banks of the Yamuna around Mathura and Vrindavan, south of Delhi, whose name derives from a Sanskrit word for a cattle pasture. Largely Hindu, they include pastoral Yadavs and Ahirs, cultivating Jats and Gujars, and Brahmin and merchant castes, and their country is the legendary childhood land of Krishna, dotted with the pilgrimage sites of Mathura, Gokul, Govardhan and Barsana; Vaishnava sadhus fixed the Braj Yatra pilgrimage circuit there in the sixteenth century. Their tongue, Braj Bhasha, is a conservative central Indo-Aryan language and was one of the two predominant literary languages of north-central India, above all through the blind sixteenth-century poet Surdas, whose Sur Sagar raised it from a village speech into a literary medium for Krishna devotion. In 1337 Braj lay under the Delhi Sultanate, and Timur slaughtered its Jat clansmen on his march of 1397. Under Mughal rule heavy taxation drove the Jats of Mathura to revolt under Gokula in 1669; their uprisings issued in the Jat kingdom of Bharatpur, founded by Badan Singh in 1722 and enlarged by Suraj Mal between 1755 and 1763.
zh: 布拉吉人是布拉杰地区的居民，那是亚穆纳河两岸、以马图拉和沃林达文为中心的牧区，在德里以南，地区名来自梵语中意为牧场的词。居民以印度教徒为主，包括游牧的亚达夫和阿希尔、务农的贾特和古贾尔，以及婆罗门和商人种姓；这里是传说中黑天童年生活的地方，分布着马图拉、戈库尔、戈瓦尔丹、巴尔萨纳等圣地，16世纪的毗湿奴派苦行僧正式定下了布拉杰朝圣路线。他们的语言布拉杰语是保守的中部印度—雅利安语言，曾是印度中北部两大主要文学语言之一，尤其靠16世纪盲诗人苏尔达斯扬名，他的《苏尔诗海》把这种乡野语言提升为赞颂黑天的文学载体。1337年，布拉杰处在德里苏丹国治下，1397年帖木儿进军途中屠杀了当地的贾特人。莫卧儿统治时期，重税逼得马图拉的贾特人在戈古拉领导下于1669年起义；这些起义最终催生了贾特人的婆罗多布尔王国，由巴丹·辛格于1722年建立，又经苏拉杰·马尔在1755至1763年间扩张。

en: The Brandenburgish are the Low German-speaking people of the western marches of Brandenburg: the Altmark, the Magdeburg Börde and the Fläming, country that in the eighth century was held by Slavic Wends such as the Hevelli and the Lutici. King Henry the Fowler subdued the area in 928 and 929, and Emperor Otto I set up the Northern March in 936 and the Archbishopric of Magdeburg in 968, whose prelates led the Christianization and colonization of the Elbe lands, until the Wendish rising of 983 overthrew the march for a century and a half. During the Ostsiedlung, Albert the Bear of the Ascanians retook Brandenburg in 1157 and founded the Margraviate, settling Saxon and Flemish colonists whose Middle Low German speech developed into the Brandenburgish dialect, while the native Wends were gradually absorbed. Magdeburg, an archiepiscopal city and Hanseatic member, gave its town law to hundreds of new settlements. The margraves became prince-electors under the Golden Bull of 1356, and after Ascanian, Wittelsbach and Luxembourg rulers the Hohenzollern Frederick I took over in 1415. Brandenburg accepted the Reformation in 1539, and the Thirty Years' War struck its worst blow when the Catholic League sacked Magdeburg in 1631, killing some twenty-five thousand people. Recovering under the Great Elector, who welcomed Huguenot refugees by the Edict of Potsdam of 1685, the margraviate became the heart of the Prussian kingdom until the Holy Roman Empire dissolved in 1806.
zh: 勃兰登堡人是勃兰登堡西部各边区——阿尔特马克、马格德堡平原和弗莱明一带——讲低地德语的居民；8世纪时这里居住着赫维利人、卢蒂奇人等斯拉夫文德部落。928至929年，捕鸟者亨利国王征服此地；奥托一世于936年设立北方边区，968年又设马格德堡大主教区，历任大主教主导了易北河土地的基督教化与殖民，而983年的文德人大起义使边区统治中断了约一个半世纪。东向殖民时期，阿斯坎尼家族的大熊阿尔布雷希特于1157年收复勃兰登堡并建立藩侯国，迁来萨克森和佛兰德斯移民，他们的中古低地德语逐渐演变为勃兰登堡方言，本地文德人则慢慢被同化。马格德堡既是大主教驻地又是汉萨同盟城市，它的城市法推广到数百座新定居点。1356年的《金玺诏书》确认藩侯为选帝侯；历经阿斯坎尼、维特尔斯巴赫和卢森堡诸家族统治后，霍亨索伦家族的腓特烈一世于1415年接管此地。勃兰登堡于1539年接受宗教改革；三十年战争给它带来最沉重的打击，1631年天主教联盟军队劫掠马格德堡，约两万五千人丧生。此后此地在大选帝侯治下恢复元气，他又以1685年的《波茨坦敕令》接纳胡格诺难民；藩侯国由此成为普鲁士王国的核心，直到1806年神圣罗马帝国解体。

en: The Bretons are a Celtic people of the Armorican peninsula, descended from Britons who crossed from Cornwall and Devon in waves between the third and ninth centuries, most densely around 450 to 600, and gave their new homeland its name of Brittany. Their language, Breton, is a Brittonic tongue closely related to Welsh and Cornish, divided into the four dialects of Leon, Tregor, Cornouaille and Vannes and strongest in the western peninsula called Lower Brittany. The migrant kingdoms of Domnonee, Cornouaille and Bro Waroch coalesced into the Duchy of Brittany around 939, which long balanced between its French and English neighbours; the Breton War of Succession of 1341 to 1364 was fought with English and French backing. The marriage of Duchess Anne to King Charles VIII began the duchy's absorption, and the Estates of Brittany voted union with the French crown in 1532. Breton identity was sustained by the cults of the seven founder saints, parish pardons, the Ankou death folklore and dances to the bombard and bagpipes, even as French made steady ground after 1539.
zh: 布列塔尼人是阿莫里卡半岛的凯尔特民族，先民是3至9世纪间（其中450至600年规模最大）从不列颠的康沃尔和德文渡海迁来的布立吞人，新家园也因他们得名布列塔尼。他们的布列塔尼语属布立吞语支，与威尔士语和康沃尔语亲缘密切，分列昂、特雷戈尔、科尔努阿耶和瓦讷四种方言，在半岛西部的下布列塔尼最为通行。移民建立的多姆诺内、科尔努阿耶和布罗瓦罗克诸王国约在939年整合为布列塔尼公国，长期在法兰西与英格兰之间周旋；1341至1364年的布列塔尼继承战争便由英法两国分别支持交战双方。女公爵安妮与法王查理八世的婚姻开启了公国的并入进程，1532年布列塔尼三级会议投票决定与法兰西王冠联合。此后法语虽在1539年后持续扩张，但七位开教圣徒的崇拜、教区朝圣节、死神安库传说以及风笛与双簧管伴奏的舞蹈，始终维系着布列塔尼人的身份认同。

en: The Bru, or Bruu, whose name means people living in the woods, are a Katuic-speaking Mon-Khmer people scattered along the Annamite Range and the middle Mekong, in what are now southern Laos, north-eastern Thailand and central Vietnam. In Laos their villages cluster around Savannakhet and Thakhek, the lands they occupy in 1337; the Vietnamese know the easternmost branch as the Van Kieu. Researchers trace their ancestors to the Mon-Khmer population that belonged to the Khmer kingdom of Angkor from the 800s to the 1200s, before Thai-speaking polities rose along the Mekong. Bru society is patriarchal, organised around swidden rice fields, hunting and fishing, and its people venerate ancestors, rice and fire spirits; communities farther west also adopted Theravada Buddhism while keeping their older animist rites.
zh: 布鲁人（又称布鲁乌）的族名意为“住在林子里的人”，是说戈都语支孟高棉语的民族，散居在长山山脉和湄公河中游一带，即今天的老挝南部、泰国东北部和越南中部。在老挝，他们的村落集中于沙湾拿吉和他曲一带，也就是1337年时他们居住的地方；最东边的支系被越南人称为云乔。研究者认为，他们的祖先属于9世纪至13世纪吴哥高棉王国治下的孟高棉人群，后来湄公河沿岸泰语政权兴起，形势才发生变化。布鲁人是父系社会，围绕刀耕火种的稻田、狩猎和渔捕组织生活，崇拜祖先、稻灵和火灵；偏西的群落还接受了上座部佛教，同时保留了更古老的万物有灵仪式。

en: The Buandigi are the Bungandidj, whose name means “people of the reeds”, the principal people of the Mount Gambier district on the border of South Australia and Victoria. In 1337 five related dialect groups, of which the Bungandidj clan was the largest, held country from the mouth of the Glenelg River to Rivoli Bay, beside the Ngarrindjerin to the west, the Bindjali and Jardwadjali to the north and the Gunditjmaran to the east. Their Kulinic Pama-Nyungan tongue was called “speech of man”, and society ran on two matrilineal marriage classes, Kumite and Kroke, each split into animal and plant totems whose members might not eat their own totem save in grief. Bands wintered inland and returned to the coast in the warm season to fish, raising mud weirs in the swamps, wicker bird traps and tall platforms from which to spot emu and kangaroo, and sleeping in mud-daubed wurlies more solid than the shepherds' huts that later replaced them. Their first sight of Europeans came in 1822 or 1823, when a ship carried off a woman from Rivoli Bay for three months; Edward Henty's founding of Portland in 1834 opened the pastoral invasion that smallpox and frontier violence made catastrophic.
zh: 布安迪格人即邦甘迪吉人，族名意为“芦苇之人”，是南澳大利亚州与维多利亚州交界甘比尔山地区的主要族群。1337年时，五个亲属方言群体据有从格莱内尔格河口到里沃利湾的土地，其中邦甘迪吉氏族最大；他们西邻纳林杰里人，北邻宾贾利人和贾德瓦贾利人，东邻甘迪特杰马拉人。他们属库林语支的帕马-牛雅语，自称其语言为“人的言语”。社会按母系分为库米特和克罗克两大通婚级别，各自由动物与植物图腾组成，族人非在悲恸之中不得食用自己的图腾。群体冬季在内陆活动，暖季回到海岸捕鱼，在沼泽中筑起泥堰、柳条捕鸟器和用于瞭望鸸鹋与袋鼠的高台，住在涂泥的伍利棚屋里——这种棚屋比后来牧人搭的茅屋还要结实。他们第一次见到欧洲人是在1822或1823年，一艘船从里沃利湾掳走一名妇女达三个月；1834年爱德华·亨蒂建立波特兰，牧地入侵由此开启，天花和边疆暴力随之带来灭顶之灾。

en: The Bubi are the Bantu-speaking indigenous people of Bioko, the volcanic island the Europeans called Fernando Pó, lying off the Cameroon coast in the Gulf of Guinea. Their ancestors crossed from the mainland in several waves, with one tradition placing the main migration in the thirteenth century, and developed in isolation a society of feuding clans speaking the Bube language. The Portuguese navigator Fernão do Pó sighted the island in 1472, and in the seventeenth century Dutch and Portuguese traders ran slave-trading posts on its shores. As slaving intensified, the Bubi abandoned the coast for the safer interior and, under the chief Molambo about 1700, began to gather their clans into a kingdom, carried on by Lorite from 1760 and Lopoa from 1810. Under the Treaty of El Pardo of 1778 Portugal ceded the island to Spain, but the Spanish garrison withdrew by 1780, leaving the Bubi kingdom intact. From 1827 the British leased Port Clarence on the north coast as a base for their anti-slave-trade squadron, while the Bubi rulers kept control of the interior through the 1830s.
zh: 布比人是比奥科岛的原住民，操班图语；这座火山岛位于几内亚湾、紧邻喀麦隆海岸，欧洲人称之为费尔南多波岛。他们的祖先分几波从大陆渡海而来，一种口述传统把主要迁徙定在13世纪；长期的孤立发展使他们形成了氏族相互争战、操布贝语的独特社会。1472年，葡萄牙航海家费尔南多·波首次望见此岛；17世纪，荷兰和葡萄牙商人先后在岛上设立奴隶贸易站。随着贩奴活动加剧，布比人放弃沿海、退守更安全的内陆，并在约1700年首领莫兰博带领下开始把诸氏族联合为王国，其后由1760年继位的洛里特和1810年继位的洛波阿延续。根据1778年的《埃尔帕多条约》，葡萄牙把该岛割让给西班牙，但西班牙驻军到1780年便撤走，布比王国得以保持完整。1827年起，英国租用北海岸的克拉伦斯港作为反奴隶贸易舰队的基地，而布比统治者在整个19世纪30年代仍控制着内陆。

en: The Bugis, who call themselves To Ugi, are the largest Austronesian people of South Sulawesi, farming the rice plains around Lake Tempe and the Walanae valley and trading from ports such as Palopo and Tosora. Between 1200 and 1600 their scattered chiefdoms grew into competing kingdoms, above all Luwu, Bone, Wajo and Soppeng, whose wealth rested on rice and the commerce that flowed through Malacca. In 1590 Bone, Wajo and Soppeng bound themselves in the Tellumpocco'e alliance, or “Three Peaks”, to resist the expanding Makassarese twin kingdom of Gowa-Tallo. Islam reached them through Minangkabau missionaries: the ruler of Luwu converted in February 1605, and after Gowa's Islamic wars of 1608 to 1611 the Bugis kingdoms, including Bone in 1611, were drawn into the new faith while keeping many older customs. When Gowa's hegemony grew unbearable, the Bone prince Arung Palakka allied with the Dutch East India Company; their victory in the Makassar War of 1666 to 1669 and the Treaty of Bongaya left Bone the leading power of the peninsula. From the late seventeenth century Bugis seafarers built a far-flung trading network, settling in Riau, the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Borneo and Sulu and founding dynasties abroad, while their homeland entered a literary golden age built on the ancient La Galigo epic. They speak Basa Ugi, written in the Lontara script.
zh: 布吉人自称 To Ugi，是南苏拉威西人数最多的南岛语系族群，在坦佩湖与瓦拉奈河谷的稻米平原务农，并从帕洛波、托索拉等港口经商。1200至1600年间，他们的零散酋邦发展成相互竞争的王国，最重要的是卢伍、波尼、瓦乔和索彭，财富来自稻米以及经马六甲流转的贸易。1590年，波尼、瓦乔与索彭结成“三峰同盟”，共同抵御望加锡人的戈瓦—塔洛孪生王国扩张。伊斯兰教随米南加保传教士而来：1605年2月卢伍统治者率先改宗，经过戈瓦1608至1611年的“伊斯兰战争”，包括1611年屈服的波尼在内，布吉诸王国都被纳入新信仰，同时保留了许多旧俗。戈瓦的霸权难以忍受，波尼王子阿隆·帕拉卡遂与荷兰东印度公司结盟，在1666至1669年的望加锡战争中获胜，《邦加亚条约》使波尼成为半岛上的首强。17世纪末起，布吉海商建立起庞大的贸易网络，移居廖内、马来半岛、苏门答腊、婆罗洲和苏禄，甚至在海外建立王朝；本土则迎来以古老史诗《拉加利戈》为基础的文学黄金时代。他们的语言布吉语用龙塔拉文字书写。

en: The Bugkalot, long known in older writings as the Ilongot or Ibilao, are an Austronesian people of the southern Sierra Madre and the Caraballo Mountains on the eastern side of Luzon, mainly in what are now Nueva Vizcaya and Nueva Ecija and along the Quirino and Aurora border. They settled along forest rivers, which supplied fish, transport and routes for trade, and lived in stateless communities without chiefs or kings, organized around kin groups and a renowned tradition of headhunting raids tied to grief and the proving of young men. Their mountain country lay across the approaches from the Spanish lowlands: Dominican missionaries entered the upper Cagayan valley from 1607 and founded the first mission settlement in 1609, and a convent was built in 1702 at Burubur at the foot of the Caraballo range. Conquest was slow and bitterly resisted, for the highlanders repeatedly refused Spanish sovereignty and withdrew deeper into the mountains, so that expeditions had to be sent generation after generation; the whole district remained attached to the old province of Cagayan and a separate politico-military province of Nueva Vizcaya was created only in the late 1830s. Their own Bugkalot language is distinct, though most also came to speak Ilocano and Tagalog through contact with the plains.
zh: 布卡洛特人在旧文献中常称伊隆戈特人或伊比劳人，是吕宋岛东部南马德雷山脉南段与卡拉巴略山区的南岛语系民族，主要分布在今新比斯开省、新怡诗夏省以及基里诺省与奥罗拉省交界的山地。他们傍森林河流而居，河流提供鱼获、交通和商路；社会没有酋长和王权，以亲属群为单位，并有著名的猎头习俗——猎头与丧亲之痛及年轻人证明勇气相联系。他们的山区横亘在西班牙人从低地深入的通道上：多明我会传教士自1607年进入上加牙因河谷，1609年建立第一个传教定居点，1702年又在卡拉巴略山麓的布鲁布尔建起修道院。征服进程缓慢且遭到激烈抵抗，山民不断拒绝西班牙的宗主权并退入更深的山林，殖民当局只得一代又一代派兵征讨；整个地区长期隶属旧的加牙因省，直到西班牙统治末期才单独设立军政性质的新比斯开省。他们有自己的布卡洛特语，但在与低地交往中也普遍兼通伊洛卡诺语和他加禄语。

en: The Buka are the people of Buka, a flat, raised-limestone island separated from the northwest coast of much larger Bougainville by the narrow, fast-flowing Buka Passage. Human settlement here reaches back to Paleolithic times, with Kilu Cave showing occupation some thirty thousand years ago, while the present inhabitants trace their languages to the Austronesian expansion of the Lapita culture roughly two and a half thousand years ago. Their Halia tongue is an Austronesian language also spoken on the Selau Peninsula of neighbouring Bougainville, rather than a Papuan one. Outside contact in the early nineteenth century came mainly from whalers: the ship Eliza called at Buka in 1806, beginning decades of visits by British, Australian and American vessels seeking water and provisions.
zh: 布卡人居住在布卡岛上；这是一座地势平坦的抬升石灰岩岛，与面积大得多的布干维尔岛西北岸之间隔着狭窄而湍急的布卡水道。人类在岛上的活动可追溯到旧石器时代，基卢洞穴留有约三万年前的居住痕迹；岛上居民的语言则源自约两千七百年前拉皮塔文化的南岛语族群扩张。他们使用的哈利亚语是南岛语系语言，也通行于邻近布干维尔岛的塞劳半岛，并非巴布亚语言。19世纪初的外来接触主要来自捕鲸船：1806年英国船只伊莱扎号到访布卡，此后数十年间，英国、澳大利亚和美国的船只不断前来补给淡水和物资。

en: The Bukawa are an Austronesian-speaking people of the Huon Gulf coast in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea, in villages from Cape Arkona to Lae and Busama. Their name comes from the village of Bugawac, and their four-dialect language is closely related to Yabem, the church and school lingua franca of the gulf.
zh: 布卡瓦人是巴布亚新几内亚莫罗贝省休恩湾沿岸说南岛语的族群，村落从阿科纳角分布到莱埃和布萨马。他们的名字来自布加瓦克村，其语言分四种方言，与休恩湾教会和学校通用的亚贝姆语关系密切。

en: The Bukidnon, whose Visayan name means highlanders or mountain dwellers and who call themselves Higaonon with the same meaning, are the Austronesian people of the great plateau of north-central Mindanao, above the ports of Cagayan and Iligan and around the Pulangi river and the Kitanglad range. Their language, Binukid, belongs to the Manobo group of Philippine languages, with the dialect of Malaybalay serving as the prestige variety, and their culture is close to that of the Manobo and Talaandig: villages under datu leaders farmed plateau rice fields and forest clearings, raised pigs and buffalo, and kept an animist ritual life of ancestor and nature spirits. For centuries the plateau remained a world apart from the coasts, where Moro fleets raided for slaves through the 1750s, burning villages and selling captives in Maguindanao and Sulu. To answer the raids the Spanish built the stone fort of La Concepcion y del Triunfo at Misamis on Panguil Bay in 1756, and in 1818 Manila reorganized Mindanao into politico-military districts, the Second District of Misamis nominally reaching across the Bukidnon plateau. Spanish authority stopped at the coastal garrisons, however, and the highlanders kept their own datus, fields and beliefs untouched throughout the period, effective colonial administration reaching their settlements only afterward.
zh: 布基农人在米沙鄢语中的名字意为“高地人”或“山民”，他们自称希加奥农，含义相同。这个南岛语系民族居住在棉兰老中北部的大高原上，地处卡加延和伊利甘等港口后方，普朗吉河与基坦格拉德山脉一带。他们的语言比努基德语属于菲律宾语言中的马诺博语组，马来巴莱方言享有标准语地位；文化上与马诺博人和塔兰迪格人相近：村落由“达图”首领治理，在高原稻田和林地上耕作，饲养猪和水牛，保留着敬拜祖灵与自然神灵的万物有灵仪式。数百年来，这片高原与沿海几乎是两个世界：18世纪50年代，摩洛舰队不断沿海掳奴，焚毁村庄，把俘虏卖到马京达瑙和苏禄。为应对袭掠，西班牙人于1756年在潘吉尔湾的米萨米斯修建石堡“康塞普西翁与凯旋堡”；1818年，马尼拉当局把棉兰老划分为若干军政区，第二米萨米斯区在名义上涵盖布基农高原。但西班牙的权威止于沿海驻军，山民在整个这一时期始终保有自己的达图、田地和信仰，殖民行政真正进入他们的聚落还要等到更晚的时候。

en: The Bukiyip, or Mountain Arapesh, are the mountain branch of the Arapesh peoples, living between Yangoru and Maprik in northern East Sepik Province. Their Torricelli-family language is noted for its elaborate noun-class system, with eighteen classes requiring agreement throughout the noun phrase.
zh: 布基伊普人又称山地阿拉佩什人，是阿拉佩什人的山地支系，住在东塞皮克省北部扬戈鲁与马普里克之间。他们的托里切利语族语言以精密的名词类别系统著称，共有18个词类，要求整个名词短语随词类协同变化。

en: The Bulgarians are a South Slavic people forged from the Slavs who settled the Balkans in the sixth and seventh centuries, the older romanized and Hellenized Thracian population, and the Bulgars, a Turkic-speaking steppe confederation whose khan Asparuh founded the First Bulgarian Empire south of the Danube in 681. The Bulgars gradually adopted the Slavic tongue, and the conversion of Boris I to Christianity in 864 opened Bulgaria's golden age: the Preslav and Ohrid schools developed the Cyrillic script and made Old Church Slavonic the literary language of Slavic Europe, while Tsar Simeon I raised the state to rival Byzantium. Byzantine conquest in 1018 ended the first empire, but the uprising of the brothers Asen and Peter restored it in 1185; under Ivan Asen II Bulgaria again stretched from the Adriatic to the Black Sea. In 1337 Tsar Ivan Alexander ruled from Tarnovo, though feudal fragmentation was already splitting the land, and the Ottomans took Tarnovo in 1393 and extinguished the empire by 1396. Under Ottoman rule the Bulgarian church was placed under the Greek patriarchate, yet village life and the Slavic language survived, and the monk Paisius of Hilandar kindled the national revival with his Slavonic-Bulgarian History of 1762.
zh: 保加利亚人是南斯拉夫民族，由6至7世纪定居巴尔干的斯拉夫人、更早的罗马化和希腊化色雷斯人，以及说突厥语的草原部落联盟保加尔人融合而成；681年，保加尔可汗阿斯帕鲁赫在多瑙河以南建立第一保加利亚帝国。保加尔人后来逐渐改用斯拉夫语，864年鲍里斯一世皈依基督教，开启了保加利亚的黄金时代：普雷斯拉夫和奥赫里德学派发展出西里尔字母，使古教会斯拉夫语成为斯拉夫欧洲的书面语言，沙皇西美昂一世更让国家足以与拜占庭抗衡。1018年拜占庭征服终结了第一帝国，但1185年阿森和彼得兄弟起义重建国家；在伊凡·阿森二世治下，保加利亚版图再度从亚得里亚海延伸至黑海。1337年，沙皇伊凡·亚历山大以特尔诺沃为都，但封建割据已使国家趋于分裂；奥斯曼人于1393年攻陷特尔诺沃，1396年帝国灭亡。奥斯曼统治时期，保加利亚教会被置于希腊牧首管辖之下，但乡村生活和斯拉夫语仍然存续；1762年，希兰达修道院的修士帕伊西写成《斯拉夫—保加利亚史》，点燃了民族复兴运动。

en: The Bullom are a West Atlantic people of the low-lying Sierra Leone coast, their name meaning low-lying land; the Bullom Shore runs from Leopard Island to Tagrin Point beside the Sierra Leone River estuary, and related communities also live across the border in Guinea. They speak Bullom languages of the Mel branch, divided into northern Bullom So and the southern Krim and Sherbro dialects, and are closely related to the Kissi. Portuguese navigators already noted them in 1507. In 1545 the Mande invaders called the Mane defeated them in a great battle near Cape Mount and overran their country in the 1540s and 1550s, planting their own chiefdoms among them. During the seventeenth century Temne expansion to the coast split the Bullom: northerners kept their name while gradually assimilating to the Temne and Susu, and southerners came to be counted as Sherbro. At Kaffu Bullom the missionary Nyländer printed a Bullom grammar in 1814, and in 1827 John Macaulay Wilson, son of a local chief, was elected king there.
zh: 布隆人是塞拉利昂低地海岸的大西洋语支族群，族名意为“低洼之地”；布隆海岸濒临大西洋与塞拉利昂河河口，从豹岛延伸到塔格兰角，几内亚边境一带也有亲缘聚落。他们讲梅尔语支的布隆诸语，分为北部的布隆索语和南部的克林、歇尔布罗方言，与基西人关系很近。葡萄牙航海家早在1507年就记载了他们。1545年，被称为马内人的曼德入侵者在芒特角附近大败布隆人，并在16世纪40至50年代席卷其地，在他们中间建立自己的酋长邦。17世纪，泰姆内人向海岸扩张，把布隆人一分为二：北部的一支保留族名，但逐渐融入泰姆内人和苏苏人；南部的一支则被视为歇尔布罗人。在卡富布隆，传教士尼伦德于1814年印行了布隆语语法书；1827年，当地酋长之子约翰·麦考利·威尔逊被推举为国王。

en: The Bulu are the southernmost of the Beti-Pahuin Bantu peoples of the Cameroonian forest, their clans, the Bulu proper of Sangmélima, Ebolowa and Kribi together with the Zaman of the Dja valley and the Yelinda and Yembana of the Nyong, spread across the wooded hills between the Sanaga River and the Gabon border. They speak Bulu, a Beti language intelligible with Ewondo and Fang, and trace their ancestry to Bantu groups who from the 700s drifted south from the central Cameroon grasslands into the equatorial forest, a movement still under way in the early 1800s as related Fang clans pushed on toward Río Muni and Gabon. Bulu society had no kings: patrilineal lineages formed independent villages under clan heads who also led the ancestral rites. Farmers cleared the forest for manioc and maize, hunters supplied bushmeat, and carvers were noted for their masks and work in wood and ivory.
zh: 布鲁人是喀麦隆森林中贝蒂-帕胡因班图诸族里最靠南的一支，其氏族分布在萨纳加河与加蓬边界之间的林木丘陵间：以桑梅利马、埃博洛瓦和克里比为中心的布鲁本部，加上贾河谷地的扎曼人以及尼永河谷地的耶林达人和延巴纳人。他们操贝蒂语组的布鲁语，与埃翁多语和芳语互通；其祖先属于班图群体，从8世纪起由喀麦隆中部草原南下进入赤道森林，到19世纪初这一迁徙仍在继续，与他们亲缘相近的芳人氏族继续向木尼河地区和加蓬推进。布鲁社会没有王权：父系世系组成各自独立的村落，由氏族首领兼管祖先祭祀。农人砍伐森林种植木薯和玉米，猎人提供野味，工匠则以面具以及木器和象牙雕刻闻名。

en: The Bunak, also called Bunaq, are a Papuan people of the mountainous interior of central Timor, their villages straddling the later border between Indonesian West Timor, notably around Lamaknen, and East Timor around Laran. Unlike their Atoni and Tetun neighbors, who speak Malayo-Polynesian languages, their language belongs to the Trans-New Guinea family and shares a common non-Austronesian vocabulary with Fataluku and Makasae, evidence of a proposed Proto-Timor-Papuan tongue. Papuan place names in their heartland suggest that the Bunak descend from the Melanesian settlers who reached Timor around 3000 BC and were already there when Austronesian migrants arrived after 2500 BC. Repeated migrations driven by population pressure and warfare gave their territory its scattered shape. With no tradition of writing, the Bunak preserved history and custom in orally recited verse, and like the southern Tetun they organize society along matrilineal lines. Portuguese influence reached Timor in the sixteenth century, and from the mid-eighteenth century Dutch expansion split the Bunak lands into a western Dutch and an eastern Portuguese sphere, though real power long remained with local traditional rulers.
zh: 布纳克人是帝汶岛中部山区的巴布亚语族群，村落横跨后来印度尼西亚西帝汶（尤以拉马克南一带为中心）与东帝汶（拉兰附近）的分界线。与说马来—波利尼西亚语言的邻族阿托尼人和德顿人不同，布纳克语属跨新几内亚语系，并与法塔卢库语、马卡萨埃语共享一批非南岛语词汇，学者据此构拟出原始帝汶巴布亚语。其腹地的巴布亚语地名表明，布纳克人是约公元前3000年抵达帝汶的美拉尼西亚定居者的后裔，在公元前2500年以后南岛语移民到来之前便已在此生息。人口压力和战乱迫使他们一再迁徙，形成了后来分散的分布格局。布纳克人没有文字传统，历史与规范靠口传韵文记诵，并与南部德顿人一样按母系组织社会。葡萄牙势力在16世纪进入帝汶，18世纪中叶荷兰的扩张又把布纳克人的土地分成西部荷兰与东部葡萄牙两个势力范围，但实际权力长期仍掌握在本地传统首领手中。

en: The Bundeli are the Indo-Aryan people of Bundelkhand, the dry hill country of central India between the Yamuna River and the Vindhya Range, whose main settlements in 1337 included Khajuraho, Konch and Rath. Their language, Bundeli or Bundelkhandi, descends from Sauraseni Apabhramsha and belongs to the Western Hindi group, closely related to Braj Bhasha, and Grierson divided it into four dialect groups. The region, once called Jejakabhukti, was the heartland of the Chandela dynasty, builders of the Khajuraho temples, until the twelfth century; it then passed to the Khangars and from the fourteenth century to the Bundela Rajputs, who gave Bundelkhand its present name. Bundeli bardic verse goes back to the Alha-Khand epic about twelfth-century heroes, while formal written literature developed under Mughal-era patronage, including the poet Kesab Das and works composed at the court of Chhatrasal of Panna. The Bundela states of Orchha, Datia and Panna submitted to the Mughals, although Chhatrasal of Panna rebelled against Aurangzeb and ruled from 1675 to 1731, and in the early nineteenth century they entered British paramountcy as tributary princely states.
zh: 本德尔人是印度中部本德尔肯德地区的印度-雅利安人，这片干旱丘陵地位于亚穆纳河与温迪亚山脉之间，1337年时的主要聚落包括克久拉霍、孔奇和拉斯。他们的语言本德尔语又称本德尔肯德语，由索拉塞尼阿帕布拉姆沙语演变而来，属西印地语支，与布拉杰语关系密切，格里尔森曾将它划分为四个方言群。该地区旧称杰贾布克蒂，12世纪前是修建克久拉霍神庙的昌德拉王朝的核心地带，此后先后归汉加尔人统治，14世纪起又被本德尔拉杰普特人取代，本德尔肯德之名即来自这一氏族。本德尔人的吟游诗歌可追溯到讲述12世纪英雄故事的史诗《阿尔哈汗德》，书面文学则在莫卧儿时期走向繁荣，诗人凯萨布·达斯以及帕纳的查特拉萨尔宫廷都产生了大量作品。奥尔恰、达蒂亚、帕纳等本德尔诸邦曾臣服于莫卧儿，不过帕纳的查特拉萨尔起兵反抗奥朗则布，于1675至1731年在位；19世纪初，这些邦又成为英国宗主权下的纳贡土邦。

en: The Bundjalung are an Aboriginal Australian people of the far north coast of New South Wales and the south-eastern corner of Queensland, their country running from around Grafton north to Beaudesert. They are not one tribe but a nation of more than fifteen related groups, among them the Arakwal, Gidabal and Minjungbal, whose dialects belong to the Yugambeh-Bundjalung language family. Their own traditions trace them to the Three Brothers who came from the sea and landed at Goanna Headland, a place occupied for at least twelve thousand years. Their coast and rivers offered some of the richest hunting and fishing grounds on the continent. In 1770 James Cook mapped the shore in Endeavour, naming Cape Byron and Mount Warning, which the Bundjalung call Wollumbin, and in 1828 Captain Henry Rous sailed into the Richmond River, the first European to explore it.
zh: 邦贾隆人是澳大利亚原住民，居住在新南威尔士州极北海岸与昆士兰州东南角，领地南起格拉夫顿一带，北至博德瑟特。他们并非单一部落，而是由阿拉克瓦尔、吉达巴尔、明琼巴尔等十余个亲缘群体组成的联盟，各方言属于尤甘贝-邦贾隆语系。据他们自己的传说，先祖是渡海而来、在戈阿纳海岬登陆的三兄弟，那片地方至少已有一万两千年的人类居住史。他们的海岸与河流是澳大利亚大陆最丰饶的渔猎场所之一。1770年，詹姆斯·库克驾“奋进号”测绘这段海岸，命名了拜伦角以及邦贾隆人称为沃伦宾的沃宁山；1828年，亨利·劳斯船长驶入里士满河，成为第一个勘探该河的欧洲人。

en: The Bungku, who call themselves To Bungku, live on the southeastern peninsula of Central Sulawesi around the town of Bungku and the Menui Islands, divided into the Lambatu, Epe, Ro'tua, Reta and Wowoni sub-groups. Their coastal polity, the Kingdom of Bungku or Tambuku, was already described as a lively trading settlement by the Spanish explorer Andrés de Urdaneta in 1525. In 1580 Sultan Babullah of Ternate made Bungku his vassal during his eastern Indonesian conquests, though the Gowa Sultanate held the overlordship from 1636 to 1667 before it reverted to Ternate; Bungku named its own king in 1672 and openly rejected Ternatean overlordship in 1689 while keeping a tributary tie. The port grew rich on slaves, iron, spices, tortoiseshell, wax and sea cucumber, with Bugis merchants from Bone and Makassar dominating its shipping, and the iron ore around Lake Matano was contested with the neighbouring Kingdom of Luwu. In the 1830s colonial observers regarded Bungku as the leading port on Sulawesi's eastern coast, while its rulers drew tribute in farm produce from the inland peoples of the mountains.
zh: 朋古人自称“多邦古”，聚居在中苏拉威西东南半岛的朋古镇一带及梅努伊群岛，分为兰巴图、埃佩、罗图阿、雷塔和沃沃尼五个支系。他们的沿海政权朋古王国又称坦布库，1525年西班牙探险家乌尔达内塔就曾把这里记述为繁忙的贸易聚落。1580年，特尔纳特苏丹巴布拉在东征印尼东部时将朋古收为附庸；1636至1667年宗主权转归戈瓦苏丹国，之后又回到特尔纳特手中。朋古于1672年自立国王，1689年公开拒绝特尔纳特的宗主权，仅保留朝贡关系。这座港口靠奴隶、铁器、香料、玳瑁、蜂蜡和海参致富，来自波尼和望加锡的布吉商人主导着航运，马塔诺湖一带的铁矿还与邻国鲁乌王国长期相争。19世纪30年代，殖民观察者已把朋古视为苏拉威西东海岸的首要港口，而其统治者还从山地内陆各族群收取农产品作为贡赋。

en: The Bourguignon are the people of Burgundy, the country of Dijon, Autun and the wooded Morvan hills, whose traditional speech is an Oïl Romance language descended from Vulgar Latin with surviving Gaulish words. The region takes its name from the Burgundians, a Germanic people who settled there in the fifth century and left a notable mark on local vocabulary, while southern dialects along the Saône such as Brionnais-Charolais absorbed Arpitan influence. A Duchy of Burgundy emerged early in the tenth century under Richard the Justiciar and was ruled from 1032 by a cadet line of the Capetians; after that line died out in 1361, the Valois duke Philip the Bold built a great Burgundian state stretching into Flanders and the Low Countries, whose Dutch and Flemish speech enriched the dialect for two centuries. The venture ended when Charles the Bold fell at Nancy in 1477 and King Louis XI annexed the duchy to the French crown, leaving the Netherlands to the Habsburgs. Bourguignon remained the vernacular of town and countryside, though Parisian French increasingly dominated official life in the following centuries.
zh: 勃艮第人生活在以第戎、欧坦和林木茂密的莫尔旺丘陵为中心的勃艮第地区，传统方言勃艮第语属奥依罗曼语，由通俗拉丁语演变而来，保留了少量高卢语词。地区得名于5世纪迁入的日耳曼勃艮第人，他们给当地方言留下了明显的词汇印记；索恩河沿岸的布里奥奈-沙罗莱等南部土语则受到阿尔卑坦语影响。10世纪初，恶人理查建立勃艮第公国，1032年起由卡佩家族的支系统治；1361年该支绝嗣后，瓦卢瓦系的大胆者菲利普以公国为基础，建起一个延伸到佛兰德斯和低地国家的庞大勃艮第国家，此后两百年间荷兰语和弗拉芒语词汇大量进入方言。1477年大胆查理战死于南锡，法王路易十一将公国并入王室领地，低地省份则归入哈布斯堡家族。勃艮第语此后仍是城乡俗语，但巴黎法语在官方生活中的地位日益压过它。

en: The Burji are a Highland East Cushitic-speaking people whose homeland lies south of Lake Chamo in southern Ethiopia, beside the Konso country. Their language carries loanwords from Oromo, Amharic and even Swahili, marking long involvement in the caravan trade between the Ethiopian highlands and the Indian Ocean coast.
zh: 布尔吉人是操高地东库希特语的族群，故乡在埃塞俄比亚南部查莫湖以南、与孔索人地区相邻。他们的语言里有来自奥罗莫语、阿姆哈拉语乃至斯瓦希里语的借词，说明他们长期参与埃塞俄比亚高原与印度洋沿岸之间的商队贸易。

en: The Burmese, or Bamar, are the Tibeto-Burman people of the Irrawaddy valley, whose ancestors moved south from the Yunnan-Tibet borderlands between the seventh and ninth centuries into the Pyu city-states of the central dry zone. They built the Pagan kingdom, which Anawrahta made the first Irrawaddy empire in the 1050s; his conquest of Mon Thaton in 1057 brought Theravada Buddhism and the Mon script from which the Burmese alphabet descends, and the Pyu were gradually absorbed into Bamar society. Mongol invasions ended Pagan in 1287, and in 1337 the Bamar heartland was divided between the rival kingdoms of Pinya and Sagaing, soon merged into Ava, founded in 1364, while the Mon held the south as Hanthawaddy. The long Ava period exhausted itself in wars with the Mon and the Shan, until the Toungoo dynasty, established in 1510, reunited the country: Tabinshwehti took Pegu in 1539 and Bayinnaung, reigning from 1551, built the largest empire Southeast Asia had yet seen, from Manipur and the Shan hills to Ayutthaya. After its collapse around 1599 the Restored Toungoo kings rebuilt a smaller, better-administered realm from Ava, until a Mon rebellion overthrew them in 1752. Alaungpaya then founded the Konbaung dynasty, crushed the Mon in 1757, sacked Ayutthaya in 1767 and annexed Arakan in 1785; the First Anglo-Burmese War of 1824 to 1826 stripped away Arakan, Tenasserim and Assam. Bamar life centers on Buddhist monasteries and the nat spirit cult.
zh: 缅人是伊洛瓦底江流域的藏缅语民族，其先民在7至9世纪间从云南与西藏交界地带南迁，定居在中部干旱区更古老的骠人城邦之间。他们建立了蒲甘王国，阿奴律陀在11世纪50年代将其扩展为伊洛瓦底江流域的第一个帝国；1057年他征服孟人城邦直通，带来了上座部佛教和孟人文字，缅文字母即由此演变而来，骠人也逐渐融入缅人社会。1287年蒙古入侵终结了蒲甘，1337年时缅人腹地分裂为彬牙和实皆两个对立王国，二者不久又被1364年建立的阿瓦王国合并，而南方孟人则以白古王朝自立。漫长的阿瓦时代在与孟人和掸人的战争中耗尽国力，1510年建立的东吁王朝重新统一全国：德彬瑞蒂于1539年攻占勃固，1551年即位的勃印曩更组建起东南亚有史以来最大的帝国，疆域从曼尼普尔和掸邦山地一直延伸到阿瑜陀耶。帝国约1599年崩溃后，东吁后期诸王在阿瓦重建了一个更小但治理更完善的国家，直到1752年孟人起义将其推翻。随后雍籍牙建立贡榜王朝，1757年击灭孟人政权，1767年攻陷阿瑜陀耶，1785年吞并阿拉干；1824至1826年的第一次英缅战争使缅甸丧失阿拉干、丹那沙林和阿萨姆。缅人的社会生活以佛教寺院为中心，上座部佛教之外还保留着纳特神灵崇拜。

en: The Buru, who call themselves Gebfuka or Gebemliar, meaning people of the land, are the principal indigenous people of Buru, the third largest island in the Maluku, divided into the Rana, Masarete, Wae Sama and Fogi groups and speaking a Central Malayo-Polynesian language. The island first appears in written records as Hutan Kadali in the Majapahit eulogy Nagarakretagama of 1365, and in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries it was claimed, only symbolically, by the sultans of Ternate and by Portugal, while Makassar traders built forts there and forced the islanders to grow cloves. A Dutch expedition drove out the Makassar in 1648 and burned their clove trees, and in 1658 the Dutch East India Company raised a fort on Kayeli Bay, relocating some two thousand villagers, including much of the tribal nobility, into thirteen settlements such as Kayeli and Bara to work new clove plantations; from these relocated clans the Kayeli people emerged as the island's loyal elite. After the Company's demise the Dutch crown reorganized Buru into fourteen raja-led regencies in 1824. The Buru kept the cult of the supreme deity Opo Hebe Snulat beneath the later spread of Islam in the north and Protestantism in the south, while farming rice, sago and spices and hunting the Buru babirusa.
zh: 布鲁人自称格布夫卡或格布姆利亚尔，意为‘大地之民’，是马鲁古第三大岛布鲁岛的主体原住民，分为拉纳、马萨雷特、瓦埃萨马和福吉四个支系，使用中部马来—波利尼西亚语族的布鲁语。布鲁岛最早的文字记载见于1365年满者伯夷的颂诗《爪哇史颂》，当时称胡坦·卡达利；16至17世纪，特尔纳特苏丹和葡萄牙都只对该岛提出过象征性的宗主权，真正活跃的是望加锡人，他们在岛上修筑工事，强迫岛民种植丁香。1648年荷兰远征队赶走望加锡人并烧毁丁香树，1658年荷兰东印度公司在卡耶利湾筑堡，把约两千名村民（包括大批部落贵族）迁到卡耶利、巴拉等13个定居点为新丁香园服役；这些迁徙氏族后来融合成卡耶利人，成为岛上效忠公司的精英阶层。公司解散后，荷兰王室于1824年把布鲁划分为14个由拉者统治的土邦。在北方伊斯兰教与南方新教传播的同时，布鲁人仍保留着对至高神奥波·赫贝·斯努拉特的崇拜，他们种植水稻、西谷和香料，猎捕布鲁鹿豚。

en: The Burusho, or Hunzakut, are the people of the Hunza, Nagar and Yasin valleys in the high Karakoram, around the fortresses of Baltit, Altit and Passu. Their Burushaski tongue is a language isolate, unrelated to the Indo-Aryan languages all around it, and they are commonly thought to be descendants of an older population driven into the mountains by the incoming Indo-Aryans. Around 1200 their valleys formed the independent principality of Hunza, whose rulers were first called Thum and later Mir and claimed descent from the soldiers of Alexander the Great; the neighbouring valley of Nagar grew into a sister Burusho kingdom. The Burusho took to Islam, and most of them came to follow its Ismaili branch. From about 1761 the Mir of Hunza recognized the suzerainty of the Qing emperor, sending an annual tribute of gold dust in exchange for silk, tea and porcelain, while his raiders also ranged across the Karakoram into the Kunlun.
zh: 布鲁绍人又称罕扎库特，居住在喀喇昆仑高地的罕萨、纳格尔和亚辛河谷，以巴尔蒂特、阿尔蒂特和帕苏的堡垒为中心。他们讲的布鲁夏斯基语是一种语言孤立语，与周围所有印度-雅利安语言都没有亲缘关系；一般认为他们是更古老居民的后裔，在迁入的印度-雅利安人挤压下退入深山。约1200年，他们的河谷形成独立的罕萨小邦，统治者最初称“苏姆”，后来称“米尔”，并自称是亚历山大大帝麾下士兵的后裔；相邻的纳格尔河谷则发展为姊妹的布鲁绍王国。布鲁绍人后来皈依伊斯兰教，其中多数归入伊斯玛仪派。约从1761年起，罕萨米尔承认清朝皇帝的宗主权，每年进贡金砂，换回丝绸、茶叶和瓷器，而其部众的劫掠活动也越过喀喇昆仑延伸到昆仑山区。

en: The Buruwai, also called Sabakor, are a Papuan people of Buruway District in Kaimana Regency, on Kamrau Bay at the western end of the Bomberai Peninsula. Their language forms the Kamrau Bay, or Sabakor, branch of the Asmat-Kamoro family, a cluster of closely related Trans-New Guinea languages of the southern New Guinea coast.
zh: 布鲁瓦伊人（又称萨巴科尔人）是巴布亚族群，住在邦贝拉伊半岛西端卡姆劳湾畔凯马纳县的布鲁瓦伊区。他们的语言属跨新几内亚语系阿斯马特-卡莫罗语族的卡姆劳湾（萨巴科尔）语支，该语族是新几内亚南岸一批亲缘很近的语言。

en: The Buryats are the northernmost Mongol people, formed around Lake Baikal from Mongolic, Turkic, Tungusic and Samoyedic forest tribes, including the Bayirku and Kurykan of the old Tiele confederation; the name Buriyad first appears in the Secret History of the Mongols, which records Jochi, son of Genghis Khan, marching north in 1207 to subdue them on the Angara, while a Tumad rising in 1217 was crushed by Dorbei the Fierce. In the late 1300s they joined the Oirats against the Eastern Mongols, and by the seventeenth century they were tribute-paying subjects of the Khalkha Tüsheet and Setsen khans, themselves levying sable tribute from Evenk and Samoyed neighbours; their core tribes were the Bulagad, Khori, Ekhired and Khongoodor, herding sheep, cattle and horses in gers. Russian Cossacks entered Transbaikalia in 1609 and reached Lake Baikal in 1643, putting down repeated Buryat revolts, and the treaties of Nerchinsk in 1689 and Kyakhta in 1727 formally transferred both shores of the lake from Mongolia to Russia. Under Russian rule the western Buryats gradually took to agriculture and Orthodoxy, while the eastern Transbaikal Buryats kept the nomadic life and turned to Tibetan Buddhism, whose first local monastery was built after the faith won official recognition in 1741.
zh: 布里亚特是分布最靠北的蒙古语族群，在贝加尔湖周围由蒙古、突厥、通古斯和萨莫耶德等森林部落融合而成，其中包括古老铁勒联盟中的拔野古和骨利干；“布里亚特”一名最早见于《蒙古秘史》，书中记载1207年成吉思汗之子术赤北上征服安加拉河一带的布里亚特人，1217年秃马惕人的起义又被朵儿伯朵黑申镇压。14世纪末，他们加入瓦剌一方对抗东蒙古；到17世纪，他们是向喀尔喀的土谢图汗和车臣汗纳贡的属部，同时又向邻近的鄂温克、萨莫耶德人征收紫貂贡，核心部落有布拉加德、豁里、埃希里德和杭古多尔，住蒙古包游牧，放养羊、牛和马。俄国哥萨克1609年进入外贝加尔，1643年抵达贝加尔湖，平定了布里亚特人的多次反抗；1689年的《尼布楚条约》和1727年的《恰克图条约》正式把贝加尔湖两岸从蒙古划入俄国。入俄之后，湖西的布里亚特人逐渐改事农耕并皈依东正教，湖东外贝加尔的布里亚特人则保持游牧生活，转而信奉藏传佛教；1741年藏传佛教获得俄国官方承认，当地第一座喇嘛寺随之建起。

en: Butonese is a collective name for the related peoples of Buton and the neighbouring islands of Southeast Sulawesi, seafarers and traders whose small vessels sailed throughout the Malay archipelago. Around the 1300s local chiefdoms united at Wolio, the future Baubau, under their first ruler Wa Kaa Kaa, whose husband was said to descend from Majapahit, and the islands had earlier been claimed as Majapahit tributaries in the Negarakertagama and the Palapa oath. The kingdom converted to Islam in the mid-sixteenth century under King La Kilaponto, who took the title Sultan Murhum Kaimuddin, guided by a scholar from Johor and under the influence of Ternate. Buton developed into an unusual constitutional monarchy with its own written constitution, the Murtabat Tujuh, formalized under Sultan La Elangi (1597-1631), complete with legislative, judicial and executive bodies. The walled royal city of Baubau grew into one of the best-fortified centres in the region, its palace fortress the largest of its kind, while Butonese farmers also grew rice, cotton and coconuts. Most Butonese are Muslim, and the Bajau sea nomads are sometimes mistakenly counted among them.
zh: 布敦人是对东南苏拉威西布敦岛及邻近岛屿各相近族群的统称，他们以航海和经商闻名，驾驶小船往来于马来群岛各地。约14世纪初，各地方首领在沃利奥（即后来的巴务巴务）联合，拥戴首位统治者瓦·卡·卡阿，其丈夫据称有满者伯夷血统；而《爪哇史颂》和帕拉帕誓约早已把这些岛屿列为满者伯夷的属邦。16世纪中叶，在柔佛学者的指引和特尔纳特的影响下，国王拉·基拉蓬多改宗伊斯兰教，改称苏丹穆尔胡姆·凯穆丁。布敦随后发展为少见的君主立宪制政权，拥有成文宪法《穆尔塔巴特·图朱》，由苏丹拉·埃兰吉（1597—1631年在位）定型，立法、司法、行政机构齐备。设防坚固的王城巴务巴务是当地最险要的中心之一，其王宫要塞规模冠绝同类；布敦农民也种植水稻、棉花和椰子。布敦人大多信奉伊斯兰教，海上游牧的巴瑶族有时会被误归入其中。

en: The Butuanon people are a Visayan ethnolinguistic group of the Agusan River delta in northeastern Mindanao, heirs to one of the earliest recorded polities in the Philippines. Their Rajahnate of Butuan, named Puduan in Chinese annals, was a gold-mining and trading port whose balangay outrigger boats sailed to China, Champa, Brunei, Srivijaya and Majapahit; a tributary mission reached the Song court in 1001, and a later envoy presented Emperor Zhenzong a memorial engraved on a gold tablet. A Chinese annal records Brunei conquering Butuan in 1304, before the rajahnate regained its freedom. In 1521 the Butuan rajah Siagu attended the first Catholic mass in the Philippines at Limasawa with Ferdinand Magellan's men. Miguel López de Legazpi granted Butuan out as an encomienda in 1571, and a Jesuit mission opened the town's first church in 1597, later handed to Recollect friars, as the old Hindu, Buddhist and animist beliefs gave way to Roman Catholicism. Their Butuanon language is a Southern Visayan tongue close to Surigaonon.
zh: 武端人是棉兰老东北部阿古桑河三角洲的米沙鄢语族群，是菲律宾最早有文字记载的政权之一的继承者。他们的武端拉贾国在中国史籍中称蒲端国，是采金与贸易港口，其巴朗盖支架船远航至中国、占城、文莱、室利佛逝和满者伯夷；1001年，一支朝贡使团抵达宋朝宫廷，后来的使者还向宋真宗进呈刻在金片上的国书。中国史籍记载，文莱于1304年征服武端，此后拉贾国又恢复独立。1521年，武端拉者西亚维在利马萨瓦出席了菲律宾的第一场天主教弥撒，与斐迪南·麦哲伦的部下同行。1571年，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮把武端封为监护征赋地，1597年耶稣会传教站在当地建成第一座教堂，后来移交重整奥斯定会修士，印度教、佛教和万物有灵的旧信仰也逐渐让位于罗马天主教。他们的武端语是南米沙鄢语的一支，与苏里高语相近。

en: The Bwende, or Babwende, are a Bantu people of the Bakongo cluster living on both sides of the border between the two Congos, chiefly north of the Congo River between the Luala and Kenke rivers. They speak Bwende, a language close to Kikongo, and their lands once formed part of the Kingdom of Kongo.
zh: 布文德人是巴刚果族群中的一支班图人，散居在两个刚果边境两侧，主要住在刚果河以北、卢阿拉河与肯凯河之间。他们讲与刚果语相近的布文德语，故土曾是刚果王国的一部分。

en: The Cabécar, who call themselves Kabekwa, are a Chibchan people of the rain-soaked Talamanca mountains of eastern Costa Rica, their settlements running from the Río Coen to the Río Reventazón between Cartago and Limón. They have lived in the region for some three thousand years and, with the closely related Bribri, form the Talamanca branch of the Chibchan family; their elders derive the name Cabécar from kabé, quetzal, and ká, place. Before the conquest they headed the strongest of the Atlantic-facing chiefdoms, gathering several viceítica-speaking groups under its shelter, and Talamanca was the one chiefdom the Spanish never fully overcame, becoming a refuge for peoples fleeing their rule. The seventeenth century brought repeated revolts: Cabécar leaders Guaycorá and Sumamará burned the Spanish town of Santiago de Talamanca in 1610, and in 1709 Comesala joined Pablo Presbere in the largest Indian rising of Costa Rica's colonial history. Living in round, conical-roofed houses and farming rotated clearings of maize, beans and cassava, the Cabécar kept their language and mountain autonomy intact through the rest of the colonial era.
zh: 卡贝卡尔人自称卡贝夸人，是哥斯达黎加东部潮湿的塔拉曼卡山区的奇布查语族群，聚落分布在卡塔戈省与利蒙省之间，从科恩河延伸到雷文塔松河。他们在这一地区已生活约三千年，与关系密切的布里布里人同属奇布查语系的塔拉曼卡分支；据长老解释，卡贝卡尔一名由意为格查尔鸟的卡贝和意为地方的卡两字合成。征服时代以前，他们统领着大西洋沿岸最强大的酋长国，把若干说维塞伊塔语的群体庇护在麾下；塔拉曼卡也是西班牙人唯一未能完全征服的酋长国，成为各族逃避殖民统治的避难所。17世纪起义不断：卡贝卡尔首领瓜伊科拉和苏马拉于1610年焚毁西班牙人的圣地亚哥德塔拉曼卡城；1709年，科梅萨拉又与巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷共同领导了哥斯达黎加殖民史上规模最大的印第安人起义。他们住圆锥形屋顶的圆形房屋，在轮歇的火烧地上种植玉米、菜豆和木薯，在整个殖民时代后期保住了自己的语言和山地自治。

en: The Cabinda culture covers the Kongo-speaking peoples of the forested Atlantic coast between the Chiloango River and the mouth of the Congo, above all the Woyo of Ngoyo and the people of Kakongo, Bakongo groups whose clans also stretch into the neighbouring Republic of the Congo. In the thirteenth century the small state of Vungu in the Mayombe hills led a confederation that included Ngoyo and Kakongo and is regarded as one of the seeds from which the Kingdom of Kongo grew. The Woyo built up the hereditary kingdom of Ngoyo, its ruler titled the Mangoyo, while Kakongo was already named in a Kongo royal title in 1535 and dealt independently with Portuguese, Dutch and English merchants from the 1620s, trading ivory, copper and slaves. By 1700 Cabinda had become the busiest slave port north of Luanda; in 1783 Ngoyo and Kakongo joined forces to destroy a Portuguese fort, but the trade hollowed out these monarchies, and Ngoyo collapsed in the 1830s when its nobles could no longer agree on a king.
zh: 卡宾达文化涵盖希卢安果河到刚果河口之间林木海岸上说刚果语的族群，主要是恩戈约的沃约人和卡孔戈人，他们都属巴刚果人，氏族还延伸到邻近的刚果（布）。13世纪，马永贝山林里的小邦丰古领导着包括恩戈约和卡孔戈在内的联盟，被视为刚果王国的源头之一。沃约人建立了世袭的恩戈约王国，君主称曼戈约；卡孔戈在1535年刚果国王的头衔中已被提及，17世纪20年代起独立与葡萄牙、荷兰和英国商人交易，出口象牙、铜和奴隶。到1700年，卡宾达已成为罗安达以北最繁忙的奴隶贸易港。1783年恩戈约与卡孔戈联手摧毁了一座葡萄牙要塞，但奴隶贸易掏空了这些君主国：19世纪30年代贵族们再也选不出国王，恩戈约就此瓦解。

en: The Caddo are a confederacy of farming peoples of the Southeastern Woodlands, whose towns and hamlets spread over present-day northeastern Texas, western Louisiana, southwestern Arkansas and southeastern Oklahoma. They were the westernmost heirs of the Mississippian world: from about 800 their Caddoan ancestors built flat-topped temple mounds around swept plazas, of which the Spiro Mounds on the Arkansas River are the grandest, and by 1200 extensive maize fields supported dense villages of potters and tattooed farmers. A head priest, the xinesi, tended the sacred fire beside each temple mound, and the people spoke Caddo, a tongue shared with the Wichita and Pawnee. The Great Drought of 1276 to 1299 and the westward migration of Siouan groups such as the Osage and Quapaw, begun about 1200, thinned their northern lands long before Europeans appeared. The Hernando de Soto expedition fought the Tula band in 1541, the Caddo's first recorded meeting with Europeans, and later Franciscan missions made few converts because villagers would not leave their sacred fires. In the early eighteenth century French traders built posts beside Caddo towns, giving rise to Natchitoches and Nacogdoches, while smallpox and measles cut deep into the population. Long courted by Spain, France and then the United States after the Louisiana Purchase of 1803, the Caddo kept their neutrality until the Indian Removal Act of 1830; in 1835 the Kadohadacho confederacy signed a treaty and moved into Texas, then part of Mexico, a land whose own name comes from the Hasinai word for friend.
zh: 卡多人是东南林地的农耕诸部联盟，村镇散布在今得克萨斯东北、路易斯安那西部、阿肯色西南和俄克拉荷马东南一带。他们是密西西比世界最西边的继承者：约800年起，卡多先民在清扫整洁的广场周围修筑平顶神庙土丘，其中阿肯色河畔的斯派罗土丘最为宏大；到1200年，成片的玉米田已能供养人口稠密的村落，村里有制陶匠和文身的农人。大祭司西内西在每座神庙土丘旁守护圣火，居民使用卡多语，与威奇塔人和波尼人的语言同源。1276至1299年的大旱，加上奥塞奇人、夸保人等苏语群体自约1200年起的西迁，早在欧洲人到来前就使他们的北方领地人烟稀疏。1541年，埃尔南多·德索托的探险队与图拉人发生冲突，这是卡多人与欧洲人最早的有据接触；后来方济各会的传教站收获寥寥，因为村民不肯抛下圣火。18世纪初，法国商人在卡多城镇旁设立商栈，纳基托什和纳科多奇斯两城由此兴起，而天花和麻疹也使人口锐减。西班牙、法国以及1803年购得路易斯安那后的美国先后拉拢卡多人，他们一直保持中立，直到1830年《印第安人迁移法》出台；1835年，卡多哈达乔联盟签约迁往当时尚属墨西哥的得克萨斯，而得克萨斯这个名字，正来自哈西奈人意为朋友的词语。

en: The Cahokia were the people of the greatest city of the Mississippian culture, which rose on the Mississippi floodplain opposite the site of present-day Saint Louis from about the year 1050. At its height around 1100 the city held fifteen to twenty thousand inhabitants and roughly one hundred and twenty earthen mounds across six square miles, linked by trade in copper, flint and marine shell from the Great Lakes to the Gulf of Mexico. Its centre was Monks Mound, a four-terraced platform rising thirty metres, the largest pre-Columbian earthwork north of Mexico, crowned by a temple or the ruler's residence; nearby timber circles, called woodhenges, marked the solstices, while the rich burials of Mound 72 display both falcon imagery and the ritual sacrifice of retainers. The city's original name and the precise identity of its people are unrecorded, though linguistic evidence points most strongly to a Dhegiha Siouan-speaking population. Prolonged drought after 1100, river floods, deforestation and political upheaval emptied the city by about 1350, leaving its plazas and mounds to be rediscovered only by later archaeologists.
zh: 卡霍基亚人是密西西比文化最大城市的居民，这座城市约1050年兴起于今圣路易斯隔密西西比河相望的泛滥平原上。1100年前后的鼎盛期，全城约有一万五千至两万居民，在六平方英里范围内分布着约一百二十座土墩，贸易网络以铜、燧石和海贝连接五大湖与墨西哥湾。城市中心是高三十米、分四层台地的僧侣丘，为墨西哥以北最大的前哥伦布时期土方工程，丘顶建有神庙或首领宅邸；附近称木阵的同心圆木桩群用于标示冬至夏至，72号墩的奢华墓葬既有隼鸟形象，也有殉葬侍从的遗迹。城市原名和居民的确切族属都没有文字留存，语言证据最有力地指向一个操德吉哈苏语的人群。1100年后的长期干旱、河水泛滥、森林耗尽和政治动荡使城市在1350年前后沦为空城，只留下广场和土墩，供后世考古学家重新发现。

en: Calima is the archaeological name for a succession of pre-Columbian societies in the warm river valleys of the Valle del Cauca in western Colombia, where settled farming life began with the Ilama culture around 1500 BCE. The Ilama were followed by the Yotoco, who expanded toward the Cauca River and the site of modern Cali, developed polychrome pottery and hammered goldwork, and lasted until about 1200 CE. The Sonso culture then flourished from roughly 800 to 1600, with more centralized chiefdoms and cast gold-and-copper work, so that Sonso-speaking communities were still living in the region when Spanish expeditions reached the valley. The label Calima itself comes from the area where their tombs, terraces and ceramics were excavated, rather than from any people known by that name.
zh: 卡利马是考古学对哥伦比亚西部考卡山谷温暖河谷中一系列前后相继的史前文化的统称。约公元前1500年，伊拉马文化在这里最早进入定居农耕生活；其后的约托科文化把疆域扩展到考卡河与今卡利一带，发展出多彩陶器和锤揲金器，延续到约1200年。接着兴盛的是松索文化，年代约为800至1600年，其酋邦权力更加集中，金器采用金铜合铸工艺，因此当西班牙探险队进入山谷时，这一地区仍生活着松索时期的社群。“卡利马”这个名称本身来自出土墓葬、梯田和陶器的地区名，而不是某个以此自称的民族。

en: The Calusa were a fishing people of Florida's southwest coast, heirs of the Caloosahatchee culture, who built a dense, hierarchical society on estuarine fisheries rather than agriculture. Their capital Calos, probably on Mound Key, ruled a realm stretching from Charlotte Harbor to Marco Island and inland to Lake Okeechobee, with the Mayaimi, Tequesta and Jaega under their influence. They met Juan Ponce de León with war canoes in 1513 and in 1521 drove off his colonizing expedition, inflicting the wound of which he died. In 1566 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded the short-lived mission of San Antón de Carlos among them and married the sister of chief Carlos, whom the Spanish later killed, abandoning the post by 1569. Long isolated after that, the Calusa had no firearms when Creek and Yamasee raiders armed by Carolina began sweeping the peninsula after 1702. Epidemics and slave raids broke their power: the Spanish evacuated 270 survivors to Cuba in 1711, and when Florida passed to Britain in 1763 the last Calusa were removed there, ending their presence in the region.
zh: 卡卢萨人是佛罗里达西南海岸的渔猎族群，承袭卡卢萨哈奇文化，凭借河口渔业而非农业建立起人口稠密、等级分明的社会。他们的都城卡洛斯可能位于芒德岛，辖境从夏洛特港延伸到马科岛，深入内陆的奥基乔比湖，迈米人、特克斯塔人和贾埃加人都受其影响。1513年，他们驾战舟迎击胡安·庞塞·德莱昂；1521年又击退其殖民远征，庞塞·德莱昂本人因伤重而死。1566年，佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯在他们中间建立了短命的圣安东·德·卡洛斯传教站，并娶首领卡洛斯的姐妹为妻；后来西班牙人杀死卡洛斯，于1569年前弃守。此后卡卢萨人长期与外界隔绝，1702年后卡罗来纳武装的克里克人和亚马西人席卷佛罗里达半岛时，他们手中没有火器。瘟疫和奴隶劫掠摧毁了他们的势力：1711年西班牙人将270名幸存者撤往古巴，1763年佛罗里达割让给英国时，最后的卡卢萨人也被迁往古巴，该族群在当地的历史就此终结。

en: The Canta were the highland people of the Chillon valley, north-east of Lima, whose principal stronghold was the hilltop settlement of Cantamarca. Their language was Cauqui, a divergent relative of Jaqaru within the Aymaran family, and the name canta itself meant either a hillside or the cord used to snare vicunas. For generations they lived scattered in village communities in the cold quechua and puna zones above the valley, until the Inca emperor Pachacutec brought the region under Cuzco's rule during his northern campaigns. When the Spanish reached the valley in 1535 they found a prosperous land, and on 8 December 1544 the native communities, including Cantamarca, were forcibly resettled in the new Spanish-style town of Canta to be instructed in the Catholic faith.
zh: 坎塔人是利马东北方奇永河谷的高原居民，主要据点是山顶聚落坎塔马卡。他们使用考基语——艾马拉语系中哈卡鲁语的一支歧异方言；“坎塔”这个词在他们的语言里意为山坡，也指捕捉骆马用的套索。他们世代以村社形式散居在河谷上方寒冷的克丘亚与普纳地带，直到印加君主帕查库特克在北方征战中将这一地区纳入库斯科的统治。1535年西班牙人抵达河谷时，这里已是一片富庶之地；1544年12月8日，包括坎塔马卡在内的原住民村社被强行迁入按西班牙样式新建的坎塔镇，以便接受天主教教化。

en: The Cappadocian Greeks are the Greek-speaking population of Cappadocia, the plateau of central-eastern Anatolia around Nevşehir, Kayseri and Konya. Greek traders and settlers arrived in the wake of Alexander the Great, and under the Hellenistic kings of Cappadocia and later Roman rule Greek became the region's common language, producing figures such as the philosopher Apollonius of Tyana. Cappadocia remained a heartland of Byzantine Christianity, its landscapes dotted with rock-cut churches and underground towns that also served as refuges during raids. After the Byzantine defeat at Manzikert in 1071 the Seljuk Turks overran the plateau and made Konya the capital of their Sultanate of Rum, bringing the Greek population under Turkish rule and making it gradually bilingual. In 1337 Cappadocia was divided among Turkish principalities such as the Karamanids, while Orthodox Greek village communities around Niğde, Aksaray and Nevşehir kept a dialect heavily mixed with Turkish. The Ottoman conquest of the Karamanid lands in the later fifteenth century incorporated them into the empire, yet Cappadocian Greek long remained in use, and Turkish was even written in Greek letters for local religious texts.
zh: 卡帕多西亚人是居住在安纳托利亚中东部高原卡帕多西亚地区（内夫谢希尔、开塞利和科尼亚一带）的说希腊语居民。希腊商人和移民随亚历山大大帝的征服而来，在希腊化的卡帕多西亚王国及后来的罗马统治下，希腊语成为当地通用语，还诞生了提亚纳的阿波罗尼奥斯这样的哲人。卡帕多西亚长期是拜占庭基督教的重镇，遍布岩洞教堂和地下城，后者也在战乱时充当避难所。1071年拜占庭在曼齐刻尔特战败后，塞尔柱突厥人占领高原，以科尼亚为鲁姆苏丹国的都城，希腊居民就此受突厥人统治并逐渐转为双语。1337年时，卡帕多西亚分属卡拉曼等突厥王公，而尼代、阿克萨赖和内夫谢希尔一带信奉东正教的希腊人村落仍保留着混入大量突厥语成分的方言。15世纪后期奥斯曼征服卡拉曼领地后，他们被纳入帝国，但卡帕多西亚希腊语仍长期使用，当地甚至有用希腊字母拼写突厥语来书写宗教文本的传统。

en: The Caquetío were an Arawak-speaking people of the arid coast of northwestern Venezuela, around Coro and the Paraguaná peninsula in Falcón and nearby Lara and Zulia, and of the islands of Aruba, Curaçao and Bonaire just across the water. Hunter-gatherers and fishermen on the mainland, they kept up close ties with island kinsmen, perhaps six hundred of whom lived on Aruba when the Spaniards reached it in 1499. In 1513 the crown declared the three islands useless, and in 1515 some two thousand Caquetío were rounded up and shipped to the mines of Hispaniola; a smaller group was returned in 1526 to cut brazilwood and divi-divi, while refugees from the mainland kept slipping into Aruba between 1529 and 1556. Their language died out by the middle of the sixteenth century. When the Dutch seized Aruba in 1636 they first expelled the natives and then reemployed them as hunters and herders of wild horses and cattle; by the later 1600s the islanders spoke Spanish and were Catholic, and in 1723 about two hundred of them crossed to the mainland to found the town of El Carrizal near Coro. Through deportations, missions and intermarriage the Caquetío were gradually absorbed into the colonial population of Venezuela and the Dutch islands.
zh: 卡克蒂奥人是阿拉瓦克语族群，住在委内瑞拉西北部干旱海岸，即法尔孔州的科罗和帕拉瓜纳半岛及附近的拉腊、苏利亚一带，也住在隔海相望的阿鲁巴、库拉索和博奈尔三岛。大陆上的卡克蒂奥人以狩猎采集和渔捞为生，与岛上的同族保持密切联系；1499年西班牙人抵达阿鲁巴时，岛上约有六百人。1513年西班牙王室宣布这三个岛屿毫无用处，1515年约两千名卡克蒂奥人被围捕并运往伊斯帕尼奥拉的矿山；1526年一小部分人被送回，从事巴西红木和迪维迪维豆的采伐，1529至1556年间又不断有大陆难民逃入阿鲁巴。他们的语言到16世纪中叶已经消亡。1636年荷兰人夺取阿鲁巴，先是驱逐原住民，随后又雇他们猎捕、放牧野马和牛群；到17世纪后期，岛民已改说西班牙语并信奉天主教，1723年约两百人渡海回到大陆，在科罗附近建立了埃尔卡里萨尔镇。在驱逐、传教和通婚之中，卡克蒂奥人逐渐融入委内瑞拉和荷兰诸岛的殖民人口。

en: The Caranqui, also called Cara or Imbaya, were the people of the far northern Ecuadorian sierra, holding the highland valleys and lakes of Imbabura and northern Pichincha from their chiefdoms of Caranqui, Cayambe and Otavalo. Their own tradition traced them to a sea-borne landing on the Bay of Caráquez, and by the tenth century they had moved up the Esmeraldas River into the Andes, where they spoke a Barbacoan tongue and raised the great stepped earthen mounds called tolas, visible at Cochasquí from about 900. Skilled traders, they sat between the Pasto country to the north, the Quitu to the south and the Yumbo lowlands to the west, and their wars and marriage alliances with the Quitu ripened into a military league against the Incas. Túpac Yupanqui broke the league, and a later revolt under Huayna Capac ended at the lake of Yahuarcocha, the blood lake, where the Caranqui and Cayambi were slaughtered after their capital fell. The Spaniards overran the region in 1534; epidemic disease and intermarriage dissolved the tribe within the colonial mestizo population, though its language lived on in local place names.
zh: 卡兰基人又称卡拉人或因巴亚人，是厄瓜多尔最北部高原的居民，据有因巴布拉和皮钦查北部的山谷与湖区，主要酋邦为卡兰基、卡扬贝和奥塔瓦洛。他们的传说称祖先由海上登陆卡拉克斯湾，10世纪时沿埃斯梅拉达斯河上溯进入安第斯山区，使用巴巴科安语族的语言，并建造名为托拉的阶梯形大土墩，约900年起的科查斯基遗址即为其遗存。他们善于经商，北接帕斯多人、南邻基多人、西连云博低地；与基多人的战争和联姻最终演变为共同对抗印加的军事联盟。图帕克·尤潘基击破联盟，后来他们在瓦伊纳·卡帕克治下再度起义，都城失陷后退守湖畔，在亚瓦尔科查（意为血湖）之战中与卡扬贝人一同遭到屠戮。1534年西班牙人征服该地区；疫病和通婚使这个部族消融于殖民时代的梅斯蒂索人口之中，但其语言仍留在当地地名里。

en: The Carentouan take their name from the great palisaded town of Carantouan on the upper North Branch of the Susquehanna, in what became Bradford County near the New York border. In 1615 Samuel de Champlain sent the interpreter Étienne Brûlé to win its people as allies against the Haudenosaunee; Brûlé found a fortified settlement of about four thousand people, with roughly eight hundred warriors, whose houses and palisades resembled those of the Wendat, and Champlain placed the town on his map of 1632. Its name was later glossed as Big Tree. Most historians identify the people of Carantouan with the Susquehannock, called Andaste by the Wendat, who had lived in scattered hamlets along this stretch of the river before drifting south toward Chesapeake Bay. A ruined hilltop earthwork at Spanish Hill in South Waverly, Pennsylvania, is the best-known candidate for the town's site. As part of the Susquehannock nation they shared its seventeenth-century collapse: overwhelmed by the Haudenosaunee in the mid-1670s, besieged on Piscataway Creek in 1675, and absorbed into the Haudenosaunee nations from 1677.
zh: 卡伦图安人得名于萨斯奎哈纳河北支上游的大型栅栏城镇卡伦图安，位置在今纽约州边界一带的布拉福德县。1615年，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰派译员艾蒂安·布吕莱前往争取该镇居民结盟，共同对付霍迪诺肖尼人；布吕莱看到的是一座约有4000居民、近800名战士的设防城镇，房屋和栅栏与温达特人的相似，尚普兰后来把它标在1632年的地图上，其名称后来被解释为“大树”。多数学者把卡伦图安人等同于萨斯奎哈诺克人（温达特人称其为安达斯特人），后者在顺流南迁切萨皮克湾之前，就以分散村落居住在这一段河岸。宾夕法尼亚州南韦弗利的西班牙山山顶有一处早已倾圮的土垒，是该镇遗址最知名的候选地。作为萨斯奎哈诺克民族的一部分，他们也经历了其17世纪的崩溃：17世纪70年代中期被霍迪诺肖尼人击溃，1675年在皮斯卡塔韦溪遭围攻后流散，从1677年起被并入霍迪诺肖尼诸族。

en: The Kalinago, whom Europeans called the Island Caribs, were the warrior people of the Windward Islands, Dominica and the southern Leewards at the coming of Columbus, and gave the Caribbean its name. Long said to be mainland Caribs who had conquered the older Igneri around 1200, they are now understood rather as a fusion of local islanders with smaller groups arriving from South America: their everyday language was the Arawakan tongue inherited from the Igneri, while men also used a Cariban pidgin to mark their mainland ties. Their reputation as raiders was such that the Taíno warned Columbus of them as soon as he arrived in 1492, and they later fought the Spanish alongside the Taíno of Puerto Rico, destroying a Franciscan church at Aguada in 1579. French colonization from 1635 squeezed them island by island; after a failed revolt on Martinique in 1660 the survivors concentrated in Dominica and Saint Vincent. There the Saint Vincent community mixed with escaped Africans to become the Garifuna, or Black Caribs, whom the British transplanted at the end of the eighteenth century to Roatán on the Central American coast, while a Kalinago community held on in Dominica.
zh: 卡利纳戈人被欧洲人称为岛屿加勒比人，是哥伦布时代向风群岛、多米尼加和小安的列斯南部的尚武族群，加勒比海的名字便得自他们。旧说认为他们是约1200年前后征服了先住民伊涅里人的大陆加勒比人，后世学界则倾向于认为，他们是本地岛民与南美洲新来的小群体融合的产物：日常使用的是承自伊涅里人的阿拉瓦克语，男子另讲一种加勒比语混合语，以示与大陆的渊源。他们以袭掠闻名，1492年哥伦布一到，泰诺人便向他警告这些强敌；后来他们还与波多黎各的泰诺人联手对抗西班牙，于1579年捣毁了阿瓜达的方济各会教堂。1635年起法国的殖民把他们逐岛压缩，1660年马提尼克起义失败后，残部聚集到多米尼加和圣文森特。圣文森特一支后来与逃亡的非洲人融合，形成加里富纳人（即黑加勒比人），18世纪末被英国迁往中美洲海岸外的罗阿坦岛；多米尼加的卡利纳戈社群则延续了下来。

en: The Casma were the people of a chain of coastal valleys in northern Peru, from the Culebras valley in the south through the Casma valley to the Chao valley, a stretch of coast about three hundred kilometres long. Their pottery appears in the archaeological record from around 700 CE, and they reoccupied and remodelled older Moche centres such as Panamarca in the Nepeña valley and El Castillo in the Santa valley, while walls at Santa and Nepena guarded their frontiers. Between 1000 and 1290 their confederation reached its greatest extent, ruled from the administrative centre of El Purgatorio in the Casma valley, with other major towns at Cerro la Cruz and Ten Ten. Expansion then brought them up against the Chimu Empire: the Punta Lobos massacre has been interpreted as a sacrifice connected with that conquest, and after a final war at the end of the fourteenth century the Casma state disappeared. At Manchan, Chimu and Casma building styles appear together, showing that Casma communities lived on under Chimu rule.
zh: 卡斯马人聚居于秘鲁北部一连串沿海河谷，南起库莱布拉斯河谷，中经卡斯马河谷，北抵乔河谷，沿海岸绵延约三百公里。他们的陶器约在700年前后出现在考古记录中，他们还重新占据并改造了内佩尼亚河谷的帕尼亚马卡、圣塔河谷的埃尔卡斯蒂略等更早的莫切遗址，并在圣塔和内佩尼亚修筑城墙守卫边界。1000至1290年间，卡斯马联盟达到极盛，以卡斯马河谷的行政中心埃尔普加托里奥为首府，塞罗拉克鲁斯和腾腾也是重要城镇。此后扩张把他们推向奇穆帝国：蓬塔洛沃斯屠杀被认为与这场征服有关，经过14世纪末的最后一场战争，卡斯马邦国灭亡。在曼昌，奇穆与卡斯马的建筑风格并存，说明卡斯马社群在奇穆统治下延续了下来。

en: The Castilians are the people of the high northern Meseta, around Burgos and Segovia, whose Romance vernacular grew from the Vulgar Latin brought to the peninsula after 210 BC; the first written traces of Castilian appear in ninth-century glosses on Latin manuscripts. Their land began as a county of the kingdom of León and became a kingdom itself in the 1000s, and after Ferdinand III united Castile and León in 1230 his crown carried the Reconquista down the Guadalquivir to Córdoba and Seville. Toledo, taken from the Muslims in 1085, became the forge of the written standard, where in the 1200s the royal chancery turned the Burgos dialect into the language of law and learning, enriched by thousands of Arabic words absorbed through Mozarabic speech; from the 1570s Madrid took Toledo's place. The marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand in 1469 joined Castile to Aragon, and the fall of Granada in 1492, the same year Columbus sailed under the Castilian flag, opened an American empire that carried Castilian across the Atlantic, while Antonio de Nebrija printed at Salamanca the first grammar of any modern European language. Cervantes's Don Quixote later gave its name to the language of that empire, and the Nueva Planta decrees of 1716 made Castilian the official Spanish of a centralized monarchy.
zh: 卡斯蒂利亚人是北部高原梅塞塔的居民，聚居于布尔戈斯、塞戈维亚一带；他们的罗曼语方言源自公元前210年后罗马人带到半岛的通俗拉丁语，现存最早的卡斯蒂利亚语痕迹见于9世纪拉丁文抄本的注释。这片土地原是莱昂王国的伯爵领，11世纪成为独立王国；1230年费尔南多三世合并卡斯蒂利亚与莱昂后，王权沿收复失地运动南下，沿瓜达尔基维尔河一直打到科尔多瓦和塞维利亚。1085年从穆斯林手中夺取的托莱多成为书面标准的熔炉：13世纪，王室文书处把布尔戈斯方言锤炼成法律与学术语言，并经莫扎拉布口语吸收了数以千计的阿拉伯语借词；1570年代起，马德里取代了托莱多的地位。1469年伊莎贝拉与费尔南多联姻，卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡合流；1492年格拉纳达陷落，同年哥伦布挂卡斯蒂利亚旗帜出航，开启了把卡斯蒂利亚语带过大西洋的美洲帝国，安东尼奥·德·内布里哈也在萨拉曼卡印出了近代欧洲语言的第一部语法书。后来塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》为这门帝国语言赢得了‘塞万提斯的语言’之名；1716年的《新基本法令》则使卡斯蒂利亚语成为中央集权君主制下的官方西班牙语。

en: The Cataguá, also called Cataguases, were a non-Tupi people of the Brazilian interior and the most numerous indigenous group in the lands that became Minas Gerais; their grip on the central, western and southern grasslands was such that the bandeirantes called the region the Campos Gerais dos Cataguases, the Country of the Cataguá. Moving north from southern Brazil, they defeated the Tupi-speaking Carijó and occupied much of their territory, earning fame as formidable warriors, and Portuguese settlers accused them, perhaps unjustly, of devouring war captives. When the Portuguese crown turned against them around 1670, paulista bandeirantes marched in to enslave or exterminate: Fernão Dias Paes Leme led some six hundred men into their lands, and Lourenço Castanho Taques is credited with breaking their power in a campaign remembered as a genocide. The surviving bands were absorbed or displaced by the gold rush that soon filled Minas Gerais with miners, and the town of Cataguases still keeps their name.
zh: 卡塔瓜人又称卡塔瓜塞斯人，是巴西内陆的非图皮族群，也是后来米纳斯吉拉斯一带人数最多的原住民；他们控制着中部、西部和南部的草原，旗兵们遂把那片地区称为卡塔瓜旷野，即卡塔瓜之地。他们从巴西南部北上，击败了说图皮语的卡里若人，占据其大片土地，以能征善战著称，葡萄牙殖民者还指控他们吞食战俘，这一罪名未必属实。约1670年，葡萄牙王室决定对他们用兵，圣保罗旗兵随之进山，意在掳人为奴或加以剿灭：费尔南·迪亚斯·帕伊斯·莱梅率约六百人攻入其地，最后由洛伦索·卡斯塔尼奥·塔克斯将他们击溃，这场行动被后世视为种族灭绝。残余群体或被同化，或被随后涌入米纳斯吉拉斯的淘金潮排挤流散，今卡塔瓜塞斯镇仍留存着他们的名字。

en: The Catalans are the people of the eastern Pyrenees and the Mediterranean littoral of the peninsula, whose Romance speech evolved from Vulgar Latin on both sides of the mountains by the 800s and slowly diverged from Old Occitan between the 1000s and the 1300s. Their counts pushed south against Muslim rule from the 700s, and when the County of Barcelona broke from the Carolingian Empire in 988 it became the heart of an expanding principality; nearly pure Catalan documents survive from 1080, and the conquests of the 1200s carried the language into the new kingdoms of Valencia and Majorca and, in the 1300s, to Alghero in Sardinia. The later Middle Ages were its golden age: Ramon Llull of Majorca, who died in 1315, wrote philosophy, science and fiction in Catalan, the Four Great Chronicles recorded the kings of Aragon, and the royal chancery forged a standardized tongue that served as an official language of Sicily and Sardinia; Martorell's chivalric romance Tirant lo Blanc appeared in 1490, and the first movable-type book printed on the peninsula was Catalan. After the union with Castile in 1479 the court turned to Spanish, and the Nueva Planta decrees of 1714 imposed Castilian in law and administration, while the Treaty of the Pyrenees in 1659 had already left the Catalans of Roussillon under France, whose revolution proscribed their language after 1789.
zh: 加泰罗尼亚人聚居于比利牛斯山东段及半岛地中海沿岸，他们的罗曼语在9世纪时已在山脉两侧从通俗拉丁语中演化成形，并在11至14世纪间与古奥克语逐渐分化。从8世纪起，各地伯爵向南扩张，蚕食穆斯林土地；988年巴塞罗那伯国脱离加洛林帝国，成为日益壮大的公国核心。接近纯加泰罗尼亚语的文书在1080年已经出现，13世纪的征服把这门语言带到新建立的瓦伦西亚王国和马略卡王国，14世纪又传到撒丁岛上的阿尔盖罗。中世纪后期是它的黄金时代：1315年去世的马略卡人拉蒙·柳利用加泰罗尼亚语撰写哲学、科学和小说，《四大编年史》记录了阿拉贡列王，王室文书处则打造出标准化的书面语，一度成为西西里和撒丁的官方语言；1490年，马托雷利的骑士传奇《骑士蒂朗》问世，半岛上第一本活字印刷书也是用加泰罗尼亚语印成的。1479年与卡斯蒂利亚联合后，宫廷转而使用西班牙语，1714年的《新基本法令》在法律和行政中强制推行卡斯蒂利亚语；而早在1659年，《比利牛斯条约》已把鲁西永的加泰罗尼亚人划归法国，法国大革命后他们的语言也在1789年遭到禁用。

en: The Iswa, 'people of the river' in their own Siouan tongue, were the people Europeans called the Catawba, the dominant power of the Carolina Piedmont along the river that now bears their name. Their country had earlier held Mississippian chiefdoms such as Joara, visited by Hernando de Soto in 1540 and by Juan Pardo, who built Fort San Juan there in 1567 before the garrison was wiped out a year later. As English settlement spread, the Iswa absorbed many dwindling neighboring bands and fought long contests with the Seneca, Lenape and Shawnee over hunting grounds, and with the Cherokee over their mountain border; colonists brokered talks at Albany in 1721 and the Treaty of Lancaster in 1744. Smallpox struck hard in 1738 and again in 1759, when it killed nearly half the nation, and a Shawnee party slew their chief King Hagler in 1763. South Carolina confirmed a reservation for them on the Catawba River the same year. They sided with the American colonists in the Revolutionary War, fleeing to Virginia when British troops reached their towns in 1780 and returning after Guilford Court House to resettle their reduced lands.
zh: 伊斯瓦人在自己的苏语中意为‘河之人’，欧洲人称之为卡托巴人，是卡罗来纳皮德蒙特的强族，沿后来以他们得名的卡托巴河而居。他们的土地上曾有约阿拉这样的密西西比文化酋邦：1540年埃尔南多·德索托到访此地，1567年胡安·帕尔多又在那里修建圣胡安堡，一年后驻军便被当地人消灭。随着英国定居者扩张，伊斯瓦人吸纳了许多日渐衰微的邻近部族，并为争夺猎场与塞内卡人、特拉华人和肖尼人长期交战，又在山区边界与切罗基人相争；殖民当局先后在1721年的奥尔巴尼会议和1744年的《兰开斯特条约》中斡旋议和。天花在1738年重创新部，1759年的瘟疫又夺去近半人口；1763年肖尼人杀死了他们的酋长黑格勒王。同年南卡罗来纳在卡托巴河畔为他们划定保留地。独立战争中他们站在美国殖民者一边，1780年英军逼近其城镇时暂避弗吉尼亚，吉尔福德法院之战后返回，在已大为缩小的土地上重新定居。

en: The Caxcan were a partly sedentary, partly nomadic people of the southern Sierra Madre, holding what is now southern Zacatecas and northern Jalisco, with chief towns at Teul, Tlaltenango, Juchipila and Teocaltiche. They lived in competing city-states under elected tlatoani and spoke a Uto-Aztecan tongue often described as an old variant of Nahuatl. In 1540 their leader Tenamaztle led them into the Mixtón Rebellion beside the Zacatecos; Spanish accounts called the Caxcan the heart of the rising, which was nevertheless crushed in 1542. They then made peace and, unlike their former allies, fought on the Spanish side through the Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590, which exposed them to raids by Zacateco and Guachichil bands. Warfare, epidemics and intermarriage over the following colonial centuries gradually merged most Caxcan communities into the mestizo population of Zacatecas and Jalisco.
zh: 卡什坎人是半定居、半游牧的族群，活动在西马德雷山脉南段，即今萨卡特卡斯州南部和哈利斯科州北部，主要城镇有特乌尔、特拉尔特南戈、胡奇皮拉和特奥卡尔蒂切。他们分成相互竞争的城邦，由推举产生的特拉托阿尼统治，说一种犹他—阿兹特克语，常被视为纳瓦特尔语的古老变体。1540年，首领特尼亚马孙特尔率他们与萨卡特科人一同加入米斯通起义；西班牙人的记载把卡什坎人称为起义的心脏，但起义仍在1542年被镇压。此后他们议和，并在1550至1590年的奇奇梅克战争中站在西班牙一方，与旧盟友反目，因而屡遭萨卡特科和瓜奇奇尔游帮袭击。在随后的殖民世纪里，战争、疫病和通婚逐渐把大多数卡什坎社区融入萨卡特卡斯与哈利斯科的混血人口。

en: The Cayas were the people of a province on the river that the Spaniards called the River of the Cayas, since identified with the Arkansas River, when the Hernando de Soto expedition reached it in 1541. Its town of Tanico was inhabited by salt-makers who scooped salty river sand into baskets, rinsed it into brine and evaporated the brine in shallow bowls, trading the salt across the Mississippi valley; the name Tanico was later applied to the Tunica, whose language is regarded as an isolate, and linguists count the Cayas among the Tunican chiefdoms of the Mississippian world of maize fields, palisaded towns and temple mounds. The Spanish visit was followed by epidemics and a century and a half of silence, and when French travelers came down the Mississippi in 1682 the Tunica had abandoned the Arkansas country for the mouth of the Yazoo River, their old lands sparsely held by the Siouan-speaking Quapaw. A French mission was set up among them around 1700, and they prospered as salt and horse middlemen, trading with the Caddoan villages to the west. Under pressure from Chickasaw wars and Anglo-American settlement they moved again, to the lower Mississippi in 1731 and to the Red River in Louisiana by the 1790s, where an American commissioner found only about twenty-five Tunica men in 1806.
zh: 1541年埃尔南多·德索托的远征队抵达卡亚斯，这是西班牙人所称卡亚斯河——今阿肯色河——畔的一个省份。省内的塔尼科镇以制盐为生：居民把含盐的河沙舀进篮子，淋出卤水，再用浅碗蒸发成盐，销往整个密西西比河谷；塔尼科这个名字后来也用来称呼图尼卡人，而图尼卡语被视为孤立语，语言学家把卡亚斯归入密西西比文化圈的图尼卡语酋邦，那个世界里遍布玉米田、栅寨城镇和神庙土丘。西班牙人离去后瘟疫接踵而来，此后是一个半世纪的沉寂；1682年法国旅行者顺密西西比河而下时，图尼卡人已放弃阿肯色故地迁到亚祖河口，旧地由讲苏语的夸保人稀疏占据。约1700年，法国人在他们中间设立传教站，图尼卡人充当食盐和马匹的中间商，与西边的卡多语村镇贸易而兴盛。在奇克索战争和英美移民的压力下他们再度迁徙：1731年移到密西西比河下游，1790年代又迁到路易斯安那的雷德河；1806年一名美国专员在那里清点到的图尼卡男子只剩约二十五人。

en: The Cayubaba are an indigenous people of the Bolivian Amazon, native to the historic Mojos plains of the Beni, west of the Mamoré River and north of Santa Ana del Yacuma, where they lived in large village communities of farmers, hunters and fishermen who took fish with woven basket traps. Their own Cayubaba tongue is a linguistic isolate, with no demonstrated relatives. The first European to enter their territory was the Jesuit Agustín Zapata in 1693, who counted seven villages, six of them holding some eighteen hundred people each and one more than two thousand. In 1704 Father Antonio Garriga gathered them into the mission of Exaltación de la Santa Cruz, and the further foundations of San Carlos, Concepción and Las Peñas merged the once numerous Cayubaba into the settled mission world of eighteenth-century Mojos, alongside the Movima and other peoples of the Beni.
zh: 卡尤巴巴人是玻利维亚亚马孙的原住民，世居贝尼地区历史上的莫霍斯平原，在马莫雷河以西、亚库马的圣安娜以北，以大型村落聚居，务农、狩猎、捕鱼，捕鱼时使用编织的篮篓陷阱。他们本族的卡尤巴巴语是一门孤立语言，没有确定的亲属语言。1693年，耶稣会士阿古斯丁·萨帕塔第一个进入他们的领地，清点出七座村庄，其中六座各有约一千八百人，另一座超过两千人。1704年，安东尼奥·加里加神父把他们并入举扬圣十字传教站；此后圣卡洛斯、康塞普西翁、拉斯佩尼亚斯等传教站相继建立，把人口一度众多的卡尤巴巴人纳入18世纪莫霍斯的定居传教世界，与莫维马等贝尼各族群共处。

en: The Cebuano people are the largest Visayan subgroup, native to Cebu and spread across Bohol, Negros Oriental, western Leyte and much of Mindanao. Chinese records of 1225 already mention their island port under the name Suwu, and Visayan tradition traces its rajahnate to Sri Lumay, a half-Malay, half-Tamil settler from Sumatra; the name Sugbu, later rendered Cebu, refers to the scorched-earth fires lit against slave raiders. Under Rajah Humabon the port traded with Japan, Siam, India and China, and in 1521 Ferdinand Magellan's expedition arrived, only for Magellan to be killed at the Battle of Mactan by the forces of Lapulapu. Humabon's household became the first Filipinos baptized as Christians, while the Spanish called these tattooed islanders pintados. In 1565 Miguel López de Legazpi overthrew Rajah Tupas and made Cebu the first Spanish settlement in the archipelago, and Cebuano auxiliaries marched with the Spaniards at the conquest of Manila in 1571. Native and Catholic devotion later met in the Sinulog festival of Cebu.
zh: 宿务人是米沙鄢人中最大的支系，原居于宿务，后扩散到保和、东内格罗斯、莱特西部和棉兰老的大片地区。1225年的中国文献已把他们的海岛港口记作束务；米沙鄢传说将其拉贾政权的建立归于来自苏门答腊、兼具马来与泰米尔血统的斯里·卢迈，苏格布一名——后来演变为宿务——源自抵御掳奴者时点燃的焦土之火。在拉者胡马邦治下，该港与日本、暹罗、印度和中国贸易；1521年斐迪南·麦哲伦的船队到此，麦哲伦本人却在麦克坦战役中被拉普拉普的部众击杀。胡马邦的家眷成为最早受洗的菲律宾基督徒，西班牙人则把这些有文身习俗的岛民称为“平塔多斯”。1565年，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮推翻拉者图帕斯，把宿务建成西班牙人在群岛的第一个据点，宿务辅兵又随西班牙人参加了1571年征服马尼拉的战事。本土信仰与天主教虔敬后来交融于宿务的仙奴诺节。

en: The Chyemdal are an Evenki clan band of the Nepa and Tokma river country in the Katanga taiga, the basin of the Lower Tunguska west of the Lena, living as nomadic reindeer herders and hunters. The Russian advance of the seventeenth century reached this district through its river routes and placed its Evenki clans under Cossack fur-tax administration.
zh: 切姆达尔人是卡坦加泰加林里涅帕河与托克马河一带的鄂温克氏族游群，位于勒拿河以西的下通古斯卡河流域，以游牧养鹿和狩猎为生。17世纪俄国势力沿水路进入这一地区，将当地鄂温克氏族置于哥萨克毛皮税管理之下。

en: The Cemuhi are the Kanak clans of the north-east coast of Grande Terre in New Caledonia, whose Cèmuhî language, also recorded as Camuhi, Camuki, Tyamuhi or Wagap after the coastal district of Wagap, is spoken around Touho, Koné and Poindimié within the Paici-Camuki customary area. Together with Paicî it forms the central-northern group of the New Caledonian languages, remote descendants of the Austronesian speech carried there by Lapita settlers after 1100 BC. Cèmuhî is a tone language in which three pitch registers distinguish words otherwise sounded alike, so that everyday speech carries something of the melodic precision of a chant. Cemuhi society turned on clans and hereditary chiefs, taro irrigation in the steep valleys and sea fishing from outrigger canoes, while the chief's great house and its rooftop carving linked the living to the ancestors. James Cook noted the Grande Terre coast in 1774, yet the steep mountains behind it kept Cemuhi villages effectively beyond European reach through the whole period to 1837.
zh: 塞穆希人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛东北沿海的卡纳克氏族群体，其塞穆希语又因沿海的瓦加普地区而被记作瓦加普语等名称，通行于帕伊西-卡穆基习俗区内的图奥、科内和普安迪米耶一带。它与派西语共同组成新喀里多尼亚语的中北部语组，是公元前1100年以后拉皮塔定居者带来的南岛语的遥远后裔。塞穆希语是声调语言，三个音高层级可以区分发音相同的词，因此日常言语也带着几分吟唱般精准的旋律。塞穆希社会以氏族和世袭酋长为核心，在陡峭山谷中灌溉芋头，驾舷外架独木舟出海捕鱼；酋长的大屋及其屋顶雕饰则连接着生者与祖先。詹姆斯·库克于1774年记录了格朗德特尔岛海岸，但沿海背后的崇山峻岭使塞穆希村落实际上处于欧洲人势力之外，这种情形一直延续到1837年。

en: The Chaima are an Indigenous people of eastern Venezuela, whose villages once spread across the country that became the states of Monagas, Anzoátegui and Sucre, around Maturín and the Cumaná coast. They spoke Chaima, a Cariban tongue of the Itoto Majun group related to Cumanagoto and Tamanaco and close to Pemón and Yukpa. After the Spanish conquest many Chaima were gathered into Capuchin missions, notably around Caripe, and by the late eighteenth century nearly all of the roughly fifteen thousand Indians in the Capuchin missions of northeastern Venezuela were Chaima; one of their number is said to have led a multi-tribal rising against the Spaniards. Alexander von Humboldt, who visited them around 1800, described their stature and customs in his travel narrative. Chaima was still in everyday use in the early nineteenth century and had been one of the three most widely spoken Indigenous languages of the province of Cumaná and Barcelona, but it then declined and did not survive as a community language.
zh: 柴马人是委内瑞拉东部的原住民，村落曾分布在后来成为莫纳加斯州、安索阿特吉州和苏克雷州的地区，即马图林与库马纳海岸一带。他们使用柴马语，属加勒比语系的伊托托—马洪语群，与库马纳戈托语、塔马纳科语有亲缘关系，并与佩蒙语和尤克帕语相近。西班牙征服后，许多柴马人被并入嘉布遣会的传教区，尤其是卡里佩一带；到18世纪末，委内瑞拉东北部嘉布遣会传教区里约一万五千名印第安人几乎全是柴马人，据说还有一位柴马人曾率领多个部落起兵反抗西班牙人。亚历山大·冯·洪堡在1800年前后到访，并在游记中记述了他们的身材与风俗。19世纪初柴马语仍是日常用语，也曾是库马纳和巴塞罗那省使用最广的三种原住民语言之一，但此后逐渐衰落，未能作为社群语言留存下来。

en: Sa'ktcihuma, the name the chroniclers rendered as Chakchiuma, means red crawfish in their Western Muskogean tongue and points to the crawfish totem of the tribe. French explorers of the late seventeenth century called them a Chicacha nation, for they shared a common origin with the Chickasaw and Choctaw and lived in the upper Yazoo River country of present-day Mississippi, where Bienville still counted four hundred families in 1702. They enter written history earlier, when Hernando de Soto, wintering among the Chickasaw, sent a detachment against them. In 1700 Carolina slave traders prompted a Quapaw raid meant to seize them for the slave markets, though the attack failed. The Chakchiuma fought on the French side in the Yazoo War, but chronic warfare cut them to sixty families by 1735, and around 1739 the enraged Chickasaw and Choctaw destroyed their villages, killing the warriors and even the village animals. Survivors were absorbed into the two neighboring nations, those joining the Choctaw forming their own Crawfish clan, while a trader in 1757 found others settled in Chickasaw towns.
zh: 萨克奇胡马（史籍作 Chakchiuma）在他们的西马斯科吉语中意为“红螯虾”，取自部落的螯虾图腾。17世纪末的法国探险者称他们为“奇克察人的一支”，因为他们与奇克索人、乔克托人同源，居住在今密西西比州的亚祖河上游地区；1702年，比安维尔在此仍数出四百户人家。他们更早便进入了文字记载：埃尔南多·德索托在奇克索人处过冬时，曾派一支部队攻打他们。1700年，卡罗来纳的奴隶贩子唆使夸保人来袭，企图掳人卖到奴隶市场，但袭击未能得逞。亚祖战争中，萨克奇胡马人站在法国一方，然而连年征战使他们到1735年只剩六十户；约1739年，被激怒的奇克索人和乔克托人摧毁了他们的村落，不仅杀尽战士，连村里的牲畜也不放过。幸存者被两个邻族吸收：并入乔克托的一支组成了自己的“螯虾氏族”，而1757年一名商人发现另一些幸存者已定居在奇克索人的村镇里。

en: The Chakma, or Changhma, are the largest hill people of the Chittagong Hill Tracts, living around Kaptai, Ramu and the ridges that the game assigns them in southeastern Bengal, with related communities in Rakhine, where they are called Daingnet. They trace back to Tibeto-Burman Sak groups who moved from upper Myanmar into the Arakan hills from roughly the tenth century and later into the Chittagong hills, where a Chakma raja ruled over thirty-one clans. A historical language shift gave them the Indo-Aryan Chakma tongue, close to Chittagonian and written in its own Brahmi-derived script, while their life rested on jhum shifting cultivation and Theravada Buddhism. When the Mughal governor Shaista Khan took lowland Chittagong in 1666 the hill kingdom kept its freedom, and treaties of 1713 and 1715 with the Mughals recognized its internal autonomy in return for tribute. The East India Company inherited the claim in 1761, fought the Chakma raja Sher Doulat Khan and his son Jan Baksh Khan from 1777 to 1787, and then signed a Calcutta treaty that left the raja to run his hills as a tributary.
zh: 查克马人又称昌马人，是吉大港山区最大的山地民族，居住在卡普泰、拉穆及游戏划给他们的孟加拉东南山岭一带；在若开也有亲缘群体，当地称他们为代内人。他们的先祖可追溯到藏缅语系的萨克人，约10世纪起从上缅甸迁入若开山区，再进入吉大港山地，后来由一位查克马拉杰统辖三十一个氏族。一次历史上的语言转换使他们改说印度—雅利安语支的查克马语，该语言接近吉大港方言，并使用源自婆罗米文的自有文字；其生计依靠“朱姆”轮歇农业，信仰上座部佛教。1666年莫卧儿总督沙伊斯塔汗夺取吉大港平原后，山地王国仍保持自由，1713年和1715年与莫卧儿的条约以纳贡为条件承认其内部自治。英国东印度公司于1761年继承这一宗主权，1777—1787年与查克马拉杰谢尔·道拉特·汗及其子詹·巴克什·汗交战，随后在加尔各答签约，保留拉杰作为纳贡者治理山区的权力。
