en: The Chalaghawtha, better known in English records as Chillicothe, were one of the five divisions of the Shawnee, alongside the Mekoche, Kispoko, Pekowi and Hathawekela, and by tradition the division that supplied the loose Shawnee confederacy with its political leadership. The chief's village carried the same name, Chillicothe, and each time war or colonial pressure forced a move the new town was called Chillicothe again. From about 1734 the Lower Shawnee Town on the Ohio River grew into a trading hub of more than 1,200 people before its abandonment in 1758. A Chillicothe then stood on the Scioto River, where Tecumseh was likely born in 1768 and where Virginia militia imposed a border settlement after Dunmore's War of 1774. The Old Chillicothe on the Little Miami River, home of the war chief Blackfish, held Daniel Boone captive for several months in 1778; Blackfish died of a wound in 1779 and George Rogers Clark burned the town in 1780. Successive Chillicothes later rose on the Great Miami, St. Mary's and Maumee rivers as the Shawnee kept retreating before American expansion.
zh: 查拉高萨人在英文文献中更常写作奇利科西，是肖尼人的五个分支之一，与梅科奇、基斯波科、佩科维和哈萨维克拉并列；按传统，松散的肖尼联盟由这一分支提供政治领袖。首领所在的村庄也叫奇利科西，每当战争或殖民压力迫使迁徙，新城镇仍沿用此名。约1734年起，俄亥俄河畔的下肖尼镇发展成逾1200人的贸易重镇，1758年被弃守。此后奇利科西先后建于赛欧托河畔，特库姆塞可能于1768年出生在那里；1774年邓莫尔战争后，弗吉尼亚民兵迫使肖尼人接受划界。小迈阿密河畔的旧奇利科西是战将黑鱼的据点，1778年丹尼尔·布恩曾被掳到村中数月；1779年黑鱼因伤死去，1780年乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克焚毁该镇。随着肖尼人在美国扩张面前不断后撤，奇利科西又相继出现在大迈阿密河、圣玛丽斯河和莫米河畔。

en: The Cham are an Austronesian seafaring people of the central Vietnamese coast, heirs of the Sa Huỳnh culture whose settlements at river mouths go back to around the first millennium BCE. From the second century CE they built Champa, not a single kingdom so much as a league of Indianized port principalities, among them Indrapura, Vijaya, Kauthara and Panduranga, that grew wealthy on the trade routes linking India and China and reached their height in the ninth and tenth centuries. Hinduism shaped Cham art and its red-brick temple sanctuaries such as Mỹ Sơn, while contacts with Muslim traders from the eleventh century slowly prepared the conversion that made the ruling dynasty Muslim by the seventeenth century. In 1337 the Cham still held the coastal strip between the Vietnamese of Đại Việt and the Khmer, but the Vietnamese Nam Tiến pressed steadily southward: Lê Thánh Tông sacked Vijaya in 1471, destroying Champa as an effective power, and the last principality of Panduranga survived as a tributary until the Nguyễn emperor Minh Mạng annexed it in 1832. Cham refugees settled in Cambodia and the Mekong Delta, where their descendants keep the Cham language and a tradition of matrilineal family and inheritance custom.
zh: 占人是越南中部沿海的南岛语系航海民族，是沙萤文化的继承者，其在河口地带的定居点可追溯到公元前一千纪。从公元2世纪起，他们建立了占婆——与其说是统一王国，不如说是因陀罗补罗、毗阇耶、古笪罗和宾童龙等印度化港口城邦组成的联盟，靠连接印度与中国的商路致富，在9至10世纪达到鼎盛。印度教塑造了占人的艺术和美山等地的红砖神庙；11世纪起与穆斯林商人的接触则为后来的改宗埋下伏笔，到17世纪占人王朝已皈依伊斯兰教。1337年时，占人仍据有夹在大越与高棉之间的沿海地带，但越南人的“南进”不断南下：1471年黎圣宗攻陷毗阇耶，占婆作为强国就此覆灭，仅剩的宾童龙公国作为附庸存续到1832年，被阮朝明命帝吞并。占人难民流落柬埔寨和湄公河三角洲，其后人仍使用占语，并保留着母系家庭与继承传统。

en: The Chamoru are the indigenous Austronesian people of the Mariana Islands, the chain that includes Guam and Saipan, whose ancestors settled the islands from island Southeast Asia around 1500 BC. They built on rows of latte stone pillars, wove and made pottery, and sailed the swift outrigger proas that Spaniards called flying canoes; they lived in matrilineal clans divided into ruling, middle and hereditary lower classes under a cult of ancestor spirits. Their Chamorro language belongs to the Malayo-Polynesian branch rather than to the Oceanic languages. Ferdinand Magellan made the first European landing on Guam in March 1521, but permanent colonization followed only in 1668, when the Jesuit Diego Luis de San Vitores opened a mission among about 180 autonomous villages. Chief Hurao besieged the new Hagåtña presidio in 1670, and in 1672 the killing of San Vitores by the chief Matå'pang at Tumon, after the baptism of Matå'pang's daughter, ignited open war. Spanish reprisals burned villages, another rebellion under Agualin besieged Hagåtña, and Governor Juan Antonio de Salas forced the people into seven planned towns in a reducción. Campaigns under José de Quiroga y Losada across Rota, Saipan and Tinian ended with the last northern islanders resettled on Guam by 1699. War, disease and resettlement broke the old order, and by 1837 the surviving Chamoru lived as Catholic subjects of Spain, their language filled with Spanish loanwords.
zh: 查莫罗人是马里亚纳群岛（包括关岛、塞班等岛）的南岛语原住民，祖先约在公元前1500年自东南亚海岛地区迁入。他们把房屋建在成排的拉提石柱上，擅长纺织、制陶和驾驶速度惊人的舷外浮杆独木舟，西班牙人称之为“飞行独木舟”；社会按母系氏族组织，分为统治、中间和世袭下层三个等级，崇拜祖先神灵。他们的查莫罗语属马来—波利尼西亚语族，而不是大洋洲语族。1521年3月麦哲伦首次在关岛登陆，但永久殖民迟至1668年才开始，耶稣会士迭戈·路易斯·德·圣维托雷斯在约180个自治村落中建立传教站。1670年酋长胡劳围攻新建的阿加尼亚要塞，1672年酋长马塔庞因女儿受洗一事在杜梦杀死圣维托雷斯，战火全面爆发。西班牙人纵火报复村庄，阿瓜林率部再度围攻阿加尼亚，总督胡安·安东尼奥·德·萨拉斯推行“集村”政策，把居民并入七座规划城镇；何塞·德·基罗加·洛萨达又在罗塔、塞班和天宁用兵，到1699年最后一批北方岛民也被迁往关岛。战争、疫病和迁村瓦解了旧秩序，到1837年，幸存的查莫罗人已是西班牙的天主教臣民，语言中充满西班牙语借词。

en: The Champenois are the people of Champagne, the broad plains between Paris and the border of the Holy Roman Empire, centred on Troyes, Reims and the Marne valley. Their tongue is an Oïl Romance language with dialects ranging from Ardennais in the north through Remois and Troyen to Langrois in the south-east, and it carries a real literary heritage: medieval trouveres such as Chardon de Reims and Theobald the Songwriter, count of Champagne and king of Navarre, composed in it. The County of Champagne became one of the commercial wonders of twelfth- and thirteenth-century Europe through its trade fairs, which drew merchants from Flanders, the Rhine, Italy and England and made Troyes an international centre of finance as well as a literary court graced by Chretien de Troyes. The country was also the cradle of the Cistercian order at Clairvaux and sent knights to every crusade between 1095 and 1270. From 1234 its counts ruled Navarre too, and the marriage of Queen Joan I to Philip IV of France carried the county into the French royal domain in the early fourteenth century, after which Parisian French slowly overshadowed the regional speech.
zh: 香槟人生活在巴黎与神圣罗马帝国边界之间的广阔平原上，以特鲁瓦、兰斯和马恩河谷为中心。他们的香槟语属奥依罗曼语，方言从北部的阿登方言、中部的兰斯方言和特鲁瓦方言一直到东南的朗格勒方言，并拥有真正的文学传统：中世纪特罗维尔诗人兰斯的沙尔东、身兼香槟伯爵与纳瓦拉国王的“歌手”蒂博等都用它写作。凭借香槟集市，香槟伯国成为12、13世纪欧洲的商业奇迹，佛兰德斯、莱茵、意大利和英格兰的商人纷至沓来，特鲁瓦既是国际金融中心，也是克雷蒂安·德·特鲁瓦等作家活跃的文学宫廷。这里还是明谷修道院所在地、西多会的摇篮，1095至1270年间的每次十字军都有香槟骑士参加。1234年起香槟伯爵同时统治纳瓦拉；纳瓦拉女王胡安娜一世与法王腓力四世联姻，伯国遂于14世纪初并入法兰西王室领地，此后巴黎法语逐渐盖过地方方言。

en: The Chaná were the southern branch of the Chaná-Timbú peoples, a family of riverine groups who in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries occupied the floodlands and islands of the Paraná from its meeting with the Paraguay down to the shores of the Río de la Plata and the lower Uruguay. Related bands, from south to north, included the Chaná themselves, the Mbegua, Timbú, Carcaraé, Coronda, Quiloaza, Mocoreta and Mepene, and the riverine ceramic tradition behind them, shaped by Guaraní influences after about 1200, is known to archaeologists as the Goya-Malabrigo culture. They were semi-nomadic hunters, fishers and gatherers who also planted small plots of corn, squash, beans and manioc and spent much of their lives in dugout canoes, camped along the waterways. Their languages, guttural in sound, are usually grouped with the Charrúa tongues; the priest Dámaso Larrañaga compiled a record of the Chaná language in 1823. Early contact brought smallpox epidemics, encomienda levies and military raids, and during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Chaná merged or scattered among the Guaraní and Charrúa, disappearing as a distinct people.
zh: 查纳人是查纳-廷布族群集团南缘的一支；16至17世纪，这批滨水民族占据着巴拉那河的滩地与岛屿，范围从巴拉那河与巴拉圭河交汇处一直延伸到拉普拉塔河两岸和乌拉圭河下游。由南向北，与他们相近的支系包括查纳、姆贝瓜、廷布、卡尔卡拉埃、科龙达、基洛阿萨、莫科雷塔和梅佩内等；支撑他们的河畔制陶传统约在1200年后受到瓜拉尼人影响，被考古学家称为戈亚-马拉布里戈文化。他们半游牧，以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，也小片种植玉米、南瓜、菜豆和木薯，大量时间生活在独木舟中，在水道边扎营。他们的语言发音喉音浓重，通常被归入查鲁亚语群；神父达马索·拉腊尼亚加曾在1823年整理过一部查纳语记录。早期接触带来了天花疫疠、委托监护征发和军事征伐，16至17世纪间，查纳人或与瓜拉尼人、查鲁亚人融合，或四散流离，最终不再作为独立民族存在。

en: The Chancay were the people of a string of river valleys on the central Peruvian coast, from the Fortaleza in the north to the Lurin, with their heartland in the Chancay and Chillon valleys about eighty kilometres north of Lima. Their civilization arose after the collapse of the Wari Empire around the year 1000 and grew into a centralized regional state ruled by curacas, whose large adobe towns clustered around pyramid mounds reached by ramps. Farmers watered the desert with reservoirs and canals, fishermen put out to sea on reed canoes, and traders carried Chancay goods into the highlands and along the coast. They were the first Peruvian culture to organize mass production: mould-made black-on-cream pottery, including the standing burial figurines called cuchimilcos, and painted textiles and gauze headdresses woven for the dead poured from specialist workshops. The southern Chancay valleys fell to the Chimu in the early fifteenth century, and by about 1450 Inca armies had occupied the whole region, bringing the independent Chancay state to an end.
zh: 钱凯人居住在秘鲁中部沿海一连串河谷中，北起福塔莱萨河，南至卢林河，核心地带在利马以北约八十公里的钱凯河谷与奇永河谷。他们的文明约在1000年瓦里帝国崩溃后兴起，发展成由酋长统治的集权区域国家，城镇以土坯建成，簇拥着带坡道的金字塔形土丘。农民用蓄水池和灌渠开垦荒漠，渔民驾芦苇舟出海，商人把钱凯货物运往高原和沿海各地。他们是第一个实现大规模生产的秘鲁文化：专业作坊大量出产模制的黑彩奶白陶器，包括用于墓葬的立式小塑像，还有为死者织造的彩绘织物和纱质头冠。15世纪初，钱凯南部河谷被奇穆征服；到1450年前后，印加军队占领整个地区，独立的钱凯邦国就此终结。

en: The Chángdé culture belongs to the north-western corner of Hunan, on the west shore of Dongting Lake and the lower Yuan River, lake plains backed by the Wuling mountains, a region known in antiquity as Wuling. Rice farming here is ancient, for the Pengtoushan site has yielded the earliest known settled rice village in China, dating back some 8,000 years. A Han county called Linyuan was established in the second century BCE, from which the Wuling commandery kept watch over the mountain tribes of western Hunan; the Tang seat was Langzhou, and the name Changde dates from 1117, when the Song created Changde county, with a superior prefecture following around 1165. Long the gateway between the Dongting country and Guizhou and Sichuan, its river markets handled the rice, timber and tung oil of the Yuan basin. Its speech is a Hunan branch of Southwestern Mandarin, bordering the Xiang dialects of central Hunan, and under the Qing the prefecture passed from Huguang to the new province of Hunan in the 1660s.
zh: 常德文化分布在湖南西北角、洞庭湖滨与沅水下游，是武陵山脉环抱的湖滨平原，古属武陵。这里种稻历史极早，彭头山遗址发现了中国已知最早的定居稻作村落，距今约八千年。公元前2世纪，汉朝在此设临沅县，其后的武陵郡借此统辖湘西山地诸部；唐代这里是朗州治所，1117年宋朝置常德县，1165年前后又升为常德府，常德之名由此确立。这里长期是洞庭湖区通往贵州、四川的门户，沿河市镇集散沅水流域的稻米、木材与桐油。常德话属于西南官话的湖南分支，与湘中一带的湘语相邻；清代17世纪60年代湖广分省，常德府划归新置的湖南省。

en: The Changos, also called Camanchacos or Camanchangos, were the maritime peoples of the desert Pacific coast from Camaná in southern Peru down to the Elqui River in northern Chile, a strip taking in Tacna, Arica, Iquique and Cobija. Their way of life reached back to the eight-thousand-year-old Chinchorro tradition of fisher-gatherers famous for mummifying their dead, and the name Chango was not a single tribe but a loose label the Spaniards applied from the mid-seventeenth century to independent coastal communities sharing the same customs; the Aymara knew them as Camanchacos after the coastal fog, the camanchaca. They knew no agriculture: village families under their own chiefs lived off tuna, mullet and shellfish, preserved fish as charqui with salt, and hunted seals for meat, fat and the skins stretched over wooden frames to make their fishing rafts, trading dried fish, guano and shells inland for maize, coca and wool. The ninth-century expansion of Tiwanaku already found these fishing villages on the Collasuyo coast, and as late as 1540 an encomienda granted to Lucas Martínez listed a Camanchaco fishing settlement at Ilo, while the chronicler Reginaldo de Lizárraga described poor, nearly naked fishermen dwelling in sheltered coves. Long organized in autonomous family bands, they kept much of their old life under Inca and then Spanish rule; in 1835 the naturalist Alcide d'Orbigny still found Chango raftsmen off Cobija running silver out to foreign ships.
zh: 昌戈人又称卡曼查科人，是散布在沙漠太平洋沿岸的海洋族群，分布范围从秘鲁南部的卡马纳一直延伸到智利北部的埃尔基河，塔克拉、阿里卡、伊基克和科维哈都在其中。他们的生计方式可追溯到拥有八千年历史、以制作木乃伊闻名的新克罗渔猎传统；昌戈并不是一个单一部落，而是西班牙人从17世纪中叶起对沿海一批习俗相近、互不统属的社区的笼统称呼，艾马拉人则因沿海特有的浓雾卡曼查卡而叫他们卡曼查科人。他们不懂农业：各个家族村落由自己的首领管辖，以金枪鱼、鲻鱼和贝类为生，用盐把鱼腌成鱼干，还捕猎海狮，取其肉、油脂，并用海狮皮绷在木架上制成捕鱼筏子；他们拿鱼干、鸟粪和贝壳与内地交换玉米、古柯和羊毛。9世纪蒂亚瓦纳科扩张时，这片科利亚苏约沿海已经有渔村存在；迟至1540年，授予卢卡斯·马丁内斯的委托监护地清单里还登记了伊洛的一个卡曼查科渔村，编年史家雷希纳尔多·德·利萨拉加也记述过住在避风小湾里、几乎赤身裸体的贫苦渔民。他们长期以自治的家族群为单位，在印加和后来的西班牙统治下保留了大量旧有生活方式；1835年，博物学家阿尔西德·道比尼仍在科维哈近海看到昌戈筏工驾着皮筏把白银运上外国商船。

en: The Changpa, whose name means northerners in Tibetan, are the semi-nomadic pastoralists of the Changtang, the high plateau of great lakes and cold grasslands running from Rutok and the lakes of western Tibet into south-eastern Ladakh. Their country was once part of Zhangzhung, the Bon kingdom of western Tibet, until it was absorbed by the expanding Tibetan Empire around 634. The Changpa herd yaks, sheep and cashmere goats, whose fine pashmina wool they traded westward to the weavers of Kashmir, and pitch black tents along seasonal migration routes. In Ladakh the nomadic Phalpa move between the Hanle valley and Lato, while the settled Fangpa keep six permanent villages there, and the two groups intermarry. They speak Changskhat, a dialect of Tibetan, and follow Tibetan Buddhism.
zh: 羌巴人在藏语中意为“北方人”，是羌塘高原的半游牧牧民；羌塘是遍布大湖和高寒草场的高原，西起日土和西藏西部的湖群，延伸至拉达克东南部。他们的故土曾是西藏西部信奉苯教的象雄王国的一部分，约634年被扩张中的吐蕃帝国吞并。羌巴人牧养牦牛、绵羊和绒山羊，所产精细的帕什米纳羊绒向西销往克什米尔的织工；他们沿季节转场路线支起黑色帐篷。在拉达克，游牧的帕尔巴人往来于汉勒河谷与拉托之间，定居的方帕人在当地保有六个固定村落，两群人互相通婚。他们讲藏语方言昌斯喀特语，信奉藏传佛教。

en: The Chanka were a warlike people of the central Peruvian Andes, related to the Quechua, whose chiefdoms grew up in the Andahuaylas valley and the Ayacucho highlands after the group migrated from Castrovirreina, and whose raids are thought to have helped bring down the Wari state. Their confederation united the Hanan Chanka or Parkos, the Urin Chanka of Andahuaylas and the Villca or Rucana groups under two paramount chiefs, the Uscovilca and the Ancovilca, and colonial chronicles describe a rich lordship at its height between 1200 and 1438. Farmers and llama herders, they worshipped a puma deity, painted their faces, carried the mummies of their ancestors into battle and made cups from the skulls of slain enemies. Inca tradition claims the Urin Chanka were already subdued around 1230, when Mayta Cápac crossed the Apurímac by a hanging bridge, but the decisive conflict came after 1430, when the Hanan Chanka besieged Cusco and were crushed at Yawarpampa by the prince Cusi Yupanqui, who then took the name Pachacuti; their leader Anccu Hualloc was captured and the survivors were resettled as mitma labourers. When the Spaniards arrived in 1532 the Chanka joined Pizarro's indigenous auxiliaries against the Inca, yet colonial rule later brought forced labour and missionary abuse, including the ten-year tyranny of the priest Juan Bautista de Albadán at Pampachiri from 1601 to 1611.
zh: 昌卡人是秘鲁中部安第斯山区的好战民族，与克丘亚人相近；他们从卡斯特罗维雷纳迁徙到安达韦拉斯河谷和阿亚库乔高原，其袭扰被认为促成了瓦里政权的崩溃。昌卡联盟把上昌卡（又称帕尔科）、安达韦拉斯的下昌卡以及维尔卡（鲁卡纳）诸部联合起来，由乌斯科维尔卡和安科维尔卡两位大酋长统辖；殖民时代的史书记载，1200—1438年间这个富庶的酋邦盛极一时。他们务农并放牧羊驼，崇拜美洲狮神，作战时涂面、肩扛祖先的木乃伊，还用被杀敌人的头骨制成饮器。印卡传说称下昌卡人早在约1230年就被迈塔·卡帕克经吊桥渡过阿普里马克河所征服；决定性的冲突发生在1430年之后：上昌卡人围攻库斯科，在亚瓦尔潘帕被王子库西·尤潘基击溃，后者随后取名帕查库特克，昌卡首领安科·瓦略克被俘，幸存者被编为米特玛迁民服役。1532年西班牙人到来时，昌卡人加入皮萨罗的印第安盟军攻打印卡，但殖民统治仍带来劳役与教士迫害，例如1601—1611年胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·阿尔瓦丹神父在潘帕奇里长达十年的暴虐统治。

en: The Chaoui are the Zenata Amazigh people of the Aurès massif in northeastern Algeria, highland shepherds whose name Shawi means shepherd and who speak Tachawit, a Zenati variety of Tamazight. The Aurès long served as a Berber redoubt: its Christian kingdom, founded by King Masties in the 480s, defied the Vandals and the Byzantines, with King Iabdas warring against the restored province of Africa. When the Arabs conquered the Maghreb the Aurès led the last resistance; after Kusaila fell at Mamma in 690, the Jerawa queen Dihya, known to the Arabs as al-Kahina, united the tribes, won the Battle of Meskiana and ruled from the mountains to Ghadames until she was slain in 703. In the Islamic era the Zenata clans of the region listed by Ibn Khaldun, the Ifren, Maghrawa and Abdalwadids among them, supplied warriors to the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, while the high valleys around Baghai and Constantine kept their Berber speech and tribal life through the Hafsid and Ottoman centuries.
zh: 沙维亚人是阿尔及利亚东北部奥雷斯山区的泽纳塔系阿马齐格人，以高山放牧为生，沙维一词意为牧人，他们操塔马齐格特语的泽纳提分支塔沙维特方言。奥雷斯向来是柏柏尔人的堡垒：480年代马斯提斯王在此建立基督教的奥雷斯王国，抗拒汪达尔人与拜占庭，伊阿卜达斯王还曾进攻拜占庭收复的阿非利加行省。阿拉伯人征服马格里布时，奥雷斯扛起了最后的抵抗：690年库赛拉在马马战役阵亡后，杰拉瓦部落的女王迪希亚（阿拉伯人称之为卡希娜）联合诸部，赢得梅斯基亚纳战役，建立起从奥雷斯山到古达米斯的政权，直至703年战死。进入伊斯兰时代后，伊本·赫勒敦记载的当地泽纳塔诸部——伊夫伦、马格拉瓦和阿卜杜勒瓦迪德等——后来为特莱姆森的扎扬王朝提供战士，而巴加伊、君士坦丁一带的高山河谷在哈夫斯与奥斯曼的数百年间始终保留柏柏尔语言和部落生活。

en: The Teochew are the Han Chinese of the Chaoshan plain in easternmost Guangdong, the eight old counties around Chaozhou, Jieyang and Chaoyang on the lower Han River, speaking Teochew, a conservative dialect of Southern Min. The coast was barely touched by the Qin conquest of 214 BC and long remained remote Yue country; the Eastern Jin set up Haiyang county in 331 and the Yi'an commandery in 413, and in 591 the Sui named the prefecture Chaozhou. Northern families drifted in through Fujian for centuries, many sojourning in Putian before crossing into the region between the Tang and the Ming, which gave Teochew its close kinship with Hokkien. In 819 the exiled Confucian writer Han Yu governed the prefecture briefly, promoting schools and leaving such a memory that the river through the city was later named the Han River. Under the Song and Ming the region became a crowded rice country of walled market towns, sending traders and coolies overseas from the eighteenth century; by 1819 Teochew planters were already opening gambier estates in Singapore, and Teochew merchants became the largest Chinese group in Siam.
zh: 潮州人是广东最东端潮汕平原上的汉族民系，聚居于韩江下游潮州、揭阳、潮阳一带的旧潮州八邑，操闽南语中保守的潮州话。公元前214年秦朝征服岭南时，这片海岸尚属化外，长期是偏远的越地；331年东晋置海阳县，413年设义安郡，591年隋朝定名潮州。数百年来北方世家经福建陆续南下，许多人在莆田短暂落脚后，于唐至明代间迁入本区，因此潮州话与闽南语关系极近。819年，因谏迎佛骨被贬的文学家韩愈出任潮州刺史，任内兴学教士，遗泽深远，穿城而过的江后来便得名韩江。宋明时期这里发展为城镇林立、人烟稠密的稻米之乡；18世纪起不断有商人与苦力出洋，1819年潮州种植者已在新加坡开辟甘蜜园，潮州商人更成为暹罗最大的华人群体。

en: The Charca or Charka were a highland people of the central Bolivian Andes, spread across what are now Chuquisaca, northern Potosí, southern Cochabamba and eastern Oruro; the Charka kingdom of Kollasuyu bound them together with neighboring groups such as the Chuwi, Chayanta and Qhara Qhara. From the east they faced repeated raids by the Ava Guaraní, whom they called Chiriguano. In the late fifteenth century the armies of the Inca Túpac Yupanqui invaded, and after several defeats their leader Copacatiraca persuaded the people to submit; Charca warriors then served in the Inca armies. The Portuguese Aleixo Garcia reached them around 1525, and in 1538 they allied with the Spaniards under Gonzalo Pizarro. The city of La Plata, later Sucre, was founded on their land in 1540 and gave its name to the colonial Audiencia of Charcas.
zh: 查克拉人即史籍中的查尔卡斯人，是玻利维亚安第斯中部的高原族群，分布在今丘基萨卡、波托西北部、科恰班巴南部和奥鲁罗东部；科利亚苏尤的查克拉王国把他们与丘维、查扬塔、卡拉卡拉等邻近族群联合在一起。他们不断遭到来自东方的阿瓦·瓜拉尼人侵扰，并把后者称为奇里瓜诺人。15世纪末，印加王图帕克·尤潘基的军队入侵，连战连败之后，首领科帕卡蒂拉卡说服族人归降，查尔卡斯战士随后加入印加军队。葡萄牙人阿莱舒·加西亚约在1525年抵达他们的土地；1538年他们与贡萨洛·皮萨罗麾下的西班牙人结盟。1540年，拉普拉塔城（即后来的苏克雷）在其土地上建立，殖民时期的查尔卡斯检审庭也得名于此。

en: The Charrúa were the semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers of the grasslands around the Río de la Plata, ranging in the sixteenth century between the Paraná and Uruguay rivers and later centred on the territory that is now Uruguay, with adjoining bands in Entre Ríos and Rio Grande do Sul. Seasonal movers, they summered on the coast fishing and gathering shellfish, fruit and roots, and wintered inland hunting deer and rhea with bolas and bows; once cattle and horses spread across the pampas, livestock raids known as malones became central to their way of life. Their encounter with Europeans was violent from the start, as chroniclers blamed them for the killing of Juan Díaz de Solís on his voyage of 1515, and together with the Chaná they long resisted colonial settlement. In the eighteenth century they warred against the Guaraní missions, pushed north and mingled with the Minuane, Guenoa, Yaro and Bohan, until colonial writers applied the name Charrúa to the whole confederacy of peoples. Their independent life ended in 1831, when the Uruguayan army of Fructuoso Rivera carried out the Massacre of Salsipuedes, killing most of the population and selling the survivors into service; the small remnant dispersed among neighbouring tribes, and their poorly attested language did not outlast them.
zh: 查鲁亚人是拉普拉塔河一带草原上的半游牧狩猎采集族群，16世纪时活动在巴拉那河与乌拉圭河之间，后来以今乌拉圭为中心，另有群体分布在恩特雷里奥斯和南里奥格兰德。他们随季节迁徙：夏天到海岸捕鱼、采集贝类、水果和块根，冬天深入内陆，用流星锤和弓箭猎鹿与美洲鸵鸟；等牛马在潘帕斯草原扩散后，劫掠牲畜的马隆突袭成了他们生活的核心。他们与欧洲人一接触就兵戎相见，编年史家把1515年探险家胡安·迪亚斯·德索利斯之死记在他们头上；他们又与查纳人联手，长期抵抗殖民定居。18世纪，他们与瓜拉尼传教区交战、向北扩张，并与米努安、格诺亚、亚罗、博安等族群通婚融合，殖民地文献遂把这一整群部族笼统称为查鲁亚。1831年，弗鲁克图奥索·里维拉的乌拉圭军队发动萨尔西普埃德斯屠杀，大部分人遇害，幸存者被卖为仆役，残部四散融入邻近部落，记录寥寥的查鲁亚语也就此消亡。

en: The Chatot, now more often called Chacato, were a Muskogean-speaking people of the Florida panhandle, occupying the upper Chipola and Apalachicola river basins in the seventeenth century. The Spanish founded two missions among their villages in 1674, but pressure to adopt full Christian practice sparked a rebellion in which the converts tried to kill a missionary; many rebels fled to the Tawasa or joined the Spanish-hostile Chiscas, while the rest resettled in missions in Apalachee Province. When Carolinian raiders and their Native allies destroyed the Apalachee missions in 1704, the surviving Chatot moved west with the Apalachee and settled around Pensacola and Mobile bays, with some later absorbed into the Choctaw. After West Florida passed to Great Britain in 1763, others crossed into Louisiana. Spanish writers called them chato, flat-nosed, perhaps for their practice of artificial cranial deformation, and the Choctawhatchee River and Bay may preserve their name.
zh: 查托特人今多称查卡托人，是佛罗里达狭地操穆斯科格语的族群，17世纪时占据奇波拉河与阿巴拉契科拉河上游盆地。1674年西班牙人在他们的村庄建立了两座传教站，但强迫全面遵行基督教仪轨激起叛乱，信徒企图杀死一名传教士；许多叛乱者逃到塔瓦萨人处或投奔与西班牙为敌的奇斯卡人，其余人迁入阿巴拉契省的传教站。1704年，卡罗来纳的袭击者及其印第安盟友摧毁阿巴拉契传教区后，幸存的查托特人随阿巴拉契人西迁，定居在彭萨科拉湾和莫比尔湾一带，部分后来被乔克托人吸收。1763年西佛罗里达划归英国后，另一些人渡河西入路易斯安那。西班牙人称他们为 chato，意为扁鼻，可能源于其人工改形头颅的习俗；乔克托哈奇河与乔克托哈奇湾的名字或即来自该族。

en: Tsamosan, also called Olympic Salish, is the branch of the Salishan family spoken by the Southwestern Coast Salish peoples of western Washington — the Lower and Upper Chehalis, Quinault and Cowlitz — whose villages lined Grays Harbor, Willapa Bay and the Chehalis River and its tributaries around the Olympic Peninsula. They had no tribes in the political sense: independent village communities, linked by language and marriage, lived on salmon runs, shellfish and game in cedar-plank longhouses, and the name Chehalis itself means sand, from the principal Lower Chehalis village at present-day Westport. Lower Chehalis words also fed into the Chinook Jargon used across the Pacific Northwest. The sea captain Robert Gray entered Grays Harbor in 1792, the first recorded European contact, and after the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Vancouver the Chehalis became key middlemen in the regional fur trade. Malaria epidemics in the 1830s, above all the outbreak of 1830, emptied whole villages and merged surviving groups, such as the Lower Chehalis and Lower Chinook of Willapa Bay.
zh: 察莫萨又称奥林匹克萨利什语，是萨利什语系的一支，由华盛顿州西部的西南海岸萨利什诸族——下切哈利斯人、上切哈利斯人、奎诺尔特人和考利茨人——使用；他们的村落分布在奥林匹克半岛周边的格雷斯港、威拉帕湾以及切哈利斯河及其支流沿岸。他们没有政治意义上的部落，而是以语言和婚姻相联系的独立村落社群，住雪松木板长屋，以鲑鱼、贝类和猎物为生；“切哈利斯”意为沙子，得名于今韦斯特波特的下切哈利斯人主要村落。下切哈利斯语的词汇也进入了通行于太平洋西北海岸的奇努克混合语。1792年，船长罗伯特·格雷驶入格雷斯港，这是有记载的首次欧洲人接触；哈德逊湾公司修建温哥华堡后，切哈利斯人成为地区毛皮贸易的重要中介。19世纪30年代的疟疾，尤其是1830年的大疫，使整村整村人口灭绝，幸存者群体彼此合并，例如威拉帕湾的下切哈利斯人与下奇努克人合为一体。

en: The Cheke Holo are an Oceanic-speaking people of Santa Isabel, the longest island in the Solomon Islands. Their language, also called Maringe, A'ara or Kubonitu, is spoken chiefly in the east of the island around Maringe and has two main dialects, Maringe and Hograno; together with Bughotu it ranks among the island's principal languages and serves as a local tongue of trade. Santa Isabel was the scene of the first European landing in the Solomon archipelago. On 7 February 1568 the Spanish expedition of Álvaro de Mendaña went ashore here and charted the island as Santa Isabel de la Estrella. The Spaniards built a settlement and a surveying brigantine, but hunger, sickness and conflict with the islanders drove them to abandon the post and withdraw to Guadalcanal.
zh: 切克霍洛人是所罗门群岛最长岛屿圣伊莎贝尔岛上说大洋洲语的族群。他们的语言又称马林格语、阿拉语或库博尼图语，主要通行于岛东部的马林格一带，下分马林格和霍格拉诺两大方言；它与布戈图语同为岛上的主要语言，并充当当地的贸易通用语。圣伊莎贝尔岛是欧洲人在所罗门群岛登陆的第一站。1568年2月7日，阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚率领的西班牙探险队在此上岸，将该岛标为圣伊莎贝尔·德拉埃斯特雷利亚。西班牙人建起定居点和一艘测量用双桅船，但饥饿、疾病以及与岛民的冲突最终迫使他们放弃据点，撤往瓜达尔卡纳尔岛。

en: The Chelkans, who call themselves Chalkandu, are a small Turkic people of the northeastern Altai taiga, speaking a Northern Altai tongue. They took shape from Turkic clans mingling with Ket, Samoyedic and other indigenous Siberian hunters, a process already under way when the Yenisei Kyrgyz dominated the region. From the thirteenth to the eighteenth century the area passed under Mongol and later Dzungar rule, and in 1756 the Chelkans submitted to the Russian Empire together with the other Altai peoples. Hunters rather than herders, they lived by chasing fur game in the mountain forests, adding cedar-nut gathering in the nineteenth century, and made their homes in polygonal log and bark yurts with conical bark roofs. Russian Orthodoxy gradually spread among them, but older shamanic practices remained alive.
zh: 切尔坎人自称“恰勒坎杜”，是阿尔泰东北部泰加林中的小型突厥语族群，讲一种北阿尔泰语。他们由突厥氏族与克特、萨莫耶德等西伯利亚土著狩猎群体混合而成，早在叶尼塞黠戛斯人称雄该地区时这一融合过程已经开始。13至18世纪，这一带先后处于蒙古和后来准噶尔的统治之下，1756年切尔坎人与其他阿尔泰民族一同归附俄罗斯帝国。他们以狩猎而非畜牧为生，在山林中猎取毛皮兽，19世纪又增加了采集雪松籽的营生，住房是多边形木架树皮屋、顶覆锥形树皮盖。俄罗斯东正教逐渐在他们中传播，但更古老的萨满习俗仍然留存。

en: The Giduwa, or Kituwa, are the Cherokee of the Middle Towns, the mountain communities of the upper Little Tennessee and Tuckasegee rivers in what is now western North Carolina, whose speech is the Middle, or Kituwah, dialect of the Iroquoian Cherokee language. They call themselves Anigiduwagi, People from Kituwa, after their oldest mother town, where a platform mound raised about the year 1000 marks the place of the communal townhouse and its ever-burning sacred fire; Nikwasi, the Star Place on the Little Tennessee, was another of the seven mother towns, counted at a hundred and sixty-two people by English missionaries in 1721. The mountain Cherokee met South Carolina traders in treaty at Nikwasi in 1727 and received Alexander Cuming there in 1730, but their towns were repeatedly burned: James Grant's expedition razed Nikwasi in 1761 during the war between Britain and the Cherokee, and Griffith Rutherford's militia destroyed it again in September 1776. Each time the people rebuilt, until in 1819 the United States forced them to cede the valley lands and withdraw into the Qualla Boundary, where the families that avoided the removals of the 1830s kept the Giduwa dialect alive.
zh: 基杜瓦人（又称基图瓦人）是切罗基人中的中城镇之民，聚居在今北卡罗来纳西部小田纳西河上游与塔卡塞吉河的山地社区，说属易洛魁语系的切罗基语中部方言，即基图瓦方言。他们自称阿尼基杜瓦吉，意为“来自基图瓦的人”；基图瓦是他们最古老的母城，约1000年堆筑的台形土墩标示着当年公共议事屋与长明圣火的所在，小田纳西河畔意为“星辰之地”的尼夸西则是七大母城之一，1721年英国传教士统计其人口为一百六十二人。山地切罗基人1727年在尼夸西与南卡罗来纳的贸易商缔约，1730年又在此接待亚历山大·卡明；但他们的城镇屡遭兵燹：1761年英国与切罗基交战期间，詹姆斯·格兰特的远征军夷平尼夸西，1776年9月格里菲思·拉瑟福德的民兵再度将其摧毁。人们每次都重建家园，直到1819年美国迫使他们割让河谷土地、退入夸拉边界；那些在19世纪30年代的强制迁徙中留下来的家族，便在那里延续着基杜瓦方言。

en: The Chewa, also called Mang'anja, are a Bantu people of central and southern Malawi and the neighbouring borderlands of Zambia and Mozambique, and the principal surviving branch of the Maravi peoples. Their oral traditions trace their origins to Malambo in the Luba country of the Congo, from where they migrated through northern Zambia into the Malawi highlands. The first Chewa kingdom arose around 1480, and by the sixteenth century its two leading clans ruled from separate centres, the Banda at Mankhamba and the Phiri at Manthimba, before the Maravi state was unified in the following century. Portuguese traders and missionaries documented contacts with its chiefs between 1608 and 1667, though they never reached its heartland. By 1750 a cluster of Maravi dynasties ruled central Malawi, and the Chewa kept their identity through their language, the mphini tattoo marks and the Nyau secret brotherhoods, whose masked Gule Wamkulu dances mark the initiation of young men. Chewa society is matrilineal, with land and lineage inherited through the mother and guarded by her brothers.
zh: 切瓦人又称曼甘贾人，是班图人的一支，主要居住在马拉维中部和南部以及赞比亚、莫桑比克毗邻边境，也是马拉维诸族最主要的后裔。据口传传统，他们起源于刚果卢巴地区的马兰博，先迁居赞比亚北部，再进入马拉维高地。第一个切瓦王国约在1480年建立；到16世纪，两大氏族各据一方，班达氏族以曼坎巴为中心，菲里氏族以曼廷巴为中心，下一世纪马拉维国家完成统一。葡萄牙商人与传教士在1608至1667年间留下了与各地酋长接触的记录，但始终未能深入其腹地。到1750年，数个马拉维王朝统治着马拉维中部，切瓦人则凭借本族语言、姆菲尼纹身和尼奥秘密兄弟会维系认同，后者戴面具表演的古勒瓦姆库卢舞是男子成年仪式的高潮。切瓦社会行母系制，土地与世系沿母方继承，并由舅父守护。

en: The Chhattisgarhi people inhabit the fertile upper Mahanadi basin of east-central India, a region known in ancient times as Dakshina Kosala and centred on Ratanpur and Raipur. Their language, Chhattisgarhi, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan tongue of the Eastern Hindi group, written in the Devanagari script and closely related to Hindi. In the early medieval period Dakshina Kosala was ruled from Sirpur by the Sharabhpuriya and Panduvamshi dynasties, and from the early eleventh century by the Kalachuris of Ratnapura, whose successors ruled as the Haihaiyavanshi kings. Holding the country for roughly seven hundred years, the dynasty split into Ratanpur and Raipur branches in the fourteenth century and later acknowledged Mughal overlordship. Maratha armies invaded in 1740, and in 1758 the Bhonsles of Nagpur annexed the kingdom. The name Chhattisgarh, traditionally explained as the land of thirty-six forts, first appeared in an official document under Maratha rule in 1795.
zh: 切蒂斯格尔人生活在印度中东部肥沃的默哈讷迪河上游盆地，这一地区古称南憍萨罗，以勒登布尔和赖布尔为中心。他们的语言切蒂斯格尔语属印度-雅利安语族东印地语支，使用天城文，与印地语关系密切。中世纪早期，南憍萨罗由设里补罗的设罗菩利亚王朝和般度王朝先后统治；11世纪初起，勒登布尔的卡拉丘里王朝掌权，其后裔以海亥耶万西王朝之名继续统治。该王朝立国约七百年，14世纪分裂为勒登布尔与赖布尔两支，后来承认莫卧儿王朝的宗主权。1740年马拉塔军队入侵，1758年那格浦尔的邦斯勒家族吞并了这个王国。切蒂斯格尔一名通常被解释为三十六座堡垒之地，在马拉塔统治时期的1795年首次见于官方文件。

en: The Chiapanec, who call themselves Soctón, are an Oto-Manguean people of the Central Depression of Chiapas in southern Mexico, centered on the city of Chiapa, now Chiapa de Corzo. Manguean speakers may have entered Chiapas as early as 200, and the Chiapanec themselves probably seized the former Zoque city of Chiapa between the ninth and tenth centuries, taking their name from it. In the Postclassic period Chiapa grew into one of the largest urban centers of the region, capital of a state controlling most of the Central Depression; a priestly oligarchy ruled it and chose two political-military leaders every year, and rivalry over the trade route to Tehuantepec kept it at odds with the neighboring Zoque, Tzotzil and Tzeltal. Spanish expeditions crossed the region in the early 1520s, and in 1528 Diego de Mazariegos organized the colonial province of Chiapa. Excessive tribute and labor demands drove the Chiapanec to abandon their towns in revolt, and their communities dwindled under colonial rule.
zh: 恰帕斯人自称索克顿人，是墨西哥南部恰帕斯中央洼地的奥托-曼格语族群，以恰帕城（今恰帕德科尔索）为中心。曼格语支的使用者可能早在200年就已进入恰帕斯，而恰帕斯人本身大概在9至10世纪攻占了原属索克人的恰帕城，并以此得名。后古典期，恰帕发展为当地最大的城市中心之一，成为控制中央洼地大部的政权都城；祭司寡头集团统治该城，每年选出两名军政首领，而围绕特万特佩克商路的争夺使他们长期与邻近的索克人、佐齐尔人和采尔塔尔人为敌。16世纪20年代初西班牙远征队穿过这一地区，1528年迭戈·马萨列戈斯设立殖民省份恰帕。过重的贡赋和劳役迫使恰帕斯人弃城反抗，他们的社群在殖民统治下日渐衰微。

en: The Chicha, or Checha, were an Andean people of the south-western altiplano, centred on the valleys of Tupiza and the rivers Angostura and Talina in what is now the Potosí department of Bolivia, with lands reaching into Jujuy and Salta in Argentina and, by influence, the Atacama puna. Their towns, among them Chilcayoj and Talina, stood along the Inca road through Collasuyo, and their society gathered several local groups into one ethnic identity in the fertile mountain valleys. The Inca Túpac Yupanqui conquered them around 1478 and dispersed many as mitimaes: some were sent north to repopulate the conquered kingdom of Quito in Ecuador, others to the Calchaquí valleys and the Quebrada de Humahuaca as a frontier barrier against the Chiriguano, and others again to the Loa valley and the Atacama lands of Chile. These resettlements began the mixing that later produced the Kolla conglomerate. Diego de Almagro's expedition crossed Chicha territory in 1536, when Tupiza was described as their capital; a Spanish official's report of 1566 still listed their roadside towns, though Quechua had by then made deep inroads under Inca rule.
zh: 希沙人又称切查人，是安第斯高原西南部的原住民，中心在今玻利维亚波托西省的图皮萨河谷及安戈斯图拉河、塔利纳河流域，领地延伸到阿根廷的胡胡伊和萨尔塔，并影响到阿塔卡马普纳。他们的城镇——如奇尔卡约赫和塔利纳——分布在穿越科利亚苏尤的印加大道沿线，其社会由若干地方群体在肥沃的山谷中融合为共同的族群。印加王图帕克·尤潘基于约1478年征服他们，把许多人作为米特马埃人拆散迁徙：一部分北迁厄瓜多尔，填补征服基多王国后的人口；一部分迁往卡尔查基河谷和乌马瓦卡峡谷，充当抵御奇里瓜诺人的前沿屏障；还有一些被送往智利的洛阿河谷和阿塔卡马地区。这些迁徙开启了族群融合，后来形成科亚人群体。1536年阿尔马格罗的远征队穿过希沙人的土地，当时图皮萨被记载为他们的首府；1566年一名西班牙官员的报告仍逐一列出印加大道旁的希沙城镇，而在印加统治下克丘亚语此时已深深渗入当地。

en: The Chickasha, or Chickasaw, are a Muskogean people whose towns spread across northern Mississippi, western Tennessee and the Alabama uplands, kin to the Choctaw and once a single people with them before the two nations split in the seventeenth century. Their migration story tells of a journey from west of the Mississippi, and archaeology links their ancestors to the collapse of the Moundville chiefdom in the fifteenth century. Hernando de Soto knew them as the Chicaza, and in the winter of 1540 a Chickasaw night raid on his camp nearly destroyed his army. From 1670 they acquired firearms from colonial merchants in Carolina, selling captives taken in raids on the Choctaw, and as British allies they fought the French and Choctaw through much of the eighteenth century, beating a French attack at the Battle of Ackia in 1736. They stood with the young United States at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and in the Creek War of 1813 to 1814, where the Colberts, descendants of a Scots trader and high-ranking Chickasaw women, rose to lead the nation. Matrilineal and counted among the Five Civilized Tribes, they nonetheless surrendered their lands in the Treaty of Pontotoc Creek of 1832 and were forced west on the Trail of Tears after 1834.
zh: 奇克索人是马斯科吉语族族群，村镇遍布密西西比北部、田纳西西部和阿拉巴马高地，与乔克托人同源，两族在17世纪才分成两个民族。他们的迁徙传说讲述了从密西西比河以西东来的历程，考古学则把其先民与15世纪蒙德维尔酋长国的崩溃联系起来。埃尔南多·德·索托称他们为奇卡萨人，1540年冬，奇克索人夜袭其营地，几乎全歼这支西班牙军队。1670年起，他们从卡罗来纳商人手中购得火器，又把袭击乔克托人掳来的俘虏卖给殖民者；作为英国盟友，他们在18世纪的大部分时间里与法国人和乔克托人作战，1736年在阿基亚之战中击退法军。他们在1794年的鹿寨之战以及1813至1814年的克里克战争中都站在年轻的美国一边，苏格兰商人与奇克索显贵女子联姻产生的科尔伯特家族，也在这一时期成为全族的领导核心。奇克索人按母系传承，被列为五大文明部落之一，却仍在1832年的《蓬托托克溪条约》中交出土地，1834年后被押上眼泪之路西迁。

en: The Tsilhqot'in, or Chilcotin, are the southernmost Athabaskan-speaking people of British Columbia, whose country Tŝilhqot'in Nen lies along the Chilko and Chilcotin rivers west of the Fraser. Their name means people of the red ochre river, and they also call themselves the Nenqayni, people of the land. Before contact they were a feared warrior nation whose influence ran from the Similkameen country to the Pacific coast and the Rocky Mountains, and they sat astride a wide trade network built on obsidian for arrowheads and stone tools. They once raided all eleven bands of the Lillooet across the mountains, carrying off captives, until a defeat in Graveyard Valley checked them. European goods first reached them in the 1780s and 1790s through the maritime sea otter trade; by 1808 the Montreal-based North West Company had posts among the Carrier people to their north, and in 1821 the Hudson's Bay Company opened Fort Alexandria on the Fraser at the edge of their lands, becoming their chief source of metal tools and guns. An epidemic that reached the region in 1836 swept neighbouring Carrier villages, a foretaste of the disease waves that followed.
zh: 齐尔科廷人是不列颠哥伦比亚省最靠南的阿萨巴斯卡语民族，家园“齐尔科廷嫩”位于弗雷泽河以西的奇尔科河与奇尔科廷河一带。他们的名字意为“红赭石河之民”，又自称嫩卡伊尼，意为“大地之民”。接触欧洲人之前，他们是令人畏惧的武士民族，势力范围从锡米尔卡明地区延伸到太平洋海岸和落基山脉，并控制着一个以黑曜石贸易为核心的广阔交换网络，黑曜石是制作箭头和石器的首选材料。他们曾翻山袭击利卢埃特人的全部十一个群体、掳走人口，直到在墓地谷战败才受到遏制。1780至1790年代，欧洲货物先经海上的海獭贸易传到他们手中；到1808年，以蒙特利尔为大本营的西北公司已在其北方的卡里尔人地区设立商站；1821年，哈德逊湾公司在弗雷泽河畔、齐尔科廷人疆域边缘开设亚历山大堡，成为他们获取金属工具和枪械的主要来源。1836年，一场疫病传入这一地区，席卷邻近的卡里尔人村落，预示了随后接踵而至的疫病浪潮。

en: The Chillque, also written Chilque, were a highland people whose name is of Aymara origin and whose Hanan and Urin moieties traced their home to the country around Lake Titicaca. They were a constellation of small tribes, among them the Masca, Aco, Papre and Cuyo, whom the Incas conquered alongside the Aymara, Umasuyu and Cotabamba nations and then turned into trusted mitimaes, resettling loyal Chillque colonies far from the Collao to watch over freshly conquered peoples; the chroniclers even numbered them among the Inca de Privilegio, peoples granted special status, and by then they spoke Quechua. In the Chili valley behind Arequipa, Chillque ayllus were planted to keep the migrant Yanahuara and Chumbivilca nations under observation, while other Hanan Chillque communities were moved into the Huamanga highlands. Andean tradition also held the province of Chilque to be a pacarina, the place where the ancestors of the Quechua had emerged from the earth. After the conquest Francisco Pizarro granted the Chillque together with the Yanahuara and Chumbivilca to the encomendero Luis de León, an award later confirmed through Pedro de la Gasca to Baltasar Díaz and then to Gómez Hernández; set to work in silver mines and textile workshops and ravaged by disease, the small garrison communities shrank fast, with only thirty-two Chillque tributaries recorded in the Arequipa visitation of 1582.
zh: 奇尔克人又译奇尔凯人，族名出自艾马拉语，分为上、下两个半边，故土在的的喀喀湖周围。他们是马斯卡、阿科、帕普雷、库约等若干部落的合称，印加人在征服艾马拉、乌马苏尤和科塔班巴等族时一并将其征服，随后把他们当作可信的米蒂马伊，把效忠的奇尔克殖民群体远远迁离科利亚奥，去监视新征服的民族；编年史家甚至把他们列为享有特权的印加民族之一，此时他们已改说克丘亚语。在阿雷基帕后方的奇利河谷，安插了奇尔克人的艾柳以监视迁徙而来的亚纳瓦拉人和琼比维尔卡人，另一些上奇尔克社区则被迁入瓦曼加高原。安第斯传统还把奇尔克省视为一处帕卡里纳，即克丘亚人祖先从地下走出的起源圣地。征服之后，皮萨罗把奇尔克人连同亚纳瓦拉人、琼比维尔卡人一起授予委托监护主路易斯·德莱昂，后来经佩德罗·德拉加斯卡之手转给巴尔塔萨尔·迪亚斯，最后又归戈麦斯·埃尔南德斯；他们被驱入银矿和纺织作坊劳作，又遭疫病摧残，这些小小的驻防社区人口锐减，1582年阿雷基帕的巡查记录里只剩下三十二名奇尔克纳税壮丁。

en: The Chimbus, or Chimbos, were a pre-Inca people of the Chimbo River valley in the Ecuadorian highlands, in what is now Bolívar Province, closely related to the Puruhá and Tomabela peoples of the surrounding sierra. During the Inca expansion of the late fifteenth century they resisted the invading armies from Peru: tradition names the chief Chimbo Cando, called the Guaranga, as their leader in the fighting at the place where the town of Guaranda later rose. After the conquest many Chimbus were deported as mitimae settlers to the region of Lake Titicaca, while Inca colonists were brought into their valley. Spanish rule began in 1534, when Sebastián de Belalcázar established the corregimiento of Chimbo, and the town of Guaranda was founded around 1571. In time the Chimbus merged with Tomabela, Puruhá and Inca communities to form the Waranka people, and their Panzaleo tongue died out during the eighteenth century as Kichwa took its place.
zh: 钦巴斯人又称钦博人，是厄瓜多尔高原钦博河谷的前印加族群，住在今玻利瓦尔省境内，与周围山地的普鲁人、托马贝拉人关系密切。15世纪末印加扩张时，他们抵抗来自秘鲁的入侵大军；传说酋长钦博·坎多（人称瓜兰加）率领族人在后来兴起瓜兰达城的地方奋战。征服之后，许多钦巴斯人作为米蒂马埃斯移民被强制迁往的的喀喀湖一带，印加殖民者则被迁入他们的河谷。西班牙人的统治始于1534年，塞巴斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔设立钦博监政区；瓜兰达城约于1571年建立。久而久之，钦巴斯人与托马贝拉、普鲁和印加群落融合，形成瓦兰卡人；他们的潘萨莱奥语在18世纪逐渐消亡，为克丘亚语所取代。

en: The Chimú are the people of Chimor, the largest kingdom of Peru's Late Intermediate Period, which grew out of the ruins of the Moche on the north Peruvian coast from about 900. Their capital, Chan Chan near modern Trujillo, was a city of adobe palaces behind walls nine metres high; beyond it, irrigated desert valleys supported farmers, fishermen and, in the capital alone, some twelve thousand artisans. Chimú potters made shiny black vessels, and their goldsmiths worked gold, silver, bronze and tumbaga. According to tradition the founder Taycanamo arrived from the sea on a balsa raft, and his descendants widened the kingdom, which conquered the Jequetepeque valley around 1320 and absorbed the Sican lands of Lambayeque around 1375, until Chimor stretched roughly a thousand kilometres along the coast. They worshipped the Moon above the Sun and valued Spondylus shells from Ecuadorian waters; at Huanchaco, archaeologists have uncovered the mass sacrifice of more than two hundred children, dated between 1400 and 1450. The Chimú spoke Quingnam, the official language of Chimor. In 1337 they were still expanding, but the Inca emperor Topa Inca Yupanqui conquered Chimor in the 1470s and carried its last ruler, Minchançaman, to Cusco. Quingnam steadily declined and was extinct by 1763.
zh: 奇穆人是奇穆王国的居民。该王国约900年在莫切文化的废墟上兴起于秘鲁北部沿海，是当地晚中间期最大的政权。都城昌昌在今特鲁希略附近，由高墙环绕的土坯宫殿组成，城墙高达9米；城外靠灌溉沙漠开辟农田，农民、渔师和仅都城就约有1.2万名的工匠支撑着国家。奇穆陶工烧制乌黑发亮的器皿，金匠加工金、银、青铜和通巴加合金。相传始祖塔伊卡纳莫乘巴尔沙木筏渡海而来，其后代不断扩张，于1320年前后征服赫克特佩克河谷，1375年前后吞并兰巴耶克的西坎故地，使奇穆沿海岸绵延约1000公里。他们崇奉月亮甚于太阳，珍视来自厄瓜多尔海域的海菊蛤贝壳；在万查科，考古学家发现了1400年至1450年间献祭200多名儿童的大型牺牲遗址。奇穆人使用金南语，它是奇穆王国的官方语言。1337年时奇穆仍在扩张，但印加君主图帕克·印卡·尤潘基于1470年代征服奇穆，将末代君主米昌萨曼掳往库斯科；金南语此后日渐衰微，到1763年已经消亡。

en: The Chincha were a coastal people of the fertile oasis valleys of southwestern Peru, whose kingdom flourished between 900 and 1450 in the Late Intermediate Period on ground earlier shaped by the Paracas, Nazca and Wari traditions; their name means ocelot in Quechua and they worshipped a jaguar god, claiming feline ancestors. From the eleventh century they built adobe pyramids and palaces at their capital La Centinela, watered maize fields with canals and fertilized them with guano, and made their valley the busiest commercial centre on the Peruvian shore. An early Spanish chronicle records thirty thousand households, among them twelve thousand farmers, ten thousand fishermen and six thousand traders: Chincha llama caravans carried goods overland to Cusco and the Collao plateau, while sailing rafts of balsa logs ran maritime routes far along the Pacific, perhaps as far as Central America, navigated by the star Chundri. Around 1480 the kingdom was absorbed into Tawantinsuyu, whose Inca rulers prized its wealth and gave the name Chinchaysuyu to their northern quarter. The first Spaniards reached the valley in 1534 and a Dominican mission followed by 1542, but introduced diseases and disorder cut the population by an estimated ninety-nine percent within eighty-five years, and Chincha never recovered its former importance.
zh: 钦查人是秘鲁西南沿海肥沃绿洲河谷的居民，其王国在900—1450年的晚中间期兴盛，立足在先前帕拉卡斯、纳斯卡与瓦里文化影响的土地上；“钦查”在克丘亚语中意为豹猫，他们崇拜美洲豹神，自称源自猫科动物。11世纪起，他们在都城拉森蒂内拉修筑土坯金字塔和宫殿，开渠灌溉玉米田并用鸟粪肥田，把河谷建成秘鲁海岸最繁忙的商业中心。据西班牙早期史书记载，当地有三万户，其中农民一万二千、渔民一万、商人六千：钦查的羊驼商队走陆路把货物运往库斯科和科利亚奥高原，带帆的巴尔沙木筏则沿太平洋开辟远海航线，可能远抵中美洲，并靠星辰“琼德里”导航。约1480年，该王国被并入塔万廷苏尤，印卡统治者看重其财富，并把帝国北部大区命名为钦查苏尤。1534年首批西班牙人进入河谷，1542年已有多明我会传教站；但外来疾病和动乱使人口在八十五年内估计减少了九成九，钦查再未恢复昔日的地位。

en: The Chinook are a group of Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest who speak Chinookan languages and have lived along the Columbia River from its gorge down to its mouth, and on the adjoining coast from Tillamook Head in Oregon to Willapa Bay in Washington, for more than twelve thousand years. Settled in cedar-plank longhouses, they drew their living from salmon runs, elk hunting and river trade, and their societies were ranked into nobles, commoners and slaves. Elite families flattened the foreheads of their children as a mark of status, which led early European visitors to call them the Flathead Indians. Their river villages made them middlemen between coastal and interior peoples, and the simplified Chinook Jargon, partly based on their language, became the lingua franca of the Northwest fur trade. The Lewis and Clark Expedition met the Lower Chinook at the mouth of the Columbia in 1805, after which maritime fur traders and repeated epidemics reduced their numbers sharply.
zh: 奇努克人是太平洋西北海岸讲奇努克语族诸语的原住民群体，一万两千多年来定居在哥伦比亚河从峡谷到入海口一带，以及南起俄勒冈蒂拉穆克角、北抵华盛顿威拉帕湾的邻近海岸。他们住在红雪松木板搭建的长屋里，以鲑鱼、猎鹿和河上贸易为生；社会分为贵族、平民和奴隶等级，上层家族把幼儿的额头压平作为身份标志，早期欧洲来客因此称他们为扁头印第安人。沿河的村庄使他们成为沿海与内陆各族之间的贸易中介，部分以其语言为基础形成的奇努克混合语，后来成为西北海岸毛皮贸易的通用语。1805年，刘易斯与克拉克探险队在哥伦比亚河口遇到下游奇努克人；此后随着海上毛皮商人的到来和疫病反复流行，奇努克人口急剧减少。

en: The Chiribaya were the people of the desert coast and nearby valleys of far southern Peru and northern Chile, their heartland lying in the Osmore valley behind the port of Ilo and their settlements running from the Tambo valley to the Lluta River and the Azapa valley near Arica, along some two hundred twenty kilometres of shoreline. Their culture took shape around 700 to 900, in the wake of the Wari and Tiwanaku empires whose colonists had first linked these lower valleys to the highlands, and its classic phase lasted until about 1360. They were never a unified state but a señorío, a loose network of villages under local caciques, organized around the Andean principle of verticality: fishermen on the coast and farmers a few miles inland, at one thousand to two thousand metres, who grew maize and chili peppers, while llamas and alpacas grazed the fog oases of the lomas, where the Chiribaya even bred a special shepherd dog for their herds. The two zones exchanged food and supplied highland peoples such as the Colla and Lupaca with maize, dried fish, fruit, shellfish and island guano, and they kept close ties with their neighbours the Churajon. In the mid-fifteenth century Inca expansion absorbed the Chiribaya communities into the Tawantinsuyu, though their coastal villages kept their old mixed farming-and-fishing life into the early Spanish decades.
zh: 奇里巴亚人生活在秘鲁最南端与智利北部相接的沙漠海岸及邻近谷地，腹地是伊洛港后方的奥斯莫尔河谷，聚落北起坦博河谷，南至柳塔河和阿里卡附近的阿萨帕谷地，沿海岸绵延约二百二十公里。其文化约在700年至900年间成形，前身是瓦里和蒂亚瓦纳科两大帝国的殖民者，正是他们最早把这些低海拔谷地与高原联系起来；奇里巴亚的鼎盛期一直延续到约1360年。他们从未形成统一国家，而是一种由各地卡西克首领分治、联系松散的领主制网络，并按安第斯的垂直分工原则组织社会：沿海住着渔民，几英里内陆海拔一千至两千米处住着种植玉米和辣椒的农民，美洲驼和羊驼在洛马斯雾生绿洲上放牧，奇里巴亚人甚至为此培育了一种专门的牧羊犬。两个区域互通有无，并向科利亚、卢帕卡等高原族群供应玉米、鱼干、水果、贝类和海岛鸟粪，还与邻族丘拉洪保持密切往来。15世纪中叶，印加扩张把奇里巴亚诸社区并入塔万廷苏尤，但沿海村落农耕兼渔捞的古老生活方式一直延续到西班牙人到来后的最初几十年。

en: The Chitarero were a Chibcha-speaking people of the eastern Andes on the border of present-day Colombia and Venezuela, holding the country from Táchira across Norte de Santander to the Pamplona basin, where the Chicamocha River marked their southern limit. Their men customarily wore a calabash gourd of maize wine, or chicha, at the waist, and the Spanish took their word for that vessel, chitarero, as the name of the whole people. They farmed the high valleys and traded with the Muisca, Guane and Lache. On 27 May 1533 they ambushed the retreating expedition of the German conquistador Ambrosius Ehinger, governor of the Welser colony of Little Venice; a poisoned arrow struck his neck and he died four days later near Chinácota, one of their own settlements. When Pamplona was refounded in 1549 the region was still said to hold some 200,000 of these people, though no separate Chitarero identity survived the colonial period.
zh: 奇塔雷罗人是讲奇布查语的族群，住在今哥伦比亚与委内瑞拉边境的安第斯山东段，疆域西起塔奇拉，横跨北桑坦德，东抵潘普洛纳盆地，奇卡莫查河构成他们的南界。他们的男子习惯在腰间挂一只盛玉米酒奇查的葫芦，西班牙人便把他们对这种容器的称呼“奇塔雷罗”当作整个族群的名字。他们在高山谷地农耕，与穆伊斯卡人、瓜内人和拉切人贸易。1533年5月27日，他们伏击了韦尔泽家族“小威尼斯”殖民地总督、德国征服者安布罗西奥·阿尔芬格撤退中的队伍；一支毒箭射中他的颈部，四天后他在奇纳科塔附近丧命，而奇纳科塔本就是奇塔雷罗人的聚落之一。1549年潘普洛纳重建时，据说这一地区仍有约20万奇塔雷罗人，但在殖民时代，独立的奇塔雷罗族群身份最终未能留存下来。

en: The Chitimacha, whose name means people who live on the Grand River, are an Indigenous people of the Atchafalaya Basin and Mississippi Delta in south-central Louisiana, where their ancestors had lived for thousands of years. Their language, Sitimaxa, is a language isolate. They built large unfortified villages of pole-and-mud houses in the swamps and bayous, grew corn, beans and squash in women-tended gardens, hunted deer and alligator, and carved cypress dugout canoes large enough for fifty people; society was matrilineal, and parents flattened the foreheads of infant boys. The four Chitimacha groups may have numbered twenty thousand before contact, but epidemics cut them to about four thousand by 1650. A long war with the French then drove them from their Bayou Lafourche villages and left many survivors sold into slavery, while in 1730 the French destroyed their neighbours the Chawasha, whose remnants joined them. The Chitimacha also absorbed the last of the Taensa and some of the Houma, and in the later eighteenth century Acadian settlers occupied much of their land, leading to intermarriage and conversion to Catholicism; unlike most southeastern peoples, they were not removed in the 1830s and remained on their bayous.
zh: 奇蒂马查人意为住在大河之畔的人，是路易斯安那中南部阿查法拉亚盆地与密西西比三角洲的原住民，其祖先在这片土地上已生活数千年；他们的语言奇蒂马查语是一门孤立语言。他们在沼泽与河湾边建起不设防的大村落，房屋以木柱为骨、糊泥而成，妇女在园圃种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男子猎鹿、捕鳄，还把柏木凿成可容五十人的独木舟；社会按母系传承，父母会把男婴的前额压平。接触欧洲人之前，奇蒂马查四大群体可能有两万人，但瘟疫使他们到1650年只剩约四千人。随后与法国人的长期战争把他们赶出拉福什河湾的村落，许多幸存者被卖为奴；1730年法国人又消灭了邻族乔瓦沙人，其残余并入奇蒂马查。他们还吸收了最后的坦萨人和部分霍马人。18世纪后期，阿卡迪亚移民占据他们的大量土地，两族通婚并改宗天主教；与东南部大多数族群不同，他们在19世纪30年代没有被强制西迁，始终留在自己的河湾之地。

en: Chitralis are the Kho people of the Hindu Kush valleys of Chitral, Mastuj, Mulkhow and Yasin, whose Khowar speech is a Dardic Indo-Aryan language counted among the most archaic living Indic tongues, preserving much Sanskrit case inflection. They began spreading from upper Chitral under the Rais dynasty, whose first chief Shah Nadir Rais is placed around 1320, and in the seventeenth century a branch, the Khushwaqt dynasty, carried Kho rule east into Yasin and Ghizer. Most Kho converted to Islam from the fourteenth century, becoming Hanafi Sunnis with an Ismaili community in the upper valleys, while their kinsmen the Kalash, confined to the Bumburet, Rumbur and Birir valleys, kept their old animist and ancestor-worshipping faith. The Kator dynasty overthrew the Rais in the seventeenth century and ruled Chitral as mehtars from its capital at Chitral town, building a kingdom that at its height stretched from the Kunar valley to Punial. Chitrali life kept its older texture too, in polo on high pastures, the pakol hat and a folklore thick with mountain fairies.
zh: 吉德拉尔人即科霍人，聚居在兴都库什山的吉德拉尔、马斯图吉、穆尔科和亚辛诸河谷，所讲的科瓦语属印度-雅利安语系达尔德语支，被认为是现存最古老的印度语言之一，保留了大量梵语格变形式。他们在拉伊斯王朝治下从上吉德拉尔向外扩张，其首位首领沙阿·纳迪尔·拉伊斯约在1320年兴起；17世纪，分支胡什瓦格特王朝把科霍人的统治向东带到亚辛和吉泽尔。多数科霍人从14世纪起皈依伊斯兰教，成为哈乃斐派逊尼穆斯林，上游河谷则有伊斯玛仪派社群；而他们的近亲卡拉什人退居本布雷特、伦布尔和比里里河谷，保留着古老的万物有灵与祖先崇拜信仰。17世纪卡托尔王朝推翻拉伊斯家族，以吉德拉尔城为都、以“梅赫塔尔”为号统治此地，王国极盛时从库纳尔河谷一直延伸到普尼亚尔。吉德拉尔人的生活也保留了更古老的肌理：高山牧场上的马球、帕科尔帽，以及充满山灵仙子的民间传说。

en: Chiyalik is the name archaeologists give to a medieval culture of the Southern Urals, lasting from the tenth to the fourteenth century and first identified at a settlement by the village of Chiyalek on the Sun river. Its sites run from the Kama tributaries Sheshma and Zay eastward to the Tobol, across the Belaya, Ik and Dema basins of Bashkortostan, the forest-steppe country that medieval Latin writers called Magna Hungaria, the ancient homeland of the Magyars. Its carriers were semi-nomadic Ugric tribes, kin of the Hungarians who stayed in the east when the main Magyar confederation moved to the Black Sea steppe and then into the Carpathian Basin. In the 1230s the Hungarian friar Julian reached Volga Bulgaria and found a Hungarian-speaking people living near the Volga and Kama, the so-called Eastern Hungarians, only a few years before the Mongol conquest swept the region. They wintered in log houses and semi-dugouts and summered in yurts, shaped round-bottom pottery and fought as light cavalry, their graves supplied with arrows, sabres, stirrups and Golden Horde coins. From the middle of the fourteenth century Kipchak Turkic nomads pressed into their lands; the Chiyalik people gradually adopted Islam and were absorbed into the Bashkirs and Volga Tatars, though genetic studies still link their remains to the Hungarians of the Carpathian Basin and to their closest linguistic relatives, the Khanty and Mansi.
zh: 奇亚利克是考古学家对南乌拉尔一处中世纪文化的命名，年代为10至14世纪，最早发现于苏尼河畔奇亚列克村旁的遗址。其遗址西起卡马河支流舍什马河与扎伊河，向东延伸至托博尔河，遍布巴什科尔托斯坦的别拉亚河、伊克河和焦马河流域，正是拉丁文献中称作“马格纳·匈牙利”（马扎尔人故地）的森林草原地带。创造这一文化的是半游牧的乌戈尔部落，他们与马扎尔人同源，在马扎尔人主体迁往黑海草原、继而进入喀尔巴阡盆地时留在了东方。13世纪30年代，匈牙利修士朱利安抵达伏尔加保加利亚，在伏尔加河与卡马河附近发现了一支仍说匈牙利语的人群，即所谓“东匈牙利人”；仅仅数年后，蒙古征服便席卷了这一地区。他们冬天住木构房屋和半地穴屋，夏天住毡帐，制作圆底陶器，以轻骑兵为作战方式，墓中随葬箭矢、马刀、马镫和金帐汗国钱币。从14世纪中期起，钦察突厥游牧民不断涌入，奇亚利克人逐渐改宗伊斯兰教，融入巴什基尔人和伏尔加鞑靼人之中；但古基因研究仍把他们的遗骸与喀尔巴阡盆地的匈牙利人以及语言上最近的亲属汉特人、曼西人联系在一起。

en: The Chahta, anglicized as Choctaw, are a Western Muskogean people of Mississippi, Alabama and Louisiana, whose language is nearly one with Chickasaw; the two peoples share a tradition of descending from a single ancestral population. They coalesced as a distinct nation in the sixteenth century, organized in three great divisions: the western Okla Falaya, the eastern Okla Tannap and the southern Okla Hannali of the Six Towns. French records first document them in the following century, and their tradition remembers the chief Tuscaloosa, who died facing Hernando de Soto at the Battle of Mabila in 1540, called the first major pitched battle between Europeans and Native Americans in North America. Through the colonial years the Choctaw traded and allied in turn with the French, British and Spanish, and after American independence they fought beside the United States in the War of 1812, where the chief Pushmataha made his name, and at the Battle of New Orleans. Classed among the Five Civilized Tribes, they nevertheless lost their lands through a series of treaties; after the Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek in 1830, most Choctaw were forcibly relocated to Indian Territory between 1831 and 1833.
zh: 乔克托人（自称恰赫塔，乔克托是英语化写法）是分布在密西西比、阿拉巴马和路易斯安那的西马斯科吉语族族群，语言与奇克索语极为接近，两族也共有同出一源的起源传说。他们在16世纪融合为独特的民族，分为三大区域：西部的奥克拉法拉亚、东部的奥克拉塔纳普，以及南部六镇之地的奥克拉汉纳利。法国文献在下一个世纪首次记载他们；乔克托人铭记首领塔斯卡卢萨，他在1540年的马比拉之战中抵抗埃尔南多·德·索托并战死，此战被称为北美原住民与欧洲人之间第一场大规模对阵战。殖民年代里，乔克托人先后与法国、英国和西班牙贸易结盟；美国独立后，他们在1812年战争中站在美国一方，酋长普什马塔哈由此成名，还参加了新奥尔良之战。乔克托人虽被列入五大文明部落，土地仍经一系列条约丧失；1830年《舞兔溪条约》之后，大部分乔克托人在1831至1833年间被强制西迁到印第安领地。

en: The Chokwe are a Bantu people spread across north-eastern Angola, the south-western Congo basin and north-western Zambia, in the savanna lands between the Kasai and the upper Zambezi; they speak Chokwe, a language of the Niger-Congo family. Their chiefs trace shared descent from the Lunda migrations of the sixteenth century, and by the seventeenth century the Chokwe were one of the twelve clans of the Lunda Empire of the Mwata Yanvo, at first serving its nobles as hunters, soldiers and tribute-bearers. After a series of civil disputes and refusals to pay tribute, they broke away from Lunda overlordship and built up their own wealthy village societies, farming with the seasons, hunting, fishing and trading wax, ivory and copper across the interior. Chokwe life was organized through matrilineal lineages and the mukanda initiation schools for boys, while their carvers became famous across the region for ancestor figures, ceremonial chairs and masks such as the female Mwana Pwo and the royal Chibinda Ilunga, memorializing the legendary hunter-prince who married the Lunda queen. Through the eighteenth century their trade and numbers grew, and by the 1830s, when Portuguese caravans first made direct contact, the Chokwe were already a rising power on the ruins of Lunda authority.
zh: 乔奎人是分布在安哥拉东北部、刚果盆地西南部和赞比亚西北部一带的班图人，地处开赛河与赞比西河上游之间的稀树草原，讲尼日尔-刚果语系的绍奎语。他们的酋长把共同世系追溯到16世纪的隆达迁徙；到17世纪，乔奎人已是姆瓦塔·扬武的隆达帝国十二氏族之一，起初以猎人、士兵和纳贡者的身份为隆达贵族效力。在一连串内部争端和拒绝纳贡之后，他们摆脱隆达人的统治，建立起自己富庶的村落社会：按季节农耕、狩猎、捕鱼，并在内陆贩运蜂蜡、象牙和铜。乔奎社会按母系血缘和名为穆坎达的男子入会学校组织起来；他们的雕刻师以祖先雕像、礼仪座椅和面具闻名四方，其中有女性形象姆瓦纳·普沃面具，以及纪念那位娶了隆达女王的传奇猎手王子奇宾达·伊隆加的王室面具。整个18世纪，乔奎人的贸易和人口不断增长；到1830年代葡萄牙商队首次与他们直接接触时，乔奎人已成为趁隆达权威瓦解而崛起的强大势力。

en: The Ch'ol are a Maya people of the northern Chiapas highlands whose Ch'ol language forms the conservative Cholan branch of the Mayan family; with its relatives Chontal, Ch'orti' and the extinct Ch'olti', it counts among the living tongues closest to the Classic Mayan of the hieroglyphic inscriptions of cities such as Palenque. At Spanish contact Ch'ol-speaking groups also held the Lacandon Jungle: the Lakandon Ch'ol had their capital at Lakam-Tun on Laguna Miramar, and in 1524 Hernán Cortés first heard of them while passing through Kejache lands. Expeditions against them began in 1559, and by the end of the sixteenth century they had abandoned Lakam-Tun and founded a new capital, Sac Balam, whose name means white jaguar. From there they raided the Guatemalan highlands and traded cacao and achiote for iron tools with the colonial towns of Verapaz throughout the seventeenth century. The Spanish stormed Sac Balam in 1695; other Ch'ol were gathered into reducciones at Palenque, Tila and Tumbalá, and the last independent Lakandon bands were forcibly relocated in 1712 and absorbed into the highland Maya.
zh: 乔尔人是恰帕斯北部高地的玛雅族群，所用乔尔语属于玛雅语系中保守的乔尔语支；它与春塔尔语、乔尔蒂语以及已消亡的乔尔蒂安语同支，是最接近帕伦克等城邦碑铭所用古典玛雅语的活语言之一。西班牙人到来时，说乔尔语的族群还据有拉坎东丛林：拉坎东乔尔人的都城在米拉马尔湖畔的拉坎通，1524年科尔特斯行经克哈切人之地时首次听说他们。1559年西班牙人开始出兵征讨，到16世纪末，拉坎东乔尔人放弃拉坎通，另建都城萨克巴兰，意为“白美洲豹”。整个17世纪，他们从那里袭击危地马拉高地，又用可可和胭脂树果与韦拉帕斯的殖民城镇交换铁器。1695年西班牙人攻陷萨克巴兰；其余乔尔人被集中迁到帕伦克、蒂拉和通巴拉的“集村”，最后一批独立的拉坎东残部于1712年被强制迁徙，逐渐融入高地玛雅人之中。

en: The Cholon were the rainforest people of the left bank of the Huallaga River, on the forested eastern slope of the Andes in what is now the Huanuco and San Martín region, their villages strung along the river from Tingo María downstream toward Valle. Cholon is the name the Spaniards gave them; in their own tongue, Seeptsá, they called themselves and their language, and Seeptsá together with the closely related Hibito formed a small language family believed to have once been an important means of communication across the eastern Andean foothills. They lived by slash-and-burn farming, hunting and fishing, while the women grew cotton and wove cloth, and for centuries they kept up trade with the highland Hibito across the Huallaga, exchanging feathers, wax, honey, cotton, coca, hardwoods and medicinal herbs for stone and metal axes. They also carried the poisonous fang of a serpent as a charm against snakebite. The outside world knew them only through missionaries: the Franciscans made first contact and founded mission villages among them in 1676, and in the eighteenth century the friar Pedro de la Mata wrote a grammar of Seeptsá, the Arte de la Lengua Cholona, while Bishop Baltasar Martínez Compañón recorded a Cholon word list between 1782 and 1785. As the colonial centuries passed, Quechua and Spanish steadily displaced the old language along the Huallaga.
zh: 乔隆人是安第斯山脉东坡雨林中瓦亚加河左岸的森林族群，生活在今天的瓦努科和圣马丁地区，村落沿瓦亚加河从廷戈玛丽亚向下游一直分布到巴列一带。乔隆是西班牙人对他们的称呼，他们用本族语自称塞普察，其语言也叫这个名字；塞普察语与关系很近的希维托语共同构成一个小语系，学界认为它曾是安第斯东部山麓一带重要的交际语言。他们以刀耕火种、狩猎和捕鱼为生，妇女种植棉花并织布；几百年来，他们与瓦亚加河对岸高原上的希维托人保持贸易，用羽毛、蜂蜡、蜂蜜、棉花、古柯、硬木和药材交换石斧与金属斧。他们还把毒蛇的毒牙带在身上当作护身符，相信能防蛇咬。外界主要通过传教士了解他们：1676年方济各会首次与他们接触并在其中建立传教村，18世纪修士佩德罗·德拉马塔撰写了塞普察语语法《乔隆语的艺术》，巴尔塔萨尔·马丁内斯·孔帕尼翁主教又在1782年至1785年间记录了一份乔隆语词汇表。随着殖民岁月推移，克丘亚语和西班牙语沿瓦亚加河逐渐取代了这种古老语言。

en: The Chono of the Ecuadorian lowlands, known to archaeology as the Milagro-Quevedo culture, held the Guayas river basin from about 400, a network of navigable waterways formed by the Daule and Babahoyo rivers in what is now Los Ríos and Guayas provinces. Probably of Amazonian origin and kin to the Omagua, they farmed the floodplain with raised fields called camellones and tola mounds, and their position between the Pacific coast and the Andes made them the great middlemen of the region: canoes carried salt, dried fish, cotton, cacao, Esmeraldas gold and copper axe-money between the Manta and Huancavilca on one side and the Cañari, Puruhá and Quitu on the other, while their potters stamped snake and frog motifs onto the ceremonial vessels called cocinas de brujo, or witches' kitchens. The Incas never entered their country in force and received only occasional tribute. After 1534 the Chono chief Guayaquile led fierce resistance and destroyed the first Spanish settlements on the gulf named after him; once subdued, the Chono country was absorbed into the Real Audiencia of Quito, its chiefs reduced to tribute collectors under the encomienda.
zh: 低地乔诺人在考古学上称米拉格罗—克韦多文化，约400年起据守瓜亚斯河流域，即道莱河与巴巴奥约河构成的通航水网，地在今洛斯里奥斯省和瓜亚斯省。他们可能源自亚马逊，与奥马瓜人有亲缘关系，以名为卡梅列内斯的台田和托拉土墩经营洪泛区农业；地处太平洋沿岸与安第斯山之间的要冲，使他们成为地区大中间商：独木舟把盐、鱼干、棉花、可可、埃斯梅拉达斯黄金和铜斧币，在曼塔人、万卡维尔卡人与佳纳利人、普鲁哈人、基多人之间转运，陶工则在名为巫师灶的礼器上压印蛇和蛙的纹样。印加人从未大举进入其地，只得到零星贡赋。1534年之后，乔诺酋长瓜亚基莱领导激烈抵抗，摧毁了以他为名的海湾畔最早的西班牙居民点；被征服后，乔诺之地并入基多检审法院，酋长们沦为监护征赋制下的收税人。

en: The Yoko t'aanob, more widely called the Chontal Maya of Tabasco, call themselves the speakers of Yoko ochoco, while the name Chontal comes from the Nahuatl word for foreigner and the older chronicles often call them the Putun. They live in the lagoon-and-river lowlands of Tabasco, a country that was the cradle of the Olmecs and later a Maya heartland. In the Terminal Classic their canoe-borne merchants came to dominate the river and coastal trade routes of the Maya lowlands, and their homeland remained a neutral meeting ground where merchants from hostile powers did business. On the eve of the conquest they were divided into six provinces, among them Potonchan, Xicalango, Acalan and Zahuatan-Chilapa, with Potonchan and Jalapa holding perhaps thirteen thousand people each; cacao, fish and maize made the region rich, and Nahua settlers in Xicalango often shared in its rule. The Spanish arrived in 1518 with Juan de Grijalva's voyage, and in 1519 Hernan Cortes met the chief Tabscoob, whose people became the first in New Spain to acknowledge the Spanish emperor and gave Cortes the interpreter La Malinche. Colonial epidemics and the spread of cattle ranching emptied most of the old towns, and Nacajuca, where the first church was built in 1614, became the only urban centre to survive the period.
zh: 琼塔尔人通常被称为塔巴斯科的琼塔尔玛雅人，自称“约科奥乔科语的使用者”；“琼塔尔”一名来自纳瓦特尔语中意为外乡人的词，较早的编年史则常称他们为普顿人。他们居住在塔巴斯科河汊纵横、潟湖遍布的低地，这里曾是奥尔梅克文明的摇篮，后来又是玛雅人的腹地。古典期末期，他们驾独木舟经商的商人逐渐控制了玛雅低地的河道与沿海商路，其故土也成为敌对强权的商人都能做买卖的中立贸易场。征服前夕，他们分为波东钱、希卡兰戈、阿克兰、萨瓦坦—奇拉帕等六个行省，仅波东钱和哈拉帕两城就各有约一万三千人口；可可、鱼和玉米使这一地区十分富庶，定居希卡兰戈的纳瓦人也常参与统治。1518年，胡安·德·格里哈尔瓦的航船最先抵达；1519年，埃尔南·科尔特斯会见首领塔布斯库布，琼塔尔人成为新西班牙最早承认西班牙皇帝的族群，并把翻译拉·马林切送给科尔特斯。殖民地时期的疫病和牧牛业的扩张使多数旧城凋敝，1614年建起第一座教堂的纳卡胡卡成为唯一幸存下来的城镇中心。

en: The Chorotega, also called the Mangue, are an Oto-Manguean-speaking people who at the time of Spanish contact in the sixteenth century occupied the Pacific lowlands of Nicaragua and Honduras, northwestern Costa Rica and, in smaller numbers, eastern El Salvador. Linguistic and archaeological evidence suggests their ancestors split from the Chiapanec and moved south out of central Mexico around the seventh century, reaching the Rivas region of Nicaragua by about 800, where Papagayo polychrome ceramics mark their arrival. Around 1200 the incoming Nicarao displaced them from Rivas onto the Nicoya Peninsula. Their towns were laid out around central plazas with temples and markets, and councils of elders appointed provincial rulers in a kind of elective monarchy. They made the painted Nicoya polychrome ware and farmed maize, cotton and tobacco. After the Spanish conquest of the sixteenth century many Chorotega were enslaved and shipped to Panama and Callao in Peru, and their communities declined under colonial rule.
zh: 乔罗特加人又称曼格人，讲奥托-曼格语系语言。16世纪与西班牙人接触时，他们分布在尼加拉瓜和洪都拉斯的太平洋低地、哥斯达黎加西北部，另有少量人住在萨尔瓦多东部。语言学和考古证据显示，其先民约在7世纪与恰帕斯人分离，自墨西哥中部南迁，约800年抵达尼加拉瓜的里瓦斯地区，帕帕加约彩陶是他们到来的标志。约1200年，迁入的尼卡拉奥人把他们从里瓦斯赶到尼科亚半岛。他们的城镇围绕中央广场修建，配有神庙和市场，长老会议以一种选举君主制的方式任命地方统治者。他们制作彩绘的尼科亚陶器，种植玉米、棉花和烟草。16世纪西班牙征服后，许多乔罗特加人被掳为奴，运往巴拿马和秘鲁的卡亚俄，其社群在殖民统治下走向衰落。

en: The Chorti are the Maya people of the borderlands where eastern Guatemala, western Honduras and northern El Salvador meet, and their speech is the closest living relative of the Classic Maya language carved on the stelae of Copan. Copan itself was their great ancestral city: founded in 426 by the king Yax K'uk' Mo', its dynasty ruled for nearly four hundred years and made the valley a centre of Maya sculpture, astronomy and hieroglyphic writing. After the Classic collapse the Chorti remained in the same hill country, and on the eve of the Spanish invasion they were organized in a confederacy called the Payaki kingdom, spanning the districts around Copan, Ocotepeque and Chiquimula. Their leader Copan Galel led the resistance against the conquistadors, first fighting near the ruins of Copan and then making a stand at Citala, where defeat forced him to surrender and accept baptism. Under colonial rule the old territory shrank to a belt of farming villages in the Guatemalan department of Chiquimula and the Honduran highlands, while in El Salvador only a few communities around Tejutla kept their Chorti ancestry. Their traditional religion honoured the gods of earth and wind, and their music and maize-based customs survived in the villages of the former Payaki lands.
zh: 乔尔蒂人是生活在危地马拉东部、洪都拉斯西部和萨尔瓦多北部交界地带的玛雅民族，他们的语言与科潘石碑铭文所用的古典玛雅语亲缘最近。科潘正是他们祖先的伟大城市：君王亚什·库克·莫于426年建城，他开创的王朝统治近四百年，使这座河谷成为玛雅雕塑、天文和象形文字的中心。古典期崩溃后，乔尔蒂人仍留在同一片丘陵地区；西班牙人入侵前夕，他们组成名为帕亚基王国的联盟，疆域涵盖科潘、奥科特佩克和奇基穆拉一带。首领科潘·加莱尔率众抵抗征服者，先在科潘遗址附近迎战，又在西塔拉固守，最终战败投降并接受洗礼。殖民统治下，古老的疆域缩小为危地马拉奇基穆拉省和洪都拉斯高地的一条农耕村落带；在萨尔瓦多，只有特胡特拉周边的少数社群保留了乔尔蒂血统。他们的传统宗教敬奉地神与风神，音乐和以玉米为核心的习俗在昔日帕亚基土地上的村庄里延续下来。

en: The Chǔ culture is the people of Hubei, the lake and river country of the middle Yangtze centred on Jiangling and Wuchang. In the Zhou era this was the kingdom of Chu, also called Jingchu, whose capital Ying stood near present-day Jingzhou and whose poets, headed by Qu Yuan, created the Songs of Chu tradition before Qin annexed the state in 223 BCE. After the Mongol conquest it formed the heart of Huguang province, a name the Ming retained after driving out the Yuan in 1368. Its river towns grew with the Yangtze and Han waterways, and their speech belongs to Southwestern Mandarin, spread through the region by the great Ming and Qing migrations that repopulated the upper Yangtze. The late Ming brought devastation: the armies of Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong ravaged Hubei in the 1630s and 1640s, the Qing took control in 1644 and 1645, and in the 1660s they split Huguang into the separate provinces of Hubei and Hunan. Wuchang and the riverside towns at the Han confluence then grew into busy inland trading cities.
zh: 楚文化的主体是湖北人，即长江中游以江陵县和武昌为中心、湖河纵横的江汉之民。周代这里是又称荆楚的楚国，郢都就在今荆州一带；公元前223年秦灭楚之前，以屈原为代表的楚国诗人开创了楚辞传统。蒙古征服后，这一带成为湖广省的核心，1368年明朝驱逐元廷后沿用了湖广的建制。凭借长江与汉水的水运，沿江城镇日渐兴盛，当地话属于西南官话，是明清大规模移民填充长江上游时扩散开来的。明末再遭兵燹：17世纪30至40年代，李自成、张献忠的军队多次蹂躏湖北，清朝在1644至1645年取得控制，17世纪60年代又将湖广分为湖北、湖南两省。此后武昌与汉水汇入长江处的几座城镇发展为清代繁忙的内陆商埠。

en: The Chugashigmuit, more commonly spelled Chugachigmiut or Chugach Sugpiaq, are an Alutiiq people of the southern Alaskan coast, centered on the Kenai Peninsula and Prince William Sound, where villages such as Nanwalek and Nuchek stood. Their autonym Sugpiaq means “real person,” and their speech is the Chugach dialect of Alutiiq, a Pacific Gulf language within the Yupik family. For millennia they lived from the sea, hunting sea mammals and fishing from skin boats, and they alternately traded and fought with the neighbouring Eyak, Ahtna and Tlingit. In 1741 they became the first indigenous Alaskans to meet Europeans when Vitus Bering's Russian expedition reached their shores. Russian fur hunters soon followed, drawing the Chugach into the sea-otter trade of Russian America, and Spanish, British and American explorers visited the sound in the later eighteenth century.
zh: 楚加奇人又称楚加奇苏格皮克人，是阿拉斯加南岸的阿鲁蒂克族群，以基奈半岛和威廉王子湾为中心，南瓦莱克、努切克等村落都在这一带。他们的自称“苏格皮克”意为“真正的人”，所说的话是阿鲁蒂克语的楚加奇方言，属于尤皮克语族下的太平洋海湾语言。数千年来他们靠海为生，乘坐皮艇捕猎海洋哺乳动物、捕鱼，并与相邻的埃亚克人、阿特纳人和特林吉特人时战时和。1741年，维图斯·白令的俄国探险队抵达他们的海岸，楚加奇人由此成为最早接触欧洲人的阿拉斯加原住民。俄国毛皮猎人随后蜂拥而至，把楚加奇人卷入俄属美洲的海獭毛皮贸易，18世纪后期西班牙、英国和美国的探险队也相继到访威廉王子湾。

en: The Chukchi are the aboriginal people of the Chukchi Peninsula and the Arctic and Bering Sea shores of far northeastern Siberia, whose ancestors held the continental Chukotka coast from the turn of the third millennium BC. They call themselves Luoravetlan, genuine people, and divide into two ways of life: the settled Maritime Chukchi, who hunted seal and walrus from coastal villages, and the nomadic Reindeer Chukchi of the inland tundra; the Russian name Chukchi comes from their word for a rich reindeer owner. Russians reached the Kolyma in 1643 and built Anadyrsk in 1649, but expeditions against them in 1701, 1709 and 1729 ended in defeat. Major Dmitry Pavlutsky ravaged their camps from the 1730s, and the extermination war of 1744 to 1747 closed with his death in battle in 1747, his head kept as a trophy. After conquest failed the empire abandoned Anadyrsk in 1764; annual trade fairs on the Anyuy from 1775 and the lower Kolyma from 1788 then drew the Chukchi into the Russian fur economy without subjecting them.
zh: 楚科奇人是西伯利亚极东北楚科奇半岛及北冰洋、白令海沿岸的原住民，其先民自公元前3000年之交便居住在楚科奇大陆海岸。他们自称卢奥拉维特兰，意为真正的人，并分为两种生计群体：沿海定居的海猎楚科奇人在村落中捕猎海豹和海象，内陆苔原的养鹿楚科奇人则随鹿群游牧；俄语中的楚科奇一名，来自他们语言里对养鹿富户的称呼。俄国人1643年进抵科雷马河，1649年建起阿纳德尔堡，但1701、1709和1729年几次出征都告失败。1730年代起，德米特里·帕夫卢茨基少校大肆焚毁营地、掠走驯鹿；1744至1747年的剿灭战争以1747年他本人战死、头颅被楚科奇人留作战利品而告终。征服失败后，俄国于1764年放弃阿纳德尔堡；1775年起在阿纽伊河、1788年起在下科雷马河每年开设集市，将楚科奇人纳入俄国的毛皮经济，却始终没有使他们臣服。

en: The Chumash are a Native American people of the central and southern California coast, whose territory ran from Morro Bay to Malibu and out over the Northern Channel Islands of Santa Cruz, Santa Rosa and San Miguel, where their ancestors have lived for at least eleven thousand years. Before contact they occupied more than 150 independent villages speaking related Chumashan languages, a language isolate. Island craftsmen turned olive shells into beads that served as currency across a trade network reaching as far as Arizona, and boatbuilders built sewn-plank canoes called tomol for fishing, whaling and travel between the islands and the mainland; Chumash rock art and basketry are among the most elaborate in California. Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo made the first European contact in 1542, but large-scale colonization began only with the Portolá expedition of 1769. Between 1772 and 1817 five Franciscan missions, including San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara, drew nearly all Chumash into the mission system, where disease and forced labour cut their population heavily. The Chumash Revolt of 1824, begun at Santa Inés, was one of the largest Native uprisings in Spanish California, and Mexico's secularization of 1833 dissolved the missions without restoring their lands.
zh: 丘马什人是加利福尼亚中南部海岸的原住民，领地从莫罗湾延伸到马利布，并包括圣克鲁斯、圣罗莎和圣米格尔三座北海峡岛屿，其祖先在这一地区至少生活了一万一千年。接触欧洲人之前，他们居住在150多个独立村落里，讲互有亲属关系的丘马什语族诸语，该语族是一门孤立语系。岛上的工匠把海螺壳制成贝珠，作为远达亚利桑那的贸易网络中的货币；造船工制造名为托莫尔的缝合木板独木舟，用于捕鱼、捕鲸以及海岛与大陆之间的往来；丘马什的岩画和编篮也属于加利福尼亚最精美的工艺之列。1542年，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略首次与他们接触，但大规模殖民要到1769年波尔托拉远征之后才开始。1772—1817年间，包括圣路易斯奥维斯波和圣巴巴拉在内的五座方济各会传教站把几乎所有丘马什人纳入传教体系，疫病和苦役使人口锐减。1824年始于圣伊内斯的丘马什起义是西属加利福尼亚规模最大的原住民反抗之一，1833年墨西哥推行世俗化，解散了传教站，却没有把土地归还给他们。

en: The Churajon were the pre-Inca people of the Arequipa region in southern Peru, held by archaeologists to have sprung from Aymara-speaking groups who moved down from the highlands into the warm coastal valleys in search of farmland. Between roughly 600 and 1400 they settled the valleys of the Chili and Tambo rivers and gradually spread over what are now the departments of Arequipa, Moquegua and Tacna, building towns, roads, canals, reservoirs and great stairways of agricultural terraces on the slopes. Their development is divided into an early phase from 800 to 1200, contemporary with the Wari empire, a middle phase of Churajon autonomy from 1200 to 1400, and a late phase under Inca influence. They were above all farmers and herders who grew maize, potatoes, oca, quinoa and chili peppers, organizing production through the Andean practice of controlling different ecological floors at different altitudes; their pottery was simple, globular or cylindrical ware painted in white, black and red with geometric motifs, and their towns of rough stone and mud housed the people as well as the cylindrical burial towers called chullpas. The type site is the sprawling urban ruins of Churajón below the Choquellampa hill, and around 1450 the expansion of the Incas brought the independent Churajon communities into the empire.
zh: 丘拉洪人是秘鲁南部阿雷基帕地区的前印加族群，考古学家认为他们源自讲艾马拉语的群体，为寻找耕地从高原下到温暖的沿海谷地。约600年至1400年间，他们在奇利河与坦博河的谷地定居，逐渐扩展到今天的阿雷基帕、莫克瓜和塔克纳各省，修建了城镇、道路、灌渠、水库以及山坡上层层叠叠的梯田。其发展分为三个阶段：800年至1200年的早期与瓦里帝国同时，1200年至1400年的中期为丘拉洪自主时期，晚期则处于印加影响之下。他们以农耕和畜牧为主，种植玉米、马铃薯、奥卡薯、藜麦和辣椒，并通过安第斯式的垂直生态分层控制来组织生产；陶器风格朴素，多为球形或筒形器，以白、黑、红三色绘出几何纹样，城镇用毛石和泥砌成，除住屋外还有被称为楚尔帕的筒形石墓塔。其代表性遗址是乔克良帕山下占地广阔的丘拉洪城址；约1450年，随着印加人扩张，独立的丘拉洪诸社区被并入印加帝国。

en: The Chutia are a Bodo-Kachari people of eastern Assam, settled cultivators who built the most advanced of the tribal states that arose after the fall of Kamarupa. Their kingdom, also called Sadiya after its capital in the far upper Brahmaputra, took shape in the early thirteenth century and rose to prominence in the later fourteenth, its earliest inscriptionally attested king being Nandisvara. The ruling house showed matrilineal traits and claimed descent from the Asuras, while the people worshipped the god Kundimama and the goddess Kechaikhati, whose temple at Sadiya was served by Deori priests even after the kingdom's fall. Ahom chronicles record a clash in the reign of Sutuphaa between 1369 and 1379 in which the Ahom king was killed, and the border wars begun in 1512 ended in 1523 and 1524 when the Ahom king Suhungmung conquered Sadiya. The Chutia were then dispersed across Upper Assam and absorbed into Ahom society, their craftsmen famed as gunmakers; in the seventeenth century many joined the Vaishnava Ekasarana movement, and their old Tibeto-Burman speech gave way to Assamese.
zh: 久蒂亚人是阿萨姆东部的博多—卡查里系族群，属定居农耕者，建立了迦摩缕波衰落之后诸部族政权中最发达的一个。他们的王国以布拉马普特拉河最上游的萨迪亚为都，又称萨迪亚国，13世纪初成形，14世纪下半叶兴起，碑铭中可考的最早国王是南迪什婆罗。王室带有母系制特征，自称阿修罗后裔；民众信奉昆迪马马男神与凯柴卡蒂女神，萨迪亚女神庙的祭司由代奥里人担任，这一安排在王国灭亡后仍延续。阿洪编年史记载，1369—1379年苏图法在位期间双方发生冲突，阿洪国王被杀；1512年起的边境战争最终在1523—1524年以阿洪国王苏洪蒙征服萨迪亚告终。此后久蒂亚人被分散到阿萨姆上游各地，融入阿洪社会，其工匠以造枪闻名；17世纪许多人皈依毗湿奴虔信派，古老的藏缅语也逐渐为阿萨姆语取代。

en: The Chuukese are a Micronesian people of the Chuuk Lagoon and its outer atolls, in the Caroline Islands of the western Pacific, and speak Chuukese, a Chuukic Micronesian language of the Austronesian family. Their ancestors were Lapita-related Austronesian settlers: excavations show people on lagoon islands by the second and first centuries BC, and a distinct Chuukese culture with widespread villages took shape from the fourteenth century. The lagoon splits into the western Faichuuk and eastern Namoneas island groups, whose clans combined fishing with taro and banana gardening in thatch-built villages and fought intermittent wars under their own chiefs. Álvaro de Saavedra made the first recorded European sighting in 1528 and Alonso de Arellano followed in 1565, and Spain later counted the lagoon among the Caroline Islands, but no foreign power established control there, so in 1837 the Chuukese still governed themselves with only occasional ships passing through.
zh: 楚克人是西太平洋加罗林群岛楚克潟湖及其外围环礁的密克罗尼西亚族群，使用南岛语系密克罗尼西亚语族楚克语支的楚克语。他们的祖先是与拉皮塔文化有关的南岛语定居者，考古发掘显示公元前2—前1世纪潟湖岛屿上已有人居，而村落广布、独具面貌的楚克文化到14世纪才正式形成。潟湖分为西部的法伊楚克与东部的纳莫尼亚斯两组岛群，各氏族在茅草村落中以捕鱼为主，兼种芋艿和香蕉，并在各自酋长率领下断断续续地争战。1528年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉留下了欧洲人最早的目击记录，1565年阿隆索·德·阿雷利亚诺再度抵达；西班牙后来把潟湖算作加罗林群岛的一部分，却从未建立实际统治。因此到1837年，楚克人仍自行管理内部事务，只有偶尔经过的船只打破宁静。

en: The Chuvan were a Yukaghir people of the Anadyr basin, roaming the upper tributaries of the Anadyr and the Anyuy in present-day Chukotka. They lived by hunting, fishing and reindeer breeding and spoke their own Yukaghir tongue, of which a word list was taken down in 1821. In the eighteenth century Chukchi raids broke their clan lands: one part of the people retreated west to the Kolyma, where they gradually adopted Russian speech and ways, while the rest were absorbed by the Koryaks and Chukchi. Mountain and coastal Chuvan groups kept their identity in the Anadyr tundra into the nineteenth century.
zh: 楚万人是尤卡吉尔人的一支，游猎于阿纳德尔河流域，在今楚科奇境内的阿纳德尔河与阿纽伊河上游支流一带。他们以狩猎、捕鱼和养驯鹿为生，说本族的尤卡吉尔语，1821年还有人为这种语言记下了词汇表。18世纪，楚科奇人的袭扰打散了他们的氏族地：一部分人西撤到科雷马河，逐渐改用俄语、接受俄式生活，其余则被科里亚克人和楚科奇人同化。山地楚万与沿海楚万两个群体在阿纳德尔苔原上把自身认同保持到了19世纪。

en: The Chuvash are the only surviving people of the Oghur branch of the Turkic family, settled in the forest-steppe between the Volga and the Sura around Cheboksary and Simbirsk. Their language split from the other Turkic tongues more than a thousand years ago and keeps the distinctive Oghur sounds r and l where other Turks have z and sh; most scholars trace it to the Volga Bulgar speech, mixed with Finnic settlers. They are thus heirs of Volga Bulgaria, whose rulers adopted Islam in 922, but the Mongols sacked the Bulgar state in 1236 and the region passed to the Golden Horde, then to the Khanate of Kazan from the fifteenth century; an inscription of 1307 already records Muslim Chuvash. The name Chuvash itself appears in foreign records only from the sixteenth century, divided into upper Virjal and lower Anatri communities. After Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in 1552 they became Russian taxpayers under the yasak tribute, losing land and being pushed into timber work and barge hauling, while Orthodox missionaries began a long campaign of baptism. Many evaded conversion by moving east among the Bashkirs, as the historian Tatishchev observed in the eighteenth century, and old keremet shrines where geese were sacrificed long survived beside the new churches; the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries also brought Chuvash schools and a growing printed literature in their own tongue.
zh: 楚瓦什人是突厥语族乌古尔语支唯一留存的民族，居住在伏尔加河与苏拉河之间、切博克萨雷和辛比尔斯克一带的森林草原上。他们的语言一千多年前就与其他突厥语分道扬镳，保留着乌古尔语特有的r和l音，而其他突厥语对应为z和sh；多数学者将其追溯到伏尔加保加尔语与芬兰语族居民融合后的形态。因此他们是伏尔加保加利亚的继承者——保加尔统治者于922年改宗伊斯兰教，但蒙古人在1236年洗劫保加尔国家，此地先归金帐汗国，15世纪起又属喀山汗国；1307年的一通铭文已记载了穆斯林楚瓦什人的存在。“楚瓦什”这个名字本身迟至16世纪才出现在外部文献中，其社会分为上游的维尔亚尔和下游的阿纳特里等群体。1552年伊凡雷帝攻占喀山后，他们成为缴纳牙萨克贡赋的俄国属民，土地不断流失，被迫从事伐木和拉纤，东正教传教士也展开长期的洗礼运动。许多人为逃避受洗东迁，投奔巴什基尔人，历史学家塔季谢夫在18世纪便有此记载；而以鹅献祭的古老克列梅特神祠，在新建教堂旁仍长期存留。18至19世纪初，楚瓦什学校陆续兴办，本民族语的印刷文学也开始成长。

en: The Chuwi, also spelled Chuis or Chuwis, were one of the Aymara lordships that took shape on the Bolivian altiplano after the collapse of Tiwanaku and flourished between about 1150 and 1477. Their valleys lay in what are now the departments of Cochabamba and Chuquisaca, around Mizque, and their ayllus formed part of the Charka kingdom of Collasuyu alongside the Chayanta, Sakaka and Qhara Qhara. First overborne by the expanding Charca, the Chuwi later became their allies; the chronicles place them at Sacaca with the Caracara and Chichas when the highland peoples made their pact with the Spaniards. Like the other Aymara señoríos they were absorbed into the Inca state under Túpac Yupanqui, keeping their dual chiefly structure within it.
zh: 丘维人在史籍中又拼作丘伊斯或丘维斯，是蒂亚瓦纳科崩溃后在玻利维亚高原上形成的艾马拉诸领地之一，兴盛于约1150年至1477年间。他们的河谷位于今科恰班巴省和丘基萨卡省境内，以米斯克一带为中心，其村社与查扬塔人、萨卡卡人、卡拉卡拉人等共同组成科利亚苏尤的查克拉王国。丘维人起初被扩张的查尔卡斯人压服，后来反成其盟友；据史籍记载，高原各族与西班牙人缔约时，丘维人曾与卡拉卡拉人、奇查人齐聚萨卡卡。和其他艾马拉领地一样，他们在图帕克·尤潘基时期被并入印加国家，并在其中保留了二元酋长制的社会结构。

en: The Chúzhōu culture covers the mountainous southwest of Zhejiang, the Lishui prefecture of Longquan, Qingtian, Suichang and Songyang, reaching across the Fujian border to Pucheng. A Chuzhou Prefecture was first set up by the Sui in 589; after centuries under the names Kuozhou and Lishui, the Yuan made it Chuzhou Route in 1276, and it became Chuzhou Prefecture under the Ming. Nearly nine-tenths of the land is mountains, and its isolated valleys made the Chuzhou division of Southern Wu one of the most fragmented groups of Wu speech, while the Ou River carried its goods downstream to the port of Wenzhou. Longquan was one of China's greatest ceramic centers: its green celadon, in large-scale production from the Northern Song, boomed after the Southern Song court moved to nearby Hangzhou, held high quality through the Yuan and early Ming, and was exported across the eastern seas for five centuries before Jingdezhen blue-and-white displaced it. The same county kept the ancient Longquan craft of sword-making, while Qingtian became known for its carved soapstone.
zh: 处州文化位于浙江西南山区，即丽水一带的龙泉、青田、遂昌、松阳等地，并翻过省界延伸到福建浦城。589年隋朝首次设置处州，此后长期在括州、丽水等名称间沿革，1276年元代改为处州路，明代定为处州府。这里近九成地面是山地，闭塞的山谷使南部吴语处州片内部分化极大，各县口音彼此难懂；瓯江则把山货顺流送到温州港。龙泉是中国历史上最大的青瓷产区之一：北宋时已大规模烧造，南宋朝廷迁到邻近的杭州后更是盛极一时，元代至明初仍保持高水平，五百多年间经海路大量外销，最终被景德镇青花瓷挤出市场。龙泉还传承着古老的铸剑技艺，青田则以青田石雕刻闻名。

en: The Ciboney, or Siboney, were the dominant Indigenous people of central Cuba at the coming of the Spanish, and were also found on the Tiburon Peninsula of western Hispaniola and possibly Jamaica.
