Scholars who treat them as Western Taíno note that their dialect was mutually intelligible with Classic Taíno and closely akin to the speech of the Lucayans in the Bahamas, though their society was less centralized: unlike the great chiefdoms of Hispaniola, the Ciboney had no island-wide political structure. They were the most numerous group on Cuba until around 1450, when Classic Taíno migrants from Hispaniola began occupying the eastern province of Oriente; after the Spanish invasion of Hispaniola the flow became a flood of refugees, among them the chief Hatuey, who was captured and burned in Cuba. Diego Velázquez began the conquest of Cuba in 1511, and within a generation war, enslavement and epidemic had broken all the island's Native communities, so that the Ciboney ceased to exist as a distinct people before the end of the sixteenth century.
zh: 西沃内人（又译西波内人）是西班牙人到来时古巴中部占主导地位的原住民，在伊斯帕尼奥拉西部的蒂布龙半岛、可能还有牙买加也有分布。将其归入“西部泰诺”的学者指出，西沃内方言与经典泰诺语可以互通，且和巴哈马卢卡约人的语言十分接近，但他们的社会集权程度较低：与伊斯帕尼奥拉的大酋邦不同，西沃内人没有全岛性的政治组织。约1450年以前，他们一直是古巴人数最多的族群；此后来自伊斯帕尼奥拉的经典泰诺移民开始占据东部的奥连特省，西班牙入侵伊斯帕尼奥拉后更引发难民潮，酋长哈图伊便是其中之一，他最终在古巴被西班牙人逮捕并烧死。1511年，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯开始征服古巴，短短一代人的时间里，战争、奴役和疫病便摧毁了岛上所有的原住民社群，到16世纪末，西沃内人已不再作为一个独立族群存在。

en: The Ciguayo were a non-Taíno people of north-eastern Hispaniola, holding the Samaná Peninsula, the coast from Nagua down to the Yuna River and the northern mountains then called Ciguay. They seem to have been heirs of an older, pre-ceramic hunter-gatherer population of the Antilles, who made no pottery and were pushed into this corner by the expansion of the farming Taíno; Ciguayo itself was a Taíno exonym meaning roughly people of the wild mountain land. Spanish observers found them taller than the Taíno, their bodies painted black and their long hair dressed with feathers, and feared them as archers who carried larger bows and poisoned arrows, a craft they shared with the Kalinago of the Lesser Antilles. Their tongue struck Ramón Pané and Las Casas as wholly unlike the common speech of the island, and it was already moribund in the sixteenth century, surviving only around Samaná; a single word, tuob for gold, was recorded, on which modern linguists have built a speculative link to the Tol language of Honduras. Their last chief, Mayobanex, sheltered the fugitive Taíno cacique Guarionex, but Spanish campaigns overran the country and both men were seized, Guarionex being shipped in chains to Spain in 1502.
zh: 西瓜约人是伊斯帕尼奥拉东北部的非泰诺族群，据有萨马纳半岛、从纳瓜向南至尤纳河的海岸，以及当时名叫西瓜伊的北部山地。他们似乎是安的列斯群岛更古老的前陶器时代狩猎采集人群的后裔，不制陶器，在务农的泰诺人扩张下被挤压到这个角落；“西瓜约”本身是泰诺语给的他称，大意是“荒野山地之民”。西班牙观察者发现他们比泰诺人更高大，身涂黑染料，长发饰以羽毛，并畏惧他们的弓箭：其弓更大，箭镞涂毒，这套射术与小安的列斯的卡利纳戈人同源。拉蒙·帕内和拉斯卡萨斯都注意到，西瓜约语与岛上的通用语言完全不同；到16世纪它已濒临消亡，只在萨马纳一带残存，记录在案的词只有一个表示“黄金”的 tuob，后世语言学家据此推测它可能与洪都拉斯的托尔语有亲缘关系。末代酋长马约瓦内克斯曾收留逃亡的泰诺酋长瓜里奥内克斯，但西班牙的征伐踏平了这片土地，两人先后被俘，瓜里奥内克斯于1502年被锁拿装船送往西班牙。

en: The Circassians, who call themselves Adyghe, are the indigenous people of the north-eastern Black Sea coast and the Kuban basin, a country the ancients called Zichia. Greek and Byzantine missions made them Christians between the third and fifth centuries, and after the fall of the Khazars they were drawn into the Kingdom of Alania and, from the tenth to thirteenth centuries, the Georgian orbit. They enter these centuries as the Kassogs, organized in rival tribal principalities under princes and nobles; Mongol raids from 1223 and later Golden Horde and Timurid attacks drove them back behind the Kuban, and Timur sacked their lands in 1395. Meanwhile Circassian mamluks seized power in Egypt in 1382, founding the Burji dynasty that ruled there until 1517. In the fifteenth century Prince Inal the Great united the tribes from his base in the Taman peninsula, created the eastern principality of Kabardia in 1434 and pushed the Crimean Tatars beyond the Kuban, but his sons split the inheritance after 1453 into the dozen tribes of later Circassia. Genoese ports linked them to Black Sea trade, while travelling Sufi preachers and the Russian threat spread Sunni Islam, which became general in the eighteenth century; the Kabardians shattered a Crimean invasion at Kanzhal in 1708, and the Treaty of Belgrade recognized Kabardia's independence in 1739. From Peter I's time Russian forts crept down the Terek and Kuban, opening the long mountain war of resistance.
zh: 切尔克斯人自称阿迪格，是黑海东北岸和库班河流域的原住民，古人称这片土地为济希亚。3至5世纪，在希腊和拜占庭传教团影响下他们皈依基督教；可萨汗国灭亡后，他们被纳入阿兰王国，并在10至13世纪处于格鲁吉亚势力范围内。这一时期他们以卡索格人之名见于记载，社会由若干敌对的部落公国组成，上有王公贵族。1223年起蒙古人入侵，其后金帐汗国和帖木儿的攻击把他们逼回库班河以南，帖木儿于1395年洗劫了他们的土地。与此同时，切尔克斯马穆鲁克于1382年在埃及夺权，建立了统治那里直至1517年的布尔吉王朝。15世纪，伊纳尔大王以塔曼半岛为基地统一诸部，1434年在东部建立卡巴尔达公国，将克里木鞑靼人逐至库班河以北；但1453年后他的儿子们瓜分遗产，形成后来切尔克斯的十二部落。热那亚港口把他们接入黑海贸易，云游的苏菲传道者和俄国的威胁则推动了逊尼派伊斯兰教的传播，到18世纪改宗已相当普遍；1708年卡巴尔达人在坎扎尔歼灭一支克里木入侵军，1739年的《贝尔格莱德条约》承认卡巴尔达独立。从彼得一世时代起，俄国堡垒沿捷列克河和库班河步步推进，开启了山民漫长的抗俄战争。

en: The Coahuilteco, whom the Spanish also called Pajalates or Pakawa, were not a single tribe but a loose web of perhaps two hundred small nomadic bands sharing related speech and customs across Coahuila, Nuevo León, Tamaulipas and Texas, from the Edwards Plateau to the northern sierras of Tamaulipas. Most camped along rivers and lagoons, hunting bison, deer and peccary, taking fish and shellfish, and gathering mesquite, agave, cactus fruit and acorns, with a little farming only in southern Tamaulipas. The missionary Damián Massanet, traveling from Candela to San Antonio in 1690 and 1691, counted thirty-nine groups along his route and found they all spoke the same language, and in 1760 Fray Bartolomé García compiled a worship manual in Coahuilteco for the San Antonio and Guerrero missions. After learning to ride, many bands took to raiding ranches and roads for horses and mules and then melting back into the desert. From the late seventeenth century Lipan Apache expansion, itself speeded by the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, drove Coahuilteco refugees into the Spanish missions around San Antonio. By the end of the eighteenth century the missions were closing, and by 1800 only a handful of named Coahuilteco bands remained, their identity dissolving into the mission and ranch populations.
zh: 科阿韦尔特科人，西班牙人又称帕哈拉特人或帕卡瓦人，并非单一部落，而是由约两百个语言习俗相近的游牧小群体结成的松散网络，散布在科阿韦拉、新莱昂、塔毛利帕斯和得克萨斯，北起爱德华兹高原，南抵塔毛利帕斯北部山地。他们大多在河流与湖沼畔扎营，猎捕野牛、鹿和西貒，捕鱼捞贝，采集牧豆、龙舌兰、仙人掌果和橡子，只有塔毛利帕斯南部略有农业。传教士达米安·马萨内特于1690和1691年从坎德拉前往圣安东尼奥，沿途清点出三十九个群体，发现他们讲的是同一种语言；1760年，修士巴托洛梅·加西亚为圣安东尼奥和格雷罗的传教站用科阿韦尔特科语编写了礼拜手册。学会骑马后，许多群体转而袭击牧场和道路，抢夺马匹骡子，再遁入沙漠。17世纪后期起，利潘阿帕奇人不断扩张，1680年的普韦布洛起义更助长了这一势头，把科阿韦尔特科难民逐入圣安东尼奥一带的西班牙传教站。到18世纪末传教站相继关闭，1800年时只剩寥寥数个仍有名号的科阿韦尔特科群体，其身份逐渐消融在传教站和牧场的居民之中。

en: The Cochimí were the hunter-gatherer people of the arid central Baja California peninsula, spread from El Rosario in the north to San Javier in the south. With no agriculture or metal, they roamed in autonomous small bands, feuding frequently with one another and living on desert game, shellfish and the seasonal pitahaya cactus fruit, whose seeds they even recovered and roasted in a so-called second harvest; shamans officiated in capes woven from donated human hair and painted wooden tablets. Their Cochimí speech forms the Yuman-Cochimí family together with the Yuman languages of the lower Colorado. Spanish seaborne explorers of the sixteenth century, among them Ulloa, Cabrillo and Vizcaíno, made the first fleeting contacts, and from 1699 the Jesuits built a mission chain across their land, beginning at San Javier and reaching Santa María by 1767. When the crown expelled the Jesuits in 1768 the Franciscans and then the Dominicans took over, but Old World epidemics had already shattered the Cochimí communities, whose surviving families were absorbed into the mission settlements.
zh: 科奇米人是下加利福尼亚半岛中部干旱地带的狩猎采集族群，分布范围北起埃尔罗萨里奥，南至圣哈维尔。他们没有农业和金属器，以自治的小群体游走荒漠，群体间常相仇杀，靠沙漠猎物、贝类和季节性的皮特阿亚仙人掌果为生，甚至把排出的仙人掌籽淘出烤熟，称为“第二次收获”；萨满身披用人发编织的斗篷、使用彩绘木牌主持仪式。他们的科奇米语与科罗拉多河下游的尤曼语族共同组成尤曼—科奇米语系。16世纪，乌略亚、卡布里略、比斯凯诺等西班牙海上探险家与他们有过短暂接触；从1699年起，耶稣会在其土地上修建一连串传教站，以圣哈维尔为起点，到1767年已延伸至圣玛丽亚。1768年王室驱逐耶稣会后，方济各会和多明我会先后接手，但旧大陆的传染病早已重创科奇米社群，幸存的家族被并入传教定居点。

en: The Cocopah, who call themselves Xawiƚƚ Kwñchawaay, the people of the cloudy river, and are also known as Kwapa, are a Yuman people of the lower Colorado River delta, where the river meets the Gulf of California between present-day Arizona, Sonora and Baja California. Their Patayan ancestors farmed the annual floodplain and combined maize and bean planting with hunting, fishing and gathering, and the historic Cocopah kept this riverine life, paddling tule-reed rafts through the delta and walking long trails to visit Paipai and Kumeyaay kin in the uplands. In 1540 Hernando de Alarcón, sailing with Coronado's expedition, became the first European to meet them, finding tall, sturdy warriors armed with wooden clubs, bows and arrows who greeted the ships with gifts of shells, beads and food; Juan de Oñate's expedition recorded their name in 1605. Their Cocopah language belongs to the Delta-California branch of the Yuman family, within the wider Hokan grouping.
zh: 哈维希‑库尼查瓦伊人即通称的科科帕人，意为“云河之民”，又称夸帕人，是科罗拉多河下游三角洲的尤曼语族群，家园在科罗拉多河注入加利福尼亚湾的河口地带，横跨今亚利桑那、索诺拉和下加利福尼亚三地。他们的祖先是帕塔扬文化的农人，在每年泛滥的滩地上种植玉米和菜豆，兼营狩猎、捕鱼和采集；历史上的科科帕人延续这种河畔生活，撑着香蒲草筏穿行三角洲，还沿古道长途跋涉，到高地探望派派人和库梅亚伊人的亲族。1540年，随科罗纳多远征队航行的埃尔南多·德·阿拉尔孔成为第一个见到他们的欧洲人，发现这些高大结实的武士手持木棒、弓箭，还以贝壳、珠串和食物相赠；1605年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特的探险队记下了他们的名字。科科帕语属尤曼语系的三角洲—加利福尼亚分支，归入更宽泛的霍坎语群。

en: The Collique, also called Colli, were the lords of the lower and middle Chillon valley on the central Peruvian coast, holding the land from the sea up to Chuquicoto, on the border with the Canta. Their polity, which flourished from about 900 to 1470, was ruled by a curaca titled Collicapac from the fortress of Collique, its main ceremonial centre. A warlike people, the Colli fought repeated wars over water and farmland, once raiding into the Lima valley; the Huarochiri Manuscript records their war against the Checa and Concha of the Yauyos, in which they lost part of their highland territory, although they still traded and built irrigation works together with the Canta. When Tupac Yupanqui's army entered the valley the Colli refused to submit, trusting in their fortress. The Inca stormed it, killed Collicapac and his warriors, and resettled the survivors; mitimaes colonists were brought in, an Ichma lord was placed over the valley, and the fortress was replaced by the tambo of Tambo Inga.
zh: 科利克人又称科利人，是秘鲁中部沿海奇永河中下游的统治者，领地从海边一直延伸到与坎塔接壤的丘基科托。他们的政权约在900至1470年间兴盛，首领称科利卡帕克，以科利克要塞为主要祭祀中心。科利人尚武，为水源和耕地连年征战，一度攻入利马河谷；《瓦罗奇里手稿》记载了他们与尧约斯人大族群中的切卡人和孔查人的战争，他们在这场战争中失去了部分高地领土，不过仍与坎塔人通商并共同修建灌溉工程。图帕克·尤潘基的军队进入河谷时，科利人自恃要塞坚固，拒绝臣服。印加人攻克要塞，杀死科利卡帕克和他的战士，将幸存者迁走，又迁入米蒂马埃斯移民，任命一位伊奇马首领统辖河谷，要塞被废弃，代之以坦博印加驿寨。

en: The Esto'k Gna, who called themselves Estok, meaning the people, were known to the Spanish as the Comecrudo, raw-meat eaters, or Carrizo, reeds. They held the lower Río Bravo delta in northern Tamaulipas and southern Texas, close to the Gulf coast, and spoke the extinct Comecrudan tongues, grouped within Coahuiltecan but distinct from the Coahuilteco language itself. Seasonally seminomadic, they wintered in sheltered canyons such as Mamulique and moved each spring to the Sabinas River to fish, hunting with bows and a few traded muskets, with dogs their only camp animals. They enter the written record in 1747, when their leader Captain Santiago answered José de Escandón's smoke signals near Matamoros and gave the names of thirty native bands along the lower river, his own people apparently the most numerous. In 1749 the mission of San Joaquín del Monte was founded near Reynosa, and in 1750 Escandón counted 149 Comecrudo settled there. When Reynosa moved downstream in 1802 most families stayed on the old bank. Through these years they bore Comanche and Kiowa raids from the plains, and the 1827 boundary commission of Manuel Mier y Terán left the last detailed portrait of their daily life.
zh: 埃斯托克纳人自称埃斯托克，意为人，西班牙人则叫他们科梅克鲁多，意为食生肉者，或称卡里索人，意为芦苇人。他们占据塔毛利帕斯北部与得克萨斯南部的布拉沃河下游三角洲，靠近墨西哥湾沿岸，讲已经消亡的科梅克鲁多诸语；这些语言归入科阿韦尔特卡语群，但与科阿韦尔特科语本身并不相同。他们过着季节性半游牧生活：冬天栖身在马穆利克这样有山丘遮蔽的峡谷，春天举队迁往萨维纳斯河捕鱼，狩猎以弓箭为主，也有少量交易得来的火枪，狗是营地中唯一饲养的家畜。1747年，他们首次见于文字记载：首领圣地亚哥上尉在马塔莫罗斯附近响应何塞·德埃斯坎东的烟火信号，报出了下游沿河三十个土著群体的名号，而他自己的部族显然是三角洲人数最多的一支。1749年，圣华金-德尔蒙特传教站在雷诺萨附近建立；1750年，埃斯坎东清点出在当地定居的科梅克鲁多人有149口。1802年雷诺萨城向下游迁移时，大多数家庭仍留在旧河岸。这一时期他们不断承受来自平原的科曼奇人和基奥瓦人的袭掠；1827年，曼努埃尔·米尔-特兰率领的边界考察队留下了关于他们日常生活最后一份详细记录。

en: The Coos are an Indigenous people of the southwest Oregon coast, whose forty to fifty villages clustered around Coos Bay and the North Bend area, neighbours to the Siuslaw, Kalapuya and Umpqua peoples. They spoke two related tongues, Hanis and Miluk, together forming the small Coosan family often grouped with the Oregon Penutian languages; the two were as close as Dutch and German, and the name Coos may derive from a Hanis word for south or an Athabaskan word for bay. Their combined population has been estimated at about two thousand in 1780. Hunters, fishers and gatherers of the estuaries and forests, they enlivened village life with foot and canoe races, dice games and shinny. Their first appearance in European records came in February 1806, when William Clark, wintering at Fort Clatsop with the Lewis and Clark expedition, heard of the Cook-koo-oose nation and met Coos captives held by the Clatsop and Tillamook, noting that they did not flatten their infants' heads as neighbouring peoples did.
zh: 库斯人是俄勒冈州西南海岸的原住民，四五十座村庄集中在库斯湾和北本德一带，与赛尤斯劳人、卡拉普亚人和安普夸人为邻。他们讲两种相近的语言——哈尼斯语和米卢克语，二者共同构成小小的库斯语族，常被归入俄勒冈佩努蒂语群；两语之近犹如荷兰语与德语，而“库斯”一名可能来自哈尼斯语中意为“南方”的词根，也可能来自阿萨巴斯卡语中意为“海湾”的词。据估计，1780年两支库斯人合计约有两千人。他们在河口湾与森林间狩猎、捕鱼、采集，村落里流行赛跑、独木舟竞速、掷骰和曲棍球游戏。欧洲人对他们的最早记载出现在1806年2月：随刘易斯与克拉克探险队在克拉特索普堡过冬的威廉·克拉克听说了“库库乌斯族”，并见到被克拉特索普人和蒂拉穆克人掳获的库斯俘虏，还注意到他们不像邻族那样压平婴儿的前额。

en: The Coosa were a Muskogean-speaking people of the South Appalachian Mississippian culture, whose paramount chiefdom was centered on the Coosawattee River in present-day northwestern Georgia. Their capital, with a plaza and three platform mounds, ruled eight villages of its own and headed a confederation of seven or more smaller chiefdoms stretching some four hundred miles across northern Georgia, eastern Tennessee and central Alabama, perhaps fifty thousand people in all. Hernando de Soto's expedition passed through in 1540 and found fertile gardens and well-stocked towns, and the Spanish expeditions of Tristán de Luna in 1560 and Juan Pardo from 1566 to 1568 followed. Old World diseases then emptied the countryside: by the close of the sixteenth century the core lands had been abandoned, and the survivors regrouped in fortified villages on the Coosa River in Alabama. The town of Coosa lived on as one of the four mother towns of the Muscogee Creek confederacy.
zh: 库萨人是操马斯科吉语的南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化族群，其最高酋长国以今佐治亚州西北部的库萨瓦蒂河为中心。都城设有广场和三座台庙，直辖八座村镇，还统领七个或更多小酋长国组成的联盟，沿阿巴拉契亚山脉绵亘约四百英里，横跨佐治亚北部、田纳西东部与阿拉巴马中部，总人口可能达五万。1540年埃尔南多·德·索托的探险队经过此地，见到丰饶的园圃和储粮充足的村镇；1560年特里斯坦·德·卢纳以及1566至1568年胡安·帕尔多率领的西班牙远征队也先后抵达。此后旧大陆传来的疫病使乡野人口锐减，到16世纪末核心地带已被废弃，幸存者退守阿拉巴马境内库萨河畔设防的村落。库萨镇后来成为马斯科吉克里克联盟的四大母镇之一。

en: The Copts are the native Christian people of Egypt, descended from the ancient Egyptians and settled chiefly in Cairo, Alexandria and the towns and villages of the Nile valley, especially Upper Egypt. Their traditional language, Coptic, is the last stage of the ancient Egyptian language, written in an alphabet based on Greek; after the Arab conquest of 641 Arabic gradually took its place in daily life, while Coptic survived as the language of the liturgy. Christianity reached Egypt in the first century through Saint Mark, and the Egyptian desert gave birth to Christian monasticism through Anthony and Pachomius. After the Council of Chalcedon in 451 the Egyptian church separated from that of the empire and became the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria. Under the caliphs and later the Mamluks, Copts paid the jizya tax and endured cycles of tolerance and persecution, with repeated tax revolts; they ceased to form a majority of Egypt's population after the fourteenth century. Under Ottoman rule they were grouped within the Armenian millet, and in the early nineteenth century Muhammad Ali opened the army and state service to them, improving their position.
zh: 科普特人是埃及本土的基督教民族，为古埃及人的后裔，主要聚居在开罗、亚历山大以及尼罗河谷地尤其是上埃及的城镇与村庄。他们的传统语言科普特语是古埃及语的最后阶段，用一套以希腊字母为基础的文字书写；641年阿拉伯征服后，阿拉伯语逐渐取代了它在日常生活中的位置，科普特语则作为礼拜用语留存。基督教于1世纪由圣马可传入埃及，埃及沙漠还因圣安东尼和帕科缪而成为基督教修道制度的摇篮。451年迦克墩公会议后，埃及教会与帝国教会决裂，发展为亚历山大科普特正教会。在历代哈里发及后来的马穆鲁克统治下，科普特人缴纳吉兹亚税，在宽容与迫害的交替中数次起义，14世纪以后不再占埃及人口的多数。奥斯曼统治时期他们被归入亚美尼亚米勒特；19世纪初穆罕默德·阿里向他们开放军队和公职，处境有所改善。

en: The Coremas were an Indigenous people of western Paraíba, counted among the Cariri nation and also named in lists of the Tarairiú tribes. They held the valley of the Piancó River, where their principal chief Piancó gave his name to the Vale do Piancó, and the Portuguese village that grew up on their lands became the town of Coremas.
zh: 科雷马斯人是帕拉伊巴西部的原住民，被归入卡里里族，也出现在塔拉伊留联盟诸部的名单中。他们住在皮安科河谷，主要酋长皮安科的名字成为该谷名称皮安科谷的由来；在他们土地上发展起来的葡萄牙村落后来成为科雷马斯镇。

en: The Cornish, who call themselves Kernowyon, are the Brittonic people of the south-western peninsula, heirs of the Dumnonii and Cornovii of the old kingdom of Dumnonia; cut off from the Welsh by the Saxon victory at Deorham, they kept their Brythonic speech, which remained almost mutually intelligible with the Breton of the migrants who crossed to Armorica. King Athelstan fixed the Tamar as their eastern border in 936, and by the late tenth century Cornwall had been incorporated into the English kingdom while keeping its own language, saints and customs. Tin mining shaped the country: the Stannary courts and parliaments governed the mines under privileges confirmed by kings from John to Edward III, and in 1337 Edward III made the earldom a duchy for his son the Black Prince, the first Duke of Cornwall. The advance of English from the fourteenth century met fierce resistance, from the Cornish rebellion of 1497 that marched on London under Michael An Gof to the Prayer Book Rebellion of 1549 against English-only worship; its defeat broke Cornish as a community language, and Dolly Pentreath, popularly its last monolingual speaker, died in 1777. The Cornish then carried their identity through the Methodist chapels of the eighteenth century and as skilled miners, whose craft took them to the mines of Mexico and North America in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 康沃尔人自称 Kernowyon，是西南半岛的布立吞人，为古杜姆诺尼亚王国杜姆诺尼人和科尔诺维人的后裔；撒克逊人在迪奥勒姆之战获胜，切断了他们与威尔士人的陆路联系，他们便保住了自己的布立吞语，这种语言与渡海迁居阿摩里卡的布列塔尼人所说的布列塔尼语几乎可以互通。936年阿塞尔斯坦国王以塔马河为其东界，到10世纪末康沃尔已被并入英格兰王国，却仍保留自己的语言、圣徒和风俗。采锡业塑造了这个地区：斯坦纳里法庭和议会专门治理矿区，其特权由约翰王到爱德华三世的历代国王确认；1337年爱德华三世把伯爵领升格为公爵领，封给儿子黑太子，是为第一任康沃尔公爵。14世纪起英语步步东进，激起激烈反抗：1497年迈克尔·安·戈夫率众进军伦敦，1549年又爆发反对英语礼拜的祈祷书叛乱；后者被镇压后，康沃尔语作为社群语言崩坏，民间传说中最后一位只会康沃尔语的多莉·彭特里思于1777年去世。此后康沃尔人靠18世纪的循道宗小教堂维系认同，并以技艺精湛的矿工身份，在19世纪初把采矿经验带到墨西哥和北美的矿山。

en: The Corsicans are the Romance people of the mountainous Mediterranean island of Corsica, heirs of the ancient Corsi tribes whose name the Romans gave to the island, later mixed with Roman, Lombard and Frankish settlers. In 1337 the island, with its towns of Bastia, Calvi, Ajaccio and Corte, was held by the Republic of Genoa, whose rule had followed that of Pisa; for centuries coastal villages also suffered Barbary slave raids, while the pastoral interior kept a society organized around clan loyalty and the vendetta. Corsicans served widely as mercenaries and condottieri, fighting at Lepanto in 1571, and Sampiero Corso led French-backed revolts against Genoa in the 1550s. Their language, Corsu, is an Italo-Dalmatian tongue akin to medieval Tuscan, and Italian long remained the island's written and official language. In 1755 Pasquale Paoli proclaimed the Corsican Republic with a constitution and a university at Corte, but Genoa sold its rights to France in 1768 and French troops overran the island in 1769, the year Napoleon Bonaparte was born at Ajaccio.
zh: 科西嘉人是地中海多山岛屿科西嘉岛上的罗曼语民族，源自古罗马人以之命名该岛的古代科尔西部落，后来又融合了罗马人、伦巴第人和法兰克人等移民。1337年，岛上的巴斯蒂亚、卡尔维、阿雅克肖、科尔泰等城镇处于热那亚共和国统治之下，此前统治该岛的是比萨；数百年来沿海村庄还不断遭到柏柏尔人的掳掠为奴，而以牧为生的内陆则维持着以宗族忠诚和血亲复仇为纽带的社会。科西嘉人大量充当雇佣兵和佣兵队长，曾参加1571年的勒班陀海战；桑皮耶罗·科尔索则在16世纪50年代领导了有法国支持的反热那亚起义。他们的语言科西嘉语属于意大利-达尔马提亚语支，与中世纪托斯卡纳语相近，而意大利语长期是岛上的书面和官方语言。1755年，帕斯夸莱·保利宣布成立科西嘉共和国，颁布宪法并在科尔泰创办大学；但热那亚于1768年把对该岛的权利卖给法国，法军于1769年占领全岛，同年拿破仑·波拿巴出生在阿雅克肖。

en: The Cossacks take their name from the Turkic word kazak, a free man, and began as bands of runaway serfs, townsmen and adventurers who from the fifteenth century settled the lawless Pontic steppe known as the Wild Fields, beyond the reach of Polish, Lithuanian and Tatar lords. On the lower Dnieper they built the Zaporozhian Sich, a fortified commonwealth beyond the rapids where the rada assembly elected its ataman, or hetman, and admitted any newcomer who accepted Orthodox Christianity; parallel communities on the Don grew into the Don Host, and further hosts followed along the Terek, Yaik and Volga. Organized into self-governing stanitsas and granted land and privilege in return for frontier military service, they policed the border against Crimean and Nogai raiders and launched their own campaigns: the Polish crown created the Registered Cossacks in 1572, while Don Cossacks under Yermak opened the conquest of Siberia in the 1580s. Repeated revolts shook both neighbouring states, above all Bohdan Khmelnytsky's rising of 1648, which created the Hetmanate and led to the Pereyaslav agreement of 1654 with Muscovy; Stenka Razin, Kondraty Bulavin and Yemelyan Pugachev led still greater rebellions on the Don and Volga. After Ivan Mazepa's defection during the Great Northern War and Catherine II's destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich in 1775, the old freedoms were curbed and many Cossacks were resettled to the Kuban and the Danube, their hosts recast as regiments of the Russian Empire.
zh: 哥萨克的名字来自突厥语“卡扎克”，意为自由人。15世纪起，逃亡农奴、市民和冒险者在波兰、立陶宛与鞑靼领主势力之外的黑海北岸草原——人称“蛮荒原野”——落脚，逐渐汇聚成这支群体。他们在第聂伯河下游险滩之外建起扎波罗热谢契，这是一个设防的自治共同体：拉达大会选举阿塔曼（亦称盖特曼），凡接受东正教的来者皆可入伙；顿河畔的同类聚落则发展为顿河军，后来捷列克河、亚伊克河和伏尔加河也相继出现军屯。哥萨克以自治集镇“斯坦尼察”编户，以戍边军役换取土地和特权，既负责抵御克里米亚与诺盖袭扰，也主动出击：波兰王室在1572年设立注册哥萨克，顿河哥萨克则在1580年代随叶尔马克开启了对西伯利亚的征服。他们的起义一再震动邻邦，其中最著名的是1648年波格丹·赫梅利尼茨基起义，它催生了盖特曼国，并促成1654年与莫斯科的佩列亚斯拉夫协议；斯坚卡·拉辛、孔德拉季·布拉文和叶梅利扬·普加乔夫还在顿河、伏尔加河领导了更大规模的反抗。大北方战争中伊凡·马泽帕倒戈，1775年叶卡捷琳娜二世又摧毁扎波罗热谢契，旧有的自由被收束，许多哥萨克被迁往库班和多瑙河，诸军屯被改编为俄罗斯帝国的军团。

en: Coweta was a Muscogee tribal town on the lower Chattahoochee River, in what the Spanish called Apalachicola Province, and one of the four mother towns of the Muscogee Confederacy alongside Kasihta, Abihka and Tuckabutche. Its valley had supported Lamar-culture farming villages with platform mounds since the fourteenth century. Along with the other Chattahoochee towns, Coweta moved east into central Georgia near the end of the seventeenth century, where the English knew its people as Ochese Creek Indians, and returned to the Chattahoochee after the Yamasee War of 1715, becoming a leading market town of the Lower Creeks. Its mico Hoboyetly, called Emperor Brim by the British, steered Coweta through that war by shifting alliances between the British, French and Spanish until his death in 1733; Malatchi Brim then held the town's leadership until 1756. The later Coweta chief William McIntosh signed the Treaty of Indian Springs in 1825, surrendering most of the Muscogees' remaining land, and was executed by men of the Creek National Council the same year, on the eve of the forced removals to Indian Territory.
zh: 考维塔是查特胡奇河下游的马斯科吉部族城镇，地处西班牙人所称的阿巴拉契科拉省，与卡西塔、阿比赫卡和塔卡巴契并称马斯科吉联盟四大母镇。早在14世纪，这一河谷就有建有台庙的拉马尔文化农耕村落。17世纪末，考维塔与查特胡奇河诸镇东迁佐治亚中部，被英国人称为奥切斯溪印第安人；1715年雅马西战争后又迁回查特胡奇河，成为下克里克诸镇的贸易中心。其酋长霍博耶特利（英称皇帝布里姆）在雅马西战争中周旋于英、法、西三方之间，直至1733年去世；马拉奇·布里姆随后依母系传统主持镇务到1756年。后来的考维塔酋长威廉·麦金托什于1825年签署《印第安斯普林斯条约》，割让马斯科吉人残余的大部分土地，同年被克里克全国委员会的人处死，此后马斯科吉人便被强制迁往印第安领地。

en: The Crimeans, or Crimean Tatars, are the Turkic people of the Crimean peninsula and the adjoining Pontic steppe, forged over centuries from the Tauri, Goths, Greeks and Khazars of the coast and the Cumans and other Kipchak nomads of the grasslands. In 1337 Crimea was the Crimean Ulus of the Golden Horde, whose Mongol rulers had absorbed the older Cuman population; during the fourteenth century the people of the ulus largely adopted Islam and their Kipchak speech became dominant. As the Horde fragmented, the clans invited Hacı Giray to the throne in 1441, founding the Crimean Khanate and the Giray dynasty, and after the Ottoman conquest of 1475 the khans ruled as the sultans' vassals. The khanate grew rich on the slave trade through the port of Kefe, its raiders sweeping the Ukrainian and Russian steppes well into the eighteenth century, while Bakhchisaray became a centre of Islamic learning. Three ways of life shaped the people: nomadic steppe herdsmen speaking a Nogai-like dialect, settled mountain and valley villagers, and the Oghuz-speaking coastal dwellers. Defeat in the Russo-Turkish War of 1768 to 1774 ended Ottoman protection, and in 1783 Russia annexed the khanate; by 1800 between one and three hundred thousand Crimeans had fled or been driven into Ottoman exile.
zh: 克里米亚人即克里米亚鞑靼人，是克里米亚半岛及邻近黑海草原上的突厥语族群，由沿海的陶里人、哥特人、希腊人、可萨人与草原上的库曼人等钦察游牧民经数百年融合而成。1337年，克里米亚还是金帐汗国的克里米亚兀鲁思，蒙古统治者吸收了更早的库曼居民；14世纪，兀鲁思的民众大多改宗伊斯兰教，钦察语也成为主导语言。金帐汗国瓦解后，各部落于1441年迎立哈吉·格来为汗，建立克里米亚汗国与格来王朝；1475年奥斯曼征服之后，汗国君主成为苏丹的附庸。汗国凭借克法港的奴隶贸易致富，骑兵深入乌克兰和俄罗斯草原劫掠，一直延续到18世纪，巴赫奇萨赖则成为伊斯兰学术中心。三种生活方式塑造了这个民族：使用诺盖式方言的草原游牧民、定居的山地与河谷村民，以及说乌古斯语的沿海居民。1768年至1774年俄土战争的失败终结了奥斯曼的庇护，俄国于1783年吞并汗国；到1800年，已有十万至三十万克里米亚人逃离或被驱赶到奥斯曼境内流亡。

en: The Croatan, later also called the Hatteras, were a small Algonquian-speaking people of the North Carolina Outer Banks, holding the islands and sounds around Roanoke, Hatteras and Ocracoke in what is now Dare County, perhaps as a branch or close ally of the Roanoke. Their name may mean council town, and their chiefs, titled werowance, ruled through persuasion and the distribution of wealth. They met English explorers with John White's expeditions of 1585 and 1587, and when White returned in 1590 the abandoned Roanoke settlement held only the word CROATOAN carved on its palisade, which he read as a sign that the lost colonists had taken shelter on Croatoan Island. The Croatan kept the friendship the English first found in the local guide Manteo, but disease and displacement shrank them to perhaps eighty people by 1701. In the Tuscarora War of 1711 they fought on the colonial side and paid for it heavily, many being driven from their islands; by the middle of the eighteenth century the Croatan had ceased to exist as a separate tribe, their descendants absorbed among neighbouring Algonquian communities and, by uncertain tradition, the Lumbee.
zh: 克洛坦人（后来亦称哈特勒斯人）是北卡罗来纳外滩群岛的一支阿尔冈昆语小族群，占据今戴尔县境内罗阿诺克岛、哈特勒斯岛、奥克拉科克岛及周边海峡与湾口，可能是罗阿诺克人的分支或亲密盟友。其名字或意为“议事镇”，首领称维罗安斯，靠说服和分发财富维系统治。他们在1585年和1587年约翰·怀特的探险中与英国人接触；1590年怀特重返时，荒废的罗阿诺克定居点栅栏上只刻着CROATOAN一词，他据此判断“失落的殖民者”已迁往克洛阿坦岛避难。克洛坦人延续了英国人最初在当地向导曼蒂奥身上得到的友谊，但疫病和流离使他们到1701年可能只剩八十人。1711年塔斯卡洛拉战争中他们站在殖民地一方作战，代价惨重，许多人被逐出岛屿；到18世纪中叶，克洛坦人已不再作为独立部落存在，后裔融入邻近的阿尔冈昆社群，另有不确定的传说称其融入了卢姆比人。

en: The Croats are a South Slavic people who settled the eastern Adriatic hinterland, Dalmatia and Pannonia in the late sixth and early seventh centuries, absorbing the remnants of the romanized coastal population. Their dukes accepted Frankish and Byzantine overlordship in turn while keeping their own line of rulers; Christianity took root early, and in 879 Pope John VIII recognized Duke Branimir as an independent prince. Around 925 Tomislav became the first Croatian king, and the Trpimirović dynasty raised the kingdom to its height under Peter Krešimir IV and Demetrius Zvonimir, with Glagolitic writing preserved in monuments such as the Baška tablet of about 1100. A succession crisis brought the Croatian crown to the Hungarian Árpáds in 1102, yet the kingdom kept its own Sabor assembly and Ban viceroy. In 1337 the Croatian nobility, led by families such as the Šubić, ruled a land contested between the Hungarian crown and Venice, which had seized the Dalmatian port cities; the Mongols had sacked Zagreb in 1242. Ottoman conquests after 1463 shrank Croatian lands to a defensive frontier, and after the Battle of Mohács in 1526 the crown passed to the Habsburgs, under whom the Croats defended the frontier against the Ottomans for the next three centuries.
zh: 克罗地亚人是南斯拉夫民族，6世纪末至7世纪初定居于亚得里亚海东岸腹地、达尔马提亚和潘诺尼亚，融合了沿海残留的罗马化居民。他们的公爵先后臣属于法兰克和拜占庭，却保留着自己的统治世系；基督教很早便在此扎根，879年教皇约翰八世承认公爵布拉尼米尔为独立君主。约925年，托米斯拉夫成为第一位克罗地亚国王，特尔皮米罗维奇王朝在佩塔尔·克雷希米尔四世和德米特里乌斯·兹沃尼米尔治下把王国推向鼎盛，约1100年的《巴什卡石碑》等文物还保留着格拉哥里文字。1102年的继承危机使克罗地亚王冠落入匈牙利阿尔帕德王朝之手，但王国仍保留自己的萨博尔议会和巴安总督。1337年，以舒比奇家族为首的克罗地亚贵族治理着这片被匈牙利王室和威尼斯争夺的土地，后者已占据达尔马提亚港口城市；1242年蒙古人还曾洗劫萨格勒布。1463年以后奥斯曼的扩张把克罗地亚领土压缩为防御前沿，1526年莫哈赤战役后王冠转入哈布斯堡家族，此后三个世纪里克罗地亚人一直在边疆对抗奥斯曼人。

en: The Cueva were the principal Indigenous people of the eastern Panamanian isthmus when Europeans arrived, holding Darién and both the Caribbean and Pacific shores from the Atrato River west to Chame and the Rio Indio. They lived in rival chiefdoms, or cacicazgos, the strongest being Pocorosa, Comagre and Careta along the Caribbean, in what is now Guna Yala, while Chochama dominated the Pacific side around the Gulf of San Miguel and the Pearl Islands. Cueva was the name the Spanish gave to their speech, which many scholars now treat as a lingua franca shared by several ethnolinguistic groups; its links to the Chibchan, Choco and Arawak families are all still debated. The first Spanish settlers, among them Vasco Nunez de Balboa, reached these chiefdoms after 1510 from Santa Maria la Antigua del Darien, and it was at Comagre that Balboa heard of a sea to the south, prompting his crossing to the Pacific in 1513. War, epidemics, slaving raids and forced labour broke the Cueva within a generation: by the 1530s they had ceased to exist as a people, the last fugitive bands either taking refuge in the mountains or joining the Guna, their traditional enemies, who expanded west into the empty lands during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
zh: 奎瓦人是欧洲人到来时巴拿马地峡东部最主要的原住民，据有达连地区以及加勒比、太平洋两海岸，范围从阿特拉托河向西直到查梅和印第奥河。他们分成彼此争战的酋邦，最强的是加勒比沿岸、今古纳亚拉境内的波科罗萨、科马格雷和卡雷塔，太平洋岸则以控制圣米格尔湾和珍珠群岛一带的乔查马为大。奎瓦是西班牙人对其语言的称呼，晚近不少学者认为它是若干族群共用的通用语，它与奇布查、乔科和阿拉瓦克三大语系的关系迄今仍无定论。1510年后，以巴尔沃亚为首的最早一批西班牙定居者从圣玛丽亚·拉安提瓜·德尔达连进入这些酋邦；正是在科马格雷，巴尔沃亚听说南方还有一片大海，遂于1513年穿越地峡抵达太平洋。战争、疫病、掳奴和苦役在一代人之间摧毁了奎瓦人：到16世纪30年代他们已不再作为独立民族存在，最后的逃亡者或遁入深山，或加入世敌古纳人，而古纳人在17至18世纪间向西扩张，占据了这些空置的土地。

en: The Cuicas were one of the two main branches of the Timoto–Cuica people, the most advanced Indigenous society of the Venezuelan Andes, whose language and ways linked them to the Chibcha world of the Muisca. The Cuicas held the mountains and foothills around present-day Trujillo and the adjacent plains, while their Timote kinsmen centred on Mérida; the Escuqueyes, Mucuchíes and Capachos were smaller tribes of the same family. They built permanent villages of stone and timber houses ringed by irrigated stone terraces, grew maize, potatoes and sweet yucca, made fine anthropomorphic ceramics and gold objects, and used cacao beans as currency in trade with Arawak and Carib neighbours. In 1549 the Cuicas and Timotes forged a war alliance at Escuque, defeated a Spanish column in open battle and drove it back to El Tocuyo. In colonial times their old settlements were reorganized into Indian parishes and few place names kept their original forms.
zh: 奎卡斯人是蒂莫托—奎卡斯人的两大支系之一，后者是委内瑞拉安第斯山区最发达的原住民社会，语言和风习都与穆伊斯卡人的奇布查文化圈相连。奎卡斯人占据今特鲁希略一带的山地、丘陵及邻近平原，亲缘的蒂莫特人则以梅里达为中心；埃斯库凯人、穆库切人和卡帕乔人都是同群体的小部落。他们的村落由石木房屋构成，四周环绕引水灌溉的石砌梯田，种植玉米、马铃薯和甜木薯，能制作精美的人形陶器和金器，并用可可豆作货币，与阿拉瓦克和加勒比邻族贸易。1549年，奎卡斯人与蒂莫特人在埃斯库克结成战时同盟，在野战中击败一支西班牙队伍，把他们逐回埃尔托库约。殖民时代，他们的旧聚落被改组为印第安人教区，保留下来的原地名已经寥寥无几。

en: The Cuitlatecs were an indigenous people of the Tierra Caliente lowlands of Guerrero, in the Balsas river basin, whose chief towns at the time of the Spanish arrival included Ajuchitlán, Totolapan and Cutzamala. Their language, Cuitlatec, was a language isolate unrelated to any other surviving Mexican tongue, and some scholars link its speakers to the earlier Mezcala culture of the region. The name by which they are known is a Mexica exonym, coined from the Nahuatl word for excrement. The sixteenth-century Relaciones geográficas still recorded Cuitlatec in Ajuchitlán and Tetela del Río and along much of the Costa Grande, and around 1550 the parish priest Martín de Espinosa y Monzón wrote a grammar of the language while serving at Ajuchitlán.
zh: 奎特拉特克人是格雷罗州火地低地、巴尔萨斯河流域的原住民，西班牙人到来时其主要城镇包括阿胡奇特兰、托托拉潘和库察马拉。他们的语言奎特拉特克语是孤立语言，与墨西哥其他现存语言都没有亲属关系，有学者认为这支族群与当地更早的梅斯卡拉文化有关。奎特拉特克这个名字是墨西加人取的外来称谓，源自纳瓦特尔语中意为粪便的词。16世纪的《地理报告》仍记载阿胡奇特兰、滨河特特拉以及大海岸大部通行奎特拉特克语；约1550年，在阿胡奇特兰任职的神父马丁·德·埃斯皮诺萨-蒙松还编写了一部该语言的语法书。

en: The Cumans, called Polovtsians by the Rus' and Kunok by the Hungarians, were the western branch of the Cuman-Kipchak confederation, Turkic nomads who for two centuries dominated the Pontic and Caspian steppe under the name of Cumania, fighting and trading with Kievan Rus', Byzantium and the Balkan kingdoms. Their world collapsed with the Mongol advance: in 1239 Khan Köten led a great body of his people into Hungary, and after 1241, when Cuman rule over the steppe ended, those who stayed east were absorbed into the Golden Horde and in time into the Tatar peoples, while others fled to Bulgaria, Byzantium and Egypt, where Cuman-born Mamluks such as Baybars rose to the sultanate. In Hungary the migrants were settled on the Great Plain, in the districts still called Greater and Little Cumania (Kunság), keeping their own chiefs, herds and Kipchak tongue; a Cuman princess, Elizabeth, became queen in 1270 and mother of Ladislaus IV. Through the later Middle Ages the Hungarian Cumans gradually adopted settled farming and the Hungarian language, yet clung to collective privileges: these were lost around 1702, when their districts were sold to the Teutonic Order, and in 1745 the Cuman and Jasz communities bought their freedom back in a celebrated collective redemption, becoming free farmers rather than serfs.
zh: 库曼人被罗斯人称为波洛韦茨人，被匈牙利人称为昆人，是库曼—钦察联盟的西支，属突厥语游牧民，两个世纪里以“库曼尼亚”之名统有黑海至里海的大草原，与基辅罗斯、拜占庭和巴尔干诸王国战和交替。蒙古人的西进摧毁了他们的世界：1239年，可汗忽滩率大批部众迁入匈牙利；1241年库曼人对草原的统治终结，留在东方的族人被并入金帐汗国，日后融入鞑靼诸族，另一些人则逃到保加利亚、拜占庭和埃及，在埃及，出身库曼的马穆鲁克人如拜巴尔斯甚至登上苏丹之位。迁入匈牙利的库曼人被安置在大平原上，即仍称大库马尼亚和小库马尼亚（昆沙格）的地区，保留着自己的酋长、畜群和钦察语；库曼公主伊丽莎白于1270年成为匈牙利王后，是拉斯洛四世的母亲。中世纪后期，匈牙利的库曼人逐渐转为定居农耕并改用匈牙利语，但始终保有集体特权：这些特权在1702年前后随领地被卖给条顿骑士团而丧失，1745年库曼人与雅斯人集体筹资赎身，赎回自由，成为自由农而非农奴。

en: The Cumanagoto were a Cariban-speaking people of the Caribbean coast of eastern Venezuela, around the gulf of Cumaná and the valleys that became the province of Nueva Andalucía. Farmers of maize, manioc and sweet potatoes who also kept coca trees, hunted and gathered, they lived in palisaded villages, wore ornaments of feathers, pearls and gold, and allowed their chiefs polygyny; like other peoples of the coast they worshipped the sun and moon and treated the frog as lord of the waters, keeping the animals as pets but whipping them when rains failed. Their resistance drew Spanish campaigns into the Tuy valleys in 1579 and 1580 under Garci González de Silva. The Catalan adventurer Joan Orpí built his short-lived Province of New Catalonia, also called the Province of the Cumanagotos, on their lands between 1633 and 1654, when it was merged into Nueva Andalucía. Tribal organization broke during the seventeenth century, though a dwindling remnant kept its identity: by 1822 only about twenty-six Cumanagoto were counted west of Cumaná, and their descendants were absorbed into the mixed population of Anzoátegui and Sucre.
zh: 库马纳戈托人是委内瑞拉东部加勒比海岸的加勒比语族群，分布在库马纳湾一带以及后来成为新安达卢西亚省的各个河谷。他们种植玉米、木薯和甘薯，栽种古柯，兼事狩猎采集；村庄设有木栅，居民佩戴羽毛、珍珠和黄金饰物，酋长实行多妻制。和海岸其他族群一样，他们崇拜太阳和月亮，把青蛙奉为水神：平日养蛙为宠，雨水不继时便鞭打青蛙。他们的反抗引来了西班牙人的征讨，1579和1580年加尔西·冈萨雷斯·德·席尔瓦两度率军攻入图伊河谷。加泰罗尼亚冒险家胡安·奥尔皮于1633至1654年在他们的土地上建立了短命的新加泰罗尼亚省，又称库马纳戈托省，1654年并入新安达卢西亚。部落组织在17世纪瓦解，但日渐稀少的遗民仍保持身份：到1822年，库马纳以西登记在册的库马纳戈托人只剩约二十六人，其后裔融入了安索阿特吉和苏克雷一带的混血人口。

en: The Cunco were a coastal branch of the Williche, the southernmost arm of the Mapuche family, holding the rainy forested shore and Chilean Coast Range between Valdivia and the Maullín River, while their kinsmen on the northern half of Chiloé were often called by the same name. They spoke Mapudungun, farmed maize, potatoes and quinoa, raised chilihueques, and spent each spring and summer on the coast gathering shellfish, hunting sea lions and fishing from wooden dalca boats, dwelling in large ruca huts under small local chiefs. After the great Mapuche rising of 1598 they became the most relentless enemies of the Spaniards in Osorno, besieging the city until its settlers abandoned it in 1602 and then destroying it. Through the rest of the seventeenth century they harried every party trying to pass between Valdivia and Chiloé, keeping the forested coast a closed and warlike frontier.
zh: 昆科人是维利切人的一支，而维利切人又是马普切大家庭最南端的支系。他们住在瓦尔迪维亚到马乌林河之间多雨多林的海岸与智利海岸山脉一带，奇洛埃岛北半部的同族也常被冠以这个名字。他们讲马普敦贡语，种植玉米、马铃薯和藜麦，饲养奇利韦克家畜，每年春夏前往海边采集贝类、猎捕海狮，乘木制达尔卡船捕鱼，在地方小酋长治理下的大鲁卡茅屋里聚居。1598年马普切人大起义后，他们成为奥索尔诺西班牙人最凶悍的对手，长期围城，直到1602年殖民者弃城而走，城市随即被毁。整个17世纪，他们不断截击试图在瓦尔迪维亚与奇洛埃之间往来的西班牙队伍，使这片森林海岸始终是一道封闭而好战的边界。

en: The Cūnhuà, or Gelong, are the people of the lower Changhua River in western Hainan, around present-day Dongfang and Changjiang, who speak Cun, a Kra–Dai language of the Hlai branch. They descend from Han settlers who reached the island after its Western Han garrison in 110 BC and intermarried with the indigenous Li, and are officially counted as Han.
zh: 仡隆人又称村人、哥隆人，聚居于海南岛西部昌化江下游的东方市和昌江黎族自治县一带，说属于壮侗语系黎语支的村话，即仡隆语。他们的祖先是公元前110年西汉在海南岛设治后陆续迁来的汉族移民，与当地黎族通婚融合，所以村话比其他黎语支语言有更多汉语借词，而仡隆人在民族划分上仍被算作汉族。

en: The Curonians were a Baltic tribe of sailors and pirates who settled the Baltic coast from the fifth century, in the lands that still bear their name: Courland in western Latvia and the Curonian Spit, with Grobiņa as their early centre. Norse sources record them raiding Sweden alongside the Estonians and clashing with Danish and Swedish kings; in 854 they rose against Swedish tribute, defending the fortress of Apuolė for eight days. They fiercely resisted the Livonian Crusade, attacking Riga in 1210 and again in 1228 with the Semigallians. The northern Curonians made peace with the crusaders in 1230 under their ruler Lammekinus, but the south fought on, and at the Battle of Durbe in 1260 Curonian troops deserted the Livonian Order and helped the Samogitians to victory. Resistance ended in 1266, when Courland was divided between the Order and the Archbishop of Riga. The northern Curonians gradually merged into the Latvians, while the southern ones were absorbed by the Samogitians; their Curonian language was extinct by the sixteenth century, leaving traces in the Samogitian and Latvian dialects of the coast.
zh: 库罗尼亚人是波罗的部落，擅长航海与劫掠，5世纪起定居波罗的海沿岸，其名留在拉脱维亚西部的库罗尼亚（库尔兰）和库尔斯沙嘴等地，早期中心为格罗宾。诺斯史料记载他们与爱沙尼亚人联手袭扰瑞典，并与丹麦、瑞典国王交战；854年他们起而抗拒瑞典的索贡，在阿普奥莱要塞坚守八天。立窝尼亚十字军期间他们顽强抵抗，1210年攻打里加，1228年又与塞米加利亚人联手再攻里加。北部库罗尼亚人于1230年在首领拉梅基努斯率领下与十字军议和，南部则继续作战；1260年杜尔贝战役中，库罗尼亚士兵临阵脱离立窝尼亚骑士团，助萨莫吉蒂亚人取胜。1266年抵抗终告失败，库尔兰被骑士团与里加大主教瓜分。北部库罗尼亚人后来逐渐融入拉脱维亚人，南部则被萨莫吉蒂亚人吸收；库罗尼亚语到16世纪已经消亡，只在沿海的萨莫吉蒂亚和拉脱维亚方言中留下底层痕迹。

en: The Cusabo were a loose group of tribes, among them the Kussoe, Stono and Itwan, living along the South Carolina coast between present-day Charleston and the Savannah River when English colonists arrived. Their language was poorly recorded and matched none of the neighbouring families, suggesting an isolate, and it died out in the eighteenth century. The founding of Charles Town in 1670 put the colony in their midst: war with the Kussoe broke out in 1671, and after further fighting the Cusabo were made to cede land and pay tribute in deerskins. They nevertheless became the colony's Settlement Indians, serving as hunters, scouts and slave-catchers, and fought for South Carolina in the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1712. A census of 1715 counted them in five villages with fewer than three hundred people. In the Yamasee War of the same year the Cusabo sided with the colonists, after which most drifted away and merged into the Muscogee to the south or the Catawba to the west.
zh: 库萨博人是由库索人、斯托诺人、伊特万人等部落组成的松散群体，英国殖民者到来时居住在今查尔斯顿到萨凡纳河之间的南卡罗来纳海岸。他们的语言留存记录很少，与邻近各语系都不相同，可能是一门孤立语言，并于18世纪消亡。1670年查尔斯镇就建在他们的土地中央：1671年殖民地与库索人开战，经过几番冲突，库萨博人被迫割让土地并以鹿皮纳贡。尽管如此，他们还是成为殖民地的“定居印第安人”，充当猎人、斥候和逃奴追捕者，并在1711—1712年的塔斯卡罗拉战争中为南卡罗来纳作战。1715年的人口统计显示他们分布在五座村庄，人口不足三百。同年亚马西战争爆发，库萨博人站在殖民者一边，战后大多数人逐渐离去，分别并入南方的马斯科吉人和西方的卡托巴人。

en: The Cuyonon people are a Visayan ethnolinguistic group from the low-lying Cuyo Islands in the Sulu Sea, who later settled the northern and central coasts of Palawan. Their language is closely related to Kinaray-a of Panay and served for centuries as the lingua franca of Palawan, understood by Tagbanwa, Agutaynen and other island peoples. Before the Spanish arrived, Cuyo was ruled by Datu Magbanua and Taytay by the Cabaylo royal family, whose people sheltered the survivors of Magellan's fleet after the Battle of Mactan in 1521. In the early seventeenth century Augustinian Recollect friars opened missions in Cuyo and Taytay, and the Spanish later walled the church towns and posted garrisons against Moro raiders; the sultan of Brunei ceded southern Palawan to Spain in 1749. Long regarded as an elite among Palawan peoples, the Cuyonon became mostly Roman Catholic.
zh: 库约农人是米沙鄢语族群，原居苏禄海中地势低平的库约群岛，后来定居巴拉望的北部和中部海岸。他们的语言与班乃的基纳拉雅语相近，数百年来一直是巴拉望的通用语，为塔格巴努瓦、阿古塔延能等岛民所通晓。西班牙人到来之前，库约由达图·马格巴努阿统治，泰泰则由卡巴伊洛王室统治；1521年麦克坦战役后，正是泰泰的居民收留了麦哲伦船队的幸存者。17世纪初，重整奥斯定会修士在库约和泰泰开设传教站，后来西班牙人又给教堂城镇筑起围墙、派驻守军，以抵御摩洛人的袭掠；1749年，文莱苏丹把南巴拉望割让给西班牙。库约农人长期被视为巴拉望诸族中的上层，后来大多成为罗马天主教徒。

en: The Czechs are a West Slavic people of Bohemia, Moravia and Czech Silesia, whose ancestors settled the Czech lands in the 500s and 600s and absorbed the remaining Celtic and Germanic populations. Their Premyslid dukes built Prague Castle around 880, and from 1198 the dynasty ruled a hereditary Kingdom of Bohemia, into which German settlers were invited from the later 1200s. In 1337 the throne belonged to John the Blind of Luxembourg, and under his son Charles IV, king from 1346 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1355, Prague became an imperial capital and in 1348 gained the first university north of the Alps. Jan Hus, burned for heresy in 1415, reformed Czech spelling and inspired the Hussite movement, whose armies under Jan Zizka defended the Bohemian Reformation through the wars of 1419 to 1434. The Kralice Bible of 1579 to 1593 fixed the literary language, but after the Bohemian Revolt ended in defeat at the White Mountain in 1620, Habsburg re-Catholicization and Germanization drove scholars such as Jan Amos Komensky into exile, and by the 1700s German dominated public life. From the mid-1700s the Czech National Revival answered with Josef Dobrovsky's grammar of 1809 and Josef Jungmann's dictionary, rebuilding a written standard for the reawakening nation.
zh: 捷克人是波希米亚、摩拉维亚和捷克西里西亚的西斯拉夫人，先民在6至7世纪定居捷克地区，同化了残留的凯尔特人和日耳曼人。普热米斯尔王朝的公爵约在880年修建布拉格城堡，1198年起这个王朝统治世袭的波希米亚王国，13世纪后期起又有德意志移民陆续迁入。1337年在位的是卢森堡王朝的盲人约翰；他的儿子查理四世1346年即位、1355年加冕神圣罗马帝国皇帝，在他治下布拉格成为帝国都城，并于1348年创办了阿尔卑斯山以北第一所大学。扬·胡斯1415年以异端罪名被烧死，他改革了捷克语正字法，也启发了胡斯运动；1419至1434年的胡斯战争中，扬·杰式卡率军保卫了波希米亚宗教改革。1579至1593年的《克拉利采圣经》确立了书面语规范，但1620年白山战役战败、波希米亚起义失败后，哈布斯堡王朝强行再天主教化和德意志化，夸美纽斯等学者被迫流亡，到18世纪德语已主导公共生活。18世纪中叶兴起的捷克民族复兴运动回应了这一局面，多布罗夫斯基1809年的语法书和荣格曼的词典为重醒的民族重建了书面标准语。

en: The Daga are a Papuan people of the Bird's Tail, the southeastern peninsula of New Guinea, whose speech, also called Dimuga or Nawp, gives its name to the small Dagan family of Trans–New Guinea languages. The Dagan languages are spoken in the Meneao Range and are the easternmost Papuan languages on the New Guinea mainland. Daga-speaking villages lie in the Rabaraba country of Milne Bay Province and in the Abau country of neighbouring Central Province, where the Daga share the mountains with related peoples such as the Maiwa.
zh: 达加人是新几内亚东南半岛“鸟尾”地区的巴布亚族群，他们的语言又称迪穆加语或诺普语，小小的达甘语族（属跨新几内亚语系）便因它得名。达甘诸语通行于梅尼奥岭，是新几内亚大陆上位置最靠东的巴布亚语言。达加人的村落分布在米尔恩湾省的拉巴尔拉巴一带和相邻中央省的阿包一带，与迈瓦人等亲缘族群共居山地。

en: The Dagbani, who call themselves Dagbamba and are often written Dagomba, are a Gur-speaking people of the plains of northern Ghana and Togo, their country named Dagbon with its court at Yendi and other chiefdoms at Tamale, Tolon and Kumbungu. Their royal line claims descent from Tohazie, a fair-skinned hunter said to have led horsemen from east of Lake Chad through Zamfara and Mali; his descendant Naa Gbewaa settled at Pusiga, and Gbewaa's son Sitobu moved south to unite the indigenous farming towns and their earth priests, the Tindaamba. Sitobu's son Naa Nyagsi, ruling from 1416 to 1432, overthrew many of the Tindaamba and built the capital Yani Dabari near Tamale, and the kings of Dagbon took the title Yaa Naa. Wars with the Gonja later drove the court east to Yendi, where Naa Zanjina, the first Muslim Yaa Naa, defeated the Gonja at Sang in the late 1600s. Wangara and Dyula traders had long carried Islam into Dagbon; under Zanjina it became the court religion, and in 1700 the Muslim school of Moliyili was founded, keeping manuscripts in Dagbani written in an Arabic-based script. Dagbon grew rich on the kola and salt trades, so that by 1788 Yendi was described as larger than Kumasi and Salaga, while unusually for the region chiefly titles and lands were also held by women, headed by the Gundo Naa.
zh: 达格邦人（英文常称达贡巴人，自称达格班巴）是加纳北部和多哥平原上说古尔语支达格邦语的民族，其国称达贡，王庭在延迪，另有塔马利、托隆、昆本古等酋长领地。王室自称出自浅肤色猎人托哈齐：他率骑手从乍得湖以东经扎姆法拉和马里西迁，后裔纳·格贝瓦阿在普西加定居；格贝瓦阿之子西托布南下，联合土著农耕城镇及其地神祭司廷丹巴。西托布之子纳·尼亚格西于1416—1432年在位，攻灭众多廷丹巴，在塔马利附近营建亚尼·达巴里为都，达贡国王自此称亚阿纳。后来与贡贾人的战争迫使王庭东迁延迪；第一位穆斯林亚阿纳纳·赞吉纳于17世纪末在桑地击败贡贾人。旺加拉和迪乌拉商人早已把伊斯兰教带入达贡，赞吉纳时代它成为宫廷宗教，1700年又创办穆斯林学堂莫利伊利，用阿拉伯字母拼写的达格邦文抄写典籍。达贡靠柯拉果和食盐贸易致富，到1788年时延迪被认为比库马西和萨拉加还要大；与当地惯例不同，女性也可拥有酋长头衔和领地，以贡多·纳为首。

en: The Dahalo are a Cushitic-speaking people of the Kenyan coast around the lower Tana River, remnants, with the neighbouring Aweer and Waata, of East Africa's early hunter-gatherer inhabitants. Formerly elephant hunters dispersed among Swahili and Bantu communities with no villages of their own, they retain click sounds from their older speech in their Cushitic tongue, also called Sanye.
zh: 达哈洛人是肯尼亚沿海塔纳河下游一带的库希特语族群，与邻近的阿维尔人、瓦塔人一样，是东非早期狩猎采集居民的孑遗。他们世代以猎象为生，散居在斯瓦希里人和班图人当中，没有自己的村庄；其库希特语又称桑耶语，保留着古老语言的咂舌音。

en: The Dai are the Chinese name for a family of Southwestern Tai peoples—Tai Lue, Tai Nüa, Tai Dam and their kin—whose languages are close to Thai and Lao and whose ancestors spread south from Yunnan into the borderlands of Vietnam and Laos. They settled the river valleys, growing wet rice in stilt-house villages and organizing themselves into muang, small principalities under local chiefs. In the twelfth century the Tai Lue raised the Jinghong kingdom in Sipsong Panna, while further south the Black Tai built Ngưu Hống, the Black River kingdom of the Sơn La and Điện Biên country, which sent tribute to the Vietnamese court as early as 1067 and fought the Trần emperors along the Black River in the early fourteenth century. In 1337 this was still a world of independent Tai muang: Ngưu Hống held the upper Black River, and related Tai chiefs ruled the hills around Xam Neua east across the Lao border. Ming armies crossing into Dai Viet subdued the Black Tai in 1416, and after the Vietnamese reconquest Lê Lợi's campaigns of 1431–1432 folded their lands into the province of Hưng Hóa, while the Tai of Yunnan kept their own hereditary chieftains under Ming and Qing tusi rule. The Yunnan Dai adopted Theravada Buddhism between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, though the Black Tai long kept their old animist rites and their own Tai script.
zh: 傣是汉人对一系列西南台语民族的统称，包括傣泐、傣那、傣担（黑泰）等支系，语言与泰语、老挝语相近，先民从云南向南迁徙，进入越南、老挝边境地带。他们栖居河谷、种植水稻，住干栏式竹楼，以“勐”为单位组成头人治理的小邦。12世纪，傣泐人在西双版纳建立景龙金殿国；更南的黑泰人则在黑水（黑河）流域的山罗、奠边一带建立牛吼政权，早在1067年就向越南李朝进贡，14世纪初又与陈朝在黑河流域交兵。1337年时这里仍是独立泰邦林立的世界：牛吼据有黑河上游，同族的泰族头人则统治着老挝边境桑怒一带的山地。明军进入安南，于1416年平定黑泰；越南复国后，黎利在1431至1432年两次用兵，把黑泰土地并入兴化省。云南的傣族则在明清土司制度下保留世袭头人，并于15至16世纪改奉上座部佛教，而黑泰人长期保留本族文字和传统的精灵崇拜。

en: The Djangadi, also written Dainggati or Dunghutti, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Macleay Valley on the northern coast of New South Wales, around the town of Kempsey. Their language Dhanggati belongs to the Yuin-Kuric group within the Pama-Nyungan family. Shell middens at Clybucca, some heaped into mounds two metres high, an ancient fish trap in Limeburners Creek and a bora ring near Crescent Head trace at least four thousand years of continuous occupation. The first outsiders reached them in the late 1820s, when ex-convict cedar cutters camped at Euroka Creek from 1827 pushed up the valley after red cedar, and in 1835 Enoch Rudder took up the first European land grant in the Kempsey district, opening the country to pastoral settlement as the period closed.
zh: 丹加蒂人（又拼邓胡蒂）是澳大利亚新南威尔士州北部海岸麦克利河谷的原住民，活动在肯普西镇一带。他们的语言丹加蒂语属于帕马-牛雅语系的尤因-库里克语组。克莱巴卡的贝丘有些堆成两米高的贝壳丘，莱姆伯纳溪的古代鱼梁和克雷森特角附近的博拉环，都证明人类在此至少连续居住了四千年。19世纪20年代末，外来者第一次进入他们的土地：1827年起，以尤罗卡溪为营地的获释伐木犯为采伐红椿木深入河谷；1835年，伊诺克·拉德在肯普西区取得第一份欧洲人的土地授予，在本时期结束之际为牧业定居打开了大门。

en: The Daju are a cluster of related Nilo-Saharan peoples whose seven groups straddle the Chad-Sudan border and the Nuba Mountains, their oldest home being the Daju Hills of the Marrah range in Darfur. A Daju kingdom emerged there perhaps as early as the twelfth century; tradition remembers a war with the Christian kingdom of Dongola around 1100, after which King Ahmed al-Daj moved his court to Meri in the Jebel Marra massif, and around 1400 the Egyptian historian al-Maqrizi described Taju as a power lying between Kanem and the Nile states. In the fourteenth century the Tunjur, moving in from the west, overthrew the Daju dynasty: the fugitive king led part of his people to Dar Sila in what is now Chad, while other bands drifted east into Kordofan, where later pressure from the Messiria Arabs and the Ngok Dinka pushed some into the Nuba Hills around Lagowa. The Tunjur brought Islam and Arabic administration, and in 1596 their last sultan married into the Fur Keira line, producing the Fur-ruled Darfur Sultanate. Most Daju had become Muslims by the fifteenth century, though the Dar Fur Daju long kept the old cult of the high god Kalge, and all remained millet and sorghum farmers organized in small clans.
zh: 达朱人是若干彼此亲缘的尼罗-撒哈拉语系族群的合称，七个支系分布在乍得与苏丹边界两侧及努巴山脉，最古老的家园在达尔富尔迈拉山脉的达朱丘陵。早在12世纪，这里就兴起了达朱王国：传说1100年前后它与基督教的栋古拉王国交战，国王艾哈迈德·达季随后把王廷迁到迈拉山地的梅里；1400年前后，埃及史学家麦格里齐把塔朱描述为夹在卡涅姆与尼罗诸王国之间的强国。14世纪，从西面迁入的通朱尔人推翻达朱王朝：逃亡的国王率部众西走今乍得境内的达尔西拉，另一些支系东迁科尔多凡，后来又在梅西里亚阿拉伯人和恩戈克丁卡人的压力下，部分退入拉戈瓦一带的努巴山区。通朱尔人带来了伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语行政；1596年，末代通朱尔苏丹与富尔人的凯拉家族联姻，由此产生富尔人主政的达尔富尔苏丹国。到15世纪，多数达朱人已成为穆斯林，但达尔富尔达朱人长期保留对至高神卡尔格的古老崇拜；各族都以种植小米、高粱为生，按小氏族聚居。

en: The Dakelh, also called the Carrier and known to themselves as the Yinka Dene, are a Northern Athabaskan, or Dene, people of the central interior of what is now British Columbia, spread across the Stuart and Babine lake country, the Nechako valley and the upper Fraser River. Their languages, Carrier and Babine-Witsuwit'en, belong to the Northern Athabaskan family; the Wet'suwet'en and Babine are Dakelh branches. Their name refers to travelling by water, while French explorers' term Carrier passed into English. Life followed a seasonal round built around salmon runs, hunting and berry gathering, within family hunting territories called keyoh held under hereditary chiefs, and Dakelh parties carried coastal trade goods along the grease trails into the interior. The explorer Simon Fraser reached them in 1806, and the North West Company built Fort St. James on Stuart Lake, later run by the Hudson's Bay Company. The Stuart Lake chief Kw'eh, born around 1755, received Fraser and in 1828 spared the life of his prisoner, the young trader James Douglas, who became the first governor of the Colony of British Columbia.
zh: 达凯尔人又称卡里尔人，自称因卡德内人，是北方阿萨巴斯卡（德内）族群的一支，生活在今不列颠哥伦比亚省中部内陆，分布于斯图尔特湖、巴宾湖一带、内查科河谷与弗雷泽河上游。他们的语言卡里尔语和巴宾—韦苏韦滕语同属北方阿萨巴斯卡语系，韦苏韦滕人与巴宾人都是达凯尔人的分支。其族名与乘船出行有关，英文常用的卡里尔一名则来自法国探险家的称呼。传统生计围绕鲑鱼汛、狩猎和采果按季节轮换，土地按世袭酋长掌管的家族领地凯约划分，族人还沿着油脂商道把海岸贸易货物运往内陆。1806年探险家西蒙·弗雷泽抵达此地，西北公司随后在斯图尔特湖畔建立圣詹姆斯堡，后来由哈德逊湾公司经营。约1755年出生的斯图尔特湖酋长克韦接待了弗雷泽，并在1828年赦免了被俘的年轻商人詹姆斯·道格拉斯，后者日后成为不列颠哥伦比亚殖民地的首任总督。

en: The Dalmatians are the Romance-speaking heirs of the romanized Illyrian coast, whose walled towns survived the Slavic settlement of the seventh century while the hinterland passed to Croatian tribes. From Zadar, Split, Trogir and Krk to Dubrovnik and Kotor, these maritime city-states kept Latin law, Catholic worship and a vulgar Latin tongue that became the Dalmatian language, divided chiefly between the Ragusan dialect of Dubrovnik and the Vegliote speech of Krk. Tied by trade to Italy and Byzantium, the cities passed between Byzantine, Croatian and Hungarian overlordship while Venice steadily built an Adriatic empire: Zadar and the northern towns accepted Venetian rule, and the Venetian language increasingly displaced native Dalmatian in business and administration. Dubrovnik, called Ragusa, took a different path and grew into an independent merchant republic, where Ragusan remained the language of legal business until the end of the fifteenth century and the Senate in 1472 still protected it against the spread of Slavic. In 1337 the Dalmatian towns thus formed a bilingual coastal civilization, Romance in civic identity and Catholic faith yet deeply interwoven with the Slavic hinterland through commerce, intermarriage and the shared Adriatic world.
zh: 达尔马提亚人是罗马化伊利里亚沿海居民的罗曼语后裔；7世纪斯拉夫人定居内陆时，他们的城墙城镇幸存下来，而腹地落入克罗地亚诸部落之手。从扎达尔、斯普利特、特罗吉尔、克尔克到杜布罗夫尼克和科托尔，这些海洋城邦保留着罗马法、天主教信仰和通俗拉丁语，后者演变为达尔马提亚语，主要分为杜布罗夫尼克的拉古萨方言和克尔克的维格利奥方言。这些城市凭借贸易与意大利和拜占庭相连，宗主权在拜占庭、克罗地亚和匈牙利之间易手，而威尼斯稳步建立起亚得里亚海霸权：扎达尔和北部城镇接受威尼斯统治，威尼斯语也在商业和行政中日益取代本土达尔马提亚语。杜布罗夫尼克（又名拉古萨）走上了不同道路，发展为独立的商业共和国；拉古萨方言直到15世纪末仍是法律公务用语，1472年元老院还立法抵制斯拉夫语的扩散。因此在1337年，达尔马提亚诸城构成了一种双语的沿海文明：市民身份和天主教信仰属于罗曼传统，又通过贸易、通婚和共同的亚得里亚世界与斯拉夫腹地深度交织。

en: The Damara, who call themselves the Daman and were once also labeled Damaqua or Bergdamara, are an indigenous people of Namibia who speak the same Khoe tongue as the Nama although genetic evidence links them closely to the Bantu Herero and Himba, suggesting ancestors who exchanged an earlier Bantu language and way of life for a Khoekhoe one. Their traditions count them, beside the San, among the oldest inhabitants of the country, with chiefs remembered as far back as the fourteenth century. They first lived between the Kunene and Kavango rivers and later drifted south to the mountains around Brandberg, Waterberg, Omatako and Erongo, combining hunting and herding with the growing of pumpkins, corn and tobacco and working as copper and iron smiths. An invasion about 1600 broke their kingdom and scattered the Damara into named clans, some taking to the Kalahari sands and others to the mountain refuges that gave them the Bergdamara, or mountain Damara, label. As Nama and Herero herdsmen occupied the central plateau, many Damara lost their land and entered their households as dependents.
zh: 达马拉人自称达曼人，旧称达马夸人或山地达马拉人，是纳米比亚的原住民；他们与纳马人使用同一种科伊语，但遗传学证据显示他们与班图系的赫雷罗人和辛巴人血缘很近，说明其祖先曾放弃早先的班图语言和生活方式，转而接受科伊科伊文化。按照他们的口传传统，达马拉人与桑人并列，是纳米比亚最古老的居民，可追忆的酋长世系早至14世纪。他们最初生活在库内内河与奥卡万戈河之间，后来南迁至布兰德山、瓦特贝格、奥马塔科和埃龙戈一带的山区，以狩猎和畜牧为生，兼种南瓜、玉米和烟草，并擅长铜、铁锻造。约1600年的一次入侵瓦解了他们的王国，达马拉人分裂为若干有名号的氏族：一支退入卡拉哈里沙地，另一支遁入群山，山地达马拉之名即由此而来。随着纳马和赫雷罗牧民占据中部高原，许多达马拉人失去土地，沦为这两族家中的依附者。

en: Dambro, better known as Pak Tai or Southern Thai, is the Southwestern Tai speech of the people of the Thai half of the Malay Peninsula, from Chumphon down to the borderlands facing the Malay sultanates. Their country had earlier been the Indianized Buddhist land of Tambralinga under Srivijayan influence, and Tai settlers made the city of Nakhon Si Thammarat, or Ligor, their chief mueang before the mid-thirteenth century. The Ram Khamhaeng inscription lists Ligor as the southernmost tributary of Sukhothai in the late thirteenth century, and after Sukhothai weakened it became the dominant Thai state on the peninsula, its Theravada monastic tradition serving as a model for the whole Sukhothai realm. In 1337 the Dambro lands were a lively frontier between Thai and Malays, Buddhism and Islam; Majapahit already recognized Ligor as belonging to Siam in 1365, and Ayutthaya enrolled it among its eight great cities in 1468. Rich from Portuguese and Dutch trade, Ligor kept its own dynasty and vassals and revolted against Ayutthaya in 1629 and again in 1688. It enjoyed a last spell of independence after the fall of Ayutthaya in 1767 until Taksin subdued it in 1769, and Rama I later reduced its ruler to an appointed governor.
zh: 巴泰人又称南泰人，所说的巴泰语属西南部台语，分布在马来半岛的泰人一侧，北起春蓬，南至与马来苏丹国相望的边疆地带。他们的土地早先曾是室利佛逝影响下印度化佛教古国丹马令的所在，13世纪中叶以前，台语移民已以那空是贪玛叻（即洛坤）为首要城邦。兰甘亨碑铭把洛坤列为13世纪末素可泰最南端的属邦；素可泰衰落后，它成为半岛上最强的泰人城邦，其上座部佛教僧团传统曾是整个素可泰的范本。1337年时，巴泰人的土地正处在泰人与马来人、佛教与伊斯兰教交汇的前沿；1365年满者伯夷已承认洛坤属于暹罗，1468年阿瑜陀耶又将其列为八大城市之一。凭借与葡萄牙人和荷兰人的贸易致富，洛坤保留了自己的王朝和属邦，并于1629年和1688年两度起兵反抗阿瑜陀耶。1767年阿瑜陀耶陷落后它一度重新独立，1769年被郑信征服，拉玛一世随后将其统治者降为任命的总督。

en: The Dan are a Mande-speaking people of the forests along the border of north-western Ivory Coast and Liberia, where they are officially called Yacouba and were once known to outsiders as Gio. Their traditions place their origins in the western Sudan, in what is now Mali and Guinea, and by the 700s they were living in the savanna of the northern Ivory Coast. Political turmoil, population growth and exhausted land drove them south of the Nimba range and into the high forest in the 900s. There they cleared fresh fields each year for rice and other staples and earned a reputation as a fierce warrior society, whose chiefs fought long wars against neighbouring Kru and other groups. Their ritual life centred on the Gle mask ceremonies and on Gor, a men's society named after the leopard and devoted to peacemaking, while their carved wooden masks became the most celebrated art of the region.
zh: 丹人是说曼德语族语言的民族，居住在科特迪瓦西北部与利比里亚交界的森林地带，官方称雅库巴人，外部旧称吉奥人。按其传统，他们的祖源在今马里和几内亚一带的西苏丹地区，8世纪时已生活在科特迪瓦北部的稀树草原上。10世纪时，因政局动荡、人口增长和地力耗竭，他们南迁越过宁巴山脉，进入高地森林。在那里他们每年开垦新地种植水稻等作物，并以善战著称，历代酋长同克鲁人等邻近群体长期交战。他们的仪式生活以格莱面具典礼和名为戈尔的男性会社为中心，戈尔在丹语中意为豹子，是一个致力于调停争端的组织；丹人雕刻的木质面具也成为该地区最负盛名的艺术品。

en: The Southern Tutchone, whose language is called Dan k'e, are an Athabaskan First Nations people of the southwestern Yukon, with country around Kluane and Aishihik lakes, Lake Laberge and the upper Yukon at Whitehorse; their historic bands include the Kluane Lake, Champagne, Aishihik and Ta'an people. For some two thousand years they kept seasonal hunting and fishing camps in this lake-and-plateau country, storing food in raised log caches and moving between salmon stations and caribou and sheep hunting grounds in small matrilineal, clan-based bands. They were linked to the Pacific coast by the Chilkat Pass, one of the few routes through the coastal mountains, along which Tlingit traders brought eulachon oil, shell ornaments and, in time, European goods in exchange for furs and hides. A glacier in their Tatshenshini territory preserved the body of a man who died around 1700, still accompanied by his clothing and clan gear, evidence of how long this way of life endured in the southern Yukon.
zh: 南塔琼人是育空西南部的阿萨巴斯卡原住民族群，其语言称丹克语，家园分布在克卢恩湖、艾希希克湖、拉伯奇湖以及怀特霍斯一带的育空河上游，历史上的群体包括克卢恩湖人、尚佩恩人、艾希希克人和塔安人。约两千年来，他们在这片湖沼高原上设有季节性渔猎营地，把食物储藏在高架木仓里，以母系氏族小群体在鲑鱼渔场与驯鹿、野羊猎场间迁徙。奇尔卡特山口是穿越海岸山脉的少数通道之一，把他们与太平洋海岸连在一起：特林吉特商人沿山路带来蜡鱼油脂、贝壳饰物，后来又带来欧洲货物，换取毛皮和兽皮。在他们的塔琴希尼领地，一座冰川保存了一名约1700年去世的男子遗体，随身衣物和氏族器物俱在，见证了这种生活方式在南育空延续的漫长岁月。

en: The Northern Tutchone, who call themselves Dan ki, are an Athabaskan First Nations people of the central Yukon, whose villages and camps line the Yukon, Pelly, Stewart and McQuesten rivers as far east as the Selwyn Mountains; their bands include the Tage Cho Hudan, or Big River people, of Carmacks and the Hucha Hudan of the Pelly crossing. The Pelly-Yukon confluence alone has served as a native camp since roughly 6000 BC. In historic times they lived as communal hunter-fishers, taking salmon in summer and caribou and moose through the winter, organized into two matrilineal moieties, Wolf and Crow, whose clans regulated marriage and ceremony. They were tied to the Pacific trade by the Chilkat Tlingit, who crossed the coastal passes with eulachon oil and, by the early nineteenth century, European goods, carrying away interior furs and hides.
zh: 北塔琼人自称丹基人，是育空中部的阿萨巴斯卡原住民族群，村落和营地沿育空河、佩利河、斯图尔特河和麦奎斯滕河分布，东抵塞尔温山脉；其群体包括卡马克斯的塔格乔胡丹人，意为大河人，以及佩利渡口的胡恰胡丹人。仅佩利河与育空河交汇处一带，约自公元前6000年起便是原住民营地。进入历史时期，他们以集体渔猎为生，夏季捕鲑鱼，冬季猎驯鹿和驼鹿，社会分为狼、鸦两个母系半偶族，由氏族规范婚姻与仪式。奇尔卡特的特林吉特人穿过海岸山口，把蜡鱼油脂以及19世纪初以后的欧洲货物带来，换走内陆的毛皮和兽皮，北塔琼人就这样被纳入太平洋贸易网络。

en: The Dane-zaa, known to Europeans as the Beaver, are an Athabaskan-speaking people of the Na-Dene family, whose name is usually translated as the Real People or those who live among the beaver. In earlier centuries they ranged even further east, from the Athabasca and Clearwater rivers and Lake Athabasca across the upper Peace River country, in what is now northern Alberta and northeastern British Columbia; Charlie Lake Cave near Fort St John shows ten thousand years of continuous indigenous occupation. They hunted bison on the Peace River prairies, moose and caribou in the woods, and followed the Dreamers, prophet-teachers whose songs and visions ordered their spiritual life. In the late eighteenth century armed Cree traders pushed them northwest, until a peace settlement around 1800 fixed the Peace River as the border between the two peoples, which is how the river got its English name. Alexander Mackenzie opened the region to the fur trade in 1793 and built Rocky Mountain Fort the next year, and the Dane-zaa provisioned the posts with bison meat and grease until the herds thinned after the Hudson's Bay Company absorbed the North West Company in 1823.
zh: 达内扎人是讲阿萨巴斯卡语、属纳-德内语系的原住民，欧洲人旧称他们为比弗人（意为“海狸人”），其族名通常解释为“真正的人”或“住在海狸中间的人”。19世纪以前，他们的活动范围比后来更靠东，从阿萨巴斯卡河、克利尔沃特河和阿萨巴斯卡湖一直延伸到皮斯河上游地区，即今天的阿尔伯塔省北部和不列颠哥伦比亚省东北部；圣约翰堡附近的查理湖洞显示，当地已有上万年连续的人类居住史。他们在皮斯河草原猎野牛，在林中猎驼鹿和驯鹿，并信奉“梦者”——以歌声和异象指导精神生活的先知。18世纪末，拥有火器的克里商人把他们向西北驱赶，约1800年双方达成和议，以皮斯河为界，皮斯河的英文名（意为“和平河”）即由此而来。亚历山大·麦肯齐于1793年将毛皮贸易引入该地区，次年建起落基山堡；达内扎人以野牛肉和油脂供应各商站，直到1823年哈德逊湾公司兼并西北公司后，野牛群日渐稀少。

en: The Dangbon, more often called Dalabon, are an Aboriginal people of Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory; Dangbon is the name given them by their Kune and Mayali neighbours, and the people themselves traditionally had no single collective name. Norman Tindale placed their country east of the Liverpool River's headwaters, around the sources of the Cadell and Mann rivers, and recorded variant names Gundangbon, Dangbun and Gumauwurk. Semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers of mixed savannah and forest, they moved with a three-season round of monsoonal wet, cool dry and hot build-up. Their society was ordered by eight subsections built on Dua and Yirritja patrimoieties and matrilineal descent, and together with neighbouring tribes they staged the Gunabibi and Yabuduruwa ceremonies in alternating years. Their Gunwinyguan language is closest to Kunwinjku, Kune, Mayali and Kunbarlang; in their cosmology the kingfisher stole fire from the crocodile, and the ancestral Nakoorkko beings laid down the law embedded in their country.
zh: 丹邦人更常见的称呼是达拉本人，是北领地阿纳姆地的原住民；“丹邦”是邻近的库内人和马亚利人对他们的称呼，他们自己传统上并没有统一的集体名称。诺曼·廷代尔把他们的地域定在利物浦河河源以东、卡德尔河与曼河河源一带，并记录了贡丹邦、丹本、古马乌武克等异名。他们在稀树草原与林地交错的环境中过着半游猎的采集生活，随季风雨季、凉旱季和热季三季轮转。其社会以杜阿和伊里查两个父系半偶族及母系继嗣为基础，划分为八个亚组；他们还与邻近部落隔年轮流举办古纳比比和亚布杜鲁瓦仪式。他们的语言属贡温古语系，与贡温朱语、库内语、马亚利语和昆巴朗语最近；在他们的宇宙观里，翠鸟从鳄鱼那里偷来了火，远古的纳库尔科祖先则把律法铭刻在大地与习俗之中。

en: The Danes are a North Germanic people of Jutland, the Danish islands and the Scanian lands, first named by the sixth-century writer Jordanes. In the Viking Age their kings held the trading town of Hedeby behind the Danevirke rampart and launched the raids that carved out the Danelaw in England and the duchy of Normandy. Gorm the Old, ruling from Jelling around 940, was the first recorded Danish king; his son Harald Bluetooth united the Danes and made them Christian around 965, and Harald's grandson Cnut the Great ruled a North Sea empire linking Denmark with England and Norway. In 1397 Queen Margaret bound Denmark to Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union, but the Stockholm Bloodbath of 1520 discredited it, and after Sweden left in 1523 Denmark and Norway remained joined under one crown. After the Count's Feud of 1534 to 1536 Lutheranism became the state religion. The seventeenth century checked Danish power: Brömsebro in 1645 cost Gotland, and the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658 surrendered Scania, Halland and Blekinge to Sweden, fixing the modern frontier. Absolute monarchy followed in 1660 with the unified Danish Code of 1683. The British bombardment of Copenhagen in 1807 and the Treaty of Kiel in 1814 detached Norway, though Denmark kept Iceland, the Faroes and Greenland. Their language descends from the Old Norse shared with the other Scandinavian peoples.
zh: 丹麦人是居住在日德兰半岛、丹麦诸岛和斯堪尼亚地区的北日耳曼民族，6世纪的作家约尔达尼斯首次记载了他们。维京时代，丹麦诸王据有丹讷维尔克长城护卫下的贸易城海泽比，并发动远征，在英格兰开辟丹麦法区、在法兰西建立诺曼底公国。约940年，老王戈姆在耶林立国，是第一位有确切记载的丹麦国王；他的儿子蓝牙王哈拉尔约于965年统一丹麦并带领国人改宗基督教，哈拉尔之孙克努特大帝更建立起连接丹麦、英格兰和挪威的北海帝国。1397年，玛格丽特一世将丹麦、挪威、瑞典结为卡尔马联盟；1520年的斯德哥尔摩惨案令联盟威信扫地，瑞典于1523年退出，丹麦与挪威继续共戴一君。1534至1536年的伯爵战争后，路德宗成为国教。17世纪丹麦国势受挫：1645年的《布勒姆瑟布鲁条约》割让哥得兰，1658年的《罗斯基勒条约》又把斯堪尼亚、哈兰和布莱金厄割给瑞典，奠定了今日边界。1660年丹麦改行君主专制，1683年颁行统一的《丹麦法典》。1807年英军炮轰哥本哈根，1814年的《基尔条约》使挪威脱离丹麦，但冰岛、法罗群岛和格陵兰仍归丹麦。丹麦语源自斯堪的纳维亚各民族共用的古诺斯语。

en: The Danu are a Burmese-speaking people of the southern Shan highlands, concentrated around Pindaya and the hills east of Kyaukse, whose tongue is a Burmish dialect close to standard Burmese. Oral tradition traces them to Burmese settlers who married Shan women during Bayinnaung's sixteenth-century expansion, and their name means archer in Pali.
zh: 达努人是掸邦南部高地讲缅语的民族，聚居于宾达亚和皎施以东山区，所说达努语是与标准缅甸语相近的缅语支方言。口传他们是16世纪勃印曩扩张时与掸人妇女通婚的缅人移民后裔，族名在巴利语中意为弓箭手。

en: The Danube Bavarians speak the Central Bavarian dialects of the Upper German family, strung along the Isar and the Danube from Passau and Salzburg through Linz to Vienna and the Austrian lowlands. Their ancestors were the Baiuvarii, a Germanic people first recorded in the 500s in the former Roman province of Raetia south of the Danube, whose name is read as “inhabitants of the land of the Boii”, after the Celtic tribe that had dwelt there before Rome. The first documented Bavarian duke, Garibald I of the Agilolfing house, ruled from Regensburg from 555, and by the 700s their Austro-Bavarian speech was well established; its split from the neighbouring Alemannic dialects became clearly marked from the 1100s onward. Henry the Lion founded Munich in 1158, and in 1156 the Eastern March was raised to the separate Duchy of Austria, fixing the border between a western Bavarian speech around Munich and Passau and an eastern one along the upper Austrian rivers, whose best-known variety is the Viennese German of the Habsburg residence. After the fall of Henry the Lion the Wittelsbachs received Bavaria in 1180, and its dukes became prince-electors in 1623. Through these centuries Central Bavarian remained the everyday speech of townsmen and peasants on both sides of the border, while Standard German served church, chancery and print.
zh: 多瑙巴伐利亚人讲的是高地德语族的中巴伐利亚方言，分布在伊萨尔河与多瑙河沿线，从帕绍、萨尔茨堡经林茨直到维也纳和奥地利低地。他们的先民是巴尤瓦里人——6世纪首次见于记载的日耳曼人，住在多瑙河以南原罗马行省雷蒂亚；其族名被解释为“波伊人之地的居民”，波伊人是罗马时代之前居住于此的凯尔特部落。555年，阿吉洛尔芬家族的加里巴尔德一世成为首位有文献可考的巴伐利亚公爵，以雷根斯堡为治所；到8世纪，他们的奥地利-巴伐利亚语已经成形，与邻近阿勒曼尼方言的分化则从12世纪起趋于明显。1158年狮子亨利建慕尼黑，1156年东部边区被升格为独立的奥地利公国，由此确定了慕尼黑、帕绍一带西部口音与奥地利上游河流一带东部口音的分界，后者最著名的变体是哈布斯堡都城的维也纳德语。狮子亨利倒台后，维特尔斯巴赫家族于1180年受封巴伐利亚，其公爵又在1623年升为选帝侯。数百年间，中巴伐利亚方言始终是边境两侧市民和农民的日常语言，而标准德语承担教会、公文与印刷的功能。

en: The Dānzhōu are the Chinese-speaking people of north-western Hainan, centred on the old prefecture of Danzhou on the Beibu Gulf coast, with offshoots in neighbouring Changjiang, Baisha and Dongfang. Their speech, the Danzhou dialect or Xianghua, the village speech, is counted among the Yue languages: their ancestors migrated from the old Gaozhou and Wuzhou prefectures of the mainland, and the Yue speech they brought had blended with the native tongue by the Tang, when the dialect took shape. The Han first opened the area with the Dan'er commandery of 110 BC; the Tang made it Danzhou in 622, with its seat at Yilun. Between 1097 and 1100 the exiled poet Su Shi lived here, teaching the classics, and later generations turned his residence into the Dongpo Academy in his memory. Under the Song the prefecture became the Nanning military prefecture; the Ming restored the name Danzhou in 1369 and merged Yilun county into it in 1439, an arrangement the Qing kept unchanged.
zh: 儋州人是海南岛西北部讲汉语的民系，以北部湾畔的旧儋州为中心，旁及昌江、白沙、东方等邻县的部分村落。他们的儋州话又叫乡话，被归入粤语一类：其先祖来自大陆的旧高州、梧州等地，带来的粤语与当地土语相融合，到唐代已经正式成形。公元前110年汉朝首置儋耳郡，开辟这一地区；622年唐朝改设儋州，治所设在义伦。1097年至1100年，被贬谪的诗人苏轼居于此地，讲学授徒，后人把他的居所载酒堂改建为东坡书院以为纪念。宋代这里改置南宁军，1369年明朝复名儋州，又于1439年把宜伦县省入州中，清代沿袭了这一建制。

en: The Dargins are a Northeast Caucasian people of central Dagestan, settled in the dry highlands between the Avars and the Caspian shore, with Akusha-Dargo as their spiritual and judicial center and fortress villages such as Kubachi, Levashi and Kadar. In the Middle Ages their principal state was the Kaitag Utsmiate, whose utsmi rulers held the mountain stronghold of Kala-Koreysh and the foothill roads linking Derbent with the Golden Horde capital at Sarai and the Italian ports of the Black Sea. The utsmi was elected from the senior princely lineage rather than inheriting by birth, and the free Dargin village unions of Utsmi-Dargo kept their arms and stubbornly limited his power, mustering as his main force in war but rejecting his taxes in peace. An ally of the Golden Horde, Kaitag was ravaged by Timur in the late fourteenth century and only recovered in the fifteenth, after which the utsmi's seat moved down to Majalis and Bashly. By then the Dargins were Sunni Muslims of the Shafi'i school, judged in their villages by qadis under sharia and customary law. Kubachi became renowned across the Caucasus and the Middle East for its silversmiths, while Kaitag embroidery ranked among the region's distinctive crafts. Russian annexation reached the Dargin lands in the campaigns of the early nineteenth century, and the utsmiate was extinguished in 1820.
zh: 达尔金人是达吉斯坦中部的东北高加索语族群，聚居于阿瓦尔人与里海沿岸之间的干旱高地，精神和司法中心是阿库沙-达尔戈，另有库巴奇、列瓦希、卡达尔等堡垒村庄。中世纪时他们的主要政权是凯塔格乌茨米亚特，其乌茨米统治者据有卡拉科雷什山城，以及连接杰尔宾特、金帐汗国都城萨莱和黑海意大利商港的山麓商路。乌茨米并非世袭，而是由王公家族中的长者推选；乌茨米-达尔戈的自由村社武装在身，顽强限制他的权力——战时是他的主力，平时却拒绝纳税。作为金帐汗国的盟友，凯塔格在14世纪末遭帖木儿蹂躏，15世纪才恢复，乌茨米的驻地随后下移至马贾利斯和巴什雷。此时达尔金人已成为沙斐仪派逊尼派穆斯林，村社由卡迪依据沙里亚法和习惯法断案。库巴奇的银匠在整个高加索和中东享有盛名，凯塔格刺绣也是当地特色工艺。19世纪初的俄国兵锋抵达达尔金人的土地，乌茨米亚特于1820年被消灭。

en: The Darumbali, or Darumbal, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Queensland coast, whose country of some ten thousand square kilometres ran from Shoalwater Bay to Yeppoon, taking in the mouth of the Fitzroy River and the Keppel Bay islands and reaching inland to the Boomer Range, Rockhampton and Gracemere. They were formed of about thirteen band societies, one branch, the Warabal, keeping to the country at the foot of the Boomer Range. Their Darumbal language, with its Guwinmal, Karunbara and Rakiwara dialects, belonged to the Pama-Nyungan family and was sharply distinct from the neighbouring Bayali tongue, with which it shared little basic vocabulary. On 27 May 1770 James Cook's Endeavour anchored in their waters and Cook named Keppel Bay after Admiral Augustus Keppel.
zh: 达伦巴尔人是昆士兰中部沿海的澳大利亚原住民，其约一万平方公里的领地从肖尔沃特湾延伸至耶蓬，包括菲茨罗伊河河口与凯珀尔湾诸岛，内陆直抵布默岭、罗克汉普顿和格雷斯米尔。他们由约十三个游群组成，其中瓦拉巴尔一支住在布默岭山麓。他们的达伦巴尔语属帕马—牛雅语系，下分古温马尔、卡伦巴拉和拉基瓦拉三种方言，与邻近的巴亚利语差异很大，基础词汇重合很少。1770年5月27日，詹姆斯·库克的奋进号停泊在他们的海域，库克以皇家海军将领奥古斯塔斯·凯珀尔之名将该海湾命名为凯珀尔湾。

en: The Daurs are a Mongolic people of the upper Amur country, the region called Dauria after them, with their ancestral lands along the Shilka, Zeya and Bureya rivers south of the Outer Khingan range; both tradition and genetic studies link them to the medieval Khitans, and their Mongolic language keeps Khitan-derived words. In the early 1600s they were settled farmers and cattle breeders living in walled towns, organized in hala surname groups split into mokon clans and already tributary to the rising Manchu power, which in 1640 crushed the Evenk–Daur federation led by Bombogor. When Russian Cossacks under Yerofei Khabarov reached the Zeya in 1650 and demanded fur tribute, the Daurs refused, saying they already paid tribute to the Shunzhi Emperor; Khabarov's men stormed Prince Guigudar's town in 1651 and seized Yaxa, later the Russian fort of Albazin. Between 1654 and 1656 the Qing resettled the Daurs on the Nen River around Qiqihar and enrolled them in the banner system, where many used Manchu as a written language, and Qing forces retook Albazin only in the 1680s.
zh: 达斡尔是黑龙江上游一带的蒙古语族民族，他们居住的地区因他们得名达乌里亚，祖居外兴安岭以南的石勒喀河、结雅河、布列亚河一带；族内传说与基因研究都把他们与中世纪的契丹人联系起来，达斡尔语中也保留着源自契丹的词汇。17世纪初，他们已是定居的农耕和畜牧者，住在有围墙的城镇里，社会按“哈拉”姓族分成若干“莫昆”氏族，并已向兴起中的满洲纳贡；1640年，清朝平定了博木博果尔领导的鄂温克—达斡尔联盟。1650年，叶罗费·哈巴罗夫率领的俄国哥萨克进抵结雅河勒索毛皮贡赋，达斡尔人以已向顺治帝纳税为由拒绝；1651年哥萨克攻破桂古达尔王公的城寨，又夺取雅克萨，后来那里成为俄国据点阿尔巴津。1654至1656年间，清朝将达斡尔人南迁到齐齐哈尔一带的嫩江流域，编入八旗，许多人从此兼用满文；清军直到17世纪80年代才收复雅克萨。

en: Degar, also called Montagnard, is a collective name for the indigenous peoples of the Central Highlands of southern Indochina, among them the Jarai, Rade, Bahnar, Koho, Mnong and Stieng. The Jarai and Rade speak Chamic tongues of the Austronesian family, kin to the language of Champa, while other highland groups speak Austroasiatic languages. Chinese annals of the fourth century record the king of Lâm Ấp subduing the tribes west of Champa, and for centuries the highlanders traded with the lowland Cham kingdoms while keeping their own village societies, based on swidden rice farming, matrilineal descent and ritual buffalo sacrifice. The Vietnamese conquest of Champa in 1471 brought lowland settlers to the coast but not to the mountains, and in 1802 the emperor Gia Long received the nominal submission of several highland chiefdoms, which kept their autonomy under tributary arrangements. Isolated by terrain, the Degar tribes preserved customs and ancestral landholding patterns distinct from both the Cham and the Vietnamese.
zh: 德加人又称蒙塔尼亚尔人，是印度支那南部中央高地各原住民群体的统称，主要包括嘉莱人、埃地人、巴拿人、格贺人、墨侬人和斯丁人。其中嘉莱人和埃地人使用南岛语系占语支的语言，与占婆的语言同源，另一些高地群体则使用南亚语系语言。4世纪的中国史籍记载林邑国王征服了占婆以西的诸部落；数百年来，高地人与低地的占婆诸王国贸易往来，同时保留着以轮垦稻作、母系继承和献祭水牛为特色的村社生活。1471年越南征服占婆后，低地移民只到达沿海而未深入山区；1802年嘉隆帝接受若干高地酋邦的名义归附，它们以朝贡形式维持自治。凭借山地的阻隔，德加诸部落保存了与占人和越南人都不相同的习俗和祖传土地制度。

en: The Dehcho, or South Slavey, are a Dene people whose Athabaskan language belongs to the Na-Dene family. Their own name, Dehcho Dene, means Mackenzie River People, and their homeland stretches along the Mackenzie and Liard rivers and the western shore of Great Slave Lake, reaching into northeastern British Columbia and northwestern Alberta. The English name Slavey comes from Awokanak, the Cree term for the northern neighbours they sometimes raided, and it gave Great Slave Lake and the Slave River their European names. The Dehcho lived in forest bands that hunted moose and caribou, fished the rivers and lakes, and travelled the waterways in birchbark canoes, gathering at places such as the meeting of the Mackenzie and Liard. Fur traders reached those waterways early: a post called Fort of the Forks opened there in 1803, and the Hudson's Bay Company rebuilt it as Fort Simpson in 1822, drawing the Dehcho into the regional fur trade. Their northern relatives around Great Bear Lake form the separate Sahtu, or North Slavey, people.
zh: 德乔人即南斯拉维人，是德内人的一支，其阿萨巴斯卡语属于纳-德内语系。他们自称“德乔·德内”，意为“马更些河人”，家园沿马更些河、利亚德河及大奴湖西岸展开，并延伸到不列颠哥伦比亚省东北部和阿尔伯塔省西北部。“斯拉维”这一英文称呼来自克里语的 Awokanak，因克里人曾不时劫掠这些北方邻人而得名，大奴湖与斯拉维河的欧洲式名称也源于此。德乔人以森林中的小群体为生，捕猎驼鹿和驯鹿，在河湖中捕鱼，乘桦皮独木舟往来水道，并在马更些河与利亚德河交汇处等地聚会。毛皮商人很早便进入这些水道：1803年河口堡商站开张，1822年哈德逊湾公司将其重建为辛普森堡，德乔人由此卷入地区毛皮贸易。他们在大熊湖一带的北方亲族另成萨赫图人，即北斯拉维人。

en: The Dehlavi are the people of the Delhi region and the Upper Doab, the fertile strip between the Ganges and the Yamuna around Meerut and Saharanpur that for centuries formed the political heartland of northern India. Their speech, Dehlavi, also called Hindavi or Old Hindi, descended from Shauraseni Prakrit and was the local dialect of the Delhi Sultanate, used by its Persian-speaking rulers to address their subjects; its earliest literary echoes appear in the verses of Amir Khusro around 1300. Under the Mughals the Persianised Dehlavi of the camps and bazaars around Delhi and Agra developed into Rekhta, the literary tongue that became Urdu, while the same dialect, later known as Khariboli, became the base of Standard Hindi, so that Dehlavi is the common ancestor of the two registers of Hindustani. The country around Delhi remained the seat of Mughal power until the empire's eighteenth-century decline: the city was sacked by Nadir Shah in 1739 and contested by Afghans and Marathas before the East India Company took Delhi and the Doab in 1803, after which Fort William College in Calcutta promoted the Delhi dialect as the standard of modern Hindustani.
zh: 德赫拉维人是德里地区及上多阿布的居民，后者是恒河与亚穆纳河之间密拉特、萨哈兰普尔一带的肥沃地带，数百年来一直是北印度的政治腹地。他们讲的德赫拉维方言又称欣达维或古印地语，由索拉塞尼俗语演变而来，是德里苏丹国的本地话，供讲波斯语的统治者与臣民沟通；现存最早的文学痕迹见于1300年前后阿米尔·库斯劳的诗篇。莫卧儿时期，德里与阿格拉周边军营和集市里深度波斯化的德赫拉维语发展为文学语言雷赫塔，即后来的乌尔都语；同一方言后来称卡里口语，又成为标准印地语的基础，因此德赫拉维方言是印度斯坦语两种语体的共同祖先。德里一带始终是莫卧儿的权力中心，直到18世纪帝国衰落：1739年德里遭纳迪尔沙洗劫，随后在阿富汗人与马拉塔人之间反复易手，1803年英国东印度公司夺取德里和多阿布，此后加尔各答的威廉堡学院把德里方言确立为印度斯坦语的规范口语。

en: The Dehwar are settled Persian-speaking farmers of the Balochistan highlands around Mastung, Kalat and Kharan; their Dehwari dialect is close to Dari and Tajik but heavily influenced by Brahui. Probably descended from the older sedentary population predating the Baloch migration, these Sunni Muslims staffed the bureaucracy of the Khanate of Kalat from the seventeenth century.
zh: 德瓦尔人是俾路支斯坦高原马斯通、卡拉特、哈兰一带的定居波斯语农民，德瓦里方言接近达里语和塔吉克语，但深受布拉灰语影响。他们可能是俾路支人迁入前古老定居者的后裔，属逊尼派，17世纪起在卡拉特汗国充任行政官吏。

en: The Denesoliné, better known as the Chipewyan, are the northernmost of the Dene peoples, speakers of an Athabaskan language of the Na-Dene family whose ancestors are traced to the ancient Taltheilei hunting culture of the barrenlands. Their own name means the original people, while Chipewyan is the Cree word for pointed skin, after the cut of their tailored caribou-hide parkas. Their homeland runs from the western shore of Hudson Bay across the Canadian Shield to Great Slave Lake and Lake Athabasca, the country of the Churchill, Reindeer and Wollaston lakes, where small nomadic bands followed the barren-ground caribou between tundra and taiga, lived in tipis, and warred with the Inuit and other Dene to their north. English traders reached them at Churchill in 1717, after the Chipewyan guide Thanadelthur had brokered peace with the rifle-armed Cree who were pressing on their eastern flank, and the Denesoliné became the chief fur middlemen of the subarctic. Their leader Matonabbee guided Samuel Hearne overland to the Coppermine River in 1770, and the North West Company built Fort Chipewyan on Lake Athabasca in 1788, around which regional groups such as the Kaí-theli-ke-hot'ínne and Thilanottine gathered to control the carrying trade.
zh: 德内苏利内人即奇佩维安人，是德内诸族中位置最北的一支，讲纳-德内语系的阿萨巴斯卡语，其祖先可追溯到荒原上古老的塔尔泰莱狩猎文化。他们的自称意为“原本的人”，而“奇佩维安”来自克里语“尖皮衣”一词，形容他们用驯鹿皮缝制的派克式皮衣剪裁。其家园从哈得孙湾西岸横跨加拿大地盾，一直延伸到大奴湖和阿萨巴斯卡湖，涵盖丘吉尔湖、赖恩迪尔湖和伍拉斯顿湖一带；流动的小群体在苔原与针叶林之间追随瘠地驯鹿，住锥形帐篷，并与北方的因纽特人及其他德内群体交战。1717年，英国商人在丘吉尔与他们接触——此前奇佩维安向导塔纳德尔图刚刚促成他们与持步枪进逼其东境的克里人议和，德内苏利内人由此成为亚北极地区最主要的毛皮贸易中间人。他们的领袖马顿纳比于1770年引导塞缪尔·黑恩陆路远征科珀曼河，西北公司又于1788年在阿萨巴斯卡湖畔建立奇佩维安堡，凯泰利凯霍廷内、蒂拉诺廷等区域群体随后聚集在商站周围，掌控转运贸易。

en: The Deori are a Tibeto-Burman people of the upper Brahmaputra valley, whose historic homeland lay around Sadiya, the Joidaam region and the Patkai foothills in eastern Assam. They call themselves Jimochãya, children of the sun, and are divided into four clans, the Dibongiya, Tengapaniya, Borgoya and Patorgoya. Their folklore ties them to the Chutia kingdom, whose kings appointed their ancestors priests of the goddess Tamreswari at Sadiya; traditionally they follow Kundism, an animist and ancestor-worshipping faith centred on the supreme god Kundi-Mama. Their language belongs to the Boro-Garo branch of Tibeto-Burman, though in time only the Dibongiya clan kept it as everyday speech while the others turned to Assamese. The Burmese invasions of 1817 to 1826 killed or carried off many Deori as captives and drove the survivors downstream to new settlements.
