zh: 代奥里人是布拉马普特拉河上游河谷的藏缅语族群，故地在阿萨姆东部的萨迪亚、焦伊达姆一带和帕特凯山麓。他们自称吉莫恰亚，意为太阳之子，分为迪邦吉亚、滕加帕尼亚、博尔戈亚和帕托尔戈亚四个氏族。他们的起源传说把自己与久蒂亚王国联系在一起：久蒂亚国王任命其祖先为萨迪亚的塔姆雷斯瓦里女神神庙的祭司。代奥里人传统信奉昆迪教，这是一种以主神昆迪—马马为中心、融合万物有灵与祖先崇拜的民间信仰。代奥里语属藏缅语族博多—加罗语支，但后来只有迪邦吉亚氏族仍在日常使用，其余各支改说阿萨姆语。1817—1826年的缅甸入侵使许多代奥里人被杀或被俘，幸存者顺流南迁，另建家园。

en: The Derung, also spelt Drung, are a Tibeto-Burman people of the steep Derung Valley in Gongshan on the upper Salween in north-western Yunnan. Their society was organized into patriarchal clans called nile, each divided into communal longhouse settlements, and their own Derung language was unwritten, so messages and records were kept by notching wooden logs. Under the Tang dynasty of 618 to 907 the Derung lands fell within the domains of Nanzhao and then the Dali Kingdom; under the Yuan and Qing dynasties, from the late thirteenth century onward, they were ruled by local Tibetan and Nakhi chiefs and sent yearly tribute to the Chinese court. Most Derung kept their animist beliefs, served by shamans who oversaw animal sacrifices, and women traditionally tattooed their faces on reaching adulthood.
zh: 独龙人是居住在云南西北部贡山独龙江峡谷、萨尔温江上游一带的藏缅语族群。他们的社会以父系氏族“尼勒”为单位，氏族之下是共居长屋的村落；独龙语没有文字，过去靠刻木记事、传递信息。618—907年的唐代，独龙地方先后归入南诏和大理国的版图；13世纪后期元朝以后直至清代，当地由藏族和纳西族首领管辖，独龙人并向中国朝廷岁贡。独龙人大多保持万物有灵信仰，由巫师主持杀牲祭祀，女子传统上在成年时纹面。

en: The Daasanach, also called the Marille or Geleba, are a Cushitic-speaking people of the lower Omo River and the shores of Lake Turkana, where Ethiopia, Kenya and South Sudan meet, tracing descent from the earlier Maliri people. Traditionally egalitarian pastoralists organized into age sets and clans, many now also farm the Omo floodplains after losing grazing lands around the lake.
zh: 达萨纳克人（又称马里莱人或格莱巴人）是操库希特语的族群，聚居在奥莫河下游与图尔卡纳湖沿岸、埃塞俄比亚、肯尼亚和南苏丹交界一带，自认是更早的马里里人的后裔。他们传统上是按年龄组和氏族组织的平等主义牧民，在环湖牧场缩小后，许多人也转而在奥莫河三角洲的季节性洪泛地上务农。

en: The Dharug are a nation of Aboriginal Australian clans whose country covered the Sydney basin, from the shores of Sydney Harbour and Botany Bay inland along the Hawkesbury and Parramatta rivers. Their language had two dialects: the inland clans, the paiendra or tool people, hunted kangaroos and emus with stone axes, while the coastal katungal, the sea people whose speech was also called Eora, built canoes and lived on fish and shellfish. British colonisation after 1788 shattered this world: smallpox in 1789 killed up to nine in ten of them in some areas, and farms spread along the Hawkesbury from 1794 blocked their food grounds, opening decades of guerrilla war. The warrior Pemulwuy led raids on Parramatta until he was shot in 1802, his head pickled and sent to Joseph Banks, and Governor Macquarie's orders of 1816 banned armed gatherings and ringed the district with military posts, breaking open resistance by the 1830s.
zh: 达鲁格人是由多个氏族组成的澳大利亚原住民族群，领地覆盖悉尼盆地，从悉尼港和植物湾沿岸一直延伸到霍克斯伯里河与帕拉马塔河上游内陆。他们的语言分两种方言：内陆氏族称派恩德拉，意为“工具之人”，用石斧猎取袋鼠和鸸鹋；沿海氏族称卡顿加尔，意为“海民”，方言又叫约拉语，他们制造独木舟，以鱼和贝类为生。1788年后的英国殖民击碎了这一世界：1789年的天花使部分地区损失多达九成人口；1794年起霍克斯伯里河畔的农场阻断了他们的取食地，引发数十年游击战。武士佩穆尔韦率众袭击帕拉马塔，直到1802年被枪杀，头颅被腌渍后送给约瑟夫·班克斯；1816年麦觉理总督下令禁止原住民携带武器聚集，并在区内遍设军事哨站，到19世纪30年代粉碎了公开抵抗。

en: The Dhivehi, who call themselves Dhivehin, are the Indo-Aryan islanders of the Maldives, a chain of twenty-six coral atolls in the Indian Ocean, with a small kindred community on Minicoy to the north. They speak Dhivehi, descended from the Elu Prakrit of ancient Sri Lanka and closely related to Sinhala though not mutually intelligible with it; it is written in the Thaana script, whose earliest surviving records are the lōmāfānu copper-plate grants of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, and the dialects of the southern atolls remain markedly different from the Malé standard. Settled for more than two and a half thousand years, the islands grew wealthy as a source of the cowrie shells used as currency across the Indian Ocean. Arab traders brought Islam in the twelfth century and the Maldives became a sultanate; the Chinese admiral Zheng He called there in 1411 and 1430. Portuguese forces seized the islands in 1558 and were driven out in 1573, after which the sultans of Malé kept their independence through the age of European sea power.
zh: 迪维希人自称迪维欣，是马尔代夫的印度—雅利安岛民，国家由印度洋上26个珊瑚环礁组成，北面的米尼科伊岛还有一小支同族。他们讲迪维希语，由古斯里兰卡的埃卢俗语演化而来，与僧伽罗语是近亲但互不相通；文字用它拿字母，现存最早记录是12至13世纪的洛马法努铜板诏令，南部环礁的方言与马累标准语差异显著。群岛有人定居已逾两千五百年，因出产在整个印度洋充当货币的贝币而富庶。12世纪阿拉伯商人带来伊斯兰教，马尔代夫成为苏丹国；郑和曾于1411年和1430年到访。1558年葡萄牙军队攻占群岛，1573年被逐走，此后马累的苏丹们在欧洲海上强权林立的时代保住了独立。

en: The Dhofari are the people of Dhofar, the monsoon-watered coast and mountains of southwestern Oman around the ports of Salalah, Mirbat and Raysut, historically the world's chief frankincense country. Its harbors, first Khor Rori and later the medieval city of Zafar at Al-Baleed, shipped incense across the Indian Ocean as far as China; Marco Polo described Zafar around 1300 as a flourishing Muslim city ruled from Aden, and Ibn Battuta and Zheng He's fleets later called there. The mountains hold the Shahri, regarded as the region's original inhabitants, who speak the South Arabian tongue of Jibbali and herd cattle and camels, while the coastal towns use the distinctive Dhofari Arabic dialect. In the Middle Ages Dhofar passed under the Kathiri sultans and then the Qara mountain tribes; Zafar declined in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries through silting harbors and Portuguese, Ottoman and Mamluk raids. By the early nineteenth century the local sheikhs ruled under the suzerainty of the sultans of Muscat.
zh: 佐法尔人生活在阿曼西南部受季风雨滋润的佐法尔海岸与山地，聚居于塞拉莱、米尔巴特和赖苏特等港口，这里自古是世界首要的乳香产地。当地港口先是豪尔罗里，后来是拜利德的中世纪城市扎法尔，把乳香经印度洋远销到中国；约1300年马可·波罗记述扎法尔是一座受亚丁管辖的繁华穆斯林城市，伊本·白图泰和郑和的船队后来也曾到访。山地里住着被视为当地最早居民的沙赫里人，他们使用南阿拉伯语的吉巴里语，牧放牛和骆驼；沿海城镇则说独特的佐法尔阿拉伯语。中世纪时，佐法尔先后归属卡蒂里苏丹国和卡拉山地部落；16至17世纪，由于港口淤塞以及葡萄牙人、奥斯曼人和马穆鲁克的侵扰，扎法尔走向衰落。到19世纪初，当地谢赫们已在马斯喀特苏丹的宗主权下治理这片土地。

en: The Dhundhari are the Indo-Aryan people of Dhundhar, the country east of the Aravalli Range around Amber, Ajmer and Ranthambore, whose Rajasthani speech is also called Jaipuri after the city that grew up in its heartland. Written in Devanagari, Dhundhari also carries a literary tradition shaped by Jain scholars, above all the seventeenth-century works of Todarmal. In the eleventh century the Kachwaha Rajput prince Dulha Rai seized the region from its Meena chiefs, and his son Kakil Dev took Amber in 1037; Amber became the dynasty's capital around 1207 and remained so for five hundred years. The Kachwahas rose with the Mughals: Raja Man Singh I, who built most of Amber Fort, was one of Akbar's foremost generals, and his grandson Mirza Raja Jai Singh I commanded imperial armies under Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb. In 1727 Sawai Jai Singh II, himself a noted astronomer who built observatories across northern India, founded the planned city of Jaipur as his new capital. Jaipur became one of the richest Rajput states of the eighteenth century, and in 1818 its rulers accepted British paramountcy as a princely state.
zh: 敦达尔人是敦达尔地区的印度-雅利安居民，这片土地位于阿拉瓦利山脉以东，安贝尔、阿杰梅尔和兰坦波尔都在境内；他们讲的敦达尔语属拉贾斯坦语支，因后来兴起于其腹地的斋浦尔城又名斋浦尔语，用天城文书写，并有耆那教学者塑造的文学传统，17世纪托达尔马尔的著作最为著名。11世纪，卡奇瓦哈拉杰普特王公杜尔哈·拉伊从米纳酋长手中夺取该地，其子卡基尔·德夫于1037年攻占安贝尔，约1207年安贝尔成为王朝首都，此后五百年间一直是卡奇瓦哈人的统治中心。卡奇瓦哈人随莫卧儿崛起：主持修建安贝尔堡主体的曼·辛格一世是阿克巴最倚重的将领之一，其孙米尔扎·拉贾·贾伊·辛格一世则在沙贾汗和奥朗则布麾下统率帝国大军。1727年，精通天文、在北印度多地修建天文台的萨瓦伊·贾伊·辛格二世建立规划城市斋浦尔作为新都。斋浦尔后来成为18世纪最富庶的拉杰普特邦国之一，1818年其统治者接受英国宗主权，成为土邦。

en: The Dimasa, whose name means people of the great waters, are one of the oldest peoples of north-eastern India and the leading tribe of the Bodo-Kachari family, speaking a Boro-Garo language of the Tibeto-Burman stock. Organised into some forty exogamous clans under village headmen called Khunang, they long kept an animist faith of spirits called Madai and twelve sacred groves known as Daikho. After the fall of ancient Kamarupa they built their own Dimasa, or Kachari, kingdom in the Dhansiri valley, with its capital at Dimapur, whose brick ruins and carved sandstone pillars recall the architecture of Bengal. Ahom chronicles record border wars from the late thirteenth century: in 1490 the Dimasa defeated an Ahom incursion, but a renewed Ahom advance under King Suhungmung killed their king Khorapha and ended with the sack of Dimapur in 1536. After a long interregnum the rulers re-established themselves at Maibong around 1558, where a clan assembly could elect and check the king, and in 1745 they inherited the Koch state of Khaspur by marriage and moved their court there, gradually adopting Hindu titles and caste. Burmese conquest overthrew them in the 1820s; the Treaty of Yandabo of 1826 briefly restored their last king Govinda Chandra, and after his death the British annexed the plains in 1832 and the hills soon after, though the Dimasa kept their clan society and old beliefs in the North Cachar hills.
zh: 底马撒人意即“大水之民”，是印度东北部最古老的族群之一，也是博多—卡查里族群中最主要的一支，操藏缅语系博多—加罗语支的语言。他们分为约四十个外婚制氏族，各村由“库南”首领管理，长期信奉万物有灵的“马代”神灵和十二处名为“代科”的圣林。古迦摩缕波王国灭亡后，他们在丹西里河流域建立了自己的底马撒王国（又称卡查里王国），以迪马普尔为都，那里的砖砌城墙和雕纹沙岩石柱显示出受孟加拉建筑风格影响的城市气象。阿洪编年史记载了13世纪末以来的边境战争：1490年底马撒人击退阿洪来犯；但阿洪国王苏洪蒙再度大举进攻，杀死其王科拉法，并于1536年攻陷迪马普尔。经过漫长的空位期，统治者约在1558年定都迈邦，由氏族代表组成的王族会议有权选举和制约国王；1745年他们通过联姻继承科奇人的卡斯普尔政权并迁都于此，逐渐采用印度教的名号和种姓。19世纪20年代缅甸征服推翻了他们，1826年《扬达波条约》后末代国王戈文达·钱德拉一度复位；他死后，英国人于1832年吞并平原、随后又吞并山区，王国告终，而底马撒人在北卡查尔山区仍保留着氏族社会和古老信仰。

en: The Diné, better known to outsiders as the Navajo, are the people of Dinétah, the country between the San Juan River and the Chama Valley in present-day New Mexico, ringed by four sacred peaks from Blanca Peak in Colorado to the San Francisco Peaks in Arizona. They call themselves Diné, “the people”, and speak Diné bizaad, a Southern Athabaskan language of the Na-Dené family, kin to the Apache tongues; their ancestors parted from other Athabaskan hunters in northwestern Canada and Alaska and began a southward migration along the Rocky Mountains roughly a thousand years ago, perhaps set in motion by the Saint Elias volcanic eruption of 803. At first hunter-gatherers, the Diné learned maize, bean and squash farming from the Pueblo peoples, with whom mid-1500s Spanish records already show them trading bison hides and stone for maize and cotton cloth. Spanish friars called them Apachu de Nabajo in the 1620s, from a Tewa word for large cultivated lands, and by the 1640s the name Navajo was in use; Spanish writers of the 1670s placed them firmly in Dinétah. During the 1700s they built up great flocks of sheep and goats taken from the Spaniards, and Diné women turned the wool into the woven blankets that became a staple of their trade and art.
zh: 迪内人在外来者口中更常被称为纳瓦霍人，他们的家园叫迪内塔，位于今新墨西哥州圣胡安河与查马河谷之间，由科罗拉多的布兰卡峰到亚利桑那的圣弗朗西斯科峰等四座圣山环绕。他们自称迪内，意思是“人民”，讲的迪内语属于纳-德内语系的南阿萨巴斯卡语支，与阿帕切诸语相近；他们的先民原是加拿大西北部和阿拉斯加的阿萨巴斯卡猎人，约一千年前沿落基山脉向南迁徙，其起因或许与803年圣伊莱亚斯山的火山喷发有关。迪内人起初以狩猎采集为生，后来向普韦布洛人学会了玉米、豆类和南瓜的种植；16世纪中叶的西班牙文献已记载他们用野牛皮和石料换取普韦布洛人的玉米和棉布。西班牙修士在17世纪20年代称他们为“纳瓦霍的阿帕切人”，该词来自特瓦语中意为大片耕地的词，到17世纪40年代“纳瓦霍”一名已通行；17世纪70年代的西班牙文献明确把他们的住地记在迪内塔。18世纪，他们用从西班牙人那里得到的绵羊和山羊建起庞大畜群，迪内妇女把羊毛织成毛毯，这种织物日后成为他们贸易与工艺的招牌。

en: The Dinga, also called Dzing or Ding, are a Bantu people of the western Democratic Republic of the Congo, living around Idiofa in the Kwilu country among the Mbuun, Pende and Yanzi. They speak Ding, a language of the Boma-Dzing group of Bantu, and share with their neighbors a matrilineal social order and belief in the supreme being Nzeem-a-mpong.
zh: 丁加人又称津格人或丁人，是刚果民主共和国西部的班图族群，住在奎卢地区的伊迪奥法一带，与姆布恩人、彭德人和扬齐人为邻。他们使用丁语，属班图语的博马—津格语群，和邻族一样行母系制，信奉至高神恩津—姆蓬。

en: The Dinka, who call themselves Muonyjang, are the largest Nilotic people of the southern Sudan, spread in many independent clans along the White Nile from Bor to Renk and through the Bahr el-Ghazal and Sobat floodplains of the Sudd. Their ancestors lived on the southern edge of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alodia in the Gezira, whose language left traces in Dinka speech; medieval Arab writers of the 1200s knew raiders called the Damadim in this region, possible ancestors of the western Nilotes, who sacked Alodia's capital Soba around 1220. As Alodia crumbled during the thirteenth century, slave raids and drought set the Dinka clans moving south into the marshes, and the founding of the Funj Sultanate in 1504 pushed the migration deeper into the south over the following three centuries. Cattle-keeping agro-pastoralists, the Dinka move with their herds between dry-season and rainy-season pastures, count wealth and marriage payments in long-horned cattle, and venerate the high god Nhialic through spear-masters and earthen shrine-mounds; rivalry over grazing along the way made the Nuer their habitual foes.
zh: 丁卡人自称穆奥尼扬，是苏丹南部最大的尼罗特民族，众多互不统属的氏族分布在白尼罗河从博尔到伦克一线，以及苏德沼泽的加扎勒河、索巴特河平原。他们的先民原居杰济拉，处在基督教努比亚王国阿洛迪亚的南缘，丁卡语里保留着努比亚语的痕迹；13世纪的阿拉伯作家记载这一带有名叫达马迪姆的劫掠者，可能就是西尼罗特人的先民，他们约在1220年洗劫了阿洛迪亚首都索巴。13世纪阿洛迪亚瓦解后，奴隶劫掠和干旱驱使丁卡各氏族南迁入泽；1504年丰吉苏丹国建立，又在此后三个世纪里把迁徙浪潮推向更南的地方。丁卡人是养牛的农牧民族，随旱雨季轮换牧场，财富和聘礼都以长角牛计算，信奉至高神恩亚利克，由长矛首领主持宗教仪式并垒筑土丘神龛；争夺牧场的长期冲突，则使努尔人成为他们的宿敌。

en: The Djabuganjdjin, also called Djabugay or Tjapukai, are the Aboriginal people of the densely forested Great Dividing Range behind Cairns, holding the plateau south and east of Mareeba, the Barron River from Mareeba to Kuranda and the country reaching north toward Port Douglas, with the rainforest edge from Tolga to Mount Molloy as their western border. Their language, Djabugay, belongs to the Yidinic branch of the Pama-Nyungan family and is closely related to Yidiny; it is one of the few Australian languages with no dual form. In their bulurru, or Dreamtime, the Rainbow Serpent Gudju Gudju, in the shape of the giant carpet snake Budadji, carved the Barron Gorge on his journey to the sea, while the ancestral brothers Damarri and Guyala shaped the land, made the plant foods and gave the people their customary law and moiety-based marriage rules.
zh: 贾布冈金人又称贾布盖人或贾普凯人，是凯恩斯后方森林茂密的大分水岭地区的原住民，领有马里巴东南面的台地、从马里巴到库兰达的巴伦河两岸，以及向北延伸至道格拉斯港的地带，西界是从托尔加到莫洛伊山的雨林边缘。他们的语言贾布盖语属于帕马-牛雅语系伊迪尼语支，与伊迪尼语关系密切，并且是少数没有双数语法形式的澳大利亚语言之一。在他们称为“布鲁鲁”的梦幻时代传说里，彩虹蛇古朱·古朱化作巨蟒布达吉，在入海途中凿出了巴伦峡谷；始祖兄弟达马里和瓜亚拉则塑造了山川大地，造出植物性食物，并为人们定下习惯法和按偶族通婚的规则。

en: The Djeoromitxi, also called Jabuti, are a small Macro-Jê people of southern Rondônia in Brazil, living around the headwaters of the Rio Branco and along the Rio Guaporé. Their language, Jabutí, forms the small Yabutian branch together with Arikapú, and their original lands were overrun by gold prospectors before indigenous territories were demarcated for them.
zh: 雅布蒂人是巴西朗多尼亚州南部的小族群，住在布兰科河源头和瓜波雷河一带。他们的雅布蒂语与阿里卡普语共同构成大环热语系下的雅布蒂语支；其世代居住的土地曾遭淘金者侵占，后来才为他们划定原住民保留地。

en: The Djirbalngani, or Dyirbal, are rainforest Aboriginal people of the Atherton Tableland in northern Queensland, once holding some one thousand one hundred square miles from Herberton south to the headwaters of the Herbert River, with Tully Falls as their eastern boundary; Ravenshoe and Millaa Millaa later grew on their land. Their language, of the Dyirbalic branch of Pama-Nyungan, sorts every noun into four genders, masculine, feminine, edible and neuter, and speakers once switched from everyday Guwal into a special mother-in-law speech, Dyalnguy, whenever their mother-in-law or father-in-law was present. The people were organized into four named sections, each with its own totem, the black eel, kite hawk, large eel and eaglehawk, and a strict rule that each section marry only into its prescribed partner section, children belonging to a third.
zh: 吉巴尔恩甘人又称迪尔巴尔人，是昆士兰北部阿瑟顿台地的雨林原住民，曾领有约一千一百平方英里土地，北起赫伯顿、南至赫伯特河上游，东以塔利瀑布为界，雷文斯霍和米拉米拉后来都建在他们的土地上。他们的语言属帕马-牛雅语系迪尔巴利语支，把所有名词归入阳性、阴性、可食性和中性四个性；当岳母或公公在场时，人们还要从日常用语“古瓦尔”切换成专门的避讳语“迪亚尔努伊”。全社会分为四个命名分支，各有黑鳗、鸢、大鳗和楔尾雕作为图腾，并实行严格的婚制：每个分支只能与指定的分支通婚，子女则归入第三个分支。

en: The Doeg, also called the Taux or Dogue, were an Algonquian-speaking people of the upper Potomac River in what became northern Virginia. One account places their earlier home in King George County, from which they split into three groups around 1557. When John Smith explored the Potomac in 1608 he found their main town, Tauxenent, on the neck of land later called Mason Neck, with hamlets at Pamacocack, the later Quantico, and along Neabsco and Powells creeks; they fished the river and grew corn. They may have been a branch of the Nanticoke of the Maryland Eastern Shore and spoke a dialect close to Piscataway. A Doeg raid in July 1675 brought savage militia reprisals that helped ignite Bacon's Rebellion, after which the Doeg cease to appear in colonial records as a distinct community.
zh: 多埃格人又称托克斯人或多格人，是波托马克河上游、今弗吉尼亚州北部的阿尔冈昆语族群。据一则记载，他们早先居住在乔治王县一带，约1557年分成三支。1608年约翰·史密斯考察波托马克河时，他们的主要城镇托克塞嫩特位于后来被称为梅森岬的半岛上，帕马科科克（后来的匡蒂科）以及尼阿布斯科溪、鲍威尔溪沿岸也有村落；居民以捕鱼和种植玉米为生。多埃格人可能是马里兰东海岸楠蒂科克人的一支，所说方言接近皮斯卡塔韦语。1675年7月多埃格人的一次袭击招致民兵的残酷报复，并成为培根叛乱的导火索之一，此后多埃格人作为一个独立群体不再见于殖民地记录。

en: The Dogon are an indigenous farming people of the sandstone cliffs and plateaus south of the Niger bend in central Mali, their country cut by the 150-kilometre Bandiagara Escarpment. They speak the Dogon languages, an isolated branch of the Niger-Congo family, and are probably descended from several groups of different origins who refused conversion to Islam and retreated from Muslim-ruled lands; one oral tradition brings them from the Mande country near Bamako, with the first settlement at Kani-Na, and they had reached the Sanga region by the fifteenth century. Perched along the cliff face for defence, their villages were repeatedly targeted by jihad expeditions and merchant slave raiders, since Islamic law classed the Dogon as pagan dar al-harb. Patrilineal clans are led by their oldest male elder, and traditional religion honours the creator Amma and the water spirits called Nommo, expressed in mask dances such as the Kanaga, the long Sigui ceremony cycle, wooden sculpture and flat-roofed cliff architecture.
zh: 多贡人是尼日尔河河曲以南、马里中部砂岩悬崖与高原上的土著农耕民族，其家园被绵延150公里的邦贾加拉陡崖横穿。他们讲的多贡诸语是尼日尔—刚果语系中一个孤立的分支；多贡人很可能是若干来源不同、拒绝改宗伊斯兰教、从穆斯林统治地区退入山中的群体的后裔。一种口传传统称他们来自巴马科附近的曼德地区，最早的聚落是卡尼-纳，到15世纪他们已推进到桑加一带。村落高踞崖壁以便防守，却仍不断遭到圣战远征和商人奴隶劫掠队的袭击，因为伊斯兰教法把多贡人视为异教的“战争之地”居民。社会按父系氏族组织，由最年长的男性长老统领；传统信仰敬奉创世神阿马和称“诺莫”的水神，通过卡纳加等面具舞、周期漫长的锡圭仪式、木雕和平顶崖居建筑表达出来。

en: The Dom are an Indo-Aryan people scattered across the Middle East and North Africa, from eastern Anatolia and the Caucasus to Syria, Iraq and Egypt. They descend from the Dom caste of the Indian subcontinent but left India by a different route and at a different time from the Romani of Europe; linguists derive both names, Domari and Romani, from the same Indo-Aryan word for a caste of itinerant musicians. Arab writers knew them as the Nawar, roaming smiths, horse traders, musicians and dancers whose groups included the Ghawazi dancers of Egypt. Under Ottoman rule their communities were woven into town life across Anatolia, and the travel writer Evliya Çelebi, visiting Komotini in 1668, recorded traditions linking the empire's peripatetic peoples to Ottoman Egypt, from which families had been moved to Rumelia after 1517. Their tongue, Domari, has no standard written form and is laced with Kurdish, Turkish, Arabic and Persian words, with a distinct Garachi dialect in northern Turkey.
zh: 多姆人是散居在中东和北非的印度-雅利安族群，分布范围从安纳托利亚东部和高加索一直延伸到叙利亚、伊拉克和埃及。他们是印度次大陆多姆种姓的后裔，但离开印度的时间和路线都与欧洲的罗姆人不同；语言学家认为，多姆语和罗姆语的名称同出一源，都来自指代游居乐师种姓的印度-雅利安语源词。阿拉伯作家称他们为纳瓦尔人，即游走四方的铁匠、马贩、乐师和舞者，埃及的加瓦齐舞女群体便出自其中。奥斯曼统治时期，他们的社团融入安纳托利亚各地的城镇生活；旅行家埃夫利亚·切莱比1668年造访科莫蒂尼时，记载了帝国境内游居群体与奥斯曼埃及相连的传统，1517年之后确有家族从埃及被迁往鲁米利亚。他们的语言多姆语没有标准书面形式，吸收了库尔德语、土耳其语、阿拉伯语和波斯语词汇，在土耳其北部还有独特的加拉奇方言。

en: The Dompu, or Dou Dompu, are an Austronesian people of central Sumbawa, between the Bimanese east and the Sumbawanese west. Their land was one of the six old chiefdoms, or kedatuan, of Sumbawa listed alongside Bima and Tambora; local tradition also connects it with the age of the Majapahit minister Gajah Mada. Anciently Buddhist in culture, Dompu was fully Islamized in the course of the seventeenth century, like its neighbours Bima and Sumbawa, and its rulers later bore the title of sultan. The catastrophe that defined Dompu history was the eruption of Mount Tambora in 1815: only twelve of its villages survived, and the shattered districts were resettled by migrants from Bima. The descendants of the old Dompu thus became effectively a subgroup of the Bimanese, and their speech survives as the Dompu dialect of the Bima language, carrying traces of the Tambora culture that the eruption destroyed.
zh: 栋普人（自称杜栋普）是松巴哇岛中部的南岛语族群，地处东部比马人与西部松巴哇人之间。栋普地方曾是松巴哇岛上与比马、坦博拉并列的六大古老酋长邦（克达图安）之一，当地传说还把它与满者伯夷重臣加查·马达的时代联系在一起。栋普古时受佛教文化影响，17世纪间与邻邦比马、松巴哇一样全面伊斯兰化，统治者后来也拥有苏丹头衔。栋普历史上最关键的劫难是1815年坦博拉火山大喷发：原有村落仅存十二座，残破的土地随后由来自比马的移民重新填补。老栋普人的后裔因此实际上成为比马人的一个支系，其语言也作为比马语的栋普方言留存下来，其中仍保留着被火山摧毁的坦博拉文化的痕迹。

en: The Dongjiang Hakka occupy the upper valley of the Dong River in north-eastern Guangdong, the counties of Longchuan, Heping, Lianping and Boluo around the later city of Heyuan, whose name means source of the river. This was among the first parts of Lingnan brought under Chinese administration: after the Qin conquest of the Hundred Yue in 214 BC the new Nanhai commandery was divided into counties including Longchuan and Boluo, and the Qin general Zhao Tuo, magistrate of Longchuan, went on to found the kingdom of Nanyue in 204 BC. The hills long kept the area a borderland of Yue, She and Yao peoples, and the present Hakka population descends mainly from migrants who came south through Jiangxi in the late Yuan and early Ming and again after the Qing coastal evacuation of the 1660s. Their speech belongs to the central Guangdong group of Hakka dialects, while a river-bank local speech of the Dong valley is classed by some scholars with Hakka and by others with Yue.
zh: 东江客家人聚居在广东东北部东江上游河谷，即后来河源市一带的龙川、和平、连平、博罗诸县；河源之名，意为河水之源。这里是岭南最早纳入中原王朝建制的地区之一：公元前214年秦朝征服百越后，新置南海郡，下设龙川、博罗等县，曾任龙川县令的秦将赵佗后来于公元前204年建立南越国。山区长期使这里成为越人、畲人和瑶人活动的边地，今天的客家居民主要是元末明初取道江西南下的移民，以及17世纪60年代清代迁界之后再次迁入者的后裔。他们的方言属客家话粤中片；东江沿岸还通行一种本地话，学者或归入客家话，或归入粤语。

en: The Doolboong, also recorded as Duulngari or Tulpung, were an Aboriginal people of the Cambridge Gulf coast, where the Northern Territory meets north-eastern Western Australia; the later port of Wyndham stands within their traditional country. Their language died out without any written record, and speakers of neighbouring Gajirrabeng and Miriwoong thought it resembled Gajirrabeng, which would place it among the Jarrakan tongues, though a Worrorran affiliation cannot be ruled out. In 1819 the naval surveyor Phillip Parker King sailed into Cambridge Gulf, naming the inlet and exploring the river later called the King River before finding no fresh water on its mudflats and withdrawing; this was the first recorded European visit to Doolboong waters.
zh: 杜隆邦人又记为杜尔恩加里或图尔庞，是剑桥湾沿岸的原住民，其地处在北领地与西澳大利亚东北部相接之处，后来的港口温德姆就建在他们的传统领地内。他们的语言没有留下任何书面记录便已消亡；邻近的吉吉拉本语和米里温语使用者认为它与吉吉拉本语相近，若如此则应归入杰拉甘语系，但也不能排除它属于沃罗拉语系。1819年，海军测量员菲利普·帕克·金驶入剑桥湾，为这座海湾命名，并考察了后来得名金河的河流，但在滩涂上找不到淡水，最终撤离；这是有记载的欧洲人首次进入杜隆邦人的水域。

en: The Dorset were a Paleo-Eskimo people of the North American Arctic, whose culture flourished from about 500 BCE until its final centuries between 1000 and 1500 CE, and takes its name from Cape Dorset, now Kinngait, where its first traces were identified. Highly adapted to extreme cold and sea-ice hunting, they took seals and walrus at their breathing holes, using distinctive triangular end-blades, burins and oil lamps carved from soapstone; unlike both their predecessors and the Inuit who followed them, they had no bows and arrows, no drills and apparently no dogs. Their artists left small, striking soapstone carvings of animals and human figures. The Dorset way of life came under double pressure in the second millennium: the Medieval Warm Period thinned and shifted the sea ice on which their hunting depended, while from the eleventh century the Thule people, ancestors of the modern Inuit, spread eastward from Alaska across the Arctic. Genetic studies show the two populations barely mixed, and Dorset settlements were progressively abandoned, though radiocarbon dates prove some groups still lived around Cambridge Bay as late as 1350. Inuit oral tradition preserves the memory of these earlier inhabitants as the Tuniit, strong but shy giants who were easily driven away; the last Dorset vanished within the following century, leaving their tools and carvings as the main record of a people the game places in their final strongholds along the eastern shores of Hudson Bay.
zh: 多尔塞特人是北美北极地区的古爱斯基摩人，其文化约从公元前500年延续到公元1000年至1500年之间的最后阶段，名称来自最早发现其遗迹的多塞特角（今金盖特）。他们高度适应严寒与海冰狩猎，在呼吸孔处捕猎海豹和海象，使用独具特色的三角形端刃器、雕刻刀和皂石油灯；与先于他们的文化及后来的因纽特人不同，多尔塞特人没有弓箭、没有钻具，似乎也没有狗。他们的艺人留下了造型生动的小型皂石动物和人像雕刻。第二个千年里，多尔塞特人的生活方式承受着双重压力：中世纪暖期使他们赖以为生的海冰变薄并北移，而从11世纪起，后世因纽特人的祖先图勒人自阿拉斯加向东扩散，遍布北极。基因研究显示两个群体几乎没有混血，多尔塞特人的定居点相继被废弃，不过碳十四测年证明，迟至1350年仍有部分群体生活在剑桥湾一带。因纽特人的口传传统把这些早先的居民记为“图尼特人”：强壮却羞怯、容易被赶走的巨人。最后一批多尔塞特人在随后的一个世纪里消失，只留下工具和雕刻作为这个民族的主要记录；游戏将他们放在哈德逊湾东岸的最后据点之中。

en: The Drehu are the Kanak people of Lifou, the largest of the Loyalty Islands off the east coast of Grande Terre in New Caledonia, their Drehu language, self-named qene drehu and once also called Lifou, being the chief tongue of the Loyalty Islands group, with communities on neighbouring Ouvéa as well. As a New Caledonian branch Oceanic language it descends from the Austronesian speech of Lapita voyagers who settled these raised limestone islands after 1100 BC, adapting taro growing to sunken pits and mastering long fishing voyages over open water. Drehu society developed powerful chiefs who were addressed in a special elevated register, qene miny, kept apart from ordinary speech; rank, shell-money exchanges and clan ceremonies ordered life on an island without streams or building stone for fortifications. Europeans only located the Loyalty Islands in the 1790s, when the English whaler William Raven mapped Maré, Lifou and Ouvéa between 1793 and 1796, after which the only outsiders the Drehu met before 1837 were the crews of occasional whaling ships.
zh: 德雷胡人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛东岸外洛亚蒂群岛中最大岛屿利富岛的卡纳克人，其德雷胡语自称“凯内·德雷胡”，旧称利富语，是洛亚蒂群岛语组的主要语言，邻近的乌韦阿岛上也有使用群体。作为新喀里多尼亚语支的大洋洲语言，它源自公元前1100年以后定居这些抬升石灰岩岛的拉皮塔航海者的南岛语；移民们把芋头种植改造为下沉式坑种，并掌握了远海长途捕鱼航行。德雷胡社会发展出权势强大的酋长，人们以一种特殊的庄重语域“凯内·米尼”对酋长说话，与日常用语严格分开；在这座没有溪流、也没有石材可供筑垒的岛上，等级、贝币交换和氏族仪式规范着全部生活。欧洲人直到18世纪90年代才发现洛亚蒂群岛：英国捕鲸人威廉·雷文于1793—1796年间测绘了马雷岛、利富岛和乌韦阿岛；此后到1837年之前，德雷胡人见到的外来者只有偶尔路过的捕鲸船。

en: The Duau are the people of Dobu, a small extinct-volcano island set in the Dawson Strait between Fergusson and Normanby at the heart of the D'Entrecasteaux group. Despite the island's modest size, their Dobuan language, an Austronesian tongue, became the lingua franca of the whole archipelago, carried abroad by their traders. Dobuan society is built on matrilineal lineages and tight village clusters, whose houses stand on piles in inward-facing circles amid coconut and betel palms, and on a subsistence economy centered on yams together with taro, bananas, sago and lagoon fishing. The island's true distinction lies in trade: as a key node of the kula ring, Dobuans sailed north to the Trobriands and south to Milne Bay on long canoe voyages, exchanging shell valuables, pots and garden produce with hereditary partners and building both wealth and renown across the Massim. Their wider world changed only in 1792, when d'Entrecasteaux's French expedition became the first Europeans to sight the D'Entrecasteaux Islands; for decades afterward Dobu remained a vigorous, independent center of ceremonial exchange.
zh: 杜奥人是多布岛的居民，这座由死火山形成的小岛坐落在当特尔卡斯托群岛中心、弗格森岛与诺曼比岛之间的道森海峡中。岛虽不大，他们的多布语却是一种南岛语言，并随商人传播成为整个群岛的通用语。多布社会以母系世系和紧密的村落群为骨架：高脚屋围成向内的圆圈，掩映在椰子树和槟榔树之间；生计经济以山药为中心，辅以芋头、香蕉、西谷和潟湖捕鱼。多布真正的不凡之处在于贸易：作为库拉交换圈的关键节点，多布人驾独木舟远航，北至特罗布里恩群岛、南抵米尔恩湾，与世袭伙伴交换贝壳贵重物、陶罐和农产品，在整个马辛地区积累财富与声望。他们的外部世界到1792年才发生变化：当特尔卡斯托率领的法国探险队成为首批望见当特尔卡斯托群岛的欧洲人；而在此后数十年间，多布始终是一个活跃而独立的仪式交换中心。

en: The Dunezza, or Dane-zaa, are an Athabaskan-speaking people of the Peace River country straddling what is now northern British Columbia and Alberta, known to Europeans as the Beaver and to the Dakelh as the Tsattine, both names meaning people who live among the beavers. Before the nineteenth century they ranged farther east around the Athabasca and Clearwater rivers and Lake Athabasca, while Charlie Lake Cave near Fort St. John shows more than ten thousand years of continuous indigenous occupation. Armed through the fur trade, the Plains Cree pushed them northwest in the late eighteenth century; the peace that followed, dividing the country with the Cree south of the Peace River and the Dane-zaa north, gave the river its name. Alexander Mackenzie met them in 1793 and built Rocky Mountain Fort at the Moberly River in 1794, and Dane-zaa hunters provisioned the posts with bison meat and grease until bison grew scarce in the early 1820s. Their Dreamer prophets had long foretold the coming of Europeans, and their teachings and songs shaped Dane-zaa life through the fur-trade era.
zh: 杜内扎人（即丹尼扎人）是说阿萨巴斯卡语的族群，生活在横跨今不列颠哥伦比亚省北部与艾伯塔省的皮斯河流域；欧洲人旧称他们为比弗人，达凯尔人则叫他们察廷人，两个名字都意为“住在海狸中间的人”。19世纪以前，他们的活动范围更靠东，远达阿萨巴斯卡河、克利尔沃特河与阿萨巴斯卡湖一带；圣约翰堡附近的查理湖洞留有超过一万年连续居住的遗迹。18世纪后期，凭借毛皮贸易获得火器的平原克里人把他们逼向西北；随后双方议和，约定克里人居于皮斯河以南、杜内扎人居于以北，皮斯河（意为和平河）便因这份和约得名。1793年亚历山大·麦肯齐与他们接触，1794年又在莫伯利河口建立落基山堡；杜内扎猎人向各商站供应野牛肉和油脂，直到19世纪20年代初野牛日渐稀少。他们的“梦者”先知早已预言欧洲人的到来，其教义与歌谣贯穿了整个毛皮贸易时代。

en: The Dusun are the largest indigenous people of northern Borneo, scattered across the hills and upland valleys of Sabah from the western coastal plains to the Kinabatangan, Padas and Labuk-Sugut river basins. The name is foreign to them: Bruneian Malays ruling the coast called these farming villagers Orang Dusun, or “people of the orchards”, while they traditionally called themselves tulun tindal, and under the Sultanate of Brunei they paid a river tax in rice and forest produce. They are not one tribe but an assemblage of more than thirty sub-groups speaking mutually intelligible Dusunic and Paitanic languages, closely related to the Murutic languages and to the languages of the Philippines. Reputed peaceful and hard-working, they were the chief rice producers of North Borneo, living in longhouses, brewing rice wine and carrying rice and damar resin to coastal markets to exchange for salt and salted fish. Their traditional religion, Momolianism, centred on rice spirits, female shamans and the Kaamatan harvest festival, and traced their origin to the legendary first settlement of Nunuk Ragang. The earliest British account, written by Thomas Forrest in 1774, already described them as the agricultural people of the northern mountains, and most long kept to these animist ways in their inland valleys.
zh: 杜顺人是婆罗洲北部最大的原住民族群，散居在沙巴的丘陵与高地河谷之间，西起西部沿海平原，东至基纳巴坦甘河、帕达斯河与拉卜—苏古河流域。“杜顺”是外来称呼：统治沿海的文莱马来人把这些务农村民称为 Orang Dusun，意为“果园之人”，他们则自称 tulun tindal，即本地人；在文莱苏丹国统治下，他们要以稻米和林产品缴纳河税。杜顺并非单一部落，而是三十多个支系的集合，各支讲彼此可通的杜顺语族和派坦语族语言，与穆鲁特语族及菲律宾诸语言关系密切。他们以勤劳平和著称，是北婆罗洲主要的稻米生产者，住长屋、酿米酒，把稻米和达玛树脂挑到沿海集市，换回食盐和咸鱼。传统信仰莫莫利安教以稻灵、女祭司和庆祝丰收的卡马坦节为核心，并把族源追溯到传说中最早的定居地努努克拉冈。1774年英国人托马斯·福里斯特留下最早的记载，称他们是北部山区的农耕民族；在此后很长时间里，内陆河谷中的杜顺人大多仍保持着这套泛灵信仰。

en: The Dyula, also called Wangara or Juula, are a Mande Muslim merchant people whose name means merchant in Manding. After Mande elites adopted Islam in the 1200s, the rulers of Mali in the following century encouraged traders to found colonies near the southern goldfields, and from the 1300s Dyula families spread from Senegambia to the Niger bend and from the edge of the Sahara to the forest belt. They settled in self-governing quarters under local rulers, running caravan firms built on the lu, a household of a father, his sons and attached men, and they created trading cities including Begho, Bouna, Bondoukou and Kong. Around 1500 the cleric al-Hajj Salim Suwari shaped their Suwarian tradition, which taught Muslims to coexist with non-Muslim rulers and keep jihad only for self-defence, so that Dyula scholars could serve even animist courts. In 1710 the Dyula leader Seku Watara united the merchant houses to build the Kong Empire over these routes; after his death around 1745 it devolved into rival Watara fiefs, while Kong itself remained a famed market for gold and kola nuts and a centre of Islamic learning.
zh: 迪尤拉人又称万加拉人或朱拉人，是曼德人中的穆斯林商人民族，其名字在曼丁哥语中就是商人的意思。13世纪曼德上层皈依伊斯兰教后，马里的统治者在接下来的一个世纪鼓励商人到南方金矿区附近建立商站；从14世纪起，迪尤拉家族的足迹从塞内冈比亚延伸到尼日尔河曲，从撒哈拉南缘延伸到森林地带。他们在各地统治者治下组建自治的商人街区，以名为卢的家族商号经营商队，商号由父亲、儿子和依附男子组成，并建起贝戈、布纳、邦杜库、孔等商业城市。约1500年，宗教学者哈吉·萨利姆·苏瓦里奠定了苏瓦里传统，主张穆斯林与非穆斯林统治者和平共处、圣战仅用于自卫，因此迪尤拉学者甚至能在信奉万物有灵论的宫廷中任职。1710年，迪尤拉首领塞库·瓦塔拉联合各商人家族，在这些商路之上建立孔格帝国；他于1745年前后去世后，帝国分裂为瓦塔拉家族各支割据的领地，而孔城仍是黄金和柯拉果的著名市场与伊斯兰学术中心。

en: The East Franconians speak the dialect of the Main valley and the surrounding hill country, from Würzburg, Bamberg and Nuremberg to Coburg, Meiningen and the Vogtland town of Plauen, a transitional speech between Central and Upper German. Franks settled the region in the sixth century, and it became the eastern heartland of the stem Duchy of Franconia; after Duke Eberhard rebelled against Otto I and died in 939, the duchy was broken up, leaving the bishops of Würzburg to bear the nominal title of Duke of Franconia while the land fragmented into bishoprics, margraviates, imperial cities and knightly estates. Saint Kilian had been martyred at Würzburg in the seventh century, Henry II founded the rich bishopric of Bamberg in 1007, and under the Hohenstaufen the region was the centre of imperial power; from about 1190 the Burgraviate of Nuremberg passed to the Zollerns, the Franconian Hohenzollern line that would later rule Brandenburg and Prussia. In 1500 to 1512 the patchwork of states was gathered into the Franconian Circle. Nuremberg, where the Luther Bible was printed, led the turn to Protestantism, but the German Peasants' War of 1525 ravaged the Würzburg countryside, the Second Margrave War of 1552 devastated many towns, and the Thirty Years' War and later witch trials hit the region hard. When Napoleon reorganised Germany in 1803 to 1806, the bishoprics and tiny lordships were mediatised and most of Franconia passed to Bavaria, which organised it into Lower, Middle and Upper Franconia.
zh: 东法兰克尼亚人讲美因河谷及周围丘陵地带的方言，范围从维尔茨堡、班贝格、纽伦堡到科堡、迈宁根和福格特兰的普劳恩，是一种介于中部德语与上部德语之间的过渡方言。6世纪法兰克人在此定居，这里后来成为法兰克尼亚部落公国的东部核心；939年埃伯哈德公爵反叛奥托一世败亡后，公国被拆解，维尔茨堡主教挂名“法兰克尼亚公爵”，而土地则碎分为主教区、藩侯国、帝国城市和骑士领地。7世纪圣基利安在维尔茨堡殉道，1007年亨利二世设立富庶的班贝格主教区；霍亨斯陶芬王朝时期这里是帝国权力中心，约1190年起纽伦堡城堡伯国落入索伦家族——即后来统治勃兰登堡和普鲁士的霍亨索伦家族的法兰克尼亚支系。1500至1512年，这些星罗棋布的小邦被编入法兰克尼亚行政圈。印刷路德圣经的纽伦堡带头改宗新教，但1525年德意志农民战争蹂躏了维尔茨堡乡野，1552年第二次藩侯战争使许多城镇残破，三十年战争和随后的猎巫浪潮又让当地遭受重创。1803至1806年拿破仑重组德意志，主教区和小领主被并吞，法兰克尼亚大部分划归巴伐利亚，成为下、中、上三个法兰克尼亚专区。

en: The Eastern Abenaki are the Algonquian-speaking bands of Maine, above all the Penobscot of the Penobscot River together with the Kennebec or Norridgewock, Androscoggin and smaller riverside groups, all members of the Wabanaki Confederacy. They combined hunting, fishing and gathering with limited maize planting, moving between coastal summer villages and inland winter camps, and the Penobscot alone may still have numbered about ten thousand when the French began settling among them. Champlain found their planting grounds on the Kennebec in 1604, but kidnappings, the fur trade and repeated epidemics soon weakened every band. Allied with the French and served by Jesuit missionaries, they raided the New England frontier through King Philip's War and Queen Anne's War; the conflict named for the missionary Sebastien Rale ended in 1724 with the storming of Norridgewock and Rale's death, after which many survivors withdrew to the Abenaki reserve of Odanak near the St. Francis River in Quebec. The Penobscot who stayed in Maine faced a scalp bounty in 1755, lost their French protector after the fall of Quebec in 1759, yet sided with the American rebels during the Revolutionary War, by when their numbers had fallen below five hundred.
zh: 东阿贝纳基人是缅因境内讲阿尔冈昆语的各部，以佩诺布斯科特河上的佩诺布斯科特人为主，还包括肯纳贝克（诺里奇沃克）、安德罗斯科金等河畔群体，全部加入了瓦巴纳基联盟。他们以狩猎、渔捞和采集为生，兼种少量玉米，按季节在海边夏村与内陆冬营之间迁徙；法国人开始在他们中间定居时，仅佩诺布斯科特一部可能仍有约一万人。1604年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰在肯纳贝克河见到他们的农田，但掳卖人口、毛皮贸易和接连的疫病很快削弱了每个部落。他们与法国结盟，由耶稣会传教士牧养，在菲利普国王战争和安妮女王战争中不断袭掠新英格兰边疆；以传教士塞巴斯蒂安·拉勒命名的那场战争于1724年以诺里奇沃克被攻破、拉勒被杀告终，此后许多幸存者退往魁北克圣弗朗索瓦河畔的阿贝纳基人保留地奥达纳克。留在缅因的佩诺布斯科特人在1755年面临悬赏割取头皮的法令，1759年魁北克陷落后又失去法国的庇护，却仍在美国独立战争中站在北美起义者一边；到那时，他们的人口已不足五百。

en: The Eastern Amazigh are the Berber-speaking communities that held out in Tripolitania and the Tunisian south, above all in the Nafusa mountains, the coastal town of Zuwarah and the island of Djerba. After the great Berber Revolt of the eighth century, Ibadi missionaries took refuge in the Nafusa and organized its people; under Imam Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afari they swept down to seize Tripoli in 757 and Kairouan in 758, until an Abbasid army broke them at Tawergha in 761. The mountains kept an independent Ibadi republic through the ninth century, allied to the Rustamids of Tahert, until the Aghlabid emir Ibrahim II defeated them at Manu in 896 and ended their imamate, executing its prisoners as heretics. Ibadi Islam and the Nafusi tongue, already appearing in sectarian manuscripts by the twelfth century, lived on in the mountain villages of Nalut, Jadu and Yafran. Zuwarah, recorded by the traveller al-Tijani in 1306 and on the Catalan Atlas of 1375, kept its Berber speech on the coast, while Djerba, Ibadi since the Arab conquest of 665, preserved the same heritage under Hafsid and then Ottoman rule.
zh: 东阿马齐格人是在的黎波里塔尼亚和突尼斯南部坚守柏柏尔语的社群，核心在奈富塞山、海滨城镇兹瓦拉和杰尔巴岛。8世纪柏柏尔大起义后，伊巴德派传教士退守奈富塞山，把山民组织起来；在伊玛目阿布·哈塔卜·马阿法里率领下，他们于757年攻占的黎波里、758年拿下凯鲁万，直到761年被阿拔斯军队在塔沃尔加击败。整个9世纪，山区维持着独立的伊巴德共和国，与塔赫特的鲁斯塔姆王朝遥相呼应；896年艾格莱卜埃米尔易卜拉欣二世在马努战役将其击败，以异端罪名处死战俘，终结了山中伊玛目政权。但伊巴德信仰和奈富塞语悄然存续，12世纪的教派手抄本中已出现奈富塞语词句，纳卢特、贾杜、耶夫兰等村落一直沿用。兹瓦拉在1306年旅行家提贾尼的记述和1375年的加泰罗尼亚地图集中均有记载，在海滨保住了柏柏尔语；665年阿拉伯征服后即信奉伊巴德派的杰尔巴，则在哈夫斯王朝和后来的奥斯曼治下保存了同一份传统。

en: The Eastern Kru are the easternmost Kru-speaking peoples of central and southern Ivory Coast: the Dida, sixty-odd tribes of the Fresco, Sassandra and Grand-Lahou lagoon coast, and the Bété, more than ninety clans of the inland forests around Gagnoa and Daloa, together with the Godie and Neyo. Dida tradition says they reached the Fresco and Sassandra shore in the 1000s, first living by fishing, then spreading into the forest as hunters and farmers, and they claim common ancestors, the Magwé, with the Bété. Bété oral history recalls a still earlier home in the Sahel and Sudanian savanna, from which warfare drove them southwest in the 1600s. Neither people knew kingship: loyalty stopped at the village or clan, and each settlement governed itself. From the 1700s the Bété took on customs from their Akan neighbors to the east, while the Ogbrougbrou Dida intermarried with lagoon peoples and fathered such Kwa-speaking groups as the Adioukrou of the Cosrou shore. The deep forest sheltered them from the slave raiders of the Sahel, and Ivorian Kru groups won a name for fighting off every slaving expedition that entered their country.
zh: 东克鲁诸族是科特迪瓦中南部最靠东的克鲁语人群：迪达人由六十多个部落组成，住在弗雷斯科、萨桑德拉和大拉乌的泻湖沿海；贝泰人则有九十多个氏族，散居加尼奥阿和达洛亚一带的内陆森林；此外还有戈迪人和内约人。迪达传统称，他们于11世纪抵达弗雷斯科和萨桑德拉海岸，起初以捕鱼为生，后来以猎人和农民的身份深入森林，并自认与贝泰人拥有共同祖先马格韦。贝泰人的口传历史则把更早的家园指向萨赫勒和苏丹草原，17世纪的战乱把他们逐向西南。两支人群都没有王权观念：认同止于村落或氏族，每个聚落自行治理。18世纪起，贝泰人从东面的阿坎邻居那里吸收了不少习俗；迪达的奥格布鲁部落则与泻湖居民通婚，繁衍出科斯鲁沿海讲夸语的阿朱克鲁人等群体。茂密森林掩护他们躲开萨赫勒来的猎奴者，科特迪瓦的克鲁各支也因击退每一支闯入其地的猎奴队伍而闻名。

en: The Eastern Pomeranians are the Low German-speaking people of the Baltic duchy of Pomerania, the Slavic land by the sea between the Oder estuary and the Vistula, whose Pomeranian and Lutici inhabitants were subdued by the Polish duke Bolesław III Wrymouth in campaigns between 1102 and 1121. His vassal Wartislaw I founded the Griffin dynasty, whose dukes ruled Pomerania for five centuries. The missionary Otto of Bamberg converted the people in visits of 1124 to 1125 and 1128, when the nobility accepted Christianity at Usedom, and a diocese was set up in 1140, later seated at Cammin. The dukes shifted between Polish, Saxon, Danish and imperial vassalage before settling under the Holy Roman Empire in 1227. During the Ostsiedlung the Griffin dukes founded towns on Magdeburg and Lübeck law, Stralsund in 1234 and Stettin from 1237 among them, settling colonists from Lower Saxony and Brandenburg whose Middle Low German speech became the East Pomeranian dialect while the native Slavs were gradually Germanized, and the coastal towns joined the Hanseatic League. Pomerania adopted Protestantism at the Treptow diet of 1534, with a church order drafted by Johannes Bugenhagen. When the last Griffin, Bogislaw XIV, died in 1637, the duchy was split: the Peace of Westphalia of 1648 gave Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg-Prussia and the west to Sweden, which ceded Stettin and the Oder estuary to Prussia by the Treaty of Stockholm in 1720; the Congress of Vienna in 1815 united all of Pomerania under the Prussian crown.
zh: 东波美拉尼亚人是波罗的海畔波美拉尼亚公国讲低地德语的居民。波美拉尼亚意为海滨之地，原住波美拉尼亚人和卢蒂奇人等斯拉夫人在1102至1121年的战事中被波兰公爵波列斯瓦夫三世征服。后者的封臣瓦季斯瓦夫一世开创格里芬王朝，该家族以公爵身份统治波美拉尼亚长达五个世纪。传教士班贝格的奥托于1124至1125年及1128年两度前来传教，贵族在乌瑟多姆接受基督教；1140年本地设立主教区，后来定驻卡缅。公爵们先后依附波兰、萨克森、丹麦和神圣罗马帝国，1227年以后固定为帝国封臣。东向殖民时期，格里芬公爵们按马格德堡法和吕贝克法兴建城镇，1234年建施特拉尔松德，1237年起建斯德丁，迁来下萨克森和勃兰登堡移民；他们的中古低地德语演变为东波美拉尼亚方言，本地斯拉夫人则逐渐日耳曼化，沿海城镇还加入了汉萨同盟。1534年，特雷普托议会定新教为公国信仰，约翰内斯·布根哈根起草了教会规章。1637年末代格里芬公爵博吉斯拉夫十四世去世，公国被瓜分：1648年《威斯特伐利亚和约》把远波美拉尼亚划给勃兰登堡-普鲁士，西部归瑞典；1720年《斯德哥尔摩条约》又使斯德丁和奥得河口转入普鲁士之手，1815年维也纳会议最终将整个波美拉尼亚并入普鲁士。

en: The Eastphalians are the people of Eastphalia, the eastern shires of the old Saxon stem duchy, lying between the Leine and the Elbe and Saale and stretching from the Lüneburg Heath to the Harz. Together with Westphalia, Angria and Nordalbingia it formed one of the four regions of Saxony, and its name means the eastern plain. In 775 the Eastphalians under their leader Hessi gave hostages and swore loyalty to Charlemagne on the Oker, and the bishoprics of Halberstadt and Hildesheim, founded in 804 and 815, anchored the region's Christianization. The Harz country was the hereditary land of Henry the Fowler, who became king in 919, and of his Ottonian descendants, who filled it with Romanesque abbeys such as Hildesheim and Quedlinburg. Bordering the Polabian Slavs beyond the Elbe, Eastphalia also became the launch pad of the Ostsiedlung, its northeastern edge forming the Altmark, the old march against the Wendish tribes. After Emperor Frederick I deposed Henry the Lion in 1180, the old region dissolved into a mosaic of states, above all the Welf Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg, the Anhalt counties, the imperial city of Goslar and the bishoprics of Magdeburg, Hildesheim and Halberstadt, whose people kept speaking the Eastphalian branch of Low German, descended from Old Saxon.
zh: 伊斯特伐利亚人是古萨克森部落公国东部诸郡——伊斯特伐利亚地区的居民，其地介于莱讷河与易北河、萨勒河之间，北起吕讷堡荒原，南至哈尔茨山。它与威斯特伐利亚、安格里亚和北阿尔宾吉亚同为萨克森四大行政区，地名意为东部平原。775年，伊斯特伐利亚人在首领赫西率领下，在奥克河畔向查理大帝交出人质并宣誓效忠；804年和815年先后设立的哈尔伯施塔特与希尔德斯海姆主教区，成为本地基督教化的支点。哈尔茨一带是919年登上王位的捕鸟者亨利及其奥托王朝后裔的世袭领地，他们在这里留下希尔德斯海姆、奎德林堡等罗曼式修道院。由于毗邻易北河彼岸的波拉布斯拉夫人，伊斯特伐利亚又是东向殖民的出发地，其东北边缘形成对付文德部落的旧边区阿尔特马克。1180年皇帝腓特烈一世废黜狮子亨利后，旧地分裂为众多邦国，首要者是韦尔夫家族的不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公国、安哈尔特诸伯国、帝国城市戈斯拉尔以及马格德堡、希尔德斯海姆和哈尔伯施塔特等主教区；这片土地上的居民继续使用源自古撒克逊语的低地德语伊斯特伐利亚分支。

en: The Edo, or Bini, are the Edoid-speaking people of the forest kingdom centered on Benin City in what is now southern Nigeria. Their first state was Igodomigodo, ruled by the Ogiso kings from around the ninth century; after a succession crisis the chiefs invited a prince from the Yoruba city of Ile-Ife, Oranmiyan, whose son Eweka founded the line of obas that ruled ever after. Benin City was already a substantial walled town by 1300, and under Oba Ewuare, who came to power in 1440, the kingdom expanded far beyond the Edo heartland and girded its capital with great moats and ramparts. Portuguese visitors arrived in 1485 and launched a trade in ivory, pepper, brass manillas and slaves that enriched the court and supplied its famous brass-casting guilds; the Benin Bronzes, naturalistic heads and plaques honoring the obas and queen mothers, count among Africa's foremost art. At its sixteenth-century height Benin held sway over neighboring Ijaw, Itsekiri, Urhobo and western Igbo communities of the Niger Delta. After civil war around 1689 and a succession struggle settled in 1721, Oba Akenzua restored stability and drew fresh wealth from the European trade.
zh: 埃多人（又称比尼人）是讲埃多伊德语的森林民族，以今尼日利亚南部的贝宁城为中心建立王国。他们最早的国家是伊戈多米戈多，约9世纪起由奥吉索诸王统治；王位继承危机之后，酋长们从约鲁巴城邦伊费请来王子奥兰米扬，其子埃韦卡开创了此后一脉相承的奥巴王系。到1300年，贝宁城已是颇具规模、建有城墙的城镇。1440年即位的奥巴·埃瓦雷把王国版图扩张到埃多核心地区之外，并在都城周围修筑了庞大的壕沟与壁垒。1485年葡萄牙人到来，开启象牙、胡椒、黄铜手镯和奴隶贸易，宫廷由此致富，并供养了著名的黄铜铸造行会；“贝宁青铜器”——纪念奥巴和王太后的写实头像与饰板——跻身非洲最杰出的艺术之列。16世纪鼎盛时，贝宁对尼日尔三角洲相邻的伊乔、伊策基里、乌尔霍博和西伊博等族群拥有宗主权。1689年前后的内战和1721年才了结的王位争斗之后，奥巴·阿肯祖阿恢复了稳定，并从对欧贸易中获得新的财富。

en: The Emberá, historically called the Chocó or Katío by the Spanish, are an indigenous people of the rainy Pacific lowlands of western Colombia, with related settlements later reaching eastern Panama and northwestern Ecuador. At the time of the conquest they held the upper and middle basins of the Atrato and San Juan rivers, and colonial documents distinguish groups such as the Citará of the Atrato lowlands and the Tatamá of the mountain foothills. Their dialects, together with Wounaan, make up the Chocó language family, which has no proven link to any other South American family. Spanish administration grouped the region into the Province of Chocó in 1739. From the late eighteenth century Emberá migrants moved down the Atrato tributaries into the Darién, where their pressure pushed the Guna toward the Caribbean coast, establishing the riverine settlements of modern Panama.
zh: 恩贝拉人在历史上被西班牙人称为乔科人或卡蒂奥人，是哥伦比亚西部多雨的太平洋低地的原住民，后来其支系的定居点远达巴拿马东部和厄瓜多尔西北部。征服之初，他们占据阿特拉托河与圣胡安河的上、中游流域；殖民档案把他们分为阿特拉托低地的西塔拉人、山麓地带的塔塔马人等群体。他们的各方言与沃南语共同构成乔科语系，该语系与南美其他语系均无确证的亲缘关系。1739年，西班牙殖民当局把这一地区划为乔科省。18世纪末起，恩贝拉移民沿阿特拉托河支流进入达连地区，其压力迫使库纳人退向加勒比海岸，并由此形成了今天巴拿马境内沿河而居的定居格局。

en: The Emilians are the people of the Po valley plain of Emilia, the region taking its name from the via Aemilia, the Roman road laid out in 187 BC from Piacenza to Rimini; in 1337 their cities of Bologna, Modena, Ferrara, Parma and Mantua were among the richest in Italy. Their speech is Emilian, an unstandardized Gallo-Italic language split into urban varieties such as Bolognese, Modenese, Parmesan, Ferrarese and Mantuan. After Lombard and Frankish rule the towns became free communes in the twelfth century, joined the Lombard League against the Hohenstaufen emperors and were long torn by Guelph and Ghibelline feuds, before passing into the hands of signori: the Este in Ferrara and later Modena, the Gonzaga in Mantua, the Farnese in Parma and Piacenza, while Bologna came under the papacy. The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, made the region a centre of legal learning, and Este courts patronized Matteo Maria Boiardo, Ludovico Ariosto and Torquato Tasso. Napoleon organized the region into the Cispadane Republic in 1797, where the Italian tricolour was first adopted; after his fall the Congress of Vienna in 1815 restored the Este and Farnese duchies under Austrian protection.
zh: 艾米利亚人是波河平原艾米利亚地区的居民，地区得名于公元前187年修建、从皮亚琴察通往里米尼的罗马大道艾米利亚大道；1337年，他们的城市博洛尼亚、摩德纳、费拉拉、帕尔马和曼托瓦都属意大利最富庶之列。他们的语言艾米利亚语是一种没有标准化的高卢-意大利语，分裂为博洛尼亚、摩德纳、帕尔马、费拉拉、曼托瓦等城市方言。历经伦巴第人和法兰克人统治后，这些城镇在12世纪成为自由公社，加入伦巴第同盟对抗霍亨斯陶芬皇朝，并长期陷于圭尔夫派与吉伯林派的争斗，随后落入各僭主之手：埃斯特家族据费拉拉、后据摩德纳，贡扎加家族据曼托瓦，法尔内塞家族据帕尔马和皮亚琴察，博洛尼亚则归属教皇。1088年创办的博洛尼亚大学使这一地区成为法学学术中心，埃斯特家族的宫廷还赞助了马泰奥·马里亚·博亚尔多、卢多维科·阿里奥斯托和托尔夸托·塔索。1797年，拿破仑把该地区组建为奇斯帕达纳共和国，意大利三色旗即在此首次采用；他倒台后，1815年的维也纳会议在奥地利保护下恢复了埃斯特和法尔内塞诸公国。

en: The ʻEnana, or Marquesans, are the indigenous Polynesian people of the Marquesas, a remote chain of volcanic islands whose north Marquesan name Te Henua ʻEnana means the land of men. Descendants of Lapita voyagers from western Polynesia settled the islands between about 1190 and 1290, and built a uniform culture on fishing, fowling and breadfruit gardens in valleys plagued by drought. Basalt adze heads quarried on Eiao were carried by sailing canoe more than 2,500 kilometres to Moʻorea, Mangareva, Tubuai, Rarotonga and Tabuaeran, proof of a wide pre-European trade network. The clans were famous warriors, practising tattooing, kava rites and ritual human sacrifice. Álvaro de Mendaña reached the southern islands in 1595 and named the group after the Marquis of Cañete, Viceroy of Peru; the American trader Joseph Ingraham visited the northern islands in 1791 and called them the Washington Islands. Late eighteenth-century visitors put the population at 80,000 to 100,000. Protestant missionaries arrived from 1797, and in 1813 Commodore David Porter claimed Nuku Hiva for the United States, though Congress never ratified the claim, while whaling ships made the islands a regular port of call.
zh: 埃纳纳人即马克萨斯人，是马克萨斯群岛的波利尼西亚原住民；这片偏远火山群岛的北马克萨斯语名称“特赫努阿·埃纳纳”意为众人之地。他们是西波利尼西亚拉皮塔航海者的后裔，约在1190年至1290年间定居群岛，在饱受干旱之苦的山谷中以捕鱼、捕鸟和种植面包果为生，发展出高度一致的文化。埃奥岛开采的玄武岩锛头由独木舟载运两千五百多公里，远销莫雷阿、芒阿雷瓦、土布艾、拉罗汤加和塔布阿埃兰，足见欧洲人到来之前贸易网络之广。各氏族以勇武著称，流行纹身、卡瓦酒仪式和人祭。阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚1595年抵达南部诸岛，以秘鲁总督卡涅特侯爵的头衔为群岛命名；美国商人约瑟夫·英格拉哈姆1791年造访北部诸岛，称之为华盛顿群岛。18世纪末的来访者估计当地人口在8万至10万之间。新教传教士自1797年起抵达，1813年海军准将戴维·波特宣布努库希瓦归美国所有，但国会始终没有批准；与此同时，捕鲸船把这里当作常规停靠港。

en: The Enawene Nawe, once called Salumã, are an Arawakan people of Mato Grosso, Brazil, living on the Iquê River, a tributary of the Juruena. They farm, fish and gather but neither hunt nor eat red meat, and order their society through clans and the annual Yaokwa ritual, which upholds the balance of the human and spirit worlds.
zh: 萨鲁马人又称埃纳韦内-纳韦人，是巴西马托格罗索州的阿拉瓦克语族群，住在茹鲁埃纳河支流伊凯河畔。他们务农、捕鱼、采集，却不狩猎、不食红肉；社会以氏族为骨架，每年举行亚夸仪式，维系人间与神灵世界的平衡。

en: The Enenlhet, better known by the Guaraní outside name Angaité, are an Indigenous people of the Paraguayan Chaco Boreal, settled mainly in the Presidente Hayes country along the Paraguay River around Puerto Casado. Their autonym Enenlhet is shared with the neighbouring Maskoy. Their language is one of the six Lengua-Maskoy tongues, grouped with Enlhet, Enxet, Sanapaná, Guaná and Toba-Maskoy. Like their Lengua-Maskoy kin, they lived as nomadic hunter-gatherers of the thorn forest, subsisting on game, fish, wild fruit and honey.
zh: 埃南列特人（他称安盖特人）是巴拉圭北查科的原住民，主要聚居在巴拉圭河沿岸阿耶斯总统省的卡萨多港一带。“安盖特”是瓜拉尼语来源的外来名字，他们本族自称埃南列特，与邻近的马斯科伊人同名。他们的语言是伦瓜-马斯科伊语系六种语言之一，与恩列特语、恩科塞特语、萨纳帕纳语、瓜纳语和托巴-马斯科伊语同系。和伦瓜-马斯科伊诸亲族一样，他们原本是荆棘林中的游牧狩猎采集者，以猎物、鱼、野果和蜂蜜为生。

en: The E'ñepá, better known in the ethnographic literature as the Panare, are a Cariban-speaking people of the Guayana Highlands in southern Venezuela, whose homeland is the Cuchivero River basin in the west of Bolívar State, south of the Orinoco. Their language, Panare or E'ñapa Woromaipu, belongs to the northern branch of the Cariban family. When Europeans first sighted the Orinoco delta in 1498, the E'ñepá were already living in these forested highlands, and for more than three centuries afterwards they remained beyond the effective reach of missionaries and colonists, keeping their traditional way of life almost untouched. They lived in small semi-permanent villages of one or several longhouses housing twenty to eighty people, combining swidden gardens of manioc with hunting tapir and deer, fishing by stunning the catch with the barbasco poison plant, and gathering palm fruit, honey and grubs. Their animist religion centred on the culture hero Mareoka and on the i'yan medicine man, while boys of ten to twelve passed into adult life through the long guayuco initiation festival, at which they received their first cotton loincloth.
zh: 埃涅帕斯人在民族志文献中更常被称为帕纳雷人，是委内瑞拉南部圭亚那高原上说加勒比语的族群，故乡在奥里诺科河以南玻利瓦尔州西部的库奇韦罗河流域。他们的语言帕纳雷语（又称埃涅帕语）属加勒比语系北支。1498年欧洲人第一次望见奥里诺科河口三角洲时，埃涅帕斯人早已生活在这片森林高地上，此后三百多年间，他们始终处于传教士和殖民者的有效控制之外，传统生活几乎未受触动。他们住在半固定的小型村落里，一间或几间长屋容纳二十至八十人，既经营木薯游耕田园，也猎捕貘和鹿，用巴尔巴斯科毒鱼植物麻醉后捕鱼，还采集棕榈果、蜂蜜和蛴螬。他们的泛灵信仰围绕文化英雄马雷奥卡和名为伊扬的医者展开，十至十二岁的男孩要在漫长的瓜尤科成年节上接受第一条棉布缠腰布，由此步入成人生活。

en: The Enets, who call themselves Encho, Mogadi or Pebay and were long known to Russians as the Yenisei Samoyeds, are a small Samoyedic people of the lower Yenisei, close in speech and custom to the Nenets and Nganasans. They formed from local north Siberian tribes merged with Samoyedic groups moving north from the middle Yenisei and the Tom basin, and were organized into patrilineal clans such as the Moggadi, Bai and Aseda. A Novgorod document of the late fifteenth century already calls them the mongolzei after the Moggadi clan, whose name means forest and gave the Russian fort of Mangazeya, founded in 1601 in their hunting grounds, its name. In the seventeenth century they wandered the Taz and Turukhan basins and the forest tundra between the lower Taz and the Yenisei, but by the end of that century pressure from Nenets to the west and Selkups and Kets to the south pushed them onto the eastern bank of the lower Yenisei, around Dudinka and Turukhansk. There they lived by reindeer, hunting and fishing under an animist reverence for earth, sun, fire and water, slowly touched by Orthodox teaching.
zh: 埃涅茨人自称恩乔、莫加迪或佩拜，长期被俄国人称为叶尼塞萨莫耶德人，是叶尼塞河下游的一支小型萨莫耶德民族，语言习俗与涅涅茨人、恩加纳桑人相近。他们由北西伯利亚本地部落与从叶尼塞河中游、托木河流域北迁的萨莫耶德群体融合而成，按父系氏族组织，如莫加迪、拜、阿谢达等氏族。15世纪末的一份诺夫哥罗德文献已根据莫加迪氏族称他们为蒙古尔泽伊人，该氏族名意为森林，1601年俄国人在他们的猎场上修建的曼加泽亚堡即由此得名。17世纪时，他们游牧于塔兹河与图鲁汉河流域以及塔兹河下游与叶尼塞河之间的森林冻土带；到17世纪末，在西方涅涅茨人、南方谢尔库普人和克特人的挤压下，他们退到叶尼塞河下游东岸的杜金卡、图鲁汉斯克一带，以养鹿、狩猎和捕鱼为生，信奉尊崇土地、太阳、火与水的万物有灵信仰，也逐渐受到东正教影响。

en: The Enggano are the small, isolated people of Enggano Island, a forested island lying off the southwestern coast of Sumatra, and rank among the oldest established populations of the region. They were unknown to outsiders until Portuguese explorers met them in the early sixteenth century, when they called themselves the E Lopeh; anthropologically their closest ties are with the Batak and Nias, though long island separation gave their culture a distinct character. Their language is one of the most unusual in the region, sharing little vocabulary with neighboring Austronesian tongues and undergoing strange sound changes, so that scholars have variously treated it as a separate primary branch, an isolate heavily influenced by Austronesian, or a member of the Northwest Sumatra barrier-island group. In 1337 the islanders were divided into five tribes under their own chiefs, organized into exogamous maternal clans called kaudar with matrilocal marriage, monogamous households and elected village councils, while ancestral land passed from mother to daughter. They farmed yams, taro, maize and coconuts, fished and hunted turtles, and carved masks and wooden figures whose style has reminded observers of Polynesian work, exchanging goods by barter in an economy with little currency.
zh: 恩加诺人是居住在苏门答腊西南近海、林木茂密的恩加诺岛上的一个人口稀少而闭塞的民族，也是这一地区最古老的定居族群之一。直到16世纪初葡萄牙探险者到来，外界才知道他们，当时他们自称“埃洛佩”；在人类学上，与他们关系最近的是巴塔克人和尼亚斯人，但长期的海岛隔绝赋予其文化鲜明的独特性。他们的语言是这一带最不寻常的语言之一：与邻近的南岛语言共有词汇很少，又经历了奇特的音变，学者们或将其视为独立的主要语支，或将其视为深受南岛语影响的孤立语言，也有人把它归入苏门答腊西北屏障岛语群。1337年时，岛民分为五个部落，各有酋长；社会按外婚制的母系氏族“考达尔”组织，实行从妻居、一夫一妻制，村落由选举产生的议事会治理，祖传土地由母亲传给女儿。他们种植薯蓣、芋头、玉米和椰子，捕鱼并猎海龟，还雕刻面具和木像——其风格令研究者联想到波利尼西亚的作品；岛上货币流通有限，人们主要以物易物。

en: The English are the people of England, forged from the Angles, Saxons and Jutes who settled lowland Britain after the Roman withdrawal and merged with the Romano-British population; calling themselves the Angelcynn, they were united into a single Kingdom of England in the tenth century under the kings of Wessex, while the Viking conquest of the Danelaw had already added a substantial Norse element. The Norman Conquest of 1066 then placed a French-speaking aristocracy over them, and the fusion of Anglo-Saxon, Norse and Norman layers, shaped by common law, the parish and the growing power of Parliament, produced the medieval English identity. In 1337, under Edward III, England entered the Hundred Years' War with France; the Black Death of 1348 and the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 loosened serfdom and speeded the rise of a yeoman society. The Wars of the Roses ended with the Tudor accession in 1485, and Henry VIII's break with Rome in 1534 made the Church of England the national church, anchoring English identity in Protestantism through the Elizabethan age, the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588 and the King James Bible of 1611. The civil wars of the 1640s, the Commonwealth and the Glorious Revolution of 1688 confirmed parliamentary monarchy, while the Acts of Union of 1707 joined England to Scotland; over the following century London became the hub of a worldwide maritime empire, and the Agricultural and Industrial Revolutions turned the English from a largely rural people into the first industrial nation.
zh: 英格兰人是英格兰的主体民族，由罗马军团撤离后移居低地不列颠的盎格鲁人、撒克逊人和朱特人与当地罗马化布立吞人融合而成；他们自称 Angelcynn，10世纪在威塞克斯诸王治下统一为英格兰王国，而丹麦法区的维京征服早已为其注入浓厚的诺斯成分。1066年诺曼征服又给他们加上了一层讲法语的贵族，盎格鲁-撒克逊、诺斯与诺曼三种底色在普通法、教区制度和日益壮大的议会之中熔铸为中世纪的英格兰认同。1337年爱德华三世在位时，英格兰投入对法百年战争；1348年的黑死病和1381年的农民起义动摇了农奴制，加快了自耕农社会的兴起。玫瑰战争以1485年都铎王朝登基告终，1534年亨利八世与罗马决裂，英格兰国教会成为国家教会，英格兰认同也在伊丽莎白时代、1588年击败西班牙无敌舰队和1611年钦定版圣经中牢牢扎根于新教。17世纪40年代的内战、共和时期与1688年光荣革命确立了议会君主制；1707年的《联合法令》使英格兰与苏格兰合并。此后一个世纪里，伦敦成为世界性海洋帝国的枢纽，农业革命与工业革命更把以乡村为主的英格兰人变成世界上第一个工业化民族。

en: The Enlhet, or Northern Lengua, are an Indigenous people of the Paraguayan Gran Chaco, living in the Boquerón and Presidente Hayes regions around settlements such as Enlhet and Yalve Sanga. Their autonym means person, and Lengua, the Spanish label that long grouped them with the southern Enxet as a single people with two dialects, refers to their speech. Their language forms part of the Lengua-Maskoy family, which also comprises Enxet, Sanapaná, Angaité, Guaná and Toba-Maskoy. Traditionally hunter-gatherers of the dry Chaco forest, they ranged in small kin bands in search of game, wild fruits and honey.
zh: 恩列特人又称北伦瓜人，是巴拉圭大查科的原住民，聚居在博克龙省和阿耶斯总统省一带的恩列特、亚尔韦桑加等地。他们的自称意为“人”；“伦瓜”是西班牙人给的称呼，长期把他们与南方的恩科塞特人视为同一民族的两种方言群体。他们的语言属伦瓜-马斯科伊语系，该语系还包括恩科塞特语、萨纳帕纳语、安盖特语、瓜纳语和托巴-马斯科伊语。他们传统上是干旱查科森林里的狩猎采集者，以小型亲族群体游徙，追逐猎物、野果和蜂蜜。

en: The Enxet, or Southern Lengua, are the southern kin of the Enlhet in the Paraguayan Gran Chaco, their traditional forest country stretching from the Paraguay River westward for about two hundred kilometres, between the González and Montelindo streams. Like the Enlhet their name means person, and they call their language enxet appeywa, the people's word, a tongue of the Lengua-Maskoy family. Long treated as the southern dialect of a single Lengua people, they speak a closely related but distinct language of their own. Hunter-gatherers of the thorn forest, they lived from game, fish, wild fruit and honey in small roaming bands.
zh: 恩科塞特人又称南伦瓜人，是恩列特人在巴拉圭大查科的南方亲族。他们传统的林地家园东起巴拉圭河，向西延伸约两百公里，北抵冈萨雷斯溪，南至蒙特林多溪。和恩列特人一样，他们的自称意为“人”；他们把自己的语言称作恩科塞特·阿佩瓦，意为“人民的语言”，属伦瓜-马斯科伊语系。他们长期被当作单一伦瓜民族的南方方言群体，其语言其实是一门独立而相近的语言。作为荆棘林中的狩猎采集者，他们结成小型游徙群体，以猎物、鱼、野果和蜂蜜为生。

en: The Eora are the coastal Aboriginal people of the Sydney basin, a name first used by British officers for the clans living around Port Jackson when the First Fleet arrived in January 1788. They numbered perhaps fifteen hundred and spoke the coastal Iyora dialect of Dharug, living from the sea in bark canoes, netting mullet, gathering oysters and feasting on turtle as the seasons turned. William Dawes recorded their speech from the woman Patyegarang, and words such as dingo, wombat and corroboree later passed into English. Contact began with kidnappings: Arabanoo was seized to serve as an intermediary, and after him Bennelong, for whom Governor Phillip built a brick hut on the point that now bears his name. In April 1789 a smallpox epidemic, called gai-galla by the Eora, swept the harbour, killing half or more of them within the first years of settlement and nearly wiping out the Cadigal clan, and the coastal dialect died out within two generations.
zh: 约拉人是悉尼盆地的沿海原住民，1788年1月第一舰队抵达时，英国军官最先用这个名字称呼杰克逊港周围的各个氏族。他们当时约有一千五百人，说达鲁格语的沿海方言伊约拉语，乘树皮独木舟取食于海，撒网捕鲻鱼、采牡蛎、随季节享用海龟。威廉·道斯根据女子帕蒂耶加朗的讲述记录了他们的语言，丁狗、袋熊、科罗博里等词后来进入英语。接触之初便伴随着绑架：阿拉巴努被掳去充当中间人，其后贝内朗也被抓走，菲利普总督还在今以他命名的海岬上为他建了一座砖屋。1789年4月，一场被约拉人称为盖加拉的天花横扫港湾，定居最初几年里半数以上的人病死，卡迪加尔氏族近乎灭绝，沿海方言也在两代人之内消亡。

en: The Erielhonan, better known as the Erie or Cat Nation, were an Iroquoian people of the lower Great Lakes, whose palisaded longhouse towns dotted the southeastern shore of Lake Erie between the Buffalo River and Presque Isle Bay, in what became western New York and northwestern Pennsylvania. Their name, recorded by French missionaries as Eriehronon and rendered La Nation du Chat, may mean 'people of the panther', and their speech was mutually intelligible with that of the Wendat and the Neutral. Organized into matrilineal clans across a loose confederacy of three settlement clusters, perhaps twelve thousand strong before epidemics, they farmed the Three Sisters and decorated their pottery with panther effigies. Disease cut their numbers in half, and in 1654 the Seneca and Onondaga turned on them: after a peace embassy was slaughtered, Haudenosaunee fighters armed with Dutch muskets stormed a last-stand palisade where two thousand Erie warriors had gathered with their families. By 1656 the confederacy was destroyed and most captives were adopted into Seneca and Onondaga communities. A remnant fled to Virginia as the Richahecrians and later to the Savannah River, where they became the slave-raiding Westo, themselves broken in the Westo War of 1680 to 1682.
zh: 伊利霍南人通常被称为伊利人或猫族，是五大湖下游的易洛魁语民族，设有栅栏的长屋城镇散布在伊利湖东南岸、布法罗河与普雷斯克艾尔湾之间，即后来的纽约州西部和宾夕法尼亚西北部。法国传教士记下的族名被译作‘猫族’，也可能意为‘豹之人’；他们的语言与休伦语、中立语可以互通。他们按母系氏族组织，结成由三个定居群组成的松散联盟，瘟疫之前约有一万二千人，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜三姐妹作物，并在陶器上饰以豹形纹样。疫病使人口减半，1654年塞内卡人与奥农达加人向他们开战：和谈使团被杀后，配备荷兰火枪的易洛魁战士攻陷了两千名伊利战士携家眷据守的最后栅栏要塞。到1656年联盟已经覆灭，多数俘虏被塞内卡和奥农达加家庭收养。一支残部逃到弗吉尼亚，被称作里查赫克里安人，后来又迁往萨凡纳河，成为以掳掠奴隶为业的韦斯托人，并在1680—1682年的韦斯托战争中被击溃。

en: The Erzyas are the eastern of the two Mordvinic peoples, speaking Erzya, a Volgaic language of the Uralic family, across the basins of the Sura and Moksha rivers and the middle Volga. A common Mordvinic speech is thought to have split into Erzya and Moksha around fifteen hundred years ago. In the early Middle Ages the Erzyas held off the Khazars, Pechenegs and Polovtsians, and as Slavic colonists pushed in from the west they fell back east toward the country around Arzamas. In the thirteenth century their ruler Purgaz headed a kingdom allied with Volga Bulgaria; the Vladimir princes stormed his fortress of Obran Osh in 1221 and founded Nizhny Novgorod on its site. Unlike the Mokshas, who submitted to the Mongols in 1237, many Erzyas withdrew into the northern forests and kept up resistance. After the mid-fourteenth century, when the Suzdal princes made Nizhny Novgorod their capital, the Erzya lands came under the Nizhny Novgorod-Suzdal principality and later Muscovy; some accepted baptism, while others moved ever eastward, reaching the trans-Volga steppe and the southern Urals by the seventeenth century, where they met the Nogais and Kalmyks. Those who remained were registered as yasak-paying Mordvins under the Russian crown.
zh: 埃尔齐亚人是两支莫尔多瓦民族中偏东的一支，使用乌拉尔语系伏尔加语支的埃尔齐亚语，分布在苏拉河、莫克沙河流域及伏尔加河中游。学界一般认为，统一的古莫尔多瓦语约在一千五百年前分化为埃尔齐亚语和莫克沙语。中世纪早期，埃尔齐亚人曾抵御可萨人、佩切涅格人和波洛伏齐人；随着斯拉夫殖民者自西涌入，他们向东退往阿尔扎马斯一带。13世纪时，首领普加兹建立了与伏尔加保加利亚结盟的王国，1221年弗拉基米尔王公攻陷其要塞奥布兰奥什，并在原址建起下诺夫哥罗德。与1237年臣服蒙古的莫克沙人不同，许多埃尔齐亚人退入北方森林继续抵抗。14世纪中叶苏兹达尔王公以下诺夫哥罗德为都后，埃尔齐亚人的土地先后并入下诺夫哥罗德-苏兹达尔公国和后来的莫斯科公国；一部分人接受洗礼，另一部分则继续东迁，到17世纪已抵达伏尔加河以东草原和南乌拉尔，与诺盖人和卡尔梅克人相遇。留在故地的人则被俄国登记为缴纳牙萨克的莫尔多瓦居民。

en: The Ese Ejja, whose autonym means simply 'the people', are a Tacanan-speaking people of the south-western Amazon, spread along the Beni and Madre de Dios rivers of Bolivia and the Tambopata and Heath rivers of eastern Peru, where their neighbours have also called them Chama, Huarayo or Tiatinagua. Their traditions recall Inca raiders reaching the Beni in the days of the early Inca rulers Sinchi Roca and Yahuar Huaca, and the first Europeans followed in 1567 with the Maldonado expedition up the Alto Madre de Dios, later joined by Domingo Álvarez de Toledo; a 1770 expedition found them holding the headwaters of the Madre de Dios and Madidi. Ese Ejja society is split into two patrilineal, exogamous halves that exchange women under cross-cousin marriage rules, with the new couple living with the wife's family. They live by slash-and-burn farming, daily fishing, hunting and gathering, and their mythology centres on Edosiquiana, mistress of all wild animals, whom hunters must respect because the animals are her kin.
zh: 埃塞哈人的自称意为“人”，是西南亚马孙地区讲塔卡纳语的族群，分布在玻利维亚的贝尼河与马德雷德迪奥斯河沿岸，以及秘鲁东部的坦博帕塔河和希思河沿岸；邻族又称他们为查马人、瓦拉约人或蒂亚蒂纳瓜人。他们的传说提到，早在印加早期君主辛奇·罗卡和亚瓦尔·瓦卡克的时代，印加袭掠者就已抵达贝尼河。1567年，马尔多纳多探险队沿上马德雷德迪奥斯河而来，多明戈·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·托莱多随后也进入此地，这是欧洲人的首次到来；1770年的一支探险队发现他们据有马德雷德迪奥斯河与马迪迪河的河源地带。埃塞哈社会分为两个父系外婚半偶族，按交表婚规则互换女子，新婚夫妇随妻方居住。他们以刀耕火种、日常捕鱼、狩猎和采集为生；神话围绕掌管一切野兽的女神埃多西基亚纳展开，猎人必须敬她，因为野兽都是她的亲属。

en: The Eshira, who call themselves Ghisir and are also known as Sira or Shira, are a Bantu people of the forests and grasslands south of the lower Ogooue River in southern Gabon, west of the Ngounie tributary and toward the Nyanga coast; the Punu are counted among their related clans. Their oral traditions remember a long migration from the east through the Congo basin, said to have run from the sixth century onward, and when Portuguese ships opened trade on the Gabonese coast in the 1470s the wanderers had not yet reached their final home. According to their own accounts they entered the country only during the eighteenth century, driven onward by wars with the Kele and other groups. Each clan then managed its own affairs under its chiefs, and Eshira villagers farmed the forest clearings while gaining wide repute as makers of tobacco and raffia-fibre cloth, which they traded to neighbouring peoples such as the Nkomi of the coast. They speak Ghisir, also called Eshira or Sira, a Bantu language of the same broad regional group as Tsogo. The clan villages preserved their independence through the eighteenth century, before the upheavals of the nineteenth-century slave and ivory trade drew them more deeply into commerce with European-backed coastal states.
zh: 埃希拉人自称吉西尔，又称西拉或希拉，是加蓬南部奥果韦河下游以南、恩古涅河以西直至尼扬加沿海一带森林和草原上的班图人，普努人也被视为与他们同族的支系。他们的口传传统保留着从东方经刚果盆地长途迁徙的记忆，据说这段迁徙从6世纪便已开始；当1470年代葡萄牙船只开辟加蓬沿海商路时，这些迁徙者尚未抵达最终的家园。按其自述，直到18世纪，因与凯莱等族群交战，他们才进入这片土地。此后每个氏族在酋长之下自行管理内部事务；村民在林中空地耕作，同时因种植烟草和织造酒椰纤维布而远近闻名，并把这些货物与沿海的恩科米人等邻族交易。他们讲吉西尔语，又称埃希拉语或西拉语，是与措戈语同属一个大区划的班图语言。整个18世纪，这些氏族村落保持着独立，直到19世纪奴隶与象牙贸易的动荡，才把他们更深地卷入由欧洲人支撑的沿海政权的商业网络。

en: The Estonians are a Finnic people of the eastern Baltic shore, whose language is kin to Finnish and Livonian rather than to the Baltic tongues of their Latvian and Lithuanian neighbours. The Roman historian Tacitus already mentioned a people called the Aesti in 98 CE, and the old Estonian endonym maarahvas, meaning land folk, survived into the nineteenth century. Divided into provinces such as Harju and Viru and the island of Saaremaa, they were among the last pagans of Europe and fell to the Northern Crusades only in the 1220s: Denmark took the north after the Battle of Lindanise in 1219, while the Livonian Order and the bishoprics held the rest. The great Saint George's Night revolt of 1343 to 1345 was crushed by the Teutonic Order, and in 1346 the Danish king sold his Estonian duchy to the Order, so that the country became part of the Livonian Confederation under a Baltic German ruling class. The Livonian War of 1558 to 1583 brought Swedish rule to northern Estonia, and the first Estonian book, the Wanradt-Koell catechism, had already been printed in 1535. Sweden lost the land to Russia in the Great Northern War by 1710, but Estonian survived as the speech of the peasant majority, whose literacy spread widely during the eighteenth century after the full Estonian Bible appeared in 1739.
zh: 爱沙尼亚人是波罗的海东岸的芬兰语族群，其语言与芬兰语、利夫语同源，却不同于邻人拉脱维亚人和立陶宛人的波罗的语。罗马史家塔西佗早在98年就提到过名为“埃斯蒂”的民族，爱沙尼亚人的古老自称“马拉赫瓦斯”（意为乡人）一直沿用到19世纪。他们分为哈尔尤、维鲁等省区和萨雷马岛，是欧洲最后接受基督教的异教徒群体之一，到13世纪20年代才被北方十字军征服：丹麦在1219年林达尼斯战役后取得北部，立窝尼亚骑士团和各主教区则占有其余地区。1343—1345年声势浩大的圣乔治之夜起义被条顿骑士团镇压，1346年丹麦国王将爱沙尼亚公国卖给骑士团，这片土地遂成为立窝尼亚邦联的一部分，由波罗的德意志贵族统治。1558—1583年的立窝尼亚战争使北爱沙尼亚转入瑞典之手，而最早的爱沙尼亚语书籍《万拉特—克尔教义问答》已于1535年印行。大北方战争中，瑞典于1710年把这片土地丢给俄国；但爱沙尼亚语始终是多数农民的语言，1739年完整的爱沙尼亚语圣经问世后，识字率在18世纪大为普及。

en: The Ette Ennaka, better known to the Spanish as the Chimilas, are an Indigenous people of northeastern Colombia whose language belongs to the Chibchan family. On the eve of the conquest their territory covered most of the Cesar River basin between the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the Serranía del Perijá, with the Ariguaní valley as its strategic heart; the Yukpa of the Perijá mountains belonged to their loose confederation of tribes. Their chief towns were Thamara, the later Tamalameque, which Spanish scribes described as a settlement of more than a thousand huts, and Upari, named after the powerful cacique Upar, whose title also gave Valledupar its name. Chimila society was stratified, with fishers, hunters, artisans, miners, goldsmiths and merchants, and they cultivated maize skilfully while worshipping a single god called Narayajana. After long contact with the colonists, around 1720 the Chimilas opened a prolonged guerrilla war against the Spanish Empire, holding out in the forests and hills long after the surrounding lowlands had been settled.
zh: 埃特恩纳卡人（西班牙人更常称他们为奇米拉人）是哥伦比亚东北部的原住民，所用语言属奇布查语系。征服前夕，他们的领地覆盖塞萨尔河流域大部，夹在圣玛尔塔内华达山脉与佩里哈山脉之间，以阿里瓜尼河谷为战略中心，佩里哈山中的尤克帕人也属于他们松散的部落联盟。他们的主要城镇有塔马拉，即后来的塔马拉梅克，西班牙书吏称这座城有上千间茅屋；另一座是乌帕里，得名于强大的酋长乌帕尔，巴耶杜帕尔的名字也来自这位酋长。埃特恩纳卡社会等级分明，渔民、猎人、工匠、矿工、金匠和商人各有分工，他们精于玉米种植，信奉唯一的神祇纳拉亚哈纳。在与殖民者长期接触之后，1720年前后奇米拉人对西班牙帝国展开了长期游击战，在周围低地被殖民开垦之后，仍退守森林与山地坚持抵抗。

en: The Eufaula, Yofalv in the Creek language, were a Muskogee-speaking tribal town of the Muscogee Creek Confederacy, perhaps an offshoot of the Kealedji or Hilibi towns of the Upper Creeks. One branch, counted among the Lower Creeks, had settled on the Chattahoochee River by 1733 or earlier, at the crossing later known as Eufaula, where deerskin trade with Georgia brought European goods and customs into the town. Other Eufaula communities remained in the Upper Creek country of eastern Alabama, and in 1832 theirs was the only Upper Creek town still entered on the federal census. Their chief Yoholo Micco traveled to Washington in 1825 to seek better terms after the Treaty of Indian Springs, but failed, and the treaty forced his people across the Chattahoochee into Alabama. In 1836, amid the removals that followed the Creek War, the Eufaula were driven west on the Trail of Tears to Indian Territory, where they rebuilt their town and gave its name to the settlement that grew into Eufaula, Oklahoma.
zh: 尤福拉人在克里克语中称 Yofalv，是马斯科吉-克里克联盟中说马斯科吉语的部族城镇，可能从上克里克的基莱吉镇或希利比镇分出。其中一支属下克里克诸城，至迟在1733年已定居查特胡奇河畔，即后来称作尤福拉的渡口；与佐治亚的鹿皮贸易把欧洲货物和习俗带进了这座城镇。另一些尤福拉社群留在亚拉巴马东部的上克里克地区，1832年联邦人口普查中，他们的城镇是唯一在册的上克里克城镇。1825年，他们的酋长约霍洛·米科前往华盛顿，试图在《印第安斯普林斯条约》后争取更宽松的条款，但未能成功，条约仍迫使部众渡过查特胡奇河迁入亚拉巴马。1836年，在克里克战争后的迁徙浪潮中，尤福拉人沿“泪水之路”被驱往西部的印第安领地，在那里重建城镇，并把名字留给了后来发展成俄克拉荷马尤福拉的定居点。

en: The Evenki are the great Tungusic people of the Siberian taiga, whose camps once ranged from the Yenisei and Lena basines across the Baikal region to the Amur and the Sea of Okhotsk. Their ancestors may be the Shiwei of the Greater Khingan recorded between the fifth and ninth centuries, and by 1600 the Evenki of the Lena and Yenisei were skilled reindeer herders, while their southern kin, the Solons and Khamnigans, had taken to horse breeding from the Mongols. They travelled the forest with domesticated reindeer carrying their loads, living in conical tents of birch bark and reindeer skin, hunting elk, wild reindeer and sable with bows until firearms spread in the eighteenth century, and ordering the world through animist spirits and shamans who travelled between the upper, middle and lower worlds. The seventeenth century brought Russian Cossacks and the yasak fur tax, collected through hostages taken from the clans; the pressure drove many bands east as far as Sakhalin. Other Evenki faced the Manchu: Qing documents knew them as Solons, enrolled them in the Eight Banners, and in the eighteenth century relocated banner companies to Hulunbuir and as far as Ili. Nominally converted to Russian Orthodoxy in that same century, the taiga Evenki kept their shamanic rites and hunting customs beneath the new faith.
zh: 鄂温克人是西伯利亚泰加林里的大通古斯语族群，游猎营地一度从叶尼塞河、勒拿河流域，经贝加尔地区一直延伸到黑龙江和鄂霍次克海沿岸。他们的祖先可能是5至9世纪大兴安岭的室韦人；到1600年前后，勒拿河与叶尼塞河的鄂温克人已是熟练的驯鹿牧民，而南方的亲族索伦人和哈米尼干人则从蒙古人那里学会了养马。他们驱使驯鹿驮运物资穿行林海，住桦树皮和鹿皮搭成的锥形帐篷，用弓箭猎取驼鹿、野鹿和紫貂，直到18世纪火器才普及；精神世界由万物有灵的神灵和能往返于上中下三界的萨满维系。17世纪，俄国哥萨克到来，靠扣押氏族首领为人质征收“雅萨克”毛皮税，许多部落不堪其扰向东远徙至库页岛。另一些鄂温克人面对的是满洲：清代文献称他们为索伦，将其编入八旗，18世纪又把旗营调往呼伦贝尔，远至伊犁。同一世纪里，他们在名义上皈依了俄罗斯东正教，但林区的鄂温克人仍在新教外壳之下保留着萨满仪式和狩猎旧俗。

en: The Evesel are the coastal Evens, the Tungus people whose self-name in the plural is evesel and whom their Yakut neighbours called Lamut, the sea people. Their grounds stretched along the Sea of Okhotsk from the Taui and Yana bays eastward toward Gizhiga, in present-day Magadan Oblast. Seventeenth-century Russian sources knew them as the Okhotsk reindeer Tungus: nomadic herders who moved with their reindeer between tundra and coast, where they also fished and hunted seals. Ivan Moskvitin heard of Tungus clans on the Taui in 1639, and Mikhail Stadukhin built the Tauisk ostrog at the river mouth in 1653 to collect their fur tribute. Orthodox missionaries worked among them from the eighteenth century, and by the nineteenth the Evens were counted among the most thoroughly Christianized peoples of the Russian North, though shamanist customs survived.
zh: 鄂韦塞尔人即沿海的鄂温人，鄂温语自称的复数形式为 эвэсэл，相邻的雅库特人则称他们为拉穆特，意为海边的人。他们的活动范围沿鄂霍次克海展开，从陶伊湾、亚纳湾向东延伸到吉日加一带，在今马加丹州境内。17世纪的俄国文献称他们为鄂霍次克养鹿通古斯人：赶着驯鹿在苔原与海岸间游牧，同时从事捕鱼和猎海豹。1639年，伊万·莫斯克维京已听说陶伊河一带有通古斯氏族；1653年，米哈伊尔·斯塔杜欣在河口修建陶伊斯克堡，向他们征收毛皮税。18世纪起东正教传教士进入他们中间，到19世纪鄂温人已被视为俄国北方基督教化最深的民族之一，但萨满教习俗仍然保留下来。

en: The Ewe are a Gbe-speaking people of the Kwa branch who live on the coast between the Volta and Mono rivers, in present-day southeast Ghana and southern Togo, in towns such as Keta, Aného and Notsie, their dialects including Anlo and Tongu. Their tradition remembers an earlier home at Ketu, on the Benin-Nigeria border; breaking away from the Aja confederacy, they founded the walled town of Notsie before dispersing westward in the 1600s to escape the tyrant Agor Akorli, and archaeology places Ewe communities in the region as early as the 1200s. They settled as independent village chiefdoms under elected elders rather than kings, farmed and fished the lagoons and wove cotton. Lying between Asante, Dahomey and Oyo, Eweland suffered slave raiding and itself sold war captives to European ships, and in 1784 the Ewe clashed with the Danes over new coastal forts. A written Ewe standard was formed in the 1800s from the coastal dialects for use in schools and churches.
zh: 埃维人是沃尔特河与莫诺河之间沿海（今加纳东南部和多哥南部）说克瓦语支格贝语族埃维语的民族，聚居凯塔、内霍、诺策等城镇，方言有安洛、通古等。口述传统中的故地是贝宁与尼日利亚边境的凯图；他们脱离阿贾联盟后筑起城墙城镇诺策，17世纪为逃避暴君阿戈尔·阿科利而向西离散，考古证据则显示埃维社群早在13世纪已在这一带活动。他们没有国王，以独立的村落酋邦为单位，由选举产生的长老治理，在潟湖周边农耕渔捞、纺织棉布。埃维地处阿散蒂、达荷美和奥约之间，既遭奴隶劫掠，也把战俘卖给欧洲商船；1784年，他们又因丹麦人修建沿海堡垒而与丹麦人交战。19世纪，以沿海方言为基础形成了书面埃维语标准，用于学校和教堂。

en: The Ewksikni are the lake-dwelling Klamath proper: ʔewksiknii is both the Klamath name for themselves and the title of their leading band, whose villages ringed Upper Klamath Lake and the Williamson, Wood and Sprague rivers in southern Oregon. They spoke Klamath-Modoc, a language of the proposed Plateau Penutian family, and lived mainly by fishing, supplemented by roots and seeds gathered across the marshes. Their tradition remembered the eruption of Mount Mazama, which left Crater Lake in their territory, and after horses reached the plateau they raided neighbours such as the Achomawi for slaves while trading dried fish at The Dalles on the Columbia. Peter Skene Ogden of the Hudson's Bay Company met them in 1826 and was trading regularly by 1829, the first sustained contact with outsiders.
zh: 尤克西克尼人即湖滨而居的克拉马斯本支：ʔewksiknii既是克拉马斯人的自称，也是其核心支派的名字，村社环绕俄勒冈南部的上克拉马斯湖以及威廉森河、伍德河和斯普拉格河分布。他们使用拟议中的高原佩努蒂语系之一的克拉马斯—莫多克语，以捕鱼为主业，辅以在沼泽采集的根茎和种籽。他们的口传传统保留了马扎马火山喷发的记忆，那次喷发在其地留下了火山口湖。马匹传入高原后，他们南下袭掠阿乔马维人等邻族掳人为奴，同时带着鱼干到哥伦比亚河上的达尔斯贸易。1826年，哈德逊湾公司的彼得·斯肯·奥格登与他们接触，到1829年已建立定期贸易，这是他们与外界最早的持续往来。

en: The Eyak are an Alaska Native people of the Northwest Coast whose villages stood on the Copper River Delta around present-day Cordova, between the Chugach Sugpiaq to the west and the Tlingit to the east. They trace their origins to interior groups who descended the Copper River to exploit its salmon runs, living in permanent winter villages such as Alaganik and Orca alongside seasonal fish camps. Their language forms its own branch of the Na-Dené family, closest to the Athabaskan languages. Small in number, the Eyak were long pressed by Chugach raiders and drawn into trade and intermarriage with the Tlingit. Russian fur traders reaching the Gulf of Alaska in the 1780s recognized them as a distinct people, mapped their territory and introduced the Orthodox faith and new diseases, which together with Tlingit assimilation sharply reduced their numbers in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 埃雅克人是西北海岸的阿拉斯加原住民，村落分布在今科尔多瓦一带的科珀河三角洲，西接楚加奇的苏皮阿克人，东邻特林吉特人。他们的先祖来自内陆，顺科珀河而下利用河口丰富的鲑鱼资源，在阿拉加尼克、奥卡等地建有固定冬村，并按季节使用捕鱼营地。埃雅克语在纳-德内语系中自成一支，与阿萨巴斯卡诸语言关系最近。埃雅克人口不多，长期遭受楚加奇人袭扰，又与特林吉特人贸易通婚、渐被同化。1780年代，俄国毛皮商人到达阿拉斯加湾，承认他们是独立的族群，在地图上标出其领地，还带来东正教和新的疾病；加上特林吉特人的同化，埃雅克人口在19世纪初大幅减少。

en: The Fang, also called Pahouin or Pangwe, are a Bantu people of the West African rainforest, spread across Rio Muni in Equatorial Guinea, northern Gabon and southern Cameroon, with smaller communities in the Congo. Glottochronology places the Proto-Fang in the Cameroon forest, part of the Bantu movements that spread south from around the 700s, and the Fang themselves pushed south only in the 1800s, leaving central Cameroon for the Gabonese and Rio Muni forests in a migration that may have been driven by slave raiding. They speak Fang, a Northwest Bantu tongue mutually intelligible with the speech of the Beti and Bulu. Fang society is patrilineal and exogamous, built of fiercely independent forest villages whose farmers and hunters were famed for their knowledge of plants and animals. Their Byeri reliquaries, wooden figures guarding the bones and skulls of ancestors, were misread by European explorers as evidence of cannibalism, a slur used to justify raids and enslavement.
zh: 芳人又称帕胡因人或庞圭人，是西非雨林中的班图族群，分布在赤道几内亚木尼河地区、加蓬北部和喀麦隆南部，在刚果也有较小的支系。语言年代学把原始芳语的故乡放在喀麦隆雨林，他们属于约8世纪起南下的班图迁徙的一部分；芳人本身则在19世纪才向南推进，为躲避奴隶袭扰等原因离开喀麦隆中部，进入加蓬和木尼河的森林。他们说的芳语属西北班图语，与贝蒂语、布卢语可以互通。芳人社会按父系继嗣、实行外婚，由高度自治的森林村落组成，村民务农狩猎，以对动植物的丰富知识闻名。他们的比耶里圣物匣用木雕守护祖先的骨骸，欧洲探险者却据此诬称芳人食人，并用这一污蔑为洗劫和奴役他们开脱。

en: The Fang, once called Pahouin by European travellers, are a Northwest Bantu people whose homeland now spans southern Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and northern and central Gabon; the Fang Gabun are the branch settled around the middle Ogooué. Over many generations Fang clans moved slowly south through the rainforest from what is now central Cameroon, driven by warfare and the search for new farmland, and reached the Moyen-Ogooué by the early 1800s, displacing or absorbing earlier inhabitants as they went. Fang society is patrilineal and exogamous, built on largely independent village lineages of farmers and hunters, and its history was carried in the Mvet, a cycle of sung oral epics. Religious life centred on the Byeri ancestor cult, whose carved wooden reliquary guardians and the white masks of the Ngil society count among the most famous works of Central African art.
zh: 芳人曾被欧洲旅行者称为帕胡人，是西北班图族群，聚居地横跨喀麦隆南部、赤道几内亚和加蓬中北部；芳加蓬即定居在奥果韦河中游一带的支系。漫长的岁月里，芳人各氏族为躲避战乱、寻找新的耕地，从喀麦隆中部一带的雨林缓慢南迁，于19世纪初抵达中奥果韦地区，沿途排挤或同化了更早的居民。芳人社会按父系血缘组织、实行外婚制，以彼此独立的农耕兼狩猎村落氏族为基础，历史则靠口头传唱的史诗《姆维特》传承。他们的宗教生活以拜里祖先崇拜为中心，祖先遗骨匣旁的木雕守护像和恩吉尔社的白色面具，是中非艺术中最著名的作品之一。

en: The Persians are the Iranian people of the Iranian plateau, native speakers of Persian, whose ancestors settled Persis, the country around Shiraz, by the ninth century BC. From that base they built the Achaemenid Empire of Cyrus and Darius, and later the Parthian and Sasanian empires, in which Middle Persian served as the language of state and letters. The Arab conquest of the seventh century brought Islam and Arabic, but Persian survived and was revived from the ninth century under Iranian dynasties such as the Samanids, who adopted the Arabic script and patronized a new literature crowned by Ferdowsi's Shahnameh around the year 1000. Persian then became the shared high language of the Islamic east under Ghaznavid, Seljuk, Mongol Ilkhanid and Timurid rule, carried from Anatolia to India by administrators and poets. In 1337, with the Ilkhanate disintegrating, the Persian heartlands were divided among local dynasties such as the Injuids and Muzaffarids until Timur's campaigns reunited them by conquest.
