Gond society is ordered into clans and lineages served by Pardhan bard-genealogists, with a nature-centred faith under the high god Kupar Lingo and its own oral folk Ramayana.
zh: 贡德人自称科伊托尔，是散居在印度中部森林山地——从维达尔巴、巴斯塔延伸到曼德拉的贡德瓦纳地区的达罗毗荼语部落族群，使用与泰卢固语同源的中南达罗毗荼语贡德语；外族称他们为贡德，名字来自达罗毗荼语 kond，意为山。13至19世纪间，他们在这片高地上建立了一连串王国。最早的昌达王国约建于1200年，靠灌溉工程和设防城镇兴盛，统治者后来迁都钱德拉布尔；14世纪，贾杜赖推翻卡拉丘里领主建立加尔哈王国；13世纪初，首领贾特巴建立德奥加尔王国。加尔哈-曼德拉的王后杜尔加瓦蒂于1564年抵御莫卧儿皇帝阿克巴时战死；德奥加尔国王巴赫特·布兰德·沙为换取奥朗则布的支持改宗伊斯兰教，并建立了那格浦尔城。贡德诸王公作为莫卧儿附庸存续到18世纪40年代，随后拉戈吉·邦斯莱率领的马拉塔军队席卷其地；第三次英马战争后，英国人接管了残存的贡德封建领地。贡德社会以氏族和世系为基本单位，有帕尔德安吟游谱师世代传诵，信奉以高位神库帕尔·林戈为核心的自然崇拜，还拥有口传的民间《贡德罗摩衍那》。

en: The Gonga are the Omotic-speaking peoples of the forested southwestern Ethiopian highlands, the Gibe country around Bonga and the upper Omo, whose related Gonga or Kefoid tongues were once shared by the populations of the medieval kingdoms of Damot and Ennarea and survive in groups such as the Kaffa, Shekkacho and Shinasha. In the thirteenth century their strongest state was Damot, south of the Blue Nile, whose kings bore the title motalami, worshipped a god called Dask and were powerful enough to exact tribute from the Muslim sultanate of Shewa and to rout the armies of the Zagwe. The Christian emperor Amda Seyon conquered Damot in 1316 and made it a tributary, so in 1337 the Gonga lands lay at the southwestern edge of the Ethiopian Empire, valued above all for their gold. Ennarea broke away from Damot later in the fourteenth century and grew into the leading kingdom of the non-Muslim south, sending gold, slaves and cattle to the emperors, whose court converted its elite to Christianity in the 1580s. From the later sixteenth century the expansion of the Macha and Borana Oromo overwhelmed the Gibe region, and after Ennarea fell around 1710 its royal clan fled south into Kaffa, while the surviving Gonga communities scattered or were absorbed by their neighbours.
zh: 贡加人是埃塞俄比亚西南部森林高原（邦加一带的吉贝地区和奥莫河上游）说奥莫特语的族群，他们彼此相近的贡加诸语又称凯福伊德语，曾是中世纪达莫特王国和恩纳里亚王国居民的共同语言，其后世使用者包括卡法人、谢卡乔人和希纳沙人等群体。13世纪时，他们最强的政权是青尼罗河以南的达莫特王国，国王称“莫塔拉米”，奉祀达斯克神，强盛到能向穆斯林的绍阿苏丹国索贡，并击溃扎格维王朝的军队。基督教皇帝阿姆达·塞约恩于1316年征服达莫特，将其降为附庸；因此在1337年，贡加人的土地处于埃塞俄比亚帝国的西南边陲，尤以黄金出产受帝国看重。恩纳里亚于14世纪后期脱离达莫特，成为非穆斯林南方最主要的王国，向皇帝进贡黄金、奴隶和牲畜，其精英阶层在16世纪80年代被朝廷发展为基督徒。16世纪后期起，马查和博拉纳奥罗莫人的扩张席卷吉贝地区，1710年前后恩纳里亚陷落，王族南逃卡法，幸存的贡加社群或四散迁徙，或被邻族同化。

en: The Gonja, whose own name is Ngbanya, are a Mandé-derived people of the savanna north of the Black Volta in present-day Ghana, their trade towns of Salaga and Bole straddling the roads between the Akan goldfields and the Niger cities. Their kingdom grew from a Mali cavalry expedition of the mid-1500s led by Prince Naba, who ruled from Buipe between 1552 and 1582; his successor Manwura took Islam through scholars from Begho, and the first Buipe mosque was built under King Amoah after 1600. After Songhai collapsed in 1591 the Mandé Ngbanya clan crossed the Black Volta under Sumaila Ndewura Jakpa, who reigned from 1622 to 1699, conquered the White Volta valley, made Yagbum his capital and by 1675 ruled through a paramount titled the Yagbongwura, posting his sons over Bole, Kpembe and the other provinces. Gonja grew rich carrying gold and kola between Begho and Hausaland, and Salaga was nicknamed the Timbuktu of the South; society split into the Ngbanya elite, the Muslim scholar class of the Karamo and commoner Nyemasi. Wars with Dagbon and Wa ended badly, and in the 1740s Gonja became a vassal of the Asante empire, which thereafter protected the Salaga trade.
zh: 贡贾人自称恩格巴尼亚，是黑沃尔特河以北草原（今加纳境内）源自曼德人的民族，商业城镇萨拉加和博莱扼守阿肯金矿区与尼日尔诸城之间的商路。其王国始于16世纪中叶马里王子纳巴率领的骑兵远征，纳巴于1552—1582年以布伊佩为都；继位的曼武拉经贝戈来的学者引荐改奉伊斯兰教，1600年后阿莫阿国王在布伊佩建起第一座清真寺。1591年桑海崩溃后，曼德系的恩格巴尼亚氏族在苏马伊拉·恩杜拉·贾克帕（1622—1699年在位）率领下渡过黑沃尔特河，征服白沃尔特河谷，定都亚格布姆，到1675年确立了称亚格邦古拉的最高酋长之位，并把诸子分封到博莱、彭贝等省。贡贾靠在贝戈与豪萨兰之间贩运黄金和柯拉果致富，萨拉加因此得了“南方廷巴克图”的绰号；社会分为恩格巴尼亚统治阶层、穆斯林学者阶层卡拉莫和平民涅马西。与达贡和瓦的战争连遭挫败，1740年代贡贾沦为阿散蒂帝国的附庸，后者此后保障了萨拉加贸易的安全。

en: The Gooniyandi, also called Konejandi, are an Aboriginal people of the Kimberley in Western Australia, whose country centres on the Fitzroy River around Fitzroy Crossing. Their language forms, with Bunuba, the small non-Pama-Nyungan Bunuban family, the two tongues as close as English and Dutch. Inland foragers organised in bands, they divided their land into walibiri river country of pools and watercourses rich in fish, crustaceans and reptiles, pindiri scrub plains where kangaroos were hunted, and ka:waro hill country holding euros; men took bustards, echidnas and emus while women gathered vegetables, honey, frogs and witchetty grubs. Commanding the Fitzroy crossing, they were intermediaries in long-distance trade: pressure-flaked stone knives known as tjimbila and sea shells called tjakuli, brought from the coast through the Warwa and Nyigina, passed through their hands to the Gija, the Djaru and the Western Desert peoples.
zh: 古尼扬迪人又称科内詹迪人，是西澳大利亚金伯利地区的原住民，领地以菲茨罗伊河上的菲茨罗伊克罗辛一带为中心。他们的语言与布努巴语共同构成非帕马‑牛雅的布努班语系，两种语言的近似程度相当于英语和荷兰语。他们以游群为单位在内陆觅食，把土地分为三类：水潭与河道纵横、盛产鱼类、甲壳类和爬行动物的瓦利比里河川地，捕猎袋鼠的平迪里灌丛平原，以及出产岩袋鼠的卡瓦罗山地；男子猎取鸨、针鼹和鸸鹋，妇女则采集植物、蜂蜜、青蛙和木蠹蛾幼虫。由于扼守菲茨罗伊河的渡口，他们是长途贸易的中间人：名为钦比拉的压制剥制石刀，以及经瓦瓦人和尼吉纳人从海岸转来、名叫贾库利的海贝，都通过他们之手流向基亚人、贾鲁人和西部沙漠诸族。

en: The Gorontalo, whose endonym is Hulontalo, are the dominant Austronesian people of the northern arm of Sulawesi, traditionally living around the bay of the same name. Their language belongs to the Philippine branch of the Austronesian family and their early kingdoms, linked by a kinship system called pohala'a, included Gorontalo, Limboto, Suwawa, Boalemo and Atinggola. These states came under the influence of the Ternate Sultanate, and Islam had spread widely among them by the time the Portuguese reached northern Sulawesi in 1525, during the rule of King Amay. The Dutch East India Company then drew the kingdoms into its network through a treaty negotiated by the Ternate governor Robertus Patbrugge, creating the Gorontalo Regency. In the eighteenth century many Gorontalo migrated to Ternate, Ambon, Buol, Banggai and Minahasa to escape the forced labour imposed by the colonial government, and by the end of the nineteenth century their homeland was fully absorbed into the Dutch East Indies.
zh: 哥伦打洛人自称胡隆塔洛人，是苏拉威西北臂地区占主导地位的南岛语族群体，传统上聚居于同名海湾一带。他们的语言属南岛语系菲律宾语支，早期的哥伦打洛、林博托、苏瓦瓦、博阿勒莫和阿廷戈拉等王国通过名为“波哈拉”的亲属制度彼此联结。这些政权曾受特尔纳特苏丹国影响，1525年葡萄牙人抵达苏拉威西北部时，在阿迈国王统治下伊斯兰教已在民间广泛传播。后来荷兰东印度公司借特尔纳特总督帕特布鲁赫与诸王国缔约，将其纳入公司体系，并设立哥伦打洛县。18世纪，许多哥伦打洛人为逃避殖民政府的强迫劳役，迁居特尔纳特、安汶、布奥尔、邦盖和米纳哈萨；到19世纪末，他们的故土被完全并入荷属东印度。

en: The Gothic culture of 1337 survives only in Crimea, where a remnant of the East Germanic Goths had lived since the third century, cut off from the great Gothic kingdoms of the west after the Ostrogothic realm collapsed under the Huns. They converted to Orthodox Christianity, and around 850 Saint Cyril found Crimean Goths still reading their scriptures in their own Germanic tongue. After the Fourth Crusade their highland district around the fortress of Doros, present-day Mangup, became the Principality of Gothia, better known as Theodoro, a small Orthodox state whose people mixed Goths with Greeks, Alans and other Crimean peoples and whose official language was Greek. In 1337 Theodoro clung to the mountains of southwestern Crimea between the Genoese trading colonies on the coast and the Mongol khanate of the steppe. The Ottomans overran it in 1475, ending Gothic self-rule, yet the language lingered: the Habsburg envoy Busbecq collected Crimean Gothic words in the sixteenth century, and travellers still reported Gothic-speaking villagers near Mangup in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries before the people merged into the Greek and Tatar population.
zh: 1337年的哥特文化仅存于克里米亚：自3世纪起，东日耳曼哥特人的一支便定居于此，在匈人击垮东哥特王国后，与西方的哥特诸王国断了联系。他们皈依了东正教，约850年圣西里尔到访时，还发现克里米亚哥特人用自己的日耳曼语诵读经文。第四次十字军东征后，他们以多罗斯要塞（今曼古普）为中心的山区形成哥提亚公国，即狄奥多罗公国；这个东正教小邦的居民混有哥特人、希腊人、阿兰人等克里米亚族群，官方语言却是希腊语。1337年时，狄奥多罗夹在沿海的热那亚商殖民地和草原上的蒙古汗国之间，据守克里米亚西南山区。1475年奥斯曼攻灭该公国，哥特人的自治告终，但语言仍余音尚存：哈布斯堡使节布斯贝克在16世纪记录了克里米亚哥特语词汇，17、18世纪仍有旅人报告曼古普一带有说哥特语的村民，此后他们便融入了希腊人和鞑靼人之中。

en: The Greater Polish are the Lechitic speaking people of Wielkopolska, the lowland country of the Warta and Notec rivers around Poznan, Gniezno and Kalisz, together with the adjoining Kuyavian lands around Inowroclaw and Wloclawek. Their forebears, the Polans, made this region the cradle of the Polish state: Poznan received the first Polish bishopric in 968 and Gniezno its archdiocese in 1000, until pagan rebellion and the Bohemian raid of 1038 drove the royal court to Krakow. The fragmentation begun in 1138 split the land into the Duchy of Greater Poland and neighboring Kuyavian duchies, only rejoined to the crown under Wladyslaw the Elbow-high in 1314; in 1331 Teutonic armies raided as far as Kalisz before being driven back. The local speech, the Greater Polish dialect group descended from the Western Slavic of the Polans, also spread with settlers into the Neumark. In 1772 Prussia took the northern Notec lands and in 1793 swallowed the whole region; the uprising of 1806 carried much of it into the Duchy of Warsaw, but the Congress of Vienna in 1815 left Poznan under Prussia as the Grand Duchy of Posen, while Kalisz passed to Russian Poland.
zh: 大波兰人是说莱赫语的族群，住在瓦尔塔河与诺泰奇河流域的大波兰低地，中心为波兹南、格涅兹诺和卡利什，也包括伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫和弗沃茨瓦韦克一带的库亚维毗邻地区。他们的先民波兰人把这里变成波兰国家的摇篮：968年波兹南设立波兰第一个主教区，1000年格涅兹诺设立大主教区，直到11世纪30年代的异教叛乱和1038年波希米亚人的洗劫迫使王室迁往克拉科夫。1138年开始的分裂使这片土地分成大波兰公国和邻近的库亚维诸公国，直到1314年才被矮子瓦迪斯瓦夫重新并入王权；1331年条顿骑士团的军队一度攻到卡利什，随后被击退。当地的大波兰方言群源自波兰人的西斯拉夫语，还随移民传到诺伊马克。1772年普鲁士夺去诺泰奇河以北的土地，1793年吞并整个地区；1806年的大波兰起义使大部分地区并入华沙公国，但1815年维也纳会议后，波兹南作为波森大公国留在普鲁士，卡利什则划归俄国治下的波兰王国。

en: The Greeks are the Greek-speaking people of the Aegean and Ionian seas, with a continuous presence in the Greek peninsula, the Aegean islands, Constantinople and the western coast of Anatolia since the Mycenaean age of the second millennium BC. Their city-states, led in different ages by Athens and Sparta, created the classical civilization of the Mediterranean, and the conquests of Alexander the Great carried Greek language and settlement across the Near East. Under Rome the Greek-speaking east remained the wealthier half of the empire, and after the foundation of Constantinople in 330 the Byzantine Empire became a Greek-speaking Christian civilization that lasted more than a thousand years. The Fourth Crusade of 1204 shattered Byzantium, and although the Palaiologan dynasty recovered Constantinople in 1261, by 1337 the empire held little beyond the capital, Thrace and the Morea, while rival Greek states such as Trebizond survived on the Black Sea coast. Ottoman conquest ended with the fall of Constantinople in 1453, after which Greeks lived as Orthodox subjects of the sultan, administered through their own millet, with leading families such as the Phanariots rising in imperial service. The Greek War of Independence that began in 1821 led to the creation of an independent Kingdom of Greece in 1832, while large Greek communities remained under Ottoman rule.
zh: 希腊人是爱琴海和伊奥尼亚海沿岸说希腊语的民族，自公元前两千年的迈锡尼时代起便连续生活在希腊半岛、爱琴海诸岛、君士坦丁堡和安纳托利亚西海岸。以雅典和斯巴达为代表的城邦创造了地中海的古典文明，亚历山大大帝的远征又把希腊语和希腊人的定居点带到近东。罗马统治下，东部希腊语地区长期是帝国较富庶的一半；330年君士坦丁堡建成后，拜占庭帝国成为延续逾千年的希腊语基督教文明。1204年第四次十字军东征重创拜占庭，尽管帕里奥洛格斯王朝于1261年收复君士坦丁堡，到1337年帝国除都城、色雷斯和摩里亚外已所剩无几，特拉比松帝国等希腊政权仍在黑海沿岸割据。奥斯曼的征服以1453年君士坦丁堡陷落告终，此后希腊人作为苏丹治下的东正教臣民经由自己的米利特体系管理，法那尔人等名门还在帝国朝中担任要职。1821年爆发的希腊独立战争最终促成1832年独立的希腊王国建立，但仍有大批希腊人社群留在奥斯曼统治之下。

en: The Gresi are a Papuan people of the Grime River hinterland in Jayapura Regency, northern Indonesian New Guinea, living in villages such as Bring, Ibub and Sunna in the Kemtuk Gresi and South Gresi districts. Their language, also recorded as Geresi or Glesi, forms the Gresi–Kemtuik branch of the small Nimboran family together with the neighbouring Kemtuik language.
zh: 格雷西人是印度尼西亚新几内亚岛北部查亚普拉县格里梅河腹地的巴布亚族群，聚居于肯图克格雷西区和南格雷西区的布林、伊布布、孙纳等村落。他们的语言又记作盖雷西语或格莱西语，与邻近的肯图伊克语共同构成小型宁博兰语系下的格雷西—肯图伊克语支。

en: The Griko are the Greek-speaking community of southern Italy, settled in the Salento peninsula of Apulia, southern Calabria and parts of Sicily including Messina and Catania. They inherit the Greek presence of Magna Graecia, founded by colonists from the eighth century BC and reinforced in the early Middle Ages, when Byzantine rule returned to southern Italy and Greek refugees settled there. Even after the Norman conquest of the eleventh century ended Byzantine government, much of Calabria and the Salento remained Greek-speaking: in the late thirteenth century Roger Bacon noted clergy and people there living entirely in Greek, and Calabrian Greeks such as Barlaam of Seminara and Leontius Pilatus taught Greek to Petrarch and Boccaccio, helping kindle the Italian Renaissance. In 1337 the Griko thus formed living enclaves of Greek speech within the Angevin and Aragonese kingdoms of the south, speaking Italiot Greek dialects that blended ancient Doric and Koine Greek with local Romance words. From the fifteenth century the Latin Church and feudal lords pressed the Byzantine rite and Greek liturgy toward Latin and Italian, and fresh refugees from the Ottoman Peloponnese in the sixteenth century only briefly strengthened the shrinking enclaves.
zh: 格里科人是意大利南部说希腊语的族群，聚居在普利亚的萨伦托半岛、卡拉布里亚南部以及西西里的墨西拿、卡塔尼亚等地。他们承袭了公元前8世纪希腊殖民者建立的“大希腊”地区的希腊传统，中世纪早期拜占庭恢复对南意大利的统治、希腊难民相继迁入，又进一步壮大了这一社群。即便11世纪诺曼征服终结了拜占庭的统治，卡拉布里亚和萨伦托的大部分地区仍通行希腊语：13世纪后期罗吉尔·培根记载当地教士和百姓完全生活在希腊语环境中，塞米纳拉的巴拉姆、莱昂蒂乌斯·皮拉图斯等卡拉布里亚希腊学者还向彼特拉克和薄伽丘传授希腊语，为意大利文艺复兴播下火种。因此在1337年，格里科人是南方安茹和阿拉贡王国境内鲜活的希腊语飞地，使用融合了古代多利亚语、通用希腊语和当地罗曼语词汇的意大利希腊语方言。从15世纪起，拉丁教会和封建领主推动拜占庭礼和希腊语礼仪转向拉丁语与意大利语，16世纪来自奥斯曼统治下伯罗奔尼撒的新难民也只是短暂充实了不断萎缩的社群。

en: The Cuachíchitl, whom the Spanish called Guachichiles, held the widest territory of any Chichimeca people, stretching from Zacatecas across San Luis Potosí and Guanajuato to north-eastern Jalisco, and north as far as Saltillo. Their Nahuatl name means red-painted heads, from the red dye with which they colored their faces and hair. They were no single kingdom but a constellation of nomadic bands and chiefdoms across the arid plateau, feared as the most aggressive agitators of resistance to the Spanish mines and roads; their archers and mobile raiding parties made them a driving force of the Chichimeca War from 1550 to 1600. The long fighting ended by negotiation rather than conquest: in November 1592 the leader Moquamalto surrendered to the friar Diego de la Magdalena and Captain Miguel Caldera, and the Spanish town of San Luis Potosí was founded on the spot, gathering Guachichil families with Tlaxcalan, Otomi and Spanish settlers into mission neighborhoods.
zh: 夸奇奇特尔人被西班牙人称为瓜奇奇尔人，在奇奇梅克诸族中占地最广，从萨卡特卡斯横跨圣路易斯波托西和瓜纳华托，延伸到哈利斯科东北部，向北远达萨尔蒂约。他们的纳瓦特尔语名字意为“涂红的头”，来自他们染红面孔和头发的颜料。他们并非统一王国，而是干旱高原上众多游牧群体和酋邦的集合，被视为鼓动抵抗西班牙矿场和道路最力的族群；弓箭手和机动袭扰队使他们成为1550至1600年奇奇梅克战争的主力。漫长的战事最终以谈判而非征服收场：1592年11月，首领莫夸马尔托向修士迭戈·德拉马格达莱纳和米格尔·卡尔德拉队长投降，西班牙人就在此地建立圣路易斯波托西城，把夸奇奇特尔家庭与特拉斯卡拉人、奥托米人和西班牙定居者一同安置在传教街区。

en: The Sikuani, also called Guahibo or Jiwi, are the principal people of the Orinoco llanos, living in the savannas between the Guaviare, Meta and Arauca rivers, straddling eastern Colombia and western Venezuela. They speak a Guahiboan language, a family of its own rather than an Arawakan one, though it has absorbed Arawak loanwords. Their life centers on bitter cassava, which women process into casabe bread and roasted fariña flour with fiber squeezers called sebucanes, while men hunt with bow and arrow, fish, and weave hammocks from cumare and moriche palm fiber. Society is patriarchal and tends toward endogamy: each named band holds its own territory, speaks its own dialect and is independent of the others, and families live in rectangular thatched houses, with a separate small hut for menstruating women. From the late 1700s the expansion of Colombian and Venezuelan cattle ranches brought sporadic but severe violence against Sikuani bands, who kept their autonomy by retreating into the remoter parts of the plains.
zh: 西夸尼人又称瓜希博人或吉维人，是奥里诺科平原的主要族群，生活在瓜维亚雷河、梅塔河与阿劳卡河之间的热带草原，地跨哥伦比亚东部和委内瑞拉西部。他们使用瓜希博语族的语言——该语族自成一家，并非阿拉瓦克语，只是吸收了阿拉瓦克语借词。生活以苦木薯为中心：妇女用名叫塞布坎的纤维压榨器把木薯加工成卡萨贝饼和炒木薯粉法里尼亚，男子则用弓箭狩猎、捕鱼，并用库马雷棕榈和莫里切棕榈纤维编织吊床。社会为父长制，倾向族内婚：每个有名号的游群各有领地、方言，彼此独立；家庭住在长方形茅草屋里，经期妇女另住小屋。从18世纪末起，哥伦比亚和委内瑞拉牧场的扩张给西夸尼游群带来零星却残酷的暴力，他们依靠退居平原更偏远的地带保持了自治。

en: The Guaycura were the nomadic hunter-gatherers of the southern half of the Baja California peninsula, holding the arid mountains and coasts from near Loreto south to Todos Santos and disputing the bay of La Paz with the Pericú. Their language had no demonstrable link to any other Native American tongue, which linguists take as a sign that their ancestors had lived isolated at the tip of the peninsula for at least five thousand years; they themselves had been pushed south in earlier centuries by the expanding Cochimí. They had no agriculture, pottery or tribal government, but moved in independent bands of a few hundred people, hunting mule deer and bighorn sheep, taking turtles and shellfish on the shore, and roasting agave hearts in stone-heated pits. The Jesuits founded missions in their territory in the eighteenth century, the Alsatian missionary Johann Jakob Baegert leaving the fullest account of their life from San Luis Gonzaga between 1751 and 1768. Numbering perhaps five thousand at contact, the Guaycura were devastated by introduced diseases, and by about 1800 their separate culture had disappeared, the survivors merging into the colonial mestizo population.
zh: 瓜伊库拉人是南下加利福尼亚半岛南半部的游牧狩猎采集族群，占据从洛雷托附近向南直到托多斯桑托斯的干旱山地与海岸，并同佩里库人争夺拉巴斯湾。他们的语言与其他任何美洲原住民语言都找不到亲缘关系，语言学家据此认为，其祖先已在半岛尽头与世隔绝地生活了至少五千年；更早的几个世纪里，他们正是被不断扩张的科奇米人挤到了南方。瓜伊库拉人没有农业、陶器，也没有部落政府，而是以数百人的独立游群为单位迁徙，猎取骡鹿和大角羊，在海岸捕捉海龟、采集贝类，并在烧热石头的土坑中烘烤龙舌兰心。18世纪，耶稣会在他们的土地上建立传教站，来自阿尔萨斯的传教士约翰·雅各布·贝格特于1751至1768年驻在圣路易斯贡萨加传教站，留下了关于他们生活最详尽的记述。瓜伊库拉人在接触之初可能约有五千人，却在传入的疫病下人口锐减；到1800年前后，他们作为独立文化已经消失，幸存者融入了殖民地的梅斯蒂索人群体。

en: Guaycuru is a collective name for the nomadic peoples of the Gran Chaco who spoke Guaicuruan languages, among them the Mbayá, Abipón, Payaguá, Toba, Mocoví and Pilagá. The word began as a Guaraní epithet meaning savage, applied first to the Mbayá and later extended to the whole family, whose bands were matrilocal, exogamous and never politically united. In the sixteenth century they lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, moving camp every few days; the riverine Payaguá paddled canoes on the Paraguay River and menaced Spanish traffic there for two hundred years. After 1542, when the governor Cabeza de Vaca destroyed a Mbayá camp near Asunción, the Guaycuruans acquired horses and iron weapons and built a raiding horse culture: by the 1600s their attacks had forced the abandonment of Concepción del Bermejo and the relocation of Santa Fe, and in 1735 a thousand Mocoví and Toba warriors sacked settlements in Salta Province. A smallpox epidemic from 1732 to 1736 and encroaching Spanish settlements broke their peak power. Jesuits opened the first lasting reduction among the Mocoví at San Javier in 1743, and five to six thousand Guaycuruans lived in missions by the early 1780s, though many drifted back to nomadism. In the early nineteenth century the independence wars split them further, some serving the new republics while other bands raided on, and large parts of the Chaco remained under Guaycuruan control.
zh: 瓜伊库鲁是对大查科地区使用瓜伊库鲁语族诸语言的游牧族群的统称，包括姆巴亚人、阿比庞人、帕亚瓜人、托巴人、莫科维人和皮拉加人等。这个词原是瓜拉尼人对姆巴亚人的蔑称，意为野蛮人，后来才扩大到整个语族；他们的游群实行从妻居和族外婚，政治上从未统一。16世纪时，他们以狩猎、渔捞和采集为生，每隔数日便迁移营地；河畔的帕亚瓜人则划独木舟往来巴拉圭河，袭扰西班牙航运达两百年之久。1542年，西班牙都督卡韦萨·德·巴卡捣毁了亚松森附近的一处姆巴亚人营地，此后瓜伊库鲁人逐渐获得马匹和铁制兵器，形成以劫掠为生的骑马文化：到17世纪，他们的攻势迫使西班牙人放弃贝尔梅霍河畔的孔塞普西翁并迁移圣菲城；1735年，上千名莫科维和托巴武士洗劫了萨尔塔省的定居点。1732—1736年的天花疫病和西班牙定居点的推进，终结了他们的鼎盛期。1743年，耶稣会在圣哈维尔为莫科维人建起第一座稳固的归化区，到18世纪80年代初已有五六千瓜伊库鲁人住在传教站里，但许多人后来又重返游牧生活。19世纪初的独立战争进一步分化了他们：一些人为新生的共和国作战，另一些游群继续劫掠，大查科的大片土地仍掌握在瓜伊库鲁人手中。

en: The Guaîtaká, also spelled Goitacá or Goytacazes, were a non-Tupi Tapuia people of the eastern Brazilian coast, holding the shore between the São Mateus River in present-day Espírito Santo and the Paraíba do Sul River in Rio de Janeiro, where Campos dos Goytacazes still carries their name. Hunter-gatherers rather than farmers, they lived on game, fish, fruit, roots and honey, and were famed as archers and as fishermen who caught sharks in the shallows; their name may derive from the Tupi word guatá, meaning wayfarer or runner. They were divided into three rival bands, the Guassu, Moppi and Jacoritô, and their fearsome reputation as warriors, together with European allegations of cannibalism, let them keep their lands free of settlements long after the rest of the coast had fallen to the Portuguese: they overran the colonies of the São Tomé captaincy in the 1540s and forced the settlers of Espírito Santo onto the island of Vitória. Because their territory barred the route between Rio de Janeiro and Bahia, the colonists turned to manhunts, poisoned brandy and smallpox-infected blankets; the Guaîtaká withdrew into the interior and by the late eighteenth century had been nearly exterminated, the survivors merging into other tribes.
zh: 瓜伊塔卡人又译戈伊塔卡人，是巴西东海岸的非图皮族群，葡语文献归入塔普亚人一类，占据今圣埃斯皮里图的圣马特乌斯河到里约热内卢的南帕拉伊巴河之间的海岸，今坎波斯-杜斯戈伊塔卡济斯镇仍以他们命名。他们不事农耕，以狩猎采集为生，食物包括猎物、鱼、水果、块根和蜂蜜，以善射和能在浅滩捕鲨闻名；族名可能来自图皮语的 guatá，意为行路者或奔跑者。他们分为瓜苏、莫皮和雅科里托三个互相敌对的群体，善战的凶悍名声加上欧洲人关于食人的传言，使他们在沿海其他地区纷纷落入葡萄牙人之手后仍长期保住故土：1540年代他们踏平了圣托梅都督辖区的殖民点，还迫使圣埃斯皮里图的殖民者退守维多利亚岛。由于其领地横亘在里约热内卢与巴伊亚之间的通道上，殖民者转而以猎杀、毒酒和沾染天花的毯子对付他们；瓜伊塔卡人退入内陆，到18世纪末几乎被消灭殆尽，幸存者融入了其他部落。

en: The Guaiteco, better known as the Chono, were nomadic canoe people of the rainy archipelagos of Chiloé, Guaitecas and Chonos off southern Chile, probably the first identifiable inhabitants of Chiloé, whose shell middens and place names still mark the islands. They travelled in wooden dalca boats with dogs aboard, the men harpooning sea lions and other marine mammals while women dived for shellfish and gathered seaweed, supplemented by potatoes from small shore gardens. Francisco de Ulloa's fleet first encountered them in 1553. From the late sixteenth century raiders sailing out of Chiloé hunted them for slaves, a trade given legal cover by Philip III's decree of 1608 even though the Chono had never rebelled, while others were bound into encomiendas. A large band sought refuge at Calbuco in 1710 and was settled on Guar Island. After the wreck of the British warship Wager in the 1740s, the Spanish authorities emptied the Guaitecas and Chonos archipelagos to deny shelter to foreign corsairs, moving the Chono north into Chiloé, where they merged with the Williche and the mestizo population; families that fled beyond the Taitao Peninsula were absorbed by the Kawésqar. By the end of the eighteenth century the Chono had vanished from the written record.
zh: 瓜伊特科人通称乔诺人，是智利南部奇洛埃、瓜伊特卡斯和乔诺斯等多雨群岛上的船居游猎民族，很可能是奇洛埃群岛最早可辨识的居民，群岛上遍布的贝丘和地名都带着他们的痕迹。他们乘木制达尔卡船出行，船上还带着狗：男子用鱼叉猎捕海狮等海洋哺乳动物，女子潜水采贝、捞取海藻，再以岸边小菜园里出产的马铃薯补充口粮。1553年，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚的船队最先遇见他们。16世纪末起，从奇洛埃出发的西班牙人把他们当作奴隶猎捕，1608年腓力三世的敕令更给这桩买卖披上合法外衣，尽管乔诺人从未反叛；另一些人则被束进委托监护制。1710年，一大群乔诺人到卡尔布科寻求庇护，被安置在瓜尔岛。18世纪40年代英国战舰韦杰号失事后，西班牙当局为杜绝外国海盗获得补给，清空了瓜伊特卡斯和乔诺斯群岛，把乔诺人北迁奇洛埃，他们在那里融入维利切人与混血人口；逃到泰陶半岛以南的家庭则被卡韦斯卡尔人吸收。到18世纪末，乔诺人已从文字记载中消失。

en: The Guale were the Indigenous people of the Georgia coast and its Sea Islands, builders of the Savannah and Irene phase Mississippian towns whose platform mounds and shell-ring villages, such as the settlement on Ossabaw Island, go back to the twelfth century. A French expedition under Jean Ribault met them in 1562, and Spanish Franciscans soon turned their country into one of the mission provinces of Spanish Florida. In 1597 the uprising led by Juanillo left five friars dead and drew brutal Spanish reprisals, though the missions were rebuilt after 1600. Their language is now judged unattested and unclassified, the vocabulary once cited as Muskogean having proved to be Muscogee. English-backed slave raids shattered the province: the Westo destroyed every Georgia mission between 1675 and 1684, and Spain abandoned the coast. Refugee Guale became the majority in the Upper Towns of the emerging Yamasee confederacy, and after the Yamasee War of 1715 the survivors merged into the Florida missions and the Lower Creeks; by 1733 they were too few to oppose the founding of Georgia.
zh: 瓜莱人是佐治亚海岸及海群岛上的原住民，是萨凡纳期与艾琳期密西西比式城镇的建造者，其台墩和贝环村落（如奥萨博岛上的聚落）可追溯到12世纪。1562年让·里博率领的法国探险队与他们相遇，西班牙方济各会士很快把他们的土地变成西属佛罗里达的传教省区之一。1597年，胡安尼略领导的起义杀死五名修道士，引来西班牙人的残酷报复，不过传教站在1600年后又得以重建。据后世学者考证，瓜莱语材料不足、系属不明，过去用来证明它属马斯科吉语的词汇其实是马斯科吉语。英国人支持的奴隶劫掠摧毁了这个传教省：1675—1684年间韦斯托人捣毁了佐治亚的所有传教站，西班牙也于1684年放弃海岸。逃难的瓜莱人在新兴的亚马西联盟上镇中占多数，1715年亚马西战争后，幸存者并入佛罗里达传教区和下克里克诸部；到1733年，他们已人丁稀少，无力阻挡佐治亚殖民地的建立。

en: The Guamar were the Chichimeca people of the Guanajuato sierras and the eastern Bajío, with bands reaching into Aguascalientes and the Jalisco border. Hunter-gatherers who called themselves Children of the Wind, they cremated their dead and scattered the ashes to the wind, painted their bodies and long hair, and lived in mobile rancherías rather than towns. Their mountain confederation gathered several smaller tribes, and the seventeenth-century writer Gonzalo de las Casas judged them the bravest, most warlike and astute of all the Chichimecas. When mines and cattle ranches invaded the Bajío, the Guamar became one of the mainstays of the Chichimeca Confederation in the Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590. Spanish arms never broke them; peace came instead through the crown's policy of offering goods, land and mission settlements, under which Guamar bands were gradually congregated and converted during the seventeenth century.
zh: 瓜马尔人是生活在瓜纳华托山区和巴希奥东部的奇奇梅克族群，游帮远达阿瓜斯卡连特斯和哈利斯科边境。他们是自称为“风之子”的狩猎采集者，火化死者并把骨灰撒入风中，在身体和长发上涂彩，居住在可移动的兰乔营地而非城镇。他们的山地联盟汇聚了若干部落；17世纪作家贡萨洛·德拉斯卡萨斯评价他们是所有奇奇梅克人中最勇敢、最好战也最机敏的一族。当矿场和牧牛场侵入巴希奥，瓜马尔人成为1550至1590年奇奇梅克战争中奇奇梅克联盟的主力之一。西班牙人的武力始终无法征服他们；和平最终靠王室以货物、土地和传教城镇招抚实现，瓜马尔诸游帮由此在17世纪逐渐被集中定居并改宗。

en: The Guaná, who call themselves Enlhet and are also named Kaskihá, are a people of the Paraguayan Chaco Boreal whose outside name was imposed by the Mbayá, who once subjugated them as the guaná-niyolola. Their tongue, vana peema, with its Layana and Echoaldi dialects, belongs to the Lengua-Maskoy family. In 1760 the Jesuit Manuel Durán gathered Guanás fleeing Mbayá rule into the San Juan Nepomuceno reduction west of the Paraguay River, which held six hundred people by the time of the Jesuit expulsion in 1768. A second San Juan Nepomuceno was founded in 1797 by Governor Lázaro de Rivera at Caazapá for the Charavaná band, who had settled along the Ipané and Aquidaban rivers to work in Asunción and escape the Mbayá; mixing with Guaraní women soon Guaranized this community.
zh: 瓜纳人自称恩列特，又名卡斯基哈，是巴拉圭北查科的族群；“瓜纳”这个外来名字来自曾征服他们的姆巴亚人，姆巴亚人把他们叫作瓜纳-尼奥洛拉。他们的语言瓦纳佩马语属伦瓜-马斯科伊语系，分拉亚纳和埃乔阿尔迪两种方言。1760年，耶稣会士曼努埃尔·杜兰把逃避姆巴亚人统治的瓜纳人收拢到巴拉圭河以西的圣胡安·内波穆塞诺归化区，到1768年耶稣会被驱逐时，那里已有六百人。1797年，总督拉萨罗·德·里维拉在卡萨帕为查拉瓦纳支另建了一座同名归化区；这些人为到亚松森做短工、躲避姆巴亚人而迁居伊帕内河与阿基达班河一带，后来因与瓜拉尼妇女通婚而很快被瓜拉尼化。

en: The Guanahatabey were the archaic hunter-gatherer people who held the western tip of Cuba, in what is now Pinar del Río Province and the neighbouring parts of Havana and Matanzas, when Europeans reached the Caribbean. They are regarded as late survivors of a much older island population that lived across the Antilles before the farming Taíno expanded: they made no pottery, built no large chiefdoms, and relied on shellfish, foraging, fishing, hunting and small-scale horticulture rather than the cassava fields of their neighbours. Their language was clearly not Taíno, for when Columbus sailed along their coast in April 1494 his Taíno interpreters could not understand a word the locals said; only a handful of place names survive from it. The conquistador Velázquez first wrote their name down in 1514, and Las Casas repeated Taíno tales of cave-dwelling fish-eaters a couple of years later, but the Spanish recorded little else. Swept into the same conquest that began in 1511, the Guanahatabey vanished as a distinct people during the sixteenth century, taking the secrets of their language and origins with them.
zh: 瓜纳哈塔贝人是欧洲人到来时占据古巴西端——今比那尔德里奥省及哈瓦那、马坦萨斯邻近地区——的古老狩猎采集族群。考古学者把他们看作远更早的加勒比岛民的孑遗：在务农的泰诺人扩张之前，这类人群曾遍布安的列斯群岛。他们不制陶器，也没有大型酋邦，不似邻人那样经营木薯田，而是靠贝类、采集、渔猎和小规模园艺为生。他们的语言显然不是泰诺语：1494年4月哥伦布沿其海岸航行时，随行的泰诺语译员完全听不懂当地人的话；该语言仅留下少量地名存世。征服者贝拉斯克斯于1514年首次记下他们的名字，几年后拉斯卡萨斯又转述了泰诺人关于“住洞穴、食鱼者”的说法，但西班牙人留下的记录仅此而已。在1511年开始的古巴征服浪潮中，瓜纳哈塔贝人于16世纪消失为独立族群，其语言和来历的秘密也随之湮没。

en: The Guancavilca were the maritime people of the southern Ecuadorian coast, holders of the Santa Elena peninsula, the Gulf of Guayaquil and Puná Island from about 600, and heirs to the older Guangala culture of the same dry shoreline. Farmers of the arid lowlands, they were above all seafarers: their great balsa rafts carried Spondylus shells, cotton cloth, obsidian mirrors and goldwork north to Mesoamerica and south to Peru and Chile, while copper axe-money served as currency at home. They carved stone monoliths for cults of rain, fertility and healing, among them the god San Biritute, and worked the gold masks characteristic of their crafts. Their language was never documented and remains unclassified. Like the Manta to their north they avoided Inca conquest, and the first Spaniards met them as independent chiefdoms at Colonche and Puná in the 1530s, until the captains Francisco Pacheco and Juan de Olmos broke their resistance; tradition links the name of Guayaquil, built on their shore, to the chief Guayas and his wife Quil.
zh: 万卡维尔卡人是厄瓜多尔南部海岸的海洋民族，约600年起据有圣埃伦娜半岛、瓜亚基尔湾和普纳岛，是同一干旱海岸上更古老的万加拉文化的继承者。他们在干旱低地务农，更是出色的航海者：大型巴尔萨木筏载着海菊蛤贝壳、棉布、黑曜石镜和金器，北抵中美洲，南达秘鲁和智利；在本地则以铜斧币充当通货。他们雕刻巨石独石，祭祀司掌雨水、丰饶和健康的神灵，圣比里图特即为其一，金面具是其工艺的代表。他们的语言没有留下文献，系属不明。与北方的曼塔人一样，他们未被印加征服；16世纪30年代，初来的西班牙人在科隆切和普纳见到的仍是独立酋邦，弗朗西斯科·帕切科与胡安·德·奥尔莫斯两位队长最终粉碎其抵抗。相传瓜亚基尔之名便来自其酋长瓜亚斯与妻子奎尔，这座城市后来就建在他们的海岸上。

en: The Guanche were the indigenous people of the Canary Islands, Atlantic outliers of the North African Amazigh world who reached the archipelago in the first millennium BC and lived there in stone-age isolation. Each island went its own way; Tenerife was split among small kingdoms, the menceyatos, ruled by menceyes. They spoke a Berber-related language, first recorded with a list of numerals by the Genoese Nicoloso da Recco in 1341, worshipped a supreme god Achamán while the demon Guayota haunted the peak of Teide, and the Tenerife islanders embalmed their dead as cave mummies. The Arab geographer al-Idrisi had already picked up tales of the islanders around 1150, but sustained contact came only with the Castilian expedition of Jean de Béthencourt, which took Lanzarote and Fuerteventura in 1402. The other islands resisted for nearly a century: the Tenerife Guanches destroyed a Castilian army at Acentejo in 1494 before defeat at Aguere and the second battle of Acentejo, and the rout of Bentor, mencey of Taoro, in 1496 ended the last independent kingdom. War, enslavement and old-world disease broke the people; survivors merged into the Spanish settler population and their language died out in the seventeenth century, though the whistled Silbo of La Gomera and many island place names live on.
zh: 关切人是加那利群岛的原住民，属北非阿马齐格世界在大西洋上的支脉，公元前1000年间渡海抵达群岛，此后长期处于石器时代的隔绝状态。各岛自成一统，特内里费更分裂为若干由门塞伊统治的小王国门塞亚特。他们操一种与柏柏尔语同源的语言，1341年热那亚人尼科洛索·达·雷科最早记录下他们的数词；他们信奉至高神阿查曼，认为恶魔瓜约塔盘踞在泰德峰顶，特内里费人还把死者制成洞穴木乃伊。阿拉伯地理学家伊德里西约在1150年就记下了岛民的传闻，但持续接触要等到卡斯蒂利亚人让·德·贝当古的远征，他于1402年攻占兰萨罗特和富埃特文图拉。其余各岛抵抗了近一个世纪：特内里费关切人1494年在阿森特霍歼灭一支卡斯蒂利亚军队，随后在阿格雷和第二次阿森特霍战役中落败，塔奥罗的门塞伊本托尔于1496年战败，最后一个独立王国覆灭。战争、掳奴和旧大陆疫病摧毁了这个民族，幸存者融入西班牙移民之中，他们的语言于17世纪消亡，只有拉戈梅拉岛的西尔博哨语和大量地名留存下来。

en: The Guǎngxìn are the Yue-speaking Han people of the middle Xi River valley, centred on Wuzhou in eastern Guangxi and the neighbouring Fengchuan and Sihui districts of western Guangdong. Their name recalls Guangxin, a county founded in 111 BC after the Han conquest of Nanyue; as the seat of Cangwu Commandery and the Jiaozhi inspectorate it was the political and cultural centre of Han-ruled Lingnan, reached from the Yangtze basin through the Lingqu Canal and the Li River. Garrisons and successive waves of northern settlers planted Chinese speech among the Baiyue peoples of this corridor, making it the earliest heartland of the Yue language, and the vernaculars of Wuzhou and Fengchuan still sit close to the prestige dialect of Guangzhou. In 997 the Song court divided the Guangnan circuit east and west of Guangxin, giving rise to the names Guangdong and Guangxi. During the Ming, campaigns against the Yao rebels of the Great Vine Gorge brought the Viceroy of Liangguang to Wuzhou, where a permanent viceroy yamen was set up in 1469; it was moved to Zhaoqing in 1564, briefly returned to Wuzhou in 1655 under the early Qing, and finally settled in Guangzhou in 1746.
zh: 广信人是西江中游河谷讲粤语的汉族民系，以广西东部的梧州为中心，兼及广东西部的封川、四会一带。其名得自广信县：公元前111年汉朝攻灭南越国后置县，广信长期是苍梧郡郡治和交趾刺史部驻地，为汉代岭南的政治与文化中心，中原人士经灵渠、漓江南下即至此地。驻军与历次北来移民把汉语带到这片百越走廊，使这里成为粤语最早的孕育之地，今天梧州、封川一带的方言仍与广州的权威口音十分接近。997年，宋朝以广信为界把广南路分为东、西两路，广东、广西由此得名。明代，为镇压大藤峡的瑶民起事，两广总督于1469年在梧州常设总督府，1564年迁往肇庆，清初1655年一度迁回梧州，最终于1746年移驻广州。

en: The Guarasugwe, also called Pauserna, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the upper Guaporé River on the Bolivia-Brazil border. Descended from Guaraní migrants from Paraguay, they once formed one people with the Guarayo but stayed independent when the Guarayo branch entered missions, keeping their Tupí tongue and customs of cross-cousin marriage and couvade in the riverside forests.
zh: 瓜拉苏圭人又称保塞尔纳人，是生活在玻利维亚与巴西边境瓜波雷河上游的图皮-瓜拉尼族群。他们是自巴拉圭北迁的瓜拉尼移民后裔，曾与瓜拉约人同属一个群体；当瓜拉约支系进入传教站时，瓜拉苏圭人留在河畔丛林中保持独立，沿用图皮语和交表婚、产翁制等习俗。

en: The Guaribes, also called Guarives or Cuaribes, were a Cariban-speaking people of the Venezuelan llanos whose villages lay along the middle and lower Guaribe River and across the Unare basin, between the Guanape River and the Quebrada Honda, in the country that became the states of Guárico and Anzoátegui. They gave their name to the later town of San José de Guaribe. The conquistador Juan de Urpín, campaigning along the Unare, was the first Spaniard to clash with them, and he founded the settlement of San Miguel del Batey on their lands. The Guaribes kept their reputation for ferocity throughout the seventeenth century: when Franciscan missionaries attempted to reduce them, they destroyed the mission and in 1679 killed the friars Sebastián Delgado and Juan de Villegas. Colonial sources describe them as indomitable and even accuse them of cannibalism, while finds of their pre-Hispanic pottery in the Guaribe valley attest to a settled village life that long predated the European arrival.
zh: 瓜里贝斯人（又称瓜里韦斯人、夸里贝斯人）是委内瑞拉平原上说加勒比语的族群，村落分布在瓜里贝河中下游及乌纳雷河流域，地处瓜纳佩河与翁达溪之间，即后来的瓜里科州和安索阿特吉州一带，圣何塞-德瓜里贝镇的名字就来自他们。征服者胡安·德·乌尔平沿乌纳雷河进军时最先与他们发生冲突，并在其土地上建立了圣米格尔-德尔巴泰伊定居点。整个17世纪，瓜里贝斯人都以凶悍著称：方济各会传教士试图驯化他们时，他们摧毁了传教点，并于1679年杀死塞巴斯蒂安·德尔加多和胡安·德·维列加斯两位修士。殖民文献称他们桀骜不驯，甚至指控他们食人；瓜里贝河谷出土的前西班牙时期陶器则证明，在欧洲人到来之前他们已过着定居的村落生活。

en: The Guarijío, who call themselves Macurawe, a name their language explains as the people of the bush, are one of the oldest peoples of the western Sierra Madre, scattered across the rugged borderlands of Sonora and Chihuahua between the Tarahumara to the south and east and the Mayo to the west. Their tongue belongs to the Tarahumaran branch of the Uto-Aztecan family. They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering in a remote country of canyons, and their villages gathered for the tuburada, festivals marking maize planting and harvest with feasting, ritual smoking of wild tobacco, processions and dancing. Jesuit missionaries entered their valleys in the 1620s and built a mission at Chínipas, but Guarijío and Guazapare rebels rose against the friars; after Spanish troops retaliated, the Guarijío dispersed and split into two separate communities, one in Sonora and one in Chihuahua, a division that shaped their later history.
zh: 瓜里希奥人自称马库拉维，按他们自己的语言，这个名字意为“山野之人”。他们是西马德雷山脉最古老的族群之一，散居在索诺拉州与奇瓦瓦州交界的崎岖峡谷地带，南面和东面是塔拉乌马拉人，西面是马约人。他们的语言属于犹他—阿兹特克语系的塔拉乌马拉语支。在这片偏远的峡谷之乡，他们以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生；各村会在玉米播种和收获时举行“图武拉达”庆典，内容包括宴饮、仪式性抽野烟草、列队游行和舞蹈。17世纪20年代，耶稣会传教士进入他们的山谷，在奇尼帕斯建起传教站，但瓜里希奥人与瓜萨帕雷人起兵反抗修士；西班牙军队前来报复之后，瓜里希奥人四散分离，形成索诺拉和奇瓦瓦两个互不统属的群体，这一分裂深刻影响了他们后来的历史。

en: The Guasave, also called Tamazula, were a nomadic coastal people of the marshy estuaries and lagoons of northwestern Sinaloa, around the rivers that later bore their name. They lived from fish, clams, pitahaya fruit and wild harvests, knew how to farm but did not hunt, went without clothing, and were noted as taller than the other tribes of the coast. Their speech, like that of their neighbors the Achire, was unlike any other language recorded in Sinaloa; some ethnologists class them with the Seri of the Sonora coast, which would place them in the Hokan sphere. In 1590 the Jesuits founded the mission of San Pedro y Pablo de Guasave among them, the first permanent Spanish establishment in their lagoon country.
zh: 瓜萨韦人又称塔马苏拉人，是游居在锡那罗亚西北部沼泽潟湖与河口地带的滨海族群，活动于后来以他们命名的河流一带。他们以鱼、蛤、火龙果和野果为生，懂得农耕但不事狩猎，不穿衣物，身材比沿海其他部族高大。他们的语言和邻族阿奇雷人一样，与锡那罗亚有记录的其他语言都不同；部分民族学家把他们归入索诺拉海岸的塞里人系统，若如此则属霍坎语圈。1590年，耶稣会在他们中间建立圣佩德罗—圣巴勃罗德瓜萨韦传教站，这是西班牙人在这片潟湖地区最早的常设据点。

en: The Guato are the nomadic canoe people of the Pantanal wetlands along the upper Paraguay River, on the border between Brazil and Bolivia, and they may be the descendants of the Xarayes, the wetland people remembered from the earliest Spanish expeditions. Juan de Ayolas marched against those tribes in 1537 and the chronicler Ulrico Schmidl left an account of them, while Alvar Nunez Cabeza de Vaca in 1555 already noted how completely their life revolved around canoes and the seasonal floods; Nuflo de Chaves led another campaign into the lagoons in 1557. Their Guato language is usually treated as an isolate, though some scholars link it to the Macro-Ge family. Masters of the dugout canoe, they built vessels on which a family could survive for weeks, men paddling and women steering, moving in small family bands rather than villages and living mainly from fish and birds taken with bow and arrow; an estimate of 1825 put their number along the upper Paraguay at about three hundred.
zh: 瓜托人是潘塔纳尔湿地的游牧船民，游居于巴西与玻利维亚边境的巴拉圭河上游一带，他们可能就是早期西班牙探险记录中湿地族群沙拉耶人的后裔。1537年胡安·德阿约拉斯曾征讨这些部落，编年史家乌尔里希·施米德尔留下了记载；1555年阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德巴卡已注意到他们的生活完全围绕独木舟和季节性洪水展开，1557年纽夫洛·德查韦斯又率军深入湖区。瓜托语通常被视为孤立语言，但也有学者将它与大热语系联系起来。他们是制造独木舟的高手，造出的船能让一家人在上面生活数周：男子划桨、女子掌舵；社会以小型家庭群体为单位而非大型村落，主要靠弓箭射鱼猎鸟为生。1825年的一项估计认为，巴拉圭河上游的瓜托人约有三百之众。

en: The Guayabe, better known as the Guayabero or Jiw, are an indigenous people of the eastern Colombian plains, originally of the Ariari basin and the Guayabero River and later settled along the gallery forests of the Guaviare. They speak a Guahibo-family language and were traditionally nomadic, canoe-using hunters and fishers who planted bitter yuca in rotating forest gardens.
zh: 瓜亚贝人更常见的名称是瓜亚贝罗人或吉夫人，是哥伦比亚东部平原的原住民，最初居住在阿里亚里河流域和瓜亚贝罗河沿岸，后来定居于瓜维亚雷河的长廊林地带。他们使用瓜希沃语族的语言，传统上以独木舟往来，游猎捕鱼，并在轮垦林地里栽种苦木薯。

en: The Guayacundos were a macro-ethnic group of the northern Peruvian Andes, spread across the highlands of present-day Ayabaca and Huancabamba in Piura and across the border into Loja in Ecuador. Colonial sources describe a loose confederation of chiefdoms, of which the Ayahuacas, Caxas and Calvas were the principal sub-groups. They fought the Inca armies when Túpac Yupanqui carried the northern Andean wars into the Piura sierra after the defeat of the Chimú late in the fifteenth century; their leader Guacall eventually negotiated peace and kept his rank under the Inca title Apo Guacal, while many warriors were deported as mitimaes toward Quito. Their centres at Caxas, Aypate and Olleros were rebuilt as Inca provincial towns with terraces, storehouses and sections of the great Inca road. In the war between Huáscar and Atahualpa the Guayacundos sided with Huáscar and were punished for it. Under Spanish rule they were split among encomiendas and reductions, and a revolt led by the curaca Cosme Chinguel around 1588 failed; within a few generations their native tongue had given way first to Quechua and then to Spanish.
zh: 瓜亚昆多人是秘鲁北部安第斯山区的一个大族群，分布在今皮乌拉大区的阿亚瓦卡和万卡班巴高原，并延伸到厄瓜多尔的洛哈一带。殖民时期的文献把他们记载为松散的酋邦联盟，主要分支包括阿亚瓦卡、卡克萨斯和卡尔瓦斯。15世纪末印加人击败奇穆人后，图帕克·尤潘基把北方安第斯战争推进到皮乌拉山区，瓜亚昆多人起而迎战；其首领瓜卡尔最终议和，以印加封衔“阿波·瓜卡尔”保住地位，许多战士却作为米蒂马埃斯移民被迁往基多等地。他们的中心卡克萨斯、艾帕特和奥列罗斯被改建为印加省级城镇，配有梯田、仓库和印加大道的路段。在瓦斯卡尔与阿塔瓦尔帕的内战中，瓜亚昆多人站在瓦斯卡尔一边，因而遭到惩处。西班牙统治时期，他们被瓜分到各个委托监护地和归化村，酋长科斯梅·钦格尔约在1588年发动的反抗也告失败；只过了几代人，他们的本族语言便先被克丘亚语、后被西班牙语取代。

en: The Guayupe were an Arawak-speaking people of the Meta piedmont in eastern Colombia, where the llanos meet the Eastern Ranges of the Andes. Their territory ran from the Upía and Guayabero rivers to the mountain slopes, between the Guahibo to the east and the Muisca to the west, and at the Spanish conquest they may have numbered more than a quarter of a million. They were farmers whose chief crop was cassava, eaten as casabe, and they lived in palisaded villages of bahareque houses arranged around a central square with a sun-oriented ceremonial temple; thorn hedges and camouflaged pitfalls made the forts hard to storm. Chiefs called caciques led an otherwise egalitarian society, and when one died his body was cremated and his successor drank the ashes mixed with chicha. They worshipped the Sun and Moon as husband and wife, with the supreme being Inaynagui and rituals using coca and tobacco. The Guayupe fought the conquistadors hard: in 1534 they wiped out ninety men of Alonso de Herrera's expedition on the Guaviare, and the German-led entrada of 1535 to 1538 had to battle its way across their land against warriors armed with bows, spears and tapir-hide shields. Colonial settlement later broke up their communities, and the Guayupe are remembered chiefly through archaeology and the accounts of missionaries such as Pedro de Aguado.
zh: 瓜尤佩人是哥伦比亚东部梅塔山麓的阿拉瓦克语族群，住在平原与安第斯山脉东科迪勒拉山相接的地带。其疆域从乌皮亚河和瓜亚贝罗河一直延伸到山坡，东接瓜希博人，西邻穆伊斯卡人；西班牙征服时，他们的人口可能超过二十五万。他们务农，主粮是木薯，制成卡萨贝饼食用；村庄设有木栅，巴哈雷克土屋围绕中央广场排列，广场上立着朝向太阳的礼仪神庙，荆棘篱和伪装的陷坑使村寨难以攻破。酋长卡西克领导着一个大体平等的社会；酋长死后遗体火化，继承人要喝下混有其骨灰的奇恰酒。他们崇拜结为夫妻的太阳神与月亮神，信奉至高神伊纳纳吉，仪式中使用古柯和烟草。瓜尤佩人顽强抵抗征服者：1534年，他们在瓜维亚雷河畔全歼阿隆索·德·埃雷拉远征队的九十人；1535至1538年德国人率领的探险队穿越其土地时，也不得不一路迎战手持弓箭、长矛和貘皮盾牌的战士。殖民定居后来瓦解了他们的社群，瓜尤佩人主要通过考古发现和佩德罗·德·阿瓜多等传教士的记载为人所知。

en: The Gubbi-Gubbi, also called the Kabi Kabi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of south-eastern Queensland, whose name comes from their word for no. Their country, well-watered rain forest kept open by regular firing, covered the Mary River basin from Wide Bay and Hervey Bay south towards Noosa and Caboolture and inland to the Coast Ranges, with the Turrbal to their south and the Wakka Wakka and Gureng-Gureng to the west. They were organised into clans around bora ceremonial grounds and spoke Gubbi Gubbi, a Waka-Kabic tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family close to the language of the neighbouring Badtjala. On 18 May 1770 James Cook's Endeavour passed their coast and he named Double Island Point at the southern end of Wide Bay. In 1829 the escaped convict James Davis took refuge among them and was accepted as Duramboi, the reincarnated son of the elder Pamby-Pamby, and lived as a Gubbi-Gubbi man.
zh: 古比古比人又称卡比卡比人，是昆士兰东南部的澳大利亚原住民，其族名来自他们语言中表示否定的词。他们的土地是一片水源充足的雨林，靠定期烧荒留出林间空地，涵盖玛丽河流域，北起宽湾与赫维湾，南至努萨和卡布尔彻，内陆抵达海岸岭；南邻图尔巴尔人，西邻瓦卡瓦卡人和古伦古伦人。他们围绕博拉仪式场分成若干氏族，使用古比古比语，属帕马—牛雅语系瓦卡—卡比语支，与邻近巴特贾拉人的语言相近。1770年5月18日，詹姆斯·库克的奋进号驶过他们的海岸，将宽湾南端的海岬命名为双岛角。1829年，逃犯詹姆斯·戴维斯投奔他们，被当作长老潘比—潘比转世的儿子杜兰博伊接纳，从此像古比古比人一样生活。

en: The Guenoa, also called Minuane or Guenoa-Minuane, were a Patagonian-type people of the wider Charrúa family, sometimes described as the northern Charrúa. At the time of the Spanish arrival they lived in three adjoining lands: the northwest of the Banda Oriental across the Uruguay River, the south of Entre Ríos, where they were called Minuanes, and the southeast of Rio Grande do Sul, where the Jesuits and Portuguese knew them as Guenoas. Their traces remain in the toldo tent sites and cerrito mounds of the southern Brazilian grasslands, and the hill of Ibití near the Arapey River was one of their sacred places. Raiding between the Guenoa and neighbouring Charrúa bands was endemic, fought over horses and women with the killing of captives. European settlement on the Río de la Plata pushed the Charrúa peoples northward, and in 1730 the Guenoa joined a general alliance of Charrúa groups; in the wars that followed they often sided with the Portuguese against Spain. As the colonial order hardened, the Guenoa were drawn into a single Charrúa identity and their separate name gradually fell out of use.
zh: 格诺亚人又称米努安人或格诺亚-米努安人，是巴塔哥尼亚类型的族群，属于广义的查鲁亚大族，有时被称作“北支查鲁亚人”。西班牙人到来时，他们分布在三片相连的土地上：乌拉圭河以东的东岸地带西北部、恩特雷里奥斯南部（在那里被称为米努安人），以及南里奥格兰德东南部（耶稣会士和葡萄牙人称之为格诺亚人）。巴西南部草原上的皮帐遗址和人工土丘留有他们的踪迹，阿拉佩河附近的伊比蒂山是他们的圣地之一。格诺亚人与邻近的查鲁亚诸部之间劫掠不断，为抢夺马匹和妇女而战，并杀死俘虏。欧洲人在拉普拉塔河畔定居后，查鲁亚诸族被迫北移；1730年，格诺亚人加入了查鲁亚诸部的大同盟，在随后的战争中又常联合葡萄牙人对抗西班牙。随着殖民统治巩固，格诺亚人被纳入统一的查鲁亚身份，他们单独的名称逐渐不再使用。

en: The Guìběi are the Pinghua-speaking Han people of the mountain corridor where Guangxi, Hunan and Guangdong meet, around the old Linhe prefecture on the He River, the present-day Hezhou. Their speech, Northern Pinghua, is one of the two main branches of Pinghua; long contact with Hunanese and South-western Mandarin has made its local varieties differ sharply from one another and from the Pinghua of the Nanning region, and some carry Xiang Chinese features. Han settlement began with the earliest migrants who entered Guangxi by way of Hunan in the first millennium, and the name Pinghua is traditionally traced to the Pingnan Army of the Northern Song: after Di Qing defeated the Zhuang rebel Nong Zhigao at the Kunlun Pass in 1053, his soldiers and their families settled the land and kept their camp speech. The Han had set up Linhe county here as early as 111 BC; the Sui made it Hezhou in 589, and in 1377 the Ming reduced Hezhou to He county under Pingyue prefecture.
zh: 桂北人是桂、湘、粤三省交界山地走廊讲平话的汉族民系，聚居于贺江流域的旧临贺郡，即今贺州一带。他们的桂北平话是平话两大支系之一，因长期与湘语和西南官话接触，各地方言彼此差异很大，也与南宁一带的桂南平话明显不同，部分方言还带有湘语特征。汉族移居始于公元后第一个千年里经湖南进入广西的早期移民；平话之名相传出自北宋的平南军，1053年狄青在昆仑关击败壮人首领侬智高后，随军将士和家眷留驻屯垦，把营中口音传了下来。早在公元前111年，汉朝已在此设置临贺县，589年隋朝改置贺州，1377年明朝降贺州为贺县，划归平乐府管辖。

en: The Guìnán are the Pinghua-speaking Han people of the Yong River basin in southern Guangxi, centred on Nanning and stretching through Hengzhou, Binyang and Laibin along the old road to Liuzhou. Their Southern Pinghua falls into the Yongjiang, Guandao and Rongjiang local types, forms a dialect continuum with the neighbouring Goulou Yue dialects, and has absorbed Zhuang words and usages; some Pinghua villages are in fact counted among the Zhuang. The Chinese city on the site began as Jinxing county in 318, was renamed Xuanhua in 598 and became Yongzhou under the Tang in 632, seat of the Lingnan West circuit from 862. In 1052 the Zhuang leader Nong Zhigao seized Yongzhou, proclaimed his own dynasty and swept east as far as Guangzhou; the Song general Di Qing took the Kunlun Pass and recovered Yongzhou in 1053, settling veterans of his Pingnan Army in the region, whom tradition credits with spreading the speech called Pinghua. In 1324 the Yuan renamed the city Nanning, and in 1368 the Ming made it Nanning prefecture, an arrangement the Qing retained.
zh: 桂南人是广西南部邕江流域讲平话的汉族民系，以南宁为中心，沿旧驿道东展至横州、宾阳、来宾一带。他们的桂南平话分为邕江、官道、融江几种地方类型，与相邻的粤语勾漏片连成方言连续体，还吸收了壮语的词汇和用法，有些平话村落甚至被划入壮族。汉人在这一带的城址始于318年的晋兴县，598年改名宣化，632年唐朝置邕州，862年起成为岭南西道的治所。1052年，壮人首领侬智高攻占邕州，自立朝廷，挥师东进直抵广州；宋将狄青于1053年夺取昆仑关、收复邕州，把平南军的老兵留驻此地，相传平话一名即来自这支军队。1324年元朝改邕州路为南宁路，1368年明朝设置南宁府，清代沿用不改。

en: The Gujaratis are the Indo-Aryan people of the Gujarat plain and the Saurashtra peninsula, whose ports at Cambay and Surat made them the great maritime traders of western India. Their language descends from Old Gujarati, the tongue of the Gujjars, which had a written literature by the twelfth century and a settled standard by about 1300 before separating from Rajasthani in the fifteenth, and it uses the Gujarati script, a cursive relative of Devanagari. In 1337 Gujarat was a province of the Delhi Sultanate, conquered by Alauddin Khalji in 1297 to 1300 after the fall of the Chaulukya kings of Patan, whose twelfth-century rulers Jayasimha Siddharaja and Kumarapala had made the region famous, long after Mahmud of Ghazni sacked Somnath in 1025. As Delhi weakened after Timur's invasion, the governor Muzaffar Shah founded an independent sultanate in 1394; Ahmad Shah built Ahmedabad in 1411, the fifteenth-century poet Narsinh Mehta shaped Gujarati letters, and Mahmud Begada and Bahadur Shah made the sultanate a sea power, until the Portuguese took Diu in 1509 and Akbar annexed the province in 1573. Under Mughal rule Surat became India's busiest port, the Gate of Mecca; after 1705 the Marathas gave the Gaekwads their state at Baroda, and British victory in the Second Anglo-Maratha War of 1802 to 1803 left Gujarat split between British districts and numerous princely states.
zh: 古吉拉特人是古吉拉特平原和索拉什特拉半岛的印度-雅利安人，坎贝、苏拉特等港口使他们成为印度西部最重要的海上商人，社群沿阿拉伯海四散分布。他们的语言源自古贾尔人的古老语言，12世纪已有书面文学，约1300年形成稳定的规范形式，15世纪与拉贾斯坦语分家，采用与天城文同源、书写更为连笔的古吉拉特文。1337年时古吉拉特是德里苏丹国的一个行省：1025年伽色尼的马哈茂德洗劫索姆纳特之后，帕坦的乔卢基印度教诸王仍在12世纪的贾亚辛哈·西达拉阇和库马拉波罗治下盛极一时，直到1297至1300年阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉将其征服。帖木儿入侵后德里衰弱，总督穆扎法尔·沙阿于1394年建立独立苏丹国，其孙艾哈迈德·沙阿1411年营建艾哈迈达巴德，15世纪的诗人纳尔辛赫·梅赫塔奠定了古吉拉特文学的风格，马哈茂德·贝加达和巴哈杜尔·沙阿又把苏丹国建成海上强国；1509年葡萄牙人夺取第乌，1573年阿克巴吞并该省。莫卧儿治下，苏拉特成为印度最繁忙的港口，号称麦加之门；1705年后马拉塔军队攻入，盖克瓦德人在巴罗达建国，东印度公司在1802至1803年的第二次英国-马拉塔战争中获胜，古吉拉特从此被分割为英国直辖区与众多土邦，盖克瓦德领地和索拉什特拉诸邦都在其列。

en: The Gula Iro, whose language they call Kulaal, are a Gula people of southeastern Chad, living north and east of the seasonally flooding Lake Iro in Moyen-Chari, between the Bola and the Bahr Salamat. Their speech is a Bua language of the Niger-Congo family, the same small group as the tongues spoken around the Chari and the Guera Massif, and is closest to Zan Gula and Bon Gula; it splits into four dialects, of which Pongal, on the north shore of the lake, is the largest. Gula oral history traces the people to the Blue Nile region, from which they moved into Darfur around 1750 and on toward the lake country of the Chad-CAR border by 1795. The nineteenth century brought repeated slave raids from Darfur, Dar al Kuti and Kara, with heavy tributes in captives and ivory, and Gula communities fled or scattered before the raiders.
zh: 古拉伊罗人是乍得东南部的古拉人支系，自称其语言为库拉尔语，住在中沙里区季节性涨落的伊罗湖以东、以北，地处博拉河与萨拉马特河之间。他们的语言属尼日尔-刚果语系的布阿语群，与沙里河和盖拉山一带的语言同属一个小语群，和赞古拉语、邦古拉语最接近；内部分为四种方言，其中湖北岸的蓬加尔方言使用人数最多。古拉人的口述历史把祖源追溯到青尼罗地区，约1750年迁入达尔富尔，到1795年前后继续迁至乍得与中非边境的湖区。19世纪，达尔富尔、达尔库提和卡拉的奴隶贩子不断来袭，索取大量人口和象牙作为贡赋，古拉社群在袭扰下四散逃亡。

en: The Gulidjan, also called the Kolakngat or Colac tribe, are an Aboriginal people of the volcanic lake plains of western Victoria, holding the country around Lake Colac between Lake Corangamite and the Barwon River, north of the Otway Ranges. Their neighbours included the Wathaurong, Djargurd Wurrung, Girai Wurrung and Gadubanud. Their language was a distinct tongue, perhaps a mixed language drawing on several neighbouring speeches, of which only around a hundred words survive; their name is said to mean belonging to sand, from their word kulak. The grasslands and lakes supplied game, tubers, eels and waterfowl. Colonisation reached them almost immediately after Melbourne was founded: the squatter Hugh Murray occupied their country in 1837, and when the explorers Joseph Gellibrand and George Hesse disappeared there the same year, the blame was put on the Gulidjan and a punitive party killed several of them. For years afterwards they resisted by driving livestock off and raiding stations, until dispossession forced them onto the Europeans' runs.
zh: 古利詹人又称科拉克恩加特人或科拉克部落，是维多利亚州西部火山湖平原上的澳大利亚原住民，领有科兰加米特湖与巴温河之间、奥特韦山脉以北的科拉克湖周围地区，邻近瓦塔武朗、贾古德武朗、吉雷武朗和加杜巴努德等族群。他们的语言自成一支，可能是融合了周边几种语言的混合语，只有约一百个词流传下来；族名据说由意为“沙子”的库拉克一词而来，含义是“属于沙地的人”。草原与湖泊为他们提供猎物、块茎、鳗鱼和水禽。墨尔本建立后，殖民浪潮几乎立刻波及此地：牧场主休·默里于1837年占下他们的土地，同年探险家约瑟夫·盖利布兰德和乔治·赫西在此失踪，罪名被安到古利詹人头上，一支惩罚队伍杀死了数名族人。此后多年他们以赶走牲畜、袭击牧场站的方式抵抗，直到土地尽失，被迫到欧洲人的牧场上谋生。

en: The Gumbaynggirr are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Mid North Coast of New South Wales, their country stretching along the coast from the Clarence River near Yamba to the Macleay River around Stuarts Point and inland as far as Guyra. Clans such as the Gumbathagang, Nimboy and Orara made up the nation, and their language, Gumbaynggir, forms one of the two Gumbaynggiric branches of the Pama-Nyungan family. The shore supported a dense foraging life, and the shell middens built up there include the largest shell deposit of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere. In their Dreaming traditions the white fig, muurrbay, holds a central place, and they made bush sweets by rolling tender acacia shoots in the tree's sap. Long shielded by rivers and forest, they remained beyond the colonial frontier for the whole period to 1837.
zh: 冈比恩格尔人是澳大利亚新南威尔士州中北海岸的原住民，领地沿海岸从扬巴附近的克拉伦斯河延伸到斯图尔茨角一带的麦克利河，内陆远至盖拉。冈巴萨冈、宁博伊、奥拉拉等氏族组成这个族群联盟，他们的语言冈比恩格尔语是帕马-牛雅语系冈比恩格里克语支的两种语言之一。海岸滋养了密集的采集生活，沿岸堆积的贝丘中有南半球规模最大的贝壳沉积。在他们的“梦幻”传统里，白皮榕树穆尔贝居于核心地位；他们还把柔嫩的金合欢嫩芽卷上树汁，做成林间甜食。凭借河流与森林的长期屏障，到1837年为止的整个时期里，他们始终处于殖民边疆之外。

en: The Gumuz, who call themselves Bega, are a Nilo-Saharan people of the Komuz group, scattered through the hot lowlands of the Blue Nile in western Ethiopia and the adjoining Fazogli district of Sudan, where archaeological sites link their linguistic ancestors to the turn of the first millennium. Their own traditions place them once in the western highlands of Gojjam, before the Amhara and Agaw drove them down into the river lowlands and raided them for slaves together with the Oromo and Sudanese traders; highlanders knew them and their neighbours by the collective name Shanqella, and the emperor Yeshaq I, who reigned from 1414 to 1429, already campaigned in the Shanqella country beyond Agawmeder. James Bruce met bow-hunting Shanqella groups on his Nile travels and described them in his book of 1790. Organized in autonomous clans that settle blood-feuds through formal mediation, the Gumuz live by shifting cultivation of sorghum, hunting and honey-gathering, keep granaries for their harvest, and venerate household and field spirits, though some clans nearest the Sudanese border had converted to Islam.
zh: 古马兹人自称贝加，属尼罗-撒哈拉语系的科穆兹语族，散居在埃塞俄比亚西部青尼罗河的炎热低地和苏丹一侧的法佐格利地区；当地考古遗址把他们的语言先民追溯到公元1千纪初。按其口传，他们原本住在戈贾姆省西部高地，后来被安哈拉人和阿高人逐入河畔低地，奥罗莫人和苏丹商人也与高地人一道掳掠他们为奴。高地居民以香格拉统称他们及邻近的深色皮肤部族；1414至1429年在位的皇帝耶沙克一世就曾远征阿加维梅德以外的香格拉地区。苏格兰探险家詹姆斯·布鲁斯在尼罗河之行中遇到以弓箭狩猎的香格拉人群，并在1790年出版的游记里作了记述。古马兹社会由自治氏族组成，氏族血仇通过正式调解机制了结；他们轮种高粱、兼事狩猎和采蜜，建有储粮谷仓，敬奉家宅与田地里的精灵，而靠近苏丹边界的一些氏族已改奉伊斯兰教。

en: The Guna, who call themselves Dule, meaning the people, speak a language of the Chibchan family and trace their origin to a Chibchan migration out of Central America into South America centuries before the conquest. At the time of European contact they lived around the Gulf of Uraba and the borders of Antioquia and Caldas, in what is now northern Colombia, and in 1500 and 1501 the expeditions of Alonso de Ojeda and Vasco Nunez de Balboa met them while probing that gulf. Their pre-contact society was made up of ranked chiefdoms, with matrilocal marriage and farming of maize, sweet potatoes and coconuts combined with fishing and river and coastal trade. Pressure from Spanish slavers and wars with neighbouring peoples set off a long migration westward through the Darien, and during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the Guna moved into the lands left empty by the destroyed Cueva chiefdoms, absorbing fugitive Cueva bands, their former enemies, and settling the Caribbean shore and the offshore islands later known as San Blas. Through this long retreat they kept their communal councils and trading networks, dealing in coconuts, canoes and cloth with Spanish, Scottish and Dutch visitors, and by the early nineteenth century they held the coast from the Darien to the Isthmus of Panama as a largely self-governing people whom no colonial power fully subdued.
zh: 古纳人自称杜勒，意为“人”，所说的语言属奇布查语系；他们的先民生前哥伦布时代若干世纪随奇布查人迁徙潮从中美洲南下南美洲。欧洲人到来时，他们居住在今哥伦比亚北部的乌拉瓦湾以及安蒂奥基亚、卡尔达斯交界处一带，1500至1501年，奥赫达和巴尔沃亚的探险队在探察该海湾时与他们相遇。接触时代的古纳社会由等级分明的酋邦组成，实行从妻居婚姻，种植玉米、甘薯和椰子，兼营捕鱼以及河海贸易。西班牙掳奴者的压迫和与邻近民族的战争迫使他们沿达连向西长途迁徙，17至18世纪间，古纳人进入已被摧毁的奎瓦诸酋邦留下的空地，吸收了世敌奎瓦人的残余部众，并在加勒比海岸和后来被称为圣布拉斯的近海岛屿定居下来。在这场漫长的退却中，他们保留了氏族议事会和贸易网络，以椰子、独木舟和布匹同西班牙人、苏格兰人和荷兰人交易，到19世纪初已据有从达连到巴拿马地峡的海岸，成为没有任何殖民势力能完全征服的自治民族。

en: The Gunbalang, also written Gambalang, Gunbulan or Walang, are an Indigenous Australian people of the Northern Territory coast. Norman Tindale assigned them about 1,600 square kilometres of country on the shore between Hawkesbury Point and Junction Bay, reaching inland some forty kilometres to Table Hill, with the Gunavidji across the estuary to their east, the Gungorogone to the southeast and the Kunwinjku to their south on the Liverpool River. Their ancestral language belongs to the Gunwinggic branch of the Macro-Gunwinyguan family, the stock of languages typical of western Arnhem Land.
zh: 贡巴朗人又拼作甘巴朗、贡布兰或瓦朗，是北领地沿海的澳大利亚原住民。诺曼·廷代尔划定其领地约1600平方公里，位于霍克斯伯里角与章克申湾之间的海岸，向内陆延伸约40公里至泰布尔山；河口对岸以东是贡纳维吉人，东南是贡戈罗贡人，南面利物浦河西岸则是昆温吉库人。他们的祖语属于大贡温古语系下的贡温吉语支，是阿纳姆地西部典型的语系。

en: The Gunditjmaran are the Gunditjmara, a people of south-western Victoria whose country runs from Warrnambool and Port Fairy to Portland and centres on the volcano Budj Bim, once called Mount Eccles; their name joins a word for country or locality with mara, “man”. In 1337 they were already river-and-lake people managing one of the most elaborate aquaculture systems on the continent: across more than a hundred square kilometres of volcanic wetland they had raised stone dams, canals, weirs and woven-basket traps to farm the short-finned eel they call kooyang, channels and ponds first dug thousands of years earlier, with stone-house settlements beside them. They smoked the catch in blackwood leaves, wore sewn possum-skin cloaks and built huts of timber and basalt. Their Dreaming tells how Budj Bim, the “High Head” creator, rose from the volcano and his lava flows became the wetlands, while the dead were borne toward the island of Deen Maar through the cave called Tarn wirrung, the road of the spirits. Whalers and sealers began using Portland from 1810, bringing epidemics; from 1834 the Henty brothers settled the district, opening the long Eumeralla guerrilla wars that earned the Gunditjmara the name of the “Fighting Gunditjmara”, after a feud over a beached whale at Portland's Convincing Ground had all but destroyed the Kilcarer Gundidj clan.
zh: 甘迪特杰马拉人即甘迪特杰马拉本身，是维多利亚州西南部的原住民族群，领地从瓦南布尔和费里港延伸到波特兰，以曾名埃克尔斯山的布吉必姆火山为中心；族名由意为土地或地方的词与意为“人”的“马拉”合成。1337年时，他们已是依河湖而居的族群，经营着澳洲大陆最精巧的水产体系之一：在一百多平方公里的火山湿地里，他们垒起石坝、水渠、堰栅和编织篮鱼栅，养殖名为库扬的短鳍鳗，这些沟渠与塘堰在数千年前即已开凿，旁边还有石屋聚落。他们用黑相思树叶熏制鳗鱼，身披缝制的负鼠皮斗篷，用木材和玄武岩搭建棚屋。他们的“梦创”信仰讲到，至高首领造物主布吉必姆从火山中现身，流出的熔岩化作湿地；死者则经由名为“精灵之路”的塔恩维伦洞穴被送往丁马尔岛。1810年起，捕鲸者和海豹猎手开始以波特兰为基地，也带来了疫病；1834年亨蒂兄弟在此定居，漫长的尤梅拉拉游击战由此爆发，甘迪特杰马拉人因此赢得“善战的甘迪特杰马拉”之名——此前波特兰“信服地”因一头搁浅鲸鱼引发的冲突，已使基尔卡雷氏族近乎灭绝。

en: The Gundungurra, also recorded as the Gandangara, are an Aboriginal people of south-eastern New South Wales, whose some 11,000 square kilometres of country took in Goulburn, the Southern Highlands and much of the Blue Mountains, following the Nepean, Wollondilly and Coxs rivers down towards Camden, with Katoomba and the Megalong Valley within it. Their name is said to combine the words for east and west, and their clans included the Therabulat of the Coxs River, the Burru Burru of Taralga, the Burragorang around Nattai and Bowral, and the Mulwaree around Goulburn; their language was very close to that of the Ngunawal. The explorer Francis Barrallier met them in the Cowpastures in 1802 and was received by the leader Goondel, and they later persuaded Governor King to protect their river yam beds, a promise kept only until he left in 1807. As land grants spread after 1811, drought and hunger drove the Gundungurra into a frontier war alongside the Darawal and Dharug, raiding farms and timing their spear attacks to the slow reloading of muskets. In 1816 Governor Macquarie sent the 46th Regiment under Captain James Wallis against them, and on the night of 17 April his troops surprised a camp on the Cataract River near Appin, shooting at least fourteen people and driving others over the cliffs; the chief Cannabaygal died there, and captured children were carried off to the Native Institution at Parramatta.
zh: 甘邓古拉人（史料亦作甘丹加拉人）是新南威尔士州东南部的原住民族群，其约一万一千平方公里的领地包括古尔本、南部高地和蓝山的大片地区，沿内皮恩河、沃隆迪利河与科克斯河向下延伸至卡姆登，卡通巴和梅加隆谷都在其中。据说其族名由意为“东”和“西”的两个词合成；他们分为若干氏族，包括科克斯河的塞拉布拉特、塔拉尔加的布鲁布鲁、纳泰与博勒尔一带的布拉戈朗，以及古尔本周边的马尔瓦里；他们的语言与恩古纳瓦尔语十分接近。1802年，探险家弗朗西斯·巴雷利耶在考帕斯彻地区遇到他们，受到首领贡德尔的接待；后来他们还说服金总督保护他们河畔的山药地，不过这一承诺只维持到1807年金总督离任。1811年后土地授地不断扩张，加上干旱和饥荒，甘邓古拉人遂联合达拉瓦勒人和达鲁格人投入边境战争：他们袭击农场，并利用火枪装填缓慢的间隙发动长矛冲锋。1816年，麦夸里总督派詹姆斯·沃利斯上尉率第四十六团前来镇压；4月17日夜，英军突袭阿平附近卡特拉克特河畔的一处营地，至少十四人被枪杀，另有一些人被赶下悬崖，首领坎纳贝加尔战死，被俘的儿童则被送往帕拉马塔的原住民学校。

en: The Gunindiri, also recorded as Goonanderry, Cundundeerie or Kunandra, are an Aboriginal people of the Barkly Tableland in the Northern Territory. Norman Tindale assigned them some 14,000 square kilometres along the headwaters of the Calvert, Robinson and Nicholson rivers, reaching south-west to Anthony Lagoon, with Cresswell Downs and Fish Waterhole lying within their country. Their speech formed the south-westernmost member of the Garawan family, alongside Garrwa and Waanyi, and was close enough to Garrwa to be counted one of its dialects, though the language was little recorded before it fell out of use.
zh: 古宁迪里人又记作古南德里、昆敦迪里或库南德拉，是北领地巴克利台地的原住民。诺曼·廷代尔划定其领地约1.4万平方公里，位于卡尔弗特河、鲁宾逊河和尼科尔森河的河源一带，西南延伸至安东尼潟湖，克雷斯韦尔当斯和菲什水洞都在其地域之内。他们的语言是加拉万语系最西南的成员，与加拉瓦语、瓦安伊语并列，且因与加拉瓦语足够接近而被视为其方言之一，不过该语言在停用前留下的记录很少。

en: The Gununa kune, better known by the Mapuche name Puelche, meaning people of the east, were the hunter-gatherers of the lands east of the Andes, from the Neuquen and Rio Negro country south to the steppes around the Chubut. Small bands led by family elders called lonko camped by rivers in tents of branches and hides, hunting guanacos, rheas and Andean deer with bows and arrows, gathering araucaria seeds and carob pods, and fishing; they crossed the mountain passes in portable larch-plank canoes to trade with the Huilliche and the Chono on the Chilean side, and wrapped themselves in fur cloaks called quillangos against the cold. Their own language, Gununa yajuch, is usually treated as an isolate only distantly linked to the Chonan tongues of their Tehuelche neighbours. In the eighteenth century they took part in the poncho fairs that linked the pampas with the Andes, but epidemics at the end of that century shattered them, and the survivors were absorbed into the Araucanized Mapuche world. During the Desert Campaign of 1833 a Gununa kune chief, Vicente Goico, served with the Argentine forces of Jose Felix Aldao.
zh: 古纳库内人更常用的名字是马普切人对他们的称呼佩尔切，意为东方之人。他们是安第斯山脉以东的狩猎采集族群，分布范围从内乌肯和内格罗河一带向南直到丘布特周围的草原。一个个小群体由称作隆科的家族长老带领，在河畔用树枝和兽皮搭帐篷而居，用弓箭猎取原驼、美洲鸵鸟和南安第斯鹿，采集南洋杉籽和角豆，也捕鱼；他们乘着可拆卸搬运的落叶松木板独木舟翻过山口，到智利一侧与维利切人和乔诺人交易，寒冷时裹上名叫基兰戈的兽皮斗篷。他们自己的古纳亚朱奇语通常被视为孤立语言，只与邻族特维尔切人的乔南语有遥远联系。18世纪，他们参加了把潘帕斯草原与安第斯山区联系起来的篷乔集市，但世纪末的瘟疫使人口锐减，幸存者被融入阿劳卡化的马普切世界。1833年荒漠远征期间，古纳库内酋长维森特·戈伊科曾随何塞·费利克斯·阿尔道的阿根廷军队作战。

en: The Gunwinggu, now usually spelt Kunwinjku, are an Aboriginal people of western Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, east of Darwin; like the other Bininj groups they call themselves Bininj, meaning the people. Their heartland lay in the hilly country south of Goulburn Island and the headwaters of the East Alligator River, including the Gumader swamps near Junction Bay and the creeks east of Oenpelli, a territory Norman Tindale estimated at about 7,300 square kilometres. Their speech is the dominant dialect of Bininj Kunwok, a chain of six mutually intelligible dialects stretching from Kakadu to the Liverpool River, and each clan also keeps a special ritual language, kundangwok, for addressing the djang spirits. For centuries before any European reached the area, Macassan trepang fishermen from Sulawesi traded on these coasts, leaving dozens of loan words in the dialects, including balanda for a European, from the Macassan word for Hollander, and their praus appear in the rock art of the Mann River.
zh: 贡温古人今多拼作贡温朱人，是北领地达尔文以东、阿纳姆地西部的原住民，与其他比宁支系一样自称“比宁”，意为“人”。他们的腹地在古尔本岛以南的丘陵地带和东鳄河河源一带，包括章克申湾附近的古马德尔沼泽以及昂佩利以东的溪涧，诺曼·廷代尔估计其领地约7300平方公里。他们的语言是比宁库沃克语最主要的方言，该方言链含六种互通的方言，分布区从卡卡杜延伸到利物浦河；每个氏族还保有一套称为昆丹沃克的仪式用语，专门用来对“江”精灵说话。在欧洲人到来之前的数百年里，来自苏拉威西的望加锡海参渔民已在这一带海岸贸易，给这些方言留下了数十个借词，例如称呼欧洲人的“巴兰达”即源自望加锡语的“荷兰人”，他们的帆船也出现在曼河沿岸的岩画中。

en: The Gurage are a cluster of Ethiopian Semitic-speaking peoples who farm the fertile, semi-mountainous country southwest of the Shewan highlands, around Lake Zway and the upper Awash. They are commonly seen as the descendants of ancient South Arabian settlers who merged with local Cushitic and Harla populations, and oral tradition also remembers military colonies planted by Emperor Amda Seyon I in the fourteenth century. The Gurage first enter written records in the royal chronicle of that same emperor, whose campaigns against the Muslim sultanate of Ifat drew their chiefs into the Ethiopian imperial orbit; by the fifteenth century Gurage clans such as the Ennemor paid tribute in horses to the Christian crown. When the Portuguese priest Francisco Alvares passed through in the 1520s he described them as fierce mountaineers stubbornly guarding their independence, and during the Adal invasion their lands were overrun by Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi until his defeat and death in 1543, while the Christian islands of Lake Zway held out throughout. Divided into many clans speaking several related languages written in the Ge'ez script, and split between Orthodox Christianity and Islam, the Gurage built their life around the cultivation of ensete, the false banana whose fermented bread, kocho, formed their staple food.
zh: 古拉盖人是说埃塞俄比亚闪米特语的族群联盟，农耕于绍阿高地西南方、兹瓦伊湖和阿瓦什河上游一带肥沃的半山区。一般认为他们是古代南阿拉伯定居者与当地库希特人、哈拉人融合的后裔，口述传统还提到14世纪阿姆达·塞约恩皇帝在此设立的军人屯垦地。古拉盖之名最早见于这位皇帝的皇家编年史，他对伊法特苏丹国的征战把当地首领纳入埃塞俄比亚帝国的势力范围；到15世纪，恩内莫尔等古拉盖部族已向基督教朝廷进贡马匹。1520年代葡萄牙传教士弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯途经此地时，称他们是顽强捍卫独立的山民。阿达尔入侵期间，其土地被艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐攻占，直到他于1543年败亡，而兹瓦伊湖中的基督教岛屿始终未陷落。古拉盖人分为许多氏族，使用数种彼此相近、用吉兹字母拼写的语言，信仰上兼有东正教和伊斯兰教；他们的生活围绕象腿蕉（假香蕉）的种植展开，用其发酵制成的阔乔面包是主粮。

en: The Gureng-Gureng are an inland Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, whose country covered the upper Burnett River from Mundubbera north to the Callide Range and east to Many Peaks, reaching west to the Great Dividing Range. They spoke a Waka-Kabic language of the Pama-Nyungan family, included clans such as the Wakgun, and took the emu as their totem.
zh: 古伦古伦人是昆士兰中部的内陆澳大利亚原住民，其领地涵盖伯内特河上游，南起蒙杜贝拉，北至卡利德岭，东达马尼峰，西抵大分水岭。他们使用帕马—牛雅语系瓦卡—卡比语支的语言，分为包括瓦昆在内的若干氏族，以鸸鹋为图腾。

en: The Gurindji are an Aboriginal people of the Victoria River district in the Northern Territory, roughly four hundred and sixty kilometres south-west of Katherine. Their language belongs to the Eastern Ngumpin, or Victoria River, branch of the Ngumpin-Yapa subgroup of Pama-Nyungan, among the northernmost Pama-Nyungan tongues, and has absorbed many loanwords from the non-Pama-Nyungan languages around it; Wanjdjirra, Malngin, Wurlayi, Ngarinman and Bilinarra form a dialect chain with it. With the Malngin, Bilinara, Mudburra and Ngarinyman they count themselves one people, the Ngumpit, sharing language and ceremony, and like the neighbouring Warlpiri they order society through inherited skin names such as Janama, Japarta, Nangala and Nawurla that fix each person's kinship to every other. Their Dreaming is anchored by Jurntakal, the snake, whose travels with other ancestor spirits give shape to their country.
zh: 古林吉人是北领地维多利亚河地区的原住民，住在凯瑟琳镇西南约四百六十公里处。他们的语言属于帕马‑牛雅语系恩贡宾‑亚帕语支的东恩贡宾分支（亦称维多利亚河分支），是分布最靠北的帕马‑牛雅语言之一，并从周围的非帕马‑牛雅语言吸收了大量借词；万吉拉、马尔恩金、武拉伊、纳林曼和比利纳拉诸语与它构成一条方言链。他们与马尔恩金人、比利纳拉人、穆德布拉人和纳林曼人自视为同一个名为贡皮特的族群，语言和仪式相通；和邻近的瓦尔皮里人一样，他们靠与生俱来的“肤名”安排社会秩序，诸如贾纳马、贾帕塔、南加拉和纳武拉，这些名字决定了每个人与所有他人的亲属关系。他们的梦境信仰以蛇灵琼塔卡尔为核心，蛇灵与其他祖灵的行迹赋予了大地以形貌。

en: The Georgian Jews, who call themselves Gurjim, are one of the oldest Jewish communities outside the Levant. Their own tradition, recorded by the eleventh-century chronicler Leonti Mroveli, brings the first settlers to Kartli after Nebuchadnezzar's capture of Jerusalem in 586 BCE, when they were granted land at Zanavi by the old capital of Mtskheta; later refugees are said to have arrived after the Roman destruction of Jerusalem and, in the sixth century, from Byzantine persecution. Archaeological finds confirm a Jewish presence at Mtskheta in late antiquity. After the Arab conquest of the late seventh century, Muslim emirs ruled Tbilisi until 1122, and in the late ninth century Abu-Imran al-Tiflisi founded there the Karaite-leaning Tiflisite sect, which endured for three centuries while most Georgian Jews kept rabbinic Judaism and maintained ties with the Baghdad academies, their piety noted by the traveller Benjamin of Tudela. Their vernacular was Judaeo-Georgian, Georgian enriched with Hebrew words and written in the Georgian or Hebrew alphabets. Unlike most of Europe, medieval and early modern Georgia knew little anti-Jewish persecution, and the community blended deeply into Georgian language and rural life while remaining distinct both from the neighbouring Mountain Jews and, later, from Ashkenazi newcomers after the Russian annexation of 1801.
zh: 格鲁吉亚犹太人自称古尔吉姆，是黎凡特以外最古老的犹太社群之一。据11世纪编年史家列昂提·姆罗韦利所记的本族传说，最早的定居者在公元前586年尼布甲尼撒攻陷耶路撒冷后来到卡尔特利，由古都姆茨赫塔的统治者安置在扎纳维；此后又有罗马摧毁耶路撒冷后的难民，以及6世纪逃避拜占庭迫害的犹太人陆续到来，考古发现也证实古代晚期姆茨赫塔已有犹太人居住。7世纪末阿拉伯征服后，穆斯林埃米尔统治第比利斯直至1122年；9世纪末，阿布·伊姆兰·提弗利西在当地创立倾向卡拉派的第比利斯派，延续了三百年，而多数格鲁吉亚犹太人仍恪守拉比犹太教，并与巴格达的经学院保持联系，旅人图德拉的本雅明曾记下他们的虔诚。他们的日常语言是犹太-格鲁吉亚语，即融入大量希伯来语词汇、可用格鲁吉亚字母或希伯来字母拼写的格鲁吉亚语。与欧洲大部分地区不同，中世纪至近代早期的格鲁吉亚几乎没有反犹迫害，该社群深度融入格鲁吉亚语言和乡村生活，同时又与邻近的山地犹太人、以及1801年俄罗斯吞并后才到来的阿什肯纳兹犹太人保持着明显区别。

en: The Gurma, who call themselves Gourmantché, are a Gur-speaking people of the eastern Burkina Faso savanna around Fada N'Gourma, with communities also in northern Togo and Benin and south-western Niger. They are close kin of the Mossi, whose oral tradition makes Diaba Lompo, eldest son of the hunter Ouédraogo, the founder of Fada N'Gourma, called Nungu in the Gulmancema tongue. The Gurma kingdom of Nungu is traditionally dated from 1204, its rulers bearing the title nunbado, and its dynasty was counted among the Mossi kingdoms descended from Ouédraogo's line. Local tradition also records later ruling clans, the Beriberi, arriving from Bornu to win power by conquest and marriage. Gurma villages combine millet farming with cattle pastoralism, and traditional belief sets a creator god, Tienu, above a world of invisible spirits.
zh: 古尔马人自称古尔芒切，是布基纳法索东部稀树草原上讲古尔语的民族，以法达恩古尔马为中心，在多哥北部、贝宁和尼日尔西南部也有聚居。他们与莫西人亲缘密切；莫西口传传统称，猎人韦德拉奥果的长子贾巴·隆波创建了法达恩古尔马，该城在古尔芒切语中称农古。古尔马人的农古王国传统上追溯到1204年，君主称“农巴多”，其王朝被列入韦德拉奥果后裔的莫西诸王国之列。当地传统还记载，后来的贝里贝里统治氏族从博尔努迁来，通过征战和联姻取得政权。古尔马村落兼营小米农耕和牧牛，传统信仰在众灵之上尊奉创世神捷努。

en: The Gurung, who call themselves Tamu, are a Tibeto-Burman people of the central Nepalese hills, living mainly around Lamjung, Gorkha, Tanahun and Pokhara in Gandaki, the same highlands the game places them in. Oral tradition derives their name from a Tibetan word meaning to bring down, recalling a southward migration from the Tibetan plateau, and their ancestry has been linked to the ancient Qiang people of Qinghai. They traditionally herded sheep and yaks across the Himalayan foothills in a semi-nomadic round, organized into many sub-clans, and their history was transmitted orally in the Gurung language, or Tamu Kyi, a Tamangic tongue written in Tibetan script. Their faith, Gurung Dharma, layers Tibetan Buddhism over older Bon and shamanic rites performed by Ghyabri and Pachyu priests, and they keep the new year at the Tamu Lhosar festival. Gurung fighters served in the Gorkhali armies that built the kingdom of Nepal in the eighteenth century, and after the Anglo-Nepalese War and the Treaty of Sugauli in 1816 they became one of the four main Gurkha tribes recruited into British and Indian military service.
zh: 古隆人自称塔穆，是尼泊尔中部山区的藏缅语族群，主要居住在甘达基地区的拉姆琼、廓尔喀、塔纳洪和博克拉一带，与游戏所划的高地一致。口头传说认为其族名来自藏语中“带下”一词，追忆他们从青藏高原南迁的经历，其族源还被联系到古代青海的羌人。他们传统上在喜马拉雅山麓半游牧地放牧绵羊和牦牛，按众多支氏族组织，历史靠口耳相传，使用塔芒语支的古隆语（又称塔穆基语），以藏文拼写。他们的信仰称古隆法，以藏传佛教覆盖更古老的苯教和萨满仪式，由格亚布里、帕丘祭司主持，并以塔穆洛萨节庆贺新年。古隆战士参加了18世纪缔造尼泊尔王国的廓尔喀军队；1816年英尼战争结束、苏高利条约签订后，他们又成为被英国和印度军方征召的四大廓尔喀部族之一。

en: The Gurunsi are not a single people but an umbrella of loosely related Gur-speaking village communities, among them the Kassena, Nankani, Nuna and Sisaala, spread across southern Burkina Faso and northern Ghana around the towns of Wa and Léo. Oral tradition traces them to the western Sudan, and they are thought to have reached their present lands by 1100. Their villages were built as defensive strongholds, for after the Mossi kingdoms arose to the north in the fifteenth century, Mossi horsemen repeatedly raided Gurunsi country for slaves without ever fully conquering it. The Kassena are known for their flat-roofed clay houses, whose walls the women paint with geometric patterns.
zh: 古伦西并非单一民族，而是对操古尔语、关系松散的一群村落共同体的统称，包括卡塞纳、南卡尼、努纳和西萨拉等支系，分布在布基纳法索南部与加纳北部的瓦城、莱奥一带。口传传统称他们来自西苏丹，一般认为到1100年时他们已迁入现居地。村落按防御据点修建：15世纪北方的莫西王国兴起后，莫西骑兵屡屡南下劫掠古伦西地区掳人为奴，却始终未能将其完全征服。卡塞纳人以平顶黏土房屋闻名，屋墙由妇女绘上几何图案。

en: The Gutes are the North Germanic people of the Baltic island of Gotland, whose name shares a common root with that of the Goths; their own Gutasaga tells how an overpopulated island sent a third of its people south through the rivers of Russia, a memory often linked to the Gothic migrations. As a trading nation they struck a voluntary treaty with the Swedish kings before the ninth century, keeping their own laws and free passage in exchange for an annual silver tribute. Viking Age Gotland grew wealthy on the eastern trade, and more Arab dirhams have been found in its hoards than anywhere else in western Eurasia. In the High Middle Ages Visby became the leading Hanseatic port of the Baltic, while the island governed itself through a landsting of twenty local things and wrote down its Gutalagen law code in Old Gutnish around 1220. Tension between Visby's German merchants and the rural farmers brought a Swedish royal intervention in 1288, and in 1361 Valdemar Atterdag of Denmark conquered the island, cutting down some fifteen hundred farmers at Mästerby. The Victual Brothers held Visby from 1394 until the Teutonic Knights took the island in 1398 and sold it to Queen Margaret in 1409; Danish governors then ruled until the Treaty of Brömsebro returned Gotland to Sweden in 1645. A Russian force briefly occupied Visby in 1808 during the Finnish War. The native Gutnish tongue, preserving Old Norse diphthongs lost elsewhere, gradually lost ground to a Gotlandic dialect of Swedish.
zh: 哥得兰人是波罗的海哥特兰岛上的北日耳曼民族，族名与哥特人同源。他们自己的《哥得兰萨迦》讲述，岛上人口过剩，三分之一的居民沿俄罗斯的河流南迁，这段记忆常被与哥特人迁徙联系起来。作为经商民族，他们在9世纪前自愿与瑞典诸王订约：保留本岛法律、换取自由通行，每年缴纳白银贡赋。维京时代的哥特兰靠东方贸易致富，岛上窖藏出土的阿拉伯迪拉姆银币之多，在欧亚大陆西部首屈一指。中世纪盛期，维斯比成为波罗的海首屈一指的汉萨港口，全岛则由二十个地方庭组成的岛庭自治，并在约1220年用古哥得兰语写下《哥得兰法》。维斯比的德意志商人与乡下农民冲突不断，1288年瑞典国王出兵干预；1361年，丹麦的瓦尔德马四世征服该岛，在迈斯特比斩杀约一千五百名农民。1394年粮食兄弟会占据维斯比，1398年条顿骑士团夺取哥特兰，又于1409年把它卖给玛格丽特女王；此后丹麦总督一直统治到1645年《布勒姆瑟布鲁条约》将哥特兰归还瑞典。1808年芬兰战争期间，俄军曾短暂占领维斯比。本土的哥得兰语保留了其他语言已失去的古诺斯语双元音，但后来逐渐让位于受哥得兰语影响的瑞典语方言。

en: The Guugu-Yimidhirri are an Aboriginal Australian people of Far North Queensland, whose traditional lands of about six hundred square miles ran from the Endeavour River in the Cooktown district north to the Jeannie River and south to the Annan River. Both coastal clans, who called themselves saltwater people, and inland clans lived by fishing, hunting and gathering, and spoke dialects of a Pama-Nyungan language later distinguished as the coastal dhalundhirr, or with the sea, and the inland waguurrga, or of the outside. In 1770 Lieutenant James Cook beached the damaged Endeavour at the mouth of the Endeavour River for seven weeks of repairs, and his crew became the first Europeans to write down an Australian language: they recorded gangurru, the word for a large kangaroo, which entered English as kangaroo, while the artist Sydney Parkinson kept a word list and sketched the local people. A quarrel over sharing a catch of turtles ended in a grass fire and gunshot wounds, after which Cook sailed on, leaving pigs that soon multiplied into a local food source.
zh: 古古‑伊米迪尔人是昆士兰远北地区的澳大利亚原住民，传统领地约六百平方英里，北起珍妮河、南至安南河，库克敦所在的恩迪沃河一带也在其中。他们既有自称“咸水人”的沿海氏族，也有内陆氏族，以渔猎和采集为生，所说的帕马-牛雅语后来分为沿海的达伦迪尔方言，意为“伴海”，和内陆的瓦古尔加方言，意为“在外”。1770年，詹姆斯·库克中尉把受损的“努力号”拖上恩迪沃河口修船七周，他的船员成为最早记录澳大利亚语言的欧洲人：他们记下了指称大型袋鼠的“甘古鲁”一词，英语里的袋鼠一词即由此而来；画师悉尼·帕金森则整理了词汇表并画下当地人的素描。后来双方因分享海龟的争执不欢而散，土著纵火焚草，船员开枪伤人；库克启航前留下的几头猪很快繁殖，成为当地的食物来源。

en: The Guwan are the Koa, or Guwa, an Aboriginal Australian people of the Upper Diamantina River catchment in western Queensland, whose country took in Winton, Kynuna and Corfield. Their language had eastern and western dialects and linked the speech of the Maiawali, Wanamara and Maithakari, and like neighbouring peoples they used an elaborate sign language.
zh: 古瓦人又称科阿人，是昆士兰西部迪亚曼蒂纳河上游流域的澳大利亚原住民，领地包括温顿、基努纳和科菲尔德一带。他们的语言分东部、西部两种方言，把马亚瓦利、瓦努马拉和马伊塔卡里诸语连接起来；和周边各族一样，他们还使用一套繁复的手势语。

en: Guwahiyi corresponds to Kuwohiyi, the Cherokee name of Keowee, meaning 'place of the mulberry patch', the principal town of the seven Lower Towns, and here denotes the Cherokee of the Lower and Middle Towns east of the Blue Ridge Mountains, in what is now western South Carolina, northern Georgia and western North Carolina. They lived in permanent river-valley towns such as Keowee and Tugaloo, and held Kituwah as their ancient mother town, from which one of their self-designations, Anigiduwagi, is derived. Their speech was the Lower dialect of Cherokee, which kept an r sound where the Overhill dialect used l. In 1716 warriors from Tugaloo killed a Muscogee Creek delegation, marking the Cherokee entry into the Yamasee War. Smallpox swept the towns in 1738 and 1739, killing nearly half their people. During the Anglo-Cherokee War of 1760 and the fighting of 1776, colonial militias destroyed Keowee and dozens of other towns, after which the survivors moved south and west into Georgia, Alabama and Tennessee.
zh: 古瓦希伊对应切罗基下城七镇首镇基奥维的切罗基语名称，意为“桑园之地”，在此指蓝岭山脉以东下城与中城的切罗基人，分布在今南卡罗来纳西部、佐治亚北部和北卡罗来纳西部。他们定居在基奥维、图加卢等永久性河谷城镇，并把基图瓦奉为古老祖城，切罗基人的自称之一“阿尼吉杜瓦吉”即由基图瓦而来。他们讲切罗基语下城方言，该方言保留颤音r，山外方言则以l对应。1716年，图加卢的武士杀死马斯科吉（克里克）使团，标志着切罗基卷入雅马西战争。1738至1739年天花席卷各城，近半数居民病死。1760年英国—切罗基战争及1776年的战事中，殖民地民兵摧毁了基奥维等数十座城镇，幸存者随后向南、向西迁入佐治亚、亚拉巴马和田纳西境内。

en: The Guwinmali, also recorded as the Koinmerburra or Koinjmal, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Queensland coast, whose lands ran from Broad Sound and the Styx River north to Cape Palmerston, taking in St Lawrence and reaching inland to the Coast Range and Marlborough. They worked the mangrove mudflats of their shoreline in bark canoes and were divided into two moieties, the Yungeru and Witteru, split into four totemic sections named for the eaglehawk, the laughing jackass, the wallaby and the curlew. Parents betrothed daughters in infancy and the marriage was sealed by a ceremonial mock capture. Their speech, Guwinmal, was a dialect of Darumbal within the Pama-Nyungan family. In 1770 James Cook's Endeavour charted this coast and named Cape Palmerston, at the northern edge of their country.
zh: 古温马尔人又称科因梅布拉人或科因马尔人，是昆士兰中部沿海的澳大利亚原住民，其土地北起帕默斯顿角，南至布罗德桑德与斯蒂克斯河，包括圣劳伦斯，并向内陆延伸到海岸岭与莫尔伯勒。他们驾树皮独木舟在海岸的红树林泥滩上劳作，社会分为云格鲁和维特鲁两个半偶族，其下再分四个图腾分支，分别以雕、笑翠鸟、沙袋鼠和杓鹬为名。父母在女儿幼年时便为其订婚，婚礼以一场仪式性的假掳走完成。他们的古温马尔语是帕马—牛雅语系达伦巴尔语的一种方言。1770年，库克的奋进号测绘了这段海岸，并将其领地北缘命名为帕默斯顿角。

en: The Gwich'in, long known to outsiders as Kutchin or by the French name Loucheux, and calling themselves Dinjii Zhuu, are an Athabaskan people of the far northwest, spread across the tundra and boreal country north of the Arctic Circle from north-eastern Alaska through the northern Yukon to the lower Mackenzie River. Their many bands, among them the Vuntut, Teetlit, Gwichyaa, Danzhit Hanlaii and Deenduu, share three exogamous clans, the Nantsaii, Chits'yaa and Tenjeraatsaii, into which everyone must marry out, and their place names trace an occupation of the region back to the early Holocene, roughly 8000 years ago. Life turned on the great caribou herds, above all the Porcupine herd, together with river salmon, and the Gwich'in became celebrated makers of snowshoes, birchbark canoes and two-way sleds, and of caribou-skin clothing decorated with beadwork and porcupine quill. Their history and laws were carried in a rich oral literature of trickster and animal tales, while two main dialects, eastern and western, divided roughly along the Alaska-Canada border.
