zh: 万卡潘帕人又称万卡班巴人，是秘鲁北部皮乌拉高原的原住民，聚居于安第斯山脉东西两列山脉之间的万卡班巴河上游。考古发现与葬俗表明他们源自亚马孙地区，与瓜亚昆多人、卡尼亚尔人和布拉卡莫罗人相邻且有亲缘关系。他们原本崇拜美洲豹，约1480年印加王图帕克·尤潘基征服该地，取缔旧有信仰、推行太阳神崇拜并派驻米特马埃移民，建立了卡哈斯和万卡班巴两座行省中心。1532年，埃尔南多·德·索托的先遣队在前往会见阿塔瓦尔帕途中经过万卡潘帕，当时它比卡哈斯更大、人口更多。西班牙统治时期，他们被以委托监护制授予迭戈·帕洛米诺，并被迁入归化村；原有语言先被克丘亚语、后被西班牙语取代，但万卡班巴一带的原住民社群一直延续到共和国时期。

en: The Huarco, also written Warku, were the people of a coastal kingdom in the Canete valley, south of Lima, contemporary with the Chimu Empire to the north. Their strongholds included the sea-facing fortress of Cerro Azul and Ungara, and their confederation held out against the Incas for four or five years during the Huarco-Inca war of the 1450s. Chroniclers record that the widowed lady curaca of the Huarco only lost her valley through cunning: the Inca queen Mama Ocllo proposed a joint ritual fishing festival in honour of the sea goddess Mama Cocha, and while the Huarco forts were emptied for the ceremony at sea, Inca troops slipped into the valley and seized the chiefdom. The victors built the great stone fortress of Cerro Azul, with stairways running down to the water, which the chronicler Pedro Cieza de Leon ranked alongside Sacsahuaman, and Tupac Yupanqui laid out the administrative centre of Incahuasi in the four-part plan of Cuzco; Huarco then entered the empire as a Chinchaysuyu province.
zh: 瓦尔科人又拼作瓦尔库人，是利马南方卡涅特河谷沿海王国的居民，与北方的奇穆帝国同时代。他们的要塞包括面朝大海的塞罗阿苏尔堡和温加拉堡；在1450年代的瓦尔科-印加战争中，瓦尔科联盟顽强抵抗了四五年。编年史家记载，他们守寡的女酋长最终败于计谋：印加王后玛玛·奥克略提议共同举办祭祀海神玛玛科查的仪式性捕鱼节，当瓦尔科各要塞因民众出海举行典礼而空虚时，印加军队潜入河谷夺取了酋长国。胜利者修建了宏伟的塞罗阿苏尔石堡，石阶一直延伸到海边，编年史家佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂把它与萨克塞瓦曼相提并论；图帕克·尤潘基又按库斯科的四区格局营建了印加瓦西行政中心，瓦尔科此后作为钦查苏尤的一个省份并入帝国。

en: The Téenek, better known as the Huastec, are a Maya people of the Gulf coast of Mexico, concentrated along the Pánuco River in the Huasteca, a region spanning Veracruz, San Luis Potosí, Tamaulipas and Hidalgo. Their autonym means people from here, and their language was the first branch to split from Proto-Mayan, perhaps in the early second millennium BCE, which makes them the northernmost outlier of the Maya world. Settled in the region since roughly 1000 BCE, they built step-pyramids and carved standing stone figures, while their painted pottery and shell work drew admiration from neighboring peoples, who also praised their musicians. Their most flourishing era was the Postclassic, after the fall of Teotihuacan. Around 1450 the Aztec emperor Moctezuma I conquered them, and Huastec towns paid tribute while keeping much of their self-rule. Spanish conquest between 1519 and the 1530s ended that order; the friar Andrés de Olmos later wrote the first European grammar of their language, while many Huastecs were shipped into slavery in the Caribbean.
zh: 瓦斯特克人是墨西哥湾沿岸的玛雅民族，自称意为“本地人”，聚居于帕努科河流域的瓦斯特卡地区，地跨韦拉克鲁斯、圣路易斯波托西、塔毛利帕斯和伊达尔戈四地。他们的语言是最早从原始玛雅语分离出来的一支，分化约在公元前两千纪初，因此也是玛雅世界最靠北的旁支。约公元前1000年起他们便定居于此，修筑阶梯金字塔，雕刻独立石像，彩绘陶器和贝壳工艺令邻族称羡，乐师也广受称道；特奥蒂瓦坎衰落之后的后古典期是他们最繁荣的阶段。约1450年，阿兹特克皇帝蒙特苏马一世征服瓦斯特克，各城在保留相当自治权的同时向阿兹特克纳贡。1519年至1530年代西班牙的征服终结了这一秩序，修士安德烈斯·德·奥尔莫斯后来写下欧洲人第一部瓦斯特克语语法，许多瓦斯特克人则被贩运到加勒比为奴。

en: The Huayla, or Huaylas, were the people of the long, fertile Callejón de Huaylas, the Santa River valley shut between the snowy ranges of the Ancash highlands, whose occupation reaches back to the Chavín horizon of around 500 BC and whose principal shrine was the temple of Pumacayán. In the Late Intermediate Period they formed a large señorío, and when the Incas pushed north the Huayla rose against them in revolts alongside the Conchucos, Piscopampas and Huari; only between 1470 and 1490, under Túpac Yupanqui and Huayna Cápac, was the valley subdued, at the cost of Pumacayán's destruction and the obligation on its curacas to send their daughters to Cusco as secondary wives. The Incas reorganized them into Hanan Huaylas and Hurin Huaylas, each with its own lords and shrines, and the maize lands of Hanan Huaylas were counted among the most fertile provinces of the empire, giving the Huayla elite a prominent place in Cusco. They claimed descent from the creator god Huari and worshipped the stone idol Macovilca at Pumacayán. The bond with the Inca dynasty served them well under the Spaniards: Contarhuacho, a daughter of the Hanan curaca and a wife of Huayna Cápac, bore Quispe Sisa, baptized Inés de Huaylas, who became the first wife of Francisco Pizarro, and in August 1536 Contarhuacho sent a large Huayla contingent to help defend Lima against Quizu Yupanqui during Manco Inca's great siege. Their valley was afterward partitioned into encomiendas and Indian reductions.
zh: 怀拉人又称瓦伊拉斯人，居住在安卡什高原雪山之间狭长肥沃的圣河谷地瓦伊拉斯走廊；人类在这一带的活动可追溯到约公元前500年的查文时期，其最重要的圣地是普马卡扬神庙。晚中间期他们形成了幅员广阔的领主政权，印加人向北扩张时，怀拉人与孔丘科人、皮斯科潘帕人和瓦里人结盟，接连起义反抗；直到1470年至1490年间，图帕克·尤潘基和瓦伊纳·卡帕克才将谷地征服，代价是普马卡扬神庙被毁，各地首领还必须把女儿送往库斯科做印加王的次妃。印加人把怀拉人分为上怀拉和下怀拉两个半边，各有首领和大神庙；上怀拉的玉米地被视为帝国最肥沃的省份之一，怀拉贵族也因此在库斯科地位显赫。他们自称是创世神瓦里的后裔，供奉普马卡扬的石像神马科维尔卡。与印加王室的联姻在西班牙时代带来好处：上怀拉首领之女孔塔瓦乔是瓦伊纳·卡帕克的妃子，生下基斯佩·西西萨（受洗后取名伊内斯·德·瓦伊拉斯），后来成为皮萨罗的第一任妻子；1536年8月曼科·印加大举围攻利马时，孔塔瓦乔又从怀拉派出大批军队，协助西班牙人抵御印加将领基苏·尤潘基。此后他们的谷地被划分为委托监护地和印第安人归化镇。

en: The Huàzhōu are the people of the old Hua prefecture in south-western Guangdong, around present-day Huazhou and its Shilong seat on the Jian River, bordering Guangxi. Their dialect forms, together with the speech of neighbouring Wuchuan, the Wu-Hua branch of Yue Chinese, one of the most distinctive varieties of western Guangdong. Its ancient voiceless initials have turned into implosive voiced stops while old voiced initials now read as unaspirated voiceless, a three-way split in the labial and dental series that sets it sharply apart from Guangzhou Cantonese. The region was first organized as Guanghua county in the Three Kingdoms era, and in 980 the Song renamed the former Bian prefecture Hua zhou, after the transforming dragon of its Shilong seat, which is the origin of the name; the Yuan made it a route, and the Ming converted it into Hua prefecture in 1368, before it was eventually reduced to a county within Gaozhou commandery.
zh: 化州人聚居在广东西南、毗邻广西的化州旧地，中心是鉴江边上的旧治石龙，即今化州市区。化州话与相邻的吴川话共同构成粤语吴化片，片名取自吴川、化州两地首字，是粤西粤语最有特色的一支：古全清声母今读内爆浊音，古全浊声母今读不送气清音，帮、端两组呈现三分格局，与广州话差别明显。这一带在三国时已置广化县，980年北宋把辩州改名为化州，取州治石龙“能变化”之义，下辖石龙、吴川两县，是化州得名之始；元代设化州路，明代又于1368年改置化州府，后来降为县，归入高州府。

en: The Huetar were the most powerful and best organised Indigenous people of Costa Rica when the Spanish arrived, occupying the centre of the country from the Pacific coast across to the Caribbean slope in a loose set of rival kingdoms rather than a single state. The greatest were Garabito, holding the Pacific basin of the Grande de Tarcoles as far as the Virilla River, Pacaca in the western Central Valley, and the eastern realm of El Guarco and Correque, which ran from the Virilla to the Chirripo plains and counted Aserri, Ujarraz and Atirro among its vassal towns. Their Chibchan speech served as a lingua franca across the isthmus, though the peoples sharing it were often at war. Huetar society was divided between hereditary chiefs, priests and shamans called sukias, commoners and slaves; they farmed maize, beans, manioc and pejibaye palms, brewed chicha for ceremonies, and belonged to the Intermediate Area culture, famed for finely carved stone metates, tables and altars, sun and moon worship, and funerary human sacrifice, but not cannibalism. From the 1560s onward the Spanish subdued the kingdoms one by one: even Garabito and the baptized Fernando Correque eventually swore vassalage, and the population was concentrated into reducciones such as Barva, Pacaca, Aserri, Orosi and Tucurrique under the encomienda. Epidemics and forced labour broke their society, and by 1675 the Indians of the Central Valley all spoke Spanish, leaving the Huetar language extinct except in place names such as Aserri, Tucurrique and Barva.
zh: 韦塔尔人是西班牙人到来时哥斯达黎加最强大、组织最严密的原住民，据有该国中部，从太平洋岸横贯加勒比坡地，但其政治形态并非统一国家，而是一批相互争战的王国。最强的是据有太平洋岸塔尔科莱斯大河盆地、延伸至比里利亚河的加拉维托，中央谷地西部的帕卡卡，以及东部埃尔瓜尔科与科雷克的领地——后者从比里利亚河一直伸展到奇里波平原，阿塞里、乌哈拉斯、阿蒂罗等城镇都是其附庸。他们的奇布查语是地峡上的通用语，但操这种语言的各族群却常常兵戎相见。韦塔尔社会分为世袭酋长、祭司和叫苏基亚的巫医、平民与奴隶几个等级；他们种植玉米、菜豆、木薯和桃椰子，仪式上饮用奇恰酒，文化上属美洲中间区传统，以精雕的石磨盘、石桌和石祭坛、日月崇拜以及葬礼人祭闻名，但并无食人习俗。16世纪60年代起，西班牙人逐个征服这些王国，连加拉维托和受洗改名费尔南多·科雷克的王公也最终称臣，人口被强行并入巴尔瓦、帕卡卡、阿塞里、奥罗西、图库里克等归化村，受委托监护制管束。疫病和苦役摧毁了他们的社会，到1675年中央谷地的印第安人已全部改说西班牙语，韦塔尔语就此消亡，只残留在阿塞里、图库里克、巴尔瓦等地名中。

en: The Huí, long called Huihui in Chinese records, are the Chinese-speaking Muslims whose ancestors were the Arab and Iranian merchants of the Silk Road and the maritime trade, some of whom arrived as early as the eighth century, when three thousand Arab mercenaries helped the Tang against the An Lushan rebellion. Settling in ports such as Guangzhou and Quanzhou and in market towns across the northwest, they married local women and gradually adopted Chinese speech and customs while keeping Islam, building mosques known as qingzhensi and following halal dietary rules. Their numbers grew sharply under the Mongol Yuan, when Central Asian Muslim soldiers, artisans and officials, classed as semu, formed the second rank of the empire below the Mongols, planting large communities in Gansu, Ningxia and Yunnan; in 1337 these communities already stretched from the Hexi Corridor to the Jiangnan cities. Under the Ming, Huí troops served in the conquest of Yunnan and were settled there as garrison farmers. In the Qing, Sufi orders took root in the northwest, and rivalry between the new Jahriyya order and the older Gedimu tradition fueled the Jahriyya revolt of the 1780s, the first of the great Huí uprisings of the imperial northwest.
zh: 回人在汉文史籍中常称回回，是说汉语的穆斯林；其祖先是丝绸之路上和海路贸易中的阿拉伯、波斯商人，早在8世纪就已来华，当时还有三千大食兵帮助唐朝平定安史之乱。他们在广州、泉州等港口和西北的商镇定居，与当地妇女通婚，逐渐改用汉语、沿袭华俗，同时保持伊斯兰教信仰，建造称“清真寺”的礼拜寺，恪守清真饮食。蒙古元朝时，中亚的穆斯林士兵、工匠和官员被划为色目人，地位仅次于蒙古人，回回人口因此大增，在甘肃、宁夏和云南形成大片聚居区；1337年时，这些社群已从河西走廊一直分布到江南城市。明代，回回军士参与平定云南，并以屯戍身份留居当地。清代，苏菲派门宦在西北扎根，新兴的哲合忍耶与老牌格底目传统之间的冲突引发了18世纪80年代的哲合忍耶起义，这是帝国西北一系列大规模回变的先声。

en: The Wixáritari, whom the Spanish called Huichol and whose adjective for themselves and their language is Wixárika, are an Indigenous people of the canyons and highlands of the Sierra Madre Occidental, across the later states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Zacatecas and Durango. Their language belongs to the Corachol group and is closely related to the Nahuan languages. Their own oral history traces them to the San Luis Potosí country, where they were part of the Guachichil nation; in the sixteenth century, as Spanish mines, encomiendas and epidemics overran that region, they took refuge in the remote Bolaños Canyon, settling among the Tepecano, intermarrying with them and jointly fighting Spanish incursions, including a combined rising at El Teúl. As early as 1587 the friar Alonso Ponce described them raiding Spanish settlements and caravans together with Guachichil war parties. Sheltered by the mountains, they kept their ancestral faith with little Catholic imprint: families lived in dispersed ranchos grouped into temple districts under councils of elder shamans, the kawiterutsixi, and each year pilgrims walked east to Wirikuta, the sacred desert of San Luis Potosí, to gather the peyote cactus at the heart of their ritual life.
zh: 维夏里卡斯人被西班牙人称为维乔尔人，他们自称“维夏里塔里”，意为“人”，修饰自身和语言时则用“维夏里卡”。这个族群生活在西马德雷山脉的峡谷与高地，分布于后来的纳亚里特、哈利斯科、萨卡特卡斯和杜兰戈诸州；他们的语言属科拉乔尔语组，与纳瓦语支关系密切。据其口述史，他们的祖地在圣路易斯波托西一带，本是瓜奇奇尔人的一部分；16世纪，当西班牙人的矿场、委托监护制和疫病席卷那片地区时，他们避入偏远的博拉尼奥斯峡谷，在特佩卡诺人的聚落间落脚，与之通婚并联手抗击西班牙人的进袭，曾在埃尔特乌尔联合起事。早在1587年，修士阿隆索·庞塞就记载他们随瓜奇奇尔人的战队一起劫掠西班牙人的定居点和商队。凭借群山庇护，他们几乎未受天主教影响，完整保留了祖先信仰：各个家族散居在名为“兰乔”的小居民点里，若干兰乔组成神庙区，由长老兼萨满的“卡维特鲁特西克斯”议事会治理；每年都有朝圣者东行，徒步前往圣路易斯波托西境内的神圣荒漠维里库塔，采集在他们仪式生活中居于核心地位的佩奥特掌。

en: The Huizhou Hakka are Hakka-speaking Han Chinese settled around Guishan, the old county of the Huiyang prefecture on the Dong River in east-central Guangdong. The name Hakka means guest families: their forebears were later migrants from the Central Plains who entered Guangdong by way of Jiangxi and took up the hilly marginal land that earlier Han settlers had passed over, while the older population of the region had included Yue, She and Yao peoples. Under the Song, Huizhou was a prefectural seat and the cultural centre of the area; in the 1090s the poet Su Shi was exiled there and renamed its Feng Lake the West Lake. A county annals records that in the late fourteenth century the whole prefecture held barely forty-five thousand people, and most present-day families descend from migrants of the late Yuan and early Ming and from Qing-era resettlement. After the coastal evacuation edicts of 1661 and 1664 emptied the coast, Hakka farmers were encouraged to move back into the cleared districts when the order was lifted from 1669. They lived in walled villages and spoke the Huiyang variety of Hakka, alongside a local Huizhou speech of disputed classification.
zh: 惠州客家人是聚居于广东中东部东江沿岸归善（旧时惠阳府治所在）一带、操客家话的汉族民系。客家意为“客居的家族”：他们的先民是较晚南下的中原移民，取道江西进入广东，落脚在早先汉族移民不愿开垦的丘陵瘠地；而当地更早的居民中还有越人、畲人和瑶人。宋代惠州是州府治所和区域文化中心，11世纪90年代诗人苏轼被贬至此，把当地的丰湖改名为西湖。据县志记载，14世纪末整个惠州府仅有四万五千余人，今天的居民大多是元末明初移民以及清代复界移民的后裔。1661年和1664年的迁界令使沿海地带为之一空，1669年禁令放宽后，客家农民被鼓励迁入已清空的地区垦殖。他们聚族而居，修筑围村，所说的是客家话的惠阳口音，另外还有一种归属存在争议的惠州本地话。

en: The Hungarians, or Magyars, speak a Ugric language of the Uralic family, a clue to origins among the hunter-herder peoples east of the southern Urals. By the early ninth century their seven tribes, joined by three rebel Kabar tribes, lived on the steppes north of the Black Sea in the land called Etelköz, and around 895, pressed by the Pechenegs, they crossed the Carpathians into the basin left politically vacant by the fall of the Avars. Under the Árpád dynasty their horsemen raided as far as Italy, France and Spain until the German victory at the Battle of Lechfeld in 955; the grand prince Stephen then accepted Christianity and was crowned king around 1000, organizing the Kingdom of Hungary around counties and bishoprics. The medieval kingdom became a major Central European power, though the Mongol invasion of 1241 to 1242 depopulated much of the Great Plain and prompted a wave of castle-building and colonization. The Ottoman victory at Mohács in 1526 split the country into three: the Turkish pashaluk in the centre, the semi-independent Principality of Transylvania, and Habsburg-ruled Royal Hungary, which kept Hungarian statehood alive through a century and a half of border warfare and anti-Habsburg risings. Christian forces retook Buda in 1686 and the Treaty of Karlowitz of 1699 restored the whole realm to the Habsburg crown; the Rákóczi war of 1703 to 1711 was the last great feudal revolt, after which an emptied Great Plain was replanted with returning Magyars and incoming Serbs, Germans and Slovaks.
zh: 匈牙利人又称马扎尔人，操乌拉尔语系乌戈尔语支语言，其族源可追溯到南乌拉尔以东的狩猎畜牧民族。9世纪初，他们的七个部落联合三支出逃的卡巴尔部落，生活在黑海以北名为“埃泰尔克兹”的草原上；约895年，受佩切涅格人逼迫，他们翻越喀尔巴阡山，进入阿瓦尔汗国崩溃后权力真空的盆地。在阿尔帕德王朝率领下，匈牙利骑兵曾远征意大利、法兰西和西班牙，直到955年在莱希费尔德战役被德意志人击败；此后大公斯蒂芬接受基督教，约1000年加冕为王，以城堡州和主教区为骨架建立匈牙利王国。中世纪的匈牙利是中欧强国，但1241至1242年的蒙古入侵使大平原人口锐减，随后掀起修建城堡、招徕移民的浪潮。1526年莫哈奇战役的惨败使国家一分为三：中部是土耳其帕夏辖区，半独立的特兰西瓦尼亚公国割据一方，哈布斯堡统治的“皇家匈牙利”则在一个半世纪的边境战争和反哈布斯堡起义中维系着匈牙利国家的延续。1686年基督教联军收复布达，1699年的《卡尔洛维茨条约》把整个王国归还哈布斯堡王冠；1703至1711年的拉科齐独立战争是最后一次大规模封建起义，此后荒芜的大平原由回流的马扎尔人与迁入的塞尔维亚人、德意志人和斯洛伐克人重新开垦。

en: The Hupa are an Athabaskan-speaking people of northwestern California, whose ancestors moved south from the north around the year 1000 and settled the Hoopa Valley on the Trinity River. Their territory followed the Trinity from its South Fork down toward its confluence with the Klamath, where it bordered the country of the Yurok. Red cedar-planked houses, dugout canoes and basket hats linked them to their northern Athabaskan kin, while sweat-house ceremonies and acorn bread were customs shared with neighboring California peoples. They fished the salmon runs of the Trinity and Klamath, maintained communal fish weirs, and traded acorns and baskets to the Yurok in exchange for salt and canoes. Their closest relatives were the Tsnungwe, Chilula and Whilkut, who spoke kindred Athabaskan dialects. Through the centuries up to 1837 the Hupa remained beyond the reach of the Spanish missions and the maritime fur trade, their valley life undisturbed by outside settlement.
zh: 胡帕人是加利福尼亚西北部讲阿萨巴斯卡语的族群，其祖先约在1000年从北方南迁，在特里尼蒂河畔的胡帕谷地定居。他们的领地沿特里尼蒂河从南支延伸到临近克拉马斯河交汇处一带，与尤罗克人的土地相接。红杉木板屋、独木舟和篮帽表明他们与北方的阿萨巴斯卡亲族同源，而汗房仪式和橡果面包则是与周边加州族群共有的习俗。他们在特里尼蒂河和克拉马斯河捕捞洄游的鲑鱼，共同维护鱼梁，并用橡果和篮子向尤罗克人交换盐和独木舟。与他们关系最近的是茨农格维人、奇卢拉人和惠尔库特人，彼此讲相近的阿萨巴斯卡方言。直到1837年，胡帕人仍处在西班牙传教站和海上毛皮贸易的势力范围之外，谷地中的生活未受外来定居者打扰。

en: The Hupe, recorded by the Spanish as Jupe or Hoipi and in Comanche as Hʉpenʉʉ, 'Timber People', were the northernmost of the three great Comanche divisions known to the Spanish before the 1750s, alongside the Yamparika and Kotsoteka. The Comanche had once been part of the Shoshone of the Great Basin, breaking away in the early eighteenth century after adopting horse culture and moving onto the plains, and the Hʉpenʉʉ were the last to leave, keeping a dialect close to Eastern Shoshone and many Great Basin customs. They made their homes in the wooded Central Plains between the Platte and Arkansas rivers, which gave them their name. In the 1750s and 1760s other Comanche divisions pushed south into Texas; the Hʉpenʉʉ followed more slowly, and in the 1780s the Spanish counted them, on the North Canadian River, among their Western Comanche. The name Hʉpenʉʉ vanished from the records in the early nineteenth century, when the band is thought to have merged into the Nokoni, Kwahadi and Penateka divisions.
zh: 胡佩人在西班牙文献中记作茹佩或奥伊皮，科曼奇语作赫佩努，意为‘林地人’，是18世纪50年代以前西班牙人所知的科曼奇三大部落群体中最靠北的一支，与扬帕里卡人、科措特卡人并列。科曼奇人本是大盆地肖肖尼人的一部分，18世纪初接受马匹文化后脱离肖肖尼、进入大平原；胡佩人是最后离开的一支，方言接近东肖肖尼语，保留了许多大盆地习俗。他们居住在普拉特河与阿肯色河之间林木较多的中部平原，族名便由此而来。18世纪50至60年代，其他科曼奇群体南下得克萨斯，胡佩人行动较缓；到80年代，西班牙人把已迁至北加拿大河的他们划入西科曼奇。19世纪初，赫佩努之名从文献中消失，一般认为该群体并入了诺科尼、夸哈迪和佩纳特卡等分支。

en: The Hūrga, also written Hurka or Hurha and called Kurka in Chinese records, were Tungusic clans of the Wild, or Haidong, Jurchens, named after the Hurka River, the present-day Mudan River. In the fourteenth century they lived in the forests and river marshes from the middle Sungari and the Mudan valley to the Ussuri and the middle Amur, country the Ming knew only loosely as the land of the Wild Jurchens. They lived mainly by fishing and hunting, dressing in sewn fish skins like their Nanai kinsmen, with pig farming and little settled agriculture, and followed a shamanic religion centred on the bear and the tiger. The Hūrga kept apart from the Ming tribute system longer than the Jianzhou and Haixi Jurchens, and after Nurhaci began unifying the Jurchens his banners marched against them repeatedly from the 1590s; the Hūrga clans of the Amur fought under their own chiefs before submitting to Hong Taiji in 1631. Many captives and submitted clans were moved south and enrolled in the new Manchu banners, while the people who stayed on the rivers became the Nanai, known to the Chinese as the Hezhe or Fish-skin Tartars, together with the Udege and Oroqen.
zh: 虎尔哈又作虎尔喀、库尔喀，是野人女真（即东海女真）中的通古斯诸部，得名于虎尔哈河，即现在的牡丹江。14世纪时，他们活动在从松花江中游、牡丹江流域到乌苏里江和黑龙江中游的森林与河沼地带，明朝只笼统地把这片地方视为野人女真之地。他们主要以渔猎为生，与近亲赫哲人一样穿着缝制的鱼皮衣，兼营养猪，定居农业很少，信奉以熊和虎为核心的萨满教。虎尔哈比建州、海西女真更晚卷入明朝的朝贡体系；努尔哈赤开始统一女真后，八旗兵从16世纪90年代起屡次征讨他们，黑龙江一带的虎尔哈各部在本族首领率领下抵抗，最终于1631年归降皇太极。许多被俘和归附的部众被南迁，编入新建的满洲八旗；留在江河之滨的人则发展为赫哲（汉人又称鱼皮鞑子）、乌德盖和鄂伦春等族。

en: The I-Kiribati are a Micronesian people who inhabit the low coral atolls of the Gilbert Islands, known to them as Tungaru, and speak Gilbertese, a Micronesian Oceanic language with northern and southern dialects. Austronesian seafarers settled the chain over many centuries, and oral traditions remember an earlier dark-skinned population followed by migrants from the west; around 1300 a large movement from Samoa added Polynesian ancestry and new clans. From the fifteenth century the northern atolls were ruled by paramount chiefs while the central and southern islands governed themselves through councils of elders, Tabiteuea remaining proudly egalitarian, and rival clans fought frequent wars over land with shark-tooth blades and coconut-fibre armour. European contact remained sporadic: Commodore John Byron chanced on Nikunau in 1765, and Captains Thomas Gilbert and John Marshall sailed through the chain in 1788, after whom the Russian admiral Adam von Krusenstern named the Gilbert Islands on his maps of 1820. Whalers and traders of the 1820s brought beachcombers and new goods, but no foreign rule, so in 1837 each atoll still ran its own affairs amid the old clan feuds.
zh: 基里巴斯人是居住在低矮珊瑚环礁群吉尔伯特群岛（他们自称通加鲁）的密克罗尼西亚族群，使用大洋洲语密克罗尼西亚语支的吉尔伯特语，分北方、南方两种方言。南岛语航海者历经许多世纪定居这串岛链，口传传统提到早先的深色皮肤居民，以及后来自西方迁入的移民；约1300年，一大批来自萨摩亚的移民又带来波利尼西亚血统和新的氏族。从15世纪起，北部环礁由最高酋长统治，中部和南部岛屿则靠长老议事会自治，塔比特韦亚更是以不分等级的平等社会著称；对立氏族为争夺土地频繁交战，武器是嵌鲨鱼齿的刀矛和椰纤维编的铠甲。欧洲人的接触一直零星：1765年海军准将约翰·拜伦偶然抵达尼库瑙，1788年托马斯·吉尔伯特与约翰·马绍尔两位船长穿过岛链，俄国海军将领亚当·冯·克鲁森施滕在1820年的地图上便以吉尔伯特命名群岛。19世纪20年代起捕鲸船和商人带来流浪汉与新奇货物，却没有外来政权；到1837年，每个环礁仍在旧日的氏族仇杀中自行其是。

en: The Ibaloi are an Igorot people of the southern Cordillera in northern Luzon, whose name means people of the houses, occupying the mountain valleys of southeastern Benguet along the Agno, Bued and Amburayan rivers, with Mount Pulag held sacred as the place where spirits rejoin their ancestors. They belong to the Austronesian world and speak Ibaloi, with its Bokod, Daklan and Kabayan dialects, alongside the Ilocano and Tagalog learned through trade. Ibaloi society was stratified between the wealthy baknang, who controlled the terraced rice fields and gold workings, cowhands, farmhands and bonded slaves, and its districts such as Kabayan became famous for their fire mummies, corpses dried over months with salt water and herbs and placed in cave coffins. The highlands yielded placer and lode gold, which the Ibaloi melted into cakes and carried down to the Pangasinan trade fairs, and community life turned on the cañao feasts with their gongs and sacrifices to ancestral and nature spirits, the anito. The gold of Benguet drew Spanish expeditions from 1572, but fortified villages and the mountain terrain let the Ibaloi and their Igorot kinsmen keep their autonomy through the whole colonial period, accepting missionaries and lowland trade without surrendering their mines or their rituals.
zh: 伊巴洛伊人是吕宋北部科迪勒拉山脉南部的伊哥洛特族群，族名意为“住在房屋里的人”，聚居于本格特省东南部沿阿格诺河、布埃德河和安布拉扬河的高山谷地，并将普拉格山奉为神灵与祖先重聚的圣地。他们属于南岛语系世界，母语是伊巴洛伊语，下分博科德、达克兰和卡巴扬三种方言，同时因贸易而兼通伊洛卡诺语和他加禄语。伊巴洛伊社会等级分明：控制梯田与金坑的富人“巴克南”之下，还有牧牛者、佃农和奴隶；卡巴扬一带更以“火木乃伊”闻名——死者遗体经盐水和草药反复熏制数月后安放在洞穴棺中。高地出产沙金和脉金，伊巴洛伊人把黄金熔成金饼，运到邦阿西楠的集市交易；社群生活围绕“卡尼奥”祭宴展开，宴上鸣锣献祭，敬拜祖先与自然神灵“阿尼托”。本格特的黄金自1572年起引来西班牙远征队，但凭借设防村落和山地地形，伊巴洛伊人与伊哥洛特亲族在整个殖民时期保住了自治：他们接纳传教士和低地贸易，却从未交出金矿，也未放弃自身的仪式。

en: The Iban are a Dayak people of north-western Borneo, spread across Sarawak, Brunei and the upper Kapuas lands of West Kalimantan, speaking a Malayic language and living in long riverside longhouses called rumah panjai. Their name was originally an exonym, a Kayan word hivan meaning wanderer; before the nineteenth century they called themselves after the rivers they settled, such as the Saribas, Skrang and Sebuyau. Iban oral traditions place their first home at Tembawai Tampun Juah in the Sanggau country and trace their leaders to the Ketungau tributary of the Kapuas. From the 1550s, driven by tribal war and the search for fresh rice land, they began crossing into Sarawak, first settling the Batang Lupar around the Undop; over five generations their longhouses pushed along the Lupar, Sadong, Saribas and Layar rivers. Some earlier peoples, such as the Bukitan and Lugat, were absorbed through intermarriage, while clashes with the Ukits, Seru, Miriek and Biliun ended in the near destruction of those groups. By the early 1800s Iban migrants were entering the Rejang basin. Their mobile, warring society was famed for headhunting, bound up with the rites of the war god Sengalang Burong, and for shifting hill-rice cultivation.
zh: 伊班人是婆罗洲西北部的达雅族群，分布于沙捞越、文莱和西加里曼丹的卡普阿斯河上游一带，使用马来语族语言，住在河畔被称为“鲁马班斋”的长屋里。伊班原本是外族对他们的称呼，源自卡扬语“希万”，意为流浪者；在19世纪以前，他们以所居河流自称，如沙里巴人、斯克兰人、士布夭人。伊班口述传统把最早的家园放在上侯地区的淡巴威·淡本朱阿，历代首领则可追溯到卡普阿斯河的克廷高支流。16世纪50年代起，受部落战争和寻找新稻田的驱动，他们开始迁入沙捞越，最先在温多河一带的鲁巴河流域定居；经过五代人，长屋群落沿鲁巴河、沙东河、沙里巴河和拉亚河扩展。布基坦人、卢加特等较早的居民通过通婚被同化，而与乌基特人、塞鲁人、米历克人和比利温人的冲突则几近毁灭了这些族群。到19世纪初，伊班移民已进入拉让江流域。这个流动好战的社会以猎首闻名，猎首与战神森加朗·布龙的仪式紧密相连，同时盛行旱稻轮作。

en: The Ibanag are an Austronesian people of the lower Cagayan River in northeastern Luzon, concentrated in the provinces of Cagayan and Isabela around Tuguegarao, Aparri and Lal-lo; their name combines the prefix i-, meaning people of, with bannag, meaning river, marking them as the river people. Their Ibanag language, closely related to Gaddang and Itawis, was promoted by the Spanish colonial authorities as the lingua franca of the whole northeastern Philippines, as they carried it from Lal-lo, the old city of Nueva Segovia, to Tuguegarao, where an Irraya dialect had previously been spoken. Spanish contact began with Juan de Salcedo's expedition of 1572, and in 1585 Juan Pablo de Carrión, after driving Japanese pirates from the north coast, established the alcaldia of Nueva Segovia at Lal-lo; encomienda grants and forced labor reached Tuguegarao by 1591, the Diocese of Nueva Segovia was decreed in 1595, and Dominican friars opened the first missions. The exactions of tribute and labor drove the headman Magalat to revolt at Tuguegarao in those early years, the first of a long series of Cagayan uprisings. From the seventeenth century onward Ilocano settlers were brought into the valley's tobacco plantations, and their language gradually overtook Ibanag as the common tongue of northern Luzon.
zh: 伊巴纳格人是吕宋东北部卡加延河下游的南岛语系民族，聚居于卡加延省和伊莎贝拉省的土格加劳、阿帕里和拉洛一带；其族名由前缀 i-（……之人）和 bannag（河流）组合而成，意为“河上之人”。他们的伊巴纳格语与加当语、伊塔维斯语亲缘很近，曾被西班牙殖民当局推广为整个菲律宾东北部的通用语：西班牙人把它从旧城新塞哥维亚所在的拉洛带到此前通行伊拉亚方言的土格加劳。西班牙人的接触始于1572年胡安·德·萨尔塞多的远征；1585年，胡安·巴勃罗·德·卡里翁在肃清北海岸的日本海盗后，于拉洛设立新塞哥维亚行政区。到1591年，监护征赋制和徭役已推行至土格加劳，1595年新塞哥维亚教区设立，多明我会修士建起最初的传教站。苛重的贡赋与劳役迫使首领马加拉特在土格加劳起事，这是卡加延一连串起义的开端。17世纪起，伊洛卡诺移民被引入谷地的烟草种植园，伊洛卡诺语逐渐取代伊巴纳格语，成为吕宋北部的通用语言。

en: Icelanders are the North Germanic nation of the North Atlantic island settled from 874, when the Norwegian chieftain Ingólfur Arnarson made his home at Reykjavík. The settlers came mainly from western Norway, bringing Gaelic wives and thralls from Ireland and Scotland, and in 930 their chieftains founded the Alþingi assembly at Þingvellir, the centre of the Icelandic Commonwealth whose settlement and feuds were recorded in Landnámabók and the Icelandic sagas. The island accepted Christianity around the year 1000, and after the Age of the Sturlungs the Old Covenant of 1262 placed it under the Norwegian crown; from 1380 it passed with Norway to the kings of Denmark. As the Little Ice Age shortened the growing seasons, the vistarband bound poor farmers to landowners for a year at a time, while dried cod became the main export, first bought by English and then German merchants. Christian III imposed the Lutheran Reformation, and the execution of the Catholic bishop Jón Arason in 1550 ended resistance; in 1602 the crown confined all Icelandic trade to Danish merchants. Hardship deepened with the Laki eruption of 1783 to 1784, whose poison clouds killed over half the livestock and a fifth of the people in the ensuing famine. A Danish adventurer, Jørgen Jørgensen, briefly ruled a self-declared Icelandic republic in 1809, and when the Treaty of Kiel separated Norway from Denmark in 1814, Iceland remained a Danish dependency. Their Icelandic tongue is a North Germanic language descended from the Old Norse of the sagas.
zh: 冰岛人是北大西洋岛屿上的北日耳曼民族。874年，挪威首领英戈尔夫·阿纳松在雷克雅未克安家，开启了岛上的定居时代。移民主要来自挪威西部，还带来了爱尔兰和苏格兰的盖尔裔妻子与奴隶。930年，各路首领在辛格韦德利创立全体大会阿尔庭，这是冰岛自由邦的核心；《定居书》和冰岛萨迦记下了拓殖经过与家族仇杀。约1000年，冰岛接受基督教；斯图龙时代的内乱之后，1262年的《旧约》使冰岛归属于挪威国王，1380年起又随挪威转归丹麦国王。小冰期令生长季缩短，“年度依附”制把贫苦农民逐年束缚在地主土地上，鳕鱼干则成为主要出口货，先由英格兰商人、后由德意志商人收购。克里斯蒂安三世强制推行路德宗改革，1550年天主教主教约恩·阿拉松被处决，抵抗告终；1602年王室又把冰岛的全部贸易限定给丹麦商人。1783至1784年拉基火山喷发，毒云毁掉一半以上牲畜，随之而来的饥荒夺去五分之一人口，苦难进一步加深。1809年，丹麦冒险家约恩·约恩森曾短暂统治一个自行宣布的冰岛共和国；1814年《基尔条约》把挪威与丹麦分开时，冰岛仍是丹麦的属地。冰岛人的语言冰岛语是由萨迦时代的古诺斯语演化而来的北日耳曼语言。

en: The Idoma are a Volta-Niger people of the country south of the Benue River, east of its confluence with the Niger in what is now central Nigeria, speaking Idomoid tongues related to those of the Igala and Alago. They never formed a single kingdom: their twenty-odd communities, each governed by a council of elders and a sacred chief called the Oche, were settled by migrants of several origins, some coming from Igala Idah and others from the Igbo marches. Many clans remember an older homeland named Apa, part of the Jukun-led Kwararafa confederacy, from which they fled northern pressure around 1700. Renowned as hunters and warriors, Idoma blacksmiths purified fighters after a killing with the ritual washing of the ogwu, while villagers smelted iron, waved cloth and carved masks for local markets. Their religion honors the high god Owoicho through the Alekwu ancestral spirits and the earth cult Aje, with the annual Alekwu festival drawing the ancestors back among the living.
zh: 伊多马人是讲沃尔特-尼日尔语的民族，居住在今尼日利亚中部、尼日尔河汇流处以东的贝努埃河以南地区，其伊多马伊德诸语与伊加拉语、阿拉戈语相近。他们从未形成统一王国：二十多个社群各自由长老议事会和称为“奥切”的神圣酋长治理，居民来源多元，有的来自伊加拉的伊达，有的来自伊博边缘地带。许多氏族还记得一个叫阿帕的故地，它是朱昆人主导的夸拉拉法联盟的一部分；约1700年，为躲避北方压力，他们从那里迁出。伊多马人以猎手和战士著称，铁匠会用“洗去奥古”的仪式净化杀过人的战士，村民还从事冶铁、织布和面具雕刻，在本地集市交易。他们的信仰通过“阿莱库”祖灵和地神“阿杰”敬奉至高神奥沃伊乔，每年的阿莱库节迎接祖灵重返生者中间。

en: The Ifugao are an Austronesian mountain people of the Cordillera range in northern Luzon, divided into the Ayangan, Kalanguya and Tuwali subgroups and speaking a cluster of Ifugao dialects. Their origins are debated, with theories tracing them to the Lingayen coast, the Magat valley or the western Cordillera. As Spain conquered the Magat lowlands, the Ifugao withdrew deeper into the mountains between 1600 and 1700 and, giving up taro for wet rice, carved their famous irrigated terraces into the hillsides as a deliberately strengthened economy; Spanish troops first entered Kiangan in the 1750s and described the terraces in 1801, but never subdued the highlands. Ifugao society rested on kinship and councils of elders, with animist baki rites led by mumbaki priests, mythology of the skyworld Kabunyan, tattoos recording headhunting exploits, the chanted hudhud epics and carved wooden bulul figures that guarded the rice granaries as ancestral spirits.
zh: 伊富高人是北吕宋科迪勒拉山区的南岛语系族群，分为阿扬甘、卡兰圭亚和图瓦利等支系，使用一组伊富高方言。关于其起源说法不一，有林加延海岸、马加特河谷和西科迪勒拉等几种推测。西班牙征服马加特低地后，伊富高人在1600年至1700年间向大山深处退却，放弃芋头改种水稻，在山坡上开凿出著名的灌溉梯田，以此强化自身经济；西班牙军队18世纪50年代才首次进入基安甘，1801年留下了关于梯田的记载，却始终未能征服这片高地。伊富高社会以血缘关系和长老议事为基础，由蒙巴基祭司主持万物有灵的巴奇仪式，流传着天界卡布尼安的神话、记录猎头战功的纹身、吟唱的《胡德霍德》史诗，以及守护粮仓、代表祖灵的木雕布鲁尔像。

en: The Igala are a Volta-Niger people of the Niger-Benue confluence in central Nigeria, with their capital and ancestral home at Idah on the Niger. Their kingdom took shape in the sixteenth century under Abutu-Eje, and the Aji-Ata dynasty is listed from 1507; its rulers bore the title Atta, the first of whom, Ebulejonu, was a woman. Sitting between the forest and the savanna and between the great river highways of the Niger and Benue, Igalaland drew influence from the Yoruba, Edo, Igbo and Jukun, and its people combined farming and hunting with river trade. Early in the sixteenth century the Igala invaded Benin but were defeated by Oba Esigie, after which Benin influence, including brass mask styles, reached the Atta's court; later Atta Ayegba won a war against the Jukun. Igala religion centers on the high god Ojo, the ancestral spirits called Ibegwu and Ifa-style divination, while its masquerade traditions echo those of its Idoma and Edo neighbors.
zh: 伊加拉人是尼日利亚中部尼日尔河与贝努埃河汇流处的沃尔特-尼日尔语民族，其都城和祖居地是尼日尔河畔的伊达。他们的王国在16世纪由阿卜图-埃杰奠定，阿吉-阿塔王朝的王统自1507年起有明确世系；君主称“阿塔”，而首任阿塔埃布勒乔努是一位女性。伊加拉地处森林与稀树草原之间，又扼守尼日尔河、贝努埃河两大水运通道，因而受到约鲁巴、埃多、伊博和朱昆诸族影响，居民兼营农耕、狩猎与河上贸易。16世纪初，伊加拉入侵贝宁，被奥巴·埃西吉击败，此后贝宁的影响（包括黄铜面具风格）传入阿塔宫廷；后来的阿塔·阿耶格巴又在对朱昆人的战争中取胜。伊加拉信仰以至高神奥乔、称为“伊贝古”的祖灵和伊法式占卜为核心，其假面传统则与相邻的伊多马和埃多文化相通。

en: The Igbo occupy the thickly forested country east of the lower Niger, one of the most densely settled regions of West Africa. Iron working there reaches back to the first millennium BCE, and the ninth- and tenth-century graves of Igbo-Ukwu held refined bronze and copper regalia. Unlike their imperial neighbors, most Igbo communities lived in decentralized village republics, ordered by lineage elders, title societies such as the Ozo and assemblies rather than kings. The great exception was the Kingdom of Nri, a ritual state whose founder Eri is said to have settled around 948 and whose first priest-king, the Eze Nri, took office in 1043, wielding religious authority across Igboland, enforcing taboos and granting sanctuary. From about 1640 the Aro Confederacy, based at Arochukwu and built around the Ibini Ukpabi oracle, spread a trading network through the hinterland, feeding slaves and later palm oil to the Niger Delta ports of Bonny and Calabar for the Atlantic trade. Igbo religion honors the high god Chukwu through the alusi spirits and the earth goddess Ala, with the New Yam festival marking the farming year; captives shipped through the Bight of Biafra carried these traditions to the Americas.
zh: 伊博人居住在尼日尔河下游以东的茂密森林地带，那里是西非人口最稠密的地区之一。当地冶铁可追溯到公元前一千纪，伊博-乌库遗址9至10世纪的墓葬中出土了精美的青铜和铜制礼器。与邻近的帝国不同，多数伊博社群实行分散的村社自治，由宗族长老、奥佐等头衔组织和村民议事会管理，而不设国王。最大的例外是恩里王国这个祭祀型国家：传说其始祖埃里约在948年定居于此，首任祭司国王“埃泽·恩里”于1043年即位，在整个伊博地区行使宗教权威，维护禁忌并提供庇护。1640年前后，以阿罗丘库为中心、围绕伊比尼·乌克帕比神谕建立的阿罗联盟在腹地铺开贸易网络，把奴隶以及后来的棕榈油输送到尼日尔三角洲的邦尼和卡拉巴尔等港口，参与大西洋贸易。伊博传统信仰通过阿卢西众神和地神阿拉敬奉至高神丘库，并用新山药节庆贺农年；经比夫拉湾被运走的俘虏把这些传统带到了美洲。

en: The Igneri were Arawakan-speaking farmers and potters who occupied the southern Lesser Antilles before the rise of the Island Caribs. Their ancestors had begun as an Arawak culture on the middle Orinoco in Venezuela around 1500 BC, drifted to the eastern coast in the barrancoid migration, and then crossed by canoe into the islands, reaching Dominica by about AD 400 and St. Croix by 650. They brought horticulture and fine ceramics with them, lived in family clans, and grew cassava for casabe bread on slash-and-burn fields while supplementing their diet by fishing, hunting and gathering shellfish; on Puerto Rico their ceremonial centre at Tibes preserves their ball courts. Archaeologists link them to the Suazoid culture, which flourished from about 1000 until roughly 1450. Later legend remembered the Igneri as the peaceful original islanders whom the warlike Kalinago conquered and replaced, but twentieth-century linguistics and archaeology told a subtler story: the Kalinago in fact spoke the Igneri Arawakan tongue, suggesting the islanders were absorbed through intermarriage and a change of identity rather than destroyed, their language living on as Island Carib.
zh: 伊涅里人是说阿拉瓦克语的农耕制陶族群，在岛屿加勒比人崛起之前居住在小安的列斯群岛南部。其先民约在公元前1500年兴起于委内瑞拉的奥里诺科河中游，属阿拉瓦克文化，后沿“巴兰科伊德迁徙”移到东部海岸，再乘独木舟进入群岛：约公元400年抵达多米尼加岛，650年前后到达圣克罗伊。他们把园艺农业和精致制陶术带到岛上，以氏族为单位生活，用刀耕火种的田地种植木薯、制作卡萨贝饼，辅以渔猎和采贝；波多黎各的蒂韦斯仪式中心还保留着他们修建的球场。考古学者把他们与约1000年至1450年间兴盛的苏阿佐伊德文化联系起来。后世传说把伊涅里人描绘成爱好和平的原住岛民，被尚武的卡利纳戈人征服取代，但20世纪的语言学和考古学给出了更细腻的解释：卡利纳戈人其实讲的就是伊涅里人的阿拉瓦克语，这说明岛民是通过通婚和身份转换被融合，而非被消灭，他们的语言也作为岛屿加勒比语延续了下来。

en: The Ijaw, who call themselves Izon, are the people of the Niger Delta, spread through its mangrove creeks and coastal towns from the Benin river to Bonny, and speaking a cluster of Ijoid languages. They live by fishing, salt-making and the river and coastal trade, their settlements built on stilts and sandbanks among the waterways. While many western clans remained decentralized village communities influenced by the nearby Kingdom of Benin, the eastern clans of Bonny, Kalabari, Nembe, Brass and Okrika developed powerful kingships and stratified canoe-house societies. From the 1400s Portuguese ships opened direct trade with these delta towns, and Bonny grew into one of the principal slave entrepots of the Bight of Biafra, its war canoes carrying cannon and crews of more than a hundred men; after the British abolition of the slave trade in 1807 the same ports exported palm oil and ivory instead. Ijaw religion is built on ancestor veneration and the water spirits called Owuamapu, honored each year with drumming and masked dances, alongside Egbesu, the leopard-totem god of justice and war.
zh: 伊乔人自称伊宗，是尼日尔三角洲的居民，散布在从贝宁河到邦尼的红树林水道和沿海城镇中，使用一组伊乔伊德语。他们以捕鱼、制盐和河海贸易为生，村落建在水道间的木桩和沙洲上。西部许多氏族仍是受邻近贝宁王国影响的分散村社，而邦尼、卡拉巴里、内姆贝、布拉斯和奥克里卡等东部氏族则发展出强有力的王权和等级分明的“独木舟家族”社会。15世纪起，葡萄牙商船与这些三角洲城镇直接通商，邦尼成长为比夫拉湾主要的奴隶贸易集散地之一，其战船上装有火炮，每艘可载百余人；1807年英国废除奴隶贸易后，这些港口转而出口棕榈油和象牙。伊乔传统信仰以祖先崇拜和称为“奥武阿马普”的水神为核心，每年以鼓乐和假面舞蹈祭祀水神，同时尊奉以豹为图腾、司掌正义与战争的埃格贝苏神。

en: The Ikogmiut, who call themselves the Kuigpagmiut, are the Central Alaskan Yup'ik people of the lower Yukon River. Their name means the people of Kuigpak, the big river, as the Yukon is known in Yup'ik, and their villages stood on the river's lower reaches and the channels of its delta. River fishing, above all for salmon, together with seasonal sea-mammal hunting on the nearby Bering Sea coast, was the basis of life in their riverside sod-house villages. In 1834 Andrei Glazunov led the first Russian expedition up the Yukon, opening the river to the Russian-American Company's fur trade and bringing the Ikogmiut their first direct contact with Europeans.
zh: 伊科格缪特人自称奎格帕格缪特，是育空河下游的中阿拉斯加尤皮克人。其名意为奎格帕克（尤皮克语意为大河，即育空河）的居民，村庄分布在育空河下游及三角洲的河道两旁。河中捕鱼、尤其是捕捞鲑鱼，加上季节性地到附近白令海岸捕猎海洋哺乳动物，是他们河岸草皮屋村庄的生计之本。1834年，安德烈·格拉祖诺夫率领第一支俄国探险队溯育空河而上，为俄美公司打开了这条河上的毛皮贸易，也让伊科格缪特人第一次直接接触到欧洲人。

en: The Ikoot, better known to outsiders as the Huave, call themselves Ikoots, meaning “us”, and are also called the Mareños, or sea people, by their Spanish-speaking neighbours. They have occupied the Pacific sandspits and lagoons of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Oaxaca for more than three thousand years, making them older in the region than the Zapotecs. Their villages, above all San Mateo del Mar, live from fishing and salt-making, trading fish and other marine products with the inland towns. Their language, called ombeayiüts or “our language”, is generally treated as an isolate with no proven relatives. In the Post-Classic period the expanding Zapotec kingdom of Zaachila, ruling from the fortress of Guiengola, confined the Ikoot to narrow coastal strips while seizing the isthmus salt pans and the trade road toward Soconusco; in the early sixteenth century Ikoot settlements still stretched along the coast as far as Tonalá in Chiapas. When the Spanish reached the isthmus in 1523, the Zapotec ruler of Tehuantepec submitted to the crown, and the Ikoot villages passed under colonial rule along with the rest of the coast.
zh: 伊科奥特人对外更常见的称呼是瓦维人，自称“伊科奥茨”，意为“我们”，说西班牙语的邻族也称他们为“海民”。他们在瓦哈卡特万特佩克地峡的太平洋沙嘴和潟湖地带已居住三千多年，比萨波特克人更早来到这一地区。他们的村庄以滨海圣马特奥最为著名，靠捕鱼和制盐为生，用渔获和海产与内陆城镇交易。他们的语言称“翁贝阿尤茨”，意为“我们的话”，学界一般将其视为没有确定亲属语言的孤立语言。后古典时期，以吉恩戈拉要塞为中心扩张的萨波特克萨奇拉王国把伊科奥特人压缩到狭窄的沿海地带，夺走了地峡的盐田和通往索科努斯科的商路；直到16世纪初，伊科奥特人的聚落仍沿海岸延伸到恰帕斯的托纳拉。1523年西班牙人抵达地峡，特万特佩克的萨波特克统治者向西班牙王室称臣，伊科奥特人的村庄也随整个沿海地区一起落入殖民统治之下。

en: The Ikpeng, also known to outsiders as the Txikão or Txicão, are a Cariban-speaking people of Mato Grosso. Their own oral history places their ancestral lands as far as the Jari River, and in early historical times they lived by the Iriri River in firm alliance with the Txipaya, before settling the converging rivers of the Teles Pires and Juruena basin, the country they already occupied in the fourteenth century. They were repeatedly at war with neighboring peoples, and pressure from raiding and Portuguese frontier expansion from the 1700s onward drove them across the Formosa Mountains into the Upper Xingu basin. Hunters, fishers and gatherers who also keep gardens of maize, manioc, cotton, gourds and urucu annatto, they lived in autonomous villages and remained beyond the reach of the colonial frontier through the whole Portuguese period.
zh: 伊克彭人（外界称特希康人）是马托格罗索的加勒比语族群，所说的伊克彭语属加勒比语系。他们的口传历史把祖地追溯到雅里河一带；在早期记载的年代，他们住在伊里里河畔，与特希帕亚人结有稳固的战时同盟，后来迁居特利斯皮里斯河与茹鲁埃纳河交汇的流域，也就是14世纪时他们所在的地方。他们与周边族群屡有战事，从18世纪起，劫掠和葡萄牙殖民边疆扩张的压力迫使他们翻越福莫萨山脉，进入上欣古盆地。伊克彭人狩猎、捕鱼、采集，也种植玉米、木薯、棉花、葫芦和胭脂树，以自治村落为单位生活，在整个葡萄牙殖民时期始终游离于殖民势力之外。

en: The Ilili, better known as the Moose Cree or West Main Cree, take their self-name Ililiw from the Algonquian word for a human being. They occupy the south-western shore of James Bay in present-day Ontario, around the Moose, Albany and Attawapiskat rivers and the islands of the bay, and speak the l-dialect of the Cree language, which together with Eastern Swampy Cree forms the Central Cree grouping. French Jesuits first recorded them in the Jesuit Relations of 1671, meeting their bands along James Bay and the Moose River, and the Hudson's Bay Company quickly followed: Charles Bayly founded Moose Factory in 1672 and 1673, the company's second post and the first English settlement in what is now Ontario, while Fort Albany was built between 1675 and 1679. Drawn into the fur trade as trappers, canoe men and middlemen, their war bands ranged far inland, appearing on the Ochagach map of about 1728 as the Monsonnis around Rainy Lake, and in 1732 two hundred Cree warriors gathered near Fort Frances for a campaign against the Dakota.
zh: 伊利利人更常见的名称是穆斯克里人或西主干克里人，自称“伊利利乌”，词源是阿尔冈昆语里“人”的词。他们住在今安大略境内詹姆斯湾西南岸，活动于穆斯河、奥尔巴尼河、阿塔瓦皮斯卡特河一带及湾内各岛，操克里语的l方言，与东沼泽克里人共同构成中部克里群体。法国耶稣会士在1671年的《耶稣会报道》中首次记录他们，在詹姆斯湾和穆斯河畔见到其群队；哈德逊湾公司随即跟进：查尔斯·贝利于1672至1673年建立穆斯工厂，这是公司的第二座商站，也是今安大略境内最早的英国人定居点，奥尔巴尼堡则建于1675至1679年间。他们以诱捕者、独木舟手和中间商身份卷入毛皮贸易，战队深入内陆，在约1728年的奥查加奇地图上以“蒙索尼”之名出现在雷尼湖一带；1732年，两百名克里战士在弗朗西斯堡附近集结，准备进攻达科他人。

en: The Sinigir were the northernmost of these Evenki bands, roaming the Ilimpeya basin beyond the Arctic Circle, where winter cold can fall to minus sixty degrees. Scholars call their descendants the Ilimpii Evenki, reindeer herders drawn into the Russian fur-tribute network during the seventeenth century.
zh: 锡尼格尔人是这些鄂温克游群中最靠北的一支，在北极圈以北的伊利姆佩亚河流域游牧，冬季气温可降至零下六十度。学界把他们的后裔称为伊利姆皮耶鄂温克人，这批驯鹿牧民在17世纪被卷入俄国的毛皮贡赋网络。

en: The Ilnu, or Ilnuatsh, are the western branch of the Innu, the Montagnais bands of the Saguenay River, Lac Saint-Jean and the western north shore of the St. Lawrence, recorded in the seventeenth century under band names such as Bersimis, Chicoutimi, Escoumains, Godbout and Tadoussac. Like the eastern Innu they were nomadic caribou hunters speaking Innu-aimun, here in its Southern Montagnais dialect, and the French encountered these southern bands earlier than any other Innu group: Tadoussac became the first great meeting place of the northern fur trade. In 1603 their leaders made the alliance with Champlain that drew them into the French wars against the Haudenosaunee, and for the rest of the seventeenth century Haudenosaunee war parties struck up the Saguenay into their hunting grounds. The Ilnu entered the French peace settlement alongside the other allied nations by signing the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701, and kept to their hunting grounds around present-day Pessamit and Mashteuiatsh.
zh: 伊尔努人（复数作伊尔努阿什）是因努人的西支，即活动在萨格奈河、圣让湖和圣劳伦斯河北岸西部的蒙塔涅诸部，17世纪的文献按部落名称他们为贝尔西米、希库蒂米、埃斯库曼、古德布和塔杜萨克等。与东部因努人一样，他们是游动的驯鹿猎人，讲因努艾蒙语的南蒙塔涅方言；法国人接触这些南部部落比接触任何其他因努群体都早，塔杜萨克由此成为北方毛皮贸易最早的大型集散地。1603年，他们的首领与萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰结盟，从此被卷入法国对易洛魁联盟的战争；整个17世纪，易洛魁战队沿萨格奈河深入，袭击他们的猎场。1701年，伊尔努人与其他同盟部族一同签署《蒙特利尔大和平》，加入法国人的和平安排，此后仍留在今天佩萨米和马什特维阿奇一带的猎场中。

en: The Ilocano are an Austronesian people of the narrow northwestern coast of Luzon, where their ancestors settled in the coastal coves between the Cordillera mountains and the sea; their autonym was Samtoy, meaning our language here, while the name Ilocano comes from i-, meaning from, and luék, meaning bay, the people from along the bay. Before the Spaniards they lived by farming, fishing and trade with Chinese and Japanese merchants and with the Cordilleran peoples of the highlands, worshipping anito spirits under gods such as the creator Parsua, the earth god Buni and the heaven lord Apo Langit. In June 1572 Juan de Salcedo sailed north with eighty men, subdued the string of settlements from Tagudin to Vigan and founded Villa Fernandina de Vigan, from which Augustinian friars carried out conversion; by 1574 Vigan was the Spanish center of the whole Ilocos coast. Colonial rule provoked repeated revolts: the Ilocos was invaded in 1660 during the Malong uprising, Pedro Almazan proclaimed himself King of Ilocos in 1661, and in 1762 Diego Silang seized Vigan and declared Free Ilocos, a revolt carried on after his assassination in 1763 by his wife Gabriela, who was captured and hanged that September. In 1807 the wine-makers of Piddig rose in the Basi Revolt against the Spanish monopoly on their sugarcane basi wine, and by the 1790s the Ilocano language was already spoken along the entire coast from Bangui to Agoo, from which Ilocano migrants later carried it across northern Luzon.
zh: 伊洛卡诺人是吕宋岛西北狭长河岸的南岛语系民族，先民定居在科迪勒拉山脉与大海之间的海湾地带；他们的自称是“萨姆托伊”，意为“我们这里的语言”，而伊洛卡诺之名来自前缀 i-（来自）和 luék（海湾），即“海湾沿岸之人”。西班牙人到来之前，他们务农、捕鱼，与中国和日本商人以及高地的科迪勒拉人贸易，信奉阿尼托精灵，崇奉造物主帕尔苏阿、地神布尼和天神阿波·兰吉等神祇。1572年6月，胡安·德·萨尔塞多率八十人北上，征服了从塔古丁到维甘的一连串聚落，建立费尔南迪纳·德·维甘城，奥斯定会修士由此展开传教；到1574年，维甘已成为整个伊洛卡诺海岸的西班牙统治中心。殖民统治激起多次起义：1660年马隆起义的战火波及伊洛卡诺，1661年佩德罗·阿尔马赞自称伊洛卡诺国王；1762年，迭戈·西朗夺取维甘，宣布建立“自由伊洛卡诺”，他在1763年遇刺后，妻子加布里埃拉·西朗继续领导起义，于同年9月被俘并处以绞刑。1807年，皮迪格的酿酒者发动巴西起义，反抗西班牙对甘蔗酒“巴西”的专卖；到18世纪90年代，伊洛卡诺语已通行于从邦吉到阿戈的整个海岸，伊洛卡诺移民后来又把它带到吕宋北部各地。

en: The Indé are the Western Apache, who call themselves Ndee or Indé, the people, in their Southern Athabaskan language. Their home is the broken mountain and plateau country of east-central Arizona, running south into Sonora and Chihuahua, where anthropologists distinguish the White Mountain, Cibecue, San Carlos and Tonto divisions, each with its own dialect and clusters of local bands; the Tonto groups lived and intermarried closely with the neighboring Yavapai. The Western Apache are linguistic kin of the Navajo, from whom they separated several centuries ago, and like other Apacheans they descend from the great Athabaskan migration out of the Canadian north. Along streams such as the White and Gila rivers they raised corn, beans and squash in irrigated fields, while hunting and gathering wild plants across the surrounding ranges. Their lands formed the western heart of the country the Spanish called Apacheria; from the 1690s their raiding parties reached into Sonora, and through the eighteenth century they fought, traded and made temporary peace with the presidios and settlements of the Spanish northern frontier.
zh: 因德人即西阿帕奇人，在他们的南阿萨巴斯卡语中自称 Ndee 或 Indé，意为“人”。他们的家园是今亚利桑那州中东部崎岖的山地与高原，并向南延伸到索诺拉和奇瓦瓦；人类学家将其分为白山、锡贝丘、圣卡洛斯和通托几个支系，各有自己的方言和若干地方群体，其中通托群体与邻近的亚瓦派人混居通婚。西阿帕奇人在语言上与纳瓦霍人同源，二者在数百年前分化；和其他阿帕奇语族群一样，他们也是从加拿大北部南迁的阿萨巴斯卡大移民的后裔。他们在怀特河、希拉河等河畔的灌溉田里种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，同时在周围山地狩猎并采集野生植物。他们的土地构成西班牙人所称“阿帕切里亚”的西部核心；17世纪末起，他们的劫掠队伍已深入索诺拉，整个18世纪，他们与西班牙北部边疆的要塞和定居点反复交战、贸易，也达成过一次次短暂的和平。

en: The Inga or Ingano are the northernmost of the Quechua-speaking peoples, settled in the mountains and foothills of southwestern Colombia, chiefly the Sibundoy valley in Putumayo and northern Nariño, with communities reaching across the borders into Ecuador and Peru. Their tradition and language point to an Inca origin: in 1492 the Inca Huayna Cápac conquered the Kamëntsá people of the Sibundoy valley and planted a Quechua-speaking colony there, whose descendants became the Inga. The Spaniards reached the valley in 1534, yet Quechua long remained an administrative tongue under the Viceroyalty of Peru, and the Inga kept their own dialect, Inga Kichwa, which a briefly established Jesuit mission later carried to neighboring groups.
zh: 因加诺人又称因加人，是讲克丘亚语的族群中分布最北的一支，居住在哥伦比亚西南部的山地和丘陵，以普图马约省的锡本多伊谷地和纳里尼奥北部为主，也有村社延伸到厄瓜多尔和秘鲁境内。他们的传统和语言都指向印加渊源：1492年，印加王瓦伊纳·卡帕克征服锡本多伊谷地的卡门茨人，在当地安置了一个讲克丘亚语的殖民村社，其后裔便是因加诺人。西班牙人于1534年进入该谷地，但克丘亚语在秘鲁总督区长期作为行政语言使用，因加诺人也保住了自己的方言因加-克丘亚语；后来一处短期设立的耶稣会传教站又把这种语言带到邻近族群中。

en: The Dex Xit'an, or Deg Xit'an, are an Athabaskan people of western Alaska, settled along the lower Yukon and the Anvik and Innoko rivers in villages such as Anvik, Shageluk and Holy Cross. Their autonym means local people and their language is Deg Xinag; the older name Ingalik, given them by their Yup'ik neighbours, is regarded as offensive. Yup'ik, Holikachuk and Dena'ina peoples border their country. They travelled the rivers in birchbark canoes in summer and by dog sled in winter, cooking in clay pots, wearing parkas and boots sewn from beaver or fish skin, with women marking their chins with two blue lines. Animist belief ordered a life built on river fishing and hunting. Russian America reached them late: in 1830 the navigator Ivan Vasiliev explored the Kuskokwim country for the Russian-American Company, and in 1835 the creole Andrei Glazanov crossed from the Yukon toward the Kuskokwim and left the first written notes on the Anvik River people.
zh: 因加利克人自称德格西坦人，是阿拉斯加西部的阿萨巴斯卡族群，聚居于育空河下游以及安维克河、伊诺科河沿岸的安维克、沙格勒克和霍利克罗斯等村落。其自称意为“本地人”，母语为德格西纳格语；因加利克是邻近尤皮克人给他们的旧称，词义带有贬义。他们的四邻是尤皮克人、霍利卡楚克人和德纳伊纳人。夏季他们乘桦皮舟往来河上，冬季驾狗拉雪橇出行，用陶罐烹煮食物，穿河狸皮或鱼皮缝制的派克大衣与靴子，女子下颌纹有两道蓝线。万物有灵信仰规范着他们以河渔和狩猎为本的生活。俄属美洲的势力很晚才到达这里：1830年，领航员伊万·瓦西里耶夫受俄美公司之命勘察库斯科奎姆河流域；1835年，克里奥尔人安德烈·格拉祖诺夫从育空河横穿至库斯科奎姆河，留下了关于安维克河居民最早的文字记录。

en: The Ingrians are the Baltic Finnic people of Ingria, the country round the Neva, the south-eastern corner of the Gulf of Finland and the south-western shore of Lake Ladoga. In the fourteenth century this meant chiefly the Izhorians, who had moved south-west from Karelia around the year 1000 and spoke the Finnic tongue later called Ingrian, together with their neighbours the Votians. Western Ingria was absorbed by the Novgorod Republic in the twelfth century, and its Finnic population adopted Eastern Orthodoxy while Novgorod and Sweden fought repeated wars across its rivers and fortresses, among them Koporye and Yama; when Moscow annexed Novgorod in 1478, some Izhorians were deported into the Russian interior. The Treaty of Stolbovo in 1617 gave Ingria to Sweden, and as Orthodox families fled east, Lutheran settlers from the Karelian Isthmus and Savonia, the Äyrämöiset and Savakot, took their place and formed a Finnish-speaking majority by the 1670s, known afterwards as the Ingrian Finns. Russia reconquered the country in 1703 and founded Saint Petersburg on the Neva, and the Treaty of Nystad in 1721 confirmed its new rulers, under whom the Ingrian Finns became serfs while keeping their Lutheran church.
zh: 英格里亚人是英格里亚地区的波罗的芬兰人，其地环涅瓦河、芬兰湾东南角和拉多加湖西南岸而居。14世纪时这里的主体是约1000年前后从卡累利阿西南迁来的伊若拉人，使用后来被称为伊若拉语的芬兰语支语言，邻近还有亲缘相近的瓦佳人。12世纪西英格里亚被诺夫哥罗德共和国吞并，当地芬兰语居民皈依东正教，诺夫哥罗德与瑞典的连番战争反复掠过科波里耶、亚姆等要塞；1478年莫斯科兼并诺夫哥罗德后，部分伊若拉人被强行迁往俄国内地。1617年《斯托尔博沃和约》把英格里亚割让给瑞典，东正教家庭纷纷东逃，来自卡累利阿地峡和萨沃尼亚的路德宗定居者艾雷迈塞人和萨瓦科特人填补空地，到17世纪70年代形成讲芬兰语的多数，即后来的英格里芬兰人。1703年俄国重新征服此地，在涅瓦河畔建立圣彼得堡，1721年《尼斯塔德和约》确认了俄国的统治，英格里芬兰人在其治下沦为农奴，但保留了路德宗教会。

en: The Inka are a Quechua-speaking people of the Peruvian highlands whose capital and sacred city was Cusco, in the valley of the Huatanay. According to their own tradition, Manco Cápac led ten ayllu clans out of Pacaritambo early in the thirteenth century to found Cusco, driving out the Huallas and other earlier peoples; his successors of the Hurin and then Hanan Cusco dynasties ruled a small city-state through repeated wars with the Ayarmaca and the Chanka. In 1337 the Inka were still only one local power among many in the Andes. The great turning point came in 1438, when the Chanka besieged Cusco and the prince Cusi Yupanqui routed them, took power as Pachacuti, and built the city-state into Tawantinsuyu, the Realm of the Four Parts, which within a century stretched from Quito to central Chile, governed through the mit'a labour system, the Qhapaq Ñan road network and quipu knotted records under the Sapa Inca, son of the sun god Inti. Francisco Pizarro's Spaniards captured the Sapa Inca Atahualpa in 1532 and executed him in 1533; Manco Inca's Neo-Inca state held out at Vilcabamba until 1572, when Túpac Amaru was captured and killed. In 1780 the kuraka José Gabriel Condorcanqui took the name Túpac Amaru II and led the great Quechua and Aymara revolt against the viceroyalty, the last major Inka revival before 1837.
zh: 印卡人是秘鲁高原上讲克丘亚语的民族，以瓦塔奈河谷中的库斯科为都城和圣城。按其自身传说，13世纪初曼科·卡帕克率领十个艾柳氏族从帕卡里坦博出发建立库斯科，逐走瓦利亚等先住民族；其后的下库斯科与上库斯科两朝君主，在同阿亚尔马卡人、昌卡人的反复战争中统治着这个小城邦。1337年时，印卡还只是安第斯众多地方势力之一。重大转折发生在1438年：昌卡人围攻库斯科，王子库西·尤潘基将其击溃，随后以帕查库特克之名掌权，把城邦扩张为塔万廷苏尤，即“四域之国”；不到一个世纪，其疆域自基多延伸至智利中部，萨帕·印卡作为太阳神因蒂之子，靠米塔劳役制、卡帕克·尼安道路网和奇普结绳记事治理国家。1532年皮萨罗率领的西班牙人俘获萨帕·印卡阿塔瓦尔帕，并于1533年将他处死；曼科·印卡的新印卡政权据守比尔卡班巴，直到1572年图帕克·阿马鲁被俘遇害。1780年，酋长何塞·加夫列尔·孔多尔坎基取名图帕克·阿马鲁二世，领导了反对总督辖区的克丘亚与艾马拉大起义，这是1837年之前最后一次大规模的印卡复兴运动。

en: The Innini are the Eastern Swampy Cree, who call themselves Omaškêkowak, the people of the muskeg, and whose individual self-name ininîw means a human being. They hold the low, boggy western coasts of James Bay and Hudson Bay in present-day Ontario, from the Albany River to the Winisk and Severn rivers, and speak the eastern dialect of Swampy Cree, an n-dialect within the Algonquian Cree continuum. Their first European encounter came early, when Henry Hudson sailed into James Bay in 1610 and 1611, and after the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Albany between 1675 and 1679 the coastal bands became known to traders as Homeguard Cree: hunters and provisioners who unloaded the company's ships, supplied goose and caribou meat and manned the posts in winter. Organized in mobile lodges and bands, they took geese in spring, fished and hunted moose and caribou inland, moving between shore and interior with the seasons while acting as intermediaries between the bay forts and more distant peoples.
zh: 因尼尼人即东沼泽克里人，自称“奥马什科戈瓦克”，意为沼泽之地的人，其个人自称“伊尼尼乌”意为“人”。他们占据今安大略境内詹姆斯湾和哈得孙湾低洼多沼泽的西岸，范围从奥尔巴尼河到威尼斯克河和塞文河，操沼泽克里语的东部方言，属于阿尔冈昆语族克里方言连续体中的n方言。他们最早接触欧洲人甚早：亨利·哈得孙于1610至1611年驶入詹姆斯湾；哈德逊湾公司在1675至1679年间建起奥尔巴尼堡后，沿岸群队被商人称为“主队”克里人，负责为公司船只卸货、供应雁和驯鹿肉，并在冬天驻守商站。他们以流动的住户和群队为单位，春天猎雁，在内陆捕鱼并猎取驼鹿和驯鹿，随季节在海岸与内陆之间往返，同时充当海湾堡垒与更远民族之间的中间人。

en: The Innu, called Montagnais by the French, are the Algonquian hunter-gatherers of Nitassinan, their vast homeland on the north shore of the St. Lawrence and the Labrador peninsula. For thousands of years they lived by seasonal caribou and moose hunts, moving with skin tents between the coast and the inland forest, and their language, Innu-aimun, belongs to the Cree–Montagnais–Naskapi continuum; the southern forest bands such as those of Seven Islands, Mingan and Natashkwan were distinguished from the northern Naskapi. At Tadoussac they became the first inland allies of the French, and in 1603 Champlain sealed an alliance with them that led, in 1609, to his joining Innu, Algonquin and Wendat warriors in a battle against the Haudenosaunee on the lake that now bears his name. The Haudenosaunee replied with deep raids into Innu hunting grounds during the Iroquois Wars of the seventeenth century, a conflict in which the Innu also clashed with the Inuit, the Mi'kmaq and the Abenaki. The wars ended for them when they signed the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701.
zh: 因努人被法国人称作蒙塔涅人，是讲阿尔冈昆语的狩猎采集民族；他们把圣劳伦斯河北岸与拉布拉多半岛上辽阔的故土称为“尼塔西南”。数千年来，他们随季节捕猎驯鹿和驼鹿，支着兽皮帐篷在海岸与内陆森林之间迁徙；他们的语言因努艾蒙语属于克里—蒙塔涅—纳斯卡皮方言连续体，其中七岛、明根、纳塔什昆等南方森林部落与北方的纳斯卡皮人有所区别。在塔杜萨克，他们成为法国人最早的内陆盟友：1603年萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰与他们缔盟，并在1609年随同因努、阿尔冈昆和温达特战士，在今天以他命名的湖畔与易洛魁联盟交战。17世纪的易洛魁战争中，易洛魁人深入袭掠因努人的猎场作为报复；同一时期因努人还与因纽特人、米克马克人和阿贝纳基人发生冲突。1701年，他们签署《蒙特利尔大和平》，战争才告结束。

en: The Tamarowa, better known as the Tamaroa, were one of the principal tribes of the Illiniwek or Illinois Confederation, the loose Algonquian-speaking union whose members called themselves the Inoka and spoke the Miami-Illinois language. Their name derives from the Illiniwek word tamarowa, meaning cut tail, a totemic designation linked to the bear or wildcat. They held both banks of the Mississippi around its confluence with the Illinois and Missouri rivers, perhaps three thousand strong in the seventeenth century, before gathering in a single village of about six hundred lodges near present-day Cahokia. A Catholic mission founded nearby in 1689 drew in the Cahokia tribe, yet the combined settlement soon shrank to ninety dwellings, evidence of steep decline from disease, alcohol and wars with the Chickasaw and Shawnee. In 1703 the Tamaroa united with the Kaskaskia at the mouth of the Kaskaskia River. Their most influential later chief, Jean Baptiste de Coigne, led a renewed Kaskaskia-Tamaroa-Cahokia alliance that sided with the American patriots during the Revolutionary War. Tamaroa leaders signed the Treaty of Edwardsville in 1818, ceding much of Illinois, and the removal treaties of the 1830s carried their descendants beyond the Mississippi into the merged Peoria community.
zh: 塔马罗瓦人（即塔马罗阿人）是伊利尼维克人，或称伊利诺伊联盟的主要部落之一。这个松散的阿尔冈昆语联盟自称 Inoka，说迈阿密-伊利诺伊语。他们的名字源于伊利尼维克语 tamarowa，意为“断尾”，是与熊或野猫相关的图腾名号。他们占据密西西比河两岸、伊利诺伊河与密苏里河汇入处一带，17世纪时约有三千人，后来聚集在今卡霍基亚附近一座约有六百座长屋的村落。1689年，法国人在附近建立天主教传教站，吸引卡霍基亚部落前来同住，但合并后的聚落很快缩减到九十户，足见疾病、烈酒以及与奇克索人、肖尼人的战争造成的锐减。1703年，塔马罗瓦人在卡斯卡斯基亚河口与卡斯卡斯基亚人合并。他们后来最有影响力的酋长让·巴蒂斯特·德库瓦涅重组了卡斯卡斯基亚、塔马罗瓦和卡霍基亚联盟，在美国独立战争中站在爱国者一方。塔马罗瓦首领于1818年签署《爱德华兹维尔条约》，割让伊利诺伊大片土地；19世纪30年代的迁徙条约又把他们的后裔带到密西西比河以西，并入皮奥里亚社群。

en: The Inuinnait, better known as the Copper Inuit or Kitlinermiut, are the Canadian Inuit of the Coronation Gulf and lower Coppermine River country, around present-day Kugluktuk, Victoria Island and southern Banks Island, north of the tree line. Descended from the Thule, they were nomadic hunter-gatherers for some three thousand years, wintering in communal snowhouses for breathing-hole seal hunting and scattering into small family bands each summer to take caribou and fish inland. Their defining craft was working the native copper of the Coppermine and the gulf into arrowheads, ulu blades and knives that were traded across the Arctic. In 1771 the Chipewyan guides of Samuel Hearne massacred an Inuinnait band at Bloody Falls on the Coppermine, the first recorded encounter with Europeans, and Sir John Franklin's expeditions of 1821 and 1825 brought further contact.
zh: 因纽奈特人更常见的称呼是铜地因纽特人，又称基特利内尔缪特人，是加拿大科罗内申湾和科珀曼河下游一带的因纽特人，活动在林木线以北的库格卢克图克、维多利亚岛和班克斯岛南部。他们是图勒人的后裔，约三千年间过着游牧狩猎采集生活：冬天住进集体雪屋，在呼吸孔捕猎海豹；夏天分成小股家族群到内陆捕驯鹿、捕鱼。他们最有代表性的技艺，是把科珀曼河和海湾出产的自然铜打造成箭头、乌卢刀刀身和刀具，这些铜器在北极各地广泛交易。1771年，塞缪尔·赫恩的奇佩瓦人向导在科珀曼河的血腥瀑布屠杀了一群因纽奈特人，这是有记载的他们与欧洲人的第一次接触；1821年和1825年约翰·富兰克林爵士的两次探险又带来了更多接触。

en: The Inuit are Arctic hunters whose ancestors, the Thule people, spread eastward from the Bering Strait and western Alaska from about the year 1000, displacing the older Dorset culture, remembered in Inuit tradition as the Tuniit, which had vanished as a distinct people by about 1500. Speaking languages of the Eskaleut family, the Inuit settled the treeless tundra from Alaska through Arctic Canada to Greenland, traveling by dog sled and kayak and living from sea mammals, fish and caribou in skin tents and snow houses. They traded and sometimes raided with Subarctic peoples to their south, whose presence checked their expansion below the tree line. The bands west of Hudson Bay, the Kivallirmiut or Caribou Inuit, were the southernmost Central Inuit and lived by the great barren-ground caribou herds; during the eighteenth century, as Dene rivals withdrew when caribou numbers fell, they took to living inland year-round. Regular contact with Europeans began after the Churchill post opened in 1717, bringing guns, trapping and whaling into their economy.
zh: 因纽特人是北极地区的狩猎民族，其祖先是图勒人，约从1000年起自白令海峡和阿拉斯加西部向东扩散，取代了更古老的多塞特文化——因纽特传说称之为图尼特人，该文化到1500年前后已作为独立族群消亡。因纽特人讲爱斯基摩-阿留申语系的语言，足迹遍及从阿拉斯加经加拿大北极地区到格陵兰的无树苔原，以狗拉雪橇和皮艇出行，靠猎捕海洋哺乳动物、捕鱼和驯鹿为生，住兽皮帐篷和雪屋。他们与南方的亚北极诸族贸易，也时有劫掠，而这些南方族群的存在阻挡了他们向林木线以南扩张。居住在哈得孙湾西岸的支系称基瓦利尔缪特人，即驯鹿因纽特人，是中部因纽特人中分布最南的一支，以追逐贫瘠苔原上的大驯鹿群为生；18世纪驯鹿数量下降，竞争对手德内人撤离，他们便开始全年在内陆生活。1717年丘吉尔商站设立后，他们与欧洲人的定期接触开始，火枪、诱兽捕兽和捕鲸随之进入其经济生活。

en: The Iñupiaq are the Alaskan branch of the Inuit, whose traditional lands run along the northern Alaskan coast from Norton Sound on the Bering Sea to the Canadian border. Their name means 'real people', from the words iñuk, person, and -piaq, real, and their local bands, among them coastal whaling groups and the inland caribou-hunting Nunamiut, often carry the suffix -miut, meaning 'people of'. They descend from the Thule whale-hunting culture that had developed in coastal Alaska by the year 1000 and later spread east across the Arctic as far as Greenland. Their language, Iñupiatun, belongs to the Inuit dialect continuum and is divided into the North Slope, Malimiut, Bering Straits and Qawiaraq dialects. From the mid-seventeenth century the cooling of the Little Ice Age contracted many coastal settlements, and from 1741 Russian voyages and fur traders opened the first sustained contact with Europeans.
zh: 因纽皮亚克人是因纽特人在阿拉斯加的一支，传统领地沿阿拉斯加北部海岸，从白令海的诺顿湾一直延伸到加拿大边境。其族名意为“真正的人”；各个地方群体，如沿海捕鲸的群体和内陆猎鹿的努纳缪特人，名称常带“缪特”后缀，意为“……之人”。他们是图勒捕鲸文化的后裔，该文化在1000年已发展于阿拉斯加沿海，后来向东扩散，穿过北极直达格陵兰。他们的语言因纽皮亚克语属于因纽特语方言连续体，分为北坡、马利缪特、白令海峡和卡维亚拉克四种方言。17世纪中叶起，小冰期的寒冷使许多沿海聚落萎缩，1741年起俄国人的航行与毛皮商人带来了与欧洲人最早的持续接触。

en: The Inuviluq, or Inuvialuit of the lower Mackenzie, are the Western Canadian Inuit of the Mackenzie Delta and the adjacent Beaufort Sea coast, whose communities include Aklavik, Inuvik and Tuktoyaktuk. They descend from the Thule Inuit who spread east from Alaska, and the delta's original Inuit were the Siglit, who hunted beluga whales and caribou and fished the countless channels of the great river they call Kuukpak. The Scottish explorer Alexander Mackenzie reached the delta's Arctic mouth by boat in 1789, the first European to do so, and Sir John Franklin surveyed the same coasts in 1825, passing through waters and channels long used as Inuit camps, fishing grounds and beluga hunting stations.
zh: 因纽维卢克人即下马更些的伊努维亚卢特人，是马更些三角洲及邻近波弗特海沿岸的西加拿大因纽特人，聚落包括阿克拉维克、伊努维克和图克托亚图克。他们是从阿拉斯加向东扩散的图勒因纽特人的后裔；三角洲最早的因纽特居民是西格利特人，捕猎白鲸和驯鹿，在他们称为库克帕克（意为大河）的马更些河无数河道中捕鱼。1789年，苏格兰探险家亚历山大·马更些乘船抵达三角洲在北冰洋的河口，成为第一个到此的欧洲人；1825年约翰·富兰克林爵士又来考察这些海岸，他经过的水域和河道，早就是因纽特人的营地、渔场和白鲸捕猎站。

en: The Iny, known in Portuguese as the Karajá, are a Macro-Jê river people of the middle Araguaia, whose villages line the river and its Javaés branch around Bananal Island across Tocantins, Goiás, Mato Grosso and Pará. They call themselves Iny and speak the Karajá language, with its Northern and Southern Karajá, Javaé and Xambioá dialects and distinct men's and women's speech. Their life follows the rhythm of the river: slash-and-burn fields of manioc, maize and bananas, seasonal fishing camps, hunting, and the ceramics and body painting developed by the women. Jesuits first reached them in 1658 and explorers in 1673, but the lasting newcomers were the São Paulo bandeirantes, who raided the Araguaia for gold and captives through the later seventeenth century. Conflict sharpened under the Portuguese crown, whose war against the river tribes in 1811 drew a fierce reply: in 1812 the Karajá and their Xavante allies destroyed the presidio of Santa Maria do Araguaia.
zh: 卡拉雅人自称伊尼，葡语称卡拉雅，是阿拉瓜亚河中游的大热语系河畔族群，村庄沿干流及其支流雅瓦埃斯河分布，环绕巴纳纳尔岛，地跨托坎廷斯、戈亚斯、马托格罗索和帕拉四州。他们说卡拉雅语，分北卡拉雅、南卡拉雅、雅瓦埃和尚比奥阿四种方言，男性和女性的用语还有明显差别。生活随河水节律安排：在刀耕火种的田地里种植木薯、玉米和香蕉，按季节设立渔营，兼事狩猎，女性还发展出制陶和身体绘纹技艺。耶稣会士最早于1658年来到他们中间，探险者则在1673年首次抵达；但影响更深远的是圣保罗的旗队，他们在17世纪后期沿阿拉瓜亚河掠夺黄金和俘虏。葡萄牙王室时期冲突加剧，1811年王室对沿河各部落开战，激起猛烈回击：1812年，卡拉雅人联合沙万特人摧毁了圣玛丽亚-杜阿拉瓜亚驻军要塞。

en: The Iranun are an Austronesian Muslim people of southwestern Mindanao, concentrated on the shores of Illana Bay, the Pulangi delta and the Polloc harbor, with their roots probably around Lake Lanao; with the Maranao and Maguindanao they form the Danao-speaking group, and their name means people of the lake. As Islam took root in the Cotabato lowlands in the early 1500s, the Iranun became Muslims and vassals and key maritime allies of the Sultanate of Maguindanao, sailing and fighting under its flag while keeping their own datus. From the 1770s Iranun war fleets raided across the South China, Sulu, Moro and Celebes seas, plundering Spanish-held coasts for slaves and trade goods so widely that their old exonym Ilanun entered Malay as lanun, the ordinary word for pirate. Their seafaring also took them into settlement: between the 1700s and 1800s Iranun colonies appeared in Sabah and in Riau and Jambi on Sumatra. Their knowledge of regional waters is preserved in the Carta Indigena Filipina, a chart drawn from Iranun sailing experience.
zh: 伊琅文人是棉兰老西南部的南岛语系穆斯林族群，聚居于伊拉纳湾沿岸、普朗吉三角洲和波洛克港一带，最早可能发源于拉瑙湖周边；他们与马拉瑙人、马京达瑙人同属达瑙语群体，族名意为“湖畔之民”。16世纪初伊斯兰教在哥打巴托低地扎根，伊琅文人随之改宗，成为马京达瑙苏丹国的属邦和最重要的海上盟友，悬挂苏丹国旗帜航行作战，同时保留自己的达图首领。18世纪70年代起，伊琅文战船横行南海、苏禄海、莫罗湾和西里伯斯海，袭掠西班牙控制的海岸，掳掠人口和财货；他们的旧称“伊拉农”因此进入马来语，变成意为海盗的常用词拉农。航海活动也带动了迁徙：18至19世纪间，沙巴、苏门答腊的廖内和占碑都出现了伊琅文定居点。他们对这片海域的地理知识，保存在根据伊琅文航海经验绘制的《菲律宾土人地图》中。

en: The Iraqis are the Arabic-speaking people of the Mesopotamian alluvium, from Baghdad and the shrine cities of Kufa and Karbala to the port of Basra, whose Mesopotamian Arabic carries a strong Aramaic substrate and splits between the older qeltu speech of the northern towns and the gelet dialect of Baghdad and the south. Arab armies took the country from the Sasanians after the battle of al-Qadisiyyah in 636, and Baghdad, founded in 762, became the capital of the Abbasid caliphate at its intellectual peak before the Mongol sack of 1258. In 1337 Iraq was held by the Jalayirid sultans, heirs of the fallen Ilkhanate, until Timur's massacre at Baghdad in 1401; Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen followed, and then the Safavids from 1508. Ottoman armies seized Baghdad in 1534, and the treaty of Zuhab in 1639 settled the Iraqi provinces under Istanbul, although Basra long ran its own affairs with Portuguese backing. From 1704 a dynasty of Georgian Mamluks ruled Iraq in near autonomy until 1831, when the Ottomans reimposed direct rule as the vilayets of Baghdad, Mosul and Basra; in 1802 Wahhabi raiders had sacked Karbala, sharpening the geography of Sunni trading towns and Shia shrine cities.
zh: 伊拉克人是美索不达米亚冲积平原上讲阿拉伯语的居民，分布于巴格达、库法和卡尔巴拉等圣城以及港口巴士拉之间；他们的美索不达米亚阿拉伯语带有浓厚的阿拉姆语底层，分为北方城镇较古老的“凯勒图”口音与巴格达和南方的“吉莱特”方言。636年卡迪西亚战役后，阿拉伯军队从萨珊王朝手中夺取此地；762年建立的巴格达成为阿拔斯哈里发国的都城，在1258年蒙古人洗城之前一直是伊斯兰世界的学术中心。1337年统治伊拉克的是灭亡的伊利汗国留下的札剌亦儿苏丹们，1401年帖木儿在巴格达大肆屠城；此后黑羊、白羊土库曼人相继入主，1508年起归萨法维王朝。1534年奥斯曼军队攻占巴格达，1639年《祖哈布条约》将伊拉克各省划归伊斯坦布尔，但巴士拉凭葡萄牙人支持长期自行其是。1704年起，格鲁吉亚马穆鲁克王朝近乎自治地统治伊拉克，直到1831年奥斯曼恢复直接统治，改设巴格达、摩苏尔、巴士拉三省；1802年瓦哈比袭击者洗劫卡尔巴拉，使逊尼派商贸城镇与什叶派圣城并立的格局更加分明。

en: The Irarutu are an Austronesian people of the interior Bomberai Peninsula in north-western New Guinea, living in the Babo and Arguni districts of Bintuni and Kaimana regencies. Their language, whose name means the people's true language in their own tongue, is now grouped with the Kei-Tanimbar languages and has seven local varieties.
zh: 伊拉鲁图人是新几内亚岛西北部邦贝拉伊半岛内陆的南岛语族族群，村落散布在宾图尼县和凯马纳县的巴博、阿尔古尼等区。他们的语言在本族语中意为“人民真正的语言”，现归入凯伊-塔宁巴尔语群，内分七种地方变体。

en: The Iresim, also recorded as Yerisiam, are an Austronesian-speaking people on the shoreline of Cenderawasih Bay in the Bird's Head region of New Guinea. Their language belongs to the Cenderawasih Bay branch of Austronesian and forms its closest pair with Yaur, the two descending from a single Proto-Yaur-Yerisiam tongue.
zh: 伊雷辛人（又记作耶雷辛人）是新几内亚岛鸟头地区极乐鸟湾沿岸的南岛语族族群，其语言属南岛语系极乐鸟湾语支，与尧尔语关系最近，二者由共同的原始尧尔-耶雷辛语分化而来。

en: The Irish are the Gaelic people of Ireland, whose island was organised into a patchwork of kin-based túatha under Brehon law, with bardic schools, a rich monastic Christianity and a tradition of missionaries such as Columba and Columbanus that made early medieval Ireland a land of saints and scholars. Viking longphorts from the ninth century grew into Dublin, Cork, Limerick and Waterford and produced the Norse-Gaels, until Brian Bóruma's victory at Clontarf in 1014 broke Norse power. The Anglo-Norman invasion of 1169 opened eight centuries of English involvement, but the Gaelic resurgence of the later Middle Ages left the Crown little beyond the Pale around Dublin; the Tudors then launched a full conquest from 1536, and Henry VIII took the title King of Ireland in 1541. The Irish rejected the Protestant Reformation and clung to Catholicism through the plantation of English and Scottish settlers, the defeat at Kinsale in 1601 and the Flight of the Earls in 1607, which ended the old Gaelic order. The Confederate wars of 1641, Cromwell's campaign of 1649 and the Williamite victory at the Boyne in 1690 entrenched a Protestant Ascendancy and the Penal Laws, which stripped the Catholic majority of land and office; after the United Irishmen rising of 1798 the Acts of Union of 1800 abolished the Dublin parliament, and Daniel O'Connell won Catholic emancipation in 1829. Throughout these centuries Irish migrants carried Gaelic and, increasingly, English speech and Catholic or Presbyterian traditions to the American colonies and beyond.
zh: 爱尔兰人是爱尔兰岛上的盖尔民族，古时全岛按血缘组成众多称作图阿特的小邦，行布雷亨法，设有吟游学校，基督教修道院传统深厚，曾出哥伦巴、高隆班等传教士，使中世纪早期的爱尔兰享有圣徒与学者之岛的名声。9世纪起维京人的长港发展为都柏林、科克、利默里克和沃特福德，并形成诺斯-盖尔人，直到1014年布赖恩·博鲁在克朗塔夫之战中击垮诺斯势力。1169年盎格鲁-诺曼人入侵，开启了英格兰介入爱尔兰的八百年；但中世纪后期的盖尔复兴使王权实际所剩无几，仅能控制都柏林周边的佩尔地区。都铎王朝1536年起全面征服，亨利八世于1541年加上爱尔兰国王头衔。爱尔兰人拒绝新教改革，坚守天主教，历经英格兰和苏格兰新教徒的移植、1601年金塞尔之败和1607年伯爵出逃，旧盖尔秩序终告终结。1641年邦联战争、1649年克伦威尔远征和1690年博因河的威廉派胜利，确立了新教优势阶层与刑法体制，信天主教的多数民众被剥夺土地和官职；1798年爱尔兰人联合会起义后，1800年的《联合法令》废除都柏林议会，丹尼尔·奥康奈尔又于1829年争取到天主教解放。数百年间，爱尔兰移民把盖尔语以及日益占上风的英语，连同天主教或长老宗传统带到北美殖民地和更远的地方。

en: The Irritila, called Laguneros by the Spanish, were the lagoon dwellers of the Comarca Lagunera, the inland basin where Coahuila meets Durango. Their villages stood around the Laguna de Mayrán, once known as the Great Lagoon of Nueva Vizcaya, and along the Nazas River, a chain of shallow lakes that gave them their name. Jesuit chronicles at Parras noted that the Irritila were not one people but more than twelve tribes speaking different tongues who used Nahuatl as a common language. They lived by hunting deer, rabbits and birds, gathering tunas, mesquite and roots, and fishing with basket traps, and some hunters swam submerged with a reed to breathe and pulled ducks under by the feet. Their bell-shaped reed huts housed a single family, and they wove colored sandals, nets and mats and wore ornaments of shell and animal vertebrae. After the Spanish founded Zacatecas in 1557 and Durango in 1563, mining expeditions reached the lagoons, and in 1594 Philip II authorized Jesuit missions in the so-called Province of the Lagoon. The expulsion of the Jesuits around 1687 emptied the mission villages, and the Irritila drifted back into the backcountry, where they vanished as a distinct people.
zh: 伊里提拉人被西班牙人称为拉古内罗人，意为湖民，生活在科阿韦拉与杜兰戈交界处的拉古内拉盆地。他们的村落环绕迈兰湖——旧称新比斯开大湖——和纳萨斯河展开，这一带串珠状的浅水湖群正是他们名号的由来。耶稣会在帕拉斯传教站的记录称，伊里提拉人并非单一民族，而是十二个以上各说不同语言的部落，彼此以纳瓦特尔语通用。他们猎鹿、兔和禽鸟，采集仙人掌果、牧豆和块根，用篮状鱼篓捕鱼；有的猎人还会口含芦苇潜游水中，揪住野鸭的脚将其拖入水里。他们住单户使用的钟形芦苇棚，编织染成红、蓝、褐各色的凉鞋、渔网和席子，佩戴贝壳和兽骨椎骨制成的饰物。1557年西班牙人建立萨卡特卡斯、1563年建立杜兰戈后，寻矿的探险队抵达湖区；1594年，腓力二世降旨准许耶稣会在所谓湖区省份传教。1687年前后耶稣会士被逐出这一地区，传教村落人去屋空，伊里提拉人退回偏远乡野，最终作为独立民族消亡。

en: The Isnag, also called Isneg or Apayao, are an Austronesian river people of the northern Cordillera, chiefly the landlocked highlands of Apayao beyond the Cagayan valley, with settlements strung along the Apayao, Abulog and Matalag rivers; their name means people who live inland, and they divide themselves into upstream Imandaya and downstream Imallod clans. Without chiefs or any political hierarchy, their villages were organized around bilateral kin groups, while brave mengal warriors led the hunting and head-taking raids, earning tattoos and the rank of kamenglan. Dominican friars opened a mission at Pudtol as early as 1610 and put up a church at Kabugao in 1684, yet the Isnag highlands remained effectively outside Spanish control throughout the period and most clans kept their animist rites. They bartered mountain beeswax, cacao and tobacco for lowland goods and were noted for the clean, solid raised houses they built on the riverbanks.
zh: 伊斯纳格人又称伊斯内格人或阿巴尧人，是科迪勒拉北部的南岛语系滨水族群，主要聚居于卡加延河谷以里的阿巴尧内陆高地，村落散布在阿巴尧河、阿布卢格河和马塔拉格河沿岸；族名意为“住在内陆的人”，内部又分为上游的伊曼达亚和下游的伊马洛德两大氏族群。他们没有酋长，也没有政治等级，村落按双边血缘氏族组织，勇敢的门加尔战士主持狩猎和猎头袭掠，凭战功获得纹身和卡门兰首领的地位。多明我会修道士早在1610年就在普德托尔建立传教点，1684年又在卡布高修建教堂，但伊斯纳格高地在整个这一时期实际上始终游离于西班牙控制之外，多数氏族保留了万物有灵仪式。他们以山中蜂蜡、可可和烟草交换低地货物，并以在河畔建造整洁坚固的高脚屋著称。

en: The Issati is the name for the peoples of the Cofitachequi country in central South Carolina, a Mississippian chiefdom on the Wateree River with towns such as Talimeco and Hymahi. Visited by Hernando de Soto in 1540 and Juan Pardo in 1566, it was destroyed by seventeenth-century slave raids and vanished after 1670, its descendants absorbed into the Catawba.
zh: 伊萨蒂是对南卡罗来纳中部科菲塔切基地区诸族的称呼，那是以沃特里河为中心的密西西比文化酋邦，拥有塔利梅科、希马希等城镇。1540年埃尔南多·德索托和1566年胡安·帕尔多先后到访；它在17世纪的奴隶袭击中被摧毁，1670年后再不见于记载，遗民被卡托巴人吸收。

en: The Istro-Romanians are the smallest of the Eastern Romance peoples, clinging to the hills and coastal towns of the Istrian peninsula. Their language is close to Romanian rather than to the extinct Dalmatian speech of the old Roman coastal cities, and most scholars think their ancestors were Vlach shepherds who moved west from Transylvania, Banat or the Timok valley during the high Middle Ages, local tradition speaking of seven caravans crossing into Istria. Byzantine writers already noted Romance-speaking islanders who called themselves Romans in the tenth century, and a document of 1329 from Buzet names a Vlach bearing the local exonym Ćići. Through the fourteenth century Vlach herders appear around Split, Trogir, Zadar and on the island of Krk, driving caravans that sold cheese, recorded in Ragusan trade as caseus vlachescus, and salt along the Adriatic. Uniquely among Eastern Romance peoples they are Catholics, worshipping under the Patriarchate of Aquileia and later Venice. Venetian rule, plague and the settling of Morlach and Slavic refugees in the fifteenth century began a long assimilation into the surrounding Croatian population, a process that continued under Austrian administration as their isolated villages around the Učka mountain shrank.
zh: 伊斯特拉-罗马尼亚人是东罗曼语民族中人数最少的一支，聚居在伊斯特拉半岛的丘陵与滨海城镇。他们的语言接近罗马尼亚语，而与罗马时代沿海城市已消亡的达尔马提亚语差别明显，因此多数学者认为，其祖先是中世纪盛期从特兰西瓦尼亚、巴纳特或蒂莫克河谷西迁的弗拉赫牧人，当地传说称有七支商队迁入伊斯特拉。早在10世纪，拜占庭作家就注意到半岛上有自称为罗马人的罗曼语居民；1329年布泽特的一份文书提到了一个带有当地别称“齐齐”的弗拉赫人。整个14世纪，斯普利特、特罗吉尔、扎达尔周边及克尔克岛上都有弗拉赫牧人的记载，他们的商队经营奶酪（拉古萨贸易文献称之为“弗拉赫奶酪”）和亚得里亚海沿岸的食盐。在东罗曼语各民族中，唯独他们是天主教徒，先后受阿奎莱亚牧首区和威尼斯管辖。15世纪威尼斯统治下的瘟疫，以及莫拉克人和斯拉夫难民的迁入，开启了他们被周边克罗地亚人长期同化的过程；随着奥地利统治下乌奇卡山周围偏远村庄日益萎缩，这一进程仍在继续。

en: The Italkim are the Jews of Italy whose presence reaches back to the Roman Republic, with epitaphs and donor inscriptions surviving from the second century BCE; the Rome community is among the oldest continuously inhabited Jewish settlements in Europe. In Hebrew they are called italkim, from the Latin italicus, and they preserve their own Italian synagogue rite, distinct from both the Ashkenazi and Sephardic rites, while speaking Judeo-Italian dialects. Early medieval learning flourished in Rome and the southern cities of Bari and Otranto: Shabbethai Donnolo, who died in 982, wrote medical and religious works, Nathan ben Jehiel compiled the Talmudic dictionary known as the Arukh, and Zedekiah ben Abraham Anaw later authored the legal compendium Shibbole ha-Leket. The papacy generally protected its Jews, and the Papal States were one of the few medieval lands from which they were never expelled, though Bologna drove them out in 1172 and Trani forced conversions in 1380. From 1492 waves of Sephardic refugees from Spain, Portugal and Provence enlarged and reshaped the communities. The Venetian Republic confined its Jews to the world's first ghetto in 1516, the Kingdom of Naples expelled its Jews in 1533, and in 1555 the papal bull Cum nimis absurdum imposed the Roman ghetto and the yellow badge, two years after Talmud copies had been burned across Italy. The mystic Moses Hayyim Luzzatto, who lived from 1707 to 1746, was the last great voice of this tradition before Napoleon's army opened the Venetian ghetto in 1797.
zh: 伊塔尔基姆即意大利本土犹太人，其历史可上溯至罗马共和国，公元前2世纪的墓志和奉献铭文仍有存世；罗马的犹太社群是欧洲延续最久的犹太定居点之一。希伯来语称他们为伊塔尔基姆，源自拉丁语中表示“意大利的”一词。他们保有自成一家的意大利会堂仪轨，与阿什肯纳兹和塞法迪仪轨均不相同，日常则说各种犹太-意大利方言。中世纪早期，经学在罗马及南部的巴里、奥特朗托兴盛：982年去世的沙贝泰·多诺洛著有医学和宗教作品，内森·本·耶希埃尔编成《塔木德》词典《阿鲁克》，西底家·本·亚伯拉罕·阿纳夫后来撰成律法汇编《拾穗集》。教廷总体上庇护治下犹太人，教皇国是中世纪少数从未驱逐犹太人的地方，但博洛尼亚仍于1172年逐犹，特拉尼也在1380年强迫犹太人改宗。1492年起，西班牙、葡萄牙和普罗旺斯的塞法迪难民大批涌入，改变并壮大了当地社群。1516年，威尼斯共和国把犹太人限制在世界上第一个隔都里；1533年那不勒斯王国驱逐犹太人；1553年意大利各地焚烧《塔木德》，两年后教皇诏书《既然荒谬》又设立罗马隔都并强令佩戴黄色标识。1707至1746年在世的神秘主义者摩西·哈伊姆·卢扎托是这一传统最后的大家，1797年拿破仑的军队打开了威尼斯隔都的大门。

en: The iTaukei, or indigenous Fijians, are an Austronesian people of the Fiji archipelago in Melanesia who speak Fijian, a Central Pacific language of the Austronesian family. Their ancestors were Lapita seafarers who reached the islands around 1100 to 1000 BC; a later Melanesian influx around the start of the Common Era, followed by centuries of contact with the Polynesian Tu'i Tonga Empire, shaped their society. They lived in rival chiefdoms on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and the smaller islands, ruled by chiefs and priests, with fortified villages, irrigated plantations, the great double-hulled drua canoes, kava rites and the revered whale's-tooth tabua. Abel Tasman first sighted the islands in 1643, James Cook visited a southern Lau island in 1774, and William Bligh charted the main waters in 1789. The sandalwood rush of 1804 to 1814 drew traders to Vanua Levu, and beachcombers such as Charlie Savage gave the island of Bau firearms and a military edge before he was killed in a raid in 1813. The sea cucumber trade of the 1820s spread muskets among the chiefs, the town of Levuka grew on Ovalau, and by the 1830s the first missionaries arrived while Bau and Rewa fought for dominance over still-independent Fijian polities.
zh: 伊陶凯人即斐济原住民，是美拉尼西亚斐济群岛的南岛语族群，使用南岛语系中太平洋语支的斐济语。他们的祖先是约公元前1100—前1000年抵达群岛的拉皮塔航海者；公元初年前后又有美拉尼西亚人迁入，加上10世纪起波利尼西亚人的图伊汤加帝国数百年影响，共同塑造了伊陶凯社会。他们在维提岛、瓦努阿岛及周边小岛形成彼此争战的酋邦，由酋长和祭司统领，村落设防、农田有灌溉渠，能建造大型双体独木舟，盛行卡瓦酒仪式，并以抹香鲸牙为贵重礼器。1643年荷兰航海者阿贝尔·塔斯曼最早望见这些岛屿，詹姆斯·库克于1774年探访南部劳群岛的一座岛屿，威廉·布莱则在1789年绘下主要水道。1804—1814年的檀香木热潮把商人引到瓦努阿岛，流浪汉查理·萨维奇等人给巴乌岛带来火器、助其取得军事优势，他本人于1813年在一次袭掠中被杀。19世纪20年代的海参贸易使火枪在各酋长间扩散，莱武卡在奥瓦劳岛上兴起；到19世纪30年代，首批传教士抵达，而巴乌与雷瓦仍在为控制这些保持独立的斐济政权而争战。

en: The Itelmens are the indigenous people of the Kamchatka Peninsula, whose Itelmen language belongs, with Chukchi and Koryak, to the Chukotko-Kamchatkan family. They settled the peninsula's river valleys, above all the Kamchatka River, living by salmon fishing, sea-mammal hunting and gathering in villages of a few hundred people organized around patriarchal households, and each river basin had its own dialect. Russian Cossacks first reached Kamchatka in the early 1650s, and the annexation that followed brought brutal suppression of local revolts and a devastating smallpox epidemic in the eighteenth century, which together cut the native population sharply. The naturalist Georg Wilhelm Steller, travelling with Vitus Bering's second Kamchatka expedition, recorded their customs in the 1740s, by which time villages had already shrunk to a few dozen inhabitants. Widespread intermarriage with Cossacks then produced the mixed, Russian-speaking Kamchadal population, and the name Itelmen came to be reserved for those who kept the old language.
zh: 伊捷尔缅人是堪察加半岛的原住民，其语言与楚科奇语、科里亚克语同属楚科奇—堪察加语系。他们定居在半岛各河流的谷地，尤其是堪察加河流域，以捕鲑鱼、猎海兽和采集为生；村落由数百人组成，以父系大家庭为中心，每个河流流域各有自己的方言。俄国哥萨克最早在17世纪50年代初抵达堪察加，随后的兼并伴随着对当地起义的残酷镇压和18世纪一场毁灭性的天花疫情，原住民人口因此锐减。博物学家格奥尔格·威廉·斯特勒随维图斯·白令的第二次堪察加考察队同行，于18世纪40年代记录了他们的风俗，那时村落已萎缩到只剩数十人。此后他们与哥萨克大量通婚，形成了讲俄语的混血堪察达尔人群体，伊捷尔缅一名逐渐只用来指称仍使用本族语言的人。

en: The Ithaktunwan, anglicized as the Yankton and meaning 'village at the end', were one of the two Western Dakota tribes of the Sioux Seven Council Fires, paired with the Yanktonai under the shared name Wičhíyena, 'those who speak like men'. In the eighteenth century they lived along the Minnesota River and the Blue Earth River around Mankato in southwestern Minnesota, closer to the Plains than the Santee Dakota of the Great Lakes. Like other Sioux they had been pushed westward out of the Lake Superior woodlands by wars with the Ojibwe and Cree, and the long Dakota-Ojibwe war cost the Dakota their villages around Leech Lake and Mille Lacs in 1736. The Western Dakota traded with the French from the late seventeenth century and took increasingly to mounted bison hunting. Within the Sioux nation the Yankton shared with the Yanktonai the traditional role of caretakers of the Pipestone Quarry, whose red stone was carved into the sacred pipes used by all the Sioux bands.
zh: 伊桑克通万人英语中称扬克顿人，名字意为‘尽头之村’，是苏族七议会之火中西达科他两部之一，与伊桑克图纳纳人合称维奇耶纳，意为‘像男人一样说话的人’。18世纪时，他们居住在明尼苏达河以及明尼苏达西南部曼卡托一带的布卢厄斯河沿岸，比五大湖边的桑蒂达科他人更靠近大平原。和其他苏人一样，他们因与奥吉布瓦人、克里人的战争而从苏必利尔湖林地西迁；在漫长的达科他—奥吉布瓦战争中，达科他人于1736年失去了利奇湖和米拉湖周围的村落。西达科他人从17世纪末起与法国人贸易，并越来越多地转向骑马猎牛。在苏族内部，伊桑克通万人与伊桑克图纳纳人共同承担着守护烟斗石采石场的传统职分，那里出产的红色石料被各苏人部落雕成神圣的仪式烟斗。
