en: The Ithanktunwanna, anglicized as the Yanktonai or 'little village at the end', were the second of the two Western Dakota tribes of the Sioux Seven Council Fires, sharing with the Yankton the name Wičhíyena. They themselves fell into two sub-groups, the Upper Yanktonai and the Lower Yanktonai, the latter also called the Húŋkpathina. Eighteenth-century accounts place them in the Minnesota River country around Mankato and the Blue Earth River, the same southwestern Minnesota hunting grounds as the Yankton. They had drifted west with the rest of the Dakota under pressure from the Ojibwe, who seized the Leech Lake and Mille Lacs country from the Dakota in 1736, and after horses reached the Sioux around 1700 they increasingly lived by mounted bison hunts on the prairies. Together with the Yankton they were the traditional quarrymen and guardians of the Pipestone Quarry, cutting the pipestone from which the Sioux made their sacred pipes.
zh: 伊桑克图纳纳人英语中称扬克顿奈人，名字意为‘尽头小村’，是苏族七议会之火中西达科他两部的另一部，与伊桑克通万人合称维奇耶纳。他们内部分为上扬克顿奈和下扬克顿奈两支，后者又名亨克帕蒂纳。18世纪的记载把他们置于明尼苏达西南部曼卡托和布卢厄斯河一带的明尼苏达河流域，与伊桑克通万人共享同一片猎场。他们随达科他各部在奥吉布瓦人的压力下逐步西迁：奥吉布瓦人于1736年从达科他人手中夺取利奇湖和米勒湖一带，而马匹约在1700年传入苏人，此后他们越来越多地靠在草原上骑马猎牛为生。他们与伊桑克通万人世代在烟斗石采石场采石并承担守护之责，苏人制作神圣烟斗的烟斗石便出自此处。

en: The Itneg, known in Spanish records as the Tingguian, or mountain dwellers, are an Austronesian Cordilleran people whose heartland is the Abra valley of northwestern Luzon; their own name derives from the Ilocano phrase iti uneg, meaning the interior. They once lived on the northern Luzon coast alongside the Ilocanos, but through the 1500s and 1600s colonial pressure and Christian Ilocano settlement drove them inland into Abra, where valley groups took to wet-rice farming while highland groups kept swidden cultivation. A bishop's letter of 1585 gives the first Spanish mention of them, and in 1598 Spanish and Ilocano forces occupied Bangued and installed an Augustinian mission behind a garrison; the friar Juan Pareja arrived in 1626 and baptized some three thousand people, yet many highland villages kept raiding the mission towns. Itneg settlements were governed by councils of panglakayen elders under customary law, headhunting feuds were closed by kalon peace pacts, and their animist faith centered on the sky creator Kadaklan. By the early 1800s the valley clans were being absorbed into Christian lowland society while the mountain subgroups kept the old rites.
zh: 伊特内格人在西班牙文献中常称廷吉安人，意为“山居者”，是科迪勒拉的南岛语系族群，核心家园在吕宋西北部的阿布拉河谷；他们的本名来自伊洛卡诺语“伊蒂·乌内格”，意思是“内地”。他们原住吕宋北部海岸，与伊洛卡诺人为邻，但16至17世纪间，殖民压力和改宗基督教的伊洛卡诺人不断拓殖，迫使他们退入阿布拉内陆：河谷支系改种水稻，山地支系仍行刀耕火种。1585年，一位主教致西班牙国王的信中首次提到他们；1598年，西班牙与伊洛科联军占领班格德，派兵驻守奥古斯丁会传教点。修道士胡安·帕雷哈1626年到此，为约三千人施洗，但许多山地村落仍不断袭掠传教城镇。伊特内格人的村落由邦拉卡延长老议事会按习惯法治理，猎头仇杀通过卡隆和约了结，其万物有灵信仰以至高天神卡达克兰为中心。到19世纪初，河谷氏族已逐渐融入基督教低地社会，山地支系则保留着旧有仪式。

en: The Itonama are an indigenous people of the Bolivian Amazon, at home in the seasonally flooded savannas of the Beni lowlands, where they have lived along the Itonomas River and the lakes of the Mamoré and Iténez provinces since their first contact with Spaniards in the seventeenth century. Their traditional language, self-named sihnipadara, meaning 'our language', is a linguistic isolate with no proven relatives. They subsisted by slash-and-burn farming, fishing, hunting and gathering in small communities led by a village council, and held animist beliefs centred on a high god called Dijnamu. In 1704 the missionary Lorenzo Legarda counted twenty-six Itonama communities numbering some six thousand people. Mission towns such as Magdalena then gathered them into settled Christian parish life, and over the eighteenth century the Itonama became a Spanish-speaking Catholic people while keeping their riverine villages and collective lands.
zh: 伊托纳马人是玻利维亚亚马孙的原住民，世居贝尼低地季节泛滥的草原，自17世纪与西班牙人首次接触以来，一直生活在伊托诺马斯河沿岸以及马莫雷省和伊特内斯省的湖区。他们的传统语言自称西尼帕达拉，意为“我们的语言”，是一门与其他已知语言都没有亲缘关系的孤立语言。伊托纳马人在村议事会带领下聚居成小村落，以刀耕火种、渔猎和采集为生，信仰万物有灵，崇奉至高神迪吉纳穆。1704年，传教士洛伦索·莱加达清点出26个伊托纳马社群，约六千人。此后马格达莱纳等传教镇把他们并入定居的天主教教区体系；整个18世纪，伊托纳马人逐渐成为讲西班牙语的天主教徒，同时保留了河畔村落和集体土地。

en: The Itza are a Maya people descended from the Chanes of the Chontal coast in Tabasco. In the Postclassic they dominated northern Yucatán from their capital Chichén Itzá, whose name means at the mouth of the well of the Itza, and ran a trade network reaching as far south as Naco in Honduras. Rivalry with the Cocom and Xiu lineages ended in the fall of Chichén Itzá around 1331, and after the Xiu drove them from Mayapan the Itza fled south in about 1441–1446 to the Petén lakes, where they built the island capital Nojpetén, called Tayasal by the Spanish, in Lake Petén Itzá. Hernán Cortés crossed their territory in 1525, and an expedition under Francisco de Mirones was massacred there in 1622, but the Itza kingdom held out behind its lake defenses until 1697, when Martín de Ursúa y Arizmendi stormed Nojpetén and captured the king Kan Ek', extinguishing the last independent native kingdom in the Americas.
zh: 伊察人是玛雅人的一支，源自塔瓦斯科琼塔尔沿海的查内斯人。后古典期，他们以奇琴伊察为都城称雄尤卡坦北部——奇琴伊察在伊察语中意为“伊察人的井口”，其贸易网络向南远达洪都拉斯的纳科。与科科姆、休两系的争霸以约1331年奇琴伊察的陷落告终；后来休人又把他们逐出玛雅潘，伊察人遂于约1441—1446年南逃佩滕湖区，在佩滕伊察湖中的岛上建起都城塔亚萨尔（伊察语称诺赫佩滕）。1525年埃尔南·科尔特斯曾穿越其地，1622年弗朗西斯科·德·米罗内斯率领的远征队在此被全歼，但伊察王国凭湖险固守到1697年，最终马丁·德·乌尔苏亚·伊·阿斯门迪攻陷塔亚萨尔、俘获国王坎·埃克，美洲最后一个独立的土著王国就此灭亡。

en: The Ivatan are an Austronesian people of the Batanes and Babuyan Islands, the northernmost islands of the Philippines, lying between Luzon and Taiwan. Their islands first served as stepping stones in the Austronesian seaborne expansion out of Taiwan around 3000 BCE, and were settled again by migrants from northern Luzon around 1200 BCE, whose descendants became the Ivatan; archaeology links them to the jade lingling-o trade network reaching Taiwan, Vietnam, Palawan and Borneo, and from about 1200 CE imported pottery shows trade with Song and Yuan China. They also traded and intermarried with the Tao of Orchid Island, whose language is close to their own Ivatan tongue, with its Basco and Itbayaten dialects. Life on the typhoon-scoured islands shaped their culture: they grew yams, taro and sweet potatoes, took flying fish and dolphinfish in spring, wore the vuyavuy-palm headgear called vakul, and built fortified hill refuges known as ijang. On 26 June 1783 Spain annexed Batanes, and in 1786 the Ivatans were forced down from their hill settlements into lowland towns; Spanish lime kilns gave them their distinctive coral-and-limestone stone houses, thick-walled against the storms, while the old anito ancestral worship gradually gave way to Catholicism.
zh: 伊巴丹人是菲律宾最北端巴丹群岛与巴布延群岛的南岛语系民族，群岛夹在吕宋与台湾之间。约公元前3000年，南岛语人群从台湾向外海上扩张时，巴丹群岛曾是中继跳板；约公元前1200年，来自吕宋北部的移民再度定居于此，他们的后裔便是伊巴丹人。考古发现表明，他们参与了连通台湾、越南、巴拉望和婆罗洲的玉石“林林奥”饰品贸易网；约1200年起，外来陶器显示他们已与中国的宋朝和元朝通商。他们还与台湾兰屿的达悟人通婚贸易，语言相近，伊巴丹语有巴斯科和伊特巴亚特两种方言。台风肆虐的海岛塑造了他们的文化：种植山药、芋头和红薯，春季捕捞飞鱼和鲯鳅，头戴用棕榈纤维编成的“瓦库尔”头笠，并在山上建有称“伊姜”的堡垒式避难所。1783年6月26日，西班牙吞并巴丹群岛，1786年伊巴丹人被强迫从山居据点迁入低地城镇；西班牙人带来的石灰窑让他们建起独有的珊瑚石灰岩厚墙石屋以抵御风暴，古老的阿尼托祖灵崇拜也逐渐让位于天主教。

en: The Iwal are the people of nine inland villages in Morobe Province on the northeast coast of New Guinea, whose speech is an Austronesian language of the South Huon Gulf group and the most conservative member of that subgroup. Neighbouring Jabem speakers call them Kaiwa, meaning highlanders, and Iwal itself is their own name for themselves.
zh: 伊瓦克人居住在新几内亚东北海岸莫罗贝省的九个内陆村落，所说的伊瓦克语属南岛语系南休恩湾语支，是该语支中最保守的语言。邻近讲雅贝姆语的人称他们为凯瓦，意为高地人，伊瓦克则是他们的自称。

en: The Iwur, also called Murop, are a Papuan people of the lowland interior of Boven Digoel Regency in South Papua, living around the Iwur River near the headwaters of the Digul. Their Iwur language belongs to the Lowland Ok branch of the Ok family of Trans-New Guinea, close to the speech of the neighbouring Muyu.
zh: 伊乌尔人以其主要方言又称穆罗普人，是南巴布亚省博文迪古尔摄政区低地内陆的巴布亚族群，住在迪古尔河上游附近的伊乌尔河一带。他们的伊乌尔语属跨新几内亚语系奥克语系的低地奥克语支，与相邻木尤人的语言关系密切。

en: The Iyiniyu are the southern branch of the East Cree, the James Bay Cree whose homeland, Eeyou Istchee, lies east and southeast of James Bay in northern Quebec. Their self-name, Iyiniw, means human being in their Algonquian tongue, and they speak the southern East Cree dialects, divided between an inland form heard around Lake Mistassini, Waswanipi and Opemiska and a coastal form used at Waskaganish on Rupert Bay. Like other Cree they were subarctic hunter-gatherers, organized in small lodges and mobile bands that took caribou and moose, fished the lakes and rivers, and gathered seasonally rather than obeying any central chief. Their entry into written history came through the fur trade: in 1668 English traders built Charles Fort at the mouth of the Rupert River on the site of Waskaganish, the first Hudson's Bay Company trading post, two years before the company itself received its charter. Renamed Fort Rupert, the post drew southern East Cree bands into supplying furs and provisioning ships, making them middlemen between the bay and inland peoples through the eighteenth century.
zh: 伊伊尼尤人是东克里人的南支，即詹姆斯湾克里人，他们的家园“埃尤伊斯奇”位于魁北克北部詹姆斯湾以东和东南一带。他们自称“伊伊尼乌”，在其阿尔冈昆语中意为“人”，操东克里语南部方言，又分为米斯塔西尼湖、瓦斯瓦尼皮和奥佩米斯卡一带的内陆话，以及鲁珀特湾畔瓦斯卡加尼什的沿海话。和其他克里人一样，他们是亚寒带的狩猎采集者，以小型住户和流动群队为单位，猎捕驯鹿和驼鹿、在河湖捕鱼、按季节聚集，没有统辖一切的酋长。他们进入有文字记载的历史始于毛皮贸易：1668年，英国商人在鲁珀特河河口、今瓦斯卡加尼什所在地修建查尔斯堡，这是哈德逊湾公司的第一座贸易站，比公司本身获得特许状还早两年。该站后改名鲁珀特堡，吸引南支东克里群队供应毛皮、为船只提供给养，使他们在整个18世纪成为海湾与内陆民族之间的中间商。

en: The Iyiyiyu are the northern coastal branch of the East Cree, whose self-name Iiyiyuu, like the other Cree autonyms, derives from the word for human being. Their camps and later villages dotted the eastern shore of James Bay and the adjacent Hudson Bay coast, at Wemindji, Chisasibi and Whapmagoostui on the Great Whale River, within the wider Cree homeland of Eeyou Istchee in northern Quebec. They speak the northern coastal East Cree dialect of the Algonquian Cree continuum, and lived as nomadic subarctic hunter-gatherers in small bands, taking caribou, geese and seals and fishing the rivers before returning to coastal rendezvous. The Hudson's Bay Company trade reached them directly in 1803, when it founded Fort George at the mouth of the La Grande River, the waterway whose Cree name Great River gives Chisasibi its name; the post was moved to the island at the river mouth in 1837. Around such forts the northern East Cree traded furs and provisions and gradually shifted from seasonal rounds to settled communities.
zh: 伊伊以尤人是东克里人的北部沿海支系，自称“伊伊尤”，和其他克里人的自称一样源自意为“人”的词。他们的营地和后来的村落散布在詹姆斯湾东岸以及邻近的哈得孙湾沿岸，包括韦明吉、奇萨西比和大白鲸河畔的瓦普马古伊斯图伊，都属于魁北克北部克里人大家园“埃尤伊斯奇”的范围。他们操阿尔冈昆语族克里方言连续体中的东克里语北部沿海方言，以小群队过着游牧式的亚寒带狩猎采集生活，猎取驯鹿、雁和海豹，在河流捕鱼，然后回到沿海聚会点。哈德逊湾公司的贸易在1803年直接延伸到他们这里：公司在拉格朗德河河口设立乔治堡，这条河的克里语名意为“大河”，奇萨西比即由此得名；1837年商站迁到河口的岛上。围绕这些堡垒，北支东克里人交易毛皮和给养，并逐渐从随季节迁徙转向定居。

en: The Iztachichimecah, whom the Spanish called the White Chichimecs, were a Guamare group of the Guanajuato borderlands made up of several tribes who did not share one language, whose two leading tribes were the Xiconaques and Cuxtaques. They joined the Guamare confederation only shortly before the Spanish arrival, after long internal wars, and lived around Tlacuitlapán beside Caxcan and Tecuexe lordships.
zh: 伊斯塔奇奇梅卡人被西班牙人称为“白奇奇梅克人”，是瓜纳华托边地由若干部落组成的瓜马尔系族群，各部语言并不统一，两大主体部落为西科纳克人和库斯塔克人。他们在长期内战后，直到西班牙人到来前不久才加入瓜马尔联盟，居住在特拉奎特拉潘一带，与卡什坎人和特库埃克人的小邦相邻。

en: The Jabirr Jabirr are an Aboriginal Australian people of the western Dampier Peninsula in the Kimberley, whose tribal lands run along the coast from Beagle Bay south to Cape Bertholet. Their language is a Western Nyulnyulan tongue closely related to Nyulnyul, with which it may have been mutually intelligible.
zh: 贾比尔贾比尔人是金伯利地区丹皮尔半岛西部的澳大利亚原住民，部落地沿比格尔湾以南的海岸延伸至贝尔托莱角。他们的语言属西纽尔纽尔语支，与纽尔纽尔语关系极近，可能可以互通。

en: The Jaitmatang, also spelled Yaithmathang and often called the Omeo people, are an Aboriginal people of the alpine country of north-eastern Victoria, holding the upper Mitta Mitta River and the plains around Omeo. Their tongue, Yaithmathang, is treated by linguists as a dialect of Ngarigo within the Pama-Nyungan family, close to the languages of the neighbouring Ngarigo and Wolgal, and distinct from the Dhudhuroa spoken immediately to their north. Early ethnographers counted groups such as the Djilamatang among their hordes. Europeans first penetrated their highland lands in 1828, after which pastoral runs and then gold diggings overran the country and the Jaitmatang were nearly swept away within a generation.
zh: 贾特马唐人又译亚伊特马唐人，常被称为奥米奥人，是维多利亚州东北部阿尔卑斯山区的澳大利亚原住民，领有米塔米塔河上游与奥米奥周围的平原。他们的语言亚伊特马唐语被语言学者视为纳里戈语的一种方言，属帕马-尼永加语系，与邻近的纳里戈人和沃尔加尔人的语言相近，而不同于北面的杜杜罗阿语。早期民族学者把吉拉马唐等群体算作他们的分支。欧洲人于1828年首次深入他们的山地，随后牧场与金矿相继侵占这片土地，仅仅一代人的时间，贾特马唐人便几乎消亡。

en: Jama Coaque is an archaeological culture of the forested Pacific coast of Ecuador, named for the territory between the Coaque and Jama rivers in northern Manabí Province, where settlement mounds and richly detailed pottery trace a continuous development from about 355 BC to the Spanish conquest. Its people combined farming with fishing, hunting and gathering from sea and rainforest, and lived in planned villages of earthen mounds; the great ceremonial mound at San Isidro, near Bahía de Caráquez, headed a hierarchy of sites that included pyramid ramps at Don Juan and ceramic and metalworking kilns at Tabuga. During the Regional Development period the society was organized as civic-religious chiefdoms, which later confederated to control river valleys and long-distance trade. Jama Coaque artisans are best known for mold-made ceramic human figures with elaborate dress and removable nose and ear ornaments, alongside sacred jaguars, parrots and hybrid beings; unlike their northern neighbours of La Tolita, they favoured the human form. The Campaces people met by the conquistadors are thought to have been the last bearers of this tradition.
zh: 哈马科阿克是厄瓜多尔林木茂盛的太平洋沿岸的一支考古文化，得名于马纳维省北部科阿克河与哈马河之间的地区；那里的人工土墩遗址和精细丰富的陶器显示，它从约公元前355年到西班牙征服期间延续发展了近两千年。其居民兼营农业与渔捞、狩猎，从海洋和雨林中获取资源，住在按规划排列的土墩村落里；卡拉克斯港附近圣伊西德罗遗址的巨大礼仪土墩统辖着一批等级化遗址，其中包括唐胡安带坡道的金字塔，以及塔布加的制陶和冶金窑址。在区域发展时期，其社会以政教合一的酋邦形式组织，后来各酋邦结成联盟，控制河谷并经营长途贸易。哈马科阿克工匠最著名的作品是模制陶人像，服饰繁复，鼻饰和耳饰可以拆卸；此外还有被视为神物的美洲豹、鹦鹉以及人兽合体的形象——与北方邻邦拉托利塔文化不同，他们更偏爱表现人形。征服者遇到的坎帕塞斯人被认为就是这一传统最后的承载者。

en: The Jamindjung, also spelt Djamindjung or Jaminjung, are an Indigenous Australian people of the Northern Territory, whose country lies between the north bank of the Victoria River and the south bank of the Fitzmaurice River, stretching about a hundred miles inland from the Timor Sea. Norman Tindale estimated their territory at some 7,000 square kilometres, running from the upper and middle Fitzmaurice to the Vambarra range and Umyxera Creek, with its southern limit at Timber Creek on the Victoria, and taking in Bradshaw and the Angalarri River. Their language belongs to the Yirram branch of the Mirndi family and is closest to the speech of the Ngaliwurru. The first European to reach their coastline was Phillip Parker King, who came to the mouth of the Victoria River on 12 September 1819 during his survey of the northern coast.
zh: 贾敏琼人（又译贾明琼）是澳大利亚北领地的原住民，领地位于维多利亚河北岸与菲茨莫里斯河南岸之间，从帝汶海向内陆延伸约100英里。诺曼·廷代尔估算其领地约7000平方公里，从菲茨莫里斯河上中游一直到万巴拉山脉和乌米克塞拉溪，南界在维多利亚河上的廷伯克里克，还包括布拉德肖和安加拉里河。他们的语言属明迪语系的伊拉姆语支，与恩加利伍鲁人的话最接近。最早抵达他们海岸的欧洲人是菲利普·帕克·金，1819年9月12日，他在考察北部海岸期间来到维多利亚河口。

en:
The Jardwadjalian are the Jardwadjali people of the upper Wimmera River country in western Victoria, their lands reaching east to the Gariwerd ranges, which settlers later named the Grampians, and west toward Lake Bringalbert. Human occupation of the Gariwerd shelters goes back more than twenty thousand years, and for the Jardwadjali and their Djab Wurrung neighbours the mountains are the heart of the Dreaming of the creator Bunjil and the two Bram brothers, who shaped and named the landforms of western Victoria. Their language shared roughly ninety percent of its vocabulary with Djab Wurrung and was mutually intelligible with it, divided into the Jagwadjali, Mardidjali and Nundadjali sub-dialects.

Epidemics reached them long before settlers did: smallpox brought by the First Fleet in 1788 travelled along the Aboriginal trade routes and down the Murray in two waves, the Wotjobaluk calling the scourge thinba micka, and by the time of European arrival the Jaadwa bands were shifting south toward the sites of later Casterton and Hamilton. In 1836 Major Thomas Mitchell crossed their country and renamed Gariwerd after the Grampian hills of Scotland, his enthusiastic reports of Australia Felix drawing the first squatters in his wake, with Edward Henty pushing up from Portland Bay in the same year.
zh:
贾德瓦贾里人即史实上的贾德瓦贾里族群，居于维多利亚州西部威默拉河上游地区，疆域东抵加里沃德山脉（移民后称格兰扁山脉），西达布林加伯特湖一带。人类在加里沃德山岩棚下的居住史超过两万年；对贾德瓦贾里人和相邻的贾布伍伦人而言，这座山是创世者本吉尔与布拉姆两兄弟梦幻传说的核心，正是他们塑造并命名了维多利亚西部的山川地貌。他们的语言与贾布伍伦语约有九成词汇相通、可以互相听懂，下分贾格瓦贾里、马迪贾里和农达贾里等次方言。

疫病比移民早得多就降临到他们身上：1788年第一舰队带来的天花沿原住民商路、顺墨累河两度传播，沃乔巴卢克人把这场瘟疫称作“辛巴·米卡”；等到欧洲人现身时，贾德瓦群体已在向南迁徙，逼近后来的卡斯特顿和汉密尔顿一带。1836年，托马斯·米切尔少校穿过他们的土地，以苏格兰的格兰扁丘陵为加里沃德重新命名，他对“幸运澳大利亚”的热情报道引来最早的占地牧场主，爱德华·亨提也在同年从波特兰湾向北推进。

en: The Djaru, or Jaru, are an Aboriginal people of the southern and south-eastern Kimberley in Western Australia, divided into groups such as the Margaret River Djaru and the northern Kodjangana. Their language is a Ngumbin tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family, kin to Walmajarri: it distinguishes single, dual and plural pronouns, has no noun genders and relatively free word order, and pairs a small set of verbs with preverbs to build complex meanings. It also contains a sign vocabulary used in hunting, directions being given by pointing the lips, and an avoidance register, the so-called mother-in-law speech, built around a single neutral verb. On their country stands Wolfe Creek Crater, which the Djaru call Kandimalal; Dreaming stories explain its round rim as the passage of a rainbow serpent from the earth, or as the place where the hot evening star fell from the sky.
zh: 贾鲁人又称贾鲁，是西澳大利亚金伯利南部和东南部的原住民，内部分为玛格丽特河贾鲁、北部科贾纳加纳等群体。他们的语言属于帕马‑牛雅语系的恩贡宾语支，与瓦尔马贾里语同源：代词分单数、双数和复数，名词没有性别，语序相当自由，动词数量不多，靠前置词与动词组合表达复杂含义。语言中还有一套狩猎时使用的手势词汇，以努嘴指示方向，并有一个围绕单个中性动词构成的回避语体，即所谓的岳母话。其领地上矗立着沃尔夫溪陨石坑，贾鲁人称之为坎迪马拉尔；在梦境传说中，它圆形的坑缘是彩虹蛇钻出大地留下的通道，也有说法认为这里是灼热的昏星从天而降的地方。

en: The Jasz are the Alanic community that survived inside the Kingdom of Hungary, descendants of Sarmatian Alans of the Pontic steppe who fled the Mongol conquest in the mid-thirteenth century. Admitted with the Cumans by King Béla IV, who hoped to use their cavalry against the Tatars, they first quarrelled with the Hungarian nobility and withdrew, then returned after the Mongol tide receded to settle the plains between the Zagyva and Tarna rivers. Their district became known as Jászság, with Jászberény as its center, where the Hungarian crown allowed them to govern themselves under their own privileges while keeping to pastoral life. A related Alanic group farther east gave its name to the market town of Jászvásár, later Iași in Moldavia. In Hungary the old Jassic tongue, a dialect of the Eastern Iranian language that became Ossetian, was no longer spoken by the sixteenth century as the Jasz adopted Hungarian, though they kept a strong separate identity. Ottoman rule covered Jászság in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries until Habsburg reconquest, and when Emperor Leopold I sold their liberties to the Teutonic Order the Jasz raised a huge ransom, winning the Act of Redemption of 1745 from Maria Theresa, which restored their self-government.
zh: 亚什人是阿兰人遗留在匈牙利王国境内的一支，先民是黑海草原上说伊朗语的萨尔马提亚系阿兰人，13世纪中叶为躲避蒙古征服而西迁。匈牙利国王贝拉四世接纳了他们和库曼人，想借其骑兵抵抗鞑靼人；他们起初与匈牙利贵族冲突而离去，蒙古退兵后又返回，定居在扎吉瓦河与塔尔纳河之间的平原。其聚居区后来称亚什沙格，以亚什贝雷尼为中心；匈牙利国王准许他们在那里凭特权自治，维持游牧生活。更东边的一支同源阿兰人则把自己的名字留给了集市小镇亚什瓦萨尔，即后来摩尔达维亚的雅西。在匈牙利，古老的亚什语（后来演变为奥塞梯语的东伊朗语方言）到16世纪已无人使用，亚什人改说匈牙利语，但保留了强烈的独特身份认同。16至17世纪，亚什沙格处于奥斯曼统治之下，其后被哈布斯堡王朝重新征服；皇帝利奥波德一世把他们的自治权卖给条顿骑士团后，亚什人筹集了巨额赎金，于1745年换取玛丽亚·特蕾西亚颁布《赎买法令》，恢复了他们的自治地位。

en: The Javanese are the Austronesian people of central and eastern Java, from the fertile slopes of Mount Merapi to the Brantas delta, whose language is the largest tongue of the Austronesian family. Indian traders brought Hinduism and Buddhism from the fifth century, and the old Mataram kingdom of the Sanjaya and Sailendra dynasties raised Borobudur and Prambanan in the eighth and ninth centuries. In 1293 Raden Wijaya founded Majapahit at Trowulan, and under Hayam Wuruk and his minister Gajah Mada, between 1350 and 1389, its sway ran across much of maritime South-East Asia. Islam then took root in the northern ports of Demak, Tuban and Gresik, spread by the nine saints known as the Wali Songo; after Majapahit's collapse the Demak sultanate dominated the coast and contested the Portuguese capture of Malacca. Power moved inland through Pajang to the Mataram Sultanate at Kotagede, which reached its height under Sultan Agung from 1613 to 1645 after the fall of Surabaya. The Dutch had built Batavia in 1619, and wars of succession drew the Dutch East India Company ever deeper into Javanese politics until Mataram split into the Surakarta and Yogyakarta courts. Prince Diponegoro's Java War of 1825 to 1830 ended in defeat and the reduction of both courts to dependencies of the Dutch East Indies.
zh: 爪哇人是爪哇岛中东部的南岛语系民族，分布在从默拉皮火山的肥沃山坡到布兰塔斯三角洲的广大地区，其语言是南岛语系中使用人数最多的语言。5世纪起，印度商人带来印度教和佛教，珊阇耶与夏连特拉两朝的古马打兰王国在8、9世纪修筑了婆罗浮屠和普兰巴南。1293年，拉登·韦查耶在特洛武兰建立满者伯夷，1350至1389年哈奄·武禄与大臣加查·马达在位时，其势力遍及海洋东南亚的大片土地。此后伊斯兰教在淡目、图班、锦石等北部港口扎根，由号称“九圣”的瓦利松戈传教士传播；满者伯夷崩溃后，淡目苏丹国称霸沿海，并与夺取马六甲的葡萄牙人抗衡。权力重心经巴章深入内陆，落到以哥打格德为都的马打兰苏丹国，1613至1645年苏丹阿贡在位时，于征服泗水后达到鼎盛。荷兰人已于1619年建巴达维亚城，连绵的继承战争把荷兰东印度公司步步卷入爪哇政局，马打兰最终分裂为梭罗与日惹两个宫廷。1825至1830年蒂博尼哥罗亲王领导的爪哇战争以失败告终，两个宫廷都被削弱为荷属东印度的附庸。

en: The Jiānghuái culture fills the country between the Yangtze and the Huai rivers, from Nanjing and Zhenjiang to Gaoyou and the hills of eastern Hubei, and speaks Jianghuai or Lower Yangtze Mandarin, which keeps a glottal stop where most other Mandarin dialects lost the old entering tone. When the north fell in the fourth century, refugees from the Central Plains flooded into Jiankang, present-day Nanjing, and a second wave of northern migrants during the Song wars formed the basis of the local speech. The region's fortune rose with the Ming: Zhu Yuanzhang took Jiqing in 1356 and renamed it Yingtian, then founded his dynasty at Nanjing in 1368, and the Jianghuai-based Nanjing koiné became the administrative Guanhua of the early Ming court. Even after the Yongle Emperor moved the capital to Beijing in 1421, Nanjing pronunciation kept its prestige into the seventeenth century. Under the Qing the city became Jiangning prefecture in 1645, while Jianghuai and northern Mandarin together formed the standard of the written vernacular.
zh: 江淮文化分布在长江与淮河之间，从南京、镇江到高邮乃至湖北东部丘陵，所说的江淮官话又称下江官话，在其他官话已经消失的古入声字上仍保留喉塞音韵尾。4世纪北方沦陷后，中原流民大量涌入建康（今南京）；宋金战争期间又有一波北方移民南下，奠定了当地话的底子。这一地区的命运随明朝攀上顶峰：朱元璋于1356年攻取集庆，改名应天，1368年在南京开国，以江淮话为底子的南京音成为明初官场通行的官话。1421年永乐帝迁都北京后，南京音的声望仍延续到17世纪。清代，南京于1645年改为江宁府，江淮官话与北方官话则一同构成了白话文的标准基础。

en: The Jiāngshān culture straddles the Zhejiang-Jiangxi border in the tangled mountains at the headwaters of the Qiantang, taking in Jiangshan, Changshan and Kaihua west of Quzhou together with Yushan, Guangfeng and Shangrao in northeastern Jiangxi. In ancient times the country belonged to Gumie and then Yue, and under the Qin in 222 BC it fell under Taimo County; the Tang founded Xijiang County here in 621, which the Wuyue kingdom renamed Jiangshan in 931, a name restored under the Yuan in 1276. Through its hills runs the Xianxia Pass road, the historic track between the Zhejiang coast and the Min river valleys of Fujian. The culture is bound together less by administration than by speech: its varieties form the Shangshan branch of Southern Wu, holding the westernmost edge of the entire Wu world at Shangrao, where Gan Chinese begins a few counties to the west. Long cut off by mountains, these county dialects diverged sharply from one another and stay only partly intelligible with the Wu of the coastal plains.
zh: 江山文化横跨浙赣边界，地处钱塘江源头的丛山之中，既包括衢州以西的江山、常山、开化，也包括赣东北的玉山、广丰和上饶。上古这里属姑蔑，后归越国，公元前222年秦代划入太末县；621年唐代置须江县，931年吴越国改名为江山县，1276年元代复名江山。仙霞岭古道穿境而过，是浙江沿海通往福建闽江流域的传统山路。把这一文化连起来的主要不是行政建制，而是方言：当地口音构成南部吴语的上山小片，上饶正处在整个吴语区的最西缘，再往西几个县便改说赣语。由于长期被山岭阻隔，各县方言分化剧烈，与沿海平原的吴语只能部分相通。

en: The Jiànníng are the inland Min people of the Wuyi Mountains in northern Fujian, centred on the old prefectural seats of Jian'ou and Jianyang in present-day Nanping. Their Northern Min speech counts among the earliest-formed Chinese dialects of Fujian. After the Han conquered the Minyue kingdom in 110 BC and moved its people to the Yangtze–Huai basin, garrison troops from the Wu and Chu regions settled the Wuyi foothills and blended their old eastern dialects with the indigenous Yue substrate. In 203 the Han set up Jian'an commandery at present-day Jian'ou, which remained the political centre of northern Fujian under the later names of Jianzhou and Jianning prefecture. Refugees of the fourth-century Yongjia disorders and the late-Tang armies of the Wang brothers, who founded the Min kingdom in 909, added further layers; in 943 Wang Yanzheng held Jianzhou as emperor of the breakaway Yin. By the early Song the local speech was already distinct from the dialects of Fuzhou and Quanzhou. Mid-Ming uprisings led to the creation of Yong'an county in 1452, after which the Shaxian and Yong'an dialects drifted into the separate Central Min group, and in 1795 the Jianning authorities printed the rhyme dictionary Jianzhou bayin to record the prestige Jian'ou pronunciation.
zh: 建宁人是福建北部武夷山山区的内陆闽系居民，中心在今南平市境内历代郡州府治所建瓯和建阳一带，所说的闽北话是福建境内形成最早的汉语方言之一。公元前110年汉朝攻灭闽越国，把闽越人迁往江淮流域，来自吴、楚故地的驻军在武夷山脚下定居，把古吴语、古楚语与当地闽越语底层融合起来。203年东汉于今建瓯设建安郡，此地先后以建州、建宁府为名，长期是闽北的政治文化中心。4世纪永嘉之乱的难民、唐末王氏兄弟于909年建立闽国时带入的中原话音，又叠加出新的语言层次；943年王延政据建州称帝，建号殷。到宋初，建州方言已与福州、泉州话明显有别。明代中叶民变之后，朝廷于1452年析沙县置永安县，沙县、永安一带的话后来演变为独立的闽中语；1795年建宁府刊行韵书《建州八音》，记录了作为闽北代表音的建瓯话音系。

en: The Jiāodōng are the people of the Shandong Peninsula, the hilly tongue of land east of Jiaozhou that juts between the Bohai Sea and the Yellow Sea. In antiquity it was the country of the Dongyi state of Lai, whose fishermen and salt-boilers traded along the rocky coast; Qi annexed Lai in 567 BC and built its eastern wall across the peninsula, the Qin ruled it as Qi Commandery, and the Han through the Donglai Commandery and the Jiaodong Kingdom, while the First Emperor visited Zhifu on his eastern tours. Fishing, salt, iron smelting and silk made it the granary of the East under the Han, and under the Tang the ports of Dengzhou and Laizhou handled the sea trade with Korea and Japan. Its people speak Jiaoliao Mandarin, a dialect carried across the gulf to Liaodong and Manchuria by generations of emigrants. Ming rule brought war to the coast: watchtowers such as the one raised at Yantai in 1398 signaled the wokou raids, and garrison guards like Lingshanwei were settled to defend the shore, while the sea ban uprooted fishing villages and drove their trade underground; under the Qing, Jiaozhou grew into the leading trading port of northern China.
zh: 胶东人是山东半岛上的居民，这片丘陵之地在胶州以东，伸入渤海与黄海之间。上古时这里是东夷莱国的疆土，莱人在岩岸间以捕鱼和煮盐为业；公元前567年齐国攻灭莱国，沿半岛修筑齐长城东段，秦代设齐郡，汉代设东莱郡和胶东国进行统治，秦始皇东巡还曾登临芝罘。渔盐、冶铁和丝织之利使这里在汉代成为“东方谷仓”；唐代，登州、莱州是通往朝鲜、日本的海上贸易港口。当地人说胶辽官话，一代又一代移民渡海而去，把这种方言带到了辽东和满洲。明代海疆多事：1398年烟台一带筑起狼烟墩台瞭望倭寇，灵山卫等卫所驻军守岸，海禁又迫使渔村内迁、贸易转入地下；入清以后，胶州发展为中国北方首屈一指的贸易港口。

en: The Jìlǔ are the plain-dwellers of southern Hebei and central and northern Shandong who speak Jilu Mandarin, the northern dialect closest to the speech of Beijing. Their country is the old Qilu land of the North China Plain, crossed by the lower Yellow River and the Grand Canal and watched over by Mount Tai. Its earliest inhabitants were the Dongyi peoples, who were absorbed when the state of Qi conquered the Lai in 567 BC; alongside Qi stood the small state of Lu at Qufu, where Confucius was born in the sixth century BC, making the region the cradle of Confucian teaching and a landscape of temples and pilgrimage. Under the Han it was organized into the Qingzhou and Yanzhou inspectorates, and in 412 the monk Faxian landed at Laoshan bearing the Buddhist scriptures he had brought from India. The Ming created the modern Shandong Province here and in 1376 moved its capital from Qingzhou to Jinan, while also administering Liaodong across the gulf from the same province. The seventeenth century brought unrest: in 1633 the Dengzhou generals Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming defected to the Manchus with their troops, and White Lotus peasant uprisings spread through the province by 1640.
zh: 冀鲁人是河北南部和山东中北部的平原居民，说冀鲁官话，这是除东北官话外与北京话最接近的北方方言。他们的乡土是华北平原上的齐鲁故地，黄河下游与大运河穿行其间，泰山屹立于此。这里最早的居民是东夷诸部，公元前567年齐国攻灭莱国后逐渐被同化；与齐并存的还有建都曲阜的小国鲁国，孔子于公元前6世纪诞生于此，使这一带成为儒学的摇篮，祠庙林立、拜谒不绝。汉代这里分属青州、兖州刺史部；412年，高僧法显携自印度取回的经卷在牢山登陆。明代在这片地区设立现在的山东省，1376年把省会从青州迁往济南，并隔海兼领辽东。17世纪这里动荡不宁：1633年登州将领孔有德、耿仲明率部投奔满洲，到1640年，白莲教农民起义已在全省蔓延。

en: The Jìn culture is the people of the Shanxi plateau, the loess country east of the Yellow River's great bend, walled by the Taihang mountains in the east and the Lüliang range in the west. In the Spring and Autumn period it was the heartland of the state of Jin, whose partition into Han, Zhao and Wei in 403 BCE opened the Warring States era; later the Xianbei Northern Wei kept their early capital at Datong before ruling all of northern China. Under the Ming, Shanxi took its present borders and became a military frontier facing the Mongol steppe, with Datong among the chief garrison commands of the Great Wall. Peace and the border trade raised its merchants into the great Jin merchants of the Ming and Qing, whose caravans carried tea and cloth to Mongolia, Russia and Central Asia and whose draft banks handled the empire's inter-provincial tax remittances; the first of these banks, Rishengchang, opened at Pingyao in 1823. Their spoken language, Jin Chinese, alone among the major speeches of northern China preserves the old entering tone.
zh: 晋文化的主体是山西高原居民，即黄河大拐弯以东、东依太行山、西凭吕梁山的黄土地居民。春秋时期，这里是晋国的核心地带；公元前403年晋国被韩、赵、魏三家瓜分，由此进入战国时代。后来鲜卑人的北魏以大同为早期都城，进而统治整个北方。明代，山西形成近似今天的省界，成为面对蒙古草原的军镇边疆，大同是长城沿线最重要的戍防重镇之一。和平与边贸造就了明清两代称雄中国的晋商：驼队把茶叶、布匹运往蒙古、俄罗斯和中亚，票号则承接帝国各省之间的税银汇兑；第一家票号日升昌于1823年在平遥开业。他们所说的晋语是中国北方各大方言中唯一保留古入声的一支。

en: The Jingili, or Jingulu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory whose country lay around Elliott, called Kulumindini in their tongue, and the natural springs of Daly Waters and Newcastle Waters; they are also joint traditional owners of the lancewood scrub country of the Bullwaddy reserve. Their own oral tradition holds that the Jingili originally migrated from the Great Western Desert. Their language, Jingulu, is an isolate branch of the non-Pama-Nyungan Mirndi family and forms, with Wambaya, Gudanji, Binbinka and Ngarnka, the West Barkly group, and the Jingili kept a well-developed sign language alongside speech. They tell of the Dreaming tracks of the Emu and the Sun passing through Daly Waters, and their later fusion with incoming Mudburra people produced the Kuwarrangu group while the two cultures remained distinct.
zh: 金吉利人（自称金乌鲁）是北领地的澳大利亚原住民，领地在他们称作库卢明迪尼的埃利奥特以及戴利沃特、纽卡斯尔沃特的天然泉群一带，也是布尔瓦迪枪木灌丛地区的共同传统所有者。他们口耳相传，祖先从大西沙漠迁徙而来。金吉利语是非帕马‑牛雅米尔恩迪语系的孤立分支，与万巴亚语、古丹吉语、宾宾卡语和纳兰卡语同属西巴克利语群；除口语外，他们还保有一套发达的手语。他们传说鸸鹋与太阳的梦创足迹经过戴利沃特；后来迁入的穆德巴拉人与他们交融，形成库瓦兰古群体，而两种文化仍各自保持独立。

en: The Jingpo, who call themselves Jinghpaw and are the largest of the Kachin peoples, are a Tibeto-Burman people of the forested Kachin Hills around Putao and the upper Nmai River, spanning the border of northern Myanmar and Yunnan, with a related branch, the Singpho, in Assam. Their ancestors came south from the Tibetan plateau and were recorded in Yunnan as the Xunchuanman, while Chinese sources from the Yuan dynasty of 1271 to 1368 long called them Yeren, the wild people. During the 1400s and 1500s they moved into the hill country of the upper Irrawaddy, and the Ming, who held China from 1368, recognized their polity there as a tusi chiefdom; the Ming Veritable Records call it Cha-shan, a domain running from the Nmai River east to Lushui in Yunnan. In the 1600s their chiefs profited from the carrying trade between the Ahom kingdom and China in ivory, copper and silver. Organized under clan chiefs, they lived in two-story bamboo longhouses, farmed hill gardens where tea was grown from at least the 1100s, and followed an animist religion of ubiquitous spirits headed by Madai, whose priests officiated at sowing, harvest and warfare.
zh: 景颇人自称景颇，是克钦诸族中人数最多的一支，属藏缅语民族，散居在葡萄和恩梅开江上游林木茂密的克钦山区，地跨缅甸北部与云南，在印度阿萨姆还有一支同源族裔。其先民从青藏高原南迁，在云南被记作寻传蛮，1271至1368年元代以后的汉文文献则长期称之为野人。15世纪至16世纪，他们迁入伊洛瓦底江上游的山地，1368年建立的明朝承认当地政权为土司，《明实录》称之为茶山，辖境西起恩梅开江、东至云南泸水。17世纪，景颇首领靠阿洪王国与中国之间的转运贸易获利，货品包括象牙、铜和白银。他们在氏族首领统属下聚居，住两层的竹木结构长屋，在山地园圃务农，至少从12世纪起就已种茶，并信奉万物有灵，以为神灵无处不在，以木代神为尊，由祭司主持播种、收获和征战的仪式。

en: The Jino, whose autonym means the people who honour the maternal uncle and was formerly rendered Youle, are a small Tibeto-Burman people of the Jino Mountains in eastern Jinghong in Xishuangbanna, a belt of subtropical rainforest famous since the late Ming for its Pu'er tea gardens. Han tea merchants began arriving in the seventeenth century, bringing new farming techniques, and in 1729 the Qing Yongzheng emperor built a brick city there and stationed five hundred soldiers; the garrison was soon withdrawn because of the malarial climate, and rule passed first to a Youle native chief and then to the Dai tusi of Cheli, who annexed it by force. They speak Jino, a Yi-branch Tibeto-Burman language without a script, keeping records by carved wooden notches, and live by hill farming, hunting, ironworking and bamboo weaving. Their society long kept matrilineal traces, and their creation epics tell of the flood siblings Mahei and Maniu and of the ancestress Yaobai, who shaped heaven and earth and scattered the tea seeds that made their mountains rich.
zh: 基诺人自称基诺，旧译攸乐，意为尊敬舅舅的民族，是西双版纳景洪东部基诺山中人口不多的藏缅语族民族；山中属亚热带雨林，自明末起便以普洱茶园闻名。17世纪，汉地茶商陆续进山，也带来了新的农耕技艺；1729年清雍正皇帝在当地修筑砖城、屯兵五百，但因瘴气太重很快裁撤，此后先设攸乐土司，继而被车里的傣族土司以武力兼并统治。基诺语属藏缅语族彝语支，没有本民族文字，过去靠刻木记事；他们以山地农耕、狩猎为生，兼营打铁与竹篾编织。基诺社会长期保留母系制遗风，创世史诗讲述洪水后的兄妹玛黑、玛妞，以及女始祖尧白开天辟地、撒下茶籽使群山富庶的故事。

en: The Jirajara, who called themselves the Xideharas, were an Indigenous people of the mountains and valleys of western Venezuela, in what are now Falcón, Lara and Yaracuy; tradition holds that they moved there from the shores of Lake Maracaibo. They lived in small, densely settled villages under patriarchal extended families and elder caciques, farming, hunting and gathering with little contact with neighbouring peoples, whom they treated as enemies. The German explorer Ambrosio Alfinger first noted them in the Serranía del Empalado in 1529, and Nicolaus Federmann crossed their lands in 1530. In 1553 Jirajara labourers joined the enslaved black miners of San Felipe de Buría in the revolt led by Miguel de Buría, who was crowned king of a mountain cumbe before Spanish troops stormed the refuge and killed him. Settlers then branded resisting Jirajaras as caribes to justify enslaving them, and long failed to take the gold-bearing Nirgua province, where the Jirajara repelled every incursion until Governor Juan de Meneses y Padilla defeated them in 1628. The town of Siquisique was founded among them in about 1685, and their tongue, closely related to Ayomán, survives only in colonial word lists as one of the isolated Jirajaran languages.
zh: 希拉哈拉人自称西德哈拉人，是委内瑞拉西部山地和山谷的原住民，分布在今法尔孔、拉腊和亚拉奎一带；相传他们是从马拉开波湖畔迁徙而来。他们住在人口稠密的小村落里，社会以父系大家族和年长的酋长为核心，务农、狩猎兼采集，与邻族往来很少，多视其为仇敌。1529年，德国探险家安布罗西奥·阿尔芬格在恩帕拉多山脉首次记下他们的踪迹；1530年，尼科劳斯·费德曼率军穿过他们的土地。1553年，希拉哈拉劳工与圣费利佩-德布里亚的黑人矿工一起，参加米格尔·德布里亚领导的起义；米格尔被拥戴为山中逃亡据点昆贝的王，直到西班牙军队攻破据点将他杀死。此后殖民者把坚持抵抗的希拉哈拉人诬称为加勒比人，以便名正言顺地奴役他们；盛产黄金的尼尔瓜省长期无法攻克，希拉哈拉人击退了一次次入侵，直到1628年被总督胡安·德梅内塞斯-帕迪利亚击败。约1685年，西班牙人在他们中间建立锡基西克镇；他们的语言与阿约曼语关系密切，只在殖民时代编成的词汇表中留下记录，被视为孤立的希拉哈拉诸语之一。

en: Jixi denotes the Ji-She branch of Hui Chinese, the speech of the historical Huizhou Prefecture in the mountainous south of Anhui, centred on Jixi and She counties and reaching into Ningguo and Jingde, with Chun'an across the Zhejiang border. Jixi itself was established as a county in 776 under the Tang dynasty. Hui dialects took shape as the Chinese brought by migrants from the Central Plains absorbed elements of the language of the indigenous Shanyue peoples; hemmed in between Wu and Gan, their classification has long been disputed. Jixihua is the leading variety of the Ji-She branch and shows clear Wu influence, and the speech of She county once served as the representative pronunciation of Huizhou speech. During the Ming and Qing dynasties Huizhou merchants carried the dialect across the empire, while newcomers speaking Jianghuai Mandarin settled in the region, widening an already sharp internal variation in which neighbouring townships could be mutually unintelligible.
zh: 绩溪指徽语的绩歙片，通行于皖南山区的古徽州府，以绩溪、歙县为中心，延伸到宁国、旌德一带，并越过省界分布于浙江淳安；绩溪本县于唐代776年建县。徽语是历代中原移民带来的汉语吸收当地土著山越语言成分而形成，夹在吴语与赣语之间，归属历来有争议。绩溪话是绩歙片的代表方言，带有明显的吴语影响；旧时徽语即以歙县县城话为代表音。明清两代，徽商足迹遍布全国，把家乡话带到各地，而说江淮官话的移民也迁入徽州地区，使本就分歧严重、邻乡之间往往难以通话的徽语内部分化进一步加大。

en: The Jola, who call themselves Ajamat and are often written Diola in French sources, are a West Atlantic people of the mangrove coasts and river flats of Lower Casamance in southern Senegal, with kindred communities in Gambia and Guinea-Bissau. They are heirs to a wet-rice civilization at least a thousand years old, farming flooded paddies alongside palm-wine tapping and livestock herding, and they probably entered the Casamance in the 1300s, absorbing the earlier Bainuk people and their rice-growing lore. Unlike the stratified kingdoms around them, most Jola villages kept an egalitarian order of family and neighbourhood wards led by elders, though Oussouye was ruled by a priest-king whose office was more sacred than secular. Their ancestral faith addresses a single high being, Emit, through village shrines and water spirits, and boys enter manhood through the bukut initiation held once in a generation; in later centuries Mandinka neighbours brought Islam to the better-connected Jola communities.
zh: 约拉人自称阿贾马特，法国文献中常写作迪奥拉人，是说西非大西洋语支语言的民族，居住在塞内加尔南部下卡萨芒斯的红树林海岸与河洲滩地上，在冈比亚和几内亚比绍也有亲缘社群。他们承袭着至少有一千年历史的水稻文明，在淹水稻田中耕作，兼事采棕榈酒和畜牧；他们大约在14世纪进入卡萨芒斯，融合了更早的拜努克人及其稻作技艺。与周围等级森严的王国不同，多数约拉村庄维持平等秩序，由长老统领家族和邻里，只有乌苏耶由一位祭司式的国王治理，其职位的宗教色彩远重于世俗权力。他们的传统信仰透过村庄神龛和水神敬拜至高神埃米特，男子要通过每隔一代人举行一次的布库特成年礼才算成人；此后几个世纪里，相邻的曼丁哥人把伊斯兰教带到了交通便利的约拉社区。

en: The Juang are an Austroasiatic people of the Gonsaika and Gonasika hills in Keonjhar, Odisha, whose Munda language is closest to Kharia; their tradition places their origin at Gonasika, source of the Baitarani River. Once called Patuas or leaf-wearers for their women's leaf girdles, they lived from the forest and bartered their woven baskets for salt, oil and food.
zh: 朱昂人是奥里萨凯翁贾尔贡赛卡和戈纳西卡丘陵的南亚语系族群，所用蒙达语与卡里亚语最接近；本族传说把发源地定在拜塔拉尼河源头的戈纳西卡山。他们曾被邻族称为“帕图阿”，即“披树叶的人”，因为妇女以树叶围腰；他们靠山林物产为生，把编织的篮子拿去换取盐、油和粮食。

en: The Djukun, or Jukun, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Kimberley coast of Western Australia, whose country centres on the town site of Broome and the shores of Roebuck Bay, shared with the neighbouring Yawuru. Their language is an Eastern Nyulnyulan tongue closely related to Yawuru. The bay's rich tidal flats drew seasonal gatherings of neighbouring groups to exchange gifts, arrange marriages and settle disputes, and shellfish middens still mark the old camping sites along its red pindan cliffs. In 1699 the English navigator William Dampier explored this coast in HMS Roebuck, after which the bay was named.
zh: 朱昆人是西澳大利亚金伯利海岸的原住民，家园以布鲁姆镇址和罗布克湾沿岸为中心，与邻族亚乌鲁人共享这片海湾。他们的语言属东纽尔纽尔语支，与亚乌鲁语亲缘很近。海湾富饶的潮间滩涂吸引邻近族群季节性聚会，交换礼物、缔结婚约、调解纠纷，红色品丹崖岸上的贝丘标示着旧日的营地。1699年，英国航海家威廉·丹皮尔乘“罗巴克号”考察这段海岸，罗布克湾便得名于他的船。

en: The Jurchens were the Tungusic-speaking tribes of Manchuria, formed in part from Mohe groups left behind after the fall of the Balhae kingdom in 926. They lived by hunting and fishing, pig farming, semi-nomadic pastoralism and scattered agriculture in the forests and river valleys of the Liao, Songhua and Amur, with no central authority binding their clans. The Wanyan clan built a tribal federation under Wugunai in the eleventh century, and in 1115 its chieftain Wanyan Aguda rebelled against the Khitan Liao dynasty and proclaimed the Jin dynasty; the chancellor Wanyan Xiyin devised a Jurchen script in 1119 or 1120, modelled on Khitan and Chinese writing. The Jin destroyed the Liao in 1125, seized northern China from the Song and ruled it until the Mongols overran the empire in 1234. The Jurchens who remained in Manchuria then passed under Mongol and, from 1368, Ming rule; the Ming classified them as Jianzhou, Haixi and Yeren groups, enrolled their chiefs in some four hundred tributary guards and ran the Nurgan Command Post from 1409 to 1434, with the eunuch Yishiha sailing the Amur and erecting bilingual steles. From the 1580s the Jianzhou leader Nurhaci united the tribes and organized them into the Eight Banners, and in 1635 his son Hong Taiji renamed the whole people Manchus.
zh: 女真是满洲地区说通古斯语的诸部，部分源自926年渤海国灭亡后留在故地的靺鞨人。他们在辽河、松花江和黑龙江的森林与河谷中以渔猎、养猪、半游牧和零星农耕为生，各部互不统属。11世纪，完颜部在乌古乃领导下结成部落联盟；1115年，首领完颜阿骨打起兵反契丹辽朝，建立金朝，大臣完颜希尹又于1119或1120年参照契丹文和汉字创制女真文。金朝于1125年攻灭辽朝，从宋朝手中夺取中国北方，统治到1234年被蒙古所灭。留在满洲的女真人先后受蒙古和1368年建立的明朝管辖；明朝把他们分为建州、海西、野人三大部，将各部首领编入约四百个朝贡卫所，并于1409至1434年设奴儿干都司，宦官亦失哈曾远航黑龙江并竖立双语石碑。16世纪80年代起，建州首领努尔哈赤统一女真各部，将其编入八旗；1635年，其子皇太极把全体族众改名为满洲。

en: The K'omoks, also spelled Comox, are the northernmost of the Coast Salish peoples, centred on the Comox Valley of eastern Vancouver Island and the inlets of the adjacent mainland, where their kinsmen lived as the Tla'amin, Klahoose and Homalco groups. Their language, Ayajuthem, belongs to the Coast Salishan branch, and their culture blended Salish customs with those of the Kwakwaka'wakw to the north: they were famed canoe builders and carvers, raised petroglyphs on Chrome Island, and distributed wealth in potlatches held at winter villages such as the Whale House on Quadra Island. A smallpox epidemic reached them indirectly in 1790, ahead of any European, and direct contact came in 1792, when George Vancouver's British ships and the Spanish expeditions of Galiano and Valdés circumnavigated Vancouver Island. Around 1830 pressure from the southward-moving Laich-kwil-tach began driving the northern K'omoks bands into the Pentlatch lands to the south.
zh: 科莫克人又译科莫克斯，是沿海萨利什人中分布最北的一支，中心在温哥华岛东岸的科莫克斯谷，对岸大陆的峡湾地带还居住着他们的同族特阿明、克拉胡斯和霍马尔科诸部。他们的语言阿雅茹滕姆属萨利什语的沿海分支，文化则融合了萨利什与北方夸扣特尔人的特点：擅长制造独木舟和木雕，在克罗姆岛留下岩画，并在夸德拉岛鲸屋等冬村举办夸富宴、散财赠礼。1790年一场天花先于欧洲人传到他们中间，造成人口大减；直接接触发生在1792年，乔治·温哥华的英国船队与加利亚诺、巴尔德斯率领的西班牙探险队环绕温哥华岛航行。1830年前后，南下扩张的莱赫奎尔塔赫部开始把科莫克北方各支逼入南部的彭特拉奇人之地。

en: The Kaantju are an Aboriginal Australian people of the interior of the Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, whose country surrounds the present town of Coen. Their name refers to the hooked end of the yuli, their word for a woomera, or spear-thrower, and their speech, with northern and southern varieties, is a dialect of the Umpila language.
zh: 坎朱人是昆士兰约克角半岛内陆的澳大利亚原住民，领地环绕今天的科恩镇。他们的族名指的是‘尤利’——即他们对投矛器沃梅拉的称呼——末端的弯钩；他们的语言分北部、南部两种变体，是翁皮拉语的一种方言。

en: The Ka'apor, formerly known to outsiders as the Urubu, are a Tupi-Guarani people whose name means forest people in their own language, from the Tupi words ka'a for forest and poro for people. They took shape as a distinct group only in the late 1600s and early 1700s, probably in the country between the Tocantins and Xingu rivers, when their ancestors fled the Portuguese-Brazilian advance into southern Pará and the trade in jungle products called drogas do sertão. Moving east across the Tocantins, they kept to the deep forest far from colonial settlements and missions. Documented village locations trace their long retreat through the Acará basin around 1810 and the Capim River around 1825, as pioneer pressure followed them eastward. Mobile slash-and-burn farmers and hunters organized under village chiefs, they kept their Tupi-Guarani speech and remained effectively unconquered and unmissionized through the end of the colonial era.
zh: 卡阿波尔人旧称乌鲁布人，是图皮-瓜拉尼语族群，族名在本族语言中意为森林之民，由图皮语中意为森林的卡阿和意为人的波罗两词合成。他们作为独立群体迟至17世纪末、18世纪初才形成，发源地可能在托坎廷斯河与欣古河之间：其祖先为躲避葡萄牙巴西人向帕拉州南部的扩张以及丛林物产贸易的掠夺，向东渡过托坎廷斯河，深入密林，远离殖民据点和传教区。有文献可考的村落位置记录了他们漫长的东撤路线：约1810年在阿卡拉河流域，约1825年迁至卡平河一带，垦荒者的压力也步步逼近。他们是流动的刀耕火种农人和猎人，以村落首领为组织核心，保留着图皮-瓜拉尼语，整个殖民时代实际上未被征服，也没有被传教。

en: The Kabye are a Gur-speaking farming people of the Kabye Mountains, part of the Atacora chain in north-central Togo, with smaller settlements across the border in Benin and Ghana. Their name means stone peasants: they build stone terraces on dry rocky ground to grow millet, yams and cotton, and hold Evala wrestling festivals to initiate young men.
zh: 卡比耶人是多哥中北部卡比耶山（阿塔科拉山脉的一部分）说古尔语支卡比耶语的农耕民族，在贝宁和加纳边境也有小片聚居地。其族名意为“石地农夫”，他们在干旱多石的坡地上垒石造梯田，种植小米、薯蓣和棉花，并以标志青年男子成年的埃瓦拉摔跤节闻名。

en: The Kabyles are a Berber people of Kabylia, the rugged coastal range east of Algiers in northern Algeria, who call themselves Iqbayliyen, or Zwawa in older Arabic sources; their name derives from the Arabic qaba'il, meaning tribes. Their mountains served as a refuge through Carthaginian, Roman, Vandal, Byzantine and Arab rule, so that lowland empires held the roads and valleys while the villages kept their own Berber speech and clan organization. In the early tenth century the Kutama tribes of Little Kabylia supplied the armies that founded the Fatimid Caliphate, and the Sanhaja Zirid dynasty, vassals of the Fatimids, likewise came from these mountains, which later passed under Hammadid and then Hafsid rule from Béjaïa. After Spain seized Béjaïa in 1510, two Berber principalities took shape: the Kingdom of Kuku, founded around 1515 by Ahmed ou el Kadhi, which even held Algiers from 1520 to 1527 before being driven back into Greater Kabylia, and the Kingdom of Beni Abbas, ruled by the Mokrani family from the fortified Kalâa of Ait Abbas in the Biban range. Both long balanced between the Spanish presidios and the Ottoman Regency of Algiers, which never fully subdued the Zwawa clans but drew on them as soldiers and allies. Kabyles farmed olives and figs on terraced slopes, made pottery and textiles, and from the late eighteenth century the Rahmaniyya Sufi order spread widely among their zawaya.
zh: 卡比尔人是柏柏尔人的一支，居住在阿尔及尔以东、北阿尔及利亚沿海的崎岖山地卡比利亚；他们自称伊克拜利延，阿拉伯旧文献中称兹瓦瓦，其名称来自阿拉伯语“卡巴伊勒”，意为部落。迦太基、罗马、汪达尔、拜占庭和阿拉伯人先后统治北非平原，而山区始终是他们的避难所：低地帝国控制道路与河谷，山村却保留着自己的柏柏尔语和氏族组织。10世纪初，小卡比利亚的库塔马部落为法蒂玛哈里发国的建立提供了军队，臣属法蒂玛的桑哈贾人齐里王朝也发源于这片山区，此后这里先后受哈马德王朝和以贝贾亚为都的哈夫斯王朝统治。1510年西班牙攻占贝贾亚后，当地形成两个柏柏尔政权：一是约1515年由艾哈迈德·乌·卡迪建立的库库王国，曾在1520至1527年占据阿尔及尔，后被逐回大卡比利亚；二是贝尼阿巴斯王国，由莫克拉尼家族以比班山脉中设防的阿伊特·阿巴斯堡为都。二者长期在西班牙沿海据点与奥斯曼的阿尔及尔摄政之间周旋，摄政始终未能彻底制服兹瓦瓦诸部，反而常招募其为兵。卡比尔人在梯田上种植橄榄和无花果，兼营陶器与纺织；18世纪末起，拉赫曼尼耶苏菲教团在他们的扎维耶中广泛传播。

en: The Gajirrawoong, also written Gadjerong or Gajerrong and recorded by Norman Tindale as the Kadjerong, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory borderlands, most of whose country lies in the north-eastern Kimberley of Western Australia. Tindale reckoned their lands at about 2,100 square kilometres, running along the coast from the mouth of the Fitzmaurice River to where the Keep River opens into Joseph Bonaparte Gulf, with an inland extension through Legune as far as Border Springs; they also frequented Quoin Island and Clump Island. Their language, Gajirrabeng, belongs to the Jarrakan group. The first European survey of their gulf was made by the French expedition of Nicolas Baudin, who named it Joseph Bonaparte Gulf in 1803.
zh: 卡杰龙人（又译加杰龙，诺曼·廷代尔即记作卡杰龙）是澳大利亚北领地边境地带的原住民，其大部分领地位于西澳大利亚州金伯利东北部。廷代尔估算其土地约2100平方公里，沿海岸从菲茨莫里斯河口延伸到基普河注入约瑟夫·波拿巴湾之处，内陆经勒古内一直到博德斯普林斯；他们还常出没于阔因岛和克伦普岛。他们的语言加杰拉本语属杰拉甘语族。最早测量他们所临海湾的是尼古拉·博丹率领的法国考察队，他于1803年将其命名为约瑟夫·波拿巴湾。

en: The Kado are the Kadu or Asak people of the northwestern hills of Burma, centred on Katha along the upper Chindwin, whose Sino-Tibetan language links them to the Ganan and Sak. Their Old Burmese name was Kantu or Sak-Kantu; the Chinese History of Yuan records them in the 1200s as Jiandu and Marco Polo knew them as Caindu. They were the dominant people of the Chindwin valley in the early second millennium, and scholars trace them to the Qiongdu migrants who entered Burma under the Tang dynasty of 618 to 907 and became a leading element of the Tagaung kingdom, with the Pyu said to have received Buddhism through them. The rise of Pagan and, after it, the migrations of the Chin and then the Shan into the Chindwin valley broke their predominance: by the 1200s many Kadu had merged into neighbouring Tibeto-Burman and Shan communities, while the mid-1200s split from the Sak, who moved toward Rakhine, left the Katha Kadu as terrace-rice cultivators under Shan and Burmese overlordship.
zh: 建都人即缅甸西北山区的卡杜人（自称阿萨克），以钦敦江上游的杰沙为中心，所说的汉藏系语言把他们与嘎南人和萨克人联系在一起。古缅语称他们为甘图或萨克-甘图；中国《元史》在1200年代的记载中称其为“建都”，马可·波罗则记作“凯恩杜”。他们在第二个千年初期是钦敦江谷地的主导族群，学者认为其源自618—907年唐代迁入缅甸的邛都人，后来成为太公王国的重要组成部分，据说骠人正是经他们而接触佛教。蒲甘崛起后，钦人、掸人又相继迁入钦敦江谷地，建都人的优势地位被打破：到1200年代，许多卡杜人已融入邻近的藏缅和掸人社群；1200年代中叶他们与迁往若开的萨克人分化，留在杰沙的卡杜人成为在掸人和缅人宗主权下耕种梯田水稻的山民。

en: The Kadu are the Nuba groups of the Kadugli district in the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan, including the Keiga and Krongo peoples; their closely related tongues form the Kadu, or Kadugli–Krongo, language family, once classed within Niger-Congo but later placed in the Nilo-Saharan family. They farm the rainy-season hills and raise cattle around Kadugli.
zh: 卡杜人是苏丹南科尔多凡努巴山区卡杜格利一带的努巴支系，包括凯加人、克龙戈人等，彼此相近的语言构成卡杜语（又称卡杜格利-克龙戈语）语族，早先被划入尼日尔-刚果语系，后改归入尼罗-撒哈拉语系。他们在雨季耕垦山地，在卡杜格利周边牧养牛群。

en:
The Caeté were a Tupi-Guarani people of the Brazilian coast, holding the shore between the mouth of the São Francisco River and the island of Itamaracá, with the Potiguara to their north and the Tupinambá to their south. They grew maize, peanuts, tobacco, squash and cotton, and had a reputation among both Indians and Portuguese as especially fierce warriors who took captives for cannibalistic rites. Portuguese slaving struck them hardest in the 1550s, and in 1556 they killed and ate the shipwrecked bishop Pero Fernandes Sardinha and his companions on the Alagoas coast. The crown answered with a declared holy war: between 1556 and 1558 Jerónimo de Albuquerque carried out an extermination campaign between the São Francisco and Cabo de Santo Agostinho, under a royal decree allowing the perpetual enslavement of everyone captured.

Further campaigns followed, including Cristóvão de Barros's revenge expedition of 1587 during the War of Sergipe, and in the 1580s the surviving Caeté migrated far north to the country between the Caeté and Turiaçu rivers in Maranhão. There the Portuguese formally created the Captaincy of Caeté in 1622, and Jesuit mission villages became the towns of Vila de Souza in 1634 and São João Batista in 1672. Rivalry over the office of village principal, the Principais created under the Native Directory, sparked the Caeté Upheaval of the 1740s and the expulsion of the Jesuits; in 1753 Vila de Souza was moved across the river and re-founded as Bragança, and the captaincy was dissolved.
zh:
卡埃特人是巴西沿海的图皮‑瓜拉尼族群，占据圣弗朗西斯科河口到伊塔马拉卡岛之间的海岸，北邻波蒂瓜拉人，南接图皮南巴人。他们种植玉米、花生、烟草、南瓜和棉花，在印第安人和葡萄牙人中间都以格外凶悍的战士著称，有俘获敌人用于食人仪式的习俗。1550年代葡萄牙人的奴隶掳掠对他们打击最烈；1556年，他们在阿拉戈斯海岸杀死并吃掉了遇船难的主教佩罗·费尔南德斯·萨尔迪尼亚及其随从。葡萄牙王室随即宣布发动圣战：1556年至1558年，热罗尼莫·德·阿尔布克尔克在圣弗朗西斯科河与圣阿戈斯蒂纽角之间展开清剿，王室法令还准许将所有俘获者永世充为奴隶。

此后征伐不断，1587年塞尔希培战争期间又有克里斯托旺·德·巴罗斯的复仇远征；1580年代，幸存的卡埃特人远迁北方，进入马拉尼昂的卡埃特河与图里亚苏河之间。1622年葡萄牙人在那里正式设立卡埃特管领辖区，耶稣会传教村先后于1634年和1672年改建为索萨镇和圣若昂巴蒂斯塔镇。围绕《印第安人指导法》设立的村落酋长一职的争夺引发了1740年代的卡埃特动乱，耶稣会士被逐；1753年索萨镇迁至河对岸重建为布拉干萨，卡埃特管领辖区也随之撤销。

en: The Kaeti, whose language is more often called Mandobo, are a Papuan people of the lowland rainforest along the Digul River in South Papua, Indonesia, notably in Mandobo District of Boven Digoel Regency. Mandobo forms the Dumut branch of the Greater Awyu family of Trans-New Guinea languages, together with the neighbouring Wambon.
zh: 凯蒂人使用的语言多称曼多博语，是印度尼西亚南巴布亚省迪古尔河沿岸低地雨林中的巴布亚族群，主要聚居于博文迪古尔摄政区的曼多博县。曼多博语与相邻的万邦语同属跨新几内亚语系大阿维尤语系的杜穆特语支。

en: The Kagwahiva, or Kawahíb, is the common self-name of a cluster of Tupi-Guarani peoples of the south-western Amazon, among them the Amondawa, Karipuna, Uru-Eu-Wau-Wau, Tenharim, Parintintín, Júma and Piripkúra, whose mutually intelligible speeches form the Kawahíva dialect cluster and find their closest kin in Apiaká. Their earliest homeland lay around the headwaters of the Tapajós and Juruena rivers, where European sources mention them from 1750. In the eighteenth century the expansion of their Munduruku enemies, followed by colonial pressure, dislocated the Kawahíb and broke them into small, highly mobile bands that scattered through the forests between the Madeira and Ji-Paraná rivers, living by hunting, gathering and small-scale farming. Early nineteenth-century travellers thus met not one tribe but a constellation of related Kagwahiva groups, each keeping the common name and language.
zh: 卡瓦希瓦人（又称卡瓦希布人）是亚马孙西南部一群图皮-瓜拉尼族群的共同自称，包括阿蒙达瓦人、卡里普纳人、乌鲁-乌瓦乌瓦乌人、特纳林人、帕林廷廷人、茹马人和皮里普库拉人等；他们彼此能通话的方言构成卡瓦希瓦方言群，亲属关系最近的是阿皮亚卡语。他们最早的家园在塔帕若斯河与茹鲁埃纳河源头一带，欧洲文献自1750年起提到他们。18世纪，世仇蒙杜鲁库人的扩张以及随之而来的殖民压力，使卡瓦希布人离散，分裂成许多流动性极强的小游群，散居在马代拉河与日巴拉那河之间的丛林中，以狩猎、采集和小规模农耕为生。因此19世纪初的旅人见到的不是一个部落，而是一系列共用族名与语言、彼此亲缘的卡瓦希瓦群体。

en: The Kahokiaki, better known in French records as the Cahokia, were an Algonquian-speaking tribe of the Illinois Confederation, and their name in the Miami-Illinois language gives this entry its title. From the sixteenth century they reoccupied the region of the long-abandoned earthen city of Cahokia on the Mississippi, though they were not the descendants of the Mississippian mound builders who had lived there before them; their own villages lay across western Illinois and eastern Missouri alongside the Tamaroa. After the French explorers Jolliet and Marquette reached them in 1673, missionaries founded the Tamaroa-Cahokia mission in 1699 when the two tribes consolidated at Cahokia, and in 1735 the Kahokiaki built a new village beside the great Monks Mound. In 1752 Shawnee and Meskwaki warriors allied to the British sacked their main settlement, and the survivors took refuge with the Michigamea. Warfare and epidemic disease had so reduced the tribe that its remnant was absorbed first by the Kaskaskia and then by the Peoria, whose descendants carry its heritage.
zh: 卡霍齐亚基人在法国文献中通常称卡霍基亚人，是操阿尔冈昆语的伊利诺伊联盟部落，本条目名称即该部在迈阿密—伊利诺伊语中的自称。16世纪起，他们重新占据密西西比河畔废弃已久的土墩城卡霍基亚一带，但并非此前居住于此的密西西比文化造墩人的后裔；他们的村庄与塔马罗亚人交错分布在伊利诺伊西部和密苏里东部。1673年法国探险家若利埃和马凯特抵达后，传教士趁两部于1699年在卡霍基亚合并之机建立了塔马罗亚—卡霍基亚传教站，1735年卡霍齐亚基人又在巨大的僧侣丘旁建起新村。1752年，与英国结盟的肖尼人和梅斯克瓦基人洗劫了他们的主要聚落，幸存者投奔米希加梅亚人。战争和瘟疫使该部人口锐减，余部先被卡斯卡斯基亚人、最终被皮奥里亚人吸收，其传统由后者的后裔延续。

en: The Kaialigamiut, who call themselves the Qaluyaarmiut, are a Central Alaskan Yup'ik regional group of Nelson Island, off the Yukon–Kuskokwim Delta in the Bering Sea. Their name comes from Qaluyaaq, the Yup'ik name for Nelson Island, itself derived from qalu, meaning a dip net, and the island held their three villages of Toksook Bay, Nightmute and Tununak. Like other Yup'ik societies they were semi-nomadic hunter-fishers who moved seasonally between coastal and inland camps to take salmon, seals and sea birds, and they wintered in semi-subterranean sod houses, with the men's communal qasgiq beside the women's family houses. They were among the named Yup'ik territorial groups of the delta when Andrei Glazunov's Russian expedition first entered the Yukon in 1834.
zh: 卡亚利格缪特人自称卡卢亚尔缪特，是白令海育空—卡斯科奎姆三角洲外纳尔逊岛上的中阿拉斯加尤皮克地域性群体。其名来自尤皮克语对纳尔逊岛的称呼“卡卢亚克”，词根“卡卢”意为抄网；岛上分布着托克苏克贝、奈特缪特和图图纳克三个村庄。和其他尤皮克社群一样，他们半游牧地从事渔猎，随季节在海岸与内陆营地之间迁徙，捕捞鲑鱼、捕猎海豹和海鸟，冬天住进半地穴式草皮屋，男子的集体会所“卡斯吉克”与女子的家庭草屋相邻而建。1834年安德烈·格拉祖诺夫的俄国探险队首次进入育空河时，他们已是三角洲上有名可称的尤皮克地域群体之一。

en: The Ka'igwu, or Principal People, are the nation better known by the Comanche rendering of their name, Kiowa. Their language belongs to the Kiowa-Tanoan family, linking these nomadic bison hunters to the Tanoan-speaking Pueblo peoples of the Rio Grande, and their oral tradition places their birth as a distinct people in the northern Missouri basin near the Yellowstone, where dogs once pulled their travois before horses reached them. Around 1650 they traveled southeast to the Black Hills of present Wyoming and South Dakota, lived there in friendship with the Crow, organized into ten bands and numbered about three thousand. Sioux pressure then drove the Cheyenne and Arapaho west into their hills, and the Ka'igwu in turn moved south, accompanied by a small Plains Apache band that shared their camps and councils, the two peoples conversing in Plains Sign Talk. In the spring of 1790 the war leader Guikate offered peace to a Comanche party near Las Vegas, New Mexico, founding the alliance that made Kiowa and Comanche joint masters of the southern plains between the Arkansas and Brazos rivers. In 1833 an Osage raid on an exposed camp near Head Mountain killed many of their families and carried off the Tai-me, the sacred figure at the heart of the Sun Dance; it was restored in 1835, when Dohasan rose to the chieftainship and led the tribe through its decades of power.
zh: 基奥瓦人自称卡伊格武，意为主体之民，外部更熟悉的名字基奥瓦来自科曼奇人对其族名的念法。他们的语言属基奥瓦—塔诺语系，使这些逐野牛而居的游牧者与格兰德河畔讲塔诺语的普韦布洛人同源；口传历史把本族形成之地放在黄石附近的密苏里河上游盆地，在得到马匹之前，他们一度靠狗拖曳雪橇架。约1650年，他们向东南迁到今怀俄明和南达科他交界处的布莱克山，与克劳人友好相邻，分为十个营地，人口约三千。后来苏族人的压力把夏延人和阿拉帕霍人西驱入山，基奥瓦人也随之南移，随行的还有一小支平原阿帕奇人——后者语言不同，却与他们同住营地、共商大事，两族用平原手势语交谈。1790年春，战将吉卡特在新墨西哥的拉斯维加斯附近向一队科曼奇人示和，由此缔盟，基奥瓦人与科曼奇人共同成为阿肯色河与布拉索斯河之间南部平原的主人。1833年，奥塞奇人袭击了海德山附近一处无备营地，杀死许多妇孺，还夺走太阳舞核心的圣物泰梅神像。1835年神像归来，太阳舞得以恢复，多汉桑也在此时成为首领，带领部落走过其强盛的数十年。

en: The Kaili, who call themselves To Kaili, are the people of the Palu valley and the Donggala and Sigi highlands of Central Sulawesi, with related settlements along the Tomini Bay coast at Parigi, Moutong and Tojo. Their name is said to come from the kaili tree that once guided sailors into Palu Bay, and they comprise more than thirty sub-groups speaking over twenty related languages, with Ledo Kaili serving as their common tongue. Their early hunter-gatherer chieftains, the Tomalanggai, gave way to the first Kaili Kingdom in the fifteenth century, and by the sixteenth century an aristocratic class, the madika, had emerged. In the following Independent Era the land was divided among the kingdoms of Palu, Banawa, Sigi, Parigi, Kulawi and Tawaeli, each ruled by a magau assisted by noble councils, and Portuguese traders were visiting their ports from the late sixteenth century. Islam reached the Palu valley in the seventeenth century through Sheikh Abdullah Raqie, known as Dato Karama, a preacher from Pagaruyung in Minangkabau who worked there from 1603 to 1650 and converted the local kings, after whom the first mosque at Palu was built.
zh: 凯里人自称“多凯里”，聚居在中苏拉威西的帕卢河谷及栋加拉、锡吉高地，并在托米尼湾沿岸的帕里吉、莫通、托约等地有亲缘聚落。据说其族名取自曾为水手指引帕卢湾航路的凯里树；他们分为三十多个支系，说二十多种亲属语言，莱多凯里语是各方言间的通用语。早期的凯里人以狩猎采集为生，首领称托马兰盖；15世纪第一个凯里王国建立，旧时代结束，到16世纪已出现名为马迪卡的贵族阶层。此后的“独立时代”里，这片土地分属帕卢、巴纳瓦、锡吉、帕里吉、库拉维和塔瓦埃利等王国，各国由称马高的国王在贵族议事会辅佐下统治，葡萄牙商人从16世纪末起已出入这些港口。17世纪，伊斯兰教传入帕卢河谷：来自米南佳保帕加鲁永的谢赫·阿卜杜拉·拉基（人称达托·卡拉马）于1603至1650年在此传教，使当地诸王皈依，帕卢的第一座清真寺随后建成。

en: The Tapayuna, who call themselves Kajkwakratxi, are a Northern Jê people of Mato Grosso, whose forest homeland lay on the Arinos river in the Tapajós basin, between the Juruena and the Aripuanã. Their language is close enough to that of the Kĩsêdjê, or Suyá, for the two to understand one another, and neighbours also called them the Western Suyá or Beiço-de-Pau, “wooden lip”, after the lip disks worn by their men. They were mostly monogamous, though a shaman might take two wives, and a new husband went to live in his father-in-law's house. Their forests held rubber trees, ores and hardwoods, but through the 1700s and 1800s the Tapayuna remained in their river villages, hunting, fishing and farming beyond the reach of the Portuguese frontier, whose soldiers, missionaries and slavers never established a lasting presence on the Arinos.
zh: 塔帕尤纳人自称卡日瓦克拉奇，是马托格罗索使用北支热语族语言的族群；他们的森林故土在塔帕若斯流域的阿里诺斯河一带，介于茹鲁埃纳河与阿里普阿南河之间。他们的语言与基塞哲人（即苏亚人）十分接近，彼此可以通话，邻族因此也称他们为西苏亚人或“木唇人”，后一个名字得自男子佩戴的唇盘。他们大体实行一夫一妻制，只有萨满可以娶两个妻子；婚后男子要搬进岳父家居住。他们的林地产橡胶树、矿藏和硬木，但在18、19世纪，塔帕尤纳人始终留在河畔村庄里狩猎、捕鱼、务农，处在葡萄牙扩张前沿的势力范围之外，军人、传教士和奴隶贩子都未能在阿里诺斯河建立持久据点。

en: The Kajoor Ri Majel, better known as the Marshallese, are the Austronesian people of the Marshall Islands, two parallel chains of low coral atolls, the eastern Ratak and western Ralik, and speak Marshallese, a Micronesian language with Ralik and Ratak dialects. Austronesian seafarers settled the atolls from around the second millennium BC, and archaeology on Majuro and Kwajalein shows established villages by the first century. They subsisted on coconuts, breadfruit, taro, pandanus and fishing, lived under ranked chiefs headed by a paramount chief for each chain, and became master navigators, sailing outrigger canoes by the stars and by reading ocean swells, which they recorded on shell-and-stick charts. Alonso de Salazar sighted the islands in 1526 and Álvaro de Saavedra landed there in 1528, but regular contact only began after the British ships commanded by Thomas Gilbert and John Marshall passed through in 1788, giving the islands their European name. Otto von Kotzebue explored the Ratak chain from 1817 and found the chief Lamari of Aur using metal hatchets to conquer neighbouring atolls and seize Majuro. From the 1820s whalers called regularly; the mutiny of the Globe at Mili in 1824 and a string of bloody clashes in the 1830s left the Marshallese still independent but deeply wary of foreign ships by 1837.
zh: 卡久里‑马绍尔人即通常所称的马绍尔人，是马绍尔群岛的南岛语族群；群岛由拉塔克东列与拉利克西列两串低矮珊瑚环礁组成，他们使用密克罗尼西亚语族的马绍尔语，分拉利克、拉塔克两种方言。南岛语航海者约在公元前两千年起陆续定居这些环礁，马朱罗和夸贾林的考古发现表明公元1世纪时已有稳定村落。他们以椰子、面包果、芋艿、露兜果和渔获为生，社会实行等级化的酋长制，两列群岛各有一位最高酋长；他们又是出色的航海者，凭星象和海浪回流驾驶舷外浮杆独木舟，并用木棍、贝壳编结的海图记录涌浪模式。1526年阿隆索·德·萨拉萨尔最先望见群岛，1528年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉一度登岛，但此后两百多年接触稀少；1788年托马斯·吉尔伯特与约翰·马绍尔率领的英国商船途经此地，群岛的欧洲名称即来自马绍尔。1817年起奥托·冯·科策布考察拉塔克列岛，发现奥尔环礁酋长拉马里靠金属短斧征服邻近环礁、攻占马朱罗。19世纪20年代起捕鲸船频频造访，1824年“环球号”在米利环礁发生哗变，30年代又接连发生流血冲突；到1837年，卡久里‑马绍尔人仍保持独立，却已对外国船只深怀戒心。

en: The Kakongo are the Bakongo people of the small kingdom of the same name, which lay on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa in the area of the present-day Republic of the Congo and Cabinda. In the thirteenth century Kakongo formed part of a confederation led by Vungu, and for part of its history it was a vassal of the Kingdom of Kongo, whose king Afonso I still claimed it in his titles in 1535. From the sixteenth century onward it was effectively independent, ruling from its inland capital of Kinguele. Portuguese merchants opened factories there in the 1620s, trading copper, ivory and slaves, and together with neighboring Ngoyo and Loango, Kakongo became a major commercial power of the coast between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries. In the 1680s it kept diplomatic ties with Soyo across the Congo River, before losing the river island of Nzari a Kongo to Soyo around 1688.
zh: 卡刚果人是同名小王国的巴刚果人，该王国位于中非大西洋沿岸，相当于今刚果共和国沿海和安哥拉卡宾达一带。13世纪时，卡刚果是温古领导的联盟成员，历史上还曾一度臣属于刚果王国，刚果国王阿方索一世在1535年的头衔中仍自称统治此地。16世纪起它基本独立，以内陆城镇金盖莱为都。17世纪20年代，葡萄牙商人在此开设商站，收购铜、象牙和奴隶；卡刚果与邻近的恩戈约、卢安果一道，在17至19世纪成为沿海重要的商业强权。17世纪80年代，它与刚果河对岸的索约保持外交往来，约1688年又把河中的恩扎里阿刚果岛输给了索约。

en: The Kalaamaya, recorded as the Kalamaia or Kalamai, are an Aboriginal people of the Wheatbelt and Goldfields-Esperance country of inland Western Australia. Their lands extended over some 88,000 square kilometres, from Bullabulling in the east to the Burracoppin and Lake Moore country in the west, and from Youanmi and Lake Barlee in the north down to Mount Holland, taking in the later Boorabbin and Southern Cross districts. Groups remembered as the Kaprun, Jungaa and Jungal were Kalaamaya bands, and Takalako was the name given them by their Njakinjaki neighbours. They were among the eastern tribes who practised circumcision as the heart of male initiation, and looked down on the south-western peoples who lacked the rite. Their language belongs to the Pama-Nyungan family. When the Swan River Colony was founded in 1829 their inland country still lay beyond the frontier, and gold prospectors only reached it in the later nineteenth century.
zh: 卡拉玛亚人（记载中也作卡拉马亚或卡拉迈）是西澳大利亚内陆小麦带与金矿区-埃斯佩兰斯地区的原住民。他们的领地约8.8万平方公里，东起布拉布林，西至布拉科平和穆尔湖一带，北起尤安米和巴利湖，南抵霍兰德山，包括后来的布拉宾和南克罗斯地区。卡普伦、荣阿、荣加尔等群体都是卡拉玛亚人的分支，塔卡拉科则是邻族恩贾金贾基对他们的称呼。他们属于东部行割礼的部族，割礼是男子入族仪式的核心，并因此轻视没有这一仪式的西南部族群。他们的语言属帕马-牛雅语系。1829年天鹅河殖民地建立时，他们的内陆土地仍在边疆之外，直到19世纪后期才有淘金者到来。

en: The Kalanga, or BaKalanga, are a southern Bantu people of the Shashe-Limpopo basin, spread across present-day Matabeleland in Zimbabwe, northern Botswana and the northern edge of South Africa. They descend from the Leopard's Kopje farming tradition of about 1050, whose villages of terraced hilltops and stone walls traded ivory, furs and feathers to the Indian Ocean coast, and they are counted among the builders of Mapungubwe, Great Zimbabwe and Khami. When drought emptied Mapungubwe around 1300, power moved first to Great Zimbabwe and then, in the fifteenth century, back west to Khami, heart of the Kalanga kingdom later known as Butua. In the seventeenth century the Rozvi dynasty, itself rooted in the Kalanga country, dominated the mining lands and repelled Portuguese traders from its inland posts, until Changamire Dombo overran Butua in 1683. Kalanga chiefdoms survived into the nineteenth century, when invasions by the Bangwato and then by Mzilikazi's Ndebele in the 1820s and 1830s broke their independence.
zh: 卡兰加人又称巴卡兰加人，是沙谢-林波波盆地的南部班图人，分布在今津巴布韦马塔贝莱兰、博茨瓦纳北部和南非北境一带。他们源自约1050年的豹穴农耕传统：其村落多建在带石墙的梯级山顶上，以象牙、毛皮和羽毛与印度洋海岸贸易；马蓬古布韦、大津巴布韦和卡米等早期国家的营建者中都有他们的身影。约1300年马蓬古布韦因干旱沦为空城后，权力先移至大津巴布韦，15世纪又西归卡米，即以卡兰加人为主体、后来被称作布图阿的王国。17世纪，同样扎根于卡兰加之地的罗兹维王朝控制了主要矿区，并把葡萄牙商人从内陆据点击退，直到昌加米雷·东博于1683年攻灭布图阿。卡兰加诸酋邦延续到19世纪，19世纪20—30年代，恩瓦托人入侵，随后姆济利卡齐率领恩德贝莱人大举压境，终结了他们的独立。

en: The Kalapuyan are the eight autonomous hunter-gatherer bands of the Willamette Valley in western Oregon, a lowland shut between the Cascade Range and the Oregon Coast Range and reaching from the Columbia River south to the Calapooya Mountains and the Umpqua. They were never a single tribe but spoke three mutually intelligible dialects of an Oregon Penutian language, Northern, Central and Southern or Yoncalla, among them the Tualatin, also called the Atfalati, the Yamhill, the Santiam and the Yoncalla of the Umpqua. Tradition holds that they entered the valley from the south and displaced earlier inhabitants. Patrilineal extended families wintered in permanent villages and scattered in summer to gather roots, berries and nuts while the men fished and hunted, shaping obsidian from the eastern volcanic ranges into arrowheads and spear points. Before contact they may have numbered fifteen thousand, and the fur trade also spread the Chinook Jargon among them. Repeated epidemics of malaria and smallpox after 1805 emptied whole villages by the 1830s, leaving the valley open to the missionaries and settlers who followed.
zh: 卡拉普亚人是俄勒冈西部威拉米特河谷里八个自治狩猎采集支派的合称，这片低地夹在喀斯喀特山脉与俄勒冈海岸山脉之间，北起哥伦比亚河，南抵卡拉普亚山和安普夸河。他们从来不是一个统一部落，而是说俄勒冈佩努蒂语三种互通方言——北支、中支和南支扬卡拉语，支派包括又称阿特法拉蒂的图瓦拉廷人、亚姆希尔人、桑蒂亚姆人和安普夸河畔的扬卡拉人。口传传统称他们自南方迁入河谷，取代了更早的居民。按父系继嗣的大家族冬天住进固定村落，夏天四散采集根茎、浆果和坚果，男子则捕鱼狩猎，并用东部火山区的黑曜石打制箭头和矛尖。接触之前他们可能有一万五千人之众，毛皮贸易还把奇努克行话带到他们中间。1805年后，疟疾和天花反复流行，到19世纪30年代，整村整村已经空无一人，为随之而来的传教士和移民敞开了河谷的大门。

en: Kalaw Lagaw Ya is the culture of the western and central Torres Strait Islanders, a Melanesian seafaring people whose home islands, including Badu and Mabuiag, lie in the shallow waters between the Cape York peninsula and the New Guinea coast. Their language belongs to the Australian Pama-Nyungan family yet carries a deep Papuan substrate in vocabulary and custom, reflecting the strait's position as a meeting point of two worlds; before the colonial era it served as the lingua franca of the entire Torres Strait cultural area, spoken on the islands, along the Papuan coast and on neighboring Cape York, with dialects such as Kalau Kawau Ya marking the westernmost communities. Islanders combined yam and tobacco gardening with hunting dugong and turtle on the reefs and sustained long-distance trade links in both directions, to the Papuan mainland and to Aboriginal Australia, exchanging canoes, shells, feathers and dance. The first European to enter their waters was the Spanish navigator Luís Vaez de Torres in 1606, after whom the strait is named; other passing explorers followed in the eighteenth century, but the islanders remained independent masters of their sea lanes until well into the nineteenth.
zh: 卡劳拉高亚人是托雷斯海峡中部和西部岛民的文化，这是一个美拉尼西亚航海民族，家园包括巴杜岛、马布亚格岛等，散布在约克角半岛与新几内亚海岸之间的浅海中。他们的语言属于澳大利亚帕马-牛雅语系，却在词汇和习俗上带有深厚的巴布亚底层，正反映出海峡作为两个世界交汇点的地位；在殖民时代之前，它是整个托雷斯海峡文化区的通用语，通行于各岛、巴布亚沿岸和邻近的约克角，最西边的社群还使用卡劳卡瓦亚等方言。岛民既种植山药和烟草，也在礁上捕猎儒艮和海龟，并维持着双向的长途贸易网：一边通往巴布亚大陆，一边通往澳大利亚原住民地区，交换独木舟、贝壳、羽毛和舞蹈。最早驶入这片水域的欧洲人是1606年的西班牙航海家路易斯·巴埃斯·德·托雷斯，海峡也以他的名字命名；18世纪又有其他探险者路过，但直到19世纪很久以后，岛民仍是自己海路的独立主人。

en: The Kalenjin are a cluster of Southern Nilotic, Kalenjin-speaking peoples, among them the Nandi, Kipsigis, Pokot, Tugen and Keiyo, whose heartland is the high escarpments and grasslands of the Rift Valley in what is now western Kenya, with related groups such as the Datooga in Tanzania. Their Nilotic-speaking ancestors drifted south from the White Nile basin in a movement that began around the fifth century and gathered pace in the eleventh, bringing pastoral Iron Age communities into Uganda and the Kenyan highlands. There they absorbed Cushitic influences, including circumcision and the ipinda age-set system, and by the eighteenth century their lands held several related communities: the Lumbwa near Mount Kenya, the Chok on the Elgeyo escarpment, the Chemwal between Mount Elgon and Uasin Gishu, and the Maliri farther west in Uganda, whom the Karamojong displaced. Cattle pastoralists and grain farmers, they were struck from about 1800 by the long Aoyate drought, which peaked in the 1830s and brought the famine of 1836, opening the troubled period remembered as the Mutai.
zh: 卡伦津人是南尼罗河语族群的集合体，包括南迪人、基普西吉斯人、波科特人、图根人、凯约人等说卡伦津语的部族，核心家园在今天肯尼亚西部裂谷一带的高崖与草原，坦桑尼亚的塔托加人等也是其亲缘群体。他们的尼罗语先祖从白尼罗河流域逐渐南徙，这一迁徙约始于5世纪，11世纪加快，把游牧的铁器时代社群带入乌干达和肯尼亚高地。他们在当地吸收了库希特文化因素，包括割礼和名为伊平达的年龄组制度；到18世纪，其土地上分布着若干亲缘社群：肯尼亚山一带的伦布瓦人、埃尔盖奥陡崖上的乔克人、埃尔冈山与瓦辛吉舒之间的切姆瓦尔人，以及更西边乌干达境内、后来被卡拉莫琼人逐走的马里里人。卡伦津人牧牛兼种谷物，约1800年起遭遇漫长的阿奥亚特干旱，19世纪30年代旱情达到顶峰并引发1836年大饥荒，开启了被称为穆泰的动荡年代。

en: The Khaliji, or Khaleeji, meaning 'of the Gulf', are the Arabs of the Persian Gulf shore of Eastern Arabia, the coast once known as the Bahrain region, running from the deserts around Wadi al-Batin and Kuwait south to Qatar. Their society has always faced the sea: pearl diving, fishing and long-distance trade shaped its towns, and they speak Gulf Arabic, a dialect shared across the whole coast. Their forebears include the merchants of Dilmun, the trading civilization centered on Bahrain from the third millennium BC, and the Nestorian Christians of pre-Islamic Beth Qatraye. After Islam came the Qarmatians and a succession of local dynasties, ending with the Jabrids, whose chief Ajwad ibn Zamil ruled the entire coast until his death in 1507; a Portuguese invasion seized Bahrain in 1521. The Bani Khalid tribe then dominated the region, driving out an Ottoman garrison in 1670, until Saudi forces took Al-Ahsa in 1793. The Najdi-origin Bani Yas confederation settled the Liwa oasis around 1700, founded Abu Dhabi in 1795 and took Dubai in 1822, building the sheikhdoms of the later Gulf states.
zh: 哈利吉人，其名意为“海湾的人”，是东阿拉伯半岛波斯湾沿岸的阿拉伯人。这条海岸旧称巴林地区，北起瓦迪巴廷与科威特一带的沙漠，南至卡塔尔。他们的社会始终面向海洋：采珠、捕鱼与长途贸易塑造了沿岸城镇，所说的海湾阿拉伯语也是整条海岸通用的方言。其先民包括公元前3000年起以巴林为中心的贸易文明迪尔蒙的商人，以及伊斯兰化以前信奉聂斯托利派基督教的贝特卡特拉耶居民。伊斯兰时代之后，卡尔马特派及一系列地方王朝相继统治这里，最后一个是贾布里德王朝，其首领阿吉瓦德·本·扎米勒在1507年去世前统治着整条海岸；1521年葡萄牙人入侵夺取巴林。此后巴尼哈立德部落掌控该地区，于1670年赶走奥斯曼守军，直到1793年沙特军队攻占哈萨。源自内志的巴尼亚斯部落联盟约于1700年定居利瓦绿洲，1795年建阿布扎比，1822年夺取迪拜，奠定了日后海湾诸酋长国的雏形。

en: Persian Jewry is among the oldest of the diaspora communities, its ancestors having been carried into Iran as Assyrian and Babylonian captives from the eighth century BCE. When Cyrus the Great conquered Babylon in 538 BCE he allowed the exiles to return to Jerusalem, but many remained, and the Book of Esther is set entirely at the Persian court. Under the Sasanians the Jews enjoyed long periods of favour, and after the Arab conquest they lived as dhimmis, paying the jizya but often prospering as physicians, scholars and artisans; their Judeo-Persian dialects, written in Hebrew letters, are attested in documents from the eighth century. Mongol rule brought sharp reversals: the Ilkhan Arghun raised the Jew Sa'd al-Dawla to the vizierate, only for him to be murdered in 1291, and after Ghazan's conversion to Islam in 1295 the Ilkhan Öljaitü destroyed synagogues and imposed a distinctive head mark, while the convert statesman Rashid al-Din of Hamadan was executed at Tabriz in 1318. Timur's conquests from 1383 scattered the communities further. The Safavids made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion in 1502 and classed Jews as ritually unclean; Abbas I at first encouraged them in his new capital of Isfahan, but Abbas II expelled them from the city in 1656 and forced conversion, permitting a return to Judaism only in 1661 under a dress badge. Nadir Shah later allowed Jews to settle in Mashhad, while the Qajar accession in 1794 opened another age of persecution.
zh: 波斯犹太人是最古老的流散犹太社群之一，其先民自公元前8世纪起作为亚述和巴比伦的俘奴被带入伊朗。公元前538年居鲁士大帝攻陷巴比伦后准许俘囚返回耶路撒冷，但许多人留了下来，《以斯帖记》的故事便完全以波斯宫廷为舞台。萨珊王朝时期他们长期受到优待；阿拉伯征服后，他们作为迪米人缴纳吉兹亚人头税，却常以医生、学者和工匠的身份发达，其用希伯来字母拼写的犹太-波斯语方言在8世纪的文书中已有实证。蒙古统治带来剧烈逆转：伊儿汗阿鲁浑任命犹太人萨德·道拉为维齐尔，他却在1291年遇害；1295年合赞改宗伊斯兰教后，完者都拆毁会堂并强令犹太人佩戴头饰标记，改宗的哈马丹名臣拉施德丁也于1318年在大不里士被处死。1383年起帖木儿的征服又使各地社群进一步流散。1502年萨法维王朝立十二伊玛目派什叶派为国教，将犹太人列为不洁之民；阿拔斯一世起初鼓励他们定居新都伊斯法罕，阿拔斯二世却在1656年把他们逐出该城并强迫改宗，直到1661年才许其恢复犹太教信仰，仍须佩戴衣饰标记。后来纳迪尔沙准许犹太人定居马什哈德，而1794年卡扎尔王朝上台又开启了一个迫害的时代。

en: The Kalinga are an Austronesian highland people of the central Cordillera in northern Luzon, whose villages line the Chico River and the floodplains of Tabuk and Rizal; their name is an Ibanag and Gaddang exonym meaning headhunter. Tabuk was settled in the 1100s, and from there the Kalinga spread into the mountain valleys of Balbalan, Lubuagan, Pasil and Tanudan, where they built irrigated rice terraces and worked local gold and copper deposits. Their society divided into poor kapos and landowning baknang, led in war by mingol head-takers and later by papangat elders, and their distinctive gift to Cordilleran life was the bodong, a formal peace pact that sealed alliances and closed feuds between villages and was later taken up by neighboring peoples. They fought with the sinawit head axe, wore batok tattoos of centipedes, snakes and ferns, and honored the creator Kabuniyan through mandadawak priestesses. Through the 1830s Spanish administration never reached their valleys, so the Kalinga kept governing themselves by pact and custom.
zh: 卡林加人是北吕宋中部科迪勒拉山区的南岛语系高地族群，村落沿奇科河及塔布克、黎刹的洪泛平原分布；“卡林加”是伊巴纳格人和加当人对他们的称呼，意为猎头者。塔布克在1100年代即已有定居点，卡林加人由此扩散到巴尔巴兰、卢布阿甘、帕西尔和塔努丹等山谷，修筑灌溉水稻梯田，并开采当地的金铜矿藏。社会分为贫穷的卡波斯与拥有田产的巴克南两层，战时由猎头勇士明戈尔领导，后来由帕潘加特长老主政；他们对科迪勒拉文化最独特的贡献是博东制度，即以正式和约缔结盟约、平息村落仇杀，后来邻近族群也纷纷效仿。他们使用西纳维特猎头斧，身上刺着蜈蚣、蛇和蕨类纹样的巴托克纹身，由曼达达瓦克女祭司主持祭祀至高造物主卡布尼安的仪式。直到1830年代，西班牙人的行政体系仍未进入这些山谷，卡林加人始终凭和约与习惯法自治。

en: The Qalispé, better known as the Kalispel or Pend d'Oreilles, are an Interior Salish people of the Northwest Plateau who call their country Kaniksu, the basin of the Flathead, Clark Fork and Pend Oreille rivers running from present-day Montana to Lake Pend Oreille and Priest Lake. Their own name means 'camas people', after the bulb that was their staple, while French traders called them Pend d'Oreille, or 'ear pendant', for their large shell earrings. They lived in some eleven bands of upstream and downstream people, summering in tipis and wintering in lodges framed of poles and woven tule mats, and traded bison hides for horses. The North West Company built the Kullyspell House trading post among them in 1809, drawing them into the fur-trade network of the early nineteenth century.
zh: 卡利斯佩人又称庞多雷人，是西北高原的内陆萨利什人，把自己的土地称作卡尼克苏，范围涵盖弗拉特黑德河、克拉克福克河与庞多雷河流域，从今蒙大拿一直延伸到庞多雷湖和普里斯特湖。他们的自称意为‘卡马夏人’，得名于作为主食的球茎；法国商人则称他们为庞多雷，意为‘耳坠’，因为他们佩戴硕大的贝壳耳环。他们分为上游和下游两大群、约十一个队群，夏季住圆锥帐篷，冬季住在木架上覆香蒲席的屋舍里，并以野牛皮换取马匹。1809年，西北公司在他们中间设立卡利斯佩尔堡贸易站，把他们纳入19世纪初的毛皮贸易网络。

en: The Kalkadooni, properly the Kalkatungu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Mount Isa country of north-western Queensland, whose lands ran from the headwaters of the Cloncurry, Leichhardt and Gregory Rivers across the Barkly Tableland and the Selwyn Range, with the Mayi-Thakurti on their eastern flank. Their language, together with the Yalarnnga speech to the south, formed the Kalkatungic branch of the Pama-Nyungan family, and like neighbouring peoples they used a developed sign language. The Selwyn Range was a trading crossroads where pituri narcotic, ochre, stone knives and axes moved between Boulia and Cloncurry; the metabasalt quarry at Lake Moondarra yielded hundreds of thousands of axe blanks, some carried a thousand kilometres along the trade routes. Rock art covers the shelters of their ranges, and they were early carriers of the Mudlunga ritual dance, which later spread across much of the continent.
zh: 卡尔卡敦人本名卡尔卡通人，是昆士兰西北部芒特艾萨一带的澳大利亚原住民，领地起自克朗克里河、莱卡特河与格雷戈里河的源头，横跨巴克利台地和塞尔温岭，东邻马伊—塔库尔蒂人。他们的语言与南方雅拉恩加人的语言共同构成帕马—牛雅语系的卡尔卡通语支；和周边各族一样，他们也使用一套发达的手势语。塞尔温岭是贸易枢纽，皮图里麻醉剂、赭石、石刀和石斧在布利亚与克朗克里之间流转；蒙达拉湖的变玄武岩石器场留下了数十万件石斧坯料，有些沿商路被贩运到上千公里之外。他们岭中的岩棚遍布岩画，还是穆德隆加仪式舞最早的传播者之一，这种舞蹈后来传遍大陆的大片地区。

en: The Kallawaya are an Andean people of the steep valleys north of La Paz, around Charazani, in a transit belt between the high Andes and the Amazon whose ecological tiers, from snowline to lowland, gave them access to a vast range of medicinal plants. They trace their healing tradition to the Tiwanaku and Mollo cultures, and as early as 700 their healers were performing complex surgery and compiling one of the Andes' largest herbal pharmacopeias, long before the Inca rise. Under the Inca Empire they held a special status: itinerant physicians who walked from community to community with their plants, served the Inca and were entrusted with carrying his litter, while governing a far larger autonomous territory than their modern villages. Their trade was guarded in a secret ritual language, Machaj juyay, built on Quechua grammar and Puquina vocabulary and taught only to initiated healers.
zh: 卡亚瓦亚人是安第斯族群，居住在拉巴斯以北、查拉萨尼一带的深峡谷地，地处高耸的安第斯山脉与亚马孙之间的过渡地带，从雪线到低地的多层生态带使他们能取得种类繁多的药用植物。他们的医术传统承袭自蒂亚瓦纳科文化和莫洛文化，早在公元700年，其医者就已施行复杂的外科手术，积累起安第斯最丰富的本草药典之一。在印加帝国治下，他们享有特殊地位：作为游走四方的医者背负药草逐村行医，侍奉印加王并负责抬他的御辇，还管辖着比今日村落广阔得多的自治领地。这门行当由一种秘传的仪式语言守护，即以克丘亚语法为骨架、以普基纳语词汇为血肉的马查赫·胡瓦伊语，只传授给入门的医者。

en: The Kam, who call themselves Gaeml and are officially known as the Dong, are a Kam–Sui people of the Tai–Kadai language family living in the borderlands of eastern Guizhou, western Hunan and northern Guangxi, with smaller communities beyond the frontier in Vietnam. They are held to descend from the ancient Rau peoples of southern China, and Chinese scholars trace them to a branch of the Bai Yue from the first century CE, who broke into many small chiefdoms after the collapse of the Yue kingdom. Their own migration legends tell of ancestors moving west from Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang and Fujian. The Kam language had no script of its own, and villagers borrowed Chinese characters to write down Kam sounds. The name Dong first appears explicitly in records of the Ming, who ruled from 1368. Under the Ming and the Qing after 1644, Kam risings repeatedly broke out against imperial rule, while Qing officials extended irrigation through the hills and enlarged the rice harvest. Kam villages were famed for timber carpentry, covered wind-and-rain bridges, wet-rice farming and polyphonic choral singing.
zh: 侗人自称“甘”，官方定名侗族，属壮侗语系侗水语支，聚居在贵州东部、湖南西部和广西北部的交界山区，也有小部分人迁居越南境内。一般认为他们是古代南方僚人的后裔，中国学者则把他们追溯到1世纪百越的一支：越国瓦解后，百越分化出众多小酋长国。侗人自己的迁徙传说称祖先从广东、广西、浙江、福建一带向西迁来。侗语本无文字，民间借用汉字记录侗语读音。“侗”这一族名最早见于1368年开国的明朝的文献。明代以及1644年入关后的清代，侗人多次举兵反抗朝廷统治，清廷则在山区推广灌溉，使稻米产量大增。侗寨以木作工艺、遮雨的风雨桥、水稻耕种和多声部合唱闻名。

en: The Kamarupi are the Indo-Aryan people of the old Kamarupa kingdom, which from the fourth century covered the Brahmaputra valley and, at its height, North Bengal, Bhutan and the northern parts of Bangladesh. Their Middle Indo-Aryan speech, Kamarupi Prakrit, grew out of Gauda-Kamarupi Prakrit and is the ancestor of both Assamese and the Kamatapuri dialects; its habits survive in the Sanskrit copper-plate inscriptions of Kamarupa's kings.
