Three dynasties ruled in turn: the Varmans, under whom the pilgrim Xuanzang visited King Bhaskaravarman in the seventh century, the Mlechchhas and the Palas, whose last kings reigned at Kamarupanagara near Guwahati until the kingdom broke up in the twelfth century. Around 1257 the ruler Sandhya moved his capital west to Kamatapur in North Bengal and founded the Kamata kingdom, the polity in which the Kamarupi of the Bengal borderlands lived in 1337. The Khen dynasty fell to the Bengal sultan Alauddin Husain Shah in 1498, and in 1515 Biswa Singha founded the Koch dynasty, whose realms later split into Koch Bihar and Koch Hajo, the latter absorbed by the Ahoms in the seventeenth century.
zh: 迦摩缕波人是古迦摩缕波王国的印度-雅利安居民。该王国从4世纪起统辖布拉马普特拉河河谷，全盛时势力扩及北孟加拉、不丹和孟加拉国北部。他们的中古印度-雅利安语迦摩缕波俗语源自高达-迦摩缕波俗语，是阿萨姆语和卡马塔普尔诸方言的共同祖先，其语言特征保存在迦摩缕波诸王的梵文铜版铭文里。迦摩缕波先后由三个王朝统治：跋摩王朝——7世纪求法僧玄奘正是在跋摩王朝的拘摩罗·跋湿迦罗跋摩在位时到访——蔑戾车王朝和波罗王朝；波罗王朝末代诸王以高哈蒂附近的迦摩缕波城为都，直到12世纪王国解体。约1257年，统治者桑提亚将都城西迁至北孟加拉的卡马塔普尔，建立卡玛塔王国，1337年孟加拉边境一带的迦摩缕波人正生活在这个政权之下。1498年，肯王朝被孟加拉苏丹阿拉乌德丁·侯赛因·沙阿攻灭；1515年比斯瓦·辛哈建立科赫王朝，其国土后来分裂为库奇比哈尔与科赫哈乔两支，后者于17世纪被阿豪姆王国吞并。

en: The Kambaata are a Cushitic people of the south-central Ethiopian highlands, whose language, Kambaatissa, belongs to the Highland East Cushitic group alongside the closely related Hadiyya and Sidama tongues and counts the Tembaaro, Alaba and Qabeena dialects. They first enter the written record in the royal chronicles of the Ethiopian emperor Yeshaq I, who reigned from 1414 to 1429, and their incorporation into the Christian Ethiopian realm in this period left the province largely Christianized. The Kambaata organized themselves into the kingdom of Kembata, ruled by kings titled Woma; the first of them, Hamlmal, also called Hamo, founded the ruling Oyeta clan, and a later king, Dagoye, enlarged its territory. A settled monarchical order is documented from the sixteenth century. The Woma kept court on Mount Hambaricho, where the Kambaata deity Abba Sarecho was believed to dwell and where the annual Gifata festival was celebrated.
zh: 坎巴塔人是埃塞俄比亚中南部高地的库希特民族，所说的坎巴塔语属高地东库希特语支，与邻近的哈迪亚语、锡达莫语关系密切，内部分滕巴罗、阿拉巴、卡比纳等方言。他们最早见于1414至1429年在位的埃塞俄比亚皇帝耶沙克一世的宫廷编年史；这一时期被纳入信奉基督教的埃塞俄比亚版图后，坎巴塔行省大体皈依了基督教。坎巴塔人建有坎巴塔王国，统治者称沃马：初代国王哈姆勒马尔（又名哈莫）开创了统治的奥耶塔氏族，后来的达戈耶王又扩张了疆土。16世纪时，这里已有稳固的君主制。沃马在汉巴里乔山设庭，坎巴塔人信奉的神祇阿巴·萨雷乔相传就居于此，一年一度的吉法塔节也在那里举行。

en: The Kambeba, also called Omagua, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the upper Amazon, whose villages once stood on the river islands and banks from the Napo to the Juruá, upstream from the site of modern Manaus and stretching into Peru. Neighbours called them Cambeba after their custom of binding a wooden board to an infant's forehead to flatten the skull, a mark of distinction they prized over the round heads of other tribes. Before European contact they were a populous, organized riverine society of chiefs and large villages, farming manioc and maize on floodplain clearings, storing manioc in flood-proof pits and moving by canoe; they were regarded as the finest canoemen on the Amazon, hunting manatee, turtle and pirarucú with lance, blowgun and clay-bullet sling. Spanish explorers met them in the 1500s, and Jesuits reached the upper Napo in 1620 and produced a catechism in their language. A smallpox epidemic was already emptying their villages when the Franciscan Laureano de la Cruz arrived in 1647 and counted fewer than five thousand survivors. From 1687 the Jesuit Samuel Fritz spent thirty-eight years among them, gathering their villages into reductions, and through the 1700s disease and colonial prejudice so reduced and dispersed them that most Kambeba abandoned their indigenous identity and merged into the river towns.
zh: 坎贝巴人又称奥马瓜人，是上亚马逊地区使用图皮-瓜拉尼语族语言的族群；他们的村庄曾分布在从纳波河到茹鲁阿河之间的亚马逊河岛屿与两岸，地当今马瑙斯以上、延伸至秘鲁境内的河段。邻族称他们为坎贝巴，源于他们用木板绑缚婴儿前额、把颅骨压平的习俗；在他们看来，这种扁平额头是优越的标志，胜过其他部落的圆头。欧洲人到来之前，坎贝巴人是人口众多、组织严密的河畔社会，有酋长和大型村落，在洪泛滩地上种植木薯和玉米，把木薯藏在防水地坑里，出行全靠独木舟；他们被视为亚马逊河上最出色的船夫，用长矛、吹箭筒和泥弹投猎海牛、河龟和巨骨舌鱼。16世纪西班牙探险家已与他们相遇；1620年耶稣会士深入上纳波河，用他们的语言编写了教理问答。1647年方济各会修士劳雷亚诺·德·拉·克鲁斯抵达时，天花正在使一座座村庄人口凋零，他统计的幸存者已不足五千人。1687年起，耶稣会士塞缪尔·弗里茨在他们中间生活了三十八年，把各村并入传教归化区；整个18世纪，疫病和殖民偏见使他们流散各地，多数坎贝巴人放弃了印第安身份，融入河畔城镇。

en: The Kambiwá, also called Cambiuá, are an Indigenous people of the Pernambuco sertão, established around Inajá, Ibimirim and Floresta. They once held the Serra Negra hills between Ibimirim and Petrolândia, still counted as their sacred territory, until pressure from white colonists drove them out; their own language survives only in short word lists and is treated as unclassified and extinct.
zh: 坎比瓦人又称坎比乌阿人，是伯南布哥腹地的原住民，聚居于伊纳雅、伊比米林和弗洛雷斯塔一带。他们原本据有伊比米林与彼得罗兰迪亚之间的塞拉内格拉山，该山仍被他们视为圣地，后在白人殖民者的压力下迁出；其本族语只留下简短词表，学界无法分类，已经消亡。

en: The Kamiare were the southern of the two Henia-Kamiare ethnicities whom Spanish documents grouped as Comechingones, holding the drier sierras and valleys of what is now San Luis province in Argentina, on the southern edge of the Sierras Pampeanas; one reading of their name takes kami as mountain country, making them the peoples of the ranges. Like their northern Henia kin they were settled farmers who also gathered wild fruit, raised animals for wool, meat and eggs, and wintered in communal stone dwellings half buried in the earth. Their dozen or so clans under curaca chiefs gathered at seasonal feasts and marked their hunting grounds with abstract rock carvings. The Spanish conquest reached them from the newly founded city of Córdoba after 1573 through encomiendas and forced resettlements, and during the seventeenth century colonial authorities moved defeated Calchaquí and Chaco groups into the same region, diluting the native communities. Epidemics and tributary labour dissolved the Kamiare chiefdoms before the century ended, and their language gave way first to Quechua and then to Spanish.
zh: 卡米亚雷人是赫尼亚-卡米亚雷两大族群中偏南的一支，占据今阿根廷圣路易斯省较干燥的山地与谷地，地处潘佩阿纳斯山脉的南缘，在西班牙文书里与北方同族一并被归为科梅钦贡人。按一种词源解释，族名中的卡米意为山岭，卡米亚雷即山岭中的诸部。他们和北方的赫尼亚人一样务农兼采集野果，饲养家畜取毛、肉和蛋，冬季栖身半埋地下的公共石屋；约十几个氏族在库拉卡酋长治理下按时节聚宴，以抽象岩画标定各自的猎场。1573年科尔多瓦建城后，西班牙人的征服经委托监护制和强制迁徙推进到他们这里；17世纪里，殖民当局又把被征服的卡尔查基人和查科各部迁入同一地区，稀释了原有的社群。瘟疫和贡赋劳役在该世纪结束前已瓦解了卡米亚雷人的酋邦，他们的语言也先让位于克丘亚语，继而被西班牙语取代。

en:
The Kamoro, also called Mimika, are a people of the southern coast of Western New Guinea, occupying the mangrove swamps, estuaries and rainforest of Mimika Regency between Etna Bay and the Otakwa River, which marks their border with the Asmat. Semi-nomadic fishers, hunters and sago gatherers, they move between river, coast and forest, and speak Kamoro, an Asmat-Kamoro language of the Trans-New Guinea phylum split into at least seven dialects, from Yamur by Etna Bay to the Mukumuga. Their self-name Kamoro means living people, while the name Mimika comes from the Mimiaika river, used by Portuguese sailors of the 1500s for the people of its banks.

Their smallest social unit is the taparu, a bilineal phratry of clans sharing a female ancestor; tradition demanded taparu exogamy and the matrilocal household, with village affairs settled in the kakurukame longhouse. Through long contact with Malukan polities such as Tidore, Namatota and Aiduma they took on titles of Malay-Molukan cast, calling their chosen paramount ruler ndati and his war leaders weyaiku. Kamoro carvers are known for the mbitoro, spirit poles up to seven metres tall whose hollow figures represent the ancestors, and for the emakame bone-house rites that honoured the dead and invoked fertility.
zh:
卡莫罗人又称米米卡人，住在新几内亚岛南部海岸，在埃特纳湾与奥塔夸河之间的米米卡县红树林沼泽、河口和热带雨林中活动，奥塔夸河也是他们与阿斯马特人的分界。他们半游牧，在河流、海岸与森林间迁徙，以渔猎和采集西谷米为生，说的卡莫罗语属跨新几内亚语系的阿斯马特-卡莫罗语群，至少分七种方言，从埃特纳湾畔的亚穆尔方言到穆库穆加方言不一而足。他们自称卡莫罗，意为活着的人；米米卡之名则来自米米艾卡河，16世纪的葡萄牙水手用这条河的名字称呼河畔居民。

他们最小的社会组织是塔帕鲁，即由共有一位女性祖先的氏族组成的双系胞族；传统上实行塔帕鲁外婚制和从妻居，村中事务在长屋卡鲁鲁卡梅里商议。由于长期与蒂多雷、纳马托塔、艾杜马等摩鹿加政权往来，他们采用了马来-摩鹿加式的头衔，把选出的最高首领称为恩达蒂，把军事首领称为韦艾库。卡莫罗工匠以姆比托罗灵柱闻名，这种高可达七米的木柱以镂空人像表现祖先；他们还举行埃马卡梅骨屋仪式，祭奠死者并祈求丰饶。

en: The Kānaka Maoli are the indigenous Polynesian people of the Hawaiian Islands, the northern apex of the Polynesian Triangle. Voyagers from the Marquesas and later from Tahiti settled the archipelago between roughly 940 and 1200, and over the centuries their society grew into rival chiefdoms ruled by hereditary chiefs called aliʻi. Land was organised in ahupuaʻa, wedge-shaped districts running from the forested uplands to the sea, complete with irrigated taro gardens and artificial fishponds, while temple platforms anchored the ritual life of each community. The islands had no single name and each was ruled separately until firearms arrived with James Cook, who sighted Kauaʻi in January 1778; the contact-era population may have been around 300,000. Kamehameha, chief of the island of Hawaiʻi, used European guns and ships to conquer Oʻahu, Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi in 1795 and completed the unification in 1810 when Kauaʻi and Niʻihau joined his Kingdom of Hawaiʻi. His son Kamehameha II abolished the ancient kapu taboos in 1819, Protestant missionaries arrived from 1820, and introduced diseases had reduced the native population to about 142,000 by the 1820s.
zh: 卡纳卡‑毛利人是夏威夷群岛的波利尼西亚原住民，住在波利尼西亚三角的北端。约940年至1200年间，来自马克萨斯群岛、其后又有来自塔希提的航海者陆续迁居该群岛；数百年间，社会发展成彼此竞争的酋邦，由世袭的阿里伊贵族统治。土地按“阿乎普阿”划分，即从山林高地一直延伸到海边的楔形区域，内有灌溉芋头园和人工鱼塘，神庙平台则维系着各社群的祭祀生活。群岛此前没有统一名称，各岛分治，直到1778年1月詹姆斯·库克望见考艾岛，火器也随之而来；接触时期的人口估计约有30万。夏威夷岛酋长卡美哈梅哈借助欧洲枪炮和船只，于1795年征服瓦胡、毛伊、莫洛凯和拉奈，又在1810年因考艾和尼豪加入而完成统一，建立夏威夷王国。其子卡美哈梅哈二世于1819年废除古老的“卡普”禁忌，新教传教士自1820年起抵达；外来疾病使原住民人口到19世纪20年代已降至约14.2万。

en: The Cañari were a tribal confederation of the southern Ecuadorian highlands, holding the country from Azuay to Saraguro around their chief town of Tumebamba, on the site of present-day Cuenca. United under an elected war leader in times of crisis, they farmed the highland valleys, kept a lunar calendar and built round, moon-shaped temples whose ruins survive at Ingapirca alongside later Inca masonry. They held out for years against Inca armies until Túpac Yupanqui and his son Huayna Capac subdued them around the turn of the sixteenth century; Tumebamba was rebuilt as a northern Inca capital, called the second Cuzco, and the Cañari adopted Kichwa while keeping much of their self-rule. In the Inca civil war they backed Huáscar, and Atahualpa punished them harshly after retaking Tumebamba. They therefore joined Francisco Pizarro against the Incas, fighting at Sacsayhuamán in 1536, and Cañari caciques such as Francisco Chilche kept their standing as Spanish allies into the 1570s, when Cañari levies served in the campaign against Tupac Amaru. Under colonial rule their own unclassified language gradually fell out of use and Kichwa took its place.
zh: 佳纳利人是厄瓜多尔南部高原的部落联盟，势力从阿苏艾延伸到萨拉古罗，以图梅班巴为中心，其地即今昆卡。他们在危急时公推一位军事首领统辖各部，在高原河谷务农，使用阴历，建造月形圆庙；这类建筑的遗迹与后来的印加石构并存于因加皮尔卡。他们抵抗印加军队多年，直到图帕克·尤潘基及其子瓦伊纳·卡帕克在16世纪之交将其征服。图梅班巴被改建为印加北部重镇，人称第二库斯科，佳纳利人改说基切瓦语，但保留了相当的自治权。印加内战中他们支持瓦斯卡尔，阿塔瓦尔帕夺回图梅班巴后施以严惩。他们因此投靠弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗对抗印加，1536年参加萨克塞瓦曼之战；以弗朗西斯科·切尔切为代表的佳纳利酋长作为西班牙盟友保有地位，16世纪70年代佳纳利士兵还参加了讨伐图帕克·阿马鲁的战事。殖民统治下，他们系属不明的本族语言逐渐废弃，为基切瓦语所取代。

en: The Kandas people live in the Patpatar area of New Ireland in the Bismarck Archipelago and speak Kandas, an Oceanic language of the Austronesian family grouped with Ramoaaina within the Meso-Melanesian cluster.
zh: 坎达斯人居住在俾斯麦群岛新爱尔兰岛的帕特帕塔尔一带，使用南岛语系大洋洲语支的坎达斯语，该语与拉莫阿艾纳语同属中美拉尼西亚语簇。

en: The Kanembu, whose name means the people of Kanem, are a Saharan-language people of the eastern and northern shores of Lake Chad, around Njimi and the Kawar oases, and the core population of the old Kanem Empire. They took to settled life in Kanem in the late twelfth century, growing wheat and millet by the lake and trading salt, ivory and slaves across the Sahara. Their rulers, the mai, became Muslims in the eleventh century, and under Mai Dunama Dabbalemi of the Sayfawa dynasty, who reigned from 1221 to 1259, Kanem conquered the Fezzan and the Hausa borderlands. In the fourteenth century attacks by the Bilala drove the Sayfawa court west to Bornu, where Kanembu settlers intermarried with local peoples and their descendants became known as the Kanuri; Kanem itself was later recovered by Mai Idris Katagarmabe. The reunited empire reached its last great age under Idris Alooma in the late sixteenth century, and after the Fula jihads of the early nineteenth century the Sayfawa gave way to the al-Kanemi shehus, while the Kanembu remained the merchant people of the Chad basin.
zh: 加奈姆布人的族名意为“加奈姆之人”，是乍得湖东岸和北岸讲撒哈拉语的民族，聚居于恩吉米和卡瓦尔绿洲一带，也是古加奈姆帝国的核心居民。12世纪末，他们在加奈姆转入定居，在湖畔种植小麦和小米，经营盐、象牙和奴隶的跨撒哈拉贸易。他们的君主称“麦伊”，11世纪皈依伊斯兰教；赛法瓦王朝的麦伊·杜纳马·达巴莱米（1221—1259年在位）时期，加奈姆征服费赞和豪萨边缘地带。14世纪，比拉拉人的进攻迫使赛法瓦朝廷西迁博尔努，迁入的加奈姆布人与当地居民通婚，后裔改称卡努里人；加奈姆本土后来由麦伊·伊德里斯·卡塔加尔马贝收复。重归统一的帝国在16世纪末伊德里斯·阿卢马时代迎来最后盛世；19世纪初的富拉尼圣战之后，赛法瓦王朝被卡内米家族的“谢胡”取代，而加奈姆布人始终是乍得盆地的商贸民族。

en: The Kangri are the people of the Kangra hills, in the Himalayan foothills of present-day Himachal Pradesh, who speak Kangri, a Western Pahari language of the Indo-Aryan family once written in the Takri script. Their country was split among small Rajput principalities, of which Kangra, ruled by the ancient Katoch dynasty, was counted the oldest and largest state of the Punjab Hills. The fort of Kangra drew plundering armies up from the plains: Mahmud of Ghazni sacked its temple treasures in 1009, and in 1333 Raja Prithvi Chand II defeated an army of Muhammad bin Tughluq that could not fight in the hills. Mughal forces serving Jahangir took the fort in 1620 after a fourteen-month siege, reducing the Katoch rajas to vassals. As Mughal power faded, Raja Sansar Chand recovered his ancestral fort in 1789 and built a short-lived hill dominion, but a Gorkha invasion in 1806 and the treaty of Jawalamukhi in 1809 delivered Kangra to Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire.
zh: 坎格拉人是康格拉山区的居民，地在今天印度喜马偕尔邦的喜马拉雅山麓，讲印度—雅利安语系西帕哈里语支的坎格拉语，旧时用塔克里字母书写。这片山地分属若干拉杰普特小邦，其中古老的卡托克王朝统治的康格拉被视为旁遮普山区最古老、最大的邦。康格拉堡一再引来平原军队的劫掠：伽色尼的马哈茂德于1009年洗劫了堡中寺院的财宝；1333年，拉杰·普里特维·昌德二世击败了不善山地作战的穆罕默德·宾·图格鲁克大军。1620年，贾汉吉尔麾下的莫卧儿军队围攻十四个月后夺取城堡，卡托克诸拉杰沦为附庸。莫卧儿势力衰落后，拉杰·桑萨尔·昌德于1789年收复祖堡，建立了短暂的山地霸业，但1806年廓尔喀入侵，1809年贾瓦拉穆基条约又把康格拉交给兰吉特·辛格的锡克帝国。

en: The Kanhgag, better known as the Kaingang, are a Jê-speaking people of the South American interior, whose traditional lands run from the Tietê River in São Paulo south through the Paraná and Santa Catarina highlands to the Ijuí River in Rio Grande do Sul, and until the nineteenth century also into Misiones in Argentina. Their culture took shape in the araucaria pine forests, whose pine nuts were a staple food. Their society is divided into two exogamic halves, kamé and kanhru, traced through the father and marked by distinct styles of body painting, straight lines and zigzags against dots and concentric circles. The Kaingang language belongs to the Southern Jê branch of the Macro-Jê trunk, quite unlike the Tupi-Guarani of the neighbouring Guaraní. Coastal groups encountered after 1500 under the name Guayaná are regarded as their ancestors, and the Xokleng were long treated as part of the same people. From the colonial era onward slave raiding and the westward push of Portuguese settlement steadily narrowed their territory, though they still held wide domains west of the Paraná in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 坎加格人（常称卡英冈人）是南美内陆说热语的族群，传统领地北起圣保罗的铁特河，南经巴拉那和圣卡塔琳娜高原，直至南里奥格兰德的伊茹伊河，19世纪以前还延伸到阿根廷的米西奥内斯。他们的文化在南洋杉林中形成，松子是重要主食。社会分为卡梅和坎鲁两个外婚半偶族，依父系传承，身体绘纹风格各异：前者用直线和锯齿纹，后者用点纹和同心圆。卡英冈语属大热语系南部分支，与邻近瓜拉尼人的图皮-瓜拉尼语截然不同。1500年以后欧洲人在沿海遇到的瓜亚纳人被视为他们的祖先，肖克兰人也曾长期被当作同一族群的一部分。殖民时代起，奴隶劫掠和葡萄牙定居点的西进不断压缩他们的领地，但到19世纪初他们仍保有巴拉那河以西的广阔土地。

en: The Kaniagmiut, or Koniag, are the Alutiiq — Sugpiaq — people of the Kodiak Archipelago off the southern Alaskan coast, speakers of the Koniag, or Kodiak, dialect within the Yupik branch of the Eskaleut languages. Their ancestors have occupied the archipelago for more than seven thousand years, and in the early nineteenth century more than sixty villages held perhaps thirteen thousand people. They lived from the rich coastal waters, taking salmon, cod, halibut, seals and whales, and wintering in semi-subterranean houses called ciqlluaq. Russian fur traders reached Kodiak in the 1780s: Grigory Shelikhov founded the first permanent Russian settlement at Three Saints Bay in 1784, the same year his men killed hundreds of Kaniagmiut at the Awa'uq Massacre on Refuge Rock. The post moved to the site of the later town of Kodiak in 1792 and became the first headquarters of Russian America, whose rulers conscripted Alutiiq hunters under hostage-taking and quotas for sea-otter pelts; Orthodox monks arrived in 1794, beginning the spread of Russian Orthodox Christianity among the islanders.
zh: 卡尼亚格缪特人又称科尼亚格人，是阿拉斯加南岸科迪亚克群岛的阿鲁蒂克人（自称苏格皮克），讲爱斯基摩-阿留申语系尤皮克语支的科尼亚格（科迪亚克）方言。他们的祖先在这片群岛上已居住七千多年，19世纪初这里有六十多个村落、人口估计达一万三千。他们靠富饶的近海水域为生，捕捞鲑鱼、鳕鱼和大比目鱼，捕猎海豹和鲸鱼，冬天住在半地穴式的“西克卢阿克”房屋里。俄国毛皮商人在18世纪80年代来到科迪亚克：格里戈里·舍利霍夫于1784年在三圣湾建立了俄国人第一个永久定居点，同年他的手下在避难岩的阿瓦乌克屠杀中杀害了数百名卡尼亚格缪特人。1792年商站迁至后来科迪亚克城的城址，成为俄属美洲最早的统治中心；殖民当局以扣押人质和摊派定额的方式强征阿鲁蒂克猎人缴纳海獭皮。1794年东正教修士抵达，俄国东正教由此开始在岛民中传播。

en: The Kanien'kehaka, the People of the Flint Place, known to English colonists as the Mohawk, are the easternmost nation of the Haudenosaunee, or Iroquois Confederacy, and hold the title Keepers of the Eastern Door. Their homeland was the Mohawk Valley west of the Hudson, where they grew corn, beans and squash from about the year 1000. In the confederacy's founding tradition the leader Hiawatha joined the Great Peacemaker in binding five warring nations under the Great Law of Peace, and in the sixteenth century they likely overwhelmed the St. Lawrence Iroquoians. In July 1609 Samuel de Champlain and his Wendat allies met a Mohawk war party near Ticonderoga and shot its chiefs with arquebuses, opening the Beaver Wars. Dutch traders built Fort Nassau on the Hudson in 1614, and after driving the Mohican eastward in 1628 the Mohawk dominated the fur trade until a smallpox epidemic in 1635 cut their numbers by nearly two thirds. During the American Revolutionary War they sided with Britain under war chief Joseph Brant, and the Sullivan Expedition of 1779 burned dozens of Haudenosaunee villages in reprisal. At the peace most Mohawk lost their New York lands and moved to Canada, where Brant founded the Six Nations of the Grand River settlement, while the Treaty of Canandaigua of 1794 confirmed their right to hold land within the United States.
zh: 卡尼恩凯哈卡人意为“燧石之地的人”，英国殖民者称其为莫霍克人，是霍迪诺肖尼（即易洛魁）联盟最东边的成员，号称“东门守护者”。他们的家园在哈得孙河以西的莫霍克河谷，约从1000年起种植玉米、豆类和南瓜。在联盟建国的传说中，领袖海华沙与大和平缔造者一起，以《大和平法》联合五个交战的民族；16世纪时，他们很可能击垮了圣劳伦斯易洛魁人。1609年7月，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰与温达特盟友在提康德罗加附近遭遇一支莫霍克战队，用火枪击毙其首领，拉开了海狸战争的序幕。1614年荷兰商人在哈得孙河修建拿骚堡；1628年莫霍克人把莫西干人向东驱赶后主导了毛皮贸易，直到1635年天花疫情使人口减少近三分之二。美国独立战争中，他们在战酋约瑟夫·布兰特带领下站在英国一边，1779年的沙利文远征焚毁数十个霍迪诺肖尼村庄作为报复。战后多数莫霍克人失去纽约的土地迁往加拿大，布兰特在那里建立了大河六族定居点；1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》确认了他们在美国境内持有土地的权利。

en: The Kanindé, also written Canindé, are an Indigenous people of Ceará, kin to the Janduí and Paiacu and descended, like them, from the Tarairiu groups of the northeastern sertão; their extinct Tarairiu tongue belonged to the Macro-Jê family and has been replaced by Portuguese. They take their name from the war leader Canindé, the foremost chief of the Janduís, who led the Cariri confederation's resistance to the Portuguese in the seventeenth century and in 1692 forced the Portuguese Crown to sign a peace treaty, which the settlers later broke. Kanindé oral tradition places their origin in the country around Mombaça, from where they migrated with their Jenipapo-Kanindé kin along the Curu River, by way of Quixadá, to the Baturité massif, where the communities of Aratuba and Canindé keep alive a hunting culture of traps and seasonal game rules alongside subsistence farming.
zh: 卡宁德人（又译卡宁德）是塞阿拉的原住民，与扬杜伊人、帕亚库人同源，和他们一样是东北腹地塔拉里乌族群的后裔；他们已经消亡的塔拉里乌语属大热语系，族人后来使用葡萄牙语。其族名来自军事首领卡宁德，他是扬杜伊人最重要的酋长，在17世纪率领卡里里部落联盟抵抗葡萄牙人，并于1692年迫使葡萄牙王室签署和约，但和约后来被殖民者撕毁。卡宁德人的口传传统把发源地定在蒙巴萨一带，后来他们与亲缘的热尼帕波-卡宁德人一起沿库鲁河迁徙，经基沙达抵达巴图里特山地；阿拉图巴和卡宁德的社群在生计农业之外，仍保留着使用陷阱、遵守狩猎季节规矩的狩猎文化。

en: The Kanisian, better known as the Canichana, are a people of the flooded Llanos de Mojos in the Bolivian Beni, whose villages stood on the Mamoré and Machupo rivers and whose language is treated as an isolate. In 1693 the Jesuit Augustín Zapata became the first outsider to enter their territory, then described as wild and inhospitable; two years later the Canichana themselves gathered on the Mamoré asking for a mission, and in 1696 Lorenzo Legarda founded San Pedro with twelve hundred of them. Floods, smallpox and fire twice forced the town to move before it settled at its final site, and its central position made it the most prosperous of the Moxos reductions, where the Canichana took to farming, woodworking and jewelry. When the Jesuits were expelled from Moxos between 1767 and 1769 San Pedro declined sharply and many Canichana drifted back into the forest.
zh: 卡尼西人更常见的称呼是卡尼查纳人，住在玻利维亚贝尼省泛滥的莫霍斯平原，村落分布在马莫雷河与马丘波河沿岸，所说的卡尼查纳语被视为孤立语言。1693年，耶稣会士奥古斯丁·萨帕塔首次进入这片被视为蛮荒的土地；两年后，卡尼查纳人自己聚集到马莫雷河畔，请求建立传教镇。1696年，洛伦索·莱加尔达率一千二百名卡尼查纳人建立圣佩德罗镇。洪水、天花和火灾使该镇两度搬迁，17世纪末才定于现址；凭居中的地理位置，它成为莫霍斯各传教镇中最繁荣的一座，卡尼查纳人在此学会农耕、木工和首饰制作。1767至1769年耶稣会被逐出莫霍斯，圣佩德罗迅速衰落，许多卡尼查纳人重新散入森林。

en: The Kankanaey are an Austronesian people of the Cordillera mountains of northern Luzon, counted among the Igorot or Cordilleran peoples. Their ancestors came with the Austronesian expansion out of Taiwan around 3000 BC, and genetic studies suggest the highland groups retained an unusually early Austronesian ancestry, close to that of the Lapita seafarers who settled the Pacific. They occupy western Mountain Province and northern Benguet, with related Applai communities on the higher eastern slopes, and built their villages around steep wet-rice terraces cut into the mountains. Traditional society centered on the dap-ay, a men's dormitory and civic council house, while girls lived in separate ebgan dormitories, and the highlands also produced gold that was traded down to Pangasinan markets. When the Spanish pushed into Benguet from 1572, drawn by that gold and by the aim of converting the highlanders, the Kankanaey and their Igorot neighbors resisted from fortified mountain settlements and were never fully brought under colonial rule, keeping their own priests, rituals and terrace economy through the entire Spanish period. Their Kankanaey language belongs to the Northern Luzon branch of Philippine Austronesian, and lowland Ilocano spread among them through trade and migration.
zh: 坎卡奈人是吕宋北部科迪勒拉山区的南岛语系民族，属于伊哥洛特人（科迪勒拉诸族）的一员。其先民在公元前3000年前后随自台湾出发的南岛语族迁徙而来，基因研究显示，这支高地人群保留了极为古老的南岛语族血统，与远航太平洋的拉皮塔人先民十分接近。他们居住在高山省西部和本格特省北部，较高的东坡上还有亲缘的阿普莱人聚落，并在陡峭山坡上开垦层层水稻梯田建立村落。传统社会以“达普艾”男子宿舍兼公民议事所为中心，少女则另住在“埃布甘”女子宿舍；山区出产的黄金沿山路运到邦阿西楠的市场交易。1572年起，西班牙人为黄金和传教侵入本格特，坎卡奈人与伊哥洛特邻族依托设防的山地聚落抵抗，始终未被彻底纳入殖民统治，在整个西班牙时期保留了自己的祭司、仪式和梯田经济。他们的坎卡奈语属于菲律宾南岛语的北吕宋支，而低地的伊洛卡诺语也随着贸易和迁徙在他们中间传播。

en: The Kannadiga are the Dravidian people of the Karnataka plateau in the southwestern Deccan, whose mother tongue, Kannada, has an unbroken literary history of roughly fifteen hundred years. The first Kannada-speaking kingdoms were the Kadambas of Banavasi and the Western Gangas, who raised Kannada to an administrative language; the Halmidi inscription of 450 is its earliest known written record, and the modern Kannada script descends from the fifth-century Kadamba script. Jain court poets flourished under the Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta from the eighth to tenth centuries, and in the twelfth century Basava led his Virashaiva religious movement from Kalyani. The Badami and Kalyani Chalukyas and the Hoysalas, whose temples stand at Belur and Halebeidu, carried this culture across the Deccan. In 1336 Harihara and Bukka founded the Vijayanagara Empire, whose capital at Hampi became the greatest Kannada-ruled state of the age until the Battle of Talikota in 1565, when the Deccan sultanates sacked the city. Afterwards the Keladi Nayakas held Ikkeri and the Wodeyar dynasty built up Mysore, while Maratha armies overran the north after 1674. Hyder Ali and his son Tipu Sultan made Mysore a major power in the later eighteenth century, until Tipu's death in the Anglo-Mysore wars of 1799 left the Kannada lands divided among the British, Mysore and the Nizam of Hyderabad.
zh: 卡纳达人是德干高原西南部卡纳塔克地区的达罗毗荼语族群，母语卡纳达语拥有约一千五百年未曾中断的书面文学史。最早的卡纳达语本土政权是巴纳瓦西的卡丹巴王朝和西恒伽王朝，它们使卡纳达语获得行政语言地位；450年的哈尔米迪铭文是现存最早的卡纳达语文献，今天的卡纳达字母则由5世纪的卡丹巴字母演变而来。8至10世纪，耆那教宫廷诗人在曼亚凯塔的罗湿陀罗拘陀王朝治下盛极一时；12世纪，巴沙瓦在格利亚尼发起维拉湿婆（林伽派）宗教运动。巴达米遮娄其、格利亚尼遮娄其和曷萨拉诸王朝把这一文化传遍德干，曷萨拉人在贝鲁尔和哈勒比杜留下了神庙。1336年，诃利诃罗与布卡建立毗奢耶那伽罗帝国，都城亨比成为当时最强大的卡纳达语政权；1565年塔利科塔战役中，德干诸苏丹国联军摧毁了亨比。此后纳亚克首领在伊凯里的凯拉迪割据，瓦迪亚尔家族经营迈索尔，马拉塔人则在1674年后席卷北部。18世纪后期，海德尔·阿里与儿子提普苏丹把迈索尔抬升为南印强国；1799年提普在英迈战争中败亡，卡纳达诸地随后被英国人、迈索尔和海得拉巴的尼扎姆瓜分。

en: The Kannauji are the Indo-Aryan people of the central Ganga-Yamuna Doab, the country around the ancient city of Kannauj, whose main centers in 1337 included Kannauj itself and Etawah. Their speech, Kannauji, is a Western Hindi language transitional between Braj Bhasha and Awadhi, which Grierson divided into the Tirhari and transitional dialects. Kannauj, the ancient Kanyakubja, was already the capital of the Panchala kingdom and later of the Maukhari dynasty, and it reached its greatest splendor as the capital of Harsha in the seventh century, when the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang described it as a vast and prosperous city. From the eighth to the tenth century it was the prize of the tripartite struggle between the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas, staying with the Pratiharas; Mahmud of Ghazni sacked it in 1018, the Gahadavalas restored its glory under Govindachandra, and Muhammad Ghori overthrew Jayachandra at Chandwar in 1193, after which Iltutmish absorbed the city into the Delhi Sultanate. Long a center of learning and perfume distillation, Kannauj passed to the Mughals, and in 1540 Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at the Battle of Kannauj on its outskirts. Under Mughal rule the region was a flourishing crown domain famed for its attar scents, before the East India Company extended its rule over the Doab in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 卡瑙杰人是恒河与亚穆纳河之间中部河间地的印度-雅利安人，聚居于古城卡瑙杰一带，1337年时的主要城镇包括卡瑙杰和埃塔瓦。他们讲的卡瑙杰语属西印地语，是布拉杰语与阿瓦德语之间的过渡语言，格里尔森将它分为蒂尔哈里方言和过渡方言两个变体。卡瑙杰古称曲女城，曾是般阇罗王国和后来穆克里王朝的都城，7世纪作为戒日王的首都达到极盛，中国求法僧玄奘称它是宏大富庶的名城。8至10世纪，它是瞿折罗-波罗提诃罗、波罗与拉什特拉库塔三朝争霸的争夺目标，最终为波罗提诃罗人保有；1018年伽色尼的马哈茂德洗劫该城，伽哈达瓦拉王朝在戈文达旃陀罗治下恢复其荣光，1193年古尔的穆罕默德在昌德瓦尔击败阇耶旃陀罗，随后伊勒杜迷失把该城并入德里苏丹国。卡瑙杰久以学术和香水蒸馏闻名，后归莫卧儿统治，1540年舍尔沙·苏利在城外的卡瑙杰战役中击败胡马雍。莫卧儿治下这一地区成为繁荣的王室领地，以阿塔尔香料著称，19世纪初随帝国衰乱落入东印度公司之手。

en: The Kanza, who call themselves Kaáⁿze and are also known as the Kaw, are one of the five Dhegiha peoples speaking a Siouan language. Their oral history tells of a westward migration from the Ohio valley: the Quapaw turned down the Mississippi, the Osage settled in central Missouri, while the Kanza halted on the Missouri River in present-day northwestern Missouri and northeastern Kansas, the state that later took its name from them. The French explorer Bourgmont left the first European account after visiting their large village in 1724, and by the late eighteenth century they had established themselves along the Kansas River, farming, hunting bison and often fighting the Pawnee. After the Louisiana Purchase of 1803 American expansion brought mounting pressure: in 1825 they ceded vast lands in Missouri and Kansas, and smallpox epidemics in 1827 and 1831 killed about five hundred of them, leaving the weakened tribe surrounded by settlers and rival nations.
zh: 坎扎人自称卡恩泽，又称卡乌人，是说苏语族语言的德吉哈五大部族之一。据他们的口述史，德吉哈人从俄亥俄河谷西迁：夸保人沿密西西比河而下，奥塞奇人留在密苏里中部，坎扎人则在今密苏里西北与堪萨斯东北一带的密苏里河畔停驻，后来的堪萨斯州便以他们命名。法国探险家布尔蒙于1724年拜访他们的大村庄，留下了最早的欧洲人记述；到18世纪末，坎扎人已在堪萨斯河沿岸定居，经营农业、捕猎野牛，并常与波尼人交战。1803年路易斯安那购地后，美国扩张使压力日增：1825年他们割让了密苏里与堪萨斯的大片土地，1827年和1831年的天花疫情又夺去约五百人的生命，元气大伤的部族就此被定居者和敌对部族包围。

en: The Kantakul, written Kaltakul in Russian documents, were a Tungus, or Evenki, clan of the Vilyuy and lower Lena taiga in Yakutia, listed in 1639 among the rods forced to pay the fur tribute, or yasak. They lived by hunting and moving with small reindeer herds through the taiga.
zh: 坎塔库尔人在俄文档案中写作卡尔塔库尔，是游猎于雅库特维柳伊河与勒拿河下游泰加林的通古斯（鄂温克）氏族，1639年被列入被迫缴纳毛皮贡赋牙萨克的氏族名册。他们以狩猎为生，赶着小规模驯鹿群在泰加林中迁徙。

en: The Kanum are a Papuan people of the marshy border country between South Papua's Merauke Regency and Papua New Guinea's Western Province, including the Wasur National Park area. Counted as a Marind subgroup, they speak Kanum, a Yam-family dialect chain, and live in clans such as the Mbanggu and Ndimar.
zh: 卡努姆人是巴布亚人的一支，住在南巴布亚马老奇县与巴布亚新几内亚西部省交界的沼泽地带，包括瓦苏尔国家公园一带。他们被视为马林德人的分支，说属亚姆语系的卡努姆语，社会分为姆班古、恩迪马尔等氏族。

en: The Kapampangan are an Austronesian people of the fertile Pampanga River basin in central Luzon, whose homeland once ran from Tondo north across the plains of Pampanga, Bataan and Tarlac; a stone adze from Candaba shows human settlement going back five thousand years, and tradeware of 1500 BC has been found at Candaba and Porac. They originally came from southern Luzon and moved north into the basin ahead of Tagalog expansion, displacing the Aeta foragers into the mountains. Around 1500 the spread of Bruneian Malay power and trade made Islam prominent on the coast, so that the Muslim ruler Tarik Sulayman of Macabebe led the Kapampangan resistance at the Battle of Bangkusay Channel in 1571, the first major fight against the newly arrived Spaniards. Once conquered, the Kapampangan became the colony's most trusted native soldiers: they helped defend Manila against the Dutch, notably in 1640, after which Governor Corcuera granted them the rare privilege of studying in the Spanish academies of Manila. Their warlike pride also fired the Kapampangan Revolt of 1660, put down with the help of the Arayat datu Juan Macapagal. In 1757 the province of Bataan was carved from their territory, and during the British occupation of Manila in 1762 Tagalog refugees flooded into Bulacan and Nueva Ecija, where most Kapampangan families eventually sold their lands and assimilated, leaving the Kapampangan language strongest in the smaller province of Pampanga.
zh: 邦板牙人是吕宋中部富饶的邦板牙河流域的南岛语系民族，故土曾从通多向北横跨邦板牙、巴丹和打拉诸平原；坎达巴出土的石锛证明人类定居可上溯五千年，坎达巴和波拉克还发现了公元前1500年的陶器与贸易瓷。他们源自吕宋南部，在他加禄人扩张之前北迁入盆地，把阿埃塔狩猎者排挤进山区。约1500年，文莱马来势力与贸易东渐，伊斯兰教在沿海兴盛，因此1571年，马卡贝贝的穆斯林首领塔里克·苏莱曼率邦板牙人在邦库赛海峡之战中抵抗初到的西班牙人，这是当地人对征服者的第一场大战。被征服后，邦板牙人成为殖民地最受信任的本土士兵，协助马尼拉抵御荷兰人，尤以1640年的战斗为著，此后科尔库埃拉总督授予他们在马尼拉西班牙学院就读的罕有特权。他们的尚武之气也催生了1660年的邦板牙起义，最后靠阿拉延的达图胡安·马卡帕加尔相助才被镇压。1757年，巴丹省从他们的土地上划出；1762年英军占领马尼拉期间，他加禄难民涌入布拉干和新怡诗夏，当地邦板牙家族大多变卖田产并被同化，邦板牙语此后只在较小的邦板牙省最为强势。

en: The Kaqchikel are a Quichean-speaking Maya people of the central Guatemalan highlands, whose late Postclassic kingdom was one of the strongest in the region. They began as warriors and allies of the neighbouring K'iche, whose king K'iq'ab granted their lords Hun-Toh and Wuqu-Batz' high titles; when court intrigue turned against them, the four Kaqchikel clans left the K'iche capital of Q'umarkaj and founded their own capital at Iximche around 1470. From there they defeated the K'iche in battle around 1491, capturing their kings and the idol of their god Tohil, and crushed a revolt of their own rebel clans in 1493. Ruled by four lords and divided between the main line at Iximche and the autonomous Chajoma branch at Mixco Viejo, the kingdom became the second power of the highlands, and its scribes later wrote its story in the Kaqchikel language using Latin letters, the work known as the Annals of the Cakchiquels. When Pedro de Alvarado arrived in 1524, the Kaqchikel first allied with the Spanish against their old K'iche and Tz'utujil rivals, and Iximche became the first capital of colonial Guatemala. Exorbitant gold tribute soon drove them to abandon the city and fight a guerrilla war from the hills; the Spanish burned Iximche and moved their capital away in 1527, and the last Kaqchikel kings surrendered in 1530.
zh: 卡克奇克尔人是说基切语支语言的玛雅民族，居住在危地马拉中部高地，他们在后古典期末期建立的王国曾是当地最强的政权之一。他们起初是邻邦基切人的战士与盟友，基切君王基卡布授予其首领温·托和乌库·巴茨高贵头衔；当宫廷阴谋转而针对他们时，卡克奇克尔的四大氏族离开基切都城库马尔卡赫，约于1470年另建都城伊希姆切。他们以此为基地，在约1491年大败基切人，俘获其君王和主神托希尔的神像，又于1493年平定了内部叛乱氏族的反抗。王国由四位首领共同治理，分为伊希姆切的主系和以旧米斯科为都、保持自治的查霍马支系，成为高地第二强权；他们的书吏后来用拉丁字母以卡克奇克尔语写下本族历史，即《卡克奇克尔编年史》。1524年佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多到来时，卡克奇克尔人先与西班牙人结盟，共同攻打宿敌基切人和楚图希尔人，伊希姆切也成为殖民地时期危地马拉的第一个首府。但西班牙人索取的黄金贡赋过于苛重，他们很快弃城进入山区打游击战；西班牙人焚毁伊希姆切并于1527年迁走首府，末代卡克奇克尔君王最终于1530年投降。

en: The Karachays are a Turkic-speaking mountain people of the central Caucasus, grazing their herds in the high valleys of the Kuban, the Bolshoy Zelenchuk and the Malka beneath Mount Elbrus. They share one language and one origin with the neighbouring Balkars: local Caucasian stock of the ancient Koban culture, with an admixture of Alans and of Kipchak soldiers who fled into the mountains after Timur's campaigns around 1395, when the Alanian kingdom of Maghas, which some place at Arkhyz in Karachay land, was destroyed. Their society is built on some thirty clans, the tukums, and they call themselves the mountaineers. Living remote among Circassian, Georgian and Ossetian neighbours, they kept their Kipchak tongue while absorbing the customs of the high Caucasus, and adopted Islam only in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, through contact with Kumyks, Nogais, Crimean Tatars and Circassians, with the Qadiri Sufi order taking root among them. The Russian conquest came late: at the Battle of Khasauka on 20 October 1828 General Georgy Emanuel's troops broke their resistance, and the elders of Kart-Dzhurt accepted the tsar's rule, keeping their own officials, courts and Sharia law. From 1831, however, Karachay fighters joined the wider mountain war against Russian garrisons.
zh: 卡拉恰伊人是高加索中部讲突厥语的山民，在厄尔布鲁士山麓的库班河、大泽连丘克河和马尔卡河高山峡谷中放牧。他们与邻近的巴尔卡尔人同源同语：族底是古代科班文化的高加索本地居民，又混入了阿兰人和钦察士兵的血统——约1395年帖木儿的征战摧毁了都城设在马加斯的阿兰王国（有学者认为马加斯就在卡拉恰伊土地上的阿尔赫兹），一批钦察士兵逃入深山，与本地人通婚融合，形成了卡拉恰伊—巴尔卡尔人。他们自称“山民”，社会由约三十个称作图库姆的氏族构成。深居于切尔克斯、格鲁吉亚和奥塞梯邻族之间，他们保住了钦察语，也吸收了高加索的风俗；伊斯兰教迟至17至18世纪才经库梅克人、诺盖人、克里米亚鞑靼人和切尔克斯人传入，卡迪林耶苏菲教团随之扎根。俄国的征服来得很晚：1828年10月20日，格奥尔基·埃马努埃尔将军的部队在哈萨乌卡之战中击溃其抵抗，卡尔特—朱尔特的长老接受沙皇统治，但保留了自己的官吏、法庭和沙里亚法。然而从1831年起，卡拉恰伊战士便加入了山区各族反对俄国驻军的广泛战事。

en: The Karajarri are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Pilbara, south-west of the Kimberley, holding the country between the coast and the Great Sandy Desert. Their Marrngu-branch Pama-Nyungan language has coastal and inland dialects, from Najanaja on the shore to Nawurtu in the eastern desert country; their neighbours include the northern Yawuru and the southern Nyangumarta.
zh: 卡拉贾里人是金伯利西南、北皮尔巴拉的澳大利亚原住民，据有海岸与大沙沙漠之间的地带。他们的语言属帕马‑牛雅语系马恩古语支，方言从沿海的纳贾纳贾到东部沙漠地带的纳武尔图，各具沿海与内陆色彩；北面的邻族是亚乌鲁人，南面是尼扬古马达人。

en: The Karrangpurru, also known as the Karranga, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory whose country lay in the Victoria River district among the Ngarinyman, Malngin and Wardaman lands. Their ethnonym adds the common suffix -purru to Karranga. Their language, Karranga, was never recorded before its speakers were overwhelmed; it is thought to have been an eastern Ngumpin tongue of the Ngumpin-Yapa group, and Patrick McConvell suggests it was a dialect of Mudburra. The Karrangpurru were decimated very early in the colonial period by introduced disease and massacres, and their grounds were absorbed into the Victoria River Downs pastoral run, leaving only a single family tracing descent from them.
zh: 卡朗普鲁人（亦称卡朗加人）是北领地的澳大利亚原住民，领地在维多利亚河区，与纳里宁曼人、马尔宁人和瓦达曼人的土地相邻。族名由“卡朗加”加上常见后缀“普鲁”构成。他们的卡朗加语在使用者大批罹难前未及记录，一般认为属恩贡宾-亚帕语群的恩贡宾东部语支，帕特里克·麦康维尔则推测它是穆德巴拉语的一种方言。殖民时代早期，传入的疾病和屠杀使卡朗普鲁人人口锐减，领地被并入维多利亚河当斯牧场，最终只有一个家族仍能追溯其血统。

en: The Karankawa were a chain of independent, seasonally wandering bands along the Gulf coast of southern Texas, from Galveston Bay toward Corpus Christi, among them the Capoque, Copane and Mariame. In groups of thirty or forty they paddled dugout canoes between coastal camps, pitching willow-framed wigwams covered in hides, and lived on fish, turtles and oysters, venison and prickly pears, using natural asphalt to fix arrowheads and waterproof their baskets. Their first European guest arrived as a castaway in 1528, when Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca, wrecked with the Narváez expedition on Galveston Island, was cared for by the Capoque and lived seven years among the coast peoples. After La Salle's Frenchmen stole their canoes and built Fort St. Louis, the Karankawa overran the fort and spared only five of its twenty settlers, and a Spanish expedition rescued the survivors in 1689. Spain answered with the presidio and mission system of La Bahía from 1722, but the Karankawa repeatedly fled the missions and raided Mission Rosario, weathering punitive campaigns between 1779 and 1789. They traded skins to English and French smugglers for muskets and attacked the pirate Jean Lafitte's men during his occupation of Galveston Island from 1817 to 1821. After Stephen Austin's colonists arrived in 1821 they were hunted in actions such as the Battle of Jones Creek in 1824, and some who fought for Mexico at the Alamo in 1836 drew heavy Texan retaliation, the opening of their final dispersal.
zh: 卡兰卡瓦人是得克萨斯南部墨西哥湾沿岸一串互不统属、随季节迁徙的游群，从加尔维斯顿湾到科珀斯克里斯蒂一带都有他们的营地，卡波克人、科帕内人、马里亚梅人都是其中的分支。他们以三四十人为一队，划着独木舟在海岸营地间转移，竖起柳枝弯成、外蒙兽皮的棚屋，以鱼、龟、牡蛎、鹿肉和仙人掌果为食，还用天然沥青固定箭头、给篮子防水。1528年，他们迎来了第一位落难的欧洲客人：纳尔瓦埃斯远征队在加尔维斯顿岛覆灭后，卡韦萨·德巴卡被卡波克人收留，在沿岸诸族中生活了七年。拉萨尔手下的法国人偷走他们的独木舟并建起圣路易堡，卡兰卡瓦人随即攻陷堡垒，二十名殖民者只留下五名活口，一支西班牙探险队于1689年救出了幸存者。西班牙人的回应是1722年起在拉巴希亚建立要塞与传教站体系，但卡兰卡瓦人屡屡逃出传教站、袭击罗萨里奥传教站，并在1779至1789年的讨伐中挺了过来。他们用兽皮向英、法走私者换取火枪，还在1817至1821年海盗让·拉菲特盘踞加尔维斯顿岛期间围攻其手下。1821年斯蒂芬·奥斯汀的移民涌入后，1824年琼斯溪之战之类的围剿接踵而至；1836年，部分卡兰卡瓦人在阿拉莫为墨西哥作战，招致得克萨斯人的惨烈报复，这也揭开了他们最终流散的序幕。

en: The Karapanã are a Tucanoan-speaking people of the Vaupés rainforests on the Colombia and Brazil border, whose clans occupy communal maloca houses and live from shifting cultivation of bitter manioc together with fishing and hunting. Exogamous marriage alliances with neighbouring peoples leave their communities multilingual.
zh: 卡拉帕纳人是讲图卡诺语族语言的族群，住在哥伦比亚与巴西边境沃佩斯河流域的雨林里；各氏族居住在公共长屋中，以轮耕方式种植苦木薯，兼事渔猎。他们与邻族实行外婚联姻，聚落里因此普遍通行多种语言。

en: The Karbi, known in older records as the Mikir and calling themselves Arleng, are a long-established Tibeto-Burman people of central Assam whose traditions remember them as plains dwellers along the Kalang and Kopili rivers before pressure from the Dimasa Kachari kings drove them into the neighbouring hills. Some placed themselves under Jaintia suzerainty, while others built a seat at Socheng in the Rongkhang range; harassment under Jaintia rule then pushed many north into the Ahom kingdom, where from the early seventeenth century they sought the protection of the Barphukan at Raha. They lived by jhum shifting cultivation organised around the annual Rongker festival, with women weaving cotton and Eri silk, and kept an animist faith handed down through ritual singers. The Burmese invasions of Assam between 1817 and 1825 scattered many Karbi into the deep forests and across the Brahmaputra.
zh: 米基尔人自称阿伦，是阿萨姆中部历史悠久的藏缅语族群，旧文献据外界对他们的称呼记作米基尔。据其传说，先民本是卡朗河与科皮利河畔的平原居民，后来在迪马萨·卡查里诸王的压力下退入邻近丘陵。一部分人接受贾因蒂亚的宗主权，另一部分在龙康岭的索成建立据点；贾因蒂亚统治下的侵扰又迫使许多人北投阿洪王国，从17世纪初起向拉哈的巴普坎寻求庇护。他们以刀耕火种的轮垦为生，生活围绕一年一度的龙克尔节庆展开，妇女纺织棉布与蓖麻蚕丝，并保有由仪式歌手传承的万物有灵信仰。1817—1825年缅甸入侵阿萨姆，使许多米基尔人逃入深山或北渡布拉马普特拉河。

en: The Karelians are a Baltic Finnic people of the lands between Lake Ladoga, the Karelian Isthmus and the White Sea, speaking a Balto-Finnic language close to Finnish. They emerged in the early Middle Ages as settlers from western Finland mixed with the local population, and archaeology shows dense settlement along the western shore of Lake Ladoga from the seventh century. Viking sagas knew them as the Kirjalir, and Scandinavian tradition credits them with the sack of Sigtuna in 1187; Russian chronicles first name them in 1143 and show them first raiding alongside Novgorod and then gradually falling under its power, with an Orthodox conversion mission in 1227. The Third Swedish Crusade of 1293 brought western Karelia under the Swedish crown, and the Treaty of Nöteborg in 1323 split the people in two, western Karelians turning Catholic and later Lutheran while their eastern kin became Orthodox under Novgorod, and eastern Karelians had spread north to the White Sea by the late fourteenth century. The Treaty of Stolbovo in 1617 placed most Karelians under Sweden, but Lutheran pressure drove an Orthodox exodus after 1658, when many migrated to Tver, Valdai and White Karelia. The Treaty of Nystad in 1721 returned the isthmus to Russia, and in 1812 the western lands were joined to the Grand Duchy of Finland; in the 1830s the Karelian folklore collected by Elias Lönnrot became the Kalevala, published in 1835.
zh: 卡累利阿人是波罗的芬兰人的一支，生活在拉多加湖、卡累利阿地峡与白海之间的土地上，使用与芬兰语相近的波罗的芬兰语支语言卡累利阿语。中世纪早期，西芬兰的定居者与当地居民融合形成了这一族群，考古发现表明7世纪起拉多加湖西岸已村落密集。维京萨迦称他们为基尔亚利人，斯堪的纳维亚传说把1187年洗劫瑞典城镇锡格蒂纳一事归于他们；俄国编年史1143年首次提到他们，记载他们起初与诺夫哥罗德联手出征，后来逐渐被其控制，1227年还有一次向他们传布东正教的尝试。1293年第三次瑞典十字军把西卡累利阿置于瑞典王权之下，1323年的《内特堡和约》将这个民族一分为二：西部的卡累利阿人先后皈依天主教和路德宗，东部同族则在诺夫哥罗德治下信奉东正教，14世纪末东卡累利阿人已向北扩散到白海。1617年《斯托尔博沃和约》使多数卡累利阿人归入瑞典，但路德宗的压力引发东正教徒外流，1658年后许多人迁往特维尔、瓦尔代和白卡累利阿。1721年《尼斯塔德和约》把卡累利阿地峡归还俄国，1812年西部土地并入芬兰大公国；19世纪30年代，埃利亚斯·伦罗特在东卡累利阿搜集的民间诗歌编成1835年出版的《卡勒瓦拉》。

en: The Karen are a loose family of some twenty Karenic-speaking Tibeto-Burman peoples, the largest being the upland S'gaw and the lowland Pwo, spread across the Irrawaddy delta, the Pegu hills and the Tenasserim border with Thailand. Linguists date their migration into Burma between roughly 300 and 800, when they followed the Salween and Irrawaddy southward, learned wet-rice farming from the older Mon-Khmer villagers and helped irrigate the Kyaukse and Minbu districts alongside Palaung, Mon and Wa communities before the Burmese pushed them on into the eastern hills and delta. They appear in Pagan inscriptions under the names Karyan and Cakraw as early as 1165 to 1167, often listed as pagoda slaves, while lowland Pwo Karen served the Mon courts as recognised original settlers and highland groups kept to rotation farming and spirit worship. Some southern Karen joined the Palaung in building up Toungoo as a rallying point against Burmese expansion. Buddhism reached the Pwo Karen through the Mon only in the late 1700s, with the Yedagon monastery on Mount Zwegabin as its literary centre, and in 1828 Tha Byu became the first Karen baptized by the American Baptist missionary George Boardman, opening the Christian chapter of Karen history.
zh: 克伦人是操克伦语支诸语言的藏缅语族群的泛称，约有二十个支系，以山地的斯高人和低地的波人为最大两支，分布在伊洛瓦底三角洲、勃固山区和与泰国接壤的丹那沙林边境。语言学者估计他们在约300—800年间沿萨尔温江和伊洛瓦底江南迁，从更古老的孟-高棉村民处学会水稻种植，并在缅人到来前与德昂人、孟人、佤人一起开凿了皎施和敏布地区的灌溉工程，随后被缅人排挤到东部山区和三角洲。早在1165—1167年的蒲甘碑铭中，他们就以“卡朗”“加觉”等名出现，常被列为佛塔奴；低地波克伦人作为公认的最早定居者供职于孟人宫廷，山地支系则维持轮作农业和精灵崇拜。一部分南方克伦人曾与德昂人合力经营东吁，作为抵御缅人扩张的据点。佛教迟至1700年代末才经孟人传入波克伦人，泽加宾山上的耶达贡寺成为其文字中心；1828年，塔布经美国浸礼会传教士乔治·博德曼施洗，成为第一位克伦基督徒，开启了克伦历史的基督教篇章。

en: The Karkar are the people of Karkar, an oval volcanic island in the Bismarck Sea some seventy kilometres off the north coast of New Guinea in Madang Province, covered in fertile volcanic soil and dominated by a central volcano with two nested calderas. They speak Waskia, a Papuan language used on roughly half of the island and in a few mainland villages, and it serves as the common language between Waskia villages and those speaking Takia, an Oceanic tongue deeply reshaped by long contact with Waskia. European ships began to reach the island in the sixteenth century: the Spanish navigator Inigo Ortiz de Retes sighted it in 1545, the Dutch voyage of Willem Schouten and Jacob le Maire named it High Island in 1616, and Abel Tasman and William Dampier passed it in turn.
zh: 卡尔卡尔人居住在卡尔卡尔岛上；这座椭圆形火山岛位于俾斯麦海，距新几内亚北岸马当省约七十公里，岛上土壤肥沃，中央矗立着一座带有两层嵌套破火山口的活火山。他们使用的瓦斯基亚语是一种巴布亚语言，通行于岛屿约一半的地区以及大陆沿岸的少数村庄，也是瓦斯基亚村落与使用塔基亚语的村落之间的通用语，而塔基亚语属大洋洲语支，因长期受瓦斯基亚语影响而发生了深刻重组。欧洲船只从16世纪起陆续抵达该岛：西班牙航海家伊尼戈·奥尔蒂斯·德雷特斯于1545年首先望见它，威廉·斯豪滕与雅各布·勒梅尔的荷兰船队在1616年将其命名为高岛，此后阿贝尔·塔斯曼和威廉·丹皮尔也曾先后经过。

en: The Karuk, whose name means upriver people in their own language, are the people of the middle Klamath River in northwestern California. Their villages lined the river from Bluff Creek near Orleans up through the country around Happy Camp and toward the present Oregon border, and they traditionally called themselves the middle of the world people. Downstream lived the Yurok, the downriver people, and the usual English names of both groups come from Karuk directional words. The Karuk language is a language isolate, sometimes assigned to the proposed Hokan family. Their economy turned on the Klamath salmon runs, acorn harvests and deer, supplemented by tobacco they sowed themselves, while basketmaking and the several-day Brush Dance, Jump Dance and Pikyavish ceremonies, held to heal the sick and renew the world, anchored village life. Alfred Kroeber estimated their population in 1770 at about fifteen hundred. The Spanish missions halted far to the south at San Francisco Bay, and although Hudson's Bay Company trappers entered the lower Klamath in 1827, the upriver Karuk were little disturbed before 1837.
zh: 卡鲁克人其名在本族语中意为“上游之人”，是加利福尼亚西北部克拉马斯河中游的族群。他们的村落沿河岸排列，从奥林斯附近的布拉夫克里克上溯，经哈皮坎普一带一直延伸到今俄勒冈州边界附近，传统自称“世界中心之人”。下游住着意为“下游之人”的尤罗克人，两族通行的英文名称都来自卡鲁克语的方位词。卡鲁克语是一种语言孤立语，有时被归入假说中的霍坎语系。他们的生计依托克拉马斯河的鲑鱼洄游、橡果收获和鹿，并自行种植烟草；编篮技艺以及持续数日的灌木舞、跳跃舞和皮克亚维什仪式——意在治病和修复世界——是村落生活的核心。人类学家艾尔弗雷德·克罗伯估计，1770年卡鲁克人约有一千五百人。西班牙传教站止步于南方遥远的旧金山湾；1827年哈德逊湾公司的捕猎者虽进入克拉马斯河下游，上游的卡鲁克人在1837年以前仍很少受到打扰。

en: Kasayi is the Luba name for the Kasai country, and under this label the game groups the western Baluba, the Luba-speaking villagers of the Kasai river basin west of the Luba heartland. Their ancestors belonged to the same Iron Age tradition that took shape in the Upemba depression from the 400s and fed the Kingdom of Luba after about 1500. As the Luba empire expanded in the 1700s, splintered Luba hunting and farming clans moved west into the lands between the upper Kasai, Lulua and Sankuru rivers, where they lived as small chiefdoms on the frontier between the Luba, Lunda and Songye worlds, often acknowledging no single king. They speak Tshiluba, also called Luba-Kasai, a Luban Bantu language shared with the neighboring Lulua, Kete and Kanyok, and keep the Luba customs of matrilineal descent and village farming of manioc, millet and bananas.
zh: “卡萨伊”是卢巴语里对开赛地区的称呼，这里用来统称西巴卢巴人，即卢巴核心区以西、开赛河流域讲卢巴语的村民。他们的祖先属于5世纪起在乌彭巴洼地形成的铁器时代传统，约1500年以后汇入卢巴王国。18世纪卢巴帝国扩张时，一些分散的卢巴狩猎和农耕氏族向西迁移，进入开赛河上游、卢卢阿河与散库鲁河之间的土地，在卢巴、隆达和松耶势力之间的边境上结成没有共主的小酋邦。他们使用的奇卢巴语又称卢巴—开赛语，属班图语卢班语支，与邻近的卢卢阿人、凯泰人和卡尼奥克人互通；他们保留卢巴人的母系继承传统，在村落里种植木薯、粟和香蕉。

en: Kashmiris are the Indo-Aryan people of the Kashmir Valley, the fertile Himalayan basin ringed by peaks whose towns are Srinagar, Baramulla, Anantnag and Kupwara. Their land was already settled in Neolithic times at Burzahom, passed under the Mauryas when Ashoka founded Srinagari, and reached an imperial peak in the eighth century under the Karkota king Lalitaditya Muktapida; the same age made Kashmir a seat of Sanskrit learning and of its own school of non-dualist Shaivism, written in the Sharada script that served Kashmiri letters from the eighth century. After Queen Didda and the Lohara dynasty, decline opened the way to Shah Mir, who in 1339 founded the Muslim Shah Mir dynasty, under which Islam spread through the valley over the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries and Persian became the court language. In 1586 the Mughals annexed Kashmir and emperors from Akbar to Aurangzeb laid out its famous gardens, but from 1753 the Afghan Durranis held the valley until the Sikhs under Ranjit Singh took it in 1819. Through all these rulers the Kashmiris kept their Dardic Koshur tongue, with its unusual verb-second word order, and its poets such as the fourteenth-century mystic Lal Ded.
zh: 克什米尔人是克什米尔谷地的印度-雅利安民族，这片群山环抱的肥沃喜马拉雅盆地中有斯利那加、巴拉穆拉、阿嫩德纳格和库普瓦拉等城镇。当地在布尔扎霍姆已有新石器时代聚落，阿育王建立斯利那加里时归入孔雀王朝，8世纪在卡尔科塔王朝国王拉尔阿迪蒂亚·穆克塔皮达治下达到帝国鼎盛；同一时期，克什米尔成为梵学重镇和自成一派的不二论湿婆教中心，8世纪起用以书写的沙拉达文也成为克什米尔书面文化的载体。迪达女王和洛哈拉王朝之后，国势衰微，沙阿·米尔于1339年建立穆斯林的沙阿·米尔王朝，伊斯兰教在14至15世纪传遍谷地，波斯语成为宫廷语言。1586年莫卧儿人兼并克什米尔，从阿克巴到奥朗则布的皇帝们在此营建著名园林；但1753年起谷地落入阿富汗杜兰尼王朝之手，直到1819年兰吉特·辛格率领锡克人将其夺取。历经这些统治者，克什米尔人始终保留着达尔德语支的克什米尔语——它有着少见的动词第二位语序——以及14世纪神秘主义诗人拉尔·德德等人的诗篇。

en: The Kashubians are the West Slavic people of Kashubia, the Baltic coastland between the mouths of the Oder and the Vistula around Gdansk, Puck and Slupsk. They descend from the Slavic Pomeranian tribes of the Migration Period, vassals in turn of Polish and Danish rulers, and alone among those tribes they kept their Slavic speech, the only surviving Pomeranian language, when medieval German settlement transformed the rest of Pomerania. In 1337 their lands were divided: the eastern heartland of Pomerelia, seized by the Teutonic Order in 1308, was ruled from Gdansk and Malbork, while the western districts of Stolp and Schlawe had passed to the Duchy of Pomerania in 1317. German burghers took the towns under the Ostsiedlung, but the fishing and farming villages stayed Kashubian, and the Kuyavian diocese of Wloclawek kept Polish as the language of the church. After the Second Peace of Thorn in 1466 Pomerelia became Royal Prussia under the Polish crown, until the partition of 1772 handed it to Prussia as West Prussia. Lutheran pastors printed the first religious books carrying Kashubian words from 1586, and in the 1820s scholars such as Christoph Mrongovius began to record the language while Germanization pressed on the villages.
zh: 卡舒比人是西斯拉夫族群，住在卡舒比地区，即奥得河与维斯瓦河口之间的波罗的海沿岸，中心为格但斯克、普茨克和斯武普斯克。他们是民族大迁徙时代波美拉尼亚斯拉夫部落的后裔，曾先后臣属波兰和丹麦君主；当德意志中世纪移民改变了波美拉尼亚其余地区时，他们是这些部落中唯一保住斯拉夫语的一支，卡舒比语也是波美拉尼亚语仅存的语言。1337年他们的土地处于分裂状态：东部腹地波梅雷利亚1308年被条顿骑士团夺取，由格但斯克和马尔堡控制；西部的斯武普斯克和斯瓦夫诺地区则在1317年并入波美拉尼亚公国。东向移民运动中，德意志市民占据城市，但渔村和农村仍说卡舒比语，弗沃茨瓦韦克的库亚维主教区也保留波兰语作为教堂用语。1466年第二次托伦和约后，波梅雷利亚成为波兰王冠治下的王室普鲁士，1772年瓜分中被普鲁士夺走，成为西普鲁士省。1586年起，路德宗牧师开始印行夹杂卡舒比语词汇的宗教书籍；19世纪20年代，在德意志化向乡村进逼之时，姆龙戈维乌斯等学者开始系统记录这种语言。

en: The Kaska Dena are an Athabaskan-speaking people of northern British Columbia and the southeastern Yukon, spread across the Dease, Liard and Pelly river country in five local bands, among them the Big Water Dwellers around Frances Lake, the Mountain Dwellers of the Dease valley, the Goat People of the Nahanni and Beaver rivers, and the Mountain Top band of the Rocky Mountain Trench. They followed a seasonal round after caribou and berries, travelled the Liard and Frances waterways by canoe, and migrated to the Pelly River salmon runs and the fishing grounds at Watson Lake. Their own trade gatherings centred on Daelyu, the place where we gather to trade, later the site of Lower Post, and the easternmost band carried furs to the North West Company post of Fort Nelson after it was founded in 1805. No company stood in their mountains, however, and in the 1820s Anglo-Canadians still counted them among the Nahani, the people of the west, whose furs reached the traders through neighbouring middlemen.
zh: 卡斯卡德内人是说阿萨巴斯卡语的族群，生活在不列颠哥伦比亚省北部与育空东南部，分布于迪斯河、利亚德河和佩利河流域，分为五个地方乐队：弗朗索瓦湖一带的“大水居民”、迪斯河谷的“山居居民”、纳汉尼河与比弗河的“野羊居民”，以及落基山沟的“山顶居民”等。他们按季节轮转追逐驯鹿、采集浆果，乘独木舟往来于利亚德河与弗朗索瓦水道，还会迁徙到佩利河的鲑鱼汛和沃森湖渔场。他们自己的贸易集会以达埃卢为中心，其地名意为“我们聚在一起交易的地方”，也就是后来洛尔波斯特商站的所在；1805年西北公司设立纳尔逊堡后，最东边的乐队把毛皮带到那里交易。但贸易公司始终没有进入他们的山区，到19世纪20年代，英裔加拿大人仍把他们算作纳哈尼人（意为西方人）的一部分，其毛皮只能经邻族中间商转到商人手中。

en: The Kaskankaham are the Kaskaskia, one of the dozen Algonquian-speaking tribes of the Illiniwek or Illinois Confederation; their name kaaskaaskia was taken from the Miami-Illinois word for a katydid. French missionaries first met them near Green Bay in 1667, and six years later Jolliet and Marquette found them at the Grand Village of the Illinois on the Illinois River near Starved Rock. In 1703 the French built a mission, fort and settlement among them at Kaskaskia on the Mississippi, which grew into the capital of Upper Louisiana and a mixed town of Illinois women, French voyageurs and, after 1718, enslaved Africans. Epidemics and unceasing wars with the Iroquois, Sioux, Meskwaki, Osage and other nations cut the tribe down from several thousand to a few hundred. After a Peoria warrior killed the Ottawa leader Pontiac in 1769, the Great Lakes tribes fell upon the Illinois and seized their valley, and in 1778 George Rogers Clark captured Kaskaskia for the American rebels. The last Illinois lands were ceded in 1832, and the surviving Kaskaskia were removed to Kansas and merged into the Confederated Peoria.
zh: 卡斯坎卡汉人即卡斯卡斯基亚人，是操阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼韦克（伊利诺伊联盟）十余部落之一；其名称卡斯卡斯基亚取自迈阿密—伊利诺伊语中对一种螽斯的称呼。1667年法国传教士在格林湾附近首次接触他们，六年后若利埃和马凯特在伊利诺伊河畔、星岩附近的伊利诺伊大村见到该部。1703年，法国人在密西西比河畔的卡斯卡斯基亚在他们中间建起传教站、要塞和聚落，这里后来发展为上路易斯安那的首府，成为一座由伊利诺伊妇女、法国皮货商和1718年后被贩来的非洲奴隶组成的混血城镇。瘟疫以及与易洛魁人、苏人、梅斯克瓦基人、奥萨吉人等部族无休止的战争，使该部从数千人锐减到数百人。1769年一名皮奥里亚战士杀死渥太华首领庞蒂亚克后，五大湖诸部猛攻伊利诺伊人并夺取其河谷；1778年乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克又为北美叛军攻占卡斯卡斯基亚。1832年，伊利诺伊人的最后土地被割让，幸存的卡斯卡斯基亚人被迁往堪萨斯，并入皮奥里亚联盟。

en: The Kaskinampo were a Muskogean-speaking tribe whose recorded history carried them across the interior Southeast. John Swanton identified them with the fortified province of Casqui in eastern Arkansas that Hernando de Soto visited in 1541, and Jacques Marquette and Louis Joliet encountered the same people on their voyage of 1673. By 1701 they had moved east to the Cumberland River and then to Pine Island on the Tennessee River, where they settled beside the Koasati; the French governor Bienville counted 150 Kaskinampo warriors that year. Once merged with the Koasati they ceased to be named separately, although Kaskinampo families still lived in the Koasati town of Coosada on the Alabama River, and during the American War of Independence its Koasati and Kaskinampo inhabitants joined Dragging Canoe's Chickamauga Cherokee.
zh: 卡斯基南波人是操穆斯科格语的部落，其有记载的历史横贯东南内陆。约翰·斯旺顿将他们考定为1541年德·索托在阿肯色东部造访的设防酋邦卡斯基；1673年，雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃在探险途中又遇到了这群人。到1701年，他们已东迁至坎伯兰河，随后又搬到田纳西河上的派恩岛，在考沙提人旁边定居；同年法国总督比安维尔清点出卡斯基南波战士150人。并入考沙提人后，他们便不再被单独提及，但卡斯基南波家庭仍住在亚拉巴马河畔的考沙提城镇克萨塔；美国独立战争期间，该镇的考沙提与卡斯基南波居民加入了拖独木舟率领的奇克莫加切罗基人。

en: The Katapas, also written Catapas, were an Intermediate Area people of the northern Costa Rican lowlands, living between the Frio and Zapote rivers around modern Guatuso and Los Chiles when the Spanish arrived in the sixteenth century. Together with their Tises neighbours they formed part of the Botos chiefdom, which paid tribute to Garabito, king of the western Huetar, and their language was probably one of the Chibchan family. In 1569 Governor Perafan de Ribera distributed the Katapas along with the Botos, Corobici and Abangares in encomienda to the town of Aranjuez, and they were resettled far from their homeland at San Ildefonso de Atapas on the Gulf of Nicoya. Cut off from their territory and held to forced labour, the transplanted community withered, and the settlement had ceased to exist by the end of the seventeenth century, taking the Katapas as a distinct people with it.
zh: 卡塔帕斯人（又译卡塔帕）是哥斯达黎加北部低地、属美洲中间区文化的族群，16世纪西班牙人到来时住在弗里奥河与萨波特河之间、今瓜图索和洛斯奇莱斯一带。他们与邻族蒂塞斯人同属博托斯酋邦，该酋邦向西部韦塔尔国王加拉维托纳贡，卡塔帕斯语很可能是奇布查语系的一支。1569年，总督佩拉凡·德·里韦拉把卡塔帕斯人连同博托斯人、科罗维西人和阿班加雷人一并以委托监护制分配给阿兰胡埃斯城，他们被远徙到尼科亚湾的圣伊尔德方索·德·阿塔帕斯安置。脱离故土又被迫服苦役，这个移植来的社群日渐凋零，到17世纪末该定居点已不复存在，卡塔帕斯人作为独立民族也随之消亡。

en: The Kâte are the inland forest people of the tip of the Huon Peninsula in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea; their name means forest, marking them off from the coastal Hâwec sea people and the northern Sopâc grass people. Their Finisterre-Huon language of the Trans-New Guinea family forms a chain of five dialects in the hills behind Finschhafen.
zh: 卡特人是巴布亚新几内亚莫罗贝省休恩半岛尖端的内陆森林居民，名字意为森林，与沿海的哈韦克人（意为海）和北部草原的索帕克人（意为草）相区别。他们在芬什港后方的山地说跨新几内亚语系菲尼斯蒂尔-休恩语支的语言，内部分为五种方言，连成一条方言链。

en: The Katla, also called the Gulud, are a Nuba people of the Katla hills in the Nuba Hills of Sudan, roughly sixty kilometres from Kadugli. Their Katla tongue forms the small Katloid family, once grouped under the old Kordofanian proposal and classed by Roger Blench as a divergent branch of Niger-Congo.
zh: 卡特拉人又称古卢德人，是苏丹努巴丘陵卡特拉山地的努巴族群，住在距卡杜格利约六十公里处。他们的卡特拉语自成小小的卡特拉语族，旧归科尔多凡语群，罗杰·布伦奇将其列为尼日尔-刚果语系中一个分化较早的支系。

en: The Kaulong are the people of the forested southwest hinterland of New Britain, in Kandrian District of Papua New Guinea's West New Britain Province. They speak Kaulong, also called Pasismanua, which is an Austronesian language rather than a Papuan one, and traditionally live as swidden farmers in scattered inland villages.
zh: 考隆人居住在巴布亚新几内亚西新不列颠省坎德里安县境内、新不列颠岛西南部的内陆林区。他们使用又称帕西斯马努阿语的考隆语，该语言属于南岛语系而非巴布亚诸语言；考隆人传统上以轮垦农业为生，村落分散在内陆地带。

en: The Kaurna-Pangkarran are the Kaurna, the people of the Adelaide Plains on the eastern shore of Gulf St Vincent, whose country ran from Cape Jervis and the Fleurieu Peninsula to Port Wakefield and as far north as Crystal Brook. Their name was probably an exonym from the Ramindjeri or Ngarrindjeri word for “men”, for the plains people called themselves after their localities; each patrilineal band held a defined estate, a pangkarra with its own stretch of coast and inland hunting ground, and the estates were grouped into larger yerta lands under two exogamous moieties, the Karuru and Mattari. In 1337 their life followed a four-season calendar, their speech a Thura-Yura language of the Pama-Nyungan family, and their Dreaming followed the culture hero Tjilbruke down the Fleurieu coast and traced the Mount Lofty Ranges to the body of the slain giant Nganno. The first Kaurna word lists were taken down in 1826, and in 1836 Colonel Light's survey party met Kaurna speakers at Rapid Bay before Adelaide was planted on Tarndanyangga, the red kangaroo place on the River Torrens, opening a colonisation that within decades nearly destroyed the old plains life.
zh: 考尔纳潘卡拉人即考尔纳人，是圣文森特湾东岸阿德莱德平原的族群，领地从杰维斯角和菲尔半岛延伸到韦克菲尔德港，北抵克里斯特尔布鲁克。他们的名字很可能源自拉明杰里人或纳林杰里人表示“人”的外来称呼，因为平原上的居民本以地名自称；每个父系氏族都拥有一块明确的世袭领地“潘卡拉”，既有自己的海岸段又有内陆猎场，若干潘卡拉又归入更大的“耶尔塔”，全社会分为卡鲁鲁和马塔里两大外婚半族。1337年时，他们依照四季历法生活，所说的语言属帕马-牛雅语系的图拉-尤拉语支；他们的梦创故事沿着菲尔海岸追随文化英雄吉尔布鲁克，又把洛夫蒂岭看作被杀死的巨人恩加诺的身躯。最早的考尔纳语词汇表记录于1826年；1836年莱特上校的测量队在拉皮德湾遇到讲考尔纳语的人，此后阿德莱德城便建在托伦斯河畔名为塔恩达尼安加的红袋鼠之地，由此开启的殖民进程仅过几十年便几乎摧毁了平原上的旧有生活。

en: The Kaviagmiut are the Iñupiaq people of the southern Seward Peninsula, west of Norton Bay, the country around present-day Nome, Sinuk and the Kigluaik Mountains. Their name lives on in the Qawiaraq dialect of Iñupiaq, still associated with Nome and its neighboring villages of Council, Mary's Igloo and Koyuk, and they were the southernmost of the Bering Strait Iñupiat groups, bordering the Yup'ik peoples of Norton Sound. They lived by sea-mammal hunting on the Bering Sea coast and by fishing the peninsula's rivers. The Seward Peninsula coasts were first seen by Europeans on Captain James Cook's voyage of 1778, when he named Cape Prince of Wales at the entrance to the Bering Strait.
zh: 卡维亚格缪特人是苏厄德半岛南部、诺顿湾以西的因纽皮亚特人，活动在今诺姆、锡努克和基格卢艾克山脉一带。他们的名字保留在因纽皮亚特语的卡维亚拉克方言中，这一方言的通行区以诺姆为中心，包括邻近的康瑟尔、玛丽冰屋、科尤克等村庄；他们是白令海峡各因纽皮亚特群体中最靠南的一支，与诺顿湾的尤皮克人为邻。他们在白令海岸捕猎海洋哺乳动物，在半岛的河流中捕鱼。1778年詹姆斯·库克船长航行经过并命名白令海峡入口处的威尔士王子角，苏厄德半岛的海岸这才第一次被欧洲人看见。

en: Kavieng takes its name from the harbour at the northern tip of New Ireland but denotes the indigenous people of the surrounding district, who speak Tigak or Omo, an Austronesian language of the Tungag-Nalik family also used on the nearby offshore islands. Dutch explorers first charted these coasts in 1616, when the area was still a network of coastal villages living from fishing and garden land.
zh: 卡维恩得名于新爱尔兰岛北端的港湾，游戏以此指称周边地区的原住民，他们操蒂加克语（又称奥莫语），属南岛语系通加格-纳利克语族，附近近海岛屿上也有人使用。1616年荷兰探险者首次测绘这一带海岸时，这里还只是一片靠渔捞和园地为生的沿海村落网络。

en: The Kawaiisu are a Southern Numic people of the Tehachapi Valley and the southern Sierra Nevada, around Lake Isabella and Walker Pass, who also ranged east across the northern Mojave Desert as far as the Panamint Valley and the edge of Death Valley on gathering trips. They call themselves Nüwa, the people; both Kawaiisu and Tehachapi Indians are names taken from their Yokuts neighbours. Split into Desert and Mountain groups, they wintered in permanent villages of sixty to a hundred people and scattered into small foraging bands in summer, living mainly on acorns and buckeye flour, deer and desert mesquite. Their closest linguistic kin were the Chemehuevi, they joined Yokuts drivers in communal antelope hunts, and their mountains hold the petroglyphs shared by the Numic peoples of the region. Their oral history and linguists alike suggest they may have come up from the desert into the Tehachapis as early as two thousand years ago; in 1770 the Kawaiisu, Chemehuevi and Koso together were estimated at about 1,500 people.
zh: 卡怀苏人是南努米克语族群，住在特哈查皮谷和内华达山脉南段，即伊莎贝拉湖与沃克山口一带，采集时还向东深入莫哈韦沙漠北部，远至帕纳明特谷和死谷边缘。他们自称“努瓦”，意为“人”；“卡怀苏”和“特哈查皮印第安人”两个外来名都来自相邻的约库茨人。他们分为沙漠群和山地群，冬天住在六七十人到上百人规模的固定村落，夏天则分散成小群觅食，主食橡子和七叶树果磨成的粉，辅以鹿肉和沙漠牧豆。与他们语言最近的是切米惠维人；他们还会同约库茨人合作围猎羚羊，其活动的山区留存着当地努米克族群共有的岩画。口述传统和语言研究都表明，他们可能早在两千年前就从沙漠进入特哈查皮山区；据估计，1770年卡怀苏人、切米惠维人和科索人合计约有1500人。

en: The Kaiabi, who call themselves Kawaiwete, perhaps meaning “we ourselves”, are a Tupi-Guarani people whose villages once dotted the upper Teles Pires and the Rio dos Peixes in northern Mato Grosso, country of forest and rivers that also reaches into southern Pará. They lived in self-reliant villages as fishermen, hunters and farmers, working a careful slash-and-burn calendar in which the forest was felled in May, cleared in June, burned in August and planted in September and October, with manioc fields growing many different varieties alongside mixed crop gardens. Their lands were rich in rubber, timber and minerals, and through the 1700s and 1800s raiding parties stormed such villages, killing the men and carrying off the women as slaves, while smallpox, measles and other introduced diseases emptied others. The Kaiabi held that the spirits of their ancestors stayed on the land where their bones lay, a belief that kept families attached to their river homelands even when colonial pressure was at its heaviest.
zh: 卡亚比人自称卡伊韦特，其名可能意为“我们自己”；他们是使用图皮-瓜拉尼语族语言的族群，村庄曾星罗棋布于马托格罗索北部的上特利斯皮里斯河与多鱼河一带，这片森林与水泽之地还延伸到帕拉州南部。他们住在自给自足的村落里，以捕鱼、狩猎和务农为生，奉行一套严密的刀耕火种历法：5月伐林、6月清场、8月焚烧、9至10月播种；木薯地里种着许多不同品种，另有混作菜园。他们的土地盛产橡胶、木材和矿物，18至19世纪，劫掠队袭击这类村庄，杀死男子、掳走妇女为奴，天花、麻疹等外来疫病又使另一些村落人口一空。卡亚比人相信，祖先的灵魂留在埋骨之地，这种信念使许多家族即便在殖民压力最重时，仍不肯离开河畔故土。

en: The Kaweinag are an Asmat sub-group of the Casuarina Coast, the swampy shore around the mouth of the Pulau River in South Papua, Indonesia. Their speech, Casuarina Coast Asmat, is the most divergent variety of the Asmat cluster within the Trans–New Guinea phylum, while they share the sago-based village life and ancestor cults of other Asmat groups.
zh: 卡韦纳格人是木麻黄海岸一带的阿斯马特支系，住在印度尼西亚南巴布亚省普劳河河口附近多沼泽的海岸。他们说的木麻黄海岸阿斯马特语是泛新几内亚语系阿斯马特语群中分歧最大的一支，同时与其他阿斯马特支系一样，过着以西谷椰为基础的村落生活、信奉祖先崇拜。

en: The Kawésqar, whom European sailors long called Alacaluf or Halakwulup, a Yahgan name meaning mussel-eater, are the canoe nomads of the rain-soaked channels of western Patagonia, between the Gulf of Penas and the Strait of Magellan. Their autonym means simply person or human being. Family groups paddled canoes eight or nine metres long, large enough to carry a household and its dog, moving endlessly among the islands to fish, hunt seals and sea lions and gather shellfish; they never farmed, and their whole material life was adapted to water, wind and cold, from seal-oil anointment to skin capes and small fires kept burning aboard the canoes. Their Kawésqar language is unrelated to the Yahgan of the channels further south. The first Europeans to meet them were the Spaniards of the Garcia Jofre de Loaisa expedition, who sighted their campfires at the western mouth of the Strait of Magellan in 1526. From the late eighteenth century British and American whalers and sealers worked their waters in growing numbers, bringing the trade goods and, more decisively, the epidemic diseases that began their decline.
zh: 卡韦斯卡尔人长期被欧洲水手称作阿拉卡卢夫或哈拉库卢普，这个雅甘语名称意为食贻贝者；他们的自称卡韦斯卡尔则只表示人。他们是西巴塔哥尼亚雨雾水道中的操舟游群，活动范围在佩尼亚斯湾与麦哲伦海峡之间。一个个家族划着长八九米、足以载下全家和狗的独木舟，在岛屿间不停迁徙，捕鱼、猎取海豹和海狮、捡拾贝类；他们从不务农，从涂抹海狮油、披兽皮斗篷到在舟中长燃不熄的火堆，全部物质生活都为水上的风雨严寒而设。他们的卡韦斯卡尔语与更南边水道中的雅甘语并无亲属关系。最早遇到他们的欧洲人是加西亚·霍夫雷·德·洛伊萨探险队的西班牙人，1526年在麦哲伦海峡西端望见了他们的营火。从18世纪末起，英美捕鲸船和猎海豹船越来越多地闯入他们的水域，既带来了交易品，也更致命地带来了传染病，卡韦斯卡尔人口由此开始衰减。

en: The Kaxarari are a Panoan-speaking people of the Brazilian borderlands with Bolivia, living between the states of Acre, Rondônia and Amazonas on tributaries of the Madeira. Their tongue is the most divergent member of the Mainline Panoan branch, and their own oral history divides the past into the time of raids, the time of captivity and the time of rights.
zh: 卡沙拉里人是巴西与玻利维亚边境地带的帕诺语族群，散居在阿克里、朗多尼亚和亚马孙三州交界、马代拉河支流一带。他们的语言是帕诺语主干分支中差异最大的一支；其口述历史把过去分为三个时代：追猎时代、囚禁时代和权利时代。

en: The Kaxixo are an indigenous people of the upper Sao Francisco basin in the interior of Minas Gerais, living around the Para River, and the game also attaches to them the name Carijo, borne by a related Tupi-Guarani population. The original Carijo were Guarani speakers who had moved from the Paraguay region to the Brazilian coast between Cananeia and the Lagoa dos Patos; their name comes from a Tupi word meaning descendants of the ancient ones, and Portuguese raiders seized so many of them as slaves that Carijo became a colonial byword for captive Indian labor. In 1554 Carijo warriors joined the attack on the young settlement of Sao Paulo. From the 1700s the Portuguese dispossessed and enslaved the Kaxixo of Minas Gerais as well, turning them into hacienda servants and day laborers alongside transported Carijo slaves, Africans and settlers; through generations of mixing they kept their identity, and a riverside cave grotto remains their sacred place.
zh: 卡希索人是米纳斯吉拉斯内陆圣弗朗西斯科河上游、帕拉河一带的原住民，游戏还给他们附上了“卡里若”这个名字，用以涵盖一支相关的图皮-瓜拉尼人群体。最早的卡里若人是说瓜拉尼语的族群，从巴拉圭地区迁到卡纳内亚至帕图斯湖之间的巴西沿海；族名来自图皮语，意为“古人的后裔”。葡萄牙劫掠者大量抓他们为奴，以至于“卡里若”在殖民时期成了印第安奴工的代名词。1554年，卡里若战士还参与了攻打初建的圣保罗定居点。从18世纪起，葡萄牙人同样掠夺并奴役米纳斯的卡希索人，把他们变成庄园仆役和雇工，与被贩运至此的卡里若奴隶、非洲人和殖民者共同生活；历经数代通婚融合，他们仍保住了族群认同，河畔的一处岩洞也始终是他们的圣地。

en: The Kayagar are a Papuan people of the South Papua lowlands, living around the Cook River inland of the Asmat coast, in present-day Mappi and Asmat Regencies of Indonesia. Their language, also called Kaygir or Wiyagar, belongs together with three neighbouring tongues to the small Kayagar family within the Trans–New Guinea phylum.
zh: 卡亚加尔人是南巴布亚低地的巴布亚族群，住在阿斯马特沿海后方内陆的库克河一带，即今印度尼西亚马皮县与阿斯马特县境内。他们的语言又称卡伊吉尔语或维雅加尔语，与邻近三种语言同属泛新几内亚语系下的小语族卡亚加尔语族。

en: The Kayambi, or Cayambis, are an Andean people of the high valley north of Quito, around the snow-capped Cayambe volcano in present-day Pichincha Province, where the Pisque River basin and the ridge of Pambamarca held their hilltop forts, or pucaras. They were often at war with their Caranqui neighbours, and they met the Inca advance with prolonged resistance: the fighting over Pambamarca is said to have lasted seventeen years before the fortresses fell, early in the sixteenth century. Conquered first under Topa Inca Yupanqui around 1470, the Kayambi joined the great northern revolt under Huayna Capac, alongside the Caranqui, Quitu and Pasto; when it was crushed, tradition places the final slaughter at the lake renamed Yawarkucha, the blood lake. Some communities then submitted and became Inca allies, and Kayambi pottery survived through the colonial period. After the Spanish conquest of 1534 their lands were broken into haciendas, whose Kayambi tenants were forced into labour, chiefly in wool processing, and the later canton erected on their old territory took the name Cayambe.
zh: 卡扬比人又称卡扬比斯人，是基多以北高河谷地带的安第斯族群，聚居于今皮钦查省积雪覆盖的卡扬贝火山周围；皮斯克河流域和潘瓦马尔卡山脊上分布着他们的山顶要塞，即普卡拉。他们常与邻族卡兰基人交战，面对印加的推进也进行了长期抵抗：争夺潘瓦马尔卡的战争据说持续了十七年，要塞才在16世纪初陷落。卡扬比人约在1470年先被图帕克·尤潘基征服，后来又在瓦伊纳·卡帕克时期联合卡兰基人、基图人和帕斯托人参加北方大起义；起义被镇压后，传说最后的屠杀发生在一座湖畔，此湖因而得名亚瓦尔科查，意为血湖。此后一些部落归顺并成为印加盟友，卡扬比陶器也一直沿用至殖民时期。1534年西班牙征服后，他们的土地被分割成大庄园，卡扬比佃农被迫服役，主要从事羊毛加工；后来在其故土上设立的县也以卡扬贝为名。

en: The Kayan are a Dayak people of the interior of Borneo, whose oral history traces them to the upper Kayan, middle Kapuas and Mahakam rivers of what is now North Kalimantan, and who later spread into Sarawak along the Baram, Bintulu and Rajang. Their migration south brought them into collision with the Iban expanding north, and wars and headhunting raids displaced many smaller tribes around them. During the 1600s one Kayan sub-group, the Uma Apan or Dayak Hupan, moved east from the Apo Kayan highlands to the coast, adopted Islam and became the nucleus of the Bulungan people and their sultanate. Kayan society was built on riverside longhouses and shifting upland-rice farms, and its men were feared headhunters whose feast of collected heads combined warrior initiation with funeral rites. They hunted with the sumpitan blowpipe, forged the malat sword as their chief trade good, carved and built boats, and recited their past in sung epics called tekna'; women bore intricate tattoos and both sexes stretched their earlobes as a mark of beauty and standing.
zh: 卡扬人是婆罗洲内陆的达雅族群，口述史把祖源追溯到今北加里曼丹的卡扬河上游、卡普阿斯河与马哈坎河中游，后来沿巴拉让河、民都鲁河和拉让江扩散到沙捞越。他们向南迁徙时与向北扩张的伊班人发生冲突，连年战争和猎首袭击迫使周围许多小部落迁徙。17世纪，卡扬的一支乌马阿潘人（又称达雅胡潘人）从阿保卡扬高原东迁至沿海，改奉伊斯兰教，成为布隆岸人及其苏丹国的核心。卡扬社会以河畔长屋和旱稻轮作农场为基础，男子是令人生畏的猎首者，其“聚首宴”把战士成年礼与丧葬仪式合而为一。他们用吹筒狩猎，锻造的马拉特剑是主要交易品，还擅长木雕和造船，并以吟唱史诗“特纳”传唱本族历史；女性纹有精细的纹身，男女都拉长耳垂，作为美貌与身份的标志。

en: The Kazani are the Kazan branch of the Volga Tatars, Sunni Muslim Turks of the middle Volga whose identity formed from the settled population of Volga Bulgaria and the Kipchak steppe Tatars of the Golden Horde. In the fourteenth century their lands belonged to the Horde, whose governors ruled from Bolghar and Kazan. After the Horde fragmented, Ulugh Muhammad seized power in Kazan around 1438 and founded the Khanate of Kazan, whose nobles called themselves the people of Kazan and conducted affairs in the Volga Turki literary language. The khanate was torn between pro-Moscow and pro-Crimean factions, and was effectively a Muscovite protectorate from 1487 to 1521. Ivan the Terrible stormed Kazan in 1552 after a siege of forty days, ending its independence; resistance in the forests continued until 1557, followed by resettlement away from the rivers and campaigns of forced baptism. The Kazani nonetheless kept their Hanafi Islam, their mosques and their Kipchak tongue, and the fair of Kazan remained the chief market of the Volga trade.
zh: 喀山人是伏尔加鞑靼人的喀山分支，即伏尔加河中游的逊尼派穆斯林突厥人，其身份由伏尔加保加利亚的定居人口与金帐汗国的钦察草原鞑靼人融合而成。14世纪时他们的土地属于金帐汗国，由汗国总督从保加尔和喀山统治。金帐汗国分裂后，兀鲁·穆罕默德约在1438年夺取喀山政权，建立喀山汗国；国中贵族自称“喀山之人”，以伏尔加突厥书面语处理公务。汗国内部亲莫斯科派与亲克里米亚派争斗不断，1487年至1521年间实际上是莫斯科的保护国。1552年，伊凡雷帝经过四十余天的围攻攻陷喀山，汗国灭亡；森林地带的抵抗持续到1557年，随后鞑靼人被迁离河畔，并遭到强迫受洗。尽管如此，喀山人仍保留了哈乃斐派信仰、清真寺和钦察语，喀山的集市也始终是伏尔加商路的头号市场。

en: The Kei are the Austronesian people of the Kei Islands in southeast Maluku, chiefly Kai Besar and Kai Kecil, who call their land Evav and speak Keiese, used as a lingua franca across the archipelago. Their oral history traces part of their ancestry to Balinese nobles of the Majapahit kingdom who landed at Ohoi-Ewur on Kai Kecil, where the princess Dit Sakmas shaped Larvul Ngabal, the red-blood and Balinese-spear customary law that still orders Kei life; other ancestors came from Sumbawa, Buton, Seram and the North Maluku sultanates. Society is patrilineal, built from nuclear households into fam clans and soa villages, split between the nine-village Ursiu and five-village Lorlim ritual federations under twenty-two traditional Rat, or rajas. When the Dutch East India Company conquered the Banda Islands in 1621, Bandanese refugees fled to Kai Besar, where their descendants still speak Bandanese, and the islands were drawn into the Dutch sphere in Maluku. The small Tanimbar Kei community kept an older Hindu-tinged ancestor cult on its remote island.
zh: 凯人是马鲁古东南部卡伊群岛（主要包括大卡伊岛和小卡伊岛）的南岛语族群，自称故乡为埃瓦夫，使用的凯语是群岛各地的通用语。根据口传历史，他们的部分祖先来自满者伯夷王国的巴厘贵族，在小卡伊岛的奥霍伊埃武尔登陆，公主迪特·萨克马斯在此创制了名为拉尔武尔·恩加巴尔的习惯法，意为‘赤血与巴厘之矛’，历来规范着凯人的生活；另一些祖先则来自松巴哇、布顿、塞兰和北马鲁古诸苏丹国。社会按父系传承，由核心家庭逐级组成氏族和村庄，分属九村联合体乌尔秀与五村联合体洛尔利姆两个仪式联盟，由22位称拉特（即拉者）的传统首领统辖。1621年荷兰东印度公司征服班达群岛后，班达难民逃到大卡伊岛，其后代仍讲班达语，卡伊群岛也被卷入荷兰在马鲁古的势力范围。偏远的塔宁巴尔凯岛上还有一小群塔宁巴尔凯人，保留着印度教色彩浓厚的古老祖先崇拜。

en: The Hakka, whose name means guest families, are latecomers among the Han of south China, farming the marginal hill country where Guangdong, Fujian and Jiangxi meet, around Chengxiang in Meizhou, the Tingzhou basin of Changting and Shanghang, and Ganzhou's Longnan and Xingguo. Their forebears were Central Plains refugees who began moving south with the collapse of the Western Jin in the early fourth century and entered the south through Jiangxi; Ganzhou served as their staging ground before they pushed on into western Fujian and eastern Guangdong, mixing along the way with She and Yao peoples. Their speech keeps archaic final consonants lost in Mandarin and is closest to Gan, the two perhaps sharing a Song-era ancestor. In the hills they built the fortified communal tulou, and under the Kangxi emperor between 1662 and 1722 the court resettled Hakka farmers in war-ruined Sichuan, offering silver grants to migrants after 1671.
zh: 客家，意为客居的人家，是华南汉人中较晚到来的一支，在广东、福建、江西三省交界的贫瘠丘陵务农，聚居于梅州程乡、闽西汀州的长汀与上杭，以及赣州的龙南、兴国一带。他们的祖先是中原难民，4世纪初西晋灭亡时开始南迁，取道江西进入华南；赣州是继续迁往闽西、粤东之前的中转站，迁徙途中他们与畲族、瑶族互通婚姻。客家话保留了官话已失去的古辅音韵尾，与赣语关系最近，两者可能源自宋代的共同祖语。客家人在山区修建聚族而居的防御性土楼；1662至1722年康熙皇帝在位时，朝廷招募客家农民填驻遭兵燹残破的四川，1671年起还给迁徙者发放白银补助。

en: The Kentaientonga were an Iroquoian-speaking people of the south shore of Lake Erie, in what became northeastern Ohio, kindred of the Erie or Cat Nation. French accounts recorded that their villages in the Cuyahoga country were destroyed by the Haudenosaunee during the Beaver Wars of the mid-seventeenth century.
zh: 肯塔恩通加人是伊利湖南岸、后来的俄亥俄东北部一带的易洛魁语民族，与又称猫族的伊利人同族。法国文献记载，他们在凯霍加地区的村落于17世纪中叶的海狸战争中被易洛魁联盟摧毁。

en: The Kenyah are more than forty related Dayak sub-groups of interior north-eastern Borneo, from the Baram and Rajang headwaters of Sarawak to the Kayan highlands of Kalimantan, whose oral traditions locate their origin on the remote Usun Apau plateau. They lived in riverside longhouses, farmed hill rice by slash-and-burn and followed the animist Adat Pu'un rites.
zh: 肯雅人是婆罗洲东北部内陆四十多个相近达雅支系的统称，分布从沙捞越的巴拉让河、拉让江源头延伸至加里曼丹的卡扬高原，口述传统把祖源放在偏远的乌松阿保高原。他们临河居住长屋，刀耕火种旱稻，奉行“阿达特普温”万物有灵仪式。

en: The Kerek are a small Chukotko-Kamchatkan seafaring people whose autonym, angqalghakku, means seaside people. Their villages dotted the Bering Sea coast from the Anadyr estuary south to the Opuka, with a northern Navarin group around Meynypilgyno and a southern group around Khatyrka, in present-day southern Chukotka. Archaeologists trace an ancient Kerek culture on this coast to about 500 BC. They lived from sea-mammal hunting and fishing, kept sled dogs and only the southern clans herded a few reindeer, remaining animists untouched by Christianity. During the Chukchi-Koryak wars of the eighteenth century the Kerek were caught between both sides, their men killed and women and children carried off, and epidemics later in the century reduced them to a remnant; nineteenth-century observers usually classed the survivors with the Koryaks or the Chukchi.
zh: 克列克人是楚科奇—堪察加语族的一支滨海小族，自称安卡尔加库，意为海边的人。他们的村落散布在白令海沿岸，北起阿纳德尔河口，南至奥普卡河，在今楚科奇南部：北方是梅内皮尔格诺一带的纳瓦林群体，南方是哈特尔卡群体。考古学家把这一海岸的古克列克文化追溯到约公元前500年。他们以猎海兽和捕鱼为生，养雪橇犬，只有南部氏族兼营少量驯鹿，始终保持万物有灵信仰，没有改宗基督教。18世纪楚科奇人与科里亚克人交战惨烈，克列克人夹在两方之间，男子被杀、妇孺被掳，世纪末的瘟疫又使人口锐减，只剩残余；19世纪的观察者通常把幸存者归入科里亚克人或楚科奇人。

en: The Keres are the Pueblo people of seven towns along the Rio Grande and its western tributaries in New Mexico: Cochiti, San Felipe, Kewa, Zia and Santa Ana in the east, and the great mesa pueblos of Acoma and Laguna in the west. Their Keresan speech is now treated as a language isolate divided into eastern and western groups, while archaeology and Cochiti oral tradition suggest that the Keres entered the Rio Grande drainage from the west in the early 1300s, after the depopulation of the El Morro valley. Acoma, perched on its sandstone mesa, had been occupied for well over a thousand years when Estevanico visited it in 1539; Coronado's men saw it the next year, and in 1599 Juan de Oñate's troops sacked the town in the Acoma Massacre, killing some 800 people and enslaving hundreds more. The survivors rebuilt, raised the huge San Esteban mission church between 1629 and 1641, and joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, after which refugees from Acoma and other rebel towns founded Laguna. Through the eighteenth century the Keres pueblos kept their matrilineal clans and kiva rituals beneath an outward Catholicism, while fending off raids by Apache, Comanche and Ute.
zh: 凯雷斯人是新墨西哥境内格兰德河及其西部支流一带七座普韦布洛的居民：东边有科奇蒂、圣费利佩、克瓦、齐亚和圣安娜，西边则是台地巨镇阿科马和拉古纳。凯雷斯语一般被视为一门语言孤立语言，分为东、西两个方言群；考古发现与科奇蒂口传都表明，凯雷斯人在14世纪初埃尔莫罗谷人口流失之后，由西方迁入格兰德河流域。雄踞砂岩台地上的阿科马在1539年埃斯特万尼科到访时已有人居住了一千多年；次年科罗纳多的部下见到了它，1599年胡安·德·奥尼亚特的军队制造阿科马大屠杀，杀死约八百人并将数百人掳为奴隶。幸存者重建家园，于1629至1641年间建起宏伟的圣埃斯特万传教教堂，并参加了1680年的普韦布洛起义；起义后来自阿科马等反叛村镇的难民建立了拉古纳。整个18世纪，凯雷斯诸镇在表面的天主教信仰之下保留着母系氏族和基瓦仪式，同时抵御阿帕奇人、科曼奇人和犹特人的袭扰。

en: The Kerewo, or Kerewa, are the people of the mangrove coast and tidal swamps of the western Gulf of Papua, around Goaribari and the mouths of the Turama and Kikori rivers. Their language forms the Kerewo–Morigi branch of the Kiwaian family, a tight cluster of Papuan languages spread across the gulf's river deltas.
zh: 克雷沃人（一译克雷瓦人）住在巴布亚湾西部的红树林海岸与潮汐沼泽地带，以戈阿里巴里及图拉马河、基科里河河口一带为中心。他们的语言构成基万语族的克雷沃-莫里吉分支，而基万语族是散布在海湾各河口三角洲的一群关系紧密的巴布亚语言。

en: The Kets are the only surviving Yeniseian-speaking people, the last heirs of an ancient population once widespread in central and southern Siberia whose distant relatives also reached North America, and their self-name ket simply means man. When Russians reached the middle Yenisei they found them scattered in small taiga clans along the Sym, Kas and Dubches rivers and on the eastern bank around the future site of Yeniseysk, living by fishing, hunting and a little reindeer breeding, with some of their bands belonging to the Skewbald Horde; the Russians lumped them with other river peoples as Ostyaks, later Yenisei Ostyaks. Their incorporation into the Russian state in the seventeenth century met stubborn resistance, answered by deportations that broke up their exogamous patriarchal clans, while debt, famine and introduced diseases shrank their numbers, until by the nineteenth century they depended on state food supplies. They kept a rich shamanist religion with several grades of shamans, animal helper spirits and household spirit images dressed in scraps of cloth, and their isolated language, wholly unlike any other tongue in Siberia, was first described by the naturalist Peter Simon Pallas in 1788.
zh: 克特人是仅存的叶尼塞语系民族，是古代曾广布于西伯利亚中南部、远亲还延伸到北美的古老人群的最后后裔；他们的自称克特意思就是“人”。俄国人到达叶尼塞河中游时，发现他们以小型泰加氏族散布在瑟姆河、卡斯河、杜布切斯河以及后来的叶尼塞斯克一带的东岸，以捕鱼、狩猎和少量养鹿为生，部分群体曾隶属于花斑帐；俄国人把他们与其他河畔民族混称为奥斯佳克人，后来才改称叶尼塞奥斯佳克人。17世纪他们被并入俄国，顽强抵抗招来的是强制迁徙，实行族外婚的父系氏族因而瓦解，加上债务、饥荒和外来疾病，人口不断缩减，到19世纪已依赖俄国的粮食补给为生。他们保留着丰富的萨满信仰：萨满分若干等级，有动物辅助精灵，还有裹着碎布的家宅神像；他们那门与西伯利亚其他语言全无亲缘的孤立语言，最早由博物学家彼得·西蒙·帕拉斯于1788年记录描述。

en: The Kete, or Bakete, are a Bantu people of the Grand Kasai plateau in the south-central Congo, living around Luiza, Dibaya, Kamiji and Mweka on the rim between the Luba and Kuba worlds. They speak Tshikete, their own Luban language within the Luba group, and are counted among the Luba-Kasai cluster, though they never formed a centralized state of their own and lived in scattered village communities of farmers and hunters. In the 1600s their chiefdoms were absorbed into the growing Kuba federation, whose royal traditions name the Kete alongside the Bushoong and the Kasai Twa as one of the kingdom's founding peoples. Kete society is organized around family and village headmen, with distinctive rites for the birth of twins, when masked dancers wearing the Mukwandayi helmet mask appear, and a weekly day of rest devoted to the ancestors.
zh: 凯泰人（自称巴凯泰人）是刚果中南部大开赛高原的班图族群，分布在卢伊扎、迪巴亚、卡米吉和姆韦卡一带，正处在卢巴与库巴两个世界的交界。他们使用自己的卢班语支语言奇凯泰语，被归入卢巴—开赛集群，但从未建立过自己的集权国家，而是以分散的农耕和狩猎村落社群生活。17世纪，他们的酋长国被日益壮大的库巴联盟吞并，库巴王室传统把凯泰人与布尚人、开赛特瓦人并列为王国的奠基族群。凯泰社会围绕家族和村落头人运转，有独特的双胞胎出生仪式：届时戴姆昆达伊头盔面具的舞者会出场表演；他们每七天还有一个敬奉祖先的休息日。

en: The Khakas are a Turkic people of the Abakan and Minusinsk basin in the upper Yenisei, formed from the Yenisei Kyrgyz together with older Tagar and Samoyedic elements of the Khakassian steppe. Their Kyrgyz forebears founded a khanate in 693 under Bars Bek, long served the Göktürks and Uyghurs as vassals, and in 840 sacked the Uyghur capital Ordu-Baliq and destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate, holding brief nominal supremacy on the steppe until the early tenth century. In 1207 the Kyrgyz submitted to Genghis Khan, and by the seventeenth century their clans, pressed by the Dzungars, were caught between Dzungar and Russian power; a 1635 treaty imposed tribute on them, and many were later deported to Dzungaria and, in 1761, to Manchuria, where their descendants survive as the Fuyu Kyrgyz.
