The Russians moved into the depopulated Minusinsk lands, built forts and farming settlements, and from the 1820s developed gold mines around Minusinsk. The people who remained, calling themselves Tadar and known to the Russians as Abakan or Minusinsk Tatars, lived by nomadic sheep and cattle herding, farming, hunting and fishing; during the nineteenth century most were converted to Russian Orthodoxy while keeping shamanic practices.
zh: 哈卡斯人是叶尼塞河上游阿巴坎与米努辛斯克盆地的突厥语民族，由叶尼塞黠戛斯人融合当地更古老的塔加尔文化和萨莫耶德成分形成。其黠戛斯先民于693年在巴尔斯别克统领下建立汗国，曾长期臣属东突厥和回鹘，840年攻陷回鹘都城斡耳朵八里、灭亡回鹘汗国，并在10世纪初以前对草原享有短暂的名义宗主权。1207年黠戛斯臣服于成吉思汗；到17世纪，其各部受准噶尔逼迫，夹在准噶尔与俄国之间，1635年的一条条约向他们强征贡赋，后来许多人被迁往准噶尔，1761年又被清朝迁到满洲，其后裔即今天的富裕柯尔克孜人。俄国人随后进入人口空虚的米努辛斯克土地，修建堡垒和农垦居民点，19世纪20年代起在米努辛斯克一带开采金矿。留居的人自称“塔达尔”，被俄国人称为阿巴坎鞑靼或米努辛斯克鞑靼，以游牧牧羊养牛、农耕、狩猎和捕鱼为生；19世纪里多数人改宗俄罗斯东正教，但仍保留萨满习俗。

en: The Khamag Mongol, the “Whole Mongol”, were the leading Mongol tribal confederation of the twelfth century, grazing the fertile basins of the Onon, Kherlen and Tuul rivers in the Khentii range and the adjacent Transbaikal forests where their Taichiud clan camped; the Khiyad, Taichuud and Jalairs formed its three core clans. First attested under the Khitan Liao, the confederation emerged as a steppe power after the Liao collapse in 1125. Its first recorded khan, Khabul of the Borjigin, drove off invasions by the Jurchen Jin; his successor Ambaghai was seized by the Tatars and executed by the Jin, and Hotula Khan answered with thirteen campaigns of revenge. After Hotula's death the Khiyad chief Yesugei, grandson of Khabul, held the confederation together until the Tatars poisoned him in 1171. His son Temujin, born on the upper Onon in 1162, was elected khan of the Khamag in 1189 and united the whole plateau as Genghis Khan in 1206, carrying the old clans into the Mongol Empire.
zh: 蒙兀意为“全体蒙古”，是12世纪最主要的蒙古部落联盟，在肯特山的鄂嫩河、克鲁伦河和土拉河肥沃流域以及相邻的外贝加尔森林游牧，泰赤乌部就驻营在北面的林地；联盟的核心氏族是乞颜、泰赤乌和札剌亦儿三支。他们在契丹人的辽朝已有记载，1125年辽亡后成为草原上的一支强权。最早见诸记载的汗是出自孛儿只斤氏的合不勒，他击退了女真金朝的入侵；继任的俺巴孩被塔塔尔人俘获、送交金朝处死，忽图剌汗为复仇对塔塔尔发动了十三次征战。忽图剌死后，合不勒之孙、乞颜部首领也速该维系着联盟，直到1171年被塔塔尔人毒杀。他的儿子铁木真1162年生于鄂嫩河上游，1189年被推举为蒙兀的汗，又于1206年统一整个高原，称成吉思汗，把这些旧氏族带入了蒙古帝国。

en: The Khampas are the Tibetans of Kham, the rugged eastern frontier of the Tibetan world cut by the gorges of the Mekong, Salween and upper Yangtze and known traditionally as the Four Rivers and Six Ranges. Songtsen Gampo's armies brought this country into the Tibetan Empire in the seventh century, planting border-taming monasteries along its eastern edge, but after the empire broke apart in the ninth century Kham never again bowed to a single ruler. Instead its valleys became a patchwork of warrior chiefdoms and monastic estates, among them Degé, Chakla, Lingtsang, Nangchen and the Hor States, where Nyingma, Kagyu and Sakya monasteries stood beside the forts of secular lords. In 1337 the country around Nyarong, Litang and Tsawarong was still ruled in just this way, by local headmen and lamas who answered to no distant king. The Mongol Güshi Khan's campaign of 1639, which overthrew the King of Beri, drew Kham into the Dalai Lama's orbit, and in 1677 its border with China was settled in Lhasa's favor. When the Qing drove the Dzungars out of Tibet in 1717–1720, however, the frontier was redrawn along the Jinsha River in 1725–1726, and the Khampa lands on the eastern bank became imperial territory under tusi chieftains. Famed as horsemen, traders and raiders, the Khampas kept their fierce local pride under whichever distant power claimed their valleys.
zh: 康巴人是康区的藏人。康区位于藏族世界的东部边疆，横断山脉中澜沧江、怒江和金沙江上游峡谷纵横，传统上称“四水六岗”。7世纪松赞干布的大军把这片土地并入吐蕃帝国，沿东境修建镇边寺院；9世纪帝国解体后，康区再未臣服于单一统治者，各河谷形成由武士头人和寺院庄园拼成的局面，德格、林葱、囊谦、昌都与霍尔诸部各据一方，宁玛、噶举、萨迦各派寺院和世俗贵族的堡垒并立。1337年时，新龙（雅垄）、理塘、察瓦戎一带仍由本地头人和喇嘛分治，不奉远方之君。1639年蒙古和硕特部固始汗出兵击灭白利土司，康区被纳入达赖喇嘛的势力范围，1677年其与中原的边界划定并归拉萨管辖。1717至1720年清军入藏驱逐准噶尔，1725至1726年边界改以金沙江为界，江东的康巴土地成为王朝治下的土司辖地。康巴人以善骑、经商和强悍善战闻名，无论名义上的宗主是谁，始终保持着强烈的地方自尊。

en: The Khandeshi are the people of the Khandesh region, the Tapti River valley in north-western Maharashtra centred on the fortress towns of Asirgarh and Burhanpur. Their Indo-Aryan tongue, Khandeshi, is also called Ahirani after the Ahir herders who were its earliest named inhabitants; the region was known as Abhiradesa in early literature, and it is written in the Devanagari script. In 1295 Ala-ud-din Khalji of Delhi took Khandesh from its Chauhan lord, and in the late fourteenth century Malik Raja founded the independent Farooqui sultanate. Akbar's armies overran the region in 1599, making Burhanpur the seat of a Mughal subah at a time when cotton, indigo and cloth trade brought it wide prosperity. Maratha raids began in 1670, the Peshwa seized Asirgarh in 1760 and parcelled the land out to the Holkar and Scindia houses, and in 1818 Khandesh passed to British rule.
zh: 坎德什人是坎德什地区的居民，其地在今马哈拉施特拉邦西北部的达布蒂河谷，以阿西尔格尔和布尔汉普尔两座要塞城镇为中心。他们说的印度—雅利安语称坎德什语，又称阿希拉尼语，得名于当地最早见于记载的阿希尔牧人；早期文献称这一带为阿比拉德萨，文字使用天城体。1295年，德里的阿拉乌德丁·哈尔吉从乔汉领主手中夺取坎德什；14世纪末，马利克·拉贾建立了独立的法鲁基苏丹国。1599年阿克巴的军队征服此地，布尔汉普尔成为莫卧儿苏巴的治所，棉花、靛蓝和布匹贸易使这一时期颇为富庶。马拉地人的袭扰始于1670年，佩什瓦于1760年攻占阿西尔格尔，把土地分封给霍尔卡尔与辛迪亚家族；1818年坎德什落入英国统治。

en: The Khanty, formerly called Ostyaks by Russians from their own word as-kho, a person of the Ob, are the Ob-Ugric people of the middle and lower Ob and Irtysh, a region known to medieval Novgorod as Yugra, and their language shares its Ugric branch with Mansi and distant Hungarian. They descend from woodland Uralic populations between the Kama and the Irtysh, with some scholars tracing a northward move from the southern Ural steppe around the year 500, and by the eleventh century Novgorodian hunters and merchants knew them as the many tribes of Yugra, each led by its own chief and split into two exogamous phratries. Later organized into clans that dealt with Russia through their knyazets, some Khanty princedoms were absorbed into the Sibir Khanate between the 1440s and the 1570s, and its capital Qashliq stood in their lands. The Russian conquest of the khanate in the 1580s opened a century of pressure: yasak tribute, hostage children, destroyed idols and mass baptisms produced only superficial Christianity, while the Khanty kept their nature cults, their shamans and the long Bear Celebration honouring the sky god Torum beside fishing, taiga trapping and reindeer herding.
zh: 汉特人过去被俄国人称为奥斯佳克人，名称来自他们自称的阿斯-霍，即鄂毕河人；他们是鄂毕河与额尔齐斯河中下游的鄂毕-乌戈尔民族，所居地区在中世纪诺夫哥罗德文献中称作尤格拉，其语言与曼西语以及遥远的匈牙利语同属乌戈尔语支。他们是卡马河与额尔齐斯河之间乌拉尔林地居民的后裔，也有学者认为他们约在500年从南乌拉尔草原北迁至此。11世纪时，诺夫哥罗德的猎人和商人已知道尤格拉诸部：每部各有首领，并分为两个实行族外婚的半偶族。后来他们按氏族组织，由王公与俄国打交道；15世纪40年代至16世纪70年代，一些汉特小公国被并入西伯利亚汗国，汗国都城卡什雷克就坐落在他们的土地上。16世纪80年代俄国征服西伯利亚汗国后，一个世纪的压迫随之而来：亚萨克贡赋、扣留儿童为人质、捣毁神像、集体洗礼，但基督教化流于表面，汉特人仍保留自然崇拜、萨满和敬拜天神托鲁姆的漫长熊节，继续以捕鱼、泰加狩猎和养鹿为生。

en: The Kharchin are a Mongol tribe of the border country between Chifeng and northwestern Liaoning, whose name goes back to the early 1200s, when Kipchak and Qanqli captives famed for brewing black kumis were enrolled in the Mongol imperial guard and called Kharachin; by the 1400s they had become a tribe of the Yüngshiyebü tümen on Chahar pastures. In 1510 Dayan Khan made them one of his right-wing tribes, and under his grandson Kundulun they spread east from the upper Luan River into the lands of the Ming Döyin, or Uriangkhan, Guards first set up in 1389, whose herdsmen gradually took the Kharchin name for themselves. Ligdan Khan of the Chahar scattered the old Yüngshiyebü Kharchin in 1628, whereupon the Uriangkhan leader Subudi led the merged tribe to submit to Hong Taiji. In 1636 and 1648, and again under the Kangxi emperor, the Qing enrolled them as the three Kharchin banners of the Josotu League, and these border Mongols increasingly settled into agriculture beside Chinese farming migrants.
zh: 喀喇沁是游牧在赤峰与辽西北交界地带的蒙古部落，族名可追溯到13世纪初：当时以酿制黑马奶酒闻名的钦察、康里降人被编入蒙古帝国的宿卫，被蒙古人称作喀喇沁；到15世纪，他们已成为察哈尔境内永谢布万户的一个部落。1510年达延汗击败亦卜剌，把喀喇沁编为右翼诸部之一；后来在达延汗之孙昆都力哈统领下，他们从滦河上游向东扩展，进入明朝1389年设立的朵颜卫，即兀良哈三卫的牧地，朵颜的兀良哈人逐渐袭用了喀喇沁之名。1628年，察哈尔的林丹汗击溃永谢布万户，旧喀喇沁溃散，兀良哈首领苏布地遂率融合后的部众归附皇太极；清朝在1636年、1648年及康熙年间先后把他们编为卓索图盟的喀喇沁三旗，这些边地蒙古人也越来越多地在汉族移民旁边定居务农。

en: The Kharia are a Munda people of the forested uplands where Jharkhand and Odisha meet, centred on the Sundargarh, Simdega and Gumla hills, whose Kharia language forms, together with Juang, its own branch of the Austroasiatic family. Like other Munda peoples they descend from Austroasiatic settlers who reached the Odisha coast from Southeast Asia by about 1500 BCE. They are divided into Hill, Delki and Dudh Kharia: the Hill Kharia remained hunters, gatherers and labourers living on game, honey and wild tubers, while the Delki and Dudh sections took to settled plough farming, and many in the plains held land as tenants under zamindars. Their villages kept close to the forest, burning fresh plots for millet, pulses and rice, and their traditional religion centred on the spirit groves and ancestor cults of the Sarna complex shared with neighbouring Munda tribes such as the Munda and Oraon.
zh: 卡里亚人是居住在贾坎德与奥里萨交界山林地带的蒙达族群，以孙达尔加尔、辛德加和古姆拉丘陵为中心，所用的卡里亚语与朱昂语共同构成南亚语系蒙达语族下的一个独立语支。和其他蒙达人一样，他们是公元前1500年左右自东南亚抵达奥里萨海岸的南亚语移民的后裔。卡里亚人分为山地卡里亚、德尔基卡里亚和杜德卡里亚三支：山地卡里亚仍以狩猎、采集和佣工为生，食物取自猎物、蜂蜜和野生块茎，德尔基和杜德两支则转为定居犁耕，平原上的许多人在柴明达尔手下充当佃农。他们的村落紧靠森林，焚烧林地轮种小米、豆类和水稻；传统信仰属邻近蒙达诸族共有的萨尔纳体系，以圣林和祖先崇拜为中心。

en: The Khas are an Indo-Aryan hill people of the western Nepalese Himalayas, whose old Khasa tongue is the ancestor of modern Nepali. From the eleventh century their rulers, the Khasa Malla kings, held a kingdom centred on Sinja in the Karnali basin, which at its height under Prithvi Malla in the mid-fourteenth century reached into western Tibet as far as Guge and Purang. Krachalla left an inscription as early as 1223, Ashoka Challa styled himself emperor of the Khashas at Bodhgaya in 1255, and Ripu Malla marked his 1312 pilgrimage to Lumbini on the Ashokan pillar; their records use an early form of Nepali written in Devanagari and mix Buddhist and Hindu devotion. After the death of Abhaya Malla the empire broke into the Baise and Chaubisi hill principalities of the Karnali, Bheri and Gandaki regions, into which Rajput immigrants from the plains were steadily absorbed. The Khas kept their language and their Shaivite Masto cult, and when the Gorkha kingdom later absorbed these hill states, the same speech spread with it to become the language of the unified Nepalese kingdom.
zh: 卡斯人是尼泊尔西部喜马拉雅山区的印度雅利安族群，其古卡斯语是今日尼泊尔语的前身。11世纪起，卡斯·马拉诸王以格尔纳利盆地的辛贾为中心建立王国；14世纪中叶普利特维·马拉在位时国势最盛，势力西入西藏的古格、普兰等地。克拉查拉早在1223年就留下铜板铭文，阿育王·查拉于1255年在菩提伽耶自称卡斯人的皇帝，里普·马拉1312年朝礼蓝毗尼并在阿育王石柱上刻铭；他们的碑铭使用天城文书写的早期尼泊尔语，兼奉佛教与印度教。阿巴亚·马拉死后，帝国瓦解为格尔纳利、贝里和甘达基地区的二十二国与二十四国山地诸邦，来自平原的拉杰普特移民也逐渐融入其中。卡斯人保留了自己的语言和湿婆派的马斯托信仰；后来廓尔喀王国吞并这些山邦时，卡斯语也随之传播，成为统一后的尼泊尔王国的语言。

en: The Khasi are an Austroasiatic people of the Khasi Hills in present-day Meghalaya, one of the handful of Mon-Khmer-speaking communities surviving in South Asia; their speech is closest to the Palaung languages of Myanmar, and oral tradition as well as linguistics point to a migration from Southeast Asia by way of Upper Burma and the Brahmaputra valley. Their society is matrilineal: property passes to the youngest daughter, men join their wife's clan after marriage, and the exogamous clans trace descent through a common female ancestress. They worshipped a formless supreme creator, U Blei Nongthaw, in the indigenous Niam Khasi religion, and the War subtribe built living root bridges by training fig-tree roots across streams. Politically the hills were split among about twenty-five small chiefdoms under syiem chiefs, alongside the related Jaintia kingdom, whose Pnar rulers of the Syiem Sutnga clan had split from an older realm in 630 and ruled the plains around Jaintiapur and Sylhet. Jaintia was briefly overrun by the Ahoms in 1707, came into contact with the East India Company after the grant of the Diwani of Bengal in 1765, and was annexed by the Company in 1835.
zh: 卡西人是今梅加拉亚邦卡西丘陵的南亚语系族群，也是南亚仅存的少数孟高棉语社群之一；他们的语言与缅甸的德昂语支最接近，口传与语言研究都显示，其先民自东南亚经上缅甸和布拉马普特拉河谷迁徙而来。卡西社会实行母系制：家产传给最年幼的女儿，男子婚后加入妻子的氏族，实行外婚制的各氏族都把世系追溯到一位共同的女性祖先。他们在本土的“卡尼亚姆·卡西”信仰中崇拜无形的至高创世神乌布莱·农索；支系瓦尔人还把榕树的根系牵引跨过溪流，编成“活树桥”。政治上，卡西丘陵分属约二十五个由“西姆”酋长统治的小酋邦，与之并存的是亲缘的詹塔王国：出身苏通加氏族的普纳尔统治者于630年从一个更古老的政权分出，统治着贾因蒂亚布尔和锡尔赫特一带的平原。詹塔于1707年一度被阿洪姆人攻灭后复国，1765年东印度公司取得孟加拉的迪万财税权后与其接触，最终在1835年被公司吞并。

en: The Khmer are an Austroasiatic people of the lower Mekong basin and one of the oldest settled populations of mainland Southeast Asia, whose rice-farming ancestors had reached the region by the early second millennium BCE. They built the port kingdom of Funan and its successor Chenla, and in 802 Jayavarman II founded the Khmer Empire, the Angkor period of Cambodian history. From a network of hydraulic cities north of the Tonlé Sap, Angkor grew into the largest pre-industrial urban complex in the world; Suryavarman II raised Angkor Wat in the early twelfth century and Jayavarman VII added the walled city of Angkor Thom and the Bayon around 1200. Hinduism and Mahayana Buddhism gradually gave way to Theravada Buddhism from the late thirteenth century. In 1337 the empire was past its peak, weakened by drought, damaged waterworks and repeated Siamese wars, and in 1431 Ayutthaya sacked Angkor, after which the court moved downriver to Longvek and then Oudong. The Longvek capital fell to Siam in 1594, and during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Vietnamese settlement of the Mekong Delta detached the lands of the lower Khmer, or Khmer Krom, from the Cambodian heartland.
zh: 高棉人是生活在湄公河下游的南亚语系民族，也是东南亚大陆最古老的定居族群之一，其从事稻作的先民在公元前两千年前后已到达这一地区。他们先后建立了港口王国扶南及其继承者真腊；802年，阇耶跋摩二世建立高棉帝国，柬埔寨历史由此进入吴哥时代。以洞里萨湖北部一系列水利城市为中心，吴哥发展为前工业时代世界上规模最大的城市综合体：苏利耶跋摩二世在12世纪初修建了吴哥窟，阇耶跋摩七世又在1200年前后增建了吴哥城和巴戎寺。13世纪末起，印度教和大乘佛教逐渐让位于上座部佛教。1337年时帝国已过鼎盛期，受干旱、水利设施损毁和对暹罗连年战争的削弱；1431年阿瑜陀耶攻陷吴哥，此后王廷先后南迁到洛韦和乌栋。洛韦于1594年被暹罗攻占，17至18世纪间，越南人对湄公河三角洲的拓殖又把下高棉人居住的土地从柬埔寨本土分割出去。

en: The Khmu, whose endonym means people, speak a Khmuic language of the Austroasiatic family and are considered the aboriginal inhabitants of northern Laos and the surrounding upper Mekong lands, where Khmuic villagers had lived for millennia before the arrival of Tai speakers. Tai migrations south gathered pace after the Mongol conquest of Yunnan in 1253, and as Lao principalities took the fertile river valleys the Khmu were pushed onto the wooded mid-altitude slopes, where they became known as Lao Theung and practised swidden farming above the lowland Lao and below the highland Hmong. In 1337 their scattered villages still reached west across the Khorat Plateau, the region the game assigns them. When Fa Ngum founded the Lao kingdom of Lan Xang in 1353, the Khmu entered it as its largest upland people, governed through their own village headmen and remembered in Lao origin legend as the elder brothers of the lowland Lao.
zh: 克木人的自称意为“人”，说南亚语系克木语支的语言，被认为是老挝北部及湄公河上游周边土地的原住民；早在泰语人群到来之前的数千年里，克木语村民就已生活在这里。泰人南迁在1253年蒙古征服云南后加快，随着佬人城邦占据肥沃的河谷，克木人被挤到林木覆盖的中山坡地，被称为“老听”，在低地佬人与高地苗瑶人之间从事刀耕火种。1337年时，他们分散的村落向西仍延伸到呵叻高原，也就是游戏分配给他们的区域。1353年法昂建立佬人国家澜沧王国时，克木人作为境内最大的山地民族加入，由本村头人管辖，并在佬人的起源传说中被记为低地佬人的兄长。

en: Khoemana, also called Korana or Griqua, is the South Khoekhoe tongue once spoken along the southern Cape coast and across the Karoo, where clans such as the Gouriqua, Outeniqua and Attequa grazed Nguni cattle and sheep when Dutch ships began calling at Table Bay. The Dutch East India Company founded its Cape station in 1652, and over the following century the Cape Khoekhoe lost grazing land in wars and epidemics and were drawn into the colonial frontier. Survivors merged with Dutch-speaking settlers, freed slaves, San and Tswana neighbors into the mounted, gun-using communities known as Basters, Oorlam, Korana and Griqua; the name Griqua is first recorded in 1730, and under leaders such as Adam Kok they trekked beyond the colonial border to the Orange and Vaal rivers, where the mission settlement of Klaarwater, later Griquatown, became their main gathering place. During the 1820s and 1830s Korana and Griqua commandos raided across the highveld, and a Griqua commando was destroyed by the Ndebele at Moordkop in 1831.
zh: 科伊马纳语又称科拉纳语或格里夸语，是南部科伊科伊人的语言，曾通行于开普南部海岸和卡鲁高原一带；当荷兰船只开始停靠桌湾时，古里夸、乌特尼夸、阿特夸等氏族正在那片土地上放牧恩古尼牛和绵羊。1652年荷兰东印度公司在开普建立据点，此后一个世纪里，开普科伊科伊人在战争和瘟疫中丧失牧场，被卷入殖民边疆。幸存者与讲荷兰语的定居者、获释奴隶、桑人和茨瓦纳邻居融合，形成骑马持枪的混合群体，分别称巴斯特人、奥兰姆人、科拉纳人和格里夸人；“格里夸”之名最早见于1730年的记载，在亚当·科克等首领率领下，他们越过殖民边界迁至奥兰治河与法尔河畔，传教站克拉尔沃特（后改名格里夸敦）成为其主要聚落地。19世纪20—30年代，科拉纳和格里夸的武装民团在高地草原四处袭掠，1831年一支格里夸民团在莫尔德科普被恩德贝莱人歼灭。

en: The Khon Muang, or Tai Yuan, are the Northern Thai people of the mountain-fringed river valleys around Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai and Phayao, who call themselves people of the mueang, the settled rice-plain towns, to distinguish themselves from the swidden-farming hill peoples. Tai Yuan settlement of the Kok and Ing river basins is documented from the eleventh century, growing out of the old chiefdom of Ngoenyang. King Mangrai united the northern Tai principalities from 1259, founded Chiang Rai in 1263, conquered the ancient Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai at Lamphun around 1292 and in 1296 laid out Chiang Mai as the capital of his new Lanna kingdom, the Land of a Million Rice Fields. From the conquered Mon the Tai Yuan took Theravada Buddhism and the Tai Tham writing system, and a shared Lanna identity coalesced during the fourteenth century. In 1337 Mangrai's dynasty ruled Chiang Mai alongside rival mueang such as Phayao and Phrae; Lanna reached its zenith under King Tilok in the fifteenth century, fighting Ayutthaya for control of the northern Chao Phraya towns. Disaster and epidemic around 1520 began its decline, and in 1558 the Burmese Toungoo conquered Chiang Mai, opening two centuries of Burmese overlordship. The Lanna nobles allied with Taksin of Siam to throw off the Burmese in 1774, and after the fall of Chiang Saen in 1804 the country passed under Siamese suzerainty while keeping its own lords and internal autonomy for most of the early nineteenth century.
zh: 傣阮人又称泰沅人、兰纳人，是清迈、清莱和帕尧一带群山环抱河谷中的北部泰人，他们自称“勐人”，即定居稻作平原城镇之民，以此与游耕山地民族相区别。泰沅人在11世纪已定居戈克河与英河流域，其前身是恩央扬酋邦。芒莱王自1259年起统一北部泰人诸邦，1263年建清莱城，约1292年征服南奔的孟人古国哈利奔猜，1296年兴建清迈作为新王国兰纳（意为“百万稻田之国”）的都城。泰沅人从被征服的孟人那里接受了上座部佛教和泰昙文，共同的兰纳认同在14世纪逐渐形成。1337年时，芒莱王朝统治着清迈，与帕尧、帕府等邻邦并存；兰纳在15世纪滴洛拉王治下达到鼎盛，为争夺湄南河上游诸城与阿瑜陀耶交战。1520年前后的灾荒和瘟疫开启了衰落，1558年缅甸东吁王朝攻占清迈，兰纳进入长达两百年的缅甸统治时期。1774年，兰纳贵族联合暹罗的郑信摆脱缅甸，1804年清盛陷落后国家转入暹罗宗主权之下，但在19世纪的大部分时间里仍保留自己的领主和内部自治。

en: The Khonds are a Dravidian tribal people of the forested Eastern Ghats, chiefly in the highlands of inland Odisha around Kandhamal, Rayagada and Koraput, with smaller groups across the border in Andhra. They speak Kui and Kuvi, Dravidian tongues closest to Gondi and traditionally written in the Odia script, and their society is organised into totemic clans led by their own headmen rather than castes. Their economy combines hunting and gathering with podu, the local form of slash-and-burn cultivation on rotating hill fields. They worshipped the earth deity Dharni together with mountain and river spirits, and the Meriah rite, in which a purchased victim was sacrificed to secure the fertility of the soil, made them notorious to early British administrators. During the Company's war against the raja of Goomsur from 1835, the Scottish officer Samuel Charters Macpherson entered the previously unmapped Khond hills in 1837, recorded their language and institutions, and prepared the reports on which the later campaigns to abolish the sacrifice were based.
zh: 孔德人是生活在东高止山森林中的达罗毗荼语系部族，主要聚居于奥里萨内陆的坎达马尔、拉亚加达和科拉普特一带高地，另有小支分布在相邻的安得拉。他们使用与贡德语亲缘最近的达罗毗荼语言库伊语和库维语，传统上以奥里亚字母书写；社会按图腾氏族组织，由本族头人统领，而不行种姓制度。生计以狩猎采集与当地称“波杜”的轮垦刀耕火种相结合。他们崇奉大地神达尔尼以及山川神灵，其中为求土地肥沃而献祭买来人牲的梅里亚仪式，令早期英国官员极为震动。1835年东印度公司对古姆苏尔王公开战后，苏格兰军官塞缪尔·查特斯·麦克弗森于1837年进入此前无人测绘的孔德山区，记录了他们的语言与制度，其报告成为后来废除人祭行动的依据。

en: The Khorasanis are the Persian-speaking people of western Khorasan, the historic eastern province of Iran, centered on Nishapur, Tus and later Mashhad, along the route between Gorgan and the Oxus. Khorasan, meaning the Eastern Land, was organized as a Sasanian province in the sixth century and became the cradle of New Persian: after the Arab conquest, literary Persian re-emerged in the cities of Khorasan and Transoxiana under the Tahirids, Saffarids and above all the Samanids, and until the thirteenth century the region was the cultural capital of the Persian world, home to scholars and poets such as Avicenna, al-Biruni and Omar Khayyam. The Mongol conquest of 1221 devastated its cities, but recovery followed under the Ilkhanate and the Timurids, who made Herat a radiant capital. In 1337 the fall of the Ilkhanate had left western Khorasan to local rulers such as the Sarbadars of Sabzevar and the Kartids of Herat, until Timur conquered the region at the end of the fourteenth century. From the sixteenth century the Safavids and the Uzbek khanates fought over Khorasan for two hundred years. Nader Shah made Mashhad the capital of his empire in 1736, and after his death the Qajars secured the western half in 1796 while Herat passed to the Afghan Durranis.
zh: 呼罗珊人指西呼罗珊的波斯语居民，其地在伊朗历史上的东方行省，以尼沙普尔、图斯及后来的马什哈德为中心，扼守戈尔甘至阿姆河一线。呼罗珊意为东方之地，6世纪被萨珊王朝设为行省，也是新波斯语的摇篮：阿拉伯征服后，文学波斯语在塔希尔、萨法尔尤其是萨曼王朝治下的呼罗珊与河中城市重新兴起，在13世纪之前这里一直是波斯世界的文化中心，伊本·西纳、比鲁尼、奥马尔·海亚姆等学者诗人辈出。1221年蒙古征服重创其城市，但伊儿汗国和帖木儿王朝时期相继恢复，赫拉特更被营建为辉煌都城。1337年伊儿汗国崩溃，西呼罗珊落入萨布泽瓦尔的萨尔巴达尔和赫拉特的卡尔提德王朝等地方政权之手，14世纪末为帖木儿征服。16世纪起，萨法维王朝与乌兹别克诸汗国为争夺呼罗珊交战两百年；纳迪尔沙于1736年以马什哈德为帝国都城，他死后卡扎尔王朝在1796年取得西半部，赫拉特则归入阿富汗的杜兰尼王朝。

en: The Khorezmians of this age are the settled town dwellers and farmers of the Khwarazm oasis and the Transoxianan cities, from Bukhara and Chach to the Fergana valley. Their forebears included the Iranian-speaking Khwarazmians and Sogdians, whose Eastern Iranian tongue survived in Khwarazm at least into the thirteenth century before giving way to Persian and to the Karluk dialects of Turkic. Turkic rule had come in the eleventh century with the Muslim Kara-Khanid khans, and by the fourteenth century the bazaar towns of the Silk Road spoke Middle Turkic, wrote in the Perso-Arabic script and kept the scholarly tradition of Khwarazmian learning such as that of the polymath al-Biruni. In 1337 the Transoxianan cities belonged to the fracturing Chagatai Khanate and the Khwarazm oasis to the Golden Horde, and later Timur the Lame made Samarkand the capital of his Timurid Empire, covering the region in mosques, madrasas and caravanserais. Out of the local Middle Turkic arose Chagatai, the classical literary language of Central Asia, brought to its height by the poet Ali-Shir Nava'i in the fifteenth century. When the Uzbek nomads of Muhammad Shaybani conquered Transoxiana after 1501, they called the conquered settled population, Turkic- and Persian-speakers alike, by the name Sart; these Karluk-speaking townspeople became the core of the later Uzbek nation under the khanates of Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand.
zh: 这一时代的花剌子模人，是花剌子模绿洲与河中各城——从布哈拉、赭时到费尔干纳谷地——的定居市民和农民。他们的祖先包括说伊朗语的花剌子模人和粟特人，其东伊朗语支的花剌子模语至少留存到13世纪，随后让位于波斯语和突厥语的葛逻禄方言。11世纪，信奉伊斯兰教的喀喇汗可汗带来突厥统治；到14世纪，丝绸之路上的商业城镇已通用中突厥语，以波斯—阿拉伯字母书写，并延续着比鲁尼等花剌子模学者的博学传统。1337年，河中诸城属于正在分裂的察合台汗国，花剌子模绿洲则属金帐汗国；后来跛子帖木儿以撒马尔罕为都建立帖木儿帝国，在境内广建清真寺、经学院和商队驿站。当地的中突厥语发展出察合台语，成为中亚的古典文学语言，15世纪经诗人阿里希尔·纳瓦伊之手推向顶峰。1501年后穆罕默德·昔班尼率领乌兹别克游牧民征服河中，把被征服的定居人口——无论说突厥语还是波斯语——统称为撒尔塔人；这些说葛逻禄语的城镇居民在布哈拉、希瓦和浩罕诸汗国治下，成为后世乌兹别克民族的核心。

en: The Khoromboy were a Yukaghir tribal group of the Laptev Sea coast, roaming the lower courses of the Omoloy and the Yana, where they spoke the Yan, or Detkil, dialect of Yukaghir. When Russian parties first met Yukaghir bands on the Yana in the 1630s, this was a small group of about a hundred and ten people, and the records sometimes call them Omoloi after their river. According to the ethnographer Boris Dolgikh, their name combines the Yukaghir words koriel, a wolf, and omo, a tribe, so that Khoromboy meant something like the wolf clan; northern Yakut used the same word for a wolf's den. Tribute, disease and pressure from reindeer-herding neighbors thinned them under Russian rule, and the Khoromboy eventually dissolved into Evenki and partly Nganasan communities.
zh: 霍龙博伊人是拉普捷夫海沿岸的尤卡吉尔部落，游猎于奥莫洛伊河和亚纳河下游，使用尤卡吉尔语的亚纳（杰特基尔）方言。17世纪30年代俄国探险队在亚纳河首次遇到尤卡吉尔人时，这个小群体约有110人，册籍有时按河名称他们为奥莫洛伊人。民族学家鲍里斯·多尔吉赫认为，族名由尤卡吉尔语“科里埃尔”（狼）和“奥莫”（部落）组合而成，意思近似“狼之族”；北部雅库特语里也用同一个词指代狼穴。在俄国统治下，贡赋、疫病和邻近养鹿民族的压力使他们不断减员，霍龙博伊人最终融入鄂温克人，还有一部分融入了恩加纳桑人。

en: The Khwe, also rendered Kxoe or Khwedam, are a San people of the Okavango Delta and the western Caprivi, whose traditional lands reach into Angola, Zambia and Botswana. Their own traditions place their ancestors around the Tsodilo Hills, and historical geography already records Khwe foragers roaming present-day Botswana, Namibia, Angola and Zambia in the first millennium before the common era. They lived in small semi-nomadic bands without chiefs, moving with the game and the seasonal waterholes, and left their mark in the rock art of the Tsodilo Hills. As Bantu-speaking herders and farmers spread through the region up to the year 1000, the Khwe traded and intermingled with them, and the clicks of their Khoe speech were absorbed into several neighbouring Bantu languages. While Dutch trekboers and their commandos destroyed San bands around the Cape frontier from 1714 to the 1790s, the Okavango country lay far beyond colonial reach, and the Khwe kept their foraging life there undisturbed.
zh: 克韦人（又译克索埃人，其语言也称克韦达姆语）是生活在奥卡万戈三角洲和卡普里维地带西部的桑人一支，传统活动范围延伸到安哥拉、赞比亚和博茨瓦纳。他们的口传传统把祖先之地指向措迪洛山；历史地理研究表明，早在公元前第一个千年，克韦狩猎采集者就活动在今博茨瓦纳、纳米比亚、安哥拉和赞比亚一带。他们结成没有酋长的半游牧小群，随猎物和季节性水洼迁徙，并在措迪洛山的岩画中留下了自己的印记。到公元1000年前后，说班图语的牧民和农民已遍布这一地区，克韦人与他们贸易、杂处，自己科伊语里的吸气音也被邻近几种班图语吸收。1714年至18世纪90年代，荷兰游牧布尔民及其民团在开普边境摧毁了一支支桑人群体，而奥卡万戈远在殖民势力范围之外，克韦人得以不受打扰地延续狩猎采集的生活。

en: The K'iche' are one of the principal Maya peoples of the Guatemalan highlands; their name means many trees, and its Nahuatl translation, Cuauhtēmallān, gave the country Guatemala its name. After the Classic collapse they built a powerful Postclassic kingdom, moving its capital from Jakawitz to Pismachi' and then, around 1400, to Q'umarkaj, called Utatlán by the Spanish, founded by the king Q'uq'umatz. Allied first with the Kaqchikel, the K'iche' conquered the K'oja of the Cuchumatanes and, under Q'uq'umatz's warlike son K'iq'ab, stretched their rule from Rabinal and Cobán to Quetzaltenango, the Motagua River and Escuintla, subduing the Mam of Zaculeu as well. A noble rebellion in 1470 drove out their Kaqchikel allies, who founded their own capital at Iximche, and after K'iq'ab died around 1475 the kingdom weakened through wars with the Kaqchikel and Tz'utujil. In March 1524 Pedro de Alvarado destroyed the K'iche' army in the Quetzaltenango valley, killing the commander Tecún Umán, then seized the ruling lords and burned Q'umarkaj to the ground. Under colonial rule the K'iche' preserved their traditions in writing: the Popol Vuh, with its creation myth and Hero Twins, was set down around 1550 and transcribed and translated by the Dominican Francisco Ximénez at Chichicastenango in 1701.
zh: 基切人是危地马拉高地最主要的玛雅族群之一；其名称意为“许多树”，纳瓦特尔语译作夸乌特马兰，“危地马拉”这个国名即由此而来。古典期崩溃后，他们建立起强盛的后古典期王国，都城先后从贾卡维茨迁至皮斯马奇，又在约1400年由国王库库马茨迁至库马尔卡赫（西班牙人称乌塔特兰）。基切人先与卡克奇克尔人结盟，征服了库丘马塔内斯的科哈人；到库库马茨好战的儿子基亚布在位时，疆域从拉比纳尔、科万一直扩展到克萨尔特南戈、莫塔瓜河和埃斯昆特拉，连萨库莱乌的玛姆人也臣服于他。1470年的贵族叛乱赶走了卡克奇克尔盟友，后者另建都城伊希姆切；基亚布约于1475年去世后，基切又在与卡克奇克尔、楚图希尔的战争中日渐衰弱。1524年3月，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多在克萨尔特南戈谷地歼灭基切军队，击杀统帅特昆·乌曼，随后擒获其执政首领并纵火将库马尔卡赫夷为平地。殖民时代，基切人以文字保存自己的传统：记载创世神话和孪生英雄故事的《波波尔·乌》约于1550年成文，1701年由多明我会修士弗朗西斯科·希门尼斯在奇奇卡斯特南戈转写并译成西班牙语。

en: The Kichesipirini, whose name means men of the great river from kiche, sipi and iriniouck, were an Algonquin nation of the Ottawa River, known to the French as the Island Indians because their main village stood on Morrison Island beside Allumette Island. The river itself they called Kitchissippi, and their country stretched along both its banks between present-day Ontario and Quebec. They may have been the first Algonquin people to meet the French: their one-eyed chief Tessouat met Samuel de Champlain in the summer of 1603, and Champlain visited the island village again in May 1613. Holding the narrows and portages of the great river, the Kichesipirini charged tolls on traders and missionaries and decided who might pass up or downstream. In 1645 they and their Huron allies made peace with the Haudenosaunee, but the settlement collapsed, and by 1650 raiding had driven them from their islands; their survivors are thought to have taken refuge among the Odawa.
zh: 基切西皮里尼人的名字由“基切”（大）、“西皮”（河）和“伊里尼乌克”（人）组成，意为“大河之人”，是渥太华河畔的阿尔冈金民族；法国人称他们为“岛上印第安人”，因为他们的主村位于阿吕梅特岛旁的莫里森岛上。渥太华河本身被他们称为“基奇西皮”，他们的地盘沿河流两岸延伸，横跨今安大略与魁北克交界一带。他们可能是最早接触法国人的阿尔冈金民族：独眼酋长泰苏阿于1603年夏天会见萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰，尚普兰又在1613年5月重访这座岛上村落。由于扼守大河的狭口和转运陆路，基切西皮里尼人向商人和传教士收取通行费，并决定谁可以上下游通行。1645年，他们与休伦盟友同霍德诺索尼人议和，但和议破裂，到1650年时袭扰已把他们逐出各岛；幸存者据认为投奔了奥达瓦人。

en: The Gija, also spelled Kija or Gidja and known to neighbours as the Lungga, are an Aboriginal people of the East Kimberley in Western Australia, whose country runs from Halls Creek towards Kununurra and takes in most of the striped sandstone domes of the Bungle Bungle Range in Purnululu, bordering Miriwoong lands around Lake Argyle. Their language belongs not to the widespread Pama-Nyungan family but to the small Jarragan family of the East Kimberley; the family takes its name from jarrag, the Gija word for language, and Gija forms its own Gijic branch alongside the Miriwoongic languages, with Kuluwarrang and Walgi recorded as possible dialects.
zh: 基亚人又拼作吉贾，邻族称之为隆加人，是西澳大利亚东金伯利地区的原住民，领地从霍尔斯克里克延伸到库努纳拉方向，波奴鲁鲁中班古鲁班古山脉的条纹砂岩穹丘大多位于其境内，在阿盖尔湖一带与米里温人的领地相接。他们的语言不属于分布广泛的帕马‑牛雅语系，而属于东金伯利一个小小的杰拉甘语系；该语系的名称就来自基亚语中意为‘语言’的词，基亚语自成吉亚语支，与米里温语支并列，库卢瓦兰语和瓦尔吉语则被记为它可能的方言。

en: The Kilivila are the people of the Trobriand Islands, a chain of flat coral atolls off the eastern tip of New Guinea, whose largest island is Kiriwina. Speaking Kilivila, an Austronesian language of the Oceanic branch, they live in settled villages under matrilineal clans that hold the land and arrange marriage and inheritance. Their economy rests on intensive yam gardening, with yams and pigs serving as stores of wealth and instruments of prestige, and their villages take part in the kula, a vast inter-island circuit in which red shell necklaces and white shell armshells circulate among lifelong trade partners reached by long seagoing canoes. The islands were unknown to Europeans until 1793, when the French expedition of Antoine Bruni d'Entrecasteaux sailed past and named the group after his officer Denis de Trobriand; in the decades that followed, whalers and other passing ships called there for water and fresh provisions, while the islanders kept their clan system, gardening magic and exchange rites essentially intact through this first age of contact.
zh: 基利维拉人是特罗布里恩群岛的居民，这片低平的珊瑚环礁位于新几内亚东端外海，最大岛屿为基里维纳岛。他们说的基利维拉语属于南岛语系大洋洲语支，村落定居，由母系氏族掌握土地并安排婚姻与继承。其经济以精耕的山药园艺为基础，山药和猪既是财富储备也是声望工具；各岛村落还参与“库拉”——一个庞大的岛际交换圈，红色贝壳项链与白色贝壳臂镯在终身贸易伙伴之间流转，人们驾驶远航独木舟前去拜访。欧洲人直到1793年才知道这些岛屿：安托万·布吕尼·当特尔卡斯托率领的法国船队经过此地，并以随船军官德尼·德·特罗布里安之名为群岛命名；此后数十年间，捕鲸船和过往船只常来补给淡水和新鲜给养，而在这最初的接触时代，岛民的氏族制度、园艺巫术和交换仪式基本保持完好。

en: The Kiliwa, who call themselves Ko'leeu, are an Indigenous people of northern Baja California, whose traditional territory stretched across the peninsula from San Felipe on the Gulf of California to San Quintín on the Pacific, between the Paipai to the north and the Cochimí to the south. They lived by hunting and gathering without agriculture: pit-roasted agave was their staff of life, supplemented in the high country by autumn acorns and pine nuts, while rabbits and deer were taken in communal drives into nets, and families trekked to the Gulf shore to fish, gather shellfish and collect salt. Their first meeting with Europeans was with Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo's ships at San Quintín in 1542, but two centuries passed before serious contact resumed, with the Jesuit Wenceslaus Linck in 1766 and the overland expedition of Gaspar de Portolà and Junípero Serra. Dominican friars then founded the mission of Santo Domingo in their territory in 1775 and San Pedro Mártir in 1794; by the time Mexico won independence in 1821, disease and mission life had reduced the Kiliwa population to a remnant.
zh: 科莱乌人外称基利瓦人，自称“科莱乌”，是下加利福尼亚半岛北部的原住民；他们的传统领地横跨半岛，东有加利福尼亚湾畔的圣费利佩，西抵太平洋沿岸的圣金廷，北邻派派人，南接科奇米人。他们不事农耕，以狩猎采集为生：坑烤龙舌兰是主食，秋季再到高地采收橡子和松子；兔子和鹿靠众人驱赶、张网围猎，各家族还会长途跋涉到海湾岸边捕鱼、采贝和取盐。1542年，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略的船队在圣金廷与他们首次相遇，但此后两个世纪接触寥寥，直到1766年耶稣会士文策斯劳斯·林克以及加斯帕尔·德·波尔托拉和胡尼佩罗·塞拉的陆路远征队先后到来。随后多明我会修士于1775年在其领地内建立圣多明各传教站，1794年又建立圣佩德罗马丁尔传教站；到1821年墨西哥赢得独立时，疫病和传教站生活已使科莱乌人口凋零，只剩残余部众。

en: The Killaka or Quillacas were one of the Aymara-speaking lordships of the southern Bolivian altiplano, holding the country around present Uyuni and the Aullagas basin south of Lake Poopó, in what is now the department of Oruro. With the Aullagas, Chichas and neighboring groups they belonged to the Charca federation, whose highland ayllus traded with the valleys and stood together against Guaraní raids from the Chaco. After the Inca conquest their land became the huamani of Quillaca, counted among the twenty-eight provinces of Collasuyo. Under Spanish rule the old chiefdom survived as Hatun Quillacas: the noble José Fernández Collque Inca Guarachi held its caciqueship from 1681 to 1734, and the town of Santuario de Quillacas preserves the people's name.
zh: 基利亚卡人又称基利亚卡斯人，是玻利维亚南部高原讲艾马拉语的族群之一，占据着波波湖以南、今乌尤尼和奥亚加斯盆地一带，即后来的奥鲁罗省境内。他们与奥亚加斯人、奇查人等邻近族群同属查尔卡斯联盟；联盟内的高原村社与河谷贸易，并合力抵御来自查科的瓜拉尼人袭扰。印加征服后，他们的土地被编为基利亚卡行省，是科利亚苏尤二十八个行省之一。西班牙统治时期，旧酋邦以大基利亚卡之名存续：贵族何塞·费尔南德斯·科尔克·印加·瓜拉奇于1681年至1734年担任其酋长，基利亚卡圣所镇的名字也来自这个族群。

en: The Killke were the pre-Inca people of the Cusco basin in the Peruvian highlands, whose archaeological culture flourished from about 900 to 1200 during the Late Intermediate Period, before Inca culture arose in the thirteenth century. Their most important monument is the great fortified complex of Saksaywaman above Cusco, whose first sections Killke builders raised in the twelfth century and which the Inca later expanded and reused. Killke pottery, first described by the archaeologist John Howland Rowe, consists mainly of globular vessels with vertical strap handles and simple geometric line decoration in black or black-on-red over a white slip. With the rise of Cusco under the early Inca rulers in the thirteenth century, Killke communities were absorbed into the Inca world, which inherited their stoneworking and ceramic traditions.
zh: 基利克人是秘鲁高原库斯科盆地的前印卡居民，其考古文化在约900—1200年的晚中间期兴盛，早于13世纪兴起的印卡文化。他们最重要的遗迹是库斯科城北的萨克塞瓦曼大型要塞建筑群：基利克工匠在12世纪建起它的最早部分，后来印卡人又加以扩建并继续使用。基利克陶器最早由考古学家约翰·豪兰·罗描述，多为带竖直带状把手的球状容器，白色陶衣上饰以黑色或黑红两色的简单几何线条。13世纪初印卡统治者在库斯科崛起后，基利克社群融入印卡世界，其石雕与制陶传统也被印卡继承。

en: The Kimaama are a Papuan people of Kolepom Island, the large, flat island off the south coast of New Guinea in present-day South Papua, Indonesia. Their main settlement of Kimaan lies in the island's southeast, and their Kimaghama tongue, together with neighbouring Riantana, forms the Central Kolopom branch of the Trans–New Guinea language family.
zh: 基马马人是科洛庞岛上的巴布亚族群；该岛地处新几内亚岛南海岸外，即今印度尼西亚南巴布亚省，地势低平。他们的主要聚落基马安位于岛的东南部，所说的基马马语与邻近的里安塔纳语共同构成泛新几内亚语系的中科洛庞语支。

en: The Kindigir are an Evenki clan whose early hunting grounds lay around the upper Lena and the northern shore of Lake Baikal. Dushkachan, on the Kichera river near the lake's northern tip, is described as one of the first settled camps of the Kindigir, and archaeology traces human occupation there to the early first millennium. The clan entered written history with the Russian conquest of the Lena country in the 1600s, when the Baikal Evenki came under yasak administration. Kindigir lineages, including a Lakshikagir branch, were later counted among the Barguzin Khamnigans, the Mongolized Evenki clans absorbed into the Buryat world east of Baikal.
zh: 金迪吉尔人是鄂温克氏族，早期猎场在勒拿河上游与贝加尔湖北岸一带。贝加尔湖北端基切拉河畔的杜什卡昌被称为金迪吉尔氏族最早的定居营地之一，考古发现表明公元第一个千年初期已有人在此活动。17世纪俄国征服勒拿河流域时，贝加尔湖沿岸的鄂温克人被纳入雅萨克税贡体系，该氏族也由此见诸文字记载。金迪吉尔的支系（包括拉克什卡吉尔分支）后来被列入巴尔古津哈米尼干人的氏族名单，这些蒙古化的鄂温克氏族在贝加尔湖以东逐渐融入布里亚特世界。

en: The Waimiri-Atroari, who call themselves Kinja, are a Cariban-speaking forest people of northern Brazil, whose villages lie in the country between the Uatumã, Negro and Branco rivers, spanning what are now the states of Roraima and Amazonas. Kin of the Kalina, they were known to earlier travellers by a string of other names, Crichaná, Jauapery and Bonari among them, and their tongue belongs to the Carib language family. Spanish and Portuguese expansion up the Amazon reached their rivers in the 1600s, though the first recorded face-to-face contact came only in 1732; in 1775 the Portuguese official Francisco Xavier Ribeiro Sampaio crossed their territory and left one of the earliest descriptions of it. The Kinja already had a firm name as warriors, and the wealth of their rivers and forests drew pioneer traders upstream, so through the 1700s and early 1800s they kept their independence by meeting intruders with their bows rather than with trade or missions.
zh: 金雅人是巴西北部使用加勒比语族语言的森林族群，村庄散布在瓦图芒河、内格罗河与布朗库河之间、地当今罗赖马州与亚马逊州交界一带。他们与卡利纳人同源，早年旅人还用克里沙纳、雅乌阿佩里、博纳里等一串名字称呼他们。17世纪西班牙和葡萄牙沿亚马逊河的扩张已抵达他们的河道，但有据可查的第一次面对面接触迟至1732年；1775年葡萄牙官员弗朗西斯科·沙维尔·里贝罗·桑帕约穿越他们的领地，留下了最早的记述之一。金雅人早已享有善战之名，而其河川与林地的丰富物产又引着拓荒商人溯流而上，因此在18世纪至19世纪初，他们不事贸易、不接纳传教，而是以弓箭迎击闯入者，守住了自身的独立。

en: The Kinugumiut, who call themselves the Kiŋikmiut, are the Iñupiaq people of the Bering Strait tip of the Seward Peninsula, around Port Clarence and Cape Prince of Wales, the site of present-day Wales, or Kiŋigin, the westernmost town on the North American mainland. They speak the Bering Strait dialect of Iñupiaq and belonged to the whaling and sea-mammal hunting culture of the strait, trading across the narrow water with the peoples of Siberian Chukotka. Captain James Cook named Cape Prince of Wales on his voyage of 1778, and in 1827 a Russian naval report listed their coastal and inland villages by name, making the Kinugumiut one of the best-documented Alaskan Inuit groups of the early contact period.
zh: 基努古缪特人自称基尼基缪特，是苏厄德半岛白令海峡一端的因纽皮亚特人，活动在克拉伦斯港和威尔士王子角一带，也就是北美大陆最西端的城镇威尔士（基尼金）的所在地。他们使用因纽皮亚特语的白令海峡方言，属于海峡地区捕鲸和捕猎海洋哺乳动物的文化圈，还跨过狭窄的海面与西伯利亚楚科奇的民族贸易。1778年詹姆斯·库克在航行中命名了威尔士王子角；1827年的一份俄国海军报告逐一记录了他们在沿海和内陆的村庄，基努古缪特人也因此成为早期接触时代记载最详尽的阿拉斯加因纽特群体之一。

en: The Kirati are a cluster of Tibeto-Burman peoples of the eastern Himalaya, including the Rai, Limbu, Sunuwar and Yakkha, whose homelands run from the hills and river valleys of eastern Nepal across Sikkim and Darjeeling. Sanskrit and Vedic texts knew the mountain peoples of this region as Kirata, and Kirati chiefs were among the earliest rulers of the Kathmandu Valley: according to tradition their king Yalambar founded a Kirat dynasty there before the Licchavi conquest in the first millennium. In the far east the Limbu country, Limbuwan, was divided into ten kingdoms, of which Morang with its capital at Bijaypur was the strongest, and the Limbu language acquired its own Sirijunga script in the ninth century. Kirati society was ordered by the Mundhum, a body of oral lore serving as law, and its people worshipped nature and ancestors through shamans, marking the planting and harvest seasons with the Sakela festivals. The independent Kirati kingdoms ended in 1774, when Prithvi Narayan Shah's Gorkha armies conquered Limbuwan after seventeen battles; the resulting treaty kept a measure of local self-rule under the traditional kipat land system.
zh: 基拉特人是喜马拉雅山东段一群藏缅语族群的统称，包括拉伊、林布、逊瓦尔和亚卡等分支，聚居地从尼泊尔东部的山区与河谷延伸到锡金和大吉岭。梵文和吠陀文献把这一带的山民称为基拉塔人；基拉特首领也是加德满都谷地最早的统治者之一，相传首领雅兰巴尔在那里建立了基拉特王朝，直到公元一千纪被离车毗人征服。在更东边的林布地区林布湾曾分成十个王国，以定都比贾伊布尔的莫朗最为强大，林布语还在9世纪有了自己的西里琼加文字。基拉特社会以口传经典《蒙德姆》为法度，崇拜自然与祖先，由萨满主持仪式，并在播种和收获季节庆祝萨克拉节。1774年，普里特维·纳拉扬·沙阿的廓尔喀军队经十七场战役征服林布湾，独立的基拉特诸王国就此终结；战后条约在传统的基帕特土地制度下保留了一定程度的地方自治。

en: The Kariri, also written Cariri or Kiriri, are a cluster of Indigenous peoples of the sertão, the dry backlands of northeastern Brazil, spread across the São Francisco River basin and the lands that became Ceará, Paraíba, Pernambuco and Bahia. Their name comes from the Tupi word kiri'ri, meaning silent or taciturn, and colonial writers classed them among the non-Tupi peoples generically called Tapuia. Related tongues such as Dzubukuá, Kipeá, Kamuru and Sapuyá formed the Kariri language family within the Macro-Jê trunk. The Dutch governor Elias Herckmann described the Carirys of the Paraíba interior as early as 1639. After the Dutch were expelled, the Kariri north of the São Francisco rose in the Confederation of the Cariris, known to the Portuguese as the Guerra dos Bárbaros of 1683 to 1713; the defeated survivors were gathered into missionary aldeias, and their name lives on in the Cariris Velhos and Cariris Novos highlands and the Vale do Cariri in Ceará. The French Capuchin Martin of Nantes had already labored among Kariri villages on the São Francisco between 1672 and 1683.
zh: 基里里人（又译卡里里）是巴西东北部干旱腹地塞尔陶的一群原住民，分布在圣弗朗西斯科河流域以及后来成为塞阿拉、帕拉伊巴、伯南布哥和巴伊亚的土地上。其名来自图皮语 kiri'ri，意为沉默或寡言；殖民地著述把他们归入非图皮族群，泛称为塔普亚人。祖布库阿语、基佩阿语、卡穆鲁语和萨普亚语等亲属语言组成大热语系下的卡里里语族。早在1639年，荷兰总督埃利亚斯·赫克曼就描述过帕拉伊巴内陆的卡里里人。荷兰人被逐出后，圣弗朗西斯科河以北的基里里人组成卡里里联盟起事，被葡萄牙人称为1683至1713年的野蛮人战争；战败的幸存者被集中到传教村落，他们的名字留在卡里里韦柳山地、卡里里诺武斯山地和塞阿拉的卡里里谷地等地名中。1672至1683年，法国嘉布遣会修士南特的马丁已在圣弗朗西斯科河畔的基里里村落传教。

en: The Kispoko were one of the five divisions, or septs, of the Shawnee, an Algonquian-speaking people of the Northeastern Woodlands, and were reckoned the smallest of the five in the eighteenth century. During the Beaver Wars they were driven from their Ohio homeland by the Iroquois Confederacy and were living among the Creek in the Upper South as early as 1650, before returning to Ohio around 1759. The division supplied the tribe's hereditary war chiefs; Chiksika, elder brother of Tecumseh, was a Kispoko war chief. In the late eighteenth century Kispoko families shared the Shawnee village of Peckuwe, near present-day Springfield, Ohio, with the Pekowi division until it was destroyed after the Battle of Piqua on 8 August 1780 during the American Revolutionary War. Most of the sept was removed west of the Mississippi in the early nineteenth century, and its descendants formed part of the Absentee-Shawnee in Indian Territory.
zh: 基斯波科人是东北林地阿尔冈昆语民族肖尼人的五大分支之一，在18世纪被认为是五支中人数最少的一支。海狸战争期间，他们被易洛魁联盟赶出俄亥俄故土，早在1650年便寄居南方腹地的克里克人之中，约1759年才返回俄亥俄。肖尼人的世袭军事首领出自这一分支，特库姆塞的长兄奇克西卡就是基斯波科的战将。18世纪末，基斯波科人与佩科维分支同住今俄亥俄州斯普林菲尔德附近的佩库韦村，直到1780年8月8日美国独立战争中的皮夸战役后村庄被毁。19世纪初，该分支大多数人被迁到密西西比河以西，其后裔成为印第安领地缺席肖尼人的一部分。

en: The Kissi are a West Atlantic people of the forested hills where Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia meet, grouped around towns such as Kissidougou and Kérouané. They speak Kissi, a Mel language of the Niger-Congo family. Their traditions recall an earlier home in the Upper Niger country south of the Futa Jallon; expelled by the Yalunka, they moved after 1600 into the forests, pushing the Limba before them while living under constant pressure from the Kuranko. Ironworking was ancient in this region and Kissi smiths were famed for their skill, their iron bars serving as trade goods when Portuguese voyagers recorded them in the early sixteenth century. They also make baskets and weave on vertical looms, and their traditional religion centers on ancestor worship and the soapstone figures called pomdo, buried images that the Kissi dig up and consult for guidance.
zh: 基西人是几内亚、塞拉利昂和利比里亚三国交界森林丘陵地带的大西洋语支族群，聚居于基西杜古、凯鲁阿内等城镇周围，讲尼日尔—刚果语系梅尔语支的基西语。他们的传统记忆把更早的家园指向富塔贾隆以南的尼日尔河上游地区；被雅隆卡人驱逐后，他们于1600年以后迁入森林，一路挤走林巴人，又始终承受着库兰科人的压力。冶铁在这一地区起源甚古，基西铁匠技艺高超，16世纪初葡萄牙航海者的记录里，他们的铁条已被当作贸易货物。基西人还擅长编篮和立式织机织布，传统宗教以祖先崇拜为核心，供奉被称为“庞多”的皂石造像；这些造像埋在土中，人们会把它们挖出，在疑难时请示指点。

en: The Kitikiti'sh, meaning raccoon-eyed people for the tattooed rings worn around their eyes, are the southern-plains villagers better known to outsiders as the Wichita. Speaking Wichita and Kichai, both Caddoan tongues, they lived in domed grass lodges in settled towns from the Arkansas to the Red River, farming maize, beans and squash, making fine pottery and riding out each winter on the bison hunt; French traders called them the Tattooed Pawnee. Their ancestors farmed the Washita and Canadian river valleys from about 900, and later built the Great Bend towns of Kansas, among them the city of Etzanoa. In 1541 Francisco Vasquez de Coronado found the wealthy farming land he called Quivira among them, counting about twenty-five villages, and in 1601 Juan de Onate described a single town of more than twelve hundred houses. Epidemics and pressure from the Apache and Osage thinned them in the seventeenth century, and after 1719 French visits to their villages near Tulsa and Neodesha, Apache attacks drove them south to the Red River by 1757. Allied with the Comanche and known to the Spanish as Nortenos, they destroyed the San Saba Mission and defeated a five-hundred-man Spanish army at the Battle of the Twin Villages. A smallpox epidemic in 1777 and 1778 killed about a third of their kin, and after the Louisiana Purchase of 1803 the surviving related bands were increasingly grouped together under the single name Wichita.
zh: 基蒂基蒂什人意为浣熊眼之人，得名于他们纹在眼睛周围的环状文身，外部世界更熟悉的称呼是威奇塔人。他们讲威奇塔语和基蔡语，两者都属卡多语系，在阿肯色河至雷德河之间的定居城镇里住着圆顶草屋，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，烧制精美陶器，每年冬天再出猎野牛；法国商人称他们为文身波尼人。其先民约900年起就在瓦希塔河和加拿大河谷务农，后来又在堪萨斯的阿肯色河大弯一带建起诸镇，埃察诺亚城便是其中之一。1541年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多在他们这里找到了他称作基维拉的富庶农乡，数出约二十五座村庄；1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特记述了一座拥有一千二百多所房屋的城镇。17世纪的瘟疫以及阿帕奇人和奥塞奇人的挤压使他们人口锐减；1719年法国人访问了他们在塔尔萨和尼奥德沙附近的村庄后，阿帕奇人的袭击又迫使他们在1757年前南撤到雷德河。他们与科曼奇人结盟，被西班牙人称作北方人，曾摧毁圣萨瓦传教站，并在双子村之战中击败一支五百人的西班牙军队。1777至1778年的天花瘟疫夺去约三分之一亲族的生命；1803年路易斯安那购地后，幸存的各亲缘部落越来越多地被笼统称为威奇塔人。

en: The Kitkehahki are one of the four bands of the Pawnee, a Caddoan-speaking people of the central Great Plains, and their name means Little Muddy Bottom Village or Little Earth Lodge Village. As the southernmost of the Pawnee South Bands they were often called the Republican Pawnee, after their earth-lodge villages on the Republican River in what is now southern Nebraska and northern Kansas. Their villagers farmed corn, beans and pumpkins in the river valley and left each season to hunt buffalo on the open plains. In the early eighteenth century the Pawnee together numbered more than twelve thousand, but pressure from the Lakota, Dakota and Cheyenne and repeated epidemics gradually weakened them. A Spanish and then an American expedition visited their main village in 1806, when Zebulon Pike persuaded the Kitkehahki to accept the American flag, and in 1818 they signed the Treaty of St. Louis as the Pawnee Republic.
zh: 基特凯哈基人是波尼人的四大分支之一，波尼人是中部大平原上说卡多语的原住民；基特凯哈基意为小泥底村或小土屋村。作为波尼南支中位置最靠南的一支，他们在共和河畔建起土屋村落，因此常被称为共和波尼人，活动范围在今天的内布拉斯加州南部和堪萨斯州北部。村民在河谷种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，每到特定季节还要前往开阔平原猎捕野牛。18世纪初波尼人总数超过一万二千，但拉科塔人、达科他人和夏延人的挤压加上接连的瘟疫，使他们逐渐衰弱。1806年，西班牙和美国的探险队先后到访他们的主营，泽布伦·派克说服基特凯哈基人接受美国国旗；1818年，他们以波尼共和国的名义签署了《圣路易斯条约》。

en: The K'itaish, whom French and Spanish scribes wrote down as Kichai, Kitsai or Keechi, were a Southern Plains people of Texas, Louisiana and Oklahoma who called themselves K'itaish. They spoke a Caddoan language kin to Pawnee, Arikara and Wichita and were closest in origin to the Pawnee. French explorers first met them on the Red River in Louisiana in 1701. Their allegiances shifted with the rivalries of the plains: early colonists called them enemies of the Caddo, and in 1712 they fought the Hainai on the Trinity River, yet they also intermarried with the Kadohadacho and took part in Caddoan confederate alliances. By 1772 their main villages stood east of the Trinity near the site of present-day Palestine, Texas. On 10 November 1837 they defeated a Texas Ranger force at the Battle of Stone Houses, though their own leader fell in the first attack.
zh: 基泰什人是南部平原的印第安部族，活动于得克萨斯、路易斯安那和俄克拉荷马一带，自称基泰什，法国和西班牙文献则记作基柴、基特赛或基奇等拼法。他们讲卡多语系的一种语言，与波尼语、阿里卡拉语和威奇塔语同系，族源上与波尼人最近。1701年，法国探险家在路易斯安那的雷德河上首次遇到他们。他们的立场随平原上的合纵连横而变化：早期殖民者把他们视为卡多人的仇敌，1712年他们还在特里尼蒂河畔与海奈人交战，但同时又与卡多哈达乔人通婚，并加入卡多联盟阵营。到1772年，他们的主要村落已位于特里尼蒂河以东，靠近今得克萨斯帕勒斯坦一带。1837年11月10日，他们在石屋之战中击败了得克萨斯游骑兵，尽管自己的首领在首轮攻击中阵亡。

en: The Kiwigapawa are the Kickapoo, an Algonquian-speaking people of the Great Lakes; Kickapoo itself is a French rendering of their word Kiwigapawa, meaning he who moves about, standing now here and now there, a name that fits their long history of migration. Closely related to the Sauk and Meskwaki, they were first met by French missionaries in southern Wisconsin in 1667, after the upheavals of the Beaver Wars had dispersed the peoples of the lower Great Lakes, and they encountered La Salle's expedition in the Illinois country in 1682. They later settled along the Wabash and in southern Illinois as members of the Wabash Confederacy with the Wea, Piankeshaw and Miami, and signed the Treaty of Greenville with the United States in 1795. Among the firmest allies of the Shawnee leader Tecumseh, they fought at Tippecanoe in 1811 and on the British side in the War of 1812. The 1819 Treaty of Edwardsville forced the cession of nearly half of Illinois, and under the prophet Kennekuk part of the nation held out before a land exchange of 1832 moved the main band from Missouri to Kansas, while other Kickapoo drifted south toward Texas.
zh: 基维加帕瓦人即基卡普人，五大湖地区的阿尔冈昆语民族；Kickapoo是法语对其本族语词Kiwigapawa的转写，意为“四处迁徙、时此时彼之人”，恰合他们不断迁移的历史。他们与索克人、梅斯夸基人关系密切；海狸战争打散了下五大湖的各族群之后，法国传教士于1667年在威斯康星南部首次见到他们，1682年又与拉萨尔的伊利诺伊探险队相遇。后来他们作为沃巴什联盟的成员，与韦阿人、皮安克肖人、迈阿密人一同定居沃巴什河沿岸和伊利诺伊南部，并于1795年与美国签订《格林维尔条约》。他们是肖尼人首领特库姆塞最坚定的盟友之一，参加了1811年的蒂珀卡努战役，并在1812年战争中站在英国一边。1819年的《爱德华兹维尔条约》迫使他们割让近半个伊利诺伊；在先知基内库克带领下，一部分人坚持留守，1832年的土地交换把主体部族从密苏里迁往堪萨斯，另一些基卡普人则向南进入得克萨斯方向。

en: The Koasati, or Coushatta, are a Muskogean people whose earliest known towns stood in the Tennessee River valley of present-day Tennessee, where Hernando de Soto's expedition met them in 1540; the Spanish knew them as the Coste. Farmers of maize, beans and squash and noted basket-makers, they drifted southwest in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, founding towns at Nickajack and Long Island on the Tennessee before settling at Coosada and joining the Muscogee Creek Confederacy as Upper Creeks, closely intermarried with the Alabama. After the French defeat in the Seven Years' War in 1763, colonial pressure pushed them further west across Mississippi into Spanish Louisiana and Texas: a Coushatta band reached the Big Thicket of eastern Texas in 1795, while kin who remained in Alabama were swept into the removals to Indian Territory in the 1830s. Their language forms, together with Alabama and the extinct Apalachee, the Apalachee-Alabama-Koasati branch of the Muskogean family.
zh: 科阿萨蒂人（又称考沙塔）是马斯科吉语族族群，已知最早的城镇在今田纳西州的田纳西河谷，1540年德·索托的探险队曾在那里与他们相遇，西班牙人称之为科斯特人。他们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，以编织篮筐闻名；17至18世纪开始向西南迁移，先后在田纳西河上的尼克杰克和长岛建镇，最后在科萨达定居，并作为上克里克一支加入马斯科吉克里克联盟，与阿拉巴莫人互通婚姻。1763年七年战争法国战败后，殖民压力把他们进一步向西推过密西西比，进入西属路易斯安那和得克萨斯：一支科阿萨蒂人于1795年抵达东得克萨斯的大灌丛，留在阿拉巴马的亲族则在19世纪30年代被强制迁往印第安领地。他们的语言与阿拉巴莫语及已消亡的阿巴拉契语同属马斯科吉语系的阿巴拉契-阿拉巴莫-科阿萨蒂语支。

en: The Koch are a Tibeto-Burman people of the lower Brahmaputra and North Bengal, organised into nine matrilineal, exogamous clans and speaking a Boro-Garo language, though many groups later adopted Indo-Aryan speech while keeping animist customs. Muslim chronicles already place the Koch, together with the Mech and the Tharu, in western Kamrup in the early thirteenth century. In the disorder after the Bengal sultan Alauddin Husain Shah seized Kamata in 1498, the Koch leader Hajo united the tribes, and his grandson Bisu overthrew the Baro-Bhuyan chieftains, took the Hindu name Biswa Singha and founded the Koch kingdom at Kamatapur in 1515. Under Nara Narayan and his brother Chilarai in the mid-sixteenth century it became the strongest power northeast of Bengal and patronised the Vaishnava revival of Sankardev. The kingdom then split permanently into Koch Bihar and Koch Hajo: Mughal armies conquered Koch Hajo in 1612, its eastern fragments became Ahom vassals, the Khaspur branch merged into the Kachari kingdom in 1745, and Koch Bihar itself survived as a Mughal-aligned state.
zh: 库奇人是布拉马普特拉河下游与北孟加拉的藏缅语族群，分为九个行母系制、实行族外婚的氏族，讲博多—加罗语支的库奇语；后来许多支系改说印度雅利安语，但保留了万物有灵的习俗。13世纪初的穆斯林史籍已把库奇人与梅奇人、塔鲁人并列为迦摩缕波西部的居民。1498年孟加拉苏丹阿拉乌丁·侯赛因·沙攻占迦摩陀之后局势大乱，库奇首领哈乔统一诸部，其孙比苏推翻巴罗—布扬诸首领，取印度教名比斯瓦·辛哈，于1515年在迦摩陀布尔建立库奇王国。16世纪中叶，在纳拉·纳拉扬与其弟奇拉莱治下，该国成为孟加拉东北最强的政权，并赞助了商羯罗提婆的毗湿奴虔信改革。王国随后永久分裂为库奇比哈尔与库奇哈乔两支：1612年莫卧儿军队征服库奇哈乔，其东部分支沦为阿洪附庸，卡斯普尔一支于1745年并入卡查里王国，而库奇比哈尔本身则作为亲莫卧儿的政权延续下来。

en: The Kochini, or Malabar Jews, are the oldest Jewish community of India, established on the Kerala coast where their own tradition places the first settlers in the generation after the Roman destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE, at the spice port of Cranganore, known to them as Shingly. Hebrew signatures on the Kollam copper plates of 849 attest to West Asian Jewish traders in the region, and a later set of royal copper plates made the Jewish leader Joseph Rabban a prince over his community, with a small principality at Anjuvannam and the right to build synagogues and own land. The traveller Benjamin of Tudela heard of thousands of Israelites on this coast in the twelfth century, and the oldest surviving Hebrew gravestone dates to 1269. In 1341 a great flood silted up Cranganore harbour, and the Jews shifted with the pepper trade to Cochin, building their first synagogue there within four years. The Portuguese who arrived in 1500 discriminated against them, and after 1492 a small stream of Sephardic exiles, later called Paradesi Jews, joined them and built their own synagogue while learning the local Judeo-Malayalam. When the Dutch took Cochin in 1663 the community gained a more tolerant ruler. In religion the Kochini followed the Sephardic rite and looked above all to the code of Maimonides, composing devotional songs in Judeo-Malayalam.
zh: 柯枝犹太人又称马拉巴尔犹太人，是印度最古老的犹太社群，定居在喀拉拉海岸；按他们自己的传说，最早的定居者是70年罗马人摧毁第二圣殿之后那一代人，落脚于香料港克兰加努尔，他们称之为辛利。849年奎隆铜盘上的希伯来文签名，证明当时已有西亚犹太商人在此活动；后来的一组王室铜盘又册封犹太领袖约瑟夫·拉班为社群之长，赐予他安朱瓦南的一小块封邑以及建造会堂、拥有土地的权利。12世纪旅人图德拉的本雅明就听说这条海岸上住着数千以色列人，现存最早的希伯来文墓碑则立于1269年。1341年一场大洪水淤塞了克兰加努尔港，犹太人随胡椒贸易迁往柯枝，四年内便在新社群建起第一座会堂。1500年到来的葡萄牙人对他们多有歧视；1492年以后又有一小股塞法迪流亡者陆续来投，后称帕拉迪西犹太人，他们建起自己的会堂，同时学用当地的犹太-马拉雅拉姆语。1663年荷兰人攻占柯枝后，社群迎来了较为宽容的统治者。信仰上，柯枝犹太人奉行塞法迪仪轨，最推崇迈蒙尼德的法典，并用犹太-马拉雅拉姆语创作礼仪诗歌。

en: The Kodava, or Coorgs, are an endogamous Dravidian hill people of Kodagu, the forested Coorg highlands of the Western Ghats in southern Karnataka, where they have lived as land-owning rice farmers and cattle herders for well over a thousand years. Their society is patrilineal and martial, honouring ancestors, nature and weapons, and a Kannada lexicon of 1398 already described them as warriors fond of hunting. Early medieval Coorg passed between the Kadambas, Gangas, Cholas and Hoysalas and then the Vijayanagara Empire. Around 1600 the Haleri Rajas made the district their own, ruling from Haleri and Madikeri; in the later eighteenth century Raja Dodda Vira Rajendra and his general Biddanda Bopu fought the invading armies of Tipu Sultan. In 1834 the East India Company defeated the last Haleri raja, Chikka Vira Raja, and annexed Coorg, and a revolt against the new order broke out at Sulya in 1837.
zh: 科达瓦人又称库尔格人，是南卡纳塔克西高止山森林高地——库尔格（科达古）地区实行内婚制的达罗毗荼语山民，千余年来以拥有土地的稻农和牧人身份在此定居。其社会按父系传承，崇尚武艺，敬奉祖先、自然和兵器；1398年的一部卡纳达语辞书已把他们描写为酷爱狩猎的武士。中世纪早期，库尔格先后在卡丹巴、恒伽、朱罗、曷萨拉诸王朝和毗奢耶那伽罗帝国治下。约1600年起，哈莱里诸王以哈莱里和马迪凯里为中心统治此地；18世纪后期，多达·维拉·拉金德拉王与其将领比丹达·博普曾抗击提普苏丹的入侵。1834年，东印度公司击败末代哈莱里王奇卡·维拉·拉贾，吞并库尔格；1837年，苏利亚又爆发反抗新秩序的起义。

en: The Kofan, who call themselves the A'i, are an ancient people of the Amazonian foothills between the Aguarico and Guamués rivers, in what is now northeast Ecuador and southern Colombia. They speak A'ingae, a language isolate, and lived by farming, hunting and river travel in dugout canoes. When the Spanish reached their country in the mid-sixteenth century, the Kofan may have numbered some fifteen thousand; they resisted fiercely, and late in that century they destroyed the Spanish town of Mocoa and forced the intruders to withdraw. The Jesuit Rafael Ferrer began missionary work among them in 1602, but soldiers and settlers following in his wake drove him out. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries sporadic expeditions sought gold, trade and converts, while European diseases steadily cut the population, leaving the Kofan a diminished but unconquered people in their forest homelands.
zh: 科凡人自称阿依人，是阿瓜里科河与瓜穆埃斯河之间亚马孙山麓地带的古老族群，分布在今厄瓜多尔东北部和哥伦比亚南部。他们使用孤立语言科凡语，以农耕、狩猎和乘独木舟在河上往来为生。16世纪中叶西班牙人抵达时，科凡人约有一万五千之众；他们激烈抵抗，在该世纪末摧毁西班牙人的莫科阿镇，迫使入侵者撤退。1602年，耶稣会士拉斐尔·费雷尔开始在他们中间传教，但尾随而来的军人和殖民者又把他赶走。17至18世纪，零星的远征队不断前来寻求黄金、贸易和皈依者，欧洲传来的疾病则持续削减其人口，使科凡人人数大减，但始终未被征服，仍守在自己的森林家园里。

en: Kohistani is the collective name for the Dardic Indo-Aryan mountain peoples of Kohistan, the land of steep forests and pastures split between the Indus, Swat and Dir valleys, around Jijal, Kalam and the upper Panjkora. They speak a cluster of related tongues, Indus Kohistani on the west bank of the Indus, Torwali in the middle Swat valley and Gawri around Kalam, and stand close to their Shina and Kashmiri neighbours. Once they ranged far more widely, for the Gibari-speaking Sultans of Swat ruled Swat, Dir, Buner and Malakand until the sixteenth century; between 1510 and 1515 the Yousafzai Pashtuns of Malak Ahmad Khan overran that sultanate and drove most Kohistanis back into the high valleys, where Pashtun settlement and conversion slowly Pashtunized groups such as the Swatis and Tirahis, who lost their old speech for Pashto. The remaining valleys kept their small languages and their old valley politics, governed by local clans rather than outside kings, and entered the British period as isolated tribal hills between the Swat, Dir and Chitral states.
zh: 科希斯坦是科希斯坦地区达尔德系印度-雅利安山地民族的统称，这片森林茂密、牧场纵横的山地分属印度河、斯瓦特和迪尔河谷，吉贾尔、卡拉姆和潘杰科拉上游都在其间。他们讲一族亲缘语言：印度河西岸的印度河科希斯坦语、斯瓦特中游的托尔瓦利语和卡拉姆一带的加夫里语，与邻近的希纳人和克什米尔人关系很近。他们的分布曾远比现在广阔：讲吉巴里语的斯瓦特苏丹国直到16世纪还统治着斯瓦特、迪尔、布内尔和马拉坎德；1510至1515年间，马拉克·艾哈迈德汗率领的优素福扎伊普什图人攻灭该苏丹国，把大部分科希斯坦人逼回高山河谷，此后普什图人的定居和传教逐渐使斯瓦提人、提拉希人等群体普什图化，放弃原有语言改用普什图语。留存下来的河谷则保住了各自的小语言和古老的河谷自治，由本地氏族而非外来君王治理，进入英属时期时仍是夹在斯瓦特、迪尔和吉德拉尔诸邦之间的闭塞部落山区。

en: The Koiali are the Mountain Koiari people of the rugged inland ranges of southeastern New Guinea, around the Efogi, Barai and Koiari villages inland from Port Moresby. Their language belongs to the Koiarian family of the Trans–New Guinea phylum and is only distantly related to the Grass Koiari speech of the coastal plains below them.
zh: 科亚利人即山地科亚里人，住在新几内亚东南部内陆崎岖山区，即莫尔兹比港后方的埃福吉、巴赖和科亚里等村落一带。他们的语言属跨新几内亚语系的科亚里安语族，与下方沿海平原的草原科亚里语只有远亲关系。

en: The Kokomini, who called themselves Gugumini, meaning good or intelligible speech, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland, perhaps a loose confederation of tribal groups rather than a single tribe. Neighbouring peoples knew them by the exonym Kookawarra, meaning poor speakers, and their territory bordered the Palmerville country on the upper Palmer River.
zh: 科科米宁人自称古古米尼，意为“清晰好懂的话”；他们是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，可能并非单一部落，而是若干部落群体的松散联盟。邻族用以意为“说话差劲者”的他称库卡瓦拉称呼他们，其领地邻近帕尔默河上游的帕默维尔一带。

en: The Kokowara, also called Kuku-Warra or Gugu-Warra, were an Aboriginal people of northern Queensland. The name given them by neighbouring tribes meant rough speech. They held about 1,800 square miles of country on the Normanby River, from Lakefield south to the Laura River, camping chiefly at Daidan on the Deighton River.
zh: 科科瓦拉人又记为库库-瓦拉或古古-瓦拉，是昆士兰北部的澳大利亚原住民。邻族给他们的名字意为“粗话”。他们在诺曼比河一带保有约1800平方英里的土地，南起莱克菲尔德直至劳拉河，主要营地在戴顿河畔的代丹。

en: The Kol people live in Pomio District on the southern side of eastern New Britain. Their language appears to be an isolate, perhaps distantly related to the poorly known Sulka language within the proposed East Papuan grouping.
zh: 科尔人居住在新不列颠岛东部南坡的波米奥区。他们的科尔语看来是一门语言孤岛，或许与记录甚少的苏尔卡语有远亲关系，同属拟议中的东巴布亚语群。

en: The Qulla or Kolla are the southernmost of the Aymara-speaking peoples of the Altiplano, whose Colla kingdom arose on the Collao plateau around Lake Titicaca after the decline of Tiwanaku, at least by the late twelfth century, and whose dead were buried in the stone chullpa towers of cemeteries such as Sillustani. Together with the other Aymara lordships they were conquered by the Inca Pachacuti around 1450; the Inca knew the Aymaras as colla and named the whole southern quarter of Tawantinsuyu Qullasuyu, while Qulla families were resettled as soldier-colonists far into the southern Andes, including the high puna around Antofalla. In 1540 the Qulla made first contact with the Spaniards and resisted for years before their lands were taken, and in 1780 the female leader Ñusta Willaq led Qulla warriors in the great Andean revolt. Their descendants in northwestern Argentina and western Bolivia speak a southern Quechua dialect, though the Qulla of the Titicaca region probably once spoke Puquina, the language associated with Tiwanaku.
zh: 科利亚人（又称科亚）是高原艾马拉诸族中分布最南的一支；蒂亚瓦纳科衰落后，他们的科利亚王国至少在12世纪末已兴起于的的喀喀湖周围的科利亚奥高原，死者葬在西卢斯塔尼等地的石造楚尔帕塔墓中。约1450年，他们与其他艾马拉王国一起被印卡的帕查库特克征服；印卡人把艾马拉人泛称为科利亚，并将塔万廷苏尤整个南部大区命名为科利亚苏尤，同时把科利亚家族作为军人殖民者远迁到安第斯南部，包括安托法亚一带的高寒荒原。1540年科利亚人首次接触西班牙人，抵抗多年后土地仍被夺去；1780年，女性首领努斯塔·维利亚克率科利亚战士参加安第斯大起义。他们在阿根廷西北部和玻利维亚西部的后裔使用南部克丘亚方言，而的的喀喀地区的科利亚人古时很可能使用与蒂亚瓦纳克文化相关的普基纳语。

en: The Kolyma Yukaghirs are the Yukaghir clans of the Kolyma River basin, part of the ancient aboriginal population of northeast Siberia and heirs of the Neolithic Ymyyakhtakh culture. They lived by fishing, hunting wild reindeer and elk, and breeding reindeer for transport, and spoke the Kolyma, or Odul, variant of the Yukaghir languages, whose wider kinship remains uncertain. At Russian contact their largest tribe was the Omoki of the lower Kolyma and Omolon, six hundred and twenty people in eleven clans in 1659; the word omok itself means clan or tribe. Tribute demands, intertribal wars and epidemics reduced them to fifty-four people by 1693. The upper-Kolyma Kogime, the clan of the Great Raven, fared better, and present-day Upper Kolyma Yukaghirs trace their descent chiefly from them. Over the colonial centuries many Kolyma Yukaghirs merged into Yakut, Even and Russian communities, while clan shamanism and the old nomadic hunting life lingered on.
zh: 科雷马尤卡吉尔人是科雷马河流域的尤卡吉尔各氏族，属于西伯利亚东北部最古老的原住民群体，是新石器时代伊米亚赫塔赫文化的后继者。他们以捕鱼、猎取野鹿和驼鹿、饲养驯鹿驮运为生，使用尤卡吉尔语的科雷马（奥杜尔）变体，这一语言与其他语系的亲缘关系始终没有定论。俄国人到来时，他们中间最大的部落是住在科雷马河和奥莫隆河下游的奥莫基人：1659年有620人，分十一个氏族，“奥莫克”一词本身就是氏族、部落的意思。贡赋、部族战争和疫病使他们到1693年只剩54人。上游科雷马的科吉梅人即“大乌鸦之族”处境稍好，后来的上科雷马尤卡吉尔人主要出自这一支。整个殖民时代里，许多科雷马尤卡吉尔人融入了雅库特人、埃文人和俄国人的社区，而氏族萨满信仰和古老的游猎生活仍延续了很久。

en: The Kombai are a Papuan people of the rainforest interior of South Papua in Indonesia, spread across the river country of Mappi and Boven Digoel regencies. Their name comes from khoba, meaning people, and their Kombai language, called khobaye-lu or human speech by its speakers, forms the Kombai-Wanggom branch of the Greater Awyu family within Trans-New Guinea. They live in patrilineal clans, each holding a forest territory called mburu with gardens of sweet potatoes, bananas and tobacco, sago groves in the swamps and grounds for hunting pig and other game with the aid of dogs; fish are taken by damming streams and stunning them with root poison. Their most distinctive custom is building treehouses: the sacred ramo dumo of the clan elder stands at the centre of the territory, guarded by bowmen against raiders, while tall walina serve as men's lookouts and low ibena houses are used by women in childbirth and for sago-grub feasts that bind ties with neighbouring clans. Like other interior Papuans, they descend from populations established on the island long before Austronesian seafarers reached its coasts around 1500 BCE.
zh: 孔拜人是印度尼西亚南巴布亚雨林内陆的巴布亚族群，分布在马皮与博文迪古尔两个摄政区的河网地带。其族名来自意为“人”的 khoba 一词，他们的孔拜语本族语称 khobaye-lu，即“人的语言”，属跨新几内亚语系大阿维尤语系的孔拜-旺贡分支。孔拜人按父系氏族聚居，每个氏族拥有名为姆布鲁的森林领地，园圃种植红薯、香蕉和烟草，沼泽经营西谷椰林，并带着猎狗猎猪和其他林兽；捕鱼时在溪流筑坝，投入有毒根茎将鱼毒晕。他们最鲜明的习俗是建造树屋：氏族长老的圣树屋拉莫杜莫 位于领地中心，由弓箭手守卫以防袭击；高耸的瓦利纳 是男子的瞭望台，低矮的伊贝纳 供妇女分娩并举办西谷虫宴，以此维系与邻近氏族的关系。和其他内陆巴布亚人一样，他们是远早于约公元前1500年南岛语航海者抵达该岛沿海之前就定居于此的古老族群之后裔。

en: The Komi are a Permian people of the Uralic family, indigenous to the forested basins of the Vychegda, Pechora and Kama rivers in north-eastern Europe. Their endonym means man, while Russian sources called the southern Komi Permyaks, after Great Perm, the land beyond, and the northern ones Zyryans; medieval Norse knew their country as Bjarmaland. They and the Udmurts descend from a single Proto-Permian people that split in the first millennium BC, and by the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Komi had themselves divided into the Permyaks of the Kama and the Zyryans, who spread north along the Vychegda, Sysola, Vym and Pechora. From the twelfth century Novgorodian fur traders entered their lands, and the Komi dukes of Great Perm ruled from the stronghold of Cherdyn. In 1365 Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow charged Stephen of Perm with their conversion; Stephen created the Old Permic, or Anbur, alphabet and became the Komi patron saint after the Perm eparchy was founded in 1383, though the shaman Pama resisted and the Permyaks were not fully baptised until their duke Mikhail accepted Christianity in 1470. Moscow nevertheless seized Cherdyn in 1472 and abolished the duchy in 1505, opening a long age of Russian colonisation. The Komi kept their hunting, fishing and gathering ways and the old mythology of rival gods En and Omöl; the eighteenth century brought Russian penal towns such as Ust-Sysolsk, and the first printed Komi book appeared in 1815.
zh: 科米人是乌拉尔语系彼尔姆语支的民族，自古以来居住在东欧东北部维切格达河、伯朝拉河与卡马河流域的森林地带。他们的自称意为“人”；俄罗斯文献把南部科米人称作彼尔姆人，得名于边远之地“大彼尔姆”，北部的则称兹梁人，北欧诺斯文献称其国为比亚马兰。语言学家推断，他们与乌德穆尔特人同源于公元前一千纪分裂的古彼尔姆人群；到16至17世纪，科米人自身又分为留守卡马河的科米-彼尔姆人和沿维切格达河、瑟索拉河、维姆河、伯朝拉河北上的科米-兹梁人。12世纪起，诺夫哥罗德毛皮商人进入此地，大彼尔姆的科米公爵以切尔登要塞为中心实行统治。1365年，莫斯科王公德米特里·顿斯科伊命彼尔姆的斯蒂芬前往传教；斯蒂芬创制了古彼尔姆字母，又称安布尔字母，1383年彼尔姆主教区设立后他被尊为科米人的主保圣人，但萨满帕马起而抵抗，彼尔姆人直到1470年公爵米哈伊尔受洗才整体归信基督教。莫斯科仍于1472年攻占切尔登，1505年废除公国，科米人由此进入漫长的被殖民时代。他们长期保持狩猎、捕鱼和采集的生计，以及善神恩与恶神奥默尔相争的古老神话；18世纪，乌斯季瑟索利斯克等俄罗斯流放城镇在他们的土地上兴起，第一本科米语印刷书则于1815年问世。

en: The Komo, also called Kumu and plural Bakomo, are a Bantu people of the northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, living in the forest country around Kisangani and stretching toward the Kivu highlands, where they share the land with related Bira and Lombi groups. Their own tradition records that they moved southwest out of the kingdom of Bunyoro, in present-day Uganda, in the early 1800s. They speak Komo, also called Kikomo, a Bantu language of the Komo-Bira group, alongside the Swahili dialect Kingwana. Their traditional religion centers on a creator named Muungu and a demiurge called Nkya, with astral legends explaining the world; before farming or hunting begins, the Komo hold rituals with sacrifices to the spirits, and belief in magic remains part of daily life.
zh: 科莫人又称库穆人（复数称巴科莫），是刚果民主共和国东北部的班图族群，住在基桑加尼周围并伸向基伍高地的森林地带，与有亲缘关系的比拉人、隆比人错居。他们自己的传说记载，19世纪初从今乌干达境内的巴尼奥罗王国向西南迁徙而来。科莫人使用科莫语，又名基科莫语，属班图语的科莫—比拉语支，也通行斯瓦希里方言金瓦纳语。他们的传统宗教以创世神穆翁古和造物主恩基亚为中心，并有星宿神话解释世界；每逢农耕或狩猎开始，都要举行仪式、向神灵献祭，对巫术的信仰也深植于日常生活。

en: The Konbudj, recorded as Ngunbudj or Gonbudj, were an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory whose language was a little-known variety of the Umbugarla–Ngumbur group within the Darwin Region languages, spoken in the western Arnhem Land country. The tongue was virtually undocumented and had died out before the Second World War.
zh: 孔布吉人在文献中记作恩贡布吉或贡布吉，是北领地的原住民，其语言属达尔文地区语群中的翁布加拉-恩贡布尔语支，通行于阿纳姆地西部一带。这种语言几乎没有留下记录，在第二次世界大战前便已消亡。

en: The Kondogir are an Evenki clan of the Lower Tunguska, or Katanga, taiga whose name survived as the Kondogirsky village council of Katangsky district. As reindeer-herding hunters they were made to pay the fur tax, or yasak, which Cossacks secured by taking hostages from leading clans in the seventeenth century.
zh: 孔多吉尔人是下通古斯卡河（卡坦加河）泰加林的鄂温克氏族，其名称在俄国行政建制中保留为卡坦加区的孔多吉尔村苏维埃。作为养鹿狩猎者，17世纪哥萨克以扣留氏族首领人质的方式迫使他们缴纳毛皮税，即雅萨克。

en: The Kongo, or Bakongo, are the Bantu people who speak the Kikongo cluster of closely related dialects and live along the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, in the west of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Angola, the Republic of the Congo and southern Gabon; their many subgroups include the Sundi, Yombe, Vili, Bwende and Solongo. Around 1390 their dynasties founded the Kingdom of Kongo, ruled from Mbanza Kongo by the Manikongo, which at its height stretched from the Atlantic to the Kwango River. The Portuguese explorer Diogo Cão reached the coast in 1483, and in 1491 King Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptized as João I; under Afonso I, who won the throne in 1509, Catholicism became the religion of the ruling elite. From the sixteenth century the slave trade to Brazil and the Caribbean reshaped Kongo society, and the Manikongo's power collapsed after the defeat and death of King António I at the Battle of Mbwila against Portuguese Angola in 1665. Rival royal houses then fought long civil wars, yet Kongo communities kept their language, clan structure and trading networks along the river routes into the nineteenth century.
zh: 刚果人又称巴刚果人，是讲彼此相近的刚果语各方言的班图人，居住在中非大西洋沿岸，即今刚果民主共和国西部、安哥拉北部、刚果共和国和加蓬南部一带，下分松迪、永贝、维利、布文德、索隆戈等许多支系。约1390年，他们的王朝建立了刚果王国，由马尼刚果以姆班扎刚果为都进行统治，鼎盛时疆域西起大西洋、东抵宽果河。1483年葡萄牙航海家迪奥戈·康抵达海岸，1491年国王恩津加·恩库武受洗取名若昂一世；1509年即位的阿方索一世治下，天主教成为统治精英的信仰。从16世纪起，输往巴西和加勒比的奴隶贸易重塑了刚果社会；1665年，国王安东尼奥一世在姆布维拉战役中被葡属安哥拉军队击败身亡，马尼刚果的权威随之崩溃。此后对立的王室家族长期内战，但刚果人社群仍保留着自己的语言、氏族制度和沿河商路网络，一直延续到19世纪。

en: The Konkani are the Indo-Aryan people of the Konkan, the narrow coastal plain between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, centred on Goa and reaching from the ports north of Bombay to Karwar in the south. They speak Konkani, a southern Indo-Aryan language of the Marathi-Konkani group, attested in stone inscriptions from the second century and first named in the verse of the thirteenth-century saint-poet Namadeva. In 1337 the coast was held by the Muslim sultanates of the Deccan, first the Bahmanis and later Bijapur, whose governors ruled Goa. In 1510 Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa for Portugal and made it the capital of the Portuguese Estado da Índia; Jesuits such as Thomas Stevens studied and printed the language in works like the Arte da lingoa Canarim, while missionary preaching and Portuguese rule drew a large share of the people into Catholicism. Other Konkani speakers migrated along the coast to Surat, Mangalore and Cochin, carrying their dialects beyond Goa.
zh: 康坎人是康坎海岸的印度—雅利安人，那是西高止山脉与阿拉伯海之间的狭长沿海平原，以果阿为中心，北起孟买以北诸港，南到卡尔瓦尔。他们讲康坎语，属印度—雅利安语南支的马拉地—康坎语组，2世纪的石刻铭文已见其形，其名称最早见于13世纪圣诗诗人纳姆德夫的诗篇。1337年，海岸由德干的穆斯林苏丹国统治，先后是巴赫曼尼苏丹国和比贾布尔苏丹国，果阿的长官即由它们委任。1510年，阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克为葡萄牙夺取果阿，将其建为葡属印度的首府；托马斯·史蒂文斯等耶稣会士学习并刊印这种语言，写成《卡纳林语工艺》等著作，传教活动与葡萄牙统治也使相当多的人皈依天主教。另一些康坎语居民沿海岸迁往苏拉特、门格洛尔和柯钦，把各方言带到果阿之外。

en: The Kono are a Mande-speaking people whose homeland is the wooded hill country of eastern Sierra Leone, with part of the tribe living across the border in Guinea. Their traditions describe them as descendants of migrants from the Mali-Guinea region who moved west as peaceful hunters and settled the land that became Kono District in the mid-1500s, and they claim to have once been a powerful people in Mali and Guinea. In later years raids by the related Mende drove them north into Koranko territory, where they were granted land to farm; when the Mende shifted further south the Kono returned to their eastern homeland, living as farmers and hunters under village chiefs.
zh: 孔诺人是说曼德语族语言的民族，家园在塞拉利昂东部林木覆盖的丘陵地带，另有部分支系居住在边界另一侧的几内亚。按其口述传统，他们是马里—几内亚地区移民的后裔，以和平猎人的身份西迁，在16世纪中叶定居于后来的孔诺地区，并称自己曾是马里和几内亚一带的强族。后来同属曼德群体的曼德人来袭，孔诺人北逃到科兰科人的地界，获准在那里耕种；曼德人继续南移后，孔诺人才重返东部家园，在村镇酋长治下务农狩猎为生。

en: The Koreans are the people of the Korean Peninsula, speaking the Korean language and tracing their ancestry to Bronze Age migrants from Manchuria who merged with the peninsula's older agricultural populations. In 1337 their land was ruled by the Goryeo dynasty of Kaesong, founded in 918, a Buddhist kingdom long overshadowed by Mongol Yuan power. In 1392 the general Yi Seong-gye overthrew Goryeo and founded the Joseon dynasty, moving the capital to Hanyang, later Seoul, and installing Neo-Confucianism as the state ideology; scholarship and office holding were dominated by the yangban elite writing in Hanja. King Sejong, ruling from 1418 to 1450, ordered the creation of the Hangul alphabet, proclaimed in 1446, and pushed the northern border to the Amnok and Tuman rivers against the Jurchens. Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasions of 1592 and 1598 devastated the peninsula until Admiral Yi Sun-sin's turtle ships and Ming intervention turned the tide. Manchu armies then invaded in 1627, forcing a pact of brotherhood, and again in 1636–1637, forcing Joseon to submit as a tributary of the Qing. The eighteenth century brought a scholarly revival under Kings Yeongjo and Jeongjo, but after 1800 power slipped to the Andong Kim in-law clan, whose corruption and persecution of Catholics accompanied mounting peasant unrest.
zh: 朝鲜人是朝鲜半岛的主体民族，讲朝鲜语，其祖先是青铜时代从满洲南下的移民，与半岛上更古老的农耕人群融合而成。1337年统治半岛的是918年建立、以开城为都的高丽王朝；这个佛教王国长期处在蒙元势力的阴影之下。1392年，将领李成桂推翻高丽，建立朝鲜王朝，把都城迁往汉阳（即后来的汉城），并将程朱理学定为国家意识形态；学问和官职由使用汉文的两班贵族垄断。1418—1450年在位的世宗大王主持创制了谚文，于1446年颁布，又对女真用兵，把北界推进到鸭绿江和图们江。1592年和1598年，丰臣秀吉两度入侵，半岛惨遭蹂躏，李舜臣的龟船和明朝援军最终扭转战局。此后满洲军队于1627年入侵，迫使朝鲜订立兄弟之盟，1636—1637年再度来攻，迫使朝鲜向清朝称臣纳贡。18世纪，英祖和正祖统治时期出现学术复兴，实学兴起；但1800年以后，安东金氏的势道政治把持朝政，腐败横行，并大肆迫害天主教徒，民变频发。

en: The Korku are the westernmost Munda-speaking people, isolated in the Satpura hills on either side of the Tapti River in southern Madhya Pradesh and northern Maharashtra, where their Austroasiatic speech is surrounded by the Dravidian Gondi language while its closest relatives lie far to the east; the Nihali, whose language is an isolate, traditionally lived in separate quarters of Korku villages. Their name combines koro, person, and ku, alive, and their forebears were hunter-gatherers of the Satpura forests before turning to settled cultivation of millet, pulses and wheat. They are organised into four subsects, the Mawasi being the largest and formerly given to raiding, and into exogamous clans with tree, animal and river totems, while village affairs rest with a panchayat under a Patel headman and Padihar priest. In the Mughal age their hills formed the remote forest fringe of the Handia sarkar under Gond chieftains. After the Marathas took the country in 1742, Korku bands joined the Pindaris in raiding towns such as Harda, which they attacked in the years after 1801, until British forces entered the region during the Third Anglo-Maratha War of 1817.
zh: 科尔库人是分布最西的蒙达语族群，孤居于中央邦南部和马哈拉施特拉邦北部、达布蒂河两岸的萨特普拉山区，其南亚语语言四周被达罗毗荼语系的贡迪语包围，最近的亲属语言却远在印度东部；使用孤立语言尼哈利语的尼哈利人，传统上就住在科尔库村落的独立街坊里。“科尔库”由“科罗”（人）和“库”（活的）两词合成。其先民本是萨特普拉森林中的狩猎采集者，后来转为定居农耕，种植小米、豆类和小麦。他们分为四个支系，以马瓦西一支人数最多，过去以劫掠为生；氏族实行外婚制，以树木、动物、河流等为图腾，村务则由帕特尔首领和帕迪哈尔祭司主持的潘查亚特会议裁断。莫卧儿时期，这片山地是贡德酋长治下汉迪亚行政区的边远林缘。1742年马拉塔人夺取该地后，科尔库武装与平达里流寇联手袭击哈尔达等城镇，1801年后仍不断寇掠，直到1817年第三次英国-马拉塔战争期间英军进入这一地区。

en: The Koroa, called Akoroa by Jacques Marquette and Courouais by later French writers, were a Mississippi Valley people of the Yazoo River basin in present-day northwest Mississippi, with villages on both banks of the great river; their speech is believed to have been a dialect of Tunica, a language isolate. They may be the Coligua polity encountered by Hernando de Soto's expedition near modern Little Rock in 1541. La Salle twice visited a Koroa town on the west bank in 1682 and found their Quinipissa allies living there. A French mission under Antoine Davion reached them in 1698, and in 1702 the priest Nicolas Foucault was killed while working among them, although the Koroa leaders themselves executed his killers. European epidemics thinned the tribe, and in 1729 the survivors joined the Yazoo and Natchez in the great revolt against the French; afterwards the Koroa ceased to exist as a separate tribe, their people being absorbed by the Tunica, Chickasaw and Natchez.
zh: 科罗阿人是密西西比河谷亚祖河流域的原住民，住在今天密西西比州西北部，在大河两岸都有村落；雅克·马凯特称他们为阿科罗阿，后来的法国文献则写作库鲁韦，他们的语言被认为是孤立语言图尼卡语的一种方言。他们可能就是1541年埃尔南多·德索托远征队在今小石城附近遇到的科利瓜政权。1682年，拉萨尔两次到访西岸的一座科罗阿集镇，发现他们的盟友基尼皮萨人也住在镇里。1698年，安托万·达维翁率领的法国传教团来到他们中间；1702年，神父尼古拉斯·富科在科罗阿人那里遇害，不过科罗阿的首领们亲自处死了凶手。欧洲传来的瘟疫使该部落人口锐减，1729年幸存者又与亚祖人、纳奇兹人联合发动反法大起义；此后科罗阿人不再作为独立部落存在，部众被图尼卡人、奇克索人和纳奇兹人吸收。

en: The Koryaks are the indigenous people of the land immediately north of the Kamchatka Peninsula, from the Bering Sea coast and the Anadyr basin in the north to Tigil in the south, and their language belongs, together with Chukchi and Alutor, to the Chukotko-Kamchatkan family. They follow two ways of life: the coastal Nemelan, or village dwellers, who fish and hunt sea mammals, and the inland Chaucu, the rich-in-reindeer people, who follow their herds across the tundra. Their ancestors shaped the Okhotsk culture of the first millennium and worked metal long before the Russians arrived. The name Koryak, from a neighboring word meaning people with the reindeer, entered written records with Vladimir Atlasov's Kamchatka campaigns of 1695, although Cossacks had already clashed with them on the Gizhiga River in 1652. Heavy warfare ran through 1708 to 1715, and in 1745 the reindeer Koryaks rose under Evonta Kosinsky alongside Chukchi and Yukaghir allies, a revolt crushed only in 1757. War and the smallpox epidemic of 1769 to 1770 cut their numbers from ten or eleven thousand in 1700 to four thousand eight hundred by 1800, after which peace, trade and Russian settlement slowly transformed their life.
zh: 科里亚克人是堪察加半岛以北地区的原住民，分布在北起阿纳德尔盆地、南至季吉利的白令海沿岸，其语言与楚科奇语、阿留托尔语同属楚科奇—堪察加语系。他们分为两种生计群体：沿海的内梅兰人意为“村居者”，以捕鱼和猎捕海兽为生；内陆的乔夫楚人意为“多鹿者”，随驯鹿群在苔原上游牧。他们的先民创造了公元1千纪的鄂霍次克文化，在俄国人到来之前很久就已掌握金属加工。“科里亚克”一名出自邻近语言，意为“拥有驯鹿的人”，最早见于哥萨克弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫1695年远征堪察加的文书，而早在1652年，哥萨克已在吉日加河与他们交战。1708—1715年战事连绵，1745年养鹿的科里亚克人在埃翁塔·科辛斯基率领下起义，并与楚科奇人、尤卡吉尔人联合，直到1757年才被镇压。战争加上1769—1770年的天花，使他们的人口从1700年的一两万人降到1800年的4800人，此后和平、贸易和俄国移民才逐渐改变了他们的生活。

en: The Kosraeans are the people of Kosrae, a small high volcanic island at the eastern end of the Caroline Islands, and speak Kosraean, one of the core Micronesian languages of the Austronesian family. Settled by the early centuries of the first millennium, the island gave rise to the walled city of Leluh, which flourished from about 1250 as the seat of a highly stratified kingdom of nobles and commoners, with matrilineal clans, feudal land tenure, shell money and stone burial pyramids for the ruling class. Álvaro de Saavedra made the first recorded European sighting in 1529 while sailing from Tidore, and Spain later claimed the island without occupying it; the first Europeans actually to land were the French crew of Louis-Isidore Duperrey's corvette La Coquille, which spent ten days at Okat Harbour in June 1824 and recorded the ruins of Leluh. Whalers followed, but as late as 1837 Kosrae remained under its own chiefs, untouched by any colonial administration.
zh: 科斯雷人是加罗林群岛东端火山小岛科斯雷的居民，使用南岛语系密克罗尼西亚语族核心语言之一的科斯雷语。该岛在公元第一个千年的早期已有居民，后来兴起有城墙环绕的莱卢城：约1250年起它成为一个等级森严的王国都城，社会分贵族与平民，氏族按母系传承，土地以封建方式保有，使用贝壳货币，统治阶层还拥有石造墓葬金字塔。1529年，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉从蒂多雷返航时留下了欧洲人最早的目击记录，西班牙后来声称拥有该岛却从未驻军；真正登岛的第一批欧洲人是路易·伊西多尔·迪佩雷率领的法国护卫舰“科基耶号”船员，1824年6月他们在奥卡特港停留十天，并记录了莱卢城遗址。此后捕鲸船相继而来，但直到1837年，科斯雷仍由本族酋长统治，没有任何殖民机构上岛。

en: Kota Gabun denotes the Bakota, a cluster of Bantu-speaking peoples of the dense forests of north-eastern Gabon, above all in the Ogooue-Ivindo around Makokou, and across the border in the neighbouring Congo; the Shake village named in the region belongs to one of their constituent groups, alongside the Kota proper, Mahongwe, Shamaye and Ndambomo. Their own traditions bring them south from overcrowded lands to the north, and their name is said to recall how the migrants gathered in one bound bundle on a riverbank during the crossing. They speak iKota, a Bantu language with many dialects, and live in patriarchal clan villages of farmers and hunters, marked by secret circumcision and widow-purification rites. The Bakota are above all famed for their mbulu-ngulu reliquary guardians: stylized wooden faces sheathed in gleaming copper plates and lamellae, set atop baskets holding the bones of important lineage ancestors, through which the living communicated with the dead and sought protection and prosperity; copper, rare and precious, itself signalled wealth and spiritual power. Carbon-14 dating places surviving Mahongwe examples around 1600, showing that the ancestor cult called bwete and its sculptural tradition were already fully developed in the seventeenth century, and they continued to flourish in the forest villages through the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.
