en: The Maden are the indigenous islanders of Salawati, the large island lying off the western tip of New Guinea's Bird's Head Peninsula in the Raja Ampat archipelago, known in their own traditions by clan names such as Banlol, Tepin, Waili, Kawit and Fiawat. Maden, or Madin, was the name their Moi neighbours used for the people of Sakabu village, and it has since fallen out of use. Their Salawati language, once also called Maden, is an Austronesian tongue of the Halmahera Sea branch, closely related to Ma'ya and Matbat and deeply marked by a Papuan substratum; it was the common speech of Salawati before Ma'ya rajas arrived from Waigeo. In local memory Salawati was once ruled by its own fun, or king, named Tusan, before the island entered the Raja Ampat order. Islam reached the archipelago in the fifteenth century, the Portuguese Jorge de Menezes sighted the Raja Ampat islands in 1526, and from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the island kingdoms, including the Salawati kingdom seated at Samate, stood under the political and economic sway of the Sultanate of Tidore, later passing to the Dutch with the rest of the Moluccan claims.
zh: 马登人是萨拉瓦蒂岛的土著居民。萨拉瓦蒂是拉贾安帕特群岛中的大岛，横卧在新几内亚岛多贝拉伊半岛西端的外海；在本族传统中，他们以班洛尔、特平、瓦伊利、卡维特、菲亚瓦特等氏族名见称。马登（又译马丁）是邻近莫伊人对萨卡布村人的称呼，后来已很少使用。他们的萨拉瓦蒂语旧称马登语，属南岛语哈马黑拉海语支，与马亚语、马特巴特语近亲，并带有深厚的巴布亚底层；在卫吉岛的马亚拉阇到来之前，它曾是萨拉瓦蒂岛的通用语言。按当地记忆，萨拉瓦蒂曾由本岛的“丰”（王）图桑统治，后来才纳入拉贾安帕特秩序。15世纪伊斯兰教传入群岛，葡萄牙人豪尔赫·德·梅内塞斯于1526年望见拉贾安帕特诸岛；16至17世纪，以萨马特为中心的萨拉瓦蒂王国等海岛政权在政治与经济上受蒂多雷苏丹国左右，最终又随摩鹿加的宗主权一并转入荷兰人之手。

en: The Madi, or Mà'dí, are a Moru-Madi speaking people of the Central Sudanic group, living along the White Nile and the borderlands of South Sudan and Uganda, around Rajaf, Gondokoro and Lado in Equatoria and the Moyo and Adjumani districts south of the river. Their oral traditions tell of a migration from the west through Amadi in southwest Uganda to the Nile, where they parted from the related Moru; outside scholars place their arrival in the region between roughly 1400 and 1700, alongside the southward movement of Nilotic peoples. Madi society is built on exogamous clans grouped into tribes, and many neighboring Moru-Madi speakers also call themselves Ma'di. From the 1820s Egyptian expansion up the White Nile carried ivory and slave traders into Equatoria; Gondokoro became the main trading station, and armed raids on the Madi lands south of it scattered communities into the forests and drove refugees south into Uganda.
zh: 马迪人是说中苏丹语支莫鲁-马迪语的族群，居住在白尼罗河畔以及南苏丹与乌干达交界地带，包括赤道地区的拉贾夫、贡多科罗、拉多一带，以及河南岸的莫约和阿朱马尼地区。他们的口述传统称先民自西方迁徙，经乌干达西南部的阿马迪抵达尼罗河，并在那里与同族的莫鲁人分离；外部学者估计他们约在1400至1700年间随尼罗特人南下而进入这一地区。马迪社会由外婚制氏族组成部落，邻近许多说莫鲁-马迪语的群体也自称马迪。19世纪20年代起，埃及势力沿白尼罗河扩张，象牙商和奴隶贩子进入赤道地区，贡多科罗成为主要商站，商队对以南马迪土地的武装袭扰使各社群四散，部分人逃入森林或南迁乌干达。

en: The Madurese are an Austronesian people native to Madura, a narrow island off the northeastern coast of Java beyond Surabaya, together with the neighbouring Kangean and Sapudi islands and the eastern salient of Java; their Madurese language belongs to the Malayo-Sumbawan branch of Austronesian. In the fourteenth century their island lay within the realm of Majapahit, whose naval colours survive in the red-and-white stripes of traditional Madurese dress. The Madurese later became Sunni Muslims, and their pondok pesantren boarding schools made them pioneers of Islamic religious learning in the archipelago. In 1624 Sultan Agung of Mataram conquered Madura and installed the Cakraningrat princely line, whose rulers repeatedly chafed at central Javanese rule. Trunajaya, a descendant of the old Madurese lords, led a great revolt in the 1670s with Makassarese allies, searing the north coast of Java and sacking Mataram's capital in 1677 before Dutch intervention crushed the rising; he was captured in 1679 and executed the next year. The Dutch East India Company gained eastern Madura in 1705 and full sovereignty in 1743, when Cakraningrat IV's resistance ended in exile at the Cape of Good Hope. Under Dutch rule the island supplied colonial troops and later salt, while Madurese migrants carried their trade, their pencak silat martial art and the bull races of karapan sapi across the archipelago.
zh: 马都拉人是南岛语系民族，世居爪哇岛东北海岸外、与泗水隔狭窄海峡相望的马都拉岛，以及附近的康厄安群岛、萨普迪群岛和爪哇岛东端；他们使用的马都拉语属南岛语系马来-松巴哇语族。14世纪时马都拉岛处在满者伯夷版图之内，满者伯夷的海军旗帜保留在马都拉传统服饰的红白条纹中。马都拉人后来改奉逊尼派伊斯兰教，他们的伊斯兰寄宿学校使该族成为群岛上伊斯兰宗教学术的先驱。1624年，马打兰苏丹国的苏丹·阿贡征服马都拉，扶植查克拉宁格拉特王公家族统治，历代王公屡屡反抗爪哇中央政权。旧马都拉王族后裔杜鲁诺佐约于17世纪70年代联合望加锡人发动大起义，席卷爪哇北海岸并于1677年攻陷马打兰首都，最终在荷兰人介入下被镇压；他于1679年被俘，次年被处死。荷兰东印度公司于1705年取得东马都拉，1743年取得全岛主权，起兵抵抗的查克拉宁格拉特四世最终被流放至好望角。荷兰统治时期，马都拉岛为殖民当局提供士兵，后来又成为食盐产地；马都拉移民则把经商传统、班卡苏拉武术和赛牛活动带到群岛各地。

en: The Maewo are an Oceanic-speaking Melanesian people of Maewo, a narrow, rain-soaked forest island 105 kilometres east of Espiritu Santo in northern Vanuatu, known to Europeans after 1768 as Aurora. The central districts speak the Sungwadaga language, also called Central Maewo or Peterara, with the related Marino tongue to the north and Baetora, or South Maewo, to the south. Their island is the wettest in Vanuatu, its dense tropical forest cut by abundant streams, waterfalls and hot springs that supply the garden villages with fresh water. The first recorded European sighting of Maewo was made by Pedro Fernandes de Queirós's Spanish expedition at the end of April 1606; Louis Antoine de Bougainville saw it again in 1768 and named it Aurora after the dawn light in which he found it.
zh: 马埃沃人是马埃沃岛上的美拉尼西亚人，操大洋洲语。马埃沃岛位于瓦努阿图北部、圣埃斯皮里图岛以东105公里，是一座狭长而多雨的森林岛，1768年后被欧洲人称作奥罗拉岛。岛的中部通行松瓦达加语，又称中马埃沃语或佩特拉拉语，北面是亲缘的马里诺语，南面是巴埃托拉语，即南马埃沃语。马埃沃是瓦努阿图降雨最多的岛，茂密的热带雨林间遍布溪流、瀑布和温泉，耕作园圃的村落便靠这些淡水资源生活。1606年4月底，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯的西班牙探险队首次有记载地望见马埃沃岛；1768年路易·安托万·德·布干维尔再次见到它，并因在晨曦中发现该岛而以意为黎明的“奥罗拉”为之命名。

en: The Magahi people occupy the old heartland of Magadha south of the Ganges, the country of Patna, Gaya, Nalanda and Bihar Sharif that was the seat of India's earliest great empires. Their language, Magahi or Magadhi, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan tongue directly descended from Magadhi Prakrit, from which it took distinct shape between the eighth and eleventh centuries alongside Bengali, Odia and Maithili; it was formerly written in the Kaithi script and later mainly in Devanagari, and has lived on chiefly through folk songs and the epic ballads of strolling bards. Magadha's Haryanka kings Bimbisara and Ajatashatru ruled from Rajgir and then from Pataliputra, founded in 490 BCE and later the capital of the Nanda, Maurya and Gupta empires; the Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and the monastic university of Nalanda stood nearby. After the Buddhist Pithipati lords of the eleventh to thirteenth centuries, the region fell to Turkic conquest under Bakhtiyar Khalji and passed in turn through the Delhi and Jaunpur sultanates. Sher Shah Suri, born in the Bihar country, built the Sur Empire in 1540; Akbar took Patna in 1574, Aurangzeb renamed it Azimabad in 1704, and after the battle of Buxar in 1764 the East India Company acquired the province.
zh: 摩揭陀人生活在恒河以南的古摩揭陀核心地带，即巴特那、加雅、那烂陀和比哈尔谢里夫一带，这里曾是印度早期几大帝国的中枢。他们的语言摩揭陀语（摩伽希语）属东印度-雅利安语支，直接承自摩揭陀俗语，于8至11世纪间与孟加拉语、奥里亚语和迈蒂利语先后分化成形；旧时使用凯提文，后来主要改用天城文，传承主要靠民间歌谣和游吟诗人的史诗弹唱。摩揭陀的诃黎王朝国王频毗娑罗与阿阇世先后以王舍城和华氏城为都，华氏城建于公元前490年，后来又成为难陀、孔雀和笈多诸帝国的都城；佛陀在菩提伽耶成道，那烂陀僧院大学就在附近。11至13世纪佛教的皮蒂帕蒂王公之后，该地区被巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉率领的突厥军队征服，又先后归入德里苏丹国和章普尔苏丹国。出身比哈尔的舍尔沙于1540年建立苏尔帝国；1574年阿克巴攻占巴特那，1704年奥朗则布将其改名为阿济马巴德；1764年布克萨尔战役后，东印度公司取得了这个省份。

en: The Magar are a Tibeto-Burman people of the Nepalese hills and one of the oldest attested tribes of Nepal, mentioned in written records from around 1100. Their traditional homeland, called Magarat, stretched from the Marsyangdi River to the Pyuthan area around Gulmi and Palpa, the same hill country the game places them in. It was split into the twelve-kingdom confederation of Bahra Magarat and the eighteen-kingdom Athara Magarat, each ruled by its own local chiefs. In the early sixteenth century the Palpa ruler Mukunda Sen even led a raid into the Kathmandu valley. The independent Magar kings lost their last forts when Dravya Shah took Ligligkot and then Gorkhakot in 1559, founding the Gorkha kingdom on Magar land. Magar fighters became the backbone of the Gorkhali armies that unified Nepal under Prithvi Narayan Shah in the later eighteenth century, and later served in the Gurkha regiments of the Anglo-Nepalese wars. Their beliefs blend Hinduism with Tibetan Buddhism and older shamanic and ancestor cults, and their own Magar language belongs to the Bodic branch of Tibeto-Burman.
zh: 马加尔人是尼泊尔山区的藏缅语族群，也是尼泊尔有记载的最古老部族之一，约1100年起便见诸文字记录。他们的传统家园称马加拉特，起自马尔相迪河，延伸到皮乌坦一带，涵盖古尔米、帕尔帕等地。这片土地分为十二邦联盟“巴拉马加拉特”和十八邦联盟“阿塔拉马加拉特”，各由本地首领统治。16世纪初，帕尔帕君主穆昆达·森甚至率军攻入加德满都谷地。1559年，德拉维亚·沙阿夺取利格利格科特，随后又攻占戈尔哈科特，在马加尔人的土地上建立廓尔喀王国，独立的马加尔诸王就此丧失最后的要塞。马加尔战士后来成为廓尔喀军队的骨干，这支军队在18世纪后期普里特维·纳拉扬·沙阿领导下统一了尼泊尔，他们又在英尼战争中加入廓尔喀部队。马加尔人的信仰混合了印度教、藏传佛教以及更古老的萨满教和祖先崇拜，本族的马加尔语属于藏缅语族博德支。

en: The Magemiut, whose own name is Marayarmiut, are a Central Alaskan Yup'ik group of the Scammon Bay area, on the low-lying coast between the mouth of the Yukon River and Nelson Island. Their name derives from Marayaaq, the Yup'ik name for Scammon Bay, which comes from maraq, meaning a marshy, muddy lowland, and the related term Mararmiut denoted the flatland dwellers of this whole stretch of coast. They lived by seasonal fishing and hunting in the water-rich tundra from sod-house villages, travelling by kayak and umiak, and were among the delta peoples reached as Russian explorers opened the Yukon to trade after Andrei Glazunov's expedition of 1834.
zh: 马格缪特人自称马拉亚尔缪特，是居住在斯卡蒙湾一带的中阿拉斯加尤皮克群体，活动于育空河口与纳尔逊岛之间地势低平的海岸。其名来自尤皮克语对斯卡蒙湾的称呼 Marayaaq，词根 maraq 意为泥泞多沼泽的低地；同源词马拉尔缪特泛指这一整段海岸的平原居民。他们在河湖密布的苔原上随季节渔猎，住在草皮屋村庄里，靠皮艇和木架皮舟在水上往来。1834年安德烈·格拉祖诺夫的探险队之后，俄国人沿育空河开展贸易，马格缪特人便是三角洲上与之接触的群体之一。

en: The Maguindanao are an Austronesian Muslim people of the Cotabato Valley in southwestern Mindanao, the foremost of the island's Moro groups; their name means people of the flood plain or people of the lake, and the Spanish rendering of it gave the whole island its name, Mindanao. A Chinese record of 1304 mentions a local polity called Wenduling, then a vassal of Brunei. Their own tradition remembers the brothers Mamalu and Tabunaway: when the Johore-born preacher Sharif Kabungsuwan brought Islam in the early 1500s, Tabunaway's lowland followers became the Maguindanao while Mamalu's people withdrew into the mountains as the Teduray. Kabungsuwan founded the Sultanate of Maguindanao, seated first at Malabang and then at Cotabato, which contested the island with the rival principality of Buayan. Spanish expeditions of 1579 and 1596 failed to conquer it, and under Sultan Kudarat its alliance stretched from the Davao Gulf to Zamboanga; a Spanish force seized Zamboanga in 1635 and defeated Kudarat in 1637, but withdrew in 1663, after which Maguindanao power reached its height. Renewed Spanish fort-building at Zamboanga in 1719 and civil war in the 1730s weakened the sultanate, and Cotabato was eventually ceded to Spain in return for a royal pension. They were also famed metalworkers, forging wavy-bladed kris swords and gongs, and custodians of epics such as Raja Indarapatra.
zh: 马京达瑙人是棉兰老西南部哥打巴托河谷的南岛语系穆斯林族群，也是岛上摩洛穆斯林中最重要的一支；族名意为“洪泛平原之民”或“湖畔之民”，西班牙人将其读音讹转，用来称呼整座棉兰老岛。1304年的中国史籍记载，当地有个名为文杜陵的政权，当时是渤泥的属国。他们自己的传统讲述了马马卢与塔布纳韦两兄弟的故事：16世纪初，出身柔佛的传教士沙里夫·卡邦苏旺带来伊斯兰教，塔布纳韦率领的低地信徒成为马京达瑙人，马马卢的部众则退入山地，成为特杜莱人。卡邦苏旺创立马京达瑙苏丹国，都城先在马拉邦，后迁哥打巴托，与布阿延公国争雄岛上。1579年和1596年的西班牙远征都未能征服它；在苏丹库达拉特治下，其同盟从达沃湾一直延伸到三宝颜。1635年西班牙军队占领三宝颜并筑城，1637年击败库达拉特，但1663年又撤出，马京达瑙的势力此后达到顶峰。1719年西班牙人在三宝颜重修要塞，18世纪30年代的内战又削弱了苏丹国，哥打巴托最终以王室年金为条件被割让给西班牙。马京达瑙人也以金工闻名，擅长打造波形刃的克里斯短剑和铜锣，并保存着《拉惹·因达拉帕特腊》等史诗。

en: The Mahafaly are a Malagasy people of the dry plains of southwestern Madagascar, around Betioky and Ampanihy, whose name is usually read as those who make holy. Their ancestors are thought to have reached the island from southeastern Africa around the twelfth century, mixing with the Austronesian population already there, and they live as farmers and zebu herders, famed above all for the massive tombs they raise for dead kings. In the 1500s a Maroserana noble called Olembetsitoto subdued the older chiefly families of the area and founded a single polity; when he withdrew into seclusion his followers held him to have become holy, making his land and people maha-faly, and ombiasy advisers thereafter spoke for the ruler as intermediaries. In June 1649 Mahafaly envoys even travelled to the French post at Fort Dauphin to hire musketeers against Masikoro raiders who had lifted the royal cattle. From about 1650 the kingdom fragmented into the Sakatovo, Menarandra, Linta and, by 1750, Onilahy kingdoms, whose rivalries included the annexation of the Antandroy province of Karimbola, while Onilahy borrowed court titles from the Antemoro. Unlike most of the island, the Mahafaly kingdoms never submitted to the Merina, and royal funerary ritual, with its volamena tombs, the posthumous renaming of kings and the obligatory shaving of mourners, remained the heart of Mahafaly identity.
zh: 马哈法利人是马尔加什人的一支，住在马达加斯加西南部贝蒂乌基和安帕尼希一带的干旱平原，族名通常解释为“使之神圣的人”。一般认为其先民约12世纪从非洲东南部抵达该岛，与早已在此的南岛语居民融合，以农耕和牧养瘤牛为生，尤以替亡故国王修建的巨石陵墓闻名。16世纪，马鲁塞拉纳贵族奥伦贝奇托托征服当地旧有的酋长家族，建立统一政权；他后来避世隐居，追随者相信他已成圣，使他的土地和人民变得“马哈-法利”，翁比亚西顾问此后便作为中介代统治者传达旨意。1649年6月，马哈法利使节甚至远赴法国人的陶拉纳鲁据点，雇佣火枪手去对付偷走王室牛群的马希科洛袭掠者。约1650年起，王国分裂为萨卡托沃、梅纳兰德拉、林塔等国，到1750年又形成奥尼拉伊王国；列国相争中，梅纳兰德拉还吞并了安坦德罗伊人的卡林博拉地区，奥尼拉伊则从安泰莫罗人那里借用宫廷称号。与岛上大多数政权不同，马哈法利诸王国始终未臣服于梅里纳，而以沃拉梅纳王陵、国王死后改名和哀悼者必须剃发为核心的王室丧葬仪式，一直是马哈法利人身份认同的核心。

en: The Mahican, or Mohican, whose name means “people of the continually flowing waters,” were an Eastern Algonquian people of the upper tidal Hudson River valley, centered on modern Albany and spreading east into the Housatonic valley of western New England. Dutch and English settlers called them the River Indians, and the French called them Loups, or wolves. They formed a confederacy of five related groups and up to forty longhouse villages, ruled by hereditary sachems under a matrilineal system of Turkey, Turtle and Wolf clans; women farmed maize, beans and squash while men fished the Hudson and hunted in the Taconics. Henry Hudson met them in 1609, and the Dutch post of Fort Orange rose in their heartland in 1624, drawing them into the fur trade and into wars with the Mohawk, whose victories in the Beaver Wars pushed many Mahican southeast after 1680 to Stockbridge in western Massachusetts. As the Stockbridge Indians they took Protestant missionaries, and their sachem Etow Oh Koam was one of the four “Indian kings” presented to Queen Anne in 1710. They fought for Britain in the French and Indian War and for the patriots in the American Revolution, losing heavily at Kingsbridge in 1778. Afterward the community moved first to the Oneida in New York and then, under Indian Removal in the 1820s and 1830s, to Wisconsin, where their descendants share the Stockbridge-Munsee Community with Munsee Lenape; a smaller group joined the Six Nations reserve on the Grand River in Ontario.
zh: 莫希干人（又译莫希坎）族名意为“奔流之水的人民”，是说东阿尔冈昆语的民族，世居哈德逊河潮汐段上游，以今奥尔巴尼一带为中心，向东越过塔科尼克山脉，延伸到新英格兰西部的胡萨托尼克河流域。荷兰人和英国人把他们与哈德逊河沿岸邻族统称为“河印第安人”，法国人则称他们为 Loups，即“狼”。他们由五个近亲群体、多达四十座长屋村落组成联盟，由世袭酋长在火鸡、龟、狼三大氏族的母系体系下治理；妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男子在哈德逊河捕鱼、在塔科尼克山区狩猎。1609年亨利·哈得逊与他们接触，1624年荷兰人的奥兰治堡贸易站在其腹心地带建立，把他们拖入毛皮贸易和与莫霍克人的战争；海狸战争中莫霍克人获胜，1680年后许多莫希干人向东南迁到马萨诸塞西部的斯托克布里奇。他们在那里以“斯托克布里奇印第安人”闻名，接纳新教传教士，酋长埃托·奥·科阿姆还在1710年作为四位“印第安国王”之一赴伦敦觐见安妮女王。他们在法国-印第安战争中为英国而战，独立战争中支持北美爱国者，1778年在金斯布里奇一役损失惨重。战后这支社群先投奔纽约州的奥奈达人，19世纪20至30年代又在印第安迁移政策下迁往威斯康星，后裔与蒙西莱纳佩人共同组成斯托克布里奇-蒙西社区；另有一小支加入安大略大河畔的六族保留地。

en: The Mahmikiwini are the downstream division of the Plains Cree, the Māmihkiyiniwak or people living downriver, whose bands held the lower Saskatchewan River, the lakes around Cedar Lake and Lake Winnipeg, and the country towards the Red River. Their Cree belongs to the Algonquian family and shades into the neighbouring Swampy Cree dialects, for their bands intermarried freely with Swampy Cree, Assiniboine and Saulteaux and gathered each summer at fishing narrows such as Opaskwayak, the wooded narrows later called The Pas. Sitting closest to Hudson Bay, they were the first Cree middlemen of the fur trade: Henry Kelsey travelled inland with Assiniboine and Cree parties as early as 1690, French traders under La Vérendrye built Fort Paskoya and Fort Bourbon in their country in the 1740s, and the Hudson's Bay Company opened Cumberland House, its first inland post, on the Saskatchewan in 1774. They provisioned the posts with bison pemmican and fish and joined the Iron Confederacy, raiding alongside the Assiniboine while the 1781 smallpox epidemic emptied many of their camps. When the Selkirk colony was planted on the Red River in 1812, its struggle with the fur companies over pemmican, including the fight at Seven Oaks in 1816, unfolded on their doorstep.
zh: 马米基维尼人是平原克里人的“下游”分支，即“马米基伊尼瓦克”，意为住在河流下游的人。他们的群体占据萨斯喀彻温河下游、锡达湖和温尼伯湖一带的湖区，并延伸到雷德河流域。其克里语属阿尔冈昆语系，并与邻近的斯旺皮克里方言相互交融，因为他们的群体常和斯旺皮克里人、纳科达人及索托人通婚，每年夏天还会在奥帕斯夸亚克等狭窄渔场聚会——那里林木葱郁，后来被称为帕斯。他们最靠近哈得孙湾，是毛皮贸易中最早的克里中间人：早在1690年，亨利·凯尔西就随纳科达和克里队伍深入内陆；18世纪40年代，拉韦朗德里麾下的法国商人在其土地上建起帕斯科亚堡和波旁堡；1774年，哈德逊湾公司又在萨斯喀彻温河畔开设其第一个内陆商站坎伯兰豪斯。他们以野牛制的肉糜饼和鱼供应商站，并加入铁联盟，与纳科达人并肩劫掠，而1781年的天花大流行使他们许多营地为之一空。1812年塞尔扣克殖民地在雷德河建立后，毛皮公司之间围绕肉糜饼的争斗——包括1816年的七橡树之战——就发生在他们的家门口。

en: The Mài are a small Chinese-speaking community of the southernmost Hainan coast, in the former Yazhou prefecture around present-day Sanya, where they hold a handful of villages such as Shuinan and Yanglan beside the Ningyuan River, surrounded by Li and Utsat settlements. They call themselves the Mai people, and their speech, Maihua, is assigned to the Yue branch in the Language Atlas of China, although linguists note heavy Hakka, Gan and Hainan Min layers and some treat it as a mixed southern variety; the Mai of Yanglan trace their ancestors to a move from Shuinan more than ten generations ago. This coast was first brought under Chinese rule with the Zhuya commandery of 110 BC, abandoned by the Han court in 46 BC, and later organised under the Yazhou prefecture of the Tang and Song, whose seat at Ningyuan stood on the old Yazhou city site west of modern Sanya.
zh: 迈人是海南岛最南端沿海的一支小型汉语社群，聚居在旧崖州、今三亚一带的水南、羊栏等少数村落，地处宁远河畔，四周与黎族和回辉人的村落为邻。他们自称迈人，所说的迈话在《中国语言地图集》里划入粤语分支，但语言学者发现其中叠有浓厚的客家话、赣语和海南闽语成分，有人把它视为南方汉语的混合变体；羊栏的迈人相传，先祖在十多代以前从水南村迁来。这一带海岸在公元前110年汉朝设置珠崖郡时纳入版图，公元前46年汉廷弃郡，唐代和宋代又先后在这里设置崖州，州治设在宁远，也就是三亚以西的崖州古城。

en: The Maia are a Trans–New Guinea people of the Bogia inland in northern Madang Province, scattered through the villages of the Almani area. Their language, also recorded under such names as Banar, Pila and Saki, splits into a main dialect and a southern dialect.
zh: 迈亚人是马当省北部博吉亚内陆的跨新几内亚语系族群，散居在阿尔马尼一带的村庄里。他们的语言也被记作巴纳尔语、皮拉语、萨基语等名称，分为主方言和南方方言两支。

en: The Maiduan peoples, whose name means person in their own Penutian-family tongues, held the central Sierra Nevada and the upper Sacramento Valley around the Feather and American Rivers. They were divided into four nearly unintelligible language groups: the Northeastern or Mountain Maidu of the high forests and Humbug Valley, the Konkow of the northwestern foothills, the Chico Maidu of the valley floor, and the southern Nisenan. In small autonomous villages led only by the heads of the men's Kuksu cult, they lived by hunting and gathering, tending oak groves with controlled burns and leaching acorn meal of its tannin for winter stores kept in woven granaries. Mountain bands built circular earth lodges dug three feet into the ground and roofed with pine bark, moving to brush shelters in summer, while their women wove baskets so fine that some strands need a magnifying glass. Their Kuksu big-head dances and the spring Bear Dance honored a world overseen by World-maker and the trickster Coyote. Lying beyond the reach of the coastal missions, they saw few Spaniards beyond occasional patrols, until the malaria epidemic of 1833 swept the Sacramento Valley and emptied many of their villages.
zh: 迈杜诸族在本族佩努蒂语中以其名意为“人”，他们据有内华达山脉中段以及费瑟河、亚美利加河一带的萨克拉门托谷地北部。他们分成四种几乎互不相通的语言群体：高山林地与亨巴格谷地的东北迈杜（又称山地迈杜）、西北山麓的康考、谷地上的奇科迈杜，以及南方的尼塞南。他们居住在自治的小村落里，唯一的头人出自男子的库克苏教团；生计靠狩猎采集，以受控烧荒养护栎林，把橡子粉滤去单宁后存入编织的粮仓过冬。山地部落建造圆形土屋，地面下挖三英尺、以松树皮盖顶，夏季则改住枝棚；妇女编织的篮器极为细密，部分纹路需借助放大镜才能看清。他们的库克苏“大头舞”和春季的熊舞，敬奉由创世主与恶作剧者郊狼主宰的世界。由于地处沿海传教站势力之外，他们除了零星巡逻队外很少见到西班牙人；直到1833年，疟疾席卷萨克拉门托谷地，许多村落为之一空。

en: The Maisouna were one of the St. Lawrence Iroquoian groups of the middle St. Lawrence valley, occupying the country between Stadacona near present Quebec City and Hochelaga at Montreal, around modern Trois-Rivières. Like their Iroquoian neighbours they spoke Laurentian, farmed maize in palisaded villages and vanished in the late sixteenth-century wars before the French returned to the river.
zh: 迈索纳人是圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的一支，住在圣劳伦斯河中游，即魁北克城附近的斯塔达科纳与蒙特利尔的奥什拉加之间，大致在今天的三河镇一带。他们与邻近的易洛魁群体一样使用劳伦琴语，在设有栅栏的村落里种植玉米，并在16世纪末的战乱中消亡，此时法国人尚未重返这条河流。

en: The Maithili people are the people of Mithila, the plain north of the Ganges around Darbhanga, Bhagalpur, Monghyr and Samastipur, a country whose ancient King Janaka and his daughter Sita appear in the Ramayana. Their language, Maithili, descends from Magadhi Prakrit and was historically written in its own Tirhuta script, also called Mithilakshara, before Devanagari became dominant. Under the Karnat dynasty, whose last king Harisimhadeva ruled until 1324, the poet Jyotirishwar Thakur composed the Varna Ratnakara, the earliest known prose work in a modern Indian language. In 1324 Ghiyasuddin Tughluq of Delhi overran Mithila and installed the Maithil Brahmin Kameshvar Jha, beginning the Oiniwar dynasty of 1325 to 1526, the polity under which the Maithili lived in 1337. Its court poet Vidyapati, writing between about 1360 and 1450 under King Shiva Simha and Queen Lakhimadevi, left more than a thousand songs that shaped Vaishnava devotion across Bengal and Assam. The last Oiniwar king was killed by the Bengal sultan Nusrat Shah in 1526, and after decades of strife the Raj Darbhanga dynasty took over the region; in the Nepal hills the Malla kings of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries made Maithili a language of their court and theatre.
zh: 迈蒂利人是弥梯罗的居民，生活在恒河以北的平原，以达尔邦格阿、巴加尔布尔、蒙吉尔和萨姆斯蒂布尔为中心；古国国王遮那竭及其女儿悉多的故事见于《罗摩衍那》。他们的迈蒂利语承自摩揭陀俗语，历史上使用本族的提尔胡塔文（又称弥梯罗克夏尔文），后来天城文逐渐成为主流。卡尔纳特王朝末代国王哈里辛哈提婆统治至1324年，其治下诗人焦蒂里什瓦尔·塔库尔写下《瓦尔纳·拉特纳卡拉》，这是已知最早用近代印度语言写成的散文作品。1324年，德里的吉亚斯丁·图格鲁克攻占弥梯罗，委任迈蒂利婆罗门卡梅什瓦尔·贾治理，开启了1325至1526年的奥伊尼瓦尔王朝，1337年的迈蒂利人正处在这个政权之下。宫廷诗人维迪亚帕蒂约在1360至1450年间侍奉湿婆·辛哈国王与拉基玛黛维王后，留下上千首诗歌，深刻影响了孟加拉和阿萨姆的毗湿奴虔信文学。1526年，奥伊尼瓦尔末代国王被孟加拉苏丹努斯拉特·沙阿杀害，经过数十年混战，达尔邦格拉杰王朝接管了这一地区；在尼泊尔山地，16至17世纪的马拉诸王也把迈蒂利语用作宫廷与戏剧语言。

en: The Maiwa are a Papuan people of the Meneao Range in the Bird's Tail of New Guinea. Their language belongs to the Dagan family of Trans–New Guinea languages, alongside the related Daga speech of the same mountains.
zh: 迈瓦人是新几内亚“鸟尾”梅尼奥岭的巴布亚族群，其语言属跨新几内亚语系的达甘语族，与同处这片山地的达加语亲缘相近。

en: The Makah are a Wakashan-speaking people of the Pacific Northwest Coast, settled at Cape Flattery and Neah Bay on the tip of the Olympic Peninsula in what is now Washington state. They call themselves qʷidiččaʔa·tx̌, the people who live by the rocks and seagulls, while the name Makah comes from a S'Klallam word meaning generous with food; their language is closest to the Nuu-chah-nulth and Ditidaht spoken across the Strait of Juan de Fuca on Vancouver Island. They have occupied Neah Bay for at least six thousand years, living in large western red cedar longhouses, weaving bark clothing and cedar-root baskets and hollowing whole trees into canoes. From these canoes they hunted gray and humpback whales with yew-wood harpoons tipped with mussel shell and towed seal-skin floats, then welcomed the whale's spirit with ceremony and divided the meat and oil at potlatches. Society was ranked by kinship to the village chief, and seals, salmon, halibut, shellfish and forest game rounded out the diet. In the early seventeenth century a mudslide buried part of the village of Ozette, preserving its houses. In 1834 a dismasted Japanese junk wrecked near Cape Flattery, and the Makah kept its three survivors as slaves before handing them on at Fort Vancouver.
zh: 马卡人是太平洋西北海岸讲瓦卡什语的民族，聚居于今华盛顿州奥林匹克半岛顶端的弗拉特里角和尼亚湾。他们自称奎迪查阿特赫人，意为“住在岩石与海鸥旁的人”；“马卡”这个外来名字来自斯克拉拉姆语，意思是“慷慨施食的人”。他们的语言与胡安·德富卡海峡对岸温哥华岛上的努查努特人（即努特卡人）和迪蒂达人的语言最接近。马卡人在尼亚湾至少居住了六千年，住西部红柏木搭建的长屋，用树皮织布做衣、用雪松根编篮，还把整根大树凿成独木舟。他们乘独木舟捕猎灰鲸和座头鲸，鱼叉以紫杉木制成、尖端嵌蚌壳，又拖着海豹皮浮具耗垮猎物；捕到鲸后要举行仪式迎接鲸灵，再在夸富宴上分食鲸肉和鲸油。社会按与村酋长的血缘亲疏排定等级，海豹、鲑鱼、大比目鱼、贝类和林中猎物则补充了日常食物。17世纪初，一场泥石流掩埋了奥泽特村的一部分，把房屋原样保存下来。1834年，一艘断了桅杆的日本帆船在弗拉特里角附近失事，马卡人将三名幸存者收为奴隶，后来在温哥华堡把他们转交出去。

en: The Maká are a Matacoan people of the Gran Chaco, whose ancestors were a Mataco tribe of the south-eastern Chaco before they adopted the horse-riding life of their Guaycuru, Vilela and Calchaquí neighbours and moved north across the Patiño marshes into the Chaco Boreal, between the Pilcomayo and Paraguay rivers. Their language belongs to the Mataco-Mataguayan branch of the Mataco-Guaicuru family and was divided into the Towolhi and Enimagá dialects. The Jesuit Sánchez Labrador met groups he called Enimaga in the central Chaco in 1761, and a Morillo report of 1780 names them as the Inimaca, showing them already established in their northern range. In those years the Maká kept up a shifting pattern of alliances, standing with the Chulupí, Enlhet and Enxet against their enemies the Pitlaxa and Toba in the endless raiding wars of the Chaco.
zh: 玛卡人是大查科的马塔科语族民族，其先民本是查科东南部的一支马塔科部落，后来效法邻族瓜伊库鲁人、比莱拉人和卡尔查基人过上骑马生活，并向北越过帕蒂尼奥沼泽，迁入皮尔科马约河与巴拉圭河之间的北查科。他们的语言属马塔科-瓜伊库鲁语系的马塔科-马塔瓜亚语支，分为托沃尔希和埃尼马加两种方言。1761年，耶稣会士桑切斯·拉布拉多在查科中部遇到被他称作埃尼马加的群体；1780年莫里略的报告又以伊尼马加之名记载他们，可见那时他们已在北方的活动区域立足。那些年里，玛卡人合纵连横，与丘卢皮人、恩莱特人和恩克塞特人结盟，共同对付仇敌皮特拉哈人和托巴人，卷入查科无休止的劫掠战争。

en: The Makasae are a Papuan, Trans-New Guinea people of eastern Timor around Baucau, Viqueque and Tutuala, whose language, grouped with Fataluku in the Eastern Timor branch of the West Bomberai family, is the most widely spoken Papuan language west of New Guinea. Their chiefdoms stood within the Portuguese sphere in eastern Timor, under indirect rule through local rulers.
zh: 马卡萨埃人是帝汶东部的巴布亚语族群，属跨新几内亚语系，主要居住在包考、维克克和图图阿拉一带；马卡萨埃语与法塔卢库语同属西邦贝拉伊语系的东帝汶语支，是新几内亚岛以外使用最广的巴布亚语言。他们的土邦处于葡萄牙在帝汶东部的势力范围内，欧洲人的统治长期借助本地首领间接施行。

en: The Makassarese are the Austronesian people of the southwestern peninsula of Sulawesi, around the port of Makassar and the rice plains of Gowa, close kin and historic rivals of the Bugis. Already listed as a Majapahit tributary in 1365, they built their own agrarian kingdoms of Gowa and Tallo, reunited as a twin state under King Tunipalangga, who reigned from 1512 to 1546. From 1607 Gowa threw Makassar open to all foreign traders, and the port became one of Southeast Asia's busiest emporiums, where Malay, Javanese, Portuguese, English and Chinese merchants met; an English factory was set up there in 1613. The court embraced Islam in 1605 under Sultan Alauddin, guided by Minangkabau scholars, and in 1611 launched the so-called Islamic wars that brought all southwest Sulawesi, including the Bugis kingdom of Bone, under Gowa's overlordship. Its resistance to the Dutch East India Company drew on this wealth: in the Makassar War of 1666 to 1669 the VOC, allied with the Bugis prince Arung Palakka, stormed the Somba Opu fortress and imposed the Treaty of Bungaya, reducing Gowa to a vassal and building Fort Rotterdam on the ruins. Dispersed Makassarese seafarers then carried trade across the archipelago and beyond, sailing their phinisi ships as far as the Australian coast in search of trepang. They speak Makassarese, a South Sulawesi language traditionally written in the Lontara script.
zh: 望加锡人是苏拉威西西南半岛的南岛语系族群，聚居于望加锡港与戈瓦的稻米平原，是布吉人的近亲，也是其历史上的劲敌。1365年的《爪哇史颂》已把望加锡列为满者伯夷的属国。他们后来建立戈瓦与塔洛两个农业王国，1512至1546年在位的图尼帕朗加将二者合并为孪生国家。1607年起，戈瓦宣布望加锡向所有外商开放，港口由此成为东南亚最繁忙的商埠之一，马来人、爪哇人、葡萄牙人、英国人和中国人汇聚于此，英国商馆也于1613年设立。1605年，宫廷在米南加保学者引导下由苏丹阿拉丁率领改宗伊斯兰教；1611年又发动所谓“伊斯兰战争”，使包括布吉人的波尼王国在内的整个苏拉威西西南臣服于戈瓦。凭借这笔财富，它顽强抵抗荷兰东印度公司：1666至1669年的望加锡战争中，公司联合布吉王子阿隆·帕拉卡攻破松巴奥普堡垒，强迫签署《邦加亚条约》，将戈瓦降为附庸，并在废墟上修建鹿特丹堡。流散的望加锡海商此后驾着菲尼西帆船往来群岛各地，甚至远抵澳大利亚海岸捕捞海参。他们讲望加锡语，属南苏拉威西语族，传统上用龙塔拉文字书写。

en: The Makhuwa, or Makua, are the dominant Bantu people of northern Mozambique, living across the lands north of the Zambezi from the coast to Lake Malawi and into the Mtwara region of southern Tanzania; their dialects include the Lolo, Lomwe, Maua and Niassa divisions of the Emakua language. Their oral traditions call the mountain of Namuli their first home, and scholars consider them settled in the region by around 1000. Farmers, hunters and skilled iron smelters who forged axes, spears and rings in community hearths, they traded food, ivory and metalwork for cloth and salt with Swahili and Gujarati merchants long before the Portuguese met them in the early 1500s. Their supreme god Muluku, opposed by the evil spirit Minepa, headed a religion of ancestor and nature spirits, while only the coastal trading communities adopted Sunni Islam. From the eighteenth century the Muslim Yao to their north raided them for slaves destined for Zanzibar, and from 1749 the Makhuwa waged a long war of attrition against the coastal Arab sultans, the Portuguese and their African allies.
zh: 马夸人（又称马库阿）是莫桑比克北部占主体的班图人，分布在赞比西河以北、从沿海直到马拉维湖的广大地区，并伸入坦桑尼亚南部的姆特瓦拉一带；埃马夸语分为洛洛、洛姆韦、马乌阿和尼亚萨等方言支系。口传传统把纳穆利山视为最初的家园，学者认为他们约1000年时已定居此地。他们务农、狩猎，又是熟练的冶铁者，在集体炉坊中打制斧头、长矛和指环，早在1500年代初葡萄牙人到来之前，就用粮食、象牙和铁器向斯瓦希里和古吉拉特商人换取布匹与食盐。他们信仰至高神穆卢库，与恶灵米内帕相对，兼奉祖先与自然神灵，只有滨海的商人群体改宗逊尼派伊斯兰教。18世纪起，北方信伊斯兰教的尧人为向桑给巴尔输出奴隶而不断劫掠马夸人；从1749年起，马夸人对沿海阿拉伯苏丹、葡萄牙人及其非洲盟友展开了长期的消耗战。

en: The Makurap are a Tupian people of the Tupari branch who have lived for centuries on the right bank of the Guaporé River in southern Rondônia, Brazil. By the 1700s the Guaporé was a strategic frontier between the Portuguese and Spanish colonies, and river traffic drew them into contact with settlers, bringing epidemics and depopulation to their riverside villages.
zh: 马库拉普人是图皮语族图帕里支系的原住民，数百年来住在巴西朗多尼亚州南部瓜波雷河的右岸。到18世纪，瓜波雷河成为葡萄牙与西班牙殖民地之间的战略边界，河上往来把他们卷入与殖民者的接触，疫病和人口锐减随之降临河畔村落。

en: The Malakula are the Melanesian peoples of Malakula, Vanuatu's second-largest island, whose coasts and interior hold nearly thirty mutually distinct Oceanic languages. Their best-known societies are the Big Nambas of the north and the Small Nambas of the south-central interior, named for the size of the leaf penis sheath worn by the men. Both order themselves through graded societies in which rank is earned by the ceremonial killing of pigs, and they traditionally bound infants' skulls so that a cone-shaped head served as a mark of high status. The first Europeans to sight Malakula were the ships of Pedro Fernandes de Queirós's Spanish expedition in 1606, and James Cook visited the island in 1774, after which British and French settlers and missionaries made it part of the contested New Hebrides.
zh: 马拉库拉人是瓦努阿图第二大岛马拉库拉岛上诸美拉尼西亚群体的统称，沿海与内陆分布着近三十种互不相通的大洋洲语。其中最著名的是北部的大南巴斯人和南部内陆中部的小南巴斯人，名字来自男子所戴叶制阴茎鞘的大小。两者都实行等级会社制度，身份要靠仪式性杀猪晋阶来赢得，传统上还会捆扎婴儿的头颅，把锥形头视为高贵身份的标志。1606年，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯的西班牙探险队首次望见马拉库拉岛，詹姆斯·库克于1774年到访；此后英国和法国的定居者与传教士相继而来，使该岛成为列强争夺的新赫布里底的一部分。

en: The Málǎo are the Yue-speaking people of the Qin-Lian coast facing the Gulf of Tonkin, around Hepu, Lingshan and Qinzhou in present-day southern Guangxi. Their speech belongs to the old local layer of Qin-Lian Yue, whose best-known form is Lianzhou speech, named after Lianzhou, the former prefecture seated at Hepu; in eastern Hepu and Pubei the Hakka call these speakers Malao, or jute people, either for the jute they grew or for the bamboo hats and linen clothes they wore, and the name attached itself to their dialect. The region entered the Chinese administrative order early: Hepu commandery was founded in 111 BCE under the Han emperor Wu, and under Wang Mang it served as a place of exile for political losers. Successive waves of Yue-speaking migrants then mixed with the indigenous Kra-Dai peoples, leaving the dialect with a noticeable Kra-Dai vocabulary beneath its Cantonese-like grammar, so much so that the old local speeches are barely mutually intelligible with the Guangzhou-style Cantonese of the newer port towns.
zh: 麻佬人是南临北部湾的钦廉沿海粤语人群，聚居在今广西南部的合浦、灵山和钦州一带。他们的话属粤语钦廉片的老派本土层，最知名的形式是因合浦旧称廉州府而得名的廉州话；在合浦东部和浦北，当地客家人把这些说廉州话的人叫作麻佬，一说因他们广种黄麻，一说因他们惯戴竹帽、身穿麻衣，这个称呼后来连方言一起叫开。这一地区进入中国行政体系很早：公元前111年汉武帝设立合浦郡，王莽当政时这里还是失势官员的流放地。此后历代粤语移民与当地壮侗系土著杂居融合，使麻佬话在近似粤语的语法之外保留了一批壮侗语来源的词汇，以至老派土话与新兴港埠通行的广州式白话之间，常常难以直接通话。

en:
The Malays are the Austronesian coastal people of the Malay Peninsula, eastern Sumatra and the shores of Borneo, bound together by Malayic languages and a trading life shaped by Indians, Chinese and the sea-nomad Orang Laut. Early in the Common Era their harbours gave rise to states such as Kedah and Langkasuka, and from the 600s most entered the mandala of Srivijaya, whose capital at Palembang made Old Malay the lingua franca of the archipelago; Chinese sources first use the name Malayu in 644. Chola raids after 1025 broke Srivijaya, and after the Javanese Pamalayu campaigns of the late 1200s the prince Sang Nila Utama, backed by the Orang Laut, founded the Kingdom of Singapura at Temasek in 1299. In 1337 that island kingdom was still the focus of Malay political life.

In 1400 Parameswara fled Temasek and founded the Malacca Sultanate, whose command of the strait made it the region's emporium. Islam, attested on the peninsula by the fourteenth-century Terengganu stone, became its state religion, fusing faith, language and court custom into a classical Malay identity later sultanates emulated. The Portuguese took Malacca in 1511, but its royal line continued in Johor from 1528 and in Perak and Pahang, while Brunei built a maritime empire in Borneo. The Dutch, allied with Johor, captured Malacca in 1641; the British leased Penang in 1786 and founded Singapore in 1819, and the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 divided the Malay world between the two powers.
zh:
马来人是马来半岛、苏门答腊东部和婆罗洲沿岸的南岛语滨海民族，以马来语族诸语言和贸易生计为纽带，并深受印度人、华人以及海上游民罗越人的影响。公元初年，他们的港口兴起了羯荼、狼牙修等邦国；7世纪起，这些港口大多进入以巨港为都的室利佛逝势力圈，古马来语由此成为群岛通用语，中国文献也在644年首次出现“末罗瑜”之名。1025年后的朱罗袭击打破了室利佛逝的霸权，13世纪末爪哇发动班马莱由远征，王子桑·尼拉·乌他马在罗越人支持下于1299年在淡马锡建立新加坡拉王国。1337年时，这个海岛王国仍是马来人政治生活的中心。

1400年，拜里米苏拉逃离淡马锡，建立马六甲苏丹国，凭借对海峡的控制成为地区商贸中心。14世纪的登嘉楼石碑已印证伊斯兰教传入半岛，此后它成为马六甲国教，信仰、语言与宫廷习俗熔铸成古典马来认同，被后来的苏丹国效仿。1511年葡萄牙人攻占马六甲，但王室血脉在1528年的柔佛以及霹雳、彭亨等地延续，文莱则在婆罗洲建立海上帝国。1641年荷兰人与柔佛结盟夺取马六甲；1786年英国租得槟榔屿，1819年开埠新加坡，1824年的《英荷条约》把马来世界划分给两个殖民强国。

en: The Malayali are the Dravidian people of Kerala, the rainy Malabar coast of southwestern India, whose mother tongue Malayalam gives the region its name, from mala meaning mountain and ali meaning person. As the Keralaputra Cheras they appear in an Ashokan rock edict of the third century BCE, and their ports throve on the Indian Ocean pepper trade with Arabia, Egypt, East Africa and China. After the Chera kingdom dissolved in the twelfth century, the country split into rival chiefdoms, among them the Zamorins of Kozhikode, Kolathunadu, Valluvanad and Venad, whose harbours welcomed Arab and Chinese merchants. In the eighth century the Kerala-born theologian Adi Shankara built his Advaita Vedanta movement, and in the fourteenth century Madhava of Sangamagrama founded the Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics, which pioneered infinite series. The age of European intervention opened when Vasco da Gama reached Kozhikode in 1498; Portuguese, Dutch and French rivals followed, until Marthanda Varma of Travancore broke Dutch power in 1741. After the Third Mysore War of 1790 to 1792 the British took northern Kerala as the Malabar District, leaving Travancore and Cochin as allied princely states.
zh: 马拉雅拉姆人是印度西南部多雨的马拉巴尔海岸——喀拉拉地区的达罗毗荼语族群，母语马拉雅拉姆语的名称由 mala（山）和 ali（人）拼成，地区也由此得名。早在公元前3世纪阿育王的石刻诏谕中，他们就以凯拉拉普特拉·哲罗之名出现，是南印四大独立王国之一；其港口靠着与阿拉伯、埃及、东非和中国的印度洋胡椒贸易而繁盛。12世纪哲罗王国解体后，国土分裂为相互竞争的酋长邦，包括科泽科德的扎莫林、科拉图纳德、瓦卢瓦纳德和韦纳德等，港中云集阿拉伯与中国商人。8世纪，出生于喀拉拉的宗教大师阿迪·商羯罗创立了不二论吠檀多体系；14世纪，桑伽马格拉马的马德哈瓦创立喀拉拉天文数学学派，率先研究无穷级数。欧洲介入的时代始于1498年瓦斯科·达伽马抵达科泽科德，葡萄牙人、荷兰人和法国人接踵而来；1741年，特拉凡哥尔的马坦达·瓦尔马击败荷兰人。1790至1792年第三次英迈战争后，英国人接管北喀拉拉设马拉巴尔县，特拉凡哥尔与科钦则成为结盟的土邦。

en: The Maleku, called Guatuso by the Spanish, are a Chibchan-speaking people of the forested northern plains of Costa Rica, in the Río Frío watershed between the Guanacaste and Central Volcanic cordilleras. Their pre-contact territory reached west to Rincón de la Vieja and took in the sacred slopes of Arenal and the Río Celeste, and their open-walled, palm-thatched villages, or palenques, were shared by several related families. Kin to the Rama of Nicaragua, they may also carry the traditions of the Botos, Tises and Katapas and of Huetar refugees who fled the Spanish conquest into these lowlands, one of the few parts of Costa Rica the conquistadors never subdued. Franciscan friars probed the rivers alone: by 1719 the Maleku were known as the warrior Indians of Río Frío, and in 1750 Francisco Zepeda counted five hundred ranchos on streams feeding the San Juan. When Tomás López entered in 1778 his party was driven back by arrows, and Maleku oral tradition remembers a priest captured on the Río La Muerte and put to death, so that at the end of the colonial era the Guatuso plains remained entirely outside Spanish control.
zh: 瓜图索人自称马莱库，是哥斯达黎加北部森林平原的奇布查语族群，住在瓜纳卡斯特山脉与中央火山山脉之间的弗里奥河流域。他们接触时代以前的领地向西延伸到林孔德拉别哈，把阿雷纳尔火山坡地和塞莱斯特河奉为圣地；无墙、棕榈顶的帕伦克村落由几个有亲缘关系的家庭共居。他们与尼加拉瓜的拉玛人同源，可能还承继了博托人、蒂塞人、卡塔帕人以及为躲避西班牙征服而逃入低地的韦塔尔难民的传统——这片低地是哥斯达黎加少数从未被征服者制服的地区之一。方济各会修士只能独自溯河探查：1719年时，瓜图索人已被称作弗里奥河的武士印第安人；1750年，弗朗西斯科·塞佩达在注入圣胡安河的各条支流上数到五百处村舍。1778年托马斯·洛佩斯入境时，他的队伍被箭雨逼退，瓜图索人的口述传统也记得一位在拉穆埃尔特河被俘后处死的神父。因此直到殖民时代结束，瓜图索平原始终不在西班牙人的控制之内。

en: The Malemiut, or Malimiut, are an Iñupiaq people of the northern Seward Peninsula and the Kotzebue Sound shore, whose historic villages included Koyuk, Shaktolik and the summer gathering place of Qikiqtaġruk, now Kotzebue. They speak the Malimiutun dialect of Iñupiaq and were divided into local groups such as the Koyugmiut, Shaktoligmiut and Tapkachmiut, living by coastal seal and beluga hunting and by fishing the rivers that drain into the sound. Qikiqtaġruk had long served as a trade fair visited even by peoples from the Asian side of the Bering Strait when the Russian explorer Otto von Kotzebue surveyed the sound in 1818, after which the Malemiut became increasingly drawn into the Russian fur trade of northwestern Alaska.
zh: 马莱缪特人是居住在苏厄德半岛北部和科策布湾沿岸的因纽皮亚特人，历史上的村庄包括科尤克、沙克图利克和夏季聚会地奇基克塔鲁克（今科策布）。他们使用因纽皮亚特语的马莱缪特方言，下分科尤格缪特、沙克托利格缪特、塔普卡奇缪特等地方群体，在沿海捕猎海豹和白鲸，在注入海湾的各条河流捕鱼。奇基克塔鲁克早就是贸易集市，连白令海峡亚洲一侧的民族也会前来；1818年俄国探险家奥托·冯·科策布考察这个海湾之后，马莱缪特人越来越深地被卷入阿拉斯加西北部的俄国毛皮贸易。

en: The Malibu were a loose complex of riverine tribes of the hot lower Magdalena wetlands of northern Colombia, whose extinct and poorly recorded languages form a family of their own, once grouped with Chibchan but of uncertain kinship. Malibu and the related Mocana, Pacabuey, Mompox and Calamari tongues were heard along the great river from Tamalameque down to Tenerife, beside the Zapatoza lagoon and on the coast south of Cartagena, country of seasonal floods, fishing and manioc fields. The tribes had no single king but acted through alliances and confederations; at the conquest the most powerful chief was Mompoj, who could bring together some fifty small peoples, among them the Malibues, Jaguas, Kimbayes and Chilloas, with the chiefs Zuzua and Mahamon as his lieutenants. The town that took his name, Santa Cruz de Mompox, was founded on 3 May 1537 by Juan Quintero de Heredia, brother of the founder of Cartagena, after his troops defeated Mompoj and the Kimbay. Encomiendas, river traffic and Old World diseases then dissolved the Malibu communities, and their languages vanished with only a handful of words preserved in Spanish chronicles.
zh: 马利布人是哥伦比亚北部马格达莱纳河下游湿热沼泽地带若干河畔部落的松散联合体，他们那些已经消亡、记录寥寥的语言自成一个语系，过去曾被归入奇布查语系，但亲属关系没有定论。马利布语及与之相近的莫卡纳语、帕卡布埃语、蒙波斯语和卡拉马里语，曾通行于从塔马拉梅克到特内里费的大河两岸、萨帕托萨湖周边以及卡塔赫纳以南的沿海地带；那里洪水季节性漫溢，居民以捕鱼和种植木薯为生。各部落没有共主，靠联盟和协约协同行动；征服时代最强大的酋长是蒙波赫，他能召集约五十个小族群，其中包括马利布、哈瓜、金巴耶和奇洛亚等部，酋长苏苏阿和马哈蒙是他的副手。1537年5月3日，卡塔赫纳建立者之弟胡安·金特罗·德·埃雷迪亚率军击败金巴耶部并降服蒙波赫之后，建立了以这位酋长命名的圣克鲁斯-德蒙波斯城。此后监护征赋制、河上贸易和旧大陆传来的疫病瓦解了马利布诸社群，他们的语言也随之消亡，只有零星词汇保存在西班牙编年史中。

en: The Malkanan, also recorded as Malgana, are an Aboriginal people of the Shark Bay hinterland of Western Australia, holding an inland plateau country running south from Hamelin Pool and the Wooramel River toward the Murchison, with the Yingkarta to their north and the Nhantan to their south. Their language belonged to the Kartu branch of the Pama–Nyungan family, and unlike the tribes to their east they did not practise ritual circumcision. In the wet season they dug water soaks and capped them with stones to keep the water through the dry months. Their oral tradition preserves the wreck of the Dutch East India Company ship Zuytdorp on their coast in 1712: survivors camped above the cliffs in houses of salvaged timber and canvas and bartered their stores for native hunting gear, and the story was still being told to British colonists more than a century afterwards. The Malkanan were a small people, sharing customs with the neighbouring Kakarakala groups and overshadowed by the Tedei and Yingkarta.
zh: 马尔卡纳人（又记作马尔加纳人）是西澳大利亚鲨鱼湾腹地的原住民，其内陆台地家园从哈梅林池和伍拉梅尔河向南延伸到默奇森河一带，北邻英加尔达人，南接恩汉塔人。他们的语言属帕马—牛雅语系的卡尔图分支；与东部诸族不同，他们不行仪式性割礼。雨季时他们挖掘蓄水坑，上面盖满石块，使存水熬过旱季。他们的口述传统保存了1712年荷兰东印度公司商船聚特多普号在其海岸失事的往事：幸存者用打捞的木材和帆布在悬崖上搭屋栖身，用储备物资交换原住民的猎具；一个多世纪后英国殖民者到来时，这个故事仍在流传。马尔卡纳人人数不多，习俗与邻近的卡拉卡拉诸群体相近，声势上被特戴人和英加尔达人盖过。

en: The Malpan, more often recorded as the Kalaako or Kalarko, were an Aboriginal people of the Goldfields-Esperance region of southern Western Australia. Their country has been mapped at some 62,000 square kilometres, running north from Green Patch and Scaddan past Widgiemooltha, taking in the later Norseman and Salmon Gums districts, bounded by the Bremer Range to the west and ending short of the Fraser Range in the east, where a red-ochre quarry named Karkanja marked the border. Their language, Galaagu, also called Malpa, is a Pama-Nyungan tongue classified as the closest relative of the Nyungar languages; neighbouring Wudjari called them Malba, the circumcised and subincised people, after their initiation rites. The Ngatjumay lay to their east and the Kalaamaya to their north-east. When the Swan River Colony was founded far to the west in 1829 this inland country was still untouched, and European explorers and prospectors only arrived decades later.
zh: 马尔帕人更常见的记载是卡拉科人（又拼卡拉尔科），是西澳大利亚南部金矿区-埃斯佩兰斯地区的原住民。他们的领地约6.2万平方公里，南起格林帕奇和斯卡登，向北越过威吉穆尔塔，包括后来的诺斯曼和萨蒙加姆斯一带，西以布雷默岭为界，东止于弗雷泽岭以西，边界上的卡尔坎贾是一处红赭石采石场。他们的语言加拉古语又称马尔帕语，属帕马-牛雅语系，被归类为努恩加诸语言最近的亲属；邻近的武贾里人称他们为马尔巴，意为受过割礼和下切礼的人，得名于其入族仪式。恩加朱梅人住在他们东边，卡拉玛亚人住在东北。1829年天鹅河殖民地在遥远的西边建立时，这片内陆地区仍无人涉足，直到数十年后欧洲探险家和淘金者才到来。

en: The Maltese are the island people of Malta, the rocky harbour islands between Sicily and the North African coast. Their language is the clearest mark of their past: Maltese descends from the Siculo-Arabic of Muslim Sicily, brought by settlers who repopulated the islands after the Aghlabid conquest of 870, and after the Norman conquest of 1091 it evolved in isolation, re-Christianized and loaded with Sicilian and Italian words until roughly half its vocabulary was Romance, while keeping a Semitic core and becoming the only Semitic language written in the Latin script. In 1337 Malta belonged to the Aragonese-ruled Kingdom of Sicily, having passed with it through Swabian and Angevin hands, and was governed locally by its nobility through the Università. In 1530 Charles V granted the islands to the Knights Hospitaller expelled from Rhodes, who made Italian their official language, survived the four-month Great Siege of 1565 against Suleiman the Magnificent and built the fortified capital of Valletta. The oldest Maltese text, Pietru Caxaro's poem Il-Kantilena, dates to the fifteenth century. Napoleon seized Malta in 1798, and after two years of local revolt the Congress of Vienna in 1815 confirmed the island under British rule.
zh: 马耳他人是马耳他群岛的岛民，这片多岩石的港湾群岛位于西西里与北非海岸之间。他们的语言最能体现其来历：马耳他语源自穆斯林西西里的西西里-阿拉伯语，由870年阿格拉布王朝征服后重新定居该岛的移民带来；1091年诺曼征服之后，它在孤立环境中演变，随着居民重新基督教化而吸收了大量西西里语和意大利语词汇，约半数词汇变成罗曼语成分，同时保留闪米特语核心，并成为唯一用拉丁字母书写的闪米特语。1337年，马耳他隶属阿拉贡人统治的西西里王国，此前曾随西西里历经施瓦本和安茹家族之手，地方事务由贵族组成的“大学”自治机构管理。1530年，查理五世把群岛封给被逐出罗德岛的医院骑士团；骑士团以意大利语为官方语言，于1565年顶住了苏莱曼大帝历时四个月的马耳他大围攻，并修建了要塞首都瓦莱塔。现存最古老的马耳他语文献是彼得鲁·卡夏罗15世纪的诗作《坎蒂莱纳》。1798年拿破仑夺取马耳他，当地起义两年后，1815年维也纳会议确认该岛由英国统治。

en: The Malto are the Malto-speaking branch of the Sauria Paharia, a Dravidian hill people of the forested Rajmahal Hills, where Jharkhand, West Bengal and Bihar meet. Their tongue is a northern Dravidian language closely related to Kurukh, and Kurukh tradition remembers the Malto as a small group that split off during a migration from the Son valley and followed the Ganges eastward into the hills. They lived by shifting jhum cultivation, hunting and gathering, moving village after a bad harvest and raiding the Bihar plains before vanishing back into the forest; the remoteness of their ridges left them unconquered by the empires claiming the region. Their religion centred on ancestral spirits and a court of nature spirits called Gosain under a sun god. Santal farmers began moving into the hills in the 1790s, and in 1832 the British government formally set aside a large tract of the Damin-i-koh for Santal cultivation; the Malto resisted the influx but were pushed into the remoter forests.
zh: 马尔托人是绍里亚·帕哈里亚人中讲马尔托语的一支，属于达罗毗荼语山地族群，聚居在今贾坎德、西孟加拉和比哈尔交界、森林密布的拉杰马哈尔丘陵。他们的马尔托语是北达罗毗荼语，与库鲁克语关系密切；库鲁克人的传说把马尔托人视为从宋河河谷迁徙时分出的一小支，沿恒河东行进入丘陵。他们以轮垦、狩猎和采集为生，收成不好便整村迁走，还时常下山袭掠比哈尔平原再退回林中；凭借偏远山势，历次宣称统治此地的帝国都未曾真正征服他们。其信仰以祖灵和一组称为戈赛因的自然精灵为核心，尊奉太阳神。桑塔尔农民从18世纪90年代开始迁入丘陵，1832年英国政府又在达明-伊-科赫正式划出大片土地供桑塔尔人开垦；马尔托人虽起而反抗，仍被排挤到更偏远的森林里。

en: The Malvi are the people of the Malwa plateau, the volcanic upland north of the Vindhya Range in west-central India, whose ancient centre was Ujjain, capital of the old Avanti kingdom. Their language is an Indo-Aryan tongue of the Rajasthani group, now written in Devanagari and formerly in the Mahajani merchant script. In 1401 the Delhi governor Dilawar Khan Ghuri made Malwa independent and built his capital at Mandu; his Ghurid line was replaced in 1436 by the Khalji sultans under Mahmud Shah, who carried Malwa's arms into Gujarat, Rajasthan and the Deccan. Rana Sanga of Mewar overran much of the sultanate in 1519, Bahadur Shah of Gujarat stormed Mandu in 1531, and in 1562 Akbar annexed Malwa as a Mughal subah. As Mughal power faded after 1700 the Marathas moved in: Malhar Rao Holkar received most of the region from the Peshwa in 1733, Ranoji Scindia made Ujjain his seat, and the Pawar brothers took Dhar and Dewas. The Holkars ruled from Indore until the Third Anglo-Maratha War of 1818 turned their state into a British princely state.
zh: 摩腊婆人是摩腊婆高原的居民，其地在印度中西部温迪亚山脉以北的火山台地，古老中心是乌贾因，即古代阿万蒂王国的都城。他们的语言属印度—雅利安语系拉贾斯坦语支，文字采用天城体，更早时则使用商人的马哈贾尼文字。1401年，德里派驻的总督迪拉瓦尔·汗·古里宣布摩腊婆独立，定都曼杜；1436年，他的古里家族被马哈茂德沙阿开创的卡尔吉苏丹王朝取代，马哈茂德把摩腊婆的兵锋推进到古吉拉特、拉贾斯坦和德干。1519年梅瓦尔的拉纳·桑伽攻占苏丹国大部，1531年古吉拉特的巴哈杜尔沙阿攻陷曼杜；1562年阿克巴兼并摩腊婆，将其划为莫卧儿的一个苏巴。1700年后莫卧儿势力衰微，马拉地人乘虚而入：马尔哈尔·拉奥·霍尔卡尔于1733年从佩什瓦手中受封摩腊婆大部，拉诺吉·辛迪亚以乌贾因为据点，帕瓦尔兄弟则取得达尔和德瓦斯。霍尔卡尔家族以印多尔为都，直到1818年第三次英国—马拉塔战争后，其土邦沦为英国的附庸邦。

en: The Mam are a Maya people of the western Guatemalan highlands and the Soconusco coast of Chiapas, speaking the Mam language of the Mayan family. Before the Spanish arrival their lordships covered much of what are now the departments of Huehuetenango, San Marcos, Quetzaltenango and Totonicapán, and their Postclassic kingdom was centered on the fortified city of Zaculeu, a site occupied since the Early Classic around the third century. From the twelfth to the fifteenth centuries the expanding K'iche' kingdom of Q'umarkaj conquered the Mam piecemeal; the Popol Vuh dates these campaigns to 1425–1470 under the king K'iq'ab, and Zaculeu became a K'iche' subject city governed by a noble lineage of the conquerors while many Mam commoners stayed on their land. In 1525 Gonzalo de Alvarado y Contreras besieged Zaculeu for several months, until its last ruler Kayb'il B'alam surrendered to starvation and the Mam lands passed under Spanish rule.
zh: 玛姆人是玛雅人的一支，分布在危地马拉西部高地和墨西哥恰帕斯州的索科努斯科沿海，使用玛雅语系的玛姆语。西班牙人到来之前，他们的诸邦占据今韦韦特南戈、圣马科斯、克萨尔特南戈和托托尼卡潘各省的广大地区，后古典期的王国以设防城市萨库莱乌为中心，该城自约3世纪的古典早期起便有人居住。12至15世纪，扩张中的基切王国（都城库马尔卡赫）逐步征服玛姆诸邦；《波波尔·乌》把这些战事系于国王基亚布，时间定为1425—1470年，萨库莱乌沦为基切属城，由征服者的一支贵族统辖，而许多玛姆平民仍留居故土。1525年，贡萨洛·德·阿尔瓦拉多·伊·孔特雷拉斯围攻萨库莱乌数月，末代君主卡伊比尔·巴拉姆因粮绝投降，玛姆之地自此归入西班牙统治。

en: The Mamaceqtaw, whom the Ojibwe and later the French called the Menominee, or wild rice people, are an Algonquian-speaking nation of Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan, who had occupied roughly ten million acres around Green Bay and the Menominee River for more than a thousand years before European contact. Mamaceqtaw means the people in their own language; the French knew them as the folles avoines, after the wild rice that, together with sturgeon, formed the backbone of their diet. French explorers met them in the mid-seventeenth century, when they may have numbered about three thousand, and drew them into the Great Lakes fur trade. They took the French side in the colonial wars and, after initially staying neutral, joined the British in the War of 1812, fighting at the Battle of Mackinac Island. From 1821 onward a series of treaties with the United States, beginning with the cession of their Michigan lands, steadily reduced their territory; Chief Oshkosh resisted pressure to move beyond the Mississippi and kept a homeland for his people on the Wolf River.
zh: 马马切陶人即奥吉布瓦人及后来的法国人所称的梅诺米尼人，意为“野稻人”，是威斯康星和密歇根上半岛的阿尔冈昆语民族；在欧洲人到来之前，他们已在格林贝和梅诺米尼河周围约一千万英亩的土地上生活了一千多年。Mamaceqtaw在本族语中意为“人民”，法国人则称他们为folles avoines（野燕麦），得名于与鲟鱼一同构成其主食的野生稻米。17世纪中叶法国探险家与他们接触，当时他们约有三千人，随后被卷入五大湖毛皮贸易。殖民战争中他们站在法国一边；1812年战争起初保持中立，后来加入英方作战，参加了麦基诺岛战役。从1821年起，与美国签订的一系列条约、最先割让的是他们在密歇根的土地，使其领地不断缩小；酋长奥什科什拒绝迁往密西西比河以西，为族人在沃尔夫河沿岸保住了家园。

en: The Mambai, also written Mambae or Manbae, are the second largest people of East Timor after the Tetun, occupying the mountainous central spine of Timor in the districts of Liquiçá, Ermera, Aileu, Ainaro and Manufahi, around centres such as Balibo. Their language belongs to the Timoric branch of the Central-Eastern Malayo-Polynesian family and splits into northwestern, northeastern-central and southern dialects. The Portuguese knew them as the Maubere, after Mau Bere, a common male name among them, and the word long served as a collective label for the island's inland peoples. Mambai farmers grow maize, rice and root crops in the highlands and traditionally live in circular houses with conical thatched roofs. Mambae was once spoken around the bay of Dili, but after the Portuguese made Dili the capital of Portuguese Timor in 1769 the urban Tetun dialect spread there, and the Tetun of Dili still carries a strong Mambai substrate.
zh: 曼拜人是东帝汶仅次于德顿人的第二大族群，居住在帝汶岛中部多山的脊梁地带，分布于利基萨、埃尔梅拉、艾莱乌、艾纳鲁和马努法希等地，巴里布一带也是其聚居区。他们的语言属中东部马来—波利尼西亚语族的帝汶语支，分为西北、东北中部和南部三种方言。葡萄牙人称他们为莫贝雷，这个称呼来自他们中间常见的男子名马乌·贝雷，长期被用作岛内内陆各族的统称。曼拜人在高地种植玉米、水稻和块根作物，传统上住在圆锥形茅草顶的圆形房屋里。曼拜语曾通行于帝力湾一带，但1769年葡萄牙将帝力定为葡属帝汶首府后，城市德顿方言在当地传播开来，帝力的德顿语也因此带有浓厚的曼拜语底层。

en: The Mamprusi are a Gur-speaking people of the grasslands north of the White Volta, in present-day northern Ghana and Togo, where they farm and raise livestock and speak Mampruli. Their kingdom of Mamprugu was founded around the 1200s when the warrior Naa Gbewaa, grandson of the legendary hunter Tohazie, settled at Pusiga and built a realm stretching into Togo and Burkina Faso. The Mamprusi count themselves the eldest branch of the Mole-Dagbamba peoples, alongside the Dagomba, Nanumba and Mossi; their king, titled the Nayiri and ruling from Nalerigu and Gambaga, held ritual seniority over the related kingdoms and even invested the Mogho Naaba of Ouagadougou, whose royal line descends from Gbewaa's daughter Yennenga. Dyula merchants brought Islam from the 1600s, and the Mamprusi gradually adopted it while keeping chiefly rituals and the ancestral tomb at Pusiga.
zh: 曼普鲁西人是白沃尔特河以北草原（今加纳北部和多哥境内）说古尔语支曼普鲁利语的民族，以农耕和畜牧为生。约13世纪，传奇猎人托哈齐之孙、武士纳·格贝瓦阿在普西加定居，建立曼普鲁古王国，版图延伸到多哥和布基纳法索。曼普鲁西人自认是莫莱-达格班巴族群（与达贡巴、纳农巴、莫西并列）中的长支；他们的国王称纳伊里，王庭设在纳莱里古和甘巴加，仪式地位高于各亲缘王国，连瓦加杜古的莫戈纳巴也由其授予权位，因为莫西王室出自格贝瓦阿之女延嫩加。17世纪（1600年代）起，迪乌拉商人带来伊斯兰教，曼普鲁西人逐渐改宗，同时保留酋长礼仪和普西加的祖先陵墓。

en: The Mamusi are an Austronesian-speaking people of East New Britain Province on the island of New Britain in the Bismarck Archipelago.
zh: 马穆西人是俾斯麦群岛新不列颠岛东新不列颠省的南岛语族群。

en: Managir, also recorded as manjagir, was one of the tribal self-designations used by Evenki bands of the Aldan and Amga taiga, south-east of the Lena in what is now southern Yakutia. These reindeer-hunting clans were drawn into the Russian yasak network as Cossacks pushed east from the Lena along the south Yakutian rivers in the 1600s.
zh: 马纳吉尔（又作 manjagir）是鄂温克游群使用过的部落自称之一，活动在勒拿河东南、今雅库特南部的阿尔丹河与阿姆加河泰加林里。17世纪哥萨克从勒拿河沿南雅库特诸河东进时，这些养鹿狩猎的氏族被纳入俄国雅萨克税网。

en: The Manao were the dominant indigenous people of the Rio Negro in the upper Amazon, whose name, meaning mother of the gods in their own Arawakan tongue, was later given to the city of Manaus. They refused to serve the Portuguese as slaves or converts and repeatedly attacked the Fort of São José da Barra, the nucleus of the future city. Under the chief Ajuricaba they united several neighbouring peoples, raided Portuguese-held villages and ran a watch system over the rivers that stopped colonial craft from sailing upstream, and the resulting Manao War, waged from the lower Rio Negro to the Rio Branco, was only put down in the 1720s. Captured in chains and shipped down the Amazon for trial at Belém, Ajuricaba broke free and drowned himself rather than face slavery, while some two thousand of his people were carried off and sold. Remnant Manao groups were last encountered on the upper Rio Negro in 1819, and the Baniwa of the same river are regarded as their descendants.
zh: 马瑙斯人是上亚马孙内格罗河流域最重要的原住民，族名在本族的阿拉瓦克语中意为众神之母，后来成了马瑙斯城名的由来。他们拒绝为葡萄牙人充当奴隶、拒绝改宗天主教，一再进攻后来发展为马瑙斯城的圣若泽达巴拉要塞。在首领阿茹里卡巴领导下，他们联合数个邻族，袭扰葡萄牙人控制的村落，并建立河上警戒体系，阻止殖民船只逆流而上；由此爆发的马瑙斯战争从内格罗河下游一直打到布朗库河，葡萄牙人直到18世纪20年代才将其镇压。阿茹里卡巴被俘后戴着锁链被押往贝伦受审，途中挣脱束缚投河自尽，宁死不为奴，他的族人约有两千人被掳走贩卖。残余的马瑙斯群体最后一次被人见到是1819年在内格罗河上游，同流域的巴尼瓦人被认为是他们的后裔。

en: The Mandara, who call themselves the Wandala, are a Chadic-speaking people of the iron-rich Mandara Mountains straddling northern Cameroon and northeastern Nigeria, where they farm sorghum in dispersed villages, breed horses and work iron, their smiths forming distinct endogamous castes. Tradition remembers a kingdom founded around 1500 by the ruler Soukda and the hunter Gaya; it appears on Fra Mauro's map of 1459 and was described by Leo Africanus in 1526 as the rich and well-governed land of Medra. About 1580 the war leader Sankre moved the capital to Dulo, and in 1614 the Borno emperor Idris Alooma personally installed his own candidate as king, drawing Mandara into Borno's orbit. Around 1715 the twenty-fifth king, Bukar Aji, took the title of sultan after Muslim visitors converted him, and Islamisation continued through the century. Under Bukar Guiana, who ruled from 1773 to 1828, Mandara defeated Borno in battle about 1781 and drew tribute from some fifteen chiefdoms; in 1809 it repelled the Fulani jihad of Modibo Adama, though renewed raids weakened it thereafter.
zh: 曼达拉人自称万达拉人，是操乍得语的族群，聚居于横跨喀麦隆北部与尼日利亚东北部、富藏铁矿的曼达拉山区，在分散的村落里种植高粱、繁育马匹并冶铁，铁匠构成内婚的特殊种姓。相传他们的王国约在1500年由女王苏克达与猎人加亚创立；1459年弗拉·毛罗的地图已标出它，1526年利奥·阿非利加努斯又把这个富庶而治理有方的国度称为梅德拉。约1580年，军事首领桑克雷把都城迁至杜洛；1614年，博尔努皇帝伊德里斯·阿卢马亲自扶立自己的人选为王，曼达拉从此被纳入博尔努的势力范围。约1715年，第二十五代国王布卡尔·阿吉在穆斯林访客的劝说下改宗，并采用苏丹称号，伊斯兰化在此后的一个世纪里持续推进。1773至1828年在位的布卡尔·圭亚那时期，曼达拉约于1781年击败博尔努，并向约十五个酋长国征收贡赋；1809年，它击退了莫迪博·阿达马发动的富拉尼圣战，但此后不断的袭扰使其日渐衰弱。

en: The Mandarese are the Austronesian people of the western coast of Sulawesi facing the Makassar Strait, around the towns of Mamuju, Majene and Polewali. Their land was never a single state but a league of seventeen small kingdoms: seven upriver realms of the Pitu Ulunna Salu, skilled in the mountains, seven estuary realms of the Pitu Ba'bana Binanga, skilled at sea, and three smaller inland domains. Coastal Mandarese became some of Sulawesi's most respected sailors and fishermen, trading dried and salted fish, coconuts and rice across the strait in their outrigger craft, a skill still celebrated in the Passandeq canoe races. Their language, Mandar, belongs to the Northern South Sulawesi group, closest to Toraja-Sa'dan, and was written in the Lontara script. In the early seventeenth century the wave of Islamisation sweeping the peninsula reached them: Gowa's campaigns of 1608 drew the Mandar coast into the Muslim Makassarese sphere, and the Mandarese adopted Islam while keeping customs close to those of their Bugis neighbours.
zh: 曼达里人是居住在苏拉威西岛西海岸、面朝望加锡海峡的南岛语系族群，聚居于马穆朱、马杰内和波莱瓦利一带。他们的土地从未形成统一国家，而是由十七个小王国组成的联盟：七个擅长山地的上游王国合称“七河源”，七个精通航海的河口王国合称“七河口”，另有三个较小的内陆王国。沿海的曼达里人是苏拉威西最受称道的水手和渔民之一，驾着舷外支架小船跨海峡贩运咸鱼、鱼干、椰子和稻米，这项技艺通过传统的帕桑德独木舟赛代代相传。他们的曼达里语属南苏拉威西语族北支，与托拉查—萨尔丹语最接近，过去用龙塔拉文字书写。17世纪初，席卷半岛的伊斯兰化浪潮波及他们：戈瓦1608年的征战把曼达里海岸纳入穆斯林望加锡势力范围，曼达里人由此改宗伊斯兰教，同时保留了与邻近布吉人类似的风俗。

en: The Mandaya are an Austronesian people of the easternmost reaches of Mindanao, holding the mountain ranges and river headwaters of the old Caraga region along the Pacific coast, in what is now Davao Oriental, with related Mansaka communities in the Davao gulf hinterland. Their name is read as man, first, and daya, upstream, so the first people upstream, and their Mandaya tongue, close to Mansaka, belongs to the Mansakan branch of Philippine languages. They were highland and river-basin farmers of upland rice and root crops, organized under datus and elders beyond the reach of coastal states: when Magellan's chronicler Pigafetta described Butuan and Caraga in 1521, the Spanish record already distinguished the Mandaya and Manobo hinterland tribes from the rajahnate's coastal villages, with which they were often at war. Their country later fell partly under the sway of the Sultanate of Maguindanao, though chiefly through tribute and trade rather than direct rule, and Islam made few converts among the mountains, where an animist cosmology of ancestor spirits and the great moon-swallowing serpent Tambanokano survived. A permanent Spanish settlement was established in the region in 1591, but garrisons and missions clung to the coast, and the Mandaya kept their valley autonomy, their weaving and their datu rivalries through the rest of the period.
zh: 曼达亚人是棉兰老最东端的南岛语系民族，据有太平洋沿岸古卡拉加地区的山脉与河源地带，即今东达沃省一带，亲缘的曼萨卡人则住在达沃湾腹地。其族名可解作“曼”（最初）与“达亚”（上游），意为“上游的初民”；他们的曼达亚语接近曼萨卡语，属于菲律宾语言的曼萨卡语支。他们在高地和河谷种植旱稻与块根作物，社会由“达图”和长老治理，游离于沿海政权之外：1521年麦哲伦的记述者皮加费塔描写武端和卡拉加时，西班牙文献已把曼达亚、马诺博等腹地部落与拉惹国治下的沿海村落区分开来，双方还时常交战。后来他们的土地部分落入马京达瑙苏丹国的势力范围，但主要是朝贡和贸易关系而非直接统治，伊斯兰教在山区几乎没有信徒，敬拜祖灵、讲述吞月巨蛇“坦巴诺卡诺”的万物有灵宇宙观得以延续。1591年西班牙在这一地区建立永久定居点，但驻军和传教仅盘踞沿海，曼达亚人在此后的岁月里保住了河谷自治、纺织技艺和达图之间的角逐。

en: The Mandaeans are a closed Gnostic ethnoreligious community of the lower Tigris and Euphrates, centered on the marshlands and river towns of southern Iraq around Basra, Wasit and Baghdad. Their own tradition, recorded in the scroll Haran Gawaita, traces them to Nasoraean migrants who left Judea for Mesopotamia in the first centuries of the Christian era, and scholars place an established Mandaean community in Sasanian Babylonia by late antiquity. They venerate John the Baptist as the final prophet and practise repeated baptism in running water, while their scriptures are written in Mandaic, an Eastern Aramaic language with its own script. Under Abbasid rule they claimed the name of the Sabians, the protected people of the book named in the Quran, to secure dhimmi status; the vizier Ibn Muqla is the earliest authority to call them Sabians, in the early tenth century. The Dominican friar Riccoldo da Monte di Croce met them in Mesopotamia around 1290, and Carmelite missionaries in Basra in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries dubbed them Christians of Saint John. Over these centuries Arabic displaced Mandaic as everyday speech, though the classical language survived in liturgy.
zh: 曼达人是生活在底格里斯河与幼发拉底河下游的封闭型诺斯替族群，聚居于伊拉克南部的沼泽与河港，以巴士拉、瓦西特和巴格达一带为中心。他们的经典《哈兰·盖瓦塔》自称源自公元最初几百年离开犹太地区东迁美索不达米亚的拿索拉人，学者认为至迟在古代晚期，萨珊王朝治下的巴比伦尼亚已有成形的曼达社群。曼达人尊施洗约翰为最后一位先知，反复在活水中举行洗礼，经典用东阿拉米语的曼达语及独有的曼达文字写成。阿拔斯王朝时期，他们自称《古兰经》中受保护的“有经人”萨比人，以取得迪米地位；10世纪初的维齐尔伊本·穆格莱是最早明确以萨比人称呼他们的权威。1290年前后，多明我会修士里科尔多·达·蒙特迪克罗切在美索不达米亚见到他们；16至17世纪驻巴士拉的加尔默罗会传教士则称他们为“圣约翰的基督徒”。这几百年间，阿拉伯语逐渐取代曼达语成为日常用语，古典曼达语只保留在礼仪之中。

en: The Mandinka, also called Malinke, are the largest of the Mandé peoples, farming the West Sudanian savanna from their homeland of Manden on the upper Niger, where towns such as Niani and Kita stood. They speak Manding languages and live in self-ruled village communities led by chiefs and elders, with a stratified society of nobles, smiths and the griot caste known as jalolu, who carry their history in song. As the Ghana Empire of Wagadu broke apart in the eleventh century, Manden split into small kingdoms until the prince Sundiata Keita defeated the Sosso around 1235 and founded the Mali Empire under the Kouroukan Fouga charter. In 1337 the Mandinka were the ruling people of the largest state in West Africa, just after the reign of Mansa Musa, whose pilgrimage to Mecca of 1324 to 1326 flooded Egypt with gold and whose patronage made Timbuktu a city of mosques and Islamic learning. Weak mansas followed: the Tuareg took Timbuktu in 1433, the Songhai seized Mema in 1465 and sacked the Malian capital in 1544, and defeat by the Moroccans at Jenne in 1599 broke the empire, which ended around 1610 when the Keita rulers withdrew to Kangaba as provincial chiefs. Mandinka migrants had meanwhile carried their speech westward under the general Tiramakhan Traore, founding the kingdom of Kaabu; in later centuries Fulani jihads from Futa Jallon and the Atlantic slave trade reshaped the scattered Mandinka kingdoms.
zh: 曼丁戈人又称马林克人，是曼德诸族中最大的一支，在尼日尔河上游的故乡曼丁一带的苏丹稀树草原务农，尼亚尼、基塔等城镇都在这一地区。他们操曼丁诸语，住在由酋长和长老自治的村社里，社会按贵族、铁匠和被称为贾卢的格里奥吟游诗人等种姓分层，历史靠歌者代代传唱。11世纪瓦加杜的加纳帝国瓦解后，曼丁分裂为众多小邦，直到王子松迪亚塔·凯塔约于1235年击败苏苏，依据《库鲁坎富加》宪章建立马里帝国。1337年，曼丁戈人是西非最大国家的统治民族，此时正值曼萨·穆萨在位之后不久——他在1324至1326年赴麦加朝觐，大量黄金涌入埃及，又在其扶持下使廷巴克图成为清真寺与伊斯兰学术之城。其后的曼萨们软弱无力：图阿雷格人1433年夺取廷巴克图，桑海人1465年攻占梅马、1544年洗劫马里都城，1599年马里在杰内被摩洛哥人击败，帝国随之崩溃，约1610年凯塔王室退居康加巴，沦为地方酋长。与此同时，曼丁戈移民在将领特拉奥雷·提拉马汉率领下把语言带到西方，建立卡布王国；在后来的几百年里，富塔贾隆的富拉尼圣战和大西洋奴隶贸易又重塑了这些分散的曼丁戈小国。

en: The Mandja are a Gbaya-related people of central Central African Republic, living around the Ouham River near the Chad border with offshoots in Cameroon and Chad, and speaking Manza, a Ubangian language close to Ngbaka. Partly nomadic in ancestry, they had no single ruler, regional chiefs gathering their clans only for war.
zh: 曼贾人是与格巴亚人相近的族群，住在中非共和国中部的乌哈姆河一带、邻近乍得边境，部分支系进入喀麦隆和乍得，操与恩格巴卡语相近的乌班吉语支语言曼扎语。他们的祖先部分过着半游牧生活，没有统一的首领，只在战时由各地酋长召集氏族。

en: The Manek'enk, called Haush by the Selk'nam and Eastern Ona by the Yahgan, were the indigenous people of the Mitre Peninsula at the far eastern tip of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego. They were probably the island's first inhabitants, until Selk'nam newcomers from the mainland killed or absorbed most of them and confined the survivors to the rainy, wind-swept peninsula. Their language belonged to the Chonan family, close to that of the Selk'nam though only mutually intelligible with difficulty. Like the Selk'nam and the Tehuelche of the mainland, they were land hunters who used no watercraft, living in patrilineal family bands that each held a strip of coast and inland hunting ground; because guanacos were scarce in their territory, they drew most of their meat from seals and sea lions and probably traded with the Selk'nam for guanaco skins. The Garcia de Nodal expedition met them at Good Success Bay in 1619, and later visits by a Jesuit in 1711, James Cook in 1769 and the Beagle with Charles Darwin in 1832 made their camps known to Europeans. Estimates from 1836 put the Manek'enk at only two or three hundred people.
zh: 马内肯克人自称马内肯克，塞尔克南人称之为豪什，雅甘人则称他们为东奥纳。他们居住在火地岛大火地岛最东端的米特雷半岛，很可能是该岛最早的居民；后来来自大陆的塞尔克南人迁入，杀死或同化了大部分马内肯克人，把幸存者压缩到多雨多风的半岛上。他们的语言属乔南语系，与塞尔克南语相近，但只能勉强互通。和塞尔克南人以及大陆上的特维尔切人一样，他们是不使用舟船的陆地猎人，按父系组成家族群，每个群体占有一条从海岸延伸到内陆猎场的土地；由于境内原驼稀少，他们的肉食主要取自海豹和海狮，并很可能与塞尔克南人交换原驼皮。1619年加西亚·德·诺达尔探险队在好成功湾与他们相遇，此后1711年的耶稣会士、1769年的詹姆斯·库克以及1832年搭载查尔斯·达尔文的贝格尔号先后到访，使他们的营地为欧洲人所知。1836年的估计认为马内肯克人只剩下两三百人。

en: The Mangareva are the Polynesian people of the Gambier Islands, a small volcanic group at the south-eastern edge of the Tuamotu, whose high islands of Mangareva, Taravai, Aukena and Akamaru ring a single lagoon. Settled from the Society Islands around the year 1000, they lived in a strictly stratified tribal society of warring clans, haunted by intermittent famine; trade by canoe linked them with the distant Pitcairn Islands until deforestation between the tenth and fifteenth centuries stripped their hills and broke the network. Their scholars developed a binary-style counting system built on units of ten, twenty, forty and eighty, centuries before the European invention of binary arithmetic, and their pantheon included the war god Tu and the demi-god Māui. The British captain James Wilson, arriving on the missionary ship Duff in 1797, was the first European visitor and named the group after Admiral James Gambier; Frederick Beechey followed in HMS Blossom in 1825. Civil war between the social classes had already shaken the islands when Catholic priests Honoré Laval and François Caret landed in 1834 and converted King Maputeoa, who was baptised in 1836.
zh: 芒阿雷瓦人是甘比尔群岛的波利尼西亚人。甘比尔是土阿莫土群岛东南端的小型火山岛群，芒阿雷瓦、塔拉瓦伊、奥克纳和阿卡马鲁等高地岛屿环绕着同一个潟湖。他们约在1000年从社会群岛迁来，生活在等级森严的部落社会里，氏族争战不断，还不时遭遇饥荒；独木舟贸易曾把他们与遥远的皮特凯恩群岛连在一起，直到10世纪至15世纪的滥伐使山岭光秃、贸易网络瓦解。当地学者还发展出以十、二十、四十、八十为单位的二进制式计数法，比欧洲人发明二进制算术早了数百年；他们的神灵包括战神图和半神毛伊。1797年，英国船长詹姆斯·威尔逊乘传教船“达夫号”最先到来，以詹姆斯·甘比尔上将之名为群岛命名；弗雷德里克·比奇1825年乘“布洛瑟姆号”继至。社会阶层之间的内战早已动摇群岛，1834年天主教神父奥诺雷·拉瓦尔和弗朗索瓦·卡雷登陆，使国王马普特奥阿皈依，并于1836年为他施洗。

en: The Manggarai, who call themselves Ata Manggarai, are the Austronesian people of western Flores, speaking Tombo Manggarai across five dialect groups. Their highlands were coveted by outside powers: the Makassarese of Gowa in Sulawesi and the Bima Sultanate of neighbouring Sumbawa both claimed overlordship. In the 1600s the tribal kingdom of Todo arose under Mashur, a prince of Minangkabau descent sent from Gowa, and Todo, Cibal and Bajo became the three greatest of the local kedaluan, or tributary chiefdoms. In 1727 the region passed to Bima as the dowry of the Makassarese princess Daeng Tamima, and Bima placed governors, or naib, over the coastal towns of Reo and Pota. An agreement of 1783 with Sultan Abdulkadim confined Muslim settlers to the coast, leaving the inland Manggarai to their ancestor cult of the creator Mori Karaeng, celebrated with buffalo sacrifices.
zh: 芒加莱人自称阿塔·芒加莱，是弗洛勒斯岛西部的南岛语族群，操分为五个方言群的通博·芒加莱语。他们的高地为外来强权所觊觎：苏拉威西戈瓦苏丹国的望加锡人和邻岛松巴哇的比马苏丹国都曾宣示宗主权。17世纪，托多部落王国在戈瓦派来、具有米南佳保血统的王子马舒尔领导下兴起，托多、奇巴尔和巴乔成为当地最大的三个克达卢安，即纳贡酋邦。1727年，随着望加锡公主达英·塔米玛出嫁，该地区作为嫁妆划归比马，比马向沿海城镇雷奥和波塔派驻名为纳伊布的总督。1783年与苏丹阿卜杜勒·卡迪姆达成的协议把穆斯林定居者限制在沿海，内陆的芒加莱人得以保留对创世神莫里·卡朗的祖先崇拜，以及献祭水牛的祭典。

en: Mangyan is the collective name for the eight indigenous peoples of Mindoro, among them the Iraya, Alangan, Tadyawan, Tawbuid, Buhid and Hanunoo, each speaking its own Austronesian language. They were once the sole inhabitants of the island that Chinese traders called Ma-i, whose trade with the Song court is recorded as early as 972: coastal Mangyan exchanged beeswax, pearls, cotton and tortoiseshell for Chinese porcelain and iron, wares still dug up in their burial caves. Originally shore dwellers, they drifted inland and up into the Mindoro mountains to escape incoming Tagalog settlers, Spanish conquest and conversion, and the slaving raids of Moro fleets, so that under Spanish rule the lowlands became Christian Tagalog country while groups such as the Iraya kept apart in the highlands, descending only to trade forest produce. The southern groups, present on the island by about 900, developed weaving, pottery and the surat Mangyan, a syllabic script of Indic origin still carved on bamboo, together with the ambahan, a seven-syllable recited poetry. Most Mangyan lived by swidden fields of upland rice, sweet potato and taro, hunting and gathering under an animist religion of rice spirits and ancestor souls, and the wars between Spaniards and Moros that depopulated the coasts in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries left the interior as their lasting refuge.
zh: 芒扬人是民都洛岛八个原住民族群的统称，包括伊拉雅、阿兰甘、塔迪亚万、陶布德、布希德和哈努诺等支系，各有自己的南岛语系语言。他们曾是这座岛的唯一居民，中国商人称该岛为“麻逸”，早在972年就有其与宋朝贸易的记载：沿海芒扬人用蜂蜡、珍珠、棉布和玳瑁交换中国瓷器和铁器，这些器物在他们的墓葬洞穴中多有出土。他们原本居住在海边，后来为躲避他加禄移民的涌入、西班牙人的征服与传教以及摩洛舰队的掳奴袭击，逐渐迁入内陆和民都洛山区；于是在西班牙统治下，低地成为信奉基督教的他加禄人的地盘，伊拉雅等支系则在高地保持孤立，只在交易山林物产时下山。约900年前后已在岛上的南部支系发展出纺织、制陶和源自印度文字体系的“苏拉特芒扬”音节文字，仍刻写在竹片上，与之相伴的还有七音节的吟诵诗“安巴汉”。多数芒扬人在高地种植旱稻、甘薯和芋头，兼事狩猎采集，信奉稻米精灵与祖灵的万物有灵信仰；17至18世纪西班牙人与摩洛人的战争使沿海人口凋零，内陆山区由此成为他们持久的避难所。

en: The Manjak, also called Manjaco or Manjaku, are a West Atlantic people of the mangrove coast of northern Guinea-Bissau, concentrated in the Bassarel and Babok lands around Cacheu, with smaller communities in Casamance and Gambia. They speak a language of the Bak group and built one of the most productive farming systems of the West African coast, the bolanhas: networks of dikes and drainage canals that turn mangrove swamp into flooded rice paddies, which early Portuguese visitors described with admiration. Their villages were held in a layered, semi-feudal order of landowners and chiefs owing rice tribute to the king of Bassarel, who presided over a loose federation of the neighbouring districts. Portuguese mariners made contact in the late 1400s and built a trading post at Cacheu, but for centuries its commanders paid tribute to Manjak rulers, whose rice lands and palm-oil groves kept them autonomous and prosperous long after the coast had been drawn into the Atlantic trade.
zh: 曼扎克人又称曼贾科人或曼贾库人，是说西非大西洋语支巴克语组语言的民族，聚居于几内亚比绍北部沿海卡谢乌一带的巴萨雷尔和巴博克地区，在卡萨芒斯和冈比亚也有较小的社群。他们建成了西非海岸最高产的农耕体系之一博兰尼亚，即凭借堤坝和排灌渠网把红树林沼泽改造成连片的淹水稻田，令早期葡萄牙访客赞叹不已。他们的村庄处在层层分封的半封建秩序中，地主和酋长向巴萨雷尔国王缴纳稻米贡赋，国王则统领邻近各区组成的松散联盟。葡萄牙航海者在15世纪末与他们接触，并在卡谢乌设立商站，但此后数百年间商站长官反而要向曼扎克统治者纳贡；在海岸被卷入大西洋贸易之后很久，曼扎克人的稻田和棕榈油林仍支撑着他们的自治与富庶。

en: Manjiang, or Man speech, is an Eastern Min dialect of the border hills where southern Zhejiang meets northern Fujian, spoken chiefly in Taishun and Cangnan counties of Wenzhou and in parts of Qingyuan. Together with the related Manhua of the Cangnan coast it forms the Man subgroup of Eastern Min, shading into the Shouning speech of Funing on the Fujian side and into Wu Chinese around Wenzhou. Its vocabulary and sounds keep a strong indigenous substratum, possibly Austroasiatic or Tai-Kadai, left by the Yue peoples before Han settlement. Local genealogies trace the speaker families mainly to migrants who came from Wenzhou and Fujian between the Tang and the Yuan. Early Ming settlers opened mines in these hills, and after a miners' revolt the court set up Taishun county in 1452, with the market town of Luoyang as its seat, to bring the mountain border under direct rule.
zh: 蛮讲又称蛮话，是浙南与闽东北交界山区的一种闽东语方言，主要通行于温州的泰顺、苍南和丽水庆元的部分地区。它和苍南沿海的蛮话亲缘相近，合称闽东语蛮讲片：往南与福建福宁片的寿宁话连成一片，往北则向温州一带的吴语过渡。蛮讲的词汇和语音保留着浓厚的土著语言底层，可能来自汉族定居之前百越人的南亚语或侗台语。当地族谱显示，蛮讲居民的家族主要是唐代至元代间从温州和福建迁入的移民后裔。明初外来移民入山采矿，矿工叛乱被镇压后，朝廷于1452年设置泰顺县，以罗阳镇为县治，把这片浙闽交界的山区纳入直接管辖。

en: The Manobo, the hispanicized form of their endonym Manuvu, meaning the native-grown people, are the largest and most varied cluster of indigenous peoples in Mindanao, whose subgroups, among them the Agusan, Cotabato, Banwaon, Higaonon, Bagobo and Bukidnon Manobo, spread through the river valleys of Agusan, Cotabato, Davao, Bukidnon and Surigao. They speak the many Manobo languages of the Austronesian family and lived by shifting rice cultivation, hunting and river trade in villages led by datus, keeping an animist religion of ancestor and forest spirits. While the Manobo held the interior, the coast of Agusan was dominated by the Indianized rajahnate of Butuan, a gold-trading port whose balangay outrigger ships carried tribute missions to the Song court from 1001 and whose wares reached China, Champa and Persia; Spanish accounts stress that the Manobo and Mandaya highlanders lay outside the rajah's authority and were often at war with the coastal towns. In 1304 Chinese annals record Brunei conquering Butuan, and when Magellan's expedition reached the area in 1521 Islam had made only superficial headway among the coast dwellers. Legazpi assigned Butuan as an encomienda in 1571, Jesuits opened a mission there in 1596 and the first church was built in 1597, yet the riverine Manobo communities beyond the settlements kept their autonomy, their datu rivalries and their forest economy through the centuries of Moro raiding and Spanish rule.
zh: 马诺博人自称“马努武”，意为“土生土长的人”，“马诺博”是其西班牙语化拼写。他们是棉兰老规模最大、支系最庞杂的原住民族群集合，阿古桑、哥打巴托、班瓦翁、希加奥农、巴戈博和布基农等支系散布在阿古桑、哥打巴托、达沃、布基农和苏里高的河谷地带。他们使用南岛语系下众多的马诺博语言，以轮垦稻作、狩猎和河上贸易为生，村落由“达图”首领统领，信奉祖灵与森林精灵的万物有灵信仰。马诺博人据有腹地，阿古桑沿海则被印度化的武端拉惹国控制：这个黄金贸易港的“巴朗盖”舷外架船自1001年起载着朝贡使团前往宋朝宫廷，商货远达中国、占婆和波斯；但西班牙人的记述强调，马诺博和曼达亚山地人不在拉惹的权威之内，还常与沿海城镇交战。1304年中国史籍记载文莱征服武端；1521年麦哲伦船队抵达时，伊斯兰教在沿海居民中只取得浅层影响。1571年黎牙实比把武端划为封地，1596年耶稣会在此开教，1597年建起第一座教堂，但定居点之外沿河而居的马诺博社群在摩洛袭掠和西班牙统治的数百年间，始终保有自治、达图间的角逐和山林经济。

en: The Manoki, historically also called Irantxe, are an Indigenous people of western Mato Grosso in Brazil, whose villages stood along rivers of the Juruena basin such as the Cravari; their oral history recalls a time when about twenty-seven communal longhouses lined the waterways. Their tongue, Irantxe, is a language isolate with no known relatives, shared with the related Mỹky band.
zh: 马诺基人旧称伊兰特谢人，是巴西马托格罗索州西部的原住民族群，村落分布在茹鲁埃纳流域的克拉瓦里河等河流沿岸；据他们口传，过去沿河曾有约二十七座集体长屋。他们使用的伊兰特谢语是一门没有已知亲属语言的孤立语言，与其亲缘支系米基人共用。

en: The Mansi, known to Russians until modern times as the Voguls, are the western Ob-Ugric people, whose speech is one of the closest relatives of Hungarian, and their ancestors once lived west of the Urals, where their traces have been found near Perm, before crossing into western Siberia in the first millennium BC and merging with the local population. Novgorod's bid for their land, called Yugra in the chronicles, began with the posadnik Uleb Ragnvaldsson's defeated expedition beyond Syktyvkar, but real Russian power reached the northern Urals only much later. In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the Mansi were organized into principalities such as Kondia, Sosva and Bardak, some loosely subject to Moscow, some to the Sibir Khanate, and their war parties raided deep into Russian districts. Yermak's Cossack offensive at the end of the sixteenth century opened decades of war: Kondia, the strongest principality, refused yasak until 1620, besieged Beryozovo in 1609 in alliance with Khanty lords and other Mansi princes, and drove out the first missionaries, while the Bardak princes of the Surgut area were crushed only after their raid on Surgut in 1691. Not until the eighteenth century did the last independent Mansi clans submit, and even then baptism sat lightly over the old bear cult, with its multi-day celebration of songs, dances and plays after a bear hunt, while hunting, fishing and reindeer remained the base of life.
zh: 曼西人在近代以前一直被俄国人称为沃古尔人，是偏西的一支鄂毕-乌戈尔民族，语言与匈牙利语亲缘最近；他们的先民原本住在乌拉尔山以西，彼尔姆附近已发现其遗迹，公元前1千纪才越过乌拉尔山进入西西伯利亚，与当地居民融合。诺夫哥罗德对编年史所称尤格拉之地的觊觎，始于行政长官乌列布·拉格瓦尔德松在瑟克特夫卡尔以外折戟的远征，但俄国的实际势力很久以后才到达北乌拉尔。15至16世纪，曼西人组成孔迪亚、索西瓦、巴尔达克等若干公国，有的松散臣属莫斯科，有的归附西伯利亚汗国，其战队还深入俄境劫掠。16世纪末叶尔马克的哥萨克攻势开启了数十年战争：最强大的孔迪亚公国在1620年前拒不缴纳亚萨克，1609年联合汉特诸王公和其他曼西领主围攻别廖佐沃，并赶走了首批传教士；苏尔古特一带的巴尔达克王公则在1691年袭击苏尔古特后才被剿灭。直到18世纪，最后一批独立的曼西氏族才臣服，而洗礼也未能覆盖古老的熊崇拜——猎熊之后要举行持续数日、载歌载舞并表演戏剧的熊节；狩猎、捕鱼和养鹿始终是他们的生计根本。

en: The Manta were the northern branch of the Manteño coastal tradition, one of the last great pre-Columbian cultures of the Ecuadorian Pacific seaboard, flourishing from about 850 along the shores of Manabí between the Bay of Caráquez and the Chone and Portoviejo rivers, with Picoazá as a leading chiefdom and ceremonial centres at Cerro de Hojas and Cerro Jaboncillo. Their towns, built of cane and palm on river-stone foundations, were linked less as a kingdom than as a trading ring, and Manteño divers harvested the Spondylus shell of the warm coastal waters, working its purple and orange valves into ornaments and currency that travelled as far as Mexico. The Incas never conquered them: the Manta bought peace with the sacred shells. They were still independent when Pedro de Alvarado explored their coast in 1534, and Francisco Pacheco founded Portoviejo among them in 1535, after which epidemic disease and colonial rule dissolved the chiefdoms into the new coastal society.
zh: 曼塔人是曼塔尼奥海洋文化传统的北支，也是厄瓜多尔太平洋沿岸最后一批重要的前哥伦布文化，约850年起活跃于马纳比省海岸，分布在卡拉克斯湾与乔内河、波托维耶霍河之间，以皮科阿萨为主要酋邦，在奥哈斯山和哈翁西约山设有祭祀中心。他们的村镇以竹藤和棕榈搭成、河卵石筑基，彼此并非王国而是类似商环的联盟；曼塔潜水员采捞暖水海域特有的海菊蛤，把紫橙双色贝壳制成饰物和货币，贸易远达墨西哥。印加人始终未能征服他们，曼塔人以这种神圣贝壳换取和平。1534年佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多勘察其海岸时，他们仍保持独立；1535年弗朗西斯科·帕切科在其地建立波托维耶霍，此后疫病与殖民统治使各酋邦消融于新的沿海社会。

en: The Manubara are a Papuan people of the Bird's Tail of New Guinea, whose speech, also called Maria or Gebi, is one of the two Manubaran languages, the other being Doromu. The Manubaran family belongs to the Trans–New Guinea phylum and is centred on Mount Brown in Central Province, where Manubara and Doromu villages share the same mountain country.
zh: 马努巴拉人是新几内亚“鸟尾”的巴布亚族群，他们的语言又称玛丽亚语或格比语，是马努巴兰语族仅有的两种语言之一，另一种是多罗穆语。马努巴兰语族属跨新几内亚语系，以中央省的布朗山为中心，马努巴拉人与多罗穆人的村落同在这片山地。

en: The Manus are the seafaring people of the Admiralty or Manus Islands, a rainforested chain of about forty islands north of New Guinea of which volcanic Manus is by far the largest. Human settlement goes back roughly forty thousand years, and islanders cultivated taro and traded obsidian across the archipelago long before the Lapita culture reached the islands around three and a half thousand years ago. The historic Manus built their villages on stilts over the sea and spoke a cluster of two dozen closely related Oceanic languages forming the Manus subgroup, the best known being Titan, also called Manus proper. Spanish ships under Álvaro de Saavedra first sighted the islands in 1528 and met canoe parties armed with bows, the Dutchman Willem Schouten followed in 1616, and Philip Carteret gave the group its European name of Admiralty Islands in 1767.
zh: 马努斯人是阿德默勒尔蒂群岛（又称马努斯群岛）上以航海为生的族群；这是新几内亚岛以北约四十个岛屿组成的雨林岛链，其中火山岛马努斯岛面积最大。人类在此定居的历史约有四万年，早在约三千五百年前拉皮塔文化到来之前，岛民就已种植芋头，并在群岛之间贩运黑曜石。历史上的马努斯人把村落建在海面之上的高脚屋里，操二十多种彼此相近的大洋洲语言，合称马努斯语群，其中最著名的是又称“真正马努斯语”的泰坦语。1528年，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨韦德拉率领的西班牙船队首次望见这群岛屿，并遭遇了乘独木舟、持弓箭而来的岛民；荷兰人威廉·斯豪滕于1616年再度到访，菲利普·卡特雷特则在1767年以欧洲语言将其命名为阿德默勒尔蒂群岛。

en: The Māʼohi, or Tahitians, are the indigenous Polynesian people of Tahiti and the other Society Islands. Their ancestors reached the islands around the year 400, sailing by way of the Cook Islands from the Samoan homeland, and they cleared the volcanic soils for gardens while building fishing canoes with tools of stone, shell, bone and wood. Their society was split into three ranks, the chiefly ariʼi, the landholding raʼatira and the commoner manahune, and rival districts fought one another with fleets of war canoes. Sustained European contact began in 1767, when Samuel Wallis brought the British ship Dolphin into Matavai Bay; Louis-Antoine de Bougainville arrived the next year. The chief Tu, later called Pōmare, used European weapons to unite Tahiti, Moorea and the neighbouring islands by 1788 and found the Pōmare dynasty, whose rulers turned to Protestantism under the London Missionary Society in the 1810s. Diseases from the visiting ships cut the population from perhaps 110,000 at contact to roughly 15,300 by 1830, while the Pōmare kings extended their influence over the Society Islands, the Austral Islands and the Tuamotu Archipelago.
zh: 毛希人即塔希提人，是塔希提岛及社会群岛其他岛屿的波利尼西亚原住民。他们的祖先约在400年从萨摩亚故土出发，经库克群岛航行至此，开垦火山沃土开辟园圃，用石、贝、骨、木制作工具，建造捕鱼独木舟。社会分为三个等级：首领阶层阿里伊、拥有土地的拉阿提拉，以及平民马纳胡内；对立的各地区常常组成战舟舰队彼此攻伐。与欧洲人的持续接触始于1767年，塞缪尔·沃利斯率英国船“海豚号”驶入马塔瓦伊湾，路易-安托万·德·布干维尔次年抵达。酋长图（后称波马雷）借助欧洲火器，于1788年统一塔希提、莫雷阿及邻近岛屿，建立波马雷王朝；19世纪10年代，王朝统治者在伦敦传道会影响下改宗新教。来访船只带来的疾病使人口从接触时的约11万锐减到1830年的约1.53万，波马雷诸王则把势力扩展到社会群岛、南方群岛和土阿莫土群岛。

en: The Maonan, who call themselves Anan, meaning local people, are a Kam-Sui people of the karst hills of northwest Guangxi, centred on Huanjiang in the Hechi country, with smaller communities in Nandan and across the border in southern Guizhou.
