Chinese records trace their ancestors to the Liao peoples known before the Tang dynasty of 618 to 907, and to the Ling tribes listed under the Song, Yuan and Ming between 960 and 1644; their name appears in chronicles as Maotan, Maonan and other spellings before settling as Maonan. They speak Maonan, a Kam-Sui language of the Kra-Dai family without a native script, writing in Chinese or Zhuang. More than four in five bear the surname Tan, a clan whose genealogy says migrants from Hunan married local women, and they live in compact clan villages of plank-and-clay stilt houses. They farm dry-land grains and rice where the valleys allow, with livestock raising as a sideline, are skilled bamboo weavers whose finely woven hats serve as betrothal gifts, and keep household shrines mixing ancestor tablets with Taoist and Chinese folk deities.
zh: 毛南人自称阿南，意为当地人，是壮侗语族侗水语支的民族，聚居在广西西北部喀斯特山区的环江（属河池地区），南丹及相邻的贵州南部也有分布。史籍把他们的祖先追溯到唐代（618—907年）以前的僚人，以及960至1644年间宋、元、明三代记载中的伶人，其族名在文献中先后写作茅滩、茆滩、茅难、冒南、毛难，最后定为毛南。他们使用的毛南语属侗水语支，没有本民族文字，书面通用汉文或壮文。八成以上的人姓谭，谭氏族谱称先祖是来自湖南的移民，与当地女子通婚；毛南村落按宗族聚居，住干栏式板土墙屋。他们种植杂粮，少数谷地种稻，兼营养畜，竹编手艺精巧，编织细密的竹帽是男女定情之物；家中神龛同时供奉祖先牌位与道教和汉族民间信仰的诸神。

en: The Māori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, descended from East Polynesian voyagers who reached the islands in ocean-going canoes, or waka, in several planned landings between roughly 1320 and 1350. Cut off for centuries, they developed their own language, mythology and crafts, and in the fifteenth century a branch moved to the Chatham Islands and became the Moriori. Their society was built on extended families, clans and tribes, the whānau, hapū and iwi, ranked into chiefs, commoners and slaves, while expert priests, the tohunga, guarded oral genealogies and skills; rival tribes competed for land and prestige from fortified hill villages, or pā. European contact began in the eighteenth century, and Māori quickly took up iron tools, potatoes and firearms. The musket trade fed the Musket Wars that opened in 1806, as many as three thousand raids and battles in which twenty to forty thousand people died and tens of thousands were enslaved, redrawing the tribal map. The Ngāpuhi chief Hongi Hika launched the first great raids from 1818, and in 1835 invading tribes destroyed the Moriori community on the Chatham Islands; by the 1830s, when the fighting peaked, every main region had been drawn into the arms race.
zh: 毛利人是新西兰的波利尼西亚原住民，先民是东波利尼西亚航海者，约在1320至1350年间分乘远洋独木舟有计划地分批抵达。此后数百年与世隔绝，发展出独有的语言、神话和工艺；15世纪一支毛利人迁往查塔姆群岛，成为莫里奥里人。其社会以大家族、氏族和部落为骨架，分为酋长、平民和奴隶，精通秘术的祭司负责口传谱系与技艺；敌对部落为土地和声威常年征战，据守称为“帕”的山顶堡垒村。18世纪欧洲人到来后，毛利人很快采用了铁器、马铃薯和火器。火枪贸易点燃了始于1806年的火枪战争：多达三千次袭击和战斗造成两万至四万人死亡、数万人被掳为奴，部落版图被彻底改写。纳普希族酋长洪吉·希卡从1818年起发动首批大规模远征，1835年入侵诸部又在查塔姆群岛摧毁莫里奥里人社群；到19世纪30年代战事达到顶峰时，各主要地区都已卷入这场军备竞赛。

en: The Mapuche, also called Araucanians, are the Indigenous people of south-central Chile and the neighbouring Andes and Pampas of Argentina, united by the Mapudungun language and a society of extended families led by lonko chiefs, who in wartime elected a toki, or axe-bearer, to command them. Archaeology places their culture in the Chilean river valleys as early as 600 to 500 BC, and they halted the southward march of the Inca Empire in the battle of the Maule River. At the coming of the Spaniards their homeland ran from the Choapa Valley to the Chiloé Archipelago, divided among Picunche, Moluche, Williche and Cunco groups. Pedro de Valdivia founded Santiago in 1541 and pushed south, but the Arauco War broke out in 1550: the toqui Caupolicán and his lieutenant Lautaro took Tucapel and killed Valdivia in 1553, while Lautaro himself fell at Mataquito in 1557. The 1598 ambush at Curalaba, in which Pelantaro killed the Spanish governor, cost the Spaniards seven cities and fixed the frontier at the Bío Bío River. The Treaty of Quilín of 1641 recognized the autonomy of the Mapuche communities, and a long succession of parliaments between lonkos and royal governors kept an uneasy peace of trade and intermittent revolt. From the seventeenth century Mapuche bands crossed the Andes, carrying their language and horse culture across Patagonia in the process known as Araucanization, and through the eighteenth century their lands stayed beyond the reach of Spanish and republican rule alike.
zh: 马普切人又称阿劳卡尼亚人，是智利中南部以及阿根廷一侧安第斯山区和潘帕斯草原的原住民，各支系共用马普敦贡语，社会以大家族为基础，平时由酋长隆科统领，战时则推举名为托基的持斧者担任战争领袖。考古发现表明，早在公元前600至前500年，智利河谷中已存在马普切文化；他们还在马乌莱河战役中挡住了印加帝国的南征。西班牙人到来时，其领地从乔阿帕河谷一直延伸到奇洛埃群岛，分为皮昆切、伍卢切、维利切和昆科等支系。1541年佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚建立圣地亚哥并向南扩张，1550年阿劳卡尼亚战争爆发：托基考波利坎与副将劳塔罗于1553年攻破图卡佩尔、击杀巴尔迪维亚，劳塔罗本人则于1557年战死马塔基托。1598年佩兰塔罗在库拉拉巴伏击战中击杀西班牙总督，西班牙人连失七城，边界从此稳定在比奥比奥河一线。1641年的《基林条约》承认马普切诸群落的自治权，此后酋长与王室总督之间通过一系列议会，在贸易与零星起义之间维持着脆弱的和平。17世纪起，马普切群体越过安第斯山，以语言和马背文化带动了席卷巴塔哥尼亚的阿劳卡尼亚化，整个18世纪，他们的土地始终独立于西班牙和各共和国的统治之外。

en: The Maran, better known as the Marra, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Gulf of Carpentaria coast in the Northern Territory, around the Roper, Towns and Limmen Bight Rivers. Their three clans, the burdal, murrungun and mambali, lived along the Limmen Bight River and, together with a Warndarrang group, formed four patrilineal semi-moieties, each with its own totems, songs and rituals. Their language Marra is one of the Marran group of Gunwinyguan, with an elaborate verb system and kin terminology. A word for flour or bread, gandirri, may be a loan from Macassan, hinting at contact with the trepang traders who visited these coasts. In 1802 Matthew Flinders became the first European to land on Maria Island off their shore, noting the fires and footprints of its inhabitants; sustained colonial intrusion came only later.
zh: 木然人又称马拉人，是澳大利亚北领地卡奔塔利亚湾沿岸的原住民，活动于罗珀河、汤斯河与利门拜特河一带。他们的布尔达尔、穆伦贡和曼巴利三个氏族沿利门拜特河而居，并与一个瓦尔达朗人群体共同组成四个父系半偶族，各有自己的图腾、歌谣和仪式。木然语是贡温古语族马拉语支的语言之一，动词体系和亲属称谓十分繁复。他们称呼面粉或面包的“甘迪里”一词可能借自望加锡语，暗示他们曾与到访这些海岸的海参商人接触。1802年，马修·弗林德斯成为第一个登上他们近海玛丽亚岛的欧洲人，并在岛上发现居民留下的篝火和脚印；欧洲人持续的闯入则是更晚的事。

en: Marajo refers to the heirs of the Marajoara tradition, the mound-building society of Marajó Island at the mouth of the Amazon, whose sites the game scatters across the island's flooded savannahs. Human settlement there began as early as 1000 BC, and from roughly the fourth century it grew into a stratified chiefdom society of perhaps a hundred thousand people, living on raised earth mounds called tesos laid out along east-west lines and farming with the help of artificial terra preta soils. Its hallmark is one of the finest ceramic traditions of pre-colonial South America: large white-slipped vessels painted in red and black, incised champlevé decoration, modeled figures and funerary urns buried under house floors for elite ancestors. Iconography suggests shamanic rites and a cosmology divided between male sun and female moon, with powerful female creator figures. The great centers were in decline by around 1400, weakened as the island's riverine exchange networks shrank, though village-level Marajoara life seems to have lingered into the colonial period; the people's original language is unattested, so the game's Arawak assignment remains a reconstruction.
zh: 马拉若指马拉若拉传统的继承者，即亚马逊河口马拉若岛上建造土丘的社会，游戏把他们的据点散布在全岛的泛滥草原上。岛上的人类定居史早至公元前1000年，约4世纪起发展为可能拥有十万人口的等级化酋邦社会：居民住在沿东西方向排列、名为“特索”的高土丘上，并借助人工黑土耕作。其标志性成就是前殖民时代南美最精美的制陶传统之一——以白色陶衣为底、绘以红黑两色的大型器皿，加上剔刻纹饰、塑像以及作为精英祖先葬具、埋在房屋地板下的骨灰瓮。图像材料显示他们行萨满仪式，宇宙观按男性太阳与女性月亮二分，并崇拜强大的女性创世神。约1400年，随着岛上河运网络萎缩，各大中心走向衰落，不过村落层面的马拉若拉生活似乎延续到了殖民时代；这些居民的原初语言没有传世记录，游戏将其归入阿拉瓦克语组只是一种复原。

en: The Marathi are the Indo-Aryan people of Maharashtra, the broad Deccan uplands of western India between the Tapti and the Krishna, and speak Marathi, a language descended from Maharashtri Prakrit and first attested in a copper-plate inscription of 739. Their medieval literature was shaped by the Varkari Bhakti saints who sang of the god Vitthal in the vernacular, from Dnyaneshwar in the late thirteenth century to Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram. In 1337 Maharashtra had recently passed from the Yadava kings of Deogiri, overthrown by the Delhi Khaljis in 1321, to the Tughluqs; it then fell to the Bahmani sultans and their successor states of Ahmadnagar and Bijapur, under whom Marathi headmen held hereditary revenue offices, the patil and deshmukh watans, and even the Adil Shahi court kept its records in Marathi. Persian vocabulary entered the language under these Muslim rulers. In the seventeenth century Shivaji Bhosale welded the Marathi chiefs and peasants into a new power and had himself crowned in 1674, founding the Maratha Empire, which carried a Marathi-ruled state from the Deccan hills into the politics of all India.
zh: 马拉地人是印度西部德干高原马哈拉施特拉的印度—雅利安人，地在达布蒂河与克里希纳河之间，讲马拉地语；该语言由摩诃剌侘俗语演化而来，最早见于739年的铜板铭文。中世纪文学由瓦尔卡里派的巴克提圣徒塑造，他们用方言颂扬维托尔神，从13世纪末的杰南德什瓦尔，到纳姆德夫、埃克纳特和图卡拉姆。1337年，马哈拉施特拉刚在1321年由德奥吉里的亚达瓦诸王转入德里卡尔吉王朝之手，又归图格鲁克王朝统治，此后落入巴赫曼尼苏丹国及其后继的艾哈迈德讷格尔、比贾布尔苏丹国；在它们治下，马拉地头人持有世袭的收税职权，即村长和德什穆克的瓦坦，就连阿迪尔沙阿朝廷也用马拉地语保存文书，波斯语词汇也在这一时期进入马拉地语。17世纪，希瓦吉·博斯莱把马拉地的首领和农民凝聚成新的力量，于1674年加冕，建立马拉塔帝国，把一个马拉地人统治的国家从德干群山带入全印度的政治舞台。

en: The Mari, long known to their neighbours as the Cheremis, are a Finno-Ugric people of the middle Volga and Kama valleys, whose name may derive from an ancient Indo-Iranian word meaning human or mortal. The Gothic writer Jordanes may mention them in the fourth century, and they appear securely in tenth-century Khazar sources as the tsarmis, from which the Russian form Cheremis comes. Through the twelfth and thirteenth centuries Novgorod and Vladimir-Suzdal pressed westward into their lands, seizing Koksharov in 1174 and founding Nizhny Novgorod in 1221, while the eastern Mari remained subjects of Volga Bulgaria. After the Mongol conquests they fell under the Golden Horde, and the new Bulgar capital of Kazan was built on old Mari territory; in 1443 the Mari became subjects of the Kazan Khanate, whose Tatar rule left a strong Turkic imprint on their language. Ivan the Terrible's conquest of Kazan in 1552 divided them: the Hill Mari of the Volga's right bank submitted, while the Meadow Mari fought on in the Cheremis Wars until 1584. Forced Christianization from around 1700 drove many families east into Bashkir lands, yet under tsarist rule the Mari kept their language and repeatedly returned to their old pre-Christian faith, whose grove sanctuaries remained central to their life.
zh: 马里人长期被邻族称为切列米斯人，是伏尔加河中游与卡马河流域的芬兰-乌戈尔民族，其族名可能源自印伊语中意为“人”或“凡人”的古老词根。哥特作家约尔达内斯在4世纪的记载或许已提到他们，而10世纪的可萨文献中明确出现了察尔米斯之名，俄语的“切列米斯”即由此而来。12至13世纪，诺夫哥罗德和弗拉基米尔-苏兹达尔向西进逼他们的土地：1174年夺取科克沙罗夫，1221年建立下诺夫哥罗德；东部的马里人则臣属于伏尔加保加利亚。蒙古征服后他们归入金帐汗国势力范围，保加利亚人的新都城喀赞就建在马里故地上；1443年马里人成为喀山汗国的属民，鞑靼人的统治给马里语留下了深刻的突厥语印记。1552年伊凡雷帝征服喀山后马里人陷入分裂：伏尔加河右岸的山地马里人臣服，草原马里人则在“切列米斯战争”中抵抗到1584年。约1700年起的强制基督教化迫使许多家庭东迁巴什基尔之地，但在沙皇统治下马里人保住了自己的语言，并一再回归古老的前基督教信仰，圣林祭祀始终是他们生活的核心。

en: The Marind, or Marind-Anim, are a Papuan people of the swampy south coast of New Guinea, holding a wide territory on both banks of the Bian River around present-day Merauke in South Papua, Indonesia. Their Marind languages form a small family of the Trans–New Guinea phylum. Traditional Marind society was split into two moieties made up of patrilineal clans, themselves divided into sub-clans, and each extended family traced its descent from a dema, an ancestral spirit that appeared in myth as a culture hero, often in plant or animal form. The Marind were feared headhunters: raids on neighbouring tribes were tied to the naming of newborn children, for the skull was thought to hold a vital force, and the taking of heads underpinned the cycle of ritual and revenge. They lived in scattered extended-family settlements through the lowland sago swamps, where clan big men guarded the traditions of the dema. Although the Dutch claimed sovereignty over western New Guinea in 1793, the Marind coast remained beyond effective European administration throughout this period.
zh: 马林德人（又称马林德-阿尼姆人）是新几内亚岛南部沼泽海岸的巴布亚族群，占据今印度尼西亚南巴布亚省马老奇一带比安河两岸的广阔土地。他们的马林德语是泛新几内亚语系下的一个小语族。传统的马林德社会分为两个半偶族，下分若干父系氏族和更小的亚氏族；每个大家族都把世系追溯到一位德玛祖先神，它们在神话中以文化英雄的身份出现，常取动植物之形。马林德人曾以猎首闻名：对邻族的袭击与新生儿的命名仪式相联，因为人们相信头骨蕴含着一种生命力，猎取头骨支撑着仪式与复仇的循环。他们在低地西谷沼泽里以分散的大家族村落而居，氏族中的大人物负责守护德玛的传统。尽管荷兰人于1793年宣称对新几内亚西部拥有主权，在这一时代里马林德海岸始终处在欧洲人的实际管辖之外。

en: The Markish are the Low German-speaking people of the core Marches of Brandenburg: the Mittelmark around Brandenburg an der Havel and Berlin, the Prignitz and the Uckermark, whose Marchian dialect is an East Low German tongue formed during the medieval Ostsiedlung. The country was originally Wendish, held by the Hevelli on the Havel, the Sprewane on the Spree and the Ukrani of the Uckermark; King Henry the Fowler subdued it in 928 and 929, and the Wendish rising of 983 threw off the Northern March for a century and a half. Albert the Bear retook the land and founded the Margraviate of Brandenburg in 1157, after which Saxon and Flemish colonists drained the marshes and planted towns, their Middle Low German speech becoming the Marchian dialect while the native Slavs were absorbed. The Ascanians extended the Mark northward, gaining the Uckermark from Pomerania by the 1250 Treaty of Landin, and Berlin was first documented in the thirteenth century. After the Ascanian line died out in 1320 the margraviate passed through Wittelsbach and Luxembourg hands until the Hohenzollern Frederick I took over in 1415 and made Berlin his capital in 1417; his successors secured the Uckermark by the Peaces of Prenzlau of 1448 and 1472. The Mark turned Protestant in 1539, was ravaged in the Thirty Years' War and resettled with Huguenots after the Edict of Potsdam of 1685, and formed the heartland of the Prussian kingdom from 1701 until the Holy Roman Empire collapsed in 1806.
zh: 马克人是勃兰登堡核心诸边区——哈弗尔河畔勃兰登堡和柏林所在的中马克、普里格尼茨与乌克马克——讲低地德语的居民，他们的马克方言是中世纪东向殖民中形成的东低地德语。此地原本是文德人的土地，分别由哈弗尔河畔的赫维利人、施普雷河畔的斯普雷瓦人和乌克马克的乌克拉尼人占据；捕鸟者亨利在928至929年将其征服，而983年的文德人大起义使北方边区统治中断了约一个半世纪。大熊阿尔布雷希特收复此地，于1157年建立勃兰登堡藩侯国；此后萨克森和佛兰德斯移民排干沼泽、广建城镇，他们的中古低地德语演变为马克方言，本地斯拉夫人则被同化。阿斯坎尼家族向北扩张，凭1250年的《兰丁条约》从波美拉尼亚取得乌克马克，柏林也在13世纪首见记载。1320年阿斯坎尼家族绝嗣，藩侯国历经维特尔斯巴赫和卢森堡家族之手，1415年霍亨索伦家族的腓特烈一世接管，并于1417年定都柏林；其继任者又通过1448年和1472年的《普伦茨劳和约》巩固了对乌克马克的占有。边区于1539年改宗新教，三十年战争中惨遭蹂躏，1685年《波茨坦敕令》后迁入胡格诺教徒重新充实人口；自1701年起这里成为普鲁士王国的核心，直到1806年神圣罗马帝国解体。

en: The Marlew are the small Papuan people whose Maklew language is spoken in Welbuti village west of Merauke in South Papua, between the Digul and Mbian rivers. Maklew belongs with neighbouring Yelmek to the proposed Trans-Fly–Bulaka River language family and is heavily influenced by the Marind language.
zh: 马莱乌人是一个小型巴布亚族群，其马莱乌语通行于南巴布亚马老奇以西、迪古尔河与姆比安河之间的韦尔布蒂村。马莱乌语与邻近的耶尔梅克语同属拟议中的跨弗莱-布拉卡河语系，并深受马林德语影响。

en: The Marovo are an Austronesian people of the New Georgia group in the Solomon Islands, living on the islands of Marovo Lagoon and the neighbouring shores of New Georgia, Vangunu and Nggatokae. Their language, which orders sentences verb–subject–object, belongs to the New Georgia cluster with Roviana. The lagoon takes its name from Marovo Island at its heart and is enclosed by a double barrier reef, making it the largest enclosed lagoon of its kind in the world. Its people live from subsistence gardens and fishing, and its carvers are known for work in ebony and hardwood. In 1568 the brigantine built by Mendaña's Spanish colonists on Santa Isabel charted nearby Vangunu, the first European contact with the lagoon's vicinity.
zh: 马罗沃人是所罗门群岛新乔治亚群岛上说南岛语的族群，居住在马罗沃潟湖内的岛礁以及邻近的新乔治亚岛、万古努岛和恩加托卡埃岛沿岸。他们的语言采用动词—主语—宾语的语序，与罗维阿纳语同属新乔治亚语群。马罗沃潟湖得名于湖中心的马罗沃岛，由双重堡礁环绕，是世界上最大的同类封闭潟湖。岛民以园圃自给农业和捕鱼为生，木雕匠人以黑檀木和硬木雕刻闻名。1568年，门达尼亚的西班牙殖民者在圣伊莎贝尔岛建造的双桅船测绘了附近的万古努岛，欧洲人由此首次接触潟湖一带。

en: The Marrithiyal, also written Marrithiel and known as the Berringen people, are an Aboriginal Australian people whose traditional country lay 160 to 210 kilometres south of Darwin, reaching from the Litchfield ranges to the Daly River, with their grounds around Woolaning and Rakula. Their language belongs to the Western Daly group of non-Pama-Nyungan tongues and had three recognised dialects, Marri Ammu, Marridan and Marrisjabin; the autonym Marrithiyal is said to combine marri, meaning speech, with thiel, the paperbark tree that filled their homeland's forests. Closely allied with the neighbouring Marringar, they shared ceremonies, songlines and resources, and told their own Dreamtime version of the rainbow serpent, which stole a wife from a flying fox and was speared in revenge.
zh: 马里西耶人又拼作马里蒂尔，亦称贝林根人，是澳大利亚原住民，传统领地位于达尔文以南160至210公里，从利奇菲尔德山地延伸到戴利河，核心地带在伍拉宁和拉库拉一带。他们的语言属于非帕马-牛雅语的西戴利语群，公认有三种方言：马里阿穆、马里丹和马里斯贾宾；族名“马里西耶”据说由意为言语的“马里”和意为白千层树的“蒂尔”组合而成，白千层林遍布他们的家园。他们与邻族马林加尔人结盟，共享仪式、歌路和资源，并流传着自己的梦幻时代彩虹蛇故事：彩虹蛇偷走了狐蝠的一个妻子，结果遭到报复，被长矛刺中。

en: The Martuthunira are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara region of Western Australia, whose traditional country centred on the lower reaches of the Fortescue River; their name means those who live around that river. Their language belongs to the Ngayarta branch of the Pama-Nyungan family. The first recorded encounter with Europeans came on 26 February 1818, when the explorer Phillip Parker King, sailing HMS Mermaid along the north-western coast, met a group paddling mangrove-log rafts between offshore islands and found a camp of about forty people on a nearby island.
zh: 马图苏尼拉人是西澳大利亚皮尔巴拉地区的原住民，传统家园以福蒂斯丘河下游为中心，族名意为住在这条河周边的人。他们的语言属于帕马‑牛雅语系的恩亚尔塔语支。有记载的首次与欧洲人接触发生在1818年2月26日：探险家菲利普·帕克·金乘“美人鱼号”沿西北海岸航行时，遇见一群人划着红树林原木筏在近海岛屿间往来，并在附近一座岛上发现了约四十人的营地。

en: The Marwari are the people of Marwar, the arid plain between the Aravalli Range and the Thar Desert in western Rajasthan, whose name means the land of death and thirst. Their tongue descends from Old Western Rajasthani, or Dingal, and is the leading language of the Rajasthani group; it is written in Devanagari and was long kept in the merchant Mahajani script, fitting a people whose Bania traders carried their ledgers and credit networks across India. The Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled the region from Mandore in the early medieval period, and after the fall of Kannauj in 1194 the Rathore Rajputs migrated west: Rao Siha settled at Pali, Rao Chunda seized Mandore, and Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur in 1459. Akbar invaded in 1561 and after the death of Rao Chandrasen in 1581 Marwar passed under direct Mughal administration. When Aurangzeb annexed it in 1679 on the death of Jaswant Singh, Durgadas Rathore led a thirty-one-year guerrilla resistance, and Jodhpur, Mewar and Jaipur formed a triple alliance to shake off Mughal rule. In 1818 Jodhpur became a British princely state in the Rajputana Agency.
zh: 马尔瓦尔人是马尔瓦尔地区的居民，其地在拉贾斯坦西部阿拉瓦利山脉与塔尔沙漠之间的干旱平原，地名本意是“死亡与干渴之地”。他们的语言承自古西拉贾斯坦语，即丁加尔语，是拉贾斯坦语支中使用最广的语言；文字用天城体，长期也通行商人的马哈贾尼文字——这与班尼亚商人携账簿和信贷网络走遍印度的传统正相契合。中世纪早期，瞿折罗—普腊蒂哈腊王朝以曼多尔为中心统治此地；1194年卡瑙季陷落后，拉托尔族拉其普特人西迁，拉奥·西哈定居巴利，拉奥·琼达攻取曼多尔，拉奥·乔达于1459年建焦特布尔城。1561年阿克巴入侵，1581年拉奥·昌德拉森死后，马尔瓦尔被莫卧儿直接管辖。1679年贾斯万特·辛格去世，奥朗则布乘机兼并其地，杜尔加达斯·拉托尔领导了长达三十一年的游击抵抗，焦特布尔、梅瓦尔和斋普尔结成三方同盟，最终摆脱莫卧儿统治。1818年，焦特布尔成为英国拉杰普塔纳专员辖区下的土邦。

en: The Masalit, also spelled Mesalit or Massalit, are farming people of the Darfur-Wadai borderlands, centred on Geneina in West Darfur with communities stretching into eastern Chad, where they grow millet, peanuts and sorghum and live in conical wood-and-thatch homesteads. Their own traditions trace a long migration from Tunisia through the central Sudan before they settled this border country. They speak Masalit, a Nilo-Saharan tongue closely related to the neighbouring Maba and Marfa languages. Islam reached them only in the 1600s with wandering Muslim mystics, and Masalit Islam long kept many older customary beliefs. Through the fourteenth to eighteenth centuries they had no state of their own, their villages and clans being split between the rival Sultanates of Darfur and Wadai, whose raiding and tribute-collect shaped their history until outside conquests rearranged the region in the later nineteenth century.
zh: 马萨利特人又译梅萨利特人，是达尔富尔与瓦达伊交界地带的农耕民族，以西达尔富尔的朱奈纳为中心，部分群落延伸到乍得东部；他们种植小米、花生和高粱，住在锥形的木架茅草屋里。按本民族的传说，他们从突尼斯出发，经中苏丹长途迁徙，才在这一带定居。他们操马萨利特语，这是一种尼罗—撒哈拉语，与邻近的马巴语和马尔法语亲缘最近。伊斯兰教直到17世纪前后才随云游的穆斯林神秘主义者传入，马萨利特人的伊斯兰信仰长期保留着大量古老的传统习俗。14至18世纪，他们没有自己的政权，村落和氏族分属相互争霸的达尔富尔苏丹国与瓦达伊苏丹国，后者的劫掠和索贡塑造了他们的历史，直到19世纪后期外来征服重塑了这一地区。

en: The Mascouten were an Algonquian-speaking people of the upper Great Lakes whose own name for themselves is unrecorded; Mascouten, meaning the little prairie people, was the Fox name for them, and the French also knew them as the Nation du Feu, or Fire Nation. In the early seventeenth century they lived in southern Michigan, and they appear under the name Asistagueroüon on Champlain's map of 1616. The Beaver Wars shattered them: raids by the Odawa, Neutral and Iroquois in the 1640s and 1650s drove them from Michigan to the shores of Lake Michigan and on toward the Mississippi, and French visitors around 1670 found perhaps two thousand survivors, already a fraction of their former strength. They split into wandering bands, one of which settled near Lake Winnebago with the Wea while another kept to the Mississippi, and they entered the French fur trade through Green Bay. Around 1712, after being nearly destroyed in the fighting of the Fox Wars, the remaining Mascouten joined the Kickapoo and Meskwaki. A band on the Wabash River is mentioned for the last time in 1779, and United States records of 1813 and 1825 count the survivors as part of the Kickapoo Prairie Band.
zh: 马斯古顿人是上五大湖地区的阿尔冈昆语部族，其自称已不可考；Mascouten是福克斯人对他们的称呼，意为“小草原之民”，法国人还称他们为“火族”。17世纪初他们住在密歇根南部，尚普兰1616年的地图以Asistagueroüon之名标出了他们。海狸战争将他们击碎：17世纪40至50年代，奥达瓦人、中立联盟和易洛魁人的袭击把他们从密歇根赶到密歇根湖沿岸，再逼向密西西比河；1670年前后法国访客见到的幸存者约两千人，已只相当于往昔实力的一小部分。他们分裂成游荡的群体，一支与韦阿人在温尼贝戈湖附近落脚，另一支留在密西西比河，并经格林贝加入法国毛皮贸易。约1712年，在福克斯战争的战火中近乎覆灭后，残存的马斯古顿人加入了基卡普人和梅斯夸基人。1779年的文献最后一次提到沃巴什河畔的一支马斯古顿人；1813年和1825年的美国档案已把幸存者计入基卡普草原群。

en: The Masmuda were one of the three great Berber confederations of the Maghreb, alongside the Sanhaja and the Zenata, settled chiefly across the plains, coasts and high mountains of present-day Morocco, with smaller groups recorded at Tlemcen, Tihert and Annaba, and others who crossed into al-Andalus. Unlike the nomadic Sanhaja, they were mostly sedentary farmers, and their aristocracy was based at Aghmat in the High Atlas. From the tenth century they lost ground to Sanhaja and Zenata newcomers, and from the twelfth century to Arab Bedouin tribes such as the Banu Hilal. Their greatest moment came when Ibn Tumart, himself a Masmuda, united their tribes around 1121, was recognized as the Mahdi and built the fortified base of Tinmel in the Atlas; his Almohad movement, completed by Abd al-Mu'min, overthrew the Almoravids with the capture of Marrakesh in 1147 and grew into a caliphate ruling the whole Maghreb and Muslim Spain. When the last Almohad caliph was killed at Marrakesh in 1269 and the Marinids took the city, Masmuda particularism returned and the confederation lost its political role. By the sixteenth century Arab tribes had occupied most of its former lowlands, leaving the Masmuda confined to mountain blocks from the Rif to the Sous, the ancestors of the Shilha Berbers.
zh: 马斯穆达是马格里布三大柏柏尔部落联盟之一，与桑哈贾、泽纳塔并列，主要定居在今摩洛哥的平原、沿海和高山地带，在特莱姆森、提阿雷特和安纳巴也有小股群落，还有一支渡海进入安达卢斯。与游牧的桑哈贾人不同，他们多为定居农民，贵族的根基在高阿特拉斯山脉的阿格马特。10世纪起，他们的土地不断被桑哈贾和泽纳塔部落蚕食，12世纪起又受到巴努希拉尔等阿拉伯贝都因部落挤压。他们最辉煌的时刻来自本族人伊本·图马特：约1121年他统一马斯穆达诸部，被承认为马赫迪，并在阿特拉斯山区建起设防据点廷迈勒；他发起的穆瓦希德运动由阿卜杜勒·慕敏继承，于1147年攻占马拉喀什、推翻穆拉比特王朝，最终发展为统治整个马格里布和穆斯林西班牙的哈里发国。1269年末代穆瓦希德哈里发在马拉喀什被杀，马林人入城，马斯穆达重新退回各自为政的部落状态，联盟从此失去政治分量。到16世纪，阿拉伯部落占据了他们旧日的大部分低地，马斯穆达人被压缩在从里夫到苏斯的山区，即施卢赫柏柏尔人的先民。

en: The Massachusett were an Eastern Algonquian people of the coastal plain around Massachusetts Bay, in the watersheds of the Charles and Neponset rivers where the city of Boston now stands; their name refers to the Great Blue Hill overlooking their country. They lived in riverside villages of domed bark houses called wetu, led by their own sachems, and grew the Three Sisters of maize, beans and squash alongside fishing, shellfishing and hunting. Samuel de Champlain met their leaders in Boston Harbor in 1605, and within a generation the Great Dying of 1616 to 1619, probably leptospirosis, carried off up to ninety percent of them, with smallpox returning in 1633. English colonists then occupied their fertile shoreline almost unopposed. Many surviving Massachusett settled in the Christian praying towns of Natick and Ponkapoag founded through John Eliot's mission, which also printed a Bible translation in their language; nevertheless Massachusett ceased to be the community's everyday speech by the 1750s and died out around the turn of the nineteenth century.
zh: 马萨诸塞人是马萨诸塞湾沿岸平原的东阿尔冈昆语民族，住在今波士顿所在的查尔斯河与尼庞西特河流域，族名取自俯瞰其家园的大蓝山。他们在河畔村落里居住，房屋是称作“维图”的树皮圆顶屋，由各自的酋长统领，种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜“三姐妹”，兼营捕鱼、采贝和狩猎。1605年，尚普兰在波士顿港会见了他们的首领；仅仅一代人后，1616—1619年的“大死亡”（很可能是钩端螺旋体病）夺去了多达九成人口，1633年天花又至。英国殖民者随后几乎未遇抵抗就占住了肥沃的海岸。幸存的马萨诸塞人许多迁入约翰·埃利奥特传教事业建立的内蒂克和庞卡波格基督教“祈祷镇”，传教事业还以他们的语言印行了圣经译本；尽管如此，到18世纪50年代马萨诸塞语已不再是社区日常用语，约在19世纪初消亡。

en: The Matagalpa were the Misumalpan-speaking people of the central Nicaraguan highlands, holding the country around Sébaco, Matagalpa and Jinotega, east of the Nahua and Chorotega towns of the Pacific slope. Sedentary farmers of maize, beans and cacao who lived in small villages of thatched houses, they developed a polished village culture between the ninth and tenth centuries, leaving carved metates, orange-slipped pottery and stone statues. They were among the first Nicaraguan peoples to meet the Spanish in arms, attacking the troops of Francisco Hernández de Córdoba and Hernando de Soto in 1525, and they kept a reputation as fierce fighters, with major uprisings in 1643, 1688 and 1773. Missionary work began at Sébaco in 1530, and from 1628 Mercedarian friars settled them in reductions such as San Pedro de Metapa; a tribute count of 1581 records only seventy-five taxpayers in the Matagalpa villages. The English privateer Henry Morgan sacked the town in 1643, and by the late eighteenth century the highlands were studded with Spanish parishes and reductions, including a Sumu settlement added at Guanuca in 1790.
zh: 马塔加尔帕人是尼加拉瓜中部高地的米苏马尔潘语族群，占据塞瓦科、马塔加尔帕和希诺特加一带，位于太平洋坡地的纳瓦人和乔罗特加人聚落以东。他们是定居农民，种植玉米、菜豆和可可，住在茅草小屋组成的村落里，在9至10世纪发展出相当成熟的村庄文化，留下了精雕的磨石、橙釉陶器和石像。他们是尼加拉瓜最早以武力迎战西班牙人的族群之一，1525年就袭击了弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德科尔多瓦和埃尔南多·德索托的军队，并以善战著称，先后在1643年、1688年和1773年发动大规模起义。传教活动于1530年在塞瓦科开始，1628年起仁慈会修士把他们安置到圣佩德罗德梅塔帕等归化村；1581年的税册记载，马塔加尔帕各村只有七十五名纳贡丁口。1643年，英国私掠者亨利·摩根洗劫了马塔加尔帕镇；到18世纪末，高地已遍布西班牙教区和归化村，1790年又在加努卡增设了一处苏莫人归化村。

en: The Matiyinini are the upstream division of the Plains Cree, whose full Cree name Natimiyininiwak means the people living upriver, in contrast to the downstream Cree further east. They spoke a western Cree dialect of the Algonquian family and occupied the upper North Saskatchewan country, the parklands around the Battle River and the Beaver River and Beaver Lake, on the edge between the plains and the boreal forest. Cree bands had moved onto the northern plains around 1740, drawn by the bison herds and by the fur trade, and the upstream Cree became members of the Iron Confederacy, the Cree and Assiniboine alliance that controlled the flow of guns and goods between the Hudson's Bay Company posts and the western nations. They hunted bison on foot and later on horseback, made pemmican for the trading posts, and trapped beaver in the forest rivers; the North West Company and Hudson's Bay Company built posts through their country from the 1790s onward. Through the later eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries they raided and were raided by the Blackfoot Confederacy across the disputed bison grounds, and the smallpox epidemic of 1781 struck their camps along with every other plains nation.
zh: 马蒂伊尼尼人是平原克里人的“上游”分支，克里语全称为“纳蒂米伊尼尼瓦克”，意为住在河流上游的人，与更东边的“下游”克里人相对。他们讲阿尔冈昆语系的克里语西部方言，占据北萨斯喀彻温河上游地区，以及巴特尔河、海狸河和海狸湖一带的疏林草原，正处在大平原与北方针叶林的交界。约1740年，克里人群体被野牛群和毛皮贸易吸引，迁入北部平原，上游克里人随之加入铁联盟——即克里人与纳科达人的同盟，掌控着哈德逊湾公司商站与西部各族之间火器和货物的流通。他们先徒步、后骑马猎取野牛，为商站制作肉糜饼，并在森林河流中诱捕海狸；18世纪90年代起，西北公司和哈德逊湾公司陆续在其土地上建立商站。18世纪后期至19世纪初，他们与黑脚联盟在有争议的野牛猎场上互相劫掠，1781年的天花大流行也和其他草原民族一样重创了他们的营地。

en: The Matlatzincas were the Oto-Pamean people of the Toluca Valley, called Matlatzinco in Nahuatl, in the central Mexican highlands, whose ceremonial capital was the city of Calixtlahuaca. Their name comes from the Nahuatl word for net, and across the mountains in Michoacán they were known as the Pirinda. The Toluca valley may be the original homeland of the Oto-Pamean peoples: the hilltop city of Teotenango flourished from 750 to 1162, and the Matlatzinca emerged as a people distinct from the southern Otomi around 750. Ruled by a theocratic nobility under three high lords, they suffered Tepanec conquest in the eleventh century and then, in 1475, the invasion of the Aztec Axayacatl, who valued the valley as a maize granary and a buffer against the Purépecha. Some Matlatzincas took service as mercenaries with the Purépecha ruler Tzitzipandáquare, while Aztec colonists resettled their homeland. During the siege of Tenochtitlan in 1521 they marched with the Malinalcas and Cohuixcas to relieve the Mexica, only to be defeated after hard campaigning by Andrés de Tapia and Gonzalo de Sandoval, after which the valley passed under Spanish rule.
zh: 马特拉钦卡人是墨西哥中部高原托卢卡谷地（纳瓦特尔语称马特拉钦科）的奥托-帕梅族群，礼仪都城为卡利斯特拉瓦卡。其族名源自纳瓦特尔语中意为网的词，在山那边的米却肯，他们被称为皮林达人。托卢卡谷地很可能是奥托-帕梅各族的原乡：山城特奥特南戈在750年至1162年间盛极一时，马特拉钦卡人也约在750年从南部奥托米人中分化出来。他们实行神权贵族统治，由三位大领主统辖；11世纪遭特帕内克人征服，1475年又被阿兹特克君主阿萨亚卡特尔入侵，后者把这片谷地视作玉米粮仓和对抗普雷佩查人的缓冲地带。一部分马特拉钦卡人受雇为普雷佩查君主齐齐潘达夸雷的雇佣兵，故土则被阿兹特克迁入纳瓦人重新填充。1521年特诺奇蒂特兰被围期间，他们与马利纳尔卡人、科维克斯卡人合兵驰援墨西加人，经苦战被安德烈斯·德·塔皮亚和贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔击败，谷地随后落入西班牙人统治。

en: The Matsigenka, also called Machiguenga, are an Arawak-speaking people of the high jungle on the eastern slopes of the Peruvian Andes, scattered through the Urubamba, Camisea, Picha, Timpía and Manu river basins in Cuzco and Madre de Dios. Their language belongs to the Campa branch of the Maipurean family and is close to Nomatsigenga, with distinct dialects on the upper and lower Urubamba and at Manu. They lived as hunter-gatherers and swidden farmers, growing manioc, maize and bananas and hunting peccary and monkeys, in small, self-sufficient family bands under their own headmen; residence was uxorilocal and kinship exogamy spread settlements widely across the forest. Their shamans dealt with the spirits of a thoroughly animist world, and families wore handwoven cotton tunics called cushmas. The dangerous Pongo de Mainique gorge on the Urubamba, gateway to their country, already lay beyond the borders of the Inca Empire at the height of its expansion in the 1400s, and Inca armies never subdued the Matsigenka valleys.
zh: 马齐根卡人又称马奇根加人，是秘鲁安第斯山脉东坡高地雨林中的阿拉瓦克语族群，散居在库斯科和马德雷德迪奥斯境内乌鲁班巴河、卡米塞亚河、皮查河、廷皮亚河和马努河流域。他们的语言属迈普雷语系坎帕语支，与诺马齐根加语相近，在乌鲁班巴河上、下游和马努一带各有方言。他们原为狩猎采集者，兼营刀耕火种，种植木薯、玉米和香蕉，猎取西貒和猴子，以自给自足的小型家族群体为单位，各有头人；婚后男子住到女家，加上族外婚规则，使聚落散布于广阔丛林。萨满应付万物有灵世界中的神灵，人们穿手织的棉质长袍库什马。乌鲁班巴河上险峻的迈尼克峡谷是进入他们地界的门户；在1400年代印加帝国扩张的鼎盛期，峡谷仍在其边界之外，印加军队始终未能征服马齐根卡人的河谷。

en: The Mattole, together with the Bear River people who shared their name for themselves, Ni'ekeni', are an Athabaskan-speaking people of the rugged coast below Cape Mendocino in northwestern California, their villages strung along the Mattole and Bear rivers. Earliest accounts place them in this country from the sixteenth century, after moving south like other California Athabaskans. Salmon, abundant in the Mattole River, was their staple and kept them close to its valley; in winter families clustered in fixed villages, and in the warmer months they scattered in single-family bands to gather plant foods. One custom marked the Mattole off from their neighbors: men, not only women, wore tattooing on the forehead. Their leaders were chosen for wealth and skill in settling disputes rather than for birth, and village decisions were taken by common discussion. The Mattole language was closely akin to the Athabaskan dialects of their Eel River neighbors, and through 1837 this coast remained beyond the reach of settlers and missions.
zh: 马托尔人以及与他们共用自称尼埃克尼的比尔河人，是加利福尼亚西北部门多西诺角以南崎岖海岸讲阿萨巴斯卡语的族群，村落散布在马托尔河与比尔河沿岸。据最早的记载，他们像其他加利福尼亚阿萨巴斯卡群体一样自北方迁来，16世纪已生活在这片土地上。马托尔河中鲑鱼繁盛，是他们的主食，也使他们不轻易远离河谷；冬季各家族聚居于固定村落，暖和月份则以单个家庭为单位四散采集植物食物。马托尔人有一项与邻族不同的习俗：不仅女性，男性也在额头刺青。他们的首领凭财富和排解纠纷的能力而非血统选出，村落事务经共同商议决定。马托尔语与东邻伊尔河诸族的阿萨巴斯卡方言关系密切；直到1837年，这段海岸仍处在定居者和传教站的势力范围之外。

en: The Matumbi are a Bantu people of the southern Tanzanian coast, south of the Rufiji delta around Kilwa and the Matumbi Highlands, including the Songosongo islands. They farm rice and coconuts and fish along the shore, living in tight-knit patrilineal clans whose remote hill country long sheltered them from the slave raids sweeping the neighbouring lowlands.
zh: 马通比人是坦桑尼亚南部沿海的班图人，聚居于鲁菲吉三角洲以南的基尔瓦和马通比高地一带，也包括松戈松戈群岛。他们种植水稻和椰子，兼营近海捕鱼，按父系氏族聚居；偏远的山地长期庇护他们躲开了席卷邻近低地的奴隶劫掠。

en: The Maung, who call themselves Warruwi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Goulburn Islands in the Arafura Sea off the Northern Territory coast. Norman Tindale reckoned their lands at about 1,300 square kilometres, covering the islands and the adjoining mainland from King River, Braithwaite Point and Junction Bay in the east to Sandy and Angularli creeks in the west. Their Maung language belongs, with Manangkardi, to the Iwaidjic branch of the Iwaidjan family. They ordered the year by close observation of nature: the peewee's arrival marked the time to dig mawain water-lily roots, brown scum on the sea the season for shark fishing, and the flowering of stringy bark the mating and hunting of turtles. They also tended their country deliberately, replanting lily and gurabel roots in billabongs and setting banyan and cabbage trees to grow for shade.
zh: 芒格人自称瓦鲁维人，是澳大利亚原住民，居住在北领地近海阿拉弗拉海中的古尔本群岛。诺曼·廷代尔估算其领地约1300平方公里，涵盖群岛及相邻大陆，东起金河、布雷斯韦特角和章克申湾，西至桑迪溪与安格阿利溪。他们的芒格语与马南卡尔迪语同属伊瓦伊詹语系的伊瓦伊贾语支。他们凭借对自然的细致观察安排岁时：鹊驼鸟飞来便到了采掘马瓦因睡莲根茎的时节，海面出现褐色浮沫意味着可以捕鲨，薄皮桉树开花则预告海龟交尾、猎龟季即将开始。他们还主动经营土地，把睡莲和古拉贝尔根茎移栽到死水潭，并栽种榕树和白菜树以取荫凉。

en: The Maxakali, who call themselves Tikmun'un or by the older autonyms Monaco and Kumanuxu, are the people of the Jequitinhonha and Mucuri valleys in northeastern Minas Gerais. The outsider name Maxakali is of unknown origin and first appears in records from the Jequitinhonha country, and it covers not one tribe but a league of related groups, among them the Pataxo, Monoxo, Kumanoxo, Kutatói, Malali, Makoni and Kutaxo, who spoke closely related tongues of the Maxakalian branch of the Macro-Ge family, a language striking for having no contrasting nasal or fricative consonants. They lived in small villages of one extended family under a leader who held both political and ritual functions, and the groups bore ritual animal names such as parrot, armadillo, caiman, deer and bee. From 1808 the systematic colonial invasion of their lands sharpened long wars with the Botocudo, so the Maxakali groups settled together in defensive confederations and at times made alliances with the settlers; in 1817 the explorer Auguste de Saint-Hilaire recorded one such group, the Malali, explaining these shifting alliances between the Jequitinhonha and the Doce rivers.
zh: 马沙卡利人自称蒂克穆温，旧称莫纳科或库马努舒，栖居在米纳斯吉拉斯东北部热基蒂尼奥尼亚河与穆库里河流域。“马沙卡利”是外人对他们的称呼，词源不明，最早见于热基蒂尼奥尼亚地区的文献；它指的不是一个部落，而是帕塔肖、莫诺肖、库马诺肖、库塔托伊、马拉利、马科尼、库塔肖等若干近亲群体的联盟，他们说大热语系马沙卡利语族的相近语言，这种语言最特别之处是没有对立的鼻音和擦音。他们以小型村落为单位，一村就是一个大家族，首领同时承担政治与仪式职能；各群体还以鹦鹉、犰狳、凯门鳄、鹿、蜜蜂等动物作为仪式名号。1808年起，殖民地对其土地的系统性入侵加剧了他们与博托库多人的长期战争，马沙卡利各群体于是合村而居，组成防御联盟，有时还与殖民者结盟。1817年，探险家奥古斯特·德圣伊莱尔在热基蒂尼奥尼亚河与多塞河之间记录下马拉利人的陈述，讲的正是这种合纵连横的关系。

en: The Mayangna, long called Sumu by their Miskito rivals, are a Misumalpan-speaking people of the Mosquito Coast in eastern Nicaragua and Honduras. Their tongues, now split into Panamahka, Tawahka and Ulwa, belong to a family whose speakers have lived in the region for some four thousand years; until Oto-Manguean and Nahua migrants reached the Pacific side of Nicaragua from the ninth century, Misumalpan languages were probably spoken across most of the country. When the English appeared on the Caribbean coast in the 1630s, the Mayangna were divided among at least nine sub-tribes whose river-basin territories stretched far into the interior. The rise of the English-armed Miskito broke their old predominance: raiding parties seized Mayangna captives for the Jamaican plantations, a trade already flourishing when the English crowned the Miskito chief Oldman in 1660. Through the eighteenth century the Mayangna retreated toward the headwaters of the Coco, Bocay and other rivers, while coastal communities paid tribute to the Miskito king; even isolated villages stayed tied into regional commerce, supplying the hardwood canoes used by the very raiders who preyed on them.
zh: 马扬格纳人长期被其对手米斯基托人称作苏莫人，是尼加拉瓜和洪都拉斯东部莫斯基托海岸的米苏马尔潘语族群。他们的语言分为帕纳马卡、塔瓦卡和乌尔瓦三支；其语系的使用者在这一地区已有约四千年历史，在9世纪说奥托—曼格语和纳瓦语的移民来到尼加拉瓜太平洋沿岸之前，米苏马尔潘语可能遍布尼加拉瓜一带的大部分地区。17世纪30年代英国人出现在加勒比海岸时，马扬格纳人分为至少九个部落，其河流流域领地一直延伸到内陆深处。得到英国人武装的米斯基托人的崛起打破了他们原有的优势：袭掠队掳走马扬格纳俘虏卖到牙买加种植园，到1660年英国人加冕米斯基托首领奥德曼时，这门掳人买卖已十分兴盛。整个18世纪，马扬格纳人向科科河、博凯河等河流的源头退却，沿海社群则要向米斯基托国王纳贡；即便是最偏僻的村庄也没有脱离区域贸易，他们用硬木制造的独木舟，恰恰供应了那些劫掠自己的人。

en: The Maybrat, who call themselves Ra ro Meibrat, are a people of the central Bird's Head Peninsula, settled around the Ayamaru Lakes in present-day Indonesia's Southwest Papua region, between the Abun to their north, the Moi to their west and the Arfak to their east. Their Maybrat language, also called Ayamaru after its principal dialect, is usually treated as an isolate and takes its name from mai, meaning language, and the Brat hill of the Ayamaru country. Maybrat life rests on hunting, fishing and swidden farming, traditionally in scattered homesteads rather than villages. Their clans are led by men called bobot, whose standing rests on wealth in Timor cloth, the trade textiles that reached New Guinea through Malukan and Malay networks; ritual specialists known as wofte deal with the spirits, while feared sorcerers called kabes fane were trained in a temple-house named wion. From the sixteenth century the peninsula's coasts passed under the loose overlordship of the Sultanate of Tidore, after the Portuguese Jorge de Menezes had first sighted them in 1526, but the lake country of the Maybrat kept its dispersed clan order beyond the reach of coastal rajas and their trade ports.
zh: 梅布拉特人自称拉罗梅布拉特，聚居在今印度尼西亚西南巴布亚地区的阿亚马鲁湖群周围，地处多贝拉伊半岛中部，北邻阿本人、西接莫伊人、东连阿尔法克人。他们的梅布拉特语又称阿亚马鲁语，得名于其主要方言，通常被视为孤立语言；族名由意为“语言”的“迈”与阿亚马鲁地方的布拉特山合成。梅布拉特人以狩猎、捕鱼和轮垦农耕为生，传统上散居在独立的家宅点，而非集居村落。各氏族由称博博特的首领领导，其地位靠积蓄帝汶布来奠定，这种织物经摩鹿加与马来贸易网流入新几内亚；称沃夫特的仪式专家长于通灵，称卡贝斯法内的可怕巫师则在名为维翁的神庙公所中受训。1526年葡萄牙人豪尔赫·德·梅内塞斯最先望见半岛海岸，16世纪起沿海地带转入蒂多雷苏丹国的松散宗主权之下，但梅布拉特人的湖乡仍维持着分散的氏族秩序，处在沿海王公与商港的势力之外。

en: The Mayi are the Aboriginal Australian peoples of the Gulf country and western Cape York Peninsula of Queensland who spoke the Mayabic languages: Mayi-Kutuna, Mayi-Kulan with its Mayi-Thakurti and Mayi-Yapi dialects, and Ngawun, the speech of the Wunumara. Once classed with the Paman languages, Mayabic is now treated as its own branch of the Pama-Nyungan family.
zh: 马伊人是对昆士兰海湾地区和约克角半岛西部若干澳大利亚原住民的统称，他们使用马伊语群诸语：马伊—库图纳语、包含马伊—塔库尔蒂和马伊—亚皮两种方言的马伊—库兰语，以及伍努马拉人所说的恩加温语。马伊语群曾被归入帕曼语，现在则被视为帕马—牛雅语系下独立的一支。

en: The Yoreme, known to outsiders as the Mayo, a name meaning people of the river bank, are an Indigenous people of the fertile valleys between the Mayo River in southern Sonora and the Fuerte River in northern Sinaloa, where the ancient Huatabampo culture left the earliest settled villages of the region. They live by farming and fishing, and their language belongs to the Cahita branch of the Uto-Aztecan family and is close kin to Yaqui. At the coming of the Spaniards they held their country in a loose defensive network with the Yaqui, Pima and other neighbouring peoples. Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán's raid of 1531 opened the wars of conquest, and Spanish settlements such as El Fuerte took root from the 1580s, but the Yoreme held out until 1599, when the captain Diego Martínez de Hurdaide defeated them and Jesuits led by Pedro Méndez began their evangelization. Resistance did not end there: in 1740 they joined the great Yaqui rising led by Juan Calixto, and after its suppression nearly a century of enforced peace and assimilation followed, during which Catholic feast cycles such as the full observance of Lent were woven into Yoreme life.
zh: 约雷梅人在外通常被称为马约人，“马约”意为“河岸之人”。他们是索诺拉州南部马约河与锡那罗亚州北部富埃尔特河之间肥沃河谷地带的原住民，古老的瓦塔万博文化曾在这一地区留下最早的定居村落。他们以农耕和捕鱼为生，语言属犹他—阿兹特克语系的卡希塔语支，与雅基语关系最近。西班牙人到来时，他们同雅基人、皮马人等邻族结成松散的防御网络，共同守护疆土。1531年努尼奥·贝尔特兰·德·古斯曼的进袭拉开了征服战争的序幕，埃尔富埃尔特等西班牙人定居点从16世纪80年代起扎下根来，但约雷梅人一直坚守到1599年，才被迭戈·马丁内斯·德·乌尔戴德率军击败，以佩德罗·门德斯为首的耶稣会士随即开始传教。抵抗并未就此停止：1740年，他们参加了胡安·卡利克斯托领导的雅基人大起义；起义被镇压后，是近一个世纪被强制和平与同化的岁月，完整守齐四旬期等天主教节庆周期也在这一过程中融入了约雷梅人的生活。

en: The Mazanderanis are the indigenous Iranian people of the Caspian coast of Tabaristan, the land between the Alborz and the sea around Sari, Amol and Astarabad, and speak Mazanderani, known to medieval geographers as Tabari. They descend from the ancient Tapuri and Amardi, and their coastal plain resisted the Arab conquest: the Dabuyid ispahbad Farrukhan the Great threw back a large Umayyad invasion in 716, and although the last Dabuyid fell to the Abbasids in 760, the mountain dynasties of the Bavandids, Qarinvandids and Baduspanids kept the interior autonomous for centuries. Zaydi Shiism took root here in the ninth and tenth centuries, and the Tabari language produced its own literature, beginning with the Marzban-nama composed by a Bavandid prince around the year 1000. The ispahbads preserved their semi-independence through the Ilkhanid and Timurid years, until Shah Abbas I incorporated Mazandaran into the Safavid Empire in 1596, ending the rule of the Baduspanids.
zh: 马赞德兰人是塔巴里斯坦里海沿岸的土著伊朗语族群，聚居于厄尔布尔士山与大海之间的萨里、阿穆尔和阿斯塔拉巴德一带，讲马赞德兰语，中世纪地理学家称之为塔巴里语。他们是古代塔普里人和阿玛蒂人的后裔，沿海平原曾顽强抵抗阿拉伯征服：达布依王朝的伊斯帕巴德法鲁汉大帝于716年击退倭马亚大军；尽管末代达布衣君主在760年亡于阿拔斯王朝，巴万德、卡伦文德和巴杜斯潘等山地王朝仍将内陆的自治维持了数百年。9至10世纪，宰德派什叶派在此扎根，塔巴里语也发展出自己的文学，最早的作品是约1000年由巴万德王公撰写的《马尔兹班纪》。历代伊斯帕巴德在伊利汗和帖木儿时期保住了半独立地位，直到1596年沙阿·阿拔斯一世将马赞德兰并入萨法维帝国，巴杜斯潘王朝的统治才告终结。

en: The Mazovians are the Lechitic West Slavs of Mazovia, the flat lowland on the middle Vistula around Płock and Warsaw. Mieszko I incorporated their tribe into the Polish state in the late tenth century. Płock was a seat of the early Piast kings and the de facto capital of Poland between 1079 and 1138. On the fragmentation of 1138 Mazovia became a duchy under a Piast cadet line, exposed to raids by Prussians, Yotvingians and Ruthenians; in 1226 Duke Conrad I called in the Teutonic Knights and enfeoffed them with Chełmno Land. It became a Polish fief in 1351 and passed fully to the Polish Crown when its last Piast duke died in 1526. Wooded and poorer than the other Polish lands, with a numerous petty nobility, it exported grain, timber and fur and stayed Catholic during the Reformation. After the Union of Lublin in 1569 Warsaw hosted the commonwealth's sejm, and in 1596 Sigismund III Vasa moved the royal capital there from Kraków. Swedish, Saxon and Russian armies ravaged the region in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries; the partitions of 1793 and 1795 gave it to Prussia, with a south-eastern strip to Austria, and in 1815 it passed to Russian-ruled Congress Poland, whose November Uprising began in Warsaw in 1830. From the late Middle Ages Mazovian settlers moved into southern Prussia, where as Masurians they adopted Protestantism. Their Mazovian dialect, marked by the mazurzenie sound shift, became the leading dialect of standard Polish.
zh: 马佐夫舍人是马佐夫舍的莱赫支西斯拉夫人，居住在普沃茨克与华沙一带、维斯瓦河中游的平坦低地。10世纪末梅什科一世将其部落并入波兰国家。普沃茨克曾是早期皮雅斯特诸王的驻地，1079至1138年间是波兰事实上的首都。1138年波兰分裂后，马佐夫舍成为皮雅斯特旁支统治的公国，屡遭普鲁士人、约特温吉亚人和鲁塞尼亚人袭扰；1226年公爵康拉德一世召来条顿骑士团，将海乌姆诺地区封给他们。1351年公国成为波兰封地，1526年末代皮雅斯特公爵去世后全境并入波兰王冠领。这里森林密布、小贵族众多，比波兰其他地区更为贫困，出口粮食、木材和毛皮，宗教改革期间仍信奉天主教。1569年卢布林联合后，华沙成为联邦瑟姆的召开地，1596年齐格蒙特三世·瓦萨把王都从克拉科夫迁到此处。17至18世纪，瑞典、萨克森和俄国军队多次蹂躏这一地区；1793和1795年的瓜分把它交给普鲁士，东南一隅归奥地利，1815年又转入俄国治下的波兰会议王国，1830年十一月起义即在华沙爆发。中世纪晚期起，马佐夫舍移民进入普鲁士南部，他们在那里被称为马祖里人并改宗新教。马佐夫舍方言以马祖里音变为特征，后来成为标准波兰语的主导方言。

en: The Mbaka, also called Ngbaka, are a Central African people living between the Ubangi River and the middle Congo, in the northwest of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and parts of the Central African Republic. They speak a Ubangian language and traditionally lived by slash-and-burn farming, hunting and fishing in fortified villages, carving dagara masks for initiation ceremonies.
zh: 姆巴卡人又称恩格巴卡人，是中非的族群，家园位于乌班吉河与刚果河中游之间，即今刚果（金）西北部及中非共和国部分地区。他们说乌班吉语系的姆巴卡语，传统上在设有防御工事的村落里以刀耕火种、狩猎和捕鱼为生，并为成年仪式雕刻“达加拉”面具。

en: The Mbala are a Bantu people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, settled in Bandundu province and around Luiza in western Kasai; their Gimbala language, heard around Kikwit, keeps a Luba substrate beneath a Kikongo lingua franca. In the eighteenth century they migrated from the Kwango toward the Kwilu valley as the Yaka kingdom took shape.
zh: 姆巴拉人是刚果民主共和国的班图族群，主要定居在班敦杜省和西开赛的路易萨一带，其金巴拉语在基奎特周边使用最广，在基孔戈通用语之下保留着明显的卢巴语底层。18世纪雅卡王国形成之际，姆巴拉等孔戈语社群从宽果地区向奎卢河流域迁徙。

en: The Mbara, also recorded as Kumbulmara or Mitjamba, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland, living along the Flinders River among neighbours such as the Yanga, Gugu-Badhun and Yirandali. They spoke the Pama–Nyungan Mbara language, which was mutually intelligible with the Yanga language of the people next door.
zh: 姆巴拉人又记为昆巴尔马拉或米詹巴，是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，居住在弗林德斯河沿岸，与阳加人、古古-巴敦人和伊兰达利人为邻。他们使用帕马-牛雅语系的姆巴拉语，与相邻阳加人的阳加语可以互通。

en: The Mbay, or Sara Mbay, are a Sara people centred on Moissala in the Moyen-Chari country of southern Chad and reaching into the Central African Republic, speaking a Bongo-Bagirmi language of the Central Sudanic branch. Like other Sara groups they were hoe-farming clans beyond the Muslim frontier, raided for slaves by the sultans of Bagirmi and Wadai.
zh: 姆贝人又称萨拉姆贝人，是萨拉人的一支，以乍得南部沙里河中游的穆瓦萨拉为中心、分布延伸到中非共和国，操中苏丹语支邦戈—巴吉尔米语组的姆贝语。他们和其他萨拉支系一样，是穆斯林边界之外的锄耕氏族，长期遭巴吉尔米和瓦达伊苏丹国掠奴。

en: The Mboma, or Bamboma, are a Bakongo people of the lower Congo River, counted among the main tribes of the Luozi region in present-day Kongo Central province. They lived by river-borne trade between the coast near the Congo estuary and the old Kongo capital, and their stone statuary was noted by early colonial observers.
zh: 姆博马人（又称巴姆博马人）是刚果河下游的一支巴刚果人，被列为今刚果中央省卢奥齐地区的主要部落之一。他们依托河运，在刚果河口沿岸与刚果旧都之间经商，殖民地早期的观察者还记载过他们的石雕艺术。

en: The Mbugu, who call themselves Va'maa or Ma'a, are a Bantu people of the western Usambara Mountains in the Tanga Region of north-eastern Tanzania, around Lushoto, and their speech is one of Africa's rare mixed languages, pairing Bantu grammar with a Cushitic vocabulary alongside a second register close to Pare. Their traditions place their earliest home near Lake Victoria, or perhaps the Serengeti plains, from where the Kwavi drove them eastward through Moshi and Same to Lasa, in the valley between the Usambara and Pare ranges. There a Maasai attack split the migrants: the Dufu turned south and merged into the Zigua, the Nango entered Usambara and became a Sambaa clan, while the six Mbugu clans doubled back into Pare before settling at Shume and spreading through Usambara to Magamba and Bumbuli. Legend holds that the Mbugu already lived in Usambara before 1650, and the Nango were certainly established there by the seventeenth century, when Mbegha founded the Kilindi dynasty of the Sambaa.
zh: 姆布古人自称瓦马阿或马阿，是坦桑尼亚东北部坦噶地区乌桑巴拉山西段卢绍托一带的班图人；他们的语言是非洲罕见的混合语之一，以班图语法搭配库希特语词汇，另有一个与帕雷语相近的语域。口传传统把最早的家园放在维多利亚湖附近，也可能是塞伦盖蒂平原，后来夸维人把他们逐向东方，经莫希和萨梅抵达乌桑巴拉山与帕雷山之间的拉萨。马赛人在拉萨的袭击使移民四散：杜富人南下并入济古拉人，南戈人进入乌桑巴拉成为香巴拉人的一个氏族，姆布古六氏族则折返帕雷，随后定居舒梅，并散布到马甘巴和本布利。传说1650年以前姆布古人已住在乌桑巴拉；到17世纪姆贝加创立香巴拉人的基林迪王朝时，南戈人确已在此立足。

en: The Mbunda, or Vambunda, are a Bantu people of southeastern Angola, in the Moxico and Cuando lands between the Lunguevungu River and the upper Zambezi, with later communities across the border in Barotseland in Zambia. Their oral tradition traces the Mbunda Kingdom to its first monarch King Mwene Nkuungu and a settlement on Zambezi tributaries, and successive kings expanded it until Mbundaland stretched south toward the Namibian border, with Lumbala Nguimbo as its capital. The kingdom fought bitter wars against the Chokwe and against the Luvale, whose slave-raiding army it routed, while Mbunda iron- and copper-workers exchanged wax, ivory and rubber with Ovimbundu caravans from the Bié Plateau for guns and cloth. In the late 1700s groups of Mbunda migrated into Barotseland, where the Lozi king Mulambwa valued them as soldiers and settled them under the Mulambwa-Chiyengele treaty; in 1830 they helped the Lozi expel the Makololo from the country.
zh: 姆本达人又称瓦姆本达人，是安哥拉东南部的班图族群，居于龙圭温古河与赞比西河上游之间的莫希科和宽多一带，后来也有部众越过边界进入赞比亚的巴罗策兰。根据口传，姆本达王国的首位君主是恩昆古王，国人最初在赞比西河支流畔定居；历代君主不断扩张，姆本达兰的疆界一度南抵纳米比亚边界，以隆巴拉·恩金博为都城。王国曾与绍奎人激烈交战，又击溃了以掳奴为目的来犯的卢瓦勒军队。姆本达人擅长冶铁炼铜，用蜡、象牙和橡胶同来自比耶高原的奥文本杜商队交换火器和布匹。18世纪末，一部分姆本达人迁入巴罗策兰，洛齐国王穆兰姆瓦看重他们的善战，依据《穆兰姆瓦-奇恩盖莱条约》将他们安置下来；1830年，他们又协助洛齐人把马科洛洛人逐出国境。

en: The Mbuun, also called Ambuun or Bunda, are a Bantu people of the western Congo basin, occupying the southeastern parts of old Bandundu province, above all the Idiofa territory along the Kwilu and its tributaries. Their oral traditions remember a long migration from the Gabon side through the lower Congo and Angola, from a land called Okoolung beyond the Kwango, before they settled in their present country. Even when the Lunda empire of the Mwata-Yamv overshadowed neighboring lands through the 1600s and 1700s, the Mbuun kept a fragmented political order of village chiefs with limited and local authority and no paramount ruler. Society is organized through matrilineal clans, a system tradition says they adopted from the neighboring Yansi, and they share with the Yanzi and Dinga belief in a supreme being called Nzeem-a-mpong. Known as pacific traders rather than warriors, the Mbuun speak Mbuun, or Mpuun, a Bantu language also recorded as Kimbuun or Gimbunda.
zh: 姆本人又称安本或本达，是刚果盆地西部的班图族群，分布在旧班敦杜省东南部，主要在奎卢河支流一带的伊迪奥法地区。口传传统称他们经历了漫长迁徙：从加蓬方向经下刚果和安哥拉，来自宽果河彼岸一处叫奥库伦的地方，才抵达今日家园。17至18世纪，姆瓦塔·亚姆夫的隆达帝国威震邻邦，姆本人却维持着分散的政治秩序，只有权力有限、只管本地的村长，没有最高统治者。其社会按母系氏族组织，传说这一制度是从邻族扬西人那里学来的；他们与扬齐人、丁加人一样信奉名为恩津-阿姆蓬的至高神。姆本人以和平商人而非战士著称，操班图语支的姆本语（亦称姆普恩、金本或金本达）。

en: The Mebengokre, meaning people of the water's source, are better known to outsiders as the Kayapo or Caiapo, a name given by neighboring peoples in the early nineteenth century and said to mean those who look like monkeys, after a men's rite with monkey masks. They speak a Je language and are divided into many subgroups, among them the Gorotire, Xikrin, Kararao and Mekragnoti, spread across Para and Mato Grosso along the Xingu and its tributaries. In the 1700s they first met Portuguese bandeirantes hunting gold and indigenous slaves in the northeast of what became Sao Paulo, and migrated westward away from the raids into the forests where they later made their homeland. Mebengokre life combines shifting slash-and-burn gardens of manioc, sweet potato, yam and papaya with hunting and fishing, and they keep hidden war gardens against times of scarcity. They paint their whole bodies in intricate black patterns, elders wear wooden lip disks and chiefs bright yellow feather headdresses, and they prize oratory above all, calling themselves the people who speak beautifully.
zh: 梅本戈克雷人（意为“水源处来的人”）在外界更常用的名字是卡亚波，这个名字是邻族在19世纪初给他们起的，据说意为“像猴子的人”，得名于一种戴猴子面具的男子仪式。他们说热语，分成戈罗蒂雷、希克林、卡拉劳、梅克拉格诺蒂等许多支系，散布在帕拉州和马托格罗索州的欣古河及其支流一带。18世纪，他们在后来成为圣保罗州的东北部首次遇到搜寻黄金和抓捕印第安奴隶的葡萄牙旗兵，随后为躲避劫掠向西迁徙，进入日后成为家园的森林。梅本戈克雷人兼营轮歇刀耕农业与渔猎，园圃里种木薯、甘薯、山药和木瓜，还藏有备战备荒的“战时园地”。他们用复杂的黑色纹样涂满全身，长者佩戴木质唇盘，酋长头戴鲜黄羽毛冠，并极度推崇演说术，自称是“说话优美的人”。

en: The Median culture covers the people of central Italy, in Lazio, Umbria and the Marche, whose vernaculars are the Central Italian dialects (dialetti mediani), descended directly from the Vulgar Latin of the Roman countryside. Romanesco, the speech of Rome, is its best-known member, alongside Umbrian and Marchigiano varieties. In 1337 these lands formed the core of the Papal States, although the popes then resided at Avignon; Rome was dominated by feuding baronial families such as the Colonna and Orsini, and in 1347 Cola di Rienzo briefly set up a popular republic there. Medieval Romanesco even had its own literature, including the chronicle of the Anonimo Romano, though Dante judged it the coarsest of Italy's vernaculars. After the papal court returned to Rome in 1377 and the city became a Renaissance capital, Romanesco was deeply reshaped by Tuscan, the basis of the emerging standard written Italian, while the smaller town dialects kept their older features. The local speech remained the everyday language of artisans and peasants while Latin and standard Italian dominated writing and official life. The upheavals of the Napoleonic years brought the short-lived Roman Republic of 1798 and French annexation from 1809 to 1814, after which papal rule was restored over the region.
zh: 中意大利文化涵盖意大利中部拉齐奥、翁布里亚和马尔凯一带的居民，他们的口语是由罗马乡间通俗拉丁语直接演变而来的中部意大利方言群，其中以罗马的罗马方言最知名，此外还有翁布里亚方言和马尔凯方言。1337年，这片土地是教皇国的核心，但教皇当时驻跸阿维尼翁；罗马由科隆纳、奥尔西尼等相互争斗的贵族家族把持，1347年科拉·迪·里恩佐还曾一度建立平民共和国。中世纪的罗马方言甚至有自己的文学，佚名作者的《罗马编年史》便是代表，尽管但丁认为它是意大利各土语中最粗鄙的一种。1377年教廷迁回罗马、罗马成为文艺复兴之都后，罗马方言深受托斯卡纳方言影响，而后者正是新兴标准意大利书面语的基础；较小城镇的方言则保留了更多古老特征。拉丁语和标准意大利语垄断了书面与官方生活，地方话始终是工匠和农民的日常用语。拿破仑战争的动荡中，1798年出现了短命的罗马共和国，1809至1814年该地被法国吞并，此后教皇统治才在这一地区恢复。

en: The Mehri are the Arabs of al-Mahra, the arid coast between Hadhramaut and Dhofar, with clans also on Socotra and in southern Oman, named after the eponymous Mahra bin Haydan and claiming Himyar descent. Sabaean inscriptions already mention them, and they keep the Mehri language, a South Arabian tongue older than Arabic in the peninsula, related to Shehri and Soqotri and chiefly carried by oral poetry; the tenth-century geographer al-Hamdani remarked how far their speech lay from classical Arabic. A delegation accepted Islam from the Prophet himself, and Mehri warriors later fought in the conquests of North Africa and Spain, while their swift Mahri camels made their name across Arabia. In 1432 the Ba Dujana clan seized Shihr from the Rasulids and built the first Mahri sultanate, settling Socotra around 1480 as a base against the Kathiri; after tribal wars in 1495 the Afrari family fixed its rule at Qishn and Socotra. A Portuguese fleet took Socotra in 1507 but abandoned it in 1511, and in 1545 Portuguese guns restored Qishn to the Mahris after a Kathiri and Ottoman seizure. The Afrari sultans then governed the frankincense coast into the nineteenth century.
zh: 迈赫拉人是生活在哈德拉毛与佐法尔之间干旱海岸迈赫拉地区的阿拉伯人，支系还分布在索科特拉岛和阿曼南部，以始祖迈赫拉·本·海丹得名，自称希木叶尔后裔。赛伯伊铭文里已有他们的记载；他们使用的迈赫拉语是半岛上早于阿拉伯语的南阿拉伯语一支，与山地语、索科特拉语相近，主要靠口传诗歌传承，10世纪的地理学家哈姆达尼就曾指出他们的语言与古典阿拉伯语相去甚远。他们的一个使团直接从先知那里接受了伊斯兰教，迈赫拉战士后来参加了征服北非和西班牙的战争，快捷的迈赫拉骆驼也名扬阿拉伯。1432年，巴杜贾纳氏族从拉苏里王朝手中夺取席赫尔，建立第一个迈赫拉苏丹国，并于约1480年定居索科特拉，作为对抗卡蒂里人的基地；1495年内战之后，阿夫拉尔家族在基什恩和索科特拉确立统治。1507年葡萄牙舰队攻占索科特拉，但1511年便弃守；1545年卡蒂里人在奥斯曼支持下夺取基什恩，又被葡萄牙人的炮火逼退，城池归还迈赫拉人。此后阿夫拉尔苏丹们在这片乳香海岸一直统治到19世纪。

en: The Meitei, or Meetei, are the Tibeto-Burman people of the Imphal valley in Kangleipak, the land now called Manipur, whose Meiteilon language is the tongue of the valley kingdom recorded in their royal chronicle, the Cheitharol Kumbaba. Growing from a clan called the Ningthouja that absorbed the other Yek Salai clans, they acquired an early written order: a proto-constitution was drafted under King Naophangba in 429, and King Loiyumba, who reigned from 1074 to 1112, promulgated the Loyumba Shinyen code in 1100. In 1337 the Meitei kingdom was already the settled power of the Imphal plain, warring with the hill tribes around it. King Ningthoukhompa routed the Moirang between 1432 and 1467, and under Kiyamba, who ruled until 1508, Brahmins arrived and Vaishnavism took root. The great rupture came under Pamheiba, known as Gharib Niwaz, who reigned from 1709 to 1748: he renamed Kangleipak as Manipur, forced the Meitei from their old Sanamahi faith into Hinduism and in 1729 burned their sacred scriptures, an event remembered as Puya Meithaba. Burmese wars then scattered the people: Alaungpaya deported Meitei horsemen in 1758 and 1759, and the Burmese occupation of 1819 to 1826 is still called the Seven Years Devastation.
zh: 梅泰人（又译梅特伊）是康莱帕克——即今天的曼尼普尔——因帕尔谷地的藏缅语民族，他们的梅泰语是这个谷地王国的语言，王族谱系载于编年史《切塔罗尔·昆巴巴》。梅泰人本为宁托贾氏族，后来兼并其他耶克·萨莱氏族结成联盟，并很早就建立了成文秩序：瑙庞巴王于429年草拟宪章初稿，1074年至1112年在位的洛伊雍巴王又在1100年颁行《洛伊雍巴·西利耶尔》法典。1337年时，梅泰王国已是因帕尔平原上根基稳固的政权，与周围的山地部落不断争战。宁托孔帕王在1432年至1467年间击溃莫伊人；到1508年去世的基亚姆巴王在位时，婆罗门迁入，毗湿奴信仰开始扎根。最大的转折发生在1709年至1748年在位的帕姆海巴（又称加里布·尼瓦兹）治下：他把康莱帕克改名为曼尼普尔，强迫梅泰人放弃古老的萨纳马希信仰、改宗印度教，并于1729年焚烧圣典，这一事件史称“普雅梅塔巴”。此后的缅甸战争使族人离散：雍笈牙在1758年至1759年掳走梅泰骑兵，1819年至1826年的缅甸占领史称“七年浩劫”。

en: The Mekoche, also spelled Mequachake and said to mean red earth, were one of the five divisions of the Algonquian-speaking Shawnee, with the Chalahgawtha, Hathawekela, Kispoko and Pekowi as the others. By Shawnee tradition the healers of the tribe were drawn from the Mekoche patrilineal division. In the later eighteenth century their villages clustered on the upper Mad River in Logan County, Ohio, the best known being Pigeon Town near present-day West Liberty; Macochee Creek still preserves their name. The settlements lay in the path of the Northwest Indian War: in October 1786 Colonel Benjamin Logan's Kentucky militia burned thirteen Shawnee towns along the Mad and Little Miami rivers, Pigeon Town among them, and killed the elderly chief Moluntha despite his surrender under the Treaty of Fort Finney. United States forces destroyed the remaining Mekoche villages in 1791, after which the division's people shared the wandering fate and later removals of the Shawnee as a whole.
zh: 梅科奇人又拼作梅夸查克，族名一说意为“红土”，是操阿尔冈昆语的肖尼人五个分支之一，与查拉高萨、哈萨维克拉、基斯波科和佩科维并列。按肖尼传统，全族的巫医都出自梅科奇这一父系分支。18世纪后期，他们的村庄集中在俄亥俄州洛根县的马德河上游，最有名的是今西利伯蒂附近的皮金镇，马科奇溪的名字即来自该分支。这些聚落正处在西北印第安战争的兵锋之下：1786年10月，本杰明·洛根上校率领肯塔基民兵焚毁了马德河与小迈阿密河沿岸的十三座肖尼村镇，皮金镇亦在其中，年迈首领莫伦塔虽依《芬尼堡条约》投降仍被杀害。1791年，美军又摧毁了梅科奇人残存的村庄，此后这支人便随整个肖尼族一同辗转迁徙，并在后来的迫迁中离开俄亥俄。

en: The Melamela are an Austronesian-speaking people of New Britain in the Bismarck Archipelago. Their language is called Meramera by the neighbouring Nakanai, while its own name Melamela simply means talk.
zh: 梅拉梅拉人是俾斯麦群岛新不列颠岛上的南岛语族群。他们语言的本族名字梅拉梅拉本意是“说话”，邻近的纳卡奈人则用另一个名字称呼这种语言。

en: The Melanau are among the earliest inhabitants of Borneo, settled in the swampy river deltas of central Sarawak around Mukah, Igan, the Rajang and Bintulu, with related communities across the border in West Kalimantan. They call themselves A-Likou, or “river people”; the name Melanau, possibly meaning “coast-dweller”, was fixed through Brunei Malay usage, though Western, Chinese and Javanese maps already speak of the land of Malano long before. Chinese records note their settlements by the thirteenth century, and in 1365 the Javanese poem Negarakertagama lists Malano among the tributaries of Majapahit. From the fourteenth century they fell under the sway of the rising Sultanate of Brunei, whose founding epic celebrates the conquest of their lands; a Dutch report of 1609 records Melanau chiefs defecting to Sambas, and around 1730 Brunei reasserted its rule over their coast. Fishing, padi and especially sago farming, boat-building and trade in sago flour, jungle produce and salt made their river towns prosperous. They speak Melanau, a North Bornean Malayo-Polynesian language with many local dialects, lived in tall stilt longhouses and buried their dead in hanging coffins and carved jerunei poles; originally animists who held the annual Kaul festival, the coastal Melanau gradually adopted Islam through long contact with Brunei Malays.
zh: 梅拉瑙人是婆罗洲最早的居民之一，聚落在砂拉越中部穆卡、伊甘、拉让江与民都鲁一带的沼泽三角洲，另有亲缘群体居住在边境对面的西加里曼丹。他们自称 A-Likou，意为“河上之人”；“梅拉瑙”一名可能意为“海岸居民”，经由文莱马来人的用法固定下来，但早在文莱兴起之前，西方、中国和爪哇的地图已用“马拉诺”称呼这片土地。中国史籍在13世纪已记载他们的聚落，1365年爪哇史诗《爪哇史颂》把马拉诺列为满者伯夷的属国之一。14世纪起，他们落入崛起的文莱苏丹国势力范围，文莱开国史诗即以征服他们的土地为开端；1609年的一份荷兰报告记载梅拉瑙首领转投三发，约1730年文莱又重新控制了这片海岸。渔业、稻作尤其是西谷椰种植、造船，以及西谷米、山货和食盐贸易，使他们的河港城镇富庶一时。他们讲梅拉瑙语——一种北婆罗洲马来—波利尼西亚语言，方言众多；传统上住高脚长屋，以悬棺和雕刻的杰鲁奈柱安葬死者。他们原本信奉泛灵信仰、举行一年一度的考尔节，沿海群体在与文莱马来人长期接触后逐渐改宗伊斯兰教。

en:
The Melpa, also called Medlpa or Mbowamb and often known as the Hagen people, are a large Papuan people of the Wahgi Valley around Mount Hagen in the Western Highlands of Papua New Guinea, with the Enga to their west and the Wahgi people to their east. They are split into northern, central and eastern territorial groups, each divided into tribes and patrilineal clans; marriage was traditionally patrilocal, often polygynous, and commonly arranged through the exchange of sisters. Highland farmers without draught animals, they work their gardens by hand: women tend the underground crops of sweet potato, yam and taro, while men grow bananas and pandanus, and every household keeps herds of pigs.

Their public life turns on the moka, a ritual cycle of reciprocal gifts of pigs in which each side tries to give more than it received; the increment, the moka itself, brings renown to the giver and underpins the influence of the Melpa big man, who leads by prestige rather than command. Their language, Melpa, is close to Chimbu and is noted for its binary counting and for a special pandanus register used during the karuka nut harvest.
zh:
梅尔帕人又称梅德尔帕人、姆博瓦姆人，常被称为哈根人，是巴布亚新几内亚西高地省哈根山一带瓦吉谷地的大型巴布亚族群，西接恩加人，东邻瓦吉人。他们分为北、中、东三个地域群体，其下再分部落和父系氏族；传统上婚后从夫居，多行一夫多妻，婚姻常通过交换姐妹缔结。作为没有役畜的高地农人，他们徒手耕作园地：妇女照料红薯、山药、芋头等地下作物，男子种植香蕉和露兜树，家家户户都养猪。

他们的公共生活围绕莫卡运转，这是一套以猪为礼物的互惠仪式循环，双方都力图送出多于收到的数量；多出的部分即莫卡，能为赠予者带来声望，支撑着梅尔帕大人物的影响力——他们靠威望而非命令来领导。他们的梅尔帕语与钦布语相近，以二进制计数法和卡鲁卡坚果收获季使用的特殊露兜语域著称。

en: The Memel were one of the named Lamut, or Even, clans of seventeenth-century Russian records, grouped with the Tiugesir and Buiaksir among the reindeer Tungus east of the Lena. They roamed the cold upper Indigirka country around Oymyakon, hunting and herding reindeer on the same nomadic round as the other Lamut clans.
zh: 梅默尔人是17世纪俄方记录中具名的拉穆特（鄂温）氏族之一，与秋格西尔、布亚克西尔并列，属于勒拿河以东的驯鹿通古斯人。他们在奥伊米亚康一带严寒的因迪吉尔卡河上游游猎，和其他拉穆特氏族一样以狩猎和牧养驯鹿为生。

en: The Mengen are an Austronesian-speaking people of New Britain in the Bismarck Archipelago. Their language comprises two rather divergent dialects, Mengen proper and Poeng.
zh: 门根人是俾斯麦群岛新不列颠岛上的南岛语族群，他们的门根语包括门根本语和彭语两个差异很大的方言。

en: The Mentawai are the Austronesian people of the rainforest islands of Siberut, Sipura and the Pagais, lying roughly a hundred miles off the west coast of Sumatra, and count among Indonesia's oldest established populations. Their ancestors are thought to have moved south from Nias in migrations beginning roughly four thousand years ago and continuing until about 500 BCE, and the archipelago then remained almost untouched by outside powers until a Dutch vessel made contact in 1621. In 1337 the Mentawai lived as semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers of the coastal forest, organized into patrilineal clans that shared stilted bamboo longhouses called uma along the rivers. Their life was governed by Arat Sabulungan, an animist order in which every animal, plant and river held a spirit, and shamans called sikerei mediated between the community, its ancestors and the forest; skulls of hunted game decorated the longhouses, while tattoos made with charcoal dye, known as titi, marked identity and status and were believed to let the ancestors recognize the wearer after death, alongside the custom of sharpening the teeth as an ideal of beauty. Their language splits into three deeply divergent island dialects, reflecting the long separation of the communities.
zh: 明打威人是西比路、西普拉和南北帕盖等雨林岛屿上的南岛语系民族，这些岛屿距苏门答腊西海岸约一百英里，他们也是印尼最古老的定居族群之一。一般认为，其先民从约四千年前起分批从尼亚斯岛南迁，迁徙一直持续到约公元前500年，此后这片群岛几乎与外部强权隔绝，直到1621年才有荷兰船只前来接触。1337年时，明打威人是沿海森林中的半游牧狩猎采集者，按父系氏族组织起来，若干家族在河畔共用高脚竹制长屋“乌玛”。他们的生活受“阿拉特·沙布隆甘”万物有灵信仰支配：每一种动物、植物和河流都有灵，称为“西克雷”的萨满在社群、祖先与森林之间充当中介；猎获动物的头骨装饰着长屋，用炭染料纹成的“蒂蒂”纹身标示身份与地位，据说能让祖先在人死后认出逝者，磨尖牙齿则是他们的审美习俗。他们的语言分为三种差异很大的岛屿方言，反映出各社群长期相互隔绝的历史。

en: The Me'phaa, called Tlapanecs in Nahuatl after their mountain capital of Tlapan, are an Oto-Manguean people of the rugged Costa Chica ranges of Guerrero, east of Acapulco. Early in the second millennium a branch of them moved down toward the coast, becoming known as the Yopi, who built the kingdom of Yopitzinco around Chilpancingo and Ayutla while their northern kin held Tlapa. Both groups were formidable bowmen whose broken terrain no Aztec army could subdue: Yopitzinco remained an independent enclave on the Mexica southern frontier, at times routing Mexica garrisons, even though its lords were still invited to the coronation festivals of Tenochtitlan, where they were known as goldworkers and worshippers of Xipe Totec. Spanish rule brought epidemics, and in 1531 the Yopi rose in a great rebellion from Cuautepec; royal troops crushed it, the survivors withdrew into the mountains, and the Yopi name faded while the Me'phaa language and identity persisted through the colonial centuries.
zh: 梅法阿人在纳瓦特尔语中按其山城首府特拉斯潘被称为特拉帕内克人，是格雷罗州阿卡普尔科以东、小海岸崎岖山区的奥托-曼格族群。第二个千年之初，其中一支南下沿海，被称为约皮人，在奇尔潘辛戈和阿尤特拉一带建立约皮钦戈王国，北方同族则据有特拉斯潘。两支都是强悍的弓箭手，凭借破碎山地令阿兹特克军队始终无法征服：约皮钦戈作为墨西加南部边疆上的独立飞地，甚至多次击溃墨西加驻军，但其领主仍会受邀前往特诺奇蒂特兰的加冕庆典，他们以金工和崇拜希佩托特克闻名。西班牙统治带来疫病，1531年约皮人从夸乌特佩克发动大起义，遭王室军队镇压，幸存者退入深山；约皮之名逐渐消失，梅法阿的语言与认同则在殖民时代延续下来。

en: The Merina are the highlander people of the central Madagascar plateau and the island's largest ethnic group. They took shape from the mingling of early Austronesian settlers, who reached Madagascar from the Indian Ocean islands before the sixth century, with later Bantu migrants and the older Vazimba population, and they speak the Merina dialect of Malagasy. By the fifteenth century Hova clans from the southeastern coast had settled in the highlands and intermarried with Vazimba ruling families. Andriamanelo, who ruled from 1540 to 1575, founded the Kingdom of Imerina and warred down the neighboring Vazimba, building fortified hilltop compounds and the first irrigated rice paddies. His son Ralambo gave the realm its name, raised its first standing army and repelled a Betsimisaraka invasion, and Andrianjaka seized the last Vazimba stronghold at Analamanga and founded Antananarivo around 1620. King Andriamasinavalona later divided Imerina among his sons, opening a long period of civil war and slave raiding until Andrianampoinimerina reunited the kingdom after 1787. His son Radama I, ruling from 1810, had conquered nearly the whole island by 1824 and opened the court to European missionaries and diplomats. Merina society was rigidly stratified into nobles, freemen, vassals and slaves, and its irrigation works made the highlands one of the most productive rice regions of the Indian Ocean.
zh: 梅里纳人是马达加斯加中部高原的高地民族，也是岛上人数最多的族群。他们由6世纪以前从印度洋诸岛渡海而来的早期南岛语系定居者、后来的班图移民以及更古老的瓦赞巴人群融合而成，讲马尔加什语的梅里纳方言。15世纪时，来自东南海岸的霍瓦氏族迁入高原，与瓦赞巴统治家族通婚。1540—1575年在位的安德里亚马内洛建立伊梅里纳王国，以战争征服邻近的瓦赞巴人，修筑设防的山顶宫城和最早的灌溉稻田。其子拉兰博为国家定名，组建第一支常备军，击退贝齐米萨拉卡人的入侵；安德里安贾卡则攻克瓦赞巴人最后的据点阿纳拉曼加，约于1620年建立塔那那利佛。后来安德里亚马西纳瓦卢纳国王把伊梅里纳分给几个儿子，开启了长期内战和奴隶劫掠时代，直到1787年后安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳重新统一王国。他的儿子拉达马一世于1810年继位，到1824年已征服几乎全岛，并向欧洲传教士和外交官开放宫廷。梅里纳社会等级森严，分为贵族、自由民、附庸和奴隶，其灌溉工程使中部高原成为印度洋上最高产的稻米产区之一。

en: The Merya were an ancient Finnic people of the Upper Volga region, placed by the Primary Chronicle around Lakes Nero and Pleshcheyevo, near the later towns of Rostov and Pereslavl-Zalessky. Jordanes lists a people called the Merens among the tributaries of the Gothic king Ermanaric, and Russian tradition records the Varangians exacting tribute from them in 859; Meryan warriors marched with Oleg of Novgorod against Smolensk and Kiev in 882 and against Constantinople in 907. Their lands entered Kievan Rus in the tenth century, after which East Slavic settlement slowly absorbed them, yet the Life of Abraham of Galich still reports pagan Merya living around Lake Galich in the fourteenth century, and they were not fully assimilated into the Russians until the seventeenth. No word of their language was written down, though Meryan hydronyms still mark the rivers of the region and link them to the neighbouring Muroma and other Volga Finns, and the hillforts of Sarskoye Gorodishche and Kleshchin were long remembered as their chief centres.
zh: 梅里亚人是上伏尔加地区的古老芬兰语支民族，《往年纪事》把他们的居地定在涅罗湖和普列谢耶沃湖一带，即后来的罗斯托夫和佩列斯拉夫尔-扎列斯基附近。约尔达内斯曾把名为梅伦人的民族列为哥特王埃尔马纳里克的纳贡者，罗斯传统则记载瓦良格人于859年向他们征收贡赋；882年梅里亚战士随诺夫哥罗德的奥列格出征斯摩棱斯克和基辅，907年又参与远征君士坦丁堡。10世纪他们的土地并入基辅罗斯，此后东斯拉夫移民逐渐将其同化，但《加利奇的亚伯拉罕行传》仍记载14世纪加利奇湖一带有信奉异教的梅里亚人，他们直到17世纪才完全融入俄罗斯人。梅里亚语没有留下任何文字记录，不过该地区河流的名称中仍保留着梅里亚语水文地名，显示他们与邻近的穆罗马人等伏尔加芬兰族群关系密切；萨尔斯科耶戈罗季谢和克列辛两处古堡长期被视为他们的主要中心。

en: The Meshchera were a Finno-Ugric people of the marshy lowlands between the Oka and Klyazma rivers, the country still called the Meshchera Lowlands east of Moscow. Their language was never written down and its affiliation is debated, though many scholars treat it as close to Mordvinic. While the related Merya and Muroma tribes had been Slavicized by the eleventh century, the Meshchera kept their identity in the forests and marshes: Russian chronicles first name them in the thirteenth century, and in 1358 Ivan II of Moscow recorded buying the village of Meshcherka from a baptized native chieftain, Alexander Ukovich, whose people were already Orthodox vassals of Muscovy. Their nobility had been converted and absorbed by the thirteenth century, while hunters, fishermen and beekeepers among the commoners retained older beliefs for longer. Further east a Meshchera polity centered on Temnikov survived into the sixteenth century, by then heavily mixed with Mordvins and Tatars, and was caught up in Ivan the Terrible's wars against Kazan; the Russian princely family of the Meshcherskys traced its nobility to these native rulers. A monastery founded at Radovitsy in the sixteenth century was still converting the last Meshchera pagans, and by the end of that century the people had merged into the Russian, Mordvin and Tatar populations.
zh: 梅谢拉人是芬诺-乌戈尔族群，居住在奥卡河与克利亚济马河之间的沼泽低地，即莫斯科以东的梅谢拉低地一带。他们的语言没有文字传世，系属存在争议，但多数学者认为它接近莫尔多瓦语。同源的梅里亚人和穆罗马人到11世纪已被斯拉夫化，梅谢拉人却在森林沼泽中长期保持自身认同：俄国编年史在13世纪首次提到他们，1358年莫斯科大公伊凡二世的遗嘱还记载，他从受洗的本地酋长亚历山大·乌科维奇手中买下梅谢尔卡村，当时这些人已是莫斯科的东正教附庸。其贵族在13世纪前便已改宗并被同化，而平民中的猎人、渔民和养蜂人更久地保留着旧有信仰。在更东面，以捷姆尼科夫为中心的梅谢拉政权一直延续到16世纪，其时已与莫尔多瓦人和鞑靼人深度融合，并卷入伊凡雷帝征服喀山的战事；俄国的梅谢尔斯基王公家族便自称源自这些本地统治者。16世纪在拉多维齐建立的修道院仍在归化最后一批梅谢拉异教徒，到该世纪末，梅谢拉人已分别融入俄罗斯人、莫尔多瓦人和鞑靼人之中。

en: The Meskwaki, whose own name Meshkwahkihaki means the red-earth people after their creation story, were called Fox by the French, who mistook the name of one clan for that of the whole tribe. An Algonquian-speaking people of the Woodland culture, by the time of sustained French contact in 1698 they held the Fox River waterway of eastern Wisconsin, the link between Green Bay and the Mississippi that New France needed for its fur trade, and numbered perhaps six and a half thousand. Disputes over this river brought the Fox Wars of 1701 to 1742: the French crown ordered their extermination in 1728, and on 9 September 1730 a French-led army in Illinois killed hundreds of Meskwaki breaking out to the east, reducing the tribe to perhaps fifteen hundred. Survivors took shelter with the Sauk, their close linguistic relatives, and from 1735 the two peoples acted together, drifting south and west along the Illinois and Iowa frontier. Meskwaki warriors joined Black Hawk's bid to reclaim Illinois lands in 1832; after the Black Hawk War the United States treated the Sauk and Meskwaki as a single Sac and Fox body for the land-cession treaties that followed.
zh: 梅斯夸基人的自称Meshkwahkihaki意为“红土之人”，源自其创世传说；法国人把其中一个氏族的名字误当作整个部落的称呼，称之为“福克斯”（狐狸）。他们是林地文化的阿尔冈昆语民族，到1698年与法国深入接触时，控制着威斯康星东部的福克斯河水道——格林贝通往密西西比河的枢纽，也是新法兰西毛皮贸易的命脉，当时人口约六千五百。围绕这条水道的争端引发了1701至1742年的福克斯战争：法国国王于1728年下令将其灭族，1730年9月9日，一支法国主导的军队在伊利诺伊屠杀了数百名向东突围的梅斯夸基人，使整个部族减员至约一千五百人。幸存者投奔语言相近的索克人，1735年起两个民族共同行动，沿伊利诺伊与艾奥瓦边境向西南迁徙。1832年梅斯夸基战士参加了黑鹰收复伊利诺伊故土的行动；黑鹰战争后，美国在随后的土地割让条约中把索克人与梅斯夸基人合并为“索克与福克斯”一个缔约单位。

en: The Messufa, also recorded as the Masufa, are one of the three great nomadic Sanhaja Berber tribes of the western Sahara, together with the Lamtuna and the Godala. Their grazing grounds and oases ran from the Touat and Gourara districts, where Timimoun and Aïn Salah still mark their country, to the rock-salt pans of Taghaza and Taoudenni. In the 1050s they joined the reformist movement of Abdallah ibn Yasin and became a founding pillar of the Almoravid empire, leading much of its eastward expansion and, like the Lamtuna, wrapping their heads in black veils and carrying black banners on campaign in al-Andalus. Their slaves worked the salt mines of Taghaza: when Ibn Battuta passed through in 1352 he found every house built of salt slabs, the town awash with Malian gold, and Messufa scouts guiding caravans across the waterless stretch to Oualata. After the Almoravids fell to the Almohads in 1147, the Messufa remained masters of the desert routes, living on the salt and gold caravans that linked Sijilmasa with the Niger bend.
zh: 梅苏法人（史籍亦作马苏法人）是西撒哈拉三大游牧桑哈贾柏柏尔部落之一，与兰图纳人、戈达拉人并称。他们的牧场和绿洲从图瓦特、古拉拉地区——提米蒙和艾因萨拉赫一带即其故地——一直延伸到塔加扎和塔奥德尼的岩盐盐沼。11世纪50年代，他们加入阿卜杜拉·本·亚辛的改革运动，成为穆拉比特帝国的奠基支柱之一，主导了帝国向东的扩张；和兰图纳人一样，他们以黑巾裹头，在安达卢斯作战时高举黑色战旗。他们的奴隶在塔加扎开采岩盐：1352年伊本·白图泰路过时，发现当地房屋全用盐板筑成，城中充斥着马里的黄金，而梅苏法向导正带领商队穿越无水沙漠前往瓦拉塔。1147年穆拉比特王朝被穆瓦希德王朝攻灭后，梅苏法人仍是沙漠商路的主人，依靠连接西吉尔马萨与尼日尔河河曲的盐金商队为生。

en: The Mewari are the people of Mewar, the hilly south-eastern quarter of Rajasthan around Chittor and Udaipur, where the Aravalli Range breaks the country into defensible valleys. Their name goes back to ancient Medapata, the land of the Meda tribe, and their speech is an Indo-Aryan language of the Rajasthani group. The Guhila Rajputs built the first kingdom of Mewar around Chittor, a fortress taken by Bappa Rawal in 728 and lost to Ala-ud-din Khalji of Delhi in 1303 amid the rite of jauhar. The Sisodia branch restored the dynasty in 1326 and led it to its height under Maharana Kumbha and Rana Sanga, who humbled the sultans of Malwa and Gujarat before Sanga fell to Babur at Khanwa in 1527. Akbar stormed Chittor in 1568, and Udai Singh II shifted his court to the new lake city of Udaipur; Maharana Pratap kept up the resistance from the hills. Later ranas such as Raj Singh reasserted independence in the Rajput-Mughal war of 1708 to 1710, and after a period of Maratha pressure Mewar accepted British suzerainty in 1818 as the Udaipur princely state.
zh: 梅瓦尔人是梅瓦尔地区的居民，其地在拉贾斯坦东南部奇托尔和乌代布尔一带的丘陵间，阿拉瓦利山脉把国土切成易守难攻的谷地。地名源自古称梅达帕塔，即梅达部落之地；他们的语言属印度—雅利安语系的拉贾斯坦语支。古希拉族拉其普特人以奇托尔为中心建立了最早的梅瓦尔王国，巴帕·拉瓦尔于728年夺取该堡，1303年它在乔哈尔自焚仪式中落入德里的阿拉乌德丁·哈尔吉之手。1326年，西索迪亚分支重建王朝，在马哈拉纳·昆巴和拉纳·桑伽治下达到鼎盛，屡次击败摩腊婆和古吉拉特的苏丹，直到桑伽于1527年在坎瓦败于巴布尔。1568年阿克巴攻陷奇托尔，乌代·辛格二世把宫廷迁往新建的湖畔之城乌代布尔，马哈拉纳·普拉塔普则在山区坚持抵抗。后来的拉纳们如拉吉·辛格趁1708至1710年的拉其普特—莫卧儿战争重新独立；经受一段马拉地人的压力后，梅瓦尔于1818年接受英国宗主权，成为乌代布尔土邦。

en: The Mewati are the people of Mewat, the rugged country between Delhi, Jaipur and Agra centred on Alwar and the hills of Tijara, which corresponds roughly to the ancient Matsya kingdom. Their language is an Indo-Aryan tongue of the Rajasthani group, with the Ahirwati dialect of the neighbouring Ahirwal country, and it is the chief marker of the Meo people, who took Islam under the early Delhi sultans and kept their old Rajput clan customs alongside it. The sultans found them hard subjects: Balban waged three brutal campaigns in Mewat between 1247 and 1266. In 1355 the Jadaun chief Sonpar Pal converted as Nahar Khan, founding the Khanzada line that ruled Mewat as tributary lords of Delhi. The last of them, Hasan Khan Mewati, fought beside Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 and died carrying Rana Sanga's standard at Khanwa in 1527. Mewat then passed to the Mughals; Akbar split it into the sarkars of Alwar, Tijara, Sahar and Rewari and enrolled Meo boys as palace guards and post runners. After Aurangzeb the region fell to the Jats of Bharatpur and then to Mahadaji Shinde's Marathas, until the Sindhias ceded Gurgaon to the British in 1803 and Alwar and Bharatpur became princely states.
zh: 梅瓦特人是梅瓦特地区的居民，其地在德里、斋普尔和阿格拉之间的崎岖地带，以阿尔瓦尔和蒂贾拉丘陵为中心，大致相当于古代的摩差国。他们的语言属印度—雅利安语系拉贾斯坦语支，邻近阿希尔瓦尔地区的阿希尔瓦蒂话是其方言；这种语言也是梅奥人的主要标志——梅奥人在德里苏丹国早期皈依伊斯兰教，同时保留了旧有的拉其普特氏族习俗。苏丹们发现这批臣民难以驯服：巴勒班在1247至1266年间对梅瓦特发动了三次残酷征伐。1355年，贾敦部首领松帕尔·帕尔改名纳哈尔汗皈依伊斯兰教，开创了作为德里附庸统治梅瓦特的汗扎达家族。末代首领哈桑·汗·梅瓦蒂先于1526年在帕尼帕特随易卜拉欣·洛迪作战，又于1527年在坎瓦举着拉纳·桑伽的战旗战死。梅瓦特随后并入莫卧儿，阿克巴把它划为阿尔瓦尔、蒂贾拉、萨哈尔和雷瓦里四个萨尔卡尔，并征召梅奥少年充当宫廷卫兵和驿卒。奥朗则布之后，此地先归珀勒德布尔的贾特人，再落于玛哈达吉·辛德的马拉地人之手；1803年辛迪亚家族根据《苏尔吉—安詹冈条约》把古尔冈割让给英国，阿尔瓦尔与珀勒德布尔则成为土邦。

en: The Meyah are the northernmost of the four sub-groups of the Arfak people of the Bird's Head Peninsula, living mainly in the Masni and North Manokwari districts on the coastal plain east of the Arfak Mountains, in present-day Indonesia's West Papua region. They speak Meyah, a Papuan language of the East Bird's Head family; it is agglutinative and head-marking, and its subject-verb-object word order was borrowed from neighbouring Austronesian languages, evidence of long contact with seafaring peoples of the coast. Their clans, including the Wonggor, Ullo and Mandacan, are shared with the neighbouring Moile, and like the other Arfak groups they farm swiddens, hunt and gather in the forest, and build the stilt houses they call mod aki aksa. The coast they face was drawn into Moluccan and Malay trade from the fifteenth century, Jorge de Menezes sailed past in 1526, and Tidore's sultans later claimed a loose overlordship over the whole peninsula. Closer to the shore than the other Arfak, the Meyah felt these pressures earliest, yet retained their own language and clan society through the age of the coastal rajas.
zh: 梅亚人是多贝拉伊半岛阿尔法克人四大支系中位置最靠北的一支，主要居住在阿尔法克山脉以东沿海平原的马斯尼和北马诺夸里两区，即今印度尼西亚西巴布亚地区。他们说梅亚语，属东鸟头语系的巴布亚语言；这是一种黏着、核心词标注的语言，主—谓—宾语序是从邻近的南岛语借来的，见证了他们与沿海航海民族的长期接触。他们的翁戈尔、乌洛、曼达坎等氏族与相邻的莫伊莱人相同；和其他阿尔法克支系一样，梅亚人轮垦耕种、在林中狩猎采集，建造本族称为莫德阿基阿克萨的高脚屋。他们面对的海岸自15世纪起被卷入摩鹿加与马来贸易，豪尔赫·德·梅内塞斯于1526年航经此地，蒂多雷的苏丹们后来又对整个半岛宣称松散的宗主权。由于比其他阿尔法克支系更靠近海岸，梅亚人最早感受到这些压力，但在沿海王公林立的时代仍保留了自己的语言和氏族社会。

en: The Tangut, who called themselves Mi-niah, were a Sino-Tibetan people of Qiangic speech whose early homes were the mountains of northwestern Sichuan and southeastern Qinghai. Under pressure from the Tibetan Empire in the early eighth century they migrated north into the Ordos and the Gansu corridor, and by the An Lushan rebellion of 755 to 763 they were the dominant power of eastern Gansu, Ningxia and northern Shaanxi. In 881 their general Li Sigong helped the Tang suppress the Huang Chao rising and received the Xia, Sui and Yin prefectures as a hereditary fief. From this base Li Yuanhao proclaimed the Western Xia in 1038, with its capital at Xingqing on the Yellow River; he commissioned the square Tangut script, imposed native dress and hairstyle, and took the Tangut surname Weiming, while the Buddhist canon was translated into Tangut and printed around 1090 in thousands of fascicles. The Western Xia endured nearly two centuries of war with the Song, Liao and Jin until Genghis Khan's six campaigns of 1205 to 1227 ended in the fall of the capital in 1227, when the last emperor was killed and the cities and archives were destroyed. Many Tangut families then entered Mongol service, ranking as Semu under the Yuan, and small communities in Anhui and Henan still spoke the language into the sixteenth century, while refugees carried the Mi-niah name west into Sichuan and Tibet.
zh: 党项人自称弥药，是操羌语支语言的汉藏语民族，最早的家园在四川西北部和青海南部的山地。8世纪初受吐蕃帝国挤压，他们北迁入鄂尔多斯和河西走廊；到755至763年安史之乱时，已成为陇东、宁夏和陕北的主导势力。881年，党项首领李思恭助唐朝镇压黄巢起义，获封夏、绥、银三州为世袭领地。以此为根基，李元昊于1038年称帝建西夏，定都黄河畔的兴庆（今银川）；他命人创制方块状的西夏文，强制推行本族发式衣冠，改用嵬名为姓，汉文大藏经也被译成西夏文，约1090年以数千卷刊行。西夏与宋、辽、金周旋近两百年，最终在成吉思汗1205至1227年的六次征伐后，于1227年都城陷落，末帝被杀，城邑典籍尽毁。此后许多党项家族投效蒙古，在元朝位列色目人；安徽、河南的小社群直到16世纪仍使用西夏语，另有遗民带着弥药之名西迁四川和西藏。

en: The Mi'kmaq, who call themselves L'nu, are the people of Mi'kma'ki, the Atlantic coastlands of present Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and the Gaspé Peninsula, with hunting grounds reaching into Maine. Organized in districts under the Grand Council of district saqamaq, they lived by a seasonal round of coastal fishing, seal and whale hunting and inland moose and caribou hunts rather than settled farming, speaking an Eastern Algonquian language later recorded in a hieroglyphic mnemonic script. European fishermen were drying cod on their shores from the 1520s, opening the fur trade, and in 1610 Grand Chief Membertou and his family accepted baptism, beginning a long alliance with the French and the Acadians. After King Philip's War the Mi'kmaq joined the Wabanaki Confederacy and fought six colonial wars against the British, who claimed Acadia by the Peace of Utrecht in 1713 without Mi'kmaq consent; raids on Halifax and Lunenburg continued until the fall of Louisbourg in 1758 and the Treaty of Paris in 1763.
