zh: 努巴人并非单一民族，而是聚居在苏丹中部科尔多凡南部努巴山区的约五十个不同族群，所操语言分属尼日尔-刚果语系和尼罗-撒哈拉语系；他们与尼罗河畔的努比亚人不同，但山区的希尔努比亚人同时被归入两者。上古时期这一带属库施王国，中世纪则归入努比亚人的阿洛迪亚和马库里亚王国。14世纪起，从埃及南下的阿拉伯部落与平原居民融合，或将残余土著逐入山区；努巴人在山中以家族院落定居，靠锄耕和牧牛为生，并以村落之间的摔跤角力闻名。高地先是避难所，后来孕育出政权：以塔加利山地为中心的塔加利王国，口述传统称其建于16世纪，但较可靠的立国者是18世纪后期的穆罕默德·瓦德·贾伊利及其子伊斯梅尔，他们统一了当地的“九十九山”。凭借干旱平原与岩地的屏障，塔加利在1821年埃及征服森纳尔后仍保持独立，三次击退埃及人的入侵。

en: The Nubians are the indigenous people of the Nile valley between southern Egypt and northern Sudan, speaking Nubian languages of the Nilo-Saharan family and descended from the populations of the Kingdom of Kush, whose archers were famed in antiquity. After Kush collapsed in the fourth century they formed three Christian kingdoms: Nobatia in the north, Makuria with its capital at Dongola, and Alodia centered on Soba near the Nile confluence. An Arab army failed to take Dongola in 652 and the resulting Baqt treaty kept the peace with Egypt until the thirteenth century, while the ninth to eleventh centuries were Makuria's golden age of cruciform churches, monastery wall paintings and Old Nubian, written in a Coptic-based alphabet from the eighth to the fifteenth century. Mamluk raids, Bedouin incursions and plague then broke the kingdoms: Muslim kings briefly ruled Makuria in the 1310s, a civil war of 1365 reduced it to a rump, and its last king is recorded around 1460; Soba fell to the Arabs or the Funj about 1500. The Funj founded the Sultanate of Sennar in 1504, bringing Islamization and Arabization, while the Ottomans occupied Lower Nubia in the 1560s. Nubian survived as a spoken tongue alongside Arabic until the Egyptian conquest of 1820 to 1821 brought the Nile valley under Muhammad Ali's rule.
zh: 努比亚人是埃及南部到苏丹北部尼罗河谷地的土著，操尼罗-撒哈拉语系的努比亚语，先民是库施王国的居民，其弓箭手在古代即负盛名。库施于4世纪灭亡后，他们建立了三个基督教王国：北方的诺巴提亚、以栋古拉为都的马库里亚，以及以两河汇流处附近索巴为中心的阿洛迪亚。652年阿拉伯军队未能攻下栋古拉，随后签订的巴克特条约维持了与埃及之间的和平，直到13世纪；9至11世纪是马库里亚的黄金时代，十字形教堂、修道院壁画和用科普特字母拼写的古努比亚语（8至15世纪的书面语）盛极一时。此后马穆鲁克的进犯、贝都因人的涌入和瘟疫摧毁了这些王国：1310年代马库里亚一度由穆斯林国王统治，1365年内战使其沦为偏安小国，最后一位国王约在1460年留下记载；索巴则在1500年前后落入阿拉伯人或丰吉人之手。丰吉人于1504年建立森纳尔苏丹国，推动了伊斯兰化和阿拉伯化，奥斯曼人又在1560年代占领下努比亚。努比亚语作为口语与阿拉伯语并存，直到1820至1821年埃及的穆罕默德·阿里征服尼罗河谷地。

en: The Nuer, who call themselves the Naath, are a Nilotic cattle-herding people of the Upper Nile marshes, speaking a Nilotic language closely related to Dinka; their ancestors once lived in the dry southern Kordofan country they called Kwer Kwong. Their traditions say they began as a Dinka section that moved south out of the Gezira and, after centuries of isolation and contact with the Luo, became a separate people. Semi-nomadic pastoralists, they built their whole society around cattle, which served as bride wealth, the measure of kinship and the center of ritual life. From the late 1700s the arrival of the Baggara Arabs and their slave raids drove the Nuer east out of Kordofan toward the Bentiu lands, opening the long expansion into Dinka and Anyuak country that continued into the nineteenth century.
zh: 努尔人自称纳阿斯，是尼罗河上游沼泽地带的尼罗语族牧牛民族，所操努尔语与丁卡语相近；其先民曾住在南部科尔多凡一片被他们称为奎尔孔的干旱之地。据他们的口述传统，努尔人原是从杰济拉南迁的一支丁卡人，经过数百年的隔绝并受卢奥人影响，才发展为独立的族群。他们是半游牧的牧民，整个社会围绕牛而运转：牛既是聘礼，也是确定亲属关系的尺度和仪式生活的中心。18世纪末，巴加拉阿拉伯人的到来及其猎奴袭击把努尔人向东赶出科尔多凡，迁往本提乌一带，由此开启了他们向丁卡人、安瓦克人土地的长期扩张，这一进程一直延续到19世纪。

en: The Nueta, known to outsiders as the Mandan, are a settled Siouan-speaking people of the upper Missouri River in present-day North Dakota; Nueta, meaning ourselves or our people, was originally the name of the villagers on the west bank, while the name Mandan reached European records through the French explorer La Vérendrye in 1738. They lived in permanent towns of large circular earth lodges built around central plazas, grew corn, beans and squash in river-bottom gardens, and grew wealthy as middlemen trading their corn surplus for bison meat, horses and guns. The smallpox outbreak of 1781 cut their thirteen clans to seven and merged their towns into two villages, which the reduced Hidatsa joined for mutual defence. The Lewis and Clark Expedition wintered beside them in 1804 and built Fort Mandan, where they met Sacagawea and took the chief Sheheke east to Washington. In 1825 the Mandan accepted United States protection in the Atkinson-O'Fallon treaty, and the painters George Catlin and Karl Bodmer recorded their earth-lodge towns and the Okipa ceremony in 1832 and 1833, before another smallpox epidemic reached the upper Missouri in 1837.
zh: 努埃塔人在外来者口中称曼丹人，是今天北达科他州境内密苏里河上游定居务农的苏语族群；努埃塔意为我们自己或我们的人，原指密苏里河西岸的村民，而曼丹这个名字是1738年由法国探险家拉韦朗德里首次记入欧洲文献的。他们居住在永久性集镇里，巨大的圆形土屋环绕中央广场排列，在河滩菜园种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，并作为中间商把剩余玉米换成野牛肉、马匹和枪支，由此致富。1781年的天花使他们的氏族从十三个减到七个，众多集镇合并为两座村落，人口大减的希达察人也来合居共同防御。1804年刘易斯与克拉克远征队在他们旁边过冬，修建曼丹堡，并在那里结识萨卡加维亚，还带酋长希赫克东行前往华盛顿。1825年，曼丹人在《阿特金森—奥法伦条约》中接受美国保护；1832年和1833年，画家乔治·卡特林与卡尔·博德默先后记录下他们的土屋集镇和奥基帕仪式，1837年又一场天花瘟疫传到密苏里河上游。

en: The Nukunu are an Aboriginal people of South Australia whose traditional lands lie along the eastern side of Spencer Gulf, around the sites of the later towns of Port Pirie and Port Augusta. Their language belongs to the Thura-Yura branch of the Pama-Nyungan family and shares roughly ninety per cent of its vocabulary with the neighbouring Ngadjuri. Nukunu country was dense with sacred sites and formed the starting point of the Urumbula songline, said to run from a great tree near Port Augusta, identified with the Milky Way, north all the way to the Gulf of Carpentaria. The British navigator Matthew Flinders surveyed Spencer Gulf in 1802, and after the colony of South Australia was founded in 1836 pastoral leases and wheat farms enclosed Nukunu lands; epidemics spreading from the Murray had already thinned the people, and within a generation only a handful of Nukunu survived. The remnants took refuge in scattered camps and intermarried with Narungga, Barngarla and Wirangu families while retaining a distinct Nukunu identity.
zh: 努库努人是南澳大利亚的原住民，传统领地位于斯潘塞湾东岸，即后来皮里港和奥古斯塔港一带。他们的语言属于帕马-牛雅语系的图拉-尤拉语支，与邻近的恩加朱里语约有九成词汇重合。努库努人的土地上遍布圣地，澳大利亚已知最长的歌路“乌鲁姆布拉”便从这里启程：传说它从奥古斯塔港附近一棵象征银河的大树起，向北一直延伸到卡奔塔利亚湾。英国航海家马修·弗林德斯于1802年勘测了斯潘塞湾；1836年南澳大利亚殖民地建立后，牧地租约和麦田圈占了努库努人的土地，而此前从墨累河一带蔓延来的疫病已使人口大减，仅仅一代人之后努库努人便所剩无几。幸存者散居于各处营地，与纳伦加拉、邦加拉和威朗古等族群通婚，同时仍保持着鲜明的努库努认同。

en: The Numee are the Kanak people of the southern tip of Grande Terre in New Caledonia and of the nearby Isle of Pines, their Numèè language, also called Naa Numee, Naa-Wee or Kwényi, being spoken around Yaté and Le Mont-Dore in the Djubéa-Kaponé customary area. Together with Ndrumbea, its close neighbour to the north-west, Numèè forms the extreme-southern branch of the New Caledonian languages, tracing back to Lapita fishing villages established on these coasts after 1100 BC. Despite the resemblance of names, Numèè is probably not the tongue that gave Nouméa its name, an honour likely belonging to Ndrumbea; the two languages share the hard consonants and compact phonology typical of the south. Numee clans farmed the valleys behind the great southern lagoon and crossed by canoe to the Isle of Pines, whose tall column pines so struck James Cook in 1774 that he named the island on the spot. He did not stay, and whalers were only occasional callers afterward, leaving the Numee world undisturbed well into the nineteenth century.
zh: 努梅人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛最南端及附近松树岛的卡纳克人，其努梅语又称克韦尼语，通行于朱贝亚-卡波内习俗区的亚泰和勒蒙多尔一带。它与西北方向的近亲恩德伦贝亚语共同组成新喀里多尼亚诸语的极南语支，可追溯至公元前1100年以后在这些海岸建立的拉皮塔渔村。尽管名字相近，努梅语很可能并不是努美阿得名的来源，这份荣耀大概属于恩德伦贝亚语；两种语言共享南方语言硬朗的辅音和紧凑的语音结构。努梅氏族在南部大潟湖后方的山谷耕作，驾独木舟渡海前往松树岛；1774年，岛上高耸的柱状松树令詹姆斯·库克印象深刻，他当即以此为该岛命名。库克并未久留，此后捕鲸船也只是偶尔到访，努梅人的世界因而在19世纪很长时间里未受打扰。

en: The Numu, better known as the Northern Paiute, are the Great Basin people whose autonym means simply 'the people'. The bands gathered here all belonged to the Humboldt River country of western Nevada: the Makuhadökadö around Battle Mountain, the Sawawaktödö or Sagebrush Eaters near Winnemucca, the Küpadökadö or Ground Squirrel Eaters on Lake Humboldt, and the Toedökadö or Tule Eaters of the Carson Sink. Each band took its name from its characteristic food and centred on a lake or wetland supplying fish and waterfowl; families gathered pine nuts in the autumn mountains and joined communal drives for rabbits and pronghorn. After horses reached the region by 1730, some eastern bands adopted a mounted, bison-hunting life and in the mid-eighteenth century split off to become the Bannock of the Snake River plains.
zh: 努穆人即更广为人知的北派尤特人，“努穆”是他们的自称，意为“人”。这里汇聚的各部都来自内华达西部的洪堡河流域：巴特尔芒廷一带的马库哈多卡多人、温尼马卡附近的萨瓦瓦克托多人（食蒿者）、洪堡湖畔的库帕多卡多人（食地松鼠者），以及卡森洼地的托埃多卡多人（食藨草者）。每个部族都以特色食物得名，围绕出产鱼和水禽的湖泊或湿地而居；各家秋天进山采松子，还合力围猎兔子和叉角羚。1730年前后马传入该地区后，东部一些部族转为骑马猎牛的生活，于18世纪中叶分离出去，成为斯内克河平原的班诺克人。

en: The Nunggubuyu are an Aboriginal Australian people of eastern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, whose traditional lands of about 7,000 square kilometres ran south from Cape Barrow and Harris Creek to the coast facing Edward Island, bounded on the west by the Rose and Walker Rivers. Their language, Wubuy, is a non-Pama-Nyungan tongue of the Gunwinyguan group, marked by intricate verb prefixes and noun classes and counted among the most grammatically complex languages in Australia. By the 1700s the Macassan trepang trade had reached their coast, and Wubuy retains at least twenty-eight Makassarese loanwords from that exchange. Nunggubuyu society is divided into the Mandayung and Mandaridja moieties, with phratries, clans and patriarchal lineages beneath them, and the Mandayung moiety holds the Gunabibi cult; clans of the neighbouring Warndarang, whose own language died out, were absorbed into Nunggubuyu communities.
zh: 努恩古布尤人是澳大利亚北领地阿纳姆地东部的原住民，其约七千平方公里的传统领地从巴罗角和哈里斯溪向南延伸到爱德华岛对岸的海岸，西界为罗斯河与沃克河。他们的语言乌布伊语属于贡温古语群，不在帕马—牛雅语系之内，以繁复的动词前缀和名词类别著称，被视为澳大利亚语法最复杂的语言之一。到18世纪，望加锡人的海参贸易已延伸到他们的海岸，乌布伊语中保留着至少28个借自望加锡语的词汇。努恩古布尤社会分为曼达永与曼达里贾两个半偶族，其下再设胞族、氏族和父系世系，曼达永半偶族执掌库纳皮皮崇拜；邻近的瓦尔达朗人的语言已经消亡，其若干氏族被吸收入努恩古布尤社群。

en: The Nunivagmiut, who call themselves the Nuniwarmiut or Nunivak Cup'ig, are the Central Alaskan Yup'ik people of Nunivak Island in the Bering Sea, with the settlement of Mekoryuk, or Mikuryarmiut, as their main community. They speak the Nunivak Cup'ig dialect of Central Alaskan Yup'ik, an Eskimo–Aleut language, and have lived on the island for roughly two thousand years, hunting sea mammals and fishing from coastal villages. When the Russian-American Company first made contact in 1821, its explorers recorded about 400 people living in sixteen villages scattered across the island.
zh: 努尼瓦格缪特人自称努尼瓦缪特（Nuniwarmiut），亦称努尼瓦克库皮格人，是白令海中努尼瓦克岛上的中阿拉斯加尤皮克人，岛上的梅科尤克（Mikuryarmiut）是其主要聚落。他们使用爱斯基摩—阿留申语系中阿拉斯加尤皮克语的努尼瓦克库皮格方言，约两千年前便在岛上定居，在沿海村庄以捕猎海洋哺乳动物和捕鱼为生。1821年俄美公司首次与他们接触时，探险家记录到全岛16个村庄中约有400名居民。

en: The Nupe are the river people of the middle Niger, occupying the fertile basin between the Niger and the Kaduna in what is now central Nigeria, with towns such as Rabba, Bida and Jebba on the trade highway of the great river. Their kingdom was forged in the fifteenth century by Tsoede, a leader of Igala origin who fled Idah, united the neighboring villages by conquest and took the title Etsu; the Nupe Kingdom is counted from 1531 and grew rich on river trade, craftwork and the labor of conquered settlements, its abstract woodcarving, patterned stools and brasswork well known across the region. The Yoruba called the Nupe Tapa, and Nupe cavalry repeatedly pressed the northern marches of the Oyo Empire. Etsu Jibiri became the first Muslim ruler around 1770, and Etsu Ma'azu, who died in 1818, brought the kingdom to its greatest power. His death opened succession wars, and in the 1820s the Fulani of the Sokoto jihad, operating from Gwandu, made Nupe their dependency; in 1835 the old kingship was recast as the Nupe Emirate, later seated at Bida.
zh: 努佩人是尼日尔河中游的河畔民族，占据今尼日利亚中部尼日尔河与卡杜纳河之间的肥沃盆地，拉巴、比达、杰巴等城镇都坐落在这条大河的贸易通道上。他们的王国在15世纪由出身伊加拉的首领措埃德缔造：他逃离伊达，以武力兼并邻近村落，自称“埃楚”；努佩王国的王统一般从1531年算起，凭借河上贸易、手工业和被征服聚落的贡赋致富，其抽象木雕、花纹坐凳和黄铜器在周边颇负盛名。约鲁巴人称努佩人为“塔帕”，努佩骑兵曾屡次进逼奥约帝国的北疆。约1770年，埃楚·吉比里成为首位穆斯林君主；1818年去世的埃楚·马阿祖则把王国推向鼎盛。他死后陷入继位战争，19世纪20年代，索科托圣战中出自冈杜的富拉尼人将努佩变为附庸；1835年，旧王国被改组为努佩埃米尔国，后来以比达为都。

en: The Nuristanis are an Indo-Iranian people of the forested Hindu Kush valleys of Kafiristan, the mountain region later called Nuristan in northeastern Afghanistan, with kindred communities in neighbouring Chitral, and their languages form a distinct Nuristani branch of the Indo-Iranian family. Because they kept their old polytheistic religion while the peoples around them adopted Islam, Muslim writers called them Kafirs and their country Kafiristan, and outside observers divided the clans by their dress into the black-robed Siah-Posh and the white-robed Safed-Posh. Historians travelling with Alexander the Great in the fourth century BC already described them as distinct from their neighbours. Mahmud of Ghazni raided their valleys in 1020 and 1021 and Timur attacked the Siah-Posh in 1398, but neither conquest proved lasting, and in the early seventeenth century the Mughal emperor Jahangir still received a Kafir delegation at Jalalabad. The clans lived in independent valley communities, farming terraced wheat and barley fields, herding goats, working iron and making wine, ordered by customary law and the worship of gods such as the creator Imra and the war god Gish. Throughout 1337 to 1837 they remained unconquered polytheists beyond the reach of the Muslim states centred on Kabul.
zh: 努里斯坦人是印度—伊朗语民族，聚居于阿富汗东北部兴都库什山区林木茂密的卡菲里斯坦（后称努里斯坦）诸河谷，邻近的吉德拉尔也有亲缘群落，他们的语言构成印度—伊朗语系下独立的努里斯坦语支。由于周围民族相继改宗伊斯兰教而他们仍守旧有的多神信仰，穆斯林作者称他们为“卡菲尔”，称其地为卡菲里斯坦；外来观察者又按服色把诸氏族分为黑衣的西亚赫波什与白衣的萨菲德波什。早在公元前4世纪，随亚历山大大帝东征的史官就称他们与邻族迥异。加兹尼的马哈茂德于1020—1021年攻入其河谷，帖木儿又在1398年讨伐西亚赫波什人，但两次征服都未能持久；17世纪初莫卧儿皇帝贾汉吉尔仍在贾拉拉巴德接见卡菲尔使团。诸氏族以独立的河谷社群而居，在梯田种植小麦和大麦、放牧山羊、冶铁并酿造葡萄酒，依习惯法和对造物神伊姆拉、战神吉什等神祇的崇拜治理内部事务。1337—1837年间，他们始终是喀布尔诸穆斯林政权势力之外未被征服的多神信徒。

en: The Nushagagmiut — “the people of Nushagak” — are a Central Alaskan Yup'ik group whose villages line the Nushagak River, called Iilgayaq in Yup'ik, and the shores of Nushagak Bay at the head of Bristol Bay. Their country, shared in its upper reaches with Athabaskan neighbours, offered one of the richest salmon fisheries in Alaska: five species of Pacific salmon ascend the river, above all the summer run of king salmon, supplemented by sea mammals taken on the bay and caribou hunted inland. Like other Yup'ik they organized village life around the men's community house, the qasgiq, and moved seasonally between fishing, hunting and trapping camps. Russian contact came late but firmly: in 1818 the Russian-American Company built Alexandrovski Redoubt on Nushagak Bay, and an Orthodox mission followed in 1837, turning Nushagak into a multi-ethnic trading centre where Yup'ik from the Kuskokwim, the Alaska Peninsula and Cook Inlet came to exchange furs and provisions.
zh: 努沙加格缪特人意为“努沙加克之人”，是中阿拉斯加尤皮克人的一支，村落分布在尤皮克语称“伊尔加亚克”的努沙加克河沿岸和布里斯托尔湾湾顶的努沙加克湾畔。他们的地盘上游与阿萨巴斯卡邻族共享，拥有阿拉斯加最富饶的鲑鱼渔场之一：五种太平洋鲑鱼溯河而上，尤以夏季的帝王鲑洄游最为壮观，此外还在海湾捕猎海洋哺乳动物、在内地猎捕驯鹿。和其他尤皮克人一样，他们的村落生活以男子会所“卡斯基格”为中心，随季节在捕鱼、狩猎和诱捕营地之间迁徙。俄国人的接触来得虽晚却根基扎实：1818年俄美公司在努沙加克湾建起亚历山德罗夫斯基棱堡，1837年又设立东正教传教站，努沙加克由此成为多族群贸易中心，来自库斯科奎姆河、阿拉斯加半岛和库克湾的尤皮克人到此交换毛皮与给养。

en: The Nutabe were a Chibchan-speaking people of the Antioquia highlands, closely related in language and customs to their southern neighbours the Tahamí. In the mid-sixteenth century they held the valley of Aburrá, where Medellín later grew, and the country between the Porce and Cauca rivers, including Itagüí, Envigado, Sabaneta and Ituango. They were above all farmers, growing maize, beans, fruit and cotton, but they also fished and washed alluvial gold from the Medellín River, and they traded their produce with neighbouring tribes across a wooden bridge over the San Andrés River called Bredunto in their tongue. Their clans were governed by local chiefs without any central king. Spanish conquest reached them in the first half of the sixteenth century and their numbers fell sharply under colonization: they destroyed the Bredunto bridge to slow the invaders, until governor Andrés de Valdivia had it rebuilt, and in the 1570s and 1580s encomenderos such as Bartolomé Sánchez Torre Blanca dragged them into forced wars against the Tahamí to sustain a profitable trade in captives. Gold seekers, disease and encomienda labour steadily broke up their communities and carried away most of their ancestral customs.
zh: 努塔贝人是说奇布查语的族群，与南邻塔哈米人语言风俗相近，住在安蒂奥基亚高地。16世纪中叶，他们占据阿武拉山谷（麦德林后来兴起于此）以及波尔塞河与考卡河之间的地区，包括伊塔圭、恩维加多、萨瓦内塔和伊图安戈一带。他们以务农为主，种植玉米、菜豆、果木和棉花，也从事捕鱼，并在麦德林河淘取沙金；他们用本族物产同邻族交易，往来要经过圣安德烈斯河上一座著名的木桥，本族语称布雷东托。各氏族由地方酋长治理，没有统一的君王。16世纪上半叶西班牙征服波及于此，殖民统治下人口骤减：他们拆毁布雷东托桥以迟滞入侵者，省长安德烈斯·德·巴尔迪维亚后来又将桥重建；16世纪70至80年代，巴托洛梅·桑切斯·托雷·布兰卡等监护主又驱使他们与塔哈米人连年苦战，以维持掳卖人口的生意。淘金热、疫病和监护征赋制下的劳役逐渐瓦解了他们的社群，大部分祖传风俗也随之流失。

en: The Nuuchi are the Ute people of the Great Basin and the Colorado Plateau, whose winter camps and hunting grounds spread from the Wasatch Range and the Utah lake country across western Colorado to the San Juan watershed. Their self-designation Núuchi-u means “the people”, and their speech is a Colorado River Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, closely related to Shoshone and Southern Paiute; Numic-speaking hunter-gatherers had spread through the Great Basin by about 1000, and ancestral Ute bands were living in southwestern Colorado and southeastern Utah by 1300, settling the Four Corners region by 1500. They lived in nearly a dozen nomadic bands that gathered only for trade, intermarriage and ceremonies such as the spring Bear Dance, moving with the game and the wild-seed harvest and trading hides and meat with the Pueblo towns to the south. By the late 1600s they had acquired horses through neighbouring tribes, and in the 1700s their first limited contacts with Spaniards drew them into the wider regional trade, while Comanche groups joined them on the eastern Colorado hunting grounds.
zh: 努奇人就是大盆地和科罗拉多高原的尤特人，他们的冬营与猎场从沃萨奇岭和犹他湖区横跨科罗拉多西部，一直延伸到圣胡安河流域。他们自称努奇乌，意思是“人民”；所说的话属于犹他-阿兹特克语系的科罗拉多河努米克语，与肖肖尼语和南派尤特语关系很近。讲努米克语的狩猎采集者约在1000年已遍布大盆地，尤特先民的游群到1300年已生活在科罗拉多西南部和犹他东南部，1500年前后定居四角地区。他们分为近十二个游牧游群，只在贸易、通婚和举行春季熊舞等仪式时聚集；平日随猎物和野生种籽的收成迁徙，并以兽皮和肉与南方的普韦布洛城镇交易。17世纪末，他们已从邻近部落获得马匹；18世纪，他们与西班牙人有了最初的有限接触，被卷入更广阔的区域贸易，与此同时科曼奇人的游群也来到科罗拉多东部的猎场，与他们共处。

en: The Nuwuvi, better known as the Southern Paiute, are Numic-speaking people of the Colorado River basin, spread across southern Nevada, northern Arizona and southern Utah in small family bands such as the Kaibab, Uinkaret and Shivwits. Their Colorado River Numic language belongs to the Uto-Aztecan family and was mutually intelligible with Ute. Beside hunting and gathering, the Nuwuvi watered corn, squash, beans and sunflowers with reservoirs and irrigation ditches on spring floodplains, and women carried tall conical gathering baskets woven from willow. Loosely organized and usually peaceful, they were exposed to slave raids from the Ute and Navajo long before Europeans appeared. The first known outsiders to meet them were the Spanish friars Domínguez and Escalante, who crossed their Utah lands in 1776.
zh: 努维人即通常所说的南派尤特人，是说努米克语的族群，散居在内华达南部、亚利桑那北部和犹他南部的科罗拉多河流域，分为凯巴布、温卡雷特、希夫维茨等家族小群。他们的科罗拉多河努米克语属于犹他—阿兹特克语系，与尤特语可以互通。除狩猎采集外，努维人还在春季泛滥平原上修筑水库和灌渠，浇灌玉米、南瓜、豆类和向日葵；妇女用柳枝编织高大的锥形采集篮。他们社会组织松散、大体和平，在欧洲人到来之前很久就常遭尤特人和纳瓦霍人掳掠为奴。有记载的最早外来者是西班牙修士多明格斯和埃斯卡兰特，两人于1776年穿过他们在犹他的土地。

en: The Nuwuvu are the Chemehuevi, the southernmost branch of the Southern Paiute, who call themselves Nüwü, meaning the people, or Tantáwats, the southern men. The name Chemehuevi was given them by their Mojave and Quechan neighbours. Like all the Numic peoples of the Great Basin, their ancestors spread out of a southern Sierra Nevada homeland beginning around two thousand years ago. Living off the sparse eastern Mojave Desert, they moved in tiny nomadic bands, each tied to a mountain range or valley: the Howaits in the Ivanpah Mountains, the Yagats along the Amargosa River, the Moviats on Cottonwood Island and the Tümplsagavatsits in the Providence Mountains. Their wider country ran from the Colorado River to the Tehachapi Mountains and from Death Valley towards the San Bernardinos. They were close cousins of the Kawaiisu and traded willow baskets of tight three-rod coiling across the desert. The anthropologist Alfred Kroeber estimated that the Chemehuevi, Kawaiisu and Koso together numbered about 1,500 people in 1770, on the eve of sustained contact. In post-contact times they gathered increasingly along the Colorado, above all in the Chemehuevi Valley that now bears their name.
zh: 努武人即切米惠维人，是南派尤特人最靠南的一支，自称“努武”，意为“人”，又称“坦塔瓦茨”，意为“南方人”；“切米惠维”这个名字来自相邻的莫哈维人和克昌人。与大盆地所有努米克族群一样，他们的祖先约在两千年前开始从内华达山脉南段的原乡向外扩散。他们依赖资源稀少的莫哈韦沙漠东部为生，以极小的游牧群体活动，每一群都依附于某条山脉或谷地：艾文山的霍瓦伊特人、阿马戈萨河沿岸的亚加特人、卡顿伍德岛的莫维亚特人、普罗维登斯山的通普萨加瓦齐特人。其活动范围东起科罗拉多河，西至特哈查皮山，北抵死谷，南达圣贝纳迪诺山一带。他们与卡怀苏人是近亲，并以三股柳芯紧编的篮器在沙漠各部间交易。人类学家克罗伯估计，1770年切米惠维人、卡怀苏人和科索人合计约有1500人，那时他们尚未与外人持续接触。与外人接触之后，他们越来越多地聚集到科罗拉多河沿岸，尤其是后来以他们命名的切米惠维谷。

en: The Nuxalk, who call themselves Nuxalkmc and were long known to outsiders as the Bella Coola, are a Northwest Coast people centred on the Bella Coola River valley and the neighbouring inlets of British Columbia, a territory they call Kulhulmcilh. Before contact their settlements numbered more than a hundred, including the villages of Kimsquit, the Dean River, South Bentinck Arm and Kwatna Inlet; an ethnographic estimate put their population in 1780 at about fourteen hundred. Their Nuxalk language forms its own branch of the Salishan family, a Salish enclave surrounded by Wakashan- and Athabascan-speaking neighbours, with many words borrowed from Heiltsuk. They lived in permanent plank-house winter villages, fishing salmon and harvesting the resources of river, forest and sea, and preserved lineage history in crests, songs and dances called smayusta, honouring deities such as the creator Alhkw'ntam and the war goddess Qamaits. In 1793 the fur trader Alexander Mackenzie reached the Pacific through Nuxalk lands, completing the first European crossing of North America north of Mexico. During the nineteenth century the surviving village groups gathered in the Bella Coola Valley under Chief Pootlass, taking the collective name Nuxalkmc.
zh: 努哈尔克人自称努哈尔克姆克（Nuxalkmc），长期被外人称作贝拉库拉人，是西北海岸的原住民族，以不列颠哥伦比亚省的贝拉库拉河谷及周边峡湾为中心，他们把这片传统领地称为库尔胡尔姆奇尔（Kulhulmcilh）。接触欧洲人之前，他们的聚落超过一百个，包括金斯基特、迪恩河、南本廷克湾和夸特纳湾等地的村庄；一项民族学估计认为，1780年前后他们的人口约为一千四百人。努哈尔克语在萨利什语系中自成一支，是被瓦卡什语和阿萨巴斯卡语邻族包围的萨利什语孤岛，并从海尔楚克语借入了大量词汇。他们居住在木板屋组成的固定冬季村落里，捕捞鲑鱼、取用河流、森林与海洋的资源，以族徽、歌谣和称为斯马尤斯塔（smayusta）的舞蹈保存谱系历史，崇奉创世神阿尔克恩塔姆（Alhkw'ntam）、战争女神卡迈茨（Qamaits）等神祇。1793年，毛皮商人亚历山大·麦肯齐取道努哈尔克人的土地抵达太平洋，完成了欧洲人在墨西哥以北首次横穿北美大陆的壮举。19世纪间，幸存下来的各村庄群体在首领普特拉斯带领下聚居于贝拉库拉河谷，共同采用努哈尔克姆克这一总称。

en: The Nyamal are an Indigenous Australian people of the Pilbara in north-western Western Australia, whose traditional lands take in the country around the de Grey River, east of the Ngarluma. Their language belongs to the Ngayarda branch of the Pama-Nyungan family.
zh: 尼亚马尔人是西澳大利亚西北部皮尔巴拉的原住民，传统家园包括恩加尔卢马人以东、德格雷河一带。他们的语言属于帕马‑牛雅语系的恩亚尔塔语支。

en: The Nyamwezi, the people of the moon or of the west in Swahili, are a Bantu people of the western plateau of central Tanzania, their homeland of Unyamwezi covering the rolling country around Tabora, Singida and Shinyanga; the Kimbu, Konongo, Sukuma and Sumbwa are kindred groups who also answer to the name Wanyamwezi, though they never formed a single state. They reached the plateau in the 1500s and lived as fishermen and shifting farmers in a patchwork of more than a hundred small chiefdoms, each with its elders, councillors and court slaves, and the Galahansa tradition confirms their presence there by the late 1600s. Poor soils pushed them onto the roads, and long-distance trade became their calling: by 1800 their caravans were carrying Katanga copper, wax, salt, ivory and slaves from the interior to the coast, and ancient Indian texts already knew them as the men of the moon. Arab and Indian merchants reached Unyamwezi in their turn by 1825, exchanging cloth and guns for ivory, and around the same time the first kingdoms, above all Unyanyembe with its trading town of Tabora, rose above the old chiefdoms as caravan wealth reshaped the plateau.
zh: 尼亚姆韦齐在斯瓦希里语中意为月亮之人或西方人，是坦桑尼亚中部西部高原的班图人，故土乌尼亚姆韦齐包括塔波拉、辛吉达和希尼安加一带的起伏台地；金布、科农戈、苏库马和松布瓦等亲缘群体对外也自称瓦尼亚姆韦齐，但从未结成统一国家。他们在1500年代进入高原，以渔猎和轮垦为生，散居在上百个小酋长国拼成的版图里，各有长老、议事官和宫廷奴隶，加拉汉萨的传说证实1600年代末他们已在此生活。贫瘠的土壤逼他们上路，长途贸易遂成本业：到1800年，他们的商队已把加丹加的铜、蜂蜡、盐、象牙和奴隶从内陆运往沿海，古印度文献早已称他们为月亮之人。阿拉伯和印度商人则在1825年前后深入乌尼亚姆韦齐，以布匹和枪支交换象牙；大约同期，最早的一批王国崛起，其中尤以控制商镇塔波拉的乌尼亚尼扬贝为强，商路财富就此重塑了整个高原。

en: The Nyangumarta are an Aboriginal Australian nation of north-western Western Australia, whose country runs along Eighty Mile Beach and inland into the Great Sandy Desert. They comprise two branches, the coastal Kundal and the inland Iparuka, and their language belongs to the Marrngu branch of the Pama-Nyungan family, alongside Karajarri and Mangarla.
zh: 尼扬古马达人是西澳大利亚西北部的原住民族，家园沿八十英里滩延伸，深入大沙沙漠腹地。他们分为沿海的昆达尔和内陆的伊帕鲁卡两支，语言属于帕马‑牛雅语系的马恩古语支，与卡拉贾里语和曼加拉语同支。

en: The Nyawaygi, also spelt Nyawigi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Halifax Bay hinterland in Far North Queensland, whose country of some two thousand three hundred square miles lay mainly on the rainforested Seaview Range southwest of the Herbert River, running southeast to Harveyside and the Reid River, with access to the coast near Ingham and a possible footing on Orpheus Island. Their neighbours included the Biyaygiri to the north, the Warrongo to the west and the Warrgamay on the coastal sclerophyll country. The people were made up of seven clans bearing the -bara suffix and divided into four marriage sections, each required to wed into a prescribed section. Their extinct Pama-Nyungan language had only twelve consonants, the smallest inventory of any Australian language, and seven verb conjugations that preserved a feature of proto-Pama-Nyungan lost in neighbouring tongues.
zh: 尼亚瓦伊吉人又称尼亚维吉人，是昆士兰远北哈利法克斯湾腹地的澳大利亚原住民，领地约两千三百平方英里，主要位于赫伯特河西南雨林覆盖的海景岭上，向东南延伸至哈维赛德和里德河，并可出入英厄姆附近的海岸，可能还据有奥菲斯岛。他们北邻比亚伊吉里人、西接沃龙戈人，沿海硬叶林地带则是瓦尔加梅人的地盘。尼亚瓦伊吉人由七个带“巴拉”后缀的氏族组成，全社会分为四个婚姻分支，每个分支只能与指定分支通婚。他们已消亡的帕马-牛雅语只有十二个辅音，是澳大利亚语言中音位最少的；其七种动词变位还保留了原始帕马-牛雅语的一项特征，而邻近语言早已失去它。

en: The Nyelayu are the Kanak people of the northernmost tip of Grande Terre in New Caledonia and of the Belep islands just offshore, their Nyâlayu language, also written Yâlayu or Nyalâyu, standing in the extreme-northern group of the New Caledonian languages. It exists in two dialects so different as to be barely mutually intelligible: Pooc, also called Haat, spoken on the Belep islands, and Puma, or Paak, spoken on the mainland around Poum in the west and Pouébo and Balade in the east. This split mirrors the sea lanes and mountain spurs that have divided far-northern clans since Lapita times around 1100 BC. Islanders and mainlanders alike lived from taro gardens, reef fishing and long canoe voyages, exchanging ornaments and shell valuables between chiefdoms. Balade, in Puma country, was the very place where James Cook came ashore in September 1774, meeting and trading with the local Kanaks and giving Europe its first close look at a New Caledonian people; even so, permanent European contact did not follow for another two generations.
zh: 涅拉尤人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛最北端及近岸贝莱普群岛的卡纳克人，其涅拉尤语也写作亚拉尤语，属新喀里多尼亚诸语的极北语组。它分为两种差异极大、几乎难以互通的方言：一是在贝莱普群岛使用的普克方言，又称哈特方言；二是在大陆西部普姆、东部普埃博和巴拉德一带使用的普马方言，又称帕克方言。这种分化映照出海路与山脊切割出的地理格局，自约公元前1100年的拉皮塔时代起，极北各氏族便因此彼此分隔。岛民与大陆居民都以芋头园、礁岩捕鱼和长程独木舟航行为生，在酋邦之间交换饰物和贝制珍品。位于普马地区的巴拉德，正是詹姆斯·库克于1774年9月登岸之处：他与当地卡纳克人会面交易，让欧洲人第一次近距离认识新喀里多尼亚人；尽管如此，固定的欧洲接触还要再过两代人才告开始。

en: The Nyikina, also spelt Nyigina, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Kimberley region of Western Australia, whose country runs along the lower Fitzroy River — the mardoowarra in their own speech — from Yeeda upstream to Noonkanbah on both banks, covering roughly 29,000 square kilometres. Their language is an eastern member of the Nyulnyulan family, closely related to Warrwa and Yawuru, which some linguists treat as dialects of a single tongue. In pre-contact times the Nyikina expanded down the Fitzroy and drove a wedge between the Warrwa clans living around King Sound. That sound was the first stretch of their coastline reached by Europeans: William Dampier explored it aboard the Cygnet in 1688, and Phillip Parker King surveyed the same shores in 1821.
zh: 尼基纳人是西澳大利亚州金伯利地区的澳大利亚原住民，领地沿菲茨罗伊河下游展开——他们在自己的语言里称这条河为马杜瓦拉——两岸从伊达向上游延伸到农坎巴，面积约2.9万平方公里。尼基纳语是纽尔纽尔语系东部的一支，与瓦尔瓦语、亚乌鲁语关系密切，部分语言学家把它们视为同一种语言的方言。在与外来者接触之前，尼基纳人沿菲茨罗伊河向下游扩张，像楔子一样插入金湾沿岸的瓦尔瓦诸氏族之间。金湾是他们海岸线上最早迎来欧洲人的地段：1688年威廉·丹皮尔乘“西格尼特号”考察了该湾，1821年菲利普·帕克·金又测量了这一带海岸。

en: The Nyimang are a sub-group of the Nuba peoples who cluster in closely built villages beneath the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan in Sudan. They speak the Nyima, or Ama, language of the Nilo-Saharan family, which had no traditional written form, and most Nyimang are Muslims.
zh: 尼芒人是努巴人的一支，聚居在苏丹南科尔多凡努巴山脚下屋舍相连的村落中。他们操尼罗-撒哈拉语系的尼芒语（又称阿马语），该语言传统上没有文字，尼芒人大多信奉伊斯兰教。

en: The Nyuril'ts are recorded as an Evenki tribe of the far northern taiga, whose name has been proposed as one origin of the place name Norilsk, in the Pyasina river country of the Taimyr. Like other Evenki groups they were reindeer hunters and herders, drawn into the Russian fur-tax network after Cossacks opened the Siberian river routes in the 1600s.
zh: 纽里尔茨人是史载的极北泰加林鄂温克部落，其名称被认为可能是泰梅尔皮亚西纳河流域诺里尔斯克地名的来源之一。他们和其他鄂温克群体一样以养鹿狩猎为生，17世纪哥萨克打通西伯利亚水路后被纳入俄国毛皮税网络。

en: The Nyurmgan are an Evenki clan of the Vilyuy basin, in the taiga plateau west of the Lena; their name, recorded in Russian as Nyurmagan, is explained as the Evenki word for having arrows, and it gave its name to the settlement of Nyurba on the Vilyuy, the future town of central Yakutia. Tungus clans had settled the Vilyuy and the Middle Lena by the 1200s, until the spread of the Yakut down the Lena pushed groups such as the Nyurmgan away from the main river. With the Russian advance of the 1600s the clan was drawn into the yasak fur-tax network, and a permanent Russian settlement grew up at Nyurba in the mid-1700s.
zh: 纽尔姆甘人是维柳伊河流域的鄂温克氏族，住在勒拿河以西的泰加林高原上。其氏族名俄文史籍记作 Нюрмаган，鄂温克语意为“拥有箭的人”，维柳伊河畔的纽尔巴聚落即因该氏族得名，后来发展成雅库特中部的城市。13世纪时，通古斯诸部已分布在维柳伊河与勒拿河中游，随着雅库特人沿勒拿河扩散，纽尔姆甘等群体被迫离开大河干流。17世纪俄国东进后，该氏族被纳入雅萨克毛皮税网络；18世纪中叶，纽尔巴形成固定的俄罗斯人定居点。

en: The Obgints are an Evenki clan band of the Vilyuy plateau in western Yakutia, whose grounds centred on the Syuldyukar country, the seat of the Sadyn Evenki national nasleg in present-day Mirninsky district. Like other Vilyuy Evenki they lived by reindeer herding and hunting and were brought into the Russian yasak system during the eastward Cossack advance of the 1600s.
zh: 奥布金茨人是雅库特西部维柳伊高原的鄂温克氏族游群，活动中心在休尔久卡尔一带，即今米尔内区萨登鄂温克民族乡的所在地。他们和维柳伊河流域的其他鄂温克人一样以养鹿狩猎为生，17世纪哥萨克东扩时被纳入俄国雅萨克体系。

en: Oconee was a Hitchiti-speaking tribal town of the Southeastern Woodlands, its people kin to the Muskogee and sharing in the Mississippian heritage of the old Ocute chiefdom of the Oconee River valley. Spanish records first name the town among the Apalachicola Province communities strung along the lower Chattahoochee River. Between 1690 and 1692 Oconee moved east with the other province towns to central Georgia, settling on the river that now bears its name near the Ocmulgee, but in 1715, at the opening of the Yamasee War, the whole cluster returned to the Chattahoochee. There the town divided. Around 1750 a faction led by Ahaya, whom the British called Cowkeeper, migrated into Florida and camped beside the Alachua Savanna, building first the town of Alachua and then Cuscowilla, which William Bartram visited in 1774 and which was then the largest Seminole settlement; Hitchiti speakers from Sabacola, Tamathli, Apalachicola and other towns swelled it, and Ahaya's band became the Alachua Seminoles, the first Florida group to break openly with the Muscogee Confederacy. The Oconee who remained on the Chattahoochee stayed among the Lower Towns through the eighteenth century and shared the later Creek fate.
zh: 奥科尼是东南林地一支说希奇蒂语的部族城镇，与马斯科吉人同源，承袭了奥科尼河谷古老的奥库特酋邦的密西西比文化遗产。西班牙文献最早在查特胡奇河下游阿巴拉契科拉省的城镇群中提到它。1690至1692年间，奥科尼随该省各城东迁佐治亚中部，在奥克马尔吉附近、今以它命名的奥科尼河畔定居；但1715年亚马西战争爆发时，整群城镇又返回查特胡奇河。城镇此后一分为二：约1750年，被英国人称为“牧牛人”的阿哈亚率一支迁入佛罗里达，在阿拉楚阿草原旁落脚，先后建起阿拉楚阿和库斯科维拉两镇——威廉·巴特伦1774年到访时，库斯科维拉已是最大的塞米诺尔聚落；来自萨巴科拉、塔马斯利、阿巴拉契科拉等城的希奇蒂语居民不断汇入，阿哈亚的部众成为阿拉楚阿塞米诺尔人，也是第一个公开与马斯科吉联盟决裂的佛罗里达群体。留在查特胡奇河的奥科尼人则整个18世纪都生活在下游诸城之中，后来与克里克人共命运。

en: The Odawa, or Ottawa, are an Anishinaabe people whose name, from the word adaawe, means traders, a role they made famous across the Great Lakes. Their oral history traces a migration from the Atlantic Dawnland to the Straits of Mackinac, where they split from the Ojibwe and Potawatomi to form with them the Council of Three Fires; their early homeland centred on Manitoulin Island and the Bruce Peninsula of Ontario. Middlemen in an intertribal network dealing in furs, cornmeal, mats and medicinal herbs, they held a near monopoly over trade passing Green Bay and Sault Ste. Marie, and before 1670 French colonists often called every Algonquian speaker of the lakes an Odawa. The Beaver Wars of the mid-seventeenth century scattered and regrouped the lake peoples, and after the French founded Fort Detroit in 1701 many Odawa moved south into Michigan and Ohio. They fought beside the French against the British in the Seven Years' War, and in 1763 the Odawa chief Pontiac led a great pan-Indian rebellion against the new British garrisons. Later, under chiefs such as Egushawa, they fought in the Northwest Indian War until defeat at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and the Treaty of Greenville of 1795 opened Ohio to settlement; after the Indian Removal Act of 1830 the Ohio bands ceded their reserves and were removed to Kansas.
zh: 渥达瓦人（又译渥太华人）是阿尼希纳贝族群的一支，其名字源自adaawe一词，意为“商人”，而他们正是以这一角色闻名五大湖地区。口传历史称他们从大西洋沿岸的“黎明之地”迁徙到麦基诺水道，在那里与奥吉布瓦人、波塔瓦托米人分开，三方结成“三火议会”联盟；他们早期的家园以安大略的马尼图林岛和布鲁斯半岛为中心。作为部落间贸易网络的中间人，他们经营毛皮、玉米粉、席垫和药草，几乎垄断了经格林贝和苏圣玛丽流通的贸易，1670年以前，法国殖民者常把五大湖区所有说阿尔冈昆语的人都称作渥达瓦人。17世纪中叶的海狸战争使湖区各民族流散重组，1701年法国人建立底特律堡后，许多渥达瓦人南迁进入密歇根和俄亥俄。七年战争中他们与法国人并肩对英作战，1763年，渥达瓦人首领庞蒂亚克领导了一场声势浩大的泛印第安人起义，反抗新进驻的英国驻军。后来在埃古沙瓦等首领带领下，他们又参加西北印第安战争，直到1794年在鹿寨战败、1795年《格林维尔条约》使俄亥俄向定居者开放；1830年《印第安迁移法》通过后，俄亥俄的各支渥达瓦人割让保留地，被迁往堪萨斯。

en: The Ofayé, who call themselves Ofaié or Opaié, are a Macro-Jê people of central Brazil, once spread in small mobile bands along the right bank of the Paraná River, from the mouth of the Sucuriú to the headwaters of the Vacaria and Ivinhema, in what is now Mato Grosso do Sul. Non-indigenous travelers named them Xavante, from a word for savanna dwellers, although they have no link with the Xavante of the Rio das Mortes; their own language forms an independent branch of the Macro-Jê family, with Guachi as a dialect. The first written mention of them dates from 1617, on the Paraná bank, and between 1716 and 1748 the gold-rush expeditions probing the Tietê, Pardo and Aquidauana rivers found them between the Serra do Maracaju and the upper Paraná. Hunter-gatherers who fished the rivers in the dry season and hunted and gathered honey in the rains, they built circular villages of palm-thatched houses and crossed the Paraná to hunt, sharing its far bank with their enemies the Kaingang. The spread of cattle ranches in the nineteenth century drove them from the Vacaria campos, the heart of their territory, toward remoter streams.
zh: 奥法耶人自称奥法耶或奥帕耶，是巴西中部的大热语系族群，曾以小型游群散布在巴拉那河右岸，从苏库里乌河口一直到瓦卡里亚河与伊维涅马河的源头，即后来的南马托格罗索州。外来殖民者称他们为沙万特人，该词意为稀树草原居民，但他们与里奥达斯莫尔特斯的沙万特人并无关系；他们自己的语言构成大热语系中一个独立语支，瓜奇语是其方言。文献中首次提到他们是在1617年，地点为巴拉那河畔；1716至1748年间，沿铁特河、帕尔杜河和阿基道阿纳河探路的淘金远征队发现，他们活动在马拉卡茹山与巴拉那河上游之间。他们以狩猎采集为生，旱季在河中捕鱼，雨季外出打猎、采蜜，用棕榈茅草屋围成圆形村落，还会渡过巴拉那河狩猎，河对岸住着他们的敌人卡因冈人。19世纪牧场扩张，把他们从领地中心的瓦卡里亚草原逼向更偏远的河溪。

en: The Ofo, also called Mosopelea or Ofogoula, were a Siouan-speaking people whose villages stood on the upper Ohio River between the Muskingum and Scioto rivers, in the heart of the old Ohio Hopewell country. The Miami-Illinois name for the Ohio River, Mosopeleacipi, meaning river of the Mosopelea, preserves their memory there. In the early 1670s, during the Beaver Wars, the Seneca and other Haudenosaunee nations overran their towns, and the Ofo fled down the Mississippi, staying briefly with the Quapaw before joining the Tunica. Around 1700 French travelers found them on the Yazoo River, and after refusing to join the Natchez wars against the French they moved further south into Louisiana, where the remnant band merged with the Tunica and Biloxi and their Siouan-Catawban language fell extinct.
zh: 奥夫人又称莫索佩利亚人或奥福古拉人，是一支说苏语的民族，村落位于俄亥俄河上游、马斯金格姆河与赛欧托河之间，正处在古俄亥俄霍普韦尔文化的中心地带。迈阿密-伊利诺伊语把俄亥俄河称作 Mosopeleacipi，意为“莫索佩利亚人之河”，仍留存着对他们的记忆。17世纪70年代初的海狸战争中，塞内卡等易洛魁联盟部族攻占了他们的村镇，奥夫人沿密西西比河南逃，先短暂寄居于夸保人处，随后投奔图尼卡人。约1700年，法国旅人在亚祖河畔见到他们；由于拒绝加入纳奇兹人对法国人的战争，他们继续南迁至路易斯安那，残余部众最终融入图尼卡人和比洛克西人，他们的苏语-卡托巴语也随之消亡。

en: The Ogulmiut are a regional group of Central Alaskan Yup'ik people on the northern coast of the Alaska Peninsula, around the Ugashik and Egegik rivers on the southern shore of Bristol Bay, where Yup'ik country bordered that of the Sugpiaq, or Alutiiq. They lived by salmon fishing and sea-mammal hunting before Russian-American Company traders entered Bristol Bay around 1800.
zh: 奥古尔缪特人是中阿拉斯加尤皮克人的一个区域群体，住在阿拉斯加半岛北岸的乌加希克河与埃格吉克河一带、布里斯托尔湾南岸，正是尤皮克人与苏格皮克人（阿鲁蒂克人）地域相接的地方。他们以捕鲑鱼和猎海洋哺乳动物为生，约1800年前后俄美公司商人进入布里斯托尔湾，将其卷入毛皮贸易。

en:
The Ohlone, once called Costanoans from the Spanish word for coast dwellers, are the Native people of the Northern California shoreline, holding the coast from San Francisco Bay through Monterey Bay to the lower Salinas Valley. They were never one people but more than fifty autonomous village lands, among them the Mutsun, Awaswas and Chochenyo, whose closely related languages form the Costanoan branch of the Utian family, formerly placed within the Penutian phylum. They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, above all by pounding acorns into meal, and shared the Kuksu ceremonial religion with other Californian groups.

The Spanish expedition of 1769 opened their country to mission rule: Franciscans founded Mission Dolores in 1776 and San Juan Bautista, which gathered the Mutsun, in 1797. Disease and forced resettlement cut their numbers sharply, and when the missions were secularized in 1834 the surviving Ohlone were left landless among the ranches of the new Mexican California.
zh:
奥洛内人旧称科斯塔诺人，名称源自西班牙语“海滨居民”，是北加州海岸的原住民，地盘从旧金山湾经蒙特雷湾延伸到萨利纳斯河谷下游。他们从来不是一个统一民族，而是五十多个各自为政的村社，穆聪人、阿瓦斯瓦斯人和乔琴约人都在其中；这些村社所说的近亲语言构成乌蒂安语系下的科斯塔诺语支，旧说曾将其归入佩努蒂大语系。他们以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，尤其靠把橡子捣成粉过活，并与加州其他族群共同信奉库克苏仪式宗教。

1769年西班牙探险队到来后，奥洛内人的土地被纳入传教体制：方济各会于1776年建立多洛雷斯传教站，1797年又建立收拢穆聪人的圣胡安·包蒂斯塔传教站。疾病和强迫迁徙使人口锐减；1834年传教站世俗化后，幸存的奥洛内人在墨西哥治下加州的大牧场之间失去了土地。

en: The Oirat are the western Mongols, forest-origin herdsmen whose name combines the Mongolic words for forest and people and whose home lay around the Altai, Tuva and the Khovd lakes. Subdued by Jochi in 1207, they joined the Mongol Empire as a valued military faction. After the Yuan lost China in 1368 the Oirat regrouped in the Altai as the Four Oirats, the Dzungar, Torghut, Dörbet and Khoshut tribes, and with Ming backing eclipsed the eastern Borjigid khans. Their strongest leader, Esen Taishi, ruled from 1438 to 1454, unified the Mongols and in 1449 captured the Zhengtong Emperor of the Ming at Tumu. Around 1615 the Oirat adopted Tibetan Buddhism, and in the 1600s the Khoshut monk Zaya Pandita gave them the Clear Script based on the Mongolian alphabet. The tribes then fanned out: Güshi Khan led the Khoshuts to conquer Amdo in 1637 and Tibet in the early 1640s, while the Torghuts migrated to the Volga by 1630, becoming the Kalmyks, whose survivors trekked back to Dzungaria in 1771. The Dzungars built the last steppe empire, with their own guns and laws, until the Qing conquest of 1755 to 1757 destroyed the khanate and much of its people.
zh: 瓦剌人是西支蒙古人，源出森林部落，其名称由蒙古语“森林”和“人”组合而成，故土在阿尔泰、图瓦和科布多湖群一带。1207年他们被术赤征服，随后成为蒙古帝国倚重的军事力量。1368年元朝退出中原后，瓦剌人在阿尔泰重组为“四瓦剌”，即准噶尔、土尔扈特、杜尔伯特和和硕特四部，并在明朝支持下压过东部的孛儿只斤系汗廷。其最强首领也先太师在1438—1454年掌权，统一蒙古，更于1449年在土木堡俘虏明英宗。约1615年，瓦剌皈依藏传佛教；17世纪，和硕特僧人咱雅班第达在蒙古文基础上为他们创制了托忒文。此后四部各奔东西：固始汗率和硕特人于1637年征服安多，又在17世纪40年代初统一西藏；土尔扈特人则于1630年前西迁伏尔加河，成为卡尔梅克人，其幸存者在1771年长途东归准噶尔。准噶尔人建立了最后的草原帝国，自造火器、自立法度，直到1755—1757年清朝的征服摧毁汗国，其部众也大量丧亡。

en: The Ojibwe, also called Ojibway or Chippewa, are the largest of the Anishinaabe peoples, whose homeland Ojibwewaki stretches around the upper Great Lakes from Lake Huron and Lake Superior west toward the plains. Their oral tradition tells of a long migration west from the Atlantic coast guided by miigis spirits, and at the Straits of Mackinac they separated from their kin the Odawa and Potawatomi, with whom they kept the alliance of the Council of Three Fires. French missionaries first mentioned them in the Jesuit Relation of 1640; armed through the fur trade, they checked the Haudenosaunee near Lake Superior in 1662, drove the Dakota from the upper Mississippi and pushed the Meskwaki out of northern Wisconsin. By the late eighteenth century they controlled most of Michigan, northern Wisconsin and Minnesota and the entire north shores of lakes Huron and Superior. Those settled at the rapids of Sault Ste. Marie were called Saulteurs, later Saulteaux, while the Mississaugas branched off toward southern Ontario. They allied with the French in the Seven Years' War and later with the British in the War of 1812, hoping to shield their lands from settler expansion. Known for birchbark canoes and scrolls, copper working, wild rice and maple sugar harvesting and the Midewiwin medicine society, the Ojibwe faced growing pressure to cede territory and, after the Indian Removal Act of 1830, resisted forced removal west of the Mississippi.
zh: 奥吉布瓦人又称奥吉布韦人或奇佩瓦人，是阿尼希纳贝诸族中人数最多的一支，家园奥吉布瓦瓦基环绕五大湖上游，从休伦湖、苏必利尔湖向西延伸到大草原边缘。他们的口传传统讲述了在米吉斯神灵指引下自大西洋沿岸西迁的漫长历程，在麦基诺水道与亲族渥达瓦人、波塔瓦托米人分开，此后三方一直维系着“三火议会”联盟。法国传教士在1640年的《耶稣会纪事》中首次提到他们；借助毛皮贸易获得火器后，他们于1662年在苏必利尔湖附近挡住了霍德诺索尼人的进攻，把达科他人逐出密西西比河上游，并迫使梅斯克瓦基人离开威斯康星北部。到18世纪末，奥吉布瓦人已控制密歇根大部、威斯康星北部、明尼苏达以及休伦湖和苏必利尔湖的整个北岸。定居在苏圣玛丽急流一带的人被称为索尔特人，即后来的索托人；米西索加人则向南安大略分出去。他们在七年战争中与法国结盟，1812年战争中又支持英国，希望借此阻挡定居者蚕食自己的土地。奥吉布瓦人以桦皮舟和桦皮卷轴、铜器加工、采集野米和枫糖以及米德维温医药社闻名；1830年《印第安迁移法》通过后，他们面临越来越大的割地压力，并抵制了被强制迁往密西西比河以西的命运。

en: The Syilx, also called the Okanagan, are an Interior Salish people of the Northwest Plateau whose homeland covers the basin of Okanagan Lake and the Okanagan River, together with the Similkameen valley and the upper Nicola River, in what is now southern British Columbia and northern Washington. They speak Nsyilxcn, an Interior Salish language, and count the Sinixt, Shuswap and Nlaka'pamux among their close kin. Syilx families followed a seasonal round, moving between fishing, hunting and root-and-berry gathering grounds, and wintered in semi-permanent villages of kekulis, round earth-covered pit houses, while summer camps used conical lodges of tule mats. Each village governed itself. The Spaxomin community of the Nicola Valley stood on the western edge of Syilx country and was linked by marriage and alliance to neighbouring Nlaka'pamux bands. Europeans first reached the wider Interior Salish region in 1793, when Alexander Mackenzie entered Shuswap territory, and the fur trader Simon Fraser travelled the Fraser River in 1808.
zh: 西尔克斯人又称奥卡诺根人，是西北高原的内陆萨利什人，家乡在今加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省南部和美国华盛顿州北部，涵盖奥卡诺根湖与奥卡诺根河流域，以及锡米尔卡明河谷和尼古拉河上游。他们讲内陆萨利什语支的恩西尔克斯肯语，与西尼克斯特人、舒斯瓦普人和恩拉卡帕穆克人是近亲。西尔克斯人按季节迁徙轮换，往返于捕鱼、狩猎和采集块根、浆果的场地；冬天住在半永久性的村落里，住房是圆形覆土坑屋“凯库利斯”，夏季营地则用芦苇席搭成锥形棚屋，各村自行管理。尼古拉河谷的斯帕克索明群落地处西尔克斯人疆域西缘，通过联姻和结盟与邻近的恩拉卡帕穆克诸部相连。欧洲人最早于1793年进入内陆萨利什地区，当时亚历山大·麦肯齐踏入舒斯瓦普人的土地；毛皮商人西蒙·弗雷泽则于1808年沿弗雷泽河而下。

en: The Olo, also called Orlei, are a Torricelli-speaking people of the Aitape hinterland in Sandaun Province, living in a chain of inland villages stretching south from the coast. Their Wapei-branch language is divided into Payi and Wapi dialects, linked by gradual dialect chaining.
zh: 奥洛人又称奥尔莱人，是桑道恩省艾塔佩腹地的托里切利语族族群，住在从海岸向南延伸的一连串内陆村庄里。他们的语言属瓦佩伊语支，分为帕伊和瓦皮两种方言，彼此以渐变的方言链相连。

en: The Lamskiye were a small Evenki band who pastured reindeer and hunted sable along the upper Olyokma and the western Stanovoy taiga, between the Lena and Amur basins. Cossacks built the ostrog of Olyokminsk at the river's mouth in 1635, drawing these Tungus hunters into the Russian fur-tribute system.
zh: 奥廖克马人是一小支鄂温克游猎群，在奥廖克马河上游与斯塔诺夫山脉西麓、勒拿河和黑龙江流域之间的泰加林里牧放驯鹿、猎取紫貂。1635年哥萨克在河口修建奥廖克明斯克堡，这支通古斯猎人随后被纳入俄国的毛皮贡赋体系。

en: The Olyuben were a tundra Yukaghir tribal group of the lower Indigirka River in northeastern Siberia. When Cossack fur collectors entered the region in the seventeenth century, the tribe was led by two princely brothers, Morle and Burulga; the meaning of its name is not recorded. Like the other Yukaghir clans they were registered as payers of fur tribute, but the smallpox epidemics that swept the lower Indigirka in the second half of the 1600s struck the small, scattered tundra band hardest. By 1700 the Olyuben had ceased to appear in the tribute records as a separate people, their lineages dying out or merging into the surrounding Yukaghir clans.
zh: 奥柳边人是东西伯利亚因迪吉尔卡河下游的苔原尤卡吉尔部落。哥萨克毛皮税征收者进入这一地区时，部落由两位酋长兄弟莫尔列和布鲁尔加率领，族名的含义已不可考。和其他尤卡吉尔氏族一样，他们被登记为毛皮贡赋的缴纳者，但17世纪下半叶反复席卷因迪吉尔卡河下游的天花，对这个人口不多、散居苔原的小群体打击最重。到1700年前后，奥柳边人已不再作为独立群体出现在贡赋册籍中，其氏族或绝嗣，或并入了周围的尤卡吉尔部落。

en: The Omaguaca, or Humahuaca, were a confederation of farming peoples in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a narrow mountain corridor in what is now Jujuy Province, Argentina, reaching south into the Salta valleys and north towards Tupiza. Their bands, among them the Tilcara, Purmamarca, Uquía and Tumbaya, grew maize on stone terraces, herded llamas, cast bronze tools and made distinctive red pottery painted with black geometric designs. The Incas, advancing with Aymara allies, annexed the valley to Collasuyo around 1400, though some scholars place it as late as 1471, turning Tilcara into an administrative centre and planting mitmae colonies, while the fortress of Pucará de Juella shows signs of resistance. Their now-extinct tongue may have been related to the Kunza of the Atacameños. After the Spanish founding of Jujuy, the curaca Viltipoco of Humahuaca and Purmamarca united the bands and destroyed the town of San Francisco de Álava in 1576; in 1594 he led several thousand warriors against San Salvador de Velasco in the Calchaquí Wars, but was defeated by Francisco de Argañaraz y Murguía. Indian cabildos at Humahuaca and Tilcara then governed the survivors under colonial rule.
zh: 奥马瓦卡人又称乌马瓦卡人，是今阿根廷胡胡伊省乌马瓦卡峡谷的农耕部落联盟，势力向南延伸到萨尔塔诸河谷，向北抵达玻利维亚的图皮萨一带。其下包括蒂尔卡拉、普尔马马尔卡、乌基亚、通巴亚等支派，在石砌梯田上种植玉米，放牧羊驼，铸造青铜器具，并烧制以黑色几何纹为特色的红陶。印加人在艾马拉盟友协助下于1400年前后（一说晚至1471年）把峡谷并入科利亚苏尤，将蒂尔卡拉建成行政中心并派驻米特马埃移民，而胡埃利亚普卡拉堡垒留下了抵抗的痕迹。他们现已消亡的语言可能与阿塔卡马人的昆萨语有亲缘关系。西班牙人建立胡胡伊城后，乌马瓦卡和普尔马马尔卡的酋长维尔蒂波科联合各支派，于1576年摧毁圣弗朗西斯科-德阿拉瓦城；1594年他在卡尔查基战争中率数千战士攻打圣萨尔瓦多-德贝拉斯科，被弗朗西斯科·德·阿加尼亚拉斯·伊·穆尔吉亚击败。此后乌马瓦卡和蒂尔卡拉的印第安人市政议会在殖民统治下管理幸存的民众。

en: The Umoho, known in history as the Omaha, are a Dhegiha Siouan people whose name means those going against the current. Around 1600 they formed one woodland people with the Quapaw near the Ohio and Wabash rivers, then migrated west and split: the Quapaw went down the Mississippi while the Omaha settled along the upper Missouri in present-day Iowa and Nebraska, with the Ponca branching off in the mid-eighteenth century. The French trader Le Sueur described an Omaha village of four hundred dwellings on the Big Sioux River in 1700, and Delisle mapped them as a wandering nation of the upper Missouri in 1718. About 1770 they became the first equestrian people of the Northern Plains, and Chief Blackbird built the Big Village, Ton-wa-tonga, in northeast Nebraska, from which the Omaha controlled the fur trade reaching up the river. A smallpox epidemic around 1800 killed about a third of the tribe, Blackbird among them. Through treaties in 1831 and 1836 they ceded their lands east of the Missouri and their hunting grounds in northwestern Missouri to the United States.
zh: 乌莫霍人即史书上的奥马哈人，属德吉哈苏语族群，族名意为“逆流而上之人”。1600年前后，他们与夸保人还是俄亥俄河与沃巴什河畔的同一个林地部族，随后西迁并分裂：夸保人沿密西西比河而下，奥马哈人定居在今艾奥瓦和内布拉斯加一带的密苏里河上游，蓬卡人则于18世纪中叶从他们中间分出。1700年，法国商人勒叙厄尔记述了大苏河畔一座有四百处住所的奥马哈村庄；1718年德利尔的地图把他们标为密苏里河上游的游居部族。约1770年，他们成为北部平原最早的骑马部族，酋长布莱克伯德在内布拉斯加东北修建大村庄通瓦通加，奥马哈人借此控制了溯河而上的毛皮贸易。1800年前后的天花疫情夺去约三分之一族人的生命，布莱克伯德也未能幸免。通过1831年和1836年的两项条约，他们把密苏里河以东的土地和密苏里西北的猎场割让给了美国。

en: The Omani are the Arabs of southeastern Arabia, settled in the ports of the Batinah coast, among them Muscat, Sohar and Sib, and in the inland strongholds of Rustaq and Nakhl beneath the Jebel Akhdar. Their forebears include the copper-trading land of Magan, known to the Sumerians, and Arab tribes led by the Azd who migrated from Yemen after the collapse of the Marib Dam. Islam reached them in the seventh century through the envoy Amr ibn al-As, and after the Battle of Dibba in 632 they adopted Ibadi Islam, a moderate Kharijite rite brought from Basra; the first elective Ibadi imamate was founded around 750. The Nabhani kings of Bahla then controlled the frankincense trade from 1154 until Portuguese fleets under Albuquerque seized Muscat in 1507, beginning 143 years of coastal rule. In 1624 Nasir bin Murshid founded the Yaruba dynasty at Rustaq, whose imams expelled the Portuguese by 1650 and built a maritime empire that took Mombasa in 1698 and Bahrain in 1700. Civil war and Persian intervention after 1718 ended the dynasty, and Ahmad bin Said founded the Al Bu Said rule in 1744; his successors made Oman an Indian Ocean power centered on Muscat and Zanzibar, and signed their first treaty with the British East India Company in 1798.
zh: 阿曼人是阿拉伯半岛东南部的阿拉伯人，聚居于巴提纳海岸的马斯喀特、苏哈尔、锡卜等港口，以及绿山脚下鲁斯塔克、纳赫勒等内陆要塞。他们的先民包括苏美尔人所知的铜贸古国马干，以及马里卜水坝溃决后从也门迁来的艾兹德等阿拉伯部落。7世纪，使者阿慕尔·本·阿斯将伊斯兰教带到这里；632年迪巴战役后，他们接受了自巴士拉传来的哈瓦利吉派温和分支艾巴德派，约750年建立起选举产生的第一个艾巴德派伊玛目国。1154年起，定都巴赫莱的纳卜哈尼诸王掌控乳香贸易，直到1507年阿尔布克尔克率领的葡萄牙舰队攻占马斯喀特，开启了长达143年的沿海统治。1624年，纳西尔·本·穆尔希德在鲁斯塔克建立雅鲁卜王朝，历代伊玛目于1650年赶走葡萄牙人，建立海上帝国，1698年夺取蒙巴萨，1700年占领巴林。1718年后的内战与波斯干涉终结了该王朝，艾哈迈德·本·赛义德于1744年建立阿布·赛义德王朝；其继承者把阿曼经营成以马斯喀特和桑给巴尔为中心的印度洋强国，并于1798年与英国东印度公司签订首个条约。

en: The Ometo are a cluster of Omotic-speaking peoples of the Afro-Asiatic family who farm the highlands and river valleys of southern Ethiopia, around the upper Omo and the lakes of the Rift Valley. They include the Wolayta, Gamo, Gofa, Dawro and Dorze, whose closely related speech forms the Ometo dialect cluster, the largest group within Omotic. Their medieval political tradition centres on the kingdom later remembered as Damot and then Wolaita, whose kings bore the title Kawo and whose Malla dynasties ruled from the thirteenth century. Adal forces briefly occupied Wolaita in the sixteenth century, after which Oromo expansion pressed the Ometo polities into smaller highland territories; King Gazenja won several victories over the Oromo in the seventeenth century, and by 1830 Wolaita had become a tributary of the Kingdom of Kaffa. The Gamo highlanders kept a strict caste order of farmers and artisan clans and were known for weaving and enset cultivation.
zh: 奥梅托人是操亚非语系奥莫特语族语言的一群族群，在埃塞俄比亚南部的高地与河谷、奥莫河上游和东非大裂谷湖泊一带务农，包括沃莱塔人、加莫人、戈法人、道罗人和多尔泽人；他们关系相近的语言构成奥梅托方言群，是奥莫特语族中最大的一支。其中世纪政治传统围绕先后被称为达莫特和沃莱塔的王国展开，国王称号为卡沃，马拉王朝自13世纪起统治此地。16世纪阿达尔军队曾短暂占领沃莱塔，此后奥罗莫人的扩张把奥梅托诸邦压缩到更小的高地领土；17世纪国王加曾贾数次击败奥罗莫人，到1830年沃莱塔已沦为卡法王国的属邦。加莫高地人保持着由农民和工匠种姓组成的严格等级秩序，以纺织和种植象腿蕉闻名。

en: The Myene are a cluster of Bantu-speaking peoples on the coast and river estuaries of Gabon, including the Mpongwe, Galwa, Nkomi, Orungu and Adyumba groups, whose villages line the lower Ogooue River around places such as Lambarene. Counted among the earliest Bantu settlers of the Gabonese coast, they lived by fishing, river and seaborne trade, and skilled woodworking, and their society was organized into matrilineal clans and villages under chiefs. When Portuguese ships reached the area in the 1470s, Myene speakers were already established along the shore, and their canoes and trading chiefs became key intermediaries in the Atlantic commerce of the following centuries, exchanging ivory, dyewood and, increasingly, slaves with European merchants. Their closely related vernaculars form the Myene language cluster, one of the most distinctive branches of the Bantu family, traditionally grouped by linguists with the neighbouring Tsogo languages. Ancestor worship and cults of nature spirits shaped religious life before the spread of Christianity, and Myene mask and canoe carving fed into the wider sculptural traditions of Gabon.
zh: 米耶内人是生活在加蓬沿海和河口地带的一群班图语族群，包括姆蓬圭、加尔瓦、恩科米、奥龙古和阿詹巴等支系，他们的村落散布在奥果韦河下游兰巴雷内一带。他们是加蓬沿海最早的班图定居者之一，以捕鱼、河海贸易和精细木工为生，社会按母系氏族和酋长治理的村落组织起来。1470年代葡萄牙船只抵达这一地区时，米耶内语族群早已在沿岸定居；在随后几个世纪里，他们的独木舟和经商酋长成为大西洋贸易的关键中间人，用象牙、染料木以及后来越来越多的奴隶与欧洲商人交换货物。他们彼此相近的土语构成米耶内语群，是班图语系中最有特色的分支之一，语言学家传统上把它与邻近的措戈诸语归为一类。在基督教传播之前，祖先崇拜和自然神灵信仰塑造了他们的宗教生活，而米耶内人的面具与独木舟雕刻也融入了加蓬更广泛的雕塑传统。

en: Omo refers to the farming and herding peoples of the lower Omo valley in southern Ethiopia, centred on the Konso country south of Lake Chamo. The Konso dwelt in walled, terraced hill towns under councils of elders and followed a generation-grading system akin to the Oromo gadaa, while South Omotic neighbours such as the Hamar herded cattle along the river.
zh: 奥莫指埃塞俄比亚南部奥莫河下游、以查莫湖以南孔索地区为中心的农牧族群。孔索人住在有围墙的山坡梯田城镇里，由长老议事会治理，实行与奥罗莫加达制相近的年龄等级制度；邻近的哈马尔人等南奥莫特语族群则沿河半农半牧。

en: The Omok were the largest of the tundra Yukaghir tribes, nomadizing along the lower Kolyma and the Omolon in present-day northeastern Sakha Republic; their name comes from a Yukaghir word omo, meaning clan or tribe. In 1659 the Russian tally counted 620 Omok in eleven clans, 155 of them fur-tribute payers, but warfare, the smallpox epidemics of 1669 and the 1690s and absorption by Even, Yakut and Russian neighbours had cut them to fifty-four people by 1693. Their language, an eastern Yukaghir tongue, survived into the eighteenth century, and a word list was recorded in 1821 by the explorer Fyodor Matyushkin.
zh: 奥莫克人是苔原尤卡吉尔诸部中最大的一支，在今萨哈共和国东北部的下科雷马河与奥莫隆河一带游牧；其族名来自尤卡吉尔语的奥莫一词，意为氏族或部落。1659年俄国的赋役册上登记有620名奥莫克人，分属11个氏族，其中155人缴纳毛皮税。但战乱、1669年和1690年代的天花，加上被邻族鄂温人、雅库特人和俄国人同化，到1693年他们只剩54人。他们的语言属尤卡吉尔语东支，18世纪尚有人使用，1821年探险家费奥多尔·马秋什金为它记下了一份词汇表。

en: The Ongamo, also called Ngasa, are an Eastern Nilotic people of the northeastern slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro in what is now Tanzania, whose language is a close relative of the Maa tongues spoken by the Maasai and Samburu. In the 1100s Ongamo speakers spread onto the plains north of the mountain, at a time when their speech was still mutually intelligible with proto-Maa; their retained vocabulary shows they grew sorghum and finger millet. Over the following five centuries the immigration of Bantu-speaking Chagga farmers up the mountain slopes steadily enclosed and reduced the Ongamo communities, who gradually gave up their language for Kichagga and were absorbed into the Chagga chiefdoms of Kilimanjaro.
zh: 翁加莫人又称恩加萨人，是东尼罗河语族群，住在今天坦桑尼亚乞力马扎罗山的东北坡，其语言与马赛人、桑布鲁人的马赛语支是近亲。12世纪，翁加莫语者扩散到乞力马扎罗山以北的平原，当时他们的语言与原始马赛语尚能互通；留存的词汇表明他们种植高粱和穇子。此后五个世纪里，说班图语的查加农民陆续迁入山坡，翁加莫社群逐渐被包围、削弱，最终放弃本族语言改用基查加语，并入乞力马扎罗山上的诸查加酋邦。

en: The Onghniaahra, recorded by the French as the Onguiaahra or Ongniaahraronon, were an Iroquoian-speaking tribe of the Neutral Confederacy of southern Ontario. Their name meant “near the big waters” or “the strait,” and they held the Niagara Peninsula at the eastern end of Neutral territory, between Lake Ontario and Lake Erie; the word Niagara itself is thought to derive from their name. Like other Neutral peoples they lived in farming villages, hunted deer and traded dressed skins and furs to the Wendat for French goods. Jesuits called the confederacy Neutral because it stood apart from the wars of the Wendat and the Haudenosaunee, but that did not save it: in 1651 Haudenosaunee armies overran the Neutral towns, and the Onghniaahra dispersed with the rest, their survivors joining neighbouring Iroquoian nations.
zh: 翁尼亚拉人在法国记载中作 Onguiaahra 或 Ongniaahraronon，是今安大略省南部中立联盟的一支易洛魁语部族。其名字意为“靠近大水”或“海峡”，他们占据中立联盟领土东端、安大略湖与伊利湖之间的尼亚加拉半岛；“尼亚加拉”一词本身就被认为源自他们的族名。和其他中立人一样，他们住在农耕村落里，猎鹿并把加工过的鹿皮和毛皮卖给温达特人，换取法国货物。耶稣会传教士称这个联盟为“中立”，因为它置身温达特人与易洛魁联盟的战争之外，但这并未挽救它：1651年易洛魁军队攻陷中立联盟的城镇，翁尼亚拉人随之离散，幸存者加入了邻近的易洛魁语民族。

en: The Onoid were a Yukaghir tribal group who held the middle and upper reaches of the Yana River in northern Siberia and spoke its Yan, or Detkil, dialect. In the Russian fur-tribute books of the later 1600s they are entered as the Yukaghirs of the Zelyansky clan. Their neighbors knew them by a harsh name: onondi means robbers or plunderers, which the ethnographer Vladimir Jochelson derived from the Yukaghir verb ono, to seize by force. Like the other Yan-dialect clans they were drawn into the tribute system, then thinned by epidemics and by warfare with Even and Evenki groups, and in the course of the colonial period the Onoid vanish from the records as a separate community.
zh: 奥诺伊德人是已消亡的尤卡吉尔部落，占据西伯利亚北部亚纳河的中游和上游，使用尤卡吉尔语的亚纳（杰特基尔）方言。17世纪下半叶的俄国毛皮贡赋册籍把他们记作泽利扬氏族的尤卡吉尔人。邻人给他们的名字颇为凶悍：“奥诺恩迪”意为强盗、劫掠者，民族学家弗拉基米尔·约赫尔松认为它出自尤卡吉尔语动词“奥诺”，即以武力夺取。和其他说亚纳方言的氏族一样，他们被纳入贡赋体系，又在疫病以及与埃文人、鄂温克人各部的战争中不断减员，最终在殖民时代作为独立群体从册籍中消失。

en: The Onojutta, or Onojutta-Haga, were a small Iroquoian-speaking people of the Juniata River valley in southern Pennsylvania, kin to the Susquehannock. By 1648 they had become forced auxiliaries of the more powerful Susquehannock and were probably absorbed into them, sharing their dispersal from the Susquehanna Valley later in the seventeenth century.
zh: 奥诺朱塔人全称奥诺朱塔—哈加人，又称朱尼亚塔人，是宾夕法尼亚南部朱尼亚塔河流域的一支小型易洛魁语族群，与萨斯奎哈诺克人同源。到1648年，他们已被迫充当更强大的萨斯奎哈诺克人的附庸，后来很可能被其同化，并在17世纪后期随之一同被逐出萨斯奎哈纳河谷。

en: The Onondadega, or People of the Hills, are the central nation of the five founding members of the Haudenosaunee, or Iroquois Confederacy, whose homeland lay among the hills south of Lake Ontario in what became Onondaga County, New York. Oral tradition holds they were the last of the five nations to accept the Great Peacemaker, joining only after Hiawatha healed the feared chief Tadodaho, an event linked to an eclipse possibly seen in 1142; the Tree of Peace was planted on their land and Onondaga became the confederacy's capital and the seat of its Grand Council. As Keepers of the Fire they supply the council's presiding officer, the Tadodaho, and fourteen of its chiefs. In the American Revolution they began neutral, but after American troops burned their main village in April 1779 they joined the British; the Sullivan Expedition devastated their towns, and at the peace many followed Joseph Brant to new lands at Six Nations in Upper Canada. Those who remained kept their reservation through the Treaty of Canandaigua of 1794, which acknowledged their right to their homeland.
zh: 奥农达加人意为“丘陵之人”，是霍迪诺肖尼（即易洛魁）联盟五个创始民族中居中的一个，家园在今纽约州奥农达加县境内、安大略湖以南的丘陵地带。口传传统称他们是五族中最后接受大和平缔造者的一个，直到海华沙治好令人畏惧的首领塔多达霍后才加入联盟，此事与可能发生在1142年的一次日食有关；和平之树栽种在他们的土地上，奥农达加由此成为联盟首府和大议会会址。作为“圣火守护者”，他们出掌议会主持者塔多达霍一职，并提供14名酋长。美国独立战争初期他们保持中立，但1779年4月美军焚毁其主要村庄后转而联英作战；沙利文远征摧毁了他们的城镇，战后许多人随约瑟夫·布兰特前往上加拿大的六族新领地。留下的人则凭1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》保住了保留地，条约承认了他们对故土的权利。

en: The Onondowaga, or Great Hill People, called Seneca by English colonists, were the westernmost of the five founding nations of the Haudenosaunee, or Iroquois Confederacy, and so were known as Keepers of the Western Door. Their homeland lay between the Genesee River and Canandaigua Lake south of Lake Ontario, where their largest town, Ganondagan, held a hundred and fifty longhouses in the seventeenth century. An eclipse remembered in oral tradition dates their entry into the confederacy to about 1142. Already the most populous of the five nations, they fought the Beaver Wars alongside the others and in 1675 crushed the Andaste, or Susquehannock, absorbing the survivors; in 1687 a French army under the Marquis de Denonville landed at Irondequoit Bay and destroyed Ganondagan, after which the Seneca leaned toward the British Covenant Chain. In the American Revolution most Seneca followed the British side, and the Sullivan Expedition of 1779 burned their towns and winter stores. The Treaty of Canandaigua of 1794 let the remnants keep lands in western New York, where the Seneca prophet Handsome Lake, who died in 1815, taught the religious code that bore his name.
zh: 奥农多瓦加人意为“大山丘之人”，英国殖民者称其为塞尼卡人，是霍迪诺肖尼（即易洛魁）联盟五个创始民族中位置最西的一个，因而号称“西门守护者”。他们的家园在安大略湖以南、杰纳西河与卡南代瓜湖之间；17世纪时，他们最大的城镇加农达甘有150座长屋。口传传统中记有一次日食，据此把他们加入联盟的时间定在约1142年。塞尼卡人本就是五族中人口最多的，又随联盟参加海狸战争，于1675年击垮安达斯特人（即萨斯奎哈诺克人）并吸收其遗民；1687年，德农维尔侯爵率领的法军在艾昂德科伊特湾登陆，摧毁加农达甘，此后塞尼卡人倒向英国的“契约链”同盟。美国独立战争中多数塞尼卡人站在英国一边，1779年的沙利文远征焚毁了他们的城镇和冬粮。1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》使遗民得以保有纽约州西部的土地；塞尼卡先知帅湖于1815年去世，他所传授的宗教规法以其名字流传。

en: The Onyot'aaka, or People of the Standing Stone, called Oneida by English colonists, are one of the five founding nations of the Haudenosaunee, or Iroquois Confederacy, with their homeland around Oneida Lake in central New York, between the Mohawk to the east and the Onondaga to the west. In the early seventeenth century their territory covered some six million acres, its boundary first fixed in the Treaty of Fort Stanwix of 1768. A matrilineal people divided into Wolf, Turtle and Bear clans, they were drawn toward the rebel colonists through the Presbyterian missionary Samuel Kirkland, who had worked among them since 1764. When the American Revolution split the confederacy, most Onyot'aaka backed the revolutionaries: about fifty fought at the Battle of Oriskany in 1777, and that same year Chief Skenandon sent maize to the starving army at Valley Forge, carried there by Polly Cooper. Loyalist raiders destroyed their main town of Kanonwalohale in retaliation. The Treaty of Canandaigua of 1794 granted them six million acres as the first reservation in the United States, but New York State later reduced it to a few dozen acres, driving many Onyot'aaka to Wisconsin and Canada in the 1820s and 1830s.
zh: 奥尼奥塔卡人意为“立石之人”，英国殖民者称其为奥奈达人，是霍迪诺肖尼（即易洛魁）联盟五个创始民族之一，家园在纽约州中部的奥奈达湖一带，东接莫霍克人、西邻奥农达加人。17世纪初他们的领地约有600万英亩，边界最早由1768年的《斯坦威克斯堡条约》划定。奥尼奥塔卡人按母系继嗣，分为狼、龟、熊三个氏族；长老会传教士塞缪尔·柯克兰自1764年起在他们中间传教，使他们逐渐倾向反叛的殖民地一方。美国独立战争导致联盟分裂时，多数奥尼奥塔卡人支持革命者：约50人参加了1777年的奥里斯卡尼战役，同年斯凯南登酋长把玉米送往福吉谷接济断粮的军队，由波利·库珀带队押送，效忠派袭击者随后摧毁了他们的主要城镇卡农瓦洛黑利。1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》授予他们600万英亩土地，这是美国第一块印第安保留地，但纽约州后来把它削减到几十英亩，迫使许多奥尼奥塔卡人在19世纪20至30年代迁往威斯康星和加拿大。

en: The Oowekyala, who call themselves Wuikinuxv, meaning the Backbone people, are an Indigenous people of the central coast of British Columbia, holding the shores of Rivers Inlet and Owikeno Lake north of Queen Charlotte Strait. Their territory once ran from the mouth of Rivers Inlet to the headwaters of Owikeno Lake, with principal villages on the Wannock River linking the lake to the sea. Their Oowekyala tongue is a Northern Wakashan language, so close to Heiltsuk that the two are treated as dialects of one Heiltsuk–Oowekyala language, and it is also related to Haisla and Kwak'wala. Like other Northwest Coast peoples, the Oowekyala lived on salmon runs, sea mammal hunting and gathering, built villages of cedar plank houses, and organized society around the potlatch. Together with the Heiltsuk and Haisla they were once loosely labelled the Northern Kwakiutl, a name later rejected as inaccurate. When European maritime fur traders reached the central coast in the 1790s, the Oowekyala were drawn into the fiercer raiding and introduced diseases of the fur-trade era.
zh: 奥维基亚拉人自称 Wuikinuxv，意为“脊梁之人”，是不列颠哥伦比亚省中部海岸的原住民，据有夏洛特皇后海峡以北的里弗斯湾与奥维基诺湖一带，其领地曾从里弗斯湾湾口一直延伸到奥维基诺湖源头，主要村庄坐落在连通湖泊与海洋的万诺克河上。他们的奥维基亚拉语属于北瓦卡什语支，与海尔楚克语极为接近，二者被视为海尔楚克—奥维基亚拉语的两种方言，也与海斯拉语和夸夸瓦拉语有亲缘关系。和西北海岸其他民族一样，奥维基亚拉人以鲑鱼洄游、海猎和采集为生，村庄由雪松木板屋组成，社会生活围绕夸富宴展开。他们曾与海尔楚克人、海斯拉人一起被笼统称为“北夸扣特尔人”，这一名称后来被认定并不准确。18世纪90年代欧洲海上毛皮商人抵达中部海岸后，奥维基亚拉人也被卷入毛皮贸易时代愈演愈烈的劫掠与外来疫病之中。

en: The Opata are the agricultural Indians of the Opateria, the mountain valleys of north-eastern and central Sonora, made up of the Eudeve, Teguima and Jova groups. From about 1350 to 1550 they lived in independent statelets strung along the Sonora, Moctezuma and Bavispe rivers, towns of two- and three-storey adobe houses surrounded by irrigated fields of maize, beans, squash and cotton, trading cotton blankets for Zuni turquoise. They were the most numerous people in Sonora when the Spanish arrived, and in 1565 they drove off the expedition of Francisco Ibarra. Epidemics then broke the statelets into scattered rancherias. Jesuits led by Pedro Mendez opened the first mission in 1628 and had twenty-two by 1688; the Opata became Spanish allies and joined campaigns against the Apache. By 1800 most were Christians speaking Spanish, yet revolts continued after Mexican independence: three hundred warriors routed a thousand Spanish soldiers and sacked a mining town near Tonichi in 1820, and the leader Dolores Gutierrez was executed by the Mexicans in 1833. Their Uto-Aztecan language was already losing ground to Spanish.
zh: 奥帕塔人是务农的印第安人，故乡奥帕特里亚位于索诺拉东北部和中部的山谷中，由奥德韦、特吉马和霍瓦三个群体组成。约1350至1550年间，他们生活在索诺拉河、蒙特苏马河和巴维斯佩河沿岸一连串独立的小邦里：镇上有两三层的土坯房，四周是灌溉的玉米、菜豆、南瓜和棉田，还用棉毯交换祖尼人的绿松石。西班牙人到来时，他们是索诺拉人口最多的民族，1565年击退了弗朗西斯科·伊瓦拉的远征。随后的瘟疫使诸小邦瓦解为分散的小村。1628年，佩德罗·门德斯率领的耶稣会士建起第一座传教站，到1688年已有22座；奥帕塔人成为西班牙人的盟友，一同出征阿帕奇人。到1800年，他们大多已是基督徒并改说西班牙语，但墨西哥独立后反抗仍未止息：1820年，三百名战士击溃一千名西班牙士兵，洗劫了托尼奇附近的矿业城镇；首领多洛雷斯·古铁雷斯于1833年被墨西哥当局处决。他们的犹他—阿兹特克语系语言此时已在西班牙语面前节节后退。

en: Orang Asli, meaning original people, is the collective name for the indigenous tribes of the Malay Peninsula, divided by custom into the nomadic Semang hunter-gatherers of the northern jungles, the slash-and-burn Senoi of the central hills, and the settled Proto-Malay farmers of the south; the first two speak Aslian languages of the Austroasiatic family, carried into the peninsula roughly 3,800 years ago. They are heirs to far older populations, going back to the Hoabinhian foragers whose cave art at Tambun in Perak may be twelve thousand years old. For most of the first millennium they traded jungle resins, incense woods and feathers for salt, cloth and iron with the Indian and Mon merchants sailing to Kedah. Contact hardened into subjection: as early as 724 Srivijayan raiders were carrying off Negrito slaves, and the Malay word sakai came to mean both these people and bondslaves. After Melaka became the region's slave emporium in the early 1500s, Acehnese expeditions and, through the 1700s and early 1800s, Minangkabau and Batak raiders sacked inland villages, killing the men and selling women and children at the river ports. Many coastal communities were Malayised and converted, while those who kept their Aslian speech and spirit cults withdrew deeper into the Perak and Pahang rainforest.
zh: 阿斯里意为“原住民”，是马来半岛各土著部族的统称，按生计分为三群：北部丛林中游猎的塞芒人、中部山区刀耕火种的塞诺伊人、南部定居农耕的原始马来人；前两群讲南亚语系的阿斯里语支语言，该语支约在3800年前传入半岛。他们也是更古老居民的后裔，可上溯到和平文化的采集者，霹雳坦本岩画的历史或达一万两千年。第一个千年的大部分时间里，他们用丛林树脂、香木和羽毛，与航行到吉打的印度和孟人商人交换盐、布匹和铁器。接触后来变成奴役：早在724年，室利佛逝的掠奴队已在掳走塞芒奴隶，马来语“萨盖”一词既指这些人，也指奴仆。1500年代初马六甲成为区域奴隶贸易中心后，亚齐的远征队，以及整个1700年代和1800年代初的米南佳保人、巴达克人袭掠者不断洗劫内陆村庄，杀害成年男子，把妇孺卖到河港为奴。许多沿海社群被马来化并改宗，保留阿斯里语言和精灵祭祀的群体则退入霹雳和彭亨的雨林深处。

en: The Orang Laut, whose name means sea people in Malay, are a collection of Malayic-speaking seafaring tribes who lived in their boats among the islands and estuaries of the Riau Archipelago, the coasts of eastern Sumatra, the southern Malay Peninsula and Singapore, living by fishing, foraging and trading sea produce. The fourteenth-century Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan left the earliest known account of them when he described the boat-dwelling inhabitants of Temasek, the site of modern Singapore, in his Daoyi Zhilüe. Historically they served the maritime powers of the region: under Srivijaya, the Sultanate of Malacca and later the Sultanate of Johor they patrolled the surrounding seas, drove off pirates and steered merchants to their rulers' ports, in return receiving titles and gifts from the court. Their influence waned as the Johor-Malacca realm broke apart and Bugis warriors took over its naval role. The Orang Laut then shifted southward, and the Orang Gelam settled on the Singapore River in service of the Temenggong, forming the bulk of Singapore's population until the British arrived in 1819.
zh: 罗越人在马来语中意为“海上之民”，是若干说马来语族语言的航海部落的统称，世代以船为家，散居于廖内群岛、苏门答腊东部海岸、马来半岛南端和新加坡一带的岛屿与河口，以捕鱼、采集和贩运海产为生。14世纪中国旅行家汪大渊在《岛夷志略》中描述了淡马锡（今新加坡）以船为家的居民，这是已知关于他们最早的记载。历史上罗越人效力于本区域的海上强权：在室利佛逝、马六甲苏丹国及后来的柔佛苏丹国治下，他们巡逻邻近海域、击退海盗、引导商人前往宗主的港口，以此换取朝廷赐予的头衔和礼物。随着柔佛—马六甲政权解体、武吉斯人接管其海军角色，罗越人的势力衰落，逐渐向南迁移；其中的奥朗格拉姆人定居新加坡河，为天猛公效力，在1819年英国人到来之前构成新加坡人口的主体。

en: The Orang Rimba, meaning people of the forest and also called Anak Dalam, are mobile animist forest dwellers of the lowland jungles of Jambi and South Sumatra, for whom Kubu is a Malay outsiders' name implying people who take refuge in the woods beyond village and mosque. Their own oral traditions trace them to the Maalau Sesat who fled into the Bukit Duabelas forests, or to refugees from the Minangkabau lands of Pagaruyung, which fits the Malay character of their speech and the matrilineal traces in their custom; their language is an upstream Malay isolect of the Malayo-Polynesian family. In 1337 they lived in small shifting camps called tubo under elected leaders titled tumenggung, moving between swidden fields and nomadic foraging for wild yams, game, fish, honey, rattan and resins, which they bartered at riverine Malay markets. Their society was strongly egalitarian, standing apart from the hierarchical and increasingly Islamic sultanates growing up along the great rivers. Neighboring Malays distinguished settled, farming Kubu groups from the deeper-forest bands who avoided outside contact, a divide between the Orang Batin Sembilan and the Orang Rimba proper that persisted into modern times.
zh: 林巴人意为“森林里的人”，又称“阿纳克达拉姆”，是占碑和南苏门答腊低地丛林中游动的万物有灵论森林居民；“库布”是马来外族对他们的称呼，意指躲避在村落与清真寺之外、以林为庇的人。他们自己的口传传统称，其先民是逃入布基杜阿贝拉斯森林的“马劳·塞萨特”人，也有说法认为他们是从米南加保帕加鲁永地区出走的难民——这与他们语言的马来语属性及习俗中的母系残余相吻合，其语言属于马来–波利尼西亚语族的上游马来语方言。1337年时，他们住在名为“图博”的小型流动营地中，由称作“图孟贡”的首领带领，在游耕田地与游牧式采集之间迁徙，挖野芋、狩猎、捕鱼、采蜜、收集藤条和树脂，再拿到河畔的马来市场以物易物。他们的社会高度平等，与大河沿岸等级分明并日益伊斯兰化的诸苏丹国保持距离。邻近的马来人把定居务农的库布群体和深林中回避外界接触的群体区分开来，后者即“巴丁森比兰人”与狭义林巴人的分野，这一区分一直延续到近代。

en: The Odia people live along the Mahanadi delta and the coast of Odisha, the ancient Kalinga and Utkala, around Puri, Cuttack and Jajpur. Their Odia language descends from Odra Prakrit, itself a daughter of Magadhi Prakrit, and passed through Proto-Odia and Old Odia stages, the earliest Old Odia inscription dating to 1051; written in its own curved Brahmic script, it kept relatively free of Persian and Arabic borrowings. The Eastern Ganga dynasty ruled the country from Kataka, modern Cuttack, after 1135: Anantavarman Chodaganga began the great temple of Jagannatha at Puri, completed under Anangabhima Deva III, and Narasingha Deva I built the sun temple of Konark. In 1337 the Ganga kings still reigned, but in 1435 Kapilendra Deva founded the Gajapati Empire, which stretched from the Ganges to the Deccan, while Sarala Das composed the Odia Mahabharata and the Panchasakha poets produced the Odia Bhagabata. The last independent king, Mukunda Deva, fell in 1568 when the Bengal sultan Sulaiman Khan Karrani and his general Kalapahad overran the country and sacked its temples. The Mughals under Raja Man Singh completed the conquest by 1593, Odisha became a separate subah with its seat at Cuttack, the Marathas took it in 1751, and the East India Company acquired it in 1803. The rajas of Khurda meanwhile remained the guardians of the Jagannatha cult through these changes.
zh: 奥里亚人生活在默哈讷迪河三角洲与奥里萨海岸，即古代的羯陵伽和乌特卡拉，以普里、克塔克和贾杰布尔为中心。他们的奥里亚语源自奥德拉俗语，而奥德拉俗语又出自摩揭陀俗语，先后经历原始奥里亚语和古奥里亚语阶段，现存最早的古奥里亚语铭文可追溯到1051年；奥里亚文是一种字形圆曲的婆罗米系文字，语言本身受波斯语和阿拉伯语的影响较小。东恒伽王朝1135年后以格塔克（今克塔克）为都，阿南塔瓦尔曼·乔达恒伽动工兴建普里的贾格纳特大神庙，工程由阿南加比马·提婆三世完成，纳拉辛哈·提婆一世则修建了科纳拉克太阳神庙。1337年在位的仍是恒伽诸王；1435年卡皮伦德拉·提婆建立加贾帕蒂帝国，疆域北起恒河、南抵德干，同一时期萨拉勒·达斯写成奥里亚语《摩诃婆罗多》，五圣诗人留下了奥里亚语《薄伽梵往世书》。末代独立国王穆昆达·提婆于1568年败亡，孟加拉苏丹苏莱曼·汗·卡拉尼派名将卡拉帕哈德攻占全国、捣毁神庙。拉杰·曼·辛格率领的莫卧儿军队到1593年完成征服，奥里萨成为以克塔克为治所的单独苏巴；1751年马拉塔人接管该地，1803年英国东印度公司取得奥里萨。在这一连串变局中，库尔达的王公始终作为贾格纳特信仰的护持者存续下来。

en: The Ormur, also called Burki or Baraki, are an Eastern Iranian people whose main settlement is Baraki Barak in the Logar valley of Afghanistan, with a second homeland at Kaniguram in South Waziristan. Their own tongue, Ormuri, belongs to the Ormuri-Parachi group of Eastern Iranian languages and its name is said to derive from the Pashto word for fire, while most Ormur also speak Pashto and are counted among the Pashtun tribes. A tradition traced to the fifth-century-BC writer Herodotus derives the Baraki from the people of Barca in Libya, whom the Persian king Darius I transplanted to a village in Bactria later called Barke during his reign of 522 to 486 BC. Whatever their origins, the Baraki were settled around Logar by the time Babur seized Kabul in 1504, and his memoirs list Ormuri, then called Birki, among the eleven or twelve languages heard around the city; Bayazid Khan, the sixteenth-century leader of the Pir Roshan movement, likewise wove Ormuri words into his work Khairul-Bayan. Around 1800 eight to ten thousand Ormur families still lived in Logar, alongside smaller communities in Waziristan.
zh: 奥尔穆尔人又称布尔基或巴拉基，是东伊朗语民族，主要聚居于阿富汗洛加尔河谷的巴拉基巴拉克，另一处故乡在南瓦济里斯坦的卡尼古拉姆。他们的母语奥尔穆尔语属东伊朗语族的奥尔穆尔—帕拉奇语支，据说其名称源自普什图语的“火”字；多数奥尔穆尔人也讲普什图语，被算作普什图部落的一支。据可追溯到公元前5世纪史家希罗多德的传说，巴拉基人源自利比亚巴尔卡城的居民，波斯国王大流士一世在公元前522—前486年在位期间把他们迁徙到巴克特里亚一处后称巴尔克的村庄。无论起源如何，到1504年巴布尔夺取喀布尔时，巴拉基人已定居洛加尔一带；巴布尔在回忆录中把当时称比尔基语的奥尔穆尔语列为喀布尔周围通行的十一二种语言之一，16世纪皮尔·罗沙尼运动领袖巴亚兹德·汗也在著作《海鲁勒·巴扬》中嵌入了奥尔穆尔语词汇。1800年前后，洛加尔仍住有八千至一万户奥尔穆尔人，瓦济里斯坦另有较小的群落。

en: The Oroch are a Tungusic people of the Tatar Strait coast, whose name comes from the Tungus word oron, a domestic reindeer; their own tradition holds that they gave up reindeer herding to settle as fishermen on the Amur estuary and the seashore. They formed on the wooded slopes of the Sikhote-Alin, between De-Kastri Bay and the Botchi River, from a mix of Evenki, Nivkh and Ainu elements, and were divided into five territorial groups, including the Tumnin and Koppi groups whose rivers give their name to the main villages. Their Southern Tungusic speech was never written, and their old self-designation nani meant “people of this place”. Qing records knew their coast as the land of the Kuerka, seal hunters who fished among the offshore islands, and Russian travellers adopted the name Oroch for them only in the 1800s.
zh: 奥罗奇是鞑靼海峡沿岸的通古斯语族群，族名来自通古斯语里意为家养驯鹿的“奥龙”；按他们自己的说法，祖先失去驯鹿后在黑龙江口和海滨定居下来，转为以捕鱼为生的定居者。他们形成于锡霍特山脉的林坡之间，北起德卡斯特里湾、南至博奇河，融合了鄂温克、尼夫赫、阿伊努等不同成分，分成五个地域群体，图姆宁和科皮两支所在的河流正是其主要村落的得名由来。他们的南通古斯语从来没有文字，古老自称“那尼”意为“本地人”。清代文献把这片海岸上的人称作库尔喀，即在外海诸岛捕鱼、捕猎海豹的“水野人”；俄国旅行者直到19世纪才采用奥罗奇这个名称来称呼他们。

en: The Orokaiva are a Papuan people of Oro Province in the Bird's Tail of New Guinea, their country lying around Popondetta between the Owen Stanley Range and the Hydrographers Range. Their speech belongs to the Binanderean branch of Trans–New Guinea, with Aeka and Hunjara as its northern and mountain varieties. Orokaiva tradition divides the people into three groups, the Umo-ke or river people, the Eva-Embo or salt-water people and the Pereho of the inland, and the Orokaiva were known as fierce fighters in the local wars over land in the Bird's Tail.
zh: 奥罗凯瓦人是新几内亚“鸟尾”奥罗省的巴布亚族群，家园在波蓬德塔周围，夹在欧文·斯坦利岭与海德拉夫岭之间。他们的语言属跨新几内亚语系的比南德雷语族，埃卡语和洪贾拉语分别是它的北方变体和山地变体。奥罗凯瓦人的传统把全族分为三支：“河人”乌莫凯、“咸水人”埃瓦恩博，以及内陆的佩雷霍；在“鸟尾”争夺土地的地方战事中，奥罗凯瓦人以骁勇善战著称。

en: The Oromo are a Cushitic people of the Ethiopian highlands, speaking Afaan Oromoo of the Cushitic branch of Afroasiatic and divided into the two great moieties of the Borana and Barentu. Originally pastoralists around the lakes of southern Ethiopia and northern Kenya, they ordered their society through the gadaa system, under which leaders were elected for eight-year terms, and venerated the single sky god of the Waaqeffanna religion. From about 1530, the collapse of both Christian Ethiopia and the Adal Sultanate in the wars of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi opened the way for the great Oromo expansions, recorded by the Ethiopian monk Bahrey in 1593: raiding parties gave way to settled clans in Bale, Shewa and beyond, and outsiders were absorbed into lineages through the Mogasa and Gudifacha adoption rituals. In the Gibe region the migrants founded kingdoms such as Limmu-Ennarea, Gera, Gomma, Gumma and Jimma, while an eastward push toward the Somali coast in the mid-seventeenth century was turned back by the Ajuran Empire. Ethiopian emperors alternately fought and courted them: around 1700 Iyasu I settled loyal Oromo bands in Gojjam and Begemder, and Iyasu II took a Yejju Oromo wife, whose son Iyoas I inherited the throne. By the later eighteenth century Oromo was the everyday language of the Gondar court, until Mikael Sehul's coup of 1769 broke Yejju power and opened the Zemene Mesafint, the long era of rival princes.
zh: 奥罗莫人是埃塞俄比亚高地的库希特民族，操亚非语系库希特语族的奥罗莫语（阿方奥罗莫语），分为博拉纳、巴伦图两大支系。他们本是游牧于埃塞俄比亚南部湖泊地带和肯尼亚北部的牧民，传统上以加达制度治理社会：领导人由选举产生，任期八年；本土信仰瓦克芬纳教，敬奉唯一的天神。1530年前后，基督教埃塞俄比亚与阿达尔苏丹国在伊玛目艾哈迈德·本·易卜拉欣·加齐的战争中两败俱伤，为奥罗莫人的大扩张打开了通道；埃塞俄比亚修士阿巴·巴里在1593年记下了这段历史。袭击队逐步转为定居氏族，深入巴莱、绍阿等地，外来者则通过莫加萨、古迪法查等收养仪式并入氏族。在吉贝地区，迁徙者建立了里姆伊那瑞亚、吉拉、戈玛、古玛、吉马等王国；17世纪中叶他们向东进逼索马里海岸，却被阿朱兰帝国击退。埃塞俄比亚皇帝对他们或战或抚：1700年前后，伊亚苏一世把效忠的奥罗莫部众安置在戈贾姆和贝格姆德尔；伊亚苏二世娶耶朱部奥罗莫女子为妻，其子伊约阿斯一世继位。到18世纪后期，奥罗莫语已是贡德尔宫廷的日常语言，直到1769年米卡埃尔·塞胡尔发动政变、摧毁耶朱部势力，开启了群雄割据的王子时代。

en: The Oroqen are a Tungusic people of the northern Manchurian forests, whose self-name means “people who keep reindeer”. Their ancestors, traced to the medieval Shiwei groups of the Amur basin, originally ranged south of the Outer Khingan Mountains and north of the Amur River, hunting deer and elk across the taiga in exogamous clan bands. Their Northern Tungusic language is close to Evenki and had no traditional script, and they lived in conical tents covered with birch bark in summer and deer hide in winter, called sierranju. In the 1600s the Russian advance into the Amur country drove part of the Oroqen south into the valleys of the Greater and Lesser Khingan, where they entered the sphere of the Manchu Qing; Qing documents knew them as the Orunchun, a fur-hunting people of the northern forests organized into the Kumar and Bilar tribal divisions.
zh: 鄂伦春是满洲北部森林里的通古斯语族群，自称意为“养驯鹿的人”。他们的先民可追溯到黑龙江流域中世纪的室韦诸部，原本在外兴安岭以南、黑龙江以北的广阔泰加林中游猎，以实行外婚制的氏族为单位猎捕鹿类。他们的鄂伦春语属北通古斯语支，与鄂温克语十分相近，传统上没有文字；住的是圆锥形帐篷斜仁柱，夏天覆以桦树皮、冬天覆以兽皮。17世纪俄国势力进入黑龙江流域，一部分鄂伦春人南迁到大、小兴安岭的河谷，由此进入满洲清朝的势力范围，清代文献称他们为俄伦春，分为库马尔、毕拉尔两部，是北方森林中以狩猎为生的部族。

en: The Osaakiiwaki, better known as the Sauk or Sac, are an Algonquian-speaking people whose own name oθaakiiwaki refers to the yellow earth of their homeland, while the Ojibwe called them Ozaagiiwag, the people at the outlet, from which Europeans derived Sauk. Driven from the St. Lawrence valley around 1600, they settled at Saginaw Bay in eastern Michigan, a region whose name means where the Sauk were; wars with the Ojibwe and Odawa around 1638 to 1640 broke their power there and pushed them west toward Green Bay. In the early eighteenth century they stood by their close allies the Meskwaki, or Fox, during the Fox Wars against New France, and after the French slaughter of Fox refugees in Illinois in 1730 the two peoples merged their fortunes and drifted west into Iowa. The leaders Black Hawk and Keokuk rose among them in this period: Keokuk sought accommodation with the United States, while Black Hawk led a band back into Illinois in 1832 and was defeated in the Black Hawk War. Repeated land cessions followed, and between 1832 and 1837 debt and pressure forced the Sauk into three relocations west of the Mississippi.
zh: 奥萨基瓦基人即通常所称的索克人（Sauk，又译萨克人），是阿尔冈昆语民族；其自称oθaakiiwaki与故土的黄土有关，奥吉布瓦人则称他们为Ozaagiiwag，意为“河口之人”，欧洲人据此转写为Sauk。约1600年他们被逐出圣劳伦斯河谷，迁至密歇根东部的萨吉诺湾，萨吉诺一名即意为“索克人故地”；1638至1640年间与奥吉布瓦人、奥达瓦人的战争摧毁了他们在当地的势力，被迫西迁至格林贝一带。18世纪初的福克斯战争中，他们支持密友梅斯夸基人（福克斯人）对抗新法兰西；1730年法国人在伊利诺伊屠戮福克斯难民后，两个民族合流并继续西迁进入艾奥瓦。这一时期他们中出现了黑鹰与基奥卡克两位首领：基奥卡克谋求与美国妥协，黑鹰则在1832年率部重返伊利诺伊，结果在黑鹰战争中战败。此后土地接连割让，1832至1837年间，债务与压力迫使索克人三次迁往密西西比河以西。

en: The Niukonska, better known to Europeans as the Osage, are a Dhegiha Siouan people who call themselves Wazhazhe, the Middle Waters people. Their traditions recall a homeland in the Ohio and Mississippi valleys from which they moved west in the seventeenth century, driven by the Beaver Wars of the Haudenosaunee, and by the 1690s they had settled along the Osage River in present-day western Missouri and taken to horses. Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met them on the Mississippi in 1673, and the Osage became firm French allies: Bourgmont built Fort Orleans in their territory in the 1720s and led an Osage delegation to Paris in 1725, while the Chouteau family of St. Louis ran the fur trade from Fort Carondelet.
