Divided into Great Osage, Little Osage and Arkansas bands, they numbered about five thousand in 1804 and dominated the country between the Missouri and Red rivers, farming and hunting bison. War with the Cherokee brought defeat at Claremore Mound, and in 1833 they destroyed a Kiowa camp at Cutthroat Gap. Through the treaties of 1818 and 1825 they ceded most of their vast lands to the United States and accepted a reservation in southern Kansas.
zh: 纽康斯卡人即欧洲人惯称的奥塞奇人，属德吉哈苏语族群，自称瓦扎热，意为“中水之人”。据他们的传统，其故地在俄亥俄河与密西西比河流域，17世纪因豪德诺索尼人的海狸战争而西迁，到17世纪90年代已定居在今密苏里西部的奥塞奇河沿岸并开始养马。1673年，马凯特和若利埃在密西西比河上与他们相遇，奥塞奇人从此成为法国的坚定盟友：18世纪20年代布尔蒙在他们的土地上修建奥尔良堡，并于1725年率领一支奥塞奇使团前往巴黎；圣路易斯的舒托家族则在卡龙德莱堡经营毛皮贸易。他们分为大奥塞奇、小奥塞奇和阿肯色三个群体，1804年约有五千人，控制着密苏里河与雷德河之间的广大地区，兼营农业与野牛猎捕。与切罗基人的战争使他们在克莱尔芒德之战中失败，1833年他们又在割喉谷摧毁了一处基奥瓦营地。通过1818年和1825年的两项条约，他们把大片故土割让给美国，接受了堪萨斯南部的保留地。

en: The Osheaga were the westernmost of the St. Lawrence Iroquoians, farming and fishing people who spoke the Laurentian language and lived in palisaded villages along the upper St. Lawrence. Their principal settlement, Hochelaga — Osheaga is a recorded variant of the name, possibly meaning big rapids after the Lachine Rapids — stood on the Island of Montreal near Mount Royal and may have held around a thousand inhabitants, who grew maize, beans and squash in the fields around it. Jacques Cartier visited in October 1535 and was welcomed there, naming the hill behind the village Mount Royal. The Osheaga were distinct from both the Wendat and the Haudenosaunee, though in contact with both. Within a single generation the villages of the St. Lawrence valley were gone: when Champlain returned in 1603 he found only abandoned sites, archaeology and later accounts pointing to Mohawk raids, European epidemics and the scattering of survivors among neighbouring nations.
zh: 奥谢阿加人是圣劳伦斯易洛魁人中位置最西的一支，属于使用劳伦琴语的农耕渔猎民族，住在圣劳伦斯河上游设有栅栏的村落里。他们的主要聚落奥什拉加——奥谢阿加是这个名字的异写，可能因附近的拉欣急流而意为“大急流”——坐落在蒙特利尔岛的皇家山附近，居民或达千人，在村外田地里种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜。1535年10月，雅克·卡蒂埃到访并受到款待，还把村后的山丘命名为皇家山。奥谢阿加人与温达特人、易洛魁联盟各族都不相同，但与双方都有往来。仅仅一代人之后，圣劳伦斯河谷的这些村落便告消失：1603年萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰重返故地时只剩废弃的遗址；考古发现和后世记载表明，原因包括莫霍克人的袭击、欧洲人带来的疫病，以及幸存者四散并入邻近各族。

en: The Otali, better known as the Overhill Cherokee, were the Cherokee communities on the western side of the Appalachian Mountains, in what is now Tennessee, along the lower Little Tennessee, Tellico and Hiwassee rivers. Their towns were settled between the late sixteenth and late seventeenth centuries, and their speech became the distinct Otali, or Overhill, dialect. Virginia traders James Needham and Gabriel Arthur reached them in 1673, opening a direct fur trade across the mountains. The leading town, or mother town, shifted between Great Tellico, Tanasi and Chota; Tanasi gave its name to the state of Tennessee, while Chota served as the de facto capital of the Cherokee Nation for most of the eighteenth century. In 1730 Sir Alexander Cuming secured the allegiance of Tanasi and had Moytoy of Tellico crowned emperor of the Cherokee. The British built Fort Loudoun among the towns in 1756, only to lose it to a Cherokee siege in 1760. Henry Timberlake's peace mission of 1761 left a detailed record of Overhill life, and the towns produced leaders such as Attakullakulla, Oconostota, Nancy Ward and Sequoyah, creator of the Cherokee syllabary. After the Cherokee-American wars, the treaty signed at the Tellico Blockhouse in 1794 opened a decade of land cessions that ended the Overhill towns' independence, as the Cherokee center of power shifted south to New Echota in Georgia.
zh: 奥塔利人即更广为人知的山外切罗基人，是阿巴拉契亚山脉西侧、今田纳西州境内小田纳西河、泰利科河与海沃西河下游一带的切罗基社群。他们的城镇建于16世纪末至17世纪末之间，所说的话发展为独特的奥塔利（山外）方言。1673年，弗吉尼亚商人詹姆斯·尼达姆和加布里埃尔·亚瑟抵达此地，打通了翻山而来的直接毛皮贸易。各城的首镇（母城）在大泰利科、塔纳西和乔塔之间转移：塔纳西后来成为田纳西州名称的来源，乔塔则在18世纪大部分时间里是切罗基联盟事实上的首府。1730年，亚历山大·卡明爵士取得塔纳西的效忠，并为泰利科的莫伊托伊加冕为切罗基人的皇帝。1756年英国人在诸城之间修建劳登堡，却在1760年的围城中失守。1761年亨利·廷伯莱克的和平使团留下了关于山外生活的详细记录；阿塔库拉库拉、奥科诺斯托塔、南希·沃德，以及创制切罗基音节文字的塞阔雅等名人都出自这些城镇。切罗基—美国战争之后，1794年在泰利科堡签订的条约开启了持续十年的土地割让，山外诸城的独立地位告终，切罗基人的权力中心南移到佐治亚的新埃科塔。

en: The Otomangueans, better known to history as the Otomi, are the principal Oto-Pamean people of the central Mexican plateau, scattered across the highlands of Hidalgo, the state of Mexico and Querétaro in towns such as Xilotepec and Metztitlan, and calling themselves by several names, including Hñähñu in the Mezquital valley. Their Oto-Manguean ancestors were among the earliest farmers of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt and may have been the first inhabitants of the Valley of Mexico, where Otomi speakers lived in Teotihuacan and later in Toltec Tula. After Teotihuacan's fall Nahua migrants pressed them eastward, and around 1100 they built the city-state of Xaltocan, only to be subdued by the Mexica and their allies in the fourteenth century; the Tepanec drove them from the valley in 1418, and they became tributaries of the Aztec Triple Alliance. During the Spanish conquest the Otomi of Tlaxcala joined Cortés against Tenochtitlan and went on to found Querétaro and colonize the Bajío, while those of the Mezquital valley kept up guerrilla resistance for years. By the 1530s their towns had been parceled into encomiendas, though Indian republics and communal lands let them keep their language; epidemics and forced resettlement, such as the 1711 transfer of families to San Luis Potosí, thinned their communities through the colonial centuries.
zh: 欧托曼格人即史书上的奥托米人，是墨西哥中部高原最主要的奥托-帕梅族群，散布在伊达尔戈州、墨西哥州和克雷塔罗州的高地，希洛特佩克、梅茨蒂特兰等城镇皆为其聚居地；不同支系自称各异，梅斯基塔尔山谷一支自称赫尼亚纽。他们的奥托-曼格语先民是跨墨西哥火山带最早的农耕者之一，可能也是墨西哥谷地最早的居民，曾生活在特奥蒂瓦坎，后来又居于托尔特克人的图拉。特奥蒂瓦坎衰落后，纳瓦语移民不断把他们向东排挤；约1100年，他们建立城邦萨尔托坎，却在14世纪被墨西加及其盟友征服，1418年又被特帕内克人逐出墨西哥谷地，沦为阿兹特克三方同盟的纳贡者。西班牙征服期间，特拉斯卡拉的奥托米人投奔科尔特斯，参与攻灭特诺奇蒂特兰，随后建立克雷塔罗城并参与殖民巴希奥地区，梅斯基塔尔山谷的支系则坚持了多年游击抵抗。到16世纪30年代，他们的城镇被瓜分为监护征赋领地，不过印第安人共和国和公社土地使其语言得以保留；整个殖民时期疫病不断，1711年还有整族家庭被迁往圣路易斯波托西，族群人口大为削减。

en: The Otuho, also called the Lotuko, are a Nilotic people of the mountainous Eastern Equatoria region of South Sudan, around the Imatong range, speaking the Lotuko language among neighbours such as the Bari and Acholi. They venerate the creator god Ajok and their ancestors, and are served by rain-makers who keep sacred rain stones for the harvest.
zh: 奥图霍人又称洛图科人，是南苏丹东赤道州山区的尼罗特民族，聚居于伊马通山脉一带，操洛图科语，与巴里人、阿乔利人等为邻。他们信奉造物主阿乔克和祖先神灵，由保存圣雨石、为收成祈雨的祈雨祭司侍奉神灵。

en: The Ōuhǎi culture occupies the estuary of the Ou River and the rugged coast of southern Zhejiang around Wenzhou, taking in Yongjia, Rui'an, Yueqing and Pingyang beneath the Zhejiang-Fujian hills. The native Ou people, a branch of the Yue, had formed the Dong'ou polity by the fourth century BC; their kingdom submitted to the Han in 138 BC, and the Jin set up Yongjia Commandery on the river in 323, its walled city laid out by the scholar Guo Pu. The Tang renamed the prefecture Wenzhou in 675, and under the Southern Song and Yuan its harbor was opened to maritime trade while the Yongjia School made the city a center of pragmatic, commerce-friendly Confucian thought. In 1348 it fell into the sphere of Fang Guozhen's coastal fleet until his surrender to the Ming in 1367. The local Oujiang speech is the most divergent branch of Wu, so hard for outsiders that some dialectologists treat it as a language of its own called Ou; a thirteenth-century local scholar, Dai Tong, wrote his study of characters in the Yongjia variety, the Liushugu, which was printed in 1320.
zh: 瓯海文化位于瓯江河口与浙南崎岖海岸，以温州为中心，括有永嘉、瑞安、乐清、平阳等地，背倚浙闽丘陵。土著瓯人是越人的一支，至迟在公元前4世纪已建立东瓯政权，东瓯于公元前138年归附汉朝；323年东晋在瓯江两岸设永嘉郡，郡城由学者郭璞主持规划。675年唐代改置温州，南宋与元代这里的港口获准开展海外贸易，永嘉学派又使温州成为讲求事功、崇尚商贾的儒学中心。1348年以后，温州落入方国珍海上势力的范围，直到1367年方国珍降明。当地的瓯江片吴语是吴语各支中分歧最大的一种，外人极难听懂，以至有学者主张把它单列为瓯语；13世纪本地学者戴侗还用永嘉方言撰写字书《六书故》，于1320年刊行。

en: The Ovimbundu, also called the Southern Mbundu, are a Bantu people of the Bié Plateau in central Angola and the coastal strip around Benguela to the west. Over the last millennium Bantu groups moving in from the north coalesced into small kingdoms including M'Balundu, Sele, Wambo and Bieno, combining plateau agriculture with cattle acquired from peoples to the south. After the Portuguese set up a colonial bridgehead at Benguela in the 1500s, the Ovimbundu kingdoms became the organizers of long-distance caravan trade, carrying wax, rubber, honey and ivory from the Chokwe, Luvale and Mbunda of the interior to the coast, while the slave trade formed part of the same network. These agreements fostered regional crafts such as metalwork and cornmeal production, and caravans led by professional trader-diviners remained the backbone of Ovimbundu life until the suppression of the slave trade in the 1800s began their decline.
zh: 奥文本杜人又称南姆本杜人，是安居安哥拉中部比耶高原及其西侧本格拉沿海地带的班图族群。过去一千年间，自北方迁入的班图群体逐渐形成姆巴伦杜、塞莱、万博、比耶诺等小王国，在高原农业之外还从南方族群购入牛只。16世纪末葡萄牙人在本格拉建立殖民据点后，奥文本杜诸王国成为长途商队贸易的组织者，把内地绍奎人、卢瓦勒人和姆本达人出产的蜡、橡胶、蜂蜜和象牙运到海岸，奴隶贸易也是这一网络的一部分。金属加工和玉米粉加工等地区性专业分工由此发展起来；每支商队都由兼任占卜师的专业领队率领，商队贸易长期是奥文本杜社会的支柱，直到19世纪奴隶贸易受到压制才走向衰落。

en: The Ovambo, also called Aawambo or Ambo, are a cluster of kindred Bantu peoples of the flat, seasonally flooded plains of northern Namibia and the Cunene region of southern Angola, a country known as Ovamboland. They comprise several tribes, among them the Ndonga, Kwambi, Ngandjera, Mbalantu and the Kwanyama, the largest of them. From the 1300s their ancestors moved southwest from the Zambia region, settling first along the Angola-Namibia border and spreading further south into Namibia in the 1600s. They kept cattle, cultivated millet and sorghum along the seasonal watercourses called oshanas, and remained almost untouched by Swahili-Arab and European traders until the 1800s. Closely related to the Herero and the Kavango, the Ovambo tribes kept their own royal lines and measured wealth chiefly in cattle long before colonial rule reached their plains.
zh: 奥万博人又称阿万博人或安博人，是若干彼此亲缘的班图部落的统称，居住在纳米比亚北部和安哥拉南部库内内地区平坦而季节性泛滥的平原上，这片土地称为奥万博兰。他们包括恩敦加、宽比、甘杰拉、姆巴兰图等部落，其中以宽亚马部最为庞大。从14世纪起，他们的祖先自赞比亚地区向西南迁徙，先在安哥拉与纳米比亚边界一带定居，又于17世纪继续向南扩展到纳米比亚。他们牧养牛只，在名为奥沙纳的季节性水道旁种植粟和高粱，在19世纪以前几乎未受斯瓦希里-阿拉伯商人和欧洲商人影响。奥万博人与赫雷罗人和卡万戈人关系密切，诸部各有王世，在殖民统治到达这片平原之前很久，就以牛只作为衡量财富的主要标准。

en: The Pacahuara are a Panoan people of the northern Bolivian Amazon, whose forest homeland runs from the Beni lowlands toward the Brazilian border between the Negro and Pacahuaras rivers. They were traditionally divided into two bands, the Sinabu and the Capuibo, and lived by shifting farming, hunting, fishing and gathering Brazil nuts and palm hearts in small, highly mobile family groups. Their unwritten Pacahuara speech belongs to the Panoan family and is close to the language of their neighbours and relatives, the Chácobo. In 1767 the Jesuit scholar Lorenzo Hervás recorded a Pacabara language spoken in the San Borja mission on the Beni, showing that Pacahuara bands had already entered the eighteenth-century Jesuit mission world of the Mamoré.
zh: 帕卡瓦拉人是玻利维亚北部亚马孙的帕诺语族群，丛林故乡从贝尼低地延伸到巴西边境一带，位于内格罗河与帕卡瓦拉斯河之间。他们传统上分为西纳布和卡普伊博两个支系，以轮垦、狩猎、捕鱼和采集巴西栗、棕榈心为生，结成流动性很强的小型家族群。他们没有文字的帕卡瓦拉语属于帕诺语系，与邻族查科博人的语言十分接近。1767年，耶稣会学者洛伦索·埃尔瓦斯记录下一种在贝尼的圣博尔哈传教站使用的帕卡巴拉语，说明帕卡瓦拉诸支系当时已经进入18世纪马莫雷河流域的耶稣会传教网络。

en: The Paici are the Kanak people of a broad band across central Grande Terre in New Caledonia, their Paicî language being spoken around Poindimié, Ponérihouen, Koné and Poya in the North Province. Paicî belongs to the New Caledonian branch of the Oceanic languages, which descend from the tongues of Lapita seafarers who settled the archipelago with their pottery and New Guinea obsidian from about 1100 BC. Like other Kanak societies, the Paici lived in clan villages under hereditary chiefs, without kings or unified states: they cleared yam and taro fields above the coast, fished the lagoon from outrigger canoes and met for ancestor ceremonies around the chief's great house. The language took its present shape over centuries of feuding and marriage exchange between these valleys. Europeans were only a rumour until James Cook sighted Grande Terre in 1774 and the Comte de Lapérouse sailed along its west coast in 1788, so the Paici world of 1337 was still one of clans, exchange paths and rival valleys untouched by any outside power.
zh: 派西人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛中部一条广阔地带的卡纳克人，其派西语通行于北方省的普安迪米耶、波内里旺、科内和波亚一带。派西语属于大洋洲语族的新喀里多尼亚语支，该语支源自拉皮塔航海者的语言；约公元前1100年起，这些航海者带着陶器和新几内亚黑曜石定居群岛。与其他卡纳克社会一样，派西人世袭酋长统领氏族村落，没有国王，也没有统一国家：他们在海岸上方开垦山药和芋田，驾舷外架独木舟在潟湖捕鱼，并聚集在酋长的大屋周围举行祭祖仪式。经过山谷之间数百年的仇杀与通婚交换，派西语逐渐成形。在詹姆斯·库克于1774年望见格朗德特尔岛、拉彼鲁兹伯爵于1788年沿其西海岸航行之前，欧洲人对他们还只是传闻；因此1337年的派西世界，仍是一个由氏族、交换路线和相互竞争的山谷组成、未受任何外来势力触动的世界。

en: The Paipai, also called Akwa'ala, are hunter-gatherer Indians of northern Baja California. Their territory ran from San Vicente on the Pacific coast almost to the Colorado River delta, between the Kiliwa to the south and the Kumeyaay and Cocopa to the north. They lived in patrilineal bands, built rectangular thatched houses, hunted with bows and cane arrows, and made pottery, basketry and rabbitskin robes. Their language belongs to the Yuman family and is close to the speech of the Yavapai and Walapai of western Arizona. Sebastian Vizcaino's coastal expedition first encountered them in 1602, and the Portola expedition of 1769 opened a period of sustained Spanish contact. The Dominicans founded the San Vicente mission in Paipai land in 1780 and added an inland station at Santa Catarina in 1797, drawing the formerly nomadic bands into settled mission life.
zh: 派派人又称阿克瓦阿拉人，是下加利福尼亚北部的狩猎采集印第安人。他们的领地从太平洋沿岸的圣维森特一直延伸到科罗拉多河三角洲附近，南接基利瓦人，北邻库梅亚伊人和科科帕人。他们按父系组成游群，建造长方形茅草屋，以弓和藤箭狩猎，并制作陶器、编织物和兔皮袍。派派语属尤曼语族，与西亚利桑那亚瓦派人、瓦拉派人的语言相近。1602年，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯卡伊诺的海岸探险队最先接触到他们；1769年波托拉远征开启了与西班牙人持续往来的时期。多明我会于1780年在派派人的土地上建立圣维森特传教站，1797年又在内地增设圣卡塔琳娜传教站，把昔日游荡的游群纳入定居的传教生活。

en: The Paiter, commonly called Suruí, are a Tupian people of the borderlands between Rondônia and Mato Grosso in Brazil, holding the Sete de Setembro land on the Rio Branco. Their self-name means the true people; they speak a Mondé-branch Tupian tongue and live by hunting, fishing, forest gathering and shifting farming.
zh: 苏鲁伊派特人通常称苏鲁伊人，是巴西朗多尼亚州与马托格罗索州交界地带的图皮语族群，居于布兰科河畔的九月七日原住民地。其自称“派特”意为真正的人，操图皮语系蒙代语支语言，以狩猎、捕鱼、林间采集和游耕为生。

en: The Palaung, who call themselves Ta'ang and are known in China as the De'ang, are an ancient Austroasiatic people of the Shan hills, straddling northern Shan State around Hsenwi, Hsipaw and Namhsan and the Dehong and Zhenkang country across the Yunnan border. Chinese sources trace them to the Pu people of the second century BC, already settled on both banks of the Salween and counted among the earliest developers of the Baoshan and Dehong uplands; their ancestors, the Golden Teeth people, held their own polity from the twelfth to the fifteenth century before its decline left them subjects of the Shan saopha chiefs under the Yuan dynasty of 1271 to 1368 and later rule. Divided into Pale, Rumai and Shwe groups speaking Palaungic Mon-Khmer languages, many also speak Shan and Burmese. They are hill farmers whose villages stand among tea gardens, every household growing tea, and most profess Theravada Buddhism, sending boys to monastery schools, while still honouring the nature spirits called nats; their women wear coloured rattan waist hoops, a dress custom traced to the Mang tribe of the Tang era.
zh: 德昂人在缅甸自称塔昂（Ta'ang），是掸邦高原古老的南亚语系民族，分布在缅甸北部掸邦的兴威、昔卜和南山一带，以及云南边境的德宏、镇康等地。中国史籍把他们追溯为公元前2世纪的濮人后裔，当时已定居怒江两岸，是开发保山、德宏山区较早的民族；其先民金齿人在12至15世纪曾建立自己的金齿国，国势衰落后，在元代（1271—1368年）及以后沦为掸族土司的属民。德昂人分为三个主要支系，操孟高棉语族佤德昂语支的语言，不少人兼通掸语和缅语。他们是山地农民，村落坐落在茶园之间，家家种茶；多数人信奉上座部佛教，送男孩入寺学习佛经，数年后还俗，同时仍祭祀称为纳的自然神灵；妇女佩戴染色藤篾腰箍，这一服饰习俗可追溯到唐代茫人部落藤篾缠腰的传统。

en:
The Palawan are the Palawa, the Aboriginal clans of the island Europeans called Van Diemen's Land and later Tasmania. Rising seas flooded the Bass Strait around 6000 BCE, cutting the island off from the mainland for some eight thousand years, so its peoples developed in isolation, organised into family clans bound to defined territories and seasonal rounds, speaking languages that colonial observers sorted into a western Nara group and an eastern Mara group. Nations such as the Tyerrernotepanner of the northern midlands, the Peerapper of the western coast and the Tommeginne of the north were among the several distinct communities covered by the collective name Palawa, their economy built on kangaroo hunting, shellfish gathering, ochre and stone tool trades, and finely built bark shelters.

Abel Tasman first sighted the island in 1642, but sustained contact began only when sealers arrived in 1798 and a British penal outpost was planted at Risdon Cove in 1803, where soldiers fired on a hunting party the following year. As sheep runs swallowed the hunting grounds, guerrilla resistance flared from 1824 into the Black War; martial law was declared in 1828 and the Black Line sweep of 1830 failed to corner the clans. George Augustus Robinson's friendly missions, aided by the negotiator Truganini, then secured their surrender, and between 1832 and 1835 the roughly 220 survivors were removed to the Wybalenna establishment on Flinders Island.
zh:
巴拉望人即帕拉瓦人，是欧洲人所称范迪门地（后称塔斯马尼亚）岛上各原住民族群的统称。约公元前6000年，上涨的海水淹没巴斯海峡，使该岛与大陆隔绝约八千年，岛上居民因而独立发展，以家族氏族为单位依附于各自的领地和季节性迁徙路线，语言被殖民者归纳为西方的纳拉语群和东方的马拉语群。北部中部的切拉诺蒂帕纳人、西海岸的佩拉佩人、北方的托梅金人等，便是帕拉瓦这个统称之下若干不同社群中的几个；他们以猎袋鼠、采贝、贸易赭石和石器、搭建精巧树皮棚屋为生。

1642年亚伯·塔斯曼首次望见此岛，但持续接触要到1798年海豹捕猎者到来之后；1803年英国在里斯登湾建立流放站，次年驻军便向一支狩猎队伍开火。随着牧羊场吞没猎场，游击战式的抵抗自1824年起升级为黑色战争：1828年当局宣布戒严，1830年的“黑线”扫荡仍未能围捕各氏族。随后乔治·奥古斯都·罗宾逊在调停人特鲁加尼尼协助下开展“友好使命”，促使他们投降；1832年至1835年间，约220名幸存者被迁往巴斯海峡弗林德斯岛上的怀巴伦纳居留地。

en: The Palawan, also called Palaw'an, are the principal indigenous people of Palawan, the long island between Mindoro and Borneo, which takes its name from them; alongside the Tagbanwa and Batak they rank among the island's oldest inhabitants and traditionally followed animist anito beliefs. They form four Palawanic-speaking subgroups divided between coastal Panimusan and highland Kunoy communities, the latter including the Tau't Bato, who take shelter in caves during the rainy season. Originally shifting cultivators of the southern interior, they built hillside houses raised on posts, hunted with poison-tipped spears and stunned fish in streams with tuba root sap. When Muslim traders and settlers from Mindanao reached the coast, many lowland Palawan adopted Islam while the highlanders kept their old rites. Chinese sources of the 1200s record the islands as the polity Sandao, a vassal of Ma-i on Mindoro, and they later passed under Brunei and Sulu overlordship. Spanish friars opened missions at Taytay in the early seventeenth century, and in 1749 the Sultan of Brunei ceded southern Palawan to Spain.
zh: 巴拉望人又称帕拉万人，是巴拉望岛的主体原住民，这座横亘在民都洛与婆罗洲之间的长岛便因他们得名；他们与塔班瓦人、巴塔克人同属岛上最古老的居民，传统上信奉万物有灵的阿尼托信仰。巴拉望人分为四个讲巴拉望语的支系，又有沿海的帕尼穆山人与山地的库诺伊人之别，后者包括雨季栖身岩洞的塔乌特·巴托人。他们原是南部内陆的游耕部族，在山坡上搭建高脚屋，用毒矛狩猎，以图巴藤的汁液毒晕溪流中的鱼。棉兰老的穆斯林商人和移民来到海岸后，许多低地巴拉望人改宗伊斯兰教，高地人则保留了旧有仪式。据13世纪中国史籍记载，巴拉望诸岛是民都洛麻逸国的属邦，后来又先后受文莱和苏禄统辖。17世纪初，西班牙修道士在泰泰建立传教点；1749年，文莱苏丹把巴拉望南部割让给西班牙。

en: The Palus, or Palouse, are a Sahaptin-speaking people of the Columbia Plateau whose villages followed the Snake River from its meeting with the Clearwater in the east down to its mouth on the Columbia, together with the Palouse River valley as far north as Rock Lake. They call themselves the Naxiyamtama, the river people, and take their common name from Pa-luš-sa, their principal village at the junction of the Palouse and Snake rivers near Palouse Falls. Upper, Middle and Lower bands made up the nation, many living in bilingual villages alongside their Nez Perce kin, while other neighbours included the Spokane, Cayuse, Walla Walla and Yakama. Seasonally nomadic, they gathered for salmon fishing, root digging, hunting, trade and dancing, and were expert horsemen who bred distinctive spotted horses, the Palouse horses from which the Appaloosa takes its name. In October 1805 the Lewis and Clark expedition met the tribe, most of whom were away on their autumn round, and gave a silver peace medal to their paramount chief Kepowhan.
zh: 帕卢斯人是哥伦比亚高原上讲萨哈普廷语的民族，村落沿蛇河分布，东起蛇河与克利尔沃特河交汇处，西至蛇河注入哥伦比亚河的河口，还包括向北延伸到罗克湖的帕卢斯河谷。他们自称纳克西亚姆塔马人，意为“河中之民”；通称则来自帕卢斯瀑布附近、帕卢斯河与蛇河交汇处的主要村落帕卢萨，族名即由此而来。全族分为上、中、下三个群体，许多人与近亲内兹珀斯人杂居于双语村落，邻族还有斯波坎人、卡尤塞人、沃拉沃拉人和雅卡马人。他们随季节迁徙，聚在一起捕捞鲑鱼、挖掘块根、狩猎、贸易和跳舞，又是出色的骑手，培育出带独特斑纹的帕卢斯马，阿帕卢萨马的名字便由此而来。1805年10月，刘易斯与克拉克探险队遇到这个部族，当时多数人正外出进行秋季采集，探险队向他们的大酋长凯波汉赠送了一枚银质和平勋章。

en: The Palta were a pre-Inca people of southern Ecuador, occupying the broad mountain valleys of present-day Loja province and the upper Zamora region. Their traditions derive them from Amazonian Jíbaro groups, kin to the Bracamoros and the Shuar, who crossed the eastern Andes and followed the Catamayo-Chira and Puyango-Tumbes river basins into the highlands, and their language belonged to the Jivaroan or Chicham family before being heavily influenced by Quechua. They formed a confederation of chiefdoms, among them the Calvas, Malacatos, Garrochamba, Ambocas and Chaparras, which recognized a common centre in the fertile Cuxibamba valley, with a population estimated at eighty to a hundred thousand on the eve of the Inca invasion. Maize and cassava farmers without writing, ploughs or draft animals, they irrigated mountain terraces through reservoirs called cochas, fertilized their fields with guano, worked pottery and metal, and bartered with gold and silver weighed by their own measures. Their warriors, armed with slings, copper axes and lances, resisted the Inca armies of Túpac Yupanqui from hilltop forts around Saraguro, but the confederation was broken and within four or five generations the Palta had lost their separate language and organization under Inca and then Spanish rule; as early as 1571 Spanish inspectors described their surviving customs, and in 1592 the Garrochamba were being drafted into the mines of Zaruma.
zh: 帕勒塔人是厄瓜多尔南部的前印卡民族，占据今洛哈省及萨莫拉上游广阔的山间河谷。据其传说，他们源自亚马孙的希瓦罗族群，与布拉卡莫罗人及舒阿尔人同源，翻越东安第斯山脉后，沿卡塔马约—奇拉河与普扬戈—通贝斯河谷进入高原；在深受克丘亚语影响之前，其语言属希瓦罗（奇查姆）语系。他们组成酋邦联盟，包括卡尔瓦斯、马拉卡托斯、加罗昌巴、安博卡斯和查帕拉斯等部，共以肥沃的库西班巴河谷为中心；印卡入侵前夕，人口估计有八万至十万。他们种植玉米和木薯，没有文字、犁和役畜，靠名为“科查”的蓄水池灌溉山坡梯田，用鸟粪肥田，兼管制陶与冶金，并按自有的度量衡以金银进行物物交换。武士配备投石索、铜斧和长矛，在萨拉古罗一带的山顶要塞中抵抗图帕克·尤潘基的印卡大军，但联盟终被击破；经过四五代人，帕勒塔人在印卡及随后的西班牙统治下失去本族语言与社会组织，1571年西班牙视察官已在记述他们残存的风俗，到1592年加罗昌巴人更被强征入萨鲁马的矿山服役。

en: The Xi'oi, better known to the Spanish as the Pame, are an Oto-Pamean people of the Sierra Gorda and the eastern Bajío, in what is now San Luis Potosí, with kindred bands reaching into Tamaulipas, Hidalgo and Querétaro. Before the conquest they were semi-nomadic hunters and traders who learned the dialects of neighbouring peoples and lived intermingled with Nahua, Otomi and Purépecha villages on the Mesoamerican frontier, adopting some settled farming. In 1522 they joined neighbouring groups in resisting the Spanish but were defeated and drawn into mission life. They took only a small part in the Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590, limiting themselves to raids on cattle ranches in the Bajío. The rugged Sierra Gorda held out longest: not until 1742 did soldiers and Franciscans subdue it, and the mission towns founded then and later in the eighteenth century settled the Xi'oi as Christian farmers.
zh: 希奥伊人在西班牙文献中更常被称为帕梅人，属奥托帕梅语族群，栖息在戈尔达山区和巴希奥东部，即今圣路易斯波托西州一带，亲缘部落远达塔毛利帕斯、伊达尔戈和克雷塔罗。征服时代之前，他们是半游牧的猎人和商人，通晓邻族方言，在中美洲北缘与纳瓦人、奥托米人和普雷佩查人的村落杂居，也学会了部分定居农业。1522年，他们联合邻族抵抗西班牙人，但战败后被纳入传教区生活。1550至1590年的奇奇梅克战争中他们参与甚少，只在巴希奥一带袭击牧牛场。崎岖的戈尔达山区坚守最久：直到1742年才被军队和方济各会士征服，此后于18世纪陆续建立的传教城镇把希奥伊人安顿为皈依基督教的定居农民。

en: The Pamiris, or Badakhshanis, are the Eastern Iranian peoples of the high Pamir valleys around Shughnan, Wakhan and the Sarikol plateau, speaking a cluster of Pamir languages led by Shughni and Wakhi. They grew from Saka tribes recorded in the mountains as early as the seventh century BC, joined by later refugees who sheltered in the inaccessible canyons from the Turkic migrations of the fifth and sixth centuries. By the tenth century the valleys held the three principalities of Wakhan, Shughnan and Kerran, and local dynasties kept them effectively independent until the sixteenth century even after Badakhshan itself was absorbed by the Ghurids in the twelfth century. Ismaili Shia Islam came through the missionary poet Nasir Khusraw, who died in Shughnan around 1088 and is still venerated as the founder of their communities; Marco Polo found the Wakhanis already Muslim when he passed through in 1274. Shughnan reached its widest power under Shah Wanji Khan between 1787 and 1799, after which its rulers paid tribute to the khans of Badakhshan.
zh: 帕米尔人又称巴达赫尚人，是生活在舒格南、瓦罕和色勒库尔高原等帕米尔高山谷地中的东伊朗语各族群，讲以舒格南语和瓦罕语为主的一组帕米尔语言。他们源自早在公元前7世纪就见于记载的萨迦部落，5至6世纪突厥人迁徙时，又有大批难民避入险峻峡谷，与之融合。到10世纪，谷地中形成了瓦罕、舒格南和凯兰三个小邦；12世纪巴达赫尚本土被古尔王朝吞并后，这些地方王朝仍实际保持独立，一直延续到16世纪。伊斯玛仪派什叶派伊斯兰教由传教诗人纳赛尔·霍斯鲁传入，他约于1088年在舒格南去世，仍被帕米尔各社团尊为奠基人；马可·波罗1274年经过瓦罕时，发现当地人已是穆斯林。1787至1799年沙阿·万吉汗在位期间，舒格南势力达到顶峰，此后其统治者转而向巴达赫尚的汗纳贡称臣。

en: The Pamlico, also recorded as Pampticough or Pomouik, were among the southernmost Algonquian peoples of the Atlantic seaboard, living on the Pamlico and Neuse rivers behind the great North Carolina sound that still bears their name, in a cluster of related Carolina Algonquian communities that included the Croatoan or Hatteras, Machapunga, Weapemeoc and Chowanoke. English knowledge of them began with Walter Raleigh’s Roanoke expeditions of 1585 and 1586, whose visitors heard them called Pomoui and whose linguist Thomas Harriot studied their language with the Roanoke guides Manteo and Wanchese. They farmed corn and vegetables in the coastal flats, fished the sounds and traveled them in distinctive dugout canoes, examples of which have turned up far along the Atlantic coast. Epidemic disease proved more destructive than war: a smallpox “great mortality” swept their towns in 1696, and when the explorer John Lawson collected their vocabulary in 1701 the whole North Carolina Algonquian population had fallen to roughly six hundred; by 1710 the Pamlico themselves occupied a single village with about fifteen fighting men. The Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1713 completed the collapse, as the Tuscarora turned on their Algonquian allies, killing or enslaving many Pamlico, and after the peace the survivors merged into the Machapunga and Tuscarora communities, their Carolina Algonquian speech surviving chiefly in Lawson’s word lists as the southernmost recorded Algonquian vocabulary of the coast.
zh: 帕姆利科人（亦作帕姆普蒂科、波穆伊克）是大西洋沿岸最靠南的阿尔冈昆民族之一，住在北卡罗来纳大海湾后方的帕姆利科河与纽斯河畔，海湾仍以他们命名；他们属于卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆群体集群，亲缘族群包括克罗阿托恩（即哈特勒斯）、马查庞加、韦佩梅奥克和乔瓦诺克。英国人对他们的了解始于1585至1586年沃尔特·雷利的罗阿诺克探险，当时的来访者听到他们自称波穆伊，学者托马斯·哈里奥特还借助罗阿诺克向导曼蒂奥和万切斯研究他们的语言。他们在滨海平原种植玉米和蔬菜，在海湾捕鱼，乘着独具特色的独木舟往来，这类独木舟的实物曾在大西洋沿岸很远的地方出土。疫病比战争更具毁灭性：1696年一场被称为“大死亡”的天花横扫各村，1701年探险家约翰·劳森采集他们的词汇时，整个北卡阿尔冈昆人口已降到约六百人；到1710年，帕姆利科人自己只剩一座村庄、约十五名战士。1711至1713年的图斯卡罗拉战争完成了最后的崩溃：图斯卡罗拉人反过来攻打自己的阿尔冈昆盟友，许多帕姆利科人被杀或被掳为奴；战后幸存者并入马查庞加人和图斯卡罗拉人，他们的卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆语主要保存在劳森的词汇表中，是有记录的沿岸最南阿尔冈昆语料。

en: The Pamona, also called To Pamona or To Pobare'e after their Bare'e language, are the people of the Lake Poso basin and the Poso River in Central Sulawesi, spreading from the lakeside highlands to the Tomini Gulf coast at Tojo. Their own traditions trace their ancestors to the Salu Moge mountains in East Luwu, from where the ruler Macoa Bawalipu of Wotu brought them down to the Mangkutana country. Before colonial rule they followed the Lamoa belief system, settling along rivers rather than the open coast to avoid raiders coming through Tomini Bay, and their villages were governed by customary chiefs such as the Datue Poso assisted by a council of elders. In 1770 the chief Pilewiti, a cousin of the ruler of Bone in South Sulawesi, founded the Kingdom of Tojo, which united the Bare'e-speaking groups of To Lage, To Tora'u, To Lalaeyo and To Rato Bongka under a dynasty blessed by the Bone court. Mandar settlers brought Islam to the Poso coast in the early nineteenth century, while the highland Pamona kept their older rites and farming life into the colonial period.
zh: 帕莫那人又称“多帕莫那”，因说巴雷埃语也叫“多波巴雷埃”，聚居在中苏拉威西的波索湖流域和波索河沿岸，从湖畔高地一直分布到托久所在的托米尼湾海岸。按照他们自己的传说，其先民来自东鲁乌的萨卢莫盖山区，是瓦图的统治者马科阿·巴瓦利普把他们迁到曼库塔纳一带，以便就近管辖。殖民时代之前，他们信奉名为拉莫阿的传统信仰，村落多沿河而建、远离开阔海岸，以防敌人从托米尼湾来袭；各村由波索达图等习惯首领在长老议事会辅佐下治理。1770年，与南苏拉威西波尼统治者同族的首领皮莱维蒂建立托久王国，把托拉盖、托托拉乌、托拉莱约和托拉托邦卡等说巴雷埃语的群体统一在得到波尼宫廷加持的王朝之下。19世纪初，曼达尔移民把伊斯兰教带到波索沿海，而高地的帕莫那人仍保留着古老的仪式和农耕生活。

en: The Panará, once known to their neighbours as the Kreen-Akrore, are a Jê-speaking people of the forests between the upper Tapajós and the Iriri, on the border of what are now Mato Grosso and Pará. The name Kreen-Akrore comes from the Mẽbêngôkre language and means “round cut head”, after their distinctive haircut, and their tall stature also earned them the label of giant Indians. They are the last descendants of the Southern Kayapó, a numerous Jê people who in the 1700s ranged across a huge swathe of central Brazil, from the north of São Paulo and southern Goiás into Mato Grosso, living by farming, hunting, fishing and gathering. When gold- and slave-hunting bandeirantes pushed into those captaincies in the eighteenth century, the Kayapó communities abandoned their old lands and drifted west; the ancestors of the Panará retreated into the least accessible forests between the Xingu and the Tapajós, where through the rest of the 1700s and the 1800s they lived beyond the reach of settlers, missions and soldiers, keeping their language and their forest life intact.
zh: 帕纳拉人旧称克林-阿克罗雷，是使用热语族语言的族群，住在上塔帕若斯河与伊里里河之间、地当今马托格罗索州与帕拉州交界的森林里。克林-阿克罗雷一名出自门本戈克雷语，意为“圆削头”，得自他们独特的发式；他们身材高大，还被称为巨人印第安人。帕纳拉人是南部卡亚波人仅存的后裔；18世纪时，南部卡亚波人人数众多，活动范围横跨巴西中部大片土地，从圣保罗北部、戈亚斯南部一直延伸到马托格罗索，以农耕、狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生。18世纪，追逐黄金和奴隶的旗队涌入这些都督辖区，卡亚波各部纷纷弃地西迁；帕纳拉人的祖先退入欣古河与塔帕若斯河之间最闭塞的林地，在18世纪余下的年代和整个19世纪，那里没有定居者、传教士或军队能够到达，他们的语言和森林生活因而完整保存下来。

en: The Panatahuas are an Arawak-speaking rainforest people of the Rupa-Rupa high jungle in what is now the Huánuco department of central Peru, holding the valleys of the Monzón and Chunatahua rivers near present Tingo María and the mouth of the Chinchao. Their language, also called Panatagua, is poorly recorded and now extinct. Chroniclers such as Guamán Poma de Ayala relate that, rather than submit to the Inca armies of Pachacútec, the Panatahuas withdrew deeper into the forest, and they kept their independence in the mountains above the Huallaga valley when the Spaniards arrived. From the 1630s Franciscan missionaries entered their territory and founded several reducciones along the Huallaga, and in 1754 the friar Alonso Abad used the Monzón river to push into Panatahuas and Cashibo country.
zh: 帕纳塔瓦斯人是今秘鲁中部瓦努科大区鲁帕-鲁帕高地雨林中的阿拉瓦克语族群，据有廷戈玛丽亚附近蒙松河与丘纳塔瓦河之间的谷地以及钦查奥河河口一带。他们的语言又称帕纳塔瓦语，记载很少，现已消亡。据瓜曼·波马·德·阿亚拉等编年史家记述，帕纳塔瓦斯人不愿臣服于帕查库特克的印加军队，退入丛林深处；西班牙人到来时，他们仍在瓦亚加河谷上游的山区保持独立。17世纪30年代起，方济各会传教士进入其地界，沿瓦亚加河建起若干归化村；1754年，修士阿隆索·阿巴德又循蒙松河深入帕纳塔瓦人和卡希博人的地区。

en: The Panche, also called the Tolima, were a warlike people of the lower western slopes of the Eastern Andes, between the Muisca high plateau and the Magdalena River, in what is now southwestern Cundinamarca and northeastern Tolima. Numbering around 30,000 at the conquest, they lived not under a single ruler but in a loose confederation of independent chiefdoms whose names, Tocaima, Guaduas, Sasaima and many others, survive as Colombian towns. They were the Muisca's chief western enemies, raiding the plateau with clubs and arrows tipped in spider and snake poison, and chroniclers such as Pedro Simón described them, with some exaggeration, as cannibals; their rock art survives at Tibacuy and nearby sites, and they practised cranial deformation. Their language is extinct and unclassified. In 1538 the Panche faced the invading Spaniards of Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada together with their Muisca rivals, and on 20 August 1538 they were routed at the Battle of Tocarema, where the zipa Sagipa fought beside the Spanish captains Juan de Céspedes and Juan de Sanct Martín. The defeat did not end their resistance, and further campaigns under Hernán Venegas Carrillo were needed before the chiefdoms were subdued, after which disease and colonial settlement greatly reduced the survivors.
zh: 潘切人又称托利马人，是勇武好战的族群，居住在东科迪勒拉山脉西麓的低地，东接穆伊斯卡人的高原，西临马格达莱纳河，即今昆迪纳马卡省西南部与托利马省东北部一带。西班牙征服时他们约有三万人，没有统一的君主，而是由若干独立的酋邦组成松散联盟；托凯马、瓜杜阿斯、萨赛马等许多族群和酋长的名字，后来都成了哥伦比亚的城镇名。他们是穆伊斯卡人在西边的主要敌手，手持硬木棒和涂有蜘蛛、毒蛇毒液的弓箭袭扰高原；佩德罗·西蒙等编年史家夸称他们食人，他们还实行颅骨改形，蒂瓦库伊等地留存有他们的岩画。潘切语已经消亡，归属不明。1538年，潘切人同时迎战贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达的西班牙入侵者和与之一道的穆伊斯卡世仇；1538年8月20日，他们在托卡雷马战役中被击溃，穆伊斯卡统治者萨吉帕与西班牙队长胡安·德·塞斯佩德斯、胡安·德·圣马丁并肩作战。战败并未结束抵抗，殖民当局又派埃尔南·贝内加斯·卡里略多次征讨，才将各酋邦征服，此后疫病和殖民定居使幸存者人口大减。

en: The Pangasinan are an Austronesian people of the Lingayen Gulf coast of western Luzon, whose name means place of salt-making, from asin, salt, after the coastal salt pans that still define their country; the inland reaches were called Caboloan, the land of bolo bamboo. Their trading towns on the gulf belonged to the maritime routes linking Southeast Asia to India, China and Japan from at least the eighth century, and Ming records note embassies from Feng-jia-shi-lan between 1403 and 1405; by the sixteenth century the Spanish called the place the Port of Japan, where Chinese and Japanese silks, porcelain and firearms were exchanged for gold, slaves and deerskins. In 1571 Martín de Goiti began the Spanish conquest, and in 1572 Juan de Salcedo landed at the mouth of the Agno River; when the Chinese corsair Limahong, driven from Manila in 1574, took refuge in Pangasinan, Salcedo dislodged him after a seven-month siege, and a Spanish province with its capital at Lingayen existed from 1580. The Pangasinan rose twice against colonial rule: in December 1660 Andres Malong of Binalatongan was proclaimed King of Pangasinan and ruled briefly until Spanish forces overthrew him in February 1661, and on 3 November 1762 Juan de la Cruz Palaris proclaimed independence after the British capture of Manila, holding out until his capture in January 1765.
zh: 邦阿西楠人是吕宋西部林加延湾沿岸的南岛语系民族，其族名意为“制盐之地”，来自意为盐的 asin，得名于沿海的盐田；内陆地区旧称卡博洛安，即渤竹之地。他们在海湾上的贸易城镇至迟从8世纪起就处在连通东南亚与印度、中国和日本的海上商路上，中国明代史籍把他们记为“冯嘉施兰”，记载其在1403至1405年间遣使朝贡；到16世纪，西班牙人把这里称作“日本港”，中国和日本的丝绸、瓷器、火器在此交换黄金、奴隶和鹿皮。1571年，马丁·德·戈伊蒂开始征服邦阿西楠，1572年胡安·德·萨尔塞多在阿格诺河口登陆；1574年，中国海盗林凤被逐出马尼拉后逃到邦阿西楠，萨尔塞多经七个月围攻将他赶走，1580年，以林加延为首府的西班牙行省正式设立。邦阿西楠人两次起兵反抗殖民统治：1660年12月，比纳拉通安的安德烈斯·马隆被推举为邦阿西楠国王，短暂独立后于1661年2月被西班牙军队推翻；1762年11月3日，趁英军攻占马尼拉，胡安·德拉克鲁斯·帕拉里斯宣布独立，坚持到1765年1月被俘。

en: The Pankará are an Indigenous people of the Pernambuco sertão, whose heartland is the Serra do Arapuá and the neighboring Serra da Cacaria in the municipality of Carnaubeira da Penha, with kindred communities at Itacuruba on the routes between the mountains and the islands of the São Francisco River. From the seventeenth century the expansion of cattle ranching into the Pajeú and São Francisco valleys, led by the great Garcia d'Ávila estates whose Casa da Torre had been built on the Bahian coast from 1551, seized indigenous lands and drove families into the mountains; eighteenth-century colonial records style these refugees revolted, dispersed and cattle thieves, and the campaigns against them ran on into the following century. The Serra da Cacaria takes its name from the broken pottery and clay pipes left behind when its villages were stormed. The Pankará speak Portuguese laced with ritual words, and the Toré dance, the jurema cult and the Encantados remain the core of their religious life.
zh: 潘卡拉人是伯南布哥干旱腹地的原住民，中心在卡瑙贝拉-达佩尼亚市的阿拉普阿山和邻近的卡卡里亚山，在伊塔库鲁巴也有亲缘社群，那里正处在山地与圣弗朗西斯科河诸岛之间的迁徙路线上。17世纪起，养牛业向帕热乌河谷和圣弗朗西斯科河谷扩张，其推动者是势力庞大的加西亚·达维拉家族地产，该家族位于巴伊亚海岸的塔楼庄园从1551年开始修建；牧场侵占原住民土地，把各个家族逼进深山。18世纪的殖民档案把这些避难者称作叛乱者、流散者和偷牛贼，针对他们的征讨一直延续到下一世纪。卡卡里亚山的名字便来自村落遭袭后留下的碎陶片和陶烟斗。潘卡拉人使用带有仪式词汇的葡萄牙语，托雷舞、茹雷马崇拜和对着魔诸灵的信仰仍是他们宗教生活的核心。

en: The Pankararu are an Indigenous people of the Pernambuco sertão, whose villages cluster around Brejo dos Padres near Tacaratu and Petrolândia on the middle São Francisco River, with related communities further south in Bahia. Their name appears in colonial and later records as Pancaré, Pankaré, Pankaruru and Pankarú, among other spellings. Like other peoples of the northeastern backlands, they were formed through the forced removals and mission aldeamentos of the Portuguese colony, which settled different ethnic groups together and blurred older identities; their own tradition remembers a grant of one square league of land to the mission that gathered their ancestors during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The neighboring district of Tacaratu, its name meaning mountain of many peaks in their language, was formally created in 1808. Their original tongue, once spoken between the Moxotó and Pajeú rivers, is known only from short word lists and was never securely classified, and the people came to speak Portuguese. The Toré dance and the cult of the Encantados, enchanted beings said to dwell in the castles hidden inside the hills, remained the center of their ritual life.
zh: 潘卡拉鲁人是伯南布哥干旱腹地的原住民，村落集中在圣弗朗西斯科河中游塔卡拉图和彼得罗兰迪亚附近的布雷若-杜斯帕德雷斯，另有亲缘社群远至巴伊亚南部。其名在殖民时期及以后的文献中又拼作潘卡雷、潘卡鲁鲁、潘卡鲁等。与东北部腹地的其他族群一样，他们是在葡萄牙殖民当局的强制迁徙和传教村落政策下形成的：不同族群被集中安置，旧有的族群界限逐渐模糊；据他们自己的传统记忆，18至19世纪时，王室曾向收容其祖先的传教村授予一平方里格的土地。邻近的塔卡拉图区于1808年正式设立，其名在潘卡拉鲁语中意为多峰之山。他们原有的语言曾通行于莫绍图河与帕热乌河之间，只留下简短词表，归属始终没有定论，族人后来改说葡萄牙语。托雷舞，以及对据说栖身山中隐秘城堡里的着魔诸灵的崇拜，一直是他们仪式生活的核心。

en:
The Paredarermean are the Paredarerme, the Oyster Bay people of Tasmania's central eastern coast, their country running around Great Oyster Bay from the Freycinet peninsula toward the Tasman Peninsula, where the related Pydairrerme shared their language, while inland the Big River people spoke a closely kindred dialect. Their Eastern Tasmanian tongue was well recorded by colonists, leaving one of the fullest word lists of any island language, and the bays and islands gave them oysters, shellfish, seals and muttonbirds beside the kangaroo hunting grounds of the coastal grasslands. Before the sealers came, the Oyster Bay and Big River districts may have held as many as two thousand people.

Seal and whale hunters began raiding their camps in the late 1810s, killing men and carrying off women, and from 1823 settlers led by George Meredith took the Swansea and Grindstone Bay country; a reprisal there ended with the warriors Musquito and Black Jack hanged in 1825. By 1828 the survivors under Tongerlongeter had joined the Big River band of Montpelliatta, and Governor Arthur answered their raids with martial law and the Black Line sweep of 1830. Robinson's missions then secured their surrender and exile to Wybalenna, where Tongerlongeter, given the name King William, died of peritonitis in June 1837, on the very day William IV died.
zh:
帕雷达勒默人即帕雷达勒梅族群，欧洲文献称牡蛎湾人，居住在塔斯马尼亚中东部海岸，疆域环绕大牡蛎湾，从弗雷西内半岛延伸到塔斯曼半岛一带，半岛上亲缘相近的皮代雷梅人也说他们的语言，内陆的大河部族则讲一种近亲方言。殖民者对他们的东塔斯马尼亚语记录详尽，留下了全岛各语言中最完整的词汇表之一；海湾与岛屿为他们提供牡蛎、贝类、海豹和鹱鸟，滨海草地则是猎袋鼠的场所。在海豹捕猎者到来之前，牡蛎湾与大河地区的人口可能多达两千。

19世纪10年代末，海豹和鲸鱼捕猎者开始劫掠他们的营地，杀害男子、掳走妇女；1823年起，乔治·梅雷迪思领头的移民占取斯旺西和磨石湾一带，当地的一次报复行动以战士穆斯基托和布莱克·杰克于1825年被绞死告终。到1828年，通格隆格特率领的残部与蒙佩利亚塔的大河游群合流，阿瑟总督以戒严和1830年的“黑线”扫荡回应他们的袭击。其后罗宾逊的使命诱使他们投降并流放怀巴伦纳，被取名“威廉国王”的通格隆格特于1837年6月因腹膜炎病逝，恰与威廉四世同一天离世。

en: Pashash was the northern branch of the Recuay tradition of the Peruvian highlands, taking its name from the archaeological site near Cabana in the Sierra de Ancash. The Recuay culture had flourished from about 200 BCE to 600 CE in the Callejon de Huaylas, heir to much of the older Chavin territory and in close, often warlike contact with the Moche of the coast; its people built the earliest fortified towns of the Andes and fired white kaolin pottery painted in black, red and white. Pashash developed from this tradition between roughly 500 and 1000 CE, with remains also found at Chacas. Excavations at the site uncovered fine Recuay-style vessels and jewellery of gilded arsenic bronze, dated to between 300 and 600 CE. In the fourteenth century the valleys of northern Ancash where these remains lie were held by small chiefdoms speaking the poorly recorded Culli language, before Inca armies reached the region.
zh: 帕沙什是秘鲁高原雷库伊传统的北部分支，得名于安卡什山脉卡瓦纳附近的考古遗址。雷库伊文化约于公元前200年至公元600年在瓦伊拉斯走廊兴盛，继承了更古老的查文文化的大片地域，并与沿海的莫切人往来密切、时常交战；雷库伊人修建了安第斯最早的设防城镇，烧制以黑、红、白三色绘饰的白色高岭陶。帕沙什在约500至1000年间由这一传统发展而来，遗存也见于查卡斯。遗址中出土了精美的雷库伊风格陶器和镀金砷铜首饰，年代在300至600年之间。14世纪时，这些遗存所在的安卡什北部山谷由使用记载稀少的库利语的小酋长国占据，后来印加军队才抵达这一地区。

en: The Pashayi are an Indo-Aryan people of the river valleys of eastern Afghanistan around Jalalabad, Laghman and the Kunar, speaking Pashayi and often also Pashto or Persian. They are regarded as indigenous to the region, possibly older than the Gandhara civilization, and were pressed into the poorer mountain valleys by waves of Ghilji Pashtun settlement. Before Islam they followed a blend of Buddhism, Hinduism and local animism with shamanic rites and a goat cult; Marco Polo in the thirteenth century found them practicing what he called sorcery, and when Babur visited Darai Nur in the early sixteenth century the town was still famed for wine and pork had only just been forbidden. In 1582 Mirza Muhammad Hakim, the Naqshbandi-minded governor of Kabul and brother of the Mughal emperor Akbar, campaigned from Laghman to Alishang and claimed the conversion of sixty-six valleys, building a fort at the Islamabad confluence. Pashtun pressure continued in the eighteenth century, when the leader Deishamir Baba conquered Darra-i Nur and brought its Kafir rulers to Islam, while Pashayi elders kept the people's identity through their marat councils.
zh: 帕沙伊人是生活在阿富汗东部贾拉拉巴德、拉格曼和库纳尔一带河谷中的印度—雅利安语族群，讲帕沙伊语，也常兼通普什图语或波斯语。他们被视为当地土著，渊源可能早于犍陀罗文明，后来在吉尔吉普什图人接连迁徙的挤压下退入较贫瘠的山谷。伊斯兰化之前，他们信奉佛教、印度教与本地万物有灵信仰的混合体，行萨满仪式并崇拜山羊；13世纪马可·波罗经过时称他们擅施巫术，16世纪初巴布尔造访达拉伊努尔时，这座城镇仍以葡萄酒闻名，吃猪肉也才刚被禁止。1582年，莫卧儿皇帝阿克巴之弟、倾向纳格什班迪教团的喀布尔长官米尔扎·穆罕默德·哈基姆从拉格曼出兵打到阿利尚，据说使66个山谷改宗，并在伊斯兰堡两河汇流处修建要塞。18世纪普什图人的压力仍在持续，首领戴沙米尔·巴巴攻占达拉伊努尔，迫使当地的卡菲尔首领们皈依伊斯兰教；而帕沙伊的长老们则依靠马拉特议事会维系着族群的认同。

en: The Passamaquoddy, who call themselves Peskotomuhkati, or pollock-spearers after the fish central to their coastal life, are an Algonquian-speaking people of the Dawnland, the country straddling present-day Maine and New Brunswick. Their homeland centres on Passamaquoddy Bay, the Bay of Fundy and the Gulf of Maine, together with the St. Croix River and its tributaries. They lived by a seasonal round, dispersing inland to hunt in winter and gathering on the coast and islands in summer to take fish, seals and shellfish, and they were one of the founding nations of the Wabanaki Confederacy alongside the Abenaki, Mi'kmaq and Maliseet. French settlers wintered on St. Croix Island in 1604, the first permanent French attempt in the region, and the Passamaquoddy thereafter took part in the long Wabanaki wars against English expansion. When the United States gained independence the new border cut their country in two, and during the early nineteenth century they were reduced to small reservations in eastern Maine.
zh: 帕萨马科迪人自称 Peskotomuhkati，意为“叉狭鳕鱼的人”，得名于这种在其滨海生活中地位极重的鱼；他们是说阿尔冈昆语的“黎明之地”族群，家园横跨今天的缅因州与新不伦瑞克省，以帕萨马科迪湾、芬迪湾、缅因湾及圣克洛伊河水系为中心。他们随季节迁徙：冬天分散到内陆狩猎，夏天聚集到海岸和岛礁捕鱼、海豹和贝类。帕萨马科迪人是瓦巴纳基联盟的创始成员之一，与阿贝纳基、米克马克和马利塞特人并肩。1604年，法国移民在圣克洛伊岛过冬，这是法国人在当地第一次长期定居的尝试；此后帕萨马科迪人卷入了瓦巴纳基人对抗英国扩张的长期战争。美国独立后，新划定的边界把他们的家园一分为二，到19世纪初，他们被压缩到缅因东部几处狭小的保留地里。

en: The Pasto were the most numerous indigenous people of the inter-Andean valleys of what is now the Colombian department of Nariño and the neighboring province of Carchi in Ecuador, where they lived beside the Quillacinga. Their name may derive from an Awa phrase meaning scorpion people. In the last decade of the fifteenth century they fought the Inca emperor Huayna Cápac, who campaigned against them from Quito; when Inca troops occupied the Ipiales district the Pasto withdrew into the western cordillera and drove the garrisons out, leaving the Incas to push on through the Cofán lands instead. They were skilled cotton weavers and ran organized markets paid in gold and cloth, and the 1558 inspection by the Quito judge García de Valverde found towns averaging close to five hundred families each. Their Barbacoan language, closely related to Awa Pit and marked by Quechua influence, gradually ceased to be spoken under colonial rule.
zh: 帕斯托人是今哥伦比亚纳里尼奥省及毗邻的厄瓜多尔卡尔奇省安第斯山间谷地中人口最多的原住民，与基利亚辛加人相邻而居；他们的名字可能源自阿瓦皮特语，意为“蝎人”。15世纪最后十年，他们对抗从基多出征的印加皇帝瓦伊纳·卡帕克：印加军队占领伊皮亚莱斯一带后，帕斯托人退入西科迪勒拉山区并驱逐了驻军，印加人只好改道科凡人的土地南下。他们善织棉布，设有组织化的市场，以黄金和织物作为支付手段；1558年基多王家审检院法官加西亚·德·巴尔韦德巡视时，发现每个村镇平均有近五百户。他们的语言属巴巴科安语族，与阿瓦皮特语相近并带有明显的克丘亚语影响，在殖民统治下逐渐消亡。

en: Patpatar denotes the Austronesian-speaking village peoples of southern New Ireland, whose closely related languages include Patpatar, also called Gelik, and the neighbouring Siar of the island's southern tip, both members of the Patpatar-Tolai group of Oceanic languages; they live from fishing and garden cultivation, and Dutch explorers first reached their coasts in 1616.
zh: 帕特帕塔尔指新爱尔兰岛南部操南岛语言的诸村落族群，他们使用的近亲语言包括又称格利克语的帕特帕塔尔语和岛屿南端的西亚尔语，二者都属大洋洲语支的帕特帕塔尔-托莱语群；岛民以渔捞和园地耕作为生，荷兰探险者于1616年首次抵达这一带海岸。

en: The Patwin, or Southern Wintu, were the southern branch of the Wintun peoples, speaking River and Hill dialects of a Penutian Wintuan language along the lower Sacramento and the plains west of it. Their village of Korusi gave the later town of Colusa its name, while the Patwin word yo-loy, a place abounding in rushes, survives in Yolo; farther south the Suisun band held the marshes between Putah Creek and Suisun Bay, and the Patwin as a whole may have numbered between two and five thousand in the eighteenth century. Like the Pomo and the Maidu they practiced the Kuksu dance religion. Spanish pressure reached them after 1800: in 1810 Gabriel Moraga's soldiers trapped and killed a hundred and twenty-five Suisun fighters, and by 1816 over three hundred of the band had been baptized into Mission San Francisco de Asis. In 1817 the cornered villagers of chief Malica burned their huts and died in the flames rather than surrender. The survivors, led by Sem-Yeto, known after baptism as Chief Solano, helped found the Sonoma mission in 1823 and in 1834 allied with Mariano Vallejo, but a smallpox epidemic in 1837 cut down the native population around Sonoma anyway.
zh: 帕特温人又称南温图人，是温顿诸族的南支，在萨克拉门托河下游及西岸平原上讲佩努蒂语系温顿语的河滨与丘陵两种方言。科卢萨城的名字便来自他们的科鲁西村；帕特温语 yo-loy 意为“芦苇繁茂之地”，约洛的地名也由此而来。更南边的绥森群体据有普塔溪与绥森湾之间的沼泽；18世纪时帕特温人总数可能在两千到五千之间。和波莫人、迈杜人一样，他们奉行库克苏舞教。1800年后西班牙人的压力波及他们：1810年，加夫列尔·莫拉加的士兵围杀了一百二十五名绥森战士；到1816年，该群体已有三百余人在阿西西的圣方济各传教站受洗。1817年，被逼入绝境的马利卡酋长村民焚毁棚屋，纵身火海，宁死不降。幸存者在塞姆-耶托（受洗后称索拉诺酋长）率领下，于1823年参与建立索诺马传教站，1834年与马里亚诺·巴列霍结盟；但1837年的一场天花仍使索诺马一带的原住民大批死亡。

en: The Pazioca, better known by the Quechua exonym Diaguita, were a group of independent chiefdoms that spoke the Cacán language in the transverse valleys of Chile's Norte Chico, from Copiapó to the Choapa, and across the Andes in north-western Argentina. Politically fragmented, each valley followed its own kuraka and dialect, trading fish and shells with the coast. Their archaeological culture grew from the El Molle and Las Ánimas complexes after about 1000, marked by advanced irrigation and pottery painted in black, white and red. The Incas subdued them after hard fighting, settling mitma colonists and imposing Cuzco-style crafts. Diego de Almagro's expedition first met the Chilean Pazioca at Copiapó in 1536, when perhaps 20,000 lived in Chile; rebellions under García Hurtado de Mendoza were crushed around 1558. The eastern groups held out through the Calchaquí Wars, rising in 1630 and only submitting after 1665. Cacán died out by the mid-eighteenth century, giving way to Quechua, Mapuche and Spanish.
zh: 帕西奥卡人更常用的名字是克丘亚语外来名“迪亚吉塔人”。他们由各自独立的酋邦组成，操卡坎语，分布在智利小北地区从科皮亚波到乔阿帕的一系列横向河谷，以及安第斯山东麓的阿根廷西北部。他们政治上四分五裂，每个河谷各有首领和方言，并与沿海交换鱼和贝类。其考古文化由埃尔莫列文化和拉斯阿尼马斯文化发展而来，约1000年形成迪亚吉塔文化，以发达的灌溉系统和黑、白、红三色彩陶为标志。印加人经过苦战将其征服，派驻米特马埃移民并推广库斯科风格工艺。1536年，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的远征队在科皮亚波首次接触智利的帕西奥卡人，当时智利境内约有两万之众；1558年前后，加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨血腥镇压了他们的反抗。安第斯山东侧的同族在卡尔查基战争中坚持更久，1630年起兵，直到1665年后才被征服。卡坎语到18世纪中期消亡，逐渐被克丘亚语、马普切语和西班牙语取代。

en: The Pech, formerly called Paya by the Spanish, are a Chibchan-speaking people of north-eastern Honduras, in the departments of Colón, Gracias a Dios and Olancho. Pech is their own name for themselves, while they call all outsiders Pech-Hakua. Migrating north from what is now Colombia, they held a broad swathe of coast and interior from the Aguán River toward the Nicaraguan border, organized into chiefdoms whose social complexity reaches back to about the year 300 and whose language carries Maya loanwords. Spanish expeditions in the early sixteenth century met the land they named Taguzgalpa and failed to subdue it, but from 1622 missionaries gathered the Pech into reductions, and colonial pressure grew steadily: a governor of the Paya was appointed in 1713, and further reductions followed at Buenaventura in 1739, Siguatepeque in 1767 and Río Tinto in 1797. Raided by the Miskito and displaced by settlers, the Pech were moved from Cape Camarón to the mouth of the Aguán in 1805, by then confined to a fraction of their old territory.
zh: 佩契人旧称帕亚人，是洪都拉斯东北部科隆、格拉西亚斯—阿迪奥斯和奥兰乔三省的奇布查语族群。佩契是他们的自称，对一切外人则称佩契—阿库阿。他们从今哥伦比亚一带北迁，曾占据从阿瓜安河延伸到尼加拉瓜边境的广阔沿海与内陆土地，社会形态为若干酋长国，其复杂社会约在公元300年即已出现，语言中还带有玛雅语借词。16世纪初的西班牙远征队遇到了这片被他们称作塔古斯加尔帕的土地，却未能将其征服；但从1622年起，传教士把佩契人集中到归化村，殖民压力不断加重：1713年殖民当局任命了管辖帕亚人的官员，1739年、1767年和1797年又先后在布埃纳文图拉、锡瓜特佩克和里奥廷托设立归化村。加上米斯基托人的袭扰和移民的排挤，佩契人于1805年从卡梅伦角被迁到阿瓜安河口，昔日领地只剩一小片。

en: Peewareewa, rendered Peoria in French records, is the Illinois-language autonym peewaareewa, meaning one who comes carrying a pack on his back. The people who bore it were one of the twelve Algonquian-speaking tribes of the Illinois Confederation, holding villages along the Illinois River and the eastern shore of the Mississippi in what became the state of Illinois, and they were partly descended from the earlier Cahokia people. The French explorers Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met a Peoria band near the mouth of the Des Moines River during their voyage of 1673, and Jesuit missions and the fur trade soon bound the tribe to New France. When France ceded the Illinois Country to Britain in 1763, the Peoria crossed the Mississippi into Spanish Missouri. They ceded their Illinois lands at the Treaty of Edwardsville in 1818 and their Missouri claims by the Treaty of Lewisville in 1832, after which they were assigned lands in Kansas and became the nucleus of the Confederated Peoria, gathering in the remnants of the Kaskaskia, Wea, Piankeshaw and Cahokia.
zh: 佩瓦雷瓦在法国文献中写作皮奥里亚，源自伊利诺伊语自称皮瓦雷瓦，意为背着行囊而来的人。使用这个名字的族群是操阿尔冈昆语的伊利诺伊联盟十二部之一，在后来成为伊利诺伊州的伊利诺伊河沿岸和密西西比河东岸建有村庄，且有一部分血统来自更早的卡霍基亚人。1673年，法国探险家雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃在探险途中于得梅因河河口遇到一支皮奥里亚队伍，耶稣会传教站和皮货贸易很快把该部与新法兰西联系在一起。1763年法国把伊利诺伊地区割让给英国后，皮奥里亚人西渡密西西比河进入西班牙属密苏里。他们在1818年的《爱德华兹维尔条约》中割让伊利诺伊土地，又在1832年的《刘易斯维尔条约》中放弃密苏里的权益，随后被安置到堪萨斯，并成为皮奥里亚联盟的核心，陆续接纳了卡斯卡斯基亚人、威亚人、皮安克肖人和卡霍基亚人的余部。

en: The Pegas, also written Pêgas or Degas, were a Cariri-family people of the Paraíba backlands, holding the Piranhas and Piancó river valleys of the high sertão, and they are also numbered among the tribes of the Tarairiú nation. The meaning of their name is uncertain, since the word pega is neither Cariri nor Tupi and may itself be Portuguese. Around 1696 the pioneer Teodósio Canate fought his way through native resistance to the Piancó and founded the settlement of Festival of Piranhas on Pegas land. Their Jesuit mission village was renamed Nossa Senhora do Bom Sucesso in 1719, and in 1738 the tribe, through the captain-major Francisco de Oliveira Lêdo, petitioned the crown for a formal land grant in the Sertão das Piranhas and obtained it; eleven missionaries in turn served the village. By royal charter of 1766 the settlement was raised to a town and named Pombal in honour of the Marquis of Pombal. Mass forced removals under the colonial administration, followed by absorption into settler society, eventually ended the Pegas as a separate people.
zh: 佩加斯人又作佩加人或德加人，是帕拉伊巴内陆的卡里里语族部落，占据高地旱区的皮拉尼亚斯河与皮安科河谷，也被列为塔拉伊留联盟诸部之一。他们族名的含义已难确考，因为“佩加”这个词既不是卡里里语也不是图皮语，本身可能就是葡萄牙语。约1696年，拓荒者特奥多西奥·卡纳特冲破原住民抵抗进抵皮安科河，在佩加斯人的土地上建立了皮拉尼亚斯庆典定居点。他们的耶稣会传教村于1719年改名为圣母邦苏塞苏村；1738年，部落通过兵头弗朗西斯科·德·奥利维拉·莱多向王室请求在皮拉尼亚斯旱区正式授予土地并获得批准，先后有十一名传教士在该村服务。1766年，王室特许状将该定居点升格为城镇，为向蓬巴尔侯爵致敬而命名为蓬巴尔。殖民当局组织的大规模强制迁徙，加上随后被定居者社会同化，最终使佩加斯人不再作为独立族群存在。

en: The Pehuenche, people of the pewen in Mapudungun, are the mountain dwellers of the south-central Andes on both the Chilean and Argentine sides, named for the monkey-puzzle tree whose pine-nut harvest, gathered in the high forests between March and May, anchored their yearly round: winters were spent in the valleys and summers above the tree line in country stretching from the Maule to the Llaima volcano and from the Diamante River to Lake Alumine. They sowed nothing, hunting guanacos and deer with bows from skin-covered pole tents and later herding feral horses for meat dried into charqui. Their own early language, perhaps Huarpean, was lost as Araucanization proceeded; by the mid-eighteenth century all Pehuenche spoke Mapudungun. They entered Spanish records with clashes south of the Tolten in 1575, and two thousand warriors under chief Quilacan sacked Chillan in 1599; after the Parliament of Quillin of 1647 they alternated parleys with raids such as those on Maule in 1657, when they opened a new Andean pass, and on San Luis in 1712. In 1767 and 1769 they turned their weapons against Mapuche rivals and Spanish settlements alike, and in 1820 they fought the Tehuelche on the Senguerr River.
zh: 佩文切在马普敦贡语里意为佩文之人，佩文就是智利南洋杉。他们是安第斯山脉中南部、智利与阿根廷两侧山区的居民，名字来自这种树木：每年3至5月在高山林中采集南洋杉松籽，是他们一年生计的重心；冬天退入山谷，夏天登上林线以上活动，疆域从马乌莱河延伸到莱马火山、从迪亚曼特河延伸到阿卢米内湖。他们不事农耕，住在覆皮的木杆帐篷里，用弓箭猎取原驼和鹿，后来又牧养野化的马，把马肉晒成肉干。他们早年可能有自己的、或许属瓦尔佩语系的语言，但随着阿劳卡化推进而消失，到18世纪中期佩文切人已普遍改说马普敦贡语。1575年他们在托尔滕河以南与西班牙人冲突，从此见诸西班牙文献；1599年酋长基拉坎率两千战士洗劫奇廉。1647年基林议会之后，他们时而谈判、时而出击，1657年袭掠马乌莱并发现了一条新的安第斯山口，1712年又洗劫圣路易斯。1767年和1769年，他们先后把矛头指向马普切对手和西班牙人定居点，1820年又在森格尔河畔与特维尔切人交战。

en: The Pekowi were one of the five divisions of the Shawnee, the Algonquian-speaking people of the Northeastern Woodlands; spellings of their name survive in such place names as Piqua, Pickawillany, Pickaway and Pequea. Shawnee ritual leaders were traditionally drawn from this patrilineal division, and its chiefs included Opessa Straight Tail, who signed treaties with William Penn's colony before leading his band west toward the Ohio Valley around 1727. From 1737 the Pekowi were led by Peter Chartier, a fur trader of mixed Pekowi and French parentage. After clashing with Pennsylvania's authorities over the sale of rum, he accepted a French commission in 1745 and led about four hundred Pekowi first to Lower Shawneetown and then into Kentucky, where they founded Eskippakithiki; Pekowi warriors fought for the French at the Battle of Fort Necessity in 1754. The division later shared the village of Peckuwe in Ohio with the Kispoko until its destruction in 1780, and in the nineteenth century the Pekowi formed part of the Absentee-Shawnee removed to Indian Territory.
zh: 佩科维人是东北林地阿尔冈昆语民族肖尼人的五大分支之一，其名称的各种拼法保留在皮夸、皮卡威拉尼、皮克威和佩奎亚等地名中。肖尼人的宗教仪式首领传统上出自这个父系分支，首领之一奥佩萨·斯特雷特泰尔曾与威廉·佩恩的殖民地签订多项条约，后于1727年前后率部西迁俄亥俄河谷。1737年起，佩科维人由兼有佩科维与法兰西血统的皮货商彼得·沙尔捷领导；他因朗姆酒贩卖问题与宾夕法尼亚当局冲突，1745年接受法国委任，率约四百名佩科维人先到下肖尼镇，再进入肯塔基建立埃斯基帕基西基聚落，佩科维战士还在1754年的必要性堡战役中为法国作战。后来该分支与基斯波科人同住俄亥俄的佩库韦村，直至1780年村庄被毁；19世纪，佩科维人作为缺席肖尼人的一部分被迁往印第安领地。

en: The Pemon are Cariban-speaking Indigenous people of the Gran Sabana, the open grassland plateau studded with flat-topped tepui mountains in what is now southeastern Venezuela, near the borders with Guyana and Brazil. They comprise several closely related groups, above all the Arekuna, Kamarakoto and Taurepang, whose speech forms the three main dialects of the Pemon language. Their villages were organized into egalitarian, decentralized communities that lived from farming, hunting and trade, and their mythology places gods and ancestor spirits on the summits of the tepuis, with the creator hero Makunaíma at the centre of their stories. Europeans did not enter their remote country until the 1700s, when missionaries travelling up the Caroní made the first contacts and began converting Pemon communities to Christianity.
zh: 佩蒙人是讲加勒比语族语言的原住民，居住在大萨瓦纳——今天委内瑞拉东南部、邻近圭亚那和巴西边境的开阔草原高原，地上矗立着平顶的特普伊山。他们由几个关系密切的支系组成，主要是阿雷库纳人、卡马拉科托人和陶雷潘人，三者的方言构成佩蒙语的三种主要土语。他们的村落实行平等而分散的社会组织，以农耕、狩猎和贸易为生；在他们的神话中，神灵和祖先之灵住在特普伊山顶，创世英雄马库奈玛居于传说的核心。欧洲人直到18世纪才进入这片偏远之地，沿卡罗尼河而上的传教士与佩蒙人首次接触，并开始促使各部落皈依基督教。

en: The Pende (singular Mupende, plural Bapende) are a Bantu people of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, divided into an Eastern and a Western group who share one identity without any central king or chief. Their society is built on matrilineal extended families and on ancestor worship addressed to the Mvumbi spirits, who are held to shape everyday success or misfortune. They once lived in the coastal strip between the Atlantic and the Cuanza River in what is now Angola, kin to the Ambundu, and their songs still recall the departure. Around 1620 the expansion of the Kingdom of Lunda drove them north into the Kwilu and Kasai country, where they settled beside the culturally similar Yaka and Suku. They speak Kipende, a Central Bantu language, and are famed for their masks and initiation art; carvers rank close to clan chiefs and alone share the chief's privilege of receiving the first portion of the harvest.
zh: 彭德人（单数称穆彭德，复数称巴彭德）是刚果民主共和国的班图族群，分为东、西两支，两支自认同族，却没有统一的国王或酋长。他们的社会以母系大家族为骨架，奉行祭拜姆温比祖灵的祖先崇拜，认为祖灵决定着日常的顺逆。彭德人原先住在今安哥拉境内大西洋与宽扎河之间的沿海地带，与姆本杜人同源，歌谣里仍吟唱着离开故土的缘由。1620年前后，隆达王国扩张，迫使他们北迁到奎卢河与开赛河流域，在文化相近的亚卡人和苏库人之间定居。彭德人使用班图语中部语支的基彭德语，以面具和入会仪式艺术闻名；雕刻匠人的地位仅次于氏族酋长，并与酋长一样享有分到收成头一份的特权。

en: The Penkwi-deka are the Painkwitikka, the Fish Eaters of the Northern Shoshone, often called the Bear Lake Shoshone after the lake country of the Idaho–Utah border. They ranged from McCammon along the Bear River and Logan River to Bear Lake and east towards the continental divide, generally north of the Cache Valley band, drawing their living from the salmon runs and other river resources rather than the buffalo hunts of their plains kin. Their Shoshone-speaking camps were part of the same fluid, intermarrying world as the Bannock and the Lemhi. Trappers entered the neighbouring Cache Valley from about 1818, when Michel Bourdon crossed it on a Mackenzie expedition, and the valley hosted the second great mountain-man rendezvous in 1826, putting the Fish Eaters in regular contact with the fur trade.
zh: 彭奎德卡人即潘奎蒂卡人，是北肖肖尼人的“食鱼者”支群，常按爱达荷—犹他边界的湖区被称为贝尔湖肖肖尼人。他们从麦卡蒙沿贝尔河、洛根河活动到贝尔湖，向东远达大陆分水岭，大体住在卡什谷支群的北面；与平原上的同族不同，他们主要依靠鲑鱼洄游和其他河川资源为生，而不是猎野牛。他们说肖肖尼语，营地与班诺克人、莱姆哈伊人同属一个松散通婚的世界。约1818年，毛皮探险家米歇尔·布尔顿随麦肯齐的探险队进入邻近的卡什谷，谷地又在1826年举办了第二届山地人大会，食鱼者由此与毛皮贸易建立了经常联系。

en: The Pennacook were a loose confederacy of Algonquian-speaking village communities of central Abenaki stock, settled along the upper Merrimack River in what is now New Hampshire, with outlying bands reaching into Massachusetts and southern Maine. Their name means at the bottom of the hill, and their main towns stood at Amoskeag Falls, later Manchester, and at Pennacook, later Concord; bands such as the Nashua, Ossipee and Naumkeag joined the alliance as it suited them. Related to but distinct from the coastal Wabanaki Confederacy, they were among the first peoples to meet English colonists and were quickly cut down by introduced epidemics, then harassed by Mohawk and Mi'kmaq raiders. In the seventeenth century the sachem Passaconaway kept the peace with New England, but King Philip's War, which began in 1675, dragged in his people anyway: his successor Wonalancet held neutral while other bands fought, and after the defeat many Pennacook were enslaved while the rest fled to the Hudson valley or to Quebec, where they merged with the Abenaki of Odanak and the Wabanaki nations.
zh: 佩纳库克人是操阿尔冈昆语的松散村社联盟，属中阿贝纳基支系，定居在今新罕布什尔州的梅里马克河上游，外围游群远达马萨诸塞和缅因南部。他们的名字意为“山脚之处”，主要城镇位于阿莫斯基格瀑布（后来的曼彻斯特）和佩纳库克村（后来的康科德），纳舒厄、奥西皮、瑙姆基格等游群视形势加入联盟。他们与沿海的瓦巴纳基联盟有亲缘关系但并非其成员，是最早接触英国殖民者的族群之一，随即被外来疫病大量削减，又遭到莫霍克人和米克马克人袭扰。17世纪，酋长帕萨科纳韦与新英格兰维持和平，但1675年爆发的菲利普国王战争仍把他的族人卷了进去：继任酋长沃纳兰塞特保持中立，另一些游群则参战；战败后许多佩纳库克人被掳为奴，其余逃到哈得孙河谷或魁北克，并入奥达纳克的阿贝纳基人和瓦巴纳基诸族。

en: The Penobscot are an Algonquian-speaking people of the Northeastern Woodlands, who made their home along the Penobscot River in present-day Maine; their self-name, Panawahpskewi, means the people of where the white rocks extend out. They lived in seasonal bands, hunting moose, caribou and beaver, fishing the river and gathering wild foods, and belonged to the Wabanaki Confederacy with the Abenaki, Passamaquoddy, Wolastoqiyik and Mi'kmaq. Contact in the sixteenth century brought a profitable fur trade but also smallpox and measles, to which they had no immunity: perhaps ten thousand Penobscot lived around 1600 and fewer than five hundred by the early nineteenth century. They sided with the French in the colonial wars, and a British scalp bounty was proclaimed against them in 1755; after France's fall at Quebec in 1759 they backed the Patriots in the American Revolution. From about 1800 they were confined to the Indian Island reservation, and between 1794 and 1833 treaties ceded nearly all of their territory to Massachusetts and then Maine.
zh: 佩诺布斯科特人是东北林地的阿尔冈昆语民族，世居今缅因州的佩诺布斯科特河沿岸；他们自称帕纳瓦普斯克维，意为“白色岩石伸出之处的人”。他们以季节性游群生活，猎捕驼鹿、北美驯鹿和海狸，在河中捕鱼并采集野生食物，与阿贝纳基人、帕萨马科迪人、沃拉斯托基人和米克马克人同属瓦巴纳基联盟。16世纪的接触带来了有利可图的毛皮贸易，也带来了他们毫无免疫力的天花和麻疹：1600年前后约有一万佩诺布斯科特人，到19世纪初已不足五百。殖民战争中他们站在法国一边，1755年英国人甚至悬赏他们的头皮；1759年法国在魁北克败亡后，他们在美国独立战争中支持爱国者一方。约1800年起他们被限制在印第安岛保留地，1794—1833年的一系列条约把几乎全部土地割让给马萨诸塞及后来的缅因。

en: The Pequttôog, or Pequot, were an Algonquian people who dominated central and eastern Connecticut, holding the coast between the Niantic and the Narragansett tribes; their name has been read as the destroyers or men of the swamp. The Mohegan were once part of the same people before splitting away in the seventeenth century. In 1633 the Dutch built the House of Good Hope trading post at Hartford and executed the Pequot sachem Tatobem; an epidemic the same year may have carried off four fifths of the population, leaving the succession to Sassacus. After the colonist John Oldham was killed in 1636, the New England colonies, joined by Mohegan and Narragansett allies, made open war. The Mystic massacre of 1637 broke Pequot power: about 1,500 warriors were killed or hunted down, while captives were enslaved, many being sold to Bermuda. The Treaty of Hartford of 1638 forbade the survivors even to call themselves Pequot. Small reserves were nevertheless granted at Mashantucket in 1666 and on the Pawcatuck River in 1683, and in the eighteenth century Christian Pequot families joined the new Brothertown community.
zh: 佩科特人自称佩科图格，族名意为“毁灭者”或“沼泽之人”，是阿尔冈昆语族的一支，曾统治康涅狄格中部和东部，据有尼安蒂克人与纳拉甘西特人之间的海岸。莫西干人本与他们同属一族，17世纪分裂出去。1633年，荷兰人在哈特福德建立好望堡贸易站，并处死了佩科特酋长塔托贝姆；同年的一场疫病可能夺去五分之四的人口，酋长之位由萨萨库斯继承。1636年殖民者约翰·奥尔德姆被杀后，新英格兰各殖民地联合莫西干、纳拉甘西特盟友公开开战。1637年的米斯蒂克屠杀摧毁了佩科特人的力量：约1500名武士战死或被追猎杀，俘虏沦为奴隶，许多人被卖到百慕大。1638年的《哈特福德条约》甚至禁止幸存者再自称佩科特人。尽管如此，殖民地仍于1666年在马尚塔基特、1683年在波卡塔克河划出小块保留地；18世纪，信奉基督教的佩科特家族加入了新组成的兄弟镇社群。

en: The Pericu were the Indians of the Cape Region, the southern tip of Baja California Sur, holding the coast from Todos Santos to La Paz and the Gulf islands of Cerralvo, Espiritu Santo and San Jose. Isolated by desert and sea, they kept the atlatl and dart alongside the bow and arrow into the seventeenth century, and buried their dead in caves as red-ochre-painted secondary bundles, the Las Palmas burial complex. Their language, distinct from neighbouring Guaycura, was never properly recorded. Spanish contact began in the 1530s, when the mutineer Fortun Ximenez reached La Paz and Hernan Cortes followed with his own expedition. Jesuit missions came later: La Paz in 1720, Santiago in 1724 and San Jose del Cabo in 1730. The Pericu Revolt of 1734 killed two missionaries and shook Spanish rule for two years, but war and Old World diseases broke the people, and by the Jesuit expulsion of 1768 their culture had vanished.
zh: 佩里库人是南下加利福尼亚最南端海角地区的印第安人，占据从托多斯桑托斯到拉巴斯的海岸，以及塞拉尔沃、埃斯皮里图桑托和圣何塞等加利福尼亚湾岛屿。沙漠与海洋造成的隔绝，使他们到17世纪仍在弓箭之外保留投矛器与短矛，并把死者以红赭石着色后二次葬入岩洞，即拉斯帕尔马斯葬俗。他们的语言与邻近的瓜伊库拉语不同，却从未得到完整记录。西班牙人的接触始于16世纪30年代：哗变者福尔通·希门尼斯最先抵达拉巴斯，随后埃尔南·科尔特斯亲率远征队而来。耶稣会先后于1720年在拉巴斯、1724年在圣地亚哥、1730年在圣何塞德尔卡沃建立传教站。1734年的佩里库起义杀死两名传教士，动摇西班牙统治达两年，但战乱与旧大陆疫病最终压垮了这个民族；到1768年耶稣会被驱逐时，佩里库文化已然消亡。

en: The Peruzzi were a Florentine banking family whose ancestors are traced to the mid-eleventh century and whose fortune grew first from the wool trade, buying English cloth finished in Bruges for the courts of Paris and Avignon before switching to large-scale grain dealing, with a monopoly on exports from France to central Italy, and then to finance. By the 1330s their company was the second-largest bank in Europe, capitalised at more than 100,000 gold florins, employing about a hundred factors across fifteen branches stretching from London to the Aegean, where their ties with the Knights Hospitaller gave them leverage at Rhodes. Popes, nobles, towns and abbeys borrowed from them, their courier network doubled as a diplomatic intelligence service, and their surviving ledgers of 1335 to 1343, with the chronicle of Giovanni Villani, remain a prime source for the period; in Florence they patronised Giotto's frescoes in their Santa Croce chapel from 1313. Loans of 600,000 florins to Edward III of England, together with the Lucchese war and the upheavals of the Hundred Years' War and the Flemish revolt, ruined the consortium, which collapsed in 1343 and was declared bankrupt in 1345 alongside the Bardi. The Peruzzi nonetheless kept their place among the leading patrician houses of Florence.
zh: 佩鲁齐是佛罗伦萨的银行家族，先祖可追溯至11世纪中叶，其财富最初来自羊毛贸易：收购在布鲁日精加工的英国呢绒，销往巴黎和阿维尼翁的宫廷；后来转营大规模粮食生意，垄断了从法国向意大利中部的粮食出口，最终投身金融业。到14世纪30年代，佩鲁齐公司已是欧洲第二大银行，资本逾10万金弗罗林，雇有约百名代理人，设有十五家分行，从伦敦一直延伸到爱琴海；在爱琴海，他们与医院骑士团的关系使其在罗得岛颇具影响力。教皇、贵族、城市和修道院都向他们借贷，其信使网络同时充当外交情报机构；留存下来的1335至1343年账簿，连同乔瓦尼·维拉尼的编年史，都是研究那个时代的首要资料。在佛罗伦萨，他们从1313年起资助乔托在圣十字圣殿的家族礼拜堂绘制壁画。向英格兰国王爱德华三世放贷60万弗罗林，再加上与卢卡的战争、百年战争的动荡和佛兰德斯起义，最终拖垮了这家财团：公司于1343年崩溃，1345年与巴尔迪银行一同宣告破产。尽管如此，佩鲁齐家族仍保住了佛罗伦萨名门望族的地位。

en: The Piankeshaw, whose Miami-Illinois autonym Peeyankihšiaki means those who split off, were a band of the Miami nation that dwelled apart from the others along the middle Wabash River, in present-day western Indiana and eastern Illinois, between the Wea to the north and the Kickapoo to the south. Their first village stood at the mouth of the Vermilion River, a second grew up near present-day Vincennes where the Embarras meets the Wabash, and in the eighteenth century they founded Pickawillany on the Great Miami River in Ohio, the future site of Piqua. Closely allied with the French, whose traders married into the band, they generally sided with the Americans during the Revolutionary War and held aloof from the Northwest Indian War, even winning a proclamation of protection from President George Washington. Retaliatory raids nevertheless drove many from the Vincennes area after the Battle of the Embarras River in 1786, and in 1818 their chief Chekommia sold the remaining lands by treaty. The surviving Piankeshaw merged with the Wea, Kaskaskia and Peoria into the Confederated Peoria.
zh: 皮安克肖人是迈阿密人的一支，其迈阿密—伊利诺伊语自称皮扬基希阿奇，意为分离出去的人。他们远离同族而居，活动在今印第安纳西部与伊利诺伊东部的沃巴什河中游，北邻威亚人，南接基卡普人。他们最早的村庄位于弗米利恩河河口，第二个村庄兴起于今温森斯附近的安巴腊河入沃巴什河处，18世纪又在俄亥俄的大迈阿密河畔建立皮卡威拉尼，即后来皮夸的所在地。他们与法国人关系密切，法国皮货商纷纷入赘该部；独立战争期间基本站在美国一边，也没有参加西北印第安战争，乔治·华盛顿总统还专门发布过保护他们的公告。但报复性袭击仍在1786年安巴腊河战役后把许多人逐出温森斯一带，1818年首领切科米亚签约出卖了剩余土地。幸存的皮安克肖人随后与威亚人、卡斯卡斯基亚人和皮奥里亚人合并为皮奥里亚联盟。

en: The Picards are the people of the chalk plains of northern France, from Amiens and Arras to Boulogne and Roman Flanders around Lille, with their speech extending into Hainaut in modern Belgium. Picard is one of the chief langues d'oil, a Gallo-Romance tongue already used in local written forms before the year 1000 and distinguished from the French of Paris by conservative sounds such as hard k where Parisian palatalized them, as in Picard keval against French cheval. In the feudal age the country was split among the six countships of Boulogne, Montreuil, Ponthieu, Amienois, Vermandois and Laonnois, and its name, from the Old French pic or pike, appears early in the thirteenth century when students from the whole northern speech area formed the Picard nation at the University of Paris. Picardy saw the Jacquerie peasant rising of 1358 during the Hundred Years' War, passed to Duke Philip the Good of Burgundy from 1419 with the Congress of Arras confirming the transfer in 1435, and was occupied by Louis XI in 1477 as the Burgundian inheritance broke apart. Along its northern edge the Picard world met Flemish, leaving bilingual towns such as Lille.
zh: 皮卡第人生活在法国北部的白垩平原上，范围从亚眠、阿拉斯到布洛涅和里尔周边的罗曼佛兰德斯，其方言还延伸到今比利时的埃诺地区。皮卡第语是主要的奥依语之一，属高卢罗曼语，早在1000年以前就有地方书面形式；它与巴黎法语的区别在于保存了较多古音，例如巴黎话腭化的音它仍发硬音 k，像皮卡第语 keval 对应法语 cheval。封建时代这里分为布洛涅、蒙特勒伊、蓬蒂厄、亚眠努瓦、韦芒杜瓦和拉昂努瓦六个伯国；其名来自古法语 pic（长矛），13世纪初已见使用，当时巴黎大学把整个北方方言区的学生划为“皮卡第民族”。百年战争期间，皮卡第在1358年爆发扎克雷农民起义；1419年起该地渐入勃艮第公爵好人菲利普之手，1435年阿拉斯会议予以确认；1477年勃艮第遗产解体，路易十一出兵占领皮卡第。在其北缘，皮卡第语世界与弗拉芒语相接，里尔等城镇因此长期双语并存。

en: The Piedmontese are the Romance-speaking people of Piedmont, the Alpine foothills of northwest Italy centered on Turin, Asti, Alessandria and Vercelli. Their land was held in Roman times by Celtic-Ligurian tribes such as the Taurini, who gave their name to Augusta Taurinorum, modern Turin, and after the fall of Rome it passed under Lombard and then Frankish rule. Their tongue, Piedmontese, is a Gallo-Italic language whose earliest surviving texts, the twelfth-century sermones subalpini, were still very close to Occitan; its many local dialects include those of Turin and Asti. In the eleventh century the counts of Savoy entered the region, while Asti and Alessandria grew into self-governing communes and the marquisates of Montferrat and Saluzzo stayed independent. Savoy became a duchy in 1416 and Duke Emanuele Filiberto moved its capital to Turin in 1563; in 1720 the dukes took the title of kings of Sardinia. Through these centuries Piedmontese remained the speech of town and countryside, while French and Tuscan served court and administration.
zh: 皮埃蒙特人是意大利西北部阿尔卑斯山麓皮埃蒙特地区讲罗曼语的居民，中心城市为都灵、阿斯蒂、亚历山德里亚和韦尔切利。罗马时代这里居住着陶里尼人等凯尔特-利古里亚部落，陶里尼人的名字留在了奥古斯塔·陶里诺鲁姆，即后来的都灵；西罗马灭亡后，该地先后沦于伦巴第人和法兰克人之手。他们的语言皮埃蒙特语属于高卢-意大利语支，现存最早的文本是12世纪的《阿尔卑斯山南布道文》，当时仍与奥克语十分接近；其方言众多，包括都灵方言和阿斯蒂方言。11世纪萨伏依伯爵势力进入该地区，阿斯蒂和亚历山德里亚发展为自治公社，蒙费拉托和萨卢佐侯爵领地则保持独立。萨伏依于1416年升为公国，埃马努埃莱·菲利贝托公爵于1563年将首都迁至都灵；1720年萨伏依公爵又取得撒丁国王头衔。在这数百年间，皮埃蒙特语始终是城乡俗语，而宫廷与行政使用法语和托斯卡纳语。

en: The Piikani, recorded by Europeans as the Peigan or Piegan and sometimes glossed as the splotchy robe people, are the westernmost of the three Niitsitapi nations of the Blackfoot Confederacy, whose Blackfoot speech they share with the Siksika and the Kainai. Their hunting grounds reached from the foothills of the Rocky Mountains along the upper Missouri, a country rich in beaver as well as bison, and in time they divided into a northern group, the Aapátohsipikani of what became Alberta, and a southern group, the Aamsskáápipikani of Montana. Before horses arrived around 1730 they hunted on foot with buffalo jumps and dog travois; mounted and armed through the fur trade, they helped drive the Shoshone from the northwestern plains, and the surveyor David Thompson recorded in 1787 that Blackfoot territory then stretched from the North Saskatchewan to the Missouri. As the keepers of the mountain approaches, the Piikani clashed with the Kootenai, Flathead and Nez Perce beyond the passes and guarded the beaver streams that the Hudson's Bay Company coveted; Rocky Mountain House, the company's busiest post in the 1830s, was used mainly by Piikani bands, while the American Fur Company opened Fort Piegan on their Missouri lands in 1831. The German prince Maximilian of Wied and the painter Karl Bodmer visited them in 1833, leaving detailed portraits of their life. Only four years later the steamboat-borne smallpox epidemic of 1837 swept through the upper Missouri camps and killed thousands, ending the Piikani's days as an unchecked plains power.
zh: 皮卡尼人在欧洲文献中又被记作佩甘人或皮甘人，其名称有时被解释为“袍子有斑痕的人”。他们是黑脚联盟三大尼齐塔皮民族中位置最西的一支，与西克西卡人、凯奈人一样说黑脚语。他们的猎场从落基山脉山麓一直延伸到密苏里河上游，这一带既多野牛又富海狸；随着时间推移，他们分成北部支系阿帕托西皮卡尼人（后来的阿尔伯塔）和南部支系阿姆斯卡皮皮卡尼人（蒙大拿）。约1730年马匹传入之前，他们徒步狩猎，使用野牛跳崖和狗拉雪橇；借助毛皮贸易获得马匹和火器后，他们参与把肖肖尼人逐出西北部平原，测量员戴维·汤普森在1787年记载，当时黑脚人的领土北起北萨斯喀彻温河、南抵密苏里河。作为山地通道的守门人，皮卡尼人与山口另一侧的库特奈人、弗拉特黑德人和内兹珀斯人交战，并守护着哈德逊湾公司觊觎的海狸河川；19世纪30年代公司最繁忙的商站落基山屋主要由皮卡尼各群体使用，美国毛皮公司则于1831年在他们的密苏里土地上开设了皮甘堡。1833年，德国的维德亲王马克西米利安与画家卡尔·博德默前来探访，留下了描绘他们生活的细致画作。仅仅四年后，1837年由汽船带来的天花瘟疫席卷密苏里河上游营地，数千人病死，皮卡尼人作为平原无敌强权的时代就此结束。

en: The Piipaash, better known to outsiders as the Maricopa, are a River Yuman people who call themselves Piipaa or Piipaash, simply meaning people; the name Maricopa comes from the Pima label Kokmalik'op, enemies in the big mountains, as heard and written down by the Spanish. For generations they lived in small villages along the Colorado River, but in the sixteenth century they began moving east to the Gila River to escape the attacks of the Quechan and Mohave. The migrants were not one tribe but several related River Yuman groups, among them the Piipaash proper, the Halchidhoma, the Kavelchadom and the Opa, who settled together for mutual protection and were lumped together by Spaniards and Mexicans under names such as Cocomaricopa. On the middle Gila and later the Salt River they built a lasting alliance with the Akimel O'odham, the Pima, farming side by side in the desert. Their eastern refuge did not bring complete safety: in 1825 a party of American trappers led by James Ohio Pattie killed about two hundred Maricopa in a revenge attack on a Gila village.
zh: 皮帕什人在外人口中更常被称为马里科帕人，属河滨尤曼族群；他们自称“皮皮”或“皮帕什”，意思就是“人”。“马里科帕”这个名字来自皮马人对他们的称呼“科克马利科普”，意为“大山里的敌人”，由西班牙人转写而成。他们原本世代居住在科罗拉多河沿岸的小村庄里，16世纪为躲避夸特桑人和莫哈维人的攻击，开始向东迁往希拉河。迁徙者并非单一部落，而是皮皮什本部、哈利奇多姆、卡维尔查多姆、奥帕等数个有亲缘关系的河滨尤曼群体；他们为互相保护而聚居，西班牙人和墨西哥人笼统称他们为“科科马里科帕”等名字。在希拉河中游及后来的盐河流域，他们与阿基梅尔·奥达姆人（即皮马人）结成持久同盟，在沙漠中并肩务农。东迁的避难所并不绝对安全：1825年，詹姆斯·俄亥俄·帕蒂率领的一队美国猎人为报复此前的一次袭击，在希拉河畔的一座村庄杀死了约二百名马里科帕人。

en: The Pijao were a warlike federation of peoples in the central Colombian Andes, spread through the Central Cordillera between the snowy massifs of Huila, Quindío and Tolima, the upper Magdalena valley and the upper Cauca, in country that later held Cali, Buga, Tuluá, Coyaima and Natagaima. They never formed a centralised state, living instead as allied chiefdoms; at the conquest two leagues stood out, one uniting the Coyaima, Natagaima, Guauro and Tamagale of the Magdalena plains and another grouping the mountain communities. Their priests, called mohanes, led an animist ritual life centred on water, mountains and idols of gold, clay and wood. Fields of maize and manioc supported dense populations, and their unclassified language was once heard from Ortega to Natagaima. The Pijao met the Spanish with long resistance, fighting over access to the Magdalena, Cauca and Saldaña rivers in the so-called Pijao wars, which dragged on for some eighty years. Between 1605 and 1615 Juan de Borja y Armendia, president of the Audiencia of Santafé, led the decisive pacification campaigns, founding Natagaima in 1606 to settle the survivors; war deaths, Catholic conversion and mixing with settlers broke the federation, though Pijao communities kept their identity around Coyaima and Natagaima.
zh: 皮豪人是哥伦比亚安第斯中部一群尚武的族群联盟，分布在乌伊拉、金迪奥和托利马等雪山之间的中科迪勒拉山脉、马格达莱纳河上游谷地和考卡河上游，后来的卡利、布加、图卢阿、科亚伊马和纳塔盖马等地都在其故土上。他们从未建立集权国家，而是以结盟的酋邦共处；征服时代当地形成两大联盟：一支联合了马格达莱纳平原上的科亚伊马、纳塔盖马、瓜罗和塔马加莱等部，另一支由山区的社群组成。他们的祭司称为莫汉，主持泛灵论仪式，崇拜水、山岳以及金、陶、木制的神像，玉米和木薯田地养活了稠密的人口；他们那种归属不明的语言曾通行于奥尔特加到纳塔盖马一带。皮豪人对西班牙人进行了长期抵抗，为争夺马格达莱纳河、考卡河和萨尔达尼亚河的控制权爆发了所谓皮豪战争，前后绵延约八十年。1605—1615年，圣菲检审庭主席胡安·德·博尔哈-阿门迪亚发动决定性的绥靖征讨，并于1606年建立纳塔盖马城安置幸存者；战争中的大量死亡、皈依天主教以及与移民混血，使联盟瓦解，不过科亚伊马和纳塔盖马一带的皮豪社群仍保住了自身的认同。

en: The Pikunche, whose Mapudungun name means people of the north, were the Mapudungun-speaking villagers of central Chile, spread from the Choapa and Aconcagua valleys south to the Bío Bío River, with the Itata marking their border with the Araucanian Mapuche. They farmed maize and potatoes in thatched adobe houses, irrigated their fields and worked copper, pottery and stone; the southern bands among them who beat back the Inca armies became known as the Promaucae. When Pedro de Valdivia invaded from 1541, the chief Michimalonco, who had already expelled the Inca governor Quilicanta, led the resistance and destroyed the newly founded Santiago, yet Spanish towns, encomiendas and haciendas gradually confined the Pikunche to planned Indian villages. During the colonial period they mingled with Spaniards, mostly Basques in the towns and Andalusians in the countryside, and with natives relocated from Araucanía, Chiloé and Cuyo, leaving their old villages for the haciendas until their Indigenous identity dissolved into the general Chilean population.
zh: 皮昆切人的名字在马普敦贡语中意为北方之人，他们是智利中部讲马普敦贡语的定居族群，分布范围从乔阿帕河、阿空加瓜河谷向南直到比奥比奥河，伊塔塔河是他们与阿劳卡尼亚马普切人之间的天然界线。他们种植玉米和马铃薯，住茅草顶土坯房，引水灌溉，并掌握冶铜、制陶和石器工艺；其中击退印加军队的南部支系后来被称为普鲁纳瓦卡人。1541年佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚入侵时，此前已驱逐印加总督基利坎塔的酋长米奇马隆科率众抵抗，摧毁了初建的圣地亚哥；但西班牙人的城镇、委托监护制和大庄园逐步把皮昆切人圈进规划的印第安人村镇。殖民时期，他们与西班牙人（城里多为巴斯克人、乡间多为安达卢西亚人）以及从阿劳卡尼亚、奇洛埃和库约迁来的原住民混居，纷纷离开旧村落户大庄园，其原住民认同最终融入智利的一般人口之中。

en: The Pima, who call themselves O'odham, or river people, are irrigation farmers of the Gila and Salt rivers in Arizona and of the Sonora and Yaqui rivers farther south; the Spanish named them Pima from a phrase meaning I don't know, heard at their first meetings. Their northern bands, the Akimel, Tohono and Hia C-ed O'odham, made up the Upper Pima of the Pimeria Alta, while the Lower Pima, including the Nevome and Cocomacaques, held the Sonoran river valleys where towns such as Ures and Pitic stood. They lived in spread-out rancheria villages, watered maize, bean and cotton fields through canals, and fought off Apache and Yavapai raiders. Father Eusebio Kino first visited their villages in 1694. In 1751 Luis Oacpicagigua united some fifteen thousand Pima in the great Pima Revolt, which killed more than a hundred settlers before he surrendered in 1752; he died in a Spanish prison in 1755, and new presidios then pinned the frontier under military rule.
zh: 皮马人自称奥奥德姆，意为河上人，是亚利桑那希拉河、盐河以及更南方索诺拉河、亚基河流域的灌溉农人；西班牙人从他们初次见面时常说的一句意为“不知道”的话，给他们取名皮马。北方的阿基梅尔、托霍诺和希亚塞德诸支构成上皮马利亚的上皮马人，下皮马人（包括内沃梅人和科科马卡克人）则占据索诺拉的河谷，乌雷斯、皮蒂克等城镇就在其地。他们住在分散的小村里，开渠灌溉玉米、菜豆和棉花，并抵御阿帕奇人与亚瓦派人的袭掠。1694年，尤西比奥·基诺神父首次走访他们的村庄。1751年，路易斯·奥克皮卡吉瓜联合约一万五千名皮马人发动大规模的皮马起义，杀死百余名移民，最终于1752年投降；他1755年死于西班牙监狱，随后西班牙人新设多处要塞，以军管锁住这条边疆。

en: The Pipil are the southernmost Nahua people of Central America, speaking Nawat, a tongue closely related to the Nahuatl of central Mexico. Their ancestors began moving south out of Mexico around the eighth century, through the Isthmus of Tehuantepec to the Pacific coast of El Salvador, where Nawat speakers had arrived by about 900; one branch pushed on to the Nicoya region and became the Nicarao. In the land they called Kuskatan, between the Paz and Lempa rivers, the Pipil built a loose confederation of city-states that became a hereditary monarchy by 1400, with irrigated cacao estates around Izalco and a cotton-textile trade reaching from central Mexico to Costa Rica. In 1524 Pedro de Alvarado invaded Cuzcatlan from the Guatemalan highlands but was repulsed within months. San Salvador, founded in 1525, was overrun in the great rising of 1526, and Diego de Alvarado reestablished it only in 1528, when the last native stronghold at Cinacantan fell. Wider revolt smouldered until the province was judged pacified in 1539, after which the Pipil lived under encomienda rule within the Captaincy General of Guatemala.
zh: 皮皮尔人是中美洲最南端的纳瓦族群，讲与墨西哥中部纳瓦特尔语相近的纳瓦特语。其先民约8世纪开始自墨西哥南迁，穿过特万特佩克地峡来到萨尔瓦多太平洋沿岸，约900年纳瓦特语使用者已抵达此地；其中一支继续南下尼科亚地区，后来成为尼卡拉奥人。在他们称为库斯卡特兰、介于帕斯河与伦帕河之间的土地上，皮皮尔人建立了松散的城邦联盟，到1400年已形成世袭君主制；伊萨尔科一带有灌溉可可庄园，棉纺织品贸易北起墨西哥中部、南达哥斯达黎加。1524年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多从危地马拉高地入侵库斯卡特兰，但数月内即被击退。1525年建立的圣萨尔瓦多在1526年的大起义中被攻陷，迭戈·德·阿尔瓦拉多直到1528年才将其重建，同年印第安人最后据点西纳坎坦陷落。更大范围的反抗持续到1539年该省被宣告平定，此后皮皮尔人在危地马拉都督辖区的委托监护制下生活。

en: The Piscataway were the dominant Algonquian people of the lower Potomac, holding the north bank of the river in southern Maryland from the falls below modern Washington toward the bay, together with Patuxent River tributaries and villages such as Moyaone, Accokeek and Potapaco; the Nacotchtank at Anacostia were among their close neighbors. Their villages paid tribute through local werowances to a paramount chief titled the Tayac, whose capital at Moyaone drew together farming communities of palisaded longhouses whose women farmed maize, beans and tobacco while men hunted and gathered oysters.
