John Smith found them on his Potomac voyage of 1608, and in 1634 the Tayac Kittamaquund granted the arriving Maryland colonists the site of St. Mary’s City as a buffer against the Susquehannock; he and his wife were converted by the Jesuit Andrew White in 1640, the year White translated a catechism into their language. The alliance soured as Maryland grew: by 1668 the western-shore Algonquians were confined to reservations, epidemics cut their numbers, and raids by the Susquehannock and Haudenosaunee drove them from their lands. After sheltering in Zekiah Swamp in 1680 and on Conoy Island after 1699, the survivors, now often called Conoy, drifted into Pennsylvania in the 1720s, about 150 strong, and placed themselves under Haudenosaunee protection alongside the Nanticoke. Late in the century most moved north through Detroit into Upper Canada, joining the Six Nations of the Grand River in Ontario, while a smaller party merged with the Meherrin and Tuscarora in the south.
zh: 皮斯卡塔韦人是波托马克河下游最重要的阿尔冈昆民族，据有今华盛顿以南瀑布线至海湾之间的马里兰南部波托马克河北岸，以及帕塔克森特河支流地带，村落包括莫亚翁、阿科基克和波塔帕科等，阿纳卡斯蒂亚的纳科奇坦克人是他们的近邻。各村通过本地酋长向尊号“塔亚克”的最高首领纳贡，塔亚克的首府莫亚翁统辖着一批设防长屋农耕社区：妇女种植玉米、豆类、南瓜和仪式用烟草，男子狩猎并采集牡蛎。1608年约翰·史密斯在波托马克河航行中发现他们；1634年塔亚克基塔马昆德把圣玛丽城的所在地授予新来的马里兰殖民者，作为抵御萨斯奎哈诺克人的缓冲，1640年他与妻子在耶稣会士安德鲁·怀特劝化下受洗，怀特同年还把教理问答译成他们的语言。随着马里兰殖民地壮大，联盟变味：到1668年西岸阿尔冈昆人已被限制在保留地里，疫病又使人口锐减，萨斯奎哈诺克人和豪德诺索尼人的袭扰更把他们逐出故土。1680年他们避入泽基亚沼泽，1699年后又栖身波托马克河上的科诺伊岛；幸存者此后常被称为科诺伊人，18世纪20年代辗转进入宾州，仅剩约一百五十人，与楠蒂科克人一同接受豪德诺索尼联盟保护。18世纪后期，多数人经底特律北迁上加拿大，加入安大略的大河六族；另有一小支南下，与梅赫林人和图斯卡罗拉人融合。

en: The Pitaguary, also called Potiguara, are a Tupi-origin Indigenous people of Ceará who hold the Serra da Aratanha lands between Maracanaú, Pacatuba and Maranguape, a short distance from Fortaleza; their name, a variant of Potiguara, appears in documents of the seventeenth to nineteenth centuries as the name of a serra, a homestead and a territory. In 1665, after the wars that pitted native peoples against Portuguese and Dutch in Ceará, the Potiguara of the region gathered into a large aldeia later called Bom Jesus da Aldeia de Parangaba, and around 1680 part of them moved off to found São Sebastião de Paupina, parent settlement of the Aldeia Nova de Pitaguari. Royal sesmaria grants followed, giving the Parangaba Indians land in the Serra de Maranguape in 1707 and 1718 and the Paupina Indians holdings in the Serra de Pacatuba in 1722. Jesuit missionaries catechized the settlements and, by Pitaguary memory, the colonial church and reservoir at Santo Antônio were raised with forced indigenous labor; the people came to speak Portuguese.
zh: 皮塔瓜里人（又称波蒂瓜拉人）是塞阿拉的图皮系原住民，保有阿拉塔尼亚山的土地，分布在马拉卡纳乌、帕卡图巴和马兰瓜佩之间，距福塔莱萨不远；其名是波蒂瓜拉的变体，在17至19世纪的文献中先后被用来称呼山地、庄园和领地。1665年，在塞阿拉原住民与葡萄牙人、荷兰人交战的动乱之后，当地波蒂瓜拉人被集中到一座大村落，后来称作帕兰加巴村善耶稣镇；1680年前后，一部分人分出去建立圣塞巴斯蒂昂-迪保皮纳，即新皮塔瓜里村的母村。此后王室接连颁发份地特许，1707年和1718年把马兰瓜佩山的土地授予帕兰加巴印第安人，1722年把帕卡图巴山的产业授予保皮纳印第安人。耶稣会在这些村落传教；按皮塔瓜里人的记忆，圣安东尼奥的殖民时期教堂和蓄水池都是用印第安人的强制劳役修建的，族人后来使用葡萄牙语。

en: The Pitahwarita, more fully Pitahawirata, were one of the three southern bands of the Pawnee, Caddoan-speaking earth-lodge villagers whose name means People Downstream; French traders called them the Tapage, or Screaming Pawnee, and English speakers the Noisy Pawnee. Until the 1770s they lived with the other southern bands and the Wichita on the Arkansas River, but Osage pressure then set the Pawnee moving north, and tradition remembers the Pitahwarita following the Chaui into Nebraska between 1774 and 1777 to build their earth lodges on the Platte while the Kitkehahki chose the Republican River. They farmed maize, beans and squash in the river bottoms and left each year for the communal bison hunt, sharing the Pawnee priesthoods, sacred bundles and unfortified towns. Their most famous hour came in about 1830, when a Pitahwarita warrior captured the Cheyenne's most sacred bundle, the Sacred Arrows, in a hard-fought defensive battle; the loss at once stopped the Cheyenne fighting, and the Skidi chief Big Eagle took the arrows into keeping. The smallpox epidemic of 1831 then halved the Pawnee nation to between six and eight thousand people, and in 1833 the Pitahwarita, listed in the document as the Pawnee Tappaye, joined the four-band treaty on the Platte that ceded the lands south of the river to the United States.
zh: 皮塔瓦里塔人又译皮塔哈维拉塔，是波尼人南方三支之一，讲卡多语，住土屋村镇，名字意为下游之人；法国商人称他们为塔帕什波尼，即喧闹的波尼人，英语则称他们为喧闹波尼。1770年代之前，他们与其他南方支派及威奇塔人同住阿肯色河流域，后来奥塞奇人的压力迫使波尼人北迁；按传统说法，皮塔瓦里塔人在1774至1777年间跟随察维人进入内布拉斯加，在普拉特河建起土屋，而基特卡哈基人则选择了里帕布利肯河。他们在河谷低地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，每年还要集体出猎野牛，并与其他波尼人共享祭司制度、圣束仪式和不设防御的城镇。他们最著名的时刻约在1830年到来：一场艰苦的防御战中，一名皮塔瓦里塔战士夺得了夏延人最神圣的圣束，即圣箭，夏延人随即停止战斗，斯基里首领大鹰将圣箭收管。1831年的天花瘟疫使整个波尼人口减半，只剩六千到八千人；1833年，皮塔瓦里塔人在文件中被列为塔帕什波尼，与四个分支一同在普拉特河畔签约，把河南的土地割让给美国。

en: Pitlaxa is the autonym of the people the Spaniards called the Pilagá, a tall and strongly built Guaycuru nation whose language belongs to the Mataco-Guaicurú family and whose closest kin were the Toba, with whom they shared alliances, dialect and family ties. They were hunters and gatherers of the eastern Chaco, living on the Paraguay River beside the Abipón, Mocoví and Toba, and gathering carob, chañar, mistol and prickly pear. The Guaraní of Paraguay named them frentones, big foreheads, from their habit of shaving the front of the head. They first enter written records in the seventeenth century, when the Jesuit Nicolás del Techo described them in 1628 under the name zapitilingas. In those years the Guaycuru peoples were pushing west through the southern and central Chaco in constant wars against the Mataco-Mataguayan groups. Spanish military pressure halted that expansion in the mid-eighteenth century and drove the Pitlaxa from the Bermejo River; by the end of the century they had settled in the marshlands between the Pilcomayo and the Paraguay, the country they still held when the Argentine frontier reached them in the nineteenth century.
zh: 皮特拉哈是这个民族的自称，西班牙人则称他们为皮拉加人。他们属瓜伊库鲁族群，身材高大、体格强健，语言归马塔科-瓜伊库鲁语系，与托巴人关系最近，双方结盟通婚、方言相近。他们是查科东部的狩猎采集者，游居于巴拉圭河畔，与阿维庞人、莫科维人和托巴人为邻，采集角豆、查尼亚尔果、米斯托尔果和仙人掌果。巴拉圭的瓜拉尼人因他们剃去前额头发的习俗，称之为“宽额人”。17世纪他们首次见于文字记载，耶稣会士尼古拉·德尔特乔在1628年曾以萨皮蒂林加之名描述他们。当时瓜伊库鲁诸部正穿越查科南部和中部向西扩张，不断与马塔科-马塔瓜亚诸群体交战。18世纪中叶，西班牙的军事压力遏止了这场扩张，把皮特拉哈人赶出贝尔梅霍河；到该世纪末，他们已在皮尔科马约河与巴拉圭河之间的沼泽地带定居，直到19世纪阿根廷边疆推进到他们面前时，仍据守着这片土地。

en: The Pochegor are an Evenki clan of the mountain taiga south of the Aldan, along the Stanovoy ranges that divide the Lena and Amur systems, country where Evenki hunters had lived for centuries before Russians appeared. The clan name is recorded in Transbaikalian records among the Barguzin Khamnigans and the Yeravnino clans: Evenki-origin lineages that took up horse and cattle pastoralism and were gradually absorbed into the Buryat and Khamnigan world. In the 1600s Cossack parties moving from Yakutsk toward the Amur, including those of Poyarkov in 1643 and Khabarov in 1667, crossed these hunting grounds, and the clan became yasak payers, while some related Evenki groups later migrated south into Mongolia and Manchuria.
zh: 波切戈尔人是阿尔丹河以南山地泰加林的鄂温克氏族，活动在分隔勒拿河与阿穆尔河两大水系的斯塔诺夫山脉一带；早在俄国人到来之前，鄂温克猎人已在此生活了数百年。该氏族名见于外贝加尔的记载，被列入巴尔古津哈米尼干人和叶拉夫宁氏族群体的名单，这些鄂温克出身的支系转而从事牛马畜牧，逐渐融入布里亚特和哈米尼干世界。17世纪，从雅库茨克奔向阿穆尔河的哥萨克队伍（如1643年的波雅尔科夫与1667年的哈巴罗夫）穿过这片猎场，波切戈尔氏族成为雅萨克缴纳者；另一些亲缘的鄂温克群体则在后来南迁蒙古和满洲。

en: The Pochutecs were a Nahua people of the Pacific coast of Oaxaca, settled around Pochutla with the neighbouring towns of Tonameca and Huatulco, and their tongue was the earliest branch to split from the Nahuan languages, perhaps as early as the fifth century, making it markedly different from the Nahuatl of the central Mexican highlands and giving it traits absorbed from the neighbouring Chatino. Cut off from the other Nahua polities by the southern mountains, they never entered the Aztec Empire: at the time of the Spanish arrival the Pochutla coast belonged to the Mixtec tributary kingdom of Tututepec, or Yucu Dzaa, founded on the Río Verde by the ruler Eight Deer in 1083 and expanded across the coastal plain until Huatulco became one of its subject towns. Pochutec merchants travelled the trade routes into the Mixtec highlands, and the isolated language survived as a distinct coast speech long after the end of the independent Nahua states, before eventually falling extinct.
zh: 波丘特克人是瓦哈卡太平洋沿岸的纳瓦族群，聚居于波丘特拉，邻近托纳梅卡和瓦图尔科等镇；他们的语言是纳瓦语族中最早分化的一支，分化时间或可早至5世纪，因此与墨西哥中部高地的纳瓦特尔语差异明显，并吸收了邻族查蒂诺语的若干特征。由于被南部山脉与其他纳瓦政权隔断，他们从未并入阿兹特克帝国：西班牙人到来时，波丘特拉海岸隶属于米斯特克人的朝贡王国图图特佩克（米斯特克语称尤库·萨阿）。该王国1083年由统治者“八鹿”在韦尔德河畔建立，势力扩张到整个沿海平原，瓦图尔科便是其属城之一。波丘特克商人沿商路深入米斯特克高地，而这种孤立的海岸语言在纳瓦诸独立政权终结之后仍长期保持自身特色，最终走向消亡。

en: The Pocumtuck, often called the Deerfield Indians, were an Algonquian people of the upper Connecticut River valley in western Massachusetts, whose main stockaded village stood on the site of modern Deerfield and gave the whole Pioneer Valley its older name of Pocumtuck Valley. Around them stood a loose confederacy of related bands, among them the Nonotuck and Norwottuck near Northampton and Hadley, the Agawam around Springfield, the Woronoco at Westfield and the Squakeag farther north near the Vermont and New Hampshire border. They spoke an R-dialect of Eastern Algonquian, akin to the Mahican of the Hudson valley, and lived by the classic Northeast combination of maize, bean and squash fields, river fishing and seasonal hunting. Early contact brought the smallpox that cut their numbers heavily, and in the colonial wars they first sided with the Tunxis and Narragansett against Uncas of the Mohegan, then joined the Wampanoag confederacy against the English in King Philip’s War of 1675 to 1676, fighting at Bloody Brook and elsewhere. After the defeat most survivors took refuge at Schaghticoke on the Hudson, and when the Seven Years’ War began in 1754 many moved again and merged into the Abenaki of Saint-François-du-Lac in Quebec. The best-remembered Pocumtuck was the war leader Wawanotewat, known as Gray Lock, who led Abenaki raids deep into Massachusetts in the 1720s and after whom Mount Greylock in the Berkshires is named.
zh: 波科姆塔克人常被称为迪尔菲尔德印第安人，是居住在马萨诸塞西部康涅狄格河上游河谷的阿尔冈昆民族，其设防主村位于今迪尔菲德，整个先驱者谷也因他们而旧称波科姆塔克谷。他们周围是一个由近亲群体组成的松散联盟，包括北安普敦和哈德利一带的诺诺塔克与诺沃塔克、斯普林菲尔德附近的阿加瓦姆、韦斯特菲尔德的沃罗诺科，以及更北边靠近佛蒙特和新罕布什尔边界的斯阔奎格。他们说东阿尔冈昆语的一种 R 方言，与哈德逊河谷的莫希干语相近，生计方式是东北林地典型的玉米、豆类、南瓜种植，辅以河上捕鱼和季节性狩猎。欧洲人接触之初，天花便使他们人口锐减；殖民战争中，他们先联合坦克西人与纳拉甘西特人对抗莫希干酋长昂卡斯，后又在1675至1676年的菲利普国王战争中加入万帕诺亚联盟对英作战，曾参加血溪等战役。战败后，多数幸存者逃到哈德逊河畔的斯卡蒂科克避难；1754年七年战争爆发时，许多人再次迁移，并入魁北克圣弗朗索瓦迪拉克的阿布纳基人。最著名的波科姆塔克人是军事领袖瓦瓦诺特瓦特，即“灰锁”，他在18世纪20年代率领阿布纳基武装深入马萨诸塞袭扰，伯克希尔山区的格雷洛克山便以他命名。

en: The Pohnpeians are the indigenous people of Pohnpei, a high volcanic island of the eastern Caroline Islands, and speak Pohnpeian, a Pohnpeic Micronesian language of the Austronesian family. Their Lapita-related ancestors settled the island more than two thousand years ago, and from the eighth or ninth century they built Nan Madol, a ceremonial centre of artificial islets and stone platforms off the eastern shore. Legend remembers the centralized Saudeleur dynasty ruling from about 1100 until the invader Isokelekel overthrew it around 1628 and replaced it with the decentralized nahnmwarki chief system; society was organized into five tribes and clans under chiefs who held the land and received tribute. Álvaro de Saavedra sighted Pohnpei in 1529 and Pedro Fernandes de Queirós passed it in 1595 without landing, so the island stayed little known to Europeans until the Russian expedition of Fyodor Litke in 1828 produced the first detailed accounts, including of the ruins of Nan Madol. Whalers and traders then called in growing numbers, beachcombers settled ashore, and in 1837 the first Catholic missionary arrived, while the Pohnpeians still ruled themselves through their own chiefs.
zh: 波纳佩人是东加罗林群岛火山大岛波纳佩的原住民，使用南岛语系密克罗尼西亚语族波纳佩语支的波纳佩语。他们与拉皮塔文化有关的祖先在两千多年前定居该岛，从8或9世纪起在东岸外海修建了由人工小岛和石台组成的祭祀中心南马都尔。据当地传说，集权的绍德雷尔王朝约于1100年起统治，1628年前后被外来者伊索克勒克勒推翻，后者代之以较为分权的“南姆瓦尔基”酋长制度；传统社会分为五大部族和若干氏族，土地归酋长所有，平民向其纳贡。1529年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉望见波纳佩，1595年佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯途经该岛却未登陆，因此直到1828年费奥多尔·利特克的俄国考察队才留下首批详细记录，其中包括南马都尔遗址。此后捕鲸船和商船造访日多，流浪汉登岛定居，1837年第一位天主教传教士抵达，而波纳佩人仍由本族酋长治理内部事务。

en: Poitevin is the langue d'oïl of the old province of Poitou in west-central France, grouped with Saintongeais within the Poitevin–Saintongeais family but marked by features absorbed from Occitan, for it arose on the old frontier between the oïl and oc speech areas. Poitou and its capital Poitiers take their names from the Pictones, the Gaulish tribe of the region, and from the time of Charlemagne the country was held by the counts of Poitou, whose inheritance passed through Eleanor of Aquitaine to the English Plantagenets. French pressure ended English claims at the Battle of Taillebourg and the Treaty of Paris in 1259, when Henry III surrendered Poitou to Louis IX. The dialect appears in charters from the thirteenth century and won its first printed book, La Gente Poitevinrie, in 1554; François Rabelais had learned it as a schoolboy at Fontenay-le-Comte. In the later sixteenth century Poitou became a stronghold of the Huguenots, and after 1685 many of its Protestant people joined the exodus or the overseas settlements, while emigrants from southern Poitou had already helped found Acadia from 1604. The Catholic lower Poitou, the future Vendée, rose against the Revolutionary government in 1793, the same years in which the old province was split into the departments of Vienne, Deux-Sèvres and Vendée.
zh: 普瓦图语是法国中西部旧行省普瓦图的奥依语，与圣通日语同属普瓦图-圣通日语族，但带有不少吸收自奥克语的特征，因为它形成于奥依语与奥克语的旧分界线上。普瓦图及其首府普瓦捷得名于当地的高卢部落皮克托内斯人；自查理曼时代起，这片土地由普瓦图伯爵统治，其继承权经阿基坦的埃莉诺转入英格兰金雀花家族之手。法国的军事压力在塔耶堡战役和1259年的《巴黎条约》后终结了英格兰的主张，亨利三世将普瓦图割让给路易九世。该方言见于13世纪以来的契约文书，1554年有了第一本印刷书《普瓦图风雅集》；拉伯雷少年时在丰特奈勒孔特求学，就学会了这种话。16世纪后期普瓦图成为胡格诺派的重镇，1685年后许多新教徒或流亡海外，或投身海外殖民地，而早在1604年起，南普瓦图的移民就已参与建立阿卡迪亚。信奉天主教的下普瓦图——即后来的旺代——于1793年起兵反抗革命政府，也就在那些年里，旧行省被划分为维埃纳、德塞夫勒和旺代三省。

en: The Polabians are the Lechitic West Slavs, also called Elbe Slavs or Wends, who settled from the sixth century along the Elbe, its tributaries and the Baltic coast, from Holstein to the Oder and the Ore Mountains. The Bavarian Geographer of 830 already counted their great confederacies: the Obotrites around the lower Elbe and Trave, the Veleti, later called Liutizi, along the Warnow and Peene with the Rani of Rügen, and the Hevelli and Sprevane on the Havel and Spree. Charlemagne treated the Obotrites as allies, but Ottonian kings built marches and bishoprics such as Brandenburg and Havelberg to subdue and convert them; the pagan rising of 983 sacked them and restored Slavic rule east of the Elbe. In the eleventh century Gottschalk built a Christian Obotrite kingdom, while the Wendish Crusade of 1147 and the campaigns of Henry the Lion and Valdemar the Great broke the last pagan principalities: Niklot died fighting in 1160, the Rani temple fortress of Arkona fell to the Danes in 1168, and the Hevelli inheritance passed to Albert the Bear and his Margraviate of Brandenburg. During the Ostsiedlung Saxon and Flemish colonists gradually Germanized the towns and countryside, so that by the fourteenth century only the Drevani of the Lüneburg Heath Wendland still kept their Slavic speech, called Polabian. Loaded with Low German loanwords and recorded in the Vocabularium Venedicum, it lasted until the last native speaker died in 1756; only the Sorbs of Lusatia kept an Elbe-Slavic identity.
zh: 波拉布人属莱赫支西斯拉夫人，又称易北斯拉夫人或文德人，6世纪起定居在易北河及其支流与波罗的海沿岸，范围从荷尔斯泰因延伸到奥得河和厄尔士山脉。830年的《巴伐利亚地理学家》已记载其几大部落联盟：活动于下易北河与特拉沃河一带的阿博德利人，分布在瓦尔诺河与佩讷河一带、后称卢蒂奇人的维莱蒂人，另有吕根岛的拉尼人，以及哈韦尔河与施普雷河畔的斯托多兰尼人和斯普雷瓦人。查理曼曾以阿博德利人为盟友，奥托王朝的国王们却设立藩侯国和勃兰登堡、哈弗尔贝格等主教区加以征服和归化；983年的异教徒大起义洗劫这些主教区，恢复了易北河以东的斯拉夫人统治。11世纪戈特沙尔克建立了基督教的阿博德利王国，而1147年的文德十字军以及狮子亨利、瓦尔德马大帝的征战摧毁了最后的异教政权：尼克洛特于1160年战死，拉尼人的圣殿要塞阿科纳于1168年落入丹麦人之手，斯托多兰尼人的遗产则传给熊阿尔布雷希特及其勃兰登堡藩侯国。东向移民运动中，萨克森和佛兰德斯殖民者逐渐使城镇与乡村德意志化，到14世纪只剩吕讷堡荒原文德兰的德拉瓦尼人还保留着斯拉夫语，即波拉布语。这种语言混入大量低地德语借词，靠《文德词汇表》等文献记录留存，1756年末代母语者去世后便告消亡；唯有卢萨蒂亚的索布人延续了易北斯拉夫人的族群身份。

en: The Polatskians were the East Slavic people of White Ruthenia, the lands around Polotsk, Minsk and Mogilev in what is now northern Belarus. They grew from the Krivichs, Slavic settlers who mixed with the local Balts from the eighth century and built Polotsk on the Western Dvina trade road. First mentioned in 862, Polotsk became the seat of its own Rus' principality under Rogvolod and, after Vladimir the Great's conquest of 980, under the Rurikid descendants of Izyaslav; Prince Vseslav, who reigned from 1044 to 1101, made it a rival of Kiev before it broke into the smaller principalities of Minsk, Vitebsk and Drutsk. In the early fourteenth century the region entered the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, where its Orthodox, Ruthenian-speaking nobles kept much of their self-rule, and Polotsk became a voivodeship in 1504. After the Union of Lublin of 1569 and the Union of Brest of 1596, many commoners joined the Uniate Church while Polish spread among the elite. The Partitions of Poland in the late eighteenth century transferred the region to the Russian Empire.
zh: 波洛茨克人是白鲁塞尼亚的东斯拉夫人，聚居在今白俄罗斯北部的波洛茨克、明斯克和莫吉廖夫一带。他们源自8世纪起迁入的斯拉夫部族克里维奇人，后者与当地波罗的人融合，并在西德维纳商路上建起波洛茨克。波洛茨克首见于862年的记载，在罗格沃洛德治下成为独立的罗斯公国；980年被弗拉基米尔大帝征服后，由留里克王朝伊贾斯拉夫的后裔统治，弗谢斯拉夫王公（1044—1101年在位）时一度与基辅分庭抗礼，其后分裂为明斯克、维捷布斯克和德鲁茨克等小公国。14世纪初，该地区并入立陶宛大公国，信奉东正教、讲鲁塞尼亚语的贵族保留了相当自治权，波洛茨克于1504年成为一个省。1569年卢布林联合和1596年布列斯特联合之后，许多平民转入合并派教会，波兰语则在精英阶层中传播。18世纪末波兰被瓜分，这一地区随之归入俄罗斯帝国。

en: The Polesians, or Poleshuks, were the East Slavic people of the Pripyat Marshes, the vast forest-and-swamp country around Pinsk, Gomel and Ovruch that now lies on the border of Belarus, Ukraine and Poland. Their name comes from the Slavic word for forest. Long before them the wetlands held the Neuri of the Milograd culture, and in the first millennium the East Slavic Dregoviches settled the lower Pripyat; their tribal name, from a word meaning swamp, marks them as marsh-dwellers. The Dregoviches had their own prince at Turov, and from the tenth century their lands formed the Principality of Turov and Pinsk, which also took in Drevlian country to the east, passed briefly under the kings of Galicia-Volhynia, and entered the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the fourteenth century. With the Union of Lublin of 1569 the marshland became part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, and the Partitions of Poland in the late eighteenth century assigned it to the Russian Empire. Its isolated wetlands kept the local Ruthenian speech and marshland ways separated from those of the surrounding peoples.
zh: 波列西耶人（又称波列舒克人）是普里皮亚季沼泽的东斯拉夫人，那是环绕平斯克、戈梅利和奥夫鲁奇的大林泽地带，位于今白俄罗斯、乌克兰和波兰交界。他们的名字来自斯拉夫语的“森林”一词。早在他们之前，这片湿地住着米洛格拉德文化的尼如人；一千纪时，东斯拉夫的德列戈维奇人定居普里皮亚季河下游，族名出自意为“沼泽”的词，点明了他们沼泽居民的身份。德列戈维奇人在图罗夫有自己的王公，10世纪起其土地组成图罗夫-平斯克公国，还囊括了东面的德列夫利安人地区，一度臣属加利西亚-沃里尼亚诸王，14世纪并入立陶宛大公国。1569年卢布林联合后，这片沼泽归入波兰立陶宛联邦，18世纪末波兰被瓜分时又划归俄罗斯帝国。闭塞的湿地使当地的鲁塞尼亚方言和沼泽生计长期与周边民族保持区别。

en: The Pomo are a Native American people of Northern California whose ancestral lands stretched from the Pacific coast between Cleone and Duncans Point inland to Clear Lake and the Russian River valley. They were never a single polity but hundreds of independent village communities speaking seven related but mutually unintelligible Pomoan languages, living by hunting, fishing and gathering with acorns as the staple. Pomo women became famous across the world for their basketry, weaving watertight cooking baskets and gift pieces decorated with woodpecker feathers, shell beads and abalone pendants, and Pomo ceremonial life centred on the Kuksu religion with its masked dances and healing rites. Contact came from several directions: the Russian American Company built Fort Ross on their coast in 1812, where the Kashaya Pomo traded and worked, while between 1821 and 1828 Spanish missionaries removed many southern Pomo to Mission San Rafael. A smallpox epidemic spreading from Fort Ross in 1837, on top of earlier cholera and smallpox outbreaks, cut their numbers drastically.
zh: 波莫人是北加利福尼亚的原住民，祖居地从克莱昂与邓肯斯角之间的太平洋海岸一直延伸到克利尔湖和俄罗斯河谷。他们从不是一个统一政权，而是数百个独立的村落社群，讲七种亲属关系相近却互不相通的波莫语族语言，以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，橡子是主食。波莫妇女的编织技艺闻名世界，能织出不漏水的炊煮篮，以及饰有啄木鸟羽毛、贝珠和鲍鱼壳坠饰的礼品篮；他们的仪式生活以库克苏信仰为中心，举行戴面具的舞蹈和治病仪式。接触从多个方向到来：俄美公司于1812年在他们的海岸修建罗斯堡，卡沙亚波莫人在那里贸易和做工；1821—1828年间，西班牙传教士把许多南部波莫人迁往圣拉斐尔传教站。1837年，一场从罗斯堡扩散的天花，加上此前的霍乱和天花疫情，使波莫人口大幅减少。

en: The Pomors, whose name means seasiders, are the Russian maritime people of the White Sea and Barents Sea coasts, descended chiefly from Novgorodian settlers who entered those waters through the Northern Dvina and Onega estuaries from the twelfth century. Their dialect preserves the old Novgorodian speech of the northern Russian frontier. Kholmogory long served as their chief town until Arkhangelsk, founded in 1584, became the window for English and Dutch trade with Muscovy. In flat-bottomed koch ships built for ice, Pomor hunters and traders ranged to Novaya Zemlya, Vaygach and the coasts of Svalbard, where they kept regular hunting stations, and opened the northern sea route into Siberia: the outpost of Pustozersk dates from 1499, and Mangazeya beyond the Yamal Peninsula grew in the early seventeenth century into a fur-and-ivory emporium of fabled wealth, until Tsar Michael closed the route under pain of death and the city withered. Their lives rested on cod and salmon fishing, seal and walrus hunting, salt boiling and the long barter trade with Norwegians in Finnmark, and their voyages blazed the trail for the Russian conquest and settlement of Siberia.
zh: 波莫尔人意为“滨海居民”，是白海与巴伦支海沿岸的俄罗斯航海族群，主要是12世纪起经北德维纳河和奥涅加河河口进入这片水域的诺夫哥罗德移民的后裔，方言里保留着北方边疆的古诺夫哥罗德语特征。霍尔莫戈雷长期是他们的首镇，1584年阿尔汉格尔斯克建立后，后者成为英国、荷兰商人与莫斯科公国贸易的窗口。波莫尔人驾驶专为冰区航行打造的平底“科奇”船，猎人和商队远至新地岛、瓦伊加奇岛和斯瓦尔巴群岛并在那里设立常设猎场，还开辟了通往西伯利亚的北方海路：1499年建立的普斯托泽尔斯克是中途要站，17世纪初亚马尔半岛以东的曼加泽亚更发展成富甲一方的毛皮与海象牙商埠，直到沙皇米哈伊尔以死罪相威胁封闭这条航路，该城才走向衰败。捕鱼（鳕鱼、鲑鱼）、猎海豹与海象、熬盐，以及同芬马克挪威人的长期易货贸易，构成他们的生计；他们的航行也为俄罗斯征服和殖民西伯利亚探出了道路。

en: The Panka, known in history as the Ponca, are the smallest of the five Dhegiha Siouan peoples and speak a language almost identical to Omaha. Their traditions recall a homeland east of the Mississippi from which they were driven, with the other Dhegiha tribes, by the Beaver Wars of the Haudenosaunee. At first European contact they lived at the mouth of the Niobrara River in northern Nebraska, and Le Sueur placed them on the upper Missouri on his map of 1701. In 1789 the fur trader Juan Baptiste Munier opened a post among some eight hundred Ponca at the Niobrara's mouth, but a smallpox epidemic soon reduced them to about two hundred by the time Lewis and Clark passed in 1804. Disaster struck again in 1824 when Lakota warriors ambushed a delegation of thirty Ponca leaders and killed all the chiefs, including the renowned Smoke-maker; only twelve survived. Unlike most Plains nations the Ponca were settled farmers, growing maize and keeping vegetable gardens beside the Missouri.
zh: 潘卡人即史书上的蓬卡人，是德吉哈苏语五大部族中人数最少的一支，所说的语言与奥马哈语几乎相同。据他们的传统，其故地在密西西比河以东，后来与其他德吉哈部族一样，因豪德诺索尼人的海狸战争而被逐走。欧洲人最初接触到他们时，他们居住在内布拉斯加北部尼奥布拉拉河注入密苏里河的河口一带，勒叙厄尔1701年的地图已把他们标在密苏里河上游。1789年，毛皮商人马尼耶在约八百名蓬卡人居住的尼奥布拉拉河口开设贸易站，但随后一场天花使人口锐减，到1804年刘易斯和克拉克经过时只剩约两百人。1824年灾祸再至：拉科塔武士伏击了一支由三十名首领组成的使团，包括著名的造烟者在内的全体酋长遇害，仅十二人生还。与大多数平原部族不同，蓬卡人是定居的农耕者，在密苏里河畔种植玉米、经营菜园。

en: The Pontic Greeks are the Greek-speaking people of Pontus, the mountainous Black Sea coast of northeastern Anatolia centered on Trebizond, Sinope and Samsun. Greeks from the Aegean founded their first colonies there around 700 BC, and the Hellenistic Kingdom of Pontus, famed for King Mithridates' wars against Rome, was annexed as a Roman province in 63 BC. Under Byzantium the region kept its Greek character, but the Seljuk conquests of the eleventh century cut it off from the rest of the Greek world and let the local Pontic dialect develop in isolation. After the Fourth Crusade seized Constantinople in 1204, a branch of the Komnenos family, backed by Georgia, founded the Empire of Trebizond, which in 1337 still ruled the Pontic shore and parts of Crimea as an independent Byzantine successor state, enriched by the Silk Road trade passing through its port. The empire outlived Constantinople itself, finally falling to Sultan Mehmed II in 1461, while its Crimean offshoot, the Principality of Theodoro, held out until 1475. Under Ottoman rule the Pontic Greeks remained Orthodox merchants, miners and peasants along the coast, though communities in the remoter highlands gradually converted to Islam and adopted Turkish.
zh: 本都人是本都地区说希腊语的居民，分布在安纳托利亚东北部濒临黑海的山岳海岸，以特拉比松、锡诺普和萨姆松为中心。来自爱琴海的希腊人约在公元前700年建立了最早的殖民地，以米特拉达梯国王抗击罗马闻名的希腊化本都王国于公元前63年被罗马吞并为行省。拜占庭时期当地保持着希腊特色，但11世纪塞尔柱人的征服使它与希腊语世界其他地区隔绝，本都希腊语方言因而在孤立中独立发展。1204年第四次十字军攻占君士坦丁堡后，科穆宁家族的一支在格鲁吉亚支持下建立特拉比松帝国；1337年时它仍是统治本都海岸和克里米亚部分地区的独立拜占庭后继政权，凭借途经其港口的丝绸之路贸易而富庶。这个帝国比君士坦丁堡本身还长寿，直到1461年才被苏丹穆罕默德二世攻灭，其克里米亚分支狄奥多罗公国则存续到1475年。奥斯曼统治下，本都人作为东正教的商人、矿工和农民留居沿海，但偏远山区的社群逐渐改宗伊斯兰教并改用突厥语。

en: The Popolocas are an Oto-Manguean people of the Tehuacán valley and the dry southern Puebla highlands, in the Tepexi and Tecamachalco country, whose languages form the Popolocan branch closest to Mazatec. Popoloca is a Mexica label for any unintelligible, non-Nahuatl speech, carrying the mocking sense of stutterer, and their ancient city of Tepexi el Viejo long anchored a network of local señoríos. Mexica expansion under Itzcóatl and his successors broke their power: Moctezuma I took Tlacotepec and Tzinacatepec, Ahuitzotl took Acatepec and Caltepec, and Moctezuma II overcame Tehuacán and Tepexi el Viejo, leaving only the lordship of Cuthá under Xopanatl independent while the rest paid tribute in lime, dyed mantles, deer hides and spear-shaft cane. Some Popoloca rulers kept their privileges by aiding the Spanish conquest, and Franciscans built the first convents at Tepeyacac in 1529 and Tecamachalco around 1540.
zh: 波波洛卡人是特瓦坎谷地和普埃布拉南部干旱高地（特佩希与特卡马查尔科一带）的奥托-曼格族群，语言构成与马萨特克语最接近的波波洛卡语支。波波洛卡本是墨西加人对一切听不懂的非纳瓦语的称呼，带有口吃者的嘲弄意味；古城特佩希埃尔维霍曾长期是当地众小邦的核心。墨西加人在伊茨科特尔及其后继者治下扩张，瓦解了他们的势力：蒙特祖马一世夺取特拉科特佩克和齐纳卡特佩克，阿维措特尔夺取阿卡特佩克和卡尔特佩克，蒙特祖马二世又攻灭特瓦坎和特佩希埃尔维霍，只有索帕纳特尔治下的库塔邦保持独立，其余地区则以石灰、染色斗篷、鹿皮和制矛杆用的芦苇纳贡。一些波波洛卡首领借协助西班牙征服保住特权，方济各会随后于1529年在特佩亚卡克、约1540年在特卡马查尔科建起最早的修道院。

en: The Poqom are the Maya peoples speaking the closely related Poqomam and Poqomchi languages of eastern and central Guatemala. Their name goes back to a word meaning the harvesting of beehives, and beekeeping, milpa farming and pottery were their traditional livelihoods. In early times their settlements stretched from the Guatemalan highlands to the Pacific coast of El Salvador, but in the eleventh century migrating Pipil groups overran the easternmost communities, leaving only a few villages behind near the present border. The people then divided into two branches: the Poqomchi in the northern hills of Verapaz, and the Poqomam farther south-east, whose confederacy of villages was centred on the city of Chinautla Viejo. Around 1470 that confederacy was conquered by the expanding K'iche kingdom, whose Kaqchikel vassals from Iximche joined the campaign; when K'iche power weakened the Poqomam briefly recovered their independence, but the Spanish arrived in the early sixteenth century and overcame their scattered chiefdoms one by one. War and newly introduced diseases cut deep into the population, and later mission resettlements and the loss of communal lands confined the survivors to small districts such as Chinautla, Palin and San Luis Jilotepeque.
zh: 波科姆人是说波科曼语和波科姆奇语这两支近亲语言的玛雅民族的合称，分布在危地马拉东部和中部。他们的名字源自意为“割取蜂巢”的词，养蜂、米尔帕耕作和制陶是传统生计。早期他们的聚落从危地马拉高地一直延伸到萨尔瓦多的太平洋海岸，但11世纪皮皮尔人的迁徙浪潮冲垮了最东边的社群，只在今边境附近留下少数村庄。此后这支民族分为两支：波科姆奇人居住在北部的韦拉帕斯山区，波科曼人住在更靠东南的地方，后者的村落联盟以旧奇瑙特拉城为中心。约1470年，这个联盟被正在扩张的基切王国征服，来自伊希姆切的卡克奇克尔附庸也参加了战事；基切势力衰落后，波科曼人一度恢复独立，但西班牙人在16世纪初到来，将他们分散的酋长国各个击破。战争和新传入的疫病使人口大幅减少，此后传教聚落的重编和公有土地的丧失，又把幸存者压缩到奇瑙特拉、帕林和圣路易斯希洛特佩克等小片地区。

en: The Portuguese are the Romance nation of the Atlantic face of Iberia, settled between the Minho and the Algarve in the old Roman provinces of Gallaecia and Lusitania, with Porto, Guimarães and Lisbon as their historic heart. Their land emerged from the Reconquista as the County of Portugal, first chartered in 868; Afonso Henriques proclaimed himself king in 1139, the Algarve was taken from the Moors in 1249, and Lisbon became the capital in 1255. Victory over Castile in 1385 brought the Aviz dynasty to power, and the Treaty of Windsor of 1386 tied Portugal to England in history's longest-lived alliance. Their Galician-Portuguese tongue, shared in the Middle Ages with the cantiga poets of Galicia, became the vehicle of the Age of Discovery: sailors trained by Henry the Navigator took Ceuta in 1415, Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498 and Cabral claimed Brazil in 1500, linking Lisbon to Nagasaki by a chain of fortified trading posts. The disaster of Alcácer Quibir in 1578 cleared the way for the Spanish Iberian Union of 1580, until the restoration of 1640 placed John IV on the throne. The Lisbon earthquake of 1755 destroyed much of the capital, French invasion followed in the Napoleonic Wars, and the loss of Brazil in 1822 ended the first era of the empire.
zh: 葡萄牙人是伊比利亚半岛大西洋沿岸的罗曼民族，聚居在米尼奥河到阿尔加维之间的旧罗马加莱西亚和卢西塔尼亚行省，波尔图、吉马良斯和里斯本是其历史腹地。他们的土地在收复失地运动中形成葡萄牙伯国，最早于868年获得特许状；阿方索·恩里克斯于1139年自立为王，1249年从摩尔人手中夺取阿尔加维，1255年里斯本成为首都。1385年战胜卡斯蒂利亚后，阿维什王朝上台，1386年的《温莎条约》使葡萄牙与英格兰结为历史上存续最久的同盟。他们的加利西亚-葡萄牙语在中世纪与加利西亚的坎蒂加诗人共用，后来成为大航海时代的载体：航海家恩里克培养的水手于1415年攻占休达，迪亚士于1488年绕过好望角，瓦斯科·达伽马于1498年抵达印度，卡布拉尔于1500年宣布占有巴西，一连串设防商站把里斯本与长崎连接起来。1578年阿尔卡塞尔·基比尔的惨败为1580年西班牙主导的伊比利亚联盟扫清了道路，直到1640年复国，若昂四世登位。1755年里斯本大地震摧毁了大半个首都，拿破仑战争期间又遭法国入侵，1822年巴西丧失，帝国的第一阶段告终。

en: The Potiguara are a Tupi-Guarani people of the northeastern Brazilian coast, whose sixteenth-century lands ran from Ceará through Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba to Pernambuco; their name is said to mean shrimp-eaters, from poty for shrimp. Around 1500 they may have numbered some 90,000, and as skilled canoeists and warriors they resisted the Portuguese longer than most Tupi groups, allying with French brazilwood traders in the Potiguara War of 1574 to 1599 against the settlers and their Tabajara rivals. In the following century they switched to the Portuguese side, and their chief António Filipe Camarão, baptized and raised among the colonists, led Potiguara warriors against the Dutch in the Pernambuco insurrection of 1645 to 1649, including the battles of Guararapes, and was rewarded with a noble title and membership in the Order of Christ. Despite epidemics and the loss of most of their territory, Potiguara communities kept a continuous foothold around the Baía da Traição in Paraíba through the colonial centuries and the early empire.
zh: 波蒂瓜拉人是巴西东北沿海的图皮-瓜拉尼族群，16世纪的领地从塞阿拉经北里奥格兰德和帕拉伊巴延伸到伯南布哥；据说其族名由意为虾的“波蒂”派生，意思是“食虾者”。1500年前后他们约有9万人，作为娴熟的独木舟手和战士，他们比大多数图皮族群更久地抵抗葡萄牙人，在1574至1599年的波蒂瓜拉战争中与做巴西木生意的法国商人结盟，对抗殖民者及其塔巴哈拉对手。进入下一世纪后他们转与葡萄牙结盟，酋长安东尼奥·费利佩·卡马朗受洗并在殖民者中长大，率领波蒂瓜拉战士在1645至1649年的伯南布哥起义中（包括瓜拉拉皮斯战役）抗击荷兰人，因此获封贵族头衔并加入基督骑士团。尽管瘟疫流行、领地大半丧失，波蒂瓜拉各社群仍在整个殖民时代和帝国初年牢牢守住帕拉伊巴的特拉桑湾一带。

en: The Powhatan were the leading Algonquian people of Tsenacommacah, the Tidewater country of coastal Virginia, where a score of river tribes lived in palisaded farming towns along the James, York and Rappahannock under local commanders titled werowance, with rank and inheritance passing through the mother’s line. From six inherited nations, including the Pamunkey, Mattaponi and Appamattuck, the paramount chief Wahunsenacawh, known to the English simply as Powhatan, built a confederacy of more than thirty tribes and perhaps fifteen to twenty thousand people, ruling from his capital at Werowocomoco when the Jamestown settlers arrived in 1607. Early contact mixed trade and hostage-taking: John Smith was seized and then released in 1607, and Wahunsenacawh’s daughter Matoaka, called Pocahontas, was captured in 1613 and married the colonist John Rolfe in 1614. After the paramount’s death in 1618 his brother Opechancanough led the great uprisings of 1622 and 1644, which killed hundreds of settlers but ended in his capture and shooting in 1646; the treaty of that year dissolved the confederacy, while measles and smallpox had already carried off at least three quarters of its people. The Treaty of Middle Plantation in 1677, following Bacon’s Rebellion of 1676 and the diplomacy of the Pamunkey queen Cockacoeske, reduced the surviving bands to tributary status on small reservations, and the Powhatan language, preserved mainly in the word lists of John Smith and William Strachey, had fallen silent by the end of the eighteenth century.
zh: 波瓦坦人是弗吉尼亚滨海“潮水之地”岑纳科马卡最主要的阿尔冈昆民族；在詹姆斯河、约克河和拉帕汉诺克河沿岸，数十个河畔部落住在设防的农耕村镇中，由尊号“维罗万斯”的本地首领统辖，等级和继承权沿母系传递。最高首领瓦亨森纳考——英国人径直称他为波瓦坦——从继承来的六个部族（包括帕蒙基、马塔波尼和阿帕马塔克）出发，建立起一个拥有三十多个部族、约一万五千至两万人的联盟，1607年詹姆斯敦殖民者到来时，他正以维罗沃科莫科为首府进行统治。早期接触中贸易与扣押人质并行：约翰·史密斯1607年被俘又获释，瓦亨森纳考的女儿马托阿卡（即波卡洪塔斯）1613年被掳，1614年嫁给殖民者约翰·罗尔夫。1618年最高首领去世后，其弟奥佩坎卡诺领导了1622年和1644年两次大起义，杀死数百名定居者，却以1646年被俘并遭枪杀告终；同年的条约解散了联盟，而麻疹和天花此前已夺去至少四分之三人口。1676年培根叛乱之后，借帕蒙基女酋科卡科埃斯克的斡旋，1677年的《中种植园条约》把幸存各支降为保留地上的纳贡部族；波瓦坦语主要靠约翰·史密斯和威廉·斯特雷奇记录的词汇表留存，到18世纪末已无人使用。

en: The Provençals are the people of Provence, the Mediterranean land between the lower Rhône, the Alps and the Italian border, whose chief towns were Aix-en-Provence, Arles, Avignon and Marseille. Their Romance speech is Occitan, the langue d'oc, in whose Old Occitan form the troubadours composed their lyric poetry from the late eleventh century. The region took its name from the Roman Provincia Romana; after Roman rule, Saracen raiders held a coastal base from 887 until Count William I defeated them at Tourtour in 973. Its medieval counts ruled from Aix, first the Bosonids, then from 1112 the counts of Barcelona and the Crown of Aragon, until in 1246 Charles of Anjou married the heiress Beatrice and tied Provence to the Angevin kings of Naples. From 1309 to 1377 Avignon housed the papal court, and the Black Death of 1348 to 1350 devastated the towns. The last native ruler, Good King René, died in 1480; in 1481 his lands passed to King Louis XI and were incorporated into the French royal domain in 1486. Provence then suffered in the Wars of Religion, notably the massacre of the Vaudois at Mérindol in 1545, while the Great Plague of Marseille of 1720 to 1722 killed some forty thousand people. During the Revolution the old province was split into departments in 1790, and the British-occupied port of Toulon was retaken in 1793 by the young artillery officer Napoleon Bonaparte.
zh: 普罗旺斯人是普罗旺斯地区的居民，这片地中海土地位于罗讷河下游、阿尔卑斯山与意大利边界之间，主要城镇有普罗旺斯地区艾克斯、阿尔勒、阿维尼翁和马赛。他们的罗曼语母语是奥克语，11世纪末起，行吟诗人正是用古奥克语创作抒情诗。地区得名于罗马人的罗马行省；罗马统治崩溃后，萨拉森掠袭者从887年起占据一处沿海据点，直到973年被威廉一世伯爵在图尔图尔击败。中世纪的伯爵们以艾克斯为治所，先是博索尼德王朝，1112年后由巴塞罗那伯爵和阿拉贡联合王国统治；1246年安茹的查理娶女继承人贝亚特丽斯为妻，普罗旺斯遂与安茹家族的那不勒斯诸王连在一起。1309至1377年教廷设在阿维尼翁，1348至1350年的黑死病使各城镇人口锐减。最后一位本地统治者贤王勒内于1480年去世，1481年他的领地传给法王路易十一，1486年正式并入法兰西王室领地。此后普罗旺斯在宗教战争中受难，尤以1545年梅兰多尔的韦尔多派屠杀为甚；1720至1722年的马赛大瘟疫又夺去约四万人的生命。大革命中，旧行省于1790年被划分为若干省，1793年被英军占领的土伦港由年轻的炮兵军官拿破仑·波拿巴收复。

en: The German-speaking Prussian society took shape after the Teutonic Order's Prussian Crusade, launched in the 1230s, broke the resistance of the pagan Old Prussians, a Baltic people. Under the Order's rule the Ostsiedlung brought in thousands of German settlers: towns such as Thorn, Kulm, Elbing and Königsberg were founded or rebuilt under Kulm and Magdeburg town law, and after the Order seized Pomerelia with Danzig in 1308 to 1309, Middle Low German served as the language of urban law, Hanseatic commerce and the Order's administration while the native Prussians were gradually assimilated and their Baltic language died out in the early eighteenth century. Defeat at Grunwald in 1410 began the Order's decline, and the Thirteen Years' War ended with the Second Peace of Thorn in 1466, which placed Danzig and western Prussia under the Polish Crown as Royal Prussia and left the Order's rump state a Polish fief. In 1525 Grand Master Albert of Brandenburg secularised that fief into the Lutheran Duchy of Prussia, the first Protestant state, whose church and schools spread High German over the older Low German speech. The Hohenzollern electors of Brandenburg inherited the duchy in 1618, won full sovereignty in the Treaties of Wehlau and Oliva of 1657 to 1660, and crowned themselves kings in Prussia at Königsberg in 1701; the First Partition of Poland in 1772 brought Royal Prussia and Danzig back under the Prussian crown.
zh: 普鲁士人的德语社会形成于条顿骑士团的普鲁士十字军之后：13世纪30年代骑士团发动远征，击垮了信奉异教的波罗的海民族古普鲁士人。在骑士团统治下，东向移民运动带来大批德意志移民：托伦、海乌姆诺、埃尔宾、柯尼斯堡等城镇依海乌姆诺法和马格德堡法建立或重建；1308至1309年骑士团夺取波美雷利亚和但泽后，中古低地德语成为城市法律、汉萨贸易和骑士团行政的语言，而本地古普鲁士人逐渐被同化，其波罗的海语言到18世纪初消亡。1410年格伦瓦德战败后骑士团由盛转衰，十三年战争以1466年第二次托伦和约告终：但泽和西普鲁士作为王家普鲁士归属波兰王室，骑士团残余国家成为波兰封邑。1525年，团长大阿尔布雷希特将封邑世俗化为路德宗的普鲁士公国，这是第一个新教国家，教会和学校使高地德语逐渐取代旧有的低地德语。1618年勃兰登堡的霍亨索伦选帝侯继承公国，1657至1660年通过韦劳条约和奥利瓦条约取得完全主权，1701年在柯尼斯堡加冕为普鲁士国王；1772年第一次瓜分波兰，王家普鲁士和但泽重归普鲁士王冠。

en: The Pruthenians, better known as the Old Prussians, were a Western Baltic people who held the Baltic coast between the Vistula Lagoon and the Curonian Lagoon, divided into clans such as the Sambians, Natangians, Bartians, Warmians and Pomesanians. Tacitus may have described their forebears as the Aesti in 98 CE, and the traveller Wulfstan recorded their funeral rites in the ninth century. The Polish kings of the tenth century failed to subdue them, and the Prussian Crusade began only in 1230, when Duke Konrad of Masovia called in the Teutonic Order. The Order's network of brick castles brought five of the seven great clans under control within a decade, but the Prussians rose five times: a first revolt in the 1240s and the Great Prussian Uprising of 1260 to 1274, ignited by the Order's disaster at Durbe and led by heroes such as Herkus Monte, nearly swept the invaders away. Resistance ended with the last rising of 1295, after which German and Dutch settlers colonised the conquered lands while Prussian communities survived as islands within the monastic state. In 1525 Grand Master Albert secularised the territory into the Lutheran Duchy of Prussia and had catechisms printed in Old Prussian, but plagues and assimilation wore the language down until it died out in the early eighteenth century, leaving only written texts from which scholars later reconstructed it.
zh: 普鲁赛尼亚人即古普鲁士人，是西波罗的族群，据有维斯瓦潟湖与库尔斯潟湖之间的波罗的海岸，分为桑比亚、纳坦吉亚、巴尔蒂亚、瓦尔米亚、波梅桑尼亚等氏族。塔西佗在98年记载的“埃斯蒂”人可能就是他们的先民，9世纪的旅行者伍尔夫斯坦记录过他们的葬俗。10世纪波兰诸王的征服均告失败，普鲁士十字军迟至1230年才因马佐维亚公爵康拉德召来条顿骑士团而开启。骑士团凭借砖砌城堡网，十年内控制七大氏族中的五个，但普鲁士人先后起义五次：13世纪40年代的第一次起义，以及1260—1274年趁骑士团杜尔贝惨败而起、由赫尔库斯·蒙特等首领领导的“大普鲁士起义”，几乎将侵略者赶下海。最后一次起义于1295年失败，此后德意志和荷兰移民迁入被征服的土地，普鲁士人的聚落则作为孤岛残存于骑士团国家之中。1525年，大团长阿尔伯特将领地世俗化为路德宗的普鲁士公国，并命人印行了古普鲁士语教义问答；但瘟疫与同化不断侵蚀这种语言，到18世纪初它已消亡，只留下书面文本供后世学者重构。

en: The Pubenenses were the farming people of the Pubén valley in southwestern Colombia, on the ground where the Spanish later built Popayán. Tradition recorded by the chronicles brings them up from the Pacific coast about a thousand years before Columbus, and they lived by raised-field agriculture, cotton weaving, domestic and ritual pottery, and goldwork in the form of nose rings, pectorals and armbands. Though described as peaceful, they kept an army and hilltop fortresses, and their neighbors included the Pasto to the south and the Pijao to the northeast. In 1535 the expedition of Pedro de Añasco and Juan de Ampudia fought its way up the Patía River, defeated the cacique Yasgüén and founded Timbío near the Pubenense heartland; Popayán itself was laid out in 1537. Pubenense resistance continued regardless, and in 1541 Ampudia was killed by a spear thrust in a battle on his return to the town.
zh: 普本人是哥伦比亚西南部普本谷地的农耕民族，西班牙人后来兴建的波帕扬城就坐落在他们的土地上。据编年史保存的传说，他们在哥伦布之前约一千年从太平洋海岸迁来，以台田农业、棉织、日用与仪式陶器为生，并擅长打造鼻环、胸饰和臂钏等金器。虽然被形容为性情平和，他们仍保有军队和设于战略要地的山寨，南面与帕斯托人为邻，东北则与皮豪人相接。1535年，佩德罗·德·阿尼亚斯科与胡安·德·安普迪亚的远征军沿帕蒂亚河而上，击败酋长亚斯古恩，在普本腹地附近建立廷比奥；波帕扬本身则于1537年划定建城。普本人的抵抗并未停止，1541年，安普迪亚在返回该城的一场战斗中被长矛刺死。

en: The Pukamuru, called Bracamoros or Pacamuros in Spanish sources, a name meaning painted face, were a loose confederation of Amazonian tribes in the watersheds of the Zamora, Chinchipe and Marañón rivers, on the border of present-day Ecuador and Peru. Among their groups were the Chinchipe, Chirinos, Tabancaras, Bagua, Chamaya and Huambos, who farmed maize, manioc and sweet potatoes in independent villages that the Spanish treated as separate provinces. Inca armies never subdued them; Pedro de Cieza de León records a failed Inca expedition around 1520, and remains of a battle between the two sides were later found at Palanda. Spanish expeditions began in 1536, Juan de Salinas y Loyola took the chief town of Cumbinamá in 1539, and Jaén de Bracamoros was founded in 1549. Forced labour under the encomienda system and disease cut the native population from about 20,000 in 1549 to roughly 1,500 by 1606, and the tribes disappeared as distinct peoples.
zh: 普卡穆鲁人在西班牙文献中被称为布拉卡莫罗人，名字意为“涂花的脸”，是生活在萨莫拉河、钦奇佩河与马拉尼翁河流域、今厄瓜多尔与秘鲁交界处的一支亚马孙部落联盟。其下包括钦奇佩、奇里诺、塔班卡拉、巴瓜、查马亚和万博等部族，各村社种植玉米、木薯和甘薯，西班牙人把它们视为各自独立的“省”。印加军队始终未能征服他们，佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂记载了约1520年的一次失败远征，帕兰达后来还出土了双方交战的遗迹。西班牙人的远征始于1536年，胡安·德·萨利纳斯·伊·洛约拉于1539年攻占重镇昆比纳马，1549年建立哈恩·德·布拉卡莫罗斯。在委托监护制的劳役和疫病打击下，当地土著人口从1549年的约两万人锐减到1606年的约一千五百人，这些部族最终不再作为独立群体存在。

en: The Pumé, whom early Spanish explorers knew by the neighbouring name of Yaruro, are a people of the Venezuelan llanos west of the Orinoco, scattered along the Arauca, Capanaparo, Meta and Apure rivers across seasonally flooded grassland. They call themselves Pumé, meaning real human, and divide into the River Pumé, who keep manioc gardens and more fixed villages on the main waterways, and the Savanna Pumé, mobile hunter-gatherers who move between dry-season and wet-season camps on the open plains. Savanna men hunt armadillos, lizards and larger game with long palm-wood bows, women gather wild tubers, and in the dry season families fish the lagoons with arrows, hooks and fish poison. Their Pumé tongue is a language isolate, already identified as unrelated to any known family in the Jesuit scholar Filippo Gilii's Saggio di storia americana of 1782. The Pumé had encountered Europeans since at least the 1600s, but contact long remained thin, especially for the savanna bands far from the river routes, which allowed their nomadic foraging life and their language to survive the colonial centuries with little change.
zh: 普梅人被早期西班牙探险家以邻族对他们的称呼“雅鲁罗人”之名记载下来，他们是奥里诺科河以西委内瑞拉稀树草原上的族群，散居在阿劳卡河、卡帕纳帕罗河、梅塔河和阿普雷河沿线随季节泛滥的草原地带。他们自称普梅，意为“真正的人”，内部分为两支：沿河普梅人在主要水道边种植木薯、村落较为固定；草原普梅人则是游猎采集者，在开阔平原上的旱季营地和雨季营地之间迁徙。草原男子用长长的棕榈木弓箭猎捕犰狳、蜥蜴和较大的野兽，妇女采集野生块茎，旱季时全家到潟湖用箭、鱼钩和鱼毒捕鱼。他们的普梅语是一门孤立语言，耶稣会学者菲利波·吉利早在1782年的《美洲史论》中就指出它与任何已知语言都没有亲缘关系。普梅人至迟在17世纪已与欧洲人接触，但往来长期稀少，远离河道的草原群体尤其如此，这使他们的游猎生活和语言在整个殖民时代几乎未受触动地保存下来。

en: The Pumi, whose autonyms include Prinmi and Peimi and whom Chinese records called Xifan or Baju, are a Tibeto-Burman highland people spread across the Muli and Lithang country of eastern Kham in southwest Sichuan and the Lanping and Ninglang hills of northwest Yunnan. They trace their descent to ancient Di-Qiang nomads who pastured on the Qinghai-Tibet plateau; pressed by the Qin state, some moved south of the Qionglai ranges before the common era, and in the thirteenth century Pumi groups from the Gongga mountains followed the Mongol armies of Kublai on the 1253 campaign against Dali and settled in northwest Yunnan, exchanging herding for settled farming. They speak Prinmi, a Qiangic Tibeto-Burman language without a true script, though Hangui priests in Muli and Ninglang kept ritual pictographs and briefly wrote the language in Tibetan letters. Their religion, led by Hangui priests, joins the old Dingba ancestor and mountain-god cult to Gelugpa and Kagyu Tibetan Buddhism, while villages around Yongning share the matrilineal Azhu family system of their Mosuo neighbours.
zh: 普米人自称普英米、普日米或培米，汉文史书称西番、巴苴，是藏缅语族的高原民族，分布在四川西南部康区东部的木里、理塘一带与云南西北的兰坪、宁蒗山地。他们源出青藏高原游牧的古氐羌人，因与秦国争战失利，部分先民在公元前即南迁到邛崃山以西；13世纪，贡嘎岭一带的普米人随忽必烈1253年征大理的蒙古军南下，在滇西北定居，由畜牧转为农耕。普米语属藏缅语族羌语支，没有正式文字，木里、宁蒗的韩规祭司保留着记载仪式的图画文字，当地还曾短暂用藏文拼写普米语。他们的信仰由韩规祭司主持，将古老的丁巴教祖先与山神崇拜同格鲁派、噶举派藏传佛教合为一体；永宁一带的村寨则与相邻的摩梭人一样实行母系的阿注家庭制度。

en: The Punan, or Punan Bah, are a Dayak people of Sarawak and the adjoining Kalimantan interior, distinct from the similarly named semi-nomadic Penan. They are thought to have been among the earliest inhabitants of central Borneo, holding the Rajang and Balui river country before later arrivals. Settled rather than wandering, they lived in longhouses called lovuk, grew hill padi by slash-and-burn alongside cassava and taro, and hunted wild boar and gathered forest produce; their society was ranked into aristocrats, commoners and slaves, and their dead nobles were placed in hut-like tombs atop tall carved poles called kelirieng. They belong to the Kajang linguistic cluster and traditionally followed the animist Besavik faith. By the early 1800s the influx of Kayan settlers and then of warlike Iban into the Rajang basin pressed the Punan back into the remoter Kakus and Kemena valleys.
zh: 普南人又称普南巴人，是沙捞越及毗邻加里曼丹内陆的达雅族群，与名字相近、半游牧的本南人并非同一群体。他们被认为是婆罗洲中部最早的居民之一，在后来者之前就占据着拉让江与巴鲁伊河流域。普南人定居而不游荡，住在名为“洛武”的长屋里，刀耕火种旱稻，兼种木薯和芋头等作物，同时猎取野猪、采集林产；社会分为贵族、平民和奴隶三个等级，贵族死者不下葬，而是安放进名为“凯利陵”的雕刻高柱顶端的小屋式陵墓中。他们属于卡章语群，传统上信奉万物有灵的贝萨维克信仰。到19世纪初，随着卡扬移民涌入、好战的伊班人继而进入拉让江流域，普南人被挤压到更偏远的卡库斯河谷与克米纳河谷。

en: The Punjabis are the Indo-Aryan people of the Punjab, the land of five rivers, the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Sutlej and Beas, now divided between northwestern India and eastern Pakistan. Their language, Punjabi, descends from the regional Prakrits; its earliest writings come from Nath yogis of the Pothohar plateau in the ninth century, and it carries the verse of Baba Farid. Unusual among Indo-Aryan tongues, Punjabi is a tonal language, written in the Gurmukhi script in the east and the Perso-Arabic Shahmukhi script in the west. In 1337 the Punjab was a province of the Delhi Sultanate, whose fourteenth-century governors already used its Persian name of five waters; in the fifteenth century the Langah sultans held the south around Multan. The Mughal conquest of 1526 made Lahore one of the greatest cities of the empire, and it was in central Punjab that Guru Nanak founded Sikhism during the sixteenth century. As Mughal power collapsed in the eighteenth century the countryside fell to rival Sikh warrior bands called misls, until Ranjit Singh united them and, taking Lahore in 1799, built the Sikh Empire over most of the region.
zh: 旁遮普人是旁遮普地区的印度—雅利安人，旁遮普意为五河之地，指杰赫勒姆河、杰纳布河、拉维河、萨特莱杰河和比亚斯河，这片土地今天分属印度西北部和巴基斯坦东部。他们的旁遮普语由当地俗语演化而来，9世纪波托哈尔高原的纳特瑜伽行者留下了最早文字，巴巴·法里德的诗篇也以它流传；它是少见的声调语言，在印度—雅利安语中颇为特殊，东部用古木基字母、西部用波斯—阿拉伯系统的沙穆基字母书写。1337年，旁遮普是德里苏丹国的一省，这个意为五河的波斯语名称在14世纪已为苏丹国官员所用；15世纪，朗加苏丹国统治着以木尔坦为中心的南部。1526年莫卧儿征服后，拉合尔成为帝国最大的城市之一；16世纪，古鲁·那纳克在中旁遮普创立锡克教。18世纪莫卧儿统治崩溃，乡村落入彼此争战的锡克军事团伙米斯尔手中，最后兰吉特·辛格将它们统一，于1799年夺取拉合尔，在旁遮普大部建立锡克帝国。

en: The Purduna, or Burduna, were an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara region of Western Australia, whose country lay between the Ashburton and Gascoyne Rivers, around the Nyang, Maroonah, Yannarie and Lyndon areas. Their language belonged to the Kanyara group alongside Thalanyji and Bayungu, sharing sixty to seventy per cent of its vocabulary with them, though sound changes such as the lenition of p and k to w set Burduna apart from its sister tongues. Like other Kanyara peoples they lived by hunting and gathering across this arid river-country, moving between permanent waters and seasonal food grounds.
zh: 珀杜纳人又称布尔杜纳人，是西澳大利亚皮尔巴拉地区的原住民，其传统领地在阿什伯顿河与加斯科因河之间，包括尼昂、马鲁纳、亚纳里和林登一带。他们的语言属于卡尼亚拉语群，与塔拉尼吉语、巴永古语有六七成词汇相通，但一系列语音演变（如双唇塞音和软腭塞音软化为半元音）使布尔杜纳语区别于同语群的其他语言。与其他卡尼亚拉族群一样，他们在这片干旱的河谷地带以狩猎采集为生，在固定水源和季节性食场之间迁徙。

en: The Purépecha are the Indigenous people of the Michoacán highlands of western Mexico, farmers and fishermen of the lake basins around Pátzcuaro and Cuitzeo, whom the Spanish later called Tarascans from a word in their tongue meaning in-law. Their language, Purépecha, is an isolate unrelated to Nahuatl and the other tongues of Mesoamerica, matching a culture that stood apart from its neighbours: Purépecha artisans worked copper and bronze into tools and weapons, built T-shaped step pyramids and crafted feather mosaics of hummingbird plumage. Around 1300 the chief Tariácuri began uniting the rival communities around Lake Pátzcuaro, placing his sons Hiripan and Tangáxuan over Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan; by his death around 1350 his lineage controlled the whole lake basin, and later kings, bearing the title irecha or cazonci, made Tzintzuntzan the capital of a centralized tributary kingdom. Under Tzitzipandáquare the realm reached the Pacific at Zacatula and the Toluca valley in 1460, but its defining struggle was with the Aztec Empire: Axayacatl's invasion of the 1470s was beaten back, the frontier was fortified at Cutzamala, and the Aztecs never succeeded in conquering Purépecha lands. When smallpox and news of the fall of Tenochtitlan reached Michoacán, Tangaxuan II submitted to Spain in 1525, but Nuño de Guzmán's invasion of 1530 sacked the kingdom and executed its king, after which Vasco de Quiroga built the colonial order of Michoacán from 1533.
zh: 普雷佩查人是墨西哥西部米却肯高地的原住民，在帕茨夸罗湖和奎采奥湖周围的湖盆务农捕鱼；西班牙人后来据其语言中意为姻亲的词称他们为塔拉斯科人。他们的普雷佩查语是与纳瓦特尔语及中美洲其他语言都无亲缘关系的孤立语言，其文化也与邻邦迥异：工匠把铜和青铜打造成工具与武器，修筑T形阶梯金字塔，还用蜂鸟羽毛制作羽毛镶嵌画。约1300年，首领塔里亚库里着手统一帕茨夸罗湖周边相互敌对的群落，把儿子伊里潘和坦加克斯安分封为伊瓦齐奥和钦聪灿的领主；到他约1350年去世时，其家族已控制整个湖盆，此后历代国王——称号为伊雷查，西班牙人译作卡松西——以钦聪灿为都，建立起集权的朝贡王国。1460年，齐齐潘达夸雷在位时王国扩张到太平洋沿岸的萨卡特拉和托卢卡河谷，而其命运中最关键的较量是与阿兹特克帝国的战争：1470年代阿兹特克君主阿哈亚卡特尔的入侵被击退，普雷佩查人在库察马拉一线加固边防，阿兹特克人始终未能征服其土地。当天花与特诺奇蒂特兰陷落的消息传到米却肯，坦加克斯安二世于1525年向西班牙称臣，但1530年努尼奥·德·古斯曼的入侵洗劫了王国并处死国王，巴斯科·德·基罗加随后自1533年起在米却肯建立殖民秩序。

en: The Puri, also called the Coroado, are an Indigenous people of southeastern Brazil whose traditional lands covered the basin of the Paraíba do Sul River together with stretches of the Rio Grande and Doce rivers, spanning the region of the present states of Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo and São Paulo. They lived in small forest bands, combining hunting and gathering with shifting farming, and spoke a language once grouped with Macro-Jê but now regarded as isolated. The Portuguese conquest of the interior dispossessed them of territory that became the economic heartland of colonial Brazil, and during the 1600s many bands withdrew northward down the Paraíba do Sul to its lower tributaries, the Pomba, Negro and Muriaé rivers, while others were settled in mission villages and put to work on farms and in the mines. Through the 1700s Puri groups kept appearing in frontier records as raiders, porters and mission Indians, their numbers worn down by disease, enslavement and assimilation, so that by the early 1800s their separate language and identity were already in retreat.
zh: 普里人又称科罗阿多人，是巴西东南部的原住民，传统领地覆盖帕拉伊巴河流域以及格兰德河与多塞河的部分地带，横跨里约热内卢、米纳斯吉拉斯、圣埃斯皮里图和圣保罗四州一带。他们以森林中的小群体为生，游猎采集之外兼事轮垦农业，所说的语言曾被归入大热语系，学界多将其视为孤立语言。葡萄牙人征服内陆后，他们被逐出这片后来成为殖民地巴西经济心脏的土地；17世纪时，许多群体沿帕拉伊巴河北迁，退入该河下游的蓬巴河、内格罗河和穆里亚埃河支流一带，另一些人则被安置在传教村，为农庄和矿山劳作。整个18世纪，普里群体作为袭扰者、挑夫和传教区印第安人不断出现在边疆记录中，人口因疾病、奴役和同化而持续损耗，到19世纪初，其独立的语言与身份已走向衰微。

en: The Puruborá, also called Migueleno or Kuyubi, are a small Indigenous people of Rondônia in western Brazil, living around the headwaters of the São Miguel River, a right-bank tributary of the Guaporé, near Costa Marques. They speak Puruborá, a Tupian language, and traditionally followed animist beliefs in the forests of the Guaporé valley.
zh: 普鲁博拉人又称米格尔诺人或库尤比人，是巴西西部朗多尼亚州的小型原住民族群，住在瓜波雷河右岸支流圣米格尔河源头一带、科斯塔马克斯附近。他们使用的普鲁博拉语属图皮语族，传统上在瓜波雷河谷的丛林中信奉万物有灵信仰。

en: The Puruhá were a cluster of highland chiefdoms in central Ecuador, across Chimborazo, Bolívar and Tungurahua, whose fertile valleys had supported farming villages and guinea-pig husbandry since the Integration period; their Elenpata ceramic phase, flourishing from about 800, ranks as their classical age. Each curaca ruled his own people, but in emergencies the chiefs met in a common assembly under a senior king, and succession passed from father to son. Their ritual life centred on the lightning god Catequil, the mythic serpent Pini and the snow-capped Chimborazo, served by jambiri shamans. The Incas conquered them under Huayna Capac, and tradition makes Paccha Duchicela of the ruling Duchicela lineage the Inca's wife and the possible mother of Atahualpa. Epidemic disease cut the population sharply after the Spanish takeover of the 1530s, and the Puruhá language, known only from fragmentary records and grouped with Cañari in the unclassified Cañar-Puruhá family, had nearly vanished by the early 1700s as Kichwa spread through the missions and estates.
zh: 普鲁哈人是厄瓜多尔中部钦博拉索、玻利瓦尔和通古拉瓦一带的高原酋邦群；自整合时期起，肥沃的河谷里就分布着农耕村落，饲养豚鼠，约800年起兴盛的埃伦帕塔陶器阶段是其古典时代。各酋邦的库拉卡各自治民，遇有大事则由众酋长在大会上共议，推一位大王主持，王位父子相传。他们的信仰围绕雷神卡特基尔、神蛇皮尼和积雪的钦博拉索山展开，由詹比里巫师主持仪式。印加王瓦伊纳·卡帕克将其征服，相传统治家族杜奇塞拉氏的帕查·杜奇塞拉被纳为王妃，可能就是阿塔瓦尔帕的生母。16世纪30年代西班牙人接管后，疫病使人口锐减；普鲁哈语仅存零星记录，与佳纳利语同归系属不明的佳纳利—普鲁哈语群，到18世纪初已近乎消亡，基切瓦语随着传教和庄园扩张普及开来。

en: The Purun awqa, better known to Spanish chronicles as the Promaucae, were Mapudungun-speaking farmers of central Chile who held the valleys between the Maipo and Maule rivers, including the valley of Rancagua. Their name is Quechua for wild enemy, the label the Inca gave to peoples beyond their rule, while the Mapuche counted them among the Pikunche, the people of the north. They irrigated their fields, made pottery, raised the hillfort of La Compañía and built a rope suspension bridge over the Cachapoal River. Late in the fifteenth century they and their allies the Antalli, Pincu and Cauqui formed an army of twenty thousand men and met the Inca army of Túpac Inca Yupanqui in the Battle of the Maule, a three-day struggle without a victor that nevertheless fixed the southern edge of the Inca Empire. They withstood Pedro de Valdivia's conquest for three years before being overrun in 1544, and in 1557 a thousand of their warriors fought beside Lautaro at Peteroa, where the Spaniards surprised and destroyed his camp. Encomiendas, planned Indian towns and intermarriage then dissolved their separate identity over the colonial centuries.
zh: 普鲁纳瓦卡人在西班牙编年史中多称普罗马乌卡人，是智利中部讲马普敦贡语的农耕族群，占据迈波河与马乌莱河之间的谷地，包括兰卡瓜谷地。其名来自克丘亚语，意为野蛮的敌人，本是印加人对帝国治外各族的称呼；马普切人则把他们归入皮昆切人，即北方人。他们引水灌溉农田、烧制陶器，筑起拉孔帕尼亚山堡，并在卡查波阿尔河上架设藤索吊桥。15世纪末，他们与安塔利、平库、考基等盟部组成两万人的军队，在马乌莱河战役迎战图帕克·尤潘基的印加大军；这场三天的恶战没有胜者，却划定了印加帝国的南界。他们抵抗佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚的征服达三年，1544年终被压服；1557年，上千名普鲁纳瓦卡战士在佩特罗阿与劳塔罗并肩据守，营地遭西班牙人突袭而覆没。此后在委托监护制、印第安人规划村镇和通婚的作用下，他们独立的族群认同在殖民时代逐渐消融。

en: The Putún, generally identified with the Chontal Maya who call themselves the Yokot'an, are a Maya people of the swampy Gulf coast in Tabasco, centered on the deltas of the Usumacinta and Grijalva rivers and the Laguna de Términos. Life on the waterways made them canoe-borne merchants and seafarers; in the Terminal Classic and Postclassic they controlled river and coastal trade routes around the Yucatán peninsula, running from the Laguna de Términos as far south as the Sula valley in Honduras. Their chief towns were Potonchán at the mouth of the Grijalva and Itzamkanac on the Candelaria river, capital of the Acalan province, while other Putún lordships included Chakán Putún and Chactemal. After the Classic Maya collapse their migrations carried them across Yucatán, and some scholars link them to the Itza who built Chichén Itzá and Mayapán. Juan de Grijalva met their warriors in 1518, and in 1519 Hernán Cortés landed at Potonchán, where the chief Tabscoob gave him the woman later known as La Malinche and the local lords became the first native vassals of New Spain.
zh: 普屯人通常被等同于春塔尔玛雅人（自称约科坦人），是塔瓦斯科沼泽化墨西哥湾沿岸的玛雅族群，聚居于乌苏马辛塔河、格里哈尔瓦河三角洲和特尔米诺斯潟湖一带。水乡生活使他们成为操独木舟的商人和航海者；在古典期末期和后古典期，他们控制着尤卡坦半岛周围的内河与沿海商路，北起特尔米诺斯潟湖，向南远达洪都拉斯的苏拉谷地。其主要城镇有格里哈尔瓦河口的波通昌和坎德拉里亚河畔的伊察姆卡纳克（阿卡拉省的首府），查坎普屯、查克特马尔等酋邦也出自普屯人。古典期玛雅崩溃后，他们的迁徙足迹遍及尤卡坦，部分学者认为他们与后来兴建奇琴伊察和玛雅潘的伊察人同源。1518年胡安·德·格里哈尔瓦曾与他们的武士交战；1519年埃尔南·科尔特斯在波通昌登陆，酋长塔布斯库布将后来被称为拉·马林切的女子赠予他，当地首领也成为新西班牙最早臣服的土著领主。

en:
The Pyemmairreneri are the Pyemmairrener nation of Tasmania's north-eastern corner, the country behind Cape Portland, which they called Tebrakunna, stretching from the Ringarooma coast and the Pipers River to the Ben Lomond plateau, known to them as turapina. Clans including the Trawlwoolway of the coast and the Plangermaireener of the highlands spoke the Northeastern Tasmanian tongue recorded as Pyemmairre, and followed a seasonal round that kept them near the warmer coast in winter and on the alpine plateau in summer, hunting kangaroos, taking seals and muttonbirds on the offshore rocks and gathering the eggs of swans and waterfowl.

Matthew Flinders and George Bass named Cape Portland during their circumnavigation of 1798, and in 1804 Colonel William Paterson planted the first northern settlement at Port Dalrymple, opening the Tamar valley to seizure. During the Black War the Trawlwoolway chief Mannalargenna led guerrilla raids on the runs, and in 1829 freed four women and a boy held for a year in John Batman's house; he later joined George Robinson's missions as a guide, but the promise that he would never be exiled was broken, and he died at the Wybalenna establishment on Flinders Island in 1835.
zh:
皮艾梅伦纳人即塔斯马尼亚东北角的皮艾梅伦纳民族，土地位于他们称作特布拉昆纳的波特兰角后方，从林加鲁马海岸和派珀斯河一直延伸到他们称为图拉皮纳的本洛蒙德高原。沿海的特劳尔伍威氏族、高地的普兰杰梅雷纳氏族等所说的东北塔斯马尼亚语言被记录为皮艾梅雷语；他们随季节迁徙，冬天留在较温暖的海边，夏天登上高山高原，猎取袋鼠，在近海礁石上捕捉海豹和鹱鸟，并采集天鹅与水禽的蛋。

1798年马修·弗林德斯与乔治·巴斯环岛航行时命名了波特兰角；1804年威廉·佩特森上校在达尔林普尔港建立北方第一个定居点，塔马河谷从此遭人侵夺。黑色战争期间，特劳尔伍威酋长曼纳兰根纳率队对牧场发动游击战，并于1829年从约翰·巴特曼家中救出被关押一年的四名妇女和一名男孩；他后来担任向导加入乔治·罗宾逊的使命，但永不流放的承诺未被兑现，最终于1835年在弗林德斯岛的怀巴伦纳居留地离世。

en: The Q'anjob'al are a Maya people of the Sierra de los Cuchumatanes in the Guatemalan department of Huehuetenango, with communities extending across the border into Chiapas; their chief towns include Santa Eulalia, called Jolom Konob in their own language, San Pedro Soloma and San Miguel Acatán. Q'anjob'al belongs, with Chuj, Akatek and Jakaltek, to the conservative Q'anjobalan branch of the Mayan family. Their own tradition tells of ancestors moving up from the Chiapas lowlands into the high mountains, where ancient ceremonial sites predate the Spanish arrival. In 1525 Pedro de Alvarado's expedition, marching from Guatemala through Acala Ch'ol country, met fierce resistance at Tecpan Puyumatlan, the stronghold that became Santa Eulalia, and Gonzalo de Alvarado reported heavy losses among the Spaniards. Through much of the seventeenth century Q'anjob'al towns such as Santa Eulalia were exposed to raids by the independent Lakandon Ch'ol, until colonial garrisons were installed to protect the frontier.
zh: 坎霍瓦尔人是危地马拉韦韦特南戈省库丘马塔内斯山脉的玛雅族群，部分村落越过边界伸入墨西哥恰帕斯；主要城镇有本族语称霍洛姆科诺布的圣欧拉里亚、圣佩德罗索洛马和圣米格尔阿卡特兰。坎霍瓦尔语与丘赫语、阿卡泰克语、哈卡尔特克语同属玛雅语系中保守的坎霍瓦尔语支。按他们自己的传说，先祖从恰帕斯低地迁入高山，当地古老的祭祀遗址远早于西班牙人的到来。1525年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多的远征队从危地马拉取道阿卡拉乔尔人之地北上，在后来成为圣欧拉里亚的要塞特克潘·普尤马特兰遭到顽强抵抗，贡萨洛·德·阿尔瓦拉多记录称西班牙人损失惨重。整个17世纪，圣欧拉里亚等坎霍瓦尔城镇还不断受到独立的拉坎东乔尔人袭扰，直到殖民当局驻军守护这条边防线。

en: The Qashqai are a confederation of Oghuz Turkic tribes in southern Persia, speaking the Qashqai tongue they call Turki alongside Persian. Turkic pastoralists began entering Iran from Central Asia in the eleventh and twelfth centuries, and Qashqai tradition holds that their ancestors came with the Mongol armies of the thirteenth century, dwelt around Ardabil in the Caucasus as clans of the Aq Qoyunlu, or White Sheep Turkoman, and were moved to the province of Fars after 1501, when Shah Ismail founded the Safavid state and charged them with guarding the Persian Gulf coast against the Portuguese. They are organized into five principal tribes, the Amale, Dere-Shorlu, Kashkollu, Shishbeyli and Eymur, under their own ilkhan. Most lived as nomadic herders, driving sheep and goats twice a year between the summer yailaq pastures of the high Zagros north of Shiraz and the warm qishlaq winter grounds around Firuzabad and Kazerun, the largest regular migration of any Persian tribe; their women's carpets and woven bags became prized across the region. In the Qajar era the confederation grew into one of the great tribal powers of southern Persia.
zh: 卡什加人是波斯南部的乌古斯突厥部落联盟，操本族语卡什加语（他们自称突厥语），同时使用波斯语。突厥牧民从11、12世纪起由中亚进入伊朗；卡什加人的传统称，其先祖随13世纪的蒙古军队而来，作为白羊王朝（白羊突厥蛮）的氏族居住在高加索的阿尔达比勒一带，1501年沙阿·伊斯玛仪建立萨法维国家后，命他们守卫波斯湾海岸、抵御葡萄牙人，他们于是南迁至法尔斯行省。他们分为阿马莱、德雷肖尔卢、卡什科卢、希什贝利和埃穆尔五大部落，由本族的伊尔汗统领。多数人以游牧为生，每年两度驱赶羊群往返于设拉子以北扎格罗斯高山的夏季牧场亚伊拉克，与菲鲁扎巴德、卡泽伦一带温暖的冬季牧场克什拉克之间，其定期迁徙规模为波斯诸部之最；卡什加妇女编织的地毯和织袋在各地备受珍视。到卡扎尔王朝时代，这个联盟已成为波斯南部最强大的部落势力之一。

en: The Kaifeng Jews are the isolated Jewish community that took root in the Song capital of Kaifeng, in Henan, probably formed from Persian Jewish merchants who travelled the Silk Road and married Chinese women; a Hebrew-letter Persian document found at Dunhuang in 718 and the Arab geographer ibn Khordadbeh's mention of Radhanite traders in China around 870 attest to this early traffic. Their synagogue, the Qingzhensi, was built in 1163, and the four stelae they erected between 1489 and 1679 record the community's history. Of the at least seven Jewish communities known in eleventh-century Chinese ports, only inland Kaifeng survived, the coastal ones vanishing in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Ming laws barring endogamy pushed the seven Jewish clans into widespread marriage with Han neighbours, and Chinese customs such as foot binding and an ancestral hall spread beside the synagogue even as the Sabbath and the festivals were kept. By the late Ming the community numbered perhaps four thousand, but the Kaifeng flood of 1642 destroyed the synagogue and killed some three thousand Jews, after which the clans joined to restore the thirteen Torah scrolls. In 1605 the examiner Ai Tian told Matteo Ricci in Beijing that his people called themselves men of Israel and were known to their neighbours as the sect that plucks the sinews. Cut off from world Jewry and lacking rabbis, the community's distinct practices had largely faded by the nineteenth century.
zh: 开封犹太人是在宋代都城河南开封扎根的孤立犹太社群，大概由沿丝绸之路而来、娶中国女子为妻的波斯犹太商人形成：敦煌出土的718年希伯来字母波斯文文书，以及阿拉伯地理学家伊本·胡尔达兹比赫约870年提到拉达尼商人已在中国活动，都说明犹太人来华之早。他们的会堂名为清真寺，建于1163年，1489至1679年间所立的四通碑刻记录了社群的来历。11世纪中国各港口已知至少有七个犹太社群，但15至16世纪沿海社群相继消失，唯有地处内陆的开封存续下来。明代禁止色目人内部通婚的法令，促使分属七姓的犹太人普遍与汉族邻里通婚，缠足、祖堂等中式风俗随之进入会堂之侧，而安息日和各节期仍被持守。晚明时其人口或有四千，但1642年开封洪水冲毁会堂，约三千犹太人遇难，事后各姓合力修复了十三部《托拉》经卷。1605年，举人艾田在北京告诉利玛窦，他的族人自称一赐乐业人，邻人则称他们为挑筋教。由于与外界犹太人隔绝、又没有拉比，到19世纪时，该社群独特的宗教仪轨已大体消散。

en: The Qeqchi are a Maya people whose pre-Hispanic homeland was the rainy hill country of central Guatemala, around the later provinces of Alta and Baja Verapaz, a region then called Tezulutlan, the land of war. Their own traditions recall a long migration from central Mexico into the Guatemalan highlands, where they settled as maize farmers under their own kings and laws. Because the population lived in scattered towns rather than one strong centre, the Spanish, who began the conquest of Guatemala in the 1520s, found them unusually difficult to subdue. Bartolome de las Casas was entrusted with a peaceful conversion of the region, and Dominican missionaries did establish churches and gather villages, but only part of the people accepted church rule, and many communities retreated into the forests rather than submit. Colonial plantations and slave raids then pressed hard on those who remained, and over the centuries Qeqchi families migrated outward into the Peten lowlands, the Caribbean coast and, eventually, southern Belize and Chiapas, making their language the most widely dispersed of all Mayan tongues. Their traditional religion centred on the Tzuultaq'a, the mountain and valley spirits who dwelt in caves and watched over rain, crops and game.
zh: 凯克奇人是玛雅人的一支，其史前时代的故土在危地马拉中部多雨的丘陵地带，即后来的上韦拉帕斯和下韦拉帕斯一带，当时这片地区称特苏卢特兰，意为“战争之地”。他们自己的传说讲述了一次从墨西哥中部迁往危地马拉高地的漫长迁徙，此后他们在君王和自己的法律治理下定居下来，以种植玉米为生。由于人口散居在众多村镇而没有一个强大的中心，16世纪20年代开始征服危地马拉的西班牙人发现他们异常难以制服。巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯受命对这一地区进行和平传教，多明我会修士确实建起教堂并聚集村落，但只有一部分人接受教会管辖，许多社群退入森林拒不臣服。随后，殖民地种植园和掳奴袭击又重压在留下来的人身上，几个世纪里，凯克奇人的家庭不断向外迁徙，进入佩滕低地、加勒比海岸，并最终到达伯利兹南部和恰帕斯，使他们的语言成为分布最广的玛雅语。他们的传统宗教以“图尔塔卡”为核心，那是栖身洞穴、司掌雨水、庄稼和猎物的山川谷地之神。

en: The Qhara Qhara, rendered cara-cara in early Spanish accounts, are an Aymara-speaking people of the southern Bolivian highlands, whose ayllus held the country around present-day Potosí. Before the Inca expansion their confederation with the Charca had its capital at Sacaca. In the late fifteenth century the armies of the Inca Túpac Yupanqui overran the region, and the Qhara Qhara became subjects of the Inca Empire. In 1538 they joined the Yampara and Charca in allying with Gonzalo Pizarro's Spaniards, and guides from these peoples revealed the silver deposits of Porco; the Cerro Rico of Potosí rose within their lands. Under Spanish rule their communities were repeatedly called on to supply Indians for the Potosí silver mines.
zh: 卡拉卡拉人在早期西班牙文献中写作卡拉-卡拉，是玻利维亚南部高原讲艾马拉语的族群，其村社占据着今波托西一带的土地。在印加扩张之前，他们与查尔卡斯人组成的联盟以萨卡卡为都城。15世纪末，印加王图帕克·尤潘基的军队攻占这一地区，卡拉卡拉人成为印加帝国的属民。1538年，他们与扬帕拉人、查尔卡斯人一同投靠贡萨洛·皮萨罗率领的西班牙人，这些族群的向导指出了波尔科的银矿，而波托西里科山正矗立在他们的土地上。西班牙统治时期，他们的村社不断被征发劳力送往波托西银矿。

en: The Qín culture is the people of Guanzhong, the Wei River plain within the mountain passes of central Shaanxi, together with the adjoining loess lands of southern Shanxi and eastern Gansu. This was the heartland of the state of Qin, whose fourth-century BCE reforms made it the strongest of the Warring States and whose ruler took the title Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor, in 221 BCE; the Han and Tang dynasties afterwards kept their capitals at Chang'an in the same plain. The Ming captured the region in 1369, gave its chief city the name Xi'an and made it the seat of Shaanxi province behind a new city wall raised in 1370. On 23 January 1556 the deadliest earthquake in recorded history struck Huaxian: some 100,000 people died at once and the registered population fell by 830,000 through famine, plague and flight. In 1644 Li Zicheng proclaimed his Shun dynasty at Xi'an before marching on Beijing, and Qing armies entered the plain the next year. Its Guanzhong speech is a branch of Central Plains Mandarin.
zh: 秦文化的主体是关中人，即陕西中部群山关隘之内的渭河平原居民，也包括相邻的晋南和陇东黄土高原居民。这里是秦国的根本之地：公元前4世纪的变法使秦国成为战国最强，公元前221年其君主称秦始皇，建立第一个统一王朝；此后汉朝、唐朝都在这片平原上的长安建都。1369年，明军攻取此地，将主城定名西安，立为陕西省会，1370年又筑起新的城墙。1556年1月23日，有记录以来死亡最多的华县大地震发生：约十万人当场遇难，加上饥荒、瘟疫和流亡，在册人口减少八十三万。1644年，李自成在西安建立大顺政权，随即进军北京；次年清军进入关中。当地的关中话属于中原官话。

en: The Qióng are the Han Chinese people of Hainan who speak Qiongzhou speech, also called Hainanese, a Min variety known in Chinese dialectology as the Qiong–Wen group. Its heartland is the coastal arc of northern and eastern Hainan around Qiongshan and Wenchang, whose speech is traditionally the prestige form. Their language descends from the Southern Min dialects of Fujian: refugees from the wars that ended the Song in 1279 moved south through the Chaoshan plains and the Leizhou Peninsula into Hainan, and long contact with the island's indigenous Li peoples and with official Mandarin so reshaped its sounds that Hainanese is no longer mutually intelligible with the Hokkien of Quanzhou and Zhangzhou, having developed implosive initials unknown in mainstream Min. The Tang-dynasty prefecture of Qiongzhou, centered on Qiongshan, gives the culture its name. Under the Ming and Qing the island was administered as part of Guangdong, and Hainanese traders and settlers carried their dialect to the ports of Southeast Asia.
zh: 琼人是说琼州话（又称海南话）的海南岛汉族居民，琼州话在汉语方言学上称琼文片，属闽语一支，核心分布在海南岛北部和东部沿海的琼山、文昌一带，文昌话向来看作其代表口音。它的祖语是福建的闽南话：1279年宋亡之际的战乱中，大批闽南人沿潮汕平原、雷州半岛南迁入岛，长期受岛上黎族等土著语言和中原官话影响，音韵大变，以至与泉州、漳州的闽南话无法互通，还发展出主流闽语没有的内爆音声母。琼人得名于唐代设在琼山的琼州；明清时期海南岛归广东省管辖，琼州商人与移民也把这种方言带到了东南亚各港埠。

en: Qiwu covers the south-western branches of Hui Chinese, taking its name from Qimen and Wuyuan, two counties of the historical Huizhou Prefecture on the mountain border between Anhui and Jiangxi. The region was opened up under the Tang dynasty, when Wuyuan was established in 740 and Qimen in 766. Its speech comprises the Xiu-Yi branch, whose leading variety is the dialect of Tunxi in Xiuning county, and the Qi-De branch spoken around Qimen and across the Jiangxi border in Fuliang and Dexing; the latter carries heavy influence from the surrounding Gan languages. Like other Hui dialects it varies sharply from one valley to the next. During the Ming and Qing dynasties Huizhou merchants from these counties travelled widely and kept their local speech alive in merchant communities far from home.
zh: 祁婺涵盖徽语西南部的几支方言，得名于地处安徽、江西两省山界上的古徽州府属县祁门与婺源。这一带在唐代得到开发，婺源于740年建县，祁门于766年建县。当地话分为两支：休黟片以休宁县屯溪话为代表；祁德片通行于祁门及江西境内的浮梁、德兴一带，受周围赣语影响很深。和其他徽语一样，这里的方言在条条山谷之间差异极大。明清两代，出外经营的徽商把乡音带到远方的商帮社群中，维系着这一方言的认同。

en: The Quandamookan are the Aboriginal Australian people of Moreton Bay in south-eastern Queensland, made up of three tribes: the Nunukul and Goenpul of North Stradbroke Island and the Ngugi of Moreton Island, whose shores and waters had been their home for many thousands of years. They moved between semi-permanent camps, fished from canoes for mullet and hunted dugong and sea turtle, with the work divided by custom between men and women. Each tribe spoke a Durubalic dialect of the Pama-Nyungan family, Jandai among the Goenpul and Moondjan among the Nunukul. In 1799 Matthew Flinders spent several weeks charting Moreton Bay, their first encounter with Europeans. They later sheltered the castaways Thomas Pamphlett, John Finnegan and Richard Parsons, whom John Oxley found living there on his 1823 voyage, and in 1824 Oxley founded a penal settlement at Redcliffe, beginning the colonial seizure of their bay.
zh: 昆达穆卡人是昆士兰东南莫顿湾的澳大利亚原住民，由三个部落组成：北斯特拉德布罗克岛的努努卡尔人和贡普尔人，以及莫顿岛的恩古吉人，湾中的海岸与水域数千年来一直是他们的家园。他们在半固定营地之间迁徙，驾独木舟捕捞鲻鱼，猎捕儒艮和海龟，劳作按习俗在男女间分工。三个部落各说帕马—牛雅语系杜鲁巴利克语支的一种方言，贡普尔人说詹代语，努努卡尔人说蒙詹语。1799年，马修·弗林德斯花了数周测绘莫顿湾，这是他们与欧洲人的第一次接触。后来他们收留了遇险的托马斯·帕姆弗莱特、约翰·芬尼根和理查德·帕森斯，约翰·奥克斯利1823年驶入湾中时发现了这三人；1824年，奥克斯利在雷德克利夫建立流放殖民地，开启了对这片海湾的殖民侵占。

en: The Ugakhpa, known in history as the Quapaw, are a Dhegiha Siouan people whose name means the Downstream people. Their oral history tells how they parted from the Omaha, Ponca, Osage and Kanza at the junction of the Missouri and Mississippi, followed the great river south and settled at the mouth of the Arkansas by the mid-seventeenth century. Algonquian neighbours called them the Akansa, from which the French derived Arkansas, naming both the river and Arkansas Post after them. At the Quapaw's request Henri de Tonti built that post in 1686, the first European settlement on the Mississippi, and the tribe became a steadfast French ally, fighting the Natchez in 1729 and in the Chickasaw Wars. French traders married Quapaw women, and the mixed settlement of Pine Bluff grew from these ties. After the Louisiana Purchase the United States acknowledged some thirty-two million acres as theirs in 1818 only to make them cede nearly all of it, and a second treaty in 1824 took the rest. Floods and hunger scattered the survivors until 1834, when the Quapaw were removed to Indian Territory beyond the Mississippi.
zh: 乌加克帕人即史书上的夸保人，属德吉哈苏语族群，族名意为“下游之人”。据他们的口述史，他们在密苏里河与密西西比河交汇处与奥马哈、蓬卡、奥塞奇和坎扎诸部分离，沿大河南下，于17世纪中叶在阿肯色河口一带定居。邻近的阿尔冈昆人把他们称作阿坎萨，法国人由此化出“阿肯色”一名，阿肯色河与阿肯色站都因他们得名。1686年，亨利·德·通蒂应夸保人之请修建阿肯色站，这是密西西比河上最早的欧洲人定居点；夸保人也成为法国的忠实盟友，参加了1729年对纳奇兹人的战争和历次奇克索战争。法国商人与夸保妇女通婚，混血聚落派恩布拉夫即由此发展而来。路易斯安那购地后，美国于1818年承认约三千二百万英亩土地归他们所有，随即迫使他们割让其中绝大部分，1824年的又一项条约拿走了余下的土地。洪水和饥荒使幸存者流离失所，最终在1834年被迁往密西西比河以西的印第安领地。

en:
The Quasmigdo, known to their neighbours as the Bidai, are an Atakapan-speaking people of eastern Texas. Their own name is Quasmigdo; Bidai is a Caddo word meaning brushwood, a reference to the densely wooded Big Thicket around the lower Trinity River where they lived. Their main villages stood on Bedias Creek, and their hunting grounds ran from the Brazos to the Neches River. Spanish explorers first noted them in 1691 near the Hasinai, and the Frenchman François Simars de Bellisle found them farming maize in 1718 and 1720, allied with the Akokisa. In the eighteenth century they numbered perhaps 600 in three bands, of which the northern Deadose had split off about 1700.

They grew maize for trade as well as food, snared game in cane pens, fished and gathered, summering on the coast and wintering inland in bearskin tents; cradleboards shaped their infants' skulls and both sexes wore tattoos. Some families joined the Spanish Mission San Francisco Xavier de Horcasitas in the 1740s, while in 1770 Bidai middlemen sold French guns to the Lipan Apaches against Spanish interests. Epidemics in 1776 and 1777 cut their numbers by at least half, and the survivors drifted into Akokisa and Koasati villages; in 1803 the Indian agent John Sibley still praised them for their honesty and punctuality.
zh:
夸斯米格多人在邻族口中称比戴人，是得克萨斯东部说阿塔卡帕语的族群。“夸斯米格多”是他们的自称；“比戴”来自卡多语，意为“灌木枝”，得名于其居住地特里尼蒂河下游林木茂密的大丛林地。他们的主村坐落在贝迪亚斯溪畔，猎场从布拉索斯河延伸到内奇斯河。1691年西班牙探险者在哈西奈人附近首次记录到他们；1718年和1720年，法国人弗朗索瓦·西马尔·德·贝利勒发现他们种植玉米，并与阿科基萨人结盟。18世纪时他们约有六百人，分三个支派，其中最北的达多斯支约于1700年分出。

他们种玉米既为口粮也用于交易，用藤笼诱捕猎物，兼事捕鱼和采集，夏天在海岸生活，冬天回内陆住熊皮帐篷；摇篮板会改变婴儿的头形，男女都文身。18世纪40年代，一些家族加入西班牙人的圣弗朗西斯科·哈维尔·德·奥尔卡西塔斯传教站；1770年，比戴中间商又不顾西班牙人的利益，把法国枪支卖给利潘阿帕奇人。1776年和1777年的瘟疫使人口减半，幸存者陆续流入阿科基萨人和科阿萨蒂人的村落；1803年印第安事务官约翰·西布利仍称赞他们诚实守时。

en: The Quechan, who call themselves Kwatsáan, meaning those who descended, and are also known as the Yuma, are a Yuman-speaking people of the lower Colorado River, around the later site of Fort Yuma near the present border of Arizona and California. Despite the similar name, they have no connection with the Quechua of the Andes. They were counted among the fiercest warriors and busiest traders of the river, exchanging goods with the Pima of southern Arizona, the pueblos of New Mexico and the peoples of the Pacific coast, and in the 1820s they and the Mohave drove their old rivals the Halchidhoma off the Colorado altogether. Their first lasting European contact came in the winter of 1774 with the Spanish explorer Juan Bautista de Anza. The chief Palma travelled to Mexico City and was baptized there in February 1777, but the friendship collapsed when mission livestock trampled Quechan fields during a drought. In July 1781 the tribe rose up, killing four priests and thirty soldiers and destroying the missions of Bicuñer and Purísima Concepción; a Spanish punitive expedition the next year never restored the lost settlements, and the river crossing remained in Quechan hands.
zh: 夸特桑人自称“夸特桑”，意为“自上游而下者”，又称尤马人，是科罗拉多河下游讲尤曼语的族群，聚居于后来尤马堡所在的今亚利桑那州与加利福尼亚州边界一带。他们虽然名字相近，却与安第斯山的克丘亚人毫无关系。夸特桑人是科罗拉多河上最好战的部族之一，也是活跃的商人，同亚利桑那南部的皮马人、新墨西哥的普韦布洛村镇以及太平洋海岸诸族群都有贸易往来；19世纪20年代，他们与莫哈维人联手，把宿敌哈利奇多姆人彻底赶出了科罗拉多河。他们与欧洲人第一次持久的接触发生在1774年冬，来者是西班牙探险家胡安·鲍蒂斯塔·德·安萨。酋长帕尔马曾远赴墨西哥城，于1777年2月在那里受洗；但传教站的牲畜在一场旱灾中踏毁了夸特桑人的农田，友谊随之破裂。1781年7月，夸特桑人起兵反抗，杀死四名神父和三十名士兵，摧毁了比库涅尔和普里西马康塞普西翁两处传教站；次年西班牙发兵讨伐，却未能重建被毁的定居点，这处河渡始终掌握在夸特桑人手中。

en: The Quimbaya were the Indigenous people of the Cauca River valley in present-day Colombia, across the country's coffee belt in what are now Quindío, Caldas and Risaralda. Settled in the region from around the first century before the common era, they reached their Classic flowering between the 300s and 600s, when their smiths mastered tumbaga, a gold and copper alloy, and cast the poporo lime vessels and seated figurines that were buried as funeral offerings in hollow-tree sarcophagi. They lived under many small cacicazgos, farmed maize and cassava, wove cotton blankets as their main industry, and traded metalwork, textiles and river-boiled salt with neighbouring peoples. After an artistic pause the late Quimbaya tradition carried these skills into the sixteenth century, when the people of the Cauca mounted fierce resistance to the conquistadors of the newly founded New Kingdom of Granada after 1539, before being broken and absorbed into colonial society.
zh: 金巴亚人是今哥伦比亚考卡河流域的原住民，活动于该国咖啡带，即今金迪奥、卡尔达斯和里萨拉尔达一带。他们约在公元前1世纪定居此地，在4世纪至7世纪进入古典鼎盛期：工匠掌握了金铜合金通巴加的冶炼，铸出波波罗石灰瓶和坐姿人像，这些器物后来作为随葬品安放在掏空树干做成的棺椁中。他们分成众多小型酋邦，种植玉米和木薯，以织造棉布毯为主要产业，并用金属器、纺织品和河水熬制的盐与邻族贸易。经过一段艺术低潮后，晚期金巴亚传统把这些技艺延续到16世纪；1539年新格拉纳达王国建立后，考卡河畔的金巴亚人对征服者展开顽强抵抗，最终被击溃并融入殖民社会。

en: The Querandí were the easternmost of the Het peoples, nomadic hunter-gatherers of the Argentine Pampas whose range ran from the country around Buenos Aires across the later provinces of La Pampa, Córdoba and Santa Fe. Their Guaraní name means men of fat, after the animal grease in their diet; the Mapuche called them Puelche and the Spaniards knew them simply as the Pampas. They lived in leather tents, were famed runners who could run down Pampas deer, ñandú and guanaco, and hunted with the bolas, a stone tied to a leather cord that became a classic weapon of the southern plains. The Caboto expedition first described them in 1528. In 1536 Pedro de Mendoza's colonists reached the Río de la Plata: after the Querandí defeated his brother Diego de Mendoza at Laguna de Rocha, they and their allies burned the newly founded Buenos Aires, which was abandoned in 1541. When Juan de Garay refounded the city in 1580 and parcelled the natives into encomiendas, resistance collapsed after Garay was killed by a Querandí cacique and Rodrigo Ortiz de Zárate campaigned against them in 1586. The Querandí then disappear as a distinct people, last listed under that name in an encomienda census of 1672.
zh: 基兰迪人是赫特诸族中位置最东的一支，作为游猎采集者游荡在阿根廷潘帕斯草原，活动范围从布宜诺斯艾利斯一带延伸到后来的拉潘帕、科尔多瓦和圣菲诸省。他们的名字来自瓜拉尼语，意为食脂之人，因日常食用动物油脂而得名；马普切人称他们为普埃尔切人，西班牙人则径直叫他们潘帕人。他们住皮帐篷，以善跑闻名，能徒步追擒潘帕斯鹿、美洲鸵和原驼，捕猎时使用皮绳拴石的流星锤，这种武器后来成为南方草原的经典兵器。1528年卡博特探险队最早记载了他们。1536年佩德罗·德·门多萨的殖民队抵达拉普拉塔河，基兰迪人在罗查湖击败其弟迭戈·德·门多萨后，又联合其他部族焚毁了初建的布宜诺斯艾利斯，该城最终于1541年废弃。1580年胡安·德·加雷重建此城，把原住民编入委托监护制；随着加雷死于一位基兰迪酋长之手，以及罗德里戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·萨拉特1586年的出兵镇压，基兰迪人作为独立族群走向消亡，其名字最后一次出现是在1672年的一份委托监护制人口册上。

en: The Quiripi were a loose set of Eastern Algonquian-speaking village peoples along the north shore of Long Island Sound, from the lower Connecticut River through southwestern Connecticut and onto central Long Island. Their best-known band, the Quinnipiac, or “long-water people,” had their main village on the site of modern New Haven; nearby groups such as the Wangunk, Podunk and Naugatuck, and the Unquachog and Montaukett across the sound, spoke the same or closely related dialects. They lived by farming maize, beans and squash, fishing and hunting, in villages moved periodically as the soil wore out, and were governed by local sachems rather than any central chief. Contact with Dutch and English traders early in the seventeenth century was followed by epidemic disease and the founding in 1638 of the first English “Indian reservation,” a small tract near New Haven for the Quinnipiac. Mission work produced a Quiripi catechism translated by Abraham Pierson in 1658, but conversion made little headway. Land sales, warfare and shrinking numbers steadily broke up the communities: many survivors joined the Tunxis and Mahican at Farmington and Stockbridge, and later the Brotherton settlement, whose people were eventually removed west to Wisconsin in the nineteenth century, while the Quiripi language itself died out around the end of the 1800s.
zh: 奎里皮人是长岛湾北岸一批说东阿尔冈昆语的松散村社群体，分布范围从康涅狄格河下游沿康涅狄格西南部一直延伸到长岛中部。其中最知名的一支是昆尼帕人，意为“长水之民”，主村就在今纽黑文一带；附近的旺贡克、波当克、诺加塔克以及海湾对岸的昂夸乔格、蒙陶克特等群体都说相同或相近的方言。他们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，兼营渔猎，村庄随地力衰退而定期迁移，由本地酋长各自管辖，没有统一的最高首领。17世纪初与荷兰、英国商人接触后，疫病随之而来；1638年英国人在纽黑文附近为昆尼帕人划出一小块土地，这是英属北美第一处“印第安保留地”。传教活动促成亚伯拉罕·皮尔逊于1658年把教理问答译成奎里皮语，但皈依收效甚微。土地买卖、战争和人口锐减不断瓦解这些社群：许多幸存者先后并入法明顿的坦克西人和斯托克布里奇的莫希干人，后来又加入布拉泽敦定居点，最终在19世纪被迁往西部的威斯康星；奎里皮语本身也在19世纪末前后消亡。

en: The Quitu were the original people of the Pichincha highlands of central-northern Ecuador, valley farmers settled south of the Guayllabamba River whose name also served for the whole network of Panzaleo chiefdoms stretching from Tungurahua and Cotopaxi to the site of Quito. Around 800 they dug deep, three-level funerary tombs on the plateau above their villages, burying their dead in a squatting posture with textiles and Spondylus shell ornaments obtained through long-distance trade run by mindalaes merchants linking the Amazon, the Yumbo country and the Pacific coast. They shared the cult of the lightning god Catequil with their neighbours, and together with the Caranqui they fought the invading Incas: the confederacy held off Túpac Yupanqui but was subdued by Huayna Capac, under whom a later revolt of the northern tribes was crushed. Quito then became an Inca city, and in 1534 it fell to the Spaniards. The chroniclers name the Puruhá-Quitu princess Paccha Duchicela, held to be the mother of Atahualpa, as a daughter of these chiefdoms.
zh: 基多人是厄瓜多尔中北部皮钦查山区的原住民，在瓜伊亚班巴河以南的河谷务农；他们的名字也用来统称从通古拉瓦、科托帕希一直延伸到基多城址一带的潘萨莱奥酋邦群。约800年，他们在村庄上方的台地挖掘三层深墓，将死者以蹲姿下葬，随葬织物和海菊蛤壳饰；这些贝壳由辛达拉商人长途贩运而来，贸易网连通亚马逊、云博人地区和太平洋沿岸。他们与邻族共同信奉雷神卡特基尔，并与卡兰基人联手抗击入侵的印加人：联盟挡住了图帕克·尤潘基，最终仍被瓦伊纳·卡帕克征服，北方各部后来的起义也遭镇压。基多此后成为印加城市，1534年落入西班牙人之手。编年史家记载，出身普鲁哈与基多的公主帕查·杜奇塞拉被认为是阿塔瓦尔帕之母，正是这些酋邦的女儿。
