In the 1720s the Yongzheng emperor drove the Dzungars out of Amdo and left the Tebbu valleys to local Tibetan chiefs and monasteries rather than to direct rule from Lhasa. Like other Amdo Tibetans, the Tebbu combined valley farming with herding on the high pastures above the gorges.
zh: 迭部人是甘肃南部岷山山区的藏族支系，聚居于白龙江峡谷的迭部和舟曲东部一带，地处安多东南边缘，讲安多藏语方言。7世纪安多被吐蕃帝国吞并，迭部地方随之进入吐蕃版图；9世纪吐蕃瓦解后，他们与安多各地同命运，归入997—1104年在位的藏族宗喀政权（唃厮啰政权）治下。13世纪的蒙古征服把这一地区纳入藏传佛教的供施关系秩序；14至16世纪，明朝在边境保有驻军，而蒙古贵族在附近仍势力强大。18世纪20年代，雍正皇帝将准噶尔人逐出安多，迭部河谷交由当地藏族首领和寺院治理，而非受拉萨直接管辖。与其他安多藏族一样，迭部人兼营河谷农耕与高山牧场的畜牧。

en: The Tecos were a Nahuatl-speaking Nahua people of the Pacific lowlands of western Mexico, centered on the valley that became Colima and the neighboring coasts of Jalisco and Michoacán. A Nahua group settled the Colima valley around the sixth century and built it into the Postclassic kingdom of Colimán, ruled by a tlatoani, whose name survives in that of the modern state. Around 1480 the Purépecha Empire invaded to seize the region's saltpeter workings, but the Tecos and their huey tlatoani Colimotl defeated the invaders near Zacoalco in the Saltpeter War and went on to make Sayula, Zapotlán and Amula their tributaries. After the fall of Tenochtitlan they beat two Spanish columns at Trojes and Tecomán, until Gonzalo de Sandoval's expedition killed Colimotl at the battle of Alima and founded the Spanish town of Colima at Caxitlán in 1523.
zh: 特科人是墨西哥西部太平洋低地的纳瓦人支系，操纳瓦特尔语西部方言，聚居于后来成为科利马的谷地以及哈利斯科、米却肯两地的邻近海岸。约6世纪，一支纳瓦人进入科利马谷地，在后古典期建立科利曼王国，首领称特拉托阿尼，国名一直保留在今天的科利马州名里。约1480年，普雷佩查帝国为夺取当地硝石矿入侵，特科人在大特拉托阿尼科利莫特尔率领下于萨科阿尔科附近打赢硝石战争，进而迫使萨尤拉、萨波特兰和阿穆拉纳贡。特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，他们在特罗赫斯和特科曼连败两支西班牙远征队，最终贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔的军队在阿利马之战击杀科利莫特尔，并于1523年在卡克斯特兰建立西班牙人的科利马城。

en: The Teimani, or Yemenite Jews, are the Jewish community of the south Arabian highlands, in 1337 settled in towns such as Sanaa, Dhamar and Thula under the Sunni Rasulid sultans. Jewish tradition and Himyarite inscriptions place their origins in Roman times, when refugees from Judea joined traders on the incense route; the Himyarite king Abu Karib converted to Judaism around 390, and his successor Dhu Nuwas fought the Christian Ethiopians before the Aksumite conquest of the sixth century. Under Islam the Jews paid the jizya poll tax as protected subjects and spoke Judeo-Arabic. In the 1160s the ruler Abd al-Nabi ibn Mahdi offered them conversion or death, until Saladin's brother Turan-Shah conquered Yemen in 1173; the crisis drew Maimonides' Epistle to Yemen. The Rasulid age of 1229 to 1474 brought prosperity, but Tahirid and Zaydi rule narrowed their liberties, and after the Zaydis drove out the Ottomans in 1630 the imam al-Mahdi Ahmad expelled the whole community to the arid province of Mawza in 1679, where as many as two-thirds perished. The survivors returned as indispensable silversmiths, weavers and mint workers, and by the eighteenth century they handled much of the coffee trade through Mokha.
zh: 也门犹太人是阿拉伯半岛南部高地的犹太社群，1337年在逊尼派拉苏里王朝苏丹治下，定居于萨那、达马尔、苏拉等城镇。犹太传统和希木叶尔铭文把他们的起源追溯到罗马时代：来自犹太地的难民随香料商路而来；希木叶尔国王阿布·卡里布于390年前后皈依犹太教，其继承者祖·努瓦斯在6世纪阿克苏姆征服之前曾与信奉基督教的埃塞俄比亚人交战。伊斯兰时代，他们作为受保护的臣民缴纳吉兹亚人头税，讲犹太-阿拉伯语。12世纪60年代，统治者阿卜杜·纳比·伊本·马赫迪逼他们在改宗和死亡之间抉择，直到1173年萨拉丁的兄弟图兰-沙阿征服也门；这场危难催生了迈蒙尼德的《致也门书》。1229至1474年的拉苏里时代带来繁荣，但塔希尔王朝和栽德派的统治压缩了他们的自由；栽德派于1630年逐出奥斯曼人后，伊玛目马赫迪·阿哈迈德在1679年把全体犹太人放逐到干旱的莫扎省，多达三分之二的人死于当地。幸存者后来作为不可替代的银匠、织工和铸币工匠返回，到18世纪已通过穆哈港掌控了相当大一部分咖啡贸易。

en: The Teke, or Bateke, also called Tyo or Tio, are a Bantu people of the savanna plateaus north of Pool Malebo, spread across the Republic of the Congo, the western Democratic Republic of the Congo and south-eastern Gabon. They built one of the oldest kingdoms of the region: a sacred king titled the Makoko ruled from the plains around Mbe, and Teke power flourished between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries, its smithing-linked kingship later influencing Loango and Kongo. In the fifteenth century the expanding Kingdom of Kongo met its match on the Teke frontier; the earliest written mention of a Teke king dates to 1507, and Tio forces killed the Kongo ruler Henrique I in 1568. Mid-seventeenth-century Dutch accounts describe a king at Monsol ruling over thirteen lesser rulers, though the kingdom was already decentralised. During the 1700s charm boxes called nkobi strengthened provincial lords at the crown's expense, and in the early 1800s wars with the Bobangi sapped the monarchy. Teke religion centred on the high god Nzambi, ancestor cults and carved figures such as the Tara-Mantsie that embodied a village elder's authority.
zh: 太凯人又称巴特凯人、特约人或蒂奥人，是生活在马莱博湖以北热带草原高原上的班图族群，分布跨刚果（布）、刚果（金）西部和加蓬东南部。他们建立了该地区最古老的王国之一：被称为马科科的神圣国王以姆贝平原一带为中心，太凯势力在12至14世纪盛极一时，其与冶铁相连的王权观念后来影响了罗安果和刚果。15世纪向东扩张的刚果王国在太凯边境受阻；文字材料最早于1507年提到太凯国王，1568年蒂奥军队还杀死了刚果国王恩里克一世。17世纪中叶荷兰人的记述称，建都蒙索尔的国王统辖十三位小君主，不过王国此时已趋于分权。18世纪，名为恩科比的符咒盒壮大了地方领主、削弱了王权；19世纪初与博班吉人的战争又进一步动摇了君主统治。太凯人的宗教以至高神恩赞比、祖先崇拜和木雕为核心，象征长老权威的“塔拉曼齐”雕像便是代表。

en: The Telengit, or Telengut, are a Turkic people of the Altai mountains and one of the principal groups later counted among the Altaians, dwelling chiefly in the Chuia steppe of the southeastern Altai; Chinese chroniclers may have recorded them as the Duolange tribe. In the fourteenth century their princes, titled Biy, built their own ulus, which Russian documents of the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries called the Teleut Land. Long balanced between the Tsardom of Russia and the Dzungar Khanate, the Telengit more than once defeated both powers and kept their independence until the Dzungars finally overran them in the eighteenth century, enrolling them as an ulus of four thousand yurts and resettling part of the people on the Ili River. When Dzungar power collapsed, these exiles made their way back to the Altai, harried on the road by Manchu, Kazakh and Khalkha raiders. Organized into two Chui volosts, they kept their separate identity and remained beyond imperial control even after the other Altaians came under Russian rule in 1756. They were nomadic and semi-nomadic herders of sheep, cattle, goats and horses, living in felt yurts and following shamanic cults later overlain by Russian Orthodoxy.
zh: 帖良古惕人（一作帖连古特）是阿尔泰山的突厥语民族，后来被归入阿尔泰人的主要支系之一，主要居住在阿尔泰东南部的楚亚草原，中国史籍可能以“多览葛”之名记载过他们。14世纪时，他们号称“比伊”的王公建立了自己的兀鲁思，16至18世纪的俄国文献称之为“铁列乌特地”。帖良古惕人长期周旋于俄罗斯沙皇国和准噶尔汗国之间，不止一次击败这两股势力，保持独立，直到18世纪终被准噶尔征服，被编为四千帐的兀鲁思，部分人被迁到伊犁河。准噶尔崩溃后，这些流亡者辗转返回阿尔泰，途中不断遭满洲、哈萨克和喀尔喀人袭掠。他们被编为楚亚两个乡，即便其他阿尔泰人已于1756年接受俄国统治，仍保持自身的独特身份，游离于帝国管控之外。他们以游牧和半游牧方式放养绵羊、牛、山羊和马，住毡帐，信奉萨满教，后来又叠加了俄罗斯东正教信仰。

en: The Teleut are a Turkic people of the upper Ob region, concentrated chiefly along the Great and Little Bachat rivers in Kemerovo Oblast, whose speech is a dialect of Southern Altai. They originated among the Tiele confederation and were once subjects of the First Turkic Khaganate. By the late sixteenth century they roamed the steppe between the Irtysh and the Ob with about four thousand tents, at that time nominal vassals of the Oirats; Russian documents of the following centuries called them White Kalmyks, although they were neither Mongolic nor Kalmyk. In 1618 Cossacks from Tomsk built the Kuznetsk ostrog on the Tom inside their grazing lands, and the Russian grip tightened through the seventeenth century until the mid-eighteenth, when the Teleut became tsarist subjects, later classed with the Altaians before being recognized as a separate people. Most were nomadic or semi-nomadic herders of horses, cattle, sheep and goats, living in conical bark-covered yurts, while some lived by taiga hunting. One offshoot, the Kalmaks, moved north in the seventeenth century, mixed with the Siberian Tatars and adopted Sunni Islam; the main body was converted to Russian Orthodoxy while keeping shamanic customs.
zh: 铁列乌特人是鄂毕河上游的突厥语民族，主要聚居在克麦罗沃州的大巴恰特河和小巴恰特河沿岸，所说的铁列乌特话是南阿尔泰语的一种方言。他们源出铁勒联盟，曾臣属于第一突厥汗国。16世纪末，他们约有四千帐，游牧于额尔齐斯河与鄂毕河之间的草原，当时在名义上臣服卫拉特人；此后几个世纪的俄国文书称他们为“白卡尔梅克”，尽管他们既不是蒙古语族，也不是卡尔梅克人。1618年，托木斯克的哥萨克在他们牧地内的托木河畔修建库兹涅茨克堡，俄国的控制在整个17世纪不断收紧，到18世纪中叶铁列乌特人成为沙皇臣民，后来长期被划入阿尔泰人，之后才被承认为单一民族。他们大多以游牧或半游牧方式放养马、牛、绵羊和山羊，住树皮覆盖的锥形毡帐，也有一些人靠泰加林狩猎为生。其分支卡尔马克人于17世纪北迁，与西伯利亚鞑靼人融合并改宗逊尼派伊斯兰教；主体居民则皈依俄罗斯东正教，同时保留萨满习俗。

en: The Telugus, known since antiquity as the Andhras, are the largest Dravidian-speaking people, native to the Godavari and Krishna river deltas and the surrounding Deccan uplands that make up modern Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Megasthenes around 310 BCE described them as a military power second only to the Mauryas, and their first great state, the Satavahana dynasty of the second century BCE to the second century CE, ruled most of the Deccan from a capital near Amaravati and traded with the Roman world, while the Amaravati school of Buddhist art carried its influence to Southeast Asia. After the Pallavas and Eastern Chalukyas, under whom Nannaya began the Telugu Mahabharata around 1025, the Kakatiya kings of Warangal united the Telugu lands between 1163 and 1323, an age in which Tikkana carried that work on and Telugu matured as a literary language. When Delhi's Tughluq armies took Warangal in 1323, the Musunuri Nayaks led the recovery, and Telugu warriors entered the service of the Vijayanagara Empire, where under Krishnadevaraya in the early sixteenth century Telugu became the language of high culture across the south. The Qutb Shahi sultans of Golconda patronised Telugu until the Mughal conquest, and in 1765 the Northern Circars passed to the British East India Company, which defeated the raja of Vizianagaram in 1792 and drew the region into the Madras Presidency.
zh: 泰卢固人古称安得拉人，是人数最多的达罗毗荼语民族，世居戈达瓦里河与克里希纳河三角洲及周边的德干高原，即今安得拉邦和特伦甘纳邦一带。约公元前310年，麦加斯梯尼记载他们的军力仅次于孔雀王朝；他们建立的第一个大国是公元前2世纪至公元2世纪的百乘王朝，以阿马拉瓦蒂附近为都统治大半个德干，并与罗马世界通商，阿马拉瓦蒂佛教艺术流派的影响远及东南亚。此后历经帕拉瓦王朝与东遮娄其王朝，南纳亚于1025年前后在东遮娄其治下开始写作泰卢固语《摩诃婆罗多》；瓦朗加尔的卡卡提亚诸王在1163至1323年间统一了泰卢固各地，诗人提卡纳在这一时期续写此书，泰卢固语也日趋成熟为文学语言。1323年德里的图格鲁克军队攻陷瓦朗加尔后，穆苏努里·纳亚克首领率众光复故土，泰卢固武士转而效力毗奢耶那伽罗帝国；在16世纪初克里希纳·德瓦·拉亚治下，泰卢固语成为南印度高雅文化的通用语言。戈尔康达的库特布沙希苏丹一直扶持泰卢固文化，直至莫卧儿征服；1765年北萨尔卡尔转归英国东印度公司，公司又于1792年击败维济亚讷格勒姆王公，将这一地区并入马德拉斯管区。

en: The Tem, also called Temba or Kotokoli, are a Gur-speaking people of central Togo, with communities also in Benin, Ghana and Burkina Faso, grouped around the market town of Sokodé. Their traditions place their earlier home along the White Volta, in present-day Burkina Faso, from which Gurma chiefdoms drifted south and, in the 1600s, coalesced into the Tchaoudjo Kingdom around Sokodé, absorbing Hausa, Yoruba and Mandinka settlers over the centuries. The Tem kept a hierarchical chiefly society and were nicknamed the lions; in the 1800s Chakosi merchants and the Egoma clan brought Islam, which then spread alongside older animist ritual rather than replacing it.
zh: 特姆人又称滕巴人或科托科利人，是多哥中部说古尔语支特姆语的民族，在贝宁、加纳和布基纳法索也有分布，聚居于集镇索科德一带。按其传统，他们早先住在白沃尔特河畔（今布基纳法索境内），后来古尔马诸酋长领地南移，于17世纪在索科德周围合并为查奥乔王国，数百年间融入了豪萨、约鲁巴和曼丁哥移民。特姆社会等级分明、酋长当权，并有“雄狮”的别称；19世纪，查科西商人和埃戈马氏族带来伊斯兰教，它与古老的万物有灵仪式并行传播，并未取而代之。

en: The Temne are a West African people of northwestern Sierra Leone, with some communities across the border in Guinea, who speak Temne, a Mel language related to Baga. Their oral traditions place their ancestral home in the Futa Jallon highlands. Migrations south began after the collapse of the Jallonkadu state and accelerated in the fifteenth century under Fula pressure, until they settled between the Kolenté and Rokel rivers, displacing the Limba to the northeast and the Bullom to the south. Rice farmers, fishermen and traders organized into independent patrilineal chiefdoms, they also kept the Poro and Bondo initiation societies. In 1642 a Susu army overran Forécariah and tried to force Islam on them, driving more Temne into Sierra Leone; Islam later spread peacefully through Muslim traders. Around 1505 Temne migrants founded the Kingdom of Koya, whose Bai kings traded with the Portuguese on the coast. Under King Naimbanna, who reigned from 1775 to 1793 and opposed the slave trade, Koya ceded the Sierra Leone peninsula by treaty in 1788, where freed slaves founded Freetown in 1792. Koya fought the British and the Susu from 1801 to 1807, losing Port Loko, but retook the port in 1815.
zh: 泰姆内人是塞拉利昂西北部的西非族群，部分聚落分布在几内亚境内，讲与巴加语相近的梅尔语支语言泰姆内语。他们的口传传统把祖地指向富塔贾隆高原。贾隆卡杜政权衰落后，泰姆内人开始南迁，15世纪在富拉人压力下迁徙加速，最终定居于科伦泰河与罗克尔河之间，把林巴人挤向东北、布隆人挤向南方。他们是以种稻为主、兼营渔猎和贸易的农民，社会由各自独立的父系酋长邦组成，并保留波洛会与邦多会等成年结社。1642年，苏苏人的军队攻占福雷卡里亚，企图强迫他们改宗伊斯兰教，更多泰姆内人因此退入塞拉利昂；后来伊斯兰教又随穆斯林商人和平传播。约1505年，南迁的泰姆内人建立科亚王国，其巴伊国王与沿海的葡萄牙人贸易。1775年至1793年在位的奈姆巴纳王反对奴隶贸易，他治下的科亚于1788年订约割让塞拉利昂半岛，获释黑奴于1792年在那里建立弗里敦。1801年至1807年科亚同英国人和苏苏人交战，失去洛科港，但于1815年夺回该港。

en: The Tenda, or Tanda, are an ethnolinguistic group of the upper Gambia basin, spread across southern Senegal, northeastern Guinea-Bissau and northern Guinea, and made up of the Bassari, Konyagui, Bedik and Badiaranke peoples. Their name is a Mandinka word for a landing place or wharf, for the Gambia River between the Nieriko and Niokolo Koba, though unnavigable, offered many fords. Caravans linking Kaabu, the Futa Jallon, the states of Senegambia, the goldfields of Bambouk and Bure and the Niger city of Djenné crossed there, and the Tenda grew up serving that traffic. They speak Tenda languages of the Senegambian branch. Between the 1670s and 1730s their country became a major source of slaves for the Atlantic trade, raided by stronger neighboring powers.
zh: 滕达人（又称坦达人）是生活在冈比亚河上游的族群语言群体，分布在塞内加尔南部、几内亚比绍东北部和几内亚北部，由巴萨里人、科尼亚吉人、贝迪克人和巴迪亚朗克人组成。他们的名字来自曼丁哥语中“渡口、码头”一词：涅里科与尼奥科洛科巴之间的冈比亚河虽无法通航，却有许多浅滩。往来于卡布、富塔贾隆、塞内冈比亚诸邦、班布克和布雷金矿以及尼日尔河畔杰内城之间的商队都从这里渡河，滕达人便在为这种转运效劳中形成。他们讲塞内冈比亚语支的滕达诸语。17世纪70年代至18世纪30年代，滕达地区成为大西洋奴隶贸易的重要奴隶来源地，屡遭强邻劫掠。

en: The Tenesch, also called Poya, were a band of the northern Tehuelche of Patagonia, ranging both sides of the Andes from the mountains of Llanquihue and Palena in Chile to the lands east and south of Nahuel Huapi Lake in the Argentine provinces of Río Negro and Chubut. Nomadic hunters organized in family groups under a chief, they lived in leather tents that moved with the seasons, pursued guanaco and the small rhea called choique, and gathered wild fruit, roots and fungi. They took to the horse early in the seventeenth century. Captain Juan Fernández crossed the Andes to Nahuel Huapi in 1620 and found Poya and Puelche camps around the lake. The Jesuit Nicolás Mascardi opened a mission there in 1670 and distinguished two dialects of their tongue, but the Poya killed him in 1673. As Mapuche bands pushed east through the Andes, calling them vuriloche, or people of the other side, the Poya were absorbed into the Mapuche world and ceased to exist as a separate people.
zh: 特内什人又称波亚人，是巴塔哥尼亚北特维尔切人的一支，活动在安第斯山脉两麓，西起智利延基韦和帕莱纳的山区，东至阿根廷内格罗河省与丘布特省境内纳韦尔瓦皮湖的东岸和南岸一带。他们是游猎民族，以家族为单位、由酋长率领，住随季节迁徙的皮帐篷，猎取原驼和名为乔伊克的小型美洲鸵，兼采野果、块根和菌类，并在17世纪初学会了养马。1620年胡安·费尔南德斯上尉翻越安第斯山抵达纳韦尔瓦皮湖，发现湖畔驻有波亚人与普埃尔切人的营地。耶稣会士尼古拉斯·马斯卡尔迪于1670年在当地开设传教站，并指出他们的语言分为两种方言，但他本人于1673年被波亚人杀死。后来马普切群体向东越过安第斯山，把他们称作武里洛切，意为山那边的人；波亚人最终融入马普切世界，不再作为独立族群存在。

en: The Tenetehara, whose best-known branch are the Guajajara, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Maranhão interior, made up of two main branches, the Guajajara and the Tembé. Their collective self-name means the true human beings, and they call their language ze'egete, the good speech. Their earliest known homeland was the middle Pindaré River, and the first recorded European contact came in 1615, when French Jesuits reached the Pindaré valley. During the 1700s Tenetehara groups spread into the Grajaú and Mearim river basins, living in strongly organized villages that combined hunting with farming and earning a wide reputation as skilled makers of tools. Their early contact history alternated between trading and allying with the Portuguese and refusing or revolting against forced settlement, which let them keep their language and village autonomy far longer than most coastal peoples.
zh: 瓜雅雅拉人是马拉尼昂内陆的图皮-瓜拉尼语族群，与滕贝人同属特内特哈拉人的两大分支；特内特哈拉意为真正的人，他们称本族语言为泽埃格特，意为优美的语言。他们已知最早的家园在平达雷河中游，有记载的首次欧洲接触发生在1615年，法国耶稣会士抵达平达雷河谷。18世纪，瓜雅雅拉群体扩展到格拉雅乌河与梅阿林河流域，在组织严密的村落中以狩猎兼农耕为生，并以善于制作工具而远近闻名。他们与殖民者的关系时而贸易、结盟，时而拒绝乃至武力反抗强制定居，因而比大多数沿海族群更久地保住了本族语言和村落自治。

en: The Tepecan were a small Tepiman-speaking people of the Bolaños River canyon in far northern Jalisco, centred on the village of Azqueltán. Their ancestors were Tepehuán who migrated south from the drought-stricken Sierra Madre Occidental in the thirteenth or fourteenth century and settled the isolated gorge, keeping a dialect closest to Southern Tepehuán. Spaniards reached the canyon in 1534, and during the eighteenth century Tepehuán lands around Azqueltán passed to Spanish ranchers and Tlaxcaltec colonists; the village's isolation let the Tepecan keep their language and identity long after neighbouring settlements lost theirs.
zh: 特佩坎人是说特皮曼语的小族群，住在哈利斯科州最北部博拉尼奥斯河的峡谷中，以阿斯特兰村为中心。他们的先民是特佩万人，在13或14世纪因西马德雷山脉北部干旱而南迁，定居在这条闭塞的峡谷里，保留了与南特佩万语最接近的方言。1534年西班牙人抵达峡谷；18世纪，阿斯特兰周围的特佩万土地落入西班牙牧场主和特拉斯卡拉殖民者之手，而阿斯特兰凭借闭塞的地势，在邻村纷纷失去原有身份之后，仍长久保有自己的语言和认同。

en: The O'dam are the southeastern Tepehuán, the mountain branch of the Tepiman-speaking peoples whose heartland is the rugged Sierra Madre Occidental of Durango around Mezquital. Tepehuán is a Nahuatl name meaning mountain dwellers; their own ancestors drifted south from the Sonora-Arizona borderlands and took up maize, beans, squash and cotton farming under Mesoamerican influence, while keeping hunter bands, shamans and decentralized villages led by elders. At the Spanish arrival they were probably the largest people of the western Sierra. They stayed neutral in the Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590, after which Franciscan and Jesuit missions gathered them into towns; repeated epidemics between 1594 and 1617 may have cut their numbers by four fifths. In 1616 the messianic leader Quautlatas raised the Tepehuán Revolt, opening with an attack on a wagon train near Santa Catarina de Tepehuanes; by its defeat in 1620 some two hundred Spaniards, ten missionaries and perhaps four thousand Tepehuán were dead. Drought and disease scattered further communities later in the seventeenth century, and after the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 the O'dam villages passed a long eighteenth century in relative isolation, blending Catholic forms with older mountain rituals.
zh: 奥达姆人即东南特佩万人，是说特皮曼语的族群中的山地一支，核心区域在杜兰戈州梅斯基塔尔一带崎岖的西马德雷山脉。“特佩万”是纳瓦特尔语他称，意为“山里人”；他们的先民从索诺拉与亚利桑那交界地带南迁，在中美洲文化影响下改种玉米、菜豆、南瓜和棉花，同时保留了狩猎队伍、萨满和由长老议事的散村传统。西班牙人到来时，他们可能是西马德雷山区最大的族群。1550至1590年奇奇梅克战争期间特佩万人保持中立，战后方济各会与耶稣会的传教站把他们集中进城镇；1594至1617年间反复流行的疫病可能使人口减少了五分之四。1616年，救世主式的领袖夸乌特拉塔斯发动特佩万起义，首战在圣卡塔利娜·德·特佩瓦内斯附近袭击一支辎重车队；到1620年起义被镇压时，约两百名西班牙人、十名传教士和可能多达四千名特佩万人丧生。17世纪后期的旱灾和疫病又拆散了更多村落，1767年耶稣会被驱逐后，奥达姆诸村在相对封闭中度过了漫长的18世纪，把天主教形式与更古老的山地仪式融合在一起。

en: The Terena are the principal surviving branch of the Guaná, the eastern group of the Chané, the southernmost Arawakan-speaking peoples of South America. Arawakan farmers spreading south from northern South America more than two thousand years ago, the Guaná settled the plains of the northern Gran Chaco west of the Paraguay River, where by the early 1700s Spanish sources describe seven large villages of a thousand people or more. They grew corn, peanuts, cotton and squash and made ceramics and woven cloth. The Guaná became subjects of the horse-riding Mbayá, a Guaycuruan people who raided them for tribute and captives yet in turn adopted Guaná agriculture and weaving. Terêna, their Arawakan tongue, originally had four varieties, Kinikinao, Terena proper, Guaná and Chané, and carries many Guaicuruan and Tupi-Guarani loanwords. In the early nineteenth century the Terena still lived in farming villages along the upper Paraguay, caught between Mbayá raiders and the Spanish and Portuguese frontier.
zh: 特雷纳人是瓜纳人现存的主要支系，瓜纳人属于查内人的东支，而查内人是南美洲分布最南的阿拉瓦克语族群。两千多年前，阿拉瓦克农耕者自南美洲北部向南扩散，瓜纳人在巴拉圭河以西的北大查科平原定居；18世纪初的西班牙文献记载，他们在那里拥有七座千人以上的大村落，种植玉米、花生、棉花和南瓜，并制作陶器与织物。瓜纳人后来沦为骑马的姆巴亚人的属民，向这个瓜伊库鲁语族群交纳贡赋、忍受掳掠，姆巴亚人却也从他们那里学会了农耕和纺织。特雷纳人的语言属阿拉瓦克语族，原有基尼基瑙、特雷纳本部、瓜纳和查内四种变体，并借入了大量瓜伊库鲁语和图皮-瓜拉尼语词汇。19世纪初，特雷纳人仍在巴拉圭河上游的农耕村落中生活，周旋于姆巴亚袭掠者与西班牙、葡萄牙殖民据点之间。

en: The Ternate are the people of the small volcanic island of Ternate off the west coast of Halmahera, dominated by Mount Gamalama and ringed by clove groves. Their tradition holds that settlers fled Halmahera around 1250 and founded villages around the volcano under chiefs called momole; in 1257 the chiefs chose Cico of Sampalu village, also called Mashur Malamo, as their first kolano, or king, of the realm then known as Gapi. Trade with Java and Malacca made Ternate the chief clove emporium of the Moluccas, and about 1322 its ruler sponsored the Moti Agreement regulating trade among the spice islands. During the 1400s Ternate conquered the Sula Islands and Seram, and under Sultan Zainal Abidin, who reigned from 1468 to 1500, the kingdom turned into an Islamic sultanate. The Portuguese built a fortress on the island in 1522 but were expelled in 1575 after Sultan Babullah avenged the 1570 murder of Sultan Hairun; Spanish and Dutch rivals landed in 1606 and 1607 and divided the island until 1663, when the Dutch East India Company became the paramount power. The Ternate speak a non-Austronesian North Halmahera language that served as the lingua franca of North Maluku, and use Ternate Malay in trade.
zh: 特尔纳特人是特尔纳特岛的居民。特尔纳特岛是哈马黑拉岛西海岸外的火山小岛，岛上的瓜马拉马火山四周遍布丁香林。据当地传说，约1250年一批移民为避乱从哈马黑拉迁出，在火山周围建立村庄，首领称莫莫莱；1257年，各族首领推举桑帕卢村的奇科（又称马舒尔·马拉莫）为第一代科拉诺，即国王，国号加皮。与爪哇和马六甲的贸易使特尔纳特成为摩鹿加首要的丁香集散地，约1322年，其君主促成了规范香料群岛贸易的莫蒂协议。15世纪，特尔纳特征服苏拉群岛和斯兰岛；1468至1500年在位的扎因·阿比丁苏丹将王国变为伊斯兰苏丹国。葡萄牙人于1522年在岛上筑堡，但哈伊伦苏丹1570年遇刺后，巴布拉苏丹起兵复仇，于1575年将葡萄牙人逐出。此后西班牙与荷兰分别于1606年、1607年登岛并瓜分特尔纳特，直到1663年西班牙人撤走，荷兰东印度公司成为最高权力。特尔纳特人操非南岛的北哈马黑拉语系语言特尔纳特语，它曾是北马鲁古的通用语，贸易场合则使用特尔纳特马来语。

en: The Teta-deka are the Tetadeka or Tipatikka, the Pinenut Eaters and the northernmost band of the Western Shoshone, who lived in the northern Utah valleys of the Bear and Weber rivers and gathered each autumn for the communal pine-nut harvest that gave them their name; trappers held a rendezvous in neighbouring Cache Valley in 1826.
zh: 泰塔德卡人即特帕蒂卡人，意为“食松籽者”，是西肖肖尼人最靠北的一支，住在犹他北部贝尔河与韦伯河的谷地，每年秋季集体采集松籽，支群因此得名；1826年，毛皮猎人在邻近的卡什谷举办集会，是他们家乡一带较早的经常性对外接触。

en: The Tetun, known as Belu on the Indonesian side of Timor, are the largest Austronesian people of central and eastern Timor, living around such centres as Balibo and Laran on both sides of the island border. Their own traditions relate that they migrated from Malacca in the fourteenth century, first settling the island's centre, where they pushed the Atoni people toward the west, and then advancing east to found four small kingdoms. Of these Wehali, centred on the fertile plain of Laran, held ritual seniority over the many Timorese principalities: its Maromak Oan, or 'son of God', was a sacral overlord served by an executive regent called the Liurai, and the southern Tetun organized society along matrilineal lines. Their language spread as a lingua franca across central and eastern Timor. When Antonio Pigafetta of the Magellan expedition visited Timor in 1522, Wewiku-Wehali was already the island's dominant power, enriched by the sandalwood trade and in contact with Muslim Makassar. Portuguese expeditions sacked Wehali in 1642 and 1665, drawing it into their colonial sphere, while after the Battle of Penfui in 1749 the Dutch East India Company expanded from Kupang and signed a treaty with the Liurai in 1756; Wehali then maneuvered between the Portuguese and Dutch rivals dividing the island.
zh: 德顿人在印度尼西亚一侧又称贝卢人，是帝汶岛中部和东部最大的南岛语族群，聚居在巴里布和拉兰等中心地带，分布于岛屿边界两侧。根据本族传说，他们在14世纪从马六甲迁徙而来，先在岛中部定居，将阿托尼人排挤到西部，继而向东推进，建立了四个小王国。其中以拉兰肥沃平原为中心的韦哈勒在众多帝汶小邦中享有仪式上的宗主地位：其君主号称马罗马克·奥安，意为‘神之子’，是神圣的共主，由称利乌赖的摄政辅佐执政，南部德顿人社会按母系传承，他们的语言也成为帝汶中部和东部的通用语。1522年麦哲伦船队的皮加费塔抵达帝汶时，韦维库—韦哈勒已是岛上最强的政权，靠檀香木贸易致富，并与穆斯林的望加锡保持往来。葡萄牙军队在1642年和1665年两度洗劫韦哈勒，将其纳入殖民势力范围；1749年彭富伊之战后，荷兰东印度公司从古邦向外扩张，于1756年与利乌赖签订条约，此后韦哈勒便在瓜分帝汶的葡萄牙与荷兰两强之间周旋。

en: The Teushen or Tehues were foot nomads of the central Patagonian steppe, between the Aonikenk to their south and the Gununa Kune to their north, ranging the country around the middle Chubut. They hunted and gathered in small bands and spoke a Chonan language close to Aonekkenk, which later absorbed it; the name Chubut survives from their word chupat.
zh: 特乌申人又称特乌斯人，是巴塔哥尼亚中部草原的徒步游群，活动在丘布特河中游一带，南接奥尼肯克人，北邻古纳库内人。他们以小群体狩猎采集为生，所说的特乌申语属乔南语系，接近后来将其同化的奥尼肯克语，丘布特这个地名就来自他们的语言。

en: The Thai, or Siamese, are the central Tai people of the Chao Phraya plain. Southwestern Tai tribes drifted southwest from what is now Guangxi in southern China between the eighth and tenth centuries and settled the valley from the tenth century onward, absorbing the older Mon and Khmer populations of the Dvaravati and Lavo lands and taking from them Theravada Buddhism, Indic statecraft and much of their vocabulary. In 1238 Si Inthrathit threw off Khmer suzerainty to found the Sukhothai Kingdom, regarded in Thai tradition as the first Thai state; Ram Khamhaeng, who reigned from 1279 to 1298, is credited with the Thai script and with anchoring Theravada Buddhism, while Sangkhalok ceramics flowed to Yuan China. In 1337 Sukhothai shared the Chao Phraya basin with Thai chiefdoms such as Suphanburi and Lavo, and in 1351 Ramathibodi I founded Ayutthaya, which reduced Sukhothai to vassalage in 1349 and annexed it in 1438 before sacking Angkor itself in 1431. Ayutthaya grew into one of the great trading powers of Asia, was captured and plundered by the Burmese Toungoo in 1569 and restored, and finally fell to a Burmese siege in 1767. Taksin reunited the realm from Thonburi, and in 1782 Rama I founded the still-reigning Chakri dynasty across the river at Bangkok.
zh: 泰人又称暹罗泰人，是湄南河平原的中部台语民族。8至10世纪间，西南部台语诸部从今中国广西一带向西南迁徙，10世纪起定居湄南河流域，融合了堕罗钵底和罗斛故地上更早的孟人与高棉人，并从他们那里接受了上座部佛教、印度式治国术和大量词汇。1238年，室利·膺沙罗铁摆脱高棉宗主权，建立素可泰王国，在泰国传统中被视为第一个泰人国家；1279至1298年在位的兰甘亨被认为创制了泰文并确立上座部佛教，宋加洛瓷器也曾远销元朝中国。1337年时，素可泰与素攀、罗斛等泰人城邦并存于湄南河流域；1351年拉玛铁菩提一世建立阿瑜陀耶，1349年迫素可泰称臣，1438年将其吞并，又在1431年攻破吴哥。阿瑜陀耶后来发展为亚洲贸易强权之一，1569年曾被缅甸东吁王朝攻陷劫掠后复国，最终在1767年的缅甸围城中覆灭。郑信以吞武里为基地重新统一全国，1782年拉玛一世在河对岸的曼谷建立却克里王朝，定都曼谷。

en: The Thalanyji, also written Dhalandji or Thalandji, are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara coast of Western Australia, their country of some 4,500 square miles following the Ashburton River, which they call Minduruu and hold to be the dwelling of the serpent Warnamankura, from the sea inland to Nanutarra and the lower Henry River; local groups such as the Djalendi and Jinigudira are counted among their bands. They spoke a Kanyara language of the Pama–Nyungan family and practised neither circumcision nor subincision. In July 1618 the Dutch ship Mauritius, with Willem Janszoon aboard, surveyed their river mouth and charted it as Willem's River, among the first west-coast features of Australia to enter European cartography when Hessel Gerritsz printed it in 1627. Their presence farther south at Exmouth Gulf has been read as evidence of a later migration.
zh: 塔兰吉人（又拼达兰吉、塔莱亚吉）是西澳大利亚皮尔巴拉海岸的原住民，约四千五百平方英里的家园沿阿什伯顿河展开：他们把这条河称作明杜鲁，认为巨蛇瓦纳曼库拉就栖身河中，领地从海边向内延伸到纳努塔拉和亨利河下游；贾伦迪、吉尼古迪拉等地方群体都是他们的支派。他们的语言属帕马—牛雅语系的坎亚拉语支，既不行割礼，也不行下切礼。1618年7月，威廉·扬松随荷兰商船毛里求斯号测绘了他们的河口，将其标为“威廉河”；1627年黑塞尔·海里茨把它印入海图，这是最早进入欧洲地图的澳大利亚西海岸地理特征之一。他们在更南边埃克斯茅斯湾的活动，则被视为一次较晚迁徙留下的痕迹。

en: The Tharawal, also written Dharawal, are the Aboriginal Australian clans who shared the Dharawal language along the coast south of Sydney, their country running from the southern shore of Botany Bay and the Georges River through Wollongong to the Shoalhaven River; the name itself means cabbage palm. Clans included the Gweagal, the Fire Clan of the Botany Bay shore, and the Wadi Wadi of the Five Islands off Port Kembla, while the Shoalhaven groups were the ancestors of the present-day Jerrinja. They ground the treated seeds of the burrawang cycad into flour cakes, fished from bark canoes and carved sandstone engravings of whales and wallabies, and whales and dolphins held special totem status. In 1770 James Cook made his first landing on the Australian east coast in Gweagal country at Botany Bay, where two men opposed the landing boats with spears until musket fire drove them back, the opening encounter of the region's colonial history.
zh: 塔拉瓦尔人（又拼达拉瓦尔）是共用达拉瓦尔语的澳大利亚原住民氏族，居住在悉尼以南的海岸，领地从植物湾南岸和乔治斯河经伍伦贡延伸到肖尔黑文河；族名本义为甘蓝棕榈。主要氏族包括植物湾沿岸的“火之氏族”格韦加尔人、肯布拉港外五岛的瓦迪瓦迪人，而肖尔黑文一带的群体正是今天杰林贾人的先祖。他们把去毒处理后的布拉旺泽米铁种子磨粉烤成饼，乘树皮独木舟捕鱼，并在砂岩上刻出鲸鱼和沙袋鼠图案，鲸鱼与海豚在他们的图腾中地位特殊。1770年，詹姆斯·库克在格韦加尔人的土地上、即植物湾首次登上澳大利亚东海岸，两名男子掷矛阻拦登陆艇，最终被火枪射击逼退，这是该地区殖民史的开端。

en: The Tharu are the indigenous people of the Terai, the marshy forest belt along the southern foot of the Himalayas. The Persian chronicle Tabaqat-i Nasiri already lists them with the Koch and the Mech as inhabitants of the country between Gauda and Tibet in 1205, and Alberuni places them in the eastern Terai as early as the tenth century. They are split into many endogamous groups, among them the Rana, Kathariya, Dangaura and Kochila, each settled along a different stretch of the plains, and they speak Indo-Aryan Tharu dialects. Their villages combined settled rice cultivation with forest gathering, and their religion centred on a host of forest deities beneath a growing Hindu influence. The Rana Tharu of the far west claim descent from Rajputs who took refuge in the Terai forests in the sixteenth century. After the Gorkha unification of Nepal in the late eighteenth century, land grants to the hill elite turned many Tharu into bonded Kamaiya labourers on their own former lands.
zh: 塔鲁人是特莱沼泽林带的原住民，这片林带沿喜马拉雅山南麓延伸。波斯史籍《塔巴加特—伊·纳西里》在1205年已把他们与库奇人、梅奇人并列为高达与西藏之间地区的居民；比鲁尼则早在10世纪就提到他们生活在东特莱。塔鲁人分为许多实行内婚制的支系，包括拉纳、卡塔里亚、当高拉和科奇拉等，各据平原的一段，讲印度雅利安语系的塔鲁方言。他们的村落把定居稻作与山林采集结合起来，信仰以众多森林神祇为中心，同时长期受到印度教影响。远西的拉纳·塔鲁人自称是16世纪避入特莱森林的拉杰普特人后裔。18世纪末廓尔喀统一尼泊尔后，山地贵族获得特莱封地，许多塔鲁人在自己昔日的土地上沦为卡迈亚债奴。

en: The Tickanwatic are the Tonkawa, whose autonym Tickanwa•tic means the real people; the familiar name Tonkawa comes from a Waco word meaning they all stay together. Their own tongue was a language isolate, unlike any neighboring speech. In 1601 they lived in northwestern Oklahoma as a loose confederation of related bands, nomadic hunters who also tended small gardens, and around the late seventeenth century they drifted south into central Texas. Apache and Wichita pressure had pushed them as far as the Red River by 1700, and European diseases and warfare reduced them from perhaps nineteen hundred people in the sixteenth century to about sixteen hundred. In the 1740s some bands settled around the short-lived San Gabriel missions, and in 1758 the Tonkawa joined Caddo, Wichita, Comanche and other allies in destroying the Lipan Apache mission of San Sabá. Continuing into Texas, they later reversed their old enmity and became allies of the Lipan, and by the 1820s they were camped on the Colorado River near the first Anglo-American colonies, whose settlers soon clashed with them over stolen livestock and corn.
zh: 蒂坎瓦蒂克人即通卡瓦人，Tickanwa•tic 是他们的自称，意为“真正的人”；“通卡瓦”这个常见名称来自维科语，意思是“他们总待在一起”。他们的本族语言是一门与周边语言都不相同的孤立语。1601年时，他们生活在今俄克拉荷马州西北部，是由若干亲缘群体组成的松散联盟，以游猎为生，也照料小片园圃；约在17世纪末，他们向南迁入得克萨斯中部。到1700年，在阿帕奇人和维希塔人的挤压下，他们已退到雷德河一线；欧洲人的疫病和连绵战事使其人口从16世纪的约一千九百人减少到约一千六百人。1740年代，部分群体定居在存在时间不长的圣加布里埃尔传教站一带；1758年，通卡瓦人联合卡多人、维希塔人、科曼切人等盟友，摧毁了利潘阿帕奇人的圣萨瓦传教站。他们继续深入得克萨斯，后来还化解旧怨与利潘人结盟；到1820年代，他们已在科罗拉多河畔、最早的英美殖民点附近扎营，而殖民者很快就因牲畜和玉米被盗与他们发生冲突。

en: The Tidore are the people of Tidore Island, off the western coast of Halmahera, and of neighbouring parts of Halmahera itself. They speak Tidore, a non-Austronesian North Halmahera language closely related to Ternate and used as a lingua franca in central Halmahera; both tongues were already being written in the late fifteenth century, the only indigenous literary traditions of their kind in the region. Their rulers, titled Kië ma-kolano, Ruler of the Mountain, headed a realm also called Duko, counted among the four kingdoms of Maluku and traced by local tradition to an eleventh-century kingship. Islam became the state religion in the late fifteenth century under Sultan Jamaluddin, and Sultan al-Mansur received the first Portuguese visitors in 1512. Rivalry with Ternate drove the Tidore into alliance with Spain, while their suzerainty ran over southern Halmahera, the Raja Ampat islands and western Papua. Spain withdrew in 1663, leaving Tidore within the Dutch orbit; in 1780 a treaty reduced it to a Dutch vassal, provoking Prince Nuku's thirty-year revolt, which briefly restored Tidorese power after 1797 before the Dutch retook the island in 1806.
zh: 蒂多雷人是蒂多雷岛及邻近哈马黑拉部分地区的居民。他们操蒂多雷语，这是一种与特尔纳特语近亲的非南岛北哈马黑拉语言，在中哈马黑拉一带充当通用语；它与特尔纳特语早在15世纪末已有文字记录，是当地仅有的两个拥有前殖民本土书面传统的非南岛语言。其君主号称“山之主”基耶·马科拉诺，王国又称杜科，位列马鲁古四大王国，当地传说将王统追溯到11世纪。15世纪末，贾马卢丁苏丹在位时伊斯兰教被定为国教；1512年，曼苏尔苏丹接待了首批葡萄牙来客。与特尔纳特的争霸促使蒂多雷与西班牙结盟，其宗主权则覆盖哈马黑拉南部、拉贾安帕特群岛和巴布亚西部。1663年西班牙人撤走，蒂多雷转入荷兰势力范围；1780年的条约把它降为荷兰附庸，激起努库亲王长达三十年的起义，1797年后蒂多雷一度重振，但荷兰人于1806年重新占领该岛。

en: The Tidung are the indigenous people of the forested northeast coast of Borneo, around the Sesayap and Sibuku rivers, Tarakan Island and the Tawau coast, in what is now North Kalimantan and Sabah. Their name means “hill people” in their own tongue, and they speak a North Bornean language belonging to the Murutic group, once written in the Jawi script. They began as hill Dayak communities of slash-and-burn farmers and coastal fishermen, and from at least the eleventh century the region was organised under the Tidung Kingdom, which may originally have been a tribal confederacy. Conversion to Islam between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, alongside contact with the Sultanate of Sulu, turned them into a self-consciously Muslim, Malayised people who called themselves Islam Dayak. The ancient period ended in 1557, when Queen Ikenawai married Radja Laoet from Sulu and a new Islamic dynasty, the Kalkan or Tenggara line, centred itself on Tarakan. Through the eighteenth century the Tidung kingdom, paired with the neighbouring Sultanate of Bulungan, ranked among the chief powers of northeast Borneo, controlling river mouths and the sea trade in forest and sea produce.
zh: 缇洞人是婆罗洲东北沿海森林地带的原住民，活动于塞萨亚普河、西布库河、打拉根岛和斗湖沿岸一带，即今印尼北加里曼丹与马来西亚沙巴接壤处。他们的自称意为“山地人”，语言属北婆罗洲语群中的穆鲁特语族，过去曾用爪夷文书写。缇洞人最初是经营刀耕火种的山地达雅社群，也有沿海渔民；最迟从11世纪起，当地形成了缇洞王国，其早期形态可能只是部落联盟。15至16世纪，在苏禄苏丹国影响下他们改宗伊斯兰教，逐渐成为自觉的穆斯林化、马来化民族，自称“穆斯林达雅”。古代时期在1557年结束：女王伊克娜瓦伊嫁给来自苏禄的拉惹·劳厄特，新的伊斯兰王朝卡尔坎（又称登加拉王朝）在打拉根建立统治中心。整个18世纪，缇洞王国与邻近的布隆岸苏丹国并称婆罗洲东北的两大势力，控制各河口以及林产品与海产的海上贸易。

en: The Tigre are the Semitic-speaking pastoralists of the arid lowlands, northern escarpments and Red Sea coast of Eritrea, around Massawa, Agordat and the Dahlak islands, with kindred groups across the border in Sudan. The name is a linguistic umbrella rather than a single lineage: it covers clans such as the Bet Asgede, Mensa', Marya and Beni-Amer who came to share the Tigre language, an Ethiopian Semitic tongue related to Ge'ez and Tigrinya, and in several of their societies the word tigre itself originally meant a tributary serf class. Arab Muslims reached the Dahlak islands as early as the eighth century and a Dahlak sultanate dominated the coastal trade in the twelfth and thirteenth, while the inland pastoral groups long kept a mixture of local Christian and ancestral custom. From the sixteenth century their grazing lands became a frontier pressed between the Ethiopian highland kingdom, the Funj sultanate of Sennar and the Ottoman garrisons of the coast. In the later eighteenth century the Na'ib family of Hergigo, governing as Ottoman deputies, made itself overlord of the Tigre-speaking clans, and from the 1820s Egyptian expansion and the preaching of the Khatmiyya Sufi order began the rapid spread of Islam that would make most Tigre Sunni Muslims.
zh: 提格雷人是生活在厄立特里亚干旱低地、北部悬崖地带和红海沿岸（马萨瓦、阿科达特、达赫拉克群岛一带）的说闪米特语的游牧民，在苏丹境内也有亲缘群体。“提格雷”是语言上的统称而非单一部族：它涵盖贝特阿斯格德、门萨、马里亚、贝尼阿米尔等逐渐共用提格雷语的氏族；提格雷语属埃塞俄比亚闪米特语，与吉兹语、提格利尼亚语同源，而在他们的若干社会里，“提格雷”一词本指纳贡的农奴阶层。阿拉伯穆斯林早在8世纪就抵达达赫拉克群岛，12至13世纪达赫拉克苏丹国控制了沿海贸易，内陆游牧群体则长期保留着当地基督教与本土习俗混合的信仰。16世纪起，他们的牧场成为埃塞俄比亚高原王国、森纳尔丰吉苏丹国和沿海奥斯曼驻军之间反复争夺的边疆。18世纪后期，以奥斯曼代理人身份统治赫尔吉戈的纳伊布家族成为提格雷各氏族的宗主；从19世纪20年代起，埃及的扩张和哈特米苏菲教团的传道推动伊斯兰教迅速传播，使多数提格雷人成为逊尼派穆斯林。

en: The Tigrinya are the Orthodox Christian highlanders of the northern Ethiopian and Eritrean plateau, farming the long-settled districts around Aksum, Adwa and Shire on one side of the Mareb River and Hamasien, Seraye and Akele Guzai, the country of Asmara and Yeha, on the other. Their homeland was the heartland of the ancient Kingdom of Aksum, which adopted Christianity in the fourth century, and after Ge'ez ceased to be a spoken vernacular its place was taken by Tigrinya, whose earliest surviving samples appear in a thirteenth-century monastic land grant. Medieval Arab geographers already knew the region as the Christian province of Tigri, and under the restored Solomonic dynasty after 1270 its provinces kept strong local lords: Emperor Amda Seyon had to subdue the defiant ruler of Enderta in the 1320s, while the monk Ewostatewos founded a reform movement whose followers spread monasteries across the Eritrean highlands in the later fourteenth century. From the mid-fifteenth century Emperor Zara Yaqob grouped the northern districts under the Bahr Negash, the ruler of the semi-autonomous province of Medri Bahri. The highlanders suffered in the Adal invasion of 1529 to 1543 and lost their Red Sea ports to the Ottomans in 1557, yet their ancient church network, centered on Aksum and its rock-hewn monasteries, kept Tigrinya identity and literacy intact through the age of rival princes.
zh: 提格利尼亚人是埃塞俄比亚北部和厄立特里亚高原上信奉东正教的山民，在马雷布河一侧耕作于阿克苏姆、阿杜瓦、希雷等开发悠久的地区，另一侧则聚居于哈马西恩、塞拉耶、阿克莱古扎伊（阿斯马拉、叶哈一带）。他们的故土是古代阿克苏姆王国的核心，该国于4世纪皈依基督教；吉兹语不再作为口语后，提格利尼亚语承接其位，现存最早的语料见于13世纪的修道院地契。中世纪阿拉伯地理学家已把这一地区称作基督教的“蒂格里”省。1270年所罗门王朝复辟后，北方各省仍保有强势的地方领主：阿姆达·塞约恩皇帝在14世纪20年代平定了恩德尔塔的割据者，修士埃沃斯塔特沃斯则发起改革运动，其追随者在14世纪后期把修道院网络铺满厄立特里亚高原。15世纪中期，扎拉·雅各布皇帝把北方诸区划归巴赫里·纳加什统辖，即半自治的梅德里·巴赫里省。1529至1543年阿达尔入侵使山民深受其苦，1557年红海港口又落入奥斯曼之手，但以阿克苏姆和岩洞修道院为中心的古老教会网络，使提格利尼亚人的身份认同和文字传统在群雄并起的年代得以保全。

en: The Tillamook are the southernmost of the Coast Salish peoples, living on the Oregon coast from Tillamook Head south to Cape Foulweather and the crest of the Coast Range, in independent village groups around Tillamook and Nehalem bays and the Siletz, Nestucca and Salmon rivers. Their name is a Chinook word for the people of the village of Nehalem. Salmon was the staple of their economy, dried and ground into meal for year-round use, and they were skilled basket-makers living in large plank houses. Franz Boas noted that their customs, including guardian-spirit quests and arranged marriages, differed from other Salish groups and showed strong influence from northern California, and their Thunderbird and Whale myth preserves the memory of the great Cascadia earthquake of 1700. Robert Gray's mate Robert Haswell made the first recorded contact in 1788, and the Lewis and Clark Expedition wintered nearby in 1805 and counted roughly 2,200 Tillamook. Smallpox epidemics in 1824 and 1829 devastated the villages, after which their numbers fell steeply.
zh: 蒂拉穆克人是海岸萨利什诸族中分布最南的一支，住在俄勒冈海岸，北起蒂拉穆克角，南抵福尔韦瑟角和海岸山脉山脊，以蒂拉穆克湾、尼哈勒姆湾以及锡莱茨河、内斯塔卡河、萨尔蒙河一带的独立村落群为家。他们的名字是奇努克语中对尼哈勒姆村居民的称呼。鲑鱼是经济支柱，人们把鲑鱼晾干磨成粉以供全年食用；他们擅长编篮，住大型木板房屋。人类学家弗朗茨·博厄斯注意到，他们的习俗（包括守护灵求索和包办婚姻）与其他萨利什群体不同，明显受北加利福尼亚部落影响；他们的雷鸟与鲸鱼神话还保存着对1700年卡斯卡迪亚大地震的记忆。1788年，罗伯特·格雷船上的大副罗伯特·哈斯韦尔首次与他们接触，1805年刘易斯与克拉克探险队在附近过冬，估计蒂拉穆克人约有2200人。1824年和1829年的天花重创了各个村落，人口从此急剧下降。

en: The Timanae were an indigenous people of the Upper Magdalena valley in what is now the Colombian department of Huila, settled along the Timaná River and the right bank of the Magdalena down to the mouth of the Suaza. The Jesuit Juan de Velasco placed their lands between the Paez to the west and the Andaquí to the east, and chroniclers name the caciques Inando, Pionza, Añolongo, Meco and Timano alongside the cacica Gaitana. Some scholars assign their language to the Chibchan family, though the evidence is too thin for a firm classification. In 1539 and 1540 Gaitana led the peoples of the Upper Magdalena in armed risings against the Spanish conquest, a resistance remembered long after the Timanae themselves were absorbed into the colonial population.
zh: 蒂马纳埃人是生活在今哥伦比亚乌伊拉省境内马格达莱纳河上游谷地的原住民，聚居于蒂马纳河沿岸以及马格达莱纳河右岸直至苏阿萨河河口一带。耶稣会士胡安·德·贝拉斯科把他们的领地记在西部派斯人与东部安达基人之间，编年史家还记下了伊南多、皮翁萨、阿尼奥隆戈、梅科、蒂马诺等酋长以及女酋长盖塔娜的名字。有学者把他们的语言归入奇布查语系，但证据不足以定论。1539至1540年，盖塔娜率领马格达莱纳河上游诸部起兵反抗西班牙征服；在蒂马纳埃人本身被殖民社会同化之后，这场抵抗仍长期流传。

en: The Timbira are a cluster of related Jê peoples of northern and northeastern Brazil, including the Apinajé, Krahô, Canela, Gavião, Krinkatí and Pukobyê, who speak Timbira dialects of the Macro-Jê trunk and often call themselves Mehím. Their name may come from a Tupi word meaning the tied ones, after the woven straw and cotton bands they wear on foreheads, arms and ankles. Their homelands run from the Parnaíba valley in Piauí west across the Maranhão cerrado to the Tocantins, combining farming villages with hunting and gathering. Contact with Portuguese colonists began in the eighteenth century: in 1728 a large Timbira force raided Oeiras, then capital of the Piauí captaincy, but cattle ranches spreading north from Bahia steadily drove them west of the Parnaíba, and by the second half of the century none remained east of the river. In northern Maranhão rice and cotton planters hunted them for slaves, and a royal charter of 1811 legalized the enslavement of resisting Indians on the Tocantins and Araguaia, opening the bloodiest phase of their conquest in the 1810s and 1820s.
zh: 廷比拉人是巴西北部和东北部一组彼此亲缘的热语族群总称，包括阿皮纳热人、克拉霍人、卡内拉人、加维昂人、克林卡蒂人和普科比埃人等，说大热语系的廷比拉方言，许多群体自称梅欣。其名称可能来自图皮语，意为“被绑缚的人”，源于他们缠在额头、手臂和脚踝上的草编或棉织饰带。他们的家园从皮奥伊的帕纳伊巴河谷向西穿过马拉尼昂的塞拉多稀树草原，一直延伸到托坎廷斯，过着农耕村落与狩猎采集相结合的生活。与葡萄牙殖民者的接触始于18世纪：1728年，一支强大的廷比拉武装袭击了当时皮奥伊都督区的首府奥埃拉斯；但从巴伊亚向北扩张的牧场不断把他们向西驱赶，到该世纪下半叶，帕纳伊巴河以东已无廷比拉人。在马拉尼昂北部，水稻和棉花种植园大肆猎捕他们为奴，1811年的一份王室特许状更允许奴役托坎廷斯河和阿拉瓜亚河流域敢于抵抗的印第安人，使19世纪10至20年代成为征服他们最血腥的阶段。

en: The Timbisha, whose name means 'rock paint' and who were once widely called the Panamint Shoshone, have held the Death Valley country of south-eastern California, from Saline Valley to the Amargosa, for more than a thousand years. They speak a Central Numic tongue of the Uto-Aztecan family, carried into the Great Basin by the Numic expansion of the 1300s, and were divided into small districts of family bands, each led by a headman and named after its principal spring-side village. In one of the driest lands of the continent they lived on mesquite, pine nuts and wild seeds, moving between seasonal camps with their woven baskets; long before any European entered the valley, Coso obsidian from their hills travelled the trade trails to coastal peoples such as the Chumash.
zh: 廷比沙人意为“岩画之人”，旧称帕纳明特休休尼人，千余年来一直据有加利福尼亚东南部的死亡谷地区，领地从萨林谷延伸到阿马戈萨一带。他们的语言属犹他—阿兹特克语系的中努米克语支，是14世纪努米克人大扩散时带入大盆地的。他们分成若干以家族为单位的小地区群，各有首领，以主要的泉畔村落命名。在这片北美最干旱的土地上，他们以牧豆、松子和野籽为生，带着编织的篮子在季节性营地间迁徙；早在欧洲人进入死亡谷之前，他们山区出产的科索黑曜石就沿商路传到楚马什人等沿海部族手中。

en: The Timiscaming are the Anishinaabe bands of Lake Timiskaming, where the Ottawa River bends on its long course from the height of land toward the Saint Lawrence. Algonquin-speaking hunters and trappers, related to the Nipissing and Odawa, they camped and fished around the lake's narrows and the Kipawa River, and their meeting place at Obadjiwan Point, the strait where the current flows, commanded the main canoe route linking Hudson Bay with Montreal, roughly the midpoint of a forty-day journey by way of Moose Factory and the Abitibi River. The French war party marching against the English bay forts used this route in 1686, and about 1679 Montreal traders had already built a post on the lake, which the Iroquois destroyed in 1688. French merchants returned in 1720 to found Fort Témiscamingue at the old Obadjiwan encampment, drawing the local bands into the fur trade as guides, canoe men and trappers. After the conquest of New France the post passed to independent traders, then to the North West Company in 1788 and the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821.
zh: 蒂米斯卡明人是蒂米斯卡明湖一带的阿尼希纳贝群队；渥太华河在此从分水岭附近折向圣劳伦斯河。他们是操阿尔冈金语的猎人和诱捕者，与尼皮辛人和奥达瓦人有亲缘关系，在湖的狭口和基帕瓦河周围营地捕鱼；他们在“奥巴吉万角”——意为“水流穿过的海峡”——的聚会点，扼守着连接哈得孙湾与蒙特利尔的独木舟主干道，走穆斯工厂和阿比蒂比河那条四十天水路，这里大约是中途站。1686年远征英国海湾堡垒的法国战队就取道这条路线；约1679年，蒙特利尔商人已在湖边建起商站，但在1688年被易洛魁人摧毁。法国商人1720年又在奥巴吉万旧营地设立蒂米斯卡明堡，把当地群队以向导、独木舟手和诱捕者的身份拉入毛皮贸易。新法兰西沦陷后，该商站先由独立商人接手，1788年归西北公司，1821年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en: The Timucua were the largest Indigenous people of northeast and north-central Florida and southeast Georgia, spread across some 35 chiefdoms that never formed a single polity. Their territory ran from the Altamaha River in Georgia to Lake George in central Florida, and their language, recorded in ten dialects, is unusually well documented thanks to the grammar and catechisms written in the seventeenth century by the Franciscan Francisco Pareja. Contact began early: Juan Ponce de León may have met Timucua groups in 1513, and in 1539 Hernando de Soto's army marched through their western villages and executed some 200 people at Napituca. French Huguenots built Fort Caroline among the Saturiwa Timucua in 1564, but the Spanish under Pedro Menéndez de Avilés destroyed it the next year and founded St. Augustine, from which missions were planted across the chiefdoms. Eurasian epidemics cut the population from an estimated 200,000 at contact to about 50,000 by 1595 and roughly 1,000 by 1700. Carolinian slave raids led by James Moore in 1703 killed or enslaved hundreds more; by 1759 only six Timucua adults remained under Spanish protection, and when Spain ceded Florida to Britain in 1763 the fewer than 100 survivors were taken to Cuba.
zh: 蒂穆夸人是佛罗里达东北部、中北部和佐治亚东南部最大的原住民族群，分散在约35个酋邦之中，从未组成统一政权。其领地北起佐治亚的奥尔塔马霍河，南抵佛罗里达中部的乔治湖；他们的语言有十种方言的记录，得益于17世纪方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·帕雷哈撰写的语法书和教理问答，蒂穆夸语的文献在同时期印第安语言中异常丰富。与欧洲人的接触开始得很早：1513年胡安·庞塞·德莱昂可能就遇到了蒂穆夸诸部；1539年埃尔南多·德·索托的军队穿过他们西部的村庄，并在纳皮图卡处决了约200人。1564年法国胡格诺派在萨图里瓦部的蒂穆夸人中修建卡罗琳堡，次年佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯率西班牙人将其摧毁并建立圣奥古斯丁，随后传教站遍布各酋邦。欧亚大陆传来的瘟疫使人口从接触之初估计的20万锐减到1595年的约5万，到1700年只剩约1000人。1703年詹姆斯·摩尔率领的卡罗来纳奴隶劫掠又杀死或掳走数百人；到1759年，受西班牙保护的蒂穆夸成年人仅剩六人。1763年西班牙把佛罗里达割让给英国时，不足百名幸存者被带往古巴。

en: The Tindé, better known as the Jicarilla Apache, are one of the Eastern Apache bands and speak a Southern Athabaskan language of the Na-dené family. Their Spanish name means little basket, after their sealed drinking baskets, while neighboring Apache called them Kinya-Inde, people of the fixed houses, because they lived more settled lives than most Apache. Traditionally they ranged the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and the plains of southern Colorado and northern New Mexico, pushing out onto the Great Plains before 1525; from the Pueblo peoples they learned farming and pottery, and they are linked archaeologically to the Dismal River culture of the western plains. Their year moved between river-bottom fields, hunting grounds and wild-plant gathering sites. From the early eighteenth century they were squeezed between the expanding colony of New Spain and raiding Comanche, who drove many Apache bands southward and began a long period of displacement and warfare on the southern plains.
zh: 廷德人即更为人熟知的希卡里亚阿帕奇人，是东阿帕奇诸支系之一，操纳-德内语系的南阿萨巴斯卡语。他们的西班牙语名字意为“小篮子”，源自其密封的饮水篮；邻近的阿帕奇支系则称他们为 Kinya-Inde，即“住固定房屋的人”，因为他们比多数阿帕奇人过着更定居的生活。其传统活动范围是桑格雷-德克里斯托山脉以及科罗拉多州南部、新墨西哥州北部的平原，早在1525年以前便已深入大平原；他们从普韦布洛人那里学会了农耕和制陶，考古上还与西部平原的迪斯默尔河文化有关。他们一年中往返于河畔农田、猎场和野生植物采集地之间。18世纪初起，他们被扩张的新西班牙殖民地和袭扰的科曼切人两面挤压，许多阿帕奇群体被迫南移，南部平原由此进入长期的流徙与战乱。

en: The Tinputz are the people of the Tinputz area on the northeast coast of Bougainville Island in eastern Papua New Guinea. Their language is an Austronesian tongue of the Northwest Solomonic group, closely related to neighbouring Saposa, Teop and Hahon, rather than a Papuan language.
zh: 廷普茨人居住在巴布亚新几内亚东部布干维尔岛东北岸的廷普茨地区。他们的语言属南岛语系西北所罗门语群，与邻近的萨波萨语、特奥普语和哈洪语关系密切，并非巴布亚语言。

en: The Tionontati, whose name means “people of the place where the mountain stands,” were an Iroquoian people whose country lay southwest of Wendake, along the Niagara Escarpment south of Georgian Bay; the French called them the Petun, or Tobacco people, for the crop they raised and traded. Organised as a confederacy of the Wolf and Deer nations, they held eight or nine palisaded longhouse villages, including Etharita, and numbered perhaps eight thousand before contact, falling to about three thousand after the epidemics of 1634 to 1640. Samuel de Champlain visited them in 1616, and their language was mutually intelligible with that of their Wendat kin, a day’s journey to the northeast. In 1649, having destroyed Wendake, the Dutch-armed Haudenosaunee overran the Petun towns in the Beaver Wars. The survivors joined Wendat and Wenro refugees among the Odawa on Manitoulin Island, and this coalescence became the Wyandot, who settled at Michilimackinac in 1671, near Detroit in 1701, and later spread into the Ohio Country.
zh: 提奥农塔特人的名字意为“山岳之地的人”，是一支易洛魁语民族，故土在温达克西南、乔治亚湾以南的尼亚加拉崖沿线；因为种植和交易烟草，法国人称之为佩腾，即烟草人。他们按狼、鹿两个民族组成联盟，拥有包括埃塔里塔在内的八九座围有木栅栏的长屋村镇，与欧洲人接触前人口约八千，经过1634年至1640年的疫病后降到约三千。1616年萨缪尔·德·尚普兰曾到访他们那里；他们与东北方仅一日路程的温达特人语言相通、习俗相近。1649年，得到荷兰火器的易洛魁联盟在摧毁温达克后，又于海狸战争中攻陷佩腾人的村镇。幸存者与温达特、温罗难民一同投奔马尼图林岛的奥达瓦人，融合形成怀安多特人，于1671年定居米基利马基诺，1701年迁到底特律附近，后来又散布到俄亥俄地区。

en: The Tiou, also written Tioux, were a Tunica-speaking people of the lower Mississippi Valley whose ancestors had lived further upriver until the collapse of the Mississippian chiefdoms in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Together with the Grigra they were adopted into the Natchez tribe and became one of its village districts, keeping their own settlement on lower St. Catherine's Creek beside the Grand Village of the Natchez in present-day Mississippi. French observers counted the Tioux village among the districts friendly to the French, in contrast to hostile villages such as White Apple. When the Natchez revolt of 1729 to 1731 ended in the destruction of the chiefdom, several hundred Natchez were shipped to Caribbean sugar plantations as slaves and the surviving villagers scattered among the Chickasaw, Muscogee and Cherokee; the Tiou disappeared from the records as a distinct group, merged into the Natchez refugees and their hosts.
zh: 提乌人又作图乌人，是密西西比河下游说图尼卡语的族群，其先民本住在更靠上游的地方，16至17世纪密西西比诸酋邦崩溃后才沿河而下。他们与格里格拉人一同被纳奇兹部落接纳，成为其村落分区之一，在今天密西西比州境内圣凯瑟琳溪下游、紧邻纳奇兹大村的地方保有自己的村落。法国观察家把提乌村算作对法友好的分区，与白苹果等敌对村落形成对比。1729至1731年的纳奇兹起义以酋邦覆灭告终，数百名纳奇兹人被运往加勒比甘蔗种植园为奴，幸存村民四散投奔奇克索人、马斯科吉人和切罗基人；提乌人作为独立群体从此不见于记载，融入纳奇兹难民及其收留者之中。

en: The Tiri are a Kanak people of the south-central coast of Grande Terre in New Caledonia, living within the Xârâcùù customary region of the South Province. Their Oceanic language, also called Tinrin or Mea, splits into Tiri proper and Mea dialects and belongs to the New Caledonian branch of the Austronesian family. The first settlers of Grande Terre were Lapita potters, who arrived around 1000 BC and whose culture underlies later Kanak societies, where each valley lived under its own clans without any island-wide chiefdom. James Cook landed on the island in 1774 and named it New Caledonia, becoming the first European to reach the Tiri homeland, though no European settlement followed in that period.
zh: 蒂里人是新喀里多尼亚大特雷岛中南部沿海的卡纳克族群，住在南部省的沙拉库习惯法区域内。他们的大洋洲语族语言又称廷林语或梅阿语，分蒂里本部和梅阿两个方言，属南岛语系新喀里多尼亚语支。大特雷岛最早的居民是约公元前1000年抵达的拉皮塔陶工，其文化构成后来卡纳克社会的底子；各山谷由自己的氏族治理，岛上并无统一的酋邦。1774年詹姆斯·库克登岛，借用苏格兰的古名将其命名为新喀里多尼亚，成为第一个抵达蒂里人家园的欧洲人，但此后一段时期并无欧洲人前来定居。

en: The Tises were a small people of the northern Costa Rican lowlands between the Kutris and Frio rivers, who at the Spanish arrival in the sixteenth century belonged to the Botos chiefdom, tributary to Garabito, king of the western Huetar. They shared their neighbours' Intermediate Area culture and probably spoke a Chibchan tongue, but little else is recorded of them.
zh: 蒂塞斯人是哥斯达黎加北部低地的小族，住在库特里斯河与弗里奥河之间，16世纪西班牙人到来时隶属向西部韦塔尔国王加拉维托纳贡的博托斯酋邦。他们与邻族同属美洲中间区文化，语言很可能属奇布查语系，此外史籍所载甚少。

en: The Tiwa, called Lalung in the Assamese chronicles, are a Tibeto-Burman people of central Assam and the adjoining Meghalaya hills, divided into hill and plains branches. Their own traditions remember a migration westward from the upper Brahmaputra, crossing the river toward Nagaon, and their language belongs with Deori and Kokborok to the Boro-Garo group of Kachari speech; it has no script of its own. In the seventeenth century Ahom chronicles note Lalung families settling in the plains alongside the Karbi. Tiwa life centred on the small principality of Gobha, whose Tiwa raja mediated trade between the plains and the Jaintia kingdom. The Gobha ruler accepted Ahom overlordship under Jayadhwaj Singha in 1659, and Gobha later served Rudra Singha as a base for his invasion of Jaintia. A Tiwa attempt to throw off Ahom rule under Siva Singha was suppressed, and during the Moamaria rebellion the area fell back under Jaintia control.
zh: 蒂瓦人在阿萨姆编年史中被称为拉隆，是藏缅语族群，分布在阿萨姆中部和毗邻的梅加拉亚丘陵，分为山地与平原两支。他们的传说记得先祖从布拉马普特拉河上游西迁，渡河前往纳冈；蒂瓦语与代奥里语、科克博罗克语同属卡查里语的博多—加罗语支，没有本族文字。17世纪的阿洪编年史已记载拉隆家族与米基尔家族在平原定居。蒂瓦人的生活以戈巴小邦为中心，其统治者出自蒂瓦氏族，在平原与贾因蒂亚王国之间居间贸易。1659年戈巴统治者向阿洪国王贾亚德瓦杰·辛哈称臣，后来戈巴又成为鲁德拉·辛哈入侵贾因蒂亚的基地。蒂瓦人在西巴·辛哈时期试图摆脱阿洪统治但被镇压，莫阿马里亚叛乱期间这一地区重新落入贾因蒂亚人之手。

en: The Tlaxcaltecs are a Nahua people of the Puebla–Tlaxcala Valley, east of the Valley of Mexico. Their ancestors counted themselves among the seven Nahuatlaca tribes that tradition says came out of Chicomoztoc; after a failed settlement at Poyauhtlan on Lake Texcoco around 1290, they moved east into the valley later named Tlaxcala, absorbing Otomi and Pinome villagers already living there. By the fourteenth century they had built Tlaxcallan, a confederation of four altepetl — Tepeticpac, Ocotelolco, Tizatlan and Quiahuiztlan — ruled not by one king but by a council of its four lords, which scholars often call a republic. Surrounded by the Mexica Triple Alliance, Tlaxcala kept its independence through more than sixty years of trade blockade and repeated flower wars. In 1519 it allied with Hernán Cortés and supplied the largest indigenous contingent in the 1521 conquest of Tenochtitlan. The crown rewarded it with rare privileges: in 1534 its governor Maxixcatzin was received by Charles V, and Tlaxcala won its own coat of arms, tax exemption and direct royal jurisdiction. From 1591 Tlaxcaltec families were sent north as model colonists among the Chichimecas, founding towns such as San Esteban de Nueva Tlaxcala beside Saltillo, while others had marched with Pedro de Alvarado into Guatemala between 1524 and 1527.
zh: 特拉斯卡拉人是生活在墨西哥谷以东普埃布拉—特拉斯卡拉谷地的纳瓦人。他们的祖先自认为是传说中出自七洞之地奇科莫斯特克的七大纳瓦特拉卡部族之一；约1290年，他们在特斯科科湖畔的波亚乌特兰立足失败后东迁，进入后来得名特拉斯卡拉的谷地，并融合了当地已有的奥托米人和皮诺梅人村落。到14世纪，他们建立了特拉斯卡拉邦联，由特佩蒂克帕克、奥科特洛尔科、蒂萨特兰和基亚维斯特兰四个阿尔特佩特尔组成；邦联不立独王，而由四城领主议事会治理，学者常称之为共和国。特拉斯卡拉被墨西加三联盟团团围住，在六十多年的贸易封锁和连绵的花之战中保持了独立。1519年，它与埃尔南·科尔特斯结盟，并为1521年攻克特诺奇蒂特兰提供了人数最多的土著盟军。西班牙王室回报以罕见特权：1534年其首领马克西克斯卡钦获查理五世接见，特拉斯卡拉赢得自己的纹章、免税待遇和直属于王室的司法地位。1591年起，特拉斯卡拉人家庭被派往北方，作为归化奇奇梅克人的模范殖民者，在萨尔蒂略旁建立了圣埃斯特万·德努埃瓦特拉斯卡拉等城镇；另一些人则在1524至1527年随佩德罗·德阿尔瓦拉多进军危地马拉。

en: The Tlicho, better known in English as the Dogrib, are a Dene people whose Athabaskan language belongs to the Na-Dene family. Their homeland lies between Great Slave Lake and Great Bear Lake in the boreal forest of the Northwest Territories, around the lakes now called Whatì, Gamèti and Wekweètì. Their own name, Tłı̨chǫ Done or Dog-Flank People, refers to a legendary descent from a supernatural dog-man. They lived in small mobile bands, following the barren-ground caribou herds on the edge of the tundra and fishing through the ice in winter, travelling by canoe, snowshoe and dog sled. The fur trade reached Great Slave Lake in the late eighteenth century, when the North West Company built Fort Providence in 1789, and the Tlicho began trading alongside neighbouring Dene groups. Long-standing rivalry with the Yellowknives, who dominated the early trade and raided their camps, turned in their favour when the Dogrib all but destroyed the Yellowknives in the 1830s; the survivors scattered or married into Tlicho bands. They also guided and supplied British expeditions, including John Franklin's winter post of Fort Franklin on Great Bear Lake in 1825.
zh: 特里乔人在英文资料中常称多格里布人，是德内人的一支，其阿萨巴斯卡语属于纳-德内语系。他们的家园位于今加拿大西北地区大奴湖与大熊湖之间的北方针叶林，环湖一带即今天的瓦蒂、加梅蒂和韦克韦蒂等地。其自称“特里乔·多内”意为“狗肋人”，得名于祖先为超自然犬人的传说。他们以流动的小群体为生，在苔原边缘追随瘠地驯鹿群，冬季破冰捕鱼，出行靠独木舟、雪鞋和狗拉雪橇。18世纪末毛皮贸易传入大奴湖地区，西北公司于1789年建立普罗维登斯堡，特里乔人开始与邻近的德内群体一起参与贸易。他们与长期称霸早期贸易并劫掠其营地的黄刀人本是世仇，19世纪30年代特里乔人几乎消灭了黄刀人，幸存者或四散离去，或通婚并入特里乔群体。他们还为英国探险队担任向导并提供补给，包括1825年约翰·富兰克林在大熊湖畔设立的富兰克林堡冬季营地。

en: The Tlingit, whose autonym Lingít means people of the tides, are a Na-Dene-speaking Northwest Coast people of the Alexander Archipelago and the Alaskan panhandle, their historic lands running from the Portland Canal north toward the Copper River delta, with inland communities on the Atlin, Teslin and Tagish lakes. In the temperate rainforest they built a complex semi-sedentary life around the salmon fisheries and other sea harvests, organised into matrilineal clans grouped under the Raven and Wolf or Eagle moieties, with hereditary chiefs, family crest histories told in the Raven Cycle, and hereditary slavery. Their river villages commanded the passes through the Coast Mountains, and the Stikine, Taku and Chilkat Tlingit grew wealthy as middlemen trading coastal goods with the Athabaskan peoples of the interior. Russians knew them as the Koloshi, and Russian settlement from the 1790s met fierce resistance: Tlingit forces destroyed the first post at Sitka in 1802, and the Russian-Tlingit War of 1802 to 1805 ended only with the Battle of Sitka in 1804, after which trade and warfare with the Russian-American Company continued side by side.
zh: 特林吉特人自称林吉特人，意为“潮汐之人”，是说纳—德内语的西北海岸族群，聚居于亚历山大群岛与阿拉斯加狭地，传统领地南起波特兰运河，北抵铜河三角洲一带，内陆的阿特林湖、特斯林湖和塔吉什湖畔也有其村落。在温带雨林中，他们围绕鲑鱼渔场和其他海产建立了复杂的半定居生活，社会按母系氏族组织，分属渡鸦与狼（亦称鹰）两个半偶族，由世袭酋长统领，家族纹章的历史通过“渡鸦传说”代代传承，并长期实行世袭奴隶制。河畔村落扼守穿越海岸山脉的通道，斯蒂金、塔库和奇尔卡特的特林吉特人充当海岸与内陆阿萨巴斯卡人之间的中间商，靠贸易积累财富。俄国人称他们为科洛希人；18世纪90年代起俄国人前来殖民，遭到猛烈抵抗：1802年特林吉特人摧毁了锡特卡的第一个据点，1802至1805年的俄特战争直到1804年锡特卡战役才告一段落，此后他们与俄美公司之间依旧贸易与交战并行。

en: The Toaripi are the people of the eastern shore of Kerema Bay in the Gulf Province of southern New Guinea. Their language, also called East Elema, is the eastern member of the Eleman family, a group of closely related Trans–New Guinea languages spoken along the bay's coast.
zh: 托亚里皮人住在新几内亚南部海湾省克雷马湾的东岸。他们的语言又称东埃勒马语，是埃勒曼语族的东支；埃勒曼语族是沿克雷马湾海岸通行的一群关系密切的跨新几内亚语言。

en: The Tobelo, who call themselves O'Hoberera Manyawa, the people living outside the forest, are the foremost people of northern and eastern Halmahera, settled along Kao Bay and the Jailolo Bay coast in sub-groups such as the Dodinga, Boeng and Kao; the nomadic Togutil of the inland rainforest are their forest-dwelling kin. They speak Tobelo, a non-Austronesian North Halmahera language of several dialects, and also use Ternate as a regional lingua franca. Their country was the heartland of Jailolo, one of the four kingdoms of Maluku, whose ruler bore the title Jika ma-kolano, Ruler of the Bay; tradition remembers Jailolo as the strongest Halmaheran realm around 1250 and as first in precedence at the Moti Island meeting of the 1320s. Its last Muslim king, Katarabumi, devised a script for the local language and with Spanish and Tidorese support resisted the Portuguese and Ternate until his fortress fell in 1551, after which the Tobelo lands passed under Ternate's suzerainty, governed through regional lords titled sangaji. Coastal Tobelo lived in bamboo stilt houses, fishing and farming sago, rice and bananas.
zh: 托贝洛人自称“林外之人”奥霍贝雷拉·马尼亚瓦，是哈马黑拉北部和东部最主要的族群，沿海湾而居，分为多丁加、邦、卡奥等支系；内陆雨林中游居的托古蒂尔人是他们的林中亲族。托贝洛人操托贝洛语，这是一种非南岛的北哈马黑拉语言，方言众多，同时也以特尔纳特语为地区通用语。他们的土地是贾伊洛洛苏丹国的核心。贾伊洛洛是马鲁古四大王国之一，君主号称“湾之主”吉卡·马科拉诺；传说它在1250年前后已是哈马黑拉最强的政权，14世纪20年代的莫蒂岛会盟中位列四国之首。末代穆斯林君主卡塔拉布米曾为当地语言创制文字，并借西班牙和蒂多雷之援抵抗葡萄牙与特尔纳特，直到1551年堡垒陷落，托贝洛之地改受特尔纳特宗主权管辖，由号称桑阿吉的地方领主治理。沿海的托贝洛人住竹制高脚屋，以捕鱼和种植西米、旱稻、香蕉为生。

en: The Toboso were an Indigenous people of the Bolsón de Mapimí, the desert basin straddling eastern Chihuahua and western Coahuila, whom the Spanish linked with the Jumanos of La Junta near Presidio, Texas and sometimes counted as part of that people. Living further south than the Jumano, they bore the brunt of Spanish slaving raids and fled from Antonio de Espejo's expedition in 1583 rather than welcome it. They hunted with sling and lance, spoke a language of their own marked by Tepehuán influence, and were old enemies of the Irritila valley tribes. From the 1640s they raided Spanish missions and Tarahumara mines to their west, and even Toboso families settled in the Monterrey missions often abandoned them and rejected Christianity, earning the Spanish label of ladinos, Indians who understood colonial ways well enough to turn them against the colonists. In the 1680s twelve Toboso bands still existed; by 1693 only four were counted, the Osatayogliglas, Guazapayogliglas, Chichitames and Sisimbles. By 1800 the Toboso left in Mexico had merged into the mestizo population, while others fled to the Texas coast, appearing in the baptismal records of Mission Refugio as late as the 1820s and joining Karankawa refugees on Matagorda Island.
zh: 托沃索人是居住在马皮米洼地的原住民，这片沙漠盆地横跨奇瓦瓦东部与科阿韦拉西部，西班牙人把他们与普雷西迪奥附近拉洪塔的胡马诺人联系在一起，有时干脆视其为胡马诺人的一支。由于住得更靠南，他们首当其冲遭受西班牙奴隶猎捕，1583年安东尼奥·德埃斯佩霍的探险队到来时，他们没有像拉洪塔人那样出迎，而是惊恐逃散。托沃索人以投石器和长矛狩猎，讲一种受特佩瓦诺语影响很深的本族语言，世代与谷地的伊里提拉诸部为敌。从17世纪40年代起，他们不断袭击西边的西班牙传教站和塔拉乌马拉人的矿山；即便是被迁入蒙特雷传教站的托沃索家庭，也大多逃离传教站、拒绝基督教，因此被西班牙人归为拉迪诺人，即熟稔殖民社会路数、并以此反过来对付殖民者的印第安人。17世纪80年代他们还有十二个部落，到1693年西班牙人只能数出四个：奥萨塔约格利格拉斯、瓜萨帕约格利格拉斯、奇奇塔梅和西辛布莱。到1800年，留在墨西哥的托沃索人已基本融入梅斯蒂索人群；另一些人逃往得克萨斯海岸，在雷富希奥传教站的洗礼记录中一直出现到19世纪20年代，还有人加入逃往马塔戈尔达岛的卡兰卡瓦人。

en: Tocobaga was a sixteenth-century chiefdom of Tampa Bay, whose principal town is identified with the Safety Harbor archaeological site and gives its name to the Safety Harbor culture. Drawing their living from the bay's fish and shellfish rather than maize, the Tocobaga met Pánfilo de Narváez's expedition with fighting in 1528 and were passed by Hernando de Soto in 1539. The missionary Luis de Cancer, who came to convert them peacefully in 1549, was clubbed to death on the Pinellas shore. The name first appears in Spanish records in 1567, when Pedro Menéndez de Avilés brokered peace between the Tocobaga and the Calusa and left a garrison that was found slaughtered a few months later. A Spanish punitive expedition in 1612 killed the Tocobaga chief alongside the Pohoy chief, and disease plus Creek and Yamasee slave raids emptied the bay. Some Tocobaga resettled in Apalachee on the Wacissa River, where a remnant survived near San Marcos de Apalachee into the 1730s before disappearing from the records, possibly among the Florida Indians evacuated to Cuba in 1763.
zh: 托科巴加是16世纪坦帕湾畔的一个酋邦，其主城被认定为赛夫蒂港考古遗址，赛夫蒂港文化也因该遗址得名。托科巴加人不靠玉米为生，而是从海湾的鱼虾贝类中获取食物。1528年，他们与潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯的远征队交战；1539年埃尔南多·德·索托又从他们的土地上经过。1549年，前来和平传教的路易斯·德·坎塞尔在皮尼拉斯海岸被棍棒打死。托科巴加之名首见于1567年的西班牙文献：当年佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯调停托科巴加与卡卢萨的冲突并留下驻军，几个月后驻军便被尽数杀死。1612年，西班牙人的惩罚性远征杀死了托科巴加首领和波霍伊首领；疫病加上克里克人与亚马西人的奴隶劫掠使坦帕湾人口一空。部分托科巴加人迁居阿巴拉契的瓦西萨河，一小支在圣马科斯·德·阿巴拉契附近存续到18世纪30年代，此后从记载中消失，可能加入了1763年被撤往古巴的佛罗里达印第安人。

en: The Togiagamiut are a Central Alaskan Yup'ik people of western Bristol Bay, whose historic village of Togiagamute stood on the eastern shore of Togiak Bay, near the later community of Togiak, Tuyuryaq in Yup'ik. Their coast blends open sea, tidal flats and the Walrus Islands, giving their year-round round a distinctive marine emphasis: besides the salmon runs shared with other Bristol Bay groups, they hunted walrus, seals and beluga, took herring and seabird eggs, and traded inland with neighbours along the Togiak River. To the east lay the country of the Nushagagmiut and to the north-west that of the Kuskokwagmiut. After Russian-American Company parties began charting Bristol Bay in the late 1790s, the Togiagamiut were drawn into the same fur-trading network that linked the bay's scattered Yup'ik villages to Nushagak and Kodiak.
zh: 托吉亚加缪特人是布里斯托尔湾西部的中阿拉斯加尤皮克族群，其历史村落托吉亚加穆特坐落在托贾克湾东岸，靠近后来的托贾克社区，尤皮克语称“图尤尔亚克”。他们的海岸融合了开阔海面、潮滩与海象群岛，使一年的生计带有鲜明的海洋色彩：除了与布里斯托尔湾其他群体共有的鲑鱼汛外，他们还捕猎海象、海豹和白鲸，捕捞鲱鱼、采集海鸟蛋，并沿托贾克河与内地邻族贸易。他们东边是努沙加格缪特人的地盘，西北是库斯科夸格缪特人的地盘。18世纪90年代末俄美公司的探险队开始测绘布里斯托尔湾后，托吉亚加缪特人被纳入同一张毛皮贸易网络，把湾内分散的尤皮克村落与努沙加克、科迪亚克连接起来。

en: The Tojolabal are a Maya people of east-central Chiapas, living around Comitán, the plains of Zapaluta where the town of La Trinitaria now stands, and the Ocosingo valley along the Guatemalan border. Their Tojol-ab'al language belongs to the Mayan family and is closest to Chuj; its name means right or straight speech, from tohol for correct and ab'al for word, and nineteenth-century documents also called the people Chaneabal. Their own oral tradition holds that they migrated north from Guatemala, and the Classic Maya city of Chinkultic, whose carved stelae span the years 591 to 897 and whose occupation lasted into the thirteenth century, stands in their former lands. Spanish control reached Comitán and the Ocosingo valley by 1528, when Diego Mazariegos organized the colonial province of Chiapa and distributed the Tojolabal towns as encomiendas; harsh tribute demands drove many to abandon their villages for the remoter mountains.
zh: 托霍拉瓦尔人是恰帕斯中东部的玛雅族群，聚居在科米坦、今拉特里尼塔里亚所在的萨帕卢塔平原以及危地马拉边境的奥科辛戈谷地一带。他们的托霍拉瓦尔语属玛雅语系，与丘赫语最接近；其名称由意为“正确”的托霍尔和意为“言语”的阿巴尔组成，即“正直的言语”，19世纪的文献还称他们为查内阿瓦尔人。按他们自己的口述传统，其先祖是从危地马拉北迁而来；古典期玛雅城邦钦库尔蒂克就坐落在他们的故土上，那里的石碑铭刻年代从591年延续到897年，城邦本身一直有人居住到13世纪。1528年西班牙势力抵达科米坦和奥科辛戈谷地，迭戈·马萨列戈斯组建殖民省份恰帕，把托霍拉瓦尔村镇划为监护征赋地；沉重的贡赋劳役迫使许多人弃村退入更深的山区。

en: The Tokelauans are the Polynesian people of three small coral atolls, Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo, lying north of Samoa. Settled from Samoa roughly a thousand years ago, the atolls may have served as a gateway into eastern Polynesia; their inhabitants lived by fish and coconut, venerated the god Tui Tokelau and were governed by chiefly clans. Though sharing one language and custom and linked by intermarriage, the three atolls stayed politically separate, with occasional wars between them, and Fakaofo, the chiefly island, long held dominion over the other two. The first European to sight the group was Commodore John Byron, who reached Atafu on 24 June 1765 and named it Duke of York's Island. In 1791 Captain Edward Edwards called at Atafu and Nukunonu while hunting the Bounty mutineers, finding houses, canoes and fishing gear but few people, and the American ship Dolphin visited in 1825.
zh: 托克劳人是阿塔富、努库诺努和法考福三座小型珊瑚环礁上的波利尼西亚人，环礁位于萨摩亚以北。他们约在一千年前由萨摩亚迁入，这片环礁可能还是通往东波利尼西亚的门户；居民以鱼和椰子为生，信奉神祇图伊·托克劳，由各氏族首领治理。三座环礁语言习俗相同、互通婚姻，政治上却各自独立，彼此间偶有战争，其中首领之岛法考福长期统治另外两岛。最早望见这群岛屿的欧洲人是海军准将约翰·拜伦，他于1765年6月24日抵达阿塔富，将其命名为约克公爵岛。1791年，爱德华·爱德华兹船长搜捕“邦蒂号”哗变者时先后造访阿塔富和努库诺努，只看到房屋、独木舟和渔具而鲜有人迹；美国船“海豚号”又于1825年前来。

en: The Tolaki are the principal people of the southeastern arm of Sulawesi, concentrated around Kendari Bay and the Konawe and Kolaka regions, and their Tolaki language belongs to the Austronesian family. Cave sites in northern Konawe show that their ancestors inhabited the peninsula thousands of years before the small local realms of Padangguni, Besulutu, Wawolesea and Watu Mendonga merged into the Konawe confederacy, whose rulers bore the title mokole. Tradition places the first king, Mokole Roro, in the fifth century with his seat at Rahambuu, the present-day Unaaha. Konawe society was divided into noble, commoner and slave classes bound together by the Kalo Sara, a rattan bracelet symbol of customary law. Bugis merchants from Makassar brought Islam to the coast from the early fifteenth century, and the kingdom officially converted under King Lakidende, who ruled from 1724 to 1786 after studying the faith in Bone. Around the Dutch-Bone War of 1824 and 1825 Bugis and Bajo traders settled in Kendari Bay, which the Dutch sailor Jacques Nicholas Vosmaer surveyed and mapped in 1828 and 1831, opening the Tolaki coast to growing colonial contact.
zh: 托拉基人是苏拉威西东南半岛的主体族群，聚居于肯达里湾及科纳韦、科拉卡一带，使用的托拉基语属南岛语系。科纳韦北部的洞穴遗址表明，早在帕当古尼、贝苏卢图、瓦沃莱塞亚、瓦图门东加等小邦合并为科纳韦联盟之前数千年，其先民已居住在这座半岛上；联盟的统治者称“莫科莱”。据传说，最早的国王莫科莱·罗罗在5世纪立国，都城设在拉汉布，即今天的乌纳阿哈。科纳韦社会分为贵族、平民和奴隶三个等级，以象征习惯法的藤镯“卡洛萨拉”维系一体。15世纪初起，来自望加锡的布吉商人把伊斯兰教带到沿海；1724至1786年在位的拉基登德国王曾在波尼研习伊斯兰教，科纳韦随后正式皈依。1824至1825年荷兰与波尼交战前后，布吉人和巴瑶商人到肯达里湾定居；荷兰水手沃斯马尔于1828至1831年测绘了这座海湾，托拉基沿海由此被卷入日益加深的殖民接触。

en: The Tolimecs were a small Indigenous people of the Costa Grande, the Pacific coast around Zacatula in western Guerrero, neighbours of the Chumbia, Pantec and Cuitlatec; their extinct language is known only from sixteenth-century records placing it in Pochutla, Tolimán and Suchitlán.
zh: 托利梅克人是墨西哥格雷罗州西部太平洋沿岸“大海岸”、萨卡特拉一带的小型原住民群体，与丘姆比亚人、潘特克人和库伊特拉特克人为邻；他们已消亡的语言仅见于16世纪文献，记载其通行于波丘特拉、托利曼和苏奇特兰。

en: The Tolomako are an Oceanic-speaking Melanesian people of the Big Bay coast on northern Espiritu Santo in Vanuatu, their language also being called Bigbay after the bay, while the closely related Tsureviu variety is counted as one of their dialects. Their speech has changed little from the ancestral Proto-North-Central Vanuatu tongue, which sets them apart from the much-transformed Sakao people farther along the same coast. Big Bay gave the Tolomako a prominent place in recorded history: in May 1606 Pedro Fernandes de Queirós's Spanish expedition anchored there, clashed with the local chief and killed him, and briefly proclaimed the island a part of the supposed great southern continent. After the Spanish departure, no Europeans returned to Santo until Louis Antoine de Bougainville in 1768 and James Cook in 1774.
zh: 托洛马科人是瓦努阿图圣埃斯皮里图岛北部大湾沿海的美拉尼西亚人，他们的语言也因大湾而别称大湾语，关系极近的楚雷维乌话被视为其方言。与同一海岸变化剧烈的萨卡奥人不同，托洛马科语与祖先的原始中北瓦努阿图语相去不远，演变十分保守。大湾使托洛马科人在有记载的历史中占有醒目位置：1606年5月，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯的西班牙探险队在此停泊，与当地酋长发生冲突并将其杀死，还一度把该岛当作传说中的南方大陆加以宣称。西班牙人离去后，直到1768年布干维尔和1774年库克到来，欧洲人才重返该岛。

en: The Tolowa, who call themselves Taa-laa-wa Dee-ni', are an Athabascan-speaking Native American nation of the far northwestern corner of California, their ancestral land of Taa-laa-waa-dvn running along the Pacific coast between Wilson Creek and the Smith River basin in Del Norte County. They held about eight permanent villages around Crescent City Harbor and Lake Earl, of which Yontocket was the foremost and a gathering place where neighbouring peoples met for ceremonies; their population has been estimated at roughly one thousand in 1770. The name Tolowa was given to them by their Yurok neighbours to the south and means people of Lake Earl, while their own word Hush means simply a person. Their language, Chetco-Tolowa, belongs to the Pacific Coast branch of the Athabascan family within Na-Dené, forming an Oregon Athabascan cluster with the neighbouring Tututni, Galice and Upper Umpqua speeches. Other neighbours were the Chetco to the north and the Karuk to the east. The large plank-house villages of the coast were already prospering when European and American ships began to visit the region in the late eighteenth-century maritime fur trade.
zh: 托洛瓦人自称 Taa-laa-wa Dee-ni'，是加利福尼亚州西北角讲阿萨巴斯卡语的原住民族，其祖居之地 Taa-laa-waa-dvn 沿太平洋海岸展开，介于威尔逊溪与德尔诺特县的史密斯河流域之间。他们在克雷森特城港和厄尔湖周围拥有约八座固定村庄，其中永托克特地位最高，是邻近各族赶来举行仪式的聚会之所；据估计，1770年前后他们的人口约为一千。“托洛瓦”这个名字来自南方的尤罗克邻居，意为“厄尔湖之民”，而他们自称的 Hush 一词仅表示“人”。他们的语言切特科—托洛瓦语属于纳-德内语系阿萨巴斯卡语族的太平洋海岸语支，与邻近的图图特尼语、加利斯语和上安普夸语同属俄勒冈阿萨巴斯卡语群。其他邻族还有北方的切特科人和东方的卡鲁克人。18世纪末海上毛皮贸易的欧洲和美国船只陆续到来时，海岸上这些木板屋大村已是一派兴旺景象。

en: The Toltecs were the people of Tula, called Tollan in Nahuatl, a city in the highlands of central Mexico whose culture dominated central Mesoamerica from roughly 950 to 1150. They emerged after the fall of Teotihuacan, combining farming migrants from the Gulf Coast with settled Chichimeca groups from the northern deserts. At its height Tula held perhaps sixty thousand people, laid out around plazas with pyramids, ball courts, columned halls and the giant warrior figures known as Atlanteans. Toltec arms and trade networks carried their influence as far as Yucatan, where the Maya city of Chichen Itza adopted much of their architecture and symbolism, though the direction of that influence is still debated. In the twelfth century Tula was sacked and abandoned amid internal conflict and pressure from nomadic newcomers, and its people scattered among the cities of central Mexico. Their prestige outlived their state: later peoples, above all the Aztecs, saw the Toltecs as the founders of civilized life, and in Nahuatl the word for Toltec came to mean a master artisan, while ruling dynasties from the Valley of Mexico to the Maya highlands claimed Toltec ancestry.
zh: 托尔特克人是图拉（纳瓦特尔语称托兰）的居民，这座城市位于墨西哥中部高原，其文化约在950年至1150年间称雄中美洲中部。他们兴起于特奥蒂瓦坎衰落之后，由来自墨西哥湾沿岸的农耕移民与北方沙漠中定居的奇奇梅克群体融合而成。鼎盛时期的图拉约有六万人口，城中广场周围遍布金字塔、球场、柱厅和被称为亚特兰蒂斯巨人的武士石像柱。托尔特克人的武力和贸易网络把影响力远播尤卡坦，玛雅城邦奇琴伊察大量采用了他们的建筑与符号，不过影响的方向学界仍有争议。12世纪，图拉在内乱和游牧新族群的压力下遭洗劫并被废弃，居民散入墨西哥中部各城。但他们的声望比政权更持久：后来的民族，尤其是阿兹特克人，把托尔特克人视为文明生活的奠基者，纳瓦特尔语中“托尔特克”一词也引申为能工巧匠，从墨西哥谷地到玛雅高地的统治王朝纷纷自称拥有托尔特克血统。

en: The Tolupan, better known in colonial records as the Jicaque, are an indigenous people of the Caribbean coast of Honduras. In late pre-Hispanic times they ranged along the Bay of Honduras from the Ulúa River to Puerto Castilla near Trujillo and inland as far as the Sulaco River, hunting and fishing, growing bitter manioc and trading maize and cochineal cactus in dugout canoes. They met the Spanish invasion with armed resistance: in 1536 their chief Cicumba fought Pedro de Alvarado's troops along the Ulúa and in the Sula valley, until he was captured and left to starve. The surviving communities kept their villages, and in 1609 Tolupan groups resettled along the Guayape and Guayambre rivers of Olancho. The label Jicaque, drawn from a K'iche' word meaning savage, was used in colonial documents for any unconverted Indians outside Spanish rule, not only for the Tolupan themselves.
zh: 希卡克人在殖民档案中更常见的名字是希卡克，自称托卢潘人，是洪都拉斯加勒比海岸的原住民。前西班牙时代晚期，他们活动于洪都拉斯湾沿岸，从乌卢阿河到特鲁希略附近的卡斯蒂利亚港，内陆远至苏拉科河，以渔猎为生，种植苦木薯，并乘独木舟贸易玉米和胭脂虫仙人掌。他们以武力抵抗西班牙入侵：1536年，首领西昆巴在乌卢阿河一带和苏拉谷地抗击佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多的军队，最终被俘并被活活饿死。幸存的社群保住了村庄，1609年，托卢潘各群体迁居奥兰乔的瓜亚佩河与瓜亚姆布雷河流域。“希卡克”一词源自基切语中意为野蛮人的词，殖民文献用它泛指一切不受西班牙统治、未改宗的印第安人，并不单指托卢潘人。

en: The Tomini, together with their Totoli kin, are the coastal people of the Gulf of Tomini in Central Sulawesi, living on both shores of the gulf around Parigi, Moutong, Dondo and Toli-Toli. They form a cluster of sub-groups that includes the Tialo, Lauje, Dondo, Tajio, Pendau, Dampelas, Totoli and Boano, each traditionally led by a hereditary chief bearing the title olongian, and they build stilt houses along the shore while inland groups farm rice and corn on the hills. In the mid-sixteenth century the Gowa Sultanate's King Tunipalangga conquered the western coast from Donggala to Tolitoli, and Islam took root among the gulf's rulers in the same period, beginning with the neighbouring sultanate of Buol in 1540. The Tomini shore then owed allegiance to the Kingdom of Parigi, where the Dutch East India Company built a fortress in the early seventeenth century, and in the eighteenth century local rulers were made to swear loyalty to the Company at Manado and Gorontalo. From the early nineteenth century Bugis and Mandar migrants, displaced by the Bone War that began in 1820, settled in the gulf and founded the Kingdom of Moutong under Magalatung, while Dutch ships became frequent visitors after 1830.
zh: 托米尼人与同族的托托利人是中苏拉威西托米尼湾两岸的沿海居民，分布在帕里吉、莫通、东多和托利托利一带。他们包括提亚洛、劳杰、东多、塔吉奥、彭道、丹佩拉斯、托托利、博阿诺等支系，各支系传统上由世袭的奥隆吉安酋长统领；沿海居民在岸边搭建高脚屋，内陆群体则在山坡上种植水稻和玉米。16世纪中叶，戈瓦苏丹国国王图尼帕朗加征服了从栋加达到托利托利的西海岸，伊斯兰教也在同一时期传入海湾诸统治者中，邻近的布奥尔于1540年成为最早的苏丹国。此后托米尼沿岸臣属帕里吉王国，荷兰东印度公司于17世纪初在帕里吉修筑堡垒；18世纪，当地统治者又被要求前往万鸦老和哥伦打洛向公司宣誓效忠。19世纪初，因1820年爆发的波尼战争而流离的布吉人和曼达尔人迁入海湾，在马加拉通率领下建立莫通王国；1830年以后，荷兰船只也开始频繁出没于此。

en: The Tonala are the Tecuexe, a Chichimeca people of Los Altos de Jalisco and the country east of Guadalajara, whose chief town was Tonallan, the later Tonalá. They held river valleys — their towns included Acatic, Mitic, Xalostotitlán and Tepatitlán — where they grew maize and beans, worked stone and wood, and cultivated agaves for pulque; tradition made them migrants from the Zacateco dispersion around La Quemada. The Tecuexe were feared fighters, and the Mexica themselves avoided a pitched battle with them at Tepatitlán. Tonallan was ruled by a queen, Cihualpilli Tzpotzinco, from her palace on the Xitépec hill, and it was at a dinner in her palace that the Mixtón War broke out in 1540. The rising united Tecuexe, Caxcan and Zacateco against the Spanish until its defeat in 1542, after which Tecuexe pueblos were absorbed into colonial New Galicia, their people still writing petitions in Nahuatl as late as 1611.
zh: 托纳拉人即特库埃克人，是哈利斯科高原和瓜达拉哈拉以东地区的奇奇梅克族群，首城为托纳兰，也就是后来的托纳拉。他们占据河谷，城镇包括阿卡蒂克、米蒂克、哈洛斯特蒂特兰和特帕蒂特兰，在那里种植玉米和菜豆，从事石工和木工，并栽种龙舌兰酿造普尔克酒；传说他们是从拉奎马达散出的萨卡特科人一支。特库埃克人善战之名远播，据说就连墨西加人在特帕蒂特兰都避免与他们正面交锋。托纳兰由女王西瓦尔皮利·茨波钦科统治，宫殿建在希特佩克山上；1540年的米斯通战争正是在她宫中的一场宴会上爆发。这场起义联合特库埃克人、卡什坎人和萨卡特科人对抗西班牙人，1542年遭到镇压；此后特库埃克诸村被并入殖民时期的新加利西亚，迟至1611年，他们仍在用纳瓦特尔语书写请愿书。

en: The Tonga, or Batonga, are a Bantu people of the middle Zambezi valley and the adjoining plateaus of southern Zambia and northern Zimbabwe, divided into Valley Tonga and Plateau Tonga groups and speaking Chitonga, a member of the Bantu Botatwe group; they are related to the Batoka of the same region, and the Iwe, Toka and Leya speak closely kindred forms of the language. Their country lay on old commercial routes: the settlement of Ingombe Ilede, near where the Lusitu joins the Zambezi, was a major trading centre around the 1500s, where salt, copper, gold, ivory and slaves from the interior were exchanged for Indian Ocean glass beads, cloth and cowrie shells. Tonga communities lived mainly by subsistence farming and cattle keeping, and Chitonga remained a purely spoken language until missionaries gave it a written form in the 1800s.
zh: 通加人又称巴通加人，是赞比西河中游河谷及邻近的赞比亚南部、津巴布韦北部高原上的班图族群，分为河谷通加和高原通加两支，操班图图塔维语群中的奇通加语；他们与同地区的巴托卡人有亲缘关系，伊韦人、托卡人和莱亚人也使用相近的语言。他们的土地处在古老商路上：位于卢西图河汇入赞比西河处附近的因贡贝·伊莱德遗址在16世纪前后是重要贸易中心，内地运来的盐、铜、黄金、象牙和奴隶在这里换取来自印度洋贸易的玻璃珠、布匹和货贝。通加诸社群主要以自给农业和养牛为生，奇通加语长期只有口语，直到19世纪传教士才为它确定了书面形式。

en: The Tongans are the Polynesian people of Tongatapu, Haʻapai and Vavaʻu, whose Lapita ancestors settled Tongatapu some three thousand years ago and made Tonga, with Samoa, a gateway for the settlement of the rest of Polynesia. From around the tenth century the islands were ruled by the Tuʻi Tonga, a line of sacred kings founded in tradition by ʻAhoʻeitu; under Momo and Tuʻitātui, who built the coral trilithon Haʻamonga ʻa Maui about 1100, their maritime empire drew tribute from Samoa, Fiji, Niue, Uvea and Futuna. The empire weakened after about 1250 when Samoa was lost to the Malietoa, and around 1470 the Tuʻi Tonga withdrew into a sacred role while the new Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua line took the everyday government, later shared with the rising Tuʻi Kanokupolu. The Dutchman Abel Tasman made the first European contact in 1643, and James Cook, who called the islands the Friendly Isles, witnessed the grand Tuʻi Tonga installation ceremonies in 1777. Rival title-holders then plunged the islands into civil war from 1799, and in 1826 the young chief Tāufaʻāhau defeated the last Tuʻi Tonga Laufilitonga at Velata on Lifuka, opening the way for the dynasty that would unite Tonga.
zh: 汤加人是汤加塔布、哈阿派和瓦瓦乌诸岛的波利尼西亚人，其拉皮塔祖先约三千年前定居汤加塔布，使汤加与萨摩亚一同成为人类迁居波利尼西亚其他地区的门户。约10世纪起，群岛由图伊汤加统治，这是一支传统上由阿霍埃图开创的神圣王系；在莫莫和图伊塔图伊治下，图伊塔图伊约于1100年建起珊瑚石三石门哈蒙加·阿·毛伊，他们的海上帝国向萨摩亚、斐济、纽埃、乌韦阿和富图纳征收贡赋。约1250年后帝国转衰，萨摩亚被马利埃托阿夺走；约1470年，图伊汤加退居神圣角色，新的图伊哈阿塔卡劳阿系接掌日常政务，后来又与崛起的图伊卡诺库波卢分权。荷兰人亚伯·塔斯曼于1643年最先抵达，詹姆斯·库克把群岛称作友好群岛，并于1777年亲眼目睹图伊汤加盛大的继位仪式。此后各头衔争夺者自1799年起把群岛拖入内战，1826年，年轻酋长陶法阿豪在利富卡的韦拉塔击败末代图伊汤加劳菲利汤加，为日后统一汤加的王朝铺平了道路。

en: The Tōngtài culture occupies the coastal lowland of central Jiangsu between the Grand Canal and the sea, centred on Taizhou, the old Hailing, and Tongzhou in present-day Nantong; its Tong-Tai or Tai-Ru speech is the easternmost branch of Jianghuai Mandarin. The country had once been Wu-speaking, and when Wu families were resettled into eastern Jiangsu in the early Ming, their speech met the Jianghuai koiné and left the dialect with a thick Wu substrate, especially around Rugao on the border with the Wu country of Changzhou. Life here was shaped by the advancing coast: Yangtze silt raised new land and tidal salt pans, and the Hailing salt administration, already set up under the Tang, made Taizhou a hub of the Lianghuai salt trade through the Ming and Qing. In 1526 the salt-worker-turned-scholar Wang Gen lectured at Anding Academy and founded the populist Taizhou School of Confucian thought, the region's best-known contribution to Ming philosophy. Its dialects fall into western, middle and eastern groups that differ chiefly in their consonants.
