The long reign of Constantin Brâncoveanu, ending with his execution at Constantinople in 1714, adorned the country with the Brâncovenesc architectural style; the Ottomans then imposed Phanariote princes from the Greek quarter of Constantinople. Under them serfdom was abolished in 1746, while repeated Russo-Turkish wars brought Russian occupation from 1768 and the protective Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca in 1774. Tudor Vladimirescu's rising of 1821 ended Phanariote rule, and after the Treaty of Adrianople in 1829 Russian-administered reform under the Regulamentul Organic opened a period of urban growth, with Bucharest overtaking the old court at Târgoviște.
zh: 瓦拉几亚人是生活在南喀尔巴阡山与多瑙河之间平原上的罗马尼亚语弗拉赫人，瓦拉几亚公国正是在这片土地上成长起来的。13世纪已有利托沃伊等本地弗拉赫督军的记载，1330年巴萨拉布一世在波萨达战役大败匈牙利国王查理一世，摆脱匈牙利宗主权，开创巴萨拉布王朝，以坎普伦格和特尔戈维什泰为统治中心。老者米尔恰于1394年在罗维内迎战奥斯曼人，并一度据有多瑙河三角洲和多布罗加；穿刺公弗拉德三世抗拒穆罕默德二世，1462年的特尔戈维什泰夜袭更让他在本土和萨克森人的小册子中都成为传奇。从16世纪20年代起，公国沦为奥斯曼的附庸，以自治换取内部统治权，但勇敢者米哈伊于1593年起兵反土，并在1600年短暂统一瓦拉几亚、特兰西瓦尼亚和摩尔多瓦。康斯坦丁·布兰科韦亚努的长期统治以1714年他在君士坦丁堡被处死告终，其间形成的“布兰科韦亚努风格”为国家留下大量建筑；此后奥斯曼人改由君士坦丁堡希腊区的法纳尔人出任王公。法纳尔时期的1746年废除了农奴制，而连绵的俄土战争带来1768年起的俄国占领和1774年提供保护的《库楚克-凯纳尔贾条约》。1821年图多尔·弗拉迪米雷斯库起义终结了法纳尔统治，1829年《阿德里安堡条约》后，俄国主导的《组织条例》改革开启了城市发展期，布加勒斯特也超过旧都特尔戈维什泰。

en: Walloon is the langue d'oïl of the southern Low Countries, spoken along the Meuse and Sambre from Liège and Namur to Dinant, Nivelles and the Ardennes; of its four dialects the Liègeois of the east is the most conservative. Its speakers descend from the Gallo-Romans of Roman Gallia Belgica, whom their Germanic neighbours called the Walha, and after the Frankish settlement the border between Romance and Germanic speech had largely crystallized by 1000. The oldest surviving langue d'oïl text, the Sequence of Saint Eulalia of around 880, shows features of this region. Walloon's own growth was shaped by the Principality of Liège, whose bishop Notker received the county of Huy in 980 and founded an ecclesiastical state that lasted eight hundred years as an autonomous estate of the Empire, never absorbed into the Seventeen Provinces; meanwhile Namur, Limbourg and Hainaut passed to the Burgundian dukes and then to the Spanish and Austrian Habsburgs. Walloon written literature appeared anonymously in the sixteenth century, but after France annexed the country in 1795 French became the language of advancement and the local speech retreated to home and workshop. After 1815 the land belonged to the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, from which it broke away in the Belgian Revolution of 1830 as part of the new Kingdom of Belgium, its coal-rich valleys already rising among the earliest industrial districts of the continent.
zh: 瓦隆语是低地国家南部的奥依语，通行于默兹河和桑布尔河沿岸，从列日、那慕尔到迪南、尼韦勒和阿登山区，分为四种地区方言，其中东部的列日话最为保守。说这种语言的人是罗马贝尔吉卡高卢行省的高卢-罗马人后裔，日耳曼邻人称之为“瓦尔哈”；法兰克人后来定居其间，罗曼语与日耳曼语的分界线到公元1000年前后已基本定型。现存最古老的奥依语文献、约880年写成的《圣欧拉利亚颂》就带有这一地区的语言特征，而瓦隆语本身的成长与列日公国的扩张密不可分：980年列日主教诺特克获得于伊伯国，建立起一个延续八百年的教会国家，作为神圣罗马帝国的自治帝国政治体，始终未被十七省联合体吞并。列日保留着自己的采邑主教，而相邻的那慕尔、林堡和埃诺等伯国则在15世纪转入勃艮第公爵之手，此后又历经西班牙和奥地利哈布斯堡家族统治。瓦隆语书面文学在16世纪以匿名作品出现，但1795年法国吞并此地后，法语成为进身之阶，本土语言退居家庭和作坊。1815年后，这片土地并入尼德兰联合王国，又在1830年比利时革命中脱离出来，成为新比利时王国的一部分；此时它富含煤矿的河谷地带已崛起为欧洲大陆最早的工业区之一。

en: The Wamesa are an Austronesian people of the neck of the Bird's Head Peninsula, around Wondama Bay and Bintuni Bay in West Papua. Their language, often called Wandamen, is a South Halmahera-West New Guinea language that served as a coastal lingua franca before Papuan Malay spread.
zh: 瓦梅萨人是南岛语族族群，散居鸟头半岛颈部的温达马湾和宾图尼湾沿岸。他们的语言旧称万达门语，属南岛语系南哈马黑拉-西新几内亚语群，在巴布亚马来语扩散之前曾是沿海通用语。

en: The Wampanoag, or Wôpanâak, are the Algonquian people of southeastern New England, whose sixty-seven villages once covered Cape Cod, the islands of Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard and the shores of Plymouth and Narragansett bays; their name means people of the dawn. They followed a seasonal round, moving between fishing stations and fields where women grew the Three Sisters of maize, beans and squash, and descent and property passed through the maternal line. Their population may have reached forty thousand before contact, but the epidemic of 1616 to 1619 killed as many as nine in ten, leaving the Patuxet village empty when the Pilgrims founded Plymouth in 1620. The Patuxet captive Tisquantum, known as Squanto, and the sachem Massasoit then helped the settlers survive, an alliance remembered through the harvest feast of 1621. The peace ended under Massasoit's son Metacom, called King Philip, whose war of 1675 to 1676 cost forty percent of the surviving Wampanoag their lives and ended with hundreds sold into slavery in Bermuda and the West Indies. The Wôpanâak dialect of Massachusett, in which John Eliot printed a Bible in 1663, gradually fell out of daily use after the American Revolution.
zh: 万帕诺亚格人（自称沃帕纳克人）是新英格兰东南部的阿尔冈昆语民族，曾有67个村落遍布科德角、楠塔基特岛和玛莎葡萄园岛，以及普利茅斯湾和纳拉甘西特湾沿岸；族名意为“黎明之人”。他们按季节轮转，在渔场和田地间迁徙，妇女种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜“三姐妹”，世系与财产沿母系传承。接触欧洲人之前他们可能多达四万人，但1616—1619年的疫病使多达九成人口丧生，1620年清教徒移民建立普利茅斯时，帕图克塞特村已经死散一空。曾被掳走的帕图克塞特人蒂斯匡特姆（即斯匡托）和酋长马萨索伊特随后帮助移民渡过难关，双方1621年的丰收宴便是后世感恩节的由来。和平在马萨索伊特之子梅塔科姆（即菲利普国王）时终结，1675—1676年的菲利普国王战争使幸存的万帕诺亚格人再减四成，数以百计的人被卖到百慕大和西印度群岛为奴。马萨诸塞语的沃帕纳克方言曾在1663年被约翰·埃利奥特用来印制圣经，美国独立战争后逐渐退出日常使用。

en: The Wampar are an Austronesian-speaking people of the Markham Valley in Morobe Province, in the Bird's Tail of New Guinea. Their speech, Wampar or Dzob Wampar, is a Lower Markham language of the Huon Gulf group, spoken in a cluster of villages across the Wampar plains inland from the gulf. Unusually for Western Oceanic languages, which are otherwise confined to the coast, the Markham languages were carried into the interior valleys, where the Wampar and their relatives live in close contact with Trans–New Guinea peoples of the surrounding mountains.
zh: 万帕尔人是新几内亚“鸟尾”莫罗贝省马卡姆河谷的南岛语族群。他们的语言万帕尔语（自称佐布万帕尔语）属休恩湾语群的下马卡姆语族，通行于休恩湾内陆万帕尔平原上的一组村落。西部大洋洲诸语通常只分布在沿海，马卡姆诸语却深入内陆河谷，万帕尔人和亲属族群因此与周围山区说跨新几内亚语言的族群长期密切往来。

en: The Wangan, also called the Babbinburra, were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Isaac Region in central Queensland, close neighbours of the Yagalingu people of the Belyando River headwaters.
zh: 旺加人又称巴宾布拉，是昆士兰中部艾萨克地区的澳大利亚原住民，与贝利安多河源头的亚加林古人比邻而居。

en: The Huanca or Wanka are a Quechua people of the Mantaro valley in the central Peruvian highlands, their name taken from the Quechua word for the stone monoliths typical of the region. Archaeologists divide their late pre-Inca history into the Wanka I phase of 1000 to 1350, when small tribal villages farmed maize, potatoes and quinoa and herded llamas, and the Wanka II phase of 1350 to 1460, marked by large fortified hilltop towns; by the fifteenth century the valley was shared among five chiefdoms, Tunanmarca, Marcavilca, Chongos, Llacsapallanga and Xauxa, long at odds with the neighbouring Xauxa and Yauyo peoples. Around 1460 the Inca army of Túpac Yupanqui entered the Mantaro and incorporated the chiefdoms into Tawantinsuyu, where the region became the province of Huanca with its administrative centre at the new city of Hatun Xauxa. During the Inca civil war the Huanca stayed loyal to the Cusco government and suffered Atahualpist reprisals, so on Pizarro's arrival they joined the Spaniards, supplying troops who helped defeat the Atahualpist general Quizquiz and later served the viceroyalty, as when over five hundred Huanca fighters marched against the rebel Girón in 1553. Their local kuraka dynasties survived under Spanish rule into the independence era.
zh: 万卡人（又称胡安卡）是秘鲁中部高原曼塔罗河谷的克丘亚民族，名称源自克丘亚语中当地常见的巨石碑“万卡”。考古学家把他们的前印卡史分为两期：1000—1350年的万卡一期，部落小村种植玉米、马铃薯和藜麦并放牧羊驼；1350—1460年的万卡二期，特征是大型设防山顶城镇的兴起。到15世纪，河谷由图南马卡、马卡维尔卡、琼戈斯、利亚克萨帕扬加和豪哈五个酋邦分据，并长期与邻族豪哈人、尧约人相争。约1460年，图帕克·尤潘基率领的印卡军队进入曼塔罗河谷，把诸酋邦并入塔万廷苏尤，当地改建为万卡省，以新建的大城哈通豪哈为行政中心。印卡内战中万卡人效忠库斯科政府，遭阿塔瓦尔帕一派报复；因此皮萨罗到来时他们倒向西班牙，出兵助其击败阿塔瓦尔帕派将领基斯基斯，此后继续为总督辖区效力，例如1553年曾有五百多名万卡战士出征反叛的希龙。他们的土著酋长世家在西班牙统治下一直延续到独立时代。

en: The Wajãpi, also recorded as Oiampi or Oyampi, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the lower Amazon and the Guiana frontier, the same lower-Xingu and Amazon-bottom country the game places them in. They speak a Tupi-Guarani language divided into the Amapari, Jari and Oyapock dialects, and live by slash-and-burn fields of cassava, sweet potato, yam and banana, supplemented by hunting and bow-and-arrow fishing. The earliest written mention, Portuguese records of 1690, describes them migrating from the lower Xingu to the Jari River and then pressing north along the Jari and Amapari into the forests between the Amazon and the Oyapock. They fought French colonists on that frontier, and a Jesuit mission founded on the Oyapock in 1738 brought European diseases and depopulation; when the Jesuits withdrew in 1763 the survivors scattered into the interior and deliberately isolated themselves, a people still numbering about six thousand in 1770. Only after 1820 did some northern groups reopen contact with French officials and Maroon communities, while most Wajãpi villages kept their distance. They were also partners in the long indigenous trade network run through the Wayana, exchanging cotton thread, hunting dogs and feather crowns for metal tools.
zh: 瓦扬皮人又被记作奥扬皮人，是亚马逊河下游与圭亚那边境的图皮—瓜拉尼语族群，活动于下兴古河与亚马逊河底地一带，与游戏的分布一致。他们使用的瓦扬皮语属图皮—瓜拉尼语，分阿马帕里、雅里、奥亚波克三种方言；生计依靠刀耕火种，种植木薯、甘薯、山药和香蕉，辅以狩猎和弓箭捕鱼。现存最早的文字记载是1690年的葡萄牙文献，记录他们从下兴古河迁至雅里河，再沿雅里河与阿马帕里河北上，进入亚马逊河与奥亚波克河之间的森林。他们在那边境与法国殖民者交战，1738年在奥亚波克河畔设立的耶稣会传教站带来欧洲疫病，造成人口锐减；1763年耶稣会士撤离后，幸存者散入内陆并主动与世隔绝，1770年时总人口仍约有六千。1820年以后，北部的一些群体才重新与法国官员和马龙人社区接触，而多数瓦扬皮村落仍保持距离。他们还参与了由瓦亚纳人串联的长途原住民贸易网，以棉线、猎犬和羽冠换取金属工具。

en: The Wapishana, also written Wapichan or Wapixana, are an Arawak-speaking people of the grasslands around Mount Roraima, in what is now northern Brazil and southern Guyana, where they share the Rupununi and Rio Branco savannahs with the Macushi and Pemon. Their tongue is the only Arawakan language of the circum-Roraima region, set amid a ring of Cariban-speaking neighbours. Their first indirect contact with Europeans came in 1498, when Columbus's third voyage reached the South American coast and goods began to move through Indigenous trade networks. From the seventeenth century Portuguese slave raiders pushed up the Branco River, and by the late 1700s Wapishana villagers were being settled and put to work around the Portuguese fort on the Rio Branco. Traditionally they lived by cassava farming, grating and toasting the root into flat bread, together with hunting deer and agouti, fishing, and crafts such as pottery and woven cotton hammocks; village leaders once practised polygyny and specialist healers treated the sick with leaf medicines and blowing rites.
zh: 瓦皮沙纳人（又拼作瓦皮昌、瓦皮夏纳）是罗赖马山一带草原上的阿拉瓦克语族群，生活在今巴西北部与圭亚那南部，在鲁普努尼和布朗库河稀树草原上与马库希人、佩蒙人相邻而居。他们的语言是罗赖马周边地区唯一的阿拉瓦克语，四周几乎都是说加勒比语的邻族。1498年哥伦布第三次航行抵达南美海岸，是他们与欧洲人的第一次间接接触，货物随即通过原住民的贸易网流转。17世纪起，葡萄牙奴隶贩子沿布朗库河向上游掳掠人口，到18世纪末，瓦皮沙纳村民已被葡萄牙人安置到布朗库河要塞附近服役。他们传统上以木薯种植为生，把木薯磨碎后烤成薄饼，同时猎捕鹿和刺豚鼠、捕鱼，并擅长制陶和编织棉布吊床；村落首领过去实行多妻制，专门的医者则用草药和吹气仪式为人治病。

en: The Wappo, who call themselves Micewal, are a Yukian-speaking people of northern California, whose villages stood in Napa Valley, Alexander Valley, the Russian River valley and on the south shore of Clear Lake. They split from their distant kin the Yuki at least five centuries ago, and their language, though unrelated to the speech of the Pomo around them, took in strong Pomo influence; the Pomo called them the northerners. Hunter-gatherers living in small bands without centralized chiefs, they built houses of branches, leaves and mud and wove baskets tight enough to hold water. With Spanish and Mexican settlement in Alta California, the Clear Lake Wappo were drawn into the mission system, which recorded at least 550 Wappo baptisms, while the Napa bands stubbornly resisted the soldiers of General Vallejo. Their resistance earned them the Spanish word for brave, from which the name Wappo derives, and the fighting ended only when the two sides signed a peace treaty in 1836.
zh: 米塞瓦尔人自称米塞瓦尔，是加利福尼亚北部讲尤基语系语言的族群，村落分布在纳帕谷、亚历山大谷、俄罗斯河谷以及克利尔湖南岸。他们与远亲尤基人至少在五个世纪前就已分化；其语言虽与周边波莫人的语言没有亲缘关系，却深受波莫语影响，波莫人把他们称为“北方人”。他们是没有统一首领、以小群活动的狩猎采集者，用树枝、树叶和泥盖房，编织的篮子细密到可以盛水。随着西班牙和墨西哥在上加利福尼亚建立殖民，克利尔湖的米塞瓦尔人被卷入传教体系，传教记录中至少有五百五十名米塞瓦尔人受洗；纳帕的各支则顽强抵抗巴列霍将军的军队。他们的抵抗为自己赢得了西班牙语中意为“勇敢者”的称号，“瓦波”一名即由此而来，战事直到1836年双方签订和约才告结束。

en: The Warao, whose name means the boat people, are the riverine inhabitants of the Orinoco Delta in eastern Venezuela, with kindred groups in Guyana, Suriname and Trinidad. Their own tradition holds that they were driven into the watery labyrinth of channels and marshes as refugees from more warlike tribes, and they may be the oldest surviving people of the Guianan coast, predating the Arawak and Carib arrivals. Life moves by dugout canoe between stilted houses raised above the floodwaters; they fish, catch crabs, harvest the moriche palm and only later took to small-scale farming, and their isolated Warao language belongs to no known family. Columbus sighted the delta coast in 1498 and Alonso de Ojeda explored the river mouth in 1499; the stilt villages he saw helped inspire the name Venezuela, or little Venice. Vicente Yáñez Pinzón charted the delta in 1500 and Diego de Ordaz sailed up the Orinoco in 1532, but the wetlands long shielded the Warao from conquest. The first mission among them was founded in 1682, and the Jesuit Joseph Gumilla published the first account of their culture in 1791; repeated Spanish and English attempts during the eighteenth century to settle them in fixed towns instead pushed many Warao to migrate toward Suriname.
zh: 瓦劳人的名字意为“船上的人”，是委内瑞拉东部奥里诺科三角洲依水而居的族群，在圭亚那、苏里南和特立尼达也有同源群体。据他们自己的传说，祖先为躲避更好战的部落，作为难民退入这片河汊与沼泽组成的水网；他们可能是圭亚那海岸最古老的存续族群，早于阿拉瓦克人和加勒比人的到来。出行全靠独木舟，房屋建在木桩上、高悬于洪水之上；他们捕鱼、捉蟹、采集莫里切棕榈，后来才兼营小规模农业，而孤立的瓦劳语不属于任何已知语系。1498年哥伦布望见三角洲海岸，1499年阿隆索·德·奥赫达探查河口，他所见的桩上村落促成了“委内瑞拉”（意为小威尼斯）这一名称。1500年维森特·亚涅斯·平松绘测三角洲，1532年迭戈·德·奥达斯溯奥里诺科河而上；但水网长期庇护瓦劳人免遭征服。1682年，他们中间建起第一座传教站，1791年耶稣会士约瑟夫·古米利亚发表了第一部记述其文化的著作；18世纪西班牙和英国当局一再试图把他们迁入固定城镇，反而促使许多瓦劳人迁往苏里南。

en: The Waray people are a Visayan ethnolinguistic group of the Eastern Visayas, occupying most of Samar, northern Leyte and the island of Biliran, where their Waray language is also called Lineyte-Samarnon. The Sohoton caves of Basey preserve stone flake tools left by ancient hunter-gatherers, while the Warays themselves descend from Iron Age Austronesian seafarers who built trading societies in contact with Chinese, Bornean and Malay merchants. In 1521 they became the first Filipinos encountered by Europeans, when Ferdinand Magellan's expedition met fishermen of Samar's east coast near Suluan Island, as recorded by Antonio Pigafetta. Jesuit missionaries reached Leyte in 1595 and within a decade had gathered much of the population into Catholic mission villages; the Spanish called these tattooed islanders Pintados, meaning the painted ones, and Bisaya. Their martial reputation survives in the saying that a Waray never retreats from a fight, and in the courtship dance kuratsa.
zh: 瓦瑞人是米沙鄢族群的一支，分布在东米沙鄢的萨马岛大部、莱特岛北部和比利兰岛，其语言瓦瑞语又称莱特-萨马尔农语。巴塞的索霍顿洞穴保存着远古狩猎采集者留下的石片工具，而瓦瑞人本身是铁器时代航海南岛移民的后裔，建立起与中国、婆罗洲和马来商人往来的贸易社会。1521年，他们成为欧洲人最早接触到的菲律宾人：斐迪南·麦哲伦的船队在苏卢安岛附近遇到萨马东海岸的渔民，此事由安东尼奥·皮加费塔记录下来。1595年耶稣会传教士抵达莱特，十年内便把大部分居民编入天主教传教村落；西班牙人把这些有文身习俗的岛民称作“平塔多斯”，意为文身者，又称他们为比沙亚人。他们尚武的名声见于“瓦瑞人打仗绝不后退”的谚语，求爱舞蹈库拉察也是其文化标志。

en: The Wardaman are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, whose traditional country of roughly 7,300 square kilometres ran from the headwaters of the upper Flora River west to the Victoria River Depot and south to Jasper Gorge, with their community centred on the Menngen Aboriginal Land Trust south-west of Katherine. They speak Wardaman, a non-Pama-Nyungan language related to those of their neighbours the Dagoman and Yangman. The Wardaman are known for their sandstone rock art, distinguishing buwarraja designs made by dreamtime beings, some at least 5,000 years old, from bulawula works made by people; the Yiwarlarlay site holds the giant images of the Lightning Brothers of dreamtime legend. European contact, shared with the Dagoman and Yangman, was violent from the outset, and as their tribal lands were turned into pastoral leases Wardaman men took up cattle-droving while women worked as station hands.
zh: 瓦达曼人是北领地的澳大利亚原住民，约7300平方公里的传统领地从弗洛拉河上游源头向西延伸至维多利亚河驿站，南抵贾斯珀峡谷，社区以凯瑟琳西南的门根原住民土地信托区为中心。他们使用非帕马-牛雅语的瓦达曼语，与邻族达戈曼人和阳曼人的语言相近。瓦达曼人以砂岩岩画闻名，把创世神灵在梦创时代留下的布瓦拉贾图案（部分至少有5000年历史）与人制作的布拉乌拉作品区分开来；伊瓦拉莱遗址保留着梦创传说中“闪电兄弟”的巨型画像。他们与达戈曼人、阳曼人一样，最初与欧洲人的接触充满暴力；随着部落领地变为牧场租地，瓦达曼男子转而赶牛，女子则在牧场帮工。

en: The Wargamaygani, or Warrgamay, are the Aboriginal people of Halifax Bay in northern Queensland, holding about fifty miles of coastline and, by one estimate, some six hundred square miles of country stretching fifteen miles into the hinterland. Their northern neighbours were the Girramay and their southern neighbours the Wulgurukaba. Their now extinct language, Warrgamay, was a Dyirbalic Pama-Nyungan tongue with three dialects: Wargamaygan on the lower Herbert River, Biyay at the river mouth around Halifax, and Hinchinbrook Biyay along the coast south of Cardwell and on Hinchinbrook Island. Clans such as the Ikelbara, Mungulbara and Karabara made up the people; initiation used tooth avulsion, scarification and nose-bone piercing rather than circumcision, polygamy was common, and a widow was married to her dead husband's brother.
zh: 瓦加梅甘人又称瓦尔加梅人，是昆士兰北部哈利法克斯湾的原住民，据估计领有约六百平方英里土地，占据约五十英里海岸线并向内陆延伸十五英里；北邻吉拉梅人，南接伍尔古鲁卡巴人。他们现已消亡的语言瓦尔加梅语是迪尔巴利语支的帕马-牛雅语，分三种方言：赫伯特河下游的瓦加梅甘方言、河口哈利法克斯一带的比亚伊方言，以及卡德韦尔以南沿海和欣钦布鲁克岛上的欣钦布鲁克比亚伊方言。他们由伊克尔巴拉、蒙古尔巴拉、卡拉巴拉等氏族组成；成年礼不行割礼，而采用拔牙、刻痕和穿鼻戴骨的仪式，一夫多妻普遍，寡妇须嫁给亡夫的兄弟。

en: The Wari, or Huari, are the people of the Middle Horizon civilization of that name, whose capital stood on the high plateau eleven kilometres north-east of modern Ayacucho. From about 500 to 1000 the Wari state spread across the south-central Andes and the Peruvian coast, planting administrative centres such as Jincamocco in the Carahuarazo valley around 600, Pikillaqta near Cuzco and Cerro Baúl in Moquegua, and drawing the oracle city of Pachacamac and the old lands of the Moche into its orbit. Its governors built fieldstone compounds plastered white and D-shaped temples, extended terrace agriculture and maize farming into the provinces, strung roads between the centres, and held power through feasts, camelid offerings and the worship of the Staff God, whose image later fed into Inca religion. Centuries of drought began to undo the state around 800: by 1000 the capital had been largely abandoned, its doorways deliberately sealed, and rival groups fought over its ruins as the Late Intermediate Period began. Small descendant communities still lived among the old cities, and Wari roads and terraces were later taken up by the Inca.
zh: 瓦里人创造了安第斯中期视野的同名文明，都城在今阿亚库乔东北11公里的高原上，约500年至1000年间兴盛于安第斯山脉中南部和秘鲁沿海一带。瓦里国家在各地广建行政治理中心，如600年前后在卡拉瓦拉索谷地设立的钦卡莫科、库斯科附近的皮卡拉克塔和莫克瓜的塞罗巴乌尔，并把神谕之城帕查卡马克以及莫切故地纳入势力范围。统治者用刷白灰的毛石围墙和D形神庙治理地方，把梯田农业和玉米耕作推广到外省，以道路连接各中心，靠宴饮、羊驼献祭和对杖神的崇拜维系统治，杖神形象后来融入印加宗教。数百年干旱从800年前后开始侵蚀这个国家：到1000年，都城大半废弃，门洞被有意封死，敌对群体在废墟间争战，晚中间期由此开端。少数后裔仍住在古城之中，而瓦里人的道路和梯田后来为印加人所承袭。

en: The Warluwarrai, known in the records as Waluwara or Walugara, are an Aboriginal people of the Georgina River country in western Queensland, taking their name from their Warluwarra language, a member of the Ngarna or Warluwaric branch of Pama-Nyungan. Norman Tindale assigned them about 18,000 square kilometres along the Georgina, from Roxborough Downs north to Carandotta and Urandangi, taking in Moonah Creek and Rochedale and reaching south-west to Pituri Creek. They were formed of several hordes, among them the Didjadidja at Roxborough, the Kapula at Carandotta and the Panggara on Moonah Creek, and their initiation life centred on the Miki ceremony, whose rites included subincision. Early word lists of their speech were collected along the same river runs, and variant names include Walukara, Warluwara and Paringgara, meaning creek dwellers.
zh: 瓦鲁瓦拉人在文献中又称瓦鲁瓦拉人或瓦卢加拉人，是昆士兰西部佐治那河流域的原住民，族名来自他们的瓦鲁瓦拉语，该语言属帕马-牛雅语的恩加尔纳（瓦鲁瓦里克）语支。诺曼·廷代尔划定其沿佐治那河的领地约1.8万平方公里，北起罗克斯伯勒当斯，北至卡兰多塔和乌兰丹吉，包括莫纳溪与罗奇代尔，西南达皮图里溪。他们由若干游群组成，已知的有罗克斯伯勒的迪贾迪贾、卡兰多塔的卡普拉和莫纳溪的潘加拉；成年礼以米基仪式为核心，仪式中包含下切礼。早期的词语记录正是在这些河畔牧道上采集的，异名还有瓦卢卡拉、瓦鲁瓦拉和意为“溪居者”的帕林加拉。

en: The Warnindilyakwan are the Aboriginal people of Groote Eylandt and the neighbouring Bickerton and Woodah Islands in the Gulf of Carpentaria; the name properly denotes one clan of the island's south-eastern Dilyakburra peninsula, and the fourteen clans of the archipelago are also known collectively as the Anindilyakwa. They speak Anindilyakwa, a language unrelated to the Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia, with an unusually complex grammar. Long before Europeans reached their waters, Macassan traders from Sulawesi sailed to the islands each monsoon, exchanging beads, metal, ceramics and fishing hooks for trepang, beeswax, ironwood and pearls bound for the Chinese market. In 1803 Matthew Flinders encountered a fleet of sixty Macassan praus under the chief Pobasso nearby, a sign of how large this seasonal trade had grown; Macassan words for tobacco, cloth and alcohol, and the tamarind tree, entered island life through these voyages.
zh: 瓦宁迪利亚夸人是卡奔塔利亚湾格鲁特岛及邻近的比克顿岛、伍达岛上的原住民；该名称本指岛屿东南部迪利亚布拉半岛的一个氏族，群岛上的十四个氏族也统称为阿宁迪利亚夸人。他们使用的阿宁迪利亚夸语不属于覆盖澳大利亚多数语言的帕马—牛雅语系，语法格外复杂。早在欧洲人到来之前，苏拉威西的望加锡商人每年季风时节便航行到这些岛屿，用珠子、金属、陶器和鱼钩换取销往中国市场的海参、蜂蜡、铁木和珍珠。1803年，马修·弗林德斯在附近遇到望加锡首领波巴索率领的六十艘帆船组成的船队，可见这种季节性贸易规模之大；望加锡语中烟草、布匹和酒的词汇以及罗望子树，都随着这些航行进入了岛上的生活。

en: The Waropen are an Austronesian-speaking coastal people of the eastern shore of Cenderawasih Bay, formerly Geelvink Bay, in northern New Guinea, their villages spanning the country around the Waropen and Mamberamo Raya districts, with the Ambumi or Waruri branch extending west into Wondama Bay. Their own tradition derives the name Waropen from a word meaning people of the interior: the ancestors are said to have come down from Mount Tonater at Wamusopedai and spread along the coast in three branches, Ambumi, Kai and Ronari. Their language, with its Ambumi, Napan and Waropen Kai dialects, is closely related to the Austronesian languages of nearby Yapen Island. Society was built on clans called da, gathered into villages called nu; in wartime and slave-raiding expeditions the clans united under a leader titled Sera, the foremost of whom bore the title Serabawah. The first recorded European encounter came on 30 May 1705, when the Dutch explorer Jacob Weyland, sailing with the ships Geelvink, Kraanvogel and Nova Guinea, reached a settlement he recorded as Erropang.
zh: 瓦罗彭人是新几内亚岛北部极乐鸟湾（旧称海尔芬克湾）东岸的南岛语系滨海族群，村落分布在瓦罗彭和大曼伯拉莫一带，西迁的安布米支系又称瓦鲁里人，远至温达马湾。按他们自己的传说，“瓦罗彭”意为“来自内陆的人”：先祖从瓦穆索佩代的托纳特山顺流下到海岸，分成安布米、卡伊和罗纳里三支扩散。他们的语言分安布米、纳潘和瓦罗彭卡伊三种方言，与邻近亚彭岛上的南岛语关系密切。传统社会以名为“达”的氏族为单位，若干氏族组成名为“努”的村落；遇战事或掳奴远征，各氏族便联合起来，拥戴一位称塞拉的首领，其中资历最高者称塞拉巴瓦。1705年5月30日，荷兰探险家雅各布·韦兰率海尔芬克号、克兰福赫尔号和新几内亚号三船抵达一处他记作埃罗庞的定居点，这是现存最早的欧洲人接触记录。

en: The Warpe, or Huarpes, were the Indigenous people of the Cuyo region east of the Andes, in what became the Argentine provinces of San Juan, Mendoza and San Luis. From the fifth century they lived in settled villages of fifty to a hundred people, farming corn, beans, squash and quinoa on the land between the Jachal and Diamante rivers. Their territory reached from the Andes to the Conlara valley, and the lagoons of Guanacache were one of their heartlands. They were never fully absorbed into the Inca Empire, though after about 1480 Inca influence brought llama herding and Quechua into their culture. They spoke two related languages, Allentiac and Millcayac, of which only fragmentary records survive. After the Spanish conquest, encomenderos moved large numbers of Warpe across the Andes to work in Chile, while the communities left around Guanacache were gradually assimilated or merged with other displaced groups during the colonial centuries.
zh: 瓦尔佩人（即瓦尔佩诸部）是安第斯山脉以东库约地区的原住民，生活在后来的阿根廷圣胡安、门多萨和圣路易斯诸省。从5世纪起，他们便以五六十人至上百人的定居村落为生，在哈查尔河与迪亚曼特河之间种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜和藜麦。其领地西起安第斯山脉、东到孔拉腊河谷，瓜纳卡切潟湖一带是他们的核心区域之一。他们从未被完全并入印加帝国，但约1480年以后，印加影响带来了养驼业和克丘亚语。瓦尔佩人讲两种亲属语言——阿伦蒂亚克语和米尔卡亚克语，这两种语言只留下零散的记录。西班牙征服后，委托监护主把大量瓦尔佩人迁过安第斯山到智利做工，留在瓜纳卡切周边的群体则在殖民时代逐渐被同化，或与其他流离的族群融合。

en: The Warumungu, also spelt Warramunga, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Northern Territory, whose country centred on Tennant Creek, on the western edge of the Barkly Tableland, where permanent waterholes along the creek drew them together in drought years. Their language is a Pama-Nyungan tongue close to Warlpiri, forming verbs through tense suffixes, and alongside spoken words the Warumungu maintain a highly developed sign language. European explorers who first encountered them in the late nineteenth century described a flourishing people, but the telegraph station, pastoral runs and later gold mines built at Tennant Creek brought dispossession and frontier violence, shared with their Kaytetye and Warlpiri neighbours, and the Warumungu were progressively pushed from their ancestral grounds.
zh: 瓦拉蒙加人是北领地中部的澳大利亚原住民，领地以巴克利台地西缘的滕南特克里克为中心，旱季时人们会汇聚到溪边常年不涸的水潭。他们的语言属帕马‑牛雅语系，与瓦尔皮里语相近，动词通过时态后缀构形；除口语外，瓦拉蒙加人还保有一套高度发达的手语。19世纪末最早接触他们的欧洲探险家曾记述这是一个繁盛的族群，但滕南特克里克建起电报站、牧场和后来的金矿后，他们与邻族凯蒂切人、瓦尔皮里人一样遭到剥夺和边疆暴力，逐渐被赶出祖先的土地。

en: The Warrwa, also spelt Warwa, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Kimberley region of Western Australia. Their country, estimated by Norman Tindale at roughly 9,800 square kilometres, follows the eastern shore of King Sound from the Fraser River to Round Hill on Stokes Bay and reaches inland to the upper Logue River; they also lived around Derby and north of Meda, with the Umiida to their north, the Unggumi to their east and the Nyikina to their south. Their speech is an eastern Nyulnyulan language so close to Nyikina that it is often classified as a Nyikina dialect. Before European contact the Nyikina pushed down the Fitzroy River and split the Warrwa clans into a western ‘little Warrwa’ and an eastern ‘big Warrwa’ around Derby and Meda. The first European to explore their coast was William Dampier, who entered King Sound aboard the Cygnet in 1688.
zh: 瓦尔瓦人是西澳大利亚州金伯利地区的澳大利亚原住民。据诺曼·廷代尔估算，其领地约9800平方公里，沿金湾东岸从弗雷泽河延伸到斯托克斯湾的朗德希尔，内陆直抵洛格河上游；他们还活动在德比一带和梅达以北，北邻乌米达人，东接翁古米人，南面是尼基纳人。瓦尔瓦语是纽尔纽尔语系东部的语言，与尼基纳语极为接近，常被归为尼基纳语的方言。在欧洲人到来之前，尼基纳人沿菲茨罗伊河向下游推进，把瓦尔瓦诸氏族切成两部分：西部的‘小瓦尔瓦’和德比、梅达一带东部的‘大瓦尔瓦’。最早考察他们海岸的欧洲人是威廉·丹皮尔，他于1688年乘‘西格尼特号’驶入金湾。

en: The Wata-deka are the Watatikka, the Ryegrass Seed Eaters of the Western Shoshone, whose winter home was Ruby Valley in north-eastern Nevada. Their country adjoined those of related Western Shoshone bands: the Tipatikka or Pinenut Eaters to the east in northern Utah, the Kuyatikka or Bitterroot Eaters of Marys River and Clover Valley, the Mahaguadüka, who gathered Mentzelia seeds along Reese River, and the Tsogwiyuyugi around Elko. Numic-speaking foragers entered the Great Basin around the fourteenth century, and by 1500 Shoshone speakers occupied most of Nevada. Like other Western Shoshone bands they took their name from their staple food, moved in small family groups between seasonal camps, and harvested pine nuts in the autumn mountains, returning to the same winter villages year after year.
zh: 瓦塔德卡人即瓦塔蒂卡人，意为“食黑麦草籽者”，属西部休休尼人，冬季聚居在内华达东北部的鲁比瓦利。与他们相邻的是同属西部休休尼人的若干部族：东边犹他北部的蒂帕蒂卡人（食松子者）、玛丽河与三叶草谷的库亚蒂卡人（食苦根者）、沿里斯河采集刺莲花籽的马哈瓜迪卡人，以及埃尔科一带的措格维尤吉人。说努米克语的采集狩猎者约在14世纪进入大盆地，到1500年前后，说休休尼语的部族已占据内华达大部。与其他西部休休尼部族一样，他们以主食得名，以小家庭为单位在季节性营地间迁徙，秋天进山采收松子，年复一年回到同一处冬村。

en: The Wathaurongi are the Wadawurrung, a nation of the Kulin alliance whose territory of about seven thousand eight hundred square kilometres centred on Corio Bay and Geelong, taking in the Bellarine Peninsula and running inland past Lake Burrumbeet toward the Ballarat country. Their land had been occupied for tens of thousands of years, and twenty-five clans, each led by a headman called a n'arweet on the coast or a nourenit inland, spoke a Kulinic language of the Pama-Nyungan family. In December 1803 the escaped convict William Buckley stumbled among them from the abandoned Sullivan Bay settlement; the band took him for the resurrected leader Murrangurk, adopted him and in time made him a headman, and he lived with them for thirty-two years until he returned to the Europeans in 1835. That same year squatters began pouring into the Geelong district, and Wadawurrung resistance, chiefly raids on sheep, was met with reprisal killings; when the headman Woolmudgin was killed in 1836, his case collapsed in court because Aboriginal people were barred from giving evidence.
zh: 瓦绍隆人即瓦达伍伦人，属库林族群联盟，领地约七千八百平方公里，以科里奥湾和吉朗为中心，涵盖贝拉林半岛，并向内陆越过伯伦比特湖延伸到巴拉瑞特一带。这片土地已被人类占据数万年之久；他们分为二十五个氏族，各有首领，沿海称“纳威特”，内陆称“诺雷尼特”，所说的语言属帕马-牛雅语系的库林语支。1803年12月，从沙利文湾流放地逃出的犯人威廉·巴克利来到他们中间；族人以为他是死而复生的首领穆兰古克，收留了他，后来还立他为首领。巴克利与他们共同生活了三十二年，直到1835年才回到欧洲人当中。同年，牧地占用者开始涌入吉朗地区，瓦绍隆人以袭击羊群为主的抵抗招来报复性屠杀；1836年首领伍尔马金被杀，案子却因原住民无权出庭作证而在法庭上不了了之。

en: The Watjarri, also spelt Wajarri or Wadjarri, are an Aboriginal people of the Murchison country in the Mid West of Western Australia. Their traditional lands covered an estimated 91,000 square kilometres, reaching the hills around the upper Lyons and Gascoyne rivers in the north, running to Byro and Dalgety Downs in the west and down to the Roderick and upper Sanford rivers in the south. Their language is one of the Kartu branch of the Pama-Nyungan family, and their word Yamatji, originally meaning a Watjarri person, later became the name for all Aboriginal people of the Murchison region. Their neighbours included the Yinggarda to the west and the Badimaya to the south-east. When the Swan River Colony was founded far to the south in 1829 this dry inland country remained beyond the colonial frontier, and pastoral leases only spread into it in the later nineteenth century.
zh: 瓦贾里人是西澳大利亚中西部默奇森地区的原住民。他们的传统领地约9.1万平方公里，北至莱昂斯河和加斯科因河上游一带的山地，西抵拜罗和达尔盖蒂当斯，南达罗德里克河与桑福德河上游。他们的语言属帕马-牛雅语系的卡尔图语支；他们的词“亚马吉”本指瓦贾里人，后来成为整个默奇森地区原住民的统称。邻族有西边的英加达人与东南的巴迪玛亚人。1829年天鹅河殖民地在遥远的南方建立时，这片干旱的内陆仍在殖民边疆之外，直到19世纪后期牧地租约才延伸进来。

en: The Waunana, also called Wounaan, Chanco or Noanamá, are one of the two peoples of the Chocó, alongside the Emberá, and speak Woun Meu, one of the surviving Chocoan languages, a family unrelated to any other in the Americas. Their ancestral homeland is the lower San Juan River and the rainy Pacific lowlands of the Chocó in western Colombia, where they practice shifting agriculture, growing maize, plantains, sugar cane and cassava, supplementing it with fishing and with fine basketry woven from werregue palm. Descent is matrilineal and polygamy is traditional; extended families live in circular thatched tambos raised on stilts against the floods, guided in matters of health and the spirits by jaibaná shamans. From the late 1700s Spanish pressure in the Chocó pushed Waunana groups, together with the Emberá, across the Darién into Panama, where they settled the river valleys of the Darién Gap.
zh: 瓦乌纳纳人又称沃南人、昌科人或诺阿纳马人，与恩贝拉人并为乔科人的两大支系，使用乔科语族仅存的语言之一沃恩梅乌语；该语族与美洲其他语言都没有亲缘关系。他们的故土在哥伦比亚西部乔科地区的圣胡安河下游和多雨的太平洋低地，在那里从事轮耕农业，种植玉米、大蕉、甘蔗和木薯，兼事渔捞，并用韦雷格棕榈编织精美的篮筐。他们按母系继嗣，传统上实行多妻制；大家族住在高脚的圆形茅草屋坦博里，以躲避洪水，健康和通灵之事则由海巴纳萨满主持。18世纪末，西班牙人在乔科的压迫迫使瓦乌纳纳人与恩贝拉人一起穿过达连地峡迁入巴拿马，在达连隘口的河谷中定居下来。

en: The Waveroo, also written Waywurru, were one of the principal groups of the Pallanganmiddang people of north-eastern Victoria, whose country took in the upper Murray lands around the Ovens and King rivers, the Wangaratta district and Mount Buffalo. Their language, Pallanganmiddang, forms together with Dhudhuroa the Upper Murray group of Pama-Nyungan and was noted by early observers as utterly unlike the speech of neighbouring peoples. The Waveroo had adopted the Kulin system of eaglehawk and crow moieties inherited through the father, with clans such as the Yowung-illam-balluk of Mount Buffalo and the Warrarak-balluk around Wangaratta intermarrying with nearby Kulin groups. The Hume and Hovell expedition crossed their country in 1824, and Major Thomas Mitchell's favourable report of 1836 opened the way for pastoral squatters who soon occupied the river flats.
zh: 瓦弗鲁人又译韦武鲁人，是维多利亚州东北部帕兰甘米唐人的主要支系之一，其领地包括欧文斯河与金河流域、旺加拉塔地区和布法罗山一带的墨累河上游土地。他们的帕兰甘米唐语与杜杜罗阿语共同构成帕马-尼永加语系的上墨累语组，早期观察者就指出它与周边族群的语言截然不同。瓦弗鲁人采用了库林人的鹰氏与鸦氏半族制度，半族身份沿父系继承；布法罗山的约温伊拉姆巴卢克和旺加拉塔周围的瓦拉拉克巴卢克等氏族，与邻近的库林族群互通婚姻。1824年休姆与霍维尔探险队穿过他们的土地，1836年托马斯·米切尔少校的有利考察报告又为牧场主敞开大门，河畔平地很快被占据。

en: Waxiang is the speech of the Waxiang people of the Wuling mountains in north-western Hunan, centred on Yuanling and reaching Dayong, the country of the later Zhangjiajie, and the neighbouring counties of Luxi, Guzhang and Yongshun. Although most Waxiang speakers are counted among the Miao, their language is a deeply divergent branch of Chinese, quite unlike the Southwestern Mandarin, Xiang and Eastern Miao tongues around it and preserving Old Chinese initials lost almost everywhere else; its name means roughly rural speech, with the first character used only for its sound. These valleys were the old Qin and Han commanderies of Qianzhong and Wuling on the edge of the Chinese world, and through the Yuan and the Ming after 1368 they remained under native tusi chieftains until the Qing replaced them with imperial officials.
zh: 瓦乡是湘西武陵山区瓦乡人的语言，以沅陵为中心，延伸到大庸（后来张家界一带）及泸溪、古丈、永顺等相邻县份。瓦乡人虽多被划入苗族，但瓦乡话是汉语中一支极为分化的方言，与周围的西南官话、湘语和苗语东部方言都很不同，保留了别处几乎消失的上古汉语声母；其名称大意是乡野之话，首字仅为记音。这些山谷地处华夏边缘，曾是秦、汉黔中郡、武陵郡的旧地；元代以及1368年建立的明代，这里长期由土著土司统辖，直到清代改土归流，才由朝廷流官治理。

en: The Wayuu, also called Guajiro, are an Arawakan-speaking people of the arid Guajira Peninsula on the Caribbean coast, straddling present-day Colombia and Venezuela. Organized into matrilineal clans, they live in scattered rancherías of five or six houses, herd goats, fish and gather, and are famed for their woven mochila bags. They were never subdued by the Spanish: the two sides remained in a more or less permanent state of war, marked by rebellions in 1701, 1727, 1741, 1757, 1761 and 1768. Uniquely among the Indigenous peoples of the region, the Wayuu adopted horses and firearms, obtaining guns from English and Dutch smugglers in exchange for pearls and brazilwood. The great Guajira rebellion of 1769 began after Spaniards seized Wayuu to build the fortifications of Cartagena; at its height some twenty thousand warriors took nearly every settlement in the region and burned them, and although Spanish reinforcements ended the rising, the Wayuu kept their autonomy and their arms through the rest of the colonial period.
zh: 瓦尤人又称瓜希罗人，是加勒比海岸干旱的瓜希拉半岛上的阿拉瓦克语族群，分布在今哥伦比亚与委内瑞拉交界一带。他们按母系氏族组织，散居在由五六间房屋组成的牧场村落里，放牧山羊、渔猎采集，以编织的莫奇拉挎包闻名。西班牙人从未征服他们：双方几乎长期处于战争状态，1701、1727、1741、1757、1761和1768年都爆发过起义。在当地原住民中，瓦尤人独树一帜地学会了使用马匹和火器，用珍珠和巴西红木向英国、荷兰走私商换取枪支。1769年的瓜希拉大起义，起因是西班牙人抓捕瓦尤人去修建卡塔赫纳防御工事；起义高潮时约两万名战士攻占并焚毁了地区内几乎所有定居点。尽管西班牙援军最终平息了起义，瓦尤人在整个殖民时代余下的时间里仍保住了自治和武装。

en: The Wea were a Miami-Illinois-speaking people of western Indiana, counted either as a subtribe of the Miami or as their close kin. Their autonym Waayaahtanwa comes from waayaahtanonki, the place of the whirlpool, the village where French writers first recorded them in 1673. In the early eighteenth century they settled the middle Wabash Valley between the sites of present-day Terre Haute and Logansport, with their chief town of Ouiatenon near modern Lafayette; the French built Fort Ouiatenon there to trade with them and the Kickapoo, and the related Pepikokia band merged into them in 1742. Numbering perhaps twelve hundred in 1765, the Wea joined Pontiac's War against the British in 1763 and later fought beside the Miami in the Revolutionary War and the frontier conflicts that followed. Under the United States removal policy they were forced across the Mississippi into Missouri and Arkansas in 1820, and the surviving Wea eventually merged with the Kaskaskia, Piankeshaw and Peoria into the Confederated Peoria.
zh: 威亚人是居于印第安纳西部、操迈阿密—伊利诺伊语的族群，被视为迈阿密人的分支或近亲。他们的自称瓦亚坦瓦源自瓦亚塔农基，意为漩涡之地，那是1673年法国文献首次记载他们时所在的村庄。18世纪初，他们定居在今特雷霍特与洛根斯波特之间的沃巴什河中游，主村维亚特农靠近今拉斐特；法国人在当地修建维亚特农堡，与他们和基卡普人贸易，同族的佩皮科基亚队伍也于1742年并入威亚人。1765年威亚人约有一千二百人，1763年参加了庞蒂亚克反英战争，后来又在独立战争及此后的边疆冲突中与迈阿密人并肩作战。在美国的迁徙政策下，他们于1820年被密西西比河以西的密苏里和阿肯色强行安置，幸存的威亚人最终与卡斯卡斯基亚人、皮安克肖人和皮奥里亚人合并为皮奥里亚联盟。

en: The Welsh, who call themselves Cymry, are the Brittonic people of the mountainous west of Britain, heirs of the Ordovices, Silures and other Iron Age tribes whose Common Brittonic speech became Old Welsh while the rest of lowland Britain turned to English. After the Roman withdrawal they formed competing kingdoms, above all Gwynedd, Powys and Deheubarth, bound together by the Welsh law codified under Hywel Dda and by a celebrated bardic tradition; Offa's Dyke, raised in the eighth century, marked the frontier with Mercia. Gruffudd ap Llywelyn briefly united the country before his death in 1063, and after the Norman Conquest marcher lords gnawed at the southern and eastern lowlands until Edward I destroyed Gwynedd in 1282, killing Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and building the castles that made the English heir Prince of Wales. The last great rising, under Owain Glyndŵr from 1400, briefly won a Welsh parliament and church of its own but collapsed within a decade. The Tudors, themselves of Welsh descent, ended the legal distinction between Wales and England with the Laws in Wales Acts of 1535 and 1542, yet William Morgan's Welsh Bible of 1588 preserved Cymraeg as a literary and congregational language. In the eighteenth century the Methodist revival made Nonconformist chapels the heart of Welsh life and the eisteddfod kept its poetry and music alive, while the coal and iron boom drew the rural Welsh into the industrial valleys of the south.
zh: 威尔士人自称 Cymry，是不列颠西部山区的布立吞人后裔，承自奥多维克人、西卢尔人等铁器时代部落；当低地不列颠普遍改说英语时，他们的通用布立吞语演变成了古威尔士语。罗马撤离后，他们形成格温内思、波伊斯、德赫巴思等相互争胜的王国，以海韦尔·达编定的威尔士法和发达的吟游传统维系共同认同；8世纪修筑的奥法堤划出了与麦西亚的边界。格鲁菲德·阿普·卢埃林曾在1063年去世前短暂统一威尔士；诺曼征服后，边境领主不断蚕食东南低地，直到爱德华一世于1282年攻灭格温内思，击杀卢埃林·阿普·格鲁菲德，广建城堡，并让英格兰王储兼领威尔士亲王头衔。最后一次大起义由欧文·格兰道尔于1400年发动，一度争得威尔士自己的议会和教会，却在十年内失败。本身有威尔士血统的都铎王朝通过1535和1542年的《威尔士法案》取消了威尔士与英格兰的法律差异，但1588年威廉·摩根的威尔士语圣经保住了威尔士语作为文学和教会语言的地位。18世纪循道宗复兴使非国教小教堂成为威尔士生活的中心，艾斯特德福德诗会延续着诗歌与音乐；与此同时，煤铁热潮把乡村威尔士人吸进南部的工业山谷。

en: The Wemba-Wemba, also written Wamba-Wamba, are an Aboriginal people of the Murray and its tributaries in north-western Victoria and the adjoining Riverina and Mallee country of New South Wales, around lake systems such as Lake Boga. Their language is a Kulin tongue of the Pama-Nyungan family, close to Woiwurrung; its name follows the common Murray basin pattern of reduplicating the word for no, wemba, and Barababaraba was among its dialects while Nari Nari may have been another. Their religious life centred on the Dreaming, which they called yemurraki. When Moravian missionaries settled at Gannawarra station to learn the language, the Wemba-Wemba deliberately switched tongues so that outsiders could not penetrate matters they meant to keep secret. The first European to cross their territory was the explorer Thomas Mitchell in 1836, whose reports of well-watered grazing plains soon drew squatters in his wake.
zh: 温巴温巴人又译万巴万巴人，是墨累河及其支流一带的澳大利亚原住民，地跨维多利亚州西北部与新南威尔士州相邻的里弗赖纳和马利地区，环居博加湖等湖系。他们的语言属帕马-尼永加语系的库林语族，与沃伊武朗语相近；其名字遵循墨累河流域常见的重叠构词，由意为“不”的温巴一词重叠而成。巴拉巴话是它的方言之一，纳里纳里话可能也是。他们的宗教生活以称为耶穆拉基的梦创时代信仰为核心。摩拉维亚传教士在加纳瓦拉牧场站住下来学习这种语言时，温巴温巴人便故意换用别的语言，不让外人探知他们有意保密的事物。1836年，探险家托马斯·米切尔成为第一个穿过他们领地的欧洲人，他对水草丰美牧原的记述很快引来了大批牧场主。

en: The Wenrohronon, or Wenro, were an Iroquoian people of western New York, whose territory lay south of Lake Ontario between the Niagara and Genesee rivers, east of the Neutral and west of the Seneca. Their name has been read as 'people at the place of the floating scum', a reference to the oil springs in their country, the first recorded petroleum source in what became the United States. Closely related to the Neutral and speaking a tongue intelligible to the Wendat, they lived in longhouse villages under matrilineal clans and farmed maize, beans and squash. Long shielded by the Neutral Confederacy against Seneca raids, they lost that protection in 1638 during the Beaver Wars, and more than six hundred refugees fled through Neutral country to the Wendat village of Ossossané on Nottawasaga Bay. When the Haudenosaunee shattered the Wendat and Petun in 1648 and 1649, the surviving Wenro fled with them and were absorbed into the people who became the Wyandot.
zh: 温罗赫农人（简称温罗人）是纽约州西部的易洛魁语民族，领地位于安大略湖以南、尼亚加拉河与杰纳西河之间，在中立族以东、塞内卡族以西。其族名被解释为‘浮渣之地的人’，得名于境内的油泉——那是后来的美国境内最早见于记载的石油来源。他们与中立族关系密切，所说的语言与休伦语可以互通，住在长屋村落中，按母系氏族组织生活，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜。海狸战争期间，长期庇护他们、抵御塞内卡人袭扰的中立联盟于1638年撤回保护，六百多名温罗难民穿过中立族领地，逃到诺塔瓦萨加湾的休伦人村落奥索萨内。1648—1649年易洛魁联盟击溃休伦人和佩顿人后，幸存的温罗人随之一同逃亡，最终并入后来形成的怀恩多特人之中。

en:
The Wergaian are the Wergaia, also called Maligundidj, the people of the mallee eucalypt bushland, in the Mallee and Wimmera country of north-western Victoria. Their estates took in the Wimmera River and the chain of lakes from Lake Hindmarsh and Lake Albacutya to the Hattah Lakes, and their language was a dialect of Wemba-Wemba in the Kulinic branch of the Pama-Nyungan family. Some twenty clans shared the country under a matrilineal order of two cockatoo moieties, the black-cockatoo gabadj and the white-cockatoo grugidj, whose skin relations determined marriage; they often intermarried with the Jardwadjali and Dja Dja Wurrung and gathered for ceremony with the Wadi Wadi and Ladji Ladji peoples to their north. In their Dreaming the eaglehawk man Bunjil made the world with the Bram Bram Ngul brothers, who shaped the first people from a tree.

The Boorong clan on Lake Tyrrell were meticulous astronomers: the rising of Arcturus told them when to harvest wood-ant larvae, the setting of Vega marked the season for malleefowl eggs, and the sun was an emu egg hurled into the dark sky by the ancestor Pupperimbul. Smallpox from the First Fleet of 1788 spread down the Murray ahead of any European, the elders naming it thinba micka, and when Major Thomas Mitchell crossed their lakes in 1836 he became the first white man most Wergaia had seen, his published reports soon drawing sheep stations behind him.
zh:
韦尔盖亚人即韦尔盖亚族群，又称马利贡迪吉，意为“马利桉灌丛之地的人”，居住在维多利亚州西北部的马利与威默拉地区。他们的领地涵盖威默拉河以及从欣德马什湖、阿尔巴库蒂亚湖到哈塔湖的湖群，语言属帕马—牛雅语系库林语支，是韦姆巴—韦姆巴语的一种方言。约二十个氏族在母系制度下共享这片土地，社会分为黑凤头鹦鹉“加巴吉”和白凤头鹦鹉“格鲁吉吉”两个偶族，氏族关系决定通婚规则；他们常与贾德瓦贾里人、贾贾伍伦人联姻，又北上与瓦迪瓦迪人、拉吉拉吉人聚会举行仪式。在他们的梦幻传说里，鹰人本吉尔与布拉姆·布拉姆·恩古尔兄弟共同创世，兄弟二人用树木塑出了最初的人。

蒂勒尔湖畔的布龙氏族是精细的天文观测者：大角星升起意味着可以采挖木蚁幼虫，织女星落下标志着眼斑冢雉的蛋可以捡拾，而太阳是始祖普佩林布尔扔进黑暗天空的一枚鸸鹋蛋。1788年第一舰队带来的天花先于任何欧洲人顺墨累河传来，长者称之为“辛巴·米卡”；1836年托马斯·米切尔少校穿过他们的湖群，成为多数韦尔盖亚人见到的第一个白人，他发表的游记很快把牧羊站引到了这里。

en: The Weskarini, also called Wàwàckeciriniwak, the people of the deer, and known to the French as La Petite Nation, were an Algonquian people of the lower Ottawa valley. Their hunting grounds lay on the north side of the Ottawa River, around the Lièvre, Rouge and Petite-Nation rivers of present-day western Quebec, and they kept close trade ties with the Wyandot of the Great Lakes. Samuel de Champlain met them on his journey up the Ottawa in 1613, and French missionaries later recorded a settled Christian community under the chief Charles Pachirini near Trois-Rivières. The Beaver Wars proved catastrophic: Iroquois raids scattered the Algonquian bands of the Ottawa valley, and Weskarini fighting strength was largely destroyed in the clashes of 1654. Survivors had already begun drifting east, and by the later seventeenth century the Weskarini ceased to appear as a separate political people, their descendants merging into other Algonquin communities of the St Lawrence and Ottawa valleys.
zh: 韦斯卡里尼人又称瓦瓦克奇里尼瓦克，意为“鹿之民”，法国人称他们为“小民族”，是渥太华河下游谷地的阿尔冈昆族群。他们的猎场位于渥太华河北岸，即今魁北克西部的列夫尔河、鲁日河和小民族河一带，并与五大湖的怀安多特人保持密切贸易往来。塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在1613年溯渥太华河而上时曾与他们相遇，后来的法国传教士还记录下首领夏尔·帕奇里尼在三河镇附近带领的定居基督徒社群。海狸战争给他们带来灭顶之灾：易洛魁人的袭扰打散了渥太华河谷的各阿尔冈昆群体，韦斯卡里尼人的武装力量在1654年的冲突中基本被摧毁。幸存者此前已开始向东流散，到17世纪后期，韦斯卡里尼人不再作为独立的政治群体出现，其后裔融入了圣劳伦斯河与渥太华河谷的其他阿尔冈昆社群。

en: The Western Abenaki are the Algonquian bands west of the Penobscot, spread across the Connecticut River valley, the lakes of Vermont and the Merrimack valley of New Hampshire: the Cowasuck, Missisquoi and Sokoki, together with the loose Pennacook confederacy whose chief villages stood at Amoskeag Falls and Pennacook, present Manchester and Concord. Under the Pennacook sachem Passaconaway they made their peace early with the English of Massachusetts, but epidemics, Mohawk raids from the west and the pressures of King Philip's War broke their villages; some captives were enslaved, while bands of refugees fled first to the Hudson valley and then north. From about 1669 Abenaki families had been crossing into New France, where the governor granted them the two seigneuries that became the Odanak reserve on the St. Francis River and the Wôlinak reserve near Bécancour. From these Quebec villages the Western Abenaki raided the New England frontier alongside the French in Queen Anne's War, striking as far as Deerfield in 1704, and kept up the fight through Father Le Loutre's War and the French and Indian War, while the descendants of the Pennacook were absorbed into the communities at Odanak.
zh: 西阿贝纳基人是佩诺布斯科特以西的阿尔冈昆语各部，分布在康涅狄格河谷、佛蒙特诸湖和新罕布什尔的梅里马克河谷，包括科瓦萨克人、密西斯阔伊人、索科基人，以及松散的彭纳库科联盟——后者的主要村落位于阿莫斯基格瀑布和彭纳库科，即今天的曼彻斯特与康科德。在彭纳库科首领帕萨科纳韦带领下，他们很早就同马萨诸塞的英国人讲和，但疫病、西方莫霍克人的袭扰和菲利普国王战争的冲击摧毁了他们的村落：一些俘虏被卖为奴，成批难民先逃往哈得孙河谷，继而北上。约从1669年起，阿贝纳基家庭陆续进入新法兰西，总督授予他们两块领地，后来发展为圣弗朗索瓦河畔的奥达纳克保留地和贝康库尔附近的沃利纳克保留地。西阿贝纳基人以这些魁北克村落为基地，在安妮女王战争中与法国人联手袭掠新英格兰边疆，1704年兵锋远至迪尔菲尔德，并在勒卢特尔神父战争和法国—印第安人战争期间持续作战；彭纳库科人的后裔则融入了奥达纳克的社群。

en: The Western Kru are the Kru-speaking peoples of the coast from southeastern Liberia to southwestern Ivory Coast around the Cavally River, among them the Klao or Kru proper, the Grebo, called Krumen on the Ivorian shore, the Bassa and the We, in towns such as Settra Kru, Cestos, San Pedro and Tabou. Their migrations out of the Sahel-edge interior, through the valleys of the Guinea highlands, reached the sea between the thirteenth and fifteenth centuries, partly to escape slave raiding by the small Manding kingdoms; Bassa oral history sets their own arrival on the coast between the eleventh and fourteenth centuries. They lived in decentralized village societies without kings, governed through the Poro and Sande bush schools, and Grebo clans were led by a high priest called the Bodio. This was the Pepper Coast of the melegueta trade, and its forests largely shielded the Kru from enslavement: their oral traditions insist they were never slaves, and men marked their foreheads with indigo tattoos as freemen. From the 1790s Krumen signed on as free sailors aboard European ships, winning fame as Atlantic navigators. The Bassa also kept a pictographic script that fell out of use during the nineteenth century, and in 1827 American colonists settled among the Glebo at Cape Palmas.
zh: 西克鲁诸族是利比里亚东南到科特迪瓦西南、卡瓦利河一带沿海讲克鲁语的人群，包括克劳人（克鲁本部）、格雷博人（在科特迪瓦一侧称克鲁门人）、巴萨人和韦人，聚居于塞特拉克鲁、塞斯托斯、圣佩德罗、塔布等城镇。他们从撒哈拉南缘的内地出发，沿几内亚高地的河谷迁徙，于13至15世纪抵达海边，部分原因是躲避曼丁小邦的猎奴袭击；巴萨人的口传历史则把本族到达海岸的时间定在11至14世纪。他们生活在没有国王的分权村社里，靠波洛会和桑德会的丛林学校维系秩序，格雷博各氏族由名为博迪奥的大祭司统领。这里曾是经营天堂椒贸易的“胡椒海岸”，密林使克鲁人大体免遭奴役：他们的口传传统坚称本族从未为奴，男子还在额头纹上靛蓝标记，以示自由人之身。从18世纪90年代起，克鲁门人以自由水手身份受雇于欧洲船只，以大西洋航行本领闻名。巴萨人还曾拥有一套象形文字，到19世纪逐渐失传；1827年，美国殖民团体在帕尔马斯角的格莱博人中间落脚定居。

en: The Western Pomeranian Low German country covers the Baltic coast from Lübeck and Mecklenburg to the mouth of the Oder, a land of lagoons, the bodden, and islands such as Rügen. In the early twelfth century it was still held by Slavic tribes, the Obotrites in Mecklenburg and the Lutici and Rani farther east, whose great temple at Arkona on Rügen was destroyed by the Danes in 1168. Conquest by Henry the Lion of Saxony, the missions of Otto of Bamberg and the Ostsiedlung then turned the region German: native princes such as the Obotrite House of Mecklenburg and the Griffin dukes of Pomerania kept their thrones but adopted German speech and customs, while new towns including Rostock, Wismar, Stralsund and Greifswald received Lübeck law, joined the Hanseatic League and grew rich on herring, beer and Baltic trade in Middle Low German. The Griffins ruled a frequently partitioned Duchy of Pomerania, absorbing the Danish Principality of Rügen in 1325, while Mecklenburg went its own way under its Obotrite dynasty. The Reformation turned the coastal cities Lutheran, and the extinction of the Griffin line in 1637, during the Thirty Years' War, let Sweden and Brandenburg partition the duchy: Swedish Pomerania, with Stralsund and Rügen, passed to the Swedish crown until the Great Northern War and the Congress of Vienna of 1815, when the whole western coast was merged into the Prussian Province of Pomerania, leaving only the Mecklenburg grand duchies outside it.
zh: 西波美拉尼亚人的低地德语家园，涵盖从吕贝克、梅克伦堡到奥得河口的波罗的海海岸，是一片潟湖（博登）与吕根等岛屿交错之地。12世纪初这里仍由斯拉夫部族占据：梅克伦堡的奥博特人，以及更东边的卢蒂奇人和拉尼人；拉尼人在吕根岛上的阿科纳大神庙于1168年被丹麦人摧毁。随后萨克森公爵狮子亨利的征服、班贝格的奥托的传教和东向移民运动使该地区德意志化：梅克伦堡的奥博特家族和波美拉尼亚的格里芬公爵等本地王公保住了爵位，却改用德语和德意志习俗；罗斯托克、维斯马、施特拉尔松德、格赖夫斯瓦尔德等新城市获得吕贝克法、加入汉萨同盟，以中古低地德语经营鲱鱼、啤酒和波罗的海贸易而致富。格里芬家族统治着屡遭分割的波美拉尼亚公国，1325年并入丹麦的吕根亲王国；梅克伦堡则在奥博特王朝治下独自发展。宗教改革使沿海城市改宗路德宗；1637年格里芬家族在三十年战争期间绝嗣，瑞典和勃兰登堡瓜分公国，领有施特拉尔松德和吕根的瑞典属波美拉尼亚归瑞典王冠所有，直到大北方战争和1815年维也纳会议，整个西海岸被并入普鲁士的波美拉尼亚省，只剩梅克伦堡两个大公国留在省外。

en: The Westphalians are the Low German people of the country between the Rhine and the Weser, from the Münsterland to the Sauerland hills. In Roman times they were part of the Saxon confederation, and the battle of the Teutoburg Forest of AD 9 was fought near Osnabrück on Westphalian ground. Charlemagne's Saxon Wars of 772 to 804 broke their resistance under Widukind and planted the bishoprics of Münster, Osnabrück and Paderborn, and Westphalia became one of the four districts of the tribal Duchy of Saxony. When Frederick Barbarossa deposed Henry the Lion in 1180, the new Duchy of Westphalia passed to the archbishops of Cologne, while the wider region fragmented into prince-bishoprics, the county of Lippe and dozens of small lordships in the Lower Rhenish–Westphalian Circle; towns such as Münster, Dortmund and Soest grew rich as Hanseatic cities speaking Westphalian Low German. The Reformation split the region between Catholics and Lutherans, and in 1534 to 1535 radical Anabaptists seized Münster and set up a communal kingdom until the prince-bishop stormed the city. Westphalia suffered heavily in the Thirty Years' War, but gave its name to the Peace of Westphalia, signed at Münster and Osnabrück in 1648, whose principle of sovereign states is known as Westphalian sovereignty. Napoleon made a short-lived Kingdom of Westphalia for his brother Jérôme in 1807 to 1813, and the Congress of Vienna in 1815 merged the region into the Prussian Province of Westphalia.
zh: 威斯特伐利亚人是莱茵河与威悉河之间的低地德语居民，家园从明斯特兰平原一直延伸到绍尔兰丘陵。罗马时代他们属于萨克森部落联盟，公元9年的条顿堡森林战役就发生在奥斯纳布吕克附近的威斯特伐利亚土地上。772至804年查理大帝的萨克森战争压垮了维杜金德领导的抵抗，也种下明斯特、奥斯纳布吕克和帕德博恩等主教区，威斯特伐利亚成为萨克森部落公国四大区之一。1180年腓特烈·巴巴罗萨废黜狮子亨利后，新设的威斯特伐利亚公国归科隆大主教所有，而更广大的地区则分裂为明斯特、奥斯纳布吕克、帕德博恩主教区、利珀伯国和数十个小领地，统属下莱茵-威斯特伐利亚行政圈；明斯特、奥斯纳布吕克、多特蒙德、苏斯特等城市讲威斯特伐利亚低地德语，靠汉萨贸易致富。宗教改革使当地在天主教与路德宗之间分裂，1534至1535年激进的再洗礼派夺取明斯特、建立公社式的“天国”，最终被主教军队攻破。三十年战争中威斯特伐利亚惨遭兵燹，却因1648年在明斯特和奥斯纳布吕克签署的威斯特伐利亚和约得名，条约确立的主权国家原则被称为“威斯特伐利亚主权”。1807至1813年拿破仑为弟弟热罗姆建立了短命的威斯特伐利亚王国，1815年维也纳会议将该地区并入普鲁士的威斯特伐利亚省。

en: The Wetarese are the Austronesian islanders of the Barat Daya chain between Timor and the Banda Sea, on Wetar, Leti, Babar and Damar, whose Timoric tongues, including the four Wetarese varieties of Wetar, are kin to Galoli of Timor. Sago farmers, fishers and traders who venerated ancestors through yene statues, they later stood within the Dutch colonial sphere in Maluku.
zh: 韦塔雷斯人是散居韦塔、勒蒂、巴巴和达马尔等西南马鲁古岛屿的南岛语族群，地处帝汶与班达海之间，其帝汶语支语言与帝汶的加洛利语相近，仅韦塔本岛就有四种差异明显的变体。他们以种植西谷、捕鱼和经商为生，用耶内小木像供奉祖先，后来处于荷兰在马鲁古的殖民势力范围内。

en: The Wet'suwet'en are a branch of the Dakelh, or Carrier, people, once classed with the Babine as the Western Carrier, living along the Bulkley River and around Burns and François lakes in the northwestern interior of what is now British Columbia. Their endonym means people of the Bulkley River, and they speak Witsuwit'en, an Athabaskan language. Their kungax oral history recalls the ancestral cedar village of Dizkle above Bulkley Canyon, abandoned after an omen of disaster, a tale paralleled among the neighbouring Gitxsan, whose version names the village Dimlahamid. Society is ordered into five matrilineal clans divided among thirteen house groups under hereditary house chiefs, acting through the feast system. The canyon village of Witset shows roughly five and a half thousand years of habitation, its salmon fishery disrupted when a rockslide blocked the runs and people resettled at Hagwilget. In 1822 the Hudson's Bay Company founded the Babine Establishment, later Fort Kilmaurs, on Babine Lake under William Brown, trading leather and salmon with the Wet'suwet'en and Babine; the post was moved and renamed Fort Babine in 1836.
zh: 韦苏韦滕人是达凯尔（卡里尔）人的一支，曾与巴宾人合称西卡里尔人，居住在今不列颠哥伦比亚省西北内陆的巴尔克利河沿岸以及伯恩斯湖、弗朗索瓦湖一带。其自称意为巴尔克利河人，使用阿萨巴斯卡语系的韦苏韦滕语。他们的口述史昆加克斯记载，祖先在巴尔克利峡谷上游建有雪松木屋村落迪兹克尔，后因灾难征兆而废弃，邻近的吉特克桑人也有类似的迪姆拉哈米德传说。社会按母系划分为五个氏族，下分十三个家族屋群，由世袭屋群酋长通过夸富宴体系治理。峡谷渔村维特塞特已有约五千五百年的居住史，一次岩崩阻断鲑鱼洄游后，居民迁往哈格威尔盖特。1822年，哈德逊湾公司由威廉·布朗主持，在巴宾湖设立巴宾贸易站，即后来的基尔茅斯堡，与韦苏韦滕人和巴宾人交换皮革和鲑鱼；1836年贸易站迁址并改称巴宾堡。

en: The Wichí, whose name means people in their own tongue, wichí lhamtés, were long known to outsiders as Mataco, a Quechua-derived label now treated as insulting. They belong to the Chaco Central and Chaco Austral, chiefly along the Bermejo and Pilcomayo rivers in present-day Argentina, with the Weenhayek branch across the border in Bolivia. Fishermen, hunters and gatherers living in kinship bands under elder chiefs, they had largely settled in riverside villages by the sixteenth century, when pressure from invading Ava Guaraní pushed some bands north and south-east. The first Spanish record of them dates to 1609, and contact followed the 1626 founding of the Ledesma fort. In 1632 they joined the Toba in destroying Santiago de Guadalcázar, and a Jesuit reduction attempted on the Bermejo in 1635 failed. Jesuits founded the San Ignacio mission for Toba and Mataco in 1756, while Franciscans opened Nuestra Señora de las Angustias de Zenta in 1779; it dwindled after San Ramón de la Nueva Orán was founded nearby in 1794.
zh: 韦奇人在本族语中的名字意为“人”，他们的语言称韦奇拉姆特斯语；外界长期称他们为马塔科人，这个源自克丘亚语的称呼后来被视为蔑称。他们分布在中查科和南查科，主要在今阿根廷的贝尔梅霍河与皮科马约河沿岸，温哈耶克一支则在玻利维亚境内。他们以渔猎和采集为生，在长老首领率领的亲族群体中生活，到16世纪已基本定居于河畔村落；当时阿瓦瓜拉尼人入侵，迫使部分支群北迁和向东南移动。西班牙人对他们最早的记载是1609年，1626年莱德斯马堡建立后双方开始接触。1632年他们联合托巴人摧毁了圣地亚哥-德瓜达尔卡萨尔；1635年耶稣会在贝尔梅霍河尝试建立归化区，未能成功。1756年耶稣会为托巴人和马塔科人创办圣伊格纳西奥传教站，方济各会则于1779年开设森塔的痛苦圣母传教站，1794年附近建起圣拉蒙-德拉努埃瓦奥兰后，该传教站便日趋衰落。

en: The Wik are a group of closely related Aboriginal peoples of the western Cape York Peninsula in northern Queensland, occupying the coastal floodplains between the Edward River and Weipa on the Gulf of Carpentaria and the forested inland country drained by the Archer, Kendall and Holroyd rivers. They speak a cluster of Paman languages within the Pama-Nyungan family, in which wik simply means speech; the Wik-Mungkan, whose language means roughly speech of eating, were the largest of the branches. Traditionally they were organized into some thirty patrilineal clans, each holding its own stretch of country and one or more totems, called pulwaiya or old forebears, whose places of origin served as ritual sites where the dead were believed to return. The clans lived by hunting, fishing and gathering on the seasonally flooded plains, moving between rivers, lagoons and bush camps. Dutch ships charted the Gulf of Carpentaria shoreline in 1623 without founding any settlement, and for the two centuries that followed the Wik country remained beyond the effective reach of Europeans.
zh: 维克人是昆士兰北部约克角半岛西部一组关系密切的原住民支系的统称，分布在卡奔塔利亚湾畔爱德华河与韦帕之间的沿海洪泛平原，以及阿彻河、肯德尔河和霍尔罗伊德河流经的内陆林地。他们使用帕马-牛雅语系下帕马语组的一组亲属语言，“维克”在这些语言里就是“话语”的意思；其中最大的支系是维克蒙坎人，其语言名称大意是“与吃有关的话”。传统上他们分为约三十个父系氏族，各有自己的领地和一个或多个图腾，图腾被称为“普尔瓦亚”，意为“古老的祖先”，图腾发源处便是举行仪式的圣地，也是人死后灵魂归去的地方。各氏族在季节性泛滥的平原上狩猎、捕鱼和采集，辗转于河流、潟湖与林地营地之间。1623年荷兰船只测绘了卡奔塔利亚湾的海岸线，但没有建立任何定居点；此后近两个世纪里，维克人的土地始终处于欧洲人势力的有效范围之外。

en: The Willetpoose grouping covers the closely allied peoples of the Walla Walla valley, at the meeting of the Walla Walla, Snake and Columbia rivers in what is now southeastern Washington and northeastern Oregon. The first are the Walla Walla, whose Sahaptin name Walúulapam means people of the Walula region and whose name is often translated as many waters; three bands held the Walla Walla River and the nearby Columbia, following a seasonal round of salmon fishing, root digging and hunting like their Palouse and Yakama neighbours. Beside them lived the Cayuse, who call themselves Liksiyu, a seminomadic people speaking a language isolate and numbering about five hundred in the eighteenth century. The Cayuse were feared horsemen who bred the swift, hardy Cayuse pony, ranged as far as the Great Plains to trade and raid, and made the weaker bands at The Dalles fishery pay them tribute in salmon. Lewis and Clark met Walla Walla chief Yellepit in 1805 and again in 1806, leaving a peace medal; David Thompson of the North West Company followed in 1811, and the company built Fort Nez Perces at the mouth of the Walla Walla River in 1818. In 1835 the missionary Samuel Parker scouted the Cayuse and Nez Perce villages for a future mission.
zh: 维勒普斯这一划分涵盖了沃拉沃拉河谷中关系紧密的诸族，其地在今华盛顿州东南部与俄勒冈州东北部，沃拉沃拉河、蛇河与哥伦比亚河交汇之处。其一是沃拉沃拉人，萨哈普廷语名字瓦卢拉帕姆意为“瓦卢拉地区之民”，族名常被解释为“众水”；他们的三个群体据有沃拉沃拉河及附近的哥伦比亚河段，和邻族帕卢斯人、雅卡马人一样按季节轮换，捕捞鲑鱼、挖掘块根、狩猎。旁边住着卡尤塞人，他们自称利克西尤，是半游牧民族，讲一种孤立语言，18世纪约有五百人。卡尤塞人是令人生畏的骑手，培育出迅捷耐劳的卡尤塞小马，远行到大平原贸易和劫掠，还迫使达尔斯渔场的弱小部落以鲑鱼纳贡。1805年和1806年，刘易斯与克拉克两度会见沃拉沃拉酋长耶勒皮特，留下一枚和平勋章；西北公司的戴维·汤普森于1811年接踵而至，该公司又于1818年在沃拉沃拉河口修建内兹珀斯堡。1835年，传教士塞缪尔·帕克到卡尤塞人和内兹珀斯人的村落考察，为日后建立传教站选址。

en: The Williche, or Huilliche, are the southernmost mainland branch of the Mapuche, whose Mapudungun name means people of the south. Their country, Futahuillimapu, ran from the rivers below Valdivia to the mainland shores opposite Chiloé, while Cunco kin held the north of the island. They farmed potatoes, maize and beans, raised the camelid chilihueque, fished from three-plank dalca boats and lived in east-facing ruca huts. The Spaniards founded Valdivia, Osorno and Castro in their lands between 1552 and 1567, but the Curalaba disaster of 1598 drew them into the general Mapuche rising and every Spanish city in their territory except Castro was destroyed. The islanders rose again with the Dutch corsair Baltazar de Cordes in 1600 and against the encomenderos in 1712, while mainland Williche kept their frontier closed through slave-raiding wars and a battle on the Bueno River in 1759. Tomás de Figueroa's expedition of 1792 broke their resistance, and the Parliament of Las Canoas of 1793 opened Futahuillimapu to Spanish haciendas and the refounding of Osorno.
zh: 维利切人是马普切人最靠南的大陆支系，名字在马普敦贡语中意为南方之人。他们的故土称富塔维利马普，从瓦尔迪维亚以南的诸河一直延伸到奇洛埃岛对岸的大陆海岸，同族的昆科人则占据奇洛埃岛北部。他们种植马铃薯、玉米和菜豆，饲养名为奇利韦克的骆驼科家畜，乘三块木板拼成的达尔卡船捕鱼，住朝东的鲁卡茅屋。1552至1567年间，西班牙人先后在他们的土地上建起瓦尔迪维亚、奥索尔诺和卡斯特罗三城；但1598年库拉拉巴惨败后，他们加入马普切人大起义，境内除卡斯特罗外的西班牙城市全部被毁。岛上的维利切人又于1600年联合荷兰海盗巴尔塔萨·德·科尔德斯起事，并在1712年起兵反抗委托监护主；大陆上的维利切人则在奴隶劫掠战争和1759年的布埃诺河之战中守住了封闭的边界。1792年托马斯·德·菲格罗阿的远征击碎了他们的抵抗，1793年的拉斯卡诺阿斯议会向西班牙大庄园开放了富塔维利马普，奥索尔诺也随之重建。

en: The Wintuan, or Northern Wintun, were the northern branch of the Wintun peoples of the Sacramento Valley, whose three related tongues, Wintu, Nomlaki and Patwin, were as close to one another as the Romance languages and had split from a common speech perhaps only two thousand years before. Their country covered the western side of the upper Sacramento Valley from the great river to the Coast Range, with the Winnemem band holding the McCloud River and calling themselves the Middle Water people, and other bands on the upper Trinity and at the foot of Mount Shasta; the volcanic Lassen Peak bore their name Amblu Kai, the Mountain Ripped Apart. In eight or more small bands they lived in semi-permanent riverside villages, netting salmon and steelhead, gathering acorns and manzanita berries, weaving cooking and storage baskets and using earth lodges as sweat houses for ritual purification. The first recorded outsiders were the trappers of Jedediah Smith in 1826 and Peter Skene Ogden in 1827. Far worse was the malaria epidemic of 1830 to 1833, which carried off an estimated three quarters of the native population of the upper and central Sacramento Valley.
zh: 温图人（又称北温顿人）是萨克拉门托谷地温顿诸族的北支。温顿人的三种亲缘语言——温图语、诺姆拉基语和帕特温语——彼此接近的程度相当于罗曼语族，约两千年前才从共同语分化。他们的地盘覆盖萨克拉门托谷地北部西侧，从大河直到海岸山脉；温内梅姆群体据有麦克劳德河，自称“中水之人”，另一些群体分布在特里尼蒂河上游和沙斯塔山脚下，火山拉森峰在他们口中名为阿姆布鲁凯，意为“撕裂之山”。他们分成八个或更多小群体，住在河畔半定居的村落里，捕捞鲑鱼和硬头鳟，采集橡子与熊果，编织烹煮和储物用的篮器，并以土屋作汗房举行净化仪式。有记录的最早外来者是1826年杰迪代亚·史密斯和1827年彼得·斯基恩·奥格登的猎人群。更可怕的是1830年至1833年的疟疾，估计夺去了萨克拉门托谷地北部和中部四分之三原住民的生命。

en: The Wipi, also called Gidra, are a Papuan people of the plains between the Fly River and the Torres Strait in Western Province, Papua New Guinea, around the Oriomo and Binaturi rivers, with Wipim the chief of their fourteen villages. Their language, also named Oriomo, belongs to the Eastern Trans-Fly family with Gizrra, Bine and Meriam Mir.
zh: 威皮人又称吉德拉人，是巴布亚新几内亚西部省弗莱河与托雷斯海峡之间平原上的巴布亚人，住在奥里莫河和比纳图里河一带，维皮姆是其十四个主要村落中最大的一个。他们的语言又名奥里莫语，与吉兹拉语、比内语和梅里亚姆米尔语同属东跨弗莱语系。

en: The Wiradjuri are the largest Aboriginal people of New South Wales, organised in hunting and gathering clans across the wide plains west of the Blue Mountains, in the country they call the land of the three rivers: the Wambuul or Macquarie, the Kalare or Lachlan, and the Murrumbidgee. Their name is said to join wiray, their word for “no”, with a suffix meaning “having”, a naming habit shared by several tribes west of the Great Dividing Range. That isolation ended in 1813, when Blaxland, Lawson and Wentworth crossed the Blue Mountains and revealed the pastures beyond; a road followed within months and the town of Bathurst was founded on Wiradjuri land. Early relations were peaceful, and the settler George Suttor took up Brucedale Station in 1822, learnt their language and befriended the warrior Windradyne, whom the British called Saturday. Under Governor Thomas Brisbane a flood of land grants then swallowed the hunting grounds and brought famine, so in 1824 the Wiradjuri rose in the guerrilla campaign remembered as the Bathurst War. Brisbane proclaimed martial law, the resistance was broken within the year, and Windradyne travelled to Parramatta at the end of 1824 to make peace; he died five years later of a wound from a tribal fight beside the Macquarie. Corroborees continued around Mudgee for decades as survivors settled on the edges of the new pastoral economy.
zh: 威拉朱里人是新南威尔士州最大的原住民族群，以从事狩猎采集的氏族为单位，分布在蓝山以西的广阔平原上。他们把自己的土地称为“三河之地”，即旺布尔河（麦夸里河）、卡拉雷河（拉克伦河）与马兰比吉河。据说其族名由意为“不”的“威雷”加上表示“拥有”的后缀构成，大分水岭以西若干部族都有类似的命名习惯。1813年，布莱克兰、劳森和温特沃思穿越蓝山，山后牧场暴露在殖民者面前，这种隔绝状态就此终结；几个月内一条公路修通，巴瑟斯特镇也建在威拉朱里人的土地上。早期关系尚属和平，1822年移民乔治·萨托圈下布鲁斯代尔牧场，学会他们的语言，并与勇士温拉丁（英国人叫他“星期六”）结为朋友。后来在托马斯·布里斯班总督治下，土地授地潮吞噬猎场、引发饥荒，威拉朱里人遂于1824年起事，展开史称“巴瑟斯特战争”的游击战。布里斯班宣布戒严，抵抗在当年内即被镇压，温拉丁于1824年底亲赴帕拉马塔议和，五年后他在麦夸里河畔一场部族冲突中受伤不治。此后数十年间马奇一带仍有歌舞集会，幸存者则在新兴牧业经济的边缘安顿下来。

en: The Wirangu are an Aboriginal people of the far west coast of South Australia. Their traditional country, estimated at some 56,000 square kilometres, ran along the coast between the Head of Bight and Streaky Bay and stretched inland as far north as Ooldea, with the country around the later town of Ceduna at its heart. Their language belongs to the Thura-Yura branch of the Pama-Nyungan family, and early ethnographers noted that the Wirangu, Banggarla and Nawu were much the same people in speech and custom. Wirangu mythology tells of a great mother snake pursued across the land by the two Wati Kutjara men; where the wounded serpent rested, red, yellow and white ochre deposits formed, the red ochre being her blood. Even before European settlement the southward-moving Kokatha had driven them from part of their country, and when the colony of South Australia was proclaimed in 1836 the Wirangu were already a partly displaced people.
zh: 威朗古人是南澳大利亚遥远西海岸的原住民。据估计，他们的传统领地约有5.6万平方公里，沿大澳大利亚湾湾头与斯特里基湾之间的海岸分布，并向内陆北延至乌尔迪一带，后来塞杜纳镇所在的地区正处于其中心。他们的语言属于帕马-牛雅语系的图拉-尤拉语支，早期民族志学者注意到，威朗古人、邦加拉人和纳乌人在语言和习俗上几乎如同一族。威朗古神话讲述一条母蛇大神被瓦蒂·库贾拉两兄弟追逐的故事：受伤的大蛇停歇之处形成了红、黄、白三色赭石矿，红赭石便是它流出的鲜血。早在欧洲人定居之前，南迁的科科塔人已把他们逐出部分领地；1836年南澳大利亚殖民地宣告成立时，威朗古人已是一个部分流离失所的民族。

en: The Wiyimpih-deka are the Wiyimpihtikka, the Buffalo Berry Eaters of the Western Shoshone, whose range centred on Big Smoky Valley in central Nevada, between the Toiyabe and Toquima ranges. Their country adjoined that of the Tsaiduka, the Tule Eaters of Railroad Valley, and other small bands of the arid interior. Numic-speaking foragers had spread through the Great Basin by the fourteenth century, and by 1500 Shoshone bands held most of Nevada. In this dry land the Wiyimpihtikka lived by the classic Desert Culture round: winter villages near water, summer family camps for rabbits, pronghorn and grass seeds, and autumn pinyon-nut harvests in the mountains, with tightly woven baskets for winnowing and carrying but no permanent fields or settled towns.
zh: 维因皮德卡人即维因皮赫蒂卡人，意为“食水牛果者”，属西部休休尼人，活动中心在内华达中部、托伊亚比岭与托奎马岭之间的大斯莫基谷。他们的领地与铁路谷的采杜卡人（食藨草者）等干旱内陆小部族相接。说努米克语的采集狩猎者到14世纪已遍及大盆地，1500年前后休休尼诸部占据了内华达大部。在这片干旱土地上，维因皮赫蒂卡人过着典型的沙漠文化生活：临水而居的冬村，夏季猎兔和叉角羚、采集草籽的家庭营地，秋天进山采收松子；他们用编织紧密的篮子扬谷盛物，却没有固定的农田或城镇。

en: The Wiyot, who call themselves Ku'wil, the people, are an Algic-speaking people of the Humboldt Bay coast of northwestern California, close kin in language and custom to the Yurok; their two tongues are the westernmost Algic languages, distantly related to the Algonquian family far to the east. Their homeland ran from the Mad River through Humboldt Bay, where Eureka and Arcata now stand, to the lower Eel River, a country of ancient redwood forest behind sandy dunes and tidal marsh. Dialect and geography made three divisions: the Mad River Wiyot in the north, the Humboldt Bay Wiyot around the bay, and the Eel River Wiyot of the southern delta. Each year they held World Renewal ceremonies, centered on the island village of Tuluwat, to begin the new year. Spanish missions never extended beyond San Francisco Bay, and although Russian sea-otter traders reached the coast in 1806 they did not stay, so the Wiyot remained among the most isolated peoples of California through the early nineteenth century.
zh: 维约特人自称库尔，意为“人”，是加利福尼亚西北部洪堡湾沿岸讲阿尔吉克语的族群，语言和习俗都与尤罗克人相近；这两种语言是分布最西的阿尔吉克语，与遥远东方的阿尔冈昆语族仅有远亲关系。他们的故土从马德河经洪堡湾（今尤里卡和阿克塔所在地）延伸到伊尔河下游，内陆是古老的红杉林，岸边则是沙丘和潮汐沼泽。按方言和地理分为三支：北方的马德河维约特人、海湾周围的洪堡湾维约特人，以及南方三角洲的伊尔河维约特人。他们每年在图卢瓦特岛村举行世界更新仪式，以此开启新的一年。西班牙传教站始终没有越过旧金山湾，俄国海獭商人虽于1806年抵达海岸却未能立足，因此直到19世纪初，维约特人仍是加利福尼亚最与世隔绝的族群之一。

en: The Wogamusin are an Upper Sepik people of western East Sepik Province, living in a handful of villages on the Wogamush and upper Sepik rivers east of the Iwam. Together with Chenapian, their language forms the small Wogamus branch within the Sepik family.
zh: 沃加穆辛人是东塞皮克省西部的上塞皮克族群，住在伊瓦姆人以东、沃加穆什河与塞皮克河上游沿岸的数个村落里。他们的语言与切纳皮安语共同构成塞皮克语族下小小的沃加穆斯分支。

en: The Wolastoqiyik, whose name means people of the shining river, are the Algonquian people of the Wolastoq, the Saint John River and its tributaries in present New Brunswick, Maine and Quebec; Europeans long called them Maliseet, from a Mi'kmaq exonym. Their close kin the Passamaquoddy held the coasts of Passamaquoddy Bay and the St. Croix River, and the two nations shared one language and both belonged to the Wabanaki Confederacy. At contact they lived in palisaded villages, growing corn, beans, squash and tobacco and moving between summer fishing grounds and winter hunting camps, with their chief village later fixed at Meductic. French traders built a fur-trade alliance and Jesuit missions drew converts, while raiding wars with the Haudenosaunee and the Innu ran through the seventeenth century. In the colonial wars the Wolastoqiyik and Passamaquoddy fought beside the French against New England, then made peace through the same series of Peace and Friendship Treaties as the Mi'kmaq between 1725 and 1779; in 1776 a Passamaquoddy delegation also made a treaty with the new United States.
zh: 沃拉斯托基维克人意为“闪光之河的人民”，是讲阿尔冈昆语的族群，世居今天新不伦瑞克、缅因和魁北克境内的圣约翰河及其支流；欧洲人长期用来自米克马克语的他称“马利西特”称呼他们。他们的近亲帕萨马阔迪人占据帕萨马阔迪湾和圣克鲁瓦河沿岸，两族共用一种语言，又都是瓦巴纳基联盟的成员。接触欧洲人之初，他们住在设有栅栏的村落里，种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜和烟草，按季节往返于夏季渔场与冬季猎营之间，后来主村设在梅达克蒂克。法国商人同他们建立了毛皮贸易同盟，耶稣会传教站也吸收了不少信徒；与此同时，17世纪里他们与易洛魁联盟、因努人之间袭掠不断。殖民战争时期，沃拉斯托基维克人与帕萨马阔迪人站在法国一边对新英格兰作战，随后又在1725至1779年间同米克马克人一样签订了一系列《和平友好条约》；1776年，帕萨马阔迪人的代表团还与新生的美国缔结了一项条约。

en: The Wolof are the largest people of Senegambia, settled across the plains of western Senegal and the lower Gambia valley, where they speak a West Atlantic language and grow millet in villages under hereditary chiefs. One tradition holds that their ancestors moved into the region as the Ghana Empire collapsed in the late 1000s, and by the 1200s they had pushed the earlier Serer inhabitants southward. Their states, among them Jolof, Cayor, Baol and Waalo, were first vassals of Mali and won independence around 1360 when the Mali succession was in dispute. United under the burba of Jolof, the Wolof empire dominated trade between the Senegal River and the Gambia, and in the 1450s the Venetian traveller Cadamosto, sailing for Portugal, found Muslim clerics counselling Wolof rulers who had not themselves adopted Islam. The empire broke up after the battle of Danki in 1549, leaving Jolof a reduced kingdom ringed by the independent states of Cayor, Baol, Waalo, Sine and Saloum, whose rivalries were sharpened by slave raiding and, in the 1700s, by the reformist jihads sweeping the Senegambian plain.
zh: 沃洛夫人是塞内冈比亚最大的民族，定居在塞内加尔西部平原和冈比亚河下游谷地，说西非大西洋语支的沃洛夫语，在世袭酋长治理的村落里种植粟米。一种说法认为，他们的祖先在11世纪末加纳帝国崩溃时迁入这一地区，到13世纪已把更早的塞雷尔居民赶往南方。他们的诸邦——乔洛夫、卡约尔、巴奥勒、瓦洛等——最初是马里的附庸，约1360年趁马里王位继承之争获得独立。在乔洛夫的布尔巴统合下，沃洛夫帝国掌控了塞内加尔河与冈比亚河之间的贸易；15世纪50年代，为葡萄牙航行的威尼斯旅行家卡达莫斯托看到，沃洛夫统治者身边已有穆斯林学者担任顾问，但统治者本人尚未皈依。1549年丹基战役后帝国解体，乔洛夫沦为局促一隅的小王国，周围环绕着独立的卡约尔、巴奥勒、瓦洛、锡内和萨卢姆诸邦；奴隶劫掠以及18世纪席卷塞内冈比亚平原的改革派圣战，加剧了这些邦国之间的纷争。

en: The Worimi are an Aboriginal Australian people of the New South Wales coast, their country running from the Hunter River estuary north to Forster and inland to the Williams River, with Port Stephens at its heart. They spoke Gathang, a tongue whose dialects were shared with the neighbouring Biripi, Gringai and Awabakal. Cook sighted and named Port Stephens in 1770, and in 1790 four escaped convicts who landed there were welcomed as ancestors returned from the sea, given wives and lived with the Worimi for five years. Governor Macquarie exchanged food with them on a visit in 1811, but from about 1815 violent red-cedar gangs poisoned relations, and John Oxley met armed resistance on his journey through the Myall Lakes in 1818. In 1826 the Australian Agricultural Company planted a settlement at Port Stephens under Robert Dawson, opening farms at Stroud and Gloucester and drawing the Worimi into the colonial economy.
zh: 沃里米人是澳大利亚新南威尔士州海岸的原住民，领地以斯提芬港为中心，南起亨特河口，北至福斯特，西抵威廉斯河。他们使用加桑语，其方言与邻近的比里皮、格林盖、阿瓦巴卡尔等群体共用。1770年，库克望见并命名了斯提芬港；1790年，四名逃犯乘船登岸，被当作从海上归来的祖先受到热情接纳，还娶妻成家，与沃里米人共同生活了五年。1811年，麦觉理总督到访并与他们交换食物。但约1815年起，凶暴的红椿木伐木帮恶化了双方关系，约翰·奥克斯利1818年穿越迈奥尔湖时便遭遇了武装抵抗。1826年，澳大利亚农业公司在罗伯特·道森主持下于斯提芬港建立定居点，在斯特劳德和格洛斯特开辟农场，把沃里米人卷入了殖民经济。

en: The Wurla, also written Worla, Ola or Waladjangarri, are an Aboriginal people of the Kimberley in Western Australia, whose tribal grounds of some twenty thousand square kilometres covered the northern side of the Wunaamin Miliwundi Range, east of the Isdell Range, reaching the Phillips Range and the headwaters of the Hann and upper Fitzroy rivers. They were organised into clans, among them the Wardia around Ellenbrae, and their south-eastern push down the Chapman and Durack rivers to Karunjie cut the traditional country between the Ngarinjin and the Gija. Neighbouring peoples knew them by exonyms: the Ngarinjin called them Waringari, while the Miriwung name Oladjau covered several groups speaking varieties of Ngarinyin, and linguists have counted their speech among the Ngarinyin dialects.
zh: 沃拉人又拼作乌尔拉、奥拉或瓦拉詹加里，是西澳大利亚金伯利地区的原住民，约两万平方公里的传统领地位于乌纳明·米利温迪岭北坡、艾斯德尔岭以东，北至菲利普斯岭以及汉恩河与菲茨罗伊河上游的源头地带。他们分为多个氏族，其中包括住在埃伦布雷一带的瓦迪亚氏族；他们向东南沿查普曼河和杜拉克河推进到卡伦吉，切断了纳林金人与基亚人传统领地之间的联系。邻族对他们各有他称：纳林金人称他们为瓦林加里，米里温人则用奥拉焦一名统称讲多种纳林金语变体的族群；语言学家也把他们的话算作纳林金语的方言之一。

en: The Wú culture is the core of the Wu-speaking world, covering the Lake Tai cities of Suzhou, Songjiang and Jiaxing, the flat and canal-laced heart of Jiangnan. Its name recalls the State of Wu of the Spring and Autumn period, whose capital Gusu stood near modern Suzhou and which, under King Helü, became one of the five hegemon states before being conquered by Yue in 473 BC. Han settlement of the region deepened after the fourth-century upheavals, when refugees from the north crossed the Yangtze and the old Jiangdong speech took shape; a second wave followed the Song court's move to Lin'an in 1127, adding a northern literary layer to the local language. In the Yuan and Ming, Suzhou became a center of commerce, silk, printing and the pingtan ballad tradition, while Songjiang cotton cloth clothed much of China. The Suzhou variety long served as the prestige dialect of all Wu speech, celebrated for its soft, lilting sound in the saying about the tender speech of Wu. In 1337 this was already among the richest and most densely populated regions of the Yuan empire, and its towns and market networks kept flourishing through the Ming and Qing.
zh: 吴文化是吴语世界的核心，覆盖苏州、松江、嘉兴、常熟等太湖沿岸城市，也就是河网密布、市镇林立的江南腹地。其名来自春秋时期的吴国：吴国都城姑苏在今苏州一带，吴王阖闾任用孙武、伍子胥，一度称霸诸侯，跻身春秋五霸，却在公元前473年被越国攻灭。4世纪北方大乱，大批流民渡江南下，古老的江东方言在此基础上逐渐成形；1127年宋廷迁居临安，又带来第二波北方移民，给当地语言加上一层北方文读层。元明时期，苏州成为商业、丝织、刻书和评弹艺术的中心，松江出产的棉布更是行销全国、衣被天下。苏州话长期充当整个吴语的权威方言，以软糯婉转著称，素有吴侬软语的说法。1337年时，这里已是元朝版图内最富庶、人口最稠密的地区之一，其市镇与商贸网络在明清两代继续繁荣。

en: The Wúchuān are the Yue people of the lower Jian River, where it enters the South China Sea on the eastern flank of the Leizhou Peninsula in south-western Guangdong. Their dialect, nicknamed Wuchuan bone, forms with Huazhou speech the Wu-Hua branch of Yue, the product of the long Hanization of local Baiyue peoples under the Gaozhou and Luozhou administrations from the Northern and Southern dynasties onward; even so, Min-speaking Leihua villages and the Kra-Dai Jizhao speech still survive along their coast. The county was created under the Sui in 598 in place of the older Pingding county, with its seat at Wuyang and named after the Wuchuan river now called the Jian, and shifted between Bian, Hua and Gao prefectures until the Ming placed it under Gaozhou prefecture in 1377, an arrangement the Qing retained. Wuchuan kept a vivid folk culture in its piaose tableaux, clay sculpture and deity-centred nianli festivals, and in 1786 it produced Lin Zhaotang, who became one of the few Guangdong scholars to take the zhuangyuan, the top rank in the imperial examination.
zh: 吴川人是鉴江下游、濒临南海的粤语人群，地处广东西南、雷州半岛东翼。他们的方言俗称吴川骨，与化州话合称粤语吴化片，是南北朝以来高州、罗州历代官署推动当地百越土著逐渐汉化的产物；即便如此，沿海仍保留着说闽语雷话，又称东话，的村落和壮侗系的吉兆话。598年隋朝废平定县置吴川县，以县东的吴川水，即今鉴江，得名，治所设在吴阳，此后先后隶属辩州、化州，明朝于1377年划归高州府，清代沿袭不变。吴川民间文化鲜活，飘色、泥塑和以地方神祇为中心的年例节庆代代相传；1786年出生的林召棠后来高中状元，是广东为数不多的科举鼎甲人物。

en: The Wulgurukaban, whose name means canoe people after the wulgurru bark canoe, are a seafaring Aboriginal grouping of the coast and islands around Townsville in north-eastern Queensland, holding roughly a thousand square miles of mainland shore, Magnetic Island, the Palm Islands and the adjoining waters of Halifax and Cleveland Bays. Local estate groups such as the Manbarra of the Palm Islands, the Gurambilbarra of Cape Pallarenda and Magnetic Island, and the Dhulginbarra of the Bohle River scrub spoke dialects of the Wulguru language, an eastern Pama-Nyungan tongue without noun classes, ranging from conservative island varieties to mainland speech that dropped initial consonants. In eight-foot bark canoes they netted fish, took turtles and dugong with turtle-shell hooks, gathered trepang and travelled between islands across open water, leaving shell middens and stone fish traps along the coast. In 1770 James Cook, sailing the Endeavour through these waters, saw them paddling such canoes between the mainland and Magnetic Island at low tide.
zh: 伍尔古鲁卡巴人的名字意为“独木舟人”，得名于当地的“伍尔古鲁”树皮独木舟，是昆士兰东北部汤斯维尔一带沿海与岛屿的航海原住民群体，领有约一千平方英里的大陆海岸、马格内蒂克岛、棕榈群岛以及相邻的哈利法克斯湾和克利夫兰湾海域。棕榈群岛的曼巴拉人、帕拉伦达角与马格内蒂克岛的古兰比尔巴拉人、博尔河灌丛地带的杜尔金巴拉人等地方群体，讲伍尔古鲁语的各方言；这种帕马-牛雅语东部语言没有名词性范畴，方言从保守的海岛变体到脱落词首辅音的大陆变体连成一片。他们乘坐八尺长的树皮独木舟撒网捕鱼，用玳瑁壳做的鱼钩捕捉海龟和儒艮，采集海参，并在开阔水面上往返各岛，沿岸留下贝丘和石砌鱼栅。1770年，詹姆斯·库克驾“努力号”经过这片水域时，就曾看见他们在退潮时划着这种独木舟往来于大陆与马格内蒂克岛之间。

en: The Wumbu, also called Wumvu or Bawoumbou, are a Bantu people of southeastern Gabon, settled in the Haut-Ogooué region around Franceville and in Ngounié province to the south. Their language, Wumbvu, belongs to the Tsogo group of Bantu languages, which is why the game lists them as Tsogo speakers.
zh: 文布人又称 Wumvu 或 Bawoumbou，是加蓬东南部的一支班图人，定居在弗朗斯维尔一带的上奥果韦省和南方的恩古涅省。他们的语言温布武语属于班图语的措戈语组，这也是游戏把他们标为措戈语使用者的原因。

en:
The Wunambal, also known as Wunambal Gaambera, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Kimberley in Western Australia, whose country — their Uunguu — surrounds York Sound and runs north from Brunswick Bay to the Admiralty Gulf and the Osborne Islands, covering roughly 9,800 square kilometres. Norman Tindale judged them perhaps the most venturesome of Australian Aboriginal peoples: partly from Makassan visitors they learnt to build rafts able to ride tides of up to twelve metres, and the Laiau and Wardana bands sailed out to reefs and islets in the Cassini and Montalivet archipelagoes. With the Worrorra and Ngarinyin they form the Wanjina Wunggurr cultural bloc, whose law and dreamtime mythology centre on the Wanjina and Wunggurr spirits.

In September 1820 Phillip Parker King, on his third Australian voyage, beached HMS Mermaid for repairs at Careening Bay on Coronation Island and stayed eighteen days. His crew met no Wunambal, but King noted bark shelters on the beach, more substantial buildings on the hill above and the remnants of sago palm nuts eaten along the coast, and he had the carpenter carve Mermaid 1820 into an ancient boab tree.
zh:
武南布尔人（又称武南布尔·甘贝雷）是西澳大利亚州北部金伯利的澳大利亚原住民，他们的领地——自称温古——环绕约克湾，从布伦瑞克湾向北延伸到阿德默勒尔蒂湾和奥斯本群岛，面积约9800平方公里。诺曼·廷代尔认为他们或许是最富冒险精神的澳大利亚原住民：他们部分地从望加锡来客那里学会了建造能扛住12米大潮的木筏，拉尧和瓦尔达纳两个群体常远航到卡西尼群岛、蒙塔尔维特群岛一带的礁岩和小岛。他们与沃罗拉人、恩加里宁人共同组成旺吉纳·温古尔文化圈，其律法和梦时代神话以旺吉纳与温古尔两类神灵为核心。

1820年9月，菲利普·帕克·金在第三次澳大利亚考察途中，把‘美人鱼号’拖到加冕岛的卡雷宁湾修理，停留了18天。船员没有遇到武南布尔人，但金在日记里记下了海滩上的树皮棚屋、山丘上更结实的房舍，以及沿海居民食用西谷椰子后留下的果核残迹；他还让船匠在一棵古老的猴面包树上刻下‘美人鱼号1820’的字样。

en: The Wunumaran are the Wanamara, an Aboriginal Australian people of north-western Queensland whose lands covered the Flinders River country, taking in Richmond and Kynuna; the Quippen-bura near Richmond may have been their northern horde. They spoke Wanamarra, also called Maykulan, one of the Mayi languages of the Pama-Nyungan family, closely linked to neighbouring Ngawun speech.
zh: 伍努马拉人即瓦努马拉人，是昆士兰西北部的澳大利亚原住民，领地覆盖弗林德斯河流域，包括里士满和基努纳；里士满附近的奎彭布拉可能是他们北部的一支游群。他们说的瓦努马拉语又称马伊库兰语，属帕马—牛雅语系的马伊语群，与邻近的恩加温语关系密切。

en: The Wurundjeri are a Woiwurrung-speaking people of the Kulin nation and, with the Boonwurrung, the traditional owners of the Yarra River valley, the country they call Naarm on which Melbourne now stands. Their clans, among them the Wurundjeri-willam and Bulug-willam, kept camps along the Yarra, or Birrarung, and at Bolin Bolin lagoon, where eels, fish and possum were taken; firestick farming kept open grassy plains thick with murnong yam daisies, the staple starch root. They also worked the diorite greenstone quarry at Mount William, whose prized axe heads were traded as far as New South Wales and Adelaide, and joined the great Kulin assemblies where hundreds gathered for ceremony, trade and marriage. In 1835 John Batman met their ngurungaeta, including Bebejan and Billibellary, at Merri Creek and, after a tanderrum ceremony, obtained the agreement later called Batman's Treaty; the colonial government annulled it, yet the treaty was used to seize some 600,000 acres, and within a few years most of the Wurundjeri river country had been taken.
zh: 伍伦杰里人是库林联盟中讲沃伊武朗语的族群，与布武朗人同为雅拉河谷的传统主人，这片他们称为纳姆的土地上后来建起了墨尔本。伍伦杰里维拉姆、布卢格维拉姆等氏族在雅拉河（本名比拉拉恩）沿岸和博林博林潟湖一带宿营，捕捉鳗鱼、鱼和负鼠；他们用火耕维持开阔的草原，上面长满作为主要淀粉来源的穆尔农山药菊。他们还开采威廉山的闪长岩绿石矿场，其珍贵的石斧毛坯远销新南威尔士和阿德莱德；库林诸族举行盛大集会时，数百人聚在一起举行仪式、贸易和联姻。1835年，约翰·巴特曼在梅里溪会见比比扬、比利贝拉里等恩贡加塔首领，在坦德鲁姆仪式之后达成了后来所称的巴特曼条约；殖民政府宣布条约无效，它却被用来侵占约六十万英亩土地，几年之内伍伦杰里人的河畔故土便大半易主。

en: The Wuthathi, also recorded as the Mutjati or Otati, are an Aboriginal people of the eastern shore of the northern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, whose country centred on the white silica dunes and coastal rivers of Shelburne Bay on the Coral Sea.
