They were one of the Kawadji, or sandbeach people, who kept camps along the shore and lived mainly by fishing in the ocean and the river mouths, gathering shellfish and seasonal foods along the beach. Their language was a dialect of Uradhi in the Paman branch of the Pama-Nyungan family. Captain Cook charted this coastline in 1770, but outsiders did not settle in their remote country until long after the period ended.
zh: 伍塔西人（也记作穆贾蒂人或奥塔蒂人）是昆士兰约克角半岛北部东岸的原住民，家园以珊瑚海畔谢尔本湾的白色硅沙沙丘和入海河流为中心。他们属于“沙滩人”群体，沿海岸设有营地，主要在海洋和河口捕鱼，在滩涂上采集贝类与时令食物。他们的语言是乌拉迪语的一种方言，属帕马-牛雅语系的帕马语组。1770年库克船长测绘了这条海岸线，但直到本时期结束很久以后，外来者才进入这片偏远之地定居。

en: The Munduruku, who call themselves Wuyjuyu, “our people”, are a Tupi-speaking people of the Brazilian Amazon whose homeland is the Tapajós river valley, a country of rainforest broken by patches of savannah known as the Tapajós fields. Their familiar name was given them by their enemies the Parintintin and means “red ants”, after their habit of attacking in great swarms; colonists came to know them as head-cutters, for they took enemy heads and dried and shrank them as ritual trophies. Their villages were built around a men's house, where all males over thirteen lived apart from the women and younger children. When recorded contact with the Portuguese began in the second half of the 1700s, the Munduruku dominated the Tapajós and were pressing the Mura people of the lower Madeira so hard that the Mura sought shelter with the colonists. Punitive expeditions could not reach the upper Tapajós, so the Portuguese switched to alliance: in 1788 the Munduruku all but destroyed the Mura, and after 1803 they lived at peace with the Brazilians, supplying food and rubber while keeping broad autonomy. The revolt that swept Pará from 1835 brought persecution again, and many communities withdrew deeper into their territory.
zh: 蒙杜鲁库人自称乌伊朱尤，意为“我们的人”，是巴西亚马逊地区使用图皮语族语言的族群，故土在塔帕若斯河流域；那里雨林连绵，间杂着被称为塔帕若斯原野的稀树草原。蒙杜鲁库这个名字来自敌人帕林廷廷人，意为“红蚁”，形容他们成群蜂拥扑向敌军的战法；殖民者则称他们为“砍头者”，因为他们砍下敌人的头颅，晒干缩制成仪式战利品。他们的村庄围绕男子公房而建，十三岁以上的男子都在公房居住，与妇女和幼童分开。18世纪下半叶葡萄牙人首次留下与他们接触的记载，当时蒙杜鲁库人称雄塔帕若斯河流域，猛攻马代拉河下游的穆拉人，逼得穆拉人投奔殖民者求生。讨伐军无法深入上塔帕若斯，葡萄牙人转而采取结盟策略：1788年蒙杜鲁库人大败穆拉人，1803年后与巴西人和平相处，为其提供粮食和橡胶，同时保留了很大的自主权。1835年席卷帕拉的起义使他们再遭迫害，许多社群退入领地深处。

en: The Wùzhōu culture fills the Jinqu basin of central Zhejiang, around Jinhua and its satellite towns of Lanxi, Dongyang, Yiwu, Yongkang and Wuyi. A county existed here from the second century BC, and in 589 the Sui created Wuzhou Prefecture with its seat at Jinhua; the Tang later split off Quzhou to the west, and after passing through the Wuyue kingdom and the Song, Wuzhou became Wuzhou Route under the Yuan in 1276. The present walled city of Jinhua dates to 1352. Its people speak the Wuzhou division of Southern Wu, a chain of related but distinct county varieties spread across the basin. The Wu River links the prefecture through the Qiantang to the southern end of the Grand Canal, making Jinhua a collecting center for rice, bamboo and forest goods; its cured ham has been famous since the Song, and the broad-halled, horse-head-gabled merchant residences built here in the Ming and Qing form the distinctive Wu-school of architecture.
zh: 婺州文化位于浙江中部的金衢盆地，以金华为中心，包括兰溪、东阳、义乌、永康、武义等卫星城邑。早在公元前2世纪这里就已设县，589年隋朝置婺州，州治设在金华；唐代又从婺州析置西边的衢州，其后历经吴越国和两宋，1276年元代升为婺州路。今天金华的城墙城制可追溯到1352年的元末。当地人说的是南部吴语婺州片，盆地内各县方言相近却各有特点。婺江经兰溪、富春江汇入钱塘江，把州城与大运河南端的水运网连在一起，使金华成为稻米、竹木等农林物产的集散中心；金华火腿自宋代起远近闻名，盆地里明清商人宅第厅堂宏敞、马头墙高耸，构成别具一格的婺派建筑。

en: The Halchidhoma, who call themselves Xalychidom Piipaa, meaning the people who live toward the water, were a river people of the lower Colorado around its junction with the Gila, on the border of present-day California and Arizona. They enter written history in 1604 and 1605, when the Spanish expedition of Juan de Oñate met the Alebdoma on the lower Colorado; when the missionary Eusebio Kino returned in 1700, the tribe had shifted about a hundred miles upriver. In the constant warfare of the Colorado tribes, the Halchidhoma sided with the Maricopa and Cocopa against the Quechan and Mohave. In the 1820s the Mohave and Quechan finally drove them from the river, and they took refuge with the Maricopa on the middle Gila. Some families then moved on to Lehi on the Salt River and kept a separate identity, while the rest merged into the Maricopa; their abandoned Colorado lands were taken over by the Chemehuevi.
zh: 哈利奇多姆人自称“哈利奇多姆·皮皮”，意为“临水而居的人”，是科罗拉多河下游、该河与希拉河汇流一带的河畔族群，活动于今加利福尼亚州与亚利桑那州交界。他们最早见于记载是在1604至1605年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特率领的西班牙远征队在科罗拉多河下游遇到了“阿莱布多马人”；1700年传教士尤西比奥·基诺再访此地时，发现该部已向上游迁移了约一百英里。在科罗拉多河诸部无休止的战事中，哈利奇多姆人与马里科帕人、科科帕人结盟，对抗夸特桑人和莫哈维人。19世纪20年代，莫哈维人与夸特桑人终于把他们逐出科罗拉多河，他们投奔希拉河中游的马里科帕人。此后一部分家族继续东迁到盐河的利希并保持独立认同，其余则融入马里科帕人；他们在科罗拉多河畔弃守的土地被切梅惠维人占据。

en: The Cxam are the ǀXam, the San people of the dry Karoo and Bushmanland in what is now South Africa's Northern Cape. Their language belonged to the ǃUi branch of the Tuu click family and was closely related to Nǁng, and their foraging bands were spread between the Strandberg, home of the clan called the Plain people, and the Katkop mountains, home of the Grass people. Like other San they had no chiefs, moved seasonally between springs and pans, and painted hunting scenes and trance visions on rock shelters; in their mythology the jackal, moon, tortoise and mongoose each had its own manner of speech. After the Dutch founded their Cape station in 1652, trekboer pastoralists pushed into the Karoo from 1714 under the loan-farm system, occupying the waterholes and shooting the game on which ǀXam bands lived. Resistance and stock-raiding brought punitive commandos, whose raids peaked in the 1730s and 1750s and became general along the frontier from the 1770s. In 1777 the Dutch East India Company formally endorsed the extermination of the San, and by the end of the century thousands had been killed or bound to frontier farmers, and the independent ǀXam bands of the Karoo had been broken.
zh: 卡姆人是生活在今南非北开普省干旱卡鲁和布须曼兰地区的桑人。他们的语言属图语系 ǃUi 语支，与努语近亲；狩猎采集小群散布在斯特兰德贝格与卡特科普山之间，前者是号称“平原人”的氏族家园，后者则是“草原人”的家园。和其他桑人一样，他们没有酋长，随季节在泉眼和盐沼间迁徙，在岩棚里留下狩猎与出神幻象的壁画；在他们的神话里，豺、月亮、龟和獴各有独特的说话方式。1652年荷兰人在开普建立据点后，游牧布尔民凭借贷农场制度从1714年起涌入卡鲁，占去水洼，射杀卡姆人赖以为生的猎物。反抗和劫掠牲畜招来报复性民团，其袭击在18世纪30年代和50年代达到高峰，18世纪70年代起更在整个边境蔓延。1777年，荷兰东印度公司正式认可对桑人的剿灭政策；到该世纪末，数以千计的桑人被杀或被迫为农场服役，卡鲁地区独立的卡姆人小群已被打散。

en: The Xaracuu are the Kanak people of south-central Grande Terre in New Caledonia, their Xârâcùù language, often called Canala after its chief town, centred on the communes of Canala, Thio and Boulouparis. Xârâcùù forms, together with its neighbour Xârâgurè, a distinct branch of the southern New Caledonian languages, themselves heirs to the Austronesian speech of Lapita villagers who first occupied these coasts between 1100 BC and AD 200. Its numerals carry special classifiers, prefixes and suffixes that sort counted things by kind, a habit of mind echoed in a society where shell money, yam stores and ceremonial gifts fixed every clan's rank. Xaracuu chiefs ruled from great houses topped with the carved flèche faîtière, overseeing taro terraces, lagoon fishing fleets and long cycles of feast and feud. James Cook sailed past in 1774 without landing, and for two generations more the only Europeans seen were passing whalers, so that well into the 1830s the Xaracuu valleys still ran entirely by their own clan politics.
zh: 哈拉库人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛中南部的卡纳克人，其哈拉库语常以重镇得名而称卡纳拉语，主要分布在卡纳拉、蒂奥和布卢帕里三市镇。哈拉库语与邻近的哈拉古雷语共同构成新喀里多尼亚南部语群中的独立分支，而南部语群承继的是公元前1100年至公元200年间最早占据这些海岸的拉皮塔村民所使用的南岛语。哈拉库语的数词带有特殊的量词、前缀和后缀，按类别区分所数之物；这种思维习惯也反映在社会中：贝币、山药储备和仪式礼物决定着每个氏族的等级。哈拉库酋长在屋顶竖着雕花矛饰的大屋里发号施令，统辖芋头梯田、潟湖捕鱼船队以及宴饮与仇杀交替的漫长周期。詹姆斯·库克于1774年途经此地但并未登陆，此后两代人的时间里，当地人见到的欧洲人只有路过的捕鲸者；直到19世纪30年代，哈拉库各山谷仍完全依照自己的氏族规则运转。

en: The Xauxa were the Quechua-speaking people of the southern Mantaro Valley in the central Peruvian highlands, who before the Incas belonged to the Xauxa-Wanka confederation and shared the valley with the Wanka to their north. They submitted to Inca expansion under Túpac Yupanqui and became renowned warriors of the empire, supplying soldiers for the campaigns as far north as Quito; the Incas built Hatun Xauxa as the administrative center of the Xauxa province, set on the great royal road between Cusco and Quito, and the body of the Emperor Wayna Qhapaq paused there on its way home from Quito. When the Inca civil war began the Xauxa sided with Huascar, whose generals Atoc and Guanca Auqui, a son of Wayna Qhapaq by a Xauxa wife, used the city as their headquarters, until Atahualpa's general Challco Chima stormed it and took savage reprisals against the loyalist population; the captive Huascar was held in its fortress before being drowned in the Andamarca River. The Xauxa then welcomed the Spaniards as liberators: Francisco Pizarro made Santa Fe de Hatun Xauxa the first Spanish capital of Peru in April 1534, drawn by its vast Inca storehouses, though Lima supplanted it the next year. Under the viceroyalty the town of Jauja declined into dependence on Tarma, and between 1742 and 1756 its mountains were swept by the great indigenous rebellion of Juan Santos Atahualpa.
zh: 豪哈人是秘鲁中部高原曼塔罗河谷南部讲克丘亚语的族群，在印加人到来之前属于豪哈-万卡联盟，与北部的万卡人分据河谷。他们在图帕克·尤潘基扩张时归顺印加，后来以善战著称，为帝国远至基多的征战提供士兵；印加人在其土地上修建大东豪哈作为豪哈省的行政中心，它坐落在连接库斯科与基多的皇家大道旁，皇帝瓦伊纳·卡帕克的灵柩从基多运回库斯科时也曾在此停驻。印加内战爆发后，豪哈人站在瓦斯卡尔一边，瓦斯卡尔的将领阿托克和瓜安卡·奥基（瓦伊纳·卡帕克与豪哈女子之子）以该城为大本营，直到阿塔瓦尔帕的大将查尔库奇马将其攻陷，并对效忠派居民施以残酷报复；被俘的瓦斯卡尔就关押在城中要塞，后来被溺死在安达马卡河。豪哈人随后把西班牙人当作解放者迎接：1534年4月，皮萨罗被印加人留下的巨大仓库吸引，将圣菲-德大东豪哈定为西属秘鲁的第一个首府，不过次年利马便取代了它。总督区时期，豪哈城日渐衰落，依附于塔尔马；1742年至1756年间，其周围山区又卷入了胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕领导的印第安人大起义。

en: The X'xegwi are the ǁXegwi, San foragers of the high grasslands around Lake Chrissie in eastern South Africa, close to the Swazi border. Their extinct Batwa tongue was an ǃKwi language of the Tuu family; they called themselves Tlouʼeʼthle, ‘people of rock and water’, while Nguni neighbours called them Abatwa and the Sotho Baroa.
zh: 泽格维人是南非东部高地草原、邻近斯威士兰边界的克里西湖一带的桑人狩猎采集者。他们已消亡的语言又称巴特瓦语，属图语系的克维语支；他们自称 Tlouʼeʼthle，意为“岩石与水之民”，恩古尼邻族称其为阿巴特瓦人，索托人则称巴罗阿人。

en: The Xetá are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Serra dos Dourados in northwestern Paraná, whose traditional lands lay along the Ivaí River and its tributaries. Their men wore wooden lip discs after the initiation ritual, which earned them the colonial label of Botocudo, and through the whole colonial period they remained almost entirely beyond Portuguese observation.
zh: 谢塔人是巴拉那州西北部多拉达山的图皮-瓜拉尼语族群，传统领地位于伊瓦伊河及其支流一带。他们的男子在成年礼后佩戴木制唇盘，因而得到博托库多这一殖民地称呼；整个殖民时期，他们几乎都处在葡萄牙人的视野之外。

en: The Xhosa are the southernmost of the Nguni peoples, Bantu-speaking agropastoralists whose clans have held the coast and hills of the Eastern Cape since at least the seventh century, when they arrived with cattle, goats, assegais and shields and absorbed the older San hunter-gatherers and Khoekhoe herders they found there. Oral tradition traces the Xhosa kingdom to the leader Tshawe, who before the fifteenth century overthrew his brother and bound the independent Nguni and Khoekhoe clans around him into one polity under the royal amaTshawe; peoples such as the Inqua, Giqwa and amaNgqosini entered it as tributaries and took up the isiXhosa tongue. Their language belongs to the Nguni branch of Bantu and carries roughly fifteen percent Khoisan vocabulary along with click consonants adopted from the same contact, while remaining largely mutually intelligible with Zulu. The Dutch foundation of the Cape in 1652 began a long colonial pressure eastward, and by the later eighteenth century the Xhosa chiefdoms were fighting the Cape frontier wars, among the longest armed resistances to European expansion in southern Africa. During the mfecane upheavals of the early nineteenth century they sheltered refugees fleeing the Zulu kingdom, incorporating them as the amaMfengu, and in 1823 missionaries produced the first printed works in isiXhosa at the Lovedale press.
zh: 科萨人是恩古尼各族中分布最南的一支，是说班图语的农牧民。至迟从7世纪起，他们的氏族便带着牛、羊、长矛和盾牌占据东开普的海岸与丘陵，并同化了当地更早的桑人猎民和科伊科伊牧民。口传传统把科萨王国追溯到首领察韦：他在15世纪以前推翻兄长，把周围独立的恩古尼和科伊科伊氏族——如因夸、吉克瓦和阿姆恩戈西尼——并入以王室阿姆察韦氏族为核心的政权，纳为附庸并让他们改用科萨语。科萨语属班图语系恩古尼语支，约有百分之十五的词汇来自科伊桑语，还在接触中吸收了吸气辅音，同时与祖鲁语大体可以互通。1652年荷兰人在开普建殖民地，开始了长期的东扩压力；到18世纪后期，科萨各酋邦投入开普边境战争，这是南部非洲历时最久的反欧洲扩张武装抵抗之一。19世纪初的姆费卡内大乱中，他们收容逃离祖鲁王国的难民，将其编为姆芬古人；1823年，传教士在洛夫代尔印刷所印出了最早的科萨语出版物。

en: Xiangxi denotes the Ji-Xu, or Chen-Xu, branch of Xiang Chinese, scattered through the Wuling mountains along the middle Yuan River in western Hunan, in the counties of Chenxi, Xupu, Luxi, Mayang and Guzhang. It stands apart from both New and Old Xiang, keeping only some of the Middle Chinese voiced initials, and sits beside the Miao and Tujia languages of the same hills. Chinese rule reached the region with the expansion of the state of Chu in the third century BCE, and Han and later dynasties kept only a loose hold on its valleys. Under the Yuan and the Ming after 1368 the native Tujia and Miao chieftains, or tusi, governed much of the area; the Qing court later replaced them with appointed officials in its gaitu guiliu reforms, tightening imperial control and drawing this remote frontier more firmly into Hunan.
zh: 湘西指湘语的吉溆片（亦称辰溆片），散布在湖南西部武陵山区、沅水中游的辰溪、溆浦、泸溪、麻阳、古丈等县。它既不同于新湘也不同于老湘，只保留了部分中古汉语浊声母，与同一片山区里的苗语、土家语并存。公元前3世纪楚国扩张，把统治延伸到这一地区；汉代以后的历代王朝对这些山谷控制松弛。元代以及1368年建立的明代，当地的土家族、苗族土司统辖着大部分地方；清代推行改土归流，以流官取代土著首领，朝廷控制加强，这片偏远边地也被更紧密地纳入湖南。

en: The Xindonga is a collective name for four small Bantu groups of southeastern Angola's Cuando Cubango country, the Cusso or Mbukushu, Dilico, Sambio and Maxico, living by subsistence farming, fishing and hunting along the Kavango and upper Zambezi. The Mbukushu, the best known of them, formed one of the five Kavango kingdoms and were famed as rain-makers.
zh: 欣东加是对安哥拉东南宽多-库邦戈地区四个班图小族群的统称，即库苏（姆库舒）、迪利科、桑比奥和马希科，他们在卡万戈河与赞比西河上游一带靠自给农业、渔猎为生。其中最知名的姆库舒人是卡万戈五王国之一，以祈雨之术闻名。

en: The Xinghua, or Putian people, are the Han Chinese of the Xinghua plain on the central Fujian coast, the two districts of Putian and Xianyou, speaking Pu-Xian, a Coastal Min tongue midway between the Eastern Min of Fuzhou and the Southern Min of Quanzhou. Putian county was first set up under the Chen dynasty in 568, and until 979 the region belonged to Quanzhou and shared its speech; in that year the Song created the separate Xinghua military prefecture, after which its dialect developed on its own, taking in Eastern Min features while keeping a Southern Min core. The coast also gave China one of its most popular cults: Lin Moniang, a shamaness of Meizhou Island born in 960, was worshipped after her death in 987 as Mazu, goddess of the sea. Song emperors recognised her temple from 1123, Zheng He earned her a new title in 1409, and after the Qing campaign against Taiwan in 1683 she was promoted to Heavenly Empress, carrying the name of Xinghua fishermen across every port of the China seas.
zh: 兴化人又称莆田人，是福建中部沿海兴化平原上的汉族民系，居莆田、仙游两地，操莆仙话——一种介于福州闽东语与泉州闽南语之间的沿海闽语。莆田县最早设于568年的陈朝；979年之前这里一直隶属泉州、方言也与泉州相通，宋朝于979年另设兴化军，此后方言独立发展，在闽南语底子上吸收了闽东语的特点。这片海岸还诞生了中国最盛行的民间信仰之一：湄洲岛巫女林默娘生于960年，987年去世后被奉为海神妈祖。1123年起宋朝皇帝敕封其庙，1409年郑和为她请得新封号，1683年清军平定台湾后她又被晋封为天后，兴化渔民的保护神由此随海上航线传遍中国沿海各港口。

en: The Xīnhuì are the people of the lower Tan River in the south-western Pearl River Delta, whose speech, with the Huicheng accent as its standard, is one of the representative dialects of the coastal Siyi or Four Counties branch of Yue, alongside the dialects of Taishan, Kaiping and Enping. Settled on land silted up at the confluence of the Tan and West Rivers, Xinhui was the scene of the Battle of Yamen in 1279, when the last Song fleet was destroyed by the Yuan navy and the boy emperor Zhao Bing perished in the sound. Under the Ming it produced Chen Baisha, born in 1428, the first Guangdong scholar to win empire-wide fame; his Baisha school of Neo-Confucianism shaped Lingnan thought for generations. The county also gave its name to Xinhui chenpi, the dried mandarin peel prized across China in cooking and medicine.
zh: 新会人聚居在珠江三角洲西南部潭江下游，所说新会话以会城腔为标准音，与台山、开平、恩平话同属粤语沿海支系四邑方言，是四邑话的代表之一。新会地处潭江与西江交汇处的冲积平原，1279年这里的崖门海面爆发崖门海战，南宋最后的水师被元朝海军歼灭，幼帝赵昺殉海，宋朝就此灭亡。明代这里诞生了生于1428年的陈献章，世称陈白沙，他是第一位名扬全国的广东学者，开创的白沙学派又称江门学派，塑造了此后数代的岭南理学；新会还以特产新会陈皮闻名，这种晒制的柑橘皮在中国饮食和医药中长期被视为佳品。

en: The Xinka are a non-Mayan people of southeastern Guatemala, possibly among the earliest inhabitants of the region, predating both the Maya and the Pipil. Their Xincan languages form an isolated family with many Mayan loanwords. Before the Spanish arrival they shared the eastern Pacific plain with the Pipil, their main territory lying in what is now Santa Rosa Department with further communities in Jutiapa. In 1524 Pedro de Alvarado, marching with 250 Spanish soldiers and some 6,000 Kaqchikel and Cholultec allies, met them at Guazacapán and stormed their principal city of Atiquipaque, near Taxisco, on 26 May 1524, against warriors fighting with spears and poisoned arrows. The survivors paid tribute in cacao, cotton, salt and vanilla, and many were enslaved and marched off to the conquest of El Salvador, which gave the locality of Los Esclavos near Cuilapa its name. After 1575 deportations emptied whole towns, and by the time Archbishop Cortés y Larraz visited the diocese of Taxisco in 1769 the Xincan tongue survived in only a few communities.
zh: 辛卡人是危地马拉东南部的非玛雅族群，可能是当地最早的居民之一，比玛雅人和皮皮尔人更早来到这里。他们的辛卡语是一个孤立语系，吸收了大量玛雅语借词。西班牙人到来之前，他们与皮皮尔人分据东部太平洋平原，主要领土在今圣罗萨省，胡蒂亚帕省也有社群。1524年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多率250名西班牙士兵和约6000名卡克奇克尔与乔卢特卡同盟军进至瓜萨卡潘，于1524年5月26日攻占他们的首要城市阿蒂基帕克（位于塔克西斯科附近），守城武士以长矛和毒箭殊死抵抗。幸存者以可可、棉花、盐和香草纳贡，许多人被掳为奴，押去参加征服萨尔瓦多的战事，奎拉帕附近的洛斯埃斯克拉沃斯（意为奴隶）便由此得名。1575年之后，人口流放使整座城镇空虚，到1769年科尔特斯·伊·拉腊斯大主教视察塔克西斯科教区时，辛卡语只在少数社群中残存。

en: New Xiang, or Chang-Yi, is the northern and eastern branch of the Xiang languages, centred on Changsha on the lower Xiang River and spoken across Yiyang, Xiangtan, Ningxiang and Xiangyin. Xiang speech descends from the Nanchu dialect formed when Chu migrants settled among the Ba, Nanman and Baiyue peoples of Hunan in the Warring States period; the Han scholar Yang Xiong already recorded this Southern Chu speech in his Fangyan. Northern migrants under the Tang brought Middle Chinese forms, and after the Mongol conquest of the Song in the thirteenth century devastated Hunan, large numbers of Jiangxi settlers arrived under the Ming after 1368, bringing Gan influence. In the speech of Changsha and the eastern lowlands this contact effaced the voiced initials of Middle Chinese, marking New Xiang off from the older dialects of the interior; the Changsha dialect is its standard representative.
zh: 新湘又称长益片，是湘语偏北、偏东的一支，以湘江下游的长沙为中心，通行于益阳、湘潭、宁乡、湘阴等地。湘语源于战国时代楚人迁入湖南、与当地巴人、南蛮、百越诸族融合而成的南楚方言，汉代扬雄的《方言》已记载这种南楚话。唐代北方移民带来中古汉语的成分；13世纪蒙古灭宋之战使湖南人口锐减，1368年明朝建立后，大批江西移民迁入，带来赣语影响。在长沙及东部低地的口音里，这种接触使中古汉语的浊声母完全消失，新湘由此与内陆保留浊音的老湘区分开来，长沙话是新湘的代表方言。

en: The Xixime were a mountain people of the Sierra Madre Occidental, in the rough border country between Sinaloa and Durango, where they lived in dispersed extended-family villages around stone cliff towns. They grew maize, chile, cotton, tobacco and squash on the slopes and gathered prickly pears, mesquite beans and wild honey, trading for sea shells with the coastal peoples; Spanish scouts in Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán's 1530 expedition thought their stone settlements made them more civilized than their neighbors. Colonial reports claim they ate captured enemies in rites meant to secure the maize harvest, though modern historians suspect such stories were exaggerated. Their long feud with the Acaxee ran across the sixteenth century, and when Jesuit missions pushed into the sierras the Xixime rose in the rebellion of 1610, calling the churches temples of disease and attacking the Acaxee for refusing to join. Francisco de Urdiñola marched in with two hundred Spanish soldiers and eleven hundred native allies and broke the revolt by October; the Xixime later backed the far larger Tepehuán Revolt of 1616.
zh: 希希梅人是西马德雷山脉的山地族群，活动在锡那罗亚与杜兰戈之间崎岖的交界地带，以大家族为单位散居在石砌崖镇周围的村落里。他们在坡地种植玉米、辣椒、棉花、烟草和南瓜，采集仙人掌果、牧豆和野蜂蜜，并用山货与沿海居民交换贝壳；1530年尼尼奥·贝尔特兰·德·古斯曼远征队的西班牙斥候认为，他们的石砌定居点比邻族更为文明。殖民文献记载，希希梅人会在祈求玉米丰收的仪式上食用俘虏，不过近代史家怀疑这类说法被夸大了。他们与阿卡塞人的世仇贯穿整个16世纪；耶稣会传教站深入山区后，希希梅人在1610年发动起义，称教堂为“疫病之庙”，并攻打拒绝加盟的阿卡塞人。弗朗西斯科·德·乌尔迪尼奥拉率两百名西班牙士兵和一千一百名原住民盟友进山，于当年10月镇压了起义；希希梅人后来又支持了规模大得多的1616年特佩万起义。

en: The Xllang are the people of the Sican, or Lambayeque, culture, which occupied the river valleys of the north Peruvian coast around modern Chiclayo from about 750 to 1375. Succeeding the Moche, they farmed the irrigated valleys of the La Leche and Lambayeque rivers and spoke Muchik. Between 900 and 1100 their religious capital at Batán Grande presided over a florescence of adobe temple mounds, fine black ceramics and arsenical-bronze and gold metallurgy; elite tombs held gold masks and tumbaga ornaments, and llama caravans carried trade as far as Ecuador and Colombia. A generation-long drought around 1020 shattered the old order: the temples of Batán Grande were burned and abandoned between 1050 and 1100, and a new capital rose at Túcume, where twenty-six great mounds were built around La Raya mountain. In 1337 the Lambayeque polities still ruled their valleys, but the expansion of Chimor ended their independence around 1375.
zh: 什扬人即西坎（又称兰巴耶克）文化的居民，约750年至1375年间生活在今秘鲁北部沿海奇克拉约一带的河谷中。他们继承莫切文化，在拉莱切河与兰巴耶克河的灌溉谷地务农，使用穆奇克语。900年至1100年，宗教中心巴丹格兰德进入鼎盛期，土坯神庙、精美黑陶以及砷青铜和黄金冶铸盛极一时，贵族墓葬出土了黄金面具和通巴加金饰，羊驼商队的贸易远达厄瓜多尔和哥伦比亚。1020年前后持续约三十年的大旱动摇了旧秩序，巴丹格兰德的神庙在1050年至1100年间被焚毁废弃，新的中心土库美在拉亚山旁建起26座大土墩。1337年时兰巴耶克诸邦仍据有各自的河谷，但奇穆王国的扩张在1375年前后终结了他们的独立。

en: The Xocó, also recorded as Shocó, Chocó or Ceocose, are an Indigenous people of the lower São Francisco River whose villages in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries ranged from Sergipe north to southern Ceará, shifting from one bank of the river to the other. They lived largely itinerant lives, repeatedly slipping away from the mission settlements where the Portuguese tried to concentrate them. In the late seventeenth century Capuchin friars founded the missions of São Pedro de Porto da Folha and Caiçara in Sergipe, gathering the Xocó together with other peoples, and in 1700 the Portuguese Crown granted the mission Indians a square league of land. Their original language, known only from short word lists, was never securely classified and is now extinct, the people speaking Portuguese. The eighteenth-century church and the ruins of the Capuchin convent still stand at São Pedro, where the Xocó kept their Toré ritual alive in secret after the missionaries forbade it.
zh: 肖科人（文献中又作绍科、乔科或塞奥科塞）是圣弗朗西斯科河下游的原住民，17至18世纪时村落分布从塞尔希培向北延伸到塞阿拉南部，并在河两岸反复迁徙。他们长期过着流动生活，一再逃离葡萄牙人试图集中安置他们的传教村。17世纪末，嘉布遣会修士在塞尔希培建立圣佩德罗-迪波尔图达福利亚和凯萨拉传教站，把肖科人与其他族群集中在一起；1700年，葡萄牙王室向传教站的印第安人授予一平方里格的土地。他们原有的语言只留下简短词表，归属始终没有定论，后来消亡，肖科人转而使用葡萄牙语。圣佩德罗保存着18世纪的教堂和嘉布遣会修道院遗迹；传教士禁止托雷仪式后，肖科人仍秘密举行这一仪式。

en: The Qxoon are the ǃXoon, San foragers of the Kalahari in Botswana and Namibia who call their language Taa or ǃXóõ. Taa is a Tuu click language with one of the largest sound inventories, most basic words beginning with a click. It forms a west-to-east dialect continuum, and some communities call themselves ʼNǀohan rather than ǃXoon.
zh: 昆人是博茨瓦纳和纳米比亚卡拉哈里的桑人狩猎采集者，把自己的语言称作 Taa（宏语，又名 ǃXóõ）。宏语属图语系，是已知音位数量最多的语言之一，大部分基本词以吸气音开头。它是一条自西向东分布的方言连续体，部分社群自称 ʼNǀohan，而不用昆人之名。

en: The Xuānzhōu culture covers the hilly country of southern Anhui between the Tianmu range and Mount Huangshan, centered on Xuancheng and taking in Wuhu, Dangtu, Ningguo, Taiping and Jingxian. In the Spring and Autumn period the land passed between the states of Wu, Yue and Chu; the Qin made it Zhang Commandery in the third century BC, and in 109 BC the Han reorganized it as Danyang Commandery with its seat at Wanling, the future Xuancheng, which became the seat of Xuancheng Commandery in 281 and has remained the regional center ever since. Its speech is the Xuanzhou division of Wu, also called Western Wu, the most internally diverse of the Wu branches, carrying strong influence from the Jianghuai Mandarin of the north together with sound innovations of its own. Through the Yuan, Ming and Qing the prefecture was known for crafts rather than politics, above all the rice paper, writing brushes and inkstones sold across China under the name of Xuan, while the same hills to the south bordered the merchant country of Huizhou.
zh: 宣州文化地处皖南山地，夹在天目山与黄山之间，以宣城为中心，范围包括芜湖、当涂、宁国、太平、泾县等地。春秋时期，这片土地在吴、越、楚三国之间几经易手；公元前3世纪秦代设鄣郡，公元前109年汉代改置丹阳郡，郡治宛陵就是后来的宣城，281年又在此设宣城郡，此后一直是区域行政中心。当地所说的宣州片吴语又称西吴语，是吴语各片中内部分化最复杂的一支，既受到北方江淮官话的强烈影响，又有自身独特的语音创新。元、明、清三代，这片州府以物产而非武功闻名，尤以宣纸、宣笔和砚台享誉全国，宣纸之名即得自宣州；群山之南，则与徽商的故里相接。

en: The Xumani, better known in Spanish records as the Jumanos, a name also spelled Xumana, were the people of La Junta, where the Río Conchos meets the Río Bravo near present-day Presidio, Texas, and they ranged across western Texas, New Mexico and northern Mexico. Cabeza de Vaca may have met them near La Junta in 1535, and Antonio de Espejo first used the name Jumano in 1582 for the farming villagers there, while related bands hunted bison on the Pecos River. Their homeland between the Pecos and the Conchos made them traders in hides, meat and salt, and around 1580 perhaps twenty to thirty thousand people lived wholly or partly as Jumanos along the two great rivers. In the seventeenth century drought and advancing Lipan and Mescalero Apache drove them to seek Spanish missions and alliances, and the chief Juan Sabeata built trade and Christian ties in the 1680s. Their language is unrecorded, with Uto-Aztecan, Tanoan and Athabascan all proposed. By 1729 the Spanish spoke of Apache Jumanos, and by 1750 the nation had dissolved, its remnants absorbed by Apache, Caddo and Wichita bands after epidemics, slaving raids and war.
zh: 舒马尼人在西班牙文献中更常见的名字是胡马诺人，这个名字也曾拼作 Xumana。他们活动在孔乔斯河与布拉沃河交汇处的拉洪塔，即今得克萨斯普雷西迪奥一带，并广泛游徙于得克萨斯西部、新墨西哥和墨西哥北部。卡韦萨·德巴卡可能于1535年在拉洪塔遇到过他们；1582年，探险家安东尼奥·德埃斯佩霍首次用胡马诺一名称呼当地务农的村人，而与他们同源的队伍则在佩科斯河上猎捕野牛。家乡处在佩科斯河与孔乔斯河之间，他们遂以兽皮、肉食和盐贸易为生；1580年前后，两条大河沿岸全部或部分过着胡马诺式生活的人口可能有两三万之众。17世纪，干旱和南下的利潘、梅斯卡莱罗阿帕奇人迫使他们求助于西班牙传教团并寻求同盟，酋长胡安·萨维亚塔在17世纪80年代积极建立贸易与基督教联系。他们的语言没有留下记录，犹他—阿兹特克、塔诺和阿萨巴斯卡三种归属都有人主张。到1729年，西班牙人已改称他们为阿帕奇胡马诺人；1750年前后，这个民族在疫病、奴隶猎捕和战争中解体，余众被阿帕奇、卡多和威奇塔诸部吸收。

en: Xuukhoe, meaning ‘people left behind’, is the self-name of the Tsʼixa-speaking San community of Mababe, on the eastern edge of the Okavango Delta in Botswana. Tsʼixa belongs to the Kalahari Khoe branch of the Khoe-Kwadi family, the name is also used by some Khwe speakers, and its speakers are foragers classed by Bantu neighbours as Basarwa. Related Shua dialects such as Deti are spoken around the nearby Makgadikgadi pans.
zh: 乌科伊意为“被留下的人”，是博茨瓦纳奥卡万戈三角洲东缘马巴比村讲茨克萨语的桑人社群的自称，部分克韦语使用者也用这个称呼。茨克萨语属科伊-夸迪语系的卡拉哈里科伊语支，这些人以狩猎采集为生，被班图邻族笼统归入巴萨尔瓦（即桑人）。与它相近的舒阿语方言（如代蒂方言）通行于附近的马卡迪卡迪盐沼一带。

en: The Yadhaigana, also called Yadhaykenu, are an Aboriginal tribe of the eastern coast at the northern tip of the Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, whose country lay north of the Wuthathi around the later site of Bamaga. Their tongue was a dialect of Uradhi, a Paman language of the Pama-Nyungan family. Their name is not their own: it was given them by Torres Strait Islanders, in whose language it means talkers or chatterers, a trace of the long maritime trade and contact between the peninsula peoples and the islanders of the strait. They were the traditional enemies of the Gudang at Cape York's tip and were counted among the warlike tribes of the far north. European ships began sailing the adjacent Torres Strait after the Spanish passage of 1606, and Captain Cook rounded Cape York in 1770, yet permanent settlement on their coast came only after the close of this period.
zh: 亚代加纳人是昆士兰约克角半岛北端东海岸的原住民部落，领地在伍塔西人以北、今巴马加一带。他们的语言是乌拉迪语的一种方言，属帕马-牛雅语系的帕马语组。亚代加纳这个名字并非自称，而来自托雷斯海峡岛民的语言，意为“话多的人”，折射出半岛族群与海峡岛民之间长期的海上贸易与往来。他们与半岛最尖端的古当人世为仇敌，被视为极北地区好战的部落之一。自1606年西班牙人首次航过邻近的托雷斯海峡后，欧洲船只开始出入这一带；1770年库克船长绕过约克角，但直到本时期结束之后，其海岸才出现永久定居点。

en: The Yagalingu, also spelt Jagalingu, were an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland whose country covered the headwaters of the Belyando River, from the Great Dividing Range east to the Drummond Range. Their language is poorly recorded and has been tentatively counted as a dialect of Bidjara, and their local groups included the Auanbura, Owanburra, Wakelbara and Kokleburra.
zh: 亚加林古人又拼写为贾加林古，是昆士兰中部的澳大利亚原住民，领地覆盖贝利安多河源头，西起大分水岭、东抵德拉蒙德山脉。他们的语言留存记录很少，曾被暂定为比贾拉语的一种方言，其地方群包括安布拉、奥万布拉、瓦克尔巴拉和科克尔布拉。

en: The Yahgan, also called Yámana, were the southernmost people on Earth, occupying the maze of islands and channels south of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego as far as Cape Horn, in five canoe-borne groups whose names, from Wakimaala on the Beagle Channel to Yeskumaala around the Horn itself, match the bays where they camped. They were nomadic hunter-gatherers who lived almost entirely from the sea: men harpooned sea lions from bark canoes, women dived in the frigid water for shellfish, and everyone gathered berries, mushrooms and the meat of stranded whales. Their language, Yámana, is a language isolate unrelated to the Chonan speech of the Selk'nam or to Kawésqar. Famous for indifference to the cold, they went mostly naked beside constant fires, slept in small domed huts and kept domesticated Fuegian dogs. Ferdinand Magellan sighted their fires in 1520, but sustained contact came only in the nineteenth century: in 1830 Robert FitzRoy of HMS Beagle seized four Yahgan, including the youth Jemmy Button, carried them to England and presented them at court, then brought them home on the voyage of 1832 that carried Charles Darwin.
zh: 雅甘人又称亚马纳人，曾是地球上分布最南的居民，占据大火地岛以南、一直延伸到合恩角的岛礁与水道网，分为五个操舟游动的群体，其名称从比格尔海峡沿岸的瓦基马拉到合恩角一带的耶斯库马拉，正对应他们宿营的各个海湾。他们是游猎采集族群，生计几乎全靠海洋：男子乘树皮独木舟猎捕海狮，女子潜入冰冷的海水捡拾贝类，全体成员还采集浆果、蘑菇并取食搁浅的鲸鱼。他们的雅甘语是孤立语言，与塞尔克南人的乔南语、卡韦斯卡尔语都没有亲属关系。雅甘人以不畏严寒著称，常在篝火旁近乎赤身露体，睡在狭小的圆顶棚屋里，并驯养火地犬。1520年斐迪南·麦哲伦曾望见他们的篝火，但持续接触要到19世纪才出现：1830年贝格尔号船长罗伯特·菲茨罗伊带走四名雅甘人，其中包括少年杰米·巴顿，把他们带到英国并带入宫廷觐见，随后又在1832年搭载查尔斯·达尔文的那次航行中把他们送回故乡。

en: The Yaka are a Bantu people of the forest and savanna between the Kwango and Wamba rivers in the southwestern Congo basin, close to the Angola border, and speak Kiyaka, an offshoot of Kikongo. In the seventeenth century Lunda migrants moving west under a leader named Kabamba founded the Yaka kingdom, blending with local Kongo-speaking groups such as the Mbala and Tsamba rather than simply ruling over them; the name Yaka itself was originally a Kongo title for warriors. An older Yaka polity had been subdued by the expanding Lunda Empire in the 1730s, and the reorganized kingdom became one of the best-structured states of the Kwango region, long resisting Portuguese and later Belgian penetration. Yaka society is organized under paramount chiefs and matrilineal clans, and its craftsmen are known for bulky upturned-nose masks, mbwoolo figurines and the mukoku slit drum used in ritual dances.
zh: 雅卡人是生活在刚果盆地西南部宽果河与万巴河之间森林和稀树草原地带的班图人，西临安哥拉边境，操基孔戈语的分支基亚卡语。17世纪，向西迁徙的隆达人在首领卡班巴率领下建立雅卡王国，与姆巴拉、昌巴等当地孔戈语族群融合而非单纯加以统治；“雅卡”本是刚果人对武士的称号。更早的雅卡政权在18世纪30年代被扩张中的隆达帝国征服，重组后的王国成为宽果地区结构最完善的政权之一，长期抵御葡萄牙及后来比利时势力的渗透。雅卡社会在最高酋长和母系氏族体系下组织起来，工匠以翘鼻大面具、姆沃洛人像和仪式舞蹈中使用的穆科科缝鼓闻名。

en: Mamachatpam is the self-name of the Lower Yakama, the largest of the five or six Sahaptin-speaking bands that outsiders gathered under the name Yakama. Their villages held the lower Yakima River east of the Cascade Range from the Selah and Wenas valleys down to the falls at Prosser, and they were also called Pa'kiut'lĕma, people of the gap, after their main village in the Union Gap, and Waptailnsim, people of the narrow river. Their upriver cousins were the Kittitas or Upper Yakama, and the related Wanapum kept the Columbia about Priest Rapids, where they cut more than three hundred petroglyphs into the basalt cliffs. All spoke Ichishkíin, a Sahaptin language of the Plateau Penutian family, and lived on Columbia salmon, camas roots and game in villages of rush-mat and tule lodges. In 1805 the Wanapum chief Cutssahnem welcomed the Lewis and Clark Expedition with food and dancing, and in 1805 or 1806 the corps met the Yakama bands themselves at the river confluences of their country.
zh: 马马查特帕姆是下雅卡马人的自称，而雅卡马本是外界对五六个萨哈普廷语支派的统称，下雅卡马是其中最大的一支。他们的村社占据喀斯喀特山脉以东的亚基马河下游，从塞拉谷和韦纳斯谷一直延伸到普罗瑟的瀑布；按其在联合隘口的主村，他们又被称为帕基乌特雷马人，意为“隘口之民”，另有瓦普泰尔辛人即“狭河之民”的称呼。上游的近亲是基蒂塔斯人，又称上雅卡马人；同语的瓦纳普姆人则守着普里斯特急流一带的哥伦比亚河，在玄武岩崖壁上凿下了三百多幅岩画。他们都说伊奇什金语，即高原佩努蒂语系的萨哈普廷语的一支，以哥伦比亚河的鲑鱼、卡马夏百合球茎和猎物为生，村落里是芦席和香蒲草搭成的屋舍。1805年，瓦纳普姆首领库察内姆以食物和歌舞迎接刘易斯与克拉克探险队；1805或1806年，探险队又在雅卡马人土地上的河流交汇处见到了雅卡马诸支派。

en: The Yalarrngan are the Yalarnnga, an Aboriginal Australian people of north-western Queensland, whose country lay around Dajarra and Cloncurry, inland from the Gulf of Carpentaria. They spoke a Pama-Nyungan language of the Kalkatungic branch, grouped by linguists with the neighbouring Kalkatungu, and early records also use variant names such as Jalanga and Yellunga.
zh: 雅拉恩加人是昆士兰西北部的澳大利亚原住民，领地位于卡奔塔利亚湾内陆的达贾拉与克朗克里一带。他们的语言属帕马—牛雅语系卡尔卡通语支，语言学家将其与邻近的卡尔卡通语划为一类；早年文献中该族也有贾兰加、耶隆加等异写。

en: The Yamasee were a multiethnic confederation forged in the seventeenth century from the survivors of shattered Georgia chiefdoms such as Ocute and Altamaha, uprooted by disease and the Westo slave raids. Spanish documents first called them the Yamasis in 1663, when they lived in five coastal villages on the Georgia and South Carolina border. Their Upper Towns were mainly Guale and their Lower Towns Hitchiti speakers, and their poorly recorded speech was close to Muskogean. In the 1680s they settled by the Savannah River and Port Royal Sound and became South Carolina's foremost Indian ally, selling captives taken in slave raids at Charles Town and forming the core of the militia that fought the Tuscarora War. Abuses by traders, mounting debts and colonial hunger for their rice lands drove them to revolt in April 1715: joined by the Muscogee, Catawba and many others, they nearly destroyed the colony before the Cherokee switched sides and the war ended in 1717. The defeated Yamasee dispersed to Spanish Florida and the Creek towns and ceased to exist as an independent people.
zh: 亚马西人是17世纪形成的多族群联盟，成员来自奥库特、奥尔塔马霍等佐治亚酋邦在疫病和韦斯托人奴隶劫掠中崩溃后的遗民。1663年西班牙文献首次称他们为亚马西人，当时他们住在佐治亚与南卡罗来纳边界的五座沿海村庄。其上层城镇以瓜莱人为主，下层城镇多说希奇蒂语，留存极少的语言与马斯科吉语相近。17世纪80年代，他们在萨凡纳河与罗亚尔港湾一带定居，成为南卡罗来纳最重要的印第安盟友，把奴隶劫掠中俘获的人卖到查尔斯镇，并构成参加塔斯卡罗拉战争的民兵主力。商人的欺压、日益沉重的债务以及殖民者对其稻田的觊觎，促使他们于1715年4月起兵：在马斯科吉人、卡托巴人等许多部族响应下，他们险些摧毁这个殖民地，直到切罗基人倒戈，战争于1717年结束。战败的亚马西人四散，有的投奔西属佛罗里达，有的加入克里克城镇，作为独立族群的亚马西人就此消亡。

en: The Yampara are an Andean people of the valleys of present-day Chuquisaca in central Bolivia, whose descendants live around Tarabuco and who gave their name to the province of Yamparáez. They may have been planted in the region as mitimaes, the colonist communities resettled under Inca policy, and by the late fifteenth century they shared the fate of the neighboring Charca when the armies of the Inca Túpac Yupanqui reached their valleys. In 1538 their cacique Kuysara built the alliance that brought Gonzalo Pizarro's Spaniards into the region, leading to the founding of the city that became Sucre. During the independence wars Yampara fighters joined the revolutionaries and helped defeat royalist troops at the battle of Jumbate in 1816.
zh: 扬帕拉人是安第斯族群，居住在今玻利维亚中部丘基萨卡的河谷地带，后裔生活在塔拉武科一带，扬帕拉埃斯县也因他们得名。他们可能是按印加政策被迁居到此的米蒂马埃斯殖民村社；到15世纪末，印加王图帕克·尤潘基的军队进入他们的河谷，扬帕拉人与邻近的查尔卡斯人同遭征服。1538年，其首领奎萨拉促成联盟，把贡萨洛·皮萨罗的西班牙人引入此地，日后发展为苏克雷的城市由此兴建。独立战争期间，扬帕拉战士加入革命军，在1816年的洪巴特战役中协助击败保王派军队。

en: The Yān culture belongs to the people of the old Yan lands, the northern frontier country around present-day Beijing, reaching from the garrison towns of the Jizhou hills to the Bohai coast. Yan was the northernmost of the Warring States, with its capital at Ji on the site of Beijing; its people were famed as straightforward frontier fighters, its generals campaigned against the Donghu and Gojoseon, and Qin Kai's wall and five commanderies guarded a trade frontier where knife money circulated between Chinese farmers and steppe nomads. Under the Tang the same country was Youzhou, a hard-bitten military command where An Lushan launched his rebellion in 755 and proclaimed a rebel Yan dynasty. The Khitan Liao made the city their southern capital Nanjing in 938, the Jurchen Jin their central capital Zhongdu in 1153, and after the Mongols razed Zhongdu in 1215 Kublai Khan built Dadu nearby between 1264 and 1293 as the capital of the Yuan. In 1337, therefore, the Yan people were subjects of the Yuan at its metropolitan heart, linked to the Yangzi delta by the Grand Canal. The Ming took Dadu in 1368 and renamed it Beiping; the Yongle Emperor, formerly enfeoffed as the Prince of Yan, rebuilt it as Beijing and moved the imperial capital there in 1420, and the Qing kept it as their seat after 1644, settling banner garrisons beside the old townspeople.
zh: 燕文化属于古燕地之民，即以现在的北京为中心、从蓟州丘陵的军镇延伸到渤海之滨的北部边疆地区。燕国是战国时代最靠北的诸侯国，都城建在今北京一带的蓟城；燕民以质朴刚毅的边地战士著称，燕将秦开东征东胡和古朝鲜，燕国修筑长城、设置五郡，护卫这条农耕汉人与草原游牧民之间用刀币交易的商路。唐代这里是重兵屯驻的幽州，755年安禄山正是在此起兵叛乱，并建立僭号燕国。938年，契丹辽朝把该城定为陪都南京，1153年女真金朝又立为中都；1215年蒙古人摧毁中都后，忽必烈于1264至1293年在附近营建大都，作为元朝都城。因此1337年时，燕人是元朝京畿腹地的臣民，凭大运河与长江三角洲相连。1368年明军攻占大都，改名北平；曾受封燕王的永乐帝将其重建为北京，于1420年迁都于此，清朝1644年入关后也继续以此为都，并在旧城居民身边驻扎八旗官兵。

en: The Yandan are the Yanda, an Aboriginal Australian people of western Queensland, whose country lay at the headwaters of the Hamilton River, north of Warenda and beside the Pitta Pitta lands. Their language is known only from a single word list, and linguists judge it to have been a Pama-Nyungan tongue close to the neighbouring Guwa.
zh: 阳达人是昆士兰西部的澳大利亚原住民，领地在沃伦达以北的汉密尔顿河源头，与皮塔皮塔人的土地相邻。他们的语言仅靠一份词汇表流传，语言学家判断它属帕马—牛雅语系，与邻近的古瓦语十分接近。

en: The Yandin were a Yukaghir tribal group of the far northern Siberian tundra, living between the lower Lena and the Yana along the middle and upper Omoloy River, where they spoke the Yan, or Detkil, variant of Yukaghir. By about 1650 the Russian tribute books counted fifty tribute-paying Yandin men, perhaps two hundred people in all, entered under the label of the stone Yukaghirs. Their name may derive from the Yukaghir word yande, a goose, or from a local prince called Uyanda. Epidemics, feuds with neighboring Even and Evenki bands and the burden of fur tribute thinned them during the colonial period, and the Yandin eventually vanish from the records as a separate group, their descendants absorbed into the surrounding peoples.
zh: 扬丁人是西伯利亚极北苔原的尤卡吉尔部落，活动在勒拿河下游与亚纳河之间的奥莫洛伊河中游和上游一带，使用尤卡吉尔语的亚纳（杰特基尔）变体。到1650年前后，俄国的贡赋册籍登记了50名纳税的扬丁男子，总人口约200人，册中称他们为“石地”尤卡吉尔人。他们的族名可能来自尤卡吉尔语“扬德”，意为鹅，也可能得名于当地酋长乌扬达。殖民时代里，疫病、与邻近埃文人和鄂温克人各部的冲突，加上毛皮贡赋的重压，使扬丁人不断衰减，最终作为独立群体从记载中消失，后裔融入周围各族。

en: The Yandyr, also recorded as Yandygir, were a small Yukaghir clan group of the Yana and Omoloy country in the far northern Siberian tundra, closely bound to the Yandin and speaking the same Yan, or Detkil, variant of Yukaghir. Their shared name is traced to the Yukaghir word for a goose, or else to the local prince Uyanda. Russian fur-tribute records of the mid-1600s list them among the stone Yukaghirs of the Lena-Yana tundra, a few hundred strong at most. Smallpox, feuds with Even and Evenki neighbors and the pressure of tribute broke the group up within a few generations, and its families were absorbed into the surrounding tundra peoples.
zh: 扬德尔人（文献中又作扬达吉尔）是西伯利亚极北苔原、亚纳河与奥莫洛伊河一带的尤卡吉尔小氏族群体，与扬丁人关系密切，使用同一种尤卡吉尔语亚纳（杰特基尔）变体。他们共同的族名可追溯到尤卡吉尔语里的“鹅”，也有人认为源自酋长乌扬达。17世纪中叶的俄国毛皮贡赋册籍把他们归入勒拿河与亚纳河之间苔原的“石地”尤卡吉尔人，总人口至多几百。天花、与邻近埃文人和鄂温克人的仇杀，加上贡赋的重压，在几代人之间就瓦解了这个群体，其家户最终融入周围的苔原各族。

en: The Yanesha, also called Amuesha, are an Arawak-speaking people of the central Peruvian rainforest, whose villages lie between roughly 200 and 1600 metres along the Palcazu, Pichis and Pachitea rivers in what are now the Pasco, Huánuco and Junín departments. Yanesha is their own name for themselves; they lived by hunting, fishing and subsistence agriculture, and their language belongs to the Maipurean, or Arawak, family shared with the Asháninka and Matsigenka. Mercedarian friars first entered their country in the later sixteenth century, but stable contact came only in the early eighteenth century, when the Franciscan Francisco de San José founded reducciones at Cerro de la Sal and Quimiri. The great indigenous rebellion led by Juan Santos Atahualpa in 1742 destroyed these missions and kept the region closed to outsiders for several decades.
zh: 亚内沙人又称阿梅沙人，是秘鲁中部雨林的阿拉瓦克语族群，村落分布在今帕斯科、瓦努科和胡宁大区海拔200至1600米的地带，沿帕尔卡苏河、皮奇斯河和帕奇特亚河而居。亚内沙是他们的自称，传统上以狩猎、渔捞和自给农业为生，其语言属迈普雷（阿拉瓦克）语系，与阿沙宁卡人、马齐根卡人的语言同系。16世纪下半叶，仁慈会修士最早进入他们的地界，但稳定的接触要到18世纪初：方济各会的弗朗西斯科·德·圣何塞在盐山和基米里建起归化村。1742年，胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕领导的印第安人大起义摧毁了这些传教站，使该地区向外界封闭了数十年。

en: The Yanga, also spelt Jangaa or Janga, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland whose lands lay around the headwaters of the Copperfield River. They spoke the Yanga language, mutually intelligible with neighbouring Mbara, and were also known as the Purkaburra; they may have been the same people as the Yukulta and Ganggalida of the Gulf country.
zh: 阳加人又拼写为詹加或詹加尔，是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，土地位于科珀菲尔德河源头一带。他们使用的阳加语与邻族姆巴拉语可以互通，别名普尔卡布拉；他们可能与海湾地区的尤库尔塔人和冈加利达人是同一群人。

en: The Yangga, also spelt Jangga, were an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, distinct from the similarly named Yanga people of the Gulf country. Their language was recorded by Norman Tindale as Jangga and counted among the dialects of Biri, and settlers also knew them as the Durroburra.
zh: 阳甘人又拼写为詹加，是昆士兰中部的澳大利亚原住民，与名字相近、住在海湾地区的阳加人并非同一群体。诺曼·廷代尔把他们的语言记为詹加语，归入比里语的方言之一；定居者还称他们为杜罗布拉人。

en: The Yángjiāng are the Yue people of the Moyang River basin on the south-western Guangdong coast, around present-day Yangjiang and Yangchun, whose speech is the eastern pillar of the Gao-Yang branch of Yue. Though packed with Cantonese vocabulary, it is not mutually intelligible with Guangzhou speech and keeps older Yue features lost in Cantonese, including a lateral fricative initial shared with Zhuang and Li. That sound, together with place names beginning with na, dong and ma, records the language of the ancient Li aborigines who lived here when Central Plains refugees first arrived during the late Han and Three Kingdoms troubles; the settlers led local sinicization while their speech absorbed Li elements. Administratively the land was Gaoliang county under the Han, became the seat of Gaozhou in 527, and gained its present name with Yangjiang county in 598. In 1048 its prefecture was renamed Nan'en, the name the region still bore around 1337, until the Ming merged it into Zhaoqing prefecture in 1368. The coastal county also built a lasting name for knives, lacquerware and fermented black beans.
zh: 阳江人是广东西南沿海漠阳江流域的粤语人群，聚居在今阳江、阳春一带，阳江话是粤语高阳片的东支支柱。它的词汇深受广州话影响，却与广州话无法互通，还保留了广州话已经失去的旧粤语特征，包括与壮语、黎语共有的边擦音声母；这个声母连同那、洞、麻字头的地名，都是汉末三国战乱中中原移民初到时，当地古南越俚人留下的语言痕迹，移民带来先进技术，主导了俚人的汉化，自己的话也吸收了俚语成分。行政上，这里汉代是合浦郡高凉县地，527年成为高州治所，598年新设阳江县，阳江之名由此而始；1048年所在的恩州改称南恩州，1337年前后这片地区仍以南恩为名，直到1368年明朝撤销恩州，把阳江、阳春并入肇庆府。这座海滨州县还以小刀、漆器和豆豉三件传统特产闻名。

en: The Yangman were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory whose country was centred on the lands around the later town of Larrimah, south-east of Katherine, and reached towards Mataranka and the Elsey country; they had occupied the area for over 40,000 years. They held that the Dreaming tracks of the Storm Bird, the channel-billed cuckoo, shaped the local landscape, and the name Larrimah means meeting place in their tongue. Their language, together with Wardaman and Dagoman, makes up the Yangmanic group of non-Pama-Nyungan languages, once classified within Gunwinyguan but now treated as a family apart.
zh: 阳曼人是北领地的澳大利亚原住民，领地以凯瑟琳东南、后来的拉里马镇所在一带为中心，延伸至马塔兰卡和埃尔西地区；他们在这片土地上已生活四万多年。阳曼人认为风暴鸟（沟嘴鹃）的梦创足迹塑造了当地地貌，“拉里马”在他们的语言中意为集会之地。阳曼语与瓦达曼语、达戈曼语共同构成非帕马-牛雅语的阳曼语组，该语组曾被划入贡温古语，后来被视为独立语族。

en: The Yanyuwa are a saltwater Aboriginal people of the southern Gulf of Carpentaria in the Northern Territory, holding the coast around and opposite the Sir Edward Pellew Group of Islands near the mouth of the McArthur River. From the 1720s Makassan trepangers from Sulawesi began visiting their shores, arriving with the December north-westerlies and leaving on the April south-easterlies, and trade relations were close enough that Yanyuwa men sometimes sailed back with the prau fleets and stayed for months at Makassar; many Gulf peoples used Makassan as a trade lingua franca and its words entered their languages. Their own tongue, Yanyuwa, is a Pama-Nyungan language of the Ngarna group, unusual in maintaining distinct men's and women's dialects that differ in noun classes, verbs and pronouns; boys grew up speaking the women's form and switched to men's speech at initiation, and many Yanyuwa also spoke the neighbouring Garrwa language.
zh: 雅纽瓦人是澳大利亚北领地卡奔塔利亚湾南岸的“海水民族”，领有麦克阿瑟河口附近爱德华·佩柳爵士群岛及其对岸的海岸。从18世纪20年代起，苏拉威西的望加锡海参商人开始到访他们的海岸，乘着12月的西北风而来，顺着4月的东南风而归；双方贸易关系密切，雅纽瓦男子有时随帆船船队回访，在望加锡一住数月。湾岸许多族群把望加锡语作为贸易通用语，望加锡词汇也进入了他们的语言。雅纽瓦语是帕马—牛雅语系纳尔纳语支的语言，独特之处在于保留着男女有别的两种方言，名词类别、动词和代词都各不相同；男孩自幼说女性方言，到成年礼时才改说男性方言，此外不少雅纽瓦人也兼通邻族的加拉瓦语。

en: The Yao, whose largest branch calls itself Iu Mien, are a highland people of southern China who speak Mienic languages of the Hmong–Mien family. Their traditions trace them to the country around Dongting Lake and Changsha in Hunan, and they venerate Panhu, the dog-ancestor of Chinese legend, as the forefather of their clans. Between 200 BCE and 900 CE they drifted south of the Yangtze into the hill ranges of Hunan, Guangxi and Guangdong, clearing highland slopes with slash-and-burn farming; under the Tang they appear in official records as the Mo Yao, highlanders excused from forced labor. From the tenth to the thirteenth centuries they came under imperial rule through the loose jimi and tusi systems, paying tribute through their own hereditary headmen. In 1337 Yao communities were thickest in the Guilin hills of Guangxi and around Lianzhou in northern Guangdong. The Ming and Qing tightened control by replacing headmen with appointed tax officials, and the Yao rose alongside the Miao in the rebellions of the 1370s and 1449; each defeat pushed communities deeper into the mountains or further south, and by about 1700 the first Mien migrants had crossed into northern Laos, with others settling in Vietnam and Thailand.
zh: 瑶族最大的支系自称优勉，是中国南方的山地民族，语言属苗瑶语系的勉语支。其传说把祖源追溯到湖南洞庭湖和长沙一带，并奉传说中的盘瓠为各姓始祖。公元前200年至公元900年间，瑶人逐渐南迁到长江以南，进入湖南、广西、广东的山岭，刀耕火种、开垦高地；唐代官方文献称他们为莫徭，是免服徭役的山民。10至13世纪，瑶族通过松散的羁縻和土司制度纳入王朝统治，由世袭头人代为纳贡。1337年时，瑶人聚落最密集的地方是广西桂林周围的山地和广东北部的连州一带。明清两代不断强化控制，以流官取代头人直接征税，瑶人遂在14世纪70年代和1449年与苗人联合起事；历次失败把一批批瑶人逼进更深的大山或更南的高原，约1700年前后，第一批勉人已进入老挝北部，另有一些定居越南和泰国。

en: The Yao are a Bantu people whose traditional homeland lies between the Rovuma and Lugenda rivers, in the Niassa highlands of what is now northern Mozambique, with later settlements around the southern end of Lake Malawi. Subsistence farmers and fishermen, they turned to long-distance trade as Arab and Swahili merchants developed the southeastern coast, carrying ivory, grain and slaves to the coast in exchange for cloth, beads and firearms. Their caravans and chiefly seats made them a power in the hinterland of Kilwa and Mikindani, and around the 1830s groups of Yao began moving into the lands east of Lake Malawi. Through these coastal contacts Islam gradually reached them, mingling with older local beliefs. They speak Chiyao, a Bantu language of the Rufiji-Ruvuma group.
zh: 亚奥人是班图人的一支，传统家园在鲁伍马河与卢任达河之间，即今天莫桑比克北部的尼亚萨高地，后来也有支系在马拉维湖南端一带定居。他们务农并兼事渔捞，随着阿拉伯和斯瓦希里商人开发东南非海岸，亚奥人转而经营长途贸易，把象牙、粮食和奴隶运往海边，换回布匹、珠饰和火器。商队和酋长领地使他们成为基尔瓦、米金达尼腹地的一股势力；到19世纪30年代，成批亚奥人开始迁入马拉维湖以东地区。也是通过与沿海的往来，伊斯兰教逐渐传入，与当地旧有信仰交融。亚奥人操齐亚奥语，属班图语系的鲁菲吉—鲁武马语支。

en: The Yapese are the people of the Yap Main Islands, four closely set high islands inside a single reef in the western Caroline Islands, and speak Yapese, an Oceanic language that forms its own branch apart from the other Micronesian languages. Settled roughly two thousand years ago by Oceanic-speaking voyagers from Melanesia, Yap developed one of the Pacific's most stratified societies, with at least seven ranked castes, villages whose rank rose or fell through warfare and tribute, men's houses and councils of elders. Yapese sailors navigated outrigger canoes by stars and swells without a compass, and the island built a pre-colonial dominion over surrounding atolls such as Ulithi and Woleai. Yap is famed for its stone money, giant calcite disks quarried chiefly in Palau and rafted home at great risk, whose worth lay in their size and in the story of their transport. Álvaro de Saavedra first sighted Yap in 1528, and Ruy López de Villalobos charted it in 1543, noting islanders hailing his ships with a Spanish-like greeting; Spain later counted Yap among its Philippine islands but never ruled it, so in 1837 its ranked villages still governed themselves.
zh: 雅浦人是西加罗林群岛雅浦主岛的居民，主岛由同一座珊瑚礁环抱的四个紧邻火山岛组成；他们使用的雅浦语属大洋洲语，却独立于其他密克罗尼西亚语言之外、自成一支。约两千年前，来自美拉尼西亚、讲大洋洲语的航海者定居于此，发展出太平洋地区等级最森严的社会之一：至少七层种姓式等级，村落的名次随战争胜负和纳贡关系升降，另有男子会馆和长老议事会。雅浦水手不靠罗盘，仅凭星象和涌浪驾驶舷外浮杆独木舟远航，并在殖民时代到来前建立了对乌利西、沃莱艾等周边环礁的宗主权。雅浦尤以石币闻名：那种巨大的方解石圆盘主要产自帕劳，人们冒极大风险用木筏运回家，价值取决于石盘大小和运输经历。1528年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉最早望见雅浦，1543年鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·比利亚洛沃斯将其绘入海图，还记下岛民以类似西班牙语的问候招呼船队；西班牙后来把雅浦算作菲律宾辖下岛屿，却从未实际统治，因此1837年时这些等级分明的村落仍自行治理。

en: The Yapahruka, whose name means Root Eaters and was later recorded by the Spanish as the Yamparika, were a Shoshone-speaking people of the Wyoming mountains and the northernmost of the kinship divisions that became the Comanche. In the fourteenth century they were still foot-borne hunter-gatherers moving in small camps, part of the Shoshonean expansion that carried Numic speakers out of the Great Basin; by 1500 some groups had crossed the Rocky Mountains to hunt bison on the Great Plains. After the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 made Spanish horses available, they took to mounted life and drifted south through Colorado, and Spaniards in New Mexico knew the Yamparika by the 1750s, when they generally lived north of the Arkansas River. Around 1790 pressure from the Cheyenne and Arapaho pushed some bands into the North Canadian River valley, where Ten Bears, orphaned by a Lakota raid and later their principal chief, grew up. In 1820 he was a key figure in making peace between the Comanche and the Ute. Through the 1830s the southward push of the Cheyenne and Arapaho finally broke the Yamparika's old ties with the Shoshone of Wyoming, leaving them a fully southern-plains people.
zh: 亚帕赫鲁卡人名字意为食根者，后来被西班牙人记作扬帕里卡人。他们原是怀俄明山区讲肖肖尼语的族群，也是后来科曼奇人各亲缘分支中位置最北的一支。14世纪时他们仍是徒步的狩猎采集者，以小型营地游走，属于努姆克语人群自大盆地向外扩散的肖肖尼扩张的一部分；到1500年，已有群体越过落基山脉到大平原猎捕野牛。1680年普韦布洛起义后西班牙马群流入，他们转为骑马生活，沿科罗拉多南下，新墨西哥的西班牙人在1750年代已知道这支人，当时他们多住在阿肯色河以北。约1790年，在夏延人和阿拉帕霍人的压力下，部分营地迁到北加拿大河谷，后来的大首领十熊幼年在拉科塔人的袭击中失去家人，就在这里长大。1820年，他在科曼奇人与犹他人的议和中扮演了关键角色。到1830年代，夏延人和阿拉帕霍人持续南压，最终切断了亚帕赫鲁卡人与怀俄明肖肖尼人的旧有联系，使他们成为完全的南部平原族群。

en: Yapen denotes the peoples of Yapen, a large mountainous island in Cenderawasih Bay off northern New Guinea, among them the Serui and Ansus communities of the coast; the island is unusually mixed in language, home both to Austronesian Yapen languages and to the Papuan Yawa tongues of its central districts. The Spanish navigator Álvaro de Saavedra made the first recorded European landing there in 1528 while sailing back from Tidore.
zh: 亚彭指亚彭岛上的诸族群，该岛是新几内亚岛北岸极乐鸟湾中的多山大岛，沿海居民包括塞鲁伊人、安苏斯人等社群；岛上语言格局格外混杂，既通行南岛语系的亚彭诸语言，中部地区又使用巴布亚语系的亚瓦诸语言。1528年，西班牙航海家阿尔瓦罗·德·萨韦德拉从蒂多雷返航途中首次有记载地登上该岛。

en: The Yaqay, also spelled Yakhai or Jaqai and known to neighbouring peoples as the Yaghai, are a Papuan people of the south coast of Mappi Regency in South Papua, Indonesia, settled along the Obaa River. Their Yaqay language, with Oba-Miwamon among its dialects, forms the Yaqay branch of the Marind-Yaqai family within the Anim languages of Trans-New Guinea.
zh: 雅凯人又拼作亚凯或贾凯，邻族称其为雅盖人，是印度尼西亚南巴布亚省马皮摄政区南海岸的巴布亚族群，沿奥巴河而居。他们的雅凯语（含奥巴-米瓦蒙等方言）构成跨新几内亚语系阿尼姆语族马林德-雅凯语系中的雅凯分支。

en: The Yaqui, who call themselves Yoeme, are the agricultural people of the lower Yaqui River valley in Sonora, where some thirty thousand of them lived in eighty villages at Spanish contact. Their first meeting with Spaniards came in 1533, when Diego de Guzman's expedition was met by warriors whose old chief drew a line in the dirt and ordered them not to cross; forty years of fighting followed, and Francisco de Ibarra failed to plant a settlement in 1565. In 1608 the Yaqui and their Mayo allies beat the Spanish in two battles, and after the peace of 1610 they themselves invited the Jesuits in 1617. For 120 years the missions kept settlers at arm's length: the Yaqui took wheat, cattle and horses and accepted Christianity while keeping their lands and unity. Encroachment by miners in the 1730s sparked the bloody Yaqui and Mayo revolt of 1740, in which six thousand people died, and the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 handed the ruined missions to Franciscans the Yaqui never trusted. After Mexican independence the leader Juan Banderas tried to unite the Yaqui, Mayo, Opata and Pima in an autonomous state, rising in 1825 until his capture and execution in 1833.
zh: 亚基人自称约梅人，是索诺拉亚基河下游的农耕民族；西班牙人接触到时，约有三万人住在八十个村庄里。他们与西班牙人的第一次照面是在1533年，迭戈·德·古斯曼的远征队遇到一队战士，年迈的首领在地上划了一条线，命令对方不得越过；此后四十年战事不断，弗朗西斯科·伊瓦拉1565年建立定居点的尝试也告失败。1608年，亚基人与马约盟友在两场战役中击败西班牙人；1610年议和后，他们又于1617年主动请来耶稣会士。此后120年间，传教站把移民挡在远处：亚基人接受小麦、牛、马和基督教，同时保住了土地与族群团结。18世纪30年代矿主的侵入引发1740年亚基—马约血腥起义，六千人丧生；1767年耶稣会被驱逐，破败的传教站转给亚基人始终不信任的方济各会。墨西哥独立后，首领胡安·班德拉斯试图联合亚基、马约、奥帕塔和皮马诸族建立自治政权，于1825年起兵，最终兵败被俘，1833年被处决。

en: The Yareba are a Papuan people of the Musa River country in the Bird's Tail of New Guinea. Their speech, also called Middle Musa, belongs to the small Yareban or Musa River family of Trans–New Guinea languages, whose members also include Moikodi and Aneme Wake.
zh: 亚雷巴人是新几内亚“鸟尾”穆萨河流域的巴布亚族群。他们的语言又称中穆萨语，属跨新几内亚语系下小小的亚雷班语族（又称穆萨河语族），同语族还包括莫伊科迪语和阿内姆韦克语。

en: The Yariguí were a Cariban-speaking people of the humid forests of the middle Magdalena valley, in what is now western Santander in Colombia, their lands running from the Minero River in the south to the Sogamoso in the north and from the Magdalena itself to the slopes of the Cordillera Oriental. Nomadic hunters and gatherers rather than settled farmers, they were split into several independent clans, among them the Arayas, Opones, Carares and Suamacaes, each led by its own cacique. At the Spanish arrival in 1536 they may have numbered some 50,000, and they met the invaders at once with war clubs, arrows, poisoned darts and ambushes; friar Pedro Simón records how they harried Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada's expedition until barely 169 of its 900 men remained. By 1570 four chiefs, Beto, Caciquillo, Martinillo and Suamacá, were leading attacks on the boats that carried settlers and goods to Vélez and Santa Fe de Bogotá along the Magdalena, Sogamoso, Carare and Opón rivers. The most celebrated leader was Pipatón, captured by the Spaniards in 1601 and maimed by having his heels cut, who escaped to fight on before surrendering late in life and dying in a Bogotá convent after 1612; his wife Yarima also led resistance. Low birth rates, growing colonial settlement and imported diseases such as smallpox and measles cut the population sharply during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, though the clans kept their forest independence long after the surrounding lands had been pacified.
zh: 亚里吉人是说加勒比语的族群，生活在马格达莱纳河中游潮湿的密林地带，即今哥伦比亚桑坦德省西部；他们的领地南起米内罗河，北至索加莫索河，西抵马格达莱纳河，东达东科迪勒拉山脉山麓。亚里吉人不定居务农，而是游猎采集的部族，分成阿拉亚、奥蓬、卡拉雷、苏阿马卡等若干个互不统属的氏族，各由一名酋长统领。1536年西班牙人初到时，他们约有五万人，随即以木棒、弓箭、毒镖和伏击迎战入侵者；修士佩德罗·西蒙记载，他们一路袭扰贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达的远征队，使其九百人最后只剩一百六十九人。到1570年，贝托、卡西基略、马蒂尼略和苏阿马卡四位酋长率众专门袭击航行在马格达莱纳河、索加莫索河、卡拉雷河和奥蓬河上、向贝莱斯和圣菲波哥大运送移民与货物的船只。最著名的首领是皮帕通：他于1601年被俘并被挑断脚跟，却逃脱后继续领导抵抗，晚年才向殖民当局投降，1612年之后死于波哥大的一座修道院；他的妻子亚里马也曾率众抗敌。由于出生率低下、殖民点不断扩张，加上天花、麻疹等欧洲传入的疫病，亚里吉人口在17、18世纪急剧减少，但周围地区被平定之后很久，这些氏族仍保持着林中的独立。

en: The Yaro, also remembered as the Yarowilcas, were a pre-Inca people of the high Andes of central Peru, formed from the highland communities that broke away when the Wari Empire collapsed around the eleventh century. Their small nation dominated the cold Bombon plateau around Lake Chinchaycocha, in what is now the Pasco region, and Yaro remains have been dated to as early as the ninth century. Around 1200 they built the citadel of Gonicutac, a three-storey complex of stone and mud with residential, agricultural and religious quarters, and from the thirteenth century their territory reached north into the Huallanca district and the lands later called Yarowilca, near Huanuco. Rather than being conquered outright, the Yaro entered the Inca Empire as a confederated nation, keeping their own lords under Cuzco's overlordship.
zh: 亚罗人又称亚罗维尔卡人，是秘鲁中部安第斯高原的前印加居民，源自11世纪前后瓦里帝国崩溃时脱离出去的高原村社。他们的小邦统治着今帕斯科一带钦查伊科查湖畔寒冷的邦邦高原，亚罗人的遗存最早可追溯到9世纪。约1200年，他们修建了戈尼库塔克堡垒城寨，这是一座石泥砌筑的三层建筑群，兼有居住、农事和祭祀功能；13世纪起，其领土向北扩展到瓦良卡地区以及瓦努科附近后来被称为亚罗维尔卡的地方。亚罗人并非被直接征服，而是以结盟邦国的身份加入印加帝国，在库斯科的宗主权下保留了自己的首领。

en: The Yaros were an Indigenous people of the lower Uruguay River, living on both banks in what became the Argentine province of Entre Ríos and the Uruguayan departments of Río Negro and Durazno. When the Spanish arrived they held the western bank, until the Charrúa pushed them south between the Negro and San Salvador rivers. They were short and thick-limbed, unlike the tall Patagonian-type Charrúa, and lived without agriculture, pottery or the bow: they fished, hunted deer, peccary and rhea, and above all gathered honey, pine nuts and carob pods, brewing a drink from pine seeds. Their only shelters were woven windbreaks set against the weather. The Yaros fought alongside the Charrúa against the Spaniards — chronicles as early as 1612 record them, under the name Chayos, killing Captain Juan Ramón, an explorer sent up the Uruguay by Sebastián Cabot. Jesuits tried to settle them at the Yapeyú reduction from 1627 and founded San Andrés de Yaros in 1657, but its people walked away within a year, preferring nomadic life. Between the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries the Yaros were broken and absorbed by the Charrúa.
zh: 亚鲁斯人是乌拉圭河下游的原住民，生活在河流两岸，即后来的阿根廷恩特雷里奥斯省以及乌拉圭的内格罗河省和杜拉斯诺省一带。西班牙人到来时，他们占据西岸，后来被查鲁亚人向南挤到内格罗河与圣萨尔瓦多河之间。他们身材矮小、四肢粗壮，与巴塔哥尼亚型的高个查鲁亚人不同；他们不事农耕，也没有陶器和弓箭，以捕鱼、猎取鹿、西貒和美洲鸵为生，尤其重视采集蜂蜜、松子和角豆荚，还用松籽酿酒。他们唯一的栖身设施是挡风的编织防风障。亚鲁斯人曾与查鲁亚人并肩对抗西班牙人——早在1612年的编年史就记载，他们被称作查约人，杀死了塞瓦斯蒂安·卡伯特派往乌拉圭河探险的胡安·拉蒙船长。耶稣会从1627年起试图把他们安置在亚佩尤传教区，又于1657年建立圣安德烈斯-德亚罗斯，但居民不出一年便离去，宁愿继续游牧生活。17世纪末至18世纪初，亚鲁斯人被查鲁亚人击溃并吸收。

en: The Yat Tindé are the Plains Apache, also called the Kiowa Apache, a small Southern Athabaskan people of the Great Plains whose other names for themselves include Ná'ishą and γát dìndé, the cedar people. Their oral tradition says they split from the Tsuut'ina, another Athabaskan group of the Canadian prairies, and they had taken to plains life by the sixteenth century, moving south until the Lakota allowed them land south of the Black Hills in what is now South Dakota and Wyoming. Archaeologists connect their early villages with the Dismal River culture of the western plains. In the early eighteenth century they lived near the upper Missouri in a permanent alliance with the Kiowa, whose language was entirely unlike their own, so the two peoples conversed in Plains Indian Sign Language; they also allied at times with the Pawnee and Arapaho. Never numerous, their whole population was estimated at only about four hundred in 1780. Around 1800 they followed the Kiowa south onto the Southern Plains, hunting bison along the eastern face of the Rocky Mountains.
zh: 亚特廷德人即平原阿帕奇人，又称基奥瓦阿帕奇人，是大平原上一支人数不多的南阿萨巴斯卡族群；他们的自称还有 Ná'ishą 和 γát dìndé，后者意为“雪松之人”。据其口传历史，他们从加拿大草原上另一支阿萨巴斯卡群体楚蒂纳人中分离出来，16世纪时已适应平原生活，随后不断南移，直到拉科塔人允许他们在今南达科他州和怀俄明州境内的黑山以南地带居住。考古学家把他们的早期村落与西部平原的迪斯默尔河文化联系在一起。18世纪初，他们生活在密苏里河上游附近，与语言完全不同的基奥瓦人结成永久同盟，双方靠平原印第安手语交谈；他们有时也与波尼人和阿拉帕霍人结盟。平原阿帕奇人人数一直不多，1780年总人口估计仅有约四百人。1800年前后，他们随基奥瓦人南迁进入南部平原，沿落基山脉东麓猎捕野牛。

en: The Yaur, also recorded as Jaur, are an Austronesian-speaking people of the eastern shore of Cenderawasih Bay, in the country that is now Nabire Regency of Central Papua. Their language belongs to the Cenderawasih Bay branch of Austronesian and, together with Iresim, descends from the reconstructed Proto-Yaur-Yerisiam, while Umar is a more distant relative within the same branch.
zh: 尧尔人（又记作扎乌尔人）是极乐鸟湾东岸的南岛语族族群，地在今中巴布亚省纳比雷县一带。其语言属南岛语系极乐鸟湾语支，与伊雷辛语同由拟构的原始尧尔-耶雷辛语分化，与同语支的乌马尔语关系则更远。

en: The Yavapai are the Upland Yuman people of west-central Arizona, whose bands once ranged over some ten million acres from the San Francisco Peaks and the Colorado River to the edge of the Gila and Salt river valleys. Archaeologists trace them to Patayan groups who moved east from the Colorado River and emerged as a distinct people around 1300; their name, given by the Mojave, means people of the sun. They lived in four roaming bands, the Tolkepaya, Yavepe, Wipukepa and Kewevkepaya, gathering wild foods and raiding in shifting alliances, often with the Western Apache against the Akimel O'odham and Maricopa. Hopi guides led the Spanish explorer Antonio de Espejo to their copper-bearing mountains in 1583, and Juan de Onate crossed their lands in 1598 and again in 1604. Smallpox carried off perhaps a quarter of them in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and the Franciscan Francisco Garces lived among them in 1776, by which time horses, metal tools and cattle raiding had reshaped their old way of life.
zh: 亚瓦派人是亚利桑那中西部的高地尤曼语族群，诸游群曾活动在约一千万英亩的土地上，北起圣弗朗西斯科峰、西抵科罗拉多河，南达希拉河与盐河谷边缘。考古学家认为他们源自从科罗拉多河向东迁徙的帕塔扬人，约1300年发展为独立民族；亚瓦派这个名字由莫哈维人所起，意为太阳之人。他们分为托尔克帕亚、亚韦佩、维普克帕和克韦夫克帕亚四个游荡游群，以采集野生食物为生，并在变幻的结盟中外出袭掠，常与西阿帕奇人联手对付阿基梅尔·奥奥德姆人和马里科帕人。1583年，霍皮向导带领西班牙探险家安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍来到他们产铜的山地；胡安·德·奥尼亚特则于1598年及1604年两度穿过其土地。17至18世纪，天花可能夺去四分之一人口，方济各会士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯于1776年在他们中间生活，那时马匹、金属工具和盗牛活动已重塑了他们的旧日生活。

en: The Yawyu were the highland people of the upper Cañete valley, in the mountains southeast of Lima, whose early culture grew from a fusion of Kauki and Aymara roots and whose language belonged to the Aymaran family. In the era of regional kingdoms they formed a confederation of tribes led by four towns, Ñaupahuasi, Ampahuasi, Vichuca and Kariachi, known together as Hatun Yauyos, with their paramount lord residing at Ñaupahuasi; the whole group was split into an upper half, Hanan Yauyos, and a lower half, Hurin Yauyos, the latter covering what is now Huarochirí. Around 1450 the prince Túpac Yupanqui, son of the Inca Pachacuti, brought them into the Inca Empire through an alliance rather than a destructive war, and Yawyu auxiliaries afterward marched with the Incas against the Chimú and the coastal kingdom of Huarco, while Yawyu mitimaes were resettled among the Huanca. When Francisco Pizarro asked for their submission in 1534 they refused, so Hernando de Soto and Diego de Agüero routed their army with cavalry, and the Yawyu later joined Manco Inca's great siege of Lima before being broken into Spanish repartimientos and, from 1571, gathered into Indian reductions such as Santo Domingo de Yauyos.
zh: 亚维尤人是利马东南山区、卡涅特河上游谷地的高原族群，其早期文化由考基与艾马拉两种传统融合而成，语言属于艾马拉语族。在区域性王国林立的时代，他们组成部落联盟，由尼亚瓦帕瓦西、安帕瓦西、比丘卡和卡里亚奇四座城镇为首，合称大亚维尤，最高首领驻于尼亚瓦帕瓦西；整个群体又分为上亚维尤与下亚维尤两半，后者大致相当于今天的瓦罗奇里。约1450年，印加王帕查库特克之子图帕克·尤潘基以结盟而非毁灭战争的方式将他们并入印加帝国，此后亚维尤援军随印加人出征奇穆和沿海的瓦尔科王国，部分亚维尤移民也被安置到万卡人的土地上。1534年皮萨罗要求他们归顺遭到拒绝，遂派埃尔南多·德·索托和迭戈·德·阿圭罗率骑兵击溃其军队；亚维尤人后来又参加了曼科·印加围攻利马的大战，最终被划入西班牙人的委托监护区，并从1571年起被集中迁入圣多明各-德亚维尤等印第安人归化镇。

en: The Yazoo were a small tribe of the lower Yazoo River in the Mississippi Delta, kinsmen and neighbours of the Tunica, Koroa and Tiou, whose now lost language is thought to have belonged with Tunica, a language isolate. French missionaries reached them at the end of the seventeenth century, but like the Chickasaw they leaned toward the English traders from Carolina, and in 1702 they helped the Koroa kill the French priest Nicholas Foucault and his three companions. A French fort and a Jesuit mission under Jean Rouel followed in 1718 and 1722. In 1729 the Yazoo and Koroa joined the Natchez revolt, killing Rouel and overwhelming the nearby French garrison after the Natchez destroyed Fort Rosalie. The French and their Choctaw allies crushed the rising: Yazoo survivors were sold into slavery on Caribbean plantations or captured and traded away by the Chickasaw, and the tribe disappeared as a separate people, its remnants merging with the Chickasaw and others.
zh: 亚祖人是密西西比三角洲亚祖河下游的小部落，与图尼卡人、科罗阿人和提乌人同族相邻；他们已经失传的语言被认为与孤立语言图尼卡语同属一类。法国传教士在17世纪末来到他们中间，但亚祖人和奇克索人一样倾向于来自卡罗来纳的英国商人，并于1702年协助科罗阿人杀死法国神父尼古拉斯·富科及其三名同伴。法国随后在1718年和1722年分别建起堡垒和让·鲁埃尔主持的耶稣会传教站。1729年，亚祖人与科罗阿人加入纳奇兹起义：纳奇兹人摧毁罗莎莉堡后，他们杀死鲁埃尔并歼灭了附近的法国驻军。法国人与乔克托盟友镇压了起义，幸存的亚祖人被卖到加勒比种植园为奴，或被奇克索人掳走转卖，这个部落就此不复为独立族群，残余者融入奇克索人等民族之中。

en: The Ychsma, more often called Ichma, were the people of the kingdom of Pachacamac on the central Peruvian coast. Their polity arose around 1100 from the ruins of the Wari Empire, covering the Lurin and Rimac valleys south and east of present-day Lima, while the Chancay dominated the coast to the north. In a desert land they extended the irrigation canal network first built by the Lima culture, watering broad orchards and fields; the lower Rimac valley alone may have held more than 150,000 people. At Pachacamac they raised at least sixteen truncated adobe pyramids with great access ramps, and other walled sanctuaries such as Mateo Salado, Huaca Huantille and Maranga studded the Lima plain. Their name, recorded as ychma in the earliest Quechua dictionaries, meant the vermilion colour made from cinnabar. Around 1470 the armies of Tupac Yupanqui, acting for his father Pachacutec, annexed the kingdom; local lords kept their rank after swearing obedience, and the Incas enlarged Pachacamac itself with a temple of the Sun and a house of chosen women.
zh: 伊奇斯马人常称伊奇马人，是秘鲁中部沿海帕查卡马克王国的居民。他们的政权约在1100年瓦里帝国崩溃后的废墟上兴起，领有利马城东南的卢林河谷与里马克河谷，而沿海北面则是钱凯人的天下。在这片荒漠土地上，他们扩建了利马文化最早开凿的灌溉渠网，滋养出大片果园和田地；仅里马克河下游就可能居住着十五万人以上。他们在帕查卡马克修建了至少十六座带巨大坡道的截顶土坯金字塔，马特奥萨拉多、万蒂列瓦卡、马兰卡等围墙圣所也星罗棋布于利马平原。他们的名字在最早的克丘亚词典中写作 ychma，意为用朱砂制成的朱红色。约1470年，图帕克·尤潘基奉其父帕查库特克之命率军吞并了这个王国；地方首领宣誓效忠后保留了地位，印加人还在帕查卡马克增建太阳神庙和选女之宫，扩大了这座圣城。

en: The Yei are a Marind sub-tribe of the lowlands along the upper Maro River near the Papua New Guinea border, in South Papua. Originating in the Fly River country, they speak a Yam, or Morehead–Maro, language closer to Papua New Guinean tongues than to Marind, and live by fishing, hunting and sago gathering in Upper and Lower Yei villages.
zh: 耶伊人是马林德人的一支，住在南巴布亚省马罗河上游、邻近巴布亚新几内亚边界的低地。他们发源于东部的弗莱河流域，所说的耶伊语属亚姆语系，又称莫尔黑德-马罗语系，与巴布亚新几内亚诸语言的关系比马林德语更近；他们分上耶伊、下耶伊两组村落，以渔捞、狩猎和采集西谷椰为生。

en: The Yela are the people of Rossel Island, a rugged, mountainous island ringed by mangroves and coral reefs and the easternmost of the Louisiade Archipelago off the eastern tip of New Guinea. Their language, Yélî Dnye, is one of the most distinctive in the region: linguists treat it as an unclassified language isolate, its resemblance to nearby Oceanic languages explained by long contact rather than common descent, and it is famous for a large inventory of doubly articulated consonants and a special women's speech in which words connected with the sea are avoided. The islanders occupy small villages along the coast and fertile valleys between the forested ridges, keeping largely to themselves behind the dangerous reefs. Europeans first sighted the island in 1606, when the Spanish expedition of Luís Vaez de Torres charted it together with Tagula as the Land of Saint Bonaventure; it received its present name from the French d'Entrecasteaux expedition of the 1790s, which named it after the officer Élisabeth-Paul-Édouard de Rossel.
zh: 耶拉人是罗塞尔岛的居民，该岛崎岖多山，四周环绕红树林与珊瑚礁，是新几内亚东端外海路易西亚德群岛最东端的岛屿。他们的语言耶利多涅语是这一地区最独特的语言之一：语言学家将其视为系属未定的孤立语言，它与邻近大洋洲语言的相似之处被归因于长期接触而非同源；该语言还以大量双重调音辅音，以及女性避讳与海有关词语的特殊女性用语而闻名。岛民在沿海和林脊间肥沃谷地的小村落中生活，凭借危险的礁障与外界保持相当的距离。欧洲人首次见到此岛是在1606年，路易斯·巴埃斯·德·托雷斯率领的西班牙探险队把它与塔古拉岛一并绘入地图，称作圣波拿文都拉之地；今名则来自18世纪90年代法国当特尔卡斯托探险队，他们以随队军官伊丽莎白-保罗-爱德华·德·罗塞尔之名为岛命名。

en: The Yelmek are a Papuan people of the lowlands west of Merauke in South Papua, settled in villages between the Digul and Mbian rivers, among them Wanam and Bibikem. Their language, also called Jelmek or Yabega, belongs with nearby Maklew to the proposed Trans-Fly–Bulaka River family, and its Wanam variety may be a distinct language.
zh: 耶尔梅克人是南巴布亚马老奇以西低地的巴布亚族群，聚居于迪古尔河与姆比安河之间的瓦南、比比肯等村落。他们的语言又称耶尔米克或雅贝加，与邻近的马莱乌语同属拟议中的跨弗莱-布拉卡河语系，其中瓦南方言可能本身就是一门独立语言。

en: Yemenis are the Arab people of south-western Arabia, concentrated in the highland cities of Sanaa and Taiz and in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden ports of Zabid, Mocha and Aden. They speak Yemeni Arabic, while the South Arabian languages Mehri and Soqotri survive in the far east and on Socotra, and society is built around powerful tribes; the northern highlands follow the Zaydi branch of Shia Islam and the lowlands the Sunni Shafi'i school. Yemen was the land of the Sabaean and Himyarite kingdoms and accepted Islam in the seventh century. The Zaidi imamate was founded at Saada in 897, while the Sunni Rasulid sultans ruled from Zabid and Taiz between 1229 and 1454, growing rich on the Red Sea trade through Aden; in 1337 Sultan al-Mujahid Ali held the lowlands while the Zaydis kept the northern mountains, having retaken Sanaa in 1324. The Tahirids succeeded the Rasulids in 1454 until the Mamluk conquest of 1517 and then the Ottomans, and Ottoman armies stormed Aden in 1538 and made Zabid the seat of Yemen Eyalet. The Qasimid imams expelled the Ottomans by 1636, after which Mocha became the great coffee emporium of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, with English, Dutch and French factories crowded along its waterfront. In the later eighteenth century the imamate fragmented into rival principalities such as Lahej, and Mocha's coffee trade drifted to newer ports.
zh: 也门人是阿拉伯半岛西南部的阿拉伯人，聚居在高原城市萨那、塔伊兹以及红海和亚丁湾沿岸的扎比德、摩卡、亚丁等港口。他们讲也门阿拉伯语，而南阿拉伯语支的马赫里语和索科特拉语仍在东部边陲和索科特拉岛通行；社会以势力强大的部落为骨架，北部高原信奉伊斯兰教什叶派的栽德派，低地则信奉逊尼派的沙斐仪派。也门曾是赛伯伊王国和希木叶尔王国的故土，7世纪皈依伊斯兰教。栽德派伊玛目政权于897年在萨达建立；1229年至1454年间，逊尼派的拉苏勒王朝苏丹以扎比德和塔伊兹为都，靠亚丁港的红海贸易致富。1337年在位的是穆贾希德·阿里苏丹，他控制低地，栽德派则保有北部山区，并已于1324年夺回萨那。1454年塔希尔王朝取而代之，1517年后又历经马穆鲁克和奥斯曼的征服；奥斯曼军队于1538年攻占亚丁，把扎比德设为也门省的治所。卡西姆王朝的伊玛目们到1636年将奥斯曼人全部逐出，此后摩卡成为17至18世纪最大的咖啡贸易港，港内挤满了英国、荷兰和法国的商馆。18世纪后期，伊玛目政权分裂为拉赫季等相互争战的小邦，摩卡的咖啡生意也逐渐转向新兴港口。

en: Yerle Qalıq, meaning the older inhabitants, is the self-name of the indigenous Siberian Tatars, used to set themselves apart from later Volga Tatar settlers. They are the native Turkic population of the forests and steppes between the Urals and the Yenisei, formed from Samoyedic, Ugric and Ket hunters who were Turkified by incoming Kipchaks from the eleventh century and later absorbed Mongol-era Tatar clans; their three main groups are the Tobol-Irtysh, Baraba and Tom Tatars. From 1242 the country belonged to the Golden Horde, and on its breakup the Taibugid khans founded the Khanate of Sibir, ruling first from Chimgi-Tura and then from Qashliq, also called Sibir, on the Irtysh. After the Shaybanid Kuchum seized the throne in 1563 and tried to enforce Islam, his raids on Russian trading posts drew the Cossack Yermak into Siberia: Kuchum was beaten at the Battle of Chuvash Cape in 1582 and finally routed on the Ob in 1598, opening the Russian conquest of Siberia. The Yerle Qalıq then became yasak-paying subjects of the tsar, living by hunting, horse breeding and river porterage; Sunni Islam of the Hanafi school, adopted from the fourteenth century and general by the late eighteenth, sat alongside surviving shamanic customs.
zh: “叶尔喀勒”意为老住户，是土著西伯利亚鞑靼人的自称，用以区别于后来迁入的伏尔加鞑靼移民。他们是乌拉尔山与叶尼塞河之间森林和草原上的本土突厥语居民，由萨莫耶德、乌戈尔和克特系猎人在11世纪起被迁入的钦察人突厥化、后来又吸收蒙古时代的鞑靼氏族而形成，主要分为托博尔-额尔齐斯、巴拉巴和托木三支。1242年起该地归属金帐汗国；金帐汗国瓦解后，泰布吉德系汗王建立失必儿汗国，先以奇姆吉-图拉为都，后迁到额尔齐斯河畔的卡什雷克（又名失必儿）。1563年昔班尼系的库楚姆夺位并强力推行伊斯兰教，他袭击俄国商站，招致哥萨克首领叶尔马克进军西伯利亚：1582年库楚姆在楚瓦什角之战中战败，1598年在鄂毕河畔被彻底击溃，俄国征服西伯利亚的序幕由此拉开。此后叶尔喀勒人成为向沙皇缴纳“亚萨克”毛皮税的属民，以狩猎、养马和河运搬驮为生；他们从14世纪起皈依、到18世纪末普遍信奉逊尼派伊斯兰教的哈乃斐学派，同时仍保留着萨满遗俗。

en: The Yi, who call themselves Nuosu (other branches say Nisu or Lolo), are a Tibeto-Burman people of the mountains of Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou and Guangxi, speaking Loloish languages close to Burmese and keeping their own syllabic script, long used by bimo priests for ritual texts. Their ancestors were the Wuman of eastern Yunnan, who supplied the warrior caste of the Nanzhao kingdom of 738–902 and later lived under the Bai-ruled Dali kingdom until the Mongol conquest of the thirteenth century. Under the Yuan they were governed through native chieftainships, while Yi clans already ruled their own states, among them Mu'ege in Guizhou, which ruled until 1279 and then survived as the Shuixi chiefdom until 1698. In 1337 the Yi of southern Sichuan held the Jianchang and Huili valleys in the country now called Liangshan, where Black Yi aristocrats ruled commoners and captives in a rigid caste order that kept imperial officials at bay for centuries. Ming reforms replaced hereditary chieftains with appointed officials, and the She-An Rebellion of 1621–1629 briefly set up a breakaway kingdom before it was crushed. Under the Qing, Ortai's campaigns of the 1720s broke the remaining chiefdoms and pressed assimilation on the Yi near Kunming; the Liangshan heartland, however, was never fully subdued and kept its old clan order long after the rest of the southwest had come under direct rule.
zh: 彝族自称诺苏，另有尼苏、罗罗等支系称呼，是分布在云南、四川、贵州、广西山区的藏缅语民族，语言属与缅甸语相近的彝语支，并拥有本民族的音节文字，长期由毕摩祭司用来传写经文。他们的先民是滇东的乌蛮，曾构成738至902年南诏国的武士阶层，南诏灭亡后又臣属于白族段氏建立的大理国，直到13世纪蒙古征服云南。元朝通过罗罗宣慰司等土司机构治理彝区，而彝族各支早已建立自己的政权，其中慕俄格国统治贵州山地至1279年，其后身水西土司一直延续到1698年。1337年时，四川南部的彝人据有建昌、会理一带的河谷，即后来的凉山地区；黑彝贵族在严格的等级制度下统治平民和掠来的奴仆，数百年间把王朝官吏拒之山外。明代大力推行改土归流，1621至1629年的奢安之乱中，彝部首领曾建立短暂的割据政权，终被镇压。清代雍正年间鄂尔泰用兵西南，摧毁残余土司，并强迫昆明附近的彝人放弃火葬、改行土葬；但凉山腹地始终未被真正征服，在西南其他地区都已纳入流官治理之后，仍长期保留着古老的家支制度。

en: The Yidinjdjin, or Yidiny, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the lowland rainforests around Cairns in Far North Queensland, whose tribal lands of about four hundred square miles ran from Deeral north to the Barron River, inland to Mount Hypipamee and east to the crest of the Prior Range. To their north lay the coastal Djabugay, while to the south their borders met the Ngajanji and the Mamu. They were divided into clans, including the Gimuy, custodians of the Cairns area, the Walubara, the Maiara, the Maimbi and the Djumbandji, and spoke the Yidiny language, a Pama-Nyungan tongue of the Yidinic branch closely akin to Djabugay.
zh: 伊丁吉人又称伊迪尼人，是昆士兰远北地区凯恩斯一带低地雨林的澳大利亚原住民，部落领地约四百平方英里，从迪拉尔向北延伸到巴伦河，内陆至希皮帕米山，东抵普赖尔岭的山脊；北邻沿海的贾布盖人，南与恩甘詹吉人和马穆人接壤。他们分成若干氏族，包括守护凯恩斯一带的吉穆伊人、瓦卢巴拉人、马亚拉人、马因比人和琼班吉人，所说的伊迪尼语是帕马-牛雅语系伊迪尼语支的语言，与贾布盖语十分接近。

en: The Yiiji, also spelt Yeidji, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Kimberley region of Western Australia, closely bound up with the people commonly called Gwini or Kwini; the labels overlap so thoroughly that the groups around the Forrest River are often treated as one Forrest River people, which also includes the Miwa. Their speech, also called Yiiji, is a dialect of Wunambal within the Worrorran family. Their territory covered about 2,600 square kilometres between Cambridge Gulf and the Milligan ranges, bordered by the Wilawila to the west and the Wirngir to the east. From the eighteenth century they were drawn into the Makassan trepang trade: Makassan visitors, whose landfalls on the Kimberley coast began between 1669 and 1763, exchanged dugout canoes and trade goods for the sea cucumber cured on their beaches.
zh: 伊吉人（又作耶吉）是西澳大利亚州金伯利地区的澳大利亚原住民，与常称格维尼或奎尼的人群关系密不可分：两个名称的所指高度重合，以至于福里斯特河一带的群体常被视为同一个福里斯特河人群体，米瓦人也包括在内。伊吉语是武南布尔语的方言，属沃罗拉语系。其领地在剑桥湾与米利根山脉之间，约2600平方公里，西邻威拉维拉人，东接维尔恩吉尔人。从18世纪起，他们被卷入望加锡人的海参贸易：1669至1763年间开始登陆金伯利海岸的望加锡客商，用独木舟和杂货交换他们在海滩上加工好的海参。

en: The Yilba, also written Ilba or Jilba, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland whose speech was counted among the dialects of Biri, the language of the coast between Mackay and Townsville. Their recorded local groups, or hordes, included the Yukkaburra, Pegulloburra and Munkeeburra.
zh: 伊尔巴人（异写吉尔巴）是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，所说的语言被归入比里语的方言，比里语通行于麦凯与汤斯维尔之间的海岸地区。有记载的地方群包括尤卡布拉、佩古洛布拉和蒙基布拉。

en: The Yinggardan, also written Yingkarta or Inggarda, are an Aboriginal people of the Gascoyne region of Western Australia, their wedge of country lying between the Gascoyne and Wooramel Rivers and running inland from the northern edge of Shark Bay, perhaps 4,200 square miles in Norman Tindale's estimate, with the Mandi and Baiyungu to their north and the Malkanan to their south. Their Kartu language had a northern and a southern dialect and was heard along the coast from Carnarvon to the Wooramel. The Mandi called them and their neighbours the Baiyungu and Maia by the shared name Kakarakala, meaning easterners, while the Nhantan to their south held them in awe as rain-making sorcerers. They enter European records through the Dutch ship Batavia, wrecked on the Houtman Abrolhos in 1629: the survivors' journal mentions the mainland people, and two convicted mutineers marooned on the coast may have ended their lives among local groups.
zh: 英加尔达人（又拼英卡尔塔、英加尔达）是西澳大利亚加斯科因地区的原住民，楔形家园夹在加斯科因河与伍拉梅尔河之间，从鲨鱼湾北缘向内陆伸展，据诺曼·廷代尔估计约四千二百平方英里，北邻曼迪人和白云古人，南接马尔卡纳人。他们的卡尔图语分北方、南方两种方言，沿海岸从卡那封一直通行到伍拉梅尔河一带。曼迪人把他们与邻近的白云古人、马亚人统称为“卡拉卡拉”，意为“东方人”；南方的恩汉塔人则敬畏他们，把他们视作能呼风唤雨的巫师。欧洲文献首次提到他们，与荷兰商船巴达维亚号有关：该船于1629年在豪特曼阿布罗柳斯群岛失事，幸存者的航海日志提到了大陆上的居民，两名被流放海岸的叛变水手或许最终就老死在当地族群之中。

en: The Yinwumi are the Yinwum, also written Jinwum, an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, neighbours of the Yupangathi groups near the peninsula's western tip. They spoke a Paman language of the North Cape York group, noted by linguists for unusual sound changes that set it apart from its relatives.
zh: 因伍姆人又译金伍姆人，是昆士兰约克角半岛北部的澳大利亚原住民，与半岛西端附近的尤潘加提诸群体相邻。他们的语言属北约克角帕曼语群，语言学家注意到它经历过一些罕见的音变，在同语群中显得与众不同。

en: The Yir-Yoront are an Aboriginal people of the south-western Cape York Peninsula in northern Queensland, whose traditional country lay along the rivers and coastal flats facing the Gulf of Carpentaria, a landscape of sandridges that gives their name its second element, yorront. Their language belongs to the Pama-Maric group of the Pama-Nyungan family, and their society was built on patrilineal clans divided into two moieties, with each person assigned a stretch of clan land through a conception totem. Because their territory had little usable stone, even stone axes reached them only through long-distance trade networks that bound neighbouring peoples together. They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering across the seasonal wetlands. In 1623 a Dutch exploratory expedition under Jan Carstenszoon landed on their coast to trade; the logbook noted that the people knew nothing of metals or spices, and of the Dutch goods only the iron pieces failed to enter their everyday use. Otherwise the Yir-Yoront remained beyond the reach of European settlement for the rest of the period.
zh: 伊尔约朗特人是昆士兰北部约克角半岛西南部的原住民，传统家园位于注入卡奔塔利亚湾的各条河流与沿海平原一带，那里沙脊纵横，他们名称的后半部分“约朗特”便与沙地有关。他们的语言属帕马-牛雅语系的帕马-马里克语组，社会以父系氏族为基础，分为两个半偶族，每个人凭出生图腾分得氏族领地的一段。由于境内缺少可用的石材，就连石斧也要靠跨族群的长途贸易网络辗转获得。他们在随季节变化的湿地上以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生。1623年，扬·卡斯滕松率领的荷兰探险队在其海岸登陆交易，航行日志记载当地人对金属和香料一无所知，而荷兰人给出的货物里，唯有铁器没有进入他们的日常生活。除此之外，在本时期余下的时间里，伊尔约朗特人始终处于欧洲人定居势力的范围之外。

en: The Yirandhali are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Flinders River country in Queensland, around Hughenden in the Shire of Flinders. Their language is assigned to the Maric branch of the Pama–Nyungan family, their neighbours along the river included the Mbara, Gugu-Badhun and Wanamara, and the same people are recorded as the Dalleburra in the Hughenden area.
zh: 伊兰达利人是昆士兰弗林德斯河流域的澳大利亚原住民，活动在弗林德斯郡的休恩登一带。他们的语言被归入帕马-牛雅语系的马里语支，沿河的邻族包括姆巴拉人、古古-巴敦人和瓦纳马拉人；在休恩登地区，同一群人又被记作达利布拉人。

en: The Yitha Yitha, recorded by early ethnographers as Jitajita or Yitayita, are an Aboriginal people of the lower Murray and lower Lachlan river country of south-western New South Wales, lying north-west of the Nari Nari and south-east of the Barindji. Their speech, rich in monosyllabic words and consonant clusters, belongs with Kureinji and Dadi Dadi to the Lower Murray group of Pama-Nyungan, and their name is a reduplication of their word for no, jita, like the names of many Riverine tribes. Each community kept a gnalla wattow, or postman, who understood every dialect within a hundred and fifty miles and whose person was sacred even among feuding tribes; these envoys arranged barter and trade between the river peoples. Charles Sturt's whaleboat expedition of 1830, descending the Murrumbidgee and following the Murray to the sea, passed through this lower Murray world, opening the country to the overlanders and squatters who came after.
