zh: 伊塔伊塔人被早期民族学者记作吉塔吉塔或伊塔伊塔人，是新南威尔士州西南部墨累河下游与拉克伦河下游河乡的澳大利亚原住民，地处纳里纳里人西北、巴林吉人东南。他们的语言多单音节词和辅音丛，与库雷因吉语、达迪达迪语同属帕马-尼永加语系的下墨累语组；族名和许多滨河族群一样，由意为“不”的吉塔一词重叠而成。每个群落都设有一名称为格纳拉瓦托的“信使”，他通晓方圆一百五十英里内的各种方言，人身即使在敌对部落之间也被视为神圣不可侵犯，负责安排滨河诸族之间的以物易人和贸易往来。1830年，查尔斯·斯特尔特的捕鲸船探险队沿马兰比吉河而下，再顺墨累河入海，穿过了这个下墨累人群世界，也为随后而来的陆路旅行者和牧场主打开了通道。

en: The Karitiana, who call themselves Yjxa, are a Tupian people of the western Amazon in Rondônia, Brazil, occupying lands south of Porto Velho on tributaries of the Madeira. They live by farming, fishing and hunting in villages that long remained beyond European reach. Their language, Karitiâna, belongs to the Arikém branch of the Tupi family and is its only surviving member, the related Arikém and Kabixiâna tongues having since died out. The first Western contacts with them are thought to date to the 1600s, but no lasting or recorded contact followed for centuries.
zh: 卡利吉亚纳人是巴西朗多尼亚州西亚马逊地区的图皮语族群，住在韦柳港以南、马代拉河支流一带，以农耕、渔猎为生，村落长期处在欧洲人的势力范围之外。他们的卡利吉亚纳语属图皮语系的阿里肯语支，是该语支仅存的语言，近亲的阿里肯语和卡比克西亚纳语都已消亡。一般认为西方人与他们的最早接触发生在17世纪，但此后数百年间都没有留下持续往来的记录。

en: The Yoli, whom the Spanish called the Conchos after the shell-littered Río Conchos, were a cluster of seminomadic bands in northern Mexico. They held the basin of the Río Conchos in Chihuahua northward to the Río Bravo, from the Sierra Madre Occidental to the ground of present-day Ojinaga and Presidio, Texas, and were split into many named tribes, among them the Chinarra and the Chiz. Their language belonged to the Uto-Aztecan stock and was so close to Tarahumara that some scholars treat it as a dialect of the same tongue. They hunted deer and rabbits with bows, took fish with nets, gathered prickly pears, roots and berries, and also farmed, dwelling in huts of wooden frames covered with hides or grass. Franciscan missionaries entered their valleys while Jesuits worked the Tarahumara mountains. In 1684 a Concho headman testified before a Spanish court that he had led dozens of local bands, pointing to loose political ties between them, while the Chiz stood apart as allies of the Jumanos.
zh: 约利人是墨西哥北部一群半游牧部族，西班牙人因贝壳遍布的孔乔斯河而称他们为孔乔人。他们占据奇瓦瓦的孔乔斯河流域，向北直到布拉沃河，范围西起西马德雷山脉，东抵奥希纳加和得克萨斯普雷西迪奥一带，下分奇纳拉人、奇斯人等许多有名号的部落。他们的语言属犹他—阿兹特克语系，与塔拉乌马拉语极为相近，有学者认为它只是后者的一种方言。约利人用弓箭猎鹿捕兔、撒网捕鱼，采集仙人掌果、块根和浆果，也从事农耕，住在木架蒙兽皮或茅草的棚屋里。方济各会传教士进入他们的谷地传教，耶稣会则在山区向塔拉乌马拉人传教。1684年，一名孔乔首领在西班牙法庭上供述自己曾统领数十个当地部落，可见各部落之间存在松散的政治联合，唯有与舒马尼人结盟的奇斯人不在其中。

en: The Yolngu are an aggregation of Aboriginal Australian clans of north-eastern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory; their name means person in the Yolngu Matha languages, and every clan belongs to either the Dhuwa or the Yirritja moiety. Their customary law, the Maḏayin, governs land ownership, trade and ceremony through song cycles and sacred sites. They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, obtained boomerangs through trade routes reaching Central Australia, and passed messages between distant clans with message sticks carried hundreds of kilometres. From about the 1500s, Macassan trepang fishermen from Sulawesi began anchoring off their coasts each monsoon season, exchanging metal tools, cloth and tobacco for pearlshell and labour; the Yolngu word for a European, Balanda, derives from this contact through the Malay term for a Dutchman. Through the early 1800s these seasonal voyages remained their main link with the outside world, while the clans kept their lands and ceremonies intact.
zh: 雍古人是澳大利亚北领地阿纳姆地东北部若干原住民氏族的合称，在他们所说的雍古玛萨诸语言中，“雍古”意为“人”，每个氏族都分属杜瓦或伊里查两大半偶族。他们的习惯法“玛达因”以歌组和圣地规范土地归属、贸易与仪式。雍古人以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，通过远达澳大利亚中部的商路换取回旋镖，并由信使带着信息杖跋涉数百公里，在遥远的氏族间传递消息。约从16世纪起，苏拉威西的望加锡海参渔民每年季风时节停泊在他们的海岸，用金属工具、布匹和烟草交换珍珠贝和劳力；雍古人称呼欧洲人的“巴兰达”一词便来自这一接触，源自马来语中对荷兰人的称呼。直到19世纪初，这种季节性航行仍是他们与外部世界的主要联系，而各氏族的土地与仪式始终完好。

en: The Yombe are a Bantu people of the Kongo group, at home in the forested Mayombe hills that straddle the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of the Congo and Cabinda, where they speak Kiyombe, a dialect of the Kongo language. Together with the Vili and neighbouring peoples they formed one of the ethnic components of the Kingdom of Loango from its rise in the 1500s, and their clans also moved within the wider political and cultural world of the Kingdom of Kongo. They have long been celebrated as carvers: their sculptors produced realistic royal and funerary figures, phemba maternity statues and nkisi nkonde nail fetishes, while men also wove and smelted iron and women made pottery. Their cosmology places the high god Ngoma Bunzi above earth and river spirits approached through ancestor shrines.
zh: 永贝人是刚果族群中的班图人，世代居住在横跨刚果（金）、刚果（布）和卡宾达的马永贝山林地带，说刚果语方言基永贝语。他们与维利人等周边族群一道，是16世纪兴起的罗安果王国的族群组成部分，其氏族也生活在刚果王国更广阔的政治文化圈内。永贝人向来以雕刻闻名：工匠制作写实的王室与墓葬雕像、称为“彭巴”的母性雕像以及“恩基西恩孔德”钉子神像，男子还从事纺织和炼铁，女子制作陶器。在他们的宇宙观里，至高神恩戈马·本齐高居天上，人们通过祖先神龛与大地神灵、河流神灵相通。

en: Yongzhou denotes the Yong-Quan branch of Xiang Chinese, strung along the Hunan-Guangxi corridor from Qidong near Hengyang through the Lingling basin of southern Hunan to Quanzhou, Xing'an and Guanyang across the Guangxi border, with outlying pockets in northern Guangdong; its main varieties are the speech of Yongzhou, Qiyang and Quanzhou. The region was ancient Lingling, where the Xiao and Xiang rivers meet; the Sui dynasty made it the prefecture of Yongzhou at the end of the sixth century. In 805 the exiled Tang writer Liu Zongyuan settled here and composed the travel essays that made its rivers and hills famous. Yong-Quan dialects keep many of the voiced initials of Middle Chinese and show heavy contact with Southwestern Mandarin. When Quanzhou was transferred to Guangxi under the Ming, its people kept their Xiang speech, so the branch still straddles the two provinces.
zh: 永州指湘语的永全片，沿湘桂走廊分布，东起衡阳附近的祁东，穿过湖南南部的零陵盆地，西抵广西境内的全州、兴安、灌阳，在广东北部也有零星分布，主要方言包括永州话、祁阳话和全州话。这一带是古零陵之地，潇水与湘江在此汇合，6世纪末隋代将零陵郡改置永州。805年，遭贬的唐代文人柳宗元谪居于此，写下使这里山水闻名的游记篇章。永全片方言保留了较多中古汉语浊声母，同时深受西南官话影响。明代全州改隶广西后，当地居民仍说湘语，这一支方言也因此横跨两省。

en: The Yorta Yorta, also recorded as Jotijota, are an Aboriginal people of the riverine country where the Goulburn River joins the Murray, spanning north-eastern Victoria and the opposite bank in New South Wales, including the red gum forests and wetlands around Barmah. Like several Murray basin peoples, their name is a reduplication of their word for no. Their speech forms a dialect continuum spoken on both sides of the Murray from west of Echuca to the Cobram and Tocumwal district and up the Goulburn as far as Shepparton; linguists treat it, with Yabula Yabula, as the Yotayotic branch of Pama-Nyungan, possibly an isolate within the family and lexically closest to Pallanganmiddang. The river provided fish, waterfowl and routes for bark canoes, and the people lived in a network of related clans sharing the one speech. European overlanders first crossed their country in the 1830s, and pastoral runs were taken up along the rivers soon afterwards.
zh: 约塔约塔人又译约提约塔人，是古尔本河汇入墨累河一带河乡的澳大利亚原住民，地跨维多利亚州东北部与新南威尔士州对岸，包括巴马周围的红桉林与湿地。和墨累河流域的几个族群一样，他们的名字由本族语言中意为“不”的词重叠而成。他们的语言是一条方言连续体，分布在墨累河两岸：西起伊丘卡以西，东至科布勒姆与托库姆瓦尔地区，并沿古尔本河上溯到谢珀顿；语言学者把它与亚布拉亚布拉语一同划为帕马-尼永加语系的约塔约特语支，在语系内可能是孤立语言，词汇上最接近帕兰甘米唐语。河流提供鱼、水禽和树皮独木舟的航路，约塔约塔人以共用同一语言的亲属氏族网络而居。19世纪30年代，欧洲陆路旅行者首次穿过他们的土地，此后沿河地带很快出现了牧场。

en: The Yoruba are one of West Africa's most urban peoples, organized since medieval times into walled city-states across Yorubaland, the forest and savanna country of what is now southwestern Nigeria and adjoining Benin and Togo. Their spiritual homeland is Ile-Ife, a city-state founded by the middle of the first millennium BCE and the seat of the Ife Empire at its height between about 1200 and 1420, whose artists produced strikingly naturalistic brass, terracotta and stone heads. Yoruba dynasties trace their descent from the semi-legendary founder Oduduwa, and each state was ruled by an oba checked by councils of chiefs, such as the Oyo Mesi. From the fifteenth century the Oyo Empire, with its cavalry and its capital at Oyo-Ile, overshadowed Ife and built a dominion stretching from the Niger to the coast, drawing tribute from Dahomey, Borgu and Nupe. Oyo's power crumbled in the early nineteenth century amid Fulani pressure and the loss of Ilorin, after which Ibadan and Abeokuta rose among the competing Yoruba states. Traditional Yoruba religion centres on the high god Olodumare and the orisha divinities, including Shango, Ogun and Eshu, whose worship spread with the Atlantic slave trade and lives on in Santeria and Candomble.
zh: 约鲁巴人是西非城市化程度最高的民族之一，中世纪起便在约鲁巴兰——今尼日利亚西南部及毗邻的贝宁、多哥的森林与稀树草原地带——建立起一座座有城墙的城邦。他们的精神故土是伊费，这座城邦早在公元前一千纪中期即已形成，1200年至1420年前后作为伊费帝国的都城达到鼎盛，其工匠创作了高度写实的黄铜、赤陶和石头头像。约鲁巴诸王朝都把世系追溯到半传说的始祖奥杜杜瓦；各城邦由奥巴（国王）统治，并受酋长会议（如奥约的“奥约·梅西”）制衡。15世纪起，拥有骑兵、定都奥约-伊莱的奥约帝国盖过伊费，建立起北起尼日尔河、南至海岸的霸权，向达荷美、博尔古和努佩索取贡赋。19世纪初，在富拉尼人的压力和伊洛林失守后，奥约霸权瓦解，伊巴丹和阿贝奥库塔等约鲁巴城邦在群雄并起中崛起。约鲁巴传统信仰以至高神奥洛杜马雷和包括香戈、奥贡、埃舒在内的奥里沙神祇为核心，随大西洋奴隶贸易外传，在桑特里亚和坎东布雷等美洲宗教中延续。

en: The Yshyr, who call themselves Ishír, a word meaning “person”, are a Zamuco-speaking people of the Gran Chaco, whose homeland lay along the Paraguay River and in the forests behind it in what is now Paraguay, with some groups later also found across the Brazilian border. They were divided into the river-dwelling Ebytoso and the forest Tomáraho, each speaking its own dialect of the Yshyr language beside the smaller Orio variety. They lived as hunter-gatherers, moving with the game and wild resources of the Chaco scrub, and the Tomáraho long kept their boys' initiation ceremonies and shamanic traditions. Jesuit missionaries studied and described their language during the 1700s, leaving its earliest written record, while the Yshyr themselves remained in the riverine woods beyond the reach of colonial settlements.
zh: 伊希尔人自称伊希尔，这个词的本意是“人”。他们是大查科草原上操萨穆科语族语言的族群，家园在今巴拉圭境内的巴拉圭河沿岸及其后方森林，也有一部分群体后来分布到巴西一侧。他们分为临河而居的埃比托索人和住在森林深处的托马拉霍人，各说伊希尔语的一种方言，另有较小的奥里奥方言。伊希尔人以狩猎采集为生，随大查科灌丛中的猎物和野生资源迁徙，托马拉霍人长期保留着男子成丁仪式和萨满传统。18世纪，耶稣会传教士研究并记录了他们的语言，留下了最早的文字记载，而伊希尔人自身仍在殖民据点之外的河岸林地中生活。

en: The Yuanga are a Kanak people of the far north of Grande Terre in New Caledonia, their Yuanga language, also called Yuaga or Nua, belonging to the extreme-northern group of New Caledonian languages and spoken around Kaala-Gomen and the inland districts of Bondé and Paimboa. These northern tongues share the Austronesian inheritance of Lapita navigators, whose pottery first appears on Grande Terre around 1100 BC, but long isolation in the island's rugged tip split them into a string of sharply distinct languages. Yuanga clans lived by the twin rhythms of coast and mountain: taro and yam gardens on the ridges, shellfish and speared fish along the reef, and ceremonial exchanges that bound rival lineages together under their chiefs. It was this northern end of Grande Terre that James Cook reached in September 1774, when he anchored near Balade among neighbouring Kanak clans and traded before sailing on. Later visitors such as the Comte de Lapérouse in 1788 were rare, and the Yuanga hills kept their customary clan life intact through 1837.
zh: 尤安加人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛最北端的卡纳克族群，其尤安加语又称尤阿加语或努阿语，属新喀里多尼亚诸语的极北语组，通行于卡拉戈门及邦代、潘博阿等内陆地区。这些北方语言共同承继着拉皮塔航海者的南岛语遗产，拉皮塔陶器约在公元前1100年首次出现于格朗德特尔岛，但岛屿崎岖北端的长期隔绝，使它们分化为一串差异鲜明的语言。尤安加氏族依海岸与山地的双重节律生活：在山脊上种植芋头和山药，沿礁岩采集贝类、叉鱼，并通过仪式交换在酋长治下把相互竞争的世系联结起来。1774年9月，詹姆斯·库克抵达的正是格朗德特尔岛的北端，他在邻近的巴拉德一带停泊，与当地卡纳克氏族交易后继续航行。此后访客稀少，1788年拉彼鲁兹伯爵的途经是少数例子，尤安加山区的氏族习俗生活因而完整保持到1837年。

en: The Maaya, or Yucatec Maya, are the Maya people of the Yucatán Peninsula, whose tongue, called Máaya t'áan, belongs to the Mayan language family. Their ancestors built the great cities of the Classic period, among them Chichen Itza and Coba, and after the upheavals of the tenth century the peninsula's political centre shifted north. In about 1221 the regional lords overthrew the rulers of Chichen Itza and founded a new capital at Mayapan, where the Cocom family held the leading role and the Xiu and other noble houses shared government; the league united northern Yucatán for more than two centuries. In 1337 Mayapan still dominated the peninsula, but in 1441 an Xiu revolt led by Ah Xiu Xupan sacked and burned the city, and Yucatán broke into rival city-states, sixteen of which the Spanish found on their arrival. The first Europeans landed in 1508, and after a shipwreck in 1511 the castaway Gonzalo Guerrero married into a Maya lord's family. Spanish conquest and the encomienda system followed from the 1520s, and introduced diseases carried off much of the native population. The Maya kept their language and communal identity through colonial rule, which ended in 1821 when Mexico became independent.
zh: 玛雅人（这里指尤卡坦玛雅人）是尤卡坦半岛的玛雅民族，所说的玛雅语自称 Máaya t'áan，属于玛雅语系。他们的先民建起奇琴伊察、科巴等古典期大城，10世纪的动荡之后，半岛政治中心北移。约1221年，各地领主推翻奇琴伊察的统治，在玛雅潘另立新都，由科科姆家族主导，希乌等贵族家族共治；这个联盟把尤卡坦北部统合了两百多年。1337年时玛雅潘仍是半岛霸主，但1441年希乌家族首领舒潘起兵，攻破并焚毁玛雅潘，尤卡坦由此分裂为互相争战的城邦，西班牙人到来时仍有十六个这样的政权。欧洲人最早于1508年登陆；1511年一艘西班牙船失事，幸存者贡萨洛·格雷罗入赘玛雅首领之家。1520年代起西班牙发动征服并推行监护征赋制，外来疫病又夺去大量人口。殖民统治下玛雅人保留了自己的语言和社群认同，直到1821年墨西哥独立。

en: The Yuè culture occupies the Qiantang River basin and the southern shore of Hangzhou Bay, around Hangzhou and Shaoxing, the Lin'an-Shaoxing belt of northern Zhejiang. It descends from the ancient State of Yue, whose capital Kuaiji stood at modern Shaoxing; under King Goujian, Yue annexed its rival Wu in 473 BC and dominated the lower Yangtze until Chu overran it in 333 BC. The Yue were famed for their bronze swords, their navy and their distinct native speech, often taken as the substrate of later Wu dialects. After the Qin made the region the Kuaiji Commandery, Han settlement and sinification deepened. In 1132 the Song court, driven south by the Jurchen, made Lin'an, modern Hangzhou, its capital; the northern migrants who followed gave the Hangzhou dialect its notably northern flavor and the whole region its literary reading layer. Through the Yuan, Ming and Qing, Hangzhou remained the southern terminus of the Grand Canal and a great commercial city, while Shaoxing supplied the empire with generations of examination graduates and the famed Shaoxing legal secretaries, and later gave its name to Yue opera.
zh: 越文化地处钱塘江流域与杭州湾南岸，以杭州、绍兴为中心，即浙北的临绍一带。它源自古代的越国：越国都城会稽就在今绍兴，越王勾践卧薪尝胆，于公元前473年攻灭世仇吴国，称霸长江下游，直到公元前333年被楚国吞并。越人以青铜宝剑、水军和独特的本土语言闻名，古越语通常被视为后世吴语的底层成分。秦代在此设会稽郡，汉人移民不断迁入，中原化程度日益加深。1132年宋廷为躲避女真人南下，以临安（今杭州）为行在，大批北方士民随行，使杭州话带上明显的北方色彩，也为整个地区的方言添了一层文读系统。元、明、清三代，杭州始终是大运河的南端终点和商业巨邑；绍兴则通过科举源源不断地向朝廷输送人才，绍兴师爷遍布各级衙门，后来的越剧也发源于此。

en: The Yuèhǎi are the Yue Chinese people of the Pearl River Delta in Guangdong, the counties around Guangzhou, Nanhai, Dongguan and Xiangshan, whose speech forms the main branch of Yue and whose Guangzhou dialect is the prestige form widely known as Cantonese. Their homeland, the Lingnan region south of the Nanling ranges, was Baiyue territory until the Qin conquest of 214 BC opened it to Han migration through the Lingqu Canal; after the fall of Qin it formed the kingdom of Nanyue until the Han absorbed it in 111 BC. Successive refugee waves at the collapse of the Han, Tang and Song blended northern speech with the indigenous Tai-related vernacular, producing a language unusually conservative in the final consonants and tonal categories of Middle Chinese. Between 917 and 971 the delta was the heartland of the Southern Han kingdom, and by 660 Guangzhou was China's largest port, trading as far as Arabia; under the Southern Song it became the cultural centre of Lingnan, home to the Yue'ou and Nanyin ballad traditions and Cantonese opera. After the lifting of the maritime bans, the British East India Company set up a chamber of commerce there in 1715, tying Yuehai merchants to the new Canton trade.
zh: 粤海人是广东珠江三角洲的粤语人群，分布在广州、南海、东莞、香山等州县，其方言构成粤语的主干粤海片，其中的广州话便是通行所称的广东话，是整个粤语的标准口音。他们的家园在五岭以南的岭南，本是百越之地；公元前214年秦朝征服岭南，汉族移民经灵渠大批南下，秦亡后这里又成为南越国疆土，直到公元前111年并入汉朝。汉、唐、宋几代末年的难民潮把北方话与当地壮侗系土语相融合，形成了在中古汉语辅音韵尾和声调上保存格外完整的粤语。917—971年，珠江三角洲是南汉国的核心地带；到660年，广州已成为中国最大的港口，商路远达阿拉伯，南宋时更成为岭南的文化中心，孕育了粤讴、南音等曲艺和粤剧。海禁解除后，英国东印度公司于1715年在广州设立商馆，粤海商人由此被卷入新的广州贸易体系。

en: The Yugurs, who call themselves Yagur or Sari Yogur and were long known as the Yellow Uyghurs, are a Turkic-Mongol pastoral people of the Qilian foothills in Gansu, pasturing around Suzhou, Ganzhou and Yongchang. Their Turkic-speaking clans trace to the Old Uyghurs of the Orkhon, and the Yaglakar tribe claims descent from the old Uyghur royal house. When the Uyghur Khaganate collapsed in 840, one branch fled south and built the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom of 870 to 1036, with its capital near Zhangye; the Tangut Western Xia overran it in 1036, and after the Mongol conquest under Subutai the people were ruled by Mongol princes, some tribes adopting a Mongolic tongue. Ming frontier guards set over them were withdrawn inside the Jiayu Pass after defeats by Moghul and Altan Khan raids, and the Yugurs migrated east to the Suzhou and Ganzhou hills, where the Qing organized them as the seven Yellow Fan tribes under a grand superintendent. They kept their Tibetan Buddhist faith while neighbouring Turkic peoples turned to Islam, adopting the Gelug order in the late sixteenth century under the third Dalai Lama and building their first Gelug monastery, Gufo, in the late Ming, while retaining shamanist cults of the heaven god Khan Tengri. Western Yugur preserves archaic Old Uyghur, Eastern Yugur is Mongolic, and the Old Uyghur alphabet remained in religious use until the 1680s.
zh: 裕固人自称尧乎尔、西喇玉固尔，历史上长期被称为黄头回鹘或撒里畏兀儿，是甘肃祁连山北麓的突厥—蒙古语族游牧民族，在肃州、甘州和永昌一带放牧。讲突厥语的部落源出鄂尔浑河的古代回鹘，亚拉格家部落还自认是回鹘王族药罗葛氏的后裔。840年回鹘汗国崩溃后，一支南下建立了870至1036年的甘州回鹘王国，都城在张掖附近；1036年西夏攻陷甘州，蒙古速不台西征后又受蒙古宗王统治，部分部落由此改讲蒙古语。明朝在其地设有曲先、安定等卫，后因被吐鲁番赛德汗和俺答汗击败，明朝把关外诸卫迁入嘉峪关内，裕固人随之东迁，在肃州附近和甘州南山定居，清代将他们编为七族黄番，封大头目为七族黄番总管。当邻近的突厥语族群纷纷改宗伊斯兰教时，他们坚守藏传佛教，16世纪末在三世达赖喇嘛影响下皈依格鲁派，明末建起最早的黄教寺院古佛寺，同时保留着祭祀天神汗腾格里的萨满遗俗。西部裕固语保存了古回鹘语的古老面貌，东部裕固语属蒙古语族，回鹘文则一直使用到17世纪80年代。

en: The Yuin are a nation of Aboriginal Australian peoples on the South Coast of New South Wales, their clans, among them the Djiringanj, Wandandian, Walbunja and Jerrinja, holding the coast from Nowra south past the Moruya River towards Cape Howe. Their related dialects, including Dhurga and Thaua, form the Yuin language group, and religious life centred on the creator being Darhumulan and the Bunan male initiation ceremony. Before 1788 perhaps eleven thousand people lived between Batemans Bay and Cape Howe on a marine economy of fishing, shellfish gathering and canoe travel, and at Twofold Bay the Yuin kept a tradition of hunting in co-operation with killer whales. Smallpox struck them in 1789 and again in 1830, while whalers and settlers moved into the coast between 1810 and 1830, bringing disease and closing in on Yuin lands as the period ended.
zh: 尤因是新南威尔士州南海岸的澳大利亚原住民族群联盟，旗下吉林甘、万达恩迪安、瓦尔本贾、杰林贾等氏族据守着从瑙拉向南经莫鲁亚河直至豪角一带的海岸。他们的亲属方言（包括杜尔加语和萨瓦语）组成尤因语组，宗教生活以创世神灵达胡穆兰和男子成年礼布南仪式为中心。1788年以前，约有一万一千人靠捕鱼、采贝和独木舟航行的海洋经济生活在巴特曼斯湾与豪角之间；在图福德湾，尤因人还保有与虎鲸合作狩猎的传统。天花先后于1789年和1830年袭来，1810至1830年间捕鲸者和移民又沿海岸涌入，带来疾病并步步逼近尤因人的土地。

en: The Yuki are an Indigenous people of northern California whose homeland centered on Round Valley and spread across much of Mendocino and Lake counties. They comprised three groups: the Ukomno'om, or Valley People, of Round Valley itself, the Huchnom outside the valley, and the Coast Yuki on the ocean side, and the name Yuki may come from a Wintu word for foreigner. Archaeologists count them among the oldest populations of California, settled in the region for thousands of years and once ranging as far south as Hood Mountain. Their language, together with that of the Wappo, makes up the small Yukian family, unrelated to any other language, and they counted in fours, using the spaces between the fingers. They lived in conical earth-covered houses, built large semi-subterranean dance houses, and based their diet on acorn mush, deer and salmon; their creator was Taikomol, the one who travels alone, attended by Coyote. In 1337 this world was still intact, and no mission or outside settler had reached Round Valley by 1837.
zh: 尤基人是加利福尼亚北部的原住民，故土以朗德瓦利为中心，遍布门多西诺县和莱克县的大部分地区。他们分为三支：朗德瓦利本地的乌科姆诺姆人（意为谷地之人）、谷地之外的赫奇诺姆人，以及海滨的海岸尤基人；“尤基”这个名称可能来自温图语，意为外乡人。考古学家把他们视为加利福尼亚最古老的居民群体之一，在该地区已定居数千年，活动范围一度南达胡德山。尤基语与瓦波语共同构成很小的尤基语系，与其他语言均无亲缘关系；他们采用四进制计数，数的是手指之间的空隙。他们住在覆土的锥形房屋里，建有半地下的大型舞房，食物以橡果糊、鹿肉和鲑鱼为主；他们信奉的创世神是独行者泰科莫尔，郊狼是其助手。1337年时这一世界仍完好无损，而到1837年为止，还没有传教站或外来定居者抵达朗德瓦利。

en: The Yukpa are an Indigenous people of the Serranía del Perijá, the mountain range straddling the border between Colombia and Venezuela, whose older territory ran from the valley of the Cesar River to the shores of Lake Maracaibo. They speak Yukpa, a language of the northern branch of the Cariban family. After the Spanish founded Valledupar on the adjacent plains in 1550, colonists knew them as Motilones, meaning shaved heads, a label also applied confusingly to the neighbouring Barí; they have likewise been called Chaqués, Macoitas and Irokas. Yukpa society was decentralized: each independent band, led by a kapeta or chief, comprised a few extended families in a small hilltop settlement, with a tomaira directing ceremonies and a tuano serving as healer and shaman. They lived from shifting slash-and-burn horticulture, rotating maize, manioc and plantains on cleared forest plots, supplemented by hunting with arrows, fishing and gathering. Dwelling in rugged mountains away from the main Spanish routes, the Yukpa kept their language and social organization largely intact through the colonial centuries.
zh: 尤克帕人是居住在佩里哈山脉的原住民，这条山脉横亘哥伦比亚与委内瑞拉边界，他们早年的领地从塞萨尔河谷一直延伸到马拉开波湖畔。他们使用的尤克帕语属加勒比语系北支。1550年西班牙人在邻近平原建立巴耶杜帕尔后，殖民者称他们为莫蒂隆人，意为“剃头的人”，这个称呼也被含糊地用在邻近的巴里人身上；此外他们还被称作查克斯人、马科伊塔人和伊罗卡人。尤克帕社会没有统一的权力中心：每个独立群体由一位卡佩塔（酋长）带领，由几户大家族组成小型山居聚落，另有托迈拉主持仪式，图阿诺担任医者和萨满。他们实行轮歇游耕，在砍伐烧荒后的林地上轮种玉米、木薯和香蕉，并以射箭狩猎、捕鱼和采集补充生计。由于身处崎岖山区、远离西班牙人的主要交通线，尤克帕人在整个殖民时代大体保留了自己的语言和社会组织。

en: The Yùlín are the Yue-speaking Han people of the basin country of south-eastern Guangxi, where the Darong, Liuwan and Yunkai mountains ring the headwaters of the Nanliu River. Their speech, the Yulin dialect, belongs to the Goulou branch of Yue and keeps roughly fourteen tones. In Han times the country was part of Yulin commandery, set up in 111 BC on the former Guilin commandery of the Qin. The Tang established Yulin prefecture in 666, and in 996 the Song moved its seat to Nanliu on the Nanliu River, the site of the modern city, earning it the name of the thousand-year Yulin. Under the Yuan the prefecture held Nanliu, Xingye and Bobai, and in 1377 the Ming added Beiliu and Luchuan, forming the five counties long known as the Yulin Five. In 1725 the Qing raised Yulin to an independent department directly under the province, governing Beiliu, Bobai, Luchuan and Xingye.
zh: 郁林人是广西东南部盆地讲粤语的汉族民系，四周被大容山、六万大山和云开大山环绕，南流江就发源于这片山地之间。他们所说的玉林话属粤语勾漏片，声调多达十四个左右。汉代初年，这一带属公元前111年汉朝在秦桂林郡故地设置的郁林郡；666年唐朝置郁林州，996年宋朝把州治迁到南流江畔的南流县，也就是今天玉林城的所在，此后城址延续逾千年，人称千年郁林。元代的郁林州领有南流、兴业、博白三个县，1377年明朝又把北流、陆川划入，号称郁林五属。1725年清朝将其升为郁林直隶州，由省直辖，下辖北流、博白、陆川、兴业四县。

en: The Yupighyt, or Siberian Yupik, call themselves Yupiget, meaning “true people”, and live in coastal villages along the Chukchi Peninsula facing the Bering Strait, with related communities on St. Lawrence Island in Alaska. Their Central Siberian Yupik language belongs to the Eskimo–Aleut family, and anthropologists regard them as descendants of Yupik groups who crossed back from Alaska into Siberia. They were maritime hunters of walrus, seal and whale, lived in dome-shaped yaranga dwellings and were organized into patrilineal clans and territorial tribes named after their ancestral villages, such as the Naukan and Chaplino groups. For centuries they traded across the Bering Strait with Alaskan natives, and from the early 1700s also with Russian seaborne traders, exchanging furs and walrus ivory while keeping their hunting grounds on the eastern Chukchi shore.
zh: 尤皮格特人即西伯利亚尤皮克人，自称尤皮格特，意为“真正的人”，居住在楚科奇半岛濒临白令海峡的沿海村落，近亲群体还分布在阿拉斯加的圣劳伦斯岛。他们的中西伯利亚尤皮克语属于爱斯基摩—阿留申语系，人类学家认为他们是从阿拉斯加回迁西伯利亚的尤皮克群体后裔。他们以捕猎海象、海豹和鲸鱼为生，住圆顶兽皮屋，社会按父系氏族和以祖居村落命名的地域部落组织起来，如瑙坎和恰普林诺两支。他们长期跨越白令海峡与阿拉斯加原住民贸易，18世纪起又与俄国海上商人交易，用毛皮和海象牙换货，始终守着楚科奇东岸的沿海猎场。

en: The Yuracaré, speakers of an isolate language they call Yurújare, are a forest people of the Bolivian lowlands, living along the Chapare, Ichilo, Isiboro and Sécure rivers between Cochabamba and Beni. They farm maize, yuca and bananas beside hunting and fishing, and bury their dead with bow and arrows for the hunting grounds below.
zh: 尤拉卡雷人是玻利维亚低地的森林族群，住在科恰班巴与贝尼之间的查帕雷河、伊奇洛河、伊西博罗河和塞库雷河沿岸，所说的尤鲁哈雷语是一门孤立语言。他们种植玉米、木薯和香蕉，兼事渔猎，并按传统把弓箭与死者一同下葬，供其在地下的猎场使用。

en: The Yuri, also recorded as the Yurimagua, were a Tupi-Guarani people of the upper Amazon, who in the late seventeenth century lived between the Jutai and Jurua rivers and along the Huallaga, south of the Maranon. The Jesuit missionary Samuel Fritz described them and their neighbours the Aysuares as warriors whose women also fought with bow and arrow. Missionaries gathered their village on the Huallaga into the reduction of Nuestra Senora de las Nieves de Yurimaguas, the settlement that later grew into the town of Yurimaguas in the Peruvian Amazon. Antonio de Alcedo's geographical dictionary of 1815 still listed the Yurimagua under that name. Communities bearing the name Yuri survived in the forests between the Caqueta and Putumayo rivers, where they lived in large communal longhouses surrounded by gardens.
zh: 由利人又称尤里马瓜人，是上亚马逊的图皮-瓜拉尼人，17世纪末居住在茹塔伊河与茹鲁阿河之间以及瓦亚加河一带、马拉尼翁河以南。耶稣会传教士塞缪尔·弗里茨记载，他们和邻族艾苏亚雷人勇武善战，连妇女也使用弓箭作战。传教士把他们在瓦亚加河畔的村庄并入“尤里马瓜斯的雪中圣母”归化村，这个聚落后来发展为秘鲁亚马逊的尤里马瓜斯镇。安东尼奥·德·阿尔塞多1815年出版的地理词典仍收录了尤里马瓜人之名。沿用由利之名的群体在卡克塔河与普图马约河之间的丛林中延续下来，居住在被果园环绕的大型公共长屋里。

en: The Yurok, who call themselves Oohl, meaning the people, are an Algic-speaking people of the lower Klamath River and the adjacent Pacific coast of northwestern California, their villages running from the river mouth south toward Trinidad and north toward Crescent City. The name Yurok comes from a Karuk word meaning downriver people, marking them off from the upriver Karuk, while coastal and river villages formed two local divisions. Native settlement along the Klamath reaches back thousands of years, and some Yurok villages date to the fourteenth century. Life centered on the salmon runs of the river, and because they held the mouth and the coast, the Yurok traded salt and dugout canoes upriver to the Hupa, receiving acorns and baskets in return. Their language, together with Wiyot, is one of the two Algic languages spoken in California. The crew of Francis Drake may have met coast Yurok in 1579, but sustained outside contact began only in 1827, when trappers of the Hudson's Bay Company reached the Klamath.
zh: 尤罗克人自称奥尔，意为“人”，是加利福尼亚西北部克拉马斯河下游及邻近太平洋沿岸讲阿尔吉克语的族群，村落从河口向南延伸至特立尼达、向北逼近克雷森特城。“尤罗克”一名来自卡鲁克语，意为“下游之人”，用以与上游的卡鲁克人相区别；他们内部又分为沿岸村落和沿河村落两个地方群体。克拉马斯河沿岸的人类定居已有上万年，尤罗克人的一些村落可追溯到14世纪。他们的生活以河中的鲑鱼洄游为中心；由于扼守河口与海岸，尤罗克人把盐和独木舟沿河向上游交易给胡帕人，换回橡果和篮子。尤罗克语与维约特语是加利福尼亚仅有的两种阿尔吉克语。1579年弗朗西斯·德雷克的船员可能曾与沿岸的尤罗克人接触，但持续的外来接触直到1827年哈德逊湾公司的捕猎者抵达克拉马斯河才开始。

en: The Yuru, also called the Juru, are an Aboriginal Australian people whose country lay along the coast of what is now northern Queensland, from Bowen north to the Burdekin River and Upstart Bay, reaching inland to the Bogie Range, with the Bindal as their neighbours. They spoke the Yuru language, a Pama-Nyungan tongue now recorded as extinct.
zh: 尤鲁人又称朱鲁人，是澳大利亚原住民的一支，其领地位于今昆士兰州北部沿海，自鲍恩向北延伸到伯德金河与阿普斯塔特湾，内陆抵达博吉岭，与宾达尔人为邻。他们使用帕马—牛雅语系的尤鲁语，该语言已被记录为消亡语言。

en: The Yuwi, or Yuwibara, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the central Queensland coast, whose country centred on the site of Mackay and ran from St Helens to Cape Palmerston and inland to the Connors Range, with the Gia to their north and the Wiri and Barada on their western and southern borders. Of the six peoples around Mackay, each perhaps five hundred strong, the Yuwi were the dominant group. They lived by hunting and gathering: the men took sea turtles and dugong off Cape Hillsborough while the women hunted freshwater turtles in the wetlands, and stone fish traps were built across the shoreline. At Cape Hillsborough boys were initiated into manhood, the dead were buried, and shell middens accumulated over centuries; canoes also carried trade from there to the Ngaro of the Whitsunday Islands. Their Yuwi language was a Biri dialect of the Pama-Nyungan family. On 1 June 1770 James Cook's Endeavour sailed this coast, naming Cape Palmerston, Slade Point and Cape Hillsborough, while Joseph Banks noted people on the shore.
zh: 尤维人又称尤维巴拉人，是昆士兰中部沿海的澳大利亚原住民，其领地以麦凯所在地为中心，北起圣海伦斯，南至帕默斯顿角，内陆抵达康纳斯岭，北邻贾人，西面和南面与维里人、巴拉达人相接。麦凯一带有六个族群，每个群体约五百人，其中尤维人势力最大。他们以渔猎采集为生：男子在希尔斯伯勒角近海捕捉海龟和儒艮，女子在湿地猎捕淡水龟，海岸上还建有多处石制鱼梁。希尔斯伯勒角是男孩举行成年礼的地方，也是族人的墓地，贝丘在那里堆积了数百年；他们还从这里驾独木舟出海，与圣灵群岛的恩加罗人贸易。他们的尤维语是帕马—牛雅语系比里语的一种方言。1770年6月1日，詹姆斯·库克的奋进号驶过这段海岸，命名了帕默斯顿角、斯莱德角和希尔斯伯勒角，约瑟夫·班克斯也记下了岸上的原住民身影。

en: The Zacatecah, or Zacatecos in Spanish accounts, were a Chichimeca people whose name comes from the Nahuatl zacatl, the grass that covered their homeland; the Aztecs called their country Zacatlan. They roamed most of what is now Zacatecas and north-eastern Durango, from the Cerro de la Bufa and Peñón Blanco north to Cuencamé, overlapping Guachichil country to the east and Tepehuán lands to the west. Most bands were nomadic hunter-gatherers who wore their hair to the waist, marked themselves with paint and tattoos, and drew praise from Spanish observers as among the finest archers alive, while settled groups in the south kept temples, ball courts and water channels around El Teul. When silver rushes brought Spanish settlers into their lands, the Zacatecah joined the Chichimeca Confederation and fought the long Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590, after which the Spanish bought peace with goods, land grants and mission towns that gradually dissolved their independent life.
zh: 萨卡特卡人在西班牙语文献中称萨卡特科斯人，是奇奇梅克诸族之一；其名来自纳瓦特尔语的萨卡特尔，即覆盖故土的一种草，阿兹特克人把他们的地方称作萨卡特兰。他们游猎于今萨卡特卡斯州大部和杜兰戈东北部，从布法山和佩尼翁布兰科向北远达昆卡梅，东面与瓜奇奇尔人、西面与特佩万人的地域交错。多数游帮是游牧狩猎采集者，发长及腰，以涂身和纹身为识，西班牙观察者盛赞他们是当世最出色的弓箭手；南部的定居民众则在埃尔特乌尔一带建有神庙、球场和引水渠。银矿潮把西班牙定居者引入他们的土地后，萨卡特卡人加入奇奇梅克联盟，参加了1550至1590年漫长的奇奇梅克战争；战后西班牙人以货物、授地和传教城镇换取和平，他们的独立生活也随之逐渐解体。

en: The Zafiraminia, whose name means descendants of Ramini, were Muslim seafarers who settled on the southeastern coast of Madagascar from about the thirteenth century, perhaps a hundred years before the better-known Antemoro. Their leaders claimed ancestry that had moved from Mecca by way of Mangalore in India, though later scholars more often trace them to Sumatra, Ramini being a medieval name for that island, or to the Bugis of Borneo. They won high standing among the local Malagasy through the knowledge and crafts they brought from overseas and kept the prized right to perform the sombili, the ritual sacrifice of cattle to the ancestors. When new Muslim migrants reached the Matitana coast around 1490 and formed themselves into the Antemoro clans, the Zafiraminia refused them marriage alliances; the rivalry that followed ended in the 1500s with the rise of the Antemoro kingdom and the loss of their former supremacy.
zh: 扎菲拉米尼亚意为“拉米尼人的后裔”，是约13世纪起定居马达加斯加东南沿海的穆斯林航海者，比名气更大的安泰莫罗人早到约一个世纪。他们的首领自称祖先经印度的门格洛尔从麦加迁来，但后世学者多认为他们来自苏门答腊——拉米尼正是该岛的中世纪名称——或婆罗洲的布吉人。他们凭海外带来的知识和技艺在当地马尔加什人中赢得崇高地位，并保有主持松比利仪式的特权，即向祖先献祭牛牲的仪式。1490年前后，新的穆斯林移民抵达马蒂塔纳海岸，组成安泰莫罗诸氏族，扎菲拉米尼亚人拒绝与之联姻；双方随后争霸，到16世纪安泰莫罗王国兴起，扎菲拉米尼亚人昔日的优势地位告终。

en: The Zaghawa, who call themselves the Beri, are Saharan-speaking pastoralists of the arid belt between Tibesti, Kanem and Darfur, where they herd cattle, camels and sheep around oasis towns such as Manan and Njimi. Arab geographers knew them by the ninth century, when al-Ya'qubi placed the Zaghawa in Kanem and credited them with a loose hegemony over the Sahelian societies stretching from Lake Chad to Darfur, backed by their grip on trans-Saharan caravan routes. The Kanem royal chronicle, the Girgam, names their early ruling line the Duguwa, and by the eleventh century Zaghawa kings were at least nominally Muslim. The rise of the Sayfawa dynasty of Kanem broke their power: writing in 1270, ibn Sa'id records that Manan ceased to be the Kanem capital when the Sayfawa moved their seat to Njimi, and the Zaghawa were pushed east into the lands later called Dar Zaghawa. After Darfur emerged as an independent state in the late fourteenth century, they kept only the desert fringes between Kanem-Bornu and the Nile, organized in stratified nomadic clans with endogamous artisan castes of blacksmiths, potters and leatherworkers.
zh: 扎加瓦人自称贝里人，是操撒哈拉语的游牧族群，活跃在提贝斯提、卡涅姆与达尔富尔之间的干旱地带，在马南、吉米等绿洲城镇周边放牧牛、骆驼和绵羊。阿拉伯地理学家早在9世纪便已记载他们：叶尔孤比把扎加瓦人置于卡涅姆，并称他们凭借对跨撒哈拉商路的控制，对乍得湖至达尔富尔一带的萨赫勒诸社会拥有松散的霸权。卡涅姆王室编年史《吉尔加姆》把其早期统治世系称为杜古瓦；到11世纪，扎加瓦诸王至少在名义上已是穆斯林。卡涅姆赛法瓦王朝的崛起打破了他们的权势：伊本·赛义德在1270年的记载中称，赛法瓦王朝把都城从马南迁往吉米，扎加瓦人被逐向东方，进入后来所称的扎加瓦之地。14世纪末达尔富尔作为独立国家兴起后，他们只保有卡涅姆—博尔努与尼罗河之间的沙漠边缘地带，以等级分明的游牧氏族为生，社会中还有铁匠、陶工和皮匠等内婚的工匠种姓。

en: The Azande are the people of the upper Uele river and the surrounding savannas, spread across what are now the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the south-east of the Central African Republic and Western Equatoria in South Sudan; their name means the people who possess much land, won by conquest. They were forged in the first half of the 1700s, when the Vungara, or Avongara, clan built a string of chiefdoms by military expansion, while the related Bandia dynasty, itself of foreign origin, adopted Zande speech and customs and came to rule over the Vungara in the early 1800s. On a king's death his sons fought for the succession, and the losers marched out to found new chiefdoms, carrying Zande rule eastward and northward until raids out of the Sudan checked their spread. Unmarried men served as warriors and labourers under the Avongara nobility, and Zande smiths were famed for their multi-bladed throwing knives. Their traditional belief centred on the supreme being Mbori, and men settled disputes through oracles, above all the poison oracle reserved for men.
zh: 阿赞德人生活在乌埃莱河上游及周边草原，分布于今刚果民主共和国东北部、中非共和国东南部和南苏丹西赤道州一带；其族名意为‘拥有大片土地的人’，得自征战传统。阿赞德民族形成于18世纪上半叶：温加拉（又称阿文加拉）氏族靠军事扩张建立起一连串酋长邦，而异族出身的班迪亚王朝采用了赞德语言和习俗，并在19世纪初统治温加拉人，两支逐渐融合为阿赞德人。国王死后诸子争夺继承权，失意者便率众外出另建酋长邦，把赞德势力向东、向北传播，直到来自苏丹方向的劫掠挡住了这股扩张势头。未婚男子在阿文加拉贵族麾下充作战士和劳力，赞德铁匠以多刃掷刀闻名。传统信仰以至高神姆博里为核心，男子借助神谕裁断纠纷，其中最重要的是只准男子参与的毒药神谕。

en: The Zapochteca, known to the Nahuatl as the Zapotecs and to themselves as Be'ena'a, the cloud people, built one of Mesoamerica's earliest urban civilizations in the three valleys of Oaxaca from about 700 BC. Their mountain capital Monte Albán, founded around 500 BC above the former chief town of San José Mogote, grew into the greatest city of the southern highlands, its Building J carved with glyphs naming the provinces its rulers had taken; the undeciphered Zapotec script is among the oldest writing in Mesoamerica. After Monte Albán declined around 700, power passed to the lake city of Zaachila, whose kings waged long wars with the Mixtecs of Tututepec and Tlaxiaco and grew rich on salt, goldwork and cochineal. Aztec expansion reached them under Ahuitzotl: his armies took Zaachila in 1495 and in 1497 besieged the cliff fortress of Guiengola for seven months, until King Cosijoeza sealed peace by marrying the tlatoani's daughter. Their son Cosijopii, the last Zaachila sovereign, allied with Pedro de Alvarado when the Spanish reached Tehuantepec, accepted baptism as Juan Cortés Sicasibí, and built the Santo Domingo convent there between 1543 and 1555.
zh: 萨波特克人自称贝埃纳阿，意为云之人，纳瓦特尔语称之为萨波特克；他们约自公元前700年起在瓦哈卡的三大谷地建立了中美洲最早的城市文明之一。约公元前500年，他们在旧酋邦圣何塞莫戈特上方的山上营建都城阿尔班山，后来成为南部高地最大的城市，城中的J号建筑刻满记载被征服省份的象形文字；其尚未破译的象形文字是中美洲最古老的书写系统之一。阿尔班山约在700年衰落后，权力转入湖城萨奇拉，其国王与图图特佩克、特拉西亚科的米斯特克人长期交战，并靠盐业、金工和胭脂虫红致富。阿维措特尔治下阿兹特克势力逼近：1495年攻占萨奇拉，1497年又将悬崖要塞吉恩戈拉围困七个月，国王柯西乔扎最终以迎娶特拉托阿尼之女缔和。他们的儿子科西霍皮是萨奇拉末代君主，西班牙人抵达特万特佩克时与佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多结盟，受洗改名胡安·科尔特斯·西卡西维，并于1543至1555年在当地修建圣多明各修道院。

en: The Zazas, who call themselves Dimli, are an Iranian people of the eastern Anatolian highlands, settled around Harput, Palu, Gerger and the Dersim mountains. Their Zaza language belongs to the Northwestern Iranian branch and shares its closest features with the Caspian languages Gilaki, Mazandarani and Talysh, pointing to an origin on the southern shore of the Caspian in the old region of Daylam. Medieval Armenian sources call them delmik or dlmik, meaning Daylamite, and trace bands of Daylamites raiding and settling westward from the tenth and eleventh centuries; the Dunbuli tribe recorded at Palu still spoke Zazaki when it moved into Dersim under Shah Ismail in the early sixteenth century. The people are divided between Sunni and Alevi Islam, a split reflected in their northern, central and southern dialects. Their medieval minstrel tradition had bards composing in both Zaza and Turkish, and an Armenian dictionary printed in 1621 already described them as a distinct Parthian nation.
zh: 扎扎人自称迪姆利，是定居在东安纳托利亚高原哈普特、帕卢、盖尔盖尔和德尔西姆山区一带的伊朗语族群。他们的扎扎语属于伊朗语族西北支，与吉兰语、马赞德兰语和塔雷什语等里海语言特征最接近，说明其祖源在里海南岸古称德莱木的地区。中世纪亚美尼亚文献称他们为德尔米克或德尔米克，意为德莱木人，并记载德莱木各部从10至11世纪起向西袭扰、迁徙；16世纪初沙阿·伊斯玛仪时代迁入德尔西姆的敦布利部落，在帕卢时仍说扎扎语。扎扎人分为逊尼派和阿列维派两支，这种分歧也体现在北、中、南三种方言上。他们的游吟传统可追溯到中世纪，游吟诗人兼用扎扎语和土耳其语创作；1621年刊印的一部亚美尼亚语词典已把他们单列为一个帕提亚民族。

en: The Zenata were a confederation of nomadic and semi-nomadic Berber tribes, ranked with the Sanhaja and Masmuda as one of the three great Berber groupings; Ibn Khaldun names the Jarawa, Maghrawa and Banu Ifran as their chief tribes. They adopted Islam in the seventh century, and a Zenata chieftain, Khalid ibn Hamid al-Zanati, led the Berber revolt of 740 against the Umayyads at the battles of the Nobles and Bagdoura, while Zenata clans also rode in the conquest of Iberia. The Miknasa founded the caravan city of Sijilmasa, and in the tenth and eleventh centuries Zenata tribes ruled as proxies of the Fatimids and the Umayyads of Cordoba, the Maghrawa holding Fez and the Banu Ifran holding Tlemcen and the Tadla until the Almoravids swept them away. Their second age of power came in the thirteenth century: the Banu Marin built the Marinid Sultanate of Fez, which from 1245 dismantled Almohad rule and under Abu al-Hasan and Abu Inan briefly dominated the whole Maghreb, while the related Zayyanids, also Zenata, ruled the Kingdom of Tlemcen from 1235. In 1337 Abu al-Hasan's armies occupied Tlemcen, the homeland of the game's Zenati tribes, and held it until 1359; the Zayyanids then recovered, only to become intermittent vassals of the Hafsids, Marinids and Aragon before the Ottomans ended their rule in the 1550s. In Morocco the Wattasids succeeded the Marinids after 1465 until the Saadian rise, and Zenata light cavalry, the jinetes, long formed the backbone of Granadan armies.
zh: 泽纳塔是游牧与半游牧柏柏尔部落的联盟，与桑哈贾、马斯穆达并称三大柏柏尔族群；伊本·赫勒敦举出其三大主部：杰拉瓦、马格拉瓦和巴努伊夫兰。他们在7世纪即皈依伊斯兰教，740年泽纳塔首领哈立德·伊本·哈米德·扎纳提领导柏柏尔大起义，在贵族之战和巴格杜拉之战中重创倭马亚军队，泽纳塔部族也曾参与对伊比利亚的征服。米克纳萨人兴建了商路名城锡吉勒马萨；10至11世纪，泽纳塔诸部作为法蒂玛人和科尔多瓦倭马亚人的代理人纵横政坛，马格拉瓦人据有非斯，巴努伊夫兰人据有特莱姆森和塔德腊，直到被穆拉比特人席卷。他们的第二个权势时代始于13世纪：巴努马林人建立以非斯为都的马林苏丹国，自1245年起逐步瓦解穆瓦希德人的统治，在阿布·哈桑和阿布·伊南治下一度称雄整个马格里布；同属泽纳塔的扎扬王朝则自1235年起统治特莱姆森王国。1337年，阿布·哈桑的军队攻占特莱姆森——即本文化诸部的故土，并占据至1359年；扎扬人虽一度复国，此后却轮番沦为哈夫斯、马林和阿拉贡的附庸，最终在1550年代被奥斯曼人终结。在摩洛哥，瓦塔斯王朝于1465年后接掌马林政权，直至萨阿德人崛起；而泽纳塔轻骑兵“赫内特”长期是格拉纳达军队的骨干。

en: The Zhongyuan, or Central Plains, are the middle and lower Yellow River country centered on Kaifeng and Luoyang, the historical heartland of Huaxia civilization and the seat of more than twenty dynastic capitals. Its people speak Central Plains Mandarin, the speech recorded in the Yuan rime book Zhongyuan Yinyun of 1324, and the same dialect group reaches the southern Shandong districts held by this culture. Kaifeng, capital of the Northern Song until 1127, entered the Ming era in 1368 as the dynasty's secondary Northern Capital, then in 1378 became the capital of Henan province. The city lay on the Yellow River floodplain: five great floods struck between 1375 and 1416, and in 1642 a Ming army cut the dikes to break Li Zicheng's siege, submerging Kaifeng so that only 30,000 of its 370,000 people remained; rebuilding began in 1662. Through these disasters the plain stayed the agricultural core of China, its grain feeding the Grand Canal fleets that supplied Beijing.
zh: 中原指黄河中下游一带，以开封、洛阳为中心，是华夏文明的核心地带，先后有二十多个王朝在此建都。中原人说中原官话，元代1324年成书的《中原音韵》记录的就是这一带的语音，该文化所及的鲁南地区也属这一方言区。开封在1127年前是北宋都城，1368年明朝建立后被定为陪都北京，1378年改为河南省会。开封地处黄河滩区，1375至1416年间连遭五次大水；1642年明军为解李自成的围城之困掘开黄河堤防，全城被淹，三十七万城中人仅余三万，1662年才开始重建。历经水患，这片平原仍是中国的农业重心，所产粮食经大运河运往北京。

en:
The Zhuang are the Tai-speaking indigenous people of Guangxi, settled along the Zuo, You and Liu river valleys of southern China and kindred to the Bouyei of Guizhou and the Tày and Nùng of northern Vietnam. Chinese histories trace them to the Xi'ou of the ancient Baiyue, and they appear under successive names such as the Liao and the Wuhu before the term Zhuang, their own word for a cave, came into use under the Song. They farmed irrigated rice in the lowland valleys, wrote their language in the Chinese-derived Sawndip characters, and ordered village life around song courts, matrilineal customs and the animist Mo faith served by bumo shamans. For centuries they were ruled through loose-rein prefectures under hereditary chieftains of the Nong, Huang and Cen clans.

The greatest of these leaders, Nong Zhigao, seized Yongzhou in 1052 and proclaimed his own dynasty before the Song general Di Qing defeated him at the Kunlun Pass in 1053; the followers he left beyond the frontier became the Nùng of Vietnam. The Song then enrolled more than fifty thousand Zhuang as frontier militia between 1064 and 1067, and under the Ming their mercenary bands were famed as wolf warriors, fighting the court's campaigns including the Big Rattan Gorge war of 1465, in which some twenty thousand people died. The Ming and Qing kept the Cen and other chiefly houses as tusi native officials while opening Chinese schools in the Zhuang country, where local rebellions continued into the Qing period.
zh:
壮族是广西本土讲侗台语的民族，聚居于左江、右江和柳江流域，与贵州的布依族以及越南北部的岱依人、侬人语言相通、习俗相近。中国史籍把他们上溯到百越中的西瓯，先后以獠、乌浒、溪峒蛮等名称出现；到宋代才有撞、僮之称，这个词在他们本族语言里意为山洞。他们在低海拔河谷经营灌溉水稻，用仿照汉字创制的方块壮字书写，村落生活围绕歌圩、母系遗俗和摩公主持的万物有灵信仰展开。历代朝廷通过羁縻州和农、黄、岑等世袭土司首领治理其地。

这些首领中最著名的是侬智高，他于1052年攻占邕州、自立朝廷，1053年被宋将狄青在昆仑关击败，留在边外的部众后来发展为越南的侬人。宋朝随后在1064年至1067年间把五万多名壮人编入乡兵；明代，壮人组成的狼兵以骁勇著称，受朝廷征调四处作战，1465年的大藤峡之役便有约两万人死亡。明朝和清朝保留岑氏等土司家族治理地方，同时在壮区开设汉学塾校，而当地的起事一直延续到清代。

en: Zo, meaning highlander, is the shared self-name of the northern Kuki-Chin peoples whom the Burmese call Chin and the Indians know as Kuki, Mizo or Zomi; all speak closely related Tibeto-Burman languages and trace their origin to migrations from the Tibetan marches into Burma. The Burmese term Chin first appears in eleventh-century inscriptions of King Kyansittha, and the scholar Gordon Luce places their first Burmese settlement in the upper Chindwin valley around the mid-700s, where Pagan knew them as friends rather than enemies. In the late 1200s they crossed into the Kale-Kabaw valley and built their capital at Khampat, until the Shan founding of Kale in 1395 drove them into the Chin Hills. From the first hill settlement of Ciimnuai the tribes fanned out: the Asho went south toward the Irrawaddy delta and the Arakan ranges, the Laimi held Falam and Hakha, and the Zomi moved north, reaching the Manipur hills by about 1554. Organised in autonomous villages under warrior chiefs, the northern Zo kept headhunting customs and animist ancestor cults beyond lowland control; when the 1834 treaty assigned the Kabaw valley to Burma, the Sukte clan of Tedim was already rising as the dominant hill power.
zh: 佐意为“山民”，是北部库基-钦语族群共同的自称：缅人称之为钦，印度方面则称库基、米佐或佐米；他们都说相近的藏缅语，先祖由青藏高原边缘陆续南迁进入缅甸。“钦”这个缅语称呼最早见于11世纪江喜陀王时代的碑铭；学者卢斯认为，他们约在700年代中叶最先定居于钦敦江上游，蒲甘缅人视其为友邻而非敌寇。1200年代末，他们渡过钦敦江进入格礼-卡包河谷，以坎巴特为都，直到1395年掸人建起格礼城，才被迫退入钦山。从山上最早的定居点出发，各部四散：阿肖人南下伊洛瓦底三角洲和若开山脉，莱米人据有法兰和哈卡，佐米人向北发展，约在1554年抵达曼尼普尔丘陵。北部佐人以武士首领治下的自治村落为单位，长期游离于低地政权之外，保留猎头习俗和万物有灵的祖先祭祀；1834年条约把卡包河谷划归缅甸时，梯顶的苏特氏族已在崛起，成为山区的主导势力。

en: The Zo'é, also called the Poturu after the wooden lip plug worn by every adult, are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Cuminapanema River basin in the forests behind Óbidos in Pará. Semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers who also grow manioc, they left no trace in colonial records and stayed entirely isolated from Portuguese settlement through the period.
zh: 佐埃人又称波图鲁人，得名于每个成年人都佩戴的木制下唇栓，是帕拉州奥比杜斯后方库米纳帕内马河流域森林中的图皮-瓜拉尼语族群。他们半游牧而居，以狩猎采集为生，兼种木薯；殖民档案中没有他们的记载，整个这一时期都与葡萄牙人的定居点完全隔绝。

en: The Zoque are an Indigenous people of southern Mexico, concentrated in the hills and river valleys of northwestern Chiapas, with older communities along the Isthmus of Tehuantepec and into Tabasco. Their several Zoque languages, often mutually unintelligible, form one branch of the Mixe-Zoque family together with the speech of the neighbouring Mixe. Because Mixe-Zoque words for maize, cacao and other cultivated things were borrowed across Mesoamerica, many scholars think the Zoque are descendants or close kin of the Olmecs, the region's first great civilization; ruins such as Chiapa de Corzo and Malpasito mark their pre-Hispanic towns, where society was divided between nobles, commoners and slaves. For much of the Post-Classic period they were pressed on several sides: the Chiapanecs fought or dominated the settlements near Chiapa, while Nahuas from Cimatan influenced those farther north. In 1494 the armies of the Aztec ruler Ahuitzotl defeated them and imposed tribute, though trade with the Mexica also brought prosperity. The Spanish conquest began in 1523 under Luis Marin, after which the Zoque were distributed among settlers for forced labour and sharply reduced by disease and exploitation.
zh: 索克人是墨西哥南部的原住民，主要聚居在恰帕斯西北部的丘陵与河谷，在特万特佩克地峡和塔巴斯科一带有更古老的社群。他们所说的多种索克语彼此常常难以互通，与相邻米赫人的语言共同构成米赫—索克语系的一支。由于玉米、可可等栽培作物的米赫—索克语词汇被中美洲各语言借用，不少学者认为索克人是当地最早的伟大文明奥尔梅克人的后裔或近亲；奇亚帕德科尔索、马尔帕西托等遗址就是他们史前时代的城镇，当时社会已分为贵族、平民和奴隶。后古典时期的大部分时间里，他们四面受压：奇亚帕内克人征伐或控制了奇亚帕附近的聚落，来自西马坦的纳瓦人则影响着更靠北的村落。1494年，阿兹特克君主奥伊佐特的军队击败索克人并强征贡赋，不过与墨西加人的贸易也带来了繁荣。1523年，路易斯·马林率军开启了西班牙人的征服，此后索克人被分封给殖民者做苦役，人口因疾病和压榨而锐减。

en: The Zuni, who call themselves A:shiwi, are a Pueblo people of the Zuni River valley in western New Mexico, a land they name Halona Idiwan'a, the Middle Place. Their ancestors irrigated maize there as early as the last centuries before Christ, and by the fourteenth century they lived in a dozen stone pueblos, later consolidated into six famous villages including Halona and Hawikuh, whose people traded salt, maize and turquoise. Their language is a linguistic isolate, and households are matrilineal and matrilocal under a katsina religion whose winter climax is the all-night Shalako dance. In 1539 the Zuni killed the Moorish guide Estevanico, the first Spaniard any Pueblo people had seen, and the next year Coronado stormed Hawikuh in search of the fabled Seven Cities of Cibola. Franciscan missions begun in 1629 were soon burned, and after joining the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 the Zuni held out on the mesa of Dowa Yalanne until 1692; by the end of the century only Halona remained of the six old towns. Spanish authority never ran deep: in 1799 just seven Spaniards lived among them, and the Franciscans abandoned their mission in 1821.
zh: 祖尼人自称阿希维，是居住在今新墨西哥西部祖尼河谷的普韦布洛族群，他们把故乡称作哈洛纳·伊迪瓦纳，意为“中央之地”。早在公元前最后几个世纪，其先民已在当地引水种植玉米；到14世纪，他们生活在十多座石砌普韦布洛中，后来整合为哈洛纳、哈维库等六座名村，以食盐、玉米和绿松石对外贸易。祖尼语是一门语言孤立语言；社会按母系计算世系、行从妻居，信仰以卡奇纳为核心，冬季通宵的沙拉科舞是仪式的高潮。1539年，祖尼人杀死了摩尔人向导埃斯特万尼科，这是普韦布洛人见到的第一个西班牙人；次年科罗纳多为寻找传说中的锡沃拉七城攻陷哈维库。1629年开始的方济各会传教站很快被焚毁，1680年祖尼人参加普韦布洛起义后，又在多瓦亚兰内台地上坚守到1692年；到17世纪末，六座古镇只剩哈洛纳一座。西班牙人的统治从未深入：1799年他们中间只住着七个西班牙人，1821年方济各会也终止了传教。

en: The Banu Kanz were a semi-nomadic Muslim dynasty of Arab Banu Hanifa stock, mixed through marriage with the Beja Hadariba, who dominated the frontier between Upper Egypt and Nubia from the tenth to the fifteenth century. In 1006 their chief Abu al-Makarim Hibatallah captured a major rebel for the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim, who rewarded him with the hereditary title Kanz al-Dawla, Treasure of the State, from which the house took its name; from their base at Aswan they guarded the gold mines of Wadi Allaqi and the caravan and Nubian trade. In 1174 the Kanz al-Dawla Ibn al-Mutawwaj rose against Saladin in a failed bid to restore the Fatimids, and after defeat at Aswan the tribe migrated south into Maris in northern Nubia, where its settlement speeded the spread of Islam and Arabic among the local Christians. Early in the fourteenth century they reached the throne of Christian Makuria: after the Mamluk sultan an-Nasir Muhammad imposed the convert Barshanbu as king at Dongola in 1317, the Kanz al-Dawla, a nephew of the deposed King Karanbas, seized the crown for himself and held it despite two Mamluk expeditions, the last in 1324. Raids on Aswan followed, and after Dongola fell to the tribesmen Mamluk power reasserted itself with the Kanz al-Dawla's surrender at Qus in 1365; Sultan Barquq then loosed the Hawwara Berbers against them, and by the early fifteenth century the Hawwara had supplanted the Banu Kanz as masters of the frontier.
zh: 巴努·坎兹是半游牧的穆斯林王朝，出身阿拉伯巴努·哈尼发部落，与贝贾人的哈达里巴部通婚融合，10世纪至15世纪称雄于上埃及与努比亚之间的边地。1006年，其首领阿布·马卡里姆·希卜图拉替法蒂玛哈里发哈基姆擒获一名大叛乱者，获赐可世袭的头衔坎兹·道拉（意为“国之宝库”），家族由此得名；他们以阿斯旺为据点，护卫阿拉吉干河的金矿以及商队和对努比亚贸易。1174年，坎兹·道拉伊本·穆塔瓦吉起兵反对萨拉丁、企图复辟法蒂玛王朝，兵败阿斯旺后全族南迁努比亚北部的马里斯，其定居加速了伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语在当地基督徒中的传播。14世纪初，他们进而登上基督教国家马库里亚的王位：1317年马穆鲁克苏丹纳绥尔·穆罕默德把改宗者巴尔尚布扶上栋古拉王位后，被废国王卡兰巴斯的侄子、时任坎兹·道拉夺取王冠，并顶住马穆鲁克两次远征（最后一次在1324年）保住王位。此后他们不断袭扰阿斯旺，栋古拉落入部落之手后，马穆鲁克重新施压，坎兹·道拉于1365年在库斯投降；苏丹巴尔库克随后放出豪瓦拉柏柏尔人对付他们，到15世纪初，豪瓦拉已取代巴努·坎兹成为边地之主。

en: The House of Aberffraw, also called the Second Dynasty of Gwynedd or the Merfynion, takes its name from its royal court at Aberffraw on Anglesey. It was founded around 826 when Merfyn Frych, a ruler from the Isle of Man with a claim through his mother, seized Gwynedd; his son Rhodri Mawr (died 878) built a Welsh hegemony and his descendants also founded the ruling line of Deheubarth. Restored after the Norman incursions by Gruffudd ap Cynan in 1098, the house reached its height under Llywelyn the Great and his grandson Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, who was recognised as Prince of Wales in 1267. Edward I's conquest ended the line's power: Llywelyn was killed in battle in 1282 and his brother Dafydd ap Gruffudd was captured and executed at Shrewsbury in 1283, the last native prince to rule Gwynedd. The family's claim lived on through exiled descendants, above all Owain Lawgoch, who campaigned against the English from France until he was assassinated in 1378. Later Welsh revolts, notably that of Owain Glyndwr after 1400, drew on the memory of the Aberffraw princes.
zh: 阿伯弗劳家族又称圭内斯第二王朝或梅尔菲尼翁家族，名字来自其在安格尔西岛上的王庭阿伯弗劳。约826年，出身马恩岛、凭借母系血统拥有继承权的梅尔芬·弗里奇夺取圭内斯，开创该王朝；其子罗德里大帝（878年去世）建立起对威尔士的霸权，后裔还另立了德赫巴思的统治世系。1098年，格鲁菲兹·阿普·南南在诺曼人入侵后恢复国势，家族在卢埃林大帝及其孙卢埃林·阿普·格鲁菲兹治下达到鼎盛，后者于1267年被承认为威尔士亲王。爱德华一世的征服终结了该家族的统治：卢埃林于1282年战死，其弟大卫·阿普·格鲁菲兹被俘，1283年在什鲁斯伯里被处死，成为最后一位统治圭内斯的本土亲王。家族的继承权由流亡后裔延续，其中最著名的是欧文·劳戈赫，他以法国为基地不断进攻英格兰，直到1378年遇刺身亡。此后的威尔士起事，尤其是1400年以后欧文·格林杜尔的起义，都借重阿伯弗劳诸王的名号。

en: The Abulafia are a Sephardic Jewish family whose Arabic-derived name, Abu l-Afiyya, took its medieval Spanish form under Muslim rule in Al-Andalus, where it was often borne by physicians and scholars. From around 1200 the family supplied leaders to the Jewish community of Toledo and Castile, including the rabbi Meir Abulafia and the kabbalists Todros ben Joseph and Abraham Abulafia. Its most famous member was Samuel ben Meir Ha-Levi Abulafia, born around 1320, who rose at the court of Pedro I of Castile from chamberlain to almojarife, or royal treasurer, and judge. He backed the king against the rebel Henry of Trastámara and attended the peace settlement with Portugal at Évora in 1358, and with his court wealth built the Synagogue of El Tránsito in Toledo between 1355 and 1357, whose Hebrew and Arabic inscriptions made it one of the finest monuments of medieval Toledo. Accused of embezzlement, he was imprisoned and tortured in 1360 and died in Seville the same year. When the Catholic Monarchs issued the Alhambra Decree in 1492, the unconverted Abulafias left Spain like other Sephardim, resettling chiefly in the Ottoman Empire and Italy.
zh: 阿布拉菲亚是塞法迪犹太人家族，其姓氏源自阿拉伯语“阿布·阿菲亚”，在穆斯林统治安达卢斯时期演化为中世纪西班牙语形式，常为医生和学者所用。约1200年起，该家族不断出掌托莱多乃至整个卡斯蒂利亚的犹太社群，代表人物有拉比梅厄·阿布拉菲亚以及卡巴拉学者托德罗斯·本·约瑟夫和亚伯拉罕·阿布拉菲亚。最著名的成员是约1320年出生的撒母耳·本·迈尔·哈列维·阿布拉菲亚：他在卡斯蒂利亚国王佩德罗一世的宫廷由内侍升任王室司库兼法官，支持国王对抗反叛者特拉斯塔马拉的恩里克，并参与1358年与葡萄牙的埃武拉和谈；他还用宫廷财富于1355—1357年在托莱多修建埃尔·特兰西托犹太会堂，建筑上的希伯来语与阿拉伯语铭文使其成为中世纪托莱多最精美的建筑之一。1360年他被控侵吞公款，遭囚禁拷打，同年死于塞维利亚。1492年天主教双王颁布《阿兰布拉宫法令》后，未改宗的阿布拉菲亚家族与其他塞法迪人一样离开西班牙，主要迁居奥斯曼帝国和意大利。

en: The Acciaioli were a Florentine noble and banking house whose line runs back to the twelfth century, when family legend brings them from Brescia to Florence as Guelph refugees from Frederick Barbarossa. In the thirteenth century they built a bank with branches stretching from Greece to Western Europe, and its collapse in 1345 only redirected their ambitions. Niccolò Acciaioli, sent to Naples in 1331, became Grand Seneschal of the kingdom and count of Melfi, Malta and Gozo, amassed estates in the Morea and Corinth, and patronised Petrarch and Boccaccio while founding the Certosa del Galluzzo outside Florence. In Greece the family reached for a crown: Nerio I Acciaioli seized Athens in 1388 and ruled the Duchy of Athens, which his house, after a brief Venetian interlude, held again from 1402 until the Ottoman conquest extinguished the last duke, Francesco II, in 1460. In Florence meanwhile Bishop Angelo Acciaioli briefly governed the city after the fall of Gauthier de Brienne in 1343, and the later Acciaioli allied first with the Albizzi and then with the Medici, Laudomia Acciaioli marrying Pierfrancesco de' Medici. The house also produced scholars and churchmen, including the cardinal Angelo II and the humanist Donato Acciaioli.
zh: 阿恰约利家族是佛罗伦萨的贵族与银行世家，世系可追溯到12世纪；据传其先祖作为圭尔夫派信徒，为躲避腓特烈·巴巴罗萨而从布雷西亚逃到佛罗伦萨。13世纪他们创办的银行分行遍布希腊到西欧，1345年银行倒闭反而促使家族另谋出路。1331年被派往那不勒斯的尼科洛·阿恰约利后来官至王国大总管，受封梅尔菲、马耳他和戈佐伯爵，在摩里亚和科林斯广置领地，还庇护彼特拉克与薄伽丘，并在佛罗伦萨城外修建加尔鲁佐修道院。在希腊，家族更进一步问鼎王座：内里奥一世于1388年夺取雅典，成为雅典公爵；其间虽有威尼斯人短暂入主，家族仍从1402年起重掌公国，直到奥斯曼人征服希腊，末代公爵弗朗切斯科二世于1460年败亡。在佛罗伦萨本土，主教安杰洛·阿恰约利曾在1343年戈蒂埃·德·布里安倒台后短暂执政；后世族人先后与阿尔比齐和美第奇家族结盟，劳多米娅·阿恰约利便嫁给了皮耶尔弗朗切斯科·德·美第奇。家族还出了红衣主教安杰洛二世和人文主义学者多纳托等教会与学术人物。

en: The Adhémar, in full Adhémar de Monteil, were a noble house of the Valentinois on the lower Rhône, whose castles included Grignan, Montélimar and La Garde. Their first famous son was Adhémar de Monteil, bishop of Le Puy, whom Pope Urban II named apostolic legate of the First Crusade: he fought at Dorylaeum and carried the Holy Lance during the breakout at Antioch, before dying of illness in 1098. The family later supplied many clerics. Aymar Adhémar de Monteil de La Garde, son of Hugues, lord of Montélimar, became bishop of Metz in 1327; he feuded with the dukes of Lorraine, built the fortress of Château-Salins, stood with the city of Metz when Count Eberhard II of Württemberg besieged it in 1350, and witnessed the imperial assembly of 1356 that enlarged the Golden Bull. He made peace with Lorraine in 1358 and died at Metz in 1361. The ancient line continued through a female branch as the Castellane-Adhémar, counts of Grignan, into the seventeenth century.
zh: 阿代马尔家族全名阿代马尔·德蒙泰伊，是罗讷河下游瓦朗蒂努瓦的贵族世家，城堡包括格里尼昂、蒙特利马尔和拉加尔德。家族最早的名人是勒皮主教阿代马尔·德蒙泰伊，教宗乌尔班二世任命他为第一次十字军的宗座使节：他在多里莱乌姆作战，在安条克突围时高举圣枪，最终于1098年病逝。这个家族后来出过许多教士。蒙特利马尔领主于格之子艾马尔·阿代马尔·德蒙泰伊·德拉加尔格于1327年出任梅斯主教；他与洛林公爵长期争斗，修建了萨兰堡要塞，1350年符腾堡伯爵埃伯哈德二世围攻梅斯时与城市并肩作战，并在1356年扩充金玺诏书的帝国会议上担任见证人。他于1358年与洛林和解，1361年在梅斯去世。古老的男系后来通过女支延续为卡斯泰拉讷-阿代马尔家族，即格里尼昂伯爵，一直延续到17世纪。

en: The Adorno were an ancient patrician house of Genoa, first documented in 1186 and tracing their line from the merchant Barisone Adorno around 1212; trade along the Ligurian Riviera gave them the wealth on which their later power rested. After the Boccanegra they led the Ghibelline popular faction and, with their perennial rivals the Fregoso, dominated the age of the popular doges from 1339 to 1527. Gabriele Adorno became the first doge of the house in 1363: his rule saw commercial treaties with Cyprus, Aragon and Portugal and the strengthening of Genoese bases in the Crimea before a tax revolt drove him out in 1370. His kinsman Antoniotto I then held the dogate no fewer than four times between 1378 and 1396, and further Adorno doges followed in Giorgio, Raffaele, Barnaba and Prospero, while branches of the family spread to Bruges, Spain, Sicily and Germany. The last of the line to rule was Antoniotto II, doge from 1522 to 1527; when Andrea Doria reformed the Genoese constitution in 1528, the Adorno and Fregoso were deliberately shut out of power and absorbed into the Pinelli albergo, ending almost two centuries of rivalry over the republic.
zh: 阿多尔诺家族是热那亚古老的贵族世家，最早见于1186年的文书，世系通常从约1212年的商人巴里松·阿多尔诺算起；沿利古里亚海岸积累的商业财富，是他们日后掌权的根基。继博卡内格拉家族之后，他们领导吉伯林派的平民阵营，与世仇弗雷戈索家族轮流主导了1339至1527年的“平民总督”时代。加布里埃莱·阿多尔诺于1363年成为家族第一位总督，任内与塞浦路斯、阿拉贡和葡萄牙缔结商约，强化了热那亚在克里米亚的据点，最终却在1370年因抗税暴动被逐。其族人安东尼奥托一世随后在1378至1396年间四度出任总督，此后乔治、拉斐尔、巴尔纳巴和普罗斯佩罗也相继登位，家族支系还远播布鲁日、西班牙、西西里和德意志。最后一位执政的族人是1522至1527年任总督的安东尼奥托二世；1528年安德烈亚·多里亚改组热那亚政体时，阿多尔诺与弗雷戈索两族被刻意排除出权力层，并入皮内利家族会馆，这场持续近两个世纪的共和国之争就此落幕。

en: The Ahom dynasty was founded in 1228 by Sukaphaa, a Tai prince of Mong Mao in present-day Myanmar, who crossed the Patkai hills with some nine thousand followers into the Brahmaputra Valley and made Charaideo his capital in 1253. His descendants, bearing the royal title Chaopha or Swargadeo, built a wet-rice kingdom on the upper Brahmaputra that gradually absorbed the older Kamarupa lands and, through Ahomisation, turned incoming settlers into subjects of a multi-ethnic state. In 1337 the throne passed through the line of Sukhaangphaa and Sukhrangpha, who held the eastern valley while weaker neighbours surrounded them. Under Suhungmung in the sixteenth century the kingdom reached its greatest expansion and the elite began its long conversion from the old Ahom religion to Hinduism. The seventeenth century saw the dynasty repel repeated Mughal invasions: Mir Jumla sacked Garhgaon in 1662, but the Ahoms won the Battle of Saraighat in 1671 and after the Battle of Itakhuli in 1682 fixed their western frontier at the Manas River. Gadadhar Singha then founded the Tungkhungia branch, which ruled until the Moamoria rebellion shattered central authority after 1769. Burmese armies intervened from 1817, and the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826 handed Assam to the British East India Company, ending nearly six hundred years of Ahom rule.
zh: 阿洪姆王朝由苏卡法于1228年开创。他本是今缅甸境内勐卯的傣族王子，率约九千人越过帕特凯山脉进入布拉马普特拉河谷，于1253年定都查莱碉。其继承者以“昭法”或“斯瓦尔加代奥”为王号，在布拉马普特拉河上游建立起水稻农业王国，逐步吞并古迦摩缕波的旧地，并通过“阿洪姆化”把各地迁入者纳入一个多民族国家。1337年前后在位的是苏康法、苏杭法一系，扼守河谷东部，四邻皆为较弱的政权。16世纪苏洪蒙在位时王国版图达到极盛，统治精英也开始从阿洪姆传统信仰改宗印度教。17世纪王朝多次击退莫卧儿帝国的入侵：1662年米尔·朱姆拉攻陷加尔冈，1671年阿洪姆人在萨拉伊加特战役中取胜，1682年伊塔库利战役后西部边界定在玛纳斯河。其后加达达尔·辛哈建立通昆吉亚支系，统治到1769年摩亚马里亚叛乱爆发、中央权威崩溃为止。1817年起缅甸军队多次入侵，1826年《杨达波条约》将阿萨姆割让给英国东印度公司，近六百年的阿洪姆统治告终。

en: The Aisu, also written Aiso in old records, were a medieval seafaring warrior clan of the Kii and Ise region; their genealogy was claimed from the Takeda line of the Seiwa Genji, though one compilation traces them to Ichijō Tadayori. They were a maritime people and are said to have led a naval force in the Mongol Kōan campaign of 1281. The Ise branch held Gokasho Castle at Gokashoura and, under the sway of the Kitabatake, took part in the Muromachi shogunate's trade missions to Ming China from 1451 onward. The clan's most famous son was Aisu Hisatada, known as Ikōsai (1452-1538), a swordsman and military theorist who founded the Kage-ryū school after years of martial pilgrimage, by tradition including a voyage to Ming China; the great swordsman Kamiizumi Nobutsuna was counted among his disciples. His son Munemichi inherited the school and in 1564 entered the service of Satake Yoshishige in Hitachi. After the destruction of the Kitabatake the Aisu likewise served the Satake, adopted the surname Hirasawa, and when the Satake were transferred to Dewa after the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 the Kage-ryū head house moved north with them.
zh: 爱洲氏（古记录中亦写作“爱曾”）是中世纪活跃于纪伊、伊势一带的海上豪族，谱系传为清和源氏武田氏之后，《续群书类从》则以一条忠赖为其祖。该族与海运关系深厚，据说在1281年元军第二次来犯的弘安之役中曾率领水军参战。伊势爱洲氏以五所浦的五所城为本据，在北畠氏影响下统领水军，自1451年起参与室町幕府的遣明贸易。家族最著名的人物是爱洲久忠，号移香斋（1452—1538年），他历经诸国武者修行，据传还曾渡海前往明朝，最终开创剑术流派阴流，剑圣上泉信纲相传即其弟子。久忠之子小七郎宗通继承流派，于1564年出仕常陆的佐竹义重。北畠氏灭亡后，爱洲一族也投奔佐竹氏并改姓平泽；1600年关原之战后佐竹氏被移封出羽，阴流本家随之迁往北方。

en: The Akamatsu were a warrior clan of Harima Province, claiming Murakami Genji descent, who rose through the wars of the early fourteenth century. Their founder Norimura, also called Enshin, answered Prince Morinaga's call in the Genko War of 1331 and was made Constable of Harima under the Kenmu government; when the court turned against him he backed Ashikaga Takauji, and his defence of Shirahata Castle in Ako pinned down Nitta Yoshisada's army, helping to decide the Battle of Minatogawa in 1336. His son Norisuke served Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiakira and the shogunal deputy Hosokawa Yoriyuki, and sheltered the young Yoshimitsu, and the Akamatsu grew into shugo lords of Harima, Bizen and Mimasaka, one of the four houses eligible to head the Samurai Dokoro. Disaster struck in 1441, when Akamatsu Mitsusuke, resentful of Shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori's favour to rival branches, murdered the shogun at his own banquet in the Kakitsu Incident; a shogunal army led by Yamana Sozen overran Harima and Mitsusuke killed himself. The house revived after its retainers recovered the imperial jewel stolen by Southern Court partisans in 1457, and Masanori regained the three provinces through service to Hosokawa Katsumoto in the Onin War. Sengoku infighting then undid them: the deputy Uragami Muramune reduced the lords to puppets until he was destroyed in 1531, after which Amago and Miyoshi invasions and the rise of Oda Nobunaga left the Akamatsu a minor family. A last lord served Hideyoshi as a small holder, and the daimyo line ended on the losing side at Sekigahara in 1600.
zh: 赤松氏是播磨国的武家豪族，自称村上源氏后裔，在14世纪初的战乱中发迹。始祖则村（法名圆心）在1331年的元弘之乱中响应护良亲王的令旨率先举兵，建武新政时被任命为播磨守护；遭到新政冷遇后他转而投靠足利尊氏，凭赤穗白旗城拖住新田义贞的大军，为1336年凑川之战尊氏获胜立下大功。其子则祐辅佐足利义诠与管领细川赖之，还曾庇护年幼的足利义满，赤松家由此成为领有播磨、备前、美作三国的守护大名，跻身有资格出任侍所长官的四家之列。1441年大祸临头：赤松满佑因不满将军足利义教优待庶流，在嘉吉之乱中于自家宴席上刺杀义教，山名持丰（宗全）率领的幕府军随即攻灭播磨，满佑自尽。1457年赤松遗臣在长禄之变中夺回被南朝劫走的神玺，家名得以复兴，政则在应仁之乱中依附细川胜元，重新拿回三国守护之职。然而战国的下克上很快将其吞噬：守护代浦上村宗架空主家，直到1531年才被讨灭，此后尼子、三好相继入侵，织田信长崛起后赤松家沦为小族，末任当主则房以一万石侍奉丰臣秀吉，其大名世系最终在1600年关原之战因站错阵营而断绝。

en: The Akana of Izumo were a branch of the Sawa clan of Iwami, a house claiming descent from the Heian scholar Miyoshi no Kiyoyuki. Early in the Nanboku-chō wars the Sawa drove out the Ki family who held Akana manor in Iishi District and extended their lands across Iwami and Izumo; Sawa Sanetsura's second son Tsunetsura was made steward of the manor, and in the time of Sawa Hiroyuki the line took the place-name Akana as his surname. In the Muromachi period the house served the Kyōgoku shugo and built up its rule over the manor with shogunal backing, usually taking the field alongside the Sawa main house. In 1518 the Akana swore allegiance to Amago Tsunehisa, who had seized power from the Kyōgoku, while the Sawa main house chose the Ōuchi, splitting the kindred just as their lands, a strategic crossroads, became a battlefield between the two powers. During the Ōuchi counterstroke after the Amago defeat at Yoshida-Kōriyama in 1540–41, Ōuchi Yoshitaka besieged Akana Castle in 1542; the head Mitsukiyo held it for two months with Amago help and slew Kumagai Naitsugu before falling to the troops of Sue Takafusa, whereupon his father Hisakiyo surrendered the castle. His two elder sons, who had sided with the Ōuchi, both died within two years, one in battle in Chikuzen and the other by his own hand, leaving his third son Morikiyo as head, favoured by Amago Haruhisa; when Mōri Motonari invaded in 1562 Morikiyo surrendered at once and led the vanguard against Gassan-Toda. The Akana then served the Mōri and the Kikkawa, fighting in Korea, until Motoyoshi abandoned the surname in 1599 for Nakagawa, under which the family lived on as Chōshū retainers.
zh: 赤穴氏是石见国人佐波氏的分家，而佐波氏自称是平安时代汉学者三善清行的后裔。南北朝初期，佐波氏把势力扩入出云，追讨了领有饭石郡赤穴庄的纪氏庄园领主，获得横跨石见、出云的领地；佐波实连的次男常连就任赤穴庄地头，到佐波弘行时取地名为姓，改称赤穴氏，石见佐波氏是其主家。室町时代，赤穴氏从属出云守护京极氏，借守护与足利将军的权威确立了对赤穴庄的支配，历次战事多与主家佐波氏共同上阵。1518年，赤穴氏向以下克上崛起的尼子经久宣誓效忠，主家佐波氏却跟随大内氏，两家就此分道扬镳；地处交通要冲的赤穴庄也随之成为周防大内氏与出云尼子氏争霸的战场。1540—1541年尼子氏攻打吉田郡山城失败后大内氏展开反攻，1542年大内义隆围攻赤穴城，当主赤穴光清得尼子援兵坚守两月，阵斩熊谷直续，最终自己也被陶隆房的部下讨杀，其父久清开城投降。光清的两个儿子诠清、定清分属大内、尼子两方，两年内一个战死筑前、一个忧惧自害，三子盛清继任家督并受尼子晴久重用。1562年毛利元就攻进出云，赤穴城首当其冲，盛清未作大的抵抗便告降服，还作为毛利军先手参加了第二次月山富田城之战。此后赤穴氏作为毛利家臣跟随吉川元春转战，其后人元奇参加了文禄庆长之役，却在1599年放弃赤穴旧姓、改姓中川，以长州藩士的身份度过了江户时代。

en: The Aki were local lords who ruled Aki district in eastern Tosa on Shikoku. Tradition makes them descendants of Soga no Akae, exiled to Tosa after backing Prince Ōtomo in the Jinshin War of 672, though other accounts give them Tachibana ancestry. The Tale of the Heike already names an Aki district chief Saneyasu, whose son Sanemitsu drowned alongside Taira no Noritsune at the battle of Dannoura in 1185. The clan grew strong in the Muromachi period under the Hosokawa, governors of Tosa, and expanded into Kami district; after heavy losses in the Ōnin War it recovered to rank among the seven great houses of Tosa, rated at five thousand kan of income and called Aki of the five thousand kan. In 1526 it defeated the neighbouring Kōsokabe, and under Aki Kunitora it married into the Ichijō house and reached its height. Kunitora's raids on the lands of Chōsokabe Motochika opened a feud; in 1569 the Aki army was crushed at the Yaryūgawa battle, and after disloyal retainers opened Aki Castle to the enemy, Kunitora killed himself and the clan was destroyed, its lands granted to Motochika's brother Kōsokabe Chikayasu.
zh: 安艺氏是统治四国土佐东部安艺郡的国人领主。传说其祖先是在672年壬申之乱中追随大友皇子、兵败后被流放土佐的苏我赤兄，也有说法称其出自橘氏。《平家物语》已提到安艺郡大领实康，其子实光在1185年坛之浦之战中随平教经投海而死。室町时代，安艺氏在土佐守护细川氏麾下势力壮大，一度向香美郡扩张；应仁之乱中连遭重创后再度复兴，跻身土佐七雄，领有五千贯俸禄，号称安艺五千贯。1526年安艺氏击败邻近的香宗我部氏，到安艺国虎时又与名门土佐一条氏联姻，达到全盛。国虎入侵长宗我部元亲的领地，两家结怨；1569年安艺军在矢流川合战中惨败，谱代家臣又内应打开安艺城，国虎自尽，安艺氏就此灭亡，旧领被封给元亲之弟香宗我部亲泰。

en: The Akizuki were a warrior house of Chikuzen province in northern Kyushu, seated at Akizuki in Asakura district. Their original surname was Ōkura: tradition derives them from a Later Han prince naturalized in Japan, and their ancestor Ōkura no Haruzane was rewarded with the Harada estate in Chikuzen for helping suppress the Fujiwara no Sumitomo revolt in the tenth century, after which the house called itself Harada. Harada Taneo, who had fought for the Taira in the Genpei War, settled at Akizuki around 1203 and took that name. In the wars after the Kamakura collapse the Akizuki fought for the imperial court at Tatarahama against Ashikaga Takauji, and in the Sengoku period they passed from Shōni to Ōuchi and then Ōtomo overlordship. In 1557 the lord Fumitaka turned to the Mōri and was killed with his heir by an Ōtomo army, all but destroying the house; his second son Tanezane restored it under Mōri protection and later allied with the Shimazu, building a domain estimated at three hundred and sixty thousand koku across Chikuzen, Chikugo and Buzen. In 1587 Tanezane submitted to Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyushu army, surrendered his ancestral lands and was moved to Takanabe in Hyūga with thirty thousand koku, where the family survived as daimyo of Takanabe domain after Akizuki Tanenaga's timely change of sides at Sekigahara in 1600.
zh: 秋月氏是九州北部筑前国的武家，本据在朝仓郡秋月。其本姓为大藏，相传始祖是归化日本的后汉王族后裔，先祖大藏春实在10世纪平定藤原纯友之乱中立功，受封筑前御笠郡原田，一度称原田氏。原田种雄曾在源平合战中为平家作战，约于1203年入居秋月并改姓秋月。镰仓幕府灭亡后的战乱中，秋月氏在多多良滨之战中属宫方，迎战足利尊氏，兵败而归。战国时代，秋月氏先后从属于少贰氏、大内氏和大友氏；1557年当主文种倒向毛利氏，与嫡子晴种一同被大友军攻杀，家族一度灭亡。次子种实逃奔毛利氏并在其庇护下复兴，后又联合岛津氏扩张势力，极盛时据有筑前六郡、筑后四郡和丰前一郡，估计达三十六万石。1587年种实向丰臣秀吉的九州大军投降，献出本领，被移封日向高锅，领三万石；1600年关原之战时秋月种长及时倒向东军，封地得到安堵，秋月氏此后以高锅藩主的身份延续至整个江户时代。

en: The Al-Abed were the local ruling family of Gafsa, the chief oasis town of the Djerid in southwestern Ifriqiya. In the Middle Ages the Djerid oases grew rich on trans-Saharan caravan trade and often stood apart under Ibadi leaders, so that under loose Hafsid overlordship a local house such as the Al-Abed could hold the town largely autonomously.
zh: 阿贝德家族是伊夫里奇亚西南部杰里德地区首要绿洲城镇加夫萨的地方统治家族。中世纪时，杰里德诸绿洲靠撒哈拉商队贸易致富，常在伊巴德派领袖治下自成一体；在哈夫斯王朝松散的宗主权下，阿贝德这样的地方家族得以高度自治地掌管该城。

en: The Al 'Ali were a Bedouin ruling house of the Banu Rabi'ah, a branch of the Tayy, and a junior line of the great Al Fadl tribe, being the descendants of Ali ibn Haditha. They held the rich Ghouta oasis around Damascus, where their seat at Qutayfa lay, together with the northern Arabian oases of Tayma and al-Jawf, and under the later Ayyubids Ali and his son Abu Bakr held the office of amir al-arab, commander of the Bedouin. When the Mamluks took Syria in 1260, the office passed to their Al Fadl kinsman Isa ibn Muhanna; Abu Bakr's brother Zamil revolted in protest, was defeated and imprisoned in Cairo, while Abu Bakr's son Muhammad briefly presided over the emirate in the early 1290s. Driven from the Hauran by the rival Al Mira in the mid-thirteenth century and overshadowed by their Al Fadl cousins in the central steppe, the Al Ali nonetheless remained a power of the Damascus countryside, and a fifteenth-century estimate still credited them with two thousand horsemen.
zh: 阿里家族是贝都因名门，属于塔伊部的巴努·拉比阿，又是大法德勒部落的支系，为阿里·伊本·哈迪塞的后裔。他们占据大马士革富庶的古塔绿洲，库泰法的驻地就在这一带，并领有阿拉伯半岛北部的泰马和焦夫绿洲；阿尤布王朝末期，阿里与其子阿布·伯克尔先后担任统辖贝都因人的阿拉伯人异密一职。1260年马穆鲁克人夺取叙利亚后，该职转入法德勒支族人伊萨·伊本·穆汉纳之手，阿布·伯克尔之弟扎米勒愤而反叛，战败后被囚于开罗，阿布·伯克尔之子穆罕默德则在13世纪90年代初短暂接管异密公署。13世纪中叶，敌对的米拉部把他们赶出哈夫兰，中部草原上又有法德勒本支相形见绌；尽管如此，阿里家族仍是大马士革乡郊的一大势力，15世纪的一份估算仍称他们能出动两千骑兵。

en: The Āl Faḍl were the leading Bedouin dynasty of the Syrian Desert, a branch of the Banu Rabiʿah from the great Banu Tayy tribe. Their forebear Faḍl ibn Rabiʿah is recorded as an emir by 1107, and the family first rose by supplying mounted auxiliaries to the Burid and Zengid rulers of Damascus in their wars against the Crusaders. The Ayyubids gave them the office of amir al-ʿarab, commander of the Bedouin tribes of northern Syria, and after the Mamluk conquest of Syria in 1260 the emir Isa ibn Muhanna made it hereditary in his line, holding fiefs at Salamiyah and, from 1281, Palmyra. Isa led the tribal right wing to victory at the Second Battle of Homs in 1281 against the Ilkhanate; his sons Muhanna and Faḍl then kept the office through much of the fourteenth century, veering between the Mamluks and the Mongols but standing high in the favour of Sultan an-Nasir Muhammad. Weakened by internal feuds in the late Mamluk period, the Āl Faḍl kept their hereditary emirate under the Ottomans, until in the mid-sixteenth century their leading house merged with the Mawali and became known as Al Abu Risha, while a rival branch retained the Āl Faḍl name in the Beqaa Valley.
zh: 法德勒家族是叙利亚沙漠首屈一指的贝都因王朝，出自大部落巴努·塔伊的巴努·拉比厄支系。其先祖法德勒·伊本·拉比厄在1107年已见载为埃米尔，家族最初因向大马士革的布里德和赞吉统治者提供骑兵辅助部队、参与对十字军的战争而兴起。阿尤布王朝授予他们阿拉伯埃米尔一职，即北叙利亚诸贝都因部落的统帅；1260年马穆鲁克征服叙利亚后，埃米尔伊萨·伊本·穆罕纳使该职位在本家族世袭，领有塞莱米耶，并于1281年起领有泰德穆尔。1281年第二次霍姆斯战役中，伊萨率部落骑兵组成右翼击败伊儿汗国；他的儿子穆罕纳和法德勒此后在14世纪大部分时间里世袭此职，在马穆鲁克与蒙古人之间摇摆，却深受苏丹纳绥尔·穆罕默德宠信。马穆鲁克后期家族因内斗衰落，奥斯曼人仍保留其世袭埃米尔之位；16世纪中叶，其主支并入马瓦利部落，改称阿布·里沙家族，另一支竞争者则在贝卡谷地沿用法德勒之名。

en: The Al Mira were the leading Bedouin dynasty of the Hauran in southern Syria, a branch of the Banu Rabi'ah of the Tayy with roots reaching back to the Jarrahid emirs of the eleventh century. Their ancestor Mira and his brother Fadl served the Damascus atabegs against the Crusaders, and after the Mamluk conquest the emir Ahmad ibn Hajji, recognized by Sultan Baybars, made his tribe the muluk al-arab, or kings of the Bedouin, of the Hauran and Transjordan, driving the Al Fadl out of the region and raiding as far as Najd and the Hejaz. Baybars allowed the Al Mira virtual independence from the amir al-arab, and a decree of 1333 charged their emir with policing the tribes, guarding the desert frontier and the Hajj routes and supplying fine horses. Around 1389 Anqa ibn Shati joined the revolt of the Mamluk emir Mintash against Sultan Barquq and was killed by the Assassins soon after. During Timur's invasion of 1400 to 1401 the tribe seized the Hauran grain harvest, provoking a Mamluk raid on their camp at Suwayda. Still led by their emir Janbay when the Ottomans conquered Syria in 1516, the Al Mira were soon eclipsed in the Hauran by the rising Sardiyya tribe.
zh: 米拉家族是南叙利亚哈夫兰首屈一指的贝都因王朝，属塔伊部的巴努·拉比阿支系，渊源可追溯到11世纪的贾拉家族异密。其先祖米拉与兄弟法德勒曾为大马士革的阿塔贝格效力，抗击十字军；马穆鲁克征服后，异密艾哈迈德·伊本·哈吉得到苏丹拜伯尔斯承认，使本族成为哈夫兰和外约旦的阿拉伯人之王，即贝都因诸王，把法德勒部逐出该地区，兵锋甚至远及内志和汉志。拜伯尔斯准许米拉部几乎不受阿拉伯人异密节制；1333年的一道苏丹敕令规定，其异密负有约束部落、守卫沙漠边境和朝觐道路、进献良马等职责。约1389年，安盖·伊本·沙提加入马穆鲁克异密明塔什反对苏丹巴尔库克的叛乱，不久便被阿萨辛派杀死。1400至1401年帖木儿入侵期间，该部夺取哈夫兰的粮收，招致马穆鲁克军队突袭其苏韦达营地。1516年奥斯曼人征服叙利亚时，他们仍在异密詹贝率领之下，但不久便在哈夫兰被兴起的萨尔迪耶部落盖过。

en: The degli Albizzi were a Florentine patrician house that came to the city from Arezzo in the twelfth century and built its fortune on wool, finance and land, dominating the Arte della Lana guild and trading as far afield as Venice, Flanders and England. In the faction fights of the 1360s they led the patrician party against the Ricci, and after the upheaval of the Ciompi revolt Tommaso, known as Maso degli Albizzi, emerged in 1382 as the head of a narrow oligarchy of wealthy families that ruled Florence for half a century; he rolled back the reforms of the Ciompi era and organised the conquest of Pisa in 1406. His son Rinaldo inherited the leadership but wasted resources on a war against Lucca and turned the Medici into mortal enemies: in 1433 he secured the banishment of Cosimo de' Medici, yet when Cosimo returned in 1434 the Signoria exiled Rinaldo instead, and he died in Ancona in 1442 after conspiring with Milan. Not every Albizzi fell with him, for his brother Luca had sided with the Medici, stayed in Florence and rose to Gonfaloniere of Justice in 1442. The house later produced the Lutheran convert Antonio, the Inquisition cardinal Francesco and Giovanna degli Albizzi Tornabuoni, immortalised in the portraits of Ghirlandaio.
zh: 德利·阿尔比齐家族是12世纪从阿雷佐迁入佛罗伦萨的贵族世家，靠羊毛、放贷和地产发家，长期把持羊毛行会，贸易远及威尼斯、佛兰德和英格兰。14世纪60年代的党派斗争中，他们率领贵族派对抗里奇家族；梳毛工起义的动荡过后，托马索（人称马索）·德利·阿尔比齐于1382年成为少数豪门寡头政权的首脑，统治佛罗伦萨达半个世纪。他废除了梳毛工时代的平权改革，并策划了1406年对比萨的征服。其子里纳尔多继任领袖，却在对卢卡的战争中空耗国力，又把美第奇家族逼成死敌：1433年他成功放逐科西莫·德·美第奇，但1434年科西莫卷土重来，执政团反将里纳尔多流放；他随后勾结米兰密谋起事，1442年死于安科纳。不过家族并非一同覆灭：其弟卢卡始终站在美第奇一边，得以留在佛罗伦萨，1442年升任正义旗手。后世族人中还有改宗路德宗的安东尼奥、出任宗教裁判所枢机的弗朗切斯科，以及被吉兰达约绘入名画的乔瓦娜·德利·阿尔比齐·托尔纳博尼。

en: The House of Albon, also called the Guigonides after the many counts named Guigues, was a great feudal family of the county of Vienne in the Dauphiné, first recorded at the town of Albon in the tenth century and raised to comital rank in the eleventh. From their castle of Albon they built up a compact principality between the Rhône and the Alps, and Count Guigues IV, who died in 1142, bore the nickname Dauphin, the Dolphin, which hardened into the title Dauphin of Viennois for his successors and gave the region its later name of Dauphiné. The senior line ended in 1228 with Béatrice of Albon, whose marriage carried the dauphinate to the Capetian dukes of Burgundy. A younger branch meanwhile ruled the county of Forez and survived until 1372, while the Beaujeu branch lasted into the seventeenth century. The last Burgundian dauphin, Humbert II, sold the Dauphiné, under financial pressure, to Philip VI of Valois by the treaty of Romans in 1349, after which the title passed to the eldest sons of the kings of France.
zh: 阿尔邦家族又名吉格家族，因多位伯爵取名吉格而得名，是多菲内维埃纳伯国的大封建家族，10世纪已见于阿尔邦镇的记载，11世纪取得伯爵头衔。他们以阿尔邦城堡为中心，在罗讷河与阿尔卑斯山之间建起一片紧凑的领地；1142年去世的吉格四世伯爵绰号“海豚”，这个绰号后来固定为其继承人“维埃努瓦多菲纳”的头衔，该地区也由此得名多菲内。长支于1228年因阿尔邦的贝阿特丽斯而绝嗣，她的婚姻把多菲纳领地并入卡佩系的勃艮第公爵一系。旁支则统治福雷伯国，延续到1372年，博热支更一直传到17世纪。末代勃艮第系多菲纳安贝尔二世因财政困窘，于1349年依《罗芒条约》把多菲内卖给瓦卢瓦的腓力六世，此后这一头衔由法国国王的长子世代承袭。

en: The Álvarez de Albornoz were a Castilian hidalgo family from the mountains of Cuenca, holders of the lordship of Albornoz. Garci Álvarez de Albornoz, the fourth lord, served as tutor to the future Alfonso XI and married into the Carrillo family, and their son Gil was born at Carrascosa del Campo around the end of 1302. Educated in canon law at Toulouse, Gil became Archbishop of Toledo in 1338 and showed himself as much a soldier as a churchman: he fought the Marinid invasion at the Battle of Río Salado in 1340 and led the armed levy of his archbishopric at the capture of Algeciras in 1344. Made a cardinal in 1350, he left Castile after Alfonso XI's death and entered papal service. From 1353 Pope Innocent VI sent him as legate to Italy, where his mercenary campaigns reconquered most of the Papal States and his Constitutiones Sanctae Matris Ecclesiae regulated their government until 1816. He crowned his career by founding the College of Saint Clement for Iberian students at Bologna in 1364, and died in 1367 after Pope Urban V named him legate at Bologna. The family lordship passed to later generations of the house, while its fame in this age rested almost entirely on the cardinal.
zh: 阿尔瓦雷斯·德·阿尔沃诺斯是卡斯蒂利亚昆卡山区的伊达尔戈贵族家族，世袭阿尔沃诺斯领主权。第四代领主加尔西·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·阿尔沃诺斯曾任后来的阿方索十一世的导师，并与卡里略家族联姻；他们的儿子希尔于1302年底前后生于卡拉斯科萨德尔坎波。希尔在图卢兹攻读教会法，1338年出任托莱多大主教，同时展现出不亚于教士的军事才能：1340年在萨拉多河战役抗击马林王朝入侵，1344年又率大主教区武装参加攻占阿尔赫西拉斯。1350年他升任枢机主教，阿方索十一世死后离开卡斯蒂利亚，转任教廷职务。1353年起，教宗英诺森六世派他以特使身份前往意大利，他率领雇佣军征战，收复了教皇国的大部分领土，其颁布的《圣母教会宪章》规范教皇国行政，一直沿用到1816年。1364年他在博洛尼亚创办面向伊比利亚学生的圣克莱门特学院，1367年获教宗乌尔班五世任命为驻博洛尼亚特使，不久后去世。家族的领主之位由后代承袭，但这个时代家族的名望几乎全系于这位枢机一身。

en: The House of d'Albret took its name from the lordship of Albret, present-day Labrit in the Landes of Gascony, where the family was already established in the ninth century. As great vassals of the English-held duchy of Aquitaine, the Albrets controlled wide lands in the Landes and at first supported the English cause when the Hundred Years' War began, then transferred their allegiance to the kings of France, whose grants of land and office steadily enlarged their power. Arnaud Amanieu, Lord of Albret, helped the French reconquer Guienne, and his son Charles d'Albret became constable of France and was killed commanding the French army at Agincourt in 1415. In 1470 the family inherited the County of Périgord and the viscounty of Limoges, and Alain the Great, who died in 1522, for a time hoped to marry the heiress of Brittany. Alain's son John became King of Navarre in 1484 by marrying Queen Catherine of Foix, but the Spanish invasion of 1512 left the Albrets with only Lower Navarre north of the Pyrenees. The last of the line, Jeanne d'Albret, Queen of Navarre, married Anthony of Bourbon and was the mother of Henry IV, who carried the Albret inheritance into the French crown.
zh: 德·阿尔布雷家族得名于阿尔布雷领地，即今天加斯科涅朗德省的拉布里，早在9世纪家族便已定居于此。作为英格兰治下阿基坦公国的大封臣，阿尔布雷家族在朗德拥有广阔领地，百年战争爆发之初一度支持英格兰一方，随后转而效忠法兰西国王，并靠法王不断封赏的土地与官职壮大势力。阿尔布雷领主阿尔诺·阿马尼厄协助法军收复吉耶讷，其子夏尔·德·阿尔布雷出任法兰西王室统帅，1415年在阿金库尔战役中指挥法军时战死。1470年家族继承了佩里戈尔伯国和利摩日子爵领，1522年去世的“伟人”阿兰曾一度希望迎娶布列塔尼女继承人。阿兰之子让于1484年娶纳瓦拉女王富瓦的卡特琳，成为纳瓦拉国王；但1512年西班牙入侵后，阿尔布雷家族只保住了比利牛斯山以北的下纳瓦拉。家族末代成员纳瓦拉女王让娜·德·阿尔布雷嫁给波旁的安托万，生下亨利四世，阿尔布雷的遗产也随之并入法兰西王冠。

en: The Alidosi were a noble family of Romagna, originating in the Santerno valley, who built their power around the city of Imola. In the thirteenth century they backed the Guelphs in the wars against the Ghibellines, and Lippo I Alidosi held Imola as de facto lord from 1278. In 1341 Pope Benedict XII enfeoffed Lippo II Alidosi with the city as pontifical vicar, beginning a formal signoria that passed through Roberto, Azzo and Bertrando Alidosi. The family lost Imola in 1424 when Filippo Maria Visconti of Milan seized the city, and withdrew to the Apennine lordship of Castel del Rio. Its most famous later member was Cardinal Francesco Alidosi, a councillor of Pope Julius II, who was accused of treason and murdered in 1511 by men of the Duke of Urbino. The Alidosi held Castel del Rio until 1638, when Pope Urban VIII drove them out.
zh: 阿利多西家族是罗马涅的贵族世家，发源于萨泰尔诺河谷，以伊莫拉城为中心建立势力。13世纪圭尔夫派与吉伯林派争斗时，他们支持圭尔夫派，利波一世·阿利多西从1278年起成为伊莫拉的实际领主。1341年，教宗本笃十二世将伊莫拉作为教宗代理人封地授予利波二世，正式开启家族的领主统治，此后历经罗伯托、阿佐和贝尔特拉多·阿利多西。1424年，米兰的菲利波·马里亚·维斯孔蒂攻占伊莫拉，家族退入亚平宁山区的卡斯特尔德尔里奥领地。家族后来最著名的成员是枢机主教弗朗切斯科·阿利多西，他是教宗儒略二世的谋臣，被控叛国后于1511年被乌尔比诺公爵的随从杀死。阿利多西家族据守卡斯特尔德尔里奥直到1638年，最终被教宗乌尔班八世逐走。

en: The Almohad dynasty, also called the Mu'minids, ruled a Berber caliphate from Marrakesh. It grew out of the preaching of Ibn Tumart, a Masmuda Berber recognized as the Mahdi around 1121, who built his base at Tinmel in the Atlas Mountains and denounced the Almoravids as impious.
