en: The Wākea dynasty represents the Aliʻi nui, the high chiefs of the island of Molokaʻi, who like the rulers of the other Hawaiian islands claimed descent from Wākea, the sky father of Hawaiian religion. With the earth mother Papahānaumoku, Wākea was held to have fathered the islands and the whole aliʻi nobility. The remembered early chiefs of Molokaʻi include Kamauaua, Keʻoloʻewa and the female rulers Kapau-a-Nuʻakea and Hualani. A small island, Molokaʻi carried little weight in the wars between Maui, Oʻahu, Kauaʻi and Hawaiʻi, and its court mattered chiefly through marriage alliances and the fame of its kahuna priests and sorcery. From the late 1600s it was repeatedly raided by its stronger neighbours, and in the later 1700s it was fully absorbed by the Maui kingdom of Kahekili II before the unification of the islands under Kamehameha I.
zh: 瓦凯亚王朝即莫洛凯岛的高级酋长“阿利伊努伊”世系。与夏威夷其他岛屿的统治者一样，莫洛凯酋长自称源自夏威夷宗教中的天神瓦凯亚：相传他与大地之母帕帕哈瑙莫库生育了诸岛和整个阿利伊贵族阶层。流传下来的早期莫洛凯酋长包括卡马瓦阿、凯奥洛埃瓦，以及女性统治者卡保-阿-努阿凯亚和华拉尼。莫洛凯岛小势弱，在毛伊、瓦胡、考艾和夏威夷诸岛的争雄中无足轻重，其王室主要靠联姻以及祭司“卡胡纳”的巫术名望维持影响。17世纪末起，它屡遭强邻进攻，到18世纪后期被卡赫基利二世的毛伊王国完全吞并，此后诸岛又在卡美哈梅哈一世治下统一。

en: The Walashma were a Muslim dynasty of the Horn of Africa that ruled the Sultanate of Ifat and later the Adal Sultanate. They rose in the thirteenth century in eastern Shewa: in 1278 they invaded the neighboring Makhzumi Sultanate of Shewa and annexed it, and in 1288 Sultan Wali Asma conquered Hubat and Adal, making Ifat the strongest Muslim power of the region. Their long contest with the Christian Solomonic emperors began in 1332, when Haqq ad-Din I was killed fighting Amda Seyon I, who installed client Walashma princes in his place. In 1403 the last Ifat sultan, Sa'ad ad-Din II, was hunted down and killed at the port of Zeila; his sons fled to Yemen and returned in 1415, when Sabr ad-Din III founded a new sultanate of Adal with its seat at Dakkar and later Harar. Sultans such as Badlay kept the wars with Ethiopia alive, though by the late fifteenth century real power was passing to emirs and imams such as Mahfuz. Under the Walashma flag the imam Ahmed Gran conquered most of Abyssinia in the 1530s before his death in 1543, and in 1577 the court moved from Harar to Aussa, where the sultanate was reorganized as an imamate and the Walashma line ended.
zh: 瓦拉什马王朝是非洲之角的穆斯林王朝，先后统治伊法特苏丹国和阿达尔苏丹国。它于13世纪在绍阿东部崛起：1278年入侵邻近的马赫祖米绍阿苏丹国并将其吞并，1288年苏丹瓦利·阿斯马又征服胡巴特和阿达尔，使伊法特成为当地最强的穆斯林政权。它与基督教所罗门王朝皇帝的长期较量始于1332年——哈格丁一世在与安达·塞永一世作战时被杀，后者转而扶植瓦拉什马族中的亲信封王。1403年，末代伊法特苏丹萨阿德丁二世被追兵围困在港口泽拉并遇害；他的儿子们逃往也门，1415年返回，萨巴尔·阿德丁三世在达卡尔、后来又在哈勒尔建立新的阿达尔苏丹国。巴德莱等苏丹继续与埃塞俄比亚交战，但到15世纪末，实权已落入马赫富兹等埃米尔和伊玛目手中。16世纪30年代，伊玛目艾哈迈德·格兰打着瓦拉什马的旗号攻占阿比西尼亚大半国土，最终于1543年败亡；1577年朝廷从哈勒尔迁往奥萨，苏丹国被改组为伊玛目国，瓦拉什马世系就此终结。

en: The counts of Waldeck sprang from the counts of Schwalenberg, whose ancestor Widekind I ruled early in the twelfth century. Waldeck Castle above the Eder in northern Hesse was first documented in 1120, and in 1180 Volkwin II of Schwalenberg gained it by marrying Luitgard, the Waldeck heiress; his branch then took the castle's name and assembled a small lordship around it. Originally a fief of the archbishopric of Mainz, the county won imperial immediacy in 1349. After Count Henry VI died in 1397 the family split into the Landau and Waldeck lines, and mounting debt together with Hesse's victory over Mainz in 1427 pushed both lines under Hessian overlordship in 1431 and 1438. A further partition in 1486 produced the Waldeck-Wildungen and Waldeck-Eisenberg branches, whose counts adopted Lutheranism in 1526 and 1529. The inheritance of the county of Pyrmont in 1626 gave the family its double name, and after the lines were reunited in 1692 the residence moved from Waldeck to Arolsen in 1655; princely rank followed in 1712.
zh: 瓦尔代克伯爵家族出自施瓦伦贝格伯爵世家，其始祖维德金德一世在12世纪初在位。北黑森埃德河畔的瓦尔代克城堡最早见于1120年的文献；1180年，施瓦伦贝格的福尔克温二世娶瓦尔代克女继承人卢特加德而得到城堡，他的支系便以城堡为姓，并在周围拼起一块小小的领地。伯国本是美因茨大主教区的封地，1349年取得帝国直辖地位。1397年伯爵亨利六世去世后，家族分裂为兰道和瓦尔代克两支；由于债台高筑，加上黑森在1427年战胜美因茨，两支分别于1431年和1438年沦为黑森的附庸。1486年再度分家，产生瓦尔代克-维尔东根与瓦尔代克-艾森贝格两支，两支伯爵先后在1526年和1529年改宗路德宗。1626年家族继承皮尔蒙特伯国，从此冠以双姓；1692年各支重新统一，而早在1655年居所已从瓦尔代克迁至阿罗尔森，1712年家族又获得诸侯爵位。

en: The Wang were the royal house of Goryeo, founded in 918 when Wang Geon, a regional lord of Songak, present-day Kaesong, overthrew the tyrant Gung Ye of Taebong and took the throne as King Taejo. He went on to absorb Silla and conquer Later Baekje, uniting the Later Three Kingdoms, and his descendants ruled from Kaesong for 474 years. From 1170 to 1270 the kings were puppets of the Goryeo military regime; after its fall the house chose vassalage to the Mongols, and under the Yuan dynasty the kings married Borjigin princesses while one of them, King Chungseon, was also enfeoffed as Prince of Shenyang. King Gongmin shook off Yuan control and restored Goryeo's independence in 1356, but the Wihwado Retreat of 1388 let General Yi Seong-gye seize power, and in 1392 Yi proclaimed the Joseon dynasty, ending Wang rule. The new regime then hunted down the direct male line: from 1392 to 1413 more than a hundred royal Wangs were killed or driven into exile, and survivors hid under other surnames, so that the present-day Kaesong Wang clan traces mainly to a single surviving branch.
zh: 王氏是高丽的王室。918年，松岳（今开城）地方豪族王建推翻泰封暴君弓裔，登基为王，是为太祖；他随后吞并新罗、攻灭后百济，统一后三国，其子孙在开城统治了474年。1170年至1270年间，国王沦为武人政权的傀儡；武人政权倒台后，王室转而臣事蒙古，元朝时高丽国王世代迎娶孛儿只斤氏公主，忠宣王还曾受封沈阳王。1356年，恭愍王摆脱元朝控制、恢复高丽独立，但1388年威化岛回军后，大将李成桂掌握实权，并于1392年建立朝鲜王朝，王氏统治就此终结。新朝随即对王氏嫡系男丁展开清算：1392年至1413年间，一百余名王族被杀或被流放，幸存者或隐姓或改用母姓，后世的开城王氏主要出自仅存的一脉。

en: The de Warennes took their name from Varenne in Normandy and came to England with the Conquest: William de Warenne, a kinsman of William the Conqueror, fought at Hastings in 1066 and was created Earl of Surrey in 1088. From castles such as Lewes and Castle Acre the family ranked among the greatest Anglo-Norman magnates, and when the direct male line failed in the twelfth century its heiress Isabel married Hamelin, an illegitimate half-brother of Henry II, whose children took the Warenne name. John de Warenne, the sixth earl, was a leading commander in the early Scottish wars, and his daughter Isabel married King John Balliol of Scotland. The seventh and last earl, another John, was born in 1286 and spent his career in the wars and crises of Edward II and Edward III's reigns: he helped capture Piers Gaveston, turned against Thomas of Lancaster, and as guardian of Edward Balliol campaigned in Scotland, where Balliol named him Earl of Strathearn in name only. He died without legitimate issue in 1347, and the Warenne inheritance passed through his sister Alice to her son Richard FitzAlan, Earl of Arundel.
zh: 德·瓦伦家族以诺曼底的瓦伦村得名，随诺曼征服来到英格兰：家族始祖威廉·德·瓦伦是征服者威廉的亲族，1066年参战黑斯廷斯，1088年受封萨里伯爵。凭借刘易斯、阿克城堡等据点，该家族跻身盎格鲁-诺曼最显贵的大封臣之列。12世纪直系男丁断绝后，女继承人伊莎贝尔嫁给亨利二世的异母私生子哈姆林，其子女改用瓦伦姓氏。第六代伯爵约翰·德·瓦伦是苏格兰战争初期的重要统帅，其女伊莎贝尔嫁给苏格兰国王约翰·巴利奥尔。第七代、也是末代伯爵约翰生于1286年，一生辗转于爱德华二世和爱德华三世朝的战争与政争：他参与擒获皮尔斯·加维斯顿，转而反对兰开斯特伯爵托马斯；作为爱德华·巴利奥尔的监护人，他随军出征苏格兰，被巴利奥尔名义上封为斯特拉森伯爵。1347年他去世时无合法子嗣，瓦伦家产经其妹爱丽丝传给其子——阿伦德尔伯爵理查德·菲茨艾伦。

en: The Wareru dynasty ruled Hanthawaddy, the Mon kingdom of lower Burma, from its capital at Martaban and later Pegu. Its founder Wareru, born Ma Gadu to a poor family near Thaton, seized the governorship of Martaban in 1285 as the Pagan Empire collapsed, and with Sukhothai's backing declared independence in 1287. He and the Pegu warlord Tarabya crushed a Pagan invasion in 1295 and 1296, after which Wareru removed his ally and united the three Mon provinces of Bassein, Pegu and Martaban, winning recognition from Yuan China in 1298. He was assassinated in 1307, but the legal code he commissioned, the Wareru Dhammathat, shaped Burmese and Siamese law for centuries. At first a loose federation and nominal vassal of Sukhothai, the kingdom became fully independent in 1330, when Binnya E Law, the reigning king in 1337, took power. Razadarit, who ruled from 1384 to 1421, unified the Mon lands and held off Ava in the Forty Years' War. Hanthawaddy then entered its golden age under rulers such as the queen Shin Sawbu and Dhammazedi, growing rich on Indian Ocean trade and famous as a center of Theravada Buddhism, until Tabinshwehti of Taungoo conquered Pegu in 1539 and Martaban in 1541. A Mon restoration of 1740 revived the kingdom briefly before Alaungpaya destroyed Pegu in 1757.
zh: 伐丽流王朝统治着下缅甸的孟人王国汉达瓦底，先后以马达班和勃固为都。开国君主伐丽流本名马都，出身直通附近的贫寒家庭，在蒲甘帝国崩溃之际于1285年夺取马达班总督之位，并在素可泰支持下于1287年宣布独立。1295至1296年，他与勃固军阀多罗跋联手击溃蒲甘大军，随后除掉盟友，统一了勃生、勃固、马达班三个孟人省份，并于1298年获得元朝中国的承认。他于1307年遇刺身亡，但他下令编纂的《伐丽流法典》影响缅甸和暹罗法律达数百年之久。汉达瓦底起初是松散的城邦联盟、素可泰的名义属邦，1330年完全独立，1337年在位的频耶埃劳正是此时登位。1384至1421年在位的罗娑陀利统一孟人诸地，在四十年战争中抵挡住北方的阿瓦。此后汉达瓦底在信修浮女王、达摩悉提等明君治下进入黄金时代，靠印度洋贸易富甲一方，并成为上座部佛教重镇。1539年东吁的德彬瑞梯攻陷勃固，1541年马达班失守。1740年孟人起义一度复兴王国，但1757年雍笈牙焚毁勃固，复兴政权告终。

en: The Washizu were a cadet branch of the Ouchi house of Suo, a family of provincial officials who claimed descent from a prince of the Korean kingdom of Baekje. When Ouchi Morifusa became the strongest man in Suo in the late twelfth century, his third son Moriyasu received the Washizu manor in Tsuno district, the site of modern Kudamatsu, and took the Washizu name. Moriyasu's son Chikamori died without an heir, and his daughter the nun Zen'ei adopted Nagahiro, a son of the Ouchi main line. Nagahiro was made constable of Suo by Emperor Go-Daigo after the fall of the Kamakura shogunate in 1333 and kept the post under the Muromachi shogunate, ruling as a rival to the Ouchi head until the succession feuds of the Kannō Disturbance ended with the Washizu submitting to the main house in 1354. Reduced to senior retainers, Washizu Hirotada built Dainei-ji in 1410 and was appointed deputy constable of Nagato in 1432, holding Fukagawa Castle; but Ouchi Norihiro turned on him, and in 1448 the family was overthrown and Hirotada killed, after which Washizu lived on only as ordinary retainers of the Ouchi and later the Mori.
zh: 鹫头氏是周防大内氏的庶流，大内家本是地方在厅官人，自称祖先是百济国王子琳圣太子的后裔。12世纪末大内盛房成为周防最有实力者时，其三子盛保领有都浓郡鹫头庄（今下松市一带），遂以鹫头为苗字。盛保之子亲盛死后无嗣，其女禅惠尼从大内宗家迎养长弘为后继。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，后醍醐天皇任命鹫头长弘为周防守护，室町幕府成立后他仍保住此职，与大内宗家当主对立；观应之扰乱中的继嗣纷争最终以1354年鹫头氏臣服大内本家告终。此后鹫头家降为重臣，鹫头弘忠于1410年创建大宁寺，1432年出任长门守护代并修筑深川城；但大内教弘随即对他翻脸，1448年举兵攻灭鹫头氏，弘忠战死，其家族此后只以大内氏、后来的毛利氏家臣身分延续。

en: The House of Wassenberg, first documented in the eleventh century and seated at Wassenberg on the Lower Rhine, grew into one of the great dynasties of the Lower Rhineland. Its earliest known ancestors were the brothers Gerard and Rutger: Gerard's line kept Wassenberg while Rutger's descendants established themselves at Kleve, so the counts of both Guelders and Cleves sprang from this one house. In 1096 Gerard IV of Wassenberg became Gerard I, Count of Guelders, and his successor Gerard II married the heiress of Zutphen, joining the two halves of Hamaland. Through the twelfth and thirteenth centuries Guelders expanded along the Meuse, Rhine and IJssel and even claimed Limburg, until defeat at the Battle of Worringen in 1288 checked its ambitions. A younger kinsman had received Heinsberg in 1082, and the Falkenburg branch split from it in 1168; its Beatrice of Falkenburg married Richard of Cornwall, King of the Romans. In 1339 Reginald II was raised to Duke of Guelders, but his sons Reginald III and Edward fought each other, Edward imprisoning his brother, and both died without male heirs. In 1371 Edward's daughters and their husbands contended for the duchy, which ultimately passed through Maria of Guelders to the House of Jülich. The Cleves branch ended with Count John in 1368, when Cleves fell to the House of the Marck.
zh: 瓦森贝格家族11世纪起见于文献，以下莱茵的瓦森贝格为驻地，后来成长为下莱茵最重要的世家之一。可考的始祖是格拉尔德与鲁特格尔兄弟：格拉尔德一支持有瓦森贝格，鲁特格尔的后裔则在克莱沃立足，因此海尔德兰与克莱沃的伯爵同出这一家族。1096年，瓦森贝格的格拉尔德四世成为海尔德兰伯爵格拉尔德一世；继任者格拉尔德二世娶聚特芬女继承人为妻，把哈马兰的两半领地合为一体。12至13世纪，海尔德兰沿默兹河、莱茵河与艾瑟尔河扩张，甚至主张林堡的继承权，直到1288年沃林根战役失利才收敛野心。家族旁支于1082年受封海因斯贝格，1168年又分出法尔肯堡支，其成员法尔肯堡的贝阿特丽切嫁给了罗马人的国王康沃尔的理查。1339年，雷金纳德二世被擢升为海尔德兰公爵，但他的儿子雷金纳德三世与爱德华兄弟阋墙，爱德华囚禁了兄长，两人又都没有男嗣。1371年，爱德华的女儿们及其夫君争夺公国，最终经海尔德兰的玛利亚之手转入于利希家族。克莱沃支则在1368年伯爵约翰死后终结，克莱沃落入马克家族之手。

en: The House of Wedel is a German noble family from Stormarn in Holstein. Its line runs back to a monastery vogt named Heinrich, documented at Ottenbüttel in 1149, and three brothers called Heinricus, Hasso and Reimbernus de Wedele appear as witnesses in a charter of 1212. In 1306 a member of the family was captured after the second battle of Uetersen and broken on the wheel. The house spread into three branches, and in 1328 Emperor Louis IV enfeoffed the lords of Wedel with Küstrin, Falkenburg, Schievelbein, Neu-Wedel and other castles in the Brandenburg Neumark, which tied its fortunes to the Margraviate of Brandenburg. Hans von Wedel acted as a negotiator between the Teutonic Knights and Poland in 1444 and 1445. Later members included Lupold von Wedel, a travel writer and mercenary leader who died about 1615, and Gustav Wilhelm von Wedel, a Danish general who in 1684 received the Norwegian countship of Jarlsberg. An East Frisian branch built the Evenburg near Leer and inherited Schloss Gödens by marriage in 1746.
zh: 魏德尔家族是来自荷尔斯泰因施托尔曼的德意志贵族世家。其世系可追溯到1149年在奥滕比特尔见诸文献的修道院护域官海因里希；1212年，海因里库斯、哈索和赖因贝努斯·德·魏德尔三兄弟在一份特许状中以见证人身份出现。1306年，家族一名成员在第二次乌特森之战后被俘，遭车裂处死。该家族分为三支，1328年皇帝路易四世把屈斯特林、法尔肯堡、希尔费尔拜因、新魏德尔等勃兰登堡新马克的城堡封给魏德尔领主，使其命运与勃兰登堡藩侯国连在一起。1444至1445年，汉斯·冯·魏德尔曾在条顿骑士团与波兰之间充当谈判人。后来的家族名人有约1615年去世的旅行作家兼雇佣兵首领卢波尔德·冯·魏德尔，以及1684年获封挪威亚尔斯贝格伯爵领的丹麦将领古斯塔夫·威廉·冯·魏德尔。其东弗里斯兰支系在莱尔附近修建埃文堡，并于1746年通过联姻继承格登斯宫。

en: The Welfs began as a Franconian clan of the Meuse and Moselle country, kin to the Carolingians. When the elder line ended with Duke Welf III of Carinthia in 1055, his estates passed to his nephew Welf IV, son of the Margrave of Este, who became Duke of Bavaria in 1070 and founded the younger Welf-Este house. The family backed the papacy in the Investiture Controversy, which is why the pope's Italian partisans were called Guelphs after them. Under Henry the Lion, Duke of Saxony from 1142 and of Bavaria again from 1156, the house reached its medieval height: he founded Munich and Lübeck, made Brunswick his capital, and led the 1147 Wendish Crusade, but his breach with Frederick Barbarossa cost him both duchies in 1180. His son Otto IV, the only Welf to wear the imperial crown, was crowned in 1209 and ruined by defeat at Bouvines in 1214. In 1235 Otto the Child received the new Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg, and the partition of 1269 split it into Brunswick and Lüneburg lines, whose branches still ruled the Saxon principalities in 1337. A younger branch took Calenberg in 1635 and chose Hanover as its seat, gained the electoral dignity in 1692, and won the British throne with George I in 1714.
zh: 韦尔夫家族发源于默兹河与摩泽尔河流域的法兰克尼亚，与加洛林王室有亲缘。1055年克恩顿公爵韦尔夫三世去世，老支男系断绝，遗产传给外甥、埃斯特藩侯之子韦尔夫四世；他于1070年成为巴伐利亚公爵，开创了年轻的韦尔夫-埃斯特支系。家族在叙任权斗争中支持教宗，意大利的教宗党因而被称作“归尔甫派”，名字即源于韦尔夫。狮子亨利1142年起任萨克森公爵、1156年又收复巴伐利亚，家族势力达到中世纪顶峰：他兴建慕尼黑和吕贝克，立不伦瑞克为都城，还领导了1147年的文德十字军；但他与腓特烈·巴巴罗萨反目，1180年被剥夺两个公国。其子奥托四世是家族唯一登上帝位的人，1209年加冕，1214年布汶战败后一蹶不振。1235年，孩童奥托受封新设立的不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公国，1269年分家形成不伦瑞克和吕讷堡两支；1337年，其众多支系仍统治着萨克森境内的各邦。1635年，一支幼支取得卡伦贝格并以汉诺威为驻地，1692年获选帝侯尊位，1714年其主乔治一世登上英国王位。

en: The counts of Werdenberg were a Swabian noble house sprung from the counts of Montfort, and through them from the counts palatine of Tübingen: Hugo II of Tübingen had married the heiress of the last count of Bregenz and brought the family lands along the Alpine Rhine. In 1230 the Montfort inheritance was partitioned and the Werdenberg line took its name from Werdenberg castle above the Rhine, now in the Swiss canton of St. Gallen. Rudolf I's sons split the territory again, founding Werdenberg-Heiligenberg and Werdenberg-Sargans in 1260, and a further division followed in 1308. The branches held scattered counties spanning present-day St. Gallen, Liechtenstein and Vorarlberg; the Vaduz line expired in 1406 and Vaduz passed to the barons of Brandis. The Werdenberg feud with the von Zimmern family and other neighbours, which escalated in 1488, helped push Emperor Frederick III and Maximilian I toward the Swabian League and the Imperial Reforms. The last influential branch, Werdenberg-Heiligenberg-Sigmaringen-Trochtelfingen, died out in 1534.
zh: 韦尔登贝格伯爵是施瓦本贵族世家，出自蒙特福特伯爵，往上可溯至蒂宾根行宫伯爵：蒂宾根的胡戈二世娶了末代布雷根茨伯爵的女继承人，为家族带来阿尔卑斯莱茵河沿岸的土地。1230年蒙特福特遗产分家，韦尔登贝格一支以莱茵河畔的韦尔登贝格城堡得名，城堡今属瑞士圣加仑州。鲁道夫一世的儿子们再度瓜分领地，于1260年形成韦尔登贝格-海利根贝格和韦尔登贝格-萨尔甘斯两支，1308年又再分家。各支的伯国散布在今圣加仑、列支敦士登和福拉尔贝格一带；瓦杜兹支于1406年绝嗣，瓦杜兹转入布兰迪斯男爵之手。15世纪末，家族与齐默恩家族及邻邦的韦尔登贝格世仇在1488年激化，促使皇帝腓特烈三世和马克西米利安一世推动组建施瓦本联盟、开展帝国改革。最后一个有影响力的支系韦尔登贝格-海利根贝格-锡格马林根-特罗希特尔芬根于1534年绝嗣。

en: The House of Wettin, one of the oldest dynasties of the Holy Roman Empire, took its name from Wettin Castle on the Saale, acquired around the year 1000; its first documented ancestor, Theodoric I, died about 982. Around 1030 the family received the Saxon Eastern March as a fief, and in 1089 Emperor Henry IV invested it with the March of Meissen. The Wettins inherited the Landgraviate of Thuringia in 1263 and in 1423 were enfeoffed with Saxe-Wittenberg and the Saxon electoral dignity, which moved their centre of power from Meissen to Wittenberg. In 1485 the Treaty of Leipzig divided the family into the senior Ernestine and junior Albertine lines. The Ernestines kept the electorate until 1547 and led the early Reformation, with Elector Frederick the Wise protecting Martin Luther at Wittenberg; after the Schmalkaldic War the electorate passed to the Albertines, who ruled as electors and, from 1806, as kings of Saxony, and also supplied two kings of Poland between 1697 and 1763. The Ernestines retained a cluster of Thuringian duchies, and from their Saxe-Coburg cadet line came Leopold I, elected king of the Belgians in 1831.
zh: 韦廷家族是神圣罗马帝国最古老的王朝之一，得名于约1000年获得的萨勒河畔韦廷城堡；其有确切记载的始祖狄奥多里克一世约卒于982年。约1030年，家族受封萨克森东马克，1089年皇帝亨利四世又把迈森马克封给它。1263年韦廷家族继承图林根领地伯国，1423年受封萨克森—维滕贝格并取得萨克森选侯资格，权力中心也从迈森移到维滕贝格。1485年的《莱比锡条约》把家族分为长支恩斯特系和幼支阿尔布雷希特系。恩斯特系保有选侯位至1547年，并在宗教改革早期站在新教一边：选侯“智者”腓特烈把马丁·路德保护在维滕贝格；施马尔卡尔登战争后选侯位转入阿尔布雷希特系之手，该支此后出任萨克森选侯并于1806年成为萨克森国王，还在1697至1763年间出过两位波兰国王。恩斯特系则保有图林根的一群小公国，其萨克森—科堡支系的利奥波德一世于1831年当选比利时国王。

en: The lords of Wiltz, later counts, were one of the oldest noble families of Luxembourg, seated above the Wiltz river in the Ardennes. Amadeus of Wiltz attended the wedding of Countess Ermesinde of Luxembourg in 1214, and Walther of Wiltz fought for the duke of Brabant at the Battle of Worringen in 1288. In the thirteenth century the family built a fortified castle on a rocky spur above the town, from which younger branches went on to hold Beaufort, Bereldange and Meysembourg. Godart of Wiltz renewed the town's charters of liberties in 1437. The title of baron came in 1536, and John V, appointed fortress commander at Thionville in 1629, styled himself count and began the present Renaissance castle in 1631. From 1656 the comital line called itself de Custine; its last count fled the French revolutionary army in 1793 and died in exile at Bamberg in 1799.
zh: 维尔茨领主家族，后来成为伯爵，是卢森堡最古老的贵族世家之一，盘踞在阿登山区维尔茨河畔的城堡中。阿马迪厄斯·德·维尔茨曾出席1214年卢森堡女伯爵埃尔梅辛德的婚礼，瓦尔特·德·维尔茨则在1288年随布拉班特公爵参加沃林根战役。13世纪时，家族在镇上方的岩石岬角修建了坚固城堡，并分出幼支领有博福特、贝雷尔丹日和梅桑堡。戈达尔·德·维尔茨于1437年重新颁发了城镇的自由特许状。1536年家族获得男爵头衔；约翰五世于1629年被任命为蒂永维尔要塞司令，开始自称伯爵，并于1631年动工修建现存的文艺复兴式城堡。1656年起，伯爵支系改姓德·屈斯蒂纳；末代伯爵在1793年逃避法国革命军出走，1799年流亡死于班贝格。

en: The Wittelsbachs descend from the Counts of Scheyern, who moved to Wittelsbach Castle near Aichach in 1119 and took their name from it. Count Palatine Otto IV's son Otto was enfeoffed with the Duchy of Bavaria in 1180 after the fall of Henry the Lion, and Duke Louis I added the Rhenish Palatinate by marriage in 1214. The house reached empire-wide power under Louis IV, elected emperor in 1328, who gathered Brandenburg, Tyrol, Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, while the Treaty of Pavia in 1329 separated the Palatinate branch. After Louis died in 1347 his sons split Bavaria into rival lines; Tyrol was ceded to the Habsburgs in 1369, Brandenburg returned to the Luxembourgs in 1373, and the Dutch counties passed to Burgundy in 1433. Bavaria was reunited in 1505, and its Catholic dukes led the German Counter-Reformation, holding Cologne from 1583 to 1761 and gaining the electoral hat in 1623 under Maximilian I. The Palatinate line produced King of the Romans Rupert in 1400 and the Bohemian Winter King Frederick V in 1619; a cadet branch ruled Sweden from 1654 to 1720, and the Palatine princess Sophia of Hanover carried the British succession to her son George I in 1714. The Bavarian Charles Albert reigned as emperor from 1742 to 1745, and in 1806 Bavaria became a kingdom under Maximilian I Joseph.
zh: 维特尔斯巴赫家族出自沙伊恩伯爵世家，1119年迁居艾夏附近的维特尔斯巴赫城堡并以此为族名。行宫伯爵奥托四世之子奥托在1180年狮子亨利倒台后受封巴伐利亚公爵，路德维希一世又于1214年通过联姻取得莱茵普法尔茨。1328年当选皇帝的路德维希四世使家族权势遍及帝国，他为家族取得勃兰登堡、蒂罗尔以及荷兰、泽兰和埃诺，而1329年的《帕维亚条约》分出了普法尔茨支系。路德维希1347年去世后，诸子把巴伐利亚分为相互竞争的支系；蒂罗尔于1369年割让给哈布斯堡家族，勃兰登堡1373年归还卢森堡家族，尼德兰诸伯国则于1433年落入勃艮第之手。巴伐利亚于1505年重新统一，信奉天主教的公爵们成为德意志反宗教改革的领袖，1583至1761年间长期占据科隆大主教之位，马克西米利安一世又在1623年取得选帝侯头衔。普法尔茨支系出了1400年的罗马人的国王鲁普雷希特和1619年的波希米亚“冬王”腓特烈五世；一支幼支在1654至1720年统治瑞典，普法尔茨公主汉诺威的索菲娅则把英国王位继承权传给儿子乔治一世（1714年）。巴伐利亚支系的卡尔·阿尔布雷希特在1742至1745年出任皇帝，巴伐利亚则于1806年在马克西米利安一世·约瑟夫治下成为王国。

en: The Wittgenstein were a comital dynasty of the Sauerland in north-western Germany, named after Wittgenstein Castle above the Lahn at what is now Bad Laasphe. They descended from Werner I of Battenberg and Wittgenstein, born around 1150, whose line also held the County of Battenberg on the Eder in Hesse. The family renounced its Battenberg lands in 1296 and kept its seat at Wittgenstein. In 1337 the county was still ruled by the last generations of the house, whose heiress Adelaide, born around 1320, married Count Salentin of Sayn-Homburg of the House of Sponheim in 1345. The inheritance passed to the Sayn line, which took the name Sayn-Wittgenstein, while the old comital family was extinct in the male line by the middle of the fourteenth century.
zh: 维特根斯坦家族是德意志西北部绍尔兰地区的伯爵世家，得名于今巴特拉斯弗附近、俯瞰拉恩河的维特根斯坦城堡。其始祖为约1150年出生的巴滕贝格与维特根斯坦的维尔纳一世，家族同时领有黑森境内埃德河畔的巴滕贝格伯国；1296年家族放弃巴滕贝格领地，以维特根斯坦为驻地。1337年时伯国仍由该家族最后几代人统治，约1320年出生的继承人阿德莱德于1345年嫁给施蓬海姆家族的塞恩-洪堡伯爵萨伦廷。遗产随后转入塞恩一脉，改称塞恩-维特根施泰因，而古老的伯爵家族到14世纪中叶已男嗣断绝。

en: The House of Württemberg grew from the lords of Beutelsbach in the Rems valley, first recorded with one Konrad in 1081 and named after their Wirtemberg castle above Stuttgart, where the family ranked as counts from the twelfth century. The fall of the Hohenstaufen in 1250 opened room for expansion, and Count Ulrich I's marriage to Mechthild of Baden in 1251 brought Stuttgart, which became the sole residence after imperial troops and Esslingen ravaged Beutelsbach in 1311. Count Eberhard I, called the Illustrious, enlarged the domain by almost half despite a royal war of 1310 to 1311 urged on by the alarmed Swabian imperial cities. His son Ulrich III, who in 1337 held the imperial landvogtei of Lower Swabia, bought the county of Vaihingen in 1339 and the Palatinate of Tübingen with its city in 1342, while Eberhard II the Quarrelsome and his brother Ulrich IV went on buying castles and towns through marriage and thrift, gaining the mint right in 1374; under Eberhard III the betrothal of his son to the countess of Montbéliard in 1397 added that French county. The Treaty of Nürtingen split the house into Stuttgart and Urach lines in 1442, but Count Eberhard V reunited the lands through the treaties of Münsingen in 1482 and Esslingen in 1492, and at the Diet of Worms in 1495 the county became the Duchy of Württemberg, from which rank the dynasty later rose to electors and, in 1806, to kings.
zh: 符腾堡家族出身于雷姆斯河谷的博伊特尔斯巴赫领主，1081年一位名叫康拉德的成员首见记载，家族得名于斯图加特附近山丘上的维滕贝格堡，12世纪起取得伯爵身份。1250年霍亨斯陶芬家族倒台后，符腾堡获得扩张空间：乌尔里希伯爵一世1251年与巴登的梅希蒂尔德联姻，取得斯图加特；1311年博伊特尔斯巴赫遭皇帝军队和帝国城市埃斯林根洗劫后，斯图加特成为唯一驻地。埃伯哈德一世（“显贵者”）尽管在1310至1311年因施瓦本帝国城市惊惧而引发的皇帝战争中受挫，仍把领地扩大了近一半。其子乌尔里希三世1337年时正担任下施瓦本帝国地方长官，他于1339年买入法伊欣根伯国，1342年又购入图宾根行宫伯爵的辖地和图宾根城；此后埃伯哈德二世（“好争者”）与其弟乌尔里希四世继续靠联姻和节俭逐座收购城堡与城镇，1374年获得铸币权。1397年，埃伯哈德三世让儿子与蒙贝利亚尔女伯爵订婚，又把这个法兰西伯国纳入家族。1442年《尼尔廷根条约》使家族分裂为斯图加特和乌拉赫两支，但埃伯哈德五世借1482年《明辛根条约》和1492年《埃斯林根条约》重新统一领地；1495年沃尔姆斯帝国议会决定，符腾堡伯国升格为公国，家族后来更进一步成为选侯，并于1806年称王。

en: The Suruga Yabe took their name from Yabe village in Udō District, where they served as local land stewards; they claimed descent from the Fujiwara line of the courtier Tsutsumi no Kanesuke. In 1200 a clansman, Yabe Jūrō Terutane, won merit in the destruction of Kajiwara Kagetoki and was enfeoffed with twenty-one villages in Hattō District of Inaba Province, where he settled and founded the separate Inaba Yabe line, while the original house remained in Suruga. In the Muromachi period the Suruga Yabe became retainers of the Imagawa lords. Tradition preserved at the Kusanagi Kubizuka Inari shrine records that they backed the wrong side in an Imagawa succession struggle, supporting Oshika Norimitsu, and were put down for it. Later Yabe Sadanori, a retainer of Imagawa Ujizane, made his home again in Yabe village and took the Yabe name; under his son Sadakiyo the house entered Tokugawa service and became hatamoto, the direct bannermen of the Tokugawa.
zh: 骏河矢部氏以有度郡矢部村（今静冈市清水区）为苗字之地，世代担任当地地头，自称出自堤中纳言藤原兼辅的藤原良门流。1200年，族人矢部十郎晖种因追讨梶原景时一族立功，受封因幡国八东郡山田村等二十一处村庄并移住当地，开创因幡矢部氏一脉，本家则留在骏河。室町时代，骏河矢部氏成为今川氏的被官；草薙首冢稻荷神社流传的说法称，他们在今川家的继承之争中支持小鹿范满，站错阵营而遭讨伐。后来今川氏真的家臣矢部定则回到矢部村定居并正式以矢部为姓，到其子定清一代转仕德川氏，成为德川家的直属旗本。

en: The Yadavarayas were a Telugu chiefly line who held Chandragiri and Narayanavanam in the hill country around Tirupati, in present-day Andhra Pradesh. Like several southern dynasties of pastoral origin, they claimed descent from Yadu and styled themselves Yadavas. Around the year 1000 Immadi Narasimha Yadavaraya built the fort at Chandragiri, and the family was among the dynasties whose endowments were inscribed on the walls of the Venkateswara temple at Tirumala. In the mid-1310s the Yadavaraya of Chandragiri joined the Hoysala king Ballala and the chief of Padaividu against the Kakatiya king Prataparudra, only to be defeated by his general Peda Rudra. Rulers such as Sriranganatha Yadavaraya still left inscriptions in the following decades, but Chandragiri passed to the Vijayanagara Empire in 1367 and the line lost its separate rule.
zh: 耶陀婆（耶陀波罗耶）是泰卢固人的首领家族，占据今安得拉邦蒂鲁帕蒂一带山区的钱德拉吉里和纳拉耶纳瓦纳姆。与若干出身游牧群体的南方王朝一样，他们自称雅度后裔，冠以耶陀婆之名。约1000年，伊马迪·纳拉辛哈·耶陀波罗耶修建了钱德拉吉里城堡，该家族也是蒂鲁马拉文卡特斯瓦拉神庙的施主之一，神庙墙上留有他们的供奉铭文。14世纪10年代中期，钱德拉吉里的耶陀波罗耶与曷萨拉国王巴拉拉及波多毗都首领联手，对抗卡卡提亚国王普拉塔帕鲁陀罗，却被其将领佩达·鲁陀罗击败。此后斯里兰加纳塔·耶陀波罗耶等统治者仍留有铭文，但钱德拉吉里于1367年并入毗奢耶那伽罗帝国，家族的独立统治告终。

en: The Yamaguchi of Musashi were a branch of the Murayama party, one of the seven warrior bands of Musashi, and claimed descent from the Kanmu Heishi line of the Taira. Taira no Yorito, who held Murayama in Tama district, founded the Murayama party, and his grandson Ietsugu settled at Yamaguchi in Iruma district, the area of present-day Tokorozawa in Saitama, near the end of the Heian period and took the place name as his family name; generations of the clan were based at Yamaguchi Castle. Yamaguchi Rokuro followed Minamoto no Yoshitomo in the Hogen War of 1156, and a clansman was wounded fighting in the Jokyu War of 1221. In the Musashi Heiikki uprising of 1368 the Yamaguchi sided with the Kawagoe clan, and their castle fell to Uesugi Noriaki, acting for the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Ujimitsu. In 1383 Takaharu, backed by the Southern Court, rose again together with his grandfather Takazane but was defeated; they set fire to Yamaguchi Castle and took their own lives. Takatada, Takaharu's son, entered Uesugi service and later served the Later Hojo of Odawara; after the Hojo fell in 1590 his descendants, including Yamaguchi Daizen, served the Tokugawa.
zh: 武藏山口氏是武藏七党之一村山党的支族，自称出自桓武平氏的平氏流。领有武藏国多摩郡村山的平赖任是村山党之祖，其孙家继在平安时代末期移居入间郡山口（今埼玉县所泽市一带），以地名为苗字，此后世代居守山口城。1156年保元之乱中，山口六郎随源义朝出征；1221年承久之乱时，亦有族人参战负伤。1368年武藏平一揆中，山口氏站在河越氏一方，山口城被镰仓公方足利氏满麾下的上杉宪显攻陷。1383年，得到南朝支持的山口高治与祖父高实再度举兵对抗氏满，兵败后焚城自尽。高治之子高忠转仕上杉氏，上杉氏衰落后又出仕小田原的后北条氏；1590年后北条氏灭亡，其后代山口大善等人转投德川氏。

en: The Yamana were a samurai house of the Seiwa Genji, tracing their line to Minamoto no Yoshishige of the Nitta family; the founder Yamana Yoshinori took his name from Yamana village in Kozuke Province, and his descendants served Minamoto no Yoritomo as gokenin in the Kamakura shogunate. Backing Ashikaga Takauji in the Nanboku-cho wars, they rose to constables, or shugo, of five provinces by 1363 and eleven at their peak, earning the nickname the One-Sixth Lord. Their revolt against Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in the Meitoku Rebellion of 1391 was crushed and cost them most of their holdings. Yamana Sozen rebuilt the family's fortunes after leading the 1441 campaign against the Akamatsu, but his feud with the deputy shogun Hosokawa Katsumoto over the shogunal succession ignited the Onin War of 1467, which wrecked Kyoto and opened the Sengoku period; Sozen died in 1473 and the clan never recovered its former power. By the late sixteenth century it held little beyond Inaba Province, where Yamana Suketoyo developed the Ikuno silver mine and built Arikoyama Castle before defeat by the Oda in 1580. His successor Toyokuni fought at Sekigahara in 1600 and was confirmed by Tokugawa Ieyasu in a small domain, which the house kept until the end of the Edo period.
zh: 山名氏是清和源氏的武家，谱系可追溯到新田家的源义重；始祖山名义范受封于上野国山名乡，遂以山名为苗字，后代在镰仓幕府作为御家人侍奉源赖朝。南北朝时他们追随足利尊氏，到1363年已担任五国守护，鼎盛时领有十一国，号称“六分一殿”。1391年山名一族起兵反对将军足利义满，即明德之乱，兵败后丧失大半领地。山名宗全因1441年讨伐赤松氏有功而重振家势，但他与管领细川胜元围绕将军继嗣问题对立，最终引发1467年的应仁之乱。战火焚毁京都，揭开了战国时代的序幕；宗全于1473年病逝，山名氏再未恢复昔日权势。到16世纪末，其领地只剩因幡国一带，山名祐丰在那里开发生野银山、修筑有子山城，于1580年败于织田氏。继任的山名丰国参加1600年的关原之战，后被德川家康确认领有小片藩地，山名家一直存续到江户时代末期。

en: The Yamashiro were a warrior family of Hizen Province in northern Kyushu and a branch of the Matsura federation, the loose league of seafaring warrior houses of the Matsura district. The line began with Yamashiro Kakoi, sixth son of Matsura Naotsura, who made his base in Kanzaki district and supplied the military strength behind Minamoto no Mitsusue, the Saga Genji steward of the retired emperor's Kanzaki manor. During the Mongol invasions of the late thirteenth century Yamashiro Kizuna fought beside the Matsura head Sashi Fususa and was killed. After the Kamakura shogunate fell the family took the Northern Court side, and in 1359 Yamashiro Hiroshi fought under Shōni Yorihisa at the Battle of the Chikugo River, also called Ōboharu. Through the Sengoku period they served the Shōni, until that house was destroyed by the rebel Ryūzōji clan with Ōuchi backing; Yamashiro Kiyoshi joined the Ōtomo and Arima attempt to restore the Shōni, but defections by the Hata and others doomed the enterprise and Hizen passed under Ryūzōji control. When Toyotomi Hideyoshi conquered Kyushu, Yamashiro Sada had his family lands confirmed, and the house afterwards served the Nabeshima lords of the Saga domain.
zh: 山代氏是九州北部肥前国的武士家族，属于松浦党——松浦郡沿海武士豪族的松散联盟——的一支。其始祖山代围是松浦直的第六子，以神埼郡为本据，为在鸟羽院领神埼庄担任庄官的嵯峨源氏源满末充当武力后盾。13世纪后期的元寇之乱中，山代阶随松浦党惣领佐志房出战，最终战死。镰仓幕府灭亡后，山代家归属北朝：1359年，山代弘在少贰赖尚麾下参加了筑后川之战（又称大保原之战）。整个战国时代他们侍奉少贰氏，直到主家被受大内氏支持而起兵的龙造寺氏攻灭；山代清曾加入大友氏与有马氏复兴少贰氏的计划，但因波多等家族倒戈而失败，肥前就此落入龙造寺的控制。丰臣秀吉平定九州时，山代贞的本领获得安堵，此后山代氏转仕佐贺藩的锅岛氏。

en: The Yamato is the imperial house of Japan, said in court tradition to descend from the sun goddess Amaterasu through the legendary first emperor Jimmu, dated to 660 BC; the earliest broadly historical sovereigns belong to the early 500s, around Emperor Keitai and Emperor Kinmei in 539, making this the oldest continuous hereditary monarchy in the world. Through the Heian centuries the emperors reigned under Fujiwara regents and then under cloistered retired emperors, while real power passed to the Taira, the Minamoto and then the Hojo regents of Kamakura. In 1272 Emperor Go-Saga's plan for alternating succession split the family into two rival lines, the Daikakuji and the Jimyoin. The Daikakuji sovereign Go-Daigo overthrew Kamakura in 1333 and briefly ruled directly in the Kenmu Restoration, but Ashikaga Takauji seized Kyoto in 1336 and enthroned a Jimyoin claimant as the Northern Court, while Go-Daigo's Southern Court held out at Yoshino until it submitted in 1392; the present imperial line descends from the Northern emperors. During the Sengoku wars the court sank into poverty, and after 1603 the Tokugawa kept it in ceremonial subjection under the court laws of 1615, with the imperial role confined to ritual, genealogy and scholarship.
zh: 大和王朝即日本皇室，宫廷传统称其为天照大神的后裔，始祖是传说中公元前660年即位的神武天皇；可考的最早君主在6世纪初，即继体天皇与539年即位的钦明天皇前后，是世界上延续最久的世袭君主制。平安时代，天皇先后受制于藤原氏的摄关政治与退位上皇的院政，实权转入平氏、源氏，继而落入镰仓北条执权之手。1272年后嵯峨天皇设计的两统迭立方案使皇室分裂为大觉寺统与持明院统两个对立支系。大觉寺统的后醍醐天皇于1333年推翻镰仓幕府，推行建武新政、短暂亲政，但足利尊氏1336年攻陷京都，拥立持明院统的北朝天皇，后醍醐的南朝在吉野坚持到1392年投降，后世皇室即出自北朝一脉。战国战乱中朝廷穷困不堪，1603年德川氏开幕后，又依1615年的《禁中并公家诸法度》将皇室置于仪式性的从属地位，其职责限于礼仪、谱系与学问。

en: The Yoshimi of Musashi were a Seiwa Genji house descended from Minamoto no Noriyori, the sixth son of Minamoto no Yoshitomo and a younger brother of the first Kamakura shōgun Minamoto no Yoritomo. Noriyori held Yoshimi Manor in the Yokumi district of Musashi and was styled the Yoshimi Palace, but after he was exiled to Izu on suspicion of treason his sons received the manor through their kinswoman the Hiki nun. In the early thirteenth century Yoshimi Tameyori, whose name matches the earliest clan member recorded in the family line, took Yoshimi as his family name and his descendants served the Kamakura shogunate as gokenin. The senior line was extinguished when Yoshimi Yoshiyo's plot against the Hōjō regents was discovered and he was executed, after which the Musashi and Noto branches carried on the name. A separate cadet house, the Iwami Yoshimi, built up power around Tsuwano and became one of the two great provincial lords of Iwami alongside the Masuda; they fought for Emperor Go-Daigo in 1333 before joining the Ashikaga, and later passed under the Ōuchi and then the Mōri. In the early seventeenth century the last head was executed by Mōri Terumoto on suspicion of treason, and the Yoshimi name was discontinued when the adopted heir reverted to the Mōri surname.
zh: 武藏吉见氏属清和源氏（河内源氏），始祖是源义朝第六子、镰仓幕府初代将军源赖朝的异母弟源范赖。范赖领有武藏国横见郡的吉见乡，被尊称为“吉见御所”，后来因涉嫌谋反被流放伊豆，他的儿子们通过姻亲比企尼受封吉见庄。13世纪初，吉见为赖正式以吉见为苗字，其后代作为御家人侍奉镰仓幕府。后来吉见义世反对北条执权的密谋败露被处死，嫡流断绝，家门由武藏吉见氏和能登吉见氏两支继承。另有一支庶流石见吉见氏以津和野为中心扩张势力，与益田氏并称石见两大国人；他们在1333年以后醍醐天皇一方起兵，后来转投足利氏，战国时代先后受大内氏和毛利氏节制。17世纪初，末代当主吉见广长被主君毛利辉元以谋反嫌疑诛杀，继承家门的养子后来恢复毛利姓，吉见的苗字就此废止。

en: The Yuasa were a great warrior clan of Kii Province, powerful from the late Heian age through the Nanboku-chō wars. They claimed Fujiwara descent, traditionally from Fujiwara no Hidesato of the Uona line of the Northern House, and held gokenin status under the Kamakura shogunate. A certain Fujiwara no Munenaga is recorded in the Kokawadera engi as a resident of Yuasa around 1099, and the first to bear the place-name as a surname was Yuasa Muneshige, who in the Heiji Disturbance of 1160 aided Taira no Kiyomori hurrying back to Kyoto from a pilgrimage to the Kumano shrines; after the shogunate was founded his Yuasa estates in Arida District were confirmed. Muneshige built the Yuasa-tō, a loose confederation of kinsmen and in-law houses that became one of the classic warrior bands of the age, and in 1238 the clan was assigned guard duty at the Hachijō crossroads in Kyoto. It also produced the eminent monk Myōe, whose maternal grandfather was Muneshige; with clan backing, including Yuasa Kageki's gift of Semui-ji, he founded Kōzan-ji and revived the Kegon school. In the Genkō War of 1331-1333 Yuasa Munefuji fought Kusunoki Masashige at Shimo-Akasaka Castle before submitting to him, and a Yuasa bandsman joined Emperor Go-Daigo's side at Tennōji in 1333. During the Nanboku-chō conflict the Yuasa-tō split between the two courts and rapidly declined, the confederation breaking up in the late fourteenth century.
zh: 汤浅氏是纪伊国的大豪族，势力从平安末期一直延续到南北朝时代。其自称藤原氏，相传为藤原北家鱼名流藤原秀乡的后裔，镰仓时代拥有御家人身份。1099年前后的《粉河寺缘起》已记载“汤浅之住人”藤原宗永；最早以汤浅为苗字的是汤浅宗重，1160年平治之乱时，他援助了正在熊野三山参诣、闻讯紧急回京的平清盛，幕府成立后其在纪伊有田郡汤浅庄等地的领地得到安堵。宗重组建了由同族和姻族构成的松散武士团“汤浅党”，成为当时武士团联合的代表，1238年汤浅一族还被任命担任京都八条辻固的警护役。家族还出过高僧明惠——其外祖父即汤浅宗重；明惠在一族资助下开创高山寺，中兴华严宗，汤浅景基还向他寄进了施无畏寺。1331—1333年元弘之乱中，汤浅宗藤在下赤坂城之战与楠木正成交锋，后归降正成；1333年的天王寺会战中，汤浅党也有人作为后醍醐天皇一方参战。南北朝时代，汤浅党内部在南朝与北朝之间分裂相争，迅速走向衰落，这个大型武士团联合在14世纪后期解体。

en: The Yūki were a Shimōsa warrior house claiming Fujiwara no Hidesato's blood through the Oyama family. Their founder Oyama Tomomitsu, who family legend even calls an unacknowledged son of Minamoto no Yoritomo, joined Yoritomo's rising and was enfeoffed with Yūki district in Shimōsa, the present Yūki city in Ibaraki. In the late Kamakura age a cadet line settled at Shirakawa, and when the Nanboku-chō wars began the two branches split: the Shirakawa Yūki served Emperor Go-Daigo's Southern Court, their chieftain Munehiro fighting with Nitta Yoshisada and his son Chikamitsu dying in an attempt on Ashikaga Takauji's life, while the main Shimōsa line followed Takauji's Northern Court and lost two heads in battle. Under the Muromachi shogunate the restored main house sat among the eight great Kantō lords, the Kantō hachiyagata, and held the shugo post of Shimotsuke. Sheltering the orphans of the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Mochiuji brought the shogunate's army down on them in the Yūki War of the 1440s and the house was briefly extinguished, then revived; the fifteenth head Masatomo and his son Masakatsu, who issued the Yūki family code in 1556, built it into a Sengoku daimyō house. Harutomo took part in Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Odawara campaign of 1590, but lacking an heir adopted Tokugawa Ieyasu's son Hideyasu. After Sekigahara Hideyasu was moved to Echizen and took the Matsudaira name, and his successor Naomoto did the same, so that the Yūki name survived only within the Yūki-Matsudaira, while the Shirakawa branch had already been destroyed by Hideyoshi.
zh: 结城氏是下总国的武家，自称经由小山氏传自藤原秀乡。始祖小山朝光（结城朝光）跟随源赖朝举兵，受封下总国结城郡，即今茨城县结城市一带；家传甚至称他是赖朝的落胤。镰仓末期，一族分出以白河为本据的庶流。南北朝动乱时两支分道扬镳：白河结城氏效忠后醍醐天皇的南朝，当主宗广随新田义贞征战，其子亲光因刺杀足利尊氏失败而死；本家下总结城氏则追随尊氏的北朝，两代当主先后战死。室町幕府时期，复兴后的本家位列关东八屋形之一，并担任下野国守护。由于收留镰仓公方足利持氏的遗孤，15世纪40年代幕府军发动结城合战，家族一度灭亡，之后才获准再兴；第十五代当主政朝号称结城中兴，其子政胜又于1556年颁布分国法《结城氏新法度》，把家族建设成战国大名。晴朝参加了丰臣秀吉1590年的小田原征伐，得以保全名位，但因无嗣而收德川家康之子秀康为养子。关原之战后秀康被转封越前并改姓松平，继嗣的直基也改称松平，结城之名只存于结城松平家；白河一支则早已被秀吉灭亡。

en:
The Zaccaria were a noble Genoese family whose fortune grew out of the eastward expansion of Genoa. After the Treaty of Nymphaeum in 1261 the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos granted them trading privileges, and from 1275 they held the port of Phocaea, whose alum mines gave them a near monopoly of the alum sold in Flanders; they also ruled the islands of Chios and Samos. Benedetto Zaccaria served as admiral of Genoa, France and Castile, and his grandson Martino married Jacqueline de la Roche, heiress of the dukes of Athens, in 1311, receiving the Moreot baronies of Veligosti and Damala as her dowry; the titular Latin emperor named him king and despot of Asia Minor, and he died at Smyrna in 1345.

Martino's son Centurione I became bailiff of the Principality of Achaea in 1364. His grandson Centurione II inherited the barony of Chalandritsa in 1401 and in 1404 bought from Ladislaus of Naples the title of Prince of Achaea, becoming the last Latin ruler of the Morea outside Byzantine suzerainty. On his death in 1432 his daughter Catherine married Thomas Palaiologos at Mystras in 1430, carrying the family claims into the Byzantine imperial house, while a son, John Asen, briefly revived the principality in 1453.
zh:
撒迦利亚家族是热那亚的贵族世家，随热那亚向东扩张而发迹。1261年《宁费昂条约》后，拜占庭皇帝米海尔八世·帕里奥洛格斯赐予他们通商特权；自1275年起家族领有福西亚港，当地的明矾矿使他们几乎垄断了销往佛兰德的明矾贸易，此外还统治着希俄斯岛和萨摩斯岛。贝内代托·撒迦利亚曾出任热那亚、法国和卡斯蒂利亚的海军统帅；其孙马蒂诺于1311年娶雅典公爵的女继承人雅克琳·德拉罗什为妻，以摩里亚的韦利戈斯蒂和达马拉两个男爵领作嫁妆，拉丁人的名誉皇帝还封他为小亚细亚国王与专制君主，他于1345年死于士麦那。

马蒂诺之子琴图廖内一世于1364年出任亚该亚侯国的摄政。其孙琴图廖内二世于1401年继承哈兰德里察男爵领，1404年又从那不勒斯国王拉迪斯劳手中购得亚该亚亲王头衔，成为摩里亚最后一个不受拜占庭宗主权约束的拉丁人统治者。他1432年去世；其女凯瑟琳已于1430年在米斯特拉斯嫁给托马斯·帕里奥洛格斯，把家族的继承权带入拜占庭皇室，其子约翰·阿森则在1453年短暂重建了亲王国。

en: The Zakarids, also called Zakarians and known in Georgia by the nickname Mkhargrdzeli, meaning long-armed, were an Armenian noble dynasty that ruled northern Armenia from Ani under Georgian and later Mongol suzerainty. First traceable in the early eleventh century and possibly an offshoot of the Armenian Pahlavuni family, they rose as vassals of the Bagrationi: Sargis Zakarian was made governor of Ani in 1161 and granted Lori in 1186. His sons Zakare and Ivane became the foremost commanders of Queen Tamar, taking Dvin in 1193 and Ani around 1199, which Tamar granted them as a hereditary principality in 1201; their victories at Shamkor in 1195 and Basen in 1203 rebuilt an Armenian realm reaching from Ani to Dvin, and they filled the Georgian offices of atabeg and amirspasalar while founding monasteries such as Harichavank and Akhtala. When the Mongols stormed Ani in 1236 they confirmed the Zakarids in their lands as direct Ilkhanid vassals. The family held Ani until around 1360, when the Kara Koyunlu Turkomen seized the city and made it their own capital, ending Zakarid rule.
zh: 扎卡良王朝（一译扎卡里扬）在格鲁吉亚语中的绰号是姆哈尔格尔泽利，意为“长臂”，是一个亚美尼亚贵族王朝，以阿尼为中心统治亚美尼亚北部，先后臣服格鲁吉亚和蒙古。该家族11世纪初已有迹可考，可能出自亚美尼亚的帕赫拉武尼家族，后来作为巴格拉季奥尼王朝的封臣崛起：萨尔吉斯·扎卡良于1161年被任命为阿尼总督，1186年受封洛里。他的儿子扎卡雷和伊万涅成为塔马尔女王麾下最杰出的将领，1193年攻取德温，约1199年拿下阿尼，塔马尔于1201年把阿尼作为世袭公国封给他们；1195年沙姆科尔之战和1203年巴森之战的胜利，使他们重建起一个从阿尼延伸到德温的亚美尼亚政权。他们还出任格鲁吉亚的阿塔伯格和全军统帅等要职，并修建了哈里昌万克、阿赫塔拉等修道院。1236年蒙古人攻陷阿尼后，确认扎卡良家族对领地的占有，使其成为伊儿汗国的直属藩臣。该家族保有阿尼直至约1360年，黑羊王朝的土库曼人夺取该城并定为自己的都城，扎卡良的统治就此终结。

en: The Zayyanids, also called the Abd al-Wadids, were a Berber Zenata dynasty that ruled the Kingdom of Tlemcen in the central Maghreb, in north-western modern Algeria, from 1235 to 1557. As the Almohad Caliphate collapsed, Yaghmurasen Ibn Zyan made Tlemcen independent around 1236, holding the rival Berber groups together and allying with the Sultan of Granada and Alfonso X of Castile against the Marinids. An eight-year Marinid siege of the city ended in 1307, and the reigns of Abu Hammu I and Abu Tashufin I in 1308–1337 marked a second peak of Zayyanid power over the central Maghreb, until the Marinids occupied Tlemcen from 1337 to 1359. Restored under Abu Hammu II, who reigned until 1389, the kingdom later weakened and passed repeatedly under the suzerainty of the Hafsids, the Marinids and Aragon. In the early sixteenth century Spain and the Ottoman regency of Algiers fought over the city; the Ottomans took Tlemcen in 1551, and the last sultan Hasan al-Abdallah fled to Spanish Oran, where he died a few years later.
zh: 宰扬王朝又称阿卜杜勒·瓦迪德王朝，是柏柏尔人泽纳塔联盟的一支，1235—1557年统治中马格里布的特莱姆森王国，疆域主要在今阿尔及利亚西北部。穆瓦希德哈里发国崩溃之际，亚格穆拉辛·伊本·齐扬约于1236年在特莱姆森独立，他压服相互竞争的柏柏尔诸部，并与格拉纳达苏丹和卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索十世结盟，共同对付马林人。马林人对特莱姆森长达八年的围攻于1307年结束；1308—1337年阿布·哈穆一世与阿布·塔舒芬一世在位期间，宰扬人对中马格里布的控制趋于稳固，国力达到第二个高峰，直到1337—1359年特莱姆森被马林人占领。阿布·哈穆二世1359—1389年在位，王国一度复兴，但此后日渐衰弱，多次沦为哈夫斯、马林和阿拉贡的附庸。16世纪上半叶，西班牙与奥斯曼的阿尔及尔摄政国争夺该城；1551年奥斯曼人占领特莱姆森，末代苏丹哈桑·阿卜杜拉逃到西班牙保护下的奥兰，数年后在那里去世，宰扬统治就此终结。

en: The Zebari are a large Kurdish tribe of the Bahdinan region in northern Iraq, traditionally holding the lands along the Great Zab river around Akre, Duhok and Amadiya. They appear among the tribes that made up the Bahdinan Kurdish emirate, whose seventeenth-century sources list a Zibari district under its own chief.
zh: 泽巴里人是伊拉克北部巴赫迪南地区的一个库尔德大部落，传统上据有大扎卜河两岸、阿克拉、杜胡克和阿马迪耶一带的土地。在组成巴赫迪南库尔德酋长国的诸部落中便有他们，17世纪的史料还记载其辖区内设有由本族酋长管辖的“兹巴里”区。

en:
The Zeno, also spelled Zen, were one of the oldest patrician houses of Venice, recorded there since the tenth century and already numbering procurators of Saint Mark and sea generals before the closing of the Great Council in 1297; family tradition claimed descent from the Roman Gens Fannia. Reniero Zeno, who had commanded the Venetian fleet against Genoa, was elected doge and reigned from 1253 until his death in 1268. Pietro Zeno died in 1345 as bailo of Negroponte after fighting the Turks at Adramyttion and in the Smyrniote crusades, and a later Pietro ruled the island of Andros for the republic from about 1384 to 1497.

The most famous member was Carlo Zeno, born in 1333. Returning with eighteen galleys on 1 January 1380, he saved Venice at the Battle of Chioggia in June, which broke Genoese pressure on the Adriatic; as captain-general of the sea he won again at Modon in 1403 and overthrew the Carraresi of Padua in 1405, though the Council of Ten later stripped him of office over a treason charge. He died in 1418 and was given a public funeral. The merchants Nicolo and Antonio Zeno left a celebrated, much-disputed account of North Atlantic voyages, while Cardinal Giovanni Battista Zeno died in 1501 and the poet and librettist Apostolo Zeno in 1750.
zh:
泽诺家族（又拼作 Zen）是威尼斯最古老的贵族世家之一，10世纪已见记载，早在1297年大议会闭锁之前就出过圣马可行政长官和海军统帅；家族传说自称源出罗马的法尼娅氏族。雷涅罗·泽诺曾统率威尼斯舰队对热那亚作战，后当选总督，1253年至1268年去世前在任。彼得罗·泽诺曾任内格罗蓬特长官，在阿德拉米蒂翁抗击突厥人并参加士麦那十字军，1345年去世；后来的另一位彼得罗则于1384年至1497年间替共和国统治安德罗斯岛。

家族最著名的成员是生于1333年的卡洛·泽诺。1380年1月1日他率十八艘桨帆船赶回威尼斯，在6月的基奥贾战役中挽救了城邦，此战瓦解了热那亚对亚得里亚海的压制；1403年他以海军统帅身份在莫东再胜热那亚，1405年又推翻帕多瓦的卡拉雷西家族，但后来十人委员会以叛国指控免去了他的职务。他于1418年去世，威尼斯为他举行了公葬。商人尼科洛与安东尼奥·泽诺兄弟留下了著名且争议颇多的北大西洋航行记述，枢机主教乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·泽诺于1501年去世，诗人、剧作家阿波斯托洛·泽诺则逝于1750年。

en: The Zerzari, also called Zarzariyya, were a Kurdish tribe of the Middle Ages, probably an offshoot of the Hadhbani confederation and among the oldest Kurdish tribes named in Arabic historiography. One of their sons, al-Adil ibn al-Sallar, became vizier of Fatimid Egypt in 1148, and Zerzari cavalry went on to serve the Zengids, the Artuqids of Diyar Bakr and the atabegs of Mosul before forming a noted unit in the Ayyubid army; tribal emirs fought under Saladin and at the siege of Acre. Originally from the Erbil region, by the fourteenth century they held a strategic mountain pocket between Rawanduz, the Qandil range and Lake Dukan, with strongholds at Rawanduz and Qala Diza, and the geographer al-Umari, who died in 1349, describes them as effectively independent of the Ilkhanids and the surrounding powers.
zh: 泽尔扎里人（又称扎尔扎里耶）是中世纪的一个库尔德部落，很可能是哈兹巴尼部落联盟的分支，也是阿拉伯史籍中最早被点名的库尔德部落之一。其族人阿迪勒·伊本·萨拉尔于1148年当上法蒂玛王朝埃及的维齐尔；泽尔扎里骑兵先后为赞吉王朝、迪亚巴克尔的阿尔图格王朝和摩苏尔的阿塔贝格效命，后来又成为阿尤布军队中的知名部队，部落埃米尔们曾在萨拉丁麾下和阿卡围城战中征战。他们最初来自埃尔比勒地区，到14世纪时据有拉万杜兹、坎迪勒山脉与杜坎湖之间的战略山区，据点设在拉万杜兹和卡拉迪扎；卒于1349年的地理学家欧麦里记载，他们当时实际上独立于伊儿汗国和周边诸强之外。

en:
The counts of Ziegenhain were a noble dynasty of the Holy Roman Empire, descended from the ninth-century count Gozmar and the counts of Reichenbach. In the twelfth century they built a compact lordship in Lower Hesse from Fulda abbey advocacies, allodial lands and fiefs of Mainz, Fulda and Hersfeld, and from 1144 they took their name from the castle of Ziegenhain raised by Gottfried I, on the site of present-day Schwalmstadt. Count Ludwig I inherited the County of Nidda in 1205, and although the lands were split between two lines from 1258, Johann I reunited them in 1330 after marrying the Nidda heiress Lukardis. In 1331 he backed the townsfolk of Fulda against their abbot and later sold the remaining advocacy rights, keeping only the hereditary marshalship of Fulda.

The dynasty ended with Johann II, called the Strong, who had succeeded in 1401 and died childless on 14 February 1450. Landgrave Ludwig I of Hesse occupied the county as an escheated fief, while the Hohenlohe claimed it through marriage; although Emperor Frederick III enfeoffed the Hohenlohe in 1450, the inheritance dispute ended in 1495 with Hesse keeping Ziegenhain and Nidda after paying nine thousand gulden in compensation, and the title count of Ziegenhain passed into the style of the Hessian landgraves.
zh:
齐根海恩伯爵家族是神圣罗马帝国的贵族王朝，先祖可追溯到9世纪的戈茨马尔伯爵和赖兴巴赫伯爵支系。12世纪时，他们凭借富尔达修道院的摄政管辖权、自主地产以及美因茨、富尔达和赫斯费尔德的封地，在下黑森建起一块连成一体的领地；1144年起，家族以戈特弗里德一世所建的齐根海恩城堡（在今施瓦尔姆施塔特境内）为姓氏。1205年，路德维希一世伯爵继承了尼达伯爵国；1258年起领地在两支间分裂，约翰一世娶尼达女继承人卢卡迪斯后，于1330年重新统一两地。1331年他支持富尔达市民反抗修道院院长，后来卖掉剩余的摄政管辖权，只保留世袭的富尔达元帅一职。

王朝终结于绰号“强者”的约翰二世：他于1401年继位，1450年2月14日去世且无子嗣。黑森领地伯爵路德维希一世以封邑收归为由出兵占领伯爵国，霍恩洛厄家族则通过联姻提出继承要求；尽管皇帝腓特烈三世在1450年把封地授予霍恩洛厄，这场继承纠纷最终于1495年以黑森取胜告终——黑森支付九千古尔登补偿金后留下了齐根海恩与尼达，“齐根海恩伯爵”头衔也并入黑森领地伯爵的称号之中。

en:
The Zorzi, also called Giorgi, were a Venetian noble family whose fortunes were made in the Latin states of Greece. One of their number, Marino Zorzi, a former ambassador to Rome, was elected the fiftieth doge of Venice in August 1311 after the revolt of Bajamonte Tiepolo, but reigned only eleven months and died in July 1312 with a reputation for sanctity.

The family's Greek dominion was the Margraviate of Bodonitsa, a Frankish fief founded in 1204 to guard the pass of Thermopylae, which passed from the Pallavicini to the Cornaro and then, in 1335, to Nicholas I Zorzi. His successor Francis ruled it for nearly forty years. The Ottoman Turks conquered Bodonitsa in 1414 under Nicholas II, and though Nicholas III retained the margravial title, the lands were never recovered. He married his daughter Chiara to Nerio II, Duke of Athens, and she later governed the duchy as regent for her young son Francesco I, carrying Zorzi blood into the last court of Latin Athens.
zh:
佐尔齐家族（又称乔治家族）是威尼斯贵族世家，在希腊的拉丁人诸国中发迹。家族成员马里诺·佐尔齐曾任驻罗马使节，1311年8月巴亚蒙特·蒂耶波洛叛乱后当选威尼斯第五十任总督，但在任仅十一个月，1312年7月便去世，生前已有圣洁之名。

家族在希腊的领地是波多尼察藩侯国。这个法兰克人封邑建于1204年，职责是扼守温泉关，先归帕拉维奇尼家族，再转科尔纳罗家族，1335年落入尼古拉一世·佐尔齐手中；继任的弗朗切斯科统治了近四十年。1414年，奥斯曼突厥人在尼古拉二世在位时攻灭波多尼察，尼古拉三世虽继续使用藩侯头衔，领地却再未收复。他把女儿基娅拉嫁给雅典公爵内里二世，基娅拉后来代幼子弗朗切斯科一世摄政雅典公国，把佐尔齐家族的血脉带入了拉丁人雅典的末代宫廷。

en: The la Zouches descend from Alan la Zouche, originally Alain de Porhoet, a Breton nobleman who settled in England under Henry II and married the heiress of Ashby in Leicestershire, which took the family's name as Ashby-de-la-Zouch. His grandson Alan (1205-1270) served Henry III as justice of Chester and of Ireland, fought for the crown at Lewes, and was killed in a brawl with the Earl of Surrey's men in Westminster Hall. A barony of la Zouche of Ashby was created in 1299, though it soon fell into abeyance, while the Harringworth branch, barons from 1308, carried the family name through the later Middle Ages; its seventh baron was attainted for supporting Richard III in 1485 and later restored, and the title lapsed into abeyance in 1625. The most eminent fourteenth-century Zouche was William (1299-1352) of the Leicestershire line, who rose through the royal wardrobe to become Lord Treasurer and, after a disputed election, Archbishop of York in 1342. As Warden of the Marches he led a division of the English army that defeated the Scots at Neville's Cross in 1346 and captured David II, and he guided his northern province through the Black Death of 1349 before dying at Cawood in 1352.
zh: 拉朱什家族的先祖阿兰·拉朱什原名阿兰·德·波尔霍埃特，是布列塔尼贵族，在亨利二世时代定居英格兰，娶了莱斯特郡阿什比的女继承人，该地后来随家族姓氏改称阿什比-德拉朱什。其孙阿兰（1205—1270）在亨利三世治下出任切斯特和爱尔兰司法官，曾在刘易斯战役中为国王作战，最终在威斯敏斯特厅与萨里伯爵随从的斗殴中伤重身亡。1299年家族受封阿什比的拉朱什男爵，但该爵位不久即转入搁置状态；延续家族的是1308年起受封的哈灵沃思支系，其第七代男爵因1485年支持理查三世被定罪，后又恢复爵位，头衔最终于1625年再次搁置。14世纪家族最显赫的人物是莱斯特支系的威廉（1299—1352）：他从王室衣库系统一路升迁至财政大臣，又在一场有争议的选举后于1342年成为约克大主教。作为边境镇守长官，他在1346年的内维尔十字战役中指挥一支英军击败苏格兰人并俘获大卫二世；1349年黑死病期间他主持北方教区的应对，1352年在卡伍德去世。

en: The Žovneški, or Lords of Sanneck, were a free noble family seated at Žovnek Castle in the March of Savinja in Lower Styria, where they are first mentioned around 1130. Long balancing between the larger dynasties that ringed their border valley, they threw in their lot with the Habsburgs: Ulrich of Sanneck fought beside King Rudolf I at the Battle on the Marchfeld in 1278, and in 1308 he surrendered his lands to the Habsburg dukes to receive them back as a fief, binding the Savinja valley to Styria. Ulrich's second marriage to Catherine of Heunburg proved decisive, for their son Frederick claimed the Heunburg inheritance, including the strategically placed Celje Castle, which entered the family's hands in 1333. In 1341 Emperor Louis IV raised Frederick to the rank of imperial count, and the house thereafter took its name from Celje as the Counts of Cilli, later princes of the Holy Roman Empire and the most powerful dynasty on the territory of modern Slovenia until their extinction in 1456, when the Habsburgs inherited their domains.
zh: 若夫内什基家族又称桑内克领主，是以下施蒂里亚萨维尼亚边区的若夫内克城堡为中心的自由贵族，约1130年前后已有记载。这个家族长期在环伺边境河谷的各大王朝之间周旋，最终倒向哈布斯堡：桑内克的乌尔里希1278年在马希费尔德战役中随国王鲁道夫一世作战，1308年又把领地献给哈布斯堡公爵再以封臣身份领回，使萨维尼亚河谷并入施蒂里亚。乌尔里希与霍伊恩堡的凯瑟琳的第二次婚姻影响深远——他们的儿子腓特烈据此主张霍伊恩堡遗产，包括战略要地采列城堡，并于1333年实际取得。1341年皇帝路易四世将腓特烈升为帝国伯爵，家族从此以采列为名，称采列伯爵，后来更跻身神圣罗马帝国诸侯，成为今斯洛文尼亚境内最有权势的王朝，直到1456年绝嗣，领地由哈布斯堡家族继承。

en: The Zraqi were the ruling house of the Kurdish Principality of Zirqan, whose emirs claimed descent from the sheikh Hassan Zerraki. In 1335 Zeydo, one of his descendants, seized Boğat Castle near Silvan and founded the principality north of Mardin, on the Diyar Bakr frontier. It reached its height under the Aq Qoyunlu, whose sultan Uzun Hasan married a Zirqan emir's daughter in 1483 and entrusted the family with Bitlis; the Safavids overran most of its lands in 1507. After the battle of Chaldiran in 1514 the Zirqan emirs made their pact with Selim I and ruled as autonomous Ottoman vassals, leaving mosques and other buildings across their districts of Ataq, Tercil and Gürdükan. Gürdükan passed to Bitlis in 1709, and when the dynasty rebelled in 1830 the Ottomans crushed it in 1835 and exiled its family to Edirne.
zh: 兹拉基家族是库尔德人的济尔坎酋长国的统治家族，历代埃米尔自称是谢赫·哈桑·泽拉基的后裔。1335年，其后人扎伊多夺取锡尔万附近的博阿特堡，在马尔丁以北、迪亚巴克尔边境建立酋长国。它在白羊王朝时期达到鼎盛：1483年白羊苏丹乌尊·哈桑迎娶一位济尔坎埃米尔之女，并把比特利斯交予该家族管辖；1507年萨法维波斯攻陷了它的大部分领土。1514年恰尔德兰战役后，济尔坎埃米尔与塞利姆一世缔约，作为奥斯曼的自治附庸继续统治，在阿塔克、泰尔吉勒和居尔迪坎等辖区留下了清真寺等建筑。1709年居尔迪坎落入比特利斯之手；1830年该家族起兵反抗，1835年被奥斯曼镇压，族人被流放至埃迪尔内，酋长国灭亡。

en: The Zrinski were a cadet branch of the great Croatian Šubić tribe. In 1347 King Louis I of Hungary needed the Šubić fortress of Ostrovica for his wars with Venice and exchanged the family's old Bribir estates for the castle of Zrin in Slavonia, south of the modern Petrinja; the grandson of Ban Paul I Šubić, George, moved there and became the first to style himself Zrinski, meaning of Zrin. The house grew into the foremost noble family of Croatia during the Ottoman wars: Nikola IV Zrinski, Ban of Croatia, died leading the epic defence of Szigetvár against Suleiman the Magnificent in 1566, and in 1547 the family moved its seat north to Čakovec in Međimurje. The seventeenth century brought both glory and ruin, as Nikola VII Zrinski won fame as a general and a Hungarian poet while his brother Petar and Petar's wife Katarina, herself a noted writer, led Croatian resistance to Habsburg centralism. Petar Zrinski and Fran Krsto Frankopan were executed for the Zrinski-Frankopan Plot in 1671, and the male line of the house died out before the end of the century.
zh: 兹林斯基家族是克罗地亚大族舒比奇的一个支系。1347年，匈牙利国王拉约什一世为对威尼斯作战，需要舒比奇家族的奥斯特罗维察要塞，便用斯拉沃尼亚境内、今彼得里尼亚以南的兹林城堡交换其祖传的布里比尔领地；克罗地亚班保罗一世·舒比奇的孙子尤拉伊迁居于此，成为第一个以“兹林的”为号、即兹林斯基的人。奥斯曼战争时期，这个家族成长为克罗地亚首屈一指的显贵：克罗地亚班尼古拉四世·兹林斯基于1566年指挥锡盖特堡保卫战、抵御苏莱曼大帝的大军，战死城头；1547年家族又把府邸北迁至梅吉穆列的查科韦茨。17世纪，家族在荣耀中走向覆灭：尼古拉七世以将领和匈牙利语诗人闻名，其弟佩塔尔与妻子、作家卡塔琳娜领导克罗地亚人反抗哈布斯堡的集权。1671年，佩塔尔·兹林斯基与弗兰·克尔斯托·弗兰科潘因“兹林斯基—弗兰科潘阴谋”被处死，家族男系也在该世纪结束前断绝。

en: The counts of Zweibrücken were a branch of the powerful House of Saarbrücken, whose water castle at a crossing of the Schwarzbach had been built around 1150. When the Saarbrücken lands were divided between 1182 and 1190, the younger son Henry I received the Zweibrücken estate and founded the comital line, and the settlement below his castle was granted town rights in 1352. In 1286 the brothers Eberhard I and Walram I split the county: Eberhard took the lordship of Lemberg and founded the Zweibrücken-Bitsch line, while Walram kept Zweibrücken itself and began the Walramide branch of the later counts Simon and Walram. Walram I ruled until 1309, followed briefly by Simon and then by Walram II, who reigned until 1366. The last Walramide count, Eberhard II, was impoverished by endless feuds and, being childless, pledged the county to the Wittelsbach counts palatine in 1385; they inherited it on his death in 1394. Joined with the County of Veldenz in 1444, the lands became the nucleus of the Principality of Palatinate Zweibrücken, while the Bitsch line survived until its male branch died out in 1570.
zh: 茨魏布吕肯伯爵出自势力显赫的萨尔布吕肯家族，其在施瓦茨巴赫渡口旁的水堡约建于1150年。1182至1190年间萨尔布吕肯领地分割时，幼子亨利一世分得茨魏布吕肯地产，开创了伯爵世系；城堡脚下的聚落于1352年获得城市权。1286年，埃伯哈德一世与瓦勒拉姆一世兄弟瓜分伯国：埃伯哈德取得伦贝格领地，开创茨魏布吕肯-比奇支系；瓦勒拉姆保留茨魏布吕肯本体，建立了后来由西蒙、瓦勒拉姆相继继承的瓦勒拉姆支系。瓦勒拉姆一世统治至1309年，随后西蒙短暂在位，接着瓦勒拉姆二世一直统治到1366年。末代瓦勒拉姆伯爵埃伯哈德二世因无休止的封建仇杀而穷困，又没有子嗣，遂于1385年把伯国抵押给维特尔斯巴赫家族的行宫伯爵，后者在他1394年死后正式继承。1444年这片领地与费尔登茨伯国合并，成为普法尔茨-茨魏布吕肯公国的核心；比奇支系则延续到1570年男系断绝。

en: Ahobilam is a pilgrimage town in the Nallamala hills of the Eastern Ghats, in Andhra Pradesh, and the chief centre of the worship of Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu. Nine shrines line a steep gorge at Upper Ahobilam, each honouring a different aspect of the deity, while Lower Ahobilam holds the Prahladavarada temple, dedicated to his mild form. The Tamil saint Thirumangai Alvar praised the place in the ninth-century Periyatirumozhi, and it was counted among the 108 Divya Desams, the canonical Vaishnava holy places. The Kakatiya and Reddi dynasties patronised the shrines in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, followed by the Vijayanagara kings: the Saluva and Tuluva dynasties built and endowed them, and Krishnadevaraya came here on pilgrimage in the sixteenth century. The Ahobila Matha monastic seat grew up at the site around the same time. After Vijayanagara's decline the temple was sacked in 1579 by Murahari Rao, a commander of the Golconda Sultanate, who carried its jewelled idol away.
zh: 阿霍比拉姆是安得拉邦东高止山脉纳拉马拉丘陵中的朝圣城镇，也是崇拜毗湿奴的人狮化身那罗辛哈的首要中心。上阿霍比拉姆的陡峭峡谷中排列着九座神龛，各奉那罗辛哈的一种化身；下阿霍比拉姆则有供奉其温和面相的帕拉拉达瓦拉达神庙。9世纪泰米尔圣徒蒂鲁芒盖·阿尔瓦尔在《佩里亚蒂鲁莫利》中赞颂此地，它因而被列为毗湿奴教一百零八座圣庙之一。13至14世纪，卡卡提亚王朝和雷迪王朝曾资助这些神龛，随后毗奢耶那伽罗诸王继之：萨卢瓦王朝和图卢瓦王朝在此营建布施，克里希纳德瓦拉亚于16世纪前来朝圣。阿霍比拉修道院也在这一时期兴起于此。毗奢耶那伽罗衰落后，神庙于1579年遭到戈尔孔达苏丹国将领穆拉哈里·拉奥的洗劫，镶宝神像被掠走。

en: Masjid al-Kazimiyya is the great Twelver Shia mosque and shrine in the Kadhimiya suburb north of Baghdad. It stands on the Quraysh cemetery laid out with the Round City by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur in 762. The seventh Imam Musa al-Kadhim was buried there in 799 after his death in Abbasid custody, and his grandson the ninth Imam Muhammad al-Jawad followed him in 834; the two tombs gave the quarter its name and made it one of the holiest grounds of Shiism, later joined by the graves of the scholars Shaykh Mufid and Nasir al-Din al-Tusi. The present building is the work of the Safavid Shah Ismail I, who rebuilt and adorned the shrine between 1502 and 1524. After the Ottomans took Baghdad in 1534, Suleiman the Magnificent added further ornament, and in 1611 Sultan Ahmed I issued a firman granting hereditary custodianship of the shrine to the al-Jamali family.
zh: 卡济米耶圣陵是巴格达北郊卡济米耶区一座宏伟的十二伊玛目派清真寺与陵墓建筑群，其地本是762年阿拔斯王朝哈里发曼苏尔营建圆城时划出的古莱什墓地。799年，第七任伊玛目穆萨·卡齐姆在阿拔斯人的囚禁中去世后安葬于此；834年，其孙第九任伊玛目穆罕默德·塔基·贾瓦德也葬在这里。两座圣墓使这片城区得名，并成为什叶派最神圣的场所之一，学者谢赫穆菲德和纳西尔丁·图西后来也安葬于此。现存建筑主要出自萨法维王朝沙阿伊斯玛仪一世之手，他在1502年至1524年间重建并装饰了圣陵。1534年奥斯曼人攻占巴格达后，苏莱曼大帝又加以增饰；1611年，苏丹艾哈迈德一世颁布敕令，将圣陵的世袭监护权授予贾马利家族。

en: Tradition holds that Mark the Evangelist founded the church of Alexandria in the first century and was martyred there, and its bishops were styling themselves popes by the third century. The Council of Chalcedon in 451 split the ancient see in two: the patriarch Dioscorus was deposed for his Miaphysite teaching, the native Egyptian majority, the Copts, kept their own non-Chalcedonian popes, and a Greek-speaking minority loyal to Constantinople formed the Melkite patriarchate. After the Arab conquest of 642 both communities lived as dhimmis, though the Coptic church, marginalized under Byzantine rule, at first fared better than the imperial Melkites, whose numbers steadily shrank. In 828 or 829 Venetian merchants smuggled the body of Saint Mark, minus the head, out of the city to Venice, where it became the treasure of St Mark's Basilica. The Fatimid era brought the persecution of al-Hakim early in the eleventh century, and in that same century the Coptic popes moved their residence from Alexandria to Cairo, where the vizier Badr al-Jamali required them to settle. Mamluk rule pressed harder still: coordinated attacks in 1321 destroyed churches and monasteries across Egypt, and the riots of 1354 drove mass conversions, after which Copts ceased to be the majority population. Under Ottoman rule the Copts were placed in the Armenian millet and faced heavy taxation alongside Catholic missionary pressure, while the Greek patriarchate survived as a small community, reviving only with the tolerance of the Muhammad Ali dynasty after 1805.
zh: 相传福音书作者马可于1世纪创立亚历山大教会并在此殉道，3世纪时当地主教已采用“教宗”称号。451年的迦克墩公会议把这座古老牧座一分为二：牧首狄奥斯库若因基督合性派主张被废，本土埃及人为主的科普特人保留了自己的非迦克墩教宗，忠于君士坦丁堡的希腊语少数派则组成麦勒基牧首区。642年阿拉伯征服后，两个群体都作为迪米人生活，而在拜占庭治下受排挤的科普特教会起初境遇反优于帝国色彩浓厚的麦勒基派，后者人数不断萎缩。828或829年，威尼斯商人把圣马可的遗体（头部除外）偷运出城送往威尼斯，成为圣马可大教堂的镇堂之宝。11世纪初法蒂玛王朝哈基姆发动迫害，同一世纪里科普特教宗们把驻地从亚历山大迁往开罗，维齐尔巴德尔·贾马利还要求他们定居于新都。马穆鲁克统治压迫更甚：1321年的协同袭击摧毁了埃及各地的教堂和修道院，1354年的暴乱引发大规模改宗，此后科普特人不再是人口多数。奥斯曼统治下科普特人被划入亚美尼亚米利特，承受重税和天主教传教的双重压力，而希腊牧首区作为小社群勉强存续，直到1805年后穆罕默德·阿里王朝的宽容政策才使其重新振兴。

en: Alexandria, on the Egyptian coast west of the Nile Delta, was founded in 331 BC by Alexander the Great on the older settlement of Rhacotis and became the capital of the Ptolemaic kingdom, famed for the Pharos lighthouse and the Great Library. It was also one of the chief cities of early Christianity and the seat of one of the five patriarchates. Its Catechetical School, led from about 190 by Clement of Alexandria and later by Origen, made the city a center of biblical theology alongside Antioch, while Gnostic teaching also took root here: Basilides taught his dualist doctrines in Alexandria between roughly 117 and 161, and his followers remained active in the Nile Delta into the late fourth century. The city's patriarch Athanasius, who in 325 attended the First Council of Nicaea as a young deacon, led the opposition to Arius from 328 to 373 through repeated exiles. Sassanid Persians occupied Alexandria in 619, Byzantine rule returned in 629, and Arab forces under Amr ibn al-As took it in 641 after a fourteen-month siege. It passed to the Ottomans in 1517 and regained some of its trade after the Mahmoudiyah Canal linked it to the Nile in 1820.
zh: 亚历山大位于尼罗河三角洲以西的埃及海岸，公元前331年由亚历山大大帝在古老聚落拉科蒂斯的基础上建立，后来成为托勒密王国的首都，以法罗斯灯塔和大图书馆闻名于世。它也是早期基督教的主要城市之一，是五大牧首区之一的所在地。城中的教理学校约从190年起由亚历山大的克雷芒主持，后来又由俄利根领导，使亚历山大与安条克并列为圣经神学的两大中心；灵知派教义也在此扎根：巴西里德约于117—161年在亚历山大传授他的二元论学说，其追随者在尼罗河三角洲一直活动到4世纪末。325年，城中的年轻执事亚他那修参加第一次尼西亚公会议，又于328—373年担任牧首，在多次流放中领导了反对阿里乌的斗争。619年萨珊波斯占领亚历山大，629年拜占庭恢复统治，641年阿姆鲁·本·阿斯率领阿拉伯军队围攻十四个月后拿下该城。1517年它转入奥斯曼帝国手中，1820年马赫穆迪亚运河将城市与尼罗河连通后，它的贸易地位有所恢复。

en: The Amamangalam Maha Vishnu Temple at Kakkur in Kerala's Kozhikode district houses Vishnu in his tortoise avatar, worshipped as Kurmavataram. Local legend counts it among the major Dashavatara temples of the Malabar coast consecrated by the warrior-sage Parashurama, who in the Keralolpathi reclaimed Kerala from the sea.
zh: 阿马曼加拉姆摩诃毗湿奴神庙位于喀拉拉邦科泽科德县卡库尔，供奉毗湿奴的龟化身“俱利摩下凡”。当地传说把它列为马拉巴尔海岸的十化身大庙之一，相传由圣仙持斧罗摩亲自开光；据《喀拉拉源流》所载，持斧罗摩曾投斧入海，从波涛中辟出喀拉拉之地。

en: The Anantheshwara Temple at Udupi, in the Tulu Nadu country of the south-western coast, is dedicated to Parashurama, the axe-wielding avatar of Vishnu, who is worshipped here in the form of a linga on a silver seat. Legends place Udupi within Parashurama Kshetra, the strip of land the hero is said to have reclaimed from the sea, and tell how King Ramabhoja venerated Parashurama on this spot; for this reason Sanskrit texts call the town Rajata Pitha, the silver seat. The shrine was founded around the 700s under the Alupa dynasty and is counted among the oldest temples of Tulu Nadu. Madhvacharya (traditionally 1238-1317), founder of the Dvaita school of Vedanta, composed many of his Tattvavada works in the temple and taught his disciples here. The temple later came under the Puttige Matha, one of the eight monastic orders of Udupi, whose Madhva Brahmins have conducted its rituals according to Madhvacharya's ordinances for some seven centuries.
zh: 阿南特什瓦拉神庙位于西南海岸图卢纳德地区的乌度比，供奉毗湿奴持斧化身持斧罗摩；在这里，持斧罗摩以安坐在银座之上的林伽形象受人敬拜。传说乌度比属于持斧罗摩从大海中索回的土地“持斧罗摩田”，国王罗摩博阇曾在此敬拜持斧罗摩，因此梵文典籍把这座城市称为罗阇塔皮塔，意为银座。神庙建于8世纪阿卢帕王朝治下，是图卢纳德最古老的神庙之一。13世纪，吠檀多二元论学派的创立者摩陀婆阿阇梨（传统纪年1238—1317年）在庙中写下多部真实论著作，并在此向弟子讲道。神庙后来归入乌度比八大道场之一的普蒂盖摩特管辖，该道场的摩陀婆婆罗门依照摩陀婆阿阇梨制定的仪轨主持祭祀，这一传统已延续约七百年。

en: The Mosque of the Andalusians stands in Fes el-Bali, the old medina of Fez, at the centre of the quarter settled by refugees from Cordoba who fled to Morocco in 818 after their failed uprising against the Umayyad emir al-Hakam I. It was founded in 859 or 860 by Maryam al-Fihri, sister of Fatima al-Fihri who was building the Qarawiyyin across the river at the same time, with further money from the Andalusi families whose name it bears. In 933 the Fatimid governor of Fez transferred the Friday sermon to it, making it the chief mosque of the Andalusian quarter, and in 956 the Umayyad caliph of Cordoba, Abd al-Rahman III, paid for its square minaret, which still stands. The Zirid amir Buluggin donated a new minbar in 980, and the whole building was almost entirely reconstructed between 1203 and 1207 on the orders of the Almohad caliph Muhammad al-Nasir, who added the monumental northern gate and a water channel feeding its ablutions house. Marinid sultans kept up the work: Abu Ya'qub Yusuf repaired it in 1295, and Abu Sa'id Uthman III founded its library in 1415, confirming it as the second mosque of Fez after the Qarawiyyin.
zh: 安达卢西亚人清真寺位于非斯老城巴利区的中心，所在街区聚居着818年科尔多瓦起义失败后、为躲避倭马亚埃米尔哈卡姆一世镇压而逃到摩洛哥的难民。859年或860年，麦尔彦·菲赫里修建了这座清真寺，她的姐姐法蒂玛·菲赫里同时在河对岸营建卡拉维因清真寺，安达卢西亚难民家庭也出资相助，清真寺便由他们得名。933年，非斯的法蒂玛王朝总督把周五讲道移到这里，使它成为安达卢西亚人区的主麻清真寺；956年，科尔多瓦的倭马亚哈里发阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼三世出资修建了方形宣礼塔，这座塔仍存于世。980年，齐尔王朝埃米尔布鲁根捐赠了新的敏拜尔讲经坛；1203年至1207年，穆瓦希德哈里发穆罕默德·纳西尔下令几乎将全寺重建，增修了宏伟的北门和向净仪房供水的水道。马林王朝的苏丹们继续经营：阿布·叶尔孤卜·优素福于1295年加以修缮，阿布·赛义德·奥斯曼三世于1415年敕建图书馆，使它成为非斯仅次于卡拉维因的第二大清真寺。

en: Angamaly, in the Malabar hinterland behind Kochi, was the ecclesiastical heart of the Saint Thomas Christians, who hold that the Apostle Thomas landed at the nearby port of Muziris in 52 and founded seven churches along the Kerala coast before his martyrdom. East Syriac settlers and missionaries from Persia reinforced the community from the third century, and under Patriarch Timothy I around 800 it was organized as the Province of India of the Church of the East, governed by bishops sent from Mesopotamia together with a hereditary local archdeacon. The bishops' seat came to rest at Angamaly, which in 1565 gave its name to the renewed Archdiocese of India. Mar Abraham, who died in 1597, was the last East Syriac prelate to rule the undivided community; two years later the Portuguese-run Synod of Diamper suppressed his see, subjected the Malabar churches to the Padroado of Goa and imposed the Latin rite. The Latinizing reforms provoked the Coonan Cross Oath of 1653, after which the Saint Thomas Christians split into rival bodies, some keeping the East Syriac liturgy and others turning to the West Syriac tradition of Antioch.
zh: 安加马利位于科钦后方的马拉巴尔内陆，是圣多马基督徒的教务中心。该群体相传使徒多马于52年在附近的穆济里斯港登陆，在喀拉拉沿海建立七座教堂，最后殉道而去。3世纪起，波斯的东叙利亚定居者和传教士不断壮大这个社群；约800年，牧首提摩太一世将其组建为聂斯脱里派东方教会的印度教省，由美索不达米亚派遣的主教与本地世袭的总执事共同治理。主教驻地最终设在安加马利，1565年重建的印度总教区也以它命名。1597年去世的马尔·亚伯拉罕是统治这个尚未分裂社群的最后一任东叙利亚教长；两年后，葡萄牙人主持的戴佩尔公会议取缔了他的牧座，把马拉巴尔各教会置于果阿的保教权之下并强行拉丁礼仪。拉丁化改革激起了1653年的“弯十字架誓约”，圣多马基督徒此后分裂为不同派别，一部分保留东叙利亚礼仪，另一部分转而尊奉安条克的西叙利亚传统。

en: Angkor Wat is the vast temple complex at Yaśodharapura, the capital of the Khmer Empire in present-day Cambodia. King Suryavarman II, who ruled from 1113 to about 1150, built it as his state temple dedicated to the Hindu god Vishnu and, most likely, as his own mausoleum; work began around 1122 and ended in 1150. Its moat, galleries and central towers reproduce the cosmic Mount Meru, and unlike other Angkorian temples it faces west. After the Chams sacked Angkor in 1178, Jayavarman VII restored the empire from nearby Angkor Thom, and Angkor Wat was gradually converted to Buddhist worship as the Khmer kings turned to Buddhism. The Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan saw it in the late thirteenth century, and Zheng He visited in the early fifteenth. When Ayutthaya brought down the Khmer Empire in 1431 the temple was not abandoned: monks maintained its ponds, and seventeenth-century inscriptions record Japanese Buddhist pilgrims settling beside Khmer villagers, one of whom celebrated the Khmer New Year there in 1632. It thus remained a living Theravada monastery long after the capital moved south.
zh: 吴哥窟是高棉帝国都城耶输陀罗补罗（在今柬埔寨）的巨型寺院建筑群。苏利耶跋摩二世（1113年至约1150年在位）将它建为供奉毗湿奴的国寺，很可能也是他自己的陵庙；工程约始于1122年，1150年完工。寺外的护城河、回廊与中央塔群象征宇宙中心须弥山，与其他吴哥寺院不同，它朝向西方。1178年占城攻陷吴哥后，阇耶跋摩七世在附近的吴哥通王城复兴帝国，随着高棉诸王改奉佛教，吴哥窟也逐渐转为佛寺。中国使臣周达观在13世纪末到此，郑和则在15世纪初造访。1431年阿瑜陀耶灭亡高棉帝国后，寺院并未被废弃：僧人持续维护寺内池塘，17世纪的碑铭还记载日本佛教巡礼者与高棉村民比邻而居，其中一人于1632年在此庆祝高棉新年。国都南迁之后很久，它仍是一座有僧人居住的上座部寺院。

en: The Council of Chalcedon in 451 fractured the ancient patriarchate of Antioch, where the disciples had first been called Christians. In 512 the Miaphysite theologian Severus was enthroned as patriarch, only to be deposed six years later; the native Syriac majority that kept his teaching was organized into a lasting hierarchy by the sixth-century bishop Jacob Baradaeus, after whom they were nicknamed Jacobites, while the Greek-speaking imperial loyalists, the Melkites, held the Chalcedonian patriarchate. Crusader rule brought the two rites unusual peace: in 1165 Emperor Manuel I forced Prince Bohemond III to restore the Orthodox hierarchy, so that Patriarch Athanasius I could reside at the cave Cathedral of Saint Peter. Mamluk conquests then scattered both flocks. In 1293 the Syriac Orthodox patriarchs settled at the Mor Hananyo monastery near Mardin, their seat for more than six centuries, and in 1342 the Greek patriarch moved his throne to Damascus, since Antioch itself had grown too unsafe. Under the Ottomans after 1517 the Melkites fell under the Rum millet of Constantinople and the Jacobites under the Armenian millet, and Latin missionary work bore bitter fruit in 1724, when the disputed election of Cyril VI Tanas split the Greek patriarchate and Pope Benedict XIII recognized his Catholic line in 1729 as the Melkite Greek Catholic Church.
zh: 451年的迦克墩公会议使这座门徒最早被称为“基督徒”的古老牧首区走向分裂。512年，基督合性派神学家塞维鲁登位为牧首，六年后即被废黜；坚守其教义的叙利亚语多数派由6世纪的主教雅各·巴拉德乌斯组织成持久的教阶体系，并因他得名“雅各派”，而操希腊语、效忠帝国的麦勒基派则掌握着迦克墩派牧首区。十字军统治时期两个仪轨难得相安：1165年皇帝曼努埃尔一世迫使公爵博希蒙德三世恢复东正教教阶，牧首亚他那修一世得以入驻洞穴式的圣伯多禄主教座堂。马穆鲁克的征服随后把两支会众打散：1293年叙利亚正教牧首们定居于马尔丁附近的哈南约修道院，在此驻锡六个多世纪；1342年，希腊牧首也把牧座迁往大马士革，因为安条克本地已不再安全。1517年后的奥斯曼统治下，麦勒基派归入君士坦丁堡的鲁姆米利特，雅各派则归入亚美尼亚米利特。拉丁传教的影响在1724年结成苦果：西里尔六世·塔纳斯的选举之争使希腊牧首区分裂，教宗本笃十三世于1729年承认其天主教一脉为麦勒基希腊天主教会。

en: Antioch, on the Orontes River in northern Syria at the site of present-day Antakya, was founded around 300 BC by Seleucus I Nicator and served as the capital of the Seleucid Empire before becoming the third greatest city of the Roman Empire. It was one of the earliest strongholds of Christianity: the New Testament records that the followers of Jesus were first called Christians there, Saint Peter is said to have preached in its cave church, and between 252 and 300 ten church assemblies met in the city, which became one of the five patriarchal sees. Constantine the Great began its Great Church in 327, while the surviving parts of the cave Church of Saint Peter go back to the fourth or fifth century. Theological dissent had deep local roots too: Paul of Samosata, patriarch of Antioch from 260 to 268, taught an adoptionist, nontrinitarian doctrine, and later Byzantine writers linked the Paulician sect to his name. Arab armies took Antioch in 637, the Byzantines recovered it in 969, and the First Crusade captured it in 1098 after an eight-month siege and made it the seat of the Principality of Antioch. Mamluk forces under Baibars sacked the city in 1268, ending Latin power in northern Syria; the Ottomans absorbed it with the conquest of Syria in 1516, and from 1831 it served as a headquarters of Ibrahim Pasha of Egypt.
zh: 安条克位于叙利亚北部的奥龙特斯河畔，即今土耳其安塔基亚一带，约公元前300年由塞琉古一世·尼卡托建立，曾是塞琉古帝国的首都，后来成为罗马帝国第三大城市。它是基督教最早的重镇之一：《新约》记载耶稣的追随者最早在这里被称为“基督徒”，相传圣伯多禄曾在城中的洞穴教堂讲道；252—300年间这里召开过十次教会会议，安条克也成为五大牧首区之一。君士坦丁大帝于327年动工修建城中的大圣堂，而洞穴式的圣伯多禄教堂现存部分可追溯至4或5世纪。神学异见在当地也渊源深厚：260—268年任安条克牧首的萨摩萨塔的保禄主张嗣子论的非三位一体教义，后来的拜占庭作者把保禄派的名称与他联系起来。637年阿拉伯军队攻占安条克，969年拜占庭将其收复；1098年第一次十字军围攻八个月后拿下该城，建立安条克公国。1268年拜巴尔斯率领马穆鲁克军队洗劫城市，终结了拉丁势力在叙利亚北部的统治；1516年奥斯曼帝国征服叙利亚时吞并安条克，1831年起它又成为埃及易卜拉欣帕夏的驻地。

en: Anuradhapura Maha Viharaya was the great Theravada monastery of Anuradhapura, the royal capital of ancient Sri Lanka. King Devanampiya Tissa founded it in the third century BCE, and its monks, the Mahaviharavasins, became the island's oldest and most orthodox Buddhist fraternity. In the fifth century it was among the foremost seats of learning in southern Asia: the scholar Buddhaghosa composed his Visuddhimagga and commentaries on the Tipitaka there, defining the Theravada doctrine followed ever since. It long rivaled the Abhayagiri and Jetavana monasteries, and the chronicle Mahavamsa records its demolition under King Mahasena in the fourth century, though the Chinese pilgrim Faxian found three thousand monks in residence around 406. In the twelfth century King Parakramabahu I threw his weight behind the Mahavihara, dissolved the rival fraternities and united the sangha under its lineage, which from Sri Lanka went on to shape the Theravada Buddhism of Southeast Asia.
zh: 阿㝹罗陀补罗寺是古代斯里兰卡王都阿努拉德普勒的上座部大寺，由天爱帝须王于公元前3世纪创建，寺中僧人组成岛上最古老、最严守传统的佛教僧团。5世纪时它是南亚首屈一指的学术中心：学者觉音在此撰写《清净道论》和三藏注疏，奠定了此后上座部佛教的教义体系。它长期与无畏山寺、祇园寺鼎立，《大史》记载它在4世纪被摩诃斯那王拆毁，但中国求法僧法显约在406年见到寺中仍有三千僧人。12世纪，波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世转而支持大寺，取缔对立僧团，将僧伽统一在大寺法脉之下；这一法脉又从斯里兰卡传出，深刻塑造了东南亚的上座部佛教。

en: The Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple stands on the southern bank of the Pamba River in central Kerala and honours Krishna in his role as Parthasarathy, the charioteer of Arjuna in the Mahabharata. It is one of the five ancient Pandava shrines of the Chengannur region, which legend credits to the five Pandava brothers one apiece; Arjuna is said to have built this one to atone for slaying the unarmed Karna. The place takes its name from the bamboo raft, made of six pieces, that carried its image to the site. Counted among the hundred and eight Divya Desams, the Vishnu temples glorified by the Tamil Alvar saints, it is built in the Kerala style and preserves wall paintings from the early 1700s. It also guards the golden Thanka Anki vestment of Ayyappan, presented by the rulers of Travancore and carried each year to Sabarimala, while its riverside steps host the celebrated Aranmula snake-boat race held every Onam season.
zh: 阿兰穆拉的阿周那之御者神庙坐落在喀拉拉中部潘巴河南岸，供奉《摩诃婆罗多》中担任阿周那御者的奎师那，即“帕塔萨拉斯瓦米”。它是琴加努尔一带五座古老的般度族神庙之一，相传五座庙分别由般度五子所建，本庙为阿周那为忏悔诛杀手无寸铁的迦尔纳之罪而建。地名源于运送神像的六根竹筏。该庙被列为毗湿奴派一百零八座迪维亚·德萨姆之一，即泰米尔阿尔瓦尔派圣徒歌颂的毗湿奴神庙，整体为喀拉拉建筑风格，庙墙保存着18世纪初的壁画。庙中还珍藏着阿亚潘的金衣“坦加安吉”，由特拉凡哥尔王公奉献，每年送往萨巴里马拉；河边石阶则在每年欧南节期间举办著名的阿兰穆拉蛇船赛。

en: The Arasavalli Sun Temple, formally the Sri Surya Narayana Swamy Devalayam, is a shrine of Surya, the sun god, in Arasavalli, a village one kilometre east of Srikakulam on the northern coast of Andhra Pradesh. Wall inscriptions ascribe its founding to Devendra Varma of the Eastern Ganga dynasty of Kalinga in the 600s CE, making it one of the oldest surviving sun temples in India. The Padma Purana credits the sage Kashyapa with installing the Surya image for the good of mankind, while a local sthalapurana tells how Indra, struck blind by the sun god after an affront to Shiva's gatekeeper Nandi, regained his sight by setting up and worshipping the icon here. The temple is built in the rekha deula form of Kalinga architecture, its curving tower kin to the Jagannath temple at Puri. The building later fell into ruin and was reconstructed in 1778 by Elamanchili Pullaji Panthulu, with further repairs paid for by the Dusi family. The annual Ratha Saptami festival is its great gathering, when pilgrims greet the rising sun at the temple gate.
zh: 阿拉萨瓦利的太阳神庙正式名称为室利·苏利耶·那罗衍那·斯瓦米神庙，供奉太阳神苏利耶，位于安得拉邦北部沿海斯里卡库兰以东一公里的阿拉萨瓦利村。庙墙铭文记载，神庙由羯陵伽东恒伽王朝的提婆因陀罗·瓦尔摩于7世纪创建，是印度现存最古老的太阳神庙之一。《莲花往世书》称迦叶波仙人为造福人类而安立了这尊苏利耶像；当地的圣地往世书则讲述，因陀罗冒犯了湿婆的守门神牛南迪，被太阳神灼瞎双眼，为复明只得在此立像供奉，重获光明。神庙采用羯陵伽建筑的雷卡德乌拉式，曲形高塔与补梨的札格纳特神庙一脉相承。建筑后来倾圮，1778年由埃拉曼奇利·普拉吉·潘图卢重建，杜西家族又捐资继续修缮。一年一度的拉特萨普塔米节是庙中最盛大的集会，香客们在庙门迎接初升的太阳。

en: Armagh in Ulster is the ecclesiastical capital of Ireland and the seat of the archbishop who bears the title Primate of All Ireland. The hill above the town had been a pagan sanctuary, named Ard Mhacha, the height of Macha, after a goddess of Gaelic tradition, before Saint Patrick founded his principal church there in 445. By the seventh century its monastery and school were the foremost in the north of Ireland, and in the early ninth century its scribes produced the Book of Armagh, one of the oldest surviving manuscripts in Old Irish. Vikings first raided it in 832, yet its prestige endured: the high king Brian Boru acknowledged it as head church of Ireland in 1004 and was buried there after Clontarf in 1014, and a national synod of 1111 confirmed its primacy. The cathedral was rebuilt in 1268, but the Tudor conquest left the town in ruins by 1601, and the church passed to the Protestant Church of Ireland, which rebuilt it under Archbishop Christopher Hampton.
zh: 位于阿尔斯特的阿马是爱尔兰的教会首府，驻节于此的大主教拥有“全爱尔兰首席主教”头衔。镇旁的山丘本是异教圣地，按盖尔传统以女神玛查之名称为阿尔德·瓦卡，即玛查之丘；445年，圣帕特里克在此建立了他的主要教堂。到7世纪，这里的修道院和学校已是爱尔兰北部首屈一指的学术中心，9世纪初抄写员在此完成《阿马书》，这是现存最古老的古爱尔兰语手抄本之一。维京人于832年首次洗劫此地，但它的威望不衰：至高王布赖恩·博鲁于1004年承认它为爱尔兰教会之首，并在1014年克朗塔夫战役后安葬于此；1111年的全国宗教会议又确认了它的首席地位。座堂于1268年重建，但都铎王朝的征服使该镇到1601年沦为废墟，教堂也转入新教的爱尔兰教会手中，后由大主教克里斯托弗·汉普顿主持重建。

en: The Artemision at Ephesus, on the coast of Ionia, was the great temple of Artemis and counted among the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. A shrine had stood on the spot since the Bronze Age, but the first stone temple was swept away by a flood in the seventh century BC; the marble temple begun around 550 BC by the architect Chersiphron and paid for by Croesus of Lydia made the sanctuary famous across the Greek world. In 356 BC a man named Herostratus burned it down merely to immortalise his name, an act that tradition placed on the very night Alexander the Great was born. Alexander offered to pay for its rebuilding, and the Ephesians refused; after his death in 323 BC they raised a still larger temple, more than a hundred and twenty-seven columns strong, decorated by sculptors such as Scopas. This building stood until Gothic raiders destroyed it in 262 AD, and although worship of Artemis lingered until about 401, the temple was never restored; by the later Middle Ages only foundations remained beside the village that grew up at Selçuk.
zh: 阿耳忒弥斯神庙位于爱奥尼亚海岸的以弗所，是供奉阿耳忒弥斯的大庙，被列为古代世界七大奇迹之一。青铜时代起此地便有神龛，但最早的石庙在公元前7世纪被洪水冲毁；约公元前550年，建筑师凯尔西弗龙主持、吕底亚国王克洛伊索斯出资兴建的大理石神庙，使圣地闻名于整个希腊世界。公元前356年，一个名叫赫洛斯特拉特的人为使自己的名字不朽而纵火烧庙，传说此事正发生在亚历山大大帝出生的当夜。亚历山大曾表示愿出资重建，被以弗所人婉拒；他们从公元前323年亚历山大去世后自费建起一座更宏伟的新庙，立柱超过一百二十七根，由斯科帕斯等雕刻家装饰。这座建筑一直矗立到262年哥特袭掠者将它摧毁；尽管对阿耳忒弥斯的崇拜延续到约401年，神庙却再未修复，到中世纪后期只剩下地基，旁侧的聚落发展为后来的塞尔丘克。

en: The Arulmigu Koniamman Temple lies on the northern bank of the Noyyal River at the heart of Coimbatore, in the Kongu Nadu country, and is dedicated to Koniamman, a form of Parvati who is honoured as the guardian goddess of the city. Local tradition derives both the goddess and the place from the chieftain Kovan: his tutelary deity Koyamma became Koniamman, while his settlement Koyampuththoor grew into Coimbatore. The English account dates the shrine to the 1000s, when the descendants of Kovan are said to have built it; Tamil sources instead credit the Irula forest people with raising it in the 1200s. After the rule of those tribal chiefs the temple declined, until in the 1700s a king of Mysore, whose kingdom had absorbed Kongu Nadu, restored it and installed the goddess in her Mahishasura Mardini form, the slayer of the buffalo demon. Together with the Perur Pateeswarar Temple it counts as one of the two historic shrines of Coimbatore.
zh: 阿卢利弥具‑拘尼阎曼神庙位于孔古纳德地区哥印拜陀市中心的诺伊尔河北岸，供奉帕尔瓦蒂的化身拘尼阎曼，她被尊为这座城市的守护女神。当地传说把女神和城市的由来都系于首领科万：他供奉的保护神科亚姆玛演变为拘尼阎曼，而他的居留地科扬普图尔则发展为哥印拜陀。英文资料称此庙建于11世纪，出自科万后裔之手；泰米尔资料则说它是13世纪前后伊鲁拉尔林中部族所建。部族首领的统治结束后神庙一度衰落，18世纪孔古纳德并入迈索尔王国，一位迈索尔国王将其重修，并以斩杀牛魔王的杜尔加形象安奉女神。它与佩鲁尔·帕提什瓦拉神庙并称哥印拜陀的两大古刹。

en: The Temple of Jupiter Heliopolitanus at Baalbek, in the Beqaa Valley of Lebanon, was the greatest sanctuary of Roman Syria and the largest temple ever dedicated to Jupiter in the empire.
