Baalbek, renamed Heliopolis after Alexander the Great's conquest in 334 BC, had long been a cult centre of the Semitic storm god Baal Haddu, whom the Greeks and Romans equated with Zeus and Jupiter; the Roman temple therefore continued an older, syncretic worship. After Augustus planted a colony of veterans there around 16 BC, work began on the colossal temple and its Great Court, largely complete by AD 60 and embellished over three centuries by Nero's tower-altar and Trajan's granite porticoes. Its fifty-four Corinthian columns, nearly twenty metres tall, were the highest in the classical world, and the podium was raised on the famed Trilithon, three blocks of about eight hundred tonnes each. Emperors consulted its oracle, and Trajan was warned there of his approaching death in about 115. Earthquakes and Christian spoliation under Theodosius damaged the temple, Justinian carried eight columns to Constantinople for Hagia Sophia, and after the Arab conquest the ruins were absorbed into medieval fortifications, rebuilt by the Mamluk sultan Qalawun in the thirteenth century after the Mongol raid of Kitbuqa. Three more columns collapsed in the earthquakes of 1759.
zh: 朱庇特·赫利奥波利斯神庙位于黎巴嫩贝卡谷地的巴勒贝克，是罗马叙利亚最宏伟的圣所，也是帝国境内献给朱庇特的最大神庙。公元前334年亚历山大大帝征服后，巴勒贝克更名为赫利奥波利斯；此地早就是闪米特风暴神巴阿勒·哈达的崇拜中心，希腊人和罗马人将他等同于宙斯和朱庇特，罗马神庙因而延续了古老的混合崇拜。约公元前16年奥古斯都在此安置退伍老兵殖民地后，这座巨庙及其大庭院动工，公元60年左右主体落成，此后三个世纪里又陆续增建了尼禄的塔状祭坛和图拉真的花岗岩柱廊。神庙的54根科林斯柱高近20米，为古典世界之最；台基建在著名的“三石”之上，每块巨石重约800吨。历代皇帝常来此求问神谕，图拉真约在115年在这里得到死期将近的警示。地震与狄奥多西时期基督徒的拆取损害了神庙，查士丁尼又将八根石柱运往君士坦丁堡修建圣索菲亚大教堂；阿拉伯征服后，废墟被纳入中世纪防御工事，怯的不花的蒙古军破坏之后，马穆鲁克苏丹嘉拉温于13世纪加以重修。1759年的地震又震塌了三根石柱。

en: High in the Garhwal Himalayas on the Alaknanda river, Badrinath is the northernmost of the four Char Dham shrines, with Puri, Dwarka and Rameswaram, and chief of the five Panch Badri; its black stone image of Vishnu as Badrinarayan, seated in the lotus posture beneath a badri tree, is one of the eight self-manifested Vishnu icons and of the 108 Divya Desams. The Vishnu Purana places the penance of sages Nara and Narayana here, and Lakshmi is said to have sheltered the meditating Vishnu as a badri, or jujube, tree, giving the shrine its name. Tradition credits Adi Shankara with founding the pilgrimage in the ninth century, recovering its image from the hot Tapt Kund springs and re-establishing worship with the Parmar rajas of Garhwal, who endowed pilgrim villages and bore the title Bolanda Badrinath, the speaking Badrinath. Garhwal kings installed the image in the present temple in the sixteenth century and enlarged it in the next, but the great earthquake of 1803 left it propped and crumbling, until the King of Jaipur rebuilt much of it. Snow closes the shrine for half the year, when the deity is notionally moved to the Narasimha temple at Jyotirmath and a ghee lamp left burning; in summer the annual fair drew pilgrims north from Haridwar. After the Gorkhas were driven out in 1815 the region passed to the East India Company, which built the first road from Haridwar and opened dispensaries along the route after a cholera outbreak in 1820.
zh: 伯德里纳特深藏加瓦尔喜马拉雅山区、坐落在阿拉卡南达河畔，是印度教四大圣地（恰尔达姆）中位置最北的一座，其余三处为普里、德瓦尔卡与拉梅斯沃勒姆；它也是五座“潘查巴德里”之首，庙里黑石雕成的巴德里纳拉扬像结跏趺坐于巴德里树下，被列为毗湿奴八处自显神像之一，也属108处圣域。《毗湿奴往世书》讲述仙人那罗与那罗延在这些山谷中苦修，传说吉祥天女曾化作一棵巴德里树（枣树）为入定的毗湿奴遮寒，神庙因此得名。传统认为9世纪的阿迪·商羯罗开创了这场朝圣：他从温热的塔普特昆德泉中找回神像，在加瓦尔的帕尔马拉杰协助下重建祭祀；拉杰的后裔们赐封村庄供养、留宿朝圣者，并拥有“会说话的伯德里纳特”头衔。16世纪加瓦尔国王把神像迁入现存神庙，17世纪又加以扩建，但1803年的大地震使庙宇倾颓、靠木架支撑，后来由斋浦尔王公主持重建。大雪每年封山半年，期间神像被象征性地迎往焦蒂尔马特的那罗辛哈神庙，庙中留一盏酥油灯长明；暖和的季节里，一年一度的节会把朝圣者从赫里德瓦尔的集会一路吸引北上。1815年廓尔喀人被逐出后，该地转归英国东印度公司，公司官员修筑了从赫里德瓦尔到此的第一条道路，并在1820年霍乱疫情后沿朝圣路线开设了医馆。

en: The patriarchal see of the Church of the East was fixed in 410 at the Council of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, whose catholicos ruled from Kokhe, the Christian quarter of the Sasanian capital. When the caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad nearby in 762, the patriarch was compelled to move into the new city, which then became the heart of a church stretching from Mesopotamia to India, Central Asia and Tang China. Under Patriarch Timothy I, who reigned from 780 to 823, Baghdad hosted missions, scholarship and a hospital he founded at the old capital. The Mongol sack of 1258 at first spared the Christians: Hulagu's wife Doquz Khatun interceded for them, and the patriarch Makkikha II, who had taken part in the surrender negotiations, was even granted the caliphal palace as a church. The Ilkhan Ghazan's conversion to Islam in 1295 ended this favor, and Timur's storm of Baghdad in 1401 shattered the community; during the fifteenth century the patriarchs withdrew to Alqosh near Mosul. The schism of 1552 then produced a rival Chaldean Catholic line when Yohannan Sulaqa was consecrated in Rome, and after decades of further splits two patriarchates, one Chaldean Catholic and one traditionalist, had settled into lasting separation by 1830.
zh: 410年的塞琉西亚-泰西封公会议确立了东方教会的牧首座堂，牧首（卡托利科斯）驻在萨珊首都基督徒聚居的科赫区。762年哈里发曼苏尔在附近兴建巴格达后，牧首被迫迁入新城，巴格达由此成为一个从美索不达米亚延伸到印度、中亚乃至唐代中国的教会的核心。780—823年在位的牧首提摩太一世时期，这里差会林立、学术繁荣，他还在旧都创办了医院。1258年蒙古人攻陷巴格达时，基督徒起初得以幸免：旭烈兀之妻脱古思可敦为他们求情，参与投降谈判的牧首马基哈二世甚至获赐哈里发宫殿作为教堂。1295年伊尔汗合赞改宗伊斯兰教，这种优待随之终结；1401年帖木儿攻破巴格达，社群遭到毁灭性打击，15世纪间牧首们退居摩苏尔附近的阿尔科什。1552年的大分裂又产生了竞争的迦勒底天主教一脉——约哈南·苏拉卡在罗马受祝圣为主教；此后又经数十年分裂，到1830年，迦勒底天主教与传统派两个牧首体系形成了持久并立的局面。

en: The Bajreshwari Mata Temple stands at Kangra, the hill fortress town of Nagarkot in the Punjab Himalayas, seat of the Katoch Rajput kings of ancient Trigarta. Its goddess Vajreshwari, whose name means Lady of the Thunderbolt, is a fierce form of Durga who slew the demon Kalikala with a divine vajra, and the shrine is counted among the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, for tradition places the falling of Sati's left breast on this spot. Long reputed one of the oldest and richest temples of northern India, it drew pilgrims and plunderers alike: Mahmud of Ghazni is said to have sacked it on his Indian campaign of 1009, though the Kangra fort above it was regarded as impregnable until the Mughal emperor Jahangir finally took it in 1622. The Katoch rajas recovered the fortress after Jahangir's death, and in the wars of the early 1800s Gurkha troops seized it in 1806 before a Sikh-Katoch alliance retook it in 1809; Ranjit Singh annexed Kangra in 1810. Through these changes of rule the goddess kept her pilgrims, and a shrine of Bhairava stands within the temple enclosure.
zh: 婆折丽湿伐梨神庙坐落于旁遮普喜马拉雅山区的冈格拉，即古称讷格尔果德的山城要塞，古特里加尔塔的卡托奇拉杰普特诸王以此为都。主神伐折丽湿伐梨之名意为金刚杵女神，是难近母的忿怒化身，相传以神赐金刚杵诛杀恶魔迦里迦罗；该庙位列五十一处性力佩特，传说萨蒂的左乳坠落于此。神庙久负北印度最古老、最富庶庙宇之名，既吸引朝圣者也招来劫掠：据说伽色尼的马哈茂德在1009年的印度远征中曾洗劫此庙，而山上的冈格拉要塞被视为坚不可破，直到1622年才被莫卧儿皇帝贾汉吉尔攻克。贾汉吉尔死后卡托奇王公收复要塞；19世纪初的战乱中，廓尔喀军队于1806年占据此地，锡克与卡托奇联军又在1809年将其夺回，兰吉特·辛格最终于1810年吞并冈格拉。尽管政权更迭，女神的香火始终不衰，庙区内还建有一座拜罗伐神殿。

en: The Bhu Varaha Swamy Temple at Srimushnam in northern Tamil Nadu is dedicated to Vishnu's boar avatar Varaha, seated with Lakshmi as Ambujavalli Thayar, and is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethras of the Vaishnava tradition. Legend says Varaha slew the asura Hiranyaksha on this spot, and that the drops of his sweat formed the temple tank Nithya Pushkarani; the central icon turns its boar face south toward the fallen demon while its human body faces the worshippers. Chola inscriptions attest the shrine's medieval antiquity: an epigraph of 1068 records gifts by Virarajendra Chola, and around 1100 Kulothunga Chola I granted a whole village to the god, whom the records call Varaha Alvar. The Vijayanagara emperors added the seven-storey gateway, and the temple was rebuilt and expanded under their vassals the Thanjavur Nayaks, above all Achuthappa Nayak between 1560 and 1614, who raised the sixteen-pillared Purushasuktha Mandapa. It became a stronghold of Madhva teaching: Madhvacharya himself repeatedly stayed here and kept his four-month vows on the site, and later saints such as Vyasatirtha and Raghavendra Tirtha also resided at the temple.
zh: 布筏罗诃斯瓦米神庙位于泰米尔纳德邦北部的斯里穆什纳姆，供奉毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃，其配偶吉祥天女以“安布贾瓦利·塔亚尔”之名同祀，被列为毗湿奴派108处阿比摩纳圣地之一。传说筏罗诃在此诛杀阿修罗王金目，他滴落的汗水汇成了庙中的尼提亚·普什卡拉尼圣池；主像的猪脸朝南、望向伏诛的妖魔，人形身躯则面向信众。朱罗王朝的铭文证明了神庙的中世纪渊源：1068年的碑刻记载毗罗罗贞陀罗·朱罗的布施，约1100年俱卢通伽·朱罗一世又向铭文中称作“筏罗诃阿尔瓦尔”的主神献上整座村庄。毗奢耶那伽罗皇帝增建了七层门楼，其后藩属坦贾武尔纳亚克王朝又重建扩建，尤其是1560至1614年间在位的阿丘塔帕·纳亚克，修建了十六柱的原人颂柱厅。这座庙还是摩陀婆派的重镇：摩陀婆阿阇梨本人曾多次驻锡、在此守四月安居誓，毗阿萨提尔塔、罗伽文德拉提尔塔等后世圣徒也长期居停于此。

en: The Biraja Temple at Jajpur, the town called Jajnagar in Muslim chronicles, is the ancient shrine that gave the place its older name of Biraja Kshetra, the field of the goddess Viraja. Tantric texts such as the Tantra Chudamani teach that the navel of Sati fell here in the old Utkala kingdom, and Adi Shankara's hymn to the eighteen Shakta Pithas invokes the presiding goddess as Girija; the Brahmayamala Tantra already pairs Vimala of Puri with Viraja of Utkala as the two great goddesses of Odisha. The present Deula-style temple was raised in the 1000s, though Jajpur had been a capital under the Somavanshi king Yayati Keshari from 473 and later under the Buddhist Bhauma-Kara dynasty of the 700s, and the town remained a centre of Tantric worship. Its two-armed Durga spears Mahishasura while pulling his tail, one foot on her lion and the other on the buffalo demon, and a separate shrine houses the rarely worshipped Bagalamukhi, one of the ten Mahavidyas. A sacred well named Nabhi Gaya draws pilgrims for rites for the dead, and an annual sixteen-day Durga Puja culminates in the animal sacrifice of Bali Dana.
zh: 毗罗阇神庙位于贾杰纳加尔，即穆斯林编年史中所称的贾杰纳加尔、今贾贾普尔；这座古庙使该地得旧名毗罗阇之野，意为女神毗罗阇的领域。《密教宝髻》等密典记载，萨蒂的肚脐落在古乌特卡拉王国的此处，商羯罗的十八性力佩特颂称主神为吉里阇；《梵鬘密续》早已将补梨的毗摩罗与乌特卡拉的毗罗阇并列为奥里萨的两大女神。现存德乌拉风格建筑约建于1000年代，而贾贾普尔自473年起便是索马万什国王耶耶迪·凯沙里的王都，700年代又为佛教婆摩-迦罗王朝的都城，始终是密教崇拜的中心。庙中双臂难近母一足踏狮、一足踩水牛魔，一手持矛刺向摩西沙修罗、一手拽其尾巴；另有独立殿堂供奉十大明妃中罕见受祀的婆伽罗穆基。庙中圣井名脐伽耶，吸引信众前来举行超度先人的仪式；每年长达十六天的难近母节以兽祭巴利达那收尾。

en: Known as Uruvela in the Buddha's lifetime, Bodh Gaya on the Phalgu River in Magadha is where Siddhartha Gautama, after six years of asceticism and a final meal of rice milk offered by the village woman Sujata, sat beneath a sacred fig tree, found the Middle Way and attained enlightenment. The tree became the Bodhi Tree, and the stone Vajrasana, the diamond throne marking the exact seat of his awakening, has been dated to the 200s BCE; nearby shrines recall the seven weeks he spent in the area, including the unblinking Animeshlocha Stupa and the jewel-walk Ratnachakrama. The Chinese pilgrims Faxian in the 400s and Xuanzang in the 600s left detailed accounts of a thriving monastic centre, which from the 1000s to the 1200s was protected by the Pithipati rajas of Magadha, who even granted land to Sri Lankan monks. Turkic invasions around the end of the 1100s shattered that Buddhist world, and the ruined site passed centuries in obscurity; the name Bodh Gaya itself only came into use in the 1700s, while pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Tibet, Nepal and Myanmar kept the memory of the place alive.
zh: 菩提伽耶在佛陀在世时称“优楼频螺”，位于摩揭陀的帕尔古河畔。悉达多·乔达摩在此经历六年苦行，又接受村女善生供养的乳糜，最后坐在一棵神圣的榕树下证得中道、觉悟成佛。那棵树后称菩提树，标记其成道之座的石制“金刚座”可追溯至公元前3世纪；周边圣迹对应他成道后停留的七周，包括目不暂舍的“不瞬塔”和名为“宝行经”的往返步道。5世纪的法显与7世纪的玄奘都曾详细记载这座繁盛的僧院中心；11至13世纪，摩揭陀的皮蒂帕蒂王公守护此地，还曾为斯里兰卡僧人赐地。12世纪末前后突厥人的入侵摧毁了这一佛教世界，荒废的遗址沉寂了数百年，“菩提伽耶”这一名称直到18世纪才通行，全靠斯里兰卡、西藏、尼泊尔和缅甸的朝圣者维系着对圣地的记忆。

en: B'olon Yej Te' Naah, the House of the Nine Sharpened Spears, is the largest pyramid at Palenque, the Maya city-state anciently called Lakamha in the Chiapas lowlands, known to archaeologists as the Temple of the Inscriptions. It was raised as the funerary monument of K'inich Janaab' Pakal, who ruled Palenque from 615 to 683; building began in the last decade of his life and was finished by his son K'inich Kan Bahlam II shortly after 683. Three tablets inside carry 617 glyphs, among the longest of all Maya inscriptions, chronicling Pakal's reign and naming his heir. A hidden stairway descends from the temple floor to the burial chamber, where the king lay in a carved sarcophagus whose lid shows him sinking into the jaws of the underworld beneath the cosmic tree, wearing a jade mosaic death mask; five sacrificed attendants were placed at the crypt's entrance to follow him into the next world. Palenque's last dated monuments fall around 799, and within a generation the city collapsed and the jungle of cedar and mahogany closed over the temple, its hidden burial chamber left undisturbed beneath the roots.
zh: 九锐矛铭文神庙，古典玛雅语意为“九支磨尖长矛之屋”，是恰帕斯低地玛雅城邦帕伦克（古称拉卡姆哈）最大的金字塔，今称铭文神庙。它是为615年至683年统治帕伦克的金尼奇·贾纳布·巴加尔修建的陵墓，工程始于他生前最后十年，由其子金尼奇·坎·巴拉姆二世在683年稍后完工。庙内三块铭文板刻有617个象形文字，是已知最长的玛雅铭文之一，记述巴加尔的统治并指定继承人。一条隐秘阶梯从庙内地面通往地下墓室，国王安卧于雕刻石棺之中，棺盖刻画他在宇宙树下沉入冥界之口的形象，脸上戴着玉片镶嵌的死亡面具；墓室入口还殉葬了五名侍从，随他前往来世。帕伦克最后的纪年碑刻约在799年，此后不出一代人城邦便告崩溃，雪松和桃花心木的丛林吞没了神庙，隐秘的墓室在树根之下始终未被惊扰。

en: Borobudur is a ninth-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in the Kedu Plain of Central Java, northwest of Yogyakarta, raised under the Sailendra dynasty from dark andesite. Its nine stacked platforms, six square and three circular, climb to a central dome ringed by seventy-two Buddha statues seated inside perforated stupas; the walls and balustrades carry 2,672 relief panels, including 1,460 narrative scenes that guide pilgrims upward from the everyday world toward enlightenment. Inscriptions of 824 and 842 record the inauguration and endowment of the sanctuary, which fused the Buddhist path to nirvana with older Javanese ancestor veneration. By the fourteenth century, as the courts of Java turned to Islam, the temple was abandoned and slowly buried under volcanic ash and jungle; the court poet Mpu Prapanca could still mention a holy place at Budur in 1365. It lay forgotten until 1814, when the British administrator Thomas Stamford Raffles, told of its location by local people, ordered the site cleared and surveyed, bringing the largest Buddhist monument in the world back to knowledge.
zh: 婆罗浮屠寺是9世纪的大乘佛教寺院，坐落在中爪哇日惹西北的克杜平原，由夏连特拉王朝用深色安山岩建成。它由九层堆叠的平台组成，下方六层为方形、上方三层为圆形，顶端是中央穹顶，周围环绕着72尊安坐于镂空佛塔中的佛像；墙壁和栏杆上共有2672块浮雕板，其中1460块叙事浮雕引导朝圣者从世俗世界拾级而上，走向觉悟。824年和842年的铭文记载了这座圣所的落成与赐地，它把佛教的涅槃之道与爪哇古老的祖先崇拜融为一体。14世纪，随着爪哇诸宫廷改宗伊斯兰教，寺院被弃置，逐渐被火山灰和丛林掩埋；宫廷诗人普拉潘查在1365年仍提到布杜尔有一处圣地。它就此湮没无闻，直到1814年，英国殖民官员托马斯·斯坦福德·莱佛士从当地人口中得知其位置，下令清理和勘测遗址，才让这座世界上最大的佛教建筑重为人知。

en: The Brihadisvara Temple, named Rajarajesvaram by its founder and still called the Big Temple of Thanjavur, stands on the south bank of the Cauvery and is the supreme monument of Chola architecture, praised as the Dakshina Meru, the Meru mountain of the south. The Chola emperor Rajaraja I built it entirely of granite between 1003 and 1010, raising a vimana tower that remains one of the tallest in South India above a sanctum holding one of the largest lingams in India; an inscription of 1011 lists more than six hundred priests, dancers, singers, jewelers and carpenters maintained by the temple, which also employed devadasis and fed pilgrims daily. Its walls carry sixty-four inscriptions of Rajaraja and twenty-nine of his son Rajendra I, along with Chola frescoes and the celebrated bronze Nataraja, Shiva as lord of the dance, first cast for this shrine. After the Chola age the temple suffered in the wars between the sultans of Madurai and the Hindu rulers of Thanjavur, but each dynasty that recovered the city repaired it: the Nayakas of the 16th and 17th centuries added the Parvati, Murugan and Nandi shrines and enclosed the complex with fort-like walls, and the Maratha kings of Thanjavur after them kept the great temple in repair. Together with the later Chola temples at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Darasuram it forms the great trio of living Chola temples.
zh: 婆利诃地湿伐罗神庙由建造者命名为“罗阇罗阇湿婆罗”，当地俗称坦贾武尔大庙，雄踞高韦里河南岸，是朱罗建筑的最高典范，被誉为“南方的须弥山”。朱罗皇帝罗阇罗阇一世于1003年至1010年间全以花岗岩建成此庙，维马纳塔楼属南印度最高的塔之列，塔下密室供奉着印度最大的林伽之一；1011年的一段铭文列出神庙供养的六百余名祭司、舞女、歌手、珠宝匠和木匠，庙中还蓄有神殿舞女，并每日向朝圣者施食。庙壁上有罗阇罗阇的铭文六十四处、其子罗贞陀罗一世的二十九处，并存有朱罗壁画和著名的舞王纳塔罗阇铜像——湿婆舞蹈之主的形象最初便是为这座神庙铸造的。朱罗时代之后，神庙在马杜赖苏丹与坦贾武尔印度教王公的战争中受损，但每一个收复该城的王朝都加以修缮：16至17世纪的纳亚克诸王增建了帕尔瓦蒂、穆卢干和南迪神祠，并以堡垒般的围墙环绕全庙，其后的坦贾武尔马拉塔国王也持续维护这座大庙。它与后来建于恒伽贡达朱罗普拉姆和达拉苏拉姆的朱罗神庙并称三大“活着的朱罗神庙”。

en: Burgos Cathedral, dedicated to the Virgin Mary, stands in the former royal capital of Castile on the pilgrim road to Santiago de Compostela. Burgos became a bishopric in 1075 under Alfonso VI, heir to the older Visigothic see of Oca, and a first Romanesque cathedral was finished there in 1096. The present Gothic church was begun on 20 June 1221, when King Ferdinand III and Bishop Maurice laid the first stone; a French master builder gave it forms modelled on the cathedrals of Paris and Reims, and the building was consecrated in 1260. Work continued for centuries: in the fifteenth century Juan de Colonia raised the openwork spires of the west front, and the late fifteenth and sixteenth centuries added the lantern dome over the transept and the richly carved Chapel of the Constable, masterpieces of flamboyant Gothic. Eighteenth-century sacristies and chapels completed the ensemble.
zh: 布尔戈斯主教座堂奉圣母马利亚为主保，坐落在卡斯蒂利亚旧日的王都，正处在前往圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉的朝圣路上。1075年，阿方索六世设立布尔戈斯主教区，承接更古老的西哥特奥卡教区；第一座罗马式主教座堂于1096年在当地落成。现存的哥特式教堂则始建于1221年6月20日，由国王费尔南多三世和主教莫里斯共同安放奠基石，一位法国建筑师傅以巴黎和兰斯主教座堂为蓝本设计形制，教堂于1260年举行祝圣礼。工程持续了数百年：15世纪，胡安·德·科洛尼亚竖起了西立面镂空的双塔尖；15世纪末至16世纪又增建了十字甬道上方的灯笼式穹顶和雕刻华丽的治安官小堂，均为火焰哥特式的杰作。18世纪添建的圣器室和小堂为整组建筑收尾。

en: Canterbury Cathedral in Kent is the seat of the archbishop of Canterbury, the foremost prelate of the English Church. It was founded in 597 by Augustine, leader of the Gregorian mission sent from Rome to convert the Anglo-Saxons, on the site of an older Roman church. After the Norman Conquest the cathedral was rebuilt between 1070 and 1077 under Archbishop Lanfranc, and rebuilt again in the Gothic style after a fire in 1174. Its greatest claim to sanctity was the shrine of Thomas Becket, the archbishop murdered before the altar by knights of Henry II in 1170; pilgrims flocked to it for the next three and a half centuries, and the east end was enlarged to hold them. In 1538 Henry VIII dissolved the priory and destroyed Becket's shrine during the English Reformation, though the cathedral church itself survived.
zh: 位于肯特的坎特伯雷座堂是坎特伯雷大主教的驻节地，而大主教是英格兰教会地位最高的教士。597年，奉罗马教廷之命前来向盎格鲁-撒克逊人传教的格里高利传教团首领奥古斯丁，在一座更古老的罗马教堂旧址上建立了这座座堂。诺曼征服后，座堂于1070至1077年间在大主教兰弗朗克主持下重建，1174年火灾后又按哥特风格重建。它最负盛名的圣迹是托马斯·贝克特圣龛：这位大主教于1170年被亨利二世的骑士杀死在祭坛前，此后三个半世纪里朝圣者纷至沓来，座堂东端也为容纳人流而扩建。1538年，亨利八世在英格兰宗教改革中解散了附属修道院并捣毁贝克特圣龛，不过座堂建筑本身得以保存。

en: The Capitolium was the greatest temple of the Roman state, crowning the Capitoline Hill above the Forum and housing the Capitoline Triad of Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina and Minerva, each with a separate cella. Vowed by King Tarquinius Priscus and finished under Tarquinius Superbus, it was traditionally dedicated in 509 BC, the first year of the Republic; Etruscan craftsmen, including Vulca of Veii, made its terracotta sculpture, and the omens attending its foundations, including a human head dug from the rock, were read as a promise that Rome would head a great empire. The wooden temple burned in 83 BC, taking the Sibylline Books with it, and the replacement, dedicated by Catulus in 69 BC, reused columns Sulla had carried off from Athens. After murdering Caesar in 44 BC, Brutus and the conspirators barricaded themselves within it. Fire destroyed it again in 69 and 80 AD; Vespasian and then Domitian rebuilt it, the latter spending twelve thousand talents of gold on the gilded roof alone. Theodosius I closed it with the other pagan temples in 392, the Vandals stripped its bronze tiles in 455 and Narses removed its statues in 571; the last ruins were demolished in the sixteenth century when the Palazzo Caffarelli was raised over the podium.
zh: 卡庇托林神庙是罗马国家最崇高的神庙，雄踞广场上方的卡庇托林山，供奉卡庇托林三神：至善至大的朱庇特、天后朱诺和密涅瓦，三者各有独立内殿。神庙由国王老塔克文许愿兴建，在骄傲者塔克文治下完工，传统上认为于公元前509年、即共和国建立的第一年落成；包括维爱的乌尔卡在内的伊特鲁里亚工匠制作了赤陶雕塑，而奠基时的种种征兆——尤其是从岩基中挖出的一颗人头——被解读为罗马将成为帝国之首的预兆。这座木构神庙于公元前83年失火，寄存其中的《西卜林书》一同化为灰烬；重建的神庙于公元前69年由卡图卢斯主持献祭，复用了苏拉从雅典掠来的石柱。公元前44年恺撒遇刺后，布鲁图斯等密谋者曾把自己关在庙中。神庙又于公元69年和80年两度焚毁，韦斯巴芗和图密善先后重建，据说仅镀金屋顶一项，图密善就耗费了一万两千塔兰特黄金。392年，狄奥多西一世将它与其他异教神庙一并关闭；455年汪达尔人剥走了铜瓦，571年纳尔塞斯移走了雕像。16世纪，卡法雷利宫建在神庙台基之上，最后的残迹也被拆毁。

en: The sanctuary of the Vera Cruz stands in the castle above Caravaca, in the Murcian hills near the old frontier with Granada, and guards a Lignum Crucis, a fragment believed to come from the True Cross. Tradition places its origin in 1231 or 1232, when the captive missionary Gínes Pérez Chirinos was made to say Mass before the Muslim ruler Zeyt-Abuzeyt: as the priest lamented the lack of a crucifix, two angels were said to bring a cross down from heaven and place it on the altar, and the ruler and his family converted and asked for baptism. The relic, venerated as the double-barred Caravaca Cross flanked by angels, was guarded first by the Knights Templar from 1266 and, after 1344, by the Order of Santiago. After 1492 Franciscan friars carried copies of it to the Americas. The medieval chapel in the castle was replaced by a Baroque basilica-sanctuary, built between 1617 and 1703.
zh: 真十字圣殿矗立在卡拉瓦卡城堡的高地上，地处穆尔西亚山区，邻近旧时与格拉纳达接壤的边地，堂内供奉着一块被认为取自真十字架的木片。相传此事源于1231或1232年：被俘的传教士希内斯·佩雷斯被迫在穆斯林统治者宰特·阿布·宰特面前主持弥撒，正当神父叹息没有十字架时，两位天使自天而降，把一座十字架放在祭坛上，统治者全家因而皈依并请求受洗。这件圣物以双横杠、两侧有天使相伴的卡拉瓦卡十字造型受人敬拜，1266年起由圣殿骑士团守护，1344年后改由圣地亚哥骑士团看管。1492年之后，方济各会修士把它的复制品带到了美洲。城堡里的中世纪小堂后来被一座巴洛克式圣殿取代，新堂建于1617至1703年间。

en: The Cave of the Patriarchs, known to Muslims as the Ibrahimi Mosque or Sanctuary of Ibrahim, stands in the Old City of Hebron over the cave that the Book of Genesis says Abraham bought as a family tomb, and which tradition holds to contain the graves of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, and Jacob and Leah. The massive rectangular enclosure above it was raised by Herod the Great between 31 and 4 BCE, the most complete Herodian building to survive. The Sasanian Persians sacked it in 614, and after the Arab conquest of 637 it was roofed and turned into a mosque. Crusaders made it a church after taking Hebron in 1100, and in 1119 a monk reopened the buried cave and claimed to find the patriarchs' bones, drawing pilgrims of all three Abrahamic faiths; Saladin retook the city in 1188 and restored it as a mosque, in which form it passed through Mamluk and Ottoman rule.
zh: 列祖之洞位于希伯伦老城，穆斯林称其为易卜拉欣清真寺或易卜拉欣圣所。据《创世记》记载，亚伯拉罕买下这里的岩洞作为家族墓地，相传洞中葬有亚伯拉罕与撒拉、以撒与利百加、雅各与利亚三对夫妇。洞上宏伟的长方形围墙由大希律王于公元前31年至前4年修建，是保存最完整的希律时期建筑。614年萨珊波斯人洗劫了此地，637年阿拉伯人征服后将其加盖屋顶、改为清真寺。1100年十字军攻占希伯伦后把它改成教堂，1119年一名修士重新打开被掩埋的岩洞，声称发现列祖遗骨，吸引三大亚伯拉罕宗教的朝圣者；1188年萨拉丁收复该城，恢复其清真寺身份，此后它先后经历马穆鲁克和奥斯曼的统治。

en: The Chamundeshwari Temple stands on the summit of the Chamundi Hills about thirteen kilometres from Mysore in Karnataka, dedicated to Chamundeshwari, a fierce form of Durga whom the kings and people of Mysore adopted as their tutelary goddess, the Nada Devi. Hindu tradition holds that Durga slew the buffalo demon Mahishasura on this very hill, and the demon's capital below came to be called Mahishuru, the name from which Mysore itself derives. The shrine is counted among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas under the name Krouncha Pitha, said to mark where a lock of Sati's hair fell. The original sanctum was built in the twelfth century under the Hoysala dynasty, its tall tower was probably raised by Vijayanagara rulers in the seventeenth century, and in 1659 a staircase of a thousand steps was cut up the hillside. Dodda Devaraja Wodeyar of Mysore installed the colossal granite Nandi on the path in 1664, and the Wodeyar maharajas remained the temple's chief patrons.
zh: 占闷提湿伐梨神庙位于卡纳塔克迈索尔城东南约13公里的占蒙迪山顶，供奉杜尔迦的忿怒相占蒙迪湿伐梨；迈索尔的君王与百姓奉她为守护女神“纳德提毗”。印度教传说杜尔迦正是在这座山上斩杀牛魔摩西沙修罗，山下魔王的都城因此得名摩西沙乌鲁，迈索尔之名即由此而来。该庙被列为十八处大性力圣地之一，古称俱伦阇圣地，相传萨蒂的一缕头发坠落于此。圣所原建于12世纪曷萨拉王朝时期，高塔大概是17世纪毗奢耶那伽罗统治者所加；1659年山腰凿出千级石阶。1664年迈索尔的多达·提婆罗阇·沃德亚尔在山道上安置了巨型花岗岩神牛南迪像，此后沃德亚尔诸土邦主一直是神庙的主要供养人。

en: The Changu Narayan Temple crowns a hilltop, also called Dolagiri, in Bhaktapur district east of Kathmandu in Nepal, and is dedicated to Vishnu in his Narayan form. Tradition places its foundation in the fourth century, making it one of the oldest Hindu temples still standing in Nepal; a legend derives its name from Champak, daughter of a Kashmiri king given in marriage to a prince of Bhaktapur, while the surrounding champak forest and village of Changu supplied the setting. Its most treasured monument is a Sanskrit pillar inscription set up by the Lichhavi king Manadeva, who ruled from 464 to 505, one of the earliest surviving inscriptions in the country and a key source for early Nepalese history. The temple was repeatedly restored after fires and earthquakes, and its courtyards gathered metalwork, woodcarvings and sculptures spanning many centuries of Nepalese art.
zh: 昌古纳拉扬神庙坐落在尼泊尔加德满都以东巴克塔普尔县一座又称多拉吉里的山顶，供奉毗湿奴的纳拉扬相。传说其始建于4世纪，是尼泊尔现存最古老的印度教神庙之一；另有传说称庙名来自一位克什米尔国王嫁给巴克塔普尔王子的女儿占芭格，庙周原本是占芭格树林与昌古村。庙中最珍贵的文物是梨查维王朝国王马纳提婆（464—505年在位）所立的梵文石柱铭文，这是尼泊尔现存最早的铭文之一，也是研究该国早期历史的关键史料。神庙历经多次火灾与地震后一再重修，院内汇集了尼泊尔艺术多个世纪的金属器、木雕与造像。

en: Chartres, southwest of Paris, is the cathedral of Our Lady built on a hill that has held a bishop's church since the fourth century, with at least five successive cathedrals on the same ground. The shrine's fame began in 876, when Charles the Bald presented the Sancta Camisa, held to be the tunic the Virgin Mary wore at the birth of Christ, and pilgrims began to converge on the town. Bishop Fulbert rebuilt after the fire of 1020 with gifts from rulers including Cnut the Great and made Chartres a leading cathedral school, where Thierry of Chartres, William of Conches and John of Salisbury helped pioneer the scholastic learning of the twelfth-century renaissance. Fire struck again on 10 June 1194, leaving only the crypt, towers and Royal Portal, and the present High Gothic cathedral rose in their place between 1194 and 1220, with its stained glass, flying buttresses and floor labyrinth; it was reconsecrated in October 1260 before King Louis IX. The Flamboyant north spire was added by Jean Texier between 1507 and 1513. During the French Revolution the church became state property and worship was suspended, but townspeople protected the sculpture and a local architect dissuaded the revolutionary committee from blowing the building up, so it survived until services resumed under Napoleon.
zh: 沙特尔位于巴黎西南，城中的圣母大教堂建在一座山丘上，自4世纪起这里就设有主教教堂，同一块土地上先后至少建过五座大教堂。圣地的声名始于876年，秃头查理献上“圣衣”，即相传圣母玛利亚在基督降生时所穿的束腰外衣，朝圣者从此络绎而来。1020年火灾后，富尔贝主教利用包括克努特大帝在内的君主捐赠重建教堂，并把沙特尔办成一流的主教学校，沙特尔的蒂耶里、孔什的威廉、索尔兹伯里的约翰等人在此开创了12世纪文艺复兴的经院学术。1194年6月10日大火再临，仅存地下室、双塔与皇家门廊；现存的盛期哥特式大教堂于1194—1220年在原址建起，配有彩色玻璃窗、飞扶壁和地面迷宫，1260年10月在路易九世面前重新祝圣。火焰哥特式的北尖塔由让·泰西耶于1507—1513年增建。法国大革命期间教堂收归国有、礼拜中止，但市民保护了雕塑，当地建筑师又劝阻革命委员会不要炸掉建筑，使它得以保存，直到拿破仑时期恢复礼拜。

en: The Chausath Yogini Temple at Hirapur, some twenty kilometres from Bhubaneswar in Orissa, is a circular, roofless tantric shrine devoted to the sixty-four yoginis, the goddess-like attendants of Durga. Local priests relate that Durga took the form of sixty-four demi-goddesses to overcome a demon and afterwards asked to be commemorated in a temple. It was built around 864 by Queen Hiradevi of the Bhauma dynasty, during the reign of Santikaradeva II, and is regarded as the oldest of India's few surviving Chausath Yogini temples. Its hypaethral plan, open to the sky so that tantric rites could honour the circle of the five elements, consists of a low sandstone ring only eight metres across, with niches for sixty-four yogini images surrounding a central figure of Kali standing on a human head; fifty-six of the dark stone statues survive. In the sixteenth century the temple is said to have been sacked and its images broken by Kalapahad, the Muslim convert general remembered as the destroyer of the Jagannath and Konark temples.
zh: 六十四瑜伽女神庙位于今印度奥里萨邦布巴内斯瓦尔以东约20公里的希拉普尔，是一座圆形无顶的怛特罗神庙，供奉侍奉杜尔加的六十四位瑜伽女。当地祭司相传，杜尔加曾化身为六十四位女神击败恶魔，战后女神们要求立庙纪念。此庙约于864年由博马王朝国王桑提迦罗提婆二世在位时的王后希拉德维主持修建，被视为印度现存为数不多的六十四瑜伽女庙中最古老的一座。神庙露天而建，以便怛特罗仪轨敬拜由五大元素构成的宇宙环；砂岩石砌的环形墙体直径仅约8米，壁龛中的六十四尊瑜伽女像环绕着中央踩在人头上的迦梨女神像，现存56尊深色石像。16世纪，改宗伊斯兰教的将领卡拉帕哈德据说曾劫掠此庙、打碎神像，他也以摧毁贾格纳特神庙和科纳克太阳神庙而闻名。

en: The Chhinnamasta Temple at Rajrappa, in the Hazaribagh country of the Indian state of Jharkhand, is a Tantric pilgrimage centre dedicated to Chhinnamasta, the self-decapitated goddess counted among the ten Mahavidyas. It sits on a hillock at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi rivers beside the Rajrappa falls, a setting read by Tantric worshippers as an image of the reversed union described in the goddess's meditation verse. The object of worship is a natural rock sheathed in an ashtadhatu, or eight-metal alloy, cover; local tribes venerated the spot long before it became established as a Chhinnamasta centre by the 1700s, and pilgrims still offer kheer and animal sacrifice. Built in a Tantric style often compared with the Kamakhya shrine in Assam, the main temple is surrounded by smaller shrines to the other Mahavidyas and to Surya, Hanuman and Shiva, and draws devotees from Bihar, Bengal and the Nepal hills as well as tribals who immerse ashes in the Damodar below.
zh: 献首女神庙位于印度贾坎德邦境内赫扎里巴克地区的拉杰拉帕，是一座怛特罗风格的朝圣中心，供奉十大明妃之一、自行断首的女神旗那摩斯塔。庙建在达莫达尔河与拜拉维河汇流处的小丘上，旁临拉杰拉帕瀑布，怛特罗信众把这一地势看作女神观想偈中“逆向交合”意象的体现。受拜的神体是一块外包八金属合金罩的天然岩石；早在18世纪这里成为旗那摩斯塔信仰中心之前，当地部落已在此礼拜，庙中仍保留供奉乳粥与杀牲献祭的习俗。主庙为怛特罗建筑风格，常被人与阿萨姆的迦摩伽耶圣庙相比；周围环绕着供奉其余明妃以及太阳神、哈奴曼、湿婆的小庙，香客来自比哈尔、孟加拉、尼泊尔山区，也有部民把亲人骨灰撒入脚下的达莫达尔河。

en: The Chintaman Ganesh Temple is the largest temple dedicated to Ganesha in Ujjain, the old Malwa city in Madhya Pradesh, standing on the Kshipra river about seven kilometres south-west of the town centre. The image enshrined there is held to be swayambhu, self-manifested rather than consecrated by human hands, and Ganesha is worshipped under the name Chintaman, the remover of worries, flanked by his two consorts, Riddhi and Siddhi. The stone building is dated to the 1000s and 1100s, when the Paramara dynasty ruled Malwa, while a local legend pushes its origins back to the age of the Ramayana and credits Sita with establishing the shrine. Its assembly hall is lined with finely carved stone pillars, and the white-washed sanctuary houses the self-born icon that draws pilgrims seeking relief from their anxieties.
zh: 除障者伽内什神庙是中央邦古城乌贾因规模最大的伽内什神庙，坐落在城西南约七公里的希普拉河畔。庙中神像相传为自行显现的自生像，而非人工安立；伽内什在此以“钦塔曼”——意为消除一切忧虑者——之名受奉，两侧配祀他的两位配偶哩迪与悉迪。这座石庙的历史可上溯至11至12世纪帕拉玛拉王朝统治摩腊婆之时，当地传说更把其渊源推到《罗摩衍那》时代，称神龛由悉多亲手建立。庙内集会厅排列着雕工精细的石柱，洁白的神龛中供奉着这尊自生像，吸引着祈求解忧的香客前来。

en: Cholollan, the place of refuge, was one of the holiest cities of central Mexico, and its great pyramid was called Tlachihualtepetl, the hand-made mountain, by the Nahuatl speakers of later ages. Six successive building campaigns from the third century BC to the ninth century AD wrapped one adobe-brick pyramid inside another, producing a monument 300 by 315 metres at the base and, at over four and a half million cubic metres, the largest pyramid on earth by volume, raised in the talud-tablero style of Teotihuacan and facing the snow-capped volcano Iztaccihuatl. The city around it may have held 100,000 people at its height, second only to Teotihuacan, but in the eighth century the population collapsed and the pyramid itself was abandoned, though the devout went on burying their dead around its flanks. When Toltec-Chichimeca invaders seized the city in the twelfth century they pushed the old Olmeca-Xicallanca people to one side and built a fresh temple to Quetzalcoatl elsewhere. By the time Hernan Cortes reached Cholula the monument had become a tree-covered hill, and in 1594 the Spanish crowned it with the church of Our Lady of Remedies, turning the ancient sanctuary into a place of Catholic pilgrimage while native rites continued on its slopes.
zh: 乔卢兰意为“避难之地”，是墨西哥中部最神圣的城市之一；后世说纳瓦特尔语的人把城中的大金字塔称作特拉奇瓦尔特佩特尔，即“人造之山”。从公元前3世纪到公元9世纪，六次相继的营建把一座土坯金字塔层层包裹在另一座之中，最终形成底边300米乘315米、体积逾450万立方米的巨构，成为世界体积最大的金字塔；它采用特奥蒂瓦坎的斜坡-壁板风格，朝向积雪覆盖的伊斯塔西瓦特尔火山。周围的城市极盛时或有10万人口，仅次于特奥蒂瓦坎，但8世纪人口骤减，金字塔本身被弃置，信徒仍继续在它的坡地周围安葬死者。12世纪托尔特克-奇奇梅卡入侵者夺取城市后，把原住民奥尔梅卡-希卡兰卡人挤到一旁，另择地点新建了一座魁札尔科亚特尔神庙。埃尔南·科尔特斯抵达乔卢拉时，这座建筑已成树木丛生的山丘；1594年，西班牙人在山顶建起雷梅迪奥斯圣母教堂，把古老圣所变为天主教朝圣地，而本土仪式仍在山坡上延续。

en: Cologne, on the Rhine, has held a bishop's church on its cathedral hill since late Roman times; the Carolingian Hildebold Cathedral, consecrated in 870, was one of the largest churches of the age and was called the Saint Peter's of the North, while the Gero Cross, carved around 960, is the oldest large crucifix north of the Alps. Pilgrimage began in 1164, when Archbishop Rainald of Dassel brought the relics of the Three Wise Men to Cologne among Frederick Barbarossa's Milanese spoils; the gilded Shrine of the Three Kings, made by Nicholas of Verdun between 1190 and 1225, then drew pilgrims from across Europe. To house it, Archbishop Konrad von Hochstaden laid the foundation stone of the present Gothic cathedral on 15 August 1248, built by Master Gerhard on the model of Amiens. The choir was consecrated in 1322, but work ceased in 1473 with the south tower raised only to belfry level, its crane a landmark for centuries, and nave work stopped around 1560. French revolutionary troops occupied Cologne in 1794: worship was suspended in 1796 and the cathedral served as a stable and warehouse, while the shrine was hidden in Westphalia and only returned in 1804. Reduced to a parish church in 1803, it regained cathedral rank in 1821 under Prussian patronage; Romantic writers and the dealer Sulpiz Boisserée, who rediscovered the 1370 façade plan and published engravings of the projected church between 1821 and 1831, made the half-built Dom a symbol of German nationhood.
zh: 科隆位于莱茵河畔，其主教座堂山丘自罗马时代晚期起就建有教堂；加洛林时代的希尔德博尔德主教座堂于870年祝圣，是当时规模最大的教堂之一，被称为“北方的圣伯多禄大殿”，堂内还收藏约960年雕刻的格罗十字架，是阿尔卑斯山以北最古老的大型十字架。朝圣热潮始于1164年，大主教达塞尔的赖纳尔德把东方三博士的圣骨带到科隆，它们是腓特烈·巴巴罗萨攻占米兰后的战利品；凡尔登的尼古拉于1190至1225年间打造了鎏金的三王圣龛，吸引了全欧洲的朝圣者。为安置圣龛，大主教康拉德·冯·霍希施塔登于1248年8月15日为现存的哥特式主教座堂奠基，由建筑师格哈德主持、以亚眠主教座堂为蓝本。唱诗班席于1322年祝圣，但工程在1473年停顿，南塔只建到钟楼高度，塔上的起重机成为数百年来的城市标志，中殿施工也在约1560年停止。1794年法国革命军队占领科隆：1796年礼拜中止，教堂被用作马厩和仓库，三王圣龛则被藏到威斯特伐利亚，1804年才迎回。1803年主教座堂被降为教区教堂，1821年在普鲁士扶持下恢复主教座堂地位；浪漫派作家与艺术品商人苏尔皮茨·布瓦塞雷重新发现1370年的立面原图，并于1821至1831年出版规划完工效果的版画，使这座半成的大教堂成为德意志民族的象征。

en: The see of Constantinople grew with the imperial capital refounded by Constantine in 330, and the council of 381 ranked its bishop second in honor only to Rome; from the consecration of Justinian's Hagia Sophia in 537 the Great Church was the heart of eastern Christian worship. The breach with Rome opened there in 1054, and between 1204 and 1261 Latin clergy held the cathedral under the Crusader occupation. After the Ottoman conquest of 1453 turned Hagia Sophia into a mosque, Mehmed II in 1454 invested the monk Gennadius as patriarch and ethnarch of all Orthodox Christians in the empire under the millet system, giving the displaced throne first the Church of the Holy Apostles and then from 1456 the Pammakaristos. The Miaphysite Armenians received their own patriarchate in the same city in 1461 under Hovakim I, whose millet also embraced the Syriac Orthodox until the later nineteenth century. The Greek throne moved again to the Vlach Saray in 1587 and in 1597 to the modest church of Saint George in the Phanar, rebuilt after fires in 1614, 1738 and 1797, which remains the patriarchal seat. In this period the Phanar saw its daughter church in Moscow recognized as a fifth patriarchate in 1589, while the Church of Greece broke away as autocephalous in 1833.
zh: 君士坦丁堡牧座随330年君士坦丁重建帝国首都而兴起，381年的公会议将其主教位列罗马之后、尊荣第二；537年查士丁尼的圣索菲亚大教堂祝圣后，这座“大圣堂”成为东方基督教崇拜的中心。1054年与罗马的决裂在此拉开，1204—1261年十字军占领期间大堂由拉丁神职人员主持。1453年奥斯曼征服后圣索菲亚被改为清真寺，穆罕默德二世于1454年立修士根纳迪乌斯为牧首，让他在米利特制度下担任帝国全体东正教徒的民族领袖；流离的牧座先驻圣使徒教堂，1456年起改驻帕玛卡里斯托斯教堂。基督合性派的亚美尼亚人也于1461年在同一座城市获得自己的宗主教区，由霍瓦基姆一世主持，其米利特还统辖叙利亚正教会，直到19世纪后期。希腊人的牧座1587年再迁至弗拉赫萨拉伊，1597年迁入法纳尔区简朴的圣乔治教堂——该堂历经1614年、1738年和1797年大火后重建，成为此后牧首的固定驻地。这一时期，法纳尔见证了莫斯科母会于1589年被承认为第五个牧首区，而希腊教会则在1833年自立为自主教会。

en: Constantinople, on the Bosporus between Europe and Asia, was refounded by Constantine the Great in 330 on the older Greek city of Byzantium and became the capital of the Byzantine Empire. Its greatest shrine was Hagia Sophia: a first Great Church was consecrated on the site in 360, and after it burned the present domed basilica was built under Justinian I between 532 and 537 as the seat of the patriarch of Constantinople. In 1054 the papal envoy delivered there the excommunication that opened the East-West Schism, and from 1204 to 1261 the cathedral was served by Catholic clergy under the Latin Empire. The capital also loomed over the heterodox movements of its Balkan hinterland: Paulician communities broken by imperial warfare were resettled in Thrace from the late ninth century, and in 970 John I Tzimiskes moved some two hundred thousand of them to the region of Philippopolis, where their dualist teaching helped feed the later Bogomil movement. When Ottoman troops stormed the city in 1453, Hagia Sophia was converted into a mosque.
zh: 君士坦丁堡地处欧亚之间的博斯普鲁斯海峡，330年由君士坦丁大帝在希腊古城拜占庭的基础上重建，成为拜占庭帝国的首都。城中最伟大的圣地是圣索菲亚大教堂：360年此地首座“大教堂”祝圣启用，后来毁于火灾，现存的穹顶巴西利卡由查士丁尼一世于532—537年修建，是君士坦丁堡牧首的座堂。1054年，教宗特使在此递交绝罚令，引发东西教会大分裂；1204—1261年拉丁帝国时期，这座大教堂由天主教神职人员主持。帝国首都也深刻影响着巴尔干腹地的异端运动：9世纪末起，被帝国战争击垮的保禄派信众被陆续迁往色雷斯，970年约翰一世·齐米斯凯斯又将约二十万人迁到菲利普波利斯一带，他们的二元论教义后来滋养了鲍格米勒派运动。1453年奥斯曼军队攻陷城市后，圣索菲亚大教堂被改为清真寺。

en: The Sanctuary of Daphne stood on a wooded plateau of springs and waterfalls about seven kilometres south of Antioch, at the site of present-day Harbiye in Turkey. Seleucus I Nicator, founder of the Seleucid dynasty, built there the Daphneion, a temple of Apollo housing a celebrated cult statue by the sculptor Bryaxis, and the shrine became one of the most famous sanctuaries of the Hellenistic east. Further temples were raised to Zeus Olympios, Artemis, Aphrodite and Isis, the springs were dedicated to nymphs, and Antiochus IV held a grand military review at Daphne in 166 BC; under Roman rule the suburb gained a stadium, quadrennial games and a theatre built by Titus from the spoils of Jerusalem. The Apollo temple also housed a renowned oracle. In 351 the Caesar Constantius Gallus placed a church holding the relics of Saint Babylas beside the decaying temple, and when the emperor Julian the Apostate restored the pagan shrine in 362 he blamed the saint's relics for silencing the oracle and had them removed; days later, on 22 October 362, fire destroyed the temple and its statue, and it was never rebuilt. The Persian army of Khosrow I sacked Daphne in 540, and after the Arab conquest of the seventh century the site was gradually abandoned.
zh: 达佛涅圣所位于安条克以南约七公里处一处林木繁茂、遍布泉水与瀑布的高地上，即今土耳其的哈尔比耶。塞琉古王朝的建立者塞琉古一世在此修建了供奉阿波罗的达佛涅翁神庙，庙内有雕刻家布拉克西斯制作的著名神像，这座圣所由此成为希腊化东方最负盛名的圣地之一。此后这里又建起供奉奥林匹斯宙斯、阿尔忒弥斯、阿芙洛狄忒和伊西斯的神庙，泉水被献给宁芙女神；公元前166年，安条克四世在达佛涅举行盛大阅兵。罗马统治时期，郊区增建了体育场、四年一度的赛会，以及提图斯用耶路撒冷战利品修建的剧场。阿波罗神庙还设有著名的神谕所。351年，副帝君士坦提乌斯·加卢斯在日渐倾颓的神庙旁修建了安放圣巴比拉遗骨的教堂；362年，重启异教圣所的尤利安皇帝认为圣徒遗骨使神谕缄默，下令迁走遗骨，然而数天后的362年10月22日，一场大火焚毁了神庙与神像，此后再未重建。540年，霍斯劳一世的波斯军队洗劫了达佛涅；7世纪阿拉伯征服后，这片圣地逐渐被废弃。

en: Delos is a small island at the centre of the Cyclades, held sacred as the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, whom Leto bore there beneath Mount Cynthus. It was first a pilgrimage centre of the Ionians, and Athens repeatedly purified it: Pisistratus cleared graves near the temple in the sixth century BC, and in 426 BC the Athenians removed all the dead and forbade births and burials on the island, which then hosted the Delian games. After the Persian Wars it became the meeting place and treasury of the Delian League, founded in 478 BC, until Pericles moved the treasury to Athens in 454 BC. Rome made Delos a free port in 166 BC, and it grew into the busiest slave market in the eastern Mediterranean, but assaults by the forces of Mithridates in 88 and 69 BC broke its prosperity. Trade shifted elsewhere, and by the second century AD Pausanias found only temple custodians on the island; it was abandoned altogether around the eighth century and was never resettled.
zh: 提洛岛是基克拉泽斯群岛中心的小岛，被尊为阿波罗与阿耳忒弥斯的诞生地——勒托在岛上的基斯诺斯山下生下这对孪生神。它最初是爱奥尼亚人的朝圣中心，雅典人多次对它举行净化：公元前6世纪庇西特拉图下令迁走神庙附近的坟墓，公元前426年雅典人又迁走全部遗骸，并禁止在岛上出生和下葬，提洛运动会随后在此举办。希波战争后，它成为公元前478年成立的提洛同盟的会址与金库所在地，直到公元前454年伯里克利把金库迁往雅典。罗马于公元前166年将提洛辟为自由港，它发展成东地中海最繁忙的奴隶市场，但公元前88年和公元前69年米特拉达梯军队的两次进攻摧毁了它的繁荣。商路改道后，2世纪保萨尼阿斯见到的岛上只剩神庙看守人；约8世纪它被彻底放弃，再无人定居。

en: Delphi was the sacred precinct of Apollo on the south-western slope of Mount Parnassus in Phocis, central Greece, and the seat of the Pythia, the most authoritative oracle of the Hellenic world. The Greeks held it to be the centre of the earth, marked by the omphalos, the navel stone in Apollo's temple; myth told how the god slew the serpent Python guarding an older oracle of Earth and made the spring and its vapours his own. On a tripod above the chasm the priestess delivered prophecies that shaped colonial ventures, laws and wars, while city-states lined the Sacred Way with treasuries, the Athenian one commemorating Marathon in 490 BC, and the Pythian Games, held every four years from 586 BC with their musical contests and laurel crowns, ranked among the four great Panhellenic festivals. The visible Doric temple was raised in the fourth century BC after earlier temples, one rebuilt by the Alcmaeonids after a fire in 548 BC, had perished. Roman rule brought plunder by Sulla in 86 BC and Nero in AD 66, partial restoration under the Flavians, and finally closure under Theodosius I in 381 during the empire's anti-pagan laws. The sanctuary then stood in ruins: the Ottomans took Phocis around 1410, the antiquary Cyriacus of Ancona recorded its remains in 1436, an earthquake in 1500 did further damage, and Byron visited the deserted site in 1809.
zh: 德尔斐是阿波罗的圣域，位于希腊中部福基斯的帕尔纳索斯山西南坡，也是皮提亚女祭司的驻地，即希腊世界最具权威的神谕所。希腊人认为这里是大地的中心，阿波罗神庙中的翁法罗斯石，即肚脐石，标示着这个中心；神话讲述阿波罗杀死守护古老大地神谕的巨蛇皮同，把泉水与雾气据为己有。女祭司坐在裂隙上方的三足凳上传达预言，殖民建邦、立法征战多取决于此；各城邦沿圣道修建宝库，雅典人的宝库即为纪念公元前490年的马拉松之战而建。始于公元前586年、每四年一届的皮提亚竞技会设有音乐比赛，胜者获桂冠，位列四大泛希腊赛会之一。现存的多立克式神庙建于公元前4世纪，此前的神庙历经劫难，其中一座曾在公元前548年火灾后由阿尔克迈翁家族重建。罗马统治时期，苏拉于公元前86年、尼禄于公元66年先后洗劫此地，弗拉维王朝曾部分修复，最终在381年狄奥多西一世镇压异教的法令中被关闭。此后圣域沦为废墟：奥斯曼人约在1410年占领福基斯，古物学家安科纳的奇里亚科于1436年记录了残存遗迹，1500年的地震又加破坏，拜伦则在1809年造访了这片荒芜之地。

en: Deo Patan, the present-day Prabhas Patan on the coast of Saurashtra, is the site of the Somnath temple, the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva. The place is a Triveni Sangam, where the Kapila, Hiran and mythical Sarasvati rivers meet the sea, and tradition says the moon god Soma bathed here to recover his lost radiance, giving the shrine its name Someshvara, lord of the moon. The Chaulukya king Mularaja built the first stone temple before 997, but in January 1026 Mahmud of Ghazni crossed the Thar desert, sacked the shrine and carried its treasures back to Ghazna. The Chaulukya king Kumarapala rebuilt it in stone around 1169, only for Ulugh Khan's army on Alauddin Khalji's 1299 Gujarat campaign to sack it again; the Chudasama king Mahipala rebuilt the temple in 1308 and his son Khengara reinstalled the lingam between 1331 and 1351, so worship had only just resumed at the 1337 opening. Zafar Khan, the Delhi governor who founded the Gujarat Sultanate, destroyed it once more in 1395, Mahmud Begada desecrated it in 1451, and Aurangzeb ordered its demolition and conversion into a mosque in 1706. In the later eighteenth century Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore built a smaller shrine beside the ruins so that the worship of the Jyotirlinga could continue.
zh: 德奥帕坦今称普拉巴什帕坦，位于萨乌拉施特拉海岸，索姆纳特神庙便坐落于此——它是湿婆十二处究提林迦中的第一处。此地是卡皮拉河、希兰河与神话中的萨拉斯瓦蒂河入海的三河汇流处；相传月神苏摩曾在此沐浴，恢复失去的光辉，神庙因此得名“苏摩湿婆罗”，即月之主。遮娄其国王穆拉罗阇在997年之前建起第一座石庙，但1026年1月，伽色尼的马哈茂德越过塔尔沙漠劫掠此庙，将财宝运回伽色尼。遮娄其国王鸠摩罗波罗约于1169年以石材重建，不料1299年阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉征伐古吉拉特时，乌鲁格汗的军队再次将其洗劫；朱达萨摩国王摩希波罗于1308年重修神庙，其子肯伽罗在1331至1351年间重新安立林伽，因此1337年开局时祭祀才刚刚恢复。德里派驻古吉拉特的总督、后来开创古吉拉特苏丹国的扎法尔汗于1395年再度毁庙，马哈茂德·贝加达1451年又加以亵渎，奥朗则布则在1706年下令拆庙改建清真寺。18世纪后期，印多尔的阿希莉娅芭伊·霍尔卡在废墟旁另建一座小庙，使究提林迦的香火得以延续。

en: The Deo Surya Mandir, also called Devark, is a sun temple dedicated to Surya in the town of Deo in Aurangabad district, Bihar, and the principal shrine of the Chhath sun-festival of the eastern Gangetic plain. Unusually for a sun temple, it faces west, towards the setting sun rather than the rising one. Historians place its first building between the 500s and the 700s, and tradition numbers it among the twelve sun temples raised by Samba, son of Krishna; a Gupta-era inscription of 642 from the area attests to local sun worship. Its recorded history begins with an inscription of 1437 in which King Bhairavendra dedicated the present temple and listed twelve of his ancestors; the text records that local Hindu chieftains restored the shrine after Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji's invasion of Bengal in the early 1200s, and some scholars argue it had first been a Buddhist temple. Built of carved stone in a blend of Nagara, Dravidian and Vesara forms, it is crowned by a dome bearing a golden urn, and draws its greatest crowds at the Chhath Puja and on Sundays.
zh: 代奥的苏利耶神庙又名代瓦尔克，是比哈尔邦奥兰加巴德县代奥镇的一座太阳神苏利耶神庙，也是恒河平原东部恰特普迦太阳神祭的首要圣地。与一般太阳神庙不同，它朝西面向落日，而非朝东迎接旭日。史家推断其最初建于6至8世纪，传统则把它列为奎师那之子商波所建十二座太阳神庙之一；当地一方642年的笈多时期铭文也证实了太阳神崇拜在此地的流行。它有文字可考的历史始于1437年的铭文：国王拜拉文德罗在铭文中为现存神庙举行奉献，并列出十二位列祖列宗；铭文还记载，在巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉于13世纪初入侵孟加拉之后，是当地的印度教酋长们修复了这座神龛，部分学者因此认为它最初可能是一座佛寺。神庙以石雕建成，融合纳加拉、达罗毗荼与毗萨拉三种样式，顶部穹隆上安放金罐；每逢恰特普迦节和周日，前来的香客最多。

en: The Dewa Sanzan are the three sacred mountains of Dewa Province in the far north of Honshu, Mount Haguro, Mount Gassan and Mount Yudono, each crowned by its own shrine, while the chief shrine on Haguro venerates the deities of all three. Tradition dates their opening as a religious centre to 593, when Prince Hachiko, son of the murdered Emperor Sushun, fled the Soga clan to Dewa and spent his life in ascetic devotion to the mountain god Haguro Gongen. The mountains became a foremost training ground of Shugendō mountain asceticism, whose founder En no Gyōja and the Shingon master Kūkai both made the pilgrimage, and summer processions of yamabushi and ordinary pilgrims trekked north to their shrines. Mount Haguro, the only one approachable all year, guards a five-storey wooden pagoda in its cedar groves, and the haiku poet Matsuo Bashō later joined the pilgrims climbing its stone path.
zh: 出羽三山是本州极北出羽国的三座圣山——羽黑山、月山和汤殿山，各有神社镇守，羽黑山顶的总社同时供奉三山之神。相传593年崇峻天皇遇弑后，皇子蜂子为躲避苏我氏逃到出羽，终生苦修，奉祀山神羽黑权现，三山由此开辟为宗教之地。这里后来成为修验道最重要的修行场，修验道始祖役行者和真言宗之祖空海都曾前来参拜，每年夏天山伏与普通信众跋涉北上，登山朝拜。羽黑山是三山之中唯一全年可登的一座，杉林中矗立着木造五重塔；俳谐师松尾芭蕉后来也沿石阶上山，加入朝圣者的行列。

en: Didyma was the oracle sanctuary of Apollo in the territory of Miletus on the Ionian coast, where a priestess gave utterance over a sacred spring and the priestly family of the Branchidae interpreted her words. The archaic temple was burned by the Persians after the naval battle of Lade in 494 BC, and its bronze Apollo, carved by Canachus of Sicyon, was carried off to Ecbatana; the spring fell silent and the site lay in ruins until Alexander the Great freed Miletus in 334 BC. The Milesians then raised one of the largest Ionic temples ever built, the work of the architects Paeonius and Daphnis, whose open inner court held the spring, a sacred laurel and a small shrine; Seleucus I brought the cult statue back from Persia around 300 BC. Galatian raiders sacked the sanctuary in 277 BC, and pirates again in 67 BC, yet Roman emperors from Trajan to Hadrian, who came as prophet in 129 AD, still patronised it. The oracle ended when Theodosius I closed the pagan temples; a Byzantine bishopric and village lingered on the site until an earthquake in 1493 toppled the temple and drove the inhabitants away.
zh: 迪迪玛是爱奥尼亚海岸米利都境内的阿波罗神谕圣地，女祭司在圣泉之上宣示神谕，再由布兰基代祭司家族解读。公元前494年拉德海战之后，波斯人焚毁了古风时期的神庙，把西库翁雕刻家卡纳科斯所作的青铜阿波罗像劫往埃克巴坦那；圣泉从此断流，遗址沦为废墟，直到公元前334年亚历山大大帝解放米利都。米利都人随后建起一座规模居希腊世界前列的爱奥尼式大庙，由建筑师帕奥尼乌斯与达夫尼斯设计，露天内院中设有圣泉、圣月桂和一座小神龛；约公元前300年，塞琉古一世把神像从波斯迎回。公元前277年加拉太人洗劫圣地，公元前67年海盗又来一次，但从图拉真到129年亲任先知的哈德良，罗马皇帝仍不断眷顾此地。狄奥多西一世关闭异教神庙后，神谕就此终结；一处拜占庭主教区和村落在此延续，直到1493年的地震震塌神庙，居民四散离去。

en: The Dilwara Temples stand in the forested hills above Mount Abu in southern Rajasthan and, with Palitana, Girnar and Shikharji, rank among the five great Svetambara pilgrimage places of the Jains. Five white-marble shrines enclosed in a single walled compound were raised between the 1000s and 1500s in the ornate Solanki, or Maru-Gurjara, style, their plain exteriors giving way to ceilings, pillars and doorways of almost lace-like marble carving. The earliest and largest, the Vimal Vasahi dedicated to Rishabhanatha, was built around 1026 by Vimal Shah, minister of the Chaulukya king Bhima I of Gujarat, and the Luna Vasahi, honouring Neminatha and famed as the peak of the complex's sculpture, was completed by 1230 under the minister brothers Vastupala and Tejpal. Alauddin Khalji's army sacked and damaged the temples in 1311 and they were repaired from 1321 onward. The brass-image Pittalhar temple was then built for the Gujarat sultan Mahmud Begada's minister, the three-storey Parshvanatha temple followed in 1458 and 1459, and the small Mahavira temple was added in 1582; Rana Kumbha of Mewar presented the black-stone Kirti Stambha pillar, and Sirohi painters decorated the newest shrine in 1764. Pilgrims still measure the merit of a Rajasthan Jain tirth against the marble halls of Dilwara.
zh: 地利缚罗寺坐落在拉贾斯坦南部阿布山上方的林丘间，与波利多拿寺、耆栗那罗山、尸佉罗时等同列耆那教白衣派五大圣地。围墙之内共有五座白色大理石神殿，建于11至16世纪，采用华丽的索兰基（马鲁-古吉拉特）风格：外墙朴素，天花、立柱与门楣却布满近乎镂空织锦般的精美石雕。最早也最大的是供奉勒舍婆那陀的毗摩罗瓦西寺，约1026年由古吉拉特遮娄其国王毗摩一世的大臣毗摩罗沙兴建；供奉涅弥那陀、雕刻水准居全寺之冠的卢那瓦西寺，则在大臣兄弟瓦斯图波罗与泰阇波罗主持下于1230年前完工。1311年阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉的军队洗劫并破坏了神庙，1321年起陆续修复。此后，为古吉拉特苏丹马哈茂德·贝加达的大臣修建的铜像寺皮陀罗诃、三层楼高的巴湿伐那陀寺（1458—1459年）和小巧的大雄寺（1582年）相继落成；梅瓦尔的贡巴王奉献了黑石荣誉柱，锡罗希的画师又于1764年为最新的殿宇绘制壁画。拉贾斯坦的耆那香客衡量各处圣地的高下，总以地利缚罗的大理石殿堂为标尺。

en: Dodona, in the mountains of Epirus, was the oldest oracle in Greece, where priests read the will of Zeus in the rustling leaves of a sacred oak. Homer already knew it, and in the Iliad Achilles prays to Zeus of Dodona from before Troy; the mother goddess Dione was honoured there beside him, and the sanctuary passed from the Thesprotians to the Molossians. Long second only to Delphi in prestige, it was made the religious capital of his kingdom by Pyrrhus around 290 BC, who rebuilt the Temple of Zeus and added a theatre and games. The Aetolians burned it in 219 BC and Philip V of Macedon restored it, but the Romans under Aemilius Paulus devastated Epirus in 167 BC, and raiders in the pay of Mithridates sacked it again around 88 BC. Pilgrims still came in Roman times: Pausanias saw the sacred oak in the second century, and the emperor Julian consulted the oracle in 362. In 391 or 392 Theodosius I closed the pagan temples and had the ancient oak cut down, though a Christian bishopric of Dodona survived into the fifth century.
zh: 多多纳位于伊庇鲁斯的群山之中，是希腊最古老的神谕所，祭司通过倾听圣橡树叶的沙沙声来解读宙斯的旨意。荷马早已提到它，《伊利亚特》中阿喀琉斯在特洛伊城下向多多纳的宙斯祈祷；母神狄俄涅在宙斯身旁同受供奉，圣地先后由塞斯普罗蒂亚人和摩罗西亚人掌控。它的威望长期仅次于德尔斐。约公元前290年，皮洛士把它定为王国的宗教首都，重建宙斯神庙，并增设剧场和赛会。公元前219年埃托利亚人将其焚毁，马其顿的腓力五世又加以修复；但公元前167年罗马人在埃米利乌斯·保卢斯率领下蹂躏伊庇鲁斯，约公元前88年受米特拉达梯雇用的袭击者再度洗劫此地。罗马时代仍有朝圣者前来：2世纪保萨尼阿斯见过那棵圣橡树，362年皇帝尤利安出征波斯前也曾求问神谕。391至392年间，狄奥多西一世关闭异教神庙并砍倒古橡树，不过多多纳的基督教主教区一直延续到5世纪。

en: The Dwarkadhish Temple stands at Dwarka, on the Saurashtra coast of Gujarat, where the Gomti river meets the sea, and houses Krishna under the name Dwarkadhish, the Lord of Dwarka. Hindu tradition holds that Krishna built the city on land reclaimed from the ocean and made it his capital after leaving Mathura. The five-storey shrine, also called the Jagat Mandir and raised on 72 pillars, is counted among the Char Dham, the four cardinal pilgrimage sites of Hinduism, and the Sapta Puri, its seven holy cities, and ranks as the 98th of the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desams; Adi Shankara visited it in the eighth century and founded the nearby Dvaraka Pitha, one of his four monasteries. Archaeological evidence traces a temple on the spot to around 200 BCE. In 1473 the Gujarat sultan Mahmud Begada sacked Dwarka and destroyed the shrine and its idol, but the present building was raised in the sixteenth century and the current image was installed by the Shankaracharya Aniruddhashrama in 1559. The poet-saint Mirabai is said to have vanished into the image here, and the reformer Vallabha made the Krishna Janmashtami festival a regular observance at the temple.
zh: 德瓦尔格之主奎师那神庙位于古吉拉特萨乌拉施特拉海岸的德瓦卡，地处戈默蒂河入海处，庙中供奉以德瓦尔格之主之名受拜的奎师那，即德瓦卡之主。印度教传统认为，奎师那离开马图拉后在填海得来的土地上建成此城，立为都城。这座五层神庙又称世界之庙，以72根石柱撑起，位列印度教四大朝圣圣地与七圣城之一，在毗湿奴派108座圣庙中排第98；8世纪时阿迪·商羯罗曾来此朝拜，并在附近建立四大僧院之一的德瓦卡寺。考古证据显示，早在公元前200年前后此地已有神庙。1473年，古吉拉特苏丹马哈茂德·贝加达洗劫德瓦卡，捣毁神庙与神像；主体建筑建于16世纪，现存神像由商羯罗查尔雅阿尼鲁达什罗摩于1559年安立。相传诗人圣女米拉巴伊在此融入神像，宗教改革家伐拉巴则把奎师那诞辰节确立为庙中的常例庆典。

en: Ek' Balam was a Yucatec Maya city in the dry northern lowlands, fifty-six kilometres northeast of Chichen Itza, whose kings ruled a kingdom there from around the start of the Common Era until its slow abandonment in the Postclassic. Its golden age ran from 770 to 840 under Ukit Kan Lek Tok', who reigned from 770 to about 800 and was buried in the great Acropolis; his tomb temple, El Trono, opens through a monster's jaguar-maw doorway and preserves some of the finest plaster sculpture in the Maya world, while a hall nearby holds the Mural of the Ninety-six Glyphs, a calligraphic masterpiece matched only at Palenque. The ballcourt was finished in 841, and sacbe roads ran from the centre toward the four cardinal points. Two concentric walls, the largest fortifications of Late Classic Yucatan and anchored at both ends on impassable cenotes, ringed the city; a rough inner wall thrown across the Great Plaza suggests a desperate last defence before the population collapsed to a tenth of its peak and the site was emptied. A Spanish Relacion Geografica of the late sixteenth century still recorded local memory of the kingdom of Talol, said to have been founded by a chief named Ek' Balam who came from the east, before the Cupul family came to dominate the district.
zh: 埃克巴拉姆是尤卡坦北部干旱低地上的尤卡坦玛雅城市，位于奇琴伊察东北56公里，其国王约自公元初年起在此统治一个王国，直到后古典期城市逐渐被弃。它的黄金时代在770年至840年间，国王乌基特·坎·莱克·托克于770年至约800年在位，死后葬入大卫城；他的陵庙“王座”以怪兽般的美洲虎巨口为门，保存着玛雅世界最精美的灰泥雕塑，附近厅堂里还有九十六字铭文壁画，其书法成就只有帕伦克的九十六字板可与之媲美。球场于841年落成，白色石砌大道从城中心通向四方。两道同心城墙环绕全城，是古典期晚期尤卡坦规模最大的防御工事，两端均以无法逾越的天然井为屏障；大广场上还仓促补筑过一道粗糙内墙，说明城破前曾有过拼死防守。此后人口锐减至鼎盛时的十分之一，城址沦为空城。16世纪末西班牙人的《地理报告》仍记录着当地对塔洛尔王国的记忆，传说它由一位来自东方、名叫埃克·巴拉姆的首领建立，后来库普尔家族成为这一地区的主宰。

en: Enryaku-ji is the great Tendai monastery on Mount Hiei, the mountain overlooking Kyoto from the border of Ōmi Province. The monk Saichō, later called Dengyō Daishi, built its first hall in 788 and, with the backing of Emperor Kanmu, brought the Chinese Tiantai teachings to Japan; in 807 he ordained a hundred disciples, who underwent twelve years of secluded study on the mountain. At its height the complex held some three thousand sub-temples, and its warrior monks made and unmade affairs in the capital. In the tenth century a succession feud split Tendai into the Mountain Order based at Enryaku-ji and the Temple Order based at Mii-dera, and armed monks repeatedly marched on Kyoto to enforce their demands. The monastery also trained the men who later founded the Pure Land, Shinshū, Sōtō Zen and Nichiren schools. In 1571 Oda Nobunaga stormed Mount Hiei, burned the buildings and put the monks to the sword; only the thirteenth-century Ruri-dō survived. Reconstruction followed under the new regime, and Tokugawa Iemitsu rebuilt the main hall in 1642.
zh: 延历寺坐落于近江国边境、俯瞰京都的比睿山上，是天台宗的总本山。僧人最澄（谥号传教大师）于788年在此建草庵，后在桓武天皇支持下将中国天台教义传入日本；807年他为百名弟子授戒，令其在山中闭关修行十二年。极盛时，山内有约三千座子院，武僧集团甚至能左右京城局势。10世纪，天台宗因法统之争分裂为以延历寺为本山的山门派和以三井寺为本山的寺门派，武装僧众多次入京强诉。后来开创净土宗、净土真宗、曹洞宗和日莲宗的祖师，都曾在这座寺院修行。1571年，织田信长攻入比睿山，焚毁堂舍、屠戮僧众，只有13世纪的琉璃堂幸免。此后寺院在新政权下逐步重建，德川家光于1642年再建了正殿。

en: Epidauros was a small polis on the Argolid peninsula facing the Saronic Gulf, ruling a territory called the Epidauria and staying independent of Argos until Roman times. It claimed to be the birthplace of Asclepius, the healer son of Apollo, and from the sixth century BC the older hilltop sanctuary of Apollo Maleatas on Mount Kynortion was joined by a new healing sanctuary of Asclepius, which became the most celebrated medical centre of the Greek world, ranking beside Olympia and Delphi. The sick slept in a great dream-dormitory, trusting that the god would prescribe their cure in a dream, while mineral springs, a gymnasium and a guest house of 160 rooms served the pilgrims; the early fourth-century temple and the nearby theatre, built by Polykleitos the Younger and famed for its acoustics, still stand. In 146 BC the Achaeans fortified the sanctuary before Mummius broke their league, and Sulla plundered it in 87 BC and pirates again before 67 BC, beginning a long decline. Hadrian's visit in 124 AD revived its fortunes: he reformed the priesthood and the games, and Antonine patrons added baths and a temple of Hygieia. Goths raided it in 395, yet as late as the middle of the fifth century the old healing centre still drew patients, now under Christian management.
zh: 厄庇道洛斯是阿尔戈利斯半岛上濒临萨罗尼科斯湾的小城邦，辖有称为厄庇道里亚的领地，在罗马时代之前一直独立于阿尔戈斯。此地相传是阿波罗之子、医神阿斯克勒庇俄斯的出生地：公元前6世纪起，基诺尔提翁山上供奉阿波罗·马莱塔斯的古老山顶圣地旁，兴起了新的阿斯克勒庇俄斯疗愈圣所，后来成为希腊世界最负盛名的医疗中心，地位与奥林匹亚、德尔斐并列。病人在大寝殿中睡卧祈梦，相信医神会在梦中指点疗方；圣泉、体育场和有160间客房的客舍接待朝圣者，公元前4世纪初的神庙与附近小波留克列特斯设计、以音响效果著称的剧场均保存完好。公元前146年，亚该亚人曾把圣所改造成堡垒，随后穆米乌斯攻灭亚该亚同盟；公元前87年苏拉洗劫此地，公元前67年之前海盗又来一次，圣所由此长期衰落。124年哈德良亲临后再度振兴，他改革祭司制度与赛会，安敦尼王朝的赞助人又增建浴场和许癸厄亚神庙。395年哥特人来袭，但直到5世纪中叶，这座古老的疗愈中心仍在基督教管理下接待病人。

en: The metropolitan see of Fars stood at Rev Ardashir, the port refounded by the Sasanian king Ardashir I in the third century and remembered by Muslim geographers as a seat of Greek and Indian learning. Tradition held that Persian merchants converted in Edessa first brought Christianity to the region. Its bishops attended the Persian synods of the early fifth century, and by 424 Fars ranked as the sixth metropolitan province of the Church of the East; around 540 its metropolitan gained authority over the Arabian dioceses of Bahrain and Oman and the island of Socotra. The see was a center of Persian Christian letters: Maʿna of Pars, installed in 540, translated the Psalms and Syriac liturgy into Pahlavi for churches as far away as India, while the jurist Simeon of Rev Ardashir later composed church law in the same province. Islamization after the Arab conquests eroded these communities faster than anywhere else in the former Sasanian realm, and the last known metropolitan, ʿAbdishoʿ, is recorded in 1138. By the Mongol era few Christians remained on the mainland, though a community at Hormuz is mentioned into the sixteenth century and the isolated Socotrans still sent a bishop to the enthronement of Yahballaha III in 1281.
zh: 法尔斯教省的都主教驻地在雷夫阿尔达希尔，即3世纪萨珊国王阿尔达希尔一世重建的港口城市，穆斯林地理学家称它为研习希腊与印度学问的学术中心。相传是在埃德萨归信的波斯商人最早把基督教带到这一地区。当地主教参加了5世纪初的波斯教会会议，到424年法尔斯已位列东方教会第六个都主教教省；约540年，其都主教又管辖巴林、阿曼等阿拉伯教区和索科特拉岛。这座牧座也是波斯基督徒的文学中心：540年就任的法尔斯的马纳把《诗篇》和叙利亚语礼仪译成巴列维语，供远至印度的教会使用，后来的法学家雷夫阿尔达希尔的西缅也在此省撰写教会法。阿拉伯征服后的伊斯兰化使这些社群的萎缩速度超过原萨珊境内任何地区，有史可考的末任都主教阿卜迪绍见于1138年的记载。蒙古时代大陆上的基督徒已所剩无几，但霍尔木兹的社群直到16世纪仍有记载，孤悬海上的索科特拉人还在1281年派主教参加了雅巴拉哈三世的登位典礼。

en: The Fatima Masumeh Shrine in Qom, in central Persia, is the mausoleum of Fatima bint Musa, honoured as Fatima al-Ma'suma, daughter of the seventh Shia Imam Musa al-Kazim and sister of the eighth Imam Ali al-Rida. In 816 she set out from Medina to join her brother in Khorasan, but her caravan was attacked by Abbasid agents at Saveh; poisoned and falling ill, she was carried to the Shia town of Qom, where she died and was buried on her host's land. Her tomb, first sheltered by a bamboo canopy, received a domed building about fifty years later at the request of Sayyida Zaynab, daughter of the ninth Imam Muhammad al-Jawad. As one of the most venerable shrines of Shiism, it drew pilgrims and seminaries, and Qom grew into a leading centre of Shia learning. In 1519 Tajlu Khanum, wife of Shah Ismail I, added an iwan and two minarets and rebuilt the tomb chamber as a domed octagon. Under the Qajars, Fath-Ali Shah merged the old courtyards in 1795 and restored the gilded dome in 1803.
zh: 纯洁者法蒂玛圣陵位于波斯中部的库姆，安葬着什叶派第七任伊玛目穆萨·卡齐姆之女、第八任伊玛目阿里·里达之妹法蒂玛·马苏梅。816年，她从麦地那动身前往呼罗珊投奔兄长，商队却在萨韦遭到阿拔斯王朝人马袭击；她中毒染病，被送往什叶派城镇库姆，不久便在那里去世，葬于接待者的土地上。她的坟墓起初只有竹棚遮盖，约五十年后，第九任伊玛目穆罕默德·塔基·贾瓦德之女赛义达·宰纳卜主持修建了穹顶建筑。作为什叶派最受尊崇的圣陵之一，它吸引了大批朝圣者和经学院，库姆也由此成为什叶派学术的重镇。1519年，沙阿伊斯玛仪一世之妻塔吉鲁·汗努姆增建了伊万拱门和两座宣礼塔，并把墓室重建为穹顶八边形。卡扎尔王朝时期，法特赫-阿里沙于1795年合并了旧有庭院，又在1803年重修鎏金穹顶。

en: The sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia at Praeneste, the modern Palestrina east of Rome, was the grandest oracular shrine of Latium, climbing the hillside in six vast terraces of concrete and porticoes to a round temple holding a gilded bronze statue of the goddess as a young warrior. Fortuna Primigenia, the first-born goddess, was shown suckling the infants Jupiter and Juno and was especially honoured by matrons, who brought their first-born children to her for protection. Pilgrims consulted her oracle by drawing the sortes, wooden lots which Cicero says the Praenestine noble Numerius Suffucius recovered from a well. The terraced complex took its monumental form around 120 BC, and Sulla, who made Praeneste a colony about 80 BC after defeating Marius, enlarged it in thanks to the goddess. The oracle survived into Christian times until Constantine and Theodosius I forbade lot-divination and closed the temple. In the Middle Ages the hill belonged to the Colonna: Pope Boniface VIII razed the town in 1298 and Eugenius IV had it destroyed again in 1437, though Stefano Colonna refortified it in 1448. After the Barberini bought Palestrina in 1630, their palace was raised over the ancient temple-theatre, preserving the round shrine within its walls.
zh: 头生子之神福尔图娜的圣所位于罗马以东的普莱内斯特，即今帕莱斯特里纳，是拉丁姆最宏伟的神谕圣地。整座建筑沿山坡层层升起，由六座宽阔的混凝土台地和柱廊组成，最高处是一座圆形神庙，里面供奉着女战神形象的镀金青铜女神像。福尔图娜意为“头生子女神”，被描绘成哺乳婴儿朱庇特和朱诺的模样，尤其受到已婚妇人的敬奉，她们会把头生孩子带到庙中祈求护佑。朝圣者通过抽取木签求问神谕，西塞罗记载，这些木签是普莱内斯特贵族努梅里乌斯·苏富基乌斯从一口井中发现的。台地建筑群约在公元前120年形成宏伟形制；苏拉击败马略后于约公元前80年在此设立殖民地，并为答谢女神而扩建圣所。神谕一直延续到基督教时代，最终君士坦丁和狄奥多西一世禁止抽签占卜并关闭了神庙。中世纪时，此山归科隆纳家族所有：1298年教宗波尼法爵八世将城镇夷为平地，1437年教宗恩仁四世再度将其摧毁，1448年斯特凡诺·科隆纳又重新筑防。1630年巴尔贝里尼家族买下帕莱斯特里纳后，在古神庙剧场上方建起家族宫殿，把圆形神庙保存在宫墙之内。

en: Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of Inari, the kami of rice and agriculture, standing in Yamashiro Province south of Kyoto at the foot of Mount Inari. It was founded in 711 by the Hata clan, a powerful immigrant kin group skilled in irrigation and sericulture, and grew from their clan tutelary shrine into the centre of the nationwide Inari cult. In 816 the shrine was moved to its present site at the request of the monk Kūkai, and in 965 Emperor Murakami numbered it among the shrines receiving imperial offerings. The present main hall dates from 1499, and the two-storey tower gate was donated by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. From the Edo period onward merchants and guilds dedicated thousands of vermilion torii gates to win the favour of Inari, honoured increasingly as the patron of trade; the dense rows called the Senbon Torii climb the mountain behind the shrine, while branch Inari shrines multiplied across Japan.
zh: 伏见稻荷大社是稻荷神的总本社，位于山城国京都以南、稻荷山麓。稻荷神最初司掌稻米与农业，神社于711年由精通灌溉与养蚕的渡来豪族秦氏创建，从秦氏的氏社发展为全国稻荷信仰的中心。816年应僧人空海之请迁至现地；965年村上天皇将它列入接受朝廷币帛的神社。现存本殿建于1499年，两层楼门由丰臣秀吉捐建。江户时代以来，商人与行会为祈求生意兴隆，纷纷献上朱红色鸟居，数以千计的鸟居在社后山腰排成“千本鸟居”；稻荷神也越来越被视为商业守护神，稻荷神社随之遍布日本各地。

en: Gelati Monastery crowns a hill above the Tskaltsitela Gorge near Kutaisi, seat of the medieval Georgian kings in Imereti. King David IV the Builder founded it in 1106 as both a monastery and an academy, and its main Church of the Blessed Virgin was completed in 1130 under his successor Demetrius I, who placed the ancient gates carried off from Ganja in 1138 at its entrance. David himself was buried there. The Gelati Academy gathered theologians and philosophers who had studied at houses such as the Mangana in Constantinople: Ioane Petritsi wrote commentaries on Proclus, Arsen Ikaltoeli compiled the Aristotle-influenced Dogmatikon, and scribes copied manuscripts in its scriptorium, so that contemporaries called the house a new Hellas and a second Athos. Its solid stone cross-shaped churches and twelfth-century murals make it the defining monument of the Georgian Golden Age.
zh: 格拉特修道院雄踞在伊梅列季库塔伊西附近、俯瞰特斯卡尔齐特拉峡谷的山丘上，库塔伊西曾是中世纪格鲁吉亚国王的都城。1106年，大卫四世（建设者）在此同时兴建修道院与学院；主教堂圣母堂于1130年在继任者德米特里一世治下完工，1138年从占贾掠来的古城门就安放在教堂入口，大卫四世本人也安葬于此。格拉特学院汇聚了曾在君士坦丁堡曼加纳修道院等地求学的神学家和哲学家：约阿内·彼得里齐为普罗克洛斯作注，阿尔森·伊卡尔托埃利编成受亚里士多德影响的《教义集》，抄写员在缮写室里传抄典籍，时人把这里称为“新希腊”和“第二阿索斯”。石砌的十字形教堂与12世纪壁画，使它成为格鲁吉亚黄金时代最具代表性的纪念建筑。

en: The Gnana Saraswati Temple stands on the bank of the Godavari at Basar in the Nirmal country of Telangana, and with Sharada Peeth in Kashmir it is one of the two most celebrated shrines of Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and learning, in the subcontinent. Tradition connects the place with the sage Vyasa, who after the Kurukshetra war sought a quiet retreat in the Dandaka forest and settled here for long prayer; his abode was called Vasara, which in the mouths of later Marathi-speakers became Basara. Historically the temple is credited to a Karnataka king named Bijialudu, who ruled the Nandagiri province from Nanded in the 500s. It is counted among three temples raised near the confluence of the Manjira and the Godavari, and after Muslim invaders destroyed its images in the medieval period a chieftain of Nandagiri reinstalled the idols in the 1600s. Saraswati occupies the sanctum with Lakshmi beside her and Mahakali close by, so Basara is honoured as an abode of the goddess trinity; families bring young children here for the Akshara abhyasam, the ceremony in which they trace their first letters before the goddess.
zh: 智慧辩才天女庙坐落于特伦甘纳尼尔默尔一带巴萨尔镇的戈达瓦里河畔，与克什米尔的辩才天女庙并称次大陆最著名的两座辩才天女萨拉斯瓦蒂神庙，萨拉斯瓦蒂是主管知识与学问的女神。相传俱卢之战后，仙人毗耶娑为寻清静居所来到丹达卡森林，选中此地长期祈祷，他的住处称“瓦萨拉”，后来受马拉地语影响读成巴萨尔。史家一般认为，此庙是6世纪以楠德德为都、统治南达吉里地区的卡纳达国王比贾卢杜所建，也是曼吉拉河与戈达瓦里河汇流处附近修建的三座神庙之一。中世纪穆斯林入侵者毁坏神像后，17世纪一位南达吉里（楠德德）的首领重新安奉了神像。圣室中萨拉斯瓦蒂居中，旁立吉祥天女，近处还有大迦梨像，巴萨尔因此被尊为三位女神同居之地；家长们带着幼童来此举行“识字礼”，让孩子在女神面前写下人生第一个字母。

en: The Guruvayur Temple stands in the town of Guruvayur in central Kerala and is dedicated to Guruvayurappan, a four-armed standing form of Krishna-Vishnu carved from shaligram stone; it is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnava tradition. Tradition holds that the idol was first worshipped in Vishnu's heaven, passed through the hands of Brahma and King Sutapas, and after Krishna's death and the drowning of Dvaraka was brought south by his disciple Uddhava and installed by Brihaspati, the guru of the gods, and Vayu, the wind god, on a spot chosen by Shiva, who withdrew to nearby Mammiyoor; the place takes its name from Guru and Vayu. A Tamil poem of the fourteenth century already calls it Kuruvayur, and by the end of the sixteenth century it was a leading Kerala pilgrimage centre, its Sanskrit name popularised by Melpathur Narayana Bhattathiri, author of the Narayaneeyam. In 1716 Dutch raiders looted it and burned its western tower, rebuilt in 1747; Hyder Ali spared it for a ransom in 1766, and in 1789 Tipu Sultan's invasion forced the priests to hide the idol at Ambalappuzha until it was reinstalled in 1792.
zh: 古鲁瓦尤尔神庙位于喀拉拉中部的古鲁瓦尤尔镇，供奉以页岩化石雕成的四臂立像古鲁瓦尤尔阿潘，即奎师那与毗湿奴的合一之相，被列为毗湿奴派传统的108座自重圣地之一。相传神像最初供奉于毗湿奴的天界，经梵天和国王苏陀波萨之手流传；奎师那升天、德瓦卡城沉入海中后，其弟子优陀婆寻获神像，由天神之师祭主仙人与风神伐由携往南方，在湿婆指定之地安立，湿婆自己则退居邻近的马米尤尔，地名也取自祭主与伐由两位的名字。14世纪的泰米尔语诗篇已称此地为库鲁瓦尤尔，到16世纪末它已是喀拉拉首屈一指的朝圣中心，《那罗衍尼耶姆》的作者梅尔帕图尔·纳拉亚纳·巴塔蒂里使它的梵文化名字广为流传。1716年，荷兰入侵者洗劫神庙、烧毁西门楼，门楼于1747年重建；1766年海德尔·阿里在索取赎金后放过神庙；1789年蒂普苏丹来犯，祭司被迫把神像秘密转移到安巴拉普扎，直到1792年才重新安立。

en: Hamp'atu is a high peak of the puna grasslands in southern Peru, venerated as an apu, one of the Andean mountain spirits whose cult reaches back to the early second millennium BCE. Its Quechua name means toad, the same word behind the volcano Ampato, and like other sacred peaks it received offerings from nearby herding communities.
zh: 安帕图圣山是秘鲁南部普纳草原的一座高峰，被尊为安第斯山神“阿普”，这一山峰崇拜可追溯至公元前第二千年纪早期。其克丘亚语名意为“蟾蜍”，安帕托火山之名也出自同一个词；与其他圣峰一样，它接受附近放牧社群的献祭。

en: Haridwar, known in ancient Sanskrit texts as Gangadvara, the gate of the Ganges, and also as Mayapuri, stands where the river leaves the Himalayan foothills and first enters the great northern plain; its later name means gateway to Hari, the god Vishnu, for pilgrims set out from here for the mountain shrines of Badrinath and Kedarnath. The Mahabharata already praises Gangadvara as a tirtha, and Puranic legend counts it among the four places where drops of amrita, the nectar of immortality, fell from the gods' pitcher, at the Brahma Kund of the Har ki Pauri ghat. Its twelve-yearly bathing fair appears to be the original Kumbh Mela, named for the zodiacal sign Kumbha, or Aquarius, under which it is held; the earliest surviving texts to use that name, dating from 1695 and 1759, apply it only to Haridwar. Timur sacked the town in 1398 and massacred pilgrims gathered on its banks, and under Mughal rule the fair grew into one of north India's greatest religious and commercial gatherings, while the armed akharas of ascetics who ran it often fought over the right to bathe first: a clash of 1760 between Shaivite Gosains and Vaishnavite Bairagis left thousands dead, cholera killed more than twenty thousand pilgrims in 1783, and another sectarian massacre followed in 1796. After the Marathas ceded the region to the East India Company in 1804, the Company disarmed the ascetic orders and policed the bathing ghats, rebuilding them after a stampede in 1820.
zh: 赫里德瓦尔在梵文古籍中称“恒河门”（Gangadvara），又名摩耶普里，地处恒河走出喜马拉雅山麓、首次进入北部大平原之处；其今名意为“诃利之门”，诃利即毗湿奴，朝圣者正是从这里启程前往伯德里纳特、凯达尔纳特等山中神庙。《摩诃婆罗多》已将恒河门称颂为圣地，往世书传说中，长生不老的甘露从众神的壶中洒落四处，此地便是其中之一，落点以赫尔基保里河坛的梵天池为标志。这里十二年一度的沐浴节会似乎是最早的大壶节：举行时刻对应宝瓶宫（Kumbha），而现存最早使用“大壶节”一名的文献——1695年的《Khulasat-ut-Tawarikh》与1759年的《Chahar Gulshan》——都只用它称呼赫里德瓦尔的节会。1398年帖木儿洗劫此城，屠杀了聚集河畔的朝圣者；莫卧儿时期，节会成长为北印度最盛大的宗教与商业集会之一，而主持节会的武装苦行僧团“阿哈拉”常为谁先沐浴相争：1760年湿婆派戈赛因与毗湿奴派拜拉吉的冲突造成数千人死亡，1783年的节会又有逾两万人死于霍乱，1796年再度发生教派屠杀。1804年马拉塔人将这一地区割让给英国东印度公司后，公司解除了苦行僧团的武装，接管河坛治安，并在1820年踩踏事件后重修了河坛。

en: The Humcha temples, known locally as basadis, stand in the Malenadu hills of Karnataka and form the greatest southern centre of the cult of Padmavati, the yakshini attendant of Parshvanatha. Tradition relates that Jinadatta Raya, a Jain prince of the Solar dynasty who fled from Mathura carrying a golden image of Padmavati, was told in a dream to found his capital where the image rested; he established the town of Pombuccapura, modern Humcha, set up a Bhattaraka seat there in the 600s or 700s, and made the place the first capital of the Santara dynasty. The surviving shrines span the centuries of Santara patronage: the ruined Paliyakka Basadi of 878 is the oldest identified, the Guddada Basadi dedicated to Bahubali dates to 898 and the Parshvanatha temple to 950, while Vira Santara raised the present Padmavati temple in 1061. Chattaladevi built the largest monument, the five-shrined Panchakuta Basadi, in 1077 in the Chalukyan style together with its forty-foot manastambha pillar. The Santaras, who later made Humcha a feudatory centre of Vijayanagara, spread Digambara Jainism through the Tulu and Malenadu lands, and an inscription of 1530 even records a viceroy of Srirangapatna converting to Jainism here under the acharya Vidyananda. The Bhattaraka seat of the Humcha Matha remains one of the few that survive, and the lakki tree of Jinadatta's dream still stands beside the Padmavati shrine.
zh: 颔遮寺在当地称巴萨迪，坐落于卡纳塔克的马拉纳德丘陵，是南印度耆那教巴湿伐那陀的夜叉女护法钵特摩婆蒂信仰最大的中心。相传出身日族的耆那王子耆那达多·罗耶背负钵特摩婆蒂金像从秣菟罗出逃，梦中受女神指点，在金像停歇之地建都；他建立的蓬布遮补罗即后来的颔遮，于7至8世纪设立巴达罗迦教座，并成为桑塔拉王朝的第一个都城。存留的殿宇见证了桑塔拉王朝数百年的护法：可考最早的是878年已成废墟的波利耶迦寺，奉祀婆卢波利的古达达寺建于898年，巴湿伐那陀寺建于950年，现存的钵特摩婆蒂殿则由毗罗·桑塔拉于1061年建成。1077年，查多罗提毗按遮娄其风格修建了当地最大的五殿式五峰寺，并立起四十英尺高的荣誉柱。桑塔拉人后来使颔遮成为毗奢耶那伽罗的藩属中心，把天衣派耆那教传播到图卢与马拉纳德各地；1530年的一通铭文甚至记载室利楞伽帕特纳的一位总督在阿阇梨吠陀难陀影响下于此改宗耆那教。颔遮寺的巴达罗迦教座是少数尚存的教座之一，耆那达多梦中所依的拉基树也依然立在钵特摩婆蒂殿旁。

en: Ich Kaan Ti'Ho was the old name of the city archaeologists call Dzibilchaltun, whose name means the place of writing on flat stones, seventeen kilometres north of Merida in northern Yucatan. Settled from about 600 BC, it grew into a regional power of more than 25,000 people at its height between 800 and 1000, holding sway over much of the northwest of the peninsula until its fortunes faded around 1100. Its most sacred building was the Temple of the Seven Dolls, named for the seven small clay figures offered beneath its floor; the sun rises straight through its eastern and western doorways at the equinoxes, and a long sacbe, the white stone road, links it to the Great Plaza and to Cenote Xlacah. That deep waterhole, the reason the city stood where it did, became a cult place into which vases, carved bones and wooden offerings were cast. Stela 10 preserves the name of one of its kings, K'alo'mte' Uk'uuw Chan Chaahk. The settlement outlived its own monuments, and after the Spanish conquest a sixteenth-century open chapel was raised among the old stones, where the Maya still lived around the ancient cenote.
zh: 七子之像神庙所在的古城，古名 Ich Kaan Ti'Ho，考古学家称其为齐比尔查尔通，玛雅语意为“扁石上有文字之处”，位于尤卡坦北部梅里达以北17公里。城址约自公元前600年便有人居住，在800年至1000年的鼎盛期发展为人口逾2.5万的区域强权，控制着半岛西北部的大片土地，直到1100年前后国势衰落。城中最神圣的建筑是七子之像神庙，因庙底地面下供奉的七尊小泥像而得名；春分、秋分时，旭日恰好穿过它东西两门升起，一条长长的白色石砌大道将神庙与大广场和什拉卡天然井相连。这口深井是城市选址于此的原因，后来成为祭祀场所，人们向井中投献陶罐、刻纹骨器和木器。10号石碑保存着一位国王的名字：卡洛姆特·乌库乌·昌·查克。聚落的寿命比它的纪念碑更长久，西班牙征服之后，16世纪的一座露天礼拜堂就建在古石之间，玛雅人仍围绕着古老的天然井居住。

en: The Imam Ali Shrine at Najaf, near Kufa in Iraq, is the foremost Shia sanctuary, holding the tomb of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, fourth of the Rashidun caliphs and the first Shia Imam; Shia tradition also places the graves of Adam and Noah within its precinct. Ali was assassinated in Kufa in 661 by the Kharijite Ibn Muljam and buried in secret at the neighbouring desert spot that grew into Najaf, his grave hidden until the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid raised the first domed shrine over it in 786. The caliph al-Mutawakkil destroyed the sanctuary in 850, but the Hamdanids rebuilt it in 923 and the Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla enlarged it in 979 with a new dome and cenotaph, walling the town and bringing it water. Fire gutted the shrine in 1354 and it was rebuilt around 1358 by the Jalayirid sultan Shaikh Awais; the Safavid shah Abbas I began a grand reconstruction in 1623, finished under Shah Safi in 1632, and in 1742 Nader Shah gilded its dome and minarets, giving it the golden skyline that drew Shia pilgrims from across the region.
zh: 伊玛目阿里圣陵位于伊拉克库法附近的纳杰夫，是什叶派最重要的圣所，安葬着穆罕默德的堂弟兼女婿、第四位正统哈里发、什叶派第一位伊玛目阿里·本·阿比·塔利卜；什叶派传统还认为阿丹和努哈也葬在陵域之内。661年，阿里在库法被哈瓦利吉派的伊本·穆勒贾姆刺杀，秘密安葬在邻近后来发展为纳杰夫的沙漠之地，陵墓位置长期保密，直到786年阿拔斯哈里发哈伦·拉希德在墓上建起第一座带穹顶的圣陵。850年哈里发穆塔瓦基勒拆毁圣所，923年哈姆丹王朝将其重建，979年白益王朝埃米尔阿杜德·道莱又加以扩建，增建新穹顶和墓棺，并为城镇筑墙、引水。1354年圣陵毁于大火，1358年前后由札剌亦儿王朝重建；萨法维王朝的阿拔斯一世于1623年启动大规模重修，1632年由萨非完成，1742年纳迪尔沙为穹顶和宣礼塔贴金，金色的天际线自此吸引着各地的什叶派朝圣者。

en: The Imam Husayn Shrine in Karbala, Iraq, marks the tomb of Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of Muhammad and the third Shia Imam, who was killed there with his family and some seventy followers at the Battle of Karbala in 680 after rising against the Umayyad caliph Yazid I. His martyrdom, commemorated every year on Ashura, is the founding tragedy of Shia Islam and made Karbala one of its holiest cities; the mass grave of the Karbala martyrs and the tombs of Husayn's young sons lie beside his own. Pilgrimage was often forbidden by rulers wary of Shia devotion: the Abbasid caliph al-Saffah raised the first substantial shrine in the 750s, but in 850 al-Mutawakkil had the tomb demolished and its pit flooded, until his successor al-Muntasir allowed pilgrims to return. The Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla rebuilt and fortified the sanctuary in 981, and after a fire in 1016 it was restored again. In 1802 Wahhabi raiders from Najd sacked Karbala, massacred its people and tore down the dome, after which the Qajar shah Fath-Ali Shah funded the rebuilding of the shrine.
zh: 伊玛目侯赛因圣陵位于伊拉克卡尔巴拉，安葬着穆罕默德的外孙、什叶派第三位伊玛目侯赛因·伊本·阿里。680年，侯赛因起兵反抗伍麦叶哈里发耶齐德一世，在卡尔巴拉战役中与家人及约七十二名追随者一同被杀。他的殉难是什叶派信仰的奠基性悲剧，每年的阿舒拉节都要举行纪念，卡尔巴拉也因此成为什叶派最神圣的城市之一；卡尔巴拉烈士的合葬墓和侯赛因两个幼子的坟墓都在他的墓旁。历代统治者常因忌惮什叶派的虔敬而禁止朝觐：阿拔斯哈里发萨法赫在8世纪50年代建起第一座像样的圣陵，850年穆塔瓦基勒却下令毁墓、向墓坑灌水，直到后继者蒙塔塞尔放行朝圣者。981年白益埃米尔阿杜德·道莱重建并加固圣所，1016年火灾后再度修复。1802年，来自内志的瓦哈比武装洗劫卡尔巴拉、屠杀居民并捣毁穹顶，事后卡扎尔王朝的法塔赫-阿里沙出资重建了圣陵。

en: The Imam Reza Shrine in Mashhad, in Khorasan in northeastern Iran, holds the tomb of Ali al-Rida, the eighth Shia Imam, and is one of the holiest and most visited sanctuaries of Shia Islam; the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid is buried at his side. In 818 the caliph al-Ma'mun had Reza poisoned at the village of Sanabad near Tus, and the grave grew into the city of Mashhad, whose name means the place of martyrdom. A dome covered the tomb by the end of the ninth century, but in 993 the Ghaznavid ruler Sebuktigin sacked the town and halted pilgrimage, until Mahmud of Ghazni restored the shrine and fortified the city after 1009. The Seljuks raised a great dome over it, and after the Mongol devastation of Khorasan in 1220 the Ilkhanid ruler Öljaitü, himself a Shia convert, renovated the shrine on a grand scale. In 1418 the Timurid empress Goharshad built the mosque that still bears her name beside the sanctuary. With the Safavid adoption of Twelver Shiism in 1501 the shrine became a royal pilgrimage centre: Shah Abbas I walked from Isfahan to Mashhad and gilded the dome between 1601 and 1607, Nader Shah later gilded the minarets, and the Qajar shahs enlarged the complex still further in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 伊玛目礼萨圣陵位于伊朗东北部呼罗珊的马什哈德，安葬着什叶派第八位伊玛目阿里·礼萨，是什叶派最神圣、朝觐者最多的圣所之一；阿拔斯哈里发哈伦·拉希德也葬在他身旁。818年，哈里发马蒙在图斯附近的萨纳巴德村毒杀礼萨，墓地周围逐渐发展成城市马什哈德，其名意为“殉道者之地”。9世纪末墓上已建起穹顶，993年伽色尼统治者塞布克特勤洗劫城镇、禁止朝觐，1009年后伽色尼的马哈茂德重修圣陵并为城市筑防。塞尔柱人在墓上建起宏伟穹顶；1220年蒙古人蹂躏呼罗珊后，改宗什叶派的伊儿汗国统治者完者都大举修缮圣陵。1418年，帖木儿王朝皇后高哈尔绍德在圣所旁建起以她命名的清真寺。1501年萨法维王朝立十二伊玛目派为国教，圣陵成为皇家朝觐中心：阿拔斯一世从伊斯法罕徒步前往马什哈德，并于1601至1607年为穹顶贴金，纳迪尔沙后来又为宣礼塔贴金，19世纪初卡扎尔诸沙进一步扩建了圣陵建筑群。

en: In Quechua a wak'a is a revered place, rock or monument where Andean communities performed ritual and invoked the spirits dwelling in it, and the Inti Wak'a at Chan Chan marks the sun shrine within the greatest city of the Peruvian coast. From about 900 Chan Chan was the capital of Chimor, whose walled palace-mausoleums, isolated ceremonial pyramids and plazas formed a sacred landscape devoted above all to the royal ancestors and to the Moon, which the Chimú ranked above the Sun. The city kept its own solar cult regardless, until the Inca emperor Túpac Yupanqui besieged it in 1470, cutting the aqueducts that fed its irrigated fields and incorporating Chimor into the Inca Empire. Inca rule then drew the local wak'a into the state cult of Inti, the sun god and divine ancestor of the ruling dynasty. When the Chimú rebelled around 1500, Huayna Cápac sacked and partly burned the city, but the adobe shrines among its ruins continued to be venerated in the following centuries.
zh: 在克丘亚语中，wak'a（瓦卡，即圣所）指受人敬拜的地点、岩石或纪念建筑，安第斯社群在此举行仪式、呼请栖居其中的神灵；昌昌的因蒂圣所所标志的，就是秘鲁沿海最宏大城市中的太阳祭祀场所。约从900年起，昌昌成为奇姆王国的都城，城内带围墙的宫殿-陵墓、独立的仪式金字塔和广场构成一片神圣景观，主要侍奉王室祖先与月亮——在奇姆人的信仰里，月亮的地位高于太阳。尽管如此，城中仍保有自己的太阳崇拜。1470年，印加皇帝图帕克·尤潘基围攻昌昌，切断灌溉渠，将奇姆并入印加帝国；此后印加统治者把当地圣所纳入太阳神因蒂——王朝的神圣祖先——的国家崇拜之中。约1500年奇姆人反叛，瓦伊纳·卡帕克洗劫并部分焚毁了昌昌，但废墟中的土坯圣所在此后数百年间仍受到敬奉。

en: The Ise Grand Shrine in Shima province is the holiest place of Shintō, built around the Naikū that houses the Yata no Kagami, the sacred mirror of the sun goddess Amaterasu and one of the imperial regalia, and the Gekū dedicated to the food goddess Toyouke. Tradition says the princess Yamatohime wandered for twenty years before choosing Ise as the goddess's dwelling, and the first shrine hall was raised by Emperor Tenmu between 678 and 686; his widow Empress Jitō carried out the first ceremonial rebuilding in 692. Since then the Shikinen Sengū has renewed every hall every twenty years on an adjacent plot, alternating between two sites so that the ancient shinmei-zukuri style of plain cypress joined without nails is handed on unchanged. An imperial princess, the Saiō, served as high priestess from the late seventh century until the fourteenth, and Emperor Murakami placed Ise first among the shrines receiving imperial offerings in 965. In the Edo period the Okage mairi pilgrimage became a mass movement: in 1625 some 3.6 million pilgrims came within fifty days, and in 1829 more than a million arrived in three days for the great festival.
zh: 伊势神宫位于志摩地区，是神道教最神圣的场所，核心为供奉天照大神、收藏三神器之一八咫镜的内宫，以及供奉食物女神丰受大神的外宫。相传倭姬命辗转二十年后选定伊势作为天照大神的居所，天武天皇于678至686年间建起第一座神殿，皇后持统天皇又于692年主持了首次式年迁宫。此后每隔二十年，所有殿舍都在相邻的地块上重建，两块地基交替使用，使不用一钉、以素朴桧木构建的神明造古制得以原样传承。从7世纪末到14世纪，由皇族女子出任的斋王担任神宫最高祭司；965年村上天皇又将伊势列为接受朝廷奉币的神社之首。江户时代，“御荫参”朝圣演变为全民运动：1625年约有360万朝圣者在50天内涌入，1829年的大祭期间，三天之内便有上百万人到访。

en: Isthmia was the sanctuary of Poseidon on the Isthmus of Corinth, famous for the Isthmian Games, one of the four great Panhellenic festivals.
