Legend traced the games to funeral rites held by Sisyphus of Corinth for the boy Melicertes, and the historical festival was constituted in 582 BC. Its central position made the precinct a meeting place as much as a shrine: after Chaeronea in 338 BC Philip II of Macedon formed the League of Corinth there, and after the Second Macedonian War the Roman general Flamininus proclaimed the freedom of the Greeks before the festival crowd. The Temple of Poseidon was burned in 480 BC and again in 390 BC; when Rome destroyed Corinth in 146 BC the sanctuary was sacked and the games passed to Sicyon, returning after Julius Caesar refounded Corinth in 44 BC. The emperor Nero performed at the games in 67 AD, but the temple was later abandoned and its stones were reused in the Hexamilion wall in the fifth century. Thereafter Isthmia passed with the rest of the Morea between Byzantines, Venetians and Ottomans, falling permanently to the Turks in 1458.
zh: 伊斯米亚是科林斯地峡上的波塞冬圣地，以伊斯米亚运动会闻名，这是希腊四大泛希腊赛会之一。传说赛会源于科林斯的西西弗斯为少年墨利刻耳忒斯举行的葬礼竞技，历史上的赛会则确立于公元前582年。因其位置居中，圣区既是神庙也是会盟之所：公元前338年喀罗尼亚战役后，马其顿的腓力二世在此组建科林斯同盟；第二次马其顿战争后，罗马将领弗拉米尼努斯在赛会人群前宣告希腊人的自由。波塞冬神庙先后于公元前480年和公元前390年遭焚毁；公元前146年罗马毁灭科林斯，圣地被洗劫，赛会移交西库翁，直到公元前44年尤利乌斯·恺撒重建科林斯后才回归。67年皇帝尼禄亲自在赛会中登台表演，但神庙后来遭废弃，5世纪时其石材被拆去修筑赫克萨米利翁城墙。此后伊斯米亚随摩里亚各地在拜占庭、威尼斯和奥斯曼之间易手，于1458年永久落入土耳其人手中。

en: Izumo Taisha on the Sea of Japan coast is among the oldest and most revered shrines of Shintō, dedicated to Ōkuninushi, the god who builds the land and binds people in marriage. The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki tell that Ōkuninushi yielded the realm of Izumo to the heavenly grandson Ninigi, whereupon Amaterasu ordered a palace built for him with colossal pillars, and that palace became this shrine. Its taisha-zukuri hall gave its name to one of the oldest shrine architectural styles, and a Heian record of about 950 describes it as a tower roughly forty-eight metres high, taller than the great hall of Tōdai-ji. Like Ise, Izumo was renewed by periodic rebuilding, every sixty or seventy years; the hall was shortened around 1200 in the Kamakura period and reconstructed in 1744 to the twenty-four metres of the present building. In the tenth lunar month the kami of all Japan were believed to gather here to arrange the year's marriages, births and deaths, so Izumo calls that month kamiarizuki, the month with gods, while the rest of Japan calls it the month without gods. As travel widened in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, it became one of the country's great goals of pilgrimage.
zh: 出云大社位于日本海沿岸，是神道教最古老、最受尊崇的神社之一，供奉经营国土、掌管人间姻缘的大国主大神。《古事记》和《日本书纪》记载，大国主将出云之地让给天孙琼琼杵尊，天照大神遂下令以巨柱为他营建宫殿，这座宫殿便是出云大社。它的本殿开创了日本最古老的神社建筑样式之一“大社造”；约950年的一份平安时代记录称，当时的本殿高约48米，甚至超过东大寺的大佛殿。与伊势神宫相似，出云大社也每隔六七十年迁宫重建一次；镰仓时代的1200年前后本殿被改建缩小，1744年又重建为现存的24米高。相传每逢阴历十月，日本全国的神祇都会聚集于此，商议来年的姻缘、生育与死亡，因此出云当地把十月称为“神在月”，日本其他地方则称“神无月”。18至19世纪交通渐便，出云大社也成为日本最重要的朝圣目的地之一。

en: The Jagannath Temple at Puri, on the Odisha coast, is dedicated to Jagannath, a form of Vishnu, and ranks among the Char Dham, the four great pilgrimage sites of Hinduism. A shrine already stood at the site, then called Purushottama Kshetra, when Adi Shankara founded the Govardhan Math there in the ninth century; the present temple was raised from the early twelfth century by Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, after his conquest of Utkala in 1112. His successor Anangabhima Deva III dedicated the whole kingdom to Jagannath and styled himself the god's servant, and the later Gajapati kings made the temple a state-sponsored religious centre. Its wooden images of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra, carved from neem wood, are replaced in a grand ceremony called Nabakalebara every twelve or nineteen years, and each summer the three deities ride through the town on towering temple cars in the Ratha Yatra, India's most famous chariot festival; the saint Chaitanya lived and worshipped here for years. In 1568 the Bengal general Kalapahar sacked Puri and burned the images, and Ramachandra Deva I of Khurda restored the cult and reinstalled new images in 1575. Mughal governors repeatedly raided the temple, whose annals record eighteen plunderings, and after the East India Company took Odisha in 1803 it taxed the pilgrims until ordered to withdraw from temple affairs in 1833.
zh: 普里的世主奎师那神庙位于奥里萨海岸，供奉毗湿奴的化身札格纳特，是印度教四大朝圣圣地之一。早在9世纪阿迪·商羯罗在此建立戈瓦尔丹寺时，这片古称布鲁绍多摩圣地的地方已有神庙；现存建筑则是东恒伽王朝的阿南塔跋摩·朱达恒伽提婆在1112年征服乌特伽罗后，于12世纪初起陆续修建的。其继任者阿南加比马·提婆三世把整个王国献给札格纳特，自称神的仆人，后来的加贾帕蒂诸王又把神庙建成国家扶持的宗教中心。庙中札格纳特、巴拉巴德拉和苏婆德拉三尊神像以楝木雕成，每隔12或19年要在名为换身仪式的大典中更换；每年夏天三尊神像乘坐高大神车穿城而过，是印度最负盛名的乘车节，圣人柴坦尼亚也曾在此居住礼拜多年。1568年，孟加拉将领卡拉帕哈尔洗劫普里、焚毁神像，库尔达的罗摩旃陀罗·提婆一世复兴信仰，于1575年重立新像。莫卧儿时代的总督一再袭击神庙，庙史记载共遭劫掠18次；1803年英国东印度公司夺取奥里萨后向朝圣者征税，直到1833年才奉命退出神庙事务。

en: The Jal Mandir, the Water Temple, rises from a lotus-covered tank at Pawapuri, the sinless town of ancient Magadha, and marks the place where Mahavira, the twenty-fourth Tirthankara, was cremated. During the rainy-season retreat of 527 BCE, Mahavira, then seventy-two years old, passed his final chaturmas at Pawapuri and attained nirvana there on the night of the Dipawali festival, the event that Jains commemorate at every Diwali. Pilgrims carried away so much of the soil sanctified by his funeral pyre that the spot became a pit and filled with water, and Mahavira's elder brother Nandivardhan is said to have raised the first shrine within the new pond. The present white-marble temple is built in the shape of a vimana chariot and houses the Charan Paduka, the foot impression of Mahavira; a stone bridge six hundred feet long joins it to the bank. Two companion shrines complete the tirth: the Gaon Mandir on the bank, marking the place of nirvana itself, and the circular Samosharana temple, whose image shows Mahavira delivering his last sermon.
zh: 水上神殿（贾尔曼迪尔）矗立在古摩揭陀波婆补罗——意即“无罪之城”——一方莲花满塘的水池中央，标志着第二十四代祖大雄火化之处。公元前527年雨季安居期间，七十二岁的大雄在波婆补罗度过最后一次夏安居，并于排灯节之夜在此涅槃，耆那教信众每逢排灯节都要纪念此事。香客纷纷取走焚化圣址的泥土，竟在原地掘出大坑、积水成塘，相传大雄的兄长难提伐弹那遂在塘中建起第一座神龛。现存殿宇以白色大理石建成，形如神车维摩那，内奉大雄的足印圣迹“恰兰帕杜迦”，一条六百英尺长的石桥把神殿与塘岸相连。圣地另有两座配殿：岸上的村庄神殿标志涅槃的确切地点，圆形的萨摩婆萨罗那神殿则供奉大雄最后讲法的造像。

en: Jerusalem stood at the heart of East Syriac piety even though it lay far from the Church of the East's Mesopotamian heartland, and its monks regarded a pilgrimage to the Holy Sepulchre as the highest of callings. Around 1275 two Chinese monks, Rabban Bar Sauma and his pupil Markos, later the patriarch Yahballaha III, set out from Khanbaliq on just such a pilgrimage, only to be turned back by warfare in Syria. In 1260 Mongol forces under the Nestorian general Kitbuqa raided Palestine, and Hulagu Khan wrote to the king of France that Jerusalem had been restored to the Christians. A permanent East Syriac community endured in the city through the Mamluk age: contemporary Franciscan records show a recognizable Nestorian presence at the Holy Sepulchre between 1348 and 1575, and in 1482 the Dominican pilgrim Felix Fabri still listed Nestorians among the many rites dwelling in Jerusalem alongside Greeks, Jacobites, Armenians and Ethiopians. The long contraction of the Church of the East after Timur's campaigns and the schism of 1552 thinned these congregations, and after the later sixteenth century the Nestorian altars at the Holy Sepulchre vanish from the pilgrim accounts, absorbed or abandoned as the larger denominations divided the shrines between them.
zh: 耶路撒冷虽远离东方教会的美索不达米亚本土，却处于东叙利亚虔诚信仰的核心，僧侣们把前往圣墓教堂朝圣视为最高志向。约1275年，两名中国修士拉班·扫马和他的学生马尔谷——即后来的牧首雅巴拉哈三世——从汗八里出发踏上这样的朝圣之旅，却因叙利亚的战事受阻而返。1260年，聂斯脱里派将领怯的不花率蒙古军袭扰巴勒斯坦，旭烈兀汗还致信法国国王，称耶路撒冷已交还基督徒。马穆鲁克时代，城中始终维持着一个东叙利亚社群：方济各会的同期记述显示，1348—1575年间圣墓教堂里一直有可辨识的聂斯脱里派存在；1482年，多明我会朝圣者法布里仍把聂斯脱里派与希腊人、雅各派、亚美尼亚人和埃塞俄比亚人并列为耶路撒冷的众多仪轨群体。帖木儿征战之后东方教会长期萎缩，1552年又发生大分裂，这些会众日益稀薄；16世纪后期以后，朝圣文献中不再见到圣墓教堂里的聂斯脱里派祭台的记载，它们在各大教派分割圣地的过程中被吞并或遭废弃。

en: The bishopric of Jerusalem, which tradition traces back to James the brother of Jesus, was raised to the rank of patriarchate by the Council of Chalcedon in 451, taking fifth place in the pentarchy after Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria and Antioch. In 637 Patriarch Sophronius surrendered the city to the caliph Umar under a covenant guaranteeing Christian protection, and the following year the Armenian Apostolic Church, which rejects Chalcedon, began appointing its own bishops in Jerusalem; their see grew into the Armenian Patriarchate of Saint James, the Miaphysite counterpart beside the Greek throne. When the crusaders took the city in 1099 the Orthodox patriarch was driven out and a Latin patriarch installed, while Greek patriarchs continued to be elected in Constantinople until Saladin's victory of 1187 allowed the patriarchate to return. Through the Mamluk and Ottoman centuries the Greek Brotherhood of the Holy Sepulchre guarded its rights in the Holy Sepulchre and the Church of the Nativity against the Franciscans, holding them through successive imperial decrees, while the Armenian quarter walled itself in during the 1340s and in 1439 lost and then bargained back its rights at the Golgotha chapel. Under Ottoman millet rule the patriarch sat as ethnarch of the local Orthodox, and after the Crimean War Russian alms and pilgrims enriched the patriarchate; in 1833 the Armenians set up Jerusalem's first printing press in their monastery.
zh: 耶路撒冷主教区传统上溯至耶稣的弟兄雅各，451年迦克墩公会议将其升格为牧首区，在罗马、君士坦丁堡、亚历山大和安条克之后位列五大牧首区之末。637年，牧首索弗罗尼乌斯在保证基督徒受保护的协约下把城市交给哈里发欧麦尔；次年，不承认迦克墩会议的亚美尼亚使徒教会开始在耶路撒冷自派主教，其座堂发展为圣雅各亚美尼亚牧首区，成为希腊牧座旁边的基督合性派对应机构。1099年十字军攻占城市后，东正教牧首被驱逐，拉丁牧首取而代之，希腊牧首仍在君士坦丁堡继续选举，直到1187年萨拉丁获胜后牧首区才得以回归。马穆鲁克和奥斯曼的数百年间，希腊人的圣墓兄弟会凭借一道道帝国敕令，在圣墓教堂和圣诞教堂守护自身权利，与方济各会抗衡；亚美尼亚人则在14世纪40年代为自己的教区筑起围墙，并在1439年失去各各他小堂的权利后又谈判取得补偿。奥斯曼米利特制度下，牧首以本地东正教徒民族领袖的身份行事；克里米亚战争后，俄国的施舍和朝圣者使牧首区财力大增，1833年亚美尼亚人在他们的修道院里开办了耶路撒冷第一家印刷所。

en: The Christian holy places of Jerusalem are gathered in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in the Old City. Around 135 the emperor Hadrian buried the venerated tomb under a temple of Aphrodite, and after Constantine's bishops cleared the site early in the fourth century, three crosses were unearthed nearby, one of them taken for the True Cross; the new basilica was consecrated in 335. In 614 Sassanid troops under Khosrow II burned the church and carried the True Cross away, and the emperor Heraclius restored both after his return to the city in 630. The Fatimid caliph al-Hakim ordered the whole building demolished in 1009, and reconstruction paid for by Constantine IX Monomachos was completed only in 1048. Crusaders who took Jerusalem in 1099 rebuilt it in the Romanesque manner and finished the work under Queen Melisende in 1149, uniting the scattered chapels under one roof. Saladin's forces occupied the church in 1187 yet soon admitted Christian pilgrims again, while the Khwarizmian sack of 1244 brought fresh destruction. Under Ottoman rule the Status Quo of 1757 fixed the rights of the rival denominations, and after the great fire of 1808 the rotunda and the shrine of the tomb were rebuilt between 1809 and 1810.
zh: 耶路撒冷的基督教圣迹集中在老城的圣墓教堂。约135年，皇帝哈德良把受尊崇的墓穴压在一座阿芙洛狄忒神殿之下；4世纪初君士坦丁的主教们清理场地后，在附近发掘出三个十字架，其中一个被认定为真十字架，新的巴西利卡于335年祝圣。614年，霍斯劳二世麾下的萨珊军队焚毁教堂并掠走真十字架，630年皇帝希拉克略重返耶路撒冷后将二者恢复。1009年，法蒂玛哈里发哈基姆下令整座拆毁教堂，由君士坦丁九世·莫诺马霍斯出资的重建工程直到1048年才完工。1099年攻占耶路撒冷的十字军以罗曼式风格重建教堂，工程在梅利桑德女王治下的1149年完成，把分散的小堂统一在同一屋顶之下。1187年萨拉丁的军队占领教堂，但很快重新允许基督徒朝圣；1244年花剌子模人的洗劫又带来新的破坏。奥斯曼统治时期，1757年的“现状协定”确定了相互竞争的各教派权利；1808年大火之后，圆形大厅与墓穴圣龛于1809—1810年重建。

en: Al-Quds, Jerusalem, is the third holiest city of Islam after Mecca and Medina, its sanctity concentrated on the Haram al-Sharif, the Noble Sanctuary in the Old City. Muslims believe that Muhammad was carried there by night from Mecca and ascended to heaven from the rock at its heart, and Jerusalem was the first qibla, the direction of early Muslim prayer, before the Kaaba took that role. After the Arab conquest of 637 the caliph Umar founded a prayer house on the platform, and in 691 to 692 the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik raised the Dome of the Rock over the holy rock, the oldest surviving Islamic monument in the world. The neighbouring Al-Aqsa Mosque, first built under the Umayyads, was rebuilt by the Abbasids in 758 and again by the Fatimid caliph al-Zahir after the earthquake of 1033. Crusaders turned the sanctuary into a church and the headquarters of the Knights Templar after 1099, until Saladin retook Jerusalem in 1187 and restored Muslim worship; Ayyubid, Mamluk and Ottoman rulers then adorned and maintained it down the centuries.
zh: 古德斯即耶路撒冷，是伊斯兰教仅次于麦加和麦地那的第三大圣城，其神圣性集中于老城的谢里夫圣地，即尊贵圣地。穆斯林相信穆罕默德夜间从麦加被带到此地，并从圣地中央的岩石登霄；在克尔白成为礼拜朝向之前，耶路撒冷曾是最早的礼拜朝向。637年阿拉伯人征服后，哈里发欧麦尔在台地上建起礼拜所；691至692年，伍麦叶哈里发阿卜杜勒-马利克在圣石之上修建岩石圆顶寺，这是世界上现存最古老的伊斯兰建筑。相邻的阿克萨清真寺始建于伍麦叶时期，758年由阿拔斯人重建，1033年地震后又由法蒂玛哈里发扎希尔重修。1099年后十字军把圣地改为教堂和圣殿骑士团总部，直到1187年萨拉丁收复耶路撒冷、恢复穆斯林礼拜；此后阿尤布、马穆鲁克和奥斯曼的统治者相继装点、维护这处圣所。

en: The Jogulamba Temple at Alampur stands where the Tungabhadra river approaches its confluence with the Krishna, in the dry uplands of the northern Deccan. The goddess Jogulamba, whose name means Mother of Yogis in Telugu, is shown in a fierce form seated on a corpse with a scorpion, frog and lizard above her head, and her shrine is counted fifth among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas; tradition holds that the upper teeth of Sati fell here when Vishnu dismembered her body. It shares its enclosure with the nine Navabrahma Shiva temples, raised in the seventh and eighth centuries under the Badami Chalukyas, and the region, praised in the Skanda Purana as the western gateway of Srisailam, was already a celebrated place of pilgrimage. In 1390 Bahmani armies sacked and largely destroyed the temple during their Deccan campaigns, although the Vijayanagara emperor Harihara Raya II counter-attacked and fortified the complex. The priests had already carried Jogulamba's image to safety in the nearby Bala Brahma temple, where it was worshipped in a secluded chamber for more than six centuries.
zh: 乔古兰巴神庙位于阿拉姆普尔，地处德干北部干旱高地、栋格珀德拉河临近与克里希纳河汇流之处。女神乔古兰巴之名在泰卢固语中意为‘瑜伽士之母’，呈忿怒相坐于尸体之上，头侧刻有蝎子、青蛙和蜥蜴；其神庙位列十八处大性力佩特的第五处，相传毗湿奴肢解萨蒂遗体时，萨蒂的上齿落在此地。神庙与九座纳瓦婆罗贺摩湿婆庙同处一院，后者建于7至8世纪的巴达米遮娄其王朝时期；《塞建陀往世书》称这一带为室利赛拉姆的西门，自古便是著名的朝圣之地。1390年，巴赫马尼苏丹的军队在德干战事中洗劫并严重摧毁了神庙，维查耶纳伽罗皇帝诃里诃罗二世随后发兵反击并加固庙区。祭司们事先已将乔古兰巴神像转移到附近的婆罗·婆罗贺摩庙，秘藏于密室中供奉达六个多世纪。

en: Jyotisar is a shrine on the Jyotisar Sarovar tank, about five kilometres west of Thanesar in the Kurukshetra region, where Hindu tradition places the opening of the great battle of the Mahabharata. Here, on the first day of fighting, Krishna is said to have answered the doubts of his friend Arjuna, who shrank from killing his own kin, with the sermon that became the Bhagavad Gita, and to have revealed his universal form before him beneath a banyan tree; a banyan venerated as an offshoot of that tree rises on a raised plinth at the water's edge. The name means the lake of light, and in the 700s the Hindu scholar Adi Shankara identified Jyotisar as the exact spot of the discourse. An old Shiva temple on the site is said to have been worshipped at by both the Kauravas and the Pandavas, and the shrine forms one of the stops on the 48-kos circumambulation of Kurukshetra.
zh: 殊帝萨是坦内萨尔以西约5公里、库鲁克谢特拉地区殊帝萨池畔的一处圣所，印度教传统把《摩诃婆罗多》大战的开端放在这一带。相传开战首日，阿周那不愿向同族挥兵，奎师那在此为他释疑，说出了后来成为《薄伽梵歌》的教言，并在一棵榕树下向他显现宇宙相；池畔高台上立着一棵榕树，被视为那棵神树的分枝。殊帝萨意为光之池，8世纪时阿迪·商羯罗确认这里正是宣说《薄伽梵歌》的确址。当地还有一座古老的湿婆庙，相传俱卢族与班度族都曾在此礼拜，这座圣所也是环库鲁克谢特拉48科斯巡礼路线上的一站。

en: The Masjid al-Haram of Mecca, the holiest site of Islam, is the sacred mosque built around the Kaaba, a cube-shaped stone building that Muslims hold to be the House of God, first raised by the prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail. The Kaaba fixes the qibla, the direction in which Muslims everywhere turn to pray. Before Islam it was a pagan sanctuary of the Quraysh housing 360 idols, chief among them Hubal; after Muhammad's entry into Mecca the idols were destroyed and the shrine rededicated to the one God. Fire gutted the building during the Umayyad siege of 683, and in 693 the caliph Abd al-Malik rebuilt it on the old Qurayshi foundations, giving it the cube form it has kept ever since. In 930 the Qarmatians carried off the Black Stone and held it until 952; after the floods of 1626 the Ottoman sultan Murad IV rebuilt the walls. Circling the Kaaba seven times is the central rite of the hajj and umrah pilgrimages, and its black cloth covering, the kiswah, is renewed every year.
zh: 禁寺是伊斯兰教最神圣的圣地麦加圣寺，寺院核心是立方体石殿克尔白。穆斯林认为克尔白是真主之屋，最早由先知易卜拉欣与其子易斯马仪修建，它标定了全世界穆斯林礼拜的朝向。前伊斯兰时代，这里是古莱什人的异教圣所，供奉着以胡巴勒为首的360尊偶像；穆罕默德进入麦加后捣毁偶像，将圣殿重新奉献给唯一的真主。683年伍麦叶军队围攻麦加时大火焚毁殿身，693年哈里发阿卜杜勒-马利克在古莱什旧基上重建，奠定了后世克尔白的立方体形制。930年卡尔马特派劫走黑石，直到952年才将其归还；1626年洪水毁墙后，奥斯曼苏丹穆拉德四世加以重修。环绕克尔白绕行七圈是朝觐和副朝的核心仪式，殿外覆盖的黑色锦幔罩幕每年更换。

en: The Kalaram Temple stands in the Panchavati quarter of Nashik on the Godavari, the forest where the Ramayana says Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spent more than two years of their fourteen-year exile. It takes its name from its black stone image of Rama, kala meaning black, flanked in the sanctum by black images of Sita and Lakshmana. A shrine of great antiquity stood here in the Rashtrakuta period of the seventh to eleventh centuries, and during the early Turkish invasions its Brahmins hid the idol in the Godavari to save it from desecration. Around 1700 the Maratha sardar Rangarao Odhekar, guided by a dream, recovered the black image from the river and rebuilt the temple and reconsecrated the deity; his own statue stands in the complex. The present building is climbed by fourteen entrance steps recalling the years of exile, rises on eighty-four pillars, and keeps a black Hanuman facing Rama's sanctum. Under Mughal rule Nashik was called Gulshanabad, and the rebuilt temple became one of the principal Rama pilgrimage places of the Maratha Deccan.
zh: 黑罗摩神庙位于纳西克的潘查瓦蒂区、戈达瓦里河畔；《罗摩衍那》中，罗摩、悉多与罗什曼那在十四年流放期间，曾在这片林间居住两年有余。庙名来自主神的黑石雕像，“卡拉”意为黑色，圣所中悉多与罗什曼那的神像也同为黑色，三像并立。此地早有古庙，历史可追溯至7至11世纪的罗湿陀罗拘陀时期；早期突厥入侵时，庙中婆罗门为保护神像，将其沉入戈达瓦里河藏起。约1700年，马拉塔的萨达尔朗加拉奥·奥德卡尔受梦境指引，从河中打捞出黑色罗摩像，重建神庙并重新为神像开光，他本人的雕像也立于庙中。现存建筑入口有十四级台阶，象征流放的十四年，全庙立有八十四根石柱，还有一尊黑色哈奴曼像正对罗摩圣所。莫卧儿治下纳西克改称古尔尚阿巴德，重建后的黑罗摩神庙成为马拉塔德干最重要的罗摩朝圣中心之一。

en: The Kalighat Kali Temple stands on a ghat of the old Bhagirathi channel in the Bengal delta, its name combining Kali with the river landing where she is worshipped. The goddess is Kali, foremost of the ten Mahavidyas and the supreme deity of the Tantric Kalikula tradition, and the shrine is counted among the fifty-one Shakta Pithas and the four original Adi Shaktipeeths, for the Puranas teach that the toes of Sati's right foot fell here when Vishnu dismembered her body. A place of goddess worship on this bank is already named in the Bengali poem Mansar Bhasan of the 1400s and again in Kavi Kankan's Chandi of the 1600s, when the shrine was tended by holy men in a riverside hamlet. The present temple was built in the Bengal ath-chala style, its eight-sloped roof imitating a thatched village hut: Santosh Roy Chowdhury began the work in 1798 under the patronage of the Sabarna Roy Choudhury zamindars and it was completed in 1809, while Kashinath Roy added the Nat Mandir hall in 1835. Pilgrims bathe the image in the Snan Yatra at the temple tank, and Kali Puja and the new moon nights draw the greatest crowds.
zh: 迦梨女神庙坐落在孟加拉三角洲古婆吉罗提河道的一处河坛上，庙名即由迦梨女神与受祀的河坛（加特）合成。主神迦梨是十大明妃之首、密教迦梨库拉传承的最高女神；此庙位列五十一处性力佩特，也是四大最初性力佩特之一，往世书称毗湿奴肢解萨蒂遗体时，其右足脚趾坠落于此。早在1400年代的孟加拉长诗《摩萨尔跋娑》和1600年代的《诗人坎坎·禅迪》中，就已提到这处河岸边的女神道场，当时神祠由河畔小村中的圣徒照看。现存庙宇采用孟加拉阿特-查拉风格，八面坡顶模仿乡村茅草屋：桑托什·罗伊·乔杜里在萨巴尔纳·罗伊·乔杜里柴明达尔家族资助下于1798年动工，1809年落成，卡西纳特·罗伊又于1835年增建了纳特曼迪尔乐舞殿。信众在庙池举行圣浴节为神像沐浴，而迦梨普迦和各朔日之夜最是人潮汹涌。

en: The Kalika Mata Temple crowns the summit of Pavagadh Hill above Champaner in eastern Gujarat, the oldest shrine in a landscape of forts and Jain and Hindu monuments. The goddess is venerated as Mahakali in the form of Durga or Chandi, her central image flanked by Kali and Bahuchara Mata, and a Kali Yantra kept in the sanctum is dated to the 900s or 1000s, the same centuries that saw the first temple on this peak. Counted among the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, the hill is hallowed as the place where a toe of Sati's right foot fell, and the Bhil and Koli tribes of the surrounding forests have worshipped the goddess here from the earliest times. Pavagadh was also a great Jain pilgrimage: in 1055 the monk Gunsagarsuri consecrated images on the hill, and from 1113 the Svetambara Achalgacch honoured Mahakali as its protecting deity, so that the shrine long served both Jain and Hindu devotees. The temple appears in the Gujarati drama Gangadas Pratap Vilasa Natakam of the 1400s, and in 1484 Mahmud Begada of Gujarat stormed the Pavagadh fort after a twenty-month siege and built his new capital of Muhammadabad, the later Champaner, on the plain below; Humayun in turn scaled the cliffs and took the fortress in 1535. Through these conquests the goddess kept her pilgrims, who still gather in thousands for the fair of Chitra Sud 8.
zh: 伽利伽·摩多神庙雄踞古吉拉特东部尚庞上方帕瓦加德山的顶峰，是这片遍布堡垒与耆那教、印度教古迹之地最古老的神祠。女神以摩诃迦梨的身份受祀，显现为难近母或禅底形态，主像两侧分立迦梨与婆呼遮罗女神；殿中珍藏的迦梨曼陀罗可断代至900至1000年代，山顶首座庙宇也建于这几个世纪。此庙位列五十一处性力佩特，圣山被视为萨蒂右足脚趾坠落之地，周围森林中的比尔人和科利人自古便在此敬拜女神。帕瓦加德同时也是耆那教大朝圣中心：1055年僧师军海苏利在此为神像开光，1113年起白衣派阿恰尔伽阇更尊摩诃迦梨为该派护法神，神祠因此长期同时服务于耆那教与印度教信众。1400年代的古吉拉特语戏剧《甘伽达什荣耀剧》已描写此庙；1484年，古吉拉特苏丹马哈茂德·贝伽达经二十个月围攻攻陷帕瓦加德要塞，在山下平原营建新都穆罕默达巴德，即后来的尚庞，1535年胡马雍又攀越悬崖夺取此堡。历经兵燹，女神香火不绝，每逢质多罗月白分八日的庙会，仍有数千信众朝山。

en: Kamakhya crowns the Nilachal hills above Guwahati in Assam and is one of the most revered centres of Tantric Hinduism, counted among the four oldest of the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, where the yoni of Sati is believed to have fallen when Shiva carried her body. The dark underground sanctum holds no image but a natural rock fissure shaped like a yoni, fed by a perennial spring and worshipped as the goddess herself; the cult grew from the Kirata and tribal worship of the region before the Mlechchha kings of Kamarupa adopted the shrine in the 9th century, and under the Palas the Kalika Purana tied Kamakhya to the legends of the Kamarupa kings. Ruined during Hussein Shah's invasion of Kamata in 1498, the temple was restored by the Koch dynasty: Vishwasingha revived the worship and his son Nara Narayan completed the rebuilding in 1565 under Chilarai, when the artisan Meghamukdam raised the present brick dome and created the Nilachal style, a hemispherical dome on a cruciform base ringed by charchala turrets. Around the main shrine stand separate temples of the ten Mahavidyas, an arrangement rare in India. The Ahoms, who took Kamrup by 1658 and secured it after the Battle of Itakhuli in 1681, added the dancing hall bearing inscriptions of 1759 and 1782 and installed Bengali Shakta mahants as its priests. The annual Ambubachi Mela celebrates the goddess's menstruation and draws Tantric pilgrims from across Bengal and Assam.
zh: 卡马基雅寺高踞阿萨姆古瓦哈蒂的尼拉查尔山，是最古老、最受尊崇的怛特罗印度教中心之一，位列五十一处性力派圣地中最古的四处；相传湿婆怀抱萨蒂遗体游荡时，萨蒂的约尼（女阴）便坠落于此。幽暗的地下密室中不立神像，只有一道天然岩石裂成约尼之形，底下常年泉水涌出，信众直接将其奉为女神本身。这种崇拜源自当地基拉塔人与部落的信仰，9世纪迦摩缕波的蔑戾车王朝率先将神庙纳入王室护持，其后波罗王朝又命人撰写《迦利迦往世书》，把卡马基雅编织进迦摩缕波诸王的创世传说。1498年侯赛因沙入侵迦摩塔王国时神庙被毁，科赫王朝的毗湿瓦辛哈恢复了香火，其子那罗·那罗延在兄弟奇拉莱主持下于1565年完成重建，工匠梅伽穆克丹垒起今日的砖穹顶，开创了十字基座上覆半球穹顶、四周环立恰尔查拉小塔的混合式“尼拉查尔风格”。主庙周围还分立着十大明妃的独立神祠，这种格局在印度十分罕见。阿洪姆人于1658年夺取迦摩缕波，又在1681年伊塔胡利之战后牢牢控制此地，他们增建了舞殿，留下1759年和1782年的铭文，并从孟加拉请来性力派高僧担任祭司。一年一度的安布巴奇节庆祝女神的月事，仍吸引着孟加拉与阿萨姆各地的怛特罗朝圣者。

en: The Kamakshi Amman Temple lies in Kanchipuram, the Pallava-era temple city south-west of Chennai, and is dedicated to Kamakshi, a supreme form of the goddess Adi Shakti. The Pallava kings, whose capital was Kanchipuram, founded the shrine between the fifth and eighth centuries, and it is counted among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas; its Varaha shrine is also honoured as one of the Divya Desams of the Tamil Vaishnavas, praised by the Alvar poet-saints in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham. The goddess is shown seated in the lotus pose holding a noose, goad, sugarcane bow and flower arrow, with a Sri Yantra before her that tradition credits to Adi Shankara, and the temple was enlarged in the 1300s and again in the 1600s. After the fall of Vijayanagara in 1565 the golden image of Kamakshi was carried from place to place for safety, kept at Tiruvarur from 1739 to 1781, and finally installed in a rebuilt Kanchipuram temple in 1783, under the care of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham.
zh: 爱目母神庙坐落于金奈西南的古城甘吉布勒姆——帕拉瓦王朝的都城，供奉至尊女神阿迪·夏克提的化身迦摩刹。帕拉瓦诸王于5至8世纪创建此庙，它被列为十八处大性力圣地之一；庙中的筏罗诃（野猪化身毗湿奴）神龛又被泰米尔毗湿奴派尊为圣庙之一，阿尔瓦尔诗圣们的《四千圣歌集》曾加以赞颂。女神像结莲花坐，手持套索、刺棒、甘蔗弓与花箭，像前供奉着相传由阿迪·商羯罗安置的室利坛城；神庙在14世纪和17世纪两度扩建。1565年毗奢耶那伽罗沦落后，为安全起见，金铸的迦摩刹像被辗转迁移，1739至1781年间安奉于提鲁瓦鲁尔，最终于1783年迎回重建的甘吉布勒姆神庙，由甘吉迦摩科提道场负责照管。

en: Kanchipuram, the City of a Thousand Temples on the Palar river in Tamil Nadu, was already famous before the common era: Patanjali mentions it, Kalidasa called it the best of cities, and it ranks among the seven Sapta Puri holy cities where Hindus seek liberation. From the sixth century it was the capital of the Pallavas, who raised its earliest stone temples, including the Kailasanathar and Vaikuntha Perumal; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang found in 640 a great seat of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain learning, and tradition names it as Bodhidharma's home. The Cholas under Aditya I took the city about 890 and made it the seat of their northern viceroy, after which it passed to the Pandyas and was disrupted by Malik Kafur's invasion of 1311, until the Vijayanagara general Kumara Kampana conquered it in 1361 and restored Hindu worship. Vijayanagara kings, above all Krishna Deva Raya, lavished grants on its shrines; after the empire fell, Golconda, Bijapur, the Marathas and the Mughals fought over it, and priests carried its temple idols south to safety between 1688 and 1707. It then passed to the Nawabs of the Carnatic and the East India Company, whose wars with France and Mysore, notably the nearby Battle of Pollilur in 1780, swirled around it. Fifteen of the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desam temples stand here, among them Varadharaja Perumal, alongside the great Shaiva temple of Ekambareswarar and the Kamakshi Amman shrine, and its silk weavers have been famous for centuries.
zh: 甘吉布勒姆位于泰米尔纳德的巴拉尔河畔，有“千庙之城”之称，早在公元前便已闻名：文法家波颠阇利的著作提到它，诗人迦梨陀娑称它为城市之最，它也是印度教七圣城“萨帕塔普里”之一，印度教徒相信在此可求得解脱。6世纪起它成为帕拉瓦王朝的都城，最早的石庙在此建起，包括凯拉萨纳特神庙与毗琨塔·佩鲁马尔神庙；640年中国求法僧玄奘到访时，这里是印度教、佛教与耆那教的大学问中心，传统还认为僧人菩提达摩出身于此。约890年，阿底提耶一世率领朱罗人攻占此城，将其设为北方副王的驻节地；此后它转入潘地亚人之手，1311年马利克·卡富尔的入侵使地方陷入混乱，直到1361年毗奢耶那伽罗将领库马拉·坎帕纳攻克此地，恢复了印度教祭祀。毗奢耶那伽罗诸王建中以克里希纳·德瓦·拉亚的赐赠最丰，直到帝国崩溃；随后戈尔孔达、比贾布尔、马拉塔与莫卧儿轮番争夺，1688至1707年间祭司们把神庙神像南运避难。此后它归卡纳蒂克纳瓦卜与英国东印度公司统治，公司与法国、迈索尔的战争——包括1780年在附近打响的波利鲁尔战役——都曾波及此城。毗湿奴派108处圣域（Divya Desam）中有15处在此，包括瓦拉达拉贾·佩鲁马尔神庙，此外还有湿婆派的埃坎巴雷什瓦拉尔大庙与迦摩克希·安曼神庙；此地的丝绸织工也已闻名数百年。

en: The Karpaka Vinayakar Temple, also called the Pillaiyarpatti Pillaiyar Temple, is a rock-cut cave shrine dedicated to Ganesha in Pillayarpatti village, Sivaganga district of Tamil Nadu. Its earliest datable layer is a seventh-century cave temple cut around 650 CE and attributed to the ruler Narasimhavarma; an inscription beside the main image calls it Desi vinayakar, while a more archaic inscription sharing features of Tamil Brahmi and early Vatteluttu script suggests parts of the site may be a few centuries older still. The six-foot bas-relief of Ganesha in the sanctum shows unusual early iconography: he has only two arms, his trunk curves to the right, giving him the local name Valampuri Vinayagar, and his left tusk is broken. The walls carry further inscriptions from the 1000s to the 1200s, and five-metal statues of the eleventh century were uncovered during restoration in the late 1800s. The temple is one of the nine ancestral shrines of the Nagarathar merchant community, whose tradition dates its ties with the place to 714 CE. Later centuries added the coloured gopuram, painted mandapams and temple tank, and the annual Brahmothsavam chariot festival and Vinayaka Chaturthi still draw large crowds of pilgrims.
zh: 羯波迦‑频那夜迦神庙又称皮莱亚尔帕蒂·皮莱亚尔神庙，是一座凿岩而成的石窟神庙，供奉伽内什，坐落在泰米尔纳德邦西瓦甘加县的皮莱亚尔帕蒂村。现存最早、可断代的部分是约650年凿成的7世纪石窟，相传由统治者纳拉辛哈瓦尔摩主持；主像旁的铭文称其为“德西·毗那夜迦”，另有一则更古的铭文兼具泰米尔婆罗米文与早期瓦泰卢图文的特征，说明遗址部分建筑可能还要早几个世纪。殿内六英尺高的伽内什浮雕呈现罕见的早期造像特征：只有双臂，象鼻向右卷曲，当地人因而称其为瓦兰普里·毗那夜迦，左牙则已折断。庙墙还保留着11至13世纪的铭文，19世纪末重修时又出土了11世纪的五金合金造像。这座神庙是纳加拉塔尔商人群体的九大祖庙之一，该群体与神庙的渊源按其传统可追溯到714年。后世又陆续增建了彩色瞿布罗高塔、绘有壁画的厅堂和庙池；每逢一年一度的婆罗摩节神车游行与伽内什节，都有大批香客前来。

en: Kashima Shrine is a Shintō shrine in Hitachi Province, east of the Kantō plain, dedicated to Takemikazuchi, a kami of thunder, war and the martial arts. Its cult dates to at least the seventh century, when a ritual hall was rebuilt in 649 on ground where the local kami was believed to have descended. The Nakatomi clan, ancestors of the Fujiwara, made it a base for extending Yamato rule over the east and for campaigns against the Emishi, and its treasury long kept a bucket said to be a trophy taken from the Emishi leader Aterui. The Engishiki ranks it as the ichinomiya, or first shrine, of Hitachi, and by the Heian period it stood with Ise and Katori among the highest shrines in the land. Minamoto no Yoritomo endowed it with estates, and the early Tokugawa shōguns rebuilt its halls: Ieyasu in 1605, Hidetada in 1619, and the tower gate given by Yorifusa in 1634. In 1687 the poet Matsuo Bashō recorded a pilgrimage there in his travel journal Kashima Kikō.
zh: 鹿岛神宫是位于常陆国、关东平原以东的神道教神社，祭祀雷神、战神与武术守护神建御雷神。其信仰至少可追溯到7世纪：据《常陆风土记》记载，649年当地在传为神明天降之处重建了祭殿。中臣氏即藤原氏的前身，以神社为据点扩张大和朝廷在东国的统治、征讨虾夷，社中宝藏长期保存着据称取自虾夷首领阿弖流为的桶。《延喜式》将它列为常陆国一宫；到平安时代，它与伊势神宫、香取神宫并列全国最高等级的神社。源赖朝向神社寄进大量庄园，德川幕府初期又由历代将军重建社殿：家康建于1605年，秀忠于1619年再建本社，赖房捐建的楼门成于1634年。1687年，诗人松尾芭蕉到此参拜，并在《鹿岛纪行》中记下这段旅程。

en: The sun temple at Katarmal, a village in the Kumaon hills above Almora, is one of the rare Surya shrines built in the medieval Himalayas. It was raised in the ninth century by Katarmalla, a king of the Katyuri dynasty that ruled Kumaon from the seventh to the eleventh century, whose masons bonded the stones with a mixture of lime and lentil paste. Around the main sanctuary of the sun god, worshipped here as Burhadita or Vraddhaditya, stand forty-four smaller temples, with further shrines to Shiva and Parvati and to Lakshmi-Narayana completing the complex. Its walls and carved wooden doors and panels carry the sculpture of the Katyuri school, blending north Indian plains traditions with local Himalayan forms. After the Katyuri collapse the region was reunited by the Chand dynasty, who moved their capital to Almora in 1563, and in 1791 Kumaon was absorbed by the expanding Kingdom of Nepal, leaving the old temple as a landmark of each successive rule.
zh: 迦吒罗末罗太阳神庙坐落在阿尔莫拉上方库马翁山区的同名村庄，是中世纪喜马拉雅山区少见的苏利耶神庙之一。它由9世纪统治库马翁的迦吒里王朝国王迦吒罗末罗兴建——该王朝在7至11世纪统辖库马翁，当时的工匠用石灰与豆糊混合成黏合剂砌石。主殿供奉被称为布里哈迪塔或弗利达迪蒂亚的太阳神，周围环绕四十四座小庙，整个建筑群还包括湿婆与帕尔瓦蒂、吉祥天女与那罗延的神龛。庙墙与雕花木门、木板上留有迦吒里流派的雕刻，融合了北印度平原传统与当地喜马拉雅风格。迦吒里王朝衰落后，昌德王朝重新统一该地区，并于1563年迁都阿尔莫拉；1791年库马翁被扩张中的尼泊尔王国兼并，这座古老神庙也成为历代政权治下的地标。

en: The Katas Raj complex rises in the Salt Range of the Pothwar plateau, near Chakwal in northern Punjab, its shrines and walkways gathered around a sacred pond held to be fed by the tears Shiva shed when Sati died. The name comes from the Sanskrit kataksha, tearful eyes, and Persian writers called the spring Chashm-e-Alam; Hindus also connect the site with the forests where the Pandavas passed their exile in the Mahabharata. A temple here was already described by the Chinese pilgrim Faxian in the 4th century, and Xuanzang in the 7th century saw a towering Buddhist stupa attributed to the age of Ashoka. The surviving Hindu temples were raised from the late 6th century onward under the Shahi kings of Gandhara and the Odi Shahi dynasty: the oldest shrine, Temple B, belongs to the late 500s, while the principal Temple A of the Satghara group was built in the 900s in Gandhara Nagara style, with trefoil arches, fluted pillars and pointed rooflines recalling the temples of Kashmir. Around the pond stand further medieval Shiva, Rama and Hanuman shrines, and later Sikh rulers added a fort and haveli, tradition saying Guru Nanak himself once visited. Ranjit Singh came on pilgrimage three times, in 1806, 1818 and 1824, and the Maha Shivaratri fair long made Katas Raj one of the great Hindu gathering places of the western Punjab.
zh: 迦多娑罗阇神庙群坐落在北旁遮普波托哈尔高原的盐岭之中，殿堂与步道环绕着一方圣池；相传萨蒂死后湿婆流下的眼泪汇聚成池，其名来自梵语“迦多刹”，意为含泪的双眼，波斯作家称之为“阿兰之泉”。印度教徒还把此地与《摩诃婆罗多》中般度五子流亡时所在的森林联系起来。4世纪中国求法僧法显已记述过这里的一座神庙，7世纪玄奘到访时，还见过一座传为阿育王时代的高大佛塔。现存印度教神庙由犍陀罗的夏希诸王与奥迪夏希王朝自6世纪末起陆续兴建：最古的“B庙”可溯至500年代末，萨塔伽拉组中的主庙“A庙”则建于900年代，采用犍陀罗那伽罗风格，三叶拱门、凹槽柱与尖顶轮廓令人联想到克什米尔神庙。池畔还分布着中世纪的湿婆、罗摩与哈奴曼诸祠，后来的锡克统治者增建了堡垒与宅邸，相传古鲁·那纳克也曾亲临。兰吉特·辛格先后于1806、1818和1824年三次前来朝觐，大湿婆夜节的庙会长期使迦多娑罗阇成为西旁遮普最重要的印度教聚地之一。

en: Katori Shrine is the ichinomiya of Shimōsa Province and the head of some four hundred branch shrines, dedicated to Futsunushi, a kami of swords and lightning who served as a general of Amaterasu. Its worship predates written records: the early eighth-century Hitachi Fudoki already knew the shrine, whose guardians the Ō clan had migrated from Kyushu, subdued local Emishi and allied with the Nakatomi of neighbouring Kashima. As a tutelary of the Fujiwara it supplied the second deity of Kasuga Taisha when that shrine was founded in Nara, and the Engishiki of 927 names it a myōjin taisha, one of only three shrines styled Jingū alongside Ise and Kashima. Minamoto no Yoritomo and Ashikaga Takauji were among its samurai patrons, while its estates drew income from fishing rights and toll barriers. The Tokugawa shogunate rebuilt the shrine in 1607 and again in 1700, the latter rebuild giving the precinct the shape it kept into the nineteenth century.
zh: 香取神宫是下总国一宫，也是全国约四百座香取神社的总本社，祭祀剑与雷之神、天照大神麾下武将经津主神。其信仰早于文字记载：8世纪初的《常陆风土记》已提到这座神社，世代奉祀的多氏从九州迁徙而来，征服当地虾夷，并与邻近鹿岛的中臣氏结盟。作为藤原氏的守护神社，奈良春日大社创建时从这里分灵，供奉经津主神为第二祭神。927年的《延喜式》将它列为名神大社，是与伊势神宫、鹿岛神宫并列、仅有的三座称“神宫”的神社。源赖朝、足利尊氏等武家先后寄进，神社还凭借渔业权和关卡关税获得收入。德川幕府于1607年、1700年两次重建社殿，1700年的重建奠定了此后社域的格局。

en: The Kattu Narasimhaperumal Temple, also called the Azhagiya Singar temple, stands in Srirangam, the temple island in the Kaveri river dominated by the great Ranganathaswamy shrine. Its presiding god is Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu, known here as Varaprasadhi, the granter of boons, and the temple is traditionally named Ekaanthanthaman Koil for its quiet, secluded setting. Although not praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabhandam and therefore not counted among the 108 Divya Desams, it is ranked among the foremost Abhimana Sthalams, the additional temples especially dear to Vishnu. An inscriptional tradition attributes its construction in the ninth century to the Pandyan king Vallabadevan, a devotee of the saint Periyalvar, while local legend claims the shrine is older than the Ranganathaswamy temple itself, with some dating it to the fifth century. In the twelfth century the Vaishnava teacher Pillai Lokachariar delivered his discourses on the secrets of the Sri Vaishnava doctrine here, and in the fifteenth century Manavala Mamunigal took charge of the temple's administration at the request of the Pandyan ruler Srisindarapandian, who provided for its upkeep.
zh: 卡图那罗辛哈佩鲁马尔神庙又称阿扎吉亚·辛加尔神庙，坐落在高韦里河中的神庙之岛斯里兰加姆，与宏伟的兰加纳塔斯瓦米神庙相邻。庙中主神是毗湿奴的人狮化身那罗辛哈，名号瓦拉普拉萨迪，意为赐福者；寺庙因环境幽静独处，传统上又被称作埃坎坦塔曼庙。它未被《四千圣诵》称颂，因而不属于108座毗湿奴圣地迪维亚·德萨姆，却被列为最重要的阿比马纳斯塔拉姆之一，即毗湿奴格外眷顾的附加圣地。据铭文传统，神庙是9世纪时虔敬圣徒佩里亚尔瓦尔的潘地亚国王瓦拉巴提婆所建；而当地传说称这座神龛比兰加纳塔斯瓦米神庙还要古老，有人将其年代上推至5世纪。12世纪，毗湿奴派导师皮莱洛卡查里亚尔曾在此宣讲室利毗湿奴派教义的秘要；15世纪，大师马纳瓦拉·马穆尼加尔应潘地亚统治者斯里辛达拉潘地亚之请接管庙务，国王则出资供养神庙。

en: Kesariyaji Tirth, better known as the Rishabhdeo temple, lies in the hills of Mewar in southern Rajasthan on the old trade road running from the seaports of Gujarat into the interior, a position that drew generous merchant patronage from its earliest years. The temple was raised in 874 during the reign of the Mewar ruler Rawal Khuyan, and an inscription of 1422 records the repairs and enlargements carried out through the 1300s and 1400s. Its holiest object is a black stone image, little more than a metre tall, of the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha, called Kesariyaji from the legend of a devotee who offered saffron, kesar, equal to the weight of his son in thanksgiving; the idol is credited with miraculous power and is honoured not only by Digambara and Svetambara Jains but also by Vaishnava Hindus, whose four-armed Vishnu stands in the circumambulatory passage together with images of Shiva and Parshvanatha. The domed main shrine is fronted by a richly carved torana and ringed by fifty-two domed subsidiary shrines, and the marble replica idols of Kesariyaji commissioned by pious merchants carried the cult of this image into Svetambara temples across western India. From the fourteenth century onward the three communities contended for control of the temple through the favour of the Mewar rulers, and in 1654 a statue of Marudevi, Rishabhanatha's mother, seated on an elephant was added before the sanctum, while the nearby Pagliyaji shrine preserves the master's footprints.
zh: 吉娑哩耶圣所通称勒舍婆提婆神庙，坐落于拉贾斯坦南部梅瓦尔的丘陵中，正处在从古吉拉特沿海港口通往内陆的古商道上，这一位置使它从早年起便得到商人的慷慨供养。神庙于874年梅瓦尔君主拉瓦尔·库扬在位时兴建，1422年的一通铭文记载了14至15世纪间的历次修缮与扩建。寺中最神圣的是一尊三尺多高的黑石第一代祖师勒舍婆那陀像，通称吉娑哩耶——得名于一位信徒如愿得子后、献上与儿子等重藏红花（kesar）谢神的传说；此像被视为具有神力，不仅天衣派与白衣派耆那教徒尊崇，毗湿奴派印度教徒也前来礼拜，绕行通道中便立有四臂毗湿奴与湿婆、巴湿伐那陀的造像。穹顶主殿前立着雕工繁丽的陀兰那门，四周环列五十二座穹顶配殿；虔诚商人订制的吉娑哩耶大理石复刻像更把这尊神像的信仰带到了西印度各地的白衣派寺庙。从14世纪起，三派信众便借梅瓦尔统治者的恩宠争夺神庙的管理权；1654年，神殿前方又增设了勒舍婆那陀之母摩卢提毗乘象的造像，附近的帕格利亚吉伞亭则供奉着祖师的足印。

en: The Kichakeshwari Temple stands at Khiching in northern Odisha, the ancient capital of the Bhanja rulers, and honours Kichakeshwari, a form of Chamunda or Kali who was the family goddess of the Bhanja dynasty and the state deity of the Mayurbhanj chiefs. The original shrine was raised in the 700s, built entirely of black chlorite in the Kalinga style contemporary with the great Brahmeshwara and Lingaraja temples of Bhubaneswar; its hundred-foot rekha tower rises on a high platform behind walls densely carved with guardian figures, serpent maidens, Ganesha and scrollwork, though vandalism left it in ruins for long periods. The sanctum holds a fearsome ten-armed skeletal image of Chamunda-Kali with sunken belly and protruding ribs, wearing a garland of skulls and seated on a corpse, and the compound also preserves an early brick shrine called the Itamundhi.
zh: 吉遮鸡湿伐梨神庙位于奥里萨北部的基青，这里曾是班阇统治者的古都。神庙供奉吉遮鸡湿伐梨，即旃蒙达（迦梨）的一种化身，她是班阇王朝的家族守护神，也是马乌尔班杰首领的国家女神。原庙建于8世纪，通体以黑绿泥石筑成，属羯陵伽风格，与布巴内斯瓦尔的梵天自在神庙和林迦罗阇神庙同期；百尺高的雷塔式圣塔立于高台之上，外壁满刻护法、蛇女、象头神与卷草纹饰，但神庙曾遭破坏，长期沦为废墟。圣所中是一尊可怖的十臂枯骨形旃蒙达—迦梨像：腹部凹陷、肋骨外露，颈挂骷髅花环，坐于一具尸身之上；庙院内还保留着一座名为伊塔蒙迪的早期砖殿。

en: The Kodandarama Temple of the Belur country survives at Hiremagalur, near Chikkamagaluru in the Malnad hills, the old Hoysala heartland a short distance from Belur. Kodandarama means Rama bearing his bow, the kodanda, and the sanctum holds Rama with Sita on his right and Lakshmana on his left, posed as a wedding scene called Kalyana-rama; an image of Hanuman shares their pedestal even though the moment shown precedes Rama's first meeting with the monkey hero. It is thought to be the oldest continuously used Rama temple in India and grew in stages, the sanctum and idol following Ganga or Chola forms, the navaranga hall added in the 1300s and the entrance hall in the 1500s, with Hoysala and Dravidian work throughout. Local tradition says Rama here humbled the proud Parashurama, who then asked to witness the wedding scene, and the village was called Bhargavapuri, the town of Bhargava, where nine siddhas once practised penance. Its subsidiary shrines honour Yoganarasimha, Sugriva, Ramanujacharya and Madhvacharya, and a one-day temple yatra is held each February or March.
zh: 拘檀陀‑罗摩神庙现存于贝卢鲁附近马尔纳德丘陵中的希雷马加卢尔，地近奇克马加卢尔，与贝卢鲁同属曷萨罗故地。“拘檀陀罗摩”意为持弓的罗摩：圣所中罗摩居中，悉多立于其右、罗什曼那立于其左，呈婚礼场景，称“吉祥罗摩”；哈奴曼像同处一座台基，尽管所表现的时刻尚在罗摩与这位猴神初遇之前。它被认为是印度仍在持续使用的最古老罗摩神庙，建造历经数个阶段：圣所与神像为西恒伽或朱罗风格，14世纪增建聚会厅，16世纪又加前门厅，整体融合曷萨拉与达罗毗荼工艺。当地圣地传说称，罗摩曾在此折服骄傲的持斧罗摩，持斧罗摩遂请求一见婚礼景象；该村古称波尔加瓦普里，意为“婆罗伽瓦之城”，传说曾有九位悉达仙人在此苦修。配殿供奉瑜伽那罗辛哈、须羯哩婆、罗摩奴阇和摩陀婆阿阇梨等，每年二三月间还会举行为期一天的游神朝圣。

en: The Kola Valvill Ramar Temple stands at Tiruvelliyangudi, about nineteen kilometres from Kumbakonam in the Kaveri delta of the Tamil country, the region the game calls Cola Nadu. Vishnu is worshipped here in a reclining form as Kola Valvill Ramar, with Lakshmi as Maragathavalli, and the shrine is counted among the 108 Divya Desams, the holy places praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham of the Alvar saints between the sixth and ninth centuries. Built in the Dravidian style, it is enclosed by granite walls around its brick shrines and two temple tanks, and entered through a multi-tiered gopuram. Legend says Vishnu appeared here to the sage Markandeya, and the place is linked to his dwarf avatar: when the demon preceptor Sukracharya took the shape of an insect to block King Bali's ritual gift of land, Vishnu blinded him with a spear point, and Sukracharya did penance here to recover his eye, his lamp of light still honoured as the Nethra Deepam. The sage Parasara is also said to have worshipped here, and tradition credits the divine architect Mayan with raising the temple in imitation of Vaikuntha on the Kaveri's banks.
zh: 拘缡伐鼻利‑罗秣神庙坐落于泰米尔地区高韦里河三角洲的蒂鲁韦利扬古迪，在贡伯戈讷姆以东约十九公里处，古时属乔拉纳德地区。庙中毗湿奴以侧卧的拘缡伐鼻利·罗秣之相受人敬拜，其配偶吉祥天女名为玛拉伽塔瓦利；它是毗湿奴派一百零八座圣庙之一，6至9世纪阿尔瓦尔圣徒的《四千圣诗》曾加以赞颂。神庙为达罗毗荼风格，砖砌神龛与两处圣池外绕花岗岩围墙，入口是多层瞿布罗门楼。传说毗湿奴曾在此向摩根德耶仙人显圣，此地又与他的侏儒化身有关：阿修罗之师苏揭罗化作虫豸堵塞水壶，阻挠巴利王行献地之礼，毗湿奴以矛尖刺瞎其目，苏揭罗在此苦行复明，他所点燃的明灯仍被尊为“眼灯”。相传仙人波罗娑罗也曾在此礼拜，而神匠摩延仿照天界毗恭吒，在高韦里河畔建起了这座神庙。

en:
The Konark Sun Temple is a vast thirteenth-century shrine of Surya on the Odisha coast, about thirty-five kilometres north-east of Puri. King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, who reigned from 1238 to 1264, built it around 1250 on the site of an older sun temple, whose image was re-consecrated within the new building. Conceived as Surya's colossal chariot, the stone complex carries twenty-four carved wheels nearly four metres across and is drawn by seven galloping horses, the twelve pairs of wheels matching the twelve months of the Hindu calendar. Rising perhaps sixty-nine metres in its prime, it was the summit of Kalinga architecture, its walls covered in divine figures and erotic mithuna reliefs; its name joins the Sanskrit words kona, angle, and arka, the sun.

An inscription of 1384 and the Akbar-era Ain-i-Akbari both describe a complete, flourishing temple, but the great sanctuary tower collapsed in the late 1500s; Kalapahar, a general of the Bengal sultanate, is believed to have sacked Konark around 1568. European sailors called the ruin the Black Pagoda, a Bay of Bengal landmark recorded as early as 1676 beside Puri's White Pagoda. In the last quarter of the 1700s Maratha rulers moved the Aruna pillar from its entrance to the Lion's Gate of the Jagannath temple in Puri, after which the site lay deserted in coastal forest until the East India Company took Odisha in 1803 and began its conservation. The annual Chandrabhaga Mela kept pilgrims coming through the centuries of decay.
zh:
科纳克太阳神庙是奥里萨海岸一座规模宏大的13世纪苏利耶神庙，位于补梨东北约三十五公里处。东恒伽王朝的那罗辛诃·提婆一世（1238—1264年在位）于约1250年在一座更古老太阳神庙的旧址上建成此庙，旧庙神像被重新开光后迎入新殿。整座石构建筑群被设计成苏利耶的巨型战车：二十四只直径近四米的精雕车轮、七匹奔腾的石马牵引战车，十二对车轮对应印度教历的十二个月。神庙盛时高约六十九米，是羯陵伽建筑艺术的巅峰，墙上布满神像与男女欢爱的米图纳浮雕。庙名由梵语“科纳”（角）与“阿尔迦”（太阳）二字合成。

1384年的一方铭文和阿克巴时代的《阿克巴则例》都还记载着一座完整兴盛的神庙，但宏伟的主殿高塔在16世纪末倒塌；一般认为，孟加拉苏丹国将领卡拉帕哈尔约在1568年洗劫了科纳克。欧洲水手把这片废墟称作“黑塔”，早在1676年的记载中它已是孟加拉湾上的航标，与补梨的“白塔”遥遥相对。18世纪最后二十五年，马拉塔统治者把庙门口的阿楼那石柱迁到补梨札格纳特神庙的狮门之前，此后遗址便荒废在沿海丛林中；直到1803年英国东印度公司取得奥里萨，保护工作才开始。一年一度的旃陀罗跋伽庙会则让香客们在庙宇残破的数百年间仍持续前来朝拜太阳神。

en: Koneswaram crowns Konesar Malai, the rocky promontory of Trincomalee on the east coast of Sri Lanka, and is the foremost of the island's five Pancha Ishwaram Shiva shrines, honoured as the Dakshina Kailasam, the Kailash of the south, and famed as the temple of a thousand pillars. Its name goes back to the Sanskrit Gokarnesvara, and Tamil tradition places it among the Paadal Petra Sthalams sung by the Tevaram poets, while the Ramayana links the cape to the demon king Ravana. Pallava craftsmen built its thousand-pillared hall between 537 and 668, and Pallava, Pandya and Chola dynasties all lavished gifts on the shrine, which entered its greatest age under the Cholas and the Sinhalese king Gajabahu II, its benefactor from 1131 to 1153; black granite bas-reliefs, gilded gopurams and tenth-century bronze images of Shiva, Parvati and Ganesha made it the marvel of the island. The end came with the Portuguese, who between 1622 and 1624 sacked the complex, threw its images into the sea and built Fort Fredrick from its stones on the summit. Some of the surviving idols were transferred in 1632 to a new temple inland, where they are still worshipped, while a single pillar of the old kovil remained standing on Swami Rock above the bay, and the annual Ther chariot festival kept the name of Koneswaram alive among the Tamils of the east coast.
zh: 亭可马里寺雄踞斯里兰卡东海岸亭可马里的科内萨尔山角，是岛上五大湿婆圣庙“潘查伊湿婆罗”中地位最高的一座，被尊为“南凯拉斯”，又以千柱庙之名著称。其名可追溯至梵语“戈卡尔纳湿婆罗”，泰米尔传统将它列为提婆罗摩圣诗所咏的帕达尔佩特拉圣地之一，《罗摩衍那》则把这处海角与魔王罗波那联系在一起。537年至668年间，帕拉瓦工匠建起千柱大厅，此后帕拉瓦、潘地亚与朱罗三朝竞相施舍，神庙在朱罗时代和僧伽罗国王迦阇巴忽二世（1131—1153年在位）的护持下进入鼎盛：黑色花岗岩浮雕、鎏金瞿布罗门楼与10世纪的湿婆、帕尔瓦蒂、伽内什铜像，使它成为全岛最壮丽的建筑。1622年至1624年，葡萄牙人洗劫庙群，将神像投入大海，并在山顶用庙石修建了弗雷德里克堡。部分幸存神像于1632年迁至内陆的新庙供奉，旧庙仅余一根石柱立在海湾上方的斯瓦米岩上；一年一度的神车节则让科内斯瓦拉姆之名在东海岸泰米尔人中代代相传。

en: The Kothandaramaswamy Temple stands at Dhanushkodi, the southernmost tip of Pamban Island, about thirteen kilometres from Rameswaram between the Bay of Bengal and the Gulf of Mannar, in the country once ruled by the Pandya kings. Dedicated to Rama, it takes its name from his bow, the kothandam held by the main idol, which is grouped with images of Lakshmana, Sita, Hanuman and Vibhishana, and the shrine is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Vaishnava tradition. Tradition identifies this shore as the place where Vibhishana, the younger brother of Ravana, fled from Lanka and surrendered to Rama after his warning to return Sita was rejected; Rama welcomed him despite the suspicions of his vanara army and, after Ravana's fall, crowned him king of Lanka here, a story painted across the shrine's inner walls. Probably raised between the tenth and fifteenth centuries, the temple shared the island's fortunes: Malik Kafur's forces raided Rameswaram in 1311, the island passed to Vijayanagara in 1520, and the Sethupati rajas of Ramanathapuram later patronised its pilgrim shrines.
zh: 拘旦陀‑罗摩斯瓦米神庙位于班本岛最南端的达那斯科迪，在拉梅斯沃勒姆以南约十三公里，扼孟加拉湾与马纳尔湾之间，古时属潘地亚诸王的国土。庙奉罗摩，得名于主神手中所持的弓“拘旦陀”，神像与罗什曼那、悉多、哈奴曼和维毗沙那并列；它位列毗湿奴派一百零八座阿比摩纳圣地之一。相传这片海岸正是维毗沙那投奔罗摩之处：罗波那的幼弟维毗沙那劝兄归还悉多未果，逃离楞伽前来归降，猴军虽疑其为奸细，罗摩仍听从哈奴曼之言接纳了他；罗波那败亡后，罗摩又在此为维毗沙那举行楞伽王位的灌顶礼，这段故事绘在神庙内壁之上。神庙约建于10至15世纪，与海岛共历沧桑：1311年马利克·卡富尔的军队洗劫拉梅斯沃勒姆，1520年海岛转入毗奢耶那伽罗治下，后来拉马纳塔普拉姆的塞图帕蒂王公又资助了岛上的朝圣神庙。

en: The Kutubiyya is the largest mosque of Marrakesh, standing in the southwestern medina near the Jemaa el-Fnaa square. Its name, the Booksellers' Mosque, comes from the book vendors who once crowded the souk at its walls, at times around a hundred strong. It was founded in 1147 by the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min immediately after he took Marrakesh from the Almoravids, whose mosques he condemned as wrongly oriented and demolished; he rebuilt the mosque entirely around 1158, and the seventy-seven-metre minaret, decorated with geometric arch motifs and crowned by a spire of copper orbs, was probably finished under Ya'qub al-Mansur around 1195. Abd al-Mu'min also moved here the Almoravid minbar commissioned in 1137 by Ali ibn Yusuf from a Cordoba workshop, a masterpiece of Islamic woodwork fitted with a mechanism that made it glide forward for prayers. As the defining monument of Almohad architecture, the Kutubiyya supplied the model for the Giralda of Seville and the Hassan Tower of Rabat. After neglect in the seventeenth century, it was restored in the eighteenth, when the ruins of its first incarnation were left abandoned beside it.
zh: 库图比亚清真寺是马拉喀什规模最大的清真寺，坐落在老城西南、杰马夫纳广场附近。它的名字意为“书商清真寺”，得名于曾云集在寺墙下集市里的书商，最盛时多达上百人。1147年，穆瓦希德王朝哈里发阿卜杜勒·慕敏从穆拉比特王朝手中夺取马拉喀什后随即修建此寺；他宣称前朝清真寺的礼拜方向有误而将其拆毁，并于1158年前后全面重建，高77米、装饰着几何拱纹、顶端冠以铜球尖顶的宣礼塔，约在1195年雅各布·曼苏尔在位时完工。阿卜杜勒·慕敏还把穆拉比特王朝的敏拜尔讲经坛移到这里：它是阿里·伊本·优素福于1137年委托科尔多瓦工匠制作的伊斯兰木雕杰作，配有机械装置，礼拜时能自行滑出。作为穆瓦希德建筑的典范，库图比亚为塞维利亚的吉拉达钟楼和拉巴特的哈桑塔提供了蓝本。17世纪它一度荒废，18世纪得到修缮，而最早一版清真寺的废墟则被弃置在旁。

en: The Krishna Janmasthan at Mathura marks the prison cell where Hindu tradition says Krishna was born to Devaki and Vasudeva, held captive by his uncle Kamsa, the king of Mathura; his great-grandson Vajranabh is credited with the first shrine on the spot. Excavations have yielded pottery and terracotta from the sixth century BCE, and the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II rebuilt a grand temple there around 400, while a late-eighth-century inscription records Rashtrakuta donations. Mahmud of Ghazni plundered Mathura in 1017 and burned its temples, and an inscription of 1150 records a new white Vishnu temple raised by one Jajja. Sikandar Lodi of Delhi destroyed the Mathura shrines early in the sixteenth century, yet the saints Chaitanya and Vallabhacharya still came to worship at the birthplace. In 1618 Raja Vir Singh Deo of Orchha built a lavish octagonal Keshavdeva temple in red sandstone, described by the French traveller Tavernier in 1650 and patronised by the Mughal prince Dara Shikoh. Aurangzeb had it demolished in 1670 and raised the Shahi Eidgah mosque on its foundations, after which Mathura passed to British control in 1804.
zh: 奎师那诞生地位于马图拉，相传奎师那正是在这里的一间囚室中降生：他的父母提婆吉和婆苏提婆被舅父、马图拉国王刚沙囚禁，相传奎师那的曾孙瓦吉拉纳巴最先在此立庙。考古发掘出土了公元前6世纪的陶器与赤陶器物；约400年，笈多皇帝旃陀罗笈多二世在此重建了宏伟的神庙，8世纪末的一块铭文还记下了罗湿陀罗拘陀人的捐献。1017年，加兹尼的马哈茂德劫掠马图拉、焚毁诸庙；1150年的铭文记载，一个名叫贾贾的人又建起一座洁白的毗湿奴神庙。16世纪初，德里苏丹锡坎达尔·洛迪捣毁马图拉的神庙，但柴坦尼亚和伐拉巴阇利耶等圣人仍来诞生地朝拜。1618年，奥尔切土王维尔·辛格·德夫耗资建起一座红砂岩筑成的八角形凯舍瓦提婆神庙，法国旅行家塔韦尼耶1650年曾记述其形制，莫卧儿王子达拉·舒科也对它加以庇护。1670年，奥朗则布下令拆毁神庙，在原址上修建皇家会礼清真寺；1804年，马图拉转入英国控制之下。

en: The Kukkuteswara Temple stands in the ancient town of Pithapuram in Andhra, known to the Gupta emperor Samudragupta's pillar inscription of about 350 as Pishtapura and later the first capital of the Eastern Chalukyas before they moved to Vengi. Dedicated to Shiva in the form of Kukkuteswara, the Lord of the Rooster, it houses a self-manifested crystal linga and a famous Nandi carved from a single stone, while its enclosure also contains the shrine of Puruhutika Devi, counted among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, so that the complex is revered in both the Saivite and the Shakta traditions. The Skanda Purana already praises Pithapuram as a holy place, and in the fourteenth century it was the birthplace of the saint Sripada Sri Vallabha. After the rule of the Velanati Chodas and the local Pitapuram Chalukyas in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, the town passed under the Reddi kings and later Muslim rulers, while the temple remained a goal of pilgrimage, its grand festivals drawing crowds for Maha Shivaratri and Navaratri.
zh: 库库特斯瓦拉神庙位于安得拉古城毗多补罗；约350年笈多皇帝沙摩陀罗·笈多的石柱铭文已称此地为毗什多补罗，后来它还是东遮娄其王朝迁都文吉之前的首个都城。神庙供奉以雄鸡形象显现的湿婆库库特斯瓦拉，内有自生水晶林伽和著名的整石雕成的难迪牛；庙院之中还有普鲁胡胡提卡女神殿，位列十八处大性力佩特，因此该建筑群同时受到湿婆派和性力派尊崇。《塞建陀往世书》早已称美毗多补罗为圣地，14世纪的圣人室利波陀·室利·瓦拉巴也诞生于此。12至13世纪，此地先后由韦拉那提·朱罗和本地的毗多补罗遮娄其统治，其后归入雷迪国王与穆斯林政权，而神庙始终是朝圣目标，湿婆夜和九夜节的盛大庆典吸引大批信众。

en: Kulpakji, also called the Kolanupaka Temple, is a Svetambara Jain temple at Kolanupaka in Telangana, not far from Bhongir. Jain tradition traces the site back roughly two millennia and credits the legendary king Bharata Chakravartin with its founding, while the surviving temple took shape from the ninth century, when the Kalachuri ruler Shankaragana granted twelve villages for its upkeep. It flourished as a Jain centre under the Rashtrakutas and Western Chalukyas: a Kannada inscription of the Chalukya king Someshvara III dated 1125 records its teachers and monasteries, and more than twenty Jain inscriptions mark it as a seat of the Kanur Gana branch of the Mula Sangha. The temple enshrines images of Rishabhanatha, Neminatha and Mahavira, the last a green-stone figure famed as Manikyaswami, which the fourteenth-century monk Jinaprabhasuri celebrated in his pilgrimage work Vividha Tirtha Kalpa.
zh: 屈禄波耆寺又称科拉努帕卡寺，是特伦甘纳邦科拉努帕卡村的一座白衣派耆那教寺庙，距邦吉尔不远。耆那教传统将该地上溯约两千年，相传为传说中的婆罗多转轮王所建；现存庙宇则成形于9世纪，当时迦罗珠利君主商羯罗伽纳曾拨赐十二座村庄供养。罗湿陀罗拘陀与西遮娄其时期，这里发展为耆那教重镇：1125年西遮娄其国王索梅什瓦拉三世的一方卡纳达语碑铭记载了当地的导师与寺院，现存的二十余方耆那教碑铭还表明它是根本僧团迦努尔伽纳支派的中心。寺内供奉勒舍婆那陀、尼弥那陀和大雄三尊祖师像，其中大雄像以绿石雕成，号称“摩尼格湿瓦米”；14世纪僧人金波罗婆苏利在其朝圣著作《诸圣地纪》中曾专门记述此像。

en: The Kumano Sanzan are the three great shrines hidden in the mountains of the Kii peninsula, Hongū, Hayatama and Nachi, whose kami were worshipped together as the Kumano Gongen, buddhas and native gods fused into one saving faith. The Nihon Shoki already records nature worship there, and the mountain streams and the great Nachi waterfall drew hermits of Shugendō long before the courts of Kyoto took notice. The first imperial pilgrimage was made by Emperor Uda in 908, and over the next 374 years emperors and retired emperors came ninety-four times; the retired Emperor Shirakawa made nine journeys from 1090 and Go-Shirakawa thirty-three, drawing the whole nobility behind them. Pilgrims followed the Kumano Kodō trails, resting at the ninety-nine Oji shrines built between the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, seeking healing and rebirth in this world and the next. In the Muromachi period the flow of samurai and peasants became so constant it was called the ant pilgrimage, and under the Tokugawa it joined the Ise pilgrimage as one of the great mass devotions of Edo Japan, while more than three thousand branch Kumano shrines carried the cult across the country.
zh: 熊野三山是深藏纪伊半岛山中的三座大社——熊野本宫大社、熊野速玉大社与熊野那智大社，三地神祇合称熊野权现，是佛教诸佛与日本本土神灵融为一体的救度信仰。《日本书纪》已记载当地的自然崇拜，那智瀑布与山间溪谷早在京都朝廷瞩目之前就吸引着修验道的隐士。908年，宇多天皇开启了首次天皇熊野参拜；此后374年间，天皇与上皇共巡幸94次，其中白河上皇自1090年起九度前来，后白河上皇更到访33次，带动整个贵族阶层争相随行。朝圣者沿熊野古道跋涉，在12至13世纪修建的九十九座王子社沿途歇脚，祈求身心疗愈与来世解脱。室町时代，武士和平民的参拜队伍连绵不绝，被称为“蚂蚁的熊野参拜”；到德川治下，它与伊势参拜并列为江户日本最盛大的群众性信仰活动，三千余座熊野分社也把这一信仰播撒到全国。

en: The Kurma Varadaraja Swamy Temple is an ancient Vishnu shrine at Kurmai near Palamaner in present-day Andhra Pradesh, where the god is worshipped in his tortoise avatar Kurma as Varadarajaswamy; it is one of only five Kurma temples in India, and local tradition credits the Pallava kings with its foundation and a local chief, Chenge Gowda, with its rebuilding.
zh: 拘利摩‑伐罗陀罗阇斯瓦米神庙是一座古老的毗湿奴神庙，位于今印度安得拉邦帕拉马内尔附近的拘利摩村，供奉以龟化身俱利摩显现、号为伐罗陀罗阇斯瓦米的毗湿奴，是全印仅有的五座俱利摩神庙之一；当地传说它由帕拉瓦诸王始建，后经地方首领琴盖·高达重建。

en: The Kurmanathaswamy Temple at Srikurmam, on the Kalinga coast of present-day Andhra Pradesh, is dedicated to Kurma, the tortoise avatar of Vishnu, and is the only known Indian temple built before the fourteenth century for that form of the god. It originally stood as a Shiva shrine, but in 1113 the Eastern Ganga king Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva converted it into a Vaishnava temple, an event recorded in its earliest inscriptions; its walls and processional corridor were raised in a fusion of Kalinga and Dravidian styles, with later additions by King Anangabhima Deva III. The sanctum houses both a tortoise image and an anthropomorphic Vishnu with Lakshmi, while 108 single-stone pillars carved with inscriptions surround the complex. Alongside Simhachalam, Srikurmam became a leading centre of Vaishnavism in medieval Kalinga and the guru-pitha of the Ganga kings of Utkala; Naraharitirtha, a disciple of Madhvacharya, later made it a seat of Madhwa religious activity and defended it against raids from the forest-dwelling Sabaras. Its worship still blends Shaivite and Vaishnavite traditions.
zh: 俱利摩神庙位于今印度安得拉邦境内羯陵伽海岸的斯里俱利摩村，供奉毗湿奴的龟化身俱利摩，是已知唯一一座在14世纪以前为这一化身修建的印度神庙。它最初是湿婆神庙，1113年东恒伽王朝国王阿南塔跋摩·朱达恒伽提婆将其改为毗湿奴派神庙，此事见于庙中最早的铭文；庙墙和绕行廊以羯陵伽与达罗毗荼混合风格建成，阿南加比马·提婆三世时期又有增建。圣所中同时供奉龟形神像以及与吉祥天女相伴的人形毗湿奴像，整座建筑由108根互不雷同的独石柱环绕，柱上刻满铭文。中世纪时，斯里俱利摩与辛哈查拉姆并称羯陵伽最重要的毗湿奴派中心，也是乌特伽罗恒伽诸王的祖师道场；摩陀婆阿阇梨的弟子那罗哈利提尔塔后来把它建成摩陀婆派的活动中心，并抵御了森林土著萨巴拉人的袭击。庙中礼拜仍兼有湿婆派与毗湿奴派的传统。

en: The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the Monastery of the Caves, overlooks the Dnipro from the Berestov hills in Kyiv. In 1051 Anthony, a monk of Mount Athos born at Liubech, settled in a cave there as a missionary of monastic life, and a community of disciples grew around him; Prince Iziaslav I gave the whole hill to the monks, who built their monastery with architects from Constantinople. It became the foremost religious and cultural centre of Kyivan Rus, whose monks wrote the Primary Chronicle and the Kyiv Caves Patericon, but its wealth drew repeated attacks: the Cumans plundered it in 1096, Andrey Bogolyubsky sacked it in 1169, Batu Khan's Mongols stormed it in 1240, and Tatar raids of 1416 and 1482 burned it to the ground. Rebuilt each time, it won stauropegion rights directly under the Patriarch of Constantinople in the later sixteenth century and took the title of lavra. After the Union of Brest it was contested between Orthodox and Catholics until the Ostrogski family secured it for Orthodoxy in 1613; under archimandrites such as Peter Mohyla its printing house, opened in the 1620s, and its school made Kyiv a centre of Orthodox learning.
zh: 基辅洞窟修道院坐落于基辅俯瞰第聂伯河的别列斯托夫山丘。1051年，出身柳别奇、曾在阿索斯山修行的修士安东尼作为修道传统的传播者回到罗斯，在山中洞穴定居，身边很快聚集起一批弟子；伊贾斯拉夫一世将整座山丘赐给修士，修道院由来自君士坦丁堡的建筑师修建。它成为基辅罗斯最重要的宗教与文化中心，修士们在此撰写《往年纪事》和《基辅洞窟修士传》，但财富也引来反复攻掠：1096年库曼人劫掠，1169年安德烈·博戈柳布斯基洗劫，1240年拔都的蒙古军攻陷，1416年和1482年又两度被鞑靼人焚毁。修道院屡毁屡建，16世纪下半叶获得君士坦丁堡牧首授予的直属特权，改称“拉夫拉”（大修道院）。布列斯特联合后，它在东正教徒与天主教徒之间几经争夺，1613年经奥斯特罗格斯基家族支持才确保留在东正教会手中；17世纪，在修道院长彼得·莫希拉等人主持下，1620年代开办的印刷所和修道院学校使基辅成为东正教的学术中心。

en: Kykkos Monastery, the Holy Royal and Stauropegial Monastery of the Virgin, stands high on the north-western face of the Troodos Mountains in Cyprus and is the island's richest Orthodox house. It was founded at the end of the eleventh century under Emperor Alexios I Komnenos, after the hermit Esaias, according to tradition, persuaded the Byzantine governor Manuel Boutoumites to fetch from Constantinople an icon of the Virgin held to have been painted by the Apostle Luke, and the emperor's daughter was healed as the icon sailed to Cyprus. The icon has been veiled ever since, its upper half hidden behind a covering said to blind anyone who looks upon it, and the Pope and Patriarch of Alexandria Gerasimos was the last man recorded to have seen it, in 1669. Fire destroyed the church three times, so nothing remains of the original buildings, and the present church dates from 1745. In 1760 Cypriots credited the veiled icon with delivering the island from a plague of locusts, while pilgrims such as the Ukrainian Vasyl Barsky, who visited in 1735, carried its fame across the Orthodox world.
zh: 基科斯修道院全称“圣母神圣皇家直属修道院”，高踞塞浦路斯特罗多斯山脉西北坡，是岛上最富有的东正教修道院。它建于11世纪末阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁皇帝在位时：相传隐修士以赛亚说服拜占庭总督曼努埃尔·布图米特斯，从君士坦丁堡请来相传为使徒路加亲手所绘的圣母圣像，圣像运往塞浦路斯途中，皇帝之女的病也因此痊愈。这尊圣像一直被遮盖，上半部藏在罩幕之后，传说窥视者会失明；有记载最后见过它的人是1669年的亚历山大教皇兼牧首格拉西莫斯。教堂历史上三次毁于火灾，原建筑已无存，现存教堂建于1745年。1760年，塞浦路斯人相信是这尊蒙面圣像使全岛躲过蝗灾；1735年到访的乌克兰朝圣者瓦西里·巴尔斯基等人，则把它的名声传遍了东正教世界。

en: The Lakshmi Narasimha Temple stands at the foot of Mangalagiri, the Auspicious Hill, in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh, and is counted among the eight great Narasimha shrines of India. It is the lowest of three Narasimha temples on the hill, the others standing on its slope and summit. Tradition holds that the Pandava Yudhishthira discovered the shrine, and its story is said to be told in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana. The Vijayanagara kings were its patrons: Krishnadevaraya visited in the sixteenth century, and a pillar inscription dated 1520 records grants of villages, while another of 1538 dates from the reign of Sadasiva Raya. After long rule by the Golconda Nawabs, the town survived a raid by Hyder Jung in 1780 and Pindari looting in 1816. The temple's landmark, an eleven-storeyed gopuram 153 feet high, was raised in 1807 to 1809 by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu of Amaravati.
zh: 拉克什米‑那罗辛哈神庙坐落在安得拉邦贡土尔县曼加拉吉里，意为吉祥山的山脚下，被列为印度八大那罗辛哈神庙之一。山上共有三座那罗辛哈神庙，它位于山脚，另外两座分别在山坡和山顶。相传神龛是般度族长子坚战发现的，其事迹载于《梵天往世书》。毗奢耶那伽罗诸王是神庙的施主：克里希纳德瓦拉亚于16世纪亲临此地，一根1520年的石柱铭文记录了村庄的施赠，另一处1538年的铭文则属于萨达希瓦·拉亚在位时期。在戈尔孔达纳瓦布长期统治之后，此地又熬过了1780年海德尔·忠格的袭击和1816年平达里匪帮的劫掠。神庙的标志——高153英尺、共十一层的戈普拉姆门楼，是阿马拉瓦蒂的王公瓦西雷迪·文卡塔德里·奈杜在1807至1809年间修建的。

en: The Lakshmi Temple is a small shrine in the Western Group at Khajuraho, the temple city raised by the Chandela dynasty in central India, and forms part of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments. It was built around 930 to 950, in the great age of Chandela construction, but its name is a misnomer: it began as the Garuda shrine of the neighbouring Lakshmana Temple, for the bird mount of Vishnu is traditionally housed in a small pavilion directly facing his master's sanctum, just as Nandi faces the linga in Shiva temples. The modest square plan, plain side walls and tiny sanctum are typical of such a vahana shrine, whose main image showed Garuda seated with Vishnu. In later centuries the doorway carvings were defaced and the statues beheaded, and a damaged image of the goddess Brahmani was placed inside, which devotees then took to worshipping as Lakshmi. It stands north of the Varaha Temple and directly faces the eastern entrance of the Lakshmana Temple.
zh: 吉祥天女神庙是中印度昌德拉王朝所建神庙之城克久拉霍西庙群中的一座小殿，属于克久拉霍古迹群的一部分。它约建于930至950年昌德拉营造的鼎盛期，但名字其实是后世误称：它最初是相邻拉克什曼纳神庙的迦楼罗神龛——按照传统，毗湿奴的坐骑迦楼罗要安奉在正对主神圣殿的小亭里，正如湿婆庙中神牛南迪正对林伽。朴素的方形台基、素面无饰的侧墙和狭小的圣室，都是这类坐骑神龛的典型形制，龛中主像原是与毗湿奴同坐的迦楼罗。后来门楣雕刻被毁、神像遭砍头，一尊破损的婆罗诃弥女神像被移入殿中，信众便把她当作吉祥天女礼拜。此庙位于筏罗诃神庙北侧，正对着拉克什曼纳神庙的东门。

en: The Lakshminarasimha Temple at Haranhalli, in the Karnataka country not far from the Hoysala capital of Dvarasamudra, is a triple-shrine Vishnu temple in the Vesara style of Hoysala architecture. It and the nearby Someshvara Temple, dedicated to Shiva, were completed in the 1230s at the expense of three wealthy brothers, Peddanna Heggade, Sovanna and Kesanna. Inscriptions show that the temple was first named after Keshava, a form of Vishnu, and only later took its present name of Lakshminarasimha. Its three sanctums hold images of Venugopala, Keshava and Lakshminarasimha, and the building blends features of the late Chalukya and early Hoysala manners: a moulded platform serving as a circumambulation path, a single soaring tower over the central shrine, and walls lined with Vaishnava reliefs and miniature decorative towers.
zh: 哈兰哈利的拉克什米那罗辛哈神庙位于迦尔纳卡萨拉地区，距曷萨拉都城德瓦拉萨穆德拉不远，是一座采用曷萨拉维萨拉风格修建的三圣所毗湿奴神庙。它与附近供奉湿婆的索梅什瓦拉神庙一样，都是13世纪30年代由佩达纳·赫加德、索万纳和凯萨纳三兄弟出资建成的。铭文显示，神庙最初以毗湿奴的化身凯沙瓦命名，后来才改用今名拉克什米那罗辛哈。三间圣所中分别供奉维努戈帕拉、凯沙瓦和拉克什米那罗辛哈像；建筑融合了遮娄其晚期与曷萨拉早期的特征：模筑台基兼作绕行通道，中央圣所上耸立独塔，墙面布满毗湿奴教浮雕和微型装饰塔。

en: Llullaillaco is a dormant stratovolcano of six thousand seven hundred and twenty-three metres in the Puna de Atacama, overlooking the driest desert of the Andes above Antofagasta; its Quechua name joins llulla, false or deceitful, and yaku, water, because the snowmelt on its slopes vanishes into the dry earth instead of feeding streams. The high peaks were apus, sacred ancestors and wak'as in Inca religion, and between 1470 and 1532 the Inca Empire occupied this far southern frontier and made the summit a stage for the capacocha rite. Children chosen from communities across the empire, perfect in body and often of noble birth, were brought to Cusco and then led along straight ceque pilgrimage routes to the mountain, prepared for months with coca leaves and chicha and buried in a chamber near the summit as offerings to the apu, entering the spirit world to intercede for harvests, weather and the cohesion of the empire. A capacocha performed here between the 1460s and the early 1500s took three children, whose bodies the freezing, rainless peak preserved along with their finery, making Llullaillaco one of the highest and most awe-inspiring sanctuaries of the Inca world.
zh: 尤耶亚科山是阿塔卡马高原上一座休眠的层状火山，海拔6723米，俯瞰安第斯山脉最干旱的沙漠，雄踞安托法加斯塔之上。其克丘亚语名由 llulla（虚假、欺瞒）与 yaku（水）组成，因为山坡上的融水渗入干涸的土地，并不汇成溪流。在印加宗教中，高峰是阿普——神圣的祖先与圣所；1470年至1532年间，印加帝国占据了这条遥远的南部边地，并把山顶作为卡帕科查祭祀的舞台。帝国各社群选出身体完美、常出身贵族的孩童，先带往库斯科，再沿笔直的塞克朝圣路线登上高山；他们经数月准备，服食古柯叶、饮用奇恰酒，最后被安放在近峰顶的墓室中献祭给阿普，进入神灵世界为丰收、天时与帝国的凝聚祈福。15世纪60年代至16世纪初，这里举行的一场卡帕科查献祭了三名孩童；寒冷无雨的峰顶将他们的遗体与华服一同保存下来，使尤耶亚科山成为印加世界海拔最高、也最令人敬畏的圣所之一。

en: The Maa Dewri Temple lies in the forested Ranchi uplands of Jharkhand, in Diuri village near Tamar, where the local Munda and Bhumij tribes had long worshipped the goddess in a sacred grove, or Sarna, known as Dewri Diri, the sacred stone of Diuri. Tradition dates the stone temple to about 1300, when Kera, a Munda king of Singhbhum, is said to have prayed here after losing a battle and, having regained his kingdom with the goddess's blessing, raised a shrine of interlocking stones without mortar and installed the three-foot, sixteen-armed image of Maa Dewri that remains the chief object of veneration. When the raja of neighbouring Tamar adopted her worship he brought a Brahmin priest with him, giving the temple its distinctive custom of six days of ritual led by the tribal Pahan and one day by a Brahmin Panda, while tribal drums accompany the puja. Devotees tie red and yellow threads on bamboo for the fulfilment of vows, returning to untie them when their prayers are answered.
zh: 提乌梨神庙位于贾坎德兰契丘陵林地中、塔马尔附近的迪乌里村；当地蒙达和布米吉部落早先是在一处名为提乌梨·迪里的圣林（萨尔纳）中敬拜这位女神，意为迪乌里的圣石。相传约1300年，辛格布姆的蒙达国王凯拉战败后在此祈祷，蒙女神庇佑而复国，遂不用灰浆、以石块交错咬合砌成石庙，并供奉高三英尺、十六臂的提乌梨女神像，作为庙中受祀的主神。邻近塔马尔的王公后来也皈依女神，随行带来婆罗门祭司，由此形成独特制度：一周六天由部落祭司帕汉主持仪轨，一天由婆罗门潘达主持，祭祀时还以部落鼓乐伴奏。信众在竹架上系上红黄丝线许愿，愿望达成后再回来解开丝线。

en: The Mahadev Temple at Deobaloda, near Durg in the Chhattisgarh country, is a sandstone Shiva shrine raised in the 1200s under the Kalachuris of Ratnapura, the Haihaya dynasty that ruled the old Dakshina Kosala region from their capital at Ratanpur. Local legend holds that it was completed in only six months, giving it the nickname six-month temple. Facing east, the building pairs a square garbhagriha sanctum with a pillared Navaranga hall, though its Nagara-style spire has not survived; the sanctum keeps a lingam about one and a half feet high behind an ornate doorway guarded by Shaiva door-keepers, with Parvati, Ganesha and Hanuman images around it. Its pillars and walls are carved with Bhairava, Vishnu, Durga slaying Mahishasura, and the fierce Tripurantaka and Gajantaka forms of Shiva, alongside musicians, dancers and scenes of hunting and bull-fighting, while a stone Nandi keeps watch before the entrance. Beside the temple lies a stepped kund of twenty-three steps, said in folk tale to hide a tunnel running as far as the ancient temple town of Arang. The shrine remained a living place of pilgrimage under the later Haihaya rajas, whose kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Marathas of Nagpur in 1740, and villagers from the surrounding country still gather there for the fair of Maha Shivaratri.
zh: 这座大天神庙位于杜尔格附近的德奥巴罗达，地处恰蒂斯加尔地区，是1200年代拉特纳普拉卡拉楚里王朝——以拉坦普尔为都、统治古达克希纳拘萨罗之地的海诃耶王朝——治下兴建的砂岩湿婆神庙。当地相传它仅用六个月便告竣工，因而得了“六月庙”的别称。神庙朝东，方形密室与柱厅那瓦朗伽相配，可惜那伽罗式塔尖已不存；密室中供着一尊约一英尺半高的林伽，华丽的庙门由湿婆教守门神守护，周围立有帕尔瓦蒂、象头神伽内什与哈奴曼像。柱间与墙面上雕刻着婆罗婆、毗湿奴、斩杀摩希修罗的杜尔迦，以及湿婆威猛的三城毁灭者与象魔毁灭者形象，还伴有乐师、舞者、狩猎和斗牛的场景；一尊石牛南迪在门前守望。庙旁是一座二十三级的圣池，民间传说池底藏着一条直通古城阿兰格的隧道。在后来的海诃耶罗阇治下，此庙始终是活跃的朝圣场所——该王国于1740年接受那格浦尔马拉塔人的宗主权——周围乡村的百姓每逢大湿婆夜节仍会聚集于此，赶庙赴会。

en: Mahakaleshwar is a Shiva temple in the ancient city of Ujjain, on the Shipra river in Malwa, and one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, the holiest abodes of Shiva. Ujjain, anciently called Avantika, was the capital of the Avanti kingdom, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, and remains one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism, where the Simhastha Kumbh Mela is held every twelve years. The lingam is held to be swayambhu, self-manifested rather than ritually installed, and the presiding image faces south as Dakshinamurti, a feature unique among the Jyotirlingas; the shrine is also counted among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, where Sati's upper lip is said to have fallen. The temple was destroyed during Iltutmish's raid on Ujjain in 1234 and 1235, when the lingam was dismantled and thrown into a neighbouring pond, and it was later attacked by the Khalji sultans Jalaluddin and Alauddin. It was rebuilt in the eighteenth century under Maratha rule by the diwan Ramachandra Sukthankar. A great fair gathers here for Maha Shivaratri, with worship lasting through the night.
zh: 摩诃迦丽湿伐罗神庙是供奉湿婆的印度教神庙，为十二处究提林迦——湿婆最神圣的居所——之一，坐落在摩腊婆希普拉河畔的古城乌贾因。乌贾因古称阿般提迦，曾是十六大国之一阿般提国的都城，也是印度教七圣城之一，每十二年举办一次僧伽斯塔壶节。庙中的林伽相传为自生显现，而非经仪式安立；主神作南面相的达克希纳穆尔蒂之形，这在十二处究提林迦中独一无二。此庙也被列为十八处大性力派圣地之一，相传萨蒂的上唇便坠落于此。1234—1235年伊勒杜迷失劫掠乌贾因时神庙被毁，林伽被拆投入邻近的池塘，其后又遭卡尔吉王朝苏丹贾拉尔乌德丁与阿拉乌德丁攻击；18世纪马拉塔统治时期，迪万罗摩旃陀罗·苏克坦卡尔将其重建。每逢大湿婆夜节，庙旁都有大型庙会，信众通宵祭拜。

en: The Mahalakshmi Temple, also called the Ambabai Mandir, is the great shrine of Kolhapur in southern Maharashtra, dedicated to Mahalakshmi, the consort of Vishnu, and counted in the Shakta tradition among the three and a half principal Shakti Peethas. Local legend tells that the goddess appeared here to slay the demon Kolhasur, whose dying wish gave the city its name, and the ancient town was known as Karvir, earning the title Dakshin Kashi, the Kashi of the South. The temple is said to have been built in 634 by the Chalukya king Karnadeva. The historian Paul Dundas, following the twelfth-century Kannada poet Brahmashiva, argues that it began as a Jain temple of the tirthankara Chandraprabha and was converted to Hindu worship amid medieval religious tensions, which fits the many Jain foundations left in Kolhapur by the Shilahara dynasty that ruled the region from about 940 to 1212. Its black-stone image of the crowned goddess, barely a metre tall, stands before a stone lion with a Shri Yantra carved on the wall behind. In 1707 the Maratha queen Tarabai made Kolhapur the capital of her own state, and the temple remained the spiritual centre of the kingdom.
zh: 大吉祥天女神庙又称安巴巴伊庙，是南马哈拉施特拉戈尔哈布尔的大庙，供奉毗湿奴的神妃大吉祥天女，在性力派传统中被列为三处半主要性力圣地之一。相传女神曾在此诛杀恶魔迦罗修罗，魔王临终请求以自己的名字命名此地，戈尔哈布尔因而得名；古城古称迦尔维尔，号称“南方迦尸”。一般认为此庙由遮娄其国王卡尔纳提婆建于634年。史学家保罗·邓达斯依据12世纪卡纳达诗人婆罗门湿婆的记载提出，它最初是供奉耆那教祖师旃陀罗波罗跋的耆那庙，在中世纪的宗教纷争中改为印度教神庙；这与940至1212年统治该地的尸拉哈拉王朝在戈尔哈布尔留下的大量耆那教遗迹正相吻合。庙中黑石女神像头戴宝冠、高不足1米，身前置石狮，背后墙壁刻有室利坛城。1707年，马拉塔女王塔拉巴伊以戈尔哈布尔为自己国家的都城，这座神庙始终是王国的精神中心。

en: The Mahavinayak Temple is one of the oldest Ganesha shrines in Odisha, standing at Chandikhole in Jajpur district, and its most striking feature is that five gods, Ganesha, Shiva, Vishnu, Durga and Surya, are worshipped together as a single deity inside one sanctum. It was raised in the 1100s under the Keshari, or Somavamshi, kings of Odisha. A legend explains the fivefold cult: when Rati, wife of the love god Kamadeva, prayed here for her husband's release from Shiva's curse, five hands reached out at once for her offering, and Brahma told her the five gods had accepted it together; a great granite stone then rose from the earth, holding their combined power. Local tradition also claims this is where Ganesha's severed head fell, and links the Baruna hill beside the temple with the Pandava king Yudhishthira, whose palace ruins are said to face the shrine.
zh: 大毗那夜迦神庙是奥里萨最古老的伽内什神庙之一，坐落在贾贾普尔县的昌迪科尔；它最独特之处，是在同一间圣室中将伽内什、湿婆、毗湿奴、杜尔迦和苏利耶五位神祇当作一位合体之神供奉。神庙于12世纪由奥里萨的凯沙里（索马瓦姆希）王朝诸王修建。当地传说解释了这种五神合一的信仰：爱神伽摩之妻拉提在此祈祷，求湿婆解除对丈夫的诅咒，献祭时同时伸出五只手来接她的供品，梵天告诉她五位神祇一同受了她的供奉；随后一块巨大的花岗岩从地中涌出，蕴含着五神的合力。当地还相传伽内什被砍落的头颅便坠落于此，神庙旁的巴鲁纳山又与般度族国王坚战有关，据说他宫殿的遗迹正对着神庙。

en: The Mallikarjuna Temple crowns the hills of Srisailam, above the Krishna river in the Deccan, and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, who is worshipped here as Mallikarjuna beside his consort Bhramaramba, a form of Parvati. Its name comes from the Telugu word mallika, jasmine, with which the lingam is said to have been adorned. Unusually, the same complex is also counted among the fifty-two Shakta Pithas and the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, where Sati's neck is believed to have fallen, and it is one of the Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the Tamil Shaiva canon. Inscriptions show a shrine here under the Satavahanas in the 2nd century, and the innermost sanctum is dated to the 7th century. The Reddi kings of the 13th and 14th centuries, devoted patrons of Bhramaramba and Mallikarjuna, added the Veerashero mandapa and cut the long Pathala Ganga stairway of more than eight hundred steps down to the Krishna, whose water is used to bathe the lingam. Most of the present halls and four gopuram gateways were built under the Vijayanagara emperors, beginning with Harihara I, who reigned from 1336 to 1355. Enclosed by walls nearly nine metres high, the temple also holds a thousand-linga shrine and a mirror hall graced by an image of dancing Nataraja, drawing pilgrims who combine worship here with a dip in the river far below.
zh: 末利迦阿周那神庙雄踞德干高原室利势罗的山巅，下临克里希纳河，是湿婆十二处究提林迦之一；湿婆在此以“末利迦阿周那”之名受奉，身旁是其配偶、帕尔瓦蒂的化身婆罗摩兰巴。庙名来自泰卢固语“末利迦”，即茉莉花，相传林伽曾以茉莉花装点。与众不同的是，同一座庙也被列入五十二处性力派圣地与十八处大性力派圣地，相传萨蒂的颈部坠落于此；它还是泰米尔湿婆圣典所赞美的帕达尔佩特拉圣地之一。铭文显示，2世纪百乘王朝时期这里已有神祠，最内殿则可追溯至7世纪。13至14世纪的雷迪诸王是婆罗摩兰巴与末利迦阿周那的虔诚信众，增建了维拉谢罗殿堂，并凿出八百余级的帕塔拉恒河石阶，直通山下的克里希纳河，河水用来为林伽沐浴。现存的主要殿堂和四座瞿布罗门楼大多由维查耶纳伽罗帝国皇帝修建，始于1336年至1355年在位的开国皇帝诃利诃罗一世。庙围高墙近九米，内有千林伽殿和饰有舞王纳塔罗阇像的镜厅，朝圣者在此礼佛之余，还会下到深谷中的河水里沐浴。

en: The Martand Sun Temple is a ruined Hindu shrine dedicated to Surya, called Martanda in Sanskrit, raised on a plateau above the Kashmir Valley near Anantnag. The chronicler Kalhana records that it was commissioned in the eighth century by Lalitaditya Muktapida, the most powerful king of the Karkota dynasty. Its colonnaded courtyard, roughly two hundred and twenty feet long and ringed by eighty-four smaller shrines around a central sanctuary that probably carried a pyramidal roof, made it the largest peristyle temple in Kashmir; its carvings blended Gandharan and Gupta forms with influences from as far as China and the Byzantine world. The sanctuary stood for some six centuries until the reign of Sikandar Shah Miri, from 1389 to 1413, when the temple was pulled down in the course of his campaign to bring the valley's Brahmanical institutions under state control. Earthquakes later shook what remained, leaving the broken colonnade that still commands a view over the whole valley.
zh: 马坦德太阳神庙是供奉太阳神苏利耶（梵语称马坦达）的印度教神庙遗址，坐落在克什米尔山谷阿嫩德纳格附近的一处高原上。史家卡尔哈纳记载，神庙由卡尔科塔王朝最强盛的国王拉利塔迪蒂亚·穆克塔皮达在8世纪敕建。它的柱廊院长约二百二十英尺，中央主殿周围环绕八十四座小神龛，主殿屋顶可能为金字塔形，是克什米尔规模最大的绕柱式神庙；殿中雕刻融合了犍陀罗、笈多乃至来自中国和拜占庭世界的风格。神庙屹立约六个世纪，直到1389—1413年西坎达尔·沙·米里在位期间，在他将山谷内婆罗门教机构纳入国家控制的行动中被拆毁。此后地震又进一步损毁了残存建筑，只剩下断裂的柱廊，仍可俯瞰整个山谷。

en: The Matsya Narayana Temple on the Omkar Hills in southern Bangalore is the only Karnataka shrine dedicated to Vishnu's fish avatar Matsya, first of his ten incarnations. As told from the Shatapatha Brahmana onward, Matsya guides Manu's ship through the great deluge and slays the demon Hayagriva to recover stolen Vedas, his icon joining Vishnu's four-armed torso to fish's body.
zh: 摩蹉那罗延神庙位于班加罗尔南部的奥姆卡尔山，是卡纳塔克邦唯一供奉毗湿奴鱼化身摩蹉的神庙，摩蹉为毗湿奴十大化身之首。从《百道梵书》起流传的神话说，摩蹉引导摩奴之舟渡过灭世大洪水，又诛杀恶魔诃耶羯哩婆夺回被盗的吠陀，造像为四臂毗湿奴上身接鱼身。

en: Mayapan, whose name means the standard of the Maya people, was the walled capital of the Yucatan Maya in the Late Postclassic, standing forty kilometres southeast of Merida with more than four thousand buildings and perhaps 17,000 people inside its ramparts. After the revolt against Chichen Itza in 1221, the regional lords, led by the general Hunac Ceel, built the new city and gave the throne to the Cocom family, who ruled through a council of nobles for more than two hundred years, keeping rival lords' kinsmen as hostages and hiring Mexican mercenaries from Tabasco. Its principal sanctuary was the Temple of Kukulcan, a four-sided, nine-terraced pyramid modelled on the Castillo of Chichen Itza and set beside the Cenote Ch'en Mul, with serpent balustrades; three unusual round temples honoured the Feathered Serpent in his wind-god aspect, while Xiu-lineage shrines bore masks of the rain god Chaac. In 1441 Ah Xiu Xupan of the rival Xiu family rose against the Cocom and slaughtered nearly the whole lineage; the capital was sacked and burned, its ceremonial centre left charred and its plazas holding mass graves of sacrificial dead. By about 1461 the city was empty, Yucatan had split into warring city-states, and the ruins entered memory chiefly through the account Friar Diego de Landa wrote down in the following century.
zh: 玛雅潘在玛雅语中意为“玛雅人的旗帜”，是后古典期晚期尤卡坦玛雅人的有城墙都城，位于梅里达东南40公里，城墙内有4000多座建筑，人口或达1.7万。1221年反抗奇琴伊察的起义之后，各地领主在将领胡纳克·塞尔主持下兴建这座新都，把王位交给科科姆家族；此后两百多年间，科科姆家族通过贵族议事会统治，把敌对领主的亲属留作人质，并从塔瓦斯科雇佣墨西哥佣兵。城中首要圣所是库库尔坎神庙，这座四面九级的金字塔仿照奇琴伊察的卡斯蒂略金字塔而建，矗立在琴穆尔天然井旁，栏杆雕满羽蛇；三座罕见的圆形神庙供奉风神面貌的羽蛇神，休家族的神龛则饰有雨神恰克的面具。1441年，敌对的休家族的阿·休·苏潘起兵反抗科科姆家族，几乎将其满门屠灭；都城遭洗劫焚毁，礼仪中心化为焦土，广场上留下埋满殉葬者的乱葬坑。到1461年前后城市已空无一人，尤卡坦分裂为互相攻战的城邦，这片废墟主要靠修士迭戈·德·兰达在下一个世纪写下的记述留存于记忆之中。

en: The Meenakshi Temple stands on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, dedicated to Meenakshi, the fish-eyed form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar, a form of Shiva. Madurai is described as a temple town in the Sangam literature of the early centuries, and a shrine there is praised in the Tevaram hymns of the Nayanar saints, numbering it among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The oldest surviving masonry was raised under the Pandya king Sadayavarman Kulasekaran I around 1190 to 1216 and enlarged by his successors, who added several gopurams. In 1311 the Khalji general Malik Kafur sacked Madurai, destroyed the temple and carried its treasure to Delhi; under the ensuing Madurai Sultanate the idols were hidden and the complex lay abandoned for some sixty years. The Vijayanagara prince Kumara Kampana reconquered the city in 1378, rebuilt the walls and reconsecrated the images, and his Nayak governors kept expanding the shrine through the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Under the Madurai Nayaks, above all Vishwanatha Nayak, it took its present form of concentric enclosures with fourteen gopurams, a thousand-pillared hall and the golden lotus pond.
zh: 鱼目女神庙坐落于马杜赖的韦盖河南岸，供奉鱼目的米纳克希，即帕尔瓦蒂的化身，以及她的配偶、湿婆化身孙达雷什瓦拉。早在纪元最初几个世纪的桑伽姆文献中，马杜赖就被描绘成一座神庙之城；那衍纳尔圣徒的《特瓦拉姆》赞歌也颂唱此地的神殿，使它跻身“赞歌之境”圣庙之列。现存最早的石构建筑由潘地亚国王萨达亚瓦尔曼·库拉塞卡兰一世在1190至1216年间修建，后继诸王又增建了多座塔门。1311年，卡尔吉王朝将领马利克·卡富尔劫掠马杜赖，摧毁神庙并把财宝运往德里；随后的马杜赖苏丹国时期，神像被藏起，庙群荒废约六十年。1378年，毗奢耶那伽罗王子库马拉·坎帕纳收复此城，重建围墙并重新安奉神像；他麾下的纳亚克诸将在15、16世纪持续扩建。到马杜赖纳亚克王朝、尤其是维什瓦纳塔·纳亚克统治时，神庙形成了今天所见的层层围合格局，共有14座塔门、千柱厅和金莲池。

en: The Meteora are a forest of sandstone pillars rising from the Thessalian plain near Trikala, whose summits hold the greatest Orthodox monastic complex in Greece after Mount Athos. Hermit monks were living in cracks and caves of the rocks as early as the ninth century, gathering only on Sundays at a chapel below the Dupiani rock, and by the eleventh century they had formed the Skete of Stagoi. Permanent monasteries came only in the fourteenth century, as Turkish raids drove monks to the inaccessible pinnacles. In 1344 Athanasios the Meteorite arrived from Mount Athos, and between 1356 and 1372 he built the Great Meteoron on the Broad Rock under the protection of Simeon Uroš, the local ruler who styled himself emperor of Serbs and Greeks; Simeon's son John Uroš abdicated to die as a monk there in the 1420s. More than twenty houses were eventually founded, reachable only by jointed ladders and hauling ropes, said to be replaced only when they broke. Theophanes built the monastery of Varlaam in 1517, keeping the finger of Saint John and the shoulder blade of Saint Andrew, and twenty-four houses once crowned the rocks.
zh: 迈泰奥拉是色萨利平原特里卡拉附近拔地而起的一片砂岩巨柱群，柱顶建有希腊仅次于阿索斯山的东正教修道院群。早在9世纪，已有隐修士在岩石裂隙和洞穴中栖身，只在周日聚到杜皮亚尼岩下的小堂礼拜；11世纪时他们组成斯塔戈伊隐修区。14世纪土耳其人不断袭扰，修士们才在难以攀援的岩柱上修建常住修道院。1344年，“流星者”阿塔纳修斯从阿索斯山率众而来，1356—1372年在当地领主、自称塞尔维亚人与希腊人皇帝的西美昂·乌罗什庇护下，于宽岩上创建大迈泰奥拉修道院；西美昂之子约翰·乌罗什后来退位出家，15世纪20年代在该院去世。这里先后建起二十多座修道院，只能靠拼接的长梯和吊绳网篮上下，据说绳索“等主让它断了”才更换。1517年，狄奥法内斯修建瓦尔拉姆修道院，院内藏有圣约翰的手指和圣安德烈的肩胛骨；岩柱之上一度共有二十四座修道院。

en: Mile was a medieval church site in the Visoko basin in central Bosnia, at the present village of Arnautovići. It first appears in written sources in 1244 as the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian, and in 1340 the Bosnian ruler Stephen II Kotromanić built there the Franciscan friary of Saint Nicholas, the first of its order in Bosnia. The estate was also one of the meeting places of the Stanak, the assembly of Bosnian nobility, and served as the coronation and burial church of the kings of Bosnia: Stephen II, who died in 1353, arranged to be buried there, and Tvrtko I was crowned king at Mile in 1377 when the Banate of Bosnia became a kingdom. Archaeologists later identified Tvrtko's tomb in the church's north wall. When the Ottomans overran the Kingdom of Bosnia in 1463, the friary's role as the ceremonial heart of the Bosnian monarchy came to an end.
zh: 米列是波斯尼亚中部维索科盆地的中世纪教堂遗址，在今阿尔瑙托维奇村一带。它最早于1244年见诸文献，当时是圣科斯马斯与达米安教堂；1340年，波斯尼亚统治者斯特凡二世·科特罗马尼奇在此修建圣尼古拉方济各会修道院，这是该修会在波斯尼亚的第一座修道院。这里也是波斯尼亚贵族会议“斯坦纳克”的召开地之一，并成为波斯尼亚诸王的加冕与安葬教堂：1353年去世的斯特凡二世安排自己葬在此地，1377年特夫尔特科一世在米列加冕为王，波斯尼亚班国由此升级为王国。考古学家后来在教堂北墙找到了特夫尔特科的陵墓。1463年奥斯曼攻灭波斯尼亚王国，这座修道院作为波斯尼亚君主制礼仪中心的历史也随之终结。
