en: The Benedictine abbey of Santa Maria de Montserrat clings to the jagged serrated mountain of Catalonia, inland from Barcelona, and enshrines the Virgin of Montserrat, a late twelfth-century Romanesque wooden statue of the Madonna and Child known affectionately as La Moreneta, the little dark one, one of Europe's Black Madonnas. The mountain had been sacred long before Christianity, and tradition says the image was hidden there around 718 as Saracen armies invaded; a cult grew around its discovery, and Abbot Oliba of Ripoll founded the monastery on the site in 1025. Pilgrims of renown included Peter Nolasco around 1203, who went on to found the Mercedarian order, and Ignatius of Loyola, who on 25 March 1522 laid down his soldier's arms before the statue before founding the Society of Jesus. The abbey's press printed its first book in 1499. French troops sacked and burned the abbey in 1811 and 1812, and in 1835 it was closed in the wave of monastic confiscations, its monks dispersed and its buildings left to decay.
zh: 圣马利亚·德·蒙特塞拉特本笃会修道院依傍在加泰罗尼亚那座锯齿状的嶙峋怪山上，位于巴塞罗那内陆，院中的圣物是蒙特塞拉特圣母像：一尊12世纪末的罗马式木雕圣母子，民间亲切地称它为“拉·莫雷内塔”，即小黑女，是欧洲的黑圣母像之一。这座山在基督教传入之前就已是圣地，相传718年前后撒拉森人入侵时，圣像被转移藏匿于此；圣像被发现后信仰渐盛，里波尔的修道院长奥利瓦于1025年在此创建修道院。著名的朝圣者包括约1203年前来的佩德罗·诺拉斯科，他后来创立了梅塞德修会；还有依纳爵·罗耀拉，他于1522年3月25日在圣像前放下军人的兵器，此后创立了耶稣会。修道院的印刷所于1499年印出第一本书。1811至1812年，法国军队洗劫并焚毁了修道院；1835年，在没收修道院产业的浪潮中它被关闭，修士散去，建筑一度荒废。

en: The Mosque of Uqba, the Great Mosque of Kairouan in central Tunisia, was founded in 670 by the Arab conqueror Uqba ibn Nafi when he laid out the city itself, making it one of the oldest mosques in the Islamic world and the model for later Maghrebi mosque building. The first building was destroyed around 690 when Berbers under Kusaila took Kairouan, and the Ghassanid general Hasan ibn al-Nu'man rebuilt it in 703. The Umayyad governor Bishr ibn Safwan enlarged it between 724 and 728 and began the square minaret, still one of the oldest surviving in the Islamic world, and the Abbasid governor Yazid ibn Hatim reconstructed it again in 774. Its present form dates to the Aghlabid emirs: Ziyadat Allah I rebuilt the mosque in 836, giving it the hypostyle prayer hall, marble courtyard and early horseshoe arches that make it a landmark of Islamic architecture, with further enlargements under Ibrahim II in 875. Scholars teaching in its halls made Kairouan a leading centre of learning until the city's decline from the mid-eleventh century, when intellectual life shifted to the Zaytuna mosque in Tunis.
zh: 乌克巴大清真寺即凯鲁万大清真寺，位于突尼斯中部的凯鲁万。670年，阿拉伯征服者奥卡巴·伊本·纳菲在营建凯鲁万城的同时修建了这座清真寺，它是伊斯兰世界最古老的清真寺之一，也成为后世马格里布清真寺的范本。最初的建筑约在690年库塞拉率领柏柏尔人攻占凯鲁万时被毁，加桑尼德将领哈桑·伊本·努阿曼于703年将其重建。倭马亚王朝总督比什尔·伊本·塞夫万在724年至728年间加以扩建，并动工修建方形宣礼塔，它也是伊斯兰世界存世最古老的宣礼塔之一；774年，阿拔斯王朝总督叶齐德·伊本·哈提姆又一次重建。清真寺现存的面貌主要来自阿格拉布王朝的埃米尔们：齐亚达特·安拉一世于836年重建全寺，建成多柱式礼拜殿、大理石庭院和早期马蹄形拱门，使之成为伊斯兰建筑的里程碑，易卜拉欣二世又在875年继续扩建。在寺中讲学的学者曾使凯鲁万成为学术重镇，直到11世纪中叶该城衰落，学术生活逐渐让位于突尼斯的宰图纳大清真寺。

en: The shrine of Moulay Idris stands in the town of Moulay Idriss Zerhoun, spread over two hills below Mount Zerhoun near Meknes, overlooking the ruins of Roman Volubilis. It holds the tomb of Idris I, a descendant of Muhammad who fled Abbasid rule after the Battle of Fakh and in 789 forged an alliance with the Berber Awraba tribe at Oualili, the old Volubilis, founding the first Islamic state in Morocco. He died in 791, possibly poisoned at the caliph Harun al-Rashid's order, and was buried under a domed qubba; his posthumous son Idris II, who took power in 803, later built Fez. The shrine was long overshadowed by Fez, and the Almoravids frowned on its saint cult, but the Marinids revived the Idrisid legacy after the alleged rediscovery of Idris I's remains in 1318, when the annual August moussem took shape. The Alaouite sultan Moulay Ismail had the mausoleum rebuilt on a grand scale between 1719 and 1721 and established its mosque as the town's Friday mosque, and Sultan Abd al-Rahman enlarged it again in 1822.
zh: 扎尔洪的穆莱·伊德里斯圣陵坐落在梅克内斯附近、扎尔洪山脚下的同名小镇，城镇分布于两座小山之上，可俯瞰古罗马城市沃吕比利斯的废墟。陵中安葬着伊德里斯一世：他是穆罕默德的后裔，在法赫战役后逃离阿拔斯王朝的势力范围，于789年在古沃吕比利斯所在地瓦利利与柏柏尔人的奥乌拉巴部落结盟，建立了摩洛哥第一个伊斯兰政权。他于791年去世，相传是被哈里发哈伦·拉希德派人毒杀，死后葬在一座穹顶拱北之下；他的遗腹子伊德里斯二世于803年亲政，后来兴建了非斯。圣陵长期被非斯的光芒掩盖，穆拉比特王朝又敌视圣徒崇拜，直到马林王朝时期，对伊德里斯家族的尊崇才重新兴起：1318年相传重新发现了伊德里斯一世的遗骸，每年八月的穆塞姆宗教节庆也在此时成形。阿拉维王朝苏丹穆莱·伊斯梅尔在1719年至1721年间下令将圣陵拆毁重建，规模更为宏大，并把陵旁清真寺定为全镇的主麻清真寺；苏丹阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼又于1822年再度扩建。

en: Mount Athos, the rocky easternmost prong of the Chalkidiki peninsula in Macedonia, is the foremost monastic centre of Eastern Orthodoxy, known in Greek as the Holy Mountain. Christian hermits had settled its forests by the fourth century, and Athonite tradition holds that the Virgin Mary was blown ashore there and consecrated the mountain as her garden. Organised monasticism took shape in the ninth century, and in 963 Athanasius the Athonite, with the backing of Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, founded the Great Lavra, turning scattered hermitages into cenobitic monasteries. Byzantine emperors and the rulers of Georgia and the Slavic Orthodox kingdoms endowed further houses, Greek, Serbian, Bulgarian and Russian among them, and the community came under the direct jurisdiction of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. After the fall of Constantinople in 1453 the monasteries kept their rights under Ottoman rule, and in the nineteenth century donations from Russia, Serbia and Romania funded a monastic revival. By tradition and later by law, women are barred from entering the peninsula.
zh: 阿索斯山是马其顿哈尔基季基半岛最东端的岩石岬角，是东正教最重要的修道中心，希腊语称“圣山”。早在4世纪，基督教隐修士已在其山林中定居；阿索斯传统称圣母玛利亚曾被风浪吹到此处，将这座山祝圣为自己的园子。9世纪起形成有组织的修道生活，963年修士阿索斯的阿塔纳修斯在皇帝尼基弗鲁斯二世·福卡斯支持下创建大劳拉修道院，把零散的隐修茅屋改造为集体修道的大型修道院。此后拜占庭皇帝以及格鲁吉亚和斯拉夫诸正教王国的统治者又捐资兴建了希腊、塞尔维亚、保加利亚、俄罗斯等民族的修道院，整个修院共同体直属于君士坦丁堡普世牧首。1453年君士坦丁堡陷落后，各修道院在奥斯曼统治下保留了特权；19世纪，来自俄罗斯、塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的捐助推动了修道复兴。依照传统和后来的法律，女性不得进入这一地区。

en: Mount Emei rises 3,099 metres on the western rim of the Sichuan basin near Jiading, the highest of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains and the bodhimanda of Samantabhadra, the bodhisattva of universal virtue, known in Chinese as Puxian. Pious tradition places the first Buddhist temple in China on its slopes in the first century. Its oldest enduring foundation is Wannian Temple, established by the monk Huichi under the Eastern Jin as Puxian Temple; rebuilt in 876 by Huitong and renamed Baishui Temple, then restored in 980 by the Northern Song monk Maozhen, it acquired a seven-metre bronze image of Samantabhadra riding his white elephant, cast under the Northern Song. The poet Li Bai sojourned there in the Kaiyuan era of the eighth century, listening to the monk Guangjun play the qin. After a Wanli-era fire the Ming court rebuilt the temple from 1600, adding the timberless Brick Hall crowned with five small pagodas. Ming and Qing patronage ringed the mountain with seventy-six monasteries, from Baoguo Temple at its foot to the Golden Summit, Jinding, at 3,077 metres, joined by a pilgrim path fifty kilometres long.
zh: 峨眉山雄踞四川盆地西缘，邻近嘉定，海拔3099米，为中国四大佛教名山之最高者，是大行普贤菩萨的道场。相传1世纪时中国最早的佛寺即建于山中。现存最古老的开山祖庭是万年寺，东晋僧人慧持创建时原名普贤寺；876年慧通重建后改称白水寺，980年北宋僧人茂真重修时铸造了高约7米的普贤骑白象铜像。8世纪开元年间，诗人李白曾驻锡寺中，听僧人广浚弹琴赋诗。明代万历年间寺院遭火，朝廷于1600年起敕令重建，增建不用寸木的无梁砖殿，殿顶饰以五座小塔。明清两代的护持使山间梵刹达76座之多，从山麓的报国寺到海拔3077米的金顶华藏寺，由一条长达50公里的朝山小径串联起来。

en: Mount Fanjing, the highest peak of the Wuling range in Tongren, Guizhou, rises 2,570 metres above the remote borderlands of three counties. Its name shortens Fantian Jingtu, the Brahma Pure Land, and Chinese Buddhism holds it as the bodhimanda of Maitreya, the future Buddha. The Han histories knew it as the Three-Valley Peak; under the Tang it was called Mount Chen and a county was planted at its foot in 716, while Buddhism reached the mountain in the Song, when Xiyan Temple, one of Guizhou's earliest monasteries, was founded in 965. The early Ming made it a flourishing Buddhist centre, formally naming it Fanjing and covering its slopes with temples; after warfare among the local tusi chiefs, the court incorporated the region into the new province of Guizhou in 1413. The Bozhou rebellion of Yang Yinglong wrecked the shrines in 1599, and in 1618 the Wanli emperor charged the monk Miaoxuan with restoring the Gold Peak, creating the imperial main temple Cheng'en with four royal monasteries around it. After the Qing conquest the Kangxi reign re-invested the mountain and enlarged its network to forty-eight hermitages, drawing pilgrims from Sichuan, Huguang and Jiangnan; on the New Gold Peak twin halls of Sakyamuni and Maitreya crown the summit, and repairs of 1822 and 1832 renewed the old Maitreya sanctuary.
zh: 梵净山是贵州铜仁武陵山脉的主峰，海拔2570米，雄踞三县交界的边远之地。山名是“梵天净土”的简称，汉传佛教以之为未来佛弥勒菩萨的道场。汉代史籍称其为三山谷，唐代改名辰山，并于716年在山西麓设置思邛县；佛教在宋代传入，965年建成的西岩寺是贵州最早的寺院之一。明初这里佛教鼎盛，正式定名梵净山，寺刹遍布峰峦；当地土司争战之后，朝廷于1413年将这一带纳入新设的贵州省。1599年播州土司杨应龙之乱使梵刹残破，1618年明神宗委派高僧妙玄主持重建金顶，形成敕赐承恩寺这一皇家正殿与四大皇庵拱卫的格局。入清之后，康熙年间再次敕封，脚庵增至48座，四川、湖广、江浙的朝山者络绎于途。新金顶之巅并立释迦、弥勒二殿；1822年与1832年的两度重修，又使这处古道场重焕光彩。

en: Mount Fuji, the perfect snow-capped volcano between Suruga and Kai, is Japan's highest peak and one of its Three Holy Mountains. In Shintō belief it is the dwelling of Konohanasakuya-hime, the blossom princess married to the heavenly grandson Ninigi, and Sengen shrines were built at its foot, led by the Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha, to pacify the fire that so often erupted from its slopes. In early times the mountain was worshipped only from afar; when the eruptions quietened in the Heian period, Shugendō ascetics made it a centre of mountain religion, and the monk Matsudai Shōnin founded a temple on the summit in the early twelfth century. The volcano stirred for the last time in the Hōei eruption of 1707 to 1708, which buried the nearby villages in ash. The Edo period also saw the rise of Fuji-kō, the pilgrim movement founded by the ascetic Hasegawa Kakugyō, whose followers climbed the cone seeking rebirth and purification, turning Fuji into one of the great mass pilgrimages of the age; in the 1830s Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji carried its image across the country and beyond.
zh: 富士山雄踞骏河与甲斐之间，是一座轮廓完美的积雪火山，也是日本最高峰和三灵山之一。神道教认为它是天孙琼琼杵尊之妻、樱花女神木花之佐久耶姬的居所，人们在山麓修建浅间神社以镇抚屡屡喷发的山火，其中以富士山本宫浅间大社为首。古时人们只能在远处遥拜这座神山；平安时代火山活动平息后，修验道的山伏把它当作山岳信仰的中心，12世纪初末代上人又在山顶建起寺院。火山最后一次喷发是1707至1708年的宝永大喷发，附近村落尽被火山灰掩埋。江户时代，苦行僧长谷川角行开创的朝圣团体“富士讲”兴起，信众攀登火山口以求重生与净化，使富士山成为当时规模最大的群众性朝圣目的地之一；19世纪30年代，北斋的《富岳三十六景》更把富士的形象传遍日本乃至海外。

en: Mount Girnar, called Raivata or Ujjayanta in ancient texts, rises above Junagadh in southern Gujarat and has drawn Jain pilgrims since before 250 BCE. It is sacred above all to Neminatha, the twenty-second Tirthankara, who is said to have renounced the world and gained omniscience in the Sahsavan grove on its slopes and to have attained nirvana on its highest peak. A cluster of some sixteen marble and granite temples, enclosed on a ledge near the summit and reached by thousands of stone steps, now marks the holy ground; the greater number belong to the Svetambara sect, though Digambara Jains also venerate the hill. The principal Neminatha temple was rebuilt in 1129 by Sajjana, governor of Saurashtra under the Solanki king Jayasimha Siddharaja, in the Maru-Gurjara style, and the Chudasama ruler Mandalika I covered it with gold plates in 1364. Other major shrines include the triple Vastupala-vihara, completed by the minister Vastupala in 1232, the Adabadji Adinatha temple with a slab carved with the twenty-four Tirthankaras in 1442, and the Samprati Raja temple of 1453. A temple to the yakshini Ambika, protectress of Neminatha, already stood before 784. With Palitana, Shikharji and Dilwara, Girnar numbers among the five great Svetambara pilgrimage mountains of India.
zh: 耆栗那罗山古称赖伐多山或乌阇衍多山，耸立在古吉拉特南部的朱纳格特，早在公元前250年以前便有耆那教香客前来朝拜。此山对第二十二祖涅弥那陀最为神圣：相传他在山坡上的萨婆斯梵林出家、证得一切智，又在最高峰上涅槃。山顶附近一处台地上环绕着约十六座大理石与花岗岩庙宇，需攀登数千级石阶方可抵达；其中多数属白衣派，天衣派也同样尊奉此山。主殿涅弥那陀寺于1129年由索兰基国王阇耶僧诃·悉达罗阇任命的萨乌拉施特拉总督萨阇那按马鲁-古吉拉特风格重建，1364年朱达萨马王朝的曼达利迦一世又为它覆上金板。其他重要殿宇包括大臣瓦斯图波罗于1232年建成的三重院瓦斯图波罗精舍、1442年刻有二十四祖师像石板的阿陀巴吉·阿底那特寺，以及1453年建成的桑波罗提罗阇寺。供奉涅弥那陀护法夜叉女安比迦的神庙则早在784年之前便已存在。耆栗那罗山与波利多拿寺、尸佉罗时、地利缚罗寺等同列印度白衣派五大朝圣名山。

en: Mount Haku is a 2,702-metre volcano on the border of Kaga and the neighbouring provinces, its snow lingering long after lower peaks have thawed; with Mount Fuji and Mount Tate it is counted among Japan's Three Holy Mountains. Its summit was first reached in 717 by the Shugendō monk Taichō, who built a chapel there, and the Hakusan faith made the mountain a goal of pilgrims for centuries. The shrine at its foot, Shirayama Hime, was reckoned the ichinomiya of Kaga and heads some two thousand Hakusan branch shrines; it first appears in court records in 853, when it received junior third rank, and prospered through the Kamakura and Muromachi periods as Hakusan shrines spread across the country. The Kaga ikki rising of 1455 cost it its estates and fire destroyed the buildings in 1480, leaving the cult in ruins for more than a century until Maeda Toshiie, lord of Kaga, restored it under Tokugawa rule. The volcano itself stirred once more in its last recorded eruption of 1659.
zh: 白山是矗立于加贺国与邻国边界、海拔2702米的火山，积雪比周围群峰存留更久，因而得名；它与富士山、立山并称日本三灵山。717年，修验道僧人泰澄首次登顶并在山顶建堂，白山信仰自此使这座山成为数百年来的朝圣目标。山麓的白山比咩神社被视为加贺国一宫，统辖全国约两千座白山神社；它最早见于853年的《日本文德天皇实录》，受封从三位，镰仓至室町初期随着白山神社在各地建立而盛极一时。1455年加贺一向一揆使神社失去庄园，1480年社殿又毁于火灾，信仰荒废了一个多世纪，直到加贺藩主前田利家在江户初期加以复兴。火山本身也在1659年有过最后一次有记载的喷发。

en: Mount Hiei rises northeast of Kyoto, the direction held to be the demon gate through which misfortune entered the capital, so its guardianship was a matter of state. The Kojiki places the kami Ōyamakui on the mountain, and at its eastern foot stands Hiyoshi Taisha, head of a network of nearly four thousand Sannō shrines, whose Sannō Gongen faith fused the mountain's Shintō cult with Buddhism. In 788 the monk Saichō founded Enryaku-ji on the summit with the backing of Emperor Kanmu, and it became the headquarters of the Tendai sect and the greatest centre of learning in medieval Japan: Hōnen, Shinran, Dōgen and Nichiren all studied there before founding their own schools. At its height the complex held some three thousand sub-temples and its own armies of warrior monks, who more than forty times carried Hiyoshi's portable shrine into Kyoto to enforce their demands. In 1571 Oda Nobunaga stormed the mountain, burned the halls and slaughtered the monks, ending that power; Toyotomi Hideyoshi, devoted to the Sannō Gongen, rebuilt the shrine from 1586, and the Tokugawa shoguns restored Enryaku-ji, its main hall rising again in 1642.
zh: 比叡山耸立于京都东北方，而东北在方位信仰中被视为灾祸侵入都城的“鬼门”，镇守此山因而关系国家安危。《古事记》记载大山咋神居住在这座山上，山东麓的日吉大社是全国近四千座山王、日吉神社的总本社，其山王权现信仰把山岳神道与佛教融为一体。788年，僧人最澄在桓武天皇支持下于山顶创建延历寺，这里后来成为天台宗总本山，也是中世日本最高的佛学重镇：法然、亲鸾、道元、日莲都曾在此求学，而后各自开宗立派。鼎盛时期，山上有约三千座子院，还拥有自己的僧兵武装，曾四十余次抬着日吉的神轿进入京都强诉。1571年，织田信长发兵攻山，焚毁堂舍、屠戮僧众，终结了这股势力；虔信山王权现的丰臣秀吉从1586年起重建神社，德川幕府又着手恢复延历寺，其正殿于1642年再度落成。

en: Mount Jiuhua, one of China's four great Buddhist mountains, rises in Qingyang county in southern Anhui, its ninety-nine peaks culminating in Shiwang Peak at 1,342 metres. Under the Han it was called Mount Lingyang and under the southern dynasties Mount Jiuzi, the Nine-Peak Mountain; the Tang poet Li Bai renamed it after celebrating its nine lotus-like peaks in verse, and Jiuhua, the Nine Glories, has been its name ever since. In 719 Kim Gyo-gak, a prince of Silla in Korea who had taken monk's vows, came to the mountain and meditated there for seventy-five years; when he died at ninety-nine his body did not decay, and the monks took him for an incarnation of the bodhisattva Dizang, known in Sanskrit as Ksitigarbha, making Jiuhua his Chinese bodhimanda. Huacheng Temple and the shrine that holds the incorrupt body, Roushen Temple, became the heart of the pilgrimage, set among old pines, bamboo groves, crags and waterfalls. The Ming and Qing saw the mountain's golden age, when as many as three hundred and sixty monasteries sheltered four to five thousand monks and nuns.
zh: 九华山是中国四大佛教名山之一，与五台山、峨眉山、普陀山并称，位于安徽南部青阳县，山中群峰99座，以十王峰最高，海拔1342米。汉代名陵阳山，南朝梁陈之际称九子山；唐代诗人李白赋诗盛赞九峰如莲花绽放，将山改名为九华，此名遂行于后世。719年，地处今朝鲜半岛的新罗王族金乔觉舍俗出家，渡海来此结庐苦修，前后山居75年，世寿99岁，入灭后肉身不坏，僧众认定他是地藏菩萨的化身，九华山由此成为地藏菩萨的根本道场。化城寺与安奉不坏肉身的肉身殿成为朝山信众的中心，古松、竹海、怪石、飞瀑环绕其间。明清两代迎来鼎盛，寺院一度多达360座，常住僧尼四五千人。

en: Mount Kōya is a wooded basin eight hundred metres high in the Kii range, ringed by eight peaks like the petals of a lotus, where the monk Kūkai founded the headquarters of esoteric Shingon Buddhism in 819. Local Shintō deities, the hunter Kariba and the goddess Niu, were said to have guided him to the site with white and black dogs, and they were later honoured as Japanese manifestations of the Buddha Vairocana. Kūkai spent his last years on the mountain and, when he died in 835, was entombed without cremation at Okunoin; the faithful hold that he entered eternal samadhi and still waits there in meditation for Maitreya, the future Buddha, drawing pilgrims to his mausoleum for more than a thousand years. Around the Danjō Garan sanctuary there grew a great monastic town of over a hundred sub-temples, the base from which Kūkai's disciples spread Shingon across Japan and the starting point of the Shikoku pilgrimage that follows his trail. Warlords and emperors endowed the mountain: Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Seigan-ji there in 1593 in memory of his mother, and the Tokugawa shoguns patronised its head temple Kongōbu-ji, the centre of the Kōyasan sect.
zh: 高野山是纪伊山脉中一座海拔800米的林间盆地，八峰环绕，形如莲花八瓣；819年，僧人空海在此建立了密教真言宗的总本山。相传当地的神道神祇狩场明神与丹生明神曾以白犬、黑犬引路，带空海寻得这片圣地，二者后来被尊为大日如来在日本的化身。空海在山上度过晚年，835年去世时按遗愿未经荼毗，葬于奥之院；信众相信他并未入灭，而是进入永恒的定境，在冥想中等待未来佛弥勒降世，千余年来朝圣者络绎不绝。以坛上伽蓝为中心，山上逐渐形成拥有上百座子院的庞大寺院町，空海的弟子由此把真言宗传遍日本，这里也成为循着大师足迹的四国遍路朝圣的起点。武将与皇室纷纷施田供养：丰臣秀吉于1593年为纪念亡母在山上修建青岩寺，德川幕府也长期护持真言宗总本山金刚峰寺。

en: Mount Lu, anciently called Kuanglu, rises above the Yangtze river and Poyang lake near Jiujiang in Jiangxi, its highest summit Dahanyang Peak reaching 1,474 metres. Between 386 and 402 the monk Huiyuan built Donglin Temple on its slopes and taught the chanting of Amitabha's name, founding the Pure Land school of Chinese Buddhism. Daoist temples were added under the Tang to house sacred scriptures, and in 940 the White Deer Grotto Academy was founded at the mountain's foot; the Song scholar Zhu Xi rebuilt it into the most celebrated Confucian academy of its age, drawing students from across the empire. Poets made the mountain a byword for landscape: Tao Yuanming lived and was buried nearby, and Su Shi wrote that no one could see Lushan's true shape while standing inside it. Ming emperors added imperial pavilions, and Buddhist, Daoist and Confucian shrines continued to share its peaks and grottoes through the Qing.
zh: 庐山古称匡庐，耸立于江西九江之侧，北临长江、东濒鄱阳湖，最高峰大汉阳峰海拔1474米。386至402年间，僧人慧远在山中创建东林寺，倡念阿弥陀佛之名，开汉传佛教净土宗之源。唐代又兴修道观以藏道经；940年，白鹿洞书院创立于山麓，宋代儒者朱熹将其重建为当时最负盛名的儒家书院，四方学子纷至沓来。庐山也因诗人而成为山水的代名词：东晋诗人陶渊明曾在附近隐居并安葬于此，苏轼则留下“不识庐山真面目，只缘身在此山中”的名句。明代帝王在此增建御碑亭等建筑，入清以后，佛、道、儒三教的寺观书院仍并存于峰峦岩洞之间。

en: Mount Misen is the 535-metre sacred peak at the heart of Itsukushima, the island in Aki Province also called Miyajima, whose soil was guarded by strict taboos of ritual purity. In 806 the monk Kūkai, later known as Kōbō Daishi, climbed the mountain, founded the Daisho-in temple and lit the Kiezu-no-hi, an eternal fire kept burning there without interruption; his iron staff was said to have taken root as a plum tree, one of the seven wonders told of the peak. The mountain drew pilgrims of the Shugendō mountain cult, while Taira no Kiyomori's lavish patronage of Itsukushima Shrine from 1168 turned the island below into one of the great cult centres of the Inland Sea. The taboo on bloodshed was broken in 1555 when Mōri Motonari defeated Sue Takafusa on the island, after which Motonari rebuilt the shrine hall in 1571.
zh: 弥山是安艺国严岛（又称宫岛）中央的圣山，海拔535米，为全岛最高峰；整座岛屿被视为神域，受严格的清净禁忌保护。806年，僧人空海（即弘法大师）登上此山，开创大圣院，并点燃“不灭之火”，此火此后一直由寺僧守护；传说他的锡杖就地生根长成梅树，是弥山七大奇景之一。弥山吸引修验道的登山行者前来修行，而平清盛自1168年起巨资营建山下的严岛神社，使该岛成为濑户内海最重要的信仰中心之一。1555年毛利元就在岛上击败陶晴贤，打破了岛上不得流血的禁忌，战后元就又于1571年重建神社正殿。

en: Mount Nantai, also called Mount Futara, is a 2,486-metre volcano above Nikkō in Shimotsuke Province, whose streams water the rice plains below and whose cone was worshipped from the Yayoi period as a go-shintai, a mountain itself housing the kami. In the eighth century the Kegon monk Shōdō Shōnin made the first recorded ascent, founding Futarasan Shrine in 767 and its summit chapel, the Oku-no-miya, in 782; the old mountain cult merged with Buddhist Shugendō, and Kūkai and the Tendai master Ennin both founded halls on its slopes, making Nikkō a centre of mountain Buddhism. The Engishiki of 927 records its shrine, and a middle shrine was raised on the shore of Lake Chuzenji in 1096. After Sengoku warfare cost it its estates, seized by the Late Hōjō clan and later Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the rise of the nearby Nikkō Tōshō-gū, mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, brought Tokugawa patronage: Hidetada rebuilt the main shrine in 1617 and the lakeside halls in 1699.
zh: 男体山又名二荒山，是耸立在下野国日光、海拔2486米的火山。山上溪流滋养山下稻田，自弥生时代起，山容本身就被当作神灵依代的御神体而受崇拜。8世纪，华严宗僧人胜道上人首次有记载地登上此山，于767年开创二荒山神社，又在782年于山顶建立奥宫；古老的山岳信仰与佛教修验道合流，空海和天台宗大师圆仁都在山中建堂，日光由此成为山岳佛教的中心。927年的《延喜式》载有这座神社；1096年，中禅寺湖畔又建起中宫。战国战乱中神社庄园被后北条氏、丰臣秀吉先后没收，进入江户时代后，邻近祭祀德川家康的日光东照宫兴起，神社得到德川家庇护：秀忠于1617年重建本社，湖畔殿堂也于1699年再建。

en: Mount Putuo is a small island in the Zhoushan archipelago off Ningbo in Zhejiang, its name taken from Potalaka, the sacred mountain of Avalokitesvara in Indian scripture, and Chinese Buddhism regards it as the bodhimanda of Guanyin, the bodhisattva of compassion. Its cult began in 916, when the Japanese monk Hui'e, bearing a Guanyin image from Mount Wutai, was driven back by storms and left the statue with an islander surnamed Zhang; the shrine that grew around it was called the Temple of the Unwilling Guanyin. In 1080 Emperor Shenzong of the Song refounded it as the Baotuo Guanyin Temple with grants of land, and later Song and Yuan rulers heaped endowments on it, sending its abbot Yishan Yining as an envoy to Japan in 1299. Ming coastal evacuations twice emptied the island, three hundred temples being burned in 1386 under Tang He and again under Jiajing in 1553; monks returned from the 1570s, and Wanli honoured the rebuilt sanctuary in 1605. Around these shrines arose the three great monasteries of Puji, Fayu founded in 1580 and Huiji founded in 1793, completing the four sacred mountains of Chinese Buddhism.
zh: 普陀山是浙江宁波外海舟山群岛中的一座小岛，山名取自印度经典中观自在菩萨的圣山补怛洛伽，汉传佛教以之为观音菩萨的道场。其香火始于916年：日本僧人慧锷从五台山请得一尊观音像东归，途经此岛时屡遇风浪不能成行，便将圣像留在岛民张氏家中供奉，由此发展出的庵堂称“不肯去观音院”。1080年，宋神宗赐额改建为宝陀观音寺并拨赐寺田，宋元历代君主频频布施，1299年寺主一山一宁还受朝廷委任出使日本。明代海禁迁海，此山两度遭劫：1386年汤和焚毁寺院300座、徙民入内地，1553年嘉靖朝再次毁寺逐僧；1570年代起僧人陆续重返，1605年万历皇帝为重建的禅寺赐额。普济、法雨（1580年始建）、慧济（1793年始建）三大寺由此次第崛起，使普陀山跻身中国四大佛教名山。

en: Mount Tate is a 3,015-metre peak in Etchū Province, the highest of the Hida range, and with Mount Fuji and Mount Haku one of Japan's Three Holy Mountains. Tradition places its opening in 701, when the hunter-ascetic Saeki no Ariyori climbed into its clouded highlands and founded the cult of Tateyama Gongen; Emperor Monmu then declared the summit country a sacred domain, and Oyama Shrine on the peak later became the ichinomiya of Etchū. The mountain god appears in a Man'yōshū poem of 747 by Ōtomo no Yakamochi and rose through the court ranks recorded in the ninth-century Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku. Under the Kamakura and Muromachi shogunates the halls drew warrior patronage: the Kamakura bakufu began raising them in 1185, Ashikaga Yoshiki sent offerings in 1492, and the Etchū deputy Jinbo Nagamasa and later Sassa Narimasa were devoted protectors. The Etchū campaign of 1585 saw Hashiba Hideyoshi burn the precinct, but Maeda Toshiie of Kaga rebuilt it and made the shrine a prayer centre of his domain, while its Shugendō order, the Tateyama Shugen, maintained the mountain cult through the Edo centuries.
zh: 立山是越中国境内、海拔3015米的高峰，为飞驒山脉最高峰，与富士山、白山并称日本三灵山。相传701年，猎人出身的修行者佐伯有赖登上云雾缭绕的高地，开创立山权现信仰，文武天皇随即将山顶一带划为灵域；峰顶的雄山神社后来成为越中国一宫。山神在747年大伴家持收入《万叶集》的和歌中已经出现，又在9世纪的《日本三代实录》里屡获神阶晋升。镰仓、室町两朝，社殿受到武家庇护：镰仓幕府于1185年起兴建社殿，足利义稙在1492年寄进供品，地方豪族神保氏与佐佐成政也先后崇敬。1585年越中征伐中，社域被羽柴秀吉烧毁，战后加贺藩主前田利家加以重建，将神社定为藩内祈愿所；其修验道法团立山修验则在整个江户时代维系着这座灵山的信仰。

en: Mount Wutai in northern Shanxi is not a single peak but a ring of five flat-topped mountains, its northern summit Yedou Feng rising 3,061 metres, the highest point in north China. Chinese Buddhism counts it first among the four great bodhisattva mountains, the bodhimanda of Manjushri, the bodhisattva of wisdom; monks identified it with the clear cold mountain of the northeast named as Manjushri's abode in the Avatamsaka Sutra, which gave the range its older name of Mount Qingliang. By the seventh century pilgrims from India and Central Asia were already travelling there, and Tang patronage left two of the oldest timber buildings still standing in China, the main hall of Nanchan Temple of 782 and the East Hall of Foguang Temple of 857. Even the ninth-century Chan master Linji Yixuan's mocking rebuke of pilgrims seeking Manjushri on Wutai did not dim its fame. Over the following dynasties Han Buddhist monasteries and Tibetan Buddhist lamaseries grew side by side on its terraces, among them Xiantong Temple, Tayuan Temple and Pusading, drawing imperial visits and endowments down to the Qing.
zh: 五台山位于山西北部，并非孤峰，而是五座峰顶平阔的台状山峰环抱而成的峰群，北台叶斗峰海拔3061米，为华北最高点。汉传佛教以五台山为四大菩萨名山之首，是智慧菩萨文殊师利的道场；古人依据《华严经》中东北方“清凉山”为文殊所居的记载将其比定于此，五台山也因此旧称清凉山。早在7世纪，印度与中亚的巡礼者已远道而来；唐代的护持留下了中国现存最古老的两座木构建筑，即782年的南禅寺大殿和857年的佛光寺东大殿。9世纪禅宗祖师临济义玄曾讥讽登五台求文殊的学人，却无损其声名。此后历代，汉传青庙与藏传黄庙在山间台地上并立，显通寺、塔院寺、菩萨顶等梵刹林立，屡获历朝皇帝巡幸施赐，香火延续至清代不衰。

en: Mount Yoshino is an eight-kilometre ridge in Yamato Province running south from the Yoshino River into the Ōmine range, its slopes studded with the temples and shrines of the Kinpusen cult. In the seventh century the ascetic En no Gyōja opened the mountain and founded Kinpusen-ji, seat of Zaō Gongen and headquarters of Kinpusen Shugendō, and blazed the Ōmine Okugakemichi trail linking Yoshino with the Kumano shrines of Kii. Cherry wood served to carve images of Zaō Gongen, and believers donated saplings: from the Heian period four groves of a thousand trees clothed the ridge, celebrated in the Kokin Wakashū and in the poems of Saigyō. Earlier still, Prince Ōama watched for omens at the Yoshino palace before seizing the throne in the Jinshin War of 672. In 1336 the dispossessed Southern Court made Yoshino its mountain capital, and four of its emperors kept court among the temples until the rival courts were reunited in 1392.
zh: 吉野山是大和国境内一条八公里长的山脊，自吉野川南岸向南延伸入大峰山脉，山坡上遍布金峰信仰的寺院与神社。7世纪，修行者役行者开辟此山，开创供奉藏王权现的金峰山寺，作为金峰修验的总本山，并踏出连接吉野与纪伊熊野三山的大峰奥驱道。藏王权现的造像以樱木雕成，信众纷纷供奉樱树树苗：自平安时代起，山脊上形成四处各千株的樱树林，《古今和歌集》和西行的和歌都曾歌咏其盛。更早以前，大海人皇子曾在吉野行宫观望征兆，随后在672年的壬申之乱中夺取皇位。1336年，失势的南朝以吉野为山间王都，四位南朝天皇在众寺之间维持朝廷，直到1392年南北两朝合一。

en: Muktagiri, also called Mendhagiri, is a Jain pilgrimage centre in the forested hills on the border of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, within reach of Gawilgarh. Known as a Siddha Kshetra, a place where liberated souls are said to have attained nirvana, it holds a cluster of fifty-two temples set around a waterfall and reached by a flight of six hundred steps. The oldest sanctuary is a rock-cut cave raised between roughly 1200 and 1400, its arched entrance carved with lotuses and small tirthankara figures and its inner hall holding some fifty-six Jain images, including a seated Mahavira at the gate. Among the later numbered shrines, the twenty-sixth temple is famed for its seven-hooded image of Parshvanatha. Pilgrims gather for the annual fair held at Diwali.
zh: 穆羯帝耆梨寺又称门达吉里，是中央邦与马哈拉施特拉邦交界山林中的耆那教朝圣中心，邻近加维尔加尔。此地被尊为“成就地”，相传有解脱者在此证得涅槃；52座寺院环绕一道瀑布分布，需登六百级石阶抵达。最古老的圣所是13至14世纪开凿的石窟，拱门雕有莲花与小型祖师像，内殿保存约56尊耆那教造像，窟门正中为结跏趺坐的大雄像。在依次编号的后世祠庙中，第26寺以七头华盖的巴湿伐那陀像著称。每年排灯节期间，信众在此举行庙会朝山。

en: Muktinath lies at 3,800 metres in the Mustang valley beneath the Thorong La pass, making it one of the highest temples in the world, and its sanctity is shared by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus know it as Mukti Kshetra, the place of liberation, one of the four great Himalayan dhams of Nepal, one of the eight self-manifested Vishnu shrines and a Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar under the Tamil name Tiru Salagramam; in Shaktism it is also counted among the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, where the head of Sati is said to have fallen, and the Vishnu Purana's Gandaki Mahatmya celebrates the nearby Kali Gandaki gorge whose shaligram stones are worshipped as Vishnu. Tibetan Buddhists call the place Chumig Gyatsa, the Hundred Waters, rank it among the twenty-four tantric abodes of the dakinis and venerate the same icon as Avalokiteshvara. The copper image itself dates to the late 1500s, while the present Newari-style pagoda with its three-tiered roof was raised in 1814 or 1815 under Queen Subarna Prabha Devi of Nepal, replacing an older clay temple of the Jumla kings; its courtyard is ringed by the hundred and eight bull-headed Mukti Dhara spouts and two sacred ponds.
zh: 穆克蒂纳特位于木斯塘谷地、通拉山口脚下，海拔3800米，是世界上海拔最高的神庙之一，由印度教徒与佛教徒共同尊奉。印度教徒称其为“解脱之地”穆克蒂克舍特拉，是尼泊尔喜马拉雅四大圣地之一、八座毗湿奴自显圣庙之一，也是提鲁芒盖·阿尔瓦尔以泰米尔名“底鲁萨拉格拉玛姆”颂唱过的“圣城庙”；在性力派传统中，它又位列五十一处性力圣地，相传萨蒂女神的头颅坠落于此，《毗湿奴往世书》的《犍陀吉利赞》还称颂了附近的卡里甘达基峡谷，河中出产的“萨拉格拉玛石”被当作毗湿奴崇拜。藏传佛教徒称此地为“楚米嘉察”，意为“百水”，将其列为二十四处空行母密乘圣地之一，并把同一尊像视为观世音菩萨的化现。铜制圣像可追溯至16世纪末，现存三层金顶的尼瓦尔式宝塔则是1814至1815年由尼泊尔王后苏巴尔纳·普拉巴·德维在久姆拉诸王旧黏土庙的原址上兴建，庭院四周环绕着一百零八个牛头造型的“解脱水口”和两座圣池。

en: The Mundeshwari Temple crowns a hill of the Kaimur plateau near the Son river in the Bhojpuri country of Bihar, its rare octagonal stone plan the earliest surviving example of Nagara architecture in the region. It houses a four-faced Shiva linga at the centre of the sanctum while the presiding deity is Mundeshwari, a ten-armed Durga as Mahishasuramardini riding a buffalo, and the Tantric manner of her worship marks this as an early eastern Indian centre of the goddess cult. Local tradition and a religious trust claim a foundation in 108, but historians date the surviving sculptures and an inscription of the raja Udayasena to about 570 to 590, showing an important temple settlement on the hill from the 600s; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang described around 636 a luminous hilltop shrine southwest of Patna that is plausibly this one, and a Brahmi seal of the Sri Lankan king Dutthagamani from the first century before Christ suggests even older pilgrimage ties. The present shrine was probably built or rebuilt in the 1500s or 1600s from the doorways and mouldings of ruined seventh-century temples, and its tower has long since fallen. Rites have continued without interruption regardless, with pilgrims gathering for Rama Navami, Shiva Ratri and the Navaratra fair.
zh: 蒙提湿伐罗神庙雄踞比哈尔博杰普尔地区宋河附近凯穆尔高原的山丘之上，罕见的八角石构平面是当地现存最早的纳加拉风格建筑实例。殿中中央供奉四面湿婆林伽，主神则是骑乘水牛、十臂诛杀摩西沙修罗形态的难近母蒙提湿伐罗；其密教化的祭祀方式表明这里是东印度较早的女神崇拜中心。当地传统和宗教信托机构声称庙宇始建于108年，但史学家据现存雕刻与乌达耶犀那王铭文判断，遗物年代约在570至590年，说明600年代山上已有重要的寺院聚落；636年前后，中国求法僧玄奘记述巴特那西南有一座发光的山顶神祠，学者认为很可能就是此处，而一枚公元前1世纪斯里兰卡国王杜多伽摩尼的婆罗米文印章，更暗示其朝圣渊源之久远。现存殿宇大约是1500至1600年间利用7世纪废庙的门框和线脚重建或改建而成，塔顶早已倾圮。但庙里的祭祀从未中断，每逢罗摩诞辰、湿婆夜和九夜节庙会，信众仍云集于此。

en: Nachiyar Koil, properly the Thirunarayur Nambi Temple, is a Sri Vaishnava shrine at Thirunarayur near Kumbakonam in the Thanjavur country, and one of the 108 Divya Desams hymned by the Alvar saints between the 500s and 800s in the Divya Prabandham. Vishnu is worshipped here as Srinivasa Perumal and Lakshmi, in her aspect of Niladevi, as Nachiyar, and unusually the goddess rather than the god is the presiding deity: legend says the sage Medhavi raised the goddess, found as a girl named Vanjulavalli beneath a vanjula tree, and gave her to Vishnu only on the condition that she always take primacy, so in every procession her image comes first. It is also the place where Vishnu is believed to have granted the Pancha Samskara initiation to the saint Thirumangai Alvar. The shrine is attributed to the early Chola king Kochengat Cholan of the late 200s, the only Vishnu temple among the many temples he is credited with, and was enlarged under the medieval Cholas and the Vijayanagara kings. Its granite enclosure and five-tiered gopuram house the famous Kal Garuda image, said to grow miraculously heavier as it is carried through each gate during the Brahmotsavam festival.
zh: 那止抴神庙的正式名称为蒂鲁纳鲁尔·南比庙，是坦贾武尔一带贡伯戈讷姆附近蒂鲁纳鲁尔村的一座室利毗湿奴派神庙，也是阿尔瓦尔圣徒在500至800年间编成的《迪维亚·普拉班达姆》颂诗所赞美的108处毗湿奴圣地之一。庙中毗湿奴以斯里尼瓦萨·佩鲁马尔之名受拜，吉祥天女则以妮拉德维的化身“那止亚尔”为主神；与众不同的是，这里主神是女神而非男神：相传仙人梅达毗在万朱拉树下捡到女婴万朱拉瓦利并收为养女，她实为吉祥天女，仙人将她许配毗湿奴时约定女神永远居于首位，所以每次出游行神，女神的神像都走在前面。相传毗湿奴还在此为圣徒蒂鲁曼盖·阿尔瓦尔传授五戒入门仪轨。此庙传为3世纪末早期朱罗国王科琴加特所建，是传说中他修建的众多神庙里唯一的毗湿奴庙，后又经中世纪朱罗诸王和毗奢耶那伽罗历代国王扩建。花岗岩围墙内立着五层塔门，庙中珍藏的黑迦楼罗像在大节出巡时，据说每过一道门都会奇迹般变重，需要不断增加抬轿人手。

en: Nageshvara, the lord of serpents, is the Jyotirlinga of the Darukavana forest, where the Shiva Purana says Shiva answered the prayers of his devotee Supriya and overcame the demon Daruka, then settled there as a pillar of light. The Purana gives no precise location, and two shrines claim the title: the Nageshwar temple at Dwarka in Gujarat, and, in the Marathwada country around Nanded, the Aundha Nagnath temple, which Maharashtra tradition honours as the eighth Jyotirlinga and the true Darukavana. The present Aundha Nagnath building dates to the 13th century and the Yadavas of Devagiri, built in the mortar-free Hemadpanti style of their minister Hemadri Pandit, with the lingam enshrined in an unusual basement sanctum. It is dear to the Varkari saints: the poet Namdev, who lived from about 1270 to 1350, is said to have been turned away by the priests while singing, whereupon the whole temple rotated to face him, which is why the image of Nandi stands at the rear rather than before the door. Damaged in the Delhi Sultanate's invasions of the Deccan, the temple was repaired in the 18th century under Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore, who rebuilt the spire in the Maratha style above the older Hemadpanti base, and its great chariot fair at Maha Shivaratri still draws crowds of pilgrims.
zh: 纳格什瓦拉意为“蛇之主”，是达鲁迦林森林的究提林迦。《湿婆往世书》说，湿婆应虔诚信众苏普里亚的祈祷降服魔王达鲁迦后，以光柱之形永驻于此。往世书并未确指地点，因此有两座神庙争夺这一名号：古吉拉特德瓦尔卡的纳格什瓦尔庙，以及南德尔一带马拉特瓦达地区的奥恩达·纳格纳特庙——马哈拉施特拉传统将后者尊为第八处究提林迦和真正的达鲁迦林。现存的奥恩达·纳格纳特建筑建于13世纪德瓦吉里亚达瓦王朝时期，采用其大臣赫马德里·潘底特所创、不用灰浆咬合石块的赫马德潘蒂风格，林伽安放在罕见的地下密室中。它也是瓦尔卡里派圣徒崇敬之地：诗人那摩提婆（约1270—1350年）唱颂时被祭司驱赶，相传整座神庙竟转向他的方向，这也是神牛南迪像立于庙后而非门前的缘由。神庙在德里苏丹国入侵德干时受损，18世纪印多尔的阿希莉娅芭伊·霍尔卡加以修缮，在古老的赫马德潘蒂基座上以马拉塔风格重建了塔尖；每逢大湿婆夜节，这里的盛大战车庙会仍吸引成群朝圣者。

en: The Nainativu Nagapooshani Amman Temple stands on Nainativu, a small island in Palk Bay off the Jaffna peninsula of Sri Lanka, dedicated to Parvati in her form Nagapooshani, also called Bhuvaneswari, with Shiva worshipped beside her as Nayinaar. The island was known in antiquity as Manipallavam and its Naga people were serpent worshippers, which gave the goddess her name; Tamil classics such as the Manimekalai and Kundalakesi already speak of the shrine, and a twelfth-century Tamil inscription from the reign of the Sinhala king Parakramabahu I, dated to his rule between 1153 and 1186, was found in the precinct; it is an edict to his Tamil officials in Jaffna on how to treat shipwrecked foreign traders. Counted among the fifty-one Shakta pithas, the ancient temple was destroyed by the Portuguese in 1620, and the present complex with its four gopuram gateway towers was raised between 1720 and 1790. It has remained the chief pilgrimage focus of the Jaffna Tamils, whose sixteen-day summer Mahostavam draws worshippers from across the region.
zh: 奈那底乌·那伽布沙尼女神神庙位于斯里兰卡贾夫纳半岛外、保克湾中的奈那底乌小岛，供奉帕尔瓦蒂的化身那伽布沙尼（又名布瓦内湿伐梨），其配偶湿婆在此称奈伊纳尔。该岛古称摩尼波罗瓦姆，岛上的那伽人崇奉蛇神，女神之名即由此而来；《摩尼湄迦莱》《昆达罗吉西》等泰米尔古典文学已提到这座神庙，庙院内还发现过12世纪的泰米尔铭文，内容是僧伽罗国王波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世（1153—1186年在位）就如何处置遇险外国商船商人向贾夫纳当地泰米尔官员颁发的敕令。此庙名列五十一处性力圣地，旧庙于1620年被葡萄牙人摧毁，现存带四座门楼的建筑群建于1720至1790年间。它始终是贾夫纳泰米尔人最重要的朝圣中心，每年夏季为期16天的大节吸引着各地信众。

en: Nanto Shichi Daiji is the collective name of the seven great imperial temples of Nara, the old Heijō-kyō capital: Daian-ji, Gangō-ji, Hōryū-ji, Kōfuku-ji, Saidai-ji, Tōdai-ji and Yakushi-ji, with Tōshōdai-ji and Hokke-ji sometimes counted to make fifteen. Founded by imperial decree in the eighth century, they were the headquarters of the six Nara schools of Buddhism and the intellectual heart of the Japanese state. Tōdai-ji, made head of the national provincial temple system under Emperor Shōmu, housed the great bronze Vairocana Buddha consecrated in 752, and its ordination platform, where the Chinese monk Ganjin ordained clergy in 754, was the rite of passage for monks including Kūkai and Saichō; Kōfuku-ji, the tutelary temple of the Fujiwara, kept its wealth and warrior monks long after the court moved to Kyoto in 794 and Nara became the southern capital. In the winter of 1180 Taira forces burned Kōfuku-ji and Tōdai-ji in the Nara siege, and Minamoto no Yoritomo entrusted the monk Chōgen with their rebuilding, which produced the Great South Gate and the giant guardian figures of Unkei and Kaikei; the Great Buddha Hall itself rose again in 1709.
zh: 南都七大寺是故都平城京奈良七座皇家大寺的合称，即大安寺、元兴寺、法隆寺、兴福寺、西大寺、东大寺和药师寺，有时加上唐招提寺、法华寺等并称南都十五大寺。它们都建于8世纪的天皇诏令之下，是日本佛教南都六宗的总本山，也是当时国家的学术中枢。圣武天皇在位时，东大寺被定为全国国分寺的总本山，寺内供奉752年开眼供养的巨型毗卢遮那铜像；754年唐朝僧人鉴真在东大寺戒坛授戒，这里从此成为日本僧人的受戒圣地，空海、最澄都曾在此登坛。兴福寺作为藤原氏的氏寺，在794年朝廷迁都京都、奈良成为南都之后，仍凭门第之盛保有财富与僧兵武装。1180年冬，平氏军队在南都烧讨中焚毁兴福寺与东大寺；源赖朝随后命僧人重源主持重建，南大门以及运庆、快庆塑造的巨型金刚力士像便诞生于这一时期，而大佛殿本身则于1709年再度落成。

en: The Narasimhaswamy Temple is a rock-cut shrine excavated into the Namagiri hill at Namakkal, near Sendamangalam in the Tamil country, and is dedicated to Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu. Its legend tells how Hanuman entrusted a shaligrama stone to Lakshmi in disguise; when she set it down it grew into this hill, and Narasimha came to dwell in the image, with Lakshmi shown upon his chest and Shiva and Brahma in adoration. Historians date the cave to the sixth to eighth centuries and the Adiyaman kings, noting parallels with the sixth-century Badami caves and Grantha-letter inscriptions like those of Mahabalipuram; one inscription names a king Gunasila around the year 500. In 1500 the Kannada Haridasa Purandarasa, called the grandfather of Carnatic music, visited and sang a hymn to Namagiri Narasimha. A fort was later raised over the same rock, passing through the hands of the Madurai Nayaks, the Sultans of Bijapur and Golconda, the kings of Mysore and finally the British in 1768.
zh: 纳拉辛哈斯瓦米神庙是凿于纳马卡尔纳马吉里山岩中的石窟神龛，位于泰米尔地区森达曼加拉姆附近，供奉毗湿奴的人狮化身那罗辛哈。相传哈奴曼曾把一块夏利格拉摩圣石托付给化身隐身的拉克什米保管，她将石头放下后，石头便长成了这座山丘，那罗辛哈从此驻跸于神像之中；神像胸前刻有拉克什米，湿婆与梵天则在一旁敬拜。学者根据形制判断石窟建于6至8世纪的阿迪亚曼诸王时期，与6世纪的巴达米石窟及摩诃巴里补罗的格兰塔字体铭文颇有相通之处；一条铭文还提到约500年在位的国王古纳希拉。1500年，被誉为卡纳提克音乐之祖的卡纳达哈里达萨圣徒普兰达拉达萨到此参拜，并为纳马吉里·那罗辛哈赋诗一首。后来山丘上又建起城堡，先后历经马杜赖奈克、比贾布尔与戈尔孔达苏丹、迈索尔君王之手，最终于1768年落入英国人手中。

en: The Narasingam temple is a Pandya rock-cut shrine at the foot of the Yanaimalai, or Elephant Hill, eight kilometres from Madurai, its Narasimha image carved out of the living rock. Inscriptions record that work began in 770 under Maran Kari, minister of the Pandya king Parantaka Nedunjadaiyan, and was finished by his brother Maran Eyinan, who added the entrance hall and consecrated the shrine. Its sthalapurana tells that the sage Romasa performed penance here to see Vishnu in his man-lion form; the god appeared as the ferocious Ugra Narasimha and was softened only by Prahlada's prayers and by Lakshmi, who took her place in him as Narasingavalli, yielding the serene Yoga Narasimha now worshipped. The nearby Chakra Theertham pool is held to have cleansed Shiva of the sin of striking off Brahma's head. The Thiruvilaiyadal Purana adds that the Elephant Hill was once a magic elephant sent against the Pandya king and turned to stone by the Narasimha mantra. Pandya-period halls and a separate shrine of the goddess Narasingavalli still frame the cave.
zh: 纳拉辛加姆神庙是一座潘地亚石窟神庙，坐落在距马杜赖八公里的亚奈马莱山，意为象山的山脚，庙中的那罗辛哈像直接从原生岩石中凿出。铭文记载，工程于770年在潘地亚国王帕兰塔卡·内敦贾达延的大臣马兰卡里主持下开工，后由其弟马兰·埃伊南续成，他增建了门厅并为神龛举行开光仪式。当地圣传称，仙人罗摩萨在此苦行，以求一见毗湿奴的人狮化身；神祇现作忿怒的乌格拉·那罗辛哈，唯有帕拉拉达的祈祷和拉克什米的到来才使他平息，拉克什米化身为纳拉辛加瓦利安住其身，庙中由此供奉着安详的瑜伽那罗辛哈。附近的恰克罗圣池相传曾为湿婆洗去砍落梵天头颅之罪。《蒂鲁维莱亚达尔往世书》还说，这座象山本是敌方用来对付潘地亚国王的神象，被那罗辛哈咒语化为石头。石窟之外，潘地亚时期的各座厅堂和女神纳拉辛加瓦利的独立神龛仍环绕四周。

en: Nashik, on the upper Godavari in northern Maharashtra, is known in the Ramayana as Panchavati, the forest retreat where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana passed part of their exile and Lakshmana cut off the nose of the demoness Shurpanakha, from which the city's name, meaning nose, is popularly derived. Twenty-eight kilometres away at Trimbak, the Godavari springs from the Brahmagiri hill beside the Trimbakeshwar temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva, unique in its single three-faced linga of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; Aurangzeb destroyed the medieval temple and the present one was rebuilt by the Maratha Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao. Every twelve years, when Jupiter enters the sign of Leo, or Simha, the Simhastha bathing fair draws pilgrims to the Godavari's banks, already described in 1695 as a gathering famous throughout the Mughal Empire, when the town was called Gulshanabad. Until 1789 the fair was held only at Trimbak, but in that year Shaivite sanyasis and Vaishnavite bairagis fought over the order of bathing, and a Peshwa copperplate claims twelve thousand ascetics died; the Peshwa then moved the Vaishnavites' bathing place to the Ram Kund in Nashik itself, splitting the festival between the two towns. The Kumbh Mela name and amrita legend were borrowed from the older Haridwar fair only in later centuries, and the Ujjain Simhastha grew from it in the eighteenth century. The Marathas held the region until 1818, when it passed to the East India Company.
zh: 纳西克位于马哈拉施特拉北部的戈达瓦里河上游，在《罗摩衍那》中称般查瓦提，是罗摩、悉多与罗什曼那流放时的林中栖居之处；罗什曼那在此割下罗刹女巨爪的鼻子，民间认为城名便源自意为“鼻子”的梵语词。距城28公里的特里姆巴克镇旁，戈达瓦里河从梵山涌出，河畔的特里姆巴克什瓦尔神庙是湿婆十二处究提林迦圣地之一，独特之处是一尊兼具梵天、毗湿奴、湿婆三面的林伽；中世纪的神庙被奥朗则布拆毁，现存的黑石建筑由马拉塔佩什瓦巴拉吉·巴吉·拉奥重建。每隔十二年，当木星进入狮子座（梵语称辛哈），狮子座节沐浴大会便把朝圣者吸引到戈达瓦里河畔——1695年的一部波斯文史书已记载这场在莫卧儿帝国全境闻名的集会，当时此城还叫古尔尚阿巴德。1789年以前节会只在特里姆巴克举行；那一年湿婆派遁世僧与毗湿奴派拜拉吉为沐浴次序大打出手，佩什瓦的铜匾铭文称有一万两千名苦行僧丧命，佩什瓦随后把毗湿奴派的沐浴地迁到纳西克城内的罗摩池，节会从此分在两地举行。“大壶节”之名和甘露传说是后世才从更古老的赫里德瓦尔节会借来的，而乌贾因的狮子座节又是18世纪从这里派生出去的。马拉塔人统治该地区直到1818年，随后转入英国东印度公司之手。

en: The Navlakha Temple stands at Ghumli, below the Barda hills in western Saurashtra, close to Bhanvad. Ghumli had first been the capital of the Saindhava dynasty from the eighth to the tenth century, and later became the seat of the Jethwa rulers, who built this shrine to the sun god Surya in the eleventh or twelfth century, making it the oldest surviving sun temple in Gujarat. Its name, meaning nine lakhs, recalls the vast sum spent on its construction. Built in the Maru-Gurjara or Solanki style, it has the largest temple platform in the region, measuring roughly forty-six by thirty metres, an east-facing entrance once crowned by a Kirti Toran arch, a covered circumambulation path around the sanctum and an eight-pillared assembly hall, with images of Brahma and Savitri, Shiva and Parvati, and Lakshmi-Narayana set in its niches. The Jethwa ruler Rana Shiyaji made Ghumli his capital again in 1220, but in 1313 the Jadeja chieftain Barmaniyaji sacked the city and drove the Jethwas to Ranpur, leaving the temple among the ruins through which later Saurashtra knew the site.
zh: 纳夫拉卡神庙位于萨乌拉施特拉西部巴尔达山麓的古姆利，邻近班瓦德。古姆利曾是8至10世纪赛恩达瓦王朝的都城，后来成为杰特瓦统治者的驻地；他们在11或12世纪修建了这座供奉太阳神苏利耶的神庙，它也是古吉拉特现存最古老的太阳神庙。庙名意为“九万”，据说来自建庙耗费的巨额资金。神庙采用马鲁-古吉拉风格（又称索兰基风格），拥有当地最大的庙台，面积约四十六米乘三十米；庙门朝东，上方曾有一座“光荣门”拱门，主殿外有绕行回廊，会堂由八根立柱支撑，壁龛中分别刻有梵天与萨维特丽、湿婆与帕尔瓦蒂、吉祥天女与那罗延的造像。1220年杰特瓦君主拉纳·希亚吉再次定都古姆利，但1313年贾德贾首领巴尔马尼亚吉攻陷并摧毁了这座城市，杰特瓦人逃往兰布尔，神庙便留在废墟之中，为后世的萨乌拉施特拉所凭吊。

en: In the Alban Hills south of Rome, the crater lake of Nemi, called Diana's Mirror by the Romans, was ringed by the sacred grove and sanctuary of Diana Nemorensis, Diana of the Wood. From the sixth century BC the grove was a common holy place of the Latin cities, and an inscription copied by Cato the Elder recorded its dedication by the Latin dictator Egerius Baebius of Tusculum; the monumental temple, archaic and Etruscan in form according to Vitruvius, was built around 300 BC. Legend traced the cult to Orestes and Iphigenia, who were said to have brought the image of the Tauric Diana to Italy, and worshippers appealed to the goddess as huntress, moon deity and helper of women in childbirth, leaving votive offerings in the grove. Its most famous rite was the priesthood of the rex Nemorensis: a runaway slave who broke a branch from the sacred oak might challenge the reigning priest to mortal combat, and if he killed him took his place as king of the grove until the next challenger prevailed. Each August the festival of the Nemoralia drew pilgrims who garlanded their boats with flowers on the lake. Julius Caesar owned a villa on the shore, Tiberius and Caligula sailed the waters to associate themselves with the cult, and Caligula built two enormous floating pleasure palaces on the lake, later sunk and forgotten.
zh: 内米湖是罗马以南阿尔班山中的火山口湖，罗马人称之为“狄安娜之镜”，湖畔环绕着林中狄安娜（狄安娜·内莫伦西斯）的圣林与圣所。从公元前6世纪起，这片圣林就是拉丁诸城共同的圣地；老加图抄录过一段献词铭文，记载它由图斯库鲁姆出身的拉丁独裁官埃格里乌斯·贝比乌斯敬献。约公元前300年，这里建起了宏伟的神庙，维特鲁威称其形制古旧、带有伊特鲁里亚风格。传说这套崇拜由俄瑞斯忒斯和伊菲革涅亚创立，据说他们把陶里斯的狄安娜神像带到了意大利。信众把女神奉为狩猎神、月神和助产之神，在林中留下大量还愿供物。这里最著名的仪式是“内米之王”祭司制：逃亡奴隶只要折下圣橡树的一根枝条，就有权向在任祭司发起生死决斗，若能杀死对方便取而代之，成为圣林之王，直到自己又被后来者杀死。每年8月的内莫拉利亚节，朝圣者乘船游湖，用花环装点船只。尤利乌斯·凯撒在湖边拥有别墅，提比略和卡利古拉都曾泛舟湖上以自附于这一崇拜，卡利古拉还在湖上建造了两艘巨大的游乐浮宫，后来沉没并被人遗忘。

en: The Nithyakalyana Perumal Temple at Thiruvidandai, a coastal village in present-day Chengalpattu district of Tamil Nadu, is dedicated to Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, worshipped here as Nithyakalyana Perumal with Lakshmi as Komalavalli Thayar. It is counted among the 108 Divya Desams, the Vishnu shrines glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham, the Tamil hymn canon of the Alvar saints. Its name means the eternal bridegroom: after Varaha slew the asura Hiranyaksha in a duel said to have lasted a thousand years and lifted the drowned earth on his tusks, the sage Kalava asked him to marry his three hundred and sixty daughters, whereupon Lakshmi took that many forms and wedded the boar god in a fresh shape on each day of the year. The original shrine was raised by the Pallavas in the seventh century, when Thiruvidandai and Mahabalipuram served as their port towns; an inscription of 959 records a lamp gift under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III, and Chola epigraphs credit Raja Raja I with founding the Panguni Uthiram festival in 1003, Rajadhiraja with additions in 1052 and Kulothunga I with further gifts in 1115. Built in the Dravidian style and following the Tenkalai mode of worship, the temple holds the Chittirai Brahmotsavam and Vaikuntha Ekadashi as its principal yearly festivals.
zh: 尼搋羯耶那·闭卢末神庙位于今泰米尔纳德邦钦格尔珀德县的沿海村庄蒂鲁维丹代，供奉毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃：主神称尼搋羯耶那·闭卢末，配偶吉祥天女称科马拉瓦利·塔亚尔。它是毗湿奴派108处迪维亚·德萨姆圣地之一，名列阿尔瓦尔圣徒的泰米尔语赞歌总集《纳拉伊拉·迪维亚·普拉班达姆》。庙名意为“永远的新郎”：相传筏罗诃与阿修罗王金目鏖战千年将其诛杀，用獠牙把沉没的大地托出海面；仙人迦罗伐恳求他迎娶自己的三百六十个女儿，吉祥天女便化出三百六十种身形，一年之中每天以一副新容貌与野猪神成婚。神庙最初由帕拉瓦王朝于7世纪修建，当时蒂鲁维丹代与马哈巴利普兰同为其港口城镇；959年的铭文记载罗湿陀罗拘陀王克里希纳三世敬献灯明，朱罗碑刻则记录罗阇罗阇一世于1003年创设潘古尼·乌蒂拉姆节、罗贾迪罗阇于1052年扩建、俱卢通伽一世于1115年再施供养。神庙为达罗毗荼风格，遵斯利毗湿奴派南支腾卡莱仪轨，每年以吉蒂赖月婆罗摩大节和毗恭吒厄卡达西节最为隆重。

en: Olympia is a sanctuary of Zeus in the Peloponnese, in the territory of Elis, where the Olympic Games were held every four years. Tradition dates the first games to 776 BC, and the sacred precinct, called the Altis, grew up around the tomb of the hero Pelops and an early altar of Zeus. The Temple of Hera was built around 600 BC, and the mid-fifth-century BC Temple of Zeus housed the gigantic chryselephantine statue of the god made by Pheidias, whose workshop stood beside the sanctuary. Treasuries of the Greek city-states lined the precinct, and the games drew crowds under the protection of an Olympic truce. Under Rome the festival was opened to all citizens of the empire, but the last ancient Olympiad was celebrated in 393 AD, shortly before the Christian emperor Theodosius I banned pagan cults; the Temple of Zeus was destroyed around 426, and floods buried the site in the seventh century. It lay forgotten until the English antiquarian Richard Chandler rediscovered it in 1766, and French and German excavators uncovered the ruins from 1829 onward.
zh: 奥林匹亚是伯罗奔尼撒半岛伊利斯境内供奉宙斯的圣地，奥林匹克运动会每四年在此举行。传统上把首届赛会定在公元前776年；名为阿尔提斯的圣区围绕英雄珀罗普斯的坟墓和一座早期宙斯祭坛发展起来。赫拉神庙建于约公元前600年，公元前5世纪中叶的宙斯神庙中安放着菲狄亚斯制作的巨型黄金象牙宙斯像，他的工坊就设在圣区旁。希腊各城邦的宝库沿圣区排列，赛会在奥林匹克休战的庇护下吸引各地人群前来。罗马统治时期，节庆向帝国所有公民开放，但最后一届古代奥运会于393年举行，不久基督教皇帝狄奥多西一世下令禁止异教崇拜；宙斯神庙约于426年被毁，7世纪的洪水又将遗址埋没。它就此湮没无闻，直到1766年英国古董商理查德·钱德勒重新发现此地，1829年起法国和德国的考古队相继发掘出这片废墟。

en: Mount Olympos is the great massif on the ancient border of Thessaly and Macedonia, whose highest summit, Mytikas, rises to nearly three thousand metres, the highest peak in Greece. In Greek belief it was the home of the Twelve Olympian gods and the throne of Zeus above the clouds, and Homer already speaks of it as the seat of the gods; the nine Muses were placed on its northern foothills in Pieria. Pilgrims climbed the peaks to sacrifice, and pottery, coins and ashes dated to around 400 BC have been found on the summit, while a sanctuary of Zeus stood on the peak of Aghios Antonios. At the eastern foot lay Dion, the sacred city of the Macedonians, dedicated to Zeus and the Twelve, which flourished from the fifth century BC to the fifth century AD. Plutarch and, later, Augustine both remarked that letters and offerings left on the summit survived wind and rain for years. Under Ottoman rule the mountain became a refuge of klephts and armatoloi, and in the sixteenth century the chapel of Prophet Elias was built on one of its high peaks.
zh: 奥林波斯山是横亘在色萨利与马其顿古边界上的巨大山体，最高峰米蒂卡斯峰海拔近三千米，为希腊第一高峰。在希腊人的信仰中，这里是奥林匹斯十二主神的居所，是宙斯凌驾云端的王座；荷马史诗已将其称为众神的座殿，九位缪斯女神的居处则被安排在北麓的皮埃里亚。朝圣者攀上山峰献祭，山顶已发现约公元前400年的陶器、钱币和灰烬，圣安东尼峰上还建有一座宙斯神庙。东麓的迪翁是马其顿人的圣城，供奉宙斯和十二主神，从公元前5世纪一直兴盛到公元5世纪。普鲁塔克以及后来的奥古斯丁都曾提到，留在山顶的字迹和祭品历经多年风吹雨打仍完好无损。奥斯曼统治时期，此山成为山贼克莱夫特和民兵武装阿尔马托利的藏身之地；16世纪，人们又在一座高峰上建起了先知以利亚礼拜堂。

en: In the remote Siwa Oasis of Egypt's Western Desert, some five hundred kilometres west of the Nile, stood the oracle of Amun, which the Greeks called Ammonium and knew as the shrine of Zeus Ammon, equating the ram-headed Egyptian god with their own Zeus while the Romans later called him Jupiter Ammon. Greek settlers from Cyrene made contact with the sanctuary in the seventh century BC, and Herodotus, who knew its spring as the Fountain of the Sun, was told the cult image there took the form of a ram. The oracle's fame was such that in about 525 BC the Persian king Cambyses II sent an army of fifty thousand men across the desert to subdue it; according to Herodotus the whole force vanished in a sandstorm, the legend of the Lost Army of Cambyses. Its greatest visitor came in 331 BC, when Alexander the Great crossed the waterless desert, supposedly guided by birds, and the priests of Ammon greeted him as the son of the god and confirmed him as legitimate pharaoh of Egypt; the Horns of Ammon then became a standard emblem of his image. Under the Ptolemies the sanctuary retained its prestige, but by the time of Strabo and Diodorus Siculus its influence had waned, and with the Christianisation of the late Roman Empire the oracle fell silent, leaving the ruined temple among the oasis palms.
zh: 阿蒙神谕所坐落于埃及西部沙漠深处的锡瓦绿洲，在尼罗河以西约五百公里处。希腊人把这里称为阿摩尼乌姆，视之为宙斯·阿蒙的圣所：他们将这位长着公羊头的埃及神等同于自己的宙斯，罗马人后来则称他为朱庇特·阿蒙。公元前7世纪，来自昔兰尼的希腊定居者与这座圣所建立了联系；希罗多德知道这里有一处被他称为“太阳泉”的泉水，并听当地人说神像呈公羊之形。神谕所声名远播，以至于公元前525年前后，波斯国王冈比西斯二世派遣五万大军横穿沙漠前去征服；据希罗多德记载，这支军队在沙暴中全军覆没，从此留下“冈比西斯失踪的军队”的传说。它最显赫的来访者是亚历山大大帝：公元前331年，他据称由飞鸟引路穿过无水的沙漠，阿蒙的祭司们以神之子的身份迎接他，并确认他为埃及的合法法老，“阿蒙之角”此后成为他形象的固定标志。托勒密王朝时期圣所仍保有威望，但到斯特拉波和西西里的狄奥多罗斯的时代，其影响力已经衰落；随着罗马帝国晚期基督教化，神谕终告沉寂，只剩神庙残迹立于绿洲的棕榈树间。

en: The cathedral of the Holy Saviour in Oviedo is the great shrine church of Asturias in northern Spain. King Fruela I founded it in 781, and his son Alfonso II, who made Oviedo the capital of the Asturian kingdom, enlarged it after 802 and established the see in 810. Beside it Alfonso raised the Cámara Santa, the Holy Chamber, to hold the relics carried north from Toledo when the Moors overran the south in 718: the bloodstained Sudarium venerated as the cloth that covered the head of Christ, kept in the silver-bound Arca Santa, together with the Cross of the Angels, the Victory Cross and the Agate Box. On 14 March 1075 King Alfonso VI, his sister and Rodrigo Díaz, the Cid, opened the relic chest after days of fasting. The twelfth-century bishop and chronicler Pelagius restored the church, and the present Gothic cathedral was begun in 1388 under Bishop Gutierre; its tall tower went up in 1528 and was finished with its octagonal spire in the mid-sixteenth century.
zh: 奥维耶多的圣救主主教座堂是西班牙北部阿斯图里亚斯最重要的圣所。781年，弗鲁埃拉一世国王创建了它；其子阿方索二世把奥维耶多定为阿斯图里亚斯王国的都城，802年后扩建教堂，并于810年设立主教区。阿方索还在教堂旁建起圣室，用来收藏718年摩尔人席卷南方时从托莱多北运的圣物：其中有被敬为基督裹头之巾、带血渍的奥维耶多圣巾，安放在包银的圣柜之中，同藏的还有天使十字、胜利十字和玛瑙盒。1075年3月14日，阿方索六世国王、他的妹妹和“熙德”罗德里戈·迪亚斯在数日斋戒后共同开启了圣物箱。12世纪时，主教兼编年史家佩拉吉乌斯修缮了教堂；现存的哥特式主教座堂于1388年在古铁雷主教主持下动工，高塔建于1528年，并在16世纪中期装上八角形尖顶后竣工。

en: Pagan, on the east bank of the Irrawaddy in central Burma, was the capital of the first kingdom to unite the lands that became Myanmar. Burman settlers moving down from the Nanzhao realm founded the walled city in the ninth century, and from 1044 it served as the seat of the Pagan kings. From the mid-eleventh century those rulers gave their patronage to Theravada Buddhism, and over two and a half centuries they and their wealthy subjects raised more than ten thousand stupas, temples and monasteries across the surrounding plain, with the greatest building boom between 1150 and 1200. Pagan became a cosmopolitan center of Pali learning, drawing monks and students from India, Sri Lanka and the Khmer Empire, although Mahayana, Hindu and nat traditions continued alongside Theravada. Repeated Mongol invasions from 1277 onward brought the kingdom down in 1287, and in 1297 Pagan ceased to be the capital of Upper Burma. It lived on as a pilgrimage town: a score of great temples such as the Ananda and Shwezigon kept their devotees, and Konbaung kings of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries sponsored fresh renovations.
zh: 蒲甘城位于缅甸中部伊洛瓦底江东岸，是首个统一今日缅甸诸地的王国——蒲甘王国的都城。9世纪，从南诏故地南迁的缅人建起这座城墙环绕的城市；1044年起，它成为蒲甘诸王的王都。11世纪中叶起，诸王扶持上座部佛教，在两个半世纪里，王室与富有的臣民在周围平原上修建了上万座佛塔、寺院与僧院，营建高潮在1150至1200年间。蒲甘也是巴利语学术的国际中心，吸引来自印度、斯里兰卡和高棉帝国的学僧，不过大乘佛教、印度教与本土纳特信仰仍与上座部并存。1277年起蒙古军队多次入侵，蒲甘王国于1287年崩溃，1297年蒲甘正式不再是上缅甸的都城。此后它作为朝圣城镇延续下来：阿难陀寺、瑞喜宫塔等二十来座大寺始终香火不断，18至19世纪的贡榜诸王还出资对它们一再重修。

en: The Palitana temples crown the twin ridges of Shatrunjaya hill above the town of Palitana in southern Gujarat and form the holiest pilgrimage complex of the Svetambara tradition of Jainism. Jains hold that the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha, also called Adinatha, delivered his first sermon on this hill and that twenty-three of the twenty-four Tirthankaras sanctified it with their visits, while his first disciple Pundarika attained nirvana here, giving the hill its older name of Pundarikgiri. The earliest shrines date to the eleventh century, and a marble image of Pundarika was consecrated as early as 1120; the fourteenth-century texts Shatrunjaya Mahatmya and Vividha Tirtha Kalpa already celebrated the site's legends and listed its many shrines. Nearly nine hundred temples, grouped into nine fortified enclosures called tuks, now cluster along the ridges, built in the ornate Maru-Gurjara style of the Solanki school in white marble; the Adinatha temple, whose hall was renovated in 1157, is the principal shrine, while the four-faced Chaumukh temple was raised in 1616. Repeated damage and rebuilding, especially from the sixteenth century onward, gave the complex its present dense fabric, and with Shikharji, Girnar, Dilwara and Ashtapad it numbers among the five great Svetambara pilgrimage places. No one, priest or pilgrim, may spend the night on the sacred hill.
zh: 波利多拿寺坐落于古吉拉特南部巴利塔纳镇上方沙特伦贾亚山的两道山脊上，是耆那教白衣派最神圣的朝圣建筑群。耆那教信众相信，第一代祖师勒舍婆那陀（又称阿底那特）曾在此山初转法轮，二十四祖中有二十三位曾登临此地使之成圣，他的首弟子蓬达哩迦更在此证得涅槃，此山因而旧名蓬达哩迦山。山上最早的殿宇可追溯至11世纪，1120年便有蓬达哩迦大理石像开光；14世纪的《沙特伦贾亚颂》与《诸圣地劫》已在颂扬此地的传说并逐一记载各处神龛。现存近九百座庙宇分成九座带围墙的图克群，沿山脊密布，以白色大理石按索兰基派繁复的马鲁-古吉拉特风格建成；主殿阿底那特寺的拜殿早在1157年便经历重修，四面造像的朝穆基寺则建于1616年。神庙屡遭损毁又反复重建，尤以16世纪以后的营建最盛，遂成连绵成片的面貌；它与尸佉罗时、耆栗那罗山、地利缚罗寺、阿湿塔婆陀并称白衣派五大圣地。按照规矩，无论祭司还是朝圣者，皆不得在圣山上过夜。

en: The Pandava Thoothar Perumal Temple, also called Thirupadagam, stands in Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu and is dedicated to Krishna as the Pandavas' envoy. Its legend retells the Mahabharata episode in which Krishna went to the Kaurava court to negotiate for the Pandavas: when Duryodhana tried to seize him from a pit hidden beneath his seat, Krishna revealed his cosmic vishvarupa form to the whole court and to the blind king Dhritarashtra. One of the hundred and eight Divya Desams sung by the Alvar saints between the 6th and 9th centuries, it ranks among the three oldest Vishnu temples of Kanchipuram and was probably built under the Pallavas in the late 700s. Chola inscriptions of the 1000s, from the reigns of Rajadhiraja and Kulothunga Chola I, record gifts of lamps, cows and gardens, and later Vijayanagara rulers added to its halls. The temple is built in the Dravidian style with a four-tiered gopuram, and its chief festival is Krishna Janmashtami.
zh: 般度族闭卢末神庙又名“底鲁帕达加姆”，位于泰米尔纳德的甘吉布勒姆，供奉作为般度族使者的奎师那。其传说重述了《摩诃婆罗多》中奎师那出使俱卢族朝堂为般度族斡旋的情节：难敌在座位下暗设陷阱企图擒拿他，奎师那当朝向盲王持国及群臣显现了宇宙相“毗湿瓦鲁帕”。该庙是6至9世纪阿尔瓦尔派圣徒颂唱的一百零八座迪维亚·德萨姆之一，也是甘吉布勒姆最古老的三座毗湿奴庙之一，可能建于8世纪末的帕拉瓦王朝时期。庙墙上留有11世纪拉贾迪拉贾和俱卢东伽·朱罗一世时期的铭文，记载信众布施灯油、牛只和园林之事，后来的维查耶纳伽尔统治者又增建了殿宇。整庙为达罗毗荼风格，立有四层门楼，最重要的节庆是奎师那诞辰节。

en: The Panniyur Sri Varahamurthy Temple at Kumbidi, near Ponnani in northern Kerala, is dedicated to Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, enthroned with the earth goddess Bhumi, and is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethras of the Vaishnava tradition. Kerala tradition calls it the first temple of the land: after the warrior-sage Parashurama reclaimed the country from the sea, runs the legend, Vishnu bade him worship his boar form, and Parashurama consecrated the image with his own hands. The shrine is said to have held primacy in Kerala for some thirteen centuries, from roughly 800 BC to 600 AD, and stone engravings found at Panniyur record a thousand-member body called the Panniyuraayiram that ran its religious rites and festivals, evidence of the temple's early-medieval wealth and regional influence. It also features in the legend of Perumthachan, the master carpenter of Kerala folklore: set to rebuild the sanctum, he cast down his chisel and measuring rod when the work was done, and the two tools were kept at the temple as relics.
zh: 般尼逾剌室利筏罗诃化身神庙位于喀拉拉北部蓬纳尼附近的昆比迪，供奉毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃，主神与大地女神布弥并坐，被列为毗湿奴派108处阿比摩纳圣地之一。喀拉拉传统称它是本地第一座神庙：相传圣仙持斧罗摩从海中辟出喀拉拉之地后，毗湿奴命他敬拜自己的野猪化身，持斧罗摩便亲手为神像开光。传说从约公元前800年到公元600年的一千三百年间，筏罗诃化身一直被尊为喀拉拉的至高神祇；在般尼逾剌发现的石刻还记录了一个名为“般尼逾罗伊拉姆”的千人团体，负责操办神庙的祭仪与节庆，足见其在中世纪早期的财富和地区影响。喀拉拉民间传说中的木匠祖师佩鲁姆塔昌也曾在此现身：他受托重修圣所，完工后弃凿尺而去，这两件工具后来作为圣物珍藏庙中。

en: Parshuram Kund is a Hindu shrine and sacred bathing pool on the Lohit River in the eastern Himalayan foothills, near Sadiya, which in 1337 lay at the heart of the Chutia kingdom. It is dedicated to Parashurama, the axe-wielding sixth avatar of Vishnu; pilgrims hold that a dip in its waters washes away sin, and the great annual gathering takes place at Makar Sankranti in January, when devotees and sadhus travel there from Assam, Manipur and Nepal. Brahmanical Vaishnavism took root at the Chutia court in the late fourteenth century, and the shrine kept drawing pilgrims after the Ahom kingdom overran Sadiya in 1523 and 1524, when the region passed under Ahom rule.
zh: 持斧罗摩池桥是洛希特河畔的印度教圣地与圣沐浴池，地处喜马拉雅山东麓、萨地亚附近，1337年时这里是楚蒂亚王国的核心地带。它供奉毗湿奴的第六化身、手持战斧的持斧罗摩；信众相信在池水中沐浴可涤除罪业，每年一月的马克尔桑克兰蒂节期间举行盛大集会，来自阿萨姆、曼尼普尔和尼泊尔的信众与苦行僧远道而来。14世纪末，婆罗门教的毗湿奴信仰在楚蒂亚宫廷扎根；1523—1524年阿洪姆王国攻占萨地亚，此地归入阿洪姆治下，而这座神庙仍持续吸引朝圣者。

en: The Parthasarathy Temple stands in Thiruvallikeni, the lily-pond quarter of Madras, and is dedicated to Krishna in his role as Parthasarathy, the charioteer of Arjuna in the Mahabharata; its image, unique among Vishnu icons in bearing a moustache, also shows the wound left by Bhishma's arrow on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. A Pallava foundation of the sixth century, traditionally credited to King Narasimhavarman I, it was enlarged under the Cholas and carries Tamil inscriptions of the Pallava king Dantivarman from the early ninth century. The Alvar saints sang of it in their Tamil hymns, and it ranks among the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desams. Vijayanagara rulers added pillared halls and sub-shrines in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, and a restoration of 1564 gave the temple much of its present form under the Tenkalai Vaishnava tradition. After Madras passed to the East India Company, the surrounding village was leased in the 1670s to Kasi Viranna, the Company's chief merchant; from 1789 the Board of Revenue supervised temple funds, until Regulation VII of 1817 and an order of 1821 withdrew the collector from its management.
zh: 阿周那之御者奎师那神庙位于马德拉斯的提鲁瓦利凯尼，意为百合池塘一带，供奉在《摩诃婆罗多》中为阿周那驾车的奎师那，尊号帕塔萨拉蒂；庙中神像留着胡须，在毗湿奴神像中独一无二，身上还带有俱卢之野战场上毗湿摩箭矢留下的伤痕。神庙始建于6世纪，相传为帕拉瓦国王纳拉辛哈跋摩一世所建，朱罗时期加以扩建，庙中保存着9世纪初帕拉瓦国王丹提跋摩的泰米尔文铭文。阿尔瓦尔圣人们在泰米尔语圣诗中歌咏此庙，它也位列毗湿奴派108座圣庙之一。15至16世纪，毗奢耶那伽罗诸王增建了柱厅与配殿，1564年的一次大修奠定了现存的格局，庙务遵奉毗湿奴派滕卡莱传统。马德拉斯落入英国东印度公司之手后，庙旁村落于17世纪70年代租给公司首席商人卡西·维兰纳；1789年起税务委员会监管庙产，直到1817年第七号条例和1821年的命令使地方税务官退出庙务管理。

en: The Parthenon is the temple of Athena on the Acropolis of Athens, the supreme monument of fifth-century BC Greek architecture. An earlier temple begun after the Battle of Marathon was still unfinished when the Persians sacked Athens and levelled the Acropolis in 480 BC. The present building was raised under Pericles between 447 and 438 BC, from designs by Iktinos and Callicrates, with sculpture directed by Pheidias; its cella housed his colossal chryselephantine Athena Parthenos, and the rear chamber held the treasury of the Delian League. In the final decade of the sixth century AD it became a church of the Virgin Mary, and under Latin rule it served as a Catholic church. After the Ottoman conquest of Athens in 1458 it was turned into a mosque, complete with a minaret, and survived largely intact until 26 September 1687, when a Venetian mortar shell ignited the Turkish gunpowder store and blew the centre apart. Lord Elgin removed about half of the surviving sculptures between 1801 and 1812, and after Greece took Athens in 1832 the minaret and later additions were cleared away.
zh: 帕特农神庙是雅典卫城上供奉雅典娜的神庙，是公元前5世纪希腊建筑的巅峰之作。马拉松战役后动工的早期神庙尚未完工，便在公元前480年波斯人洗劫雅典、铲平卫城时被毁。现存建筑建于伯里克利执政时期，公元前447年开工、前438年落成，由伊克蒂诺斯与卡利克拉特设计，雕刻由菲狄亚斯主持；内殿安放着他制作的巨型黄金象牙雅典娜·帕特农像，后殿则储存提洛同盟的金库。6世纪最后十年，它被改为供奉圣母马利亚的教堂，拉丁人统治时期又成为天主教堂。1458年奥斯曼征服雅典后，它被改建为清真寺并添建宣礼塔，大体完好地保存到1687年9月26日——那天威尼斯人的迫击炮弹引爆了土耳其人的火药库，炸塌了建筑中央。1801至1812年间，埃尔金伯爵运走了约半数幸存雕刻；1832年希腊收复雅典后，宣礼塔和后世添建的建筑被清除。

en: The Pathirakali Amman Temple is a Hindu shrine in Trincomalee on the east coast of Sri Lanka, dedicated to Bhadrakali, a fierce form of the goddess Kali. It forms the Kali temple of the ancient Koneswaram temple compound, the easternmost of the five Pancha Ishwaram Shiva shrines of the island, and is built in the classical Tamil style. Tamil tradition counts it among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas, marking the place where the goddess's waist fell; the Tantra Chudamani list of fifty-one peethas instead places her anklets there. Pilgrims visited before the eleventh century, and the Chola emperor Rajendra I enlarged the shrine early in that century, leaving an inscription still displayed on the premises. Together with Koneswaram it takes part in the annual Ther Thiruvillah procession. When the Portuguese destroyed the Koneswaram complex between 1622 and 1624 and built a fort from its rubble, some of the original idols were installed in a new temple built in 1632, while the Amman shrine continued to be venerated as the seat of the peetha.
zh: 贤迦梨母神庙位于今斯里兰卡东海岸的亭可马里，供奉迦梨女神的凶相化身巴德拉迦梨，是古代科内斯瓦拉姆神庙群中的迦梨神殿；该庙群是岛上五处伊什瓦拉姆湿婆圣庙中位置最东的一座，建筑采用古典泰米尔风格。泰米尔传统把它列入十八处大性力圣地，传说女神的腰肢坠落于此；怛特罗典籍所列的五十一座圣地名单则称坠落于此的是女神的脚镯。11世纪以前已有香客前来，朱罗皇帝拉金德拉一世在11世纪初大规模扩建此庙，他留下的铭文仍陈列庙中。它每年与科内斯瓦拉姆神庙共同举行提鲁维拉节游行。1622至1624年间葡萄牙人摧毁科内斯瓦拉姆庙群，并用其残料修建堡垒，部分原始神像被移入1632年新建的庙宇，而这座安曼神殿仍作为性力圣地受人礼拜。

en: Pella, in the marshy lowlands of Lower Macedonia beside the Thermaic Gulf, was raised from a modest town into the capital of the Macedonian kingdom by Archelaus I around 400 BC, while the old capital Aigai kept its role as the royal burial ground. Euripides spent his last years at the new court and staged the Bacchae there, and in the following centuries Pella was the birthplace of Philip II in 382 BC and of Alexander the Great in 356 BC. Religion followed the crown: the Argead kings claimed descent from Heracles and ultimately from Zeus, and acted themselves as high priests and patrons of the kingdom's cults; within the grid-planned city stood temples of Aphrodite, Cybele and Demeter, and its pebble mosaics show Dionysus riding a leopard. The city was at its richest under Cassander and Antigonus II, and remained the seat of Philip V and Perseus in their wars with Rome. After the defeat at Pydna the Romans sacked Pella in 168 BC and carried its treasury to Italy. An earthquake around 90 BC destroyed much of it, though the Via Egnatia kept the rebuilt town alive; Cicero stopped there in 58 BC, and between 45 and 30 BC it became the colony Colonia Iulia Augusta Pella. Lucian could already call it insignificant around 180 AD, and after a late rename to Diocletianopolis it shrank in Byzantine times to a fortified village.
zh: 佩拉位于下马其顿的沼泽低地、濒临塞尔迈湾，约公元前400年被阿奇拉一世从普通城镇扩建为马其顿王国的新都，旧都埃盖则继续作为王室陵寝所在地。欧里庇得斯在新宫廷度过晚年，《酒神的伴侣》在此首演；此后几个世纪里，腓力二世于公元前382年、亚历山大大帝于公元前356年相继出生于此。宗教与王权相伴：阿吉德王朝自称是赫拉克勒斯的后裔、最终可上溯至宙斯，国王本人兼任王国的最高祭司与各崇拜的赞助人；按方格规划的城中建有阿芙洛狄忒、西布莉和得墨忒耳的神庙，卵石镶嵌画还描绘着骑豹的狄俄尼索斯。城市在卡山德和安提柯二世治下最为富庶，也是腓力五世和珀尔修斯对罗马作战时的都城。皮德纳战败后，罗马人于公元前168年洗劫佩拉，把国库运回意大利。约公元前90年的地震摧毁了大半个城市，但埃格纳提亚大道使重建后的城镇维持生机；西塞罗曾于公元前58年在此停留，公元前45至前30年间它成为罗马殖民地‘尤利亚·奥古斯塔·佩拉’。约180年卢奇安已称它无足轻重，后来一度更名戴克里先诺波利斯，到拜占庭时代缩为一处设防村落。

en: The Altar of Zeus at Pergamon, on a terrace of the acropolis of the Attalid capital in Asia Minor, was raised by King Eumenes II in the first half of the second century BC, after the Treaty of Apamea of 188 BC had made Pergamon the chief power of western Anatolia under Roman protection. Its colossal base, more than thirty-five metres wide, carried the Great Frieze, a high-relief Gigantomachy showing the Olympian gods battling the Giants, while the inner court was ringed by a second frieze on the life of Telephus, son of Heracles and legendary founder of the city; later classical lists counted the altar among the wonders of the world. Its fire altar ceased to be used with the rise of Christianity, and in the seventh century the acropolis was fortified against the Arabs, the monument being partly dismantled for building stone before the Arabs took the city in 716. Pergamon passed to the Turks in the thirteenth century, and in the fifteenth century the humanist Cyriacus of Ancona described the overgrown ruins, while in 1625 agents of the Earl of Arundel carried two frieze panels to England.
zh: 帕加马的宙斯祭坛位于小亚细亚阿塔罗斯王朝都城的卫城台地上，由国王欧迈尼斯二世建于公元前2世纪上半叶。公元前188年的《阿帕米亚条约》使帕加马在罗马庇护下成为安纳托利亚西部的首要强国，祭坛正是这一时期的产物。它宽逾35米的巨大基座上环绕着宏伟的高浮雕饰带，刻画奥林匹斯诸神与巨人厮杀的“巨人之战”；内院则有第二道饰带，讲述赫拉克勒斯之子、城市传说建立者忒勒福斯的生平。后世的古典名录曾把这座祭坛列为世界奇迹之一。随着基督教兴起，祭坛上的圣火祭祀停止；7世纪时卫城为抵御阿拉伯人而加固城防，祭坛在716年阿拉伯人攻陷城市前被部分拆毁，石材挪作他用。13世纪帕加马落入土耳其人之手，15世纪人文主义者安科纳的奇里亚科记述了杂草丛生的废墟；1625年，阿伦德尔伯爵的手下又将两块浮雕饰板运回了英格兰。

en: The Polali Rajarajeshwari Temple is a goddess shrine at Polali in the Tulu-speaking coast of Karnataka, a place called Pural in old Tulu and Paliapura in Sanskrit, where the river bends sharply beside the town. Local inscriptions date the temple around its clay icon to the 700s, and tradition names King Suratha as its builder, said to have offered his own jewelled crown to the goddess, who was known in early records as Porala Devi. The Persian envoy Abdul Razzak, visiting in 1448, described a temple of molten brass raised on four platforms with a five-to-six-foot image whose eyes were red rubies. The principal image now venerated is a ten-foot stucco Rajarajeshwari modelled from clay mixed with herbal compounds, and every twelve years the idols are freshly coated with a medicinal earth in the Lepashta Gandha rite. Smaller shrines honour Subramanya, Bhadrakali, Mahaganapati and Saraswati, while the wooden roof of the entrance hall is carved with figures of the gods and its other roofs are sheeted in copper.
zh: 波罗利·罗阇罗誓湿伐梨神庙位于卡纳塔克讲图卢语的沿海地带，古图卢语称此地为普鲁拉尔，梵语称波利阿普罗，河水流经镇旁急转，或即地名由来。当地铭文显示，环绕泥塑神像的庙宇建于8世纪；传说建庙者是苏拉陀王，他曾把自己镶满宝石的王冠献给女神，早期文献中女神被称为波罗罗提毗。1448年波斯使节阿卜杜勒·拉扎克到访时，记载此庙以熔铜筑成、立于四层台基之上，五六尺高的神像双目嵌有红宝石。现存的主像是一尊10尺高的罗阇罗誓湿伐梨灰泥像，以拌有草药的黏土塑成；每隔12年还要在“勒帕什塔·甘陀”仪式中用药泥为诸神像重新敷身。配殿供奉室建陀、巴德拉迦梨、大象头神与辩才天女；门厅木顶雕满诸神形象，其余殿顶则覆以铜板。

en: Prayag, the ancient name of the city later called Allahabad and present-day Prayagraj, lies beside the Triveni Sangam, the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna with the invisible, mythical Sarasvati. Its Sanskrit name means place of sacrifice, for tradition holds that Brahma performed the first sacrifice there, and a dip at the sangam in the month of Magha is praised in the Mahabharata and the Puranas as washing away sin and winning heaven. The annual Magh Mela held on these banks is the oldest of the great Indian bathing festivals; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang described in 644 the vast quinquennial assembly held there by King Harsha, with crowds of pilgrims bathing at the river junction. Through the sultanate and Mughal periods the fair continued, and Akbar built his Allahabad fort overlooking the sangam; by the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries it was organised by the akharas, the armed bands of Hindu ascetics, whose rival claims to bathe first at the most auspicious moment sometimes ended in bloody clashes. The great twelve-yearly Kumbh gathering of later times grew out of this ancient Magh Mela.
zh: 普拉亚格是这座城市的古名，后称安拉阿巴德，即今普拉亚格拉吉；城旁便是特里韦尼桑加姆——恒河、亚穆纳河与隐而不见的神话之河萨拉斯瓦蒂河的三河汇流处。其梵语名意为“祭祀之地”，相传梵天曾在此举行第一场祭祀；《摩诃婆罗多》和诸往世书都称，在摩伽月于汇流处沐浴可洗清罪孽、得升天界。河畔一年一度的摩伽节是印度最古老的大型沐浴节会：644年，中国求法僧玄奘在《大唐西域记》中记载了戒日王在此举行的无遮大会，以及成群朝圣者在河口沐浴的盛况。进入苏丹国与莫卧儿时期后节会依旧延续，阿克巴还在俯瞰汇流处修建了安拉阿巴德城堡；到17、18世纪，节会由印度教苦行僧的武装僧团“阿哈拉”主持，各僧团为争取在最吉祥的时刻最先沐浴而相争，有时酿成流血冲突。后世那场十二年一度的大壶节盛会，正是从这一古老的摩伽节发展而来。

en: The Prophet's Mosque in Medina is the second holiest site of Islam after the Sacred Mosque of Mecca. Muhammad himself built it in 622, after the hijra, on land bought from two orphans and paid for by his companion Abu Ayyub al-Ansari; the original open-air building of palm trunks and beaten clay served at once as a place of prayer, a law court and a school. The Umayyad caliph al-Walid I rebuilt it on a grand scale between 705 and 715 with Byzantine materials and craftsmen, bringing the graves of Muhammad and of the first two caliphs, Abu Bakr and Umar, within its walls. In 1279 the Mamluk sultan Qalawun raised a wooden dome over the prophet's tomb, rebuilt in stone under Qaitbay in the fifteenth century and again under the Ottoman sultan Mahmud II in 1817; this is the Green Dome, the mosque's most famous landmark. Suleiman the Magnificent renewed its walls and minarets, and the marble minbar of Murad III dates to 1590. When Wahhabi forces held Medina between 1805 and 1813 they stripped the tomb of its ornaments but spared the dome.
zh: 先知清真寺位于麦地那，是伊斯兰教仅次于麦加禁寺的第二大圣寺。622年穆罕默德迁徙麦地那后亲自兴建，地基购自两名孤儿，由其弟子艾布·阿尤布·安萨里出资；最初是棕榈木梁柱、夯土屋顶的露天建筑，兼作礼拜场所、法庭和学校。伍麦叶哈里发瓦利德一世于705至715年间征调拜占庭材料和工匠大举重建，将穆罕默德以及前两任哈里发阿布·伯克尔、欧麦尔的陵墓纳入寺内。1279年马穆鲁克苏丹嘉拉温在先知墓上建起木构穹顶，15世纪卡伊特拜时期改为石构，1817年奥斯曼苏丹马哈茂德二世再次重建，这便是寺内最著名的标志绿穹顶。苏莱曼大帝翻修了寺墙和宣礼塔，穆拉德三世的大理石宣讲台则建于1590年。1805至1813年瓦哈比派占据麦地那期间，墓上装饰被剥除，但穹顶得以幸免。

en: The Pyramid of the Magician is the tallest and most famous monument of Uxmal, a great Maya city of the Puuc Hills in western Yucatan that held perhaps 25,000 people at its height. Work on the first temple pyramid began in the sixth century, and for four hundred years successive builders wrapped older temples inside new ones, giving the structure its unusual elliptical base and steep, rounded sides. Its upper temples blend Puuc and Chenes styles, their doorways framed by giant masks of the rain god Chaac, and the western stairway is aligned to face the setting sun at the summer solstice. Maya folk legend, recorded after the Spanish conquest, held that no mortal hands raised it: a magician-god, Itzamna, was said to have built it in a single night, while another tale told of a dwarf hatched from an egg who built the pyramid overnight to save his life and then ruled Uxmal. The city's great building age ended around 1000, after which the pyramid fell into ruin, and during the Spanish conquest of Yucatan it was looted and left to the forest, its old cult long silent.
zh: 魔法师金字塔是乌斯马尔最高、最著名的建筑。乌斯马尔是尤卡坦西部普克丘陵的玛雅大城，极盛时约有2.5万人。最早的神庙金字塔于6世纪动工，此后四百年间，历代建造者把旧神庙层层包裹在新建筑之内，形成它独特的椭圆形底座和陡峭圆弧形侧面。上层神庙融合普克风格与切内斯风格，门道由雨神恰克的巨大面具环绕，西阶梯的朝向正对着夏至日的落日。西班牙征服后记录下来的玛雅民间传说称，此塔并非凡人所建：一说魔法之神伊察姆纳一夜之间将它造成，另一说讲一个从蛋中孵出的矮人为保命连夜建起金字塔，随后统治了乌斯马尔。乌斯马尔的大兴土木时代在1000年前后终结，金字塔随之倾颓；西班牙征服尤卡坦期间它遭劫掠，被弃于丛林之中，古老的崇拜早已沉寂。

en: Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez began as a mosque founded in 857 or 859 by Fatima al-Fihri, the daughter of a wealthy merchant whose family had migrated to Fez from Kairouan, which gave the institution its name. In 919 or 933 the Friday sermon was transferred to it, making it the chief mosque of the city, and it grew into one of the leading centres of learning of the Islamic world. The Almoravids greatly expanded the building, and the earliest clear evidence of regular teaching there dates to 1121. Under the Almohad sultan Muhammad al-Nasir, between 1199 and 1213, it received the great bronze chandelier that still hangs in its prayer hall, counted among the finest of the western Islamic world. The Marinid period marked its intellectual apogee: the water clocks and the Dar al-Muwaqqit timekeeper's chamber served its astronomers, a chandelier cast from a church bell brought from Gibraltar was installed in 1337, and Sultan Abu Inan founded its library in 1349. Besides the Quran and Maliki law, its curriculum covered grammar, logic, medicine, mathematics, astronomy and geography, drawing students from across Morocco and Muslim West Africa.
zh: 非斯的卡拉维因最初是一座清真寺，857年或859年由富商之女法蒂玛·菲赫里出资修建，她的家族从凯鲁万迁居非斯，这座学府也因此得名。919年或933年，周五聚礼的讲道转移到此，它由此成为全城的主麻清真寺，并逐步成长为伊斯兰世界首屈一指的学术中心之一。穆拉比特王朝大规模扩建了建筑，关于寺内常规教学最早的明确记载出现在1121年。穆瓦希德王朝苏丹穆罕默德·纳西尔在位期间（1199—1213年），寺中添置了巨大的青铜吊灯，它高悬于礼拜殿内，被视为西方伊斯兰世界最精美的吊灯之一。马林王朝时期是它学术上的巅峰：水钟和授时室为天文学家服务，1337年又安装了用从直布罗陀带回的教堂铜钟改铸的吊灯，苏丹阿布·伊南于1349年敕建了图书馆。除《古兰经》和马立克派教法外，其课程还涵盖语法、逻辑、医学、数学、天文和地理，吸引着摩洛哥各地和穆斯林西非的学生。

en: Nevado Queva, or Quewar, is a volcano in the Andes of northwestern Argentina, rising to 6,140 metres as the highest peak of the Nevados de los Pastos Grandes. Its broad summit crater holds extensive pre-Columbian ruins, including a large stone platform raised by the Incas after the southern Andes were drawn into the Inca province of Qullasuyu: Topa Inca Yupanqui, who ruled from 1471 to 1493, subdued the Qulla people, and the Argentine northwest was fully absorbed under his successor Huayna Capac. In Andean religion high peaks were venerated as apu, mountain spirits held to protect the communities below and to receive offerings, and the Inca state placed shrines on their summits to anchor its rule over the highlands. Quewar's crater sanctuary belongs to this cult of sacred mountains, which also practised high-altitude child sacrifice on its most revered peaks.
zh: 奎瓦尔圣山是阿根廷西北部安第斯山脉中的一座火山，海拔6140米，为洛斯帕斯托斯格兰德斯火山群的最高峰。其宽阔的山顶火山口内留有大量前哥伦布时期遗迹，包括印加人修筑的一座巨型石砌平台。南部安第斯被并入印加的科利亚苏尤行省后，1471至1493年在位的图帕克·印卡·尤潘基征服了科利亚人，阿根廷西北部则在其继承人瓦伊纳·卡帕克治下被彻底吞并。在安第斯传统中，高耸的山峰被尊为“阿普”，即护佑山下社群、接受献祭的山神，印加政权还在山顶营建神龛，以巩固对高原的统治。奎瓦尔的火山口圣所便属于这一圣山崇拜，该崇拜还会在最受尊崇的山峰上举行高空童祭。

en: Quri Kancha, meaning golden temple in Cusco Quechua and originally called Intikancha or Intiwasi, was the foremost sanctuary of the Inca Empire and the principal shrine of Inti, the sun god and divine ancestor of the Inca dynasty, standing at the heart of the capital Cusco. The emperor Pachakuti rebuilt it in the fifteenth century, facing its curved walls with sheets of gold and filling its courtyard with golden statues and life-size golden plants, while the mummies of seven deceased Incas, adorned with golden masks and bracelets, sat on a golden bench attended by the cloistered Mama-cunas, who wove temple cloth and brewed ritual chicha. Its precisely cut ashlar blocks, fitted without mortar, were meant to display the empire's power to mobilise labour. When the Spanish held Atahualpa for ransom in 1533, much of the gold they demanded came from Quri Kancha; the conquerors then demolished the temple and raised the Church and Convent of Santo Domingo on its foundations, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1650. The Inca stonework survived every quake while the colonial building above it cracked, and the sunken chambers and curved wall of the House of the Sun remained standing beneath the convent.
zh: 库里坎查在库斯科克丘亚语中意为“黄金神庙”，最初称因蒂坎查或因蒂瓦西，是印加帝国最重要的圣所，也是太阳神、印加王朝神圣祖先因蒂的主庙，坐落在都城库斯科的中心。15世纪，皇帝帕查库特克重建此庙，弧形墙面贴满金板，庭院中摆满金像与真人大小的黄金植物；七具已故印加君主的木乃伊佩戴金面具和金镯，安坐在黄金长凳上，由隐居的“妈妈库纳”侍奉——她们纺织祭服、酿造仪式用的奇恰酒。神庙石块经精心琢凿、不用灰浆即严丝合缝，意在展示帝国征调劳力的无上权力。1533年西班牙人囚禁阿塔瓦尔帕索取赎金时，所敛黄金大多来自库里坎查；随后征服者拆毁神庙，在其地基上建起圣多明我教堂与修道院，并在1650年地震后重建。历次地震中，殖民建筑屡屡开裂，印加石墙却安然无恙，太阳神殿的下沉厅堂与弧形高墙仍矗立在修道院之下。

en: The Radha Damodar Temple lies at the foot of the Girnar hills near Junagadh in southern Gujarat, beside the sacred Damodar Kund, where pilgrims bathe and scatter the ashes of the dead in the hope of moksha. Its black-stone image of Damodar, a four-armed form of Krishna holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, stands with Radha at his side, and Vaishnavas regard Damodar as the presiding lord of the whole Girnar pilgrimage. Tradition credits the first installation of the idols to Vajranabha, Krishna's grandson, and a Suryavanshi ruler named Chandraketpur is said to have built the early shrine; it was renovated in 462 under the Gupta emperor Skandagupta. The present pink-sandstone complex, with its inner sanctum, pillared hall of roughly 84 columns and two spires, also houses sub-shrines to Balarama, Revati and Ganesha. In the fifteenth century the Gujarati poet-saint Narsinh Mehta came to bathe in the tank and composed his morning hymns on its banks.
zh: 拉妲奎师那神庙位于古吉拉特南部朱纳格特附近的吉尔纳尔山脚下，紧邻圣湖达莫达尔池，朝圣者在此沐浴、撒下逝者骨灰，以求灵魂解脱。庙中黑石神像为四臂达莫达尔，即奎师那的名号之一，手持法螺、神盘、仙杖与莲花，身旁伴立拉妲；毗湿奴信徒奉达莫达尔为整个吉尔纳尔朝圣地的主神。相传神像最早由奎师那之孙瓦吉拉纳巴安立，日族国王旃陀罗吉德布尔修建了早期祠庙，462年笈多皇帝塞建陀笈多又加以重修。现存建筑群以粉红砂岩筑成，内有圣所、约84根柱子支撑的柱厅和两座尖塔，还附祀巴拉拉马、雷瓦蒂与象头神。15世纪时，古吉拉特语诗人圣女纳尔辛赫·梅赫塔常来池畔沐浴，并在湖边写下他的晨祷诗篇。

en: The Rajagopalaswamy Temple stands at Mannargudi in the Tamil country south of Nagapattinam, and is dedicated to Rajagopalaswamy, Krishna as the royal cowherd, seated with his queens Rukmini and Satyabhama; Hindus also call it Dakshina Dwaraka, the Southern Dwarka, and rank it first among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams. A stone inscription credits the original shrine to Kulothunga Chola I, who reigned from 1070 to 1122, and the town grew up around it under the name Rajadhiraja Chaturvedimangalam. Later Chola kings, including Rajaraja III and Rajendra III, enlarged it, and Hoysala inscriptions and Vijayanagara grants record continued patronage. The Thanjavur Nayaks made it their dynastic shrine: Vijayaraghava Nayak, who ruled from 1634 to 1673, built the present temple, its thousand-pillared hall, the 47-metre main gopuram and the granite enclosure wall praised in Tamil as the beauty of Mannargudi. The vast Haridra Nadhi tank beside it is among the largest temple tanks in India, and Maratha records show the shrine remained richly endowed in later centuries.
zh: 牧童主奎师那神庙位于纳加帕蒂南以南泰米尔地区的曼纳古迪，供奉牧童国王形象的奎师那，尊号罗阇戈帕拉斯瓦米，神像两侧伴立王后鲁格米尼与萨蒂亚巴玛；印度教徒又称它为南德瓦卡，并把它列为108座自重圣地之首。据石刻记载，最早的祠庙由1070至1122年在位的库洛通加·朱罗一世修建，城镇也围绕神庙兴起，当时名为罗贾迪罗阇·查图尔韦迪曼加兰。其后罗阇罗阇三世、罗贞陀罗三世等朱罗国王相继扩建，曷萨拉铭文和毗奢耶那伽罗的赐地文书都记载了持续的供奉。坦贾武尔纳亚克王朝把它立为王室家庙：1634至1673年在位的维贾亚拉加瓦·纳亚克建成现存神庙、千柱厅、47米高的正门门楼和花岗石围墙，那道围墙在泰米尔语中被誉为曼纳古迪之美。庙旁的哈里德拉池是印度最大的庙池之一，马拉塔人的档案也显示这座神庙在其后的世纪里仍拥有丰厚庙产。

en: Ram Janmabhoomi, the birthplace of Rama, lies within the old fortress of Ramkot at Ayodhya, on the Sarayu river in Awadh. The Ramayana presents Ayodhya as the capital of Kosala and the city where Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, was born, and Hindus count it the foremost of India's seven sacred cities. The settlement was known as Saketa in the early centuries and took the name Ayodhya under the Guptas, with devotion to Rama already attested there by inscriptions of the early centuries of the common era.
