In 1337 the city belonged to the Delhi Sultanate, passing in 1394 to the Sharqi rulers of Jaunpur and later to the Lodi kings and the Mughals. In 1528 and 1529 Mir Baqi, a commander of the emperor Babur, built the Babri Masjid on Ramkot; Hindu tradition holds that it replaced a temple marking Rama's birthplace, and devotees continued to worship Rama at a platform beside the mosque, as European travellers and missionaries recorded from the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The site remained one of the great Vaishnava pilgrimage goals of northern India under the Nawabs of Awadh.
zh: 罗摩降诞处位于阿瓦德阿约提亚的罗摩科特古堡之内，地处萨拉育河畔，相传是罗摩的诞生地。《罗摩衍那》称阿约提亚为拘萨罗的都城，也是毗湿奴第七化身罗摩降生之城；在印度教七大圣城中，它位列第一。这座城市早期名为娑枳多，笈多王朝时期改称阿约提亚，公元最初几个世纪的铭文已证明当地存在罗摩崇拜。1337年该城属德里苏丹国，1394年转归江布尔的沙尔吉王朝，其后又先后落入洛迪王朝和莫卧儿手中。1528—1529年，皇帝巴布尔的将领米尔·巴基在罗摩科特修建巴布里清真寺；印度教传统认为它取代了一座标记罗摩诞生地的神庙，信众仍在寺旁的平台上敬拜罗摩，17至18世纪的欧洲旅行家和传教士都留下了相关记载。在阿瓦德的纳瓦卜们治下，此地始终是北印度毗湿奴派最重要的朝圣目的地之一。

en: The Ramanathaswamy Temple occupies the island of Rameswaram at the tip of Tamil Nadu, where the Ramayana says Rama set up and worshipped a Shiva lingam before building his bridge to Lanka, praying for victory over Ravana and asking the god to remain there as the lord of Rama, Rameshvara. The shrine is therefore one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, a Char Dham pilgrimage destination and one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung by the Nayanar saints Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar. The Pandya kings enlarged it in the 1100s and the Sri Lankan ruler Parakrama Bahu aided its sanctum, but in 1311 Malik Kafur's Delhi army sacked the island and destroyed its temples. The Jaffna kings Jeyaveera and Gunaveera Cinkaiariyan rebuilt the sanctum between 1380 and the early 1400s, even ferrying stone from Trincomalee, and the present structure took shape in the 1600s under the Ramnad Sethupathi rajas, whose builders gave it the longest pillared corridor of any Hindu temple in India.
zh: 拉马纳塔斯瓦米神庙位于泰米尔纳德南端的拉梅斯沃勒姆岛。《罗摩衍那》记载，罗摩在此架设通往楞伽的大桥之前，亲手安设并敬拜了一座湿婆林伽，祈求战胜罗波那，并请湿婆永驻此岛，是为“罗摩之主”拉梅什瓦拉。该庙因此位列湿婆十二处林伽圣地、印度教四大朝圣圣地之一，也是纳亚纳尔派圣徒阿帕尔、桑班达尔和孙达拉尔颂唱过的276处“圣歌之地”之一。12世纪潘地亚诸王扩建神庙，斯里兰卡国王波罗迦罗摩巴忽也曾助建圣所；但1311年马利克·卡富尔率领的德里军队洗劫该岛、毁坏神庙。1380年至15世纪初，贾夫纳国王贾亚维拉·辛凯阿里扬与继任者古纳维拉重修圣所，甚至从亭可马里渡海运来石材；今日所见的神庙主要成型于17世纪拉姆纳德的塞图帕蒂王公治下，其修建者为它打造了印度所有印度教神庙中最长的柱廊。

en: The Ramapuram Sree Rama Temple is an ancient Vishnu shrine in Ramapuram village near Pala, in the Kerala hinterland, believed to be roughly a thousand years old and counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnavite tradition. Its sanctum, circular and roofed in copper with a golden finial, houses a four-armed image of Rama facing east, cast in panchaloha, the traditional alloy of five sacred metals. Tradition holds that Rama rested and meditated at this spot during his exile from Ayodhya while searching for Sita, and that his three brothers settled nearby: Lakshmana at Koodapulam, Bharata at Amanakara and Satrughna at Methiri. Their four shrines, all within a few kilometres, form the Nalambalam complex, and a circuit of them in the Karkidaka month, called the Ramayana month, is known as Nalambala Darshanam. A board of three Nambudiri Brahmin houses has long managed the temple's lands and worship.
zh: 拉默布勒姆的罗摩神庙是喀拉拉内陆帕拉附近拉默布勒姆村的一座古老毗湿奴神庙，相传已有约千年历史，被列为毗湿奴派传统的108座自重圣地之一。圆形圣所覆以铜顶、上立金宝瓶，其中供奉面朝东方的四臂罗摩像，神像以五种圣金属合成的五合金铸成。相传罗摩被逐出阿约提亚、寻找悉多时在此歇息禅修，他的三个弟弟也在附近定居：罗什曼那在库达普拉姆，婆罗多在阿默纳卡拉，设睹卢祇那在梅蒂里。四座神庙相距不过数公里，合称四庙群；在卡尔基达卡月，又称《罗摩衍那》月，巡拜四庙的活动称为四庙朝觐。庙产与祭祀长期由三个南布迪里婆罗门家族组成的庙务委员会管理。

en: The Ramchaura Mandir stands at Rambhadra in Hajipur, the town on the north bank of the Ganga opposite Patna, where the Gandak joins the great river. Its central object of worship is a set of footprints: local tradition holds that Rama passed this way on the road to Janakpur in Mithila, where he would win Sita as his bride, and left his footprints here. The name pairs Rama with chaura, the Bhojpuri word for orchid, and the shrine has been tended for centuries by the Bari Sangat, a monastic math whose mahants succeed one another as guru and disciple across more than twenty generations, while antiquities excavated at the site are kept in the Patna Museum. Pilgrims gather above all for Rama Navami, the birthday of Rama, when a small fair is held. In 1337 Hajipur was a ferry village of the Delhi Sultanate's Tirhut; it was fortified and renamed by Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah of Bengal in the mid-fourteenth century, and the armies of Akbar twice stormed it, in 1572 and 1574, while subduing the Karrani rulers of Bengal.
zh: 罗摩兰花神庙位于哈吉普尔的兰巴德拉，该镇坐落在恒河北岸、与巴特那隔河相望，甘达基河便在此汇入恒河。庙中最重要的崇拜对象是一组足印：当地传说罗摩前往弥萨罗的贾纳克布尔、去赢得悉多为妻的途中经过此地，留下了足印。庙名由“罗摩”与博杰普尔语中意为兰花的“乔拉”组成；数百年来，神庙由名为巴里桑伽特的修道道场管理，历代马汉特以师徒相承，已传二十余代，庙址出土的古物则收藏于巴特那博物馆。朝圣者最看重罗摩诞辰节，届时会举办小型庙会。1337年时，哈吉普尔还是德里苏丹国蒂尔胡特境内的一处渡口村落；14世纪中叶，孟加拉的沙姆斯丁·伊利亚斯·沙阿在此筑城并以自己的名字为其命名，阿克巴的军队又在1572和1574年两度攻破此城，以征服孟加拉的卡拉尼王朝统治者。

en: Srirangam, an island town between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers near Tiruchirappalli, holds the foremost of the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desams: the temple of Ranganatha, Vishnu reclining on the serpent Shesha, whom the Tamil Alvar saints glorified in the Divya Prabandham and whom Sri Vaishnavas call simply the Koyil, the temple. Early Chola kings built and rebuilt the shrine, and from the eleventh century the teachers Nathamuni, Yamunacharya and above all Ramanuja made it the headquarters of the Sri Vaishnava tradition, its halls becoming a centre of devotional song and Sanskrit learning. Disaster came with the Delhi Sultanate: Malik Kafur's raid of 1311 carried off the golden image, and the invasion of Muhammad bin Tughluq in 1327 left the temple deserted after a defence in which tradition numbers thirteen thousand devotees dead, so that in 1337 the Ranganatha icon was being carried secretly from village to village while the Madurai Sultanate ruled the land. Only after Kumara Kampana's Vijayanagara forces overthrew that sultanate was the image reinstalled in 1371; a niche still honours Thulukha Nachiyar, the Sultan's daughter of legend who loved the idol. Vijayanagara kings and their Nayaka governors then fortified and enlarged the complex over two centuries, adding gopurams, the thousand-pillared hall, granaries, a hospital and a free kitchen recorded in more than eight hundred inscriptions. The temple follows the Thenkalai tradition, whose twenty-one-day Margazhi festival grew into one of the great annual gatherings of the Tamil country.
zh: 斯里兰加姆是蒂鲁吉拉伯利附近、高韦里河与科利达姆河之间的岛上城镇，拥有毗湿奴派108处圣域中地位最高的一座：兰加纳塔神庙，供奉倚躺在神蛇舍沙身上的毗湿奴；泰米尔阿尔瓦尔圣徒在圣歌集《四千圣歌集》中赞颂它，室利毗湿奴派信徒干脆只称它为“庙”（Koyil）。早期朱罗王修建并重建了这座神庙，11世纪起，纳塔穆尼、亚穆纳查里雅，尤其是罗摩奴阇，把这里建成室利毗湿奴派的大本营，殿宇成为虔诚歌咏与梵学的中心。灾难随德里苏丹国而来：1311年马利克·卡富尔的劫掠把金像掳走，1327年穆罕默德·宾·图格鲁克的入侵又使神庙荒废——相传一万三千名信徒在保卫战中丧生，因此1337年时，兰加纳塔神像正被人秘密辗转于各村之间，当地则处在马杜赖苏丹国治下。直到库马拉·坎帕纳率领毗奢耶那伽罗军队推翻该苏丹国，神像才于1371年重新安奉；庙中还保留着一个壁龛，纪念传说中深爱神像的苏丹之女图卢卡·纳奇亚尔。此后两百年间，毗奢耶那伽罗诸王与其纳亚卡总督修筑城墙、扩建庙宇，增建瞿布罗塔门、千柱厅、粮仓、医院与施食厨房，这一切都记载在八百余条铭文里。该庙奉行滕卡莱传统，其长达21天的马尔加兹节是泰米尔地区一年一度的盛大集会。

en: Rila Monastery lies in a deep valley of the Rila Mountains south of Sofia, founded around the cave of the hermit Ivan of Rila, who died in 946 during the reign of Tsar Peter I. His disciples built the first houses near his retreat, and the tsars of the Second Bulgarian Empire endowed it until it became the spiritual centre of medieval Bulgaria. The feudal lord Hrelja rebuilt it on its present site in the 1330s and 1340s, leaving his fortified tower of 1334–1335 and a church of 1343, the oldest parts of the complex. Ottoman raids at the end of the fourteenth century ended in its destruction in the mid-fifteenth, but it was rebuilt at the century's close by three brothers from Dupnitsa with gifts from Mara Branković, the Russian church and the Russian monastery on Mount Athos, and Ivan's relics were brought from Tarnovo in 1469. Through the centuries of foreign rule it kept Bulgarian letters alive, and after a fire of 1833 the whole complex was rebuilt from 1834 in the style of the Bulgarian National Revival, its residential wings rising around a new five-domed church.
zh: 里拉修道院位于索非亚以南里拉山脉的深谷中，围绕隐修士里拉的伊万的洞穴而建；伊万于946年沙皇彼得一世在位时去世，弟子们在他的隐修处旁建起最早的房舍，第二保加利亚帝国历代沙皇不断捐资，使它成为中世纪保加利亚的精神中心。14世纪30至40年代，封建领主赫雷利亚在现址重建修道院，留下1334—1335年的防御塔和1343年的小教堂，这是建筑群中最古老的部分。14世纪末奥斯曼入侵后劫掠不断，修道院于15世纪中叶被毁；15世纪末，在玛拉·布兰科维奇、俄罗斯教会和阿索斯山罗斯修道院的捐助下，杜普尼察地区的三兄弟将其重建，伊万的圣骨也于1469年从特尔诺沃迁来。在外族统治的漫长岁月里，它维系着保加利亚语言与文化；1833年大火后，全院自1834年起按保加利亚民族复兴风格重建，宿舍楼环绕着新建的五穹顶教堂拔地而起。

en: The Rome Patriarchal See is the most venerable of the Christian bishoprics, held in tradition to have been founded by Saint Peter, chief of the apostles, who was martyred in Rome under Nero and buried on the Vatican hill beside the Circus of Nero. As the see of the former imperial capital, it stood first among the five great patriarchates of the early Church, the Pentarchy. Constantine the Great raised a basilica over Peter's tomb between 318 and 322, and for twelve centuries Old St. Peter's was the principal shrine of western Christendom: popes were crowned there, and Charlemagne was crowned emperor in it in 800. Saracens sacked the basilica in 846, after which Pope Leo IV enclosed the Vatican with the Leonine Wall. The see broke communion with Constantinople in the schism of 1054. By the fifteenth century the old church was structurally unsafe; the present Renaissance basilica, designed in turn by Bramante, Michelangelo and Maderno, was built from 1506 and consecrated in 1626.
zh: 罗马牧座是基督教最古老的主教座，相传由使徒之首圣彼得创立；他在尼禄治下于罗马殉道，葬在梵蒂冈山的尼禄竞技场旁。作为帝国旧都的主教座，它在早期教会五大牧首区中位列首席。君士坦丁大帝于318—322年间在圣彼得墓上建起一座大殿，此后一千二百年间，老圣彼得大殿一直是西方基督教的首要圣所：教皇在此加冕，800年查理曼也在此加冕为帝。846年撒拉森人洗劫大殿，教皇利奥四世随后修筑利奥城墙将梵蒂冈围住。1054年教会大分裂，罗马与君士坦丁堡断绝共融。到15世纪，老教堂已岌岌可危；现存的文艺复兴式大殿由布拉曼特、米开朗基罗和马代尔诺先后主持设计，1506年动工，1626年祝圣。

en: Rome, on the Tiber in central Italy, was the capital of the Roman Empire and became one of the principal holy cities of Christianity. Tradition holds that the apostles Peter and Paul were martyred there under Nero after the Great Fire of 64, and the bishops of Rome, later called popes, claimed succession from Peter. The faith was remembered in the city's catacombs, and after Constantine's legalization of Christianity the Old Saint Peter's Basilica rose over the apostle's tomb in 313, while the Lateran became the papal cathedral. Early heterodox teachers were drawn to the capital as well: the Gnostic Valentinus founded a school in Rome around the middle of the second century, and Marcion of Sinope, who distinguished the God of Jesus from the creator of the world, was excommunicated by the Roman church in about 144. In 846 Arab raiders looted the two apostolic basilicas outside the walls. Pope Boniface VIII proclaimed the first Christian Jubilee in 1300, but from 1309 to 1377 the papacy resided at Avignon and Rome fell into neglect; Gregory XI's return in 1377 opened the decades of the Western Schism, after which Renaissance popes rebuilt the city and began the new Saint Peter's Basilica.
zh: 罗马位于意大利中部的台伯河畔，曾是罗马帝国的首都，后来成为基督教的主要圣城之一。相传64年罗马大火之后，宗徒圣伯多禄与圣保禄在尼禄治下殉道于此，后来被称为教宗的罗马主教们声称自己是伯多禄的继承者。信徒们在城市的地下墓穴中坚守信仰，君士坦丁使基督教合法化后，老圣伯多禄大殿于313年建在这位宗徒的陵墓之上，拉特朗则成为教宗的主教座堂。早期的异端教师也被帝国首都吸引：灵知派的瓦伦廷约在2世纪中叶于罗马创办学派，而区分耶稣之上主与创世造物主的锡诺普人马吉安，约在144年被罗马教会革出教门。846年，阿拉伯袭掠者洗劫了城墙外的两座宗徒圣殿。1300年教宗卜尼法斯八世宣布首个基督教禧年，但1309—1377年教宗迁居阿维尼翁，罗马日渐荒废；1377年格列高利十一世返回罗马，开启了持续数十年的西方教会大分裂，此后文艺复兴时期的教宗们重建城市，并动工修建新的圣伯多禄大殿。

en: Saint Catherine's Monastery stands at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt, on the site where Moses is said to have seen the burning bush. Empress Helena, mother of Constantine the Great, built a chapel over the bush in the fourth century, and between 548 and 565 Emperor Justinian I enclosed it within a great fortified monastery, the oldest Christian house still continuously inhabited. A pilgrim's journal of the 380s already records monks on the mountain. The supposed body of Catherine of Alexandria, martyred in the early fourth century, was later brought there, and her relics made it a major pilgrimage centre, after which the house was renamed in her honour. Its library became one of the richest in Christendom, holding the fourth-century Codex Sinaiticus and the earliest surviving icons of Christ Pantocrator. In the seventh century the desert hermits around it disappeared and only the walled monastery survived, and a Fatimid mosque was built within its walls in 1106. Under Ottoman rule the once multiethnic community, whose monks had included Arabs, Syrians, Georgians and Slavs, became almost entirely Greek, sustained from the 1480s by alms from the princes of Wallachia.
zh: 圣埃卡特里纳修道院坐落在埃及西奈山脚下，相传这里就是摩西见到燃烧荆棘的地方。4世纪时，君士坦丁大帝之母海伦娜皇后在荆棘之上修建小堂；548—565年间，查士丁尼一世下令将其围入一座防御坚固的大修道院，这是世界上持续有人居住的最古老基督教修道院。一份380年代的朝圣游记已记载山上有修士修行。后来，4世纪初殉道的亚历山大的凯瑟琳的遗骸据传被移送到此，她的圣骨使这里成为重要的朝圣中心，修道院也以她的名字命名。院内藏书是基督教世界最丰富的收藏之一，藏有4世纪的《西奈抄本》和现存最早的全能者基督圣像。7世纪时，周围的沙漠隐修士消失，唯有高墙环绕的修道院幸存；1106年院内又建成一座法蒂玛王朝清真寺。奥斯曼时期，这个曾由阿拉伯、叙利亚、格鲁吉亚和斯拉夫修士组成的多民族共同体几乎完全希腊化，从1480年代起靠瓦拉几亚王公的施舍维持。

en: Samarkand, the great Sogdian city on the Silk Road, met Christianity early: some of its quarters were Christian by the fourth century, a Nestorian see was created in the fifth, and early in the eighth century it was raised to a metropolitanate of the Church of the East. Sogdian merchants carried this faith along the caravan routes to the Turkic steppe and China, while Sogdian manuscripts preserve the disputes between local Christians and Manichaeans. The Arab conquest of about 712 under Qutayba ibn Muslim brought persecution, and many believers fled or converted to Islam; archaeologists have nonetheless uncovered the ruins of Nestorian churches at Afrasiyab, the ancient town beside Samarkand. The city gave the Church of the East one of its best-loved saints, Mar Sergius, to whom monasteries from Central Asia to China were dedicated and whose vision was credited with the conversion of the Kerait Turks around 1007. Under Mongol rule after 1220 Christian bishoprics were again permitted, and between 1329 and 1359 a Catholic eparchy even served several thousand believers after the Chagatai khan Eljigidey accepted baptism, with a church of Saint John the Baptist in the city. Islam soon reasserted itself, and as Timur made Samarkand his capital in 1370 the old East Syriac congregations had dwindled to isolated remnants that died out in the following centuries.
zh: 丝绸之路上的粟特名城撒马尔罕很早就接触了基督教：4世纪时城中部分城区已有基督徒，5世纪设立聂斯脱里派主教座，8世纪初更升为东方教会的都主教教省。粟特商人沿商路把这一信仰带到突厥草原和中国，粟特语文献中还保留着当地基督徒与摩尼教徒的辩难。约712年屈底波·伊本·穆斯林率阿拉伯军队征服此地，带来迫害，许多信徒逃亡或改宗伊斯兰教；但考古学家仍在撒马尔罕旁的古城阿弗拉西亚布发掘出聂斯脱里派教堂遗址。这座城市还为东方教会贡献了最受爱戴的圣徒之一马·薛里吉思，从中亚到中国都有以他命名的修道院，约1007年克烈部突厥人归信也被归于他的显现。1220年蒙古统治之后，教会再度获准建立主教区；1329—1359年间，随着察合台汗燕只吉台受洗，城中甚至有一个服务数千信徒的天主教教区，并建有圣若翰洗者堂。但伊斯兰教很快重新占据上风，1370年帖木儿定都撒马尔罕时，古老的东叙利亚会众已萎缩为零星残余，并在随后几个世纪里绝迹。

en: The Sanctuary of the Great Gods on the island of Samothrace, off the Thracian coast, was the principal seat of the mystery cult of the Cabeiri, chthonic deities whose secret names initiates were forbidden to divulge and who were invoked as protectors of sailors. Its rites drew worshippers from across the Greek world: the historian Herodotus and the Spartan commander Lysander were both initiates, and Plato and Aristophanes refer to the mysteries. Plutarch records that Philip II of Macedon met Olympias while both were being initiated, and after Alexander the Great the Ptolemies and Antigonids vied to embellish the sanctuary, building the Ptolemaion, the rotunda of Arsinoe II and, around 325 BC, the Hieron. The Winged Victory of Samothrace was dedicated there in the second century BC. Hadrian visited the shrine and Varro described its rites, before the sanctuary was closed during the late-Roman persecution of pagan cults.
zh: 色雷斯沿海的萨摩色雷斯岛上的众神圣殿，是卡比里秘仪的主要中心。卡比里是一组冥土神祇，受秘仪者不得泄露他们的秘名，水手们奉其为保护神。它的仪式吸引了整个希腊世界的信众：历史学家希罗多德和斯巴达统帅莱山德都曾入教，柏拉图和阿里斯托芬的作品也提到过这套秘仪。普鲁塔克记载，马其顿的腓力二世正是在受秘仪时结识了奥林匹亚丝。亚历山大大帝之后，托勒密王朝和安提柯王朝竞相装点这座圣殿，先后兴建了托勒密门廊、阿尔西诺伊二世圆厅，以及约公元前325年建成的众神殿。公元前2世纪，萨摩色雷斯的胜利女神像被敬献于此。哈德良曾亲临参拜，瓦罗也曾记述其仪式；到罗马帝国晚期迫害异教崇拜时，这座圣殿终被关闭。

en: Santiago de Compostela, in Galicia in northwestern Spain, is the shrine where the apostle Saint James the Great is said to be buried. Tradition holds that in 814 the hermit Pelagius saw strange lights above the Libredon forest; Bishop Theodomirus of Iria identified the spot as the apostle's tomb, King Alfonso II of Asturias built a chapel and came as its first pilgrim, and churches followed in 829 and 899. In 997 the Cordoban commander Al-Mansur burned the church, though he left the tomb itself untouched and carried its gates and bells to Córdoba, from where Ferdinand III returned them after taking the city in 1236. The present Romanesque cathedral was begun in 1075 under Alfonso VI and Bishop Diego Peláez, modeled on Saint-Sernin in Toulouse, and was consecrated in 1211; Master Mateo completed its sculpted Pórtico da Gloria in 1188, and the twelfth-century Codex Calixtinus guided the pilgrims of the Way of Saint James. Raised to an archiepiscopal see in 1120 and given a university in 1495, Compostela was ranked by Pope Alexander VI in 1492 among the three great pilgrimages of Christendom with Rome and Jerusalem. In 1589 the relics were hidden from English and Dutch raiders, and the baroque Obradoiro facade was finished in 1740.
zh: 圣地亚哥‑德孔波斯特拉位于西班牙西北部的加利西亚，相传是宗徒大圣雅各伯安葬的圣所。传说814年隐士佩拉吉乌斯看见利布雷东森林上空有异光，伊里亚主教特奥多米罗认定此处为宗徒之墓，阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索二世在此修建小堂并成为第一位朝圣者，829年和899年又先后建起教堂。997年，科尔多瓦统帅阿尔曼苏尔焚毁教堂，但没有触动墓穴本身，还把堂门和铜钟掠往科尔多瓦；1236年费尔南多三世攻占该城后才将它们运回。现存的罗曼式大教堂1075年在阿方索六世与主教迭戈·佩莱斯主持下开工，以图卢兹的圣塞尔南教堂为蓝本，1211年祝圣；马特奥大师于1188年完成雕刻精美的荣耀门廊，12世纪的《卡利克斯特斯抄本》则为圣雅各之路的朝圣者指引行程。圣地亚哥于1120年升格为总主教区，1495年增设大学；1492年教宗亚历山大六世把它与罗马、耶路撒冷并列为基督教世界三大朝圣地。1589年，为躲避英国和荷兰袭掠者，圣物被转移藏匿；巴洛克风格的奥布拉多伊洛立面则于1740年完工。

en: The monastery of Santo Toribio de Liébana lies in a steep valley of the Cantabrian Mountains, near the town of Potes in northern Spain. A community was already established there in the sixth century, when a cleric named Turibius retired with companions to follow the Benedictine rule; the house was first dedicated to Saint Martin of Tours and only took its present name in the eleventh century. It owes its fame to the Lignum Crucis venerated within its walls, said to be the largest surviving fragment of the True Cross, the left arm of the cross, brought from the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem by Saint Turibius of Astorga in the early fifth century and carried to this remote valley for safety in the eighth. In that same century the monk Beatus of Liébana wrote and illustrated his Commentary on the Apocalypse at the monastery. The present church was built in 1256, and on 23 September 1512 Pope Julius II granted the house the privilege of a jubilee year, its Door of Forgiveness opening to pilgrims alongside Rome, Jerusalem and Santiago. In 1837 the Mendizábal confiscations drove the monks out.
zh: 圣托里比奥修道院坐落在西班牙北部波特斯镇附近、坎塔布连山脉的幽深山谷中。6世纪时，一位名叫托里比奥的教士带着同伴退隐于此，遵行本笃会规，修道团体就此建立；修道院最初奉图尔的圣马丁为主保，直到11世纪才改用今名。它的盛名来自院内供奉的真十字架木段，相传那是现存最大的真十字架残片，即十字架的左臂，5世纪初由阿斯托尔加的圣托里比奥从耶路撒冷圣墓教堂带回，8世纪时为避乱转运到这座偏僻山谷。同在8世纪，修士列瓦纳的比亚图斯在此撰写并手绘了他的《启示录注》。现存教堂建于1256年；1512年9月23日，教皇尤利乌斯二世颁诏授予该院禧年特权，宽恕之门向朝圣者开启，使它与罗马、耶路撒冷和圣地亚哥并列。1837年，门迪萨瓦尔的没收法令把修士们逐出了修道院。

en: The Serapeum of Alexandria was the chief temple of Serapis, a Graeco-Egyptian god formed from the Egyptian Osiris-Apis and given the attributes of Zeus, Hades and Dionysus. Ptolemy I Soter promoted the new cult in the early third century BC to bind the Greek and Egyptian subjects of his kingdom, and the great sanctuary itself was raised on a rocky plateau in the city's Greek quarter mainly under Ptolemy III Euergetes, between 246 and 222 BC. Ancient accounts describe it as the largest and most magnificent temple in Alexandria: besides the cult statue it housed a daughter collection of the Library of Alexandria, while subterranean galleries served the mysteries of Serapis and the precinct also held shrines of Isis and Harpocrates. The temple was first damaged in the Kitos War of AD 116 and restored under Hadrian, then rebuilt and enlarged by the Romans around 181 to 217; the giant column still standing on the site, misnamed Pompey's Pillar, was erected for Diocletian between 298 and 302. As worship of Serapis and Isis spread across the empire the Serapeum became the last great stronghold of pagan Alexandria, and in 391, after Theodosius I banned temple visits, rioting Christians led by Bishop Theophilus stormed it; the sanctuary was sacked and formally closed in July 392, and a church and the Monastery of Metanoia later rose among its ruins.
zh: 亚历山大塞拉比斯神庙是塞拉比斯神的主庙。塞拉比斯是一位希腊化埃及神，由埃及的奥西里斯—阿皮斯融合而成，又兼具宙斯、哈迪斯和狄俄尼索斯的神格。公元前3世纪初，托勒密一世·索塔尔为凝聚王国内的希腊与埃及臣民而大力推行这一新崇拜；宏伟的圣所本身则主要建于托勒密三世·尤厄格忒斯在位期间，即公元前246年至前222年，坐落在亚历山大城希腊区的一处岩石高地上。古人称它是全城最大、最壮丽的神庙：除神像外，庙中还藏有亚历山大图书馆的分馆藏书，地下长廊用于举行塞拉比斯秘仪，围墙内另有伊西斯和哈尔波克拉特斯的小神殿。神庙在公元116年的基托斯战争中首次被毁，哈德良时期予以修复，罗马人又在181年至217年前后重建扩建；遗址上矗立的巨柱被误称为“庞贝柱”，实为298年至302年间为戴克里先所立。随着塞拉比斯与伊西斯崇拜传遍帝国，这座神庙成了异教亚历山大最后的大本营。391年狄奥多西一世下令禁止参拜神庙后，主教提阿非罗率领的基督徒暴动者攻入庙中，圣所遭洗劫并于392年7月正式关闭，后来在废墟上建起了教堂和梅塔诺亚修道院。

en: The Shankari Devi Temple at Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's eastern coast is the goddess shrine of the great Koneswaram complex, crowning the Swami Rock promontory above the Indian Ocean. Worshipped as Ambal or Shankari Devi, the consort of the Shiva of Koneswaram, she is counted among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, the holiest seats of the Goddess in Shaktism, and the hymn attributed to Adi Shankara names this Sri Lankan seat as Sri Sankari Pitham. The wider Koneswaram complex, one of the five ancient Ishwarams of the island, is already mentioned in the Vayu Purana around the fourth century and was enlarged under Tamil dynasties, with the Chola prince Kulakottan rebuilding the shrine and its endowments; the Sinhalese king Gajabahu II was also recorded as its patron in the twelfth century. Between 1622 and 1624 the Portuguese destroyed the temples on the promontory and raised a fort from their stones, but the goddess's idols were rescued and installed in a new temple in the town in 1632, where her worship continued.
zh: 商羯丽女神庙位于斯里兰卡东海岸的亭可马里，是雄踞斯瓦米岩海角、俯瞰印度洋的科内斯瓦兰神庙群中的女神殿。女神被尊为安巴尔或商羯丽·提毗，即科内斯瓦兰湿婆的神妃，位列性力派最神圣的十八处大性力佩特之一，托名商羯罗的十八圣地颂将这座斯里兰卡圣地称作斯里·商羯里佩特。所属的科内斯瓦兰是岛上五大古湿婆神庙之一，4世纪前后的《风神往世书》已有记载，后经泰米尔诸王朝扩建，朱罗王子库拉科坦曾重修神庙及其供养田产，12世纪的僧伽罗国王迦阇巴忽二世也被碑铭记为护法。1622至1624年间，葡萄牙人捣毁海角上的诸庙，用庙石修建堡垒，但女神神像被抢救出来，于1632年安置在城中新建的庙宇，香火得以延续。

en: The Shankhapur Temple is the great Svetambara Jain tirtha of Shankheshwar in northern Gujarat, near Radhanpur, known in early Jain literature as Shankhpur. It is dedicated to Parshvanatha, whose white seated image, nearly six feet tall, is counted among the hundred and eight foremost Parshvanatha idols of the Svetambara tradition. A temple stood on the banks of the Rupen river by 1098, when Sajjan Shah rebuilt it, and the minister brothers Vastupala and Tejpal renovated it in 1229 under the teacher Vardhamansuri; king Durjansalya enlarged it again a generation later. The complex was destroyed in the fourteenth century during the raids of Alauddin Khalji, rebuilt in the sixteenth century under the monk Vijaysensuri, and consecrated anew by the Jain community in 1703 before the present temple rose in 1811. Under the Mughals Shah Jahan granted the village to the Ahmedabad banker Shantidas Jhaveri. For Svetambara pilgrims its rank stands second only to Mount Shatrunjaya at Palitana.
zh: 商羯罗补罗寺即古吉拉特北部商凯什瓦尔镇的白衣派耆那教大圣地，邻近拉丹布尔，在早期耆那教文献中名为商羯罗补罗。寺院供奉巴湿伐那陀，主像为高约1.8米的白色结跏趺坐像，被列为白衣派最重要的一百零八尊巴湿伐那陀像之一。鲁彭河畔早有寺院，1098年由萨詹·沙阿重建；1229年，大臣兄弟瓦斯图帕拉与泰杰帕拉奉导师伐达摩那苏利之命加以修葺，一代人之后国王杜尔贾纳萨利亚又大规模扩建。14世纪阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉入侵时寺院被毁，16世纪在僧人毗阇耶先苏利倡导下重建，1703年由耆那教僧团重新安像，现存建筑则建于1811年。莫卧儿时期，沙贾汗曾将此村封赐给艾哈迈达巴德的银行家尚蒂达斯·贾维里。在白衣派信众心中，其地位仅次于帕利塔纳的沙特伦贾亚山。

en: The Shankhodara Temple stands on Bet Dwarka, also called Shankhodhar, the conch-shell island two kilometres off Okha in Gujarat and counted among the lands of Krishna's legendary Dvaraka. It is one of India's few prominent shrines dedicated to Matsya, Vishnu's fish avatar, who guided Manu through the great flood and recovered the Vedas from the demon Hayagriva.
zh: 商拘陀罗神庙位于贝特德瓦尔卡岛（又称商拘达尔岛，意为海螺之岛），距古吉拉特奥卡港两公里，被视为黑天神传说中的德瓦尔卡疆域的一部分。它是全印为数不多的著名摩蹉神庙之一，供奉毗湿奴的鱼化身摩蹉——正是它引导摩奴渡过大洪水，并从恶魔诃耶羯哩婆手中夺回吠陀。

en: Sharada Peeth, the seat of Sharada, as the goddess Saraswati is called in Kashmir, is a ruined temple and ancient temple-university in the Neelum Valley at Sharda, high in the Himalayas of Kashmir. From the sixth to the twelfth century it ranked among the foremost centres of learning in South Asia, its library drawing scholars from distant lands; the Sharada script in which Kashmir wrote its Sanskrit takes its name from the place, and Kashmir itself was known as Sharada Desh, the country of Sharada. As one of the great Shakti Peethas it marks the spot where Sati's right hand is said to have fallen, and Kashmiri Pandits rank it with Martand and Amarnath among their three holiest pilgrimages. The stone temple is plausibly a work of the Karkota emperor Lalitaditya Muktapida, who reigned from 724 to 760, and by the eighth century pilgrims came from as far as Bengal; Al-Biruni listed it among the most celebrated Hindu shrines of the age. In 1422 the Kashmiri sultan Zain-ul-Abidin visited to seek a vision of the goddess, and in the sixteenth century Abu'l-Fazl described it as a stone temple held in great veneration. Under later Mughal and Afghan rule the valley passed to local Muslim chiefs and the old pilgrimage dwindled.
zh: 辩才天女庙的“沙尔达”是克什米尔对辩才天女萨拉斯瓦蒂的称呼，这座已成废墟的神庙兼古代庙学位于克什米尔山地沙尔达的尼勒姆河谷。6至12世纪间，它是南亚首屈一指的学术中心之一，藏书楼吸引远方学者前来；克什米尔书写梵文所用的沙尔达字母便得名于此，克什米尔本身也被称作“沙尔达之国”。作为大性力圣地之一，相传萨蒂的右手坠落于此；克什米尔班智达把它与马尔坦德太阳神庙、阿马尔纳特神庙并列为三大巡礼圣地。石庙很可能出自卡尔科塔王朝皇帝拉利塔迭多·穆克塔毗达之手，他在位时间为724至760年；到8世纪时，远自孟加拉的香客已络绎而来，比鲁尼也曾把它列入当时最负盛名的印度教神庙。1422年，克什米尔苏丹扎因·乌勒·阿比丁亲来求见女神；16世纪，阿布勒·法兹勒称其为一座备受尊崇的石庙。后来在莫卧儿和阿富汗统治下，河谷落入地方穆斯林首领之手，古老的巡礼逐渐衰微。

en: Śikharjī, also called Sammed Śikhar, rises on Parasnath hill in the forests of Jharkhand and is the most exalted pilgrimage place of the Jains, honoured equally by the Digambara and Svetambara sects. Its name means the venerable peak of concentration, for tradition holds that twenty of the twenty-four Tirthankaras, foremost among them Parshvanatha, the twenty-third, attained moksha here through meditation; Parshvanatha's liberation is placed in 772 BCE and gives the hill its name of Parasnath. The site is already named as a tirth in the Jnatrdharmakatha, one of the earliest Jain canonical texts, and a thirteenth-century palm-leaf Kalpa Sutra depicts Parshvanatha's nirvana on this peak. In the thirteenth century Vastupala, minister of the Vaghela kings of Gujarat, built a temple housing twenty Tirthankara images. Mughal emperors treated the hill with favour: Akbar issued a firman in 1583 entrusting it to the Jain community under the monk Harivijaya Suri and forbidding the killing of animals nearby, and an Agra merchant financed new temples in 1670. The Jagat Seth bankers of Murshidabad became patrons from 1725; Mahtabchand rebuilt the main temples in 1768, and in 1825 Kushalchand consecrated each of the twenty liberation sites together with a Jal Mandir and pilgrim rest houses. Both sects share the worship of the ancient idols on the summit.
zh: 尸佉罗时又称三密陀尸佉罗，耸立于贾坎德邦丛林中的波尔史伐陀山，是耆那教天衣派与白衣派共同尊奉的最高朝圣圣地。其名意为“可敬的禅定之峰”，相传二十四祖中有二十位——其中最著名的是第二十三祖巴湿伐那陀——在此禅定证得解脱；巴湿伐那陀于公元前772年涅槃，此山也因此得名波尔史伐陀山。早在耆那教最古老的经典之一《若提陀法经》中，此地已被列为圣地，13世纪的贝叶经《劫经》上还绘有巴湿伐那陀在此山涅槃的场景。13世纪，古吉拉特瓦盖拉王朝的大臣瓦斯图波罗建庙，供奉二十尊祖师像。莫卧儿皇帝对圣山优礼有加：阿克巴于1583年颁布敕令，将山体交由僧人哈里毗阇耶·苏利领导的耆那教团体管理，并禁止在附近杀生；1670年，一位阿格拉商人又出资在山上兴建新庙。1725年起，穆尔希达巴德的银行世家贾格特·塞特家族成为护法：马赫塔卜昌德于1768年重建主要殿宇，1825年库沙尔昌德又逐一为二十处解脱圣地举行开光，并修建水上神殿与香客客栈。山顶的古老神像由天衣、白衣两派共同奉祀。

en: Shikoku Henro is the great Buddhist pilgrimage of Japan's island of Shikoku, a circuit of eighty-eight temples linked to the monk Kūkai, posthumously called Kōbō Daishi, who was born at Zentsū-ji on the island in 774 and founded the esoteric Shingon school after returning from study in Tang China. Popular tradition holds that he visited or founded many of the temples himself. The route winds through the four old provinces of Awa, Tosa, Iyo and Sanuki, and its stages mirror the path to enlightenment, from the first awakening through discipline and bodhi to nirvana. Pilgrims, known as henro, walk in white robes with sedge hats and staffs, chanting the Heart Sutra at each temple, while local people give them alms along the way. Monks from Mount Kōya spread the Kōbō Daishi cult and its legends, such as that of Emon Saburō, and under the Edo shogunate pilgrims travelled with permits and temple-stamp books. By the eighteenth century smaller copies of the circuit had appeared across Japan, evidence of its wide popularity.
zh: 四国遍路是日本四国岛上的佛教巡礼路线，由八十八所与空海有关的寺院组成。空海谥号弘法大师，774年生于岛上的善通寺，曾入唐求法，回国后开创密教真言宗；相传他曾亲身巡拜或开创了其中许多寺院。路线环绕阿波、土佐、伊予、赞岐四国旧地，各段依次象征发心、修行、菩提、涅槃的觉悟之路。巡礼者称遍路，身穿白衣、头戴菅笠、手持金刚杖，每到一寺诵《般若心经》，沿途居民常向他们施舍。高野山的僧人四处弘扬弘法大师信仰与卫门三郎等传说；江户幕府时代，遍路须持通行许可、携带纳经帐沿路盖印。到18世纪，日本各地已出现规模较小的仿制巡路，可见其流行之广。

en: Shravanabelagola is a Jain pilgrimage town in Karnataka in southern India, set between the Chandragiri and Vindhyagiri hills. Tradition holds that the sage Bhadrabahu and his pupil Chandragupta Maurya, founder of the Mauryan empire, meditated on Chandragiri, where the former emperor is said to have died around 298 BCE after taking Jain ascetic vows, and memorials to later monks and donors cover the hill. On Vindhyagiri stands the fifty-eight-foot monolithic statue of Gommateshwara, also called Bahubali, commissioned in 981 by Chavundaraya, general of the Western Ganga kings of Talakad, and counted among the largest freestanding monolithic statues in the world. Under Western Ganga and later Hoysala patronage the town accumulated more than five hundred Jain inscriptions and temples, among them the Akkana Basadi and the Chandragupta Basadi. Every twelve years devotees gather for the Mahamastakabhisheka, anointing the great statue with water, turmeric, sandalwood paste and gold and silver flowers.
zh: 室罗伐拿白泽是印度南部卡纳塔克的耆那教朝圣城镇，坐落在旃陀罗山与温迪亚山两座丘陵之间。相传祖师婆达罗巴忽与其弟子、孔雀帝国的开创者旃陀罗笈多·孔雀曾在旃陀罗山修行，这位退位帝王约于公元前298年立下耆那教出家誓愿后在此离世，山上遍布历代僧人和施主的纪念塔。温迪亚山上矗立着高约18米的整块岩石雕像戈玛特什瓦拉，又称巴霍巴利，由西恒伽王朝塔拉卡德的将领查蒙达罗阇于981年出资开凿，被视为世界最大的独立整块岩石雕像之一。在西恒伽及后来曷萨拉诸王的护持下，此地积累了五百多方耆那教碑铭，以及阿迦那寺、旃陀罗笈多寺等庙宇。每隔十二年，信众齐聚于此举行大灌顶盛典，以清水、姜黄、檀香膏和金银花朵为大像涂油供奉。

en: The Shri Idagunji Maha Ganapati Temple is a Hindu shrine dedicated to Ganesha at Idagunji, a village in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka on India's west coast, near the Sharavathi river where it runs towards the Arabian Sea. It is one of the six celebrated Ganesha temples along the stretch of coast known as the Ganesha Coast. A local legend tells how the sage Valakhilya, his penance on the river bank beset by obstacles, was advised by the divine sage Narada to invoke Vighneshwara, the remover of hindrances; Ganesha was prevailed upon to leave Kailasha and dwell in the Sharavathi valley, the divine architect Vishwakarma carved his icon, and devotees raised a temple around it in the 400s or 500s CE. The stone image is unusual: Ganesha has two tusks instead of one and only two arms, with a granite bell at his waist and no serpent coiled around his belly. The icon is popularly reckoned to be more than two thousand years old, and pilgrims come to meditate before its unusually serene face.
zh: 室利伊陀郡时‑摩诃伽那波底神庙是供奉伽内什的印度教神庙，位于印度西海岸卡纳塔克邦北卡纳达县的伊陀郡时村，靠近流向阿拉伯海的舍拉沃蒂河。它是被称为“伽内什海岸”的沿海地带六大伽内什名庙之一。相传仙人瓦拉吉利耶在河畔苦行时屡遭障碍，圣仙那罗陀建议他祈请除障之神毗那夜迦；众仙于是恳请伽内什离开凯拉萨山驻留舍拉沃蒂河谷，神匠毗首羯磨为其雕造神像，信徒们约在4至5世纪绕像建庙。这尊石像造型罕见：伽内什长着两根象牙而非一根，只有双臂，腰悬花岗岩石铃，腹上也没有盘蛇。民间认为此像已有两千多年历史，香客们来此在它异常宁静的面容前冥想祈愿。

en: Shri Mayureshwar Mandir is a Hindu temple dedicated to Ganesha in Morgaon, about sixty-five kilometres from Pune in Maharashtra. Its name means Lord of the Peacock: the Ganesha Purana tells how Ganesha incarnated as the six-armed, white-skinned Mayuresvara, rode a peacock and slew the demon Sindhu. Morgaon is the adhya pitha, the foremost seat of the Ganapatya sect that worships Ganesha as the Supreme Being, and the starting and ending point of the Ashtavinayaka pilgrimage of eight Ganesha temples around Pune; the Mudgala Purana devotes twenty-two chapters to its greatness, and its holiness is compared with that of Kashi. The temple's origins are tied to the Ganapatya saint Morya Gosavi, whose lifetime is variously placed between the 1200s and the 1600s, and the poet-saint Samarth Ramdas (1608–1682) composed his famous arati Sukhakarta Dukhaharta before its icon. In the 1700s the Peshwa rulers of the Maratha Empire, who honoured Ganesha as their family deity, enriched the shrine with land and cash donations.
zh: 孔雀之主神庙是一座供奉伽内什的印度教神庙，位于马哈拉施特拉邦浦那以东约六十五公里的莫尔冈。庙名意为“孔雀之主”：《伽内什往世书》记载，伽内什曾化身为六臂白肤的摩由雷湿婆罗，骑孔雀诛杀了恶魔信度。莫尔冈是奉伽内什为至高神的伽那帕提亚教派最首要的圣地，也是浦那周边阿什塔维纳亚克八座伽内什神庙巡礼的起点与终点；《穆德伽罗往世书》用二十二章篇幅赞颂其神圣，其地位可与圣城迦尸相比。神庙的兴起与伽那帕提亚派圣徒摩利亚·戈萨维有关，此人的生活年代有13至17世纪之间的多种说法；诗人圣徒萨马尔特·拉姆达斯（1608—1682）正是在庙中神像前写下了著名的敬神歌《苏尔迦尔多·杜克尔赫尔多》。18世纪时，以伽内什为家族保护神的马拉塔帝国佩什瓦们广赠土地与钱财，使神庙愈加兴盛。

en: Shwedagon Pagoda is the gilded stupa that crowns Singuttara Hill at Dagon, the settlement later known as Yangon in Lower Burma, and is the most sacred Buddhist site in the country. Tradition holds that two merchant brothers received eight hairs from the Buddha and that the local king enshrined them on the hill together with relics of the three earlier Buddhas; archaeology instead points to a Mon foundation between the sixth and tenth centuries. The pagoda enters the royal chronicles in 1362, when King Binnya U of Hanthawaddy rebuilt it to a height of eighteen meters. Queen Shin Saw Pu raised it again to forty meters in the fifteenth century and covered it in gold, and by the early sixteenth century it was Burma's most celebrated pilgrimage destination. Earthquakes repeatedly damaged it, and the quake of 1768 threw down its spire; King Hsinbyushin rebuilt the top in 1775, giving the stupa essentially its present form.
zh: 大光金塔是矗立在下缅甸大光（后来的仰光）丁固达拉山上的鎏金窣堵坡，也是缅甸最神圣的佛教圣地。相传两位商人兄弟从佛陀处求得八根头发，当地国王将其与过去三佛的圣物一同供奉在这座山上；考古学家则认为它实际建于6至10世纪，出自孟族之手。1362年，罕达瓦底的频耶陀努王重修此塔，将其加高到18米，这是它首次见于王室编年史。15世纪，女王信绍布又把塔加高到40米并全身贴金；到16世纪初，它已成为缅甸最负盛名的朝圣之地。此后数百年间地震屡有破坏，1768年的大地震震塌塔尖，1775年辛标信王重建塔顶，大光金塔由此基本形成今天的样貌。

en: This shrine preserves the tomb of Abu Said ibn Khalaf al-Tamimi al-Baji, known to pilgrims as Sidi Bou Said, an Arab Sufi saint of Tunisia born in 1156. Trained in the school of the great Andalusian mystic Abu Madyan, he left his native region of Beja to study in Syria and made the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1207, where he stayed for three years before returning to Tunisia in 1210. He then gave up worldly life for prayer and meditation in Tunis, and his reputation for piety drew many disciples, among them Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili, founder of the Shadhili order, while he is also said to have met the philosopher Ibn Arabi during his years in the east. Sidi Bou Said used to withdraw to a lighthouse on the hill above Carthage, and when he died in 1231 he was buried there; his sanctuary gave the surrounding settlement its present name and became one of the most venerated Sufi pilgrimage places of the Tunis region.
zh: 这座圣陵安放着突尼斯阿拉伯苏菲圣徒阿布·赛义德·伊本·赫莱夫·塔米米·巴吉的陵墓，朝圣者通称他为西迪·布·赛义德。他生于1156年，出自安达卢西亚大神秘主义者阿布·马德扬门下，后离开故乡贝贾地区赴叙利亚求学，1207年前往麦加朝觐并停留三年，1210年返回突尼斯。此后他弃绝世俗，在突尼斯城潜心祈祷与冥想，虔诚之名吸引了众多弟子，沙兹里教团的创始人阿布·哈桑·沙兹里便出自其门下；据说他在东方期间还曾与哲人伊本·阿拉比相会。西迪·布·赛义德常到迦太基附近山上的一座灯塔隐修，1231年去世后即安葬于此；他的圣所使周边聚落得名西迪布赛义德，并成为突尼斯地区最受尊崇的苏菲朝圣地之一。

en: The Abu Madyan shrine is the religious complex of mosque, madrasa, mausoleum and hammam at al-Ubbad outside Tlemcen in western Algeria, built around the tomb of the Andalusian Sufi master Abu Madyan Shu'ayb. Born near Seville around 1126, he learned weaving in Morocco, studied mysticism in Fez and under Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani in Mecca, then settled at Bougie, where disciples such as Ibn Arabi gathered around him. His fame alarmed the Almohad authorities, and when Caliph Ya'qub al-Mansur summoned him to Marrakesh he died on the journey in 1198, near the Ysser river, and was buried at al-Ubbad; the people of Tlemcen adopted him as their patron saint, and Caliph Muhammad al-Nasir soon raised a mausoleum over his grave. The Marinid rulers of Tlemcen enriched the sanctuary in the fourteenth century, founding the present mosque in 1339 and its madrasa eight years later, where Ibn Khaldun once taught, alongside a palace for visiting sultans.
zh: 阿布·迈迪安圣陵是阿尔及利亚西部特莱姆森郊外欧巴德的一组宗教建筑群，由清真寺、经学院、圣陵和浴室组成，围绕安达卢西亚苏菲大师阿布·迈迪安·舒艾卜的坟墓而建。他约1126年生于塞维利亚附近，早年在摩洛哥学习织布，后在非斯研习神秘主义，又赴麦加师从阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔·吉拉尼，最后定居贝贾亚，伊本·阿拉比等弟子云集其门下。他的声望引起穆瓦希德当局忌惮，哈里发雅各布·曼苏尔召他前往马拉喀什，他却在1198年行至伊塞尔河附近时病逝，葬于欧巴德；特莱姆森民众奉他为守护圣徒，哈里发穆罕默德·纳西尔很快在他墓上建起圣陵。14世纪统治特莱姆森的马林王朝大兴土木扩充圣所，现存清真寺建于1339年，八年后又建起经学院，伊本·赫勒敦曾在此讲学，旁边还修有供苏丹巡幸时居住的宫殿。

en: Sonagiri, the golden mountain, known in older texts as Swarnagiri, is a Digambara Jain pilgrimage place in the Datia district of central India, not far from Gwalior. White temples with tall spires have crowded its hill from the 800s onward; seventy-seven shrines stand on the hill itself and more than a hundred belong to the whole tirth. Jain tradition holds that the eighth Tirthankara Chandraprabha seventeen times held his Samavasarana, the divine preaching assembly, on this spot, and the acharya Shubh Chandra and the sage Bhartrihari are said to have practised austerities here, attained nirvana and composed their religious works, making the hill a favoured retreat for monks striving for liberation. The principal shrine is temple number fifty-seven, which houses an eleven-foot image of Chandraprabha affectionately called Bade Baba, flanked by altars of Shitalanatha and Parshvanatha, together with a forty-three-foot column of honour and a sculpted model of the Samavasarana. Pilgrims gather each spring for the chariot festival after Holi and for the ceremony of replacing the golden flag on the main spire.
zh: 苏那耆梨意为“金山”，古称苏伐那耆梨，是印度中部德蒂亚地区、距瓜廖尔不远的一处天衣派耆那教圣地。自9世纪起，一座座白墙高塔的庙宇便陆续布满山头：山上有七十七座神龛，整个圣所的庙宇则超过一百座。耆那教传统认为，第八代祖师旃陀罗波罗跋曾十七次在此召开神圣讲法集会萨摩婆萨罗那；阿阇梨输旃陀罗与仙人婆利睹梨诃利相传也在此苦修、证得涅槃并撰写了大量宗教典籍，此山因而成为僧人追求解脱的热门隐修地。主殿是编号第五十七的神庙，内供十一英尺高的旃陀罗波罗跋像，信众昵称“大巴巴”，两侧另有湿多罗那陀与巴湿伐那陀的法坛，殿前立着四十三英尺高的荣誉柱，还有一座萨摩婆萨罗那的雕刻模型。每年春天洒红节之后，香客云集参加乘车节，并举行更换主塔金旗的仪式。

en: The Sreevaraham Lakshmi Varaha Temple stands in the Sreevaraham quarter of Thiruvananthapuram, a short distance from the great Padmanabhaswamy Temple, the patron shrine of the kings of Travancore. Its principal image is Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, seated with Lakshmi on his lap, a pairing rarely seen: this is one of only three Varaha temples in Kerala and among the few shrines in India where the boar is shown with his consort. Local tradition claims the site is of immense antiquity, though no early building records survive. With the rise of Travancore the Vishnu shrines of the city entered the patronage of its maharajas: Marthanda Varma dedicated his whole kingdom to Padmanabha in 1750, and in 1795 Dharma Raja moved the capital from Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram. Built in the typical Kerala style, the temple has a round sanctum roofed with copper plates, a square outer nalambalam and a gilded flagpost, and its tank is the largest temple pond in Kerala; priests who came to the Padmanabhaswamy Temple for the Murajapam recitation took their ritual bath here, and boat races are held on the water during Onam. The annual festival falls in the Malayalam month of Meenam, alongside the Painguni festival of the neighbouring great temple, with Varaha Jayanti celebrated in the same month.
zh: 斯里瓦拉哈姆吉祥天女·筏罗诃神庙位于特里凡得琅的斯里瓦拉哈姆区，距特拉凡哥尔王室的护法神庙帕德马纳巴史瓦米大庙仅一步之遥。庙中主神为毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃，吉祥天女坐于其膝上，这种双双同祀的形象十分罕见：全喀拉拉只有三座筏罗诃庙，它是其中之一，也是全印少数把筏罗诃与配偶合祀的神庙。当地传说该庙渊源极为古远，但早期营建记录已无存。随着特拉凡哥尔崛起，城内的毗湿奴神庙归入诸摩诃罗阇的护持：1750年马尔坦达·瓦尔马把整个王国献给帕德马纳巴，1795年达尔马罗阇又把都城从帕德马纳巴普兰迁至特里凡得琅。庙宇为典型喀拉拉风格，圆形圣所覆以铜板顶，方形外圈纳兰巴兰环绕，立有镏金旗杆；庙前圣池是喀拉拉最大的寺庙池塘，前来帕德马纳巴史瓦米庙参加穆拉贾帕姆诵经法会的婆罗门都在此沐浴，欧南节时池中还举行赛船。一年一度的神庙大节在马拉雅拉姆历米纳姆月，与邻庙的潘古尼节同期，同月还隆重庆祝筏罗诃诞辰。

en: The Sri Sharadamba Temple stands in the town of Sringeri in Karnataka, on the banks of the Tunga river, and is dedicated to Sharadamba, the local form of Saraswati, goddess of learning. Tradition holds that Adi Shankara founded the shrine in the eighth century and built beside it his first monastery, the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, the southern of the four cardinal mathas he established across India, with his disciple Sureshvaracharya as its first pontiff. The temple forms the heart of a larger complex that also includes the Vidya Shankara shrine and the pontiff's residence, and the matha has preserved Sanskrit manuscripts and Advaita Vedanta scholarship through an unbroken line of Jagadgurus. In 1791, during the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Pindari raiders sacked and destroyed the temple; on hearing the news Tipu Sultan, then ruler of Mysore, wrote letters of condolence to the Shankaracharya and sent money, gifts and armed protection so that the shrine could be rebuilt.
zh: 斯灵盖里辩才天女庙位于卡纳塔克的斯灵盖里镇、栋格河畔，供奉辩才天女萨拉斯瓦蒂的当地化身夏拉丹巴。相传8世纪时阿迪·商羯罗创建此庙，并在庙旁建立了他的第一座寺院——斯灵盖里夏拉道场，即他在印度所立四大根本道场中主管南方的一座，其弟子苏雷什瓦拉查亚为首任方丈。神庙是整个道场建筑群的核心，群内还包括吠陀商羯罗殿和方丈居所；历代祖师传承不断，道场长期保存梵文写本、研习不二吠檀多。1791年第三次英迈战争期间，平达里流寇洗劫并摧毁了神庙；迈索尔统治者提普苏丹闻讯后致函商羯罗查尔雅慰问，并拨款、献礼、派兵护卫，使神庙得以重建。

en: Studenica Monastery lies in the wooded hills of central Serbia, the mother church of all Serbian temples. Stefan Nemanja, founder of the medieval Serb state, began it in the late twelfth century and took his monastic vows there on abdicating in 1196 before retiring to Hilandar on Mount Athos, where he died in 1199. His youngest son Rastko, later Saint Sava, brought Nemanja's relics back to Studenica, and under his care it became the political and spiritual centre of the Nemanjić realm. Its white-marble Church of the Virgin, frescoed in 1208–1209, blends Romanesque and Byzantine forms in the style later called the Raška School; King Radoslav added its exonarthex in the 1230s, and King Milutin built the smaller King's Church of Saints Joachim and Anna in 1314. After the Ottoman conquest of Serbia in 1459 the house suffered repeated Turkish assaults, and an earthquake and a fire in the early seventeenth century destroyed much of its archive, though a restoration of 1569 had already renewed its frescoes.
zh: 斯图代尼察修道院位于塞尔维亚中部的林木丘陵中，是所有塞尔维亚教堂的母堂。中世纪塞尔维亚国家的缔造者斯特凡·涅曼雅于12世纪末兴建此院，1196年退位时在此发愿修道，之后退隐阿索斯山的希利安达里乌修道院，1199年在那里去世。他的幼子拉斯特科——即后来的圣萨瓦——将涅曼雅的圣骨迎回斯图代尼察；在圣萨瓦主持下，这里成为涅曼吉奇王朝治下塞尔维亚的政治与精神中心。白色大理石砌成的圣母堂于1208—1209年绘制壁画，融合罗马式与拜占庭风格，即后来所称的拉什卡学派；拉多斯拉夫国王在1230年代增建外前廊，米卢廷国王又于1314年修建了较小的国王堂（约阿希姆与亚拿堂）。1459年奥斯曼征服塞尔维亚后，修道院屡遭土耳其人攻掠，17世纪初又遇地震和火灾，大量档案被毁，此前1569年的一次大修曾重绘壁画。

en: Sumela Monastery clings to a sheer cliff in the Pontic Mountains south of Trebizond, at about 1,200 metres above the Altındere valley. Tradition places its foundation around 386, in the reign of Theodosius I, by two Athenian monks, Barnabas and Sophronios, and it was famed for an icon of the Theotokos believed to have been painted by the Apostle Luke. The Byzantine general Belisarius restored and enlarged it in the sixth century on the orders of Justinian, but its great age came with the Empire of Trebizond. The monastery took its present form in the thirteenth century, and Emperor Alexios III, whom legend says the Virgin saved from a storm, confirmed its freedom and tax exemptions in a chrysobull of 1365, making it one of the richest houses in Pontus. After the Ottoman conquest of Trebizond in 1461, Mehmed II took the monastery under his protection and later sultans renewed its privileges. It remained a living centre of Greek Orthodox life, and from 1682 it housed the Phrontisterion of Trapezous, the foremost Greek school of the Black Sea coast, drawing monks and pilgrims for centuries.
zh: 苏梅拉修道院嵌在特拉比松以南本都山脉的绝壁上，海拔约1200米，俯瞰阿尔滕代雷山谷。相传它由雅典修士巴拿巴和索夫罗尼奥斯于386年前后、狄奥多西一世在位时创建，以一幅传说出自使徒路加之手的圣母圣像闻名。6世纪时，拜占庭将军贝利萨留奉查士丁尼之命修复并扩建了修道院；而它的鼎盛期伴随着特拉比松帝国而来。修道院在13世纪形成今天的格局，传说曾被圣母从风暴中救下的皇帝阿莱克修斯三世于1365年颁布金玺诏书，确认其自治权和免税特权，使它成为本都最富有的修道院之一。1461年奥斯曼征服特拉比松后，穆罕默德二世将修道院置于自己的保护之下，此后历代苏丹都延续了它的特权。它始终是希腊正教生活的活跃中心，1682年起更收容了黑海沿岸首屈一指的希腊学府特拉比松学园，数百年间吸引着修士与朝圣者。

en: Sumiyoshi Taisha is the head shrine of the Sumiyoshi cult and the ichinomiya of Settsu Province, standing beside the old port of Suminoe no Tsu on the Seto coast. Its founding in 211 is attributed to the local magnate Tamomi no Sukune, acting on an oracle given to Empress Jingū, who is herself enshrined there beside the three Sumiyoshi kami, protectors of seafarers and gods of war on the sea. The shrine guarded the Yamato embassies that sailed to China from the port below it, and its hereditary priests of the Tsumori clan boarded those ships; as Jingū was mother of the deified Emperor Ōjin, it also ranks as an ancestor shrine of Hachiman and protector of the Kawachi Minamoto line. In 965 Emperor Murakami numbered it among the sixteen shrines receiving imperial offerings, and poets honoured it as one of the three guardian kami of waka. Its honden, built in the shrine's own Sumiyoshi-zukuri style of raised pillars and plank walls, is the oldest surviving example of the form.
zh: 住吉大社是住吉信仰的总本社、摄津国一宫，坐落于濑户内海沿岸的古港住吉津旁。相传211年，当地豪族田裳见宿祢奉神功皇后所得神谕创社，神功皇后本人也与住吉三神合祀于此；住吉三神是航海者的保护神、海上的战神。神社庇佑从山下港口出发的大和遣华使船，世袭神职的津守氏也随船同行；由于神功皇后是神格化的应神天皇之母，住吉大社又被视为八幡神的祖社、河内源氏一脉的守护神。965年，村上天皇将它列入十六座接受朝廷币帛的神社；歌人则尊它为和歌三神之一。社内本殿采用以神社命名的“住吉造”样式，立柱立于石基、板壁横铺，是这一样式现存最古老的实例。

en: Suryanar Kovil is a Hindu temple dedicated to Surya, the sun god, standing in the Kaveri delta near Kumbakonam in Tamil country. It is one of the nine Navagraha temples of Tamil Nadu and the only one among them with separate shrines for all nine planetary deities, the other eight arranged to face the central shrine of Surya and his two consorts, Usha and Chhaya. An inscription records that the present stone building was raised under the Chola king Kulottunga I, who reigned from 1070 to 1120, and was first named Kulottungachola-Marttandalaya; later rulers of Vijayanagara added to it. Built in the Dravidian style behind a five-tiered gopuram, the temple draws pilgrims of the Navagraha circuit, who come to appease the planets that are believed to govern their horoscopes. Its liturgical fame reached the Carnatic composer Muthuswami Dikshitar, who included a hymn to its sun deity among his works in the early nineteenth century.
zh: 苏利耶纳尔神庙是供奉太阳神苏利耶的印度教神庙，坐落在泰米尔地区贡伯戈讷姆附近的高韦里河三角洲。它是泰米尔纳德九大格罗诃（九曜）神庙之一，也是其中唯一为全部九位星神各设神龛的一座：其余八座神龛都朝向中央苏利耶与其两位配偶乌莎、恰雅的神龛。庙中铭文记载，现存石构建筑由朱罗国王库洛通加一世（1070—1120年在位）兴建，最初名为库洛通加朱罗-马坦达罗耶，后又经毗奢耶那伽罗统治者增建。神庙为达罗毗荼风格，门前立有五层瞿布罗高塔，吸引九曜巡礼路线上的朝圣者前来安抚据说掌管个人星命的诸星。它在宗教音乐上的声名也传到了卡纳提克作曲家穆图斯瓦米·迪克西特尔那里，他在19世纪初的作品中为庙中的太阳神写下了一首颂歌。

en: The Suryavinayak Temple is a Ganesha shrine on a forested hill about two kilometres south of Bhaktapur in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal, and one of the four principal Ganesha temples of the valley; its name, the temple of the rising sun, comes from the eastward-facing image. Local tradition carries its origins back to the Licchavi period, around the 500s CE, when King Vishnu Dev Barma is said to have founded it. The present brick temple in the shikhara style is much younger: an inscription records that it was completed in 1833. Inside the sanctum rests a stone Ganesha adorned with metalwork, fronted by a pillar carved with his mouse mount and a stone water spout for offerings. Pilgrims from Kathmandu, Patan and Banepa gather here especially on Tuesdays and in the month of Magha, holding that worship of Suryavinayak brings good fortune and sound judgment.
zh: 苏利耶毗那夜迦神庙是尼泊尔加德满都谷地的一座伽内什神庙，坐落在巴克塔普尔以南约两公里的林木山丘上，是谷地四大伽内什神庙之一；庙名意为“旭日之庙”，因神像面朝东方而得名。当地传统把其渊源追溯到约6世纪的李查维时期，相传由毗湿奴·提婆·巴尔马国王肇建。现存的悉卡罗式砖庙则晚得多：庙中铭文记载它于1833年落成。圣室中供奉着以金属工艺装饰的石雕伽内什，庙前立有雕着其坐骑神鼠的石柱，还有用于敬献清水的石雕水口。加德满都、帕坦和巴内帕的香客尤其爱在每周周二和摩伽月前来，相信敬拜苏利耶毗那夜迦能带来好运与明辨之心。

en: Svetitskhoveli Cathedral rises in Mtskheta, the old capital of the Georgian kingdom of Kartli at the meeting of the Mtkvari and Aragvi rivers, on the spot where Saint Nino founded the first Georgian church after King Mirian III made Christianity the state religion in 337. Georgian tradition holds that a Jew of Mtskheta named Elias brought back Christ's mantle from the crucifixion in Jerusalem, and that his sister Sidonia was buried holding it; a cedar grew from her grave, and when its wood was used for the church, the seventh pillar hung in the air until Nino's prayers brought it down, shedding a liquid that healed the sick. Its name means the life-giving pillar. King Vakhtang Gorgasali built a basilica there in the late fifth century, and the present cross-domed cathedral was raised in 1010–1029 by the architect Arsukidze under Catholicos Melchizedek I. It became the burial church of Georgian kings, was wrecked by Tamerlane at the end of the fourteenth century and rebuilt with a new dome in the fifteenth, and received its defensive wall in 1787 under King Erekle II.
zh: 生命之柱主教座堂矗立在姆茨赫塔——格鲁吉亚卡特利王国的旧都，库拉河与阿拉格维河交汇处。337年米利安三世立基督教为国教后，圣尼诺在此建立了格鲁吉亚第一座教堂。按格鲁吉亚传统，姆茨赫塔犹太人埃利亚斯从耶路撒冷殉难地带回基督的外衣，他的妹妹西多尼亚抱着圣衣离世，便与圣衣一同下葬；墓上长出一棵雪松，木料用于建堂时，第七根柱子悬在空中，经圣尼诺彻夜祈祷才落下，并流出能治病的液体，教堂因此得名“生命之柱”。5世纪末，瓦赫坦·戈尔加萨利王在此修建巴西利卡；现存的十字穹顶教堂由建筑师阿尔苏基泽于1010—1029年在卡托利科斯科斯梅尔基塞德克一世主持下建成。这里后来成为格鲁吉亚历代国王的安葬地，14世纪末被帖木儿摧毁，15世纪重建并加盖新穹顶，1787年又在埃雷克勒二世治下修筑了防御墙。

en: Swayambhu, the self-arisen one, crowns a hill west of Kathmandu and is among the oldest Buddhist stupa complexes in Nepal, though Hindus also worship there and the resident monkeys have earned it the nickname the Monkey Temple. The Swayambhu Purana tells how the Kathmandu valley was once a lake bearing a thousand-petalled lotus of radiant light, until the bodhisattva Manjushri cut the gorge at Chobar to drain the waters and reveal the self-sprung flame, which King Prachandadev of Gauda enshrined beneath a stupa. Tradition brings Ashoka here in the 200s BCE, and a damaged inscription records building works ordered by the Licchavi king Vrsadeva in 640; over the centuries the hill hosted Nagarjuna, Vasubandhu and, on their journeys to Tibet, Shantarakshita and Padmasambhava. In the 1400s the Indian abbot Sariputra of Bodh Gaya rebuilt the dilapidated stupa with a Malla king's support, the Tibetan master Tsangnyon Heruka carried out a three-month restoration in 1504 at the invitation of the king of Kathmandu, and Pratap Malla of Kathmandu added the great eastern stairway in the 1600s. Its white dome, four-eyed Buddha cube and gilded thirteen-tier spire embody the Vajrayana cosmos of Newar Buddhism.
zh: 四眼天神庙本名“斯瓦扬布”，意为“自生者”，雄踞加德满都以西的山丘，是尼泊尔最古老的佛塔建筑群之一；印度教徒也来此礼拜，庙中群猴聚居，又有“猴庙”的俗称。《斯瓦扬布往世书》称，加德满都谷地曾是一片大湖，湖上生出放射光明的千瓣莲花，后来菩萨文殊师利以剑劈出乔巴尔峡谷排干湖水，使自生之光显露，孟加拉高尔国王普拉昌达戴夫便在光上建塔供奉。相传阿育王在公元前3世纪曾来朝礼，一通残碑则记载了离车毗国王弗栗沙提婆于640年下令兴修的工程；此后龙树、世亲，以及入藏途中的寂护与莲花生都曾驻锡此山。15世纪，菩提伽耶的印度上座沙利子经在马拉国王支持下重建了倾颓的佛塔；1504年藏地大师仓央·海如伽受加德满都国王之邀，用三个月完成又一次修缮；17世纪普拉塔普·马拉又增修了宏伟的东山门石阶。白色覆钵、绘有佛陀四面慧眼的方台和鎏金十三层相轮，共同体现了尼瓦尔佛教的密教宇宙观。

en: The Tara Tarini Temple crowns the Kumari hills, also called Purnagiri, above the Rushikulya river in Ganjam district of Odisha, and is dedicated to two sister goddesses, Tara and Tarini, worshipped together as forms of Adi Shakti. It ranks among the four Adi Shakti Pithas and the four Tantra pithas, identified in Puranic legend as the Sthana pitha where the breasts of Sati fell when Vishnu dismembered her body; the companion pithas are Kamakhya, Vimala and Kalighat, and the Kalika Purana itself names Tara Tarini in this list. The sanctum holds two ancient stone faces of the goddesses adorned with gold and silver ornaments, a pair of brass processional heads between them, and even a small image of the Buddha, reflecting the shrine's role as a cradle of the Buddhist Tara cult. The Hindi and Odia traditions present it as the patron goddess of ancient Kalinga and of the sea-going merchants who sailed from the nearby ports to Java and Sumatra, and the nine hundred and ninety-nine stone steps climbing the hill are said to have been paid for by a merchant saved from shipwreck. Each spring the Chaitra Jatra draws crowds who bring their children for the auspicious first tonsure.
zh: 多罗·多梨尼神庙坐落在奥里萨甘贾姆县勒湿俱利亚河畔的库马里山（又称富那吉里山）上，供奉一对姐妹女神多罗与多梨尼，二者被视为阿迪·夏克提的化身而合祀。它是四大阿迪·夏克提圣地、也是四大怛特罗圣地之一，往世书传说认定这里是毗湿奴分解萨蒂遗体时其双乳坠落之地，称“双乳圣地”；同组圣地还有迦摩伽耶、维摩罗与迦利卡特，《迦利迦往世书》的名单中即列有多罗·多梨尼之名。圣所中供着两尊古老的女神石面，饰以金银妆奁，中间夹着两尊黄铜巡行头像，甚至还有一尊小型佛像，反映出此庙也是佛教多罗女神信仰的发源地之一。印地语与奥里雅语传统把她奉为古代羯陵伽的守护神，也是从附近港口远航爪哇、苏门答腊的海商们的守护神；通往山顶的九百九十九级石阶，相传是一位遇海难生还的商人捐资修建的。每年春季的遮伊陀罗节期间，香客云集，纷纷带孩子来此行吉祥的首次剃发礼。

en: Tarapith is a Tantric pilgrimage village on the Dwarka river in Birbhum district of Bengal, famed for its temple of Tara, the second of the ten Mahavidya goddesses, and for the cremation ground beside it. The shrine is recognised as both a Shakti pitha and a Siddha pitha: Puranic works such as the Kalika Purana and the Devi Bhagavata Purana hold that the third eye of Sati fell at this spot, making it one of the fifty-one seats of the goddess. Tradition makes the sage Vashistha its first worshipper; a legend told in the Rudrayamala relates how he failed to win Tara's favour until he travelled to Mahachina, beyond the Himalayas, and learned the left-handed kaula rites, after which the goddess appeared before him as a mother suckling Shiva and turned into the stone image still venerated in the sanctum. The adjoining smashana, or cremation ground, is among the most celebrated places of Tantric practice in Shaktism, where ascetics seek enlightenment amid funeral pyres on the model of Vashistha's austerities, and the temple remains one of the three great Shakta centres of Bengal alongside Kalighat and Nabadwip.
zh: 多罗比他寺是孟加拉比尔布姆县德瓦尔卡河畔的一座怛特罗朝圣村落，以供奉十大明妃中第二位多罗女神的神庙及庙旁的火葬场闻名。该圣地同时被视为性力圣地与成就圣地；《迦利迦往世书》《女神薄伽梵往世书》等往世书认为，萨蒂的第三只眼坠落于此，使它成为五十一处女神圣地之一。相传仙人婆私吒是此地最早的礼拜者；《楼陀罗耶密罗》中的传说讲述他如何久求多罗而不得，直到远赴喜马拉雅山外的“大支那”学得左道俱洛仪轨，女神才化为哺乳湿婆的母亲形象现身，并变成圣所中世代供奉的石像。毗邻的火葬场是性力派最著名的怛特罗修行场所之一，修行者效仿婆私吒的苦行，在焚尸烟火之间寻求觉悟；与迦利卡特、诺博迪维普并列，多罗比他寺长期是孟加拉三大性力派中心之一。

en: The Telesterion was the great initiation hall at Eleusis in Attica, the centre of the Eleusinian Mysteries held in honour of Demeter and Persephone, the most famous secret rites of Greek religion. A hall stood on the site by the seventh century BC, and each year the nine-day festival brought thousands of initiates, who were shown sacred relics inside and forbidden to reveal what they had seen. The Persians burned the building in 480 BC; it was rebuilt under Pericles from a design by Iktinos, the architect of the Parthenon, and Philon added a Doric portico of twelve columns around 318 BC. Sacked by the Costoboci in 170 AD, it was rebuilt on a larger scale by Marcus Aurelius, the only layman ever admitted to its innermost shrine. The emperor Theodosius I closed the mysteries in 392, and in 396 the Goths of Alaric sacked Eleusis and destroyed the Telesterion, which was never rebuilt.
zh: 泰勒斯台里昂神庙是阿提卡厄琉息斯的宏大入会大厅，也是祭祀得墨忒耳与珀耳塞福涅的厄琉息斯秘仪的中心，这是希腊宗教中最著名的秘密仪式。早在公元前7世纪此地已有会堂，每年为期九天的节庆吸引数以千计的入会者，他们在堂内瞻仰圣物，并发誓不得透露所见。公元前480年波斯人焚毁了建筑，后来在伯里克利主持下按帕特农神庙建筑师伊克蒂诺斯的设计重建；约公元前318年，菲隆又增建了一座有十二根多立克柱的门廊。170年它被科斯托博克人洗劫，马可·奥勒留将其按更大规模重建，他也是唯一获准进入最内殿的俗人。392年皇帝狄奥多西一世取缔了秘仪，396年阿拉里克率领的哥特人洗劫厄琉息斯并摧毁了泰勒斯台里昂神庙，此后它再未重建。

en: The Temple of the Great Jaguar rises on the east side of the Great Plaza of Tikal, the city its own inscriptions called Yax Mutal, in the Peten rainforest of northern Guatemala. Dated to about 732, this Peten-style limestone step pyramid is crowned by a towering roof comb and takes its name from a carved lintel showing its king enthroned on a jaguar seat; it is also called the Temple of Ah Cacao after the ruler buried within it. That ruler was Jasaw Chan K'awiil I, who took the throne in 682 after a hundred and thirty years of silence in Tikal's records and broke the power of the rival city Calakmul in a battle of 695, opening Tikal's greatest age. The pyramid was his funerary monument, while the smaller Temple II across the plaza held the tomb of his queen, Lady Lahan Unen Mo'. His son Yik'in Chan K'awiil carried on the dynasty, but Tikal's fortunes faded with the Classic collapse: building ceased, the palaces were burned, the population drained away generation by generation, and by the end of the tenth century the jungle had swallowed the empty city and the jaguar temple with it.
zh: 大美洲虎神庙矗立在蒂卡尔大广场东侧。蒂卡尔在自身碑铭中自称亚什穆塔尔，位于危地马拉北部的佩滕雨林。这座佩滕风格的石灰岩阶梯金字塔约建于732年，顶端高耸着屋顶冠饰，因一块雕有国王端坐美洲虎王座的门楣而得名；它也被称为阿·卡考神庙，得名于葬在庙中的国王。这位国王是贾索·昌·卡维尔一世，他于682年登上王位，结束了蒂卡尔铭文中断一百三十年的沉寂，并在695年的战役中击溃宿敌卡拉克穆尔，开启了蒂卡尔最鼎盛的时代。金字塔是他的陵墓，广场对面较小的二号神庙则安葬着他的王后拉汉·乌嫩·莫。他的儿子伊金·昌·卡维尔延续了王朝，但随着古典期崩溃，蒂卡尔盛极而衰：营造停止，宫殿被焚，人口一代代流失，到10世纪末丛林已吞没这座空城，也吞没了美洲虎神庙。

en: The Temple of K'uk'ulkan, called El Castillo by the Spanish, is the great step pyramid at the heart of Chichen Itza in the northern Yucatan lowlands, raised to the Maya Feathered Serpent deity K'uk'ulkan, counterpart of the Quetzalcoatl worshipped in central Mexico. An inner temple was built between about 600 and 800, and the present pyramid, thirty metres tall with a base fifty-five metres across, took its final form around the ninth to eleventh centuries. Stairways climb all four sides; each has ninety-one steps, and counting the top platform they add up to three hundred and sixty-five, the days of the Maya solar year. Feathered serpents run down the northern balustrade, and at the equinoxes the setting sun casts triangles of shadow that seem to make the serpent crawl down the pyramid to earth. Chichen Itza had already declined as a regional power by 1100, and colonial Maya chronicles credit Hunac Ceel of Mayapan with its conquest in the thirteenth century, yet pilgrims still came to its sacred cenote. Spaniards under Montejo the Younger briefly held the ruins in 1532 and 1534 before being driven out, and Friar Diego de Landa described the pyramid in 1566, when the old city had become a ranch amid the forest.
zh: 羽蛇神庙在西班牙语中称卡斯蒂略，是尤卡坦北部低地奇琴伊察城中心的大阶梯金字塔，供奉玛雅人的羽蛇神库库尔坎，与墨西哥中部崇拜的魁札尔科亚特尔相对应。内层神庙约建于600年至800年间，现存金字塔高30米、底边长55米，在9至11世纪前后形成最终形制。金字塔四面各有一道阶梯，每道91级，加上顶部平台合计365级，正合玛雅太阳历的一年天数。北阶梯的栏杆雕有羽蛇，春分、秋分时夕阳投下的三角形阴影连成一线，仿佛羽蛇正沿金字塔爬行而下。奇琴伊察在1100年之前已衰落为地区强国，殖民地时期的玛雅编年史称玛雅潘的胡纳克·塞尔于13世纪征服了它，但朝圣者仍前往城中的圣井。1532年至1534年，小蒙特霍率领的西班牙人曾短暂占据废墟，随后被赶走；1566年修士迭戈·德·兰达记述这座金字塔时，古城已沦为丛林中的牧场。

en: The Temple of Confucius at Qufu in Shandong stands on the site of the philosopher's own house, which the Duke of Lu turned into a shrine soon after his death in 479 BC. It grew into the chief seat of the Confucian cult when Emperor Gao of the Han offered sacrifices there in 205 BC, setting a precedent followed by twelve emperors in person and by nearly two hundred imperial deputations. The original three-room house was replaced during a Sui rebuilding of 611, and Song works of the eleventh century laid out courtyards and hundreds of rooms; after a fire of 1214 under the Jin, the Yuan had restored the whole complex by 1302, and in 1331 it was enclosed by walls modelled on the imperial palace. The Ming rebuilding after another fire in 1499 gave the temple its present scale, its nine courtyards, yellow roof-tiles and the great Dacheng Hall deliberately echoing the Forbidden City, and Qing repairs following the fire of 1724 were completed by 1730. Together with the Kong Family Mansion and the Cemetery of Confucius, it forms the Three Confucian Sites, the destination of scholars and officials who came to venerate the master and his teachings.
zh: 山东曲阜的孔庙建于哲学家孔子的故宅之上，公元前479年孔子去世后不久，鲁君便将这座故宅辟为祭祀之所。公元前205年汉高祖亲临曲阜祭孔，开创了皇帝祀孔的先例，此后共有12位皇帝亲诣曲阜20次，派遣大臣致祭更达196次，孔庙由此成为孔门祀典的中心。原来的三间故宅在611年隋代重建时被拆除，11世纪宋代的扩建奠定了多进院落、数百间房舍的格局；1214年金朝时庙毁于火，到1302年元代已将整组建筑修复，1331年又仿照皇宫修筑了围墙。1499年再遭火灾后，明代重建奠定了现存规模，九进院落、黄色琉璃瓦和宏伟的大成殿都刻意仿效紫禁城；1724年火灾后的清代修缮于1730年完工。孔庙与孔府、孔林合称“三孔”，历代士人官员前来瞻仰这位先师及其学说，络绎不绝。

en: Teotihuacan, in the Valley of Mexico forty kilometres northeast of Mexico City, was the greatest city of ancient Mesoamerica, settled from about 100 BC and already a religious centre of the Mexican plateau by the first century. At its height around 450 it held perhaps 100,000 people, laid out along the Avenue of the Dead between the Pyramid of the Moon and the Ciudadela, whose Temple of the Feathered Serpent was ringed with sculpted serpent heads; the Pyramid of the Sun, sixty-five metres tall, still ranks among the largest pyramids on earth. Its talud-tablero architecture and obsidian trade reached as far as the Maya world, where a Teotihuacan king called Spearthrower Owl installed his own dynasts at Tikal in 378. Droughts linked to the climate crisis of 535 and 536 brought famine, and around 550 the temples and palaces along the great avenue were burned in an uprising and the city collapsed. Centuries later the Aztecs found the ruins and named them Teotihuacan, the birthplace of the gods, believing the universe had been created there; they came as pilgrims to the empty pyramids. In 1409 the resettled town received its own ruler, in 1418 it fell to Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco, and from 1427 it passed under the Aztec Empire as an Acolhua vassal, its sanctity outliving its power by a thousand years.
zh: 特奥蒂瓦坎位于墨西哥谷地、墨西哥城东北40公里，是古代美索美洲最伟大的城市，约自公元前100年起有人定居，1世纪时已是墨西哥高原的宗教中心。450年前后的鼎盛期，城中约有10万人口，城市沿死者大道展开，北端是月亮金字塔，南端是城堡区，区内的羽蛇神庙外墙环绕着雕刻的蛇头；高65米的太阳金字塔位列世界最大的金字塔之一。它的斜坡-壁板建筑风格和黑曜石贸易远播玛雅世界，378年，一位被学者称为“掷矛者猫头鹰”的特奥蒂瓦坎君王还在蒂卡尔扶立了自己的王族。535年至536年气候剧变引发连年旱灾和饥荒，约550年，大道两旁的神庙宫殿在一场起义中被焚，城市就此崩溃。数百年后，阿兹特克人发现这片废墟，将它命名为特奥蒂瓦坎，意为“众神诞生之地”，相信宇宙即开辟于此，并前来空旷的金字塔朝圣。1409年，重新有人聚居的城镇获封自己的统治者；1418年它落入阿斯卡波察尔科的特索索莫克之手；1427年起又作为阿科卢阿人的附庸并入阿兹特克帝国，它的神圣地位比其权势多延续了一千年。

en: Saint Peter's in the Vatican stands on the west bank of the Tiber in Rome, above the tomb of the apostle Peter and the former Circus of Nero. Constantine I ordered the first basilica built between 318 and 322, and for twelve centuries the Old Saint Peter's was the stage of papal ceremony: Charlemagne was crowned emperor there in 800, and in 846 Saracen raiders crossed the undefended ground outside the city walls, sacked the shrine and damaged the apostle's tomb, prompting Pope Leo IV to ring the Vatican with the Leonine Walls. By the fifteenth century the old church was structurally unsound, and after the popes returned from Avignon, Nicholas V and then Julius II decided on complete replacement. Work on the present Renaissance basilica began in 1506 under Donato Bramante; Michelangelo took over the design in 1547 and gave the church its great dome, Carlo Maderno added the long nave and facade, and the building was completed in 1626. Gian Lorenzo Bernini then furnished it with the bronze baldachin over the papal altar and the colonnaded square in front, while Michelangelo's Pietà remained among its most venerated sculptures.
zh: 梵蒂冈的圣伯多禄大殿坐落在罗马台伯河西岸，建在宗徒伯多禄的陵墓与昔日尼禄竞技场的遗址之上。君士坦丁一世于318—322年下令修建首座大殿，此后十二个世纪里，老圣伯多禄大殿一直是教宗礼仪的舞台：800年查理曼在此加冕为帝；846年撒拉森袭掠者穿过城墙外不设防的地带洗劫圣所、破坏宗徒陵墓，促使教宗利奥四世环绕梵蒂冈修筑利奥城墙。到15世纪，老堂结构已岌岌可危，教宗从阿维尼翁返回后，尼古拉五世继而尤利乌斯二世决定彻底重建。现存的文艺复兴式大殿于1506年在多纳托·布拉曼特主持下开工；米开朗基罗1547年接掌设计，为教堂留下宏伟穹顶，卡洛·马代尔诺增建长中殿与立面，整座建筑于1626年完工。随后詹洛伦佐·贝尼尼为教堂配上教宗祭坛上方的青铜华盖和殿前带柱廊的广场，而米开朗基罗的《圣殇》始终是殿内最受崇敬的雕塑之一。

en: Thirukkadigai, also called Sholingapuram, is a Vishnu temple at Sholinghur in the Tamil country, praised in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham of the Alvar saints and counted among the 108 Divya Desams. Its name comes from the belief that worship lasting a kadigai, about twenty-four minutes, is enough to win the deity's blessing; the Vishnu and Padma Puranas call the place Kadigai, and the sage Vishwamitra is said to have earned the title of Brahmarishi here. Three shrines occupy twin hills: Yoga Narasimha on the larger hill, reached by more than 1,300 steps, Bhaktavatsala Perumal at its foot, and a four-armed Hanuman on the smaller hill. Inscriptions record gifts from Kulothunga Chola III and other early rulers, and the teacher Manavala Mamunigal is said to have expounded the Thirupavai here. The temple follows the Tenkalai tradition. In July 1781 the hills around it were the scene of the Battle of Sholinghur, fought between the British and Hyder Ali of Mysore.
zh: 蒂鲁卡迪盖又名绍林加普兰，是泰米尔地区绍林古尔的一座毗湿奴神庙，因受到阿尔瓦尔圣徒《四千圣诗》的赞颂而被列为一百零八座圣庙之一。其名源于一种信仰：在此礼拜仅需一卡迪盖，约二十四分钟，便可获得神祇赐福；《毗湿奴往世书》和《莲花往世书》都称此地为卡迪盖，相传众友仙人正是在此证得梵仙之号。两座山丘上分布着三处神龛：大山丘上是需攀登1300余级台阶的瑜伽那罗辛哈，山脚是巴克塔瓦察拉·佩鲁马尔，小山丘上则有四臂哈奴曼。铭文记载了库洛通加·朱罗三世等早期统治者的布施，宗师马纳瓦拉·马穆尼加尔相传曾在此宣讲《蒂鲁帕瓦伊》。神庙遵行滕卡莱派仪轨。1781年7月，神庙周围的丘陵成为绍林古尔战役的战场，英军与迈索尔的海德尔·阿里在此交锋。

en: Thirukkavalampadi, also called the Gopalakrishna Perumal Temple, is a small Vishnu shrine at Thirunangur near Sirkali on the Tamil Nadu coast, not far from Karaikal. Vishnu is worshipped here as the cowherd Krishna, Gopalakrishna, flanked by Rukmini and Satyabhama, and the place takes its name from a legend in which Krishna rescued an elephant, kavalam meaning elephant and padi a place. It is one of the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams, said to mark the eleven forms Vishnu assumed to calm Shiva's furious dance after the death of Sati, and it is glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the canon of the Alvar saints compiled from the 600s to the 800s, above all by Thirumangai Alvar. Built in the Dravidian style with a three-tiered gopuram, the temple joins the other ten shrines of the group each year in the Thai-month Mangalasasana festival, when their festival images are carried together on Garuda mounts.
zh: 底禄迦伐蓝波地又称“戈帕拉克里希纳·佩鲁马尔神庙”，是泰米尔纳德沿海锡尔卡利附近蒂鲁南古尔村的一座小型毗湿奴神庙，离加里加尔不远。庙中毗湿奴以牧童奎师那（戈帕拉克里希纳）之像受供，鲁格米尼与萨蒂亚芭玛分立两侧；庙名源于奎师那在此拯救一头大象的传说，“迦伐兰”意为大象，“波地”意为地方。它是蒂鲁南古尔十一座迪维亚·德萨姆之一，相传标记着毗湿奴为平息湿婆在萨蒂死后狂舞而化现的十一种形象；6至9世纪阿尔瓦尔派圣徒编成的《四千圣咏》对此庙有所歌颂，尤以提鲁芒盖·阿尔瓦尔的颂诗为多。神庙为达罗毗荼风格，建有三层门楼；每年泰历泰月的“曼加拉萨萨纳”节上，它与其余十座同组神庙的节庆神像一同乘迦楼罗舆驾会聚。

en: The Thiruvallam Sree Parasurama Temple stands on the banks of the Karamana River just outside Thiruvananthapuram, in the land known to tradition as Parasurama Kshetram. It is the only temple in Kerala dedicated to Parashurama, the axe-bearing sixth avatar of Vishnu, who in legend hurled his axe into the sea and made the waters retreat from Gokarna to Kanyakumari; Brahmins are said to have raised the shrine in gratitude after he granted them the reclaimed land as a gift. Counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Vaishnava tradition, it honours Shiva with equal standing and is one of the few Hindu temples where Brahma also receives worship, alongside subsidiary shrines for Matsya, Krishna, Ayyappa and Veda Vyasa. The present structure was last renovated between the 1100s and 1200s. The temple draws pilgrims for the ancestor-rite of Balitharpanam on the new-moon day of the Malayalam month of Karkidakam, when devotees bathe in the river before offering homage to their forefathers.
zh: 耻卢伐蓝‑室利持斧罗摩神庙坐落在特里凡得琅城外的卡拉马纳河畔，这片土地在传统上被称为持斧罗摩田。它是喀拉拉唯一一座供奉持斧罗摩的神庙；持斧罗摩是毗湿奴的第六化身，传说他把战斧掷入大海，令海水从戈卡尔纳退到坎尼亚库马里，又将这片新生的土地施予婆罗门，婆罗门感念其恩，建起了这座庙。它位列毗湿奴派108座阿比摩纳圣地之一，庙中湿婆享有同等尊位，还是少数同时供奉梵天的印度教神庙，配殿中另祀摩蹉、黑天、阿亚潘和毗耶娑等神祇。现存建筑最后一次重修是在12至13世纪。每逢马拉雅拉姆历卡尔基达卡月的新月日，信众先在河中沐浴，再行名为巴利塔尔帕南的祭祖之礼，追荐先人，这座神庙因此吸引大批朝圣者。

en: Thommanon is a small but finely finished Hindu temple standing just east of the Victory Gate of Angkor Thom, opposite its companion shrine Chau Say Tevoda on the road to Ta Keo. Most scholars attribute it to Suryavarman II, who reigned from 1113 to 1150 and built Angkor Wat itself, so the tower rose at the moment classical Khmer architecture reached its peak, though a few place its devata carvings as early as the reign of Jayavarman VI around 1100. It was dedicated to both Shiva and Vishnu, reflecting Suryavarman's promotion of the Vaishnava cult alongside the older linga worship of the court. Built of sandstone on a single-towered plan, the temple opens east through a gopura gateway and a mandapa antechamber into the central sanctuary crowned by a prasat tower, with every doorway framed by carved pediments; unlike its neighbour Chau Say Tevoda, its upper structure used no wood beams encased in stone, which is why it has survived the centuries in better repair. Its chief glory is the crowd of devatas, divine female figures in flowered crowns and pleated sampot skirts, their fingers held in the distinctive devata mudra also seen at Angkor Wat. The enclosure walls and the separate library have vanished, leaving the gateways and central tower above the forest floor as a compact monument of the Angkor Wat style.
zh: 塔玛侬神庙是一座小巧而精致的印度教神庙，坐落在吴哥通胜利门东侧，在通往塔凯奥的路上与姊妹神庙周萨神庙遥遥相对。多数学者认为它建于苏利耶跋摩二世（1113—1150年在位）时代——这位国王正是吴哥窟的建造者，因此此塔落成之时，正值高棉古典建筑的巅峰；也有少数学者根据飞天浮雕把它提早到约1100年阇耶跋摩六世在位时。神庙同时供奉湿婆与毗湿奴，体现出苏利耶跋摩在宫廷传统的林伽崇拜之外大力提倡毗湿奴信仰。整庙以砂岩建成，采用单塔布局：朝东依次经过瞿布罗门楼和曼达波前室，才进入上方冠以普拉萨塔的中央密室，每道门框都饰有雕花山墙。与邻近的周萨神庙不同，它的上部结构没有使用外石内木的梁架，这也是它历经数百年保存得更为完好的原因。庙中最动人的是成群的提婆妲女神像：花冠华服、褶裙曳地，手指摆出吴哥窟中也能见到的独特“提婆妲手印”。围墙与独立的经藏已湮没无存，只余门楼和中央塔矗立在林地之上，成为吴哥窟风格的一座精致缩影。

en: The Thrikkakara Vamanamoorthy Temple, at Thrikkakara near Kochi in Kerala, is one of India's principal shrines dedicated to Vamana, the dwarf avatar of Vishnu, and is counted among the 108 Divya Desams. Tradition ascribes its founding to the sage Parashurama and gives the site an age of some two thousand years. The main icon shows Vamana about to set his foot on the Asura king Mahabali, recalling the legend in which the dwarf, granted three paces of land by the generous king, swelled to gigantic size as Trivikrama and strode across earth, heaven and the netherworld, leaving Bali only his own head for the third step and granting him rule of the underworld for his humility. This legend is the heart of Onam, Kerala's great harvest festival, which welcomes Bali's annual return: the temple is the ceremonial centre of Onam, and its records preserve the earliest known mention of the festival, dated to 861. In the eighteenth century, after Marthanda Varma of Travancore and the East India Company annexed the territory from the Kingdom of Kochi, the Onam celebrations were jointly conducted by the local chiefs under the leadership of the Maharaja of Travancore, and the temple's feast drew devotees across religious lines.
zh: 特里卡卡拉的筏摩那穆尔蒂神庙位于喀拉拉的科钦附近，是印度供奉毗湿奴侏儒化身筏摩那的主要神庙之一，位列108座迪维亚·德萨姆圣地。相传神庙由仙人持斧罗摩开创，历史可上溯约两千年。主尊塑像表现筏摩那正准备把脚踏在阿修罗王钵利身上：传说侏儒筏摩那向慷慨的钵利求赐三步之地，应允之后便化身为巨人三步神毗讫罗摩，一步跨大地，一步跨天国，第三步已无地可跨，钵利便低头献出自己的头颅，筏摩那嘉其谦卑，命他统治阴间。这个传说正是喀拉拉盛大丰收节欧南节的核心，欧南节迎请的便是钵利每年一次的归来；特里卡卡拉神庙是欧南节的礼仪中心，庙中档案还保存着已知最早的欧南节记载，年代为861年。18世纪，特拉凡哥尔的玛尔坦达·瓦尔马与英国东印度公司从科钦王国手中夺取此地后，欧南节改由各地首领在特拉凡哥尔大君主持下共同举办，庙中的圣宴也吸引了不同信仰的民众前来。

en: Outside the walls of Tibur, modern Tivoli, where the Via Tiburtina descends the Aniene gorge on its way from the Abruzzi highlands to Rome, stood the sanctuary of Hercules Victor, the greatest Italic shrine of the hero god and second in the Mediterranean only to the one at Gades in Spain. Hercules was the town's patron, worshipped as the warrior Invictus after a victory over the Aequi, as Hercules Saxanus, protector of the travertine quarries, and as guarantor of trade, flocks and sworn bargains; tradition held that the oil merchant Marcus Octavius Herennius brought the cult from Tibur to Rome and built the round temple of Hercules in the Forum Boarium. The monumental complex was raised in two phases between the 160s and 82 BC, its terraced substructures modelled on the sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia at nearby Praeneste. The road was carried through the precinct in a vaulted via tecta, and the old bridge toll became offerings and tithes to the god; warehouses, banks, inns and an oracular pool, where answers were read from objects thrown into the spring, made it a fabulously wealthy pilgrimage and market centre. The octastyle temple with its colossal Hercules statue and yellow-painted gabled roof dominated the gorge and was visible from Rome. Augustus often judged cases under its arcades, the theatre was completed in his reign, and Hadrian later built his great villa on the plain below Tibur.
zh: 赫拉克勒斯·维克托圣所位于蒂布尔（今蒂沃利）城墙外，控扼着提布尔提那大道从阿布鲁佐高地沿阿涅内河峡谷通往罗马的要道。它是意大利本土最大的英雄神圣所，在地中海世界仅次于西班牙加的斯的那一座。赫拉克勒斯是这座城市的保护神：人们因战胜埃魁人而奉他为战神“无敌者”，又奉他为石灰华采石场的保护神“萨克萨努斯”，以及贸易、牧群和契约誓言的担保者。相传油商马库斯·屋大维·赫伦尼乌斯把这一崇拜从蒂布尔带到罗马，并在牛市广场建起了圆形的赫拉克勒斯神庙。这座宏伟建筑群分两期建成于公元前2世纪60年代至前82年，台地式底层结构仿效了附近普拉埃内斯特的头生子之神福尔图娜圣所；大道经由拱顶的“有顶之路”穿过圣所，原先的过桥税改为向神敬献的供物和什一税。仓库、钱庄、客栈，以及一处凭投入泉中之物解读答复的神谕池，使这里成为财富惊人的朝圣与贸易中心。八柱围柱式神庙中矗立着赫拉克勒斯巨像，涂成黄色的人字屋顶高踞峡谷之上，在罗马城都能望见。奥古斯都常在它的柱廊下审理案件，剧场也在他在位时完工；哈德良后来又在蒂布尔下方的平原上营建了自己的宏大别墅。

en: The Great Mosque of Tinmal stands in the High Atlas village of Tinmal, on the Tizi-n-Test pass road between Marrakesh and the Sous region. Tinmal was the first capital of the Almohad movement, where Ibn Tumart settled his followers in 1124 or 1125 and made his base for war on the Almoravids; when he died in 1130 he was buried there, and his tomb became a sanctuary and place of pilgrimage. A first mosque was raised at once, and after the Almohad conquest of Marrakesh the caliph Abd al-Mu'min built the present mosque in 1148, some traditions giving 1153 or 1154. Craftsmen from Marrakesh gave it the same hypostyle plan and mihrab style as the Kutubiyya, though on the smaller scale of a mountain town, and later Almohad rulers were laid to rest beside it. Tinmal also served as the dynasty's last redoubt: when the Marinids overran Morocco, the remaining Almohad leaders made their final stand here until they were defeated and captured in 1275.
zh: 廷马尔大清真寺坐落在大阿特拉斯山区的廷马尔村，扼守连接马拉喀什与苏斯地区的提济恩泰斯特山口。廷马尔是穆瓦希德运动的第一个都城：1124年或1125年，伊本·图马特把追随者安置在这里，以此为基地向穆拉比特王朝开战。他于1130年去世后葬在此地，坟墓逐渐发展为圣所和朝圣地，当时便建起了第一座清真寺。穆瓦希德人攻占马拉喀什后，哈里发阿卜杜勒·慕敏于1148年修建了现存的这座清真寺，也有史料将始建年代记作1153年或1154年。来自马拉喀什的工匠赋予它与库图比亚清真寺相同的多柱式布局和米哈拉布风格，只是规模与山镇相称，后来的穆瓦希德君主也安葬在寺旁。廷马尔还是这个王朝最后的据点：马林王朝席卷摩洛哥时，残余的穆瓦希德首领在此负隅顽抗，直到1275年兵败被俘。

en: Titi'kaka is the Aymara name of the Island of the Sun, a rocky island in the southern part of Lake Titicaca facing Pomata, which Inca belief held to be the birthplace of the sun god Inti. The chronicler Bernabé Cobo recorded two versions of the origin myth set at a sandstone crag on the island called Titi Qala: in one, people long without daylight watched the Sun rise from the rock and took it for his dwelling place; in the other, the island was the first land to emerge after a great flood, when the Sun came out from behind the crag to light the sky again. Manco Cápac, first of the Incas and son of Inti, was said to have issued from the same rock. Human settlement on the island reached back to the third millennium before Christ, and a Tiwanaku ritual centre already stood above the crag before the Inca conquest of the southern lake in the fifteenth century turned Titi Qala into one of the great pilgrimage destinations of the empire, ranked with the oracle of Pachacamac. The tenth Inca, Túpac Yupanqui, who reigned from about 1471 to 1493, built a temple at the sacred rock together with a convent for chosen women and an inn for pilgrims, whose boats crossed the cold lake from towns such as Pomata.
zh: Titi'kaka 是太阳岛的艾马拉语名称。这座岩石岛屿位于的的喀喀湖南部，与波马塔隔湖相望，印加人相信太阳神因蒂就诞生在这里。编年史家贝尔纳韦·科博记录了两则以岛上砂岩圣岩“蒂蒂卡拉”为舞台的起源神话：一说人们久困黑暗，忽见太阳从岩后升起，便将此岩视为太阳的居所；另一说称洪水退去时太阳岛最先露出水面，太阳也从圣岩后方重新升起照亮天空。印加初代君主、因蒂之子曼科·卡帕克据说也从这块岩石中走出。岛上人类定居史可追溯至公元前第三个千年，在印加于15世纪征服湖南部地区之前，圣岩上方已有一处蒂亚瓦纳科仪式中心；征服之后，蒂蒂卡拉成为帝国最重要的朝圣地之一，地位堪比帕查卡马克神谕所。第十代印加图帕克·尤潘基（约1471—1493年在位）在圣岩旁修建神庙，又为选拔出来的圣女建了修道院、为朝圣者建了旅舍；朝圣者的船只便从波马塔等城镇出发，横渡寒冷的湖水而来。

en: The primatial cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption in Toledo is the senior church of Spain, its archbishop holding the title Primate of the Spains granted by Pope Urban II in 1088. A Visigothic cathedral stood on the site from at least 587, when King Reccared abjured Arianism there, and the councils of Toledo made the city the ecclesiastical heart of the Visigothic kingdom. After the Muslim conquest the church was replaced by the city's great mosque, which Alfonso VI converted to Christian use when he reconquered Toledo in 1085. The present High Gothic building, modelled on Bourges Cathedral, was begun in 1226 under Ferdinand III with five naves laid over the mosque's old footprint, and the vaults of the central nave were closed only in 1493, under the Catholic Monarchs. Known as Dives Toletana, the Rich Toledan, it houses the Mozarabic Chapel preserving the old Hispano-Mozarabic rite and the enormous gilded monstrance made by Enrique de Arfe between 1517 and 1524 for Cardinal Cisneros, carried each year in the Corpus Christi procession. Several kings of Castile lie buried in its chapels.
zh: 托莱多的圣母升天首席主教座堂是西班牙地位最高的教堂，其大主教拥有教皇乌尔班二世于1088年颁赐的“西班牙首席主教”头衔。587年，雷卡雷多国王在此宣布弃绝阿里乌斯派，说明至迟那时此地已有一座西哥特主教座堂；历次托莱多会议也使这座城市成为西哥特王国的教会中心。穆斯林征服后，教堂被城中的大清真寺取代，阿方索六世于1085年收复托莱多后又将清真寺改为基督教堂。现存的盛期哥特式建筑以布尔日主教座堂为蓝本，1226年在费尔南多三世治下动工，五条中殿恰好覆盖旧清真寺的基址，中殿拱顶直到1493年天主教双王时期才合拢。它素有“富庶的托莱多人”之称，院内的莫萨拉布小堂保留着古老的西班牙-莫萨拉布礼仪；恩里克·德·阿尔费于1517至1524年为西斯内罗斯枢机打造的巨大镀金圣体光，每年基督圣体节游行时抬出。多位卡斯蒂利亚国王也安葬在各小堂中。

en: Tōllān, the archaeological site of Tula in the present-day Mexican state of Hidalgo northwest of Mexico City, was known in Nahuatl as Tollan Xicocotitlan and rose after the decline of Teotihuacan as the capital of the Toltecs. An earlier settlement called Tula Chico flourished from about 650 to 900, and the great ceremonial center of Tula Grande reached its height between 900 and 1150, housing perhaps sixty thousand people on a grid of avenues and plazas. Its most sacred monument was the Pyramid of Quetzalcoatl, crowned by towering basalt columns carved as Toltec warriors, and the feathered-serpent cult centered here spread across central Mexico. A long drought and pressure from migrating Chichimeca groups undermined the city, whose ceremonial center was burned and abandoned in the twelfth century. The site was never entirely deserted, and later peoples remembered Tollan as the legendary city of wisdom and craftsmanship linked to the priest-king Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl; when the Spanish arrived, scribes and feather workers still lived among its ruins, and the Aztecs traced their own royal legitimacy back to its Toltec rulers.
zh: 图拉圣城即今墨西哥城西北伊达尔戈州的图拉遗址，纳瓦特尔语名为托兰-希科科蒂特兰，在特奥蒂瓦坎衰落后崛起，成为托尔特克人的都城。早期聚落“小图拉”约兴盛于650—900年，宏伟的礼仪中心“大图拉”在900—1150年达到鼎盛，按网格布局的街道与广场上生活着约六万居民。城中最神圣的建筑是羽蛇神金字塔，塔顶矗立着雕成托尔特克武士形象的高大玄武岩柱，以此为中心的羽蛇神信仰传遍了墨西哥中部。长期干旱和南下的奇奇梅卡诸部的压力削弱了城市，礼仪中心在12世纪被焚毁废弃。但遗址从未完全荒废，后世各民族把图拉传颂为与祭司王塞·阿卡特·托皮尔钦·魁札尔科亚特尔相连的智慧与工艺之城；西班牙人到来时，仍有书吏和羽毛工匠居住在废墟之间，阿兹特克人也将自己王权的合法性追溯到这里的托尔特克统治者。

en: Trichambaram Temple is a Krishna shrine at Taliparamba in the Kannur district of northern Kerala, founded around the 900s under the Mushika dynasty and praised in the eleventh-century Sanskrit court poem the Mūṣikavaṃśa. Its central image shows Krishna in his ferocious Raudra posture after slaying the tyrant Kamsa, and the temple counts among the Abhimana Kshethrams, a list of the most esteemed Vaishnavite shrines. The sanctum walls carry carvings and murals painted in the 1400s and 1500s. A separate Durga shrine stands in the middle of a temple tank, one of the hundred and eight Durgalayas of ancient Kerala, while smaller shrines honour Shiva, Ganesha, Shasta and the serpent deities.
zh: 多梨占婆蓝神庙是北喀拉拉坎努尔县塔利帕兰巴的一座奎师那神庙，约建于10世纪穆希卡王朝时期，11世纪的梵语宫廷史诗《穆希迦世系》曾加以称颂。庙中主像呈现奎师那诛杀暴君刚沙之后的愤怒相，该庙也被列入毗湿奴派最受尊崇的圣庙名录。圣所墙壁上保留着15至16世纪绘制的雕刻与壁画。庙中水池中央另有一座杜尔迦神龛，是古代喀拉拉一百零八座杜尔迦庙之一；周围的小庙则供奉湿婆、象头神、夏斯塔和蛇神。

en: The Krishna Matha at Udupi, on the Karnataka coast, was established in 1285 by Madhvacharya, the philosopher who founded the Dvaita, or dualist, school of Vedanta. Tradition holds that he brought the image of Krishna from Dwarka hidden inside a block of gopichandana clay and installed it here; the deity faces west and is viewed through the nine-holed silver window called the Navagraha Kindi, while an outer window, the Kanakana Kindi, commemorates the 16th-century devotee-poet Kanakadasa. Madhvacharya also founded eight surrounding monasteries, the Ashta Mathas, whose swamis take turns to run the shrine: under the paryaya system, worship and administration pass from one matha to the next every two years, a rotation that has made Udupi the enduring centre of the Madhva Vaishnavite tradition and one of South India's busiest pilgrimage kitchens.
zh: 乌杜比的奎师那神庙位于卡纳塔克沿海的乌杜比，1285年由哲学家摩陀伐建立，他也是吠檀多二元论学派（德瓦伊塔）的奠基人。相传他把从德瓦尔卡迎来的奎师那像藏在一块戈皮旃檀泥块中带来并安奉于此；神像面朝西方，信众须通过名为“九曜窗”的九孔银窗瞻仰，外侧的“迦纳迦窗”则纪念16世纪的虔信诗人迦纳迦达萨。摩陀伐还在周边建立了八座修道院，即“八马特”；八院的斯瓦米依照“帕里亚亚”制度每两年轮流接管神庙的祭祀与行政，使乌杜比长期成为摩陀伐毗湿奴派传统的中心，也是南印度最繁忙的朝圣供餐地之一。

en: The Ulagalantha Perumal Temple, also called the Trivikrama Temple, stands at Tirukkoyilur in the Tamil country, south of Tiruvannamalai. Vishnu is worshipped here as Ulagalantha Perumal, the lord who measured the world, with Lakshmi as Poongothai, and the shrine is counted among the 108 Divya Desams, glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham of the Alvar saints. It was first raised by the medieval Cholas and later enriched by the kings of Vijayanagara and the Nayaks of Madurai; its eleven-tiered rajagopuram, rising fifty-nine metres, is the third tallest temple tower in the Tamil land.
