zh: 拜宁语是一个小型非南岛语（即巴布亚语）语族，由新不列颠岛东部加泽尔半岛的拜宁人使用，成员包括马里语、卡克特语、凯拉克语、辛巴利语和乌拉语，每一种都对应独立的氏族身份；西南方已消亡、未留下语言记录的马科尔科尔语也曾是其近邻，该语族看来与陶利尔—布塔姆语族有远亲关系。拜宁人很可能是公元前1500年前后南岛航海者到达之前很久便居住在俾斯麦群岛的巴布亚人群体的后裔，被视为加泽尔半岛最早的居民。17世纪起，迁徙而来的托莱人占据了土地肥沃、火山众多的东北海岸，加上拉包尔一带数百年来的火山喷发，拜宁人被迫退入后来以他们命名的内陆拜宁山脉。他们以刀耕火种的园圃农业为生，主粮是芋头；最著名的传统是夜间的火舞，在其发源地卡克特语地区称作阿图图：舞者佩戴卡瓦特和翁翁式高大的树皮布面具，在火堆的余烬上跳跃穿行，这种仪式最初用于庆贺新生儿降生。

en: Balinese is a Malayo-Polynesian language of the Austronesian family, the chief language of the island of Bali and the head of the Bali–Sasak–Sumbawa subgroup, which also includes Sasak of Lombok and the Sumbawa language. It is also spoken on Nusa Penida, in western Lombok and eastern Java, and splits into Lowland and Highland varieties. Its Austronesian core carries a heavy Indian layer: Sanskrit and Old Javanese, or Kawi, reached Bali in the first millennium, and the Balinese script, a Brahmic abugida almost identical to the Javanese alphabet, first appears in ninth-century inscriptions. When the Majapahit minister Gajah Mada conquered the island in 1343, defeating its king at Bedulu, Javanese letters and literature became the language of court and temple. After Majapahit collapsed around 1500, fleeing Javanese aristocrats carried still more Kawi tradition to Bali, where Kawi serves as the ceremonial and religious register beside the everyday speech called Kapara Balinese. In the 1500s the Gelgel king Dalem Baturenggong carried Balinese rule and speech into Lombok and western Sumbawa. Gelgel fragmented after 1651; a new royal seat was set up at Klungkung in 1686, and the island split into nine competing kingdoms, which kept their courts and literary language independent through the 1700s, even though Dutch ships had first visited in 1597 and the VOC had since taken little interest in Bali.
zh: 巴厘语是南岛语系马来—波利尼西亚语族的语言，是巴厘岛的主要语言，也是巴厘—萨萨克—松巴哇语群的核心，该语群还包括龙目岛的萨萨克语和松巴哇岛的松巴哇语。它还通行于珀尼达岛、龙目岛西部和爪哇东部，内部低地和高地两种变体并存。巴厘语的南岛语底层之上覆盖着深厚的印度文化层：梵语和古爪哇语（卡维语）在第一个千年传入巴厘，而巴厘字母这种与爪哇字母几乎相同的婆罗米系元音附标文字，最早见于9世纪的碑铭。1343年，满者伯夷的重臣加查·马达在贝杜鲁击败巴厘国王、征服全岛，爪哇文字和文学从此成为宫廷与寺院的语言。约1500年满者伯夷覆灭后，出逃的爪哇贵族又把更多卡维传统带到巴厘，卡维语在当地一直作为礼仪和宗教语体使用，与称卡帕拉巴厘语的日常口语并存。16世纪，格尔格尔国王巴图伦贡把巴厘的统治和语言带到龙目岛和松巴哇岛西部。1651年后格尔格尔走向分裂，1686年新王庭设于克隆孔，全岛形成九个相互争战的小王国；它们在整个18世纪保持独立，维系着宫廷和文学语言，而荷兰船只虽早在1597年便已到访，荷兰东印度公司此后却长期对巴厘岛兴趣不大。

en: Balochi is a Northwestern Iranian language, the speech of the Baloch tribes whose original homeland lay east and south-east of the Caspian Sea and whose grammar preserves features close to Parthian and Median. The Baloch began drifting eastward in the late Sasanian period, and by the 800s and 900s Arab geographers such as Ibn Khordadbeh and al-Muqaddasi described them as living between Kerman, Khorasan, Sistan and Makran; the Seljuk invasion of Kerman in the 1100s pushed many tribes farther into the Makran coast and the hills that now form Balochistan. The language survives as a dialect continuum of three main groups, Western Rakhshani, Southern Makrani and Eastern Soleimani, with the isolated Koroshi dialect spoken in Fars. It had no written standard of its own until the 1800s, being set down in Persian script only when the need arose, while literacy among the Baloch ran instead to Persian and, in later centuries, Urdu.
zh: 俾路支语是伊朗语族西北支的语言，由原居里海东南一带的俾路支部落使用，语法上保留了与帕提亚语和米底语相近的特征。俾路支人在萨珊王朝晚期开始向东迁徙，到9至10世纪，伊本·胡尔达兹比赫、穆卡达西等阿拉伯地理学家已把他们记载为居住在克尔曼、呼罗珊、锡斯坦和莫克兰之间的族群；12世纪塞尔柱人入侵克尔曼，又迫使许多部落继续东迁，进入莫克兰沿海和今俾路支地区的山地。俾路支语是一种方言连续体，主要分为西支拉赫沙尼、南支莫克兰尼和东支苏莱曼尼三大方言，另有孤立的科罗希方言通行于法尔斯。直到19世纪它都没有自己的书面规范，只在必要时用波斯字母拼写，俾路支人的读写则借助波斯语，后来又借助乌尔都语。

en: Baltic is the Indo-European speech group of the south-eastern Baltic shore, which with the Slavic languages forms the conservative Balto-Slavic branch. It divides into Western Baltic, whose members included Old Prussian, Sudovian and Galindian, and Eastern Baltic, represented by Lithuanian and Latvian, with Samogitian and Aukštaitian as Lithuanian dialects. Baltic once reached from the Vistula to the Dnieper, as river names still show, until Slavic and Germanic expansion confined it to the coast. The Roman historian Tacitus noted the Baltic Aesti as early as 98, but the Balts resisted Christianization longer than other Europeans and wrote little: the first attestation is an Old Prussian epigram of about 1369. The Teutonic Knights conquered Prussia in the thirteenth century, and German settlement reduced Old Prussian to extinction by the early eighteenth century, hastened by the plague and famine of 1709 to 1711. Lithuanian first appeared in print in Martynas Mažvydas's catechism of 1547 and Latvian in a catechism of 1585, leaving the two Eastern Baltic tongues as the living heirs.
zh: 波罗的语是波罗的海东南岸的印欧语群体，与斯拉夫语言同属波罗的‑斯拉夫语族，被视为最保守的印欧语言之一。它分为两支：西波罗的语包括古普鲁士语、索多维亚语和加林迪亚语，东波罗的语以立陶宛语和拉脱维亚语为代表，萨莫吉希亚话和奥克什泰蒂亚话则是立陶宛语的方言。波罗的语一度从维斯瓦河流域延伸到第聂伯河流域，留存下来的河流名称仍可作证，后来斯拉夫和日耳曼语言扩张，才把它压缩到沿海一带。罗马史家塔西佗早在98年就记载过波罗的的埃斯蒂人，但波罗的各族比欧洲其他民族更久地抗拒基督教，书面文献出现很晚：最早的实证是约1369年的一首古普鲁士语短诗。条顿骑士团13世纪征服普鲁士，德国移民的涌入使古普鲁士语日渐衰微，到18世纪初终于消亡，1709至1711年的瘟疫和饥荒更加速了它的末路。立陶宛语首次印行于马尔蒂纳斯·马日维达斯1547年的教理问答，拉脱维亚语则见于1585年的教理问答，这两门东波罗的语言成了该语族仅存的活语言。

en: Bangi, also called Bobangi, is a Bantu language spoken on both banks of the Ubangi and Congo rivers around their confluence, from Mbandaka to Bolobo, in both the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo. It is the language of the Bobangi river traders, and its dialects include Bonga, Likuba, Likwala, Mpama and Nunu-Bobangi. In the early 1800s Bobangi canoe merchants carried it between Stanley Pool and the mouth of the Ubangi, and their wars against the declining Tio Kingdom opened the river stretches to their commerce, making Bangi the leading trade language of the western Congo. Its vocabulary forms the main lexical base of Lingala, the restructured river language that later grew out of it.
zh: 班吉语又称博班吉语，是一门班图语，通行于乌班吉河与刚果河汇流处的两岸，从姆班达卡到博洛博一带，地跨刚果（金）与刚果（布）。它是博班吉河商的语言，方言包括邦加、利库巴、利夸拉、姆帕马和努努-博班吉等。19世纪初，博班吉独木舟商人把它带到斯坦利潭与乌班吉河口之间；他们与衰落中的蒂奥王国交战，为自己的商业打开了河段，班吉语由此成为刚果河西部河段首要的贸易语言。它的词汇构成了林加拉语的主要词源基础，林加拉语便是后来由它重组演变出的河流语言。

en: Bantoid is the great Benue-Congo division of the Niger-Congo family, split into Northern and Southern Bantoid; the southern branch contains the several hundred Bantu languages that give the group its name and spread across most of subequatorial Africa. Its linguistic homeland lies in the borderlands of eastern Nigeria and western Cameroon, around the Benue valley, where the smaller non-Bantu Bantoid tongues are still spoken. From this nucleus the ancestors of the Bantu began one of Africa's great prehistoric migrations: farming villages with pottery traditions existed in the region by 5000 BC, iron working is attested by about 400 BC, and moving in two streams through and around the Congo rainforest, Bantu speakers had reached central Angola and the country west of Lake Victoria by around 500 BC and the south of the continent by about 300 AD. Bantoid languages are built around elaborate noun-class systems, and the closely related grammars and shared root words of Bantu tongues still bear witness to this common origin.
zh: 类班图语是尼日尔—刚果语系贝努埃—刚果语支下的一大分支，分为北类班图语和南类班图语两组；南组包含数百种班图语言，整个语支也因此得名，班图诸语遍布撒哈拉以南非洲的大半地区。它的语言故园在尼日利亚东部与喀麦隆西部交界的贝努埃河谷一带，较小的非班图类班图语言仍留存在那里。班图人的祖先正是从这个核心出发，展开了非洲史前大迁徙之一：公元前5000年当地已有农业村落和制陶传统，约公元前400年已使用铁器；移民分两路穿过或绕过刚果雨林，约公元前500年抵达安哥拉中部和维多利亚湖以西地区，约公元300年到达非洲南部。类班图诸语以繁复的名词分类体系为骨架，班图诸语彼此接近的语法和共通词根，仍见证着这段共同起源。

en: Barbakoan, or Barbacoan, is a language family spread across the rainy Pacific lowlands and the neighbouring Andes of south-western Colombia and northern Ecuador. Around 1337 its varieties served a chain of peoples: the Pasto around the highland frontier at Ipiales and Tulcán, the Cara or Caranqui in the lake country north of Quito, the Awa on the forested Pacific slope, the Tsáchila and Chachi in the coastal jungles of Esmeraldas and Santo Domingo, and the Guambiano and Puben groups near Popayán, while the Jama Coaque occupied the Ecuadorian coast. In the late fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries Inca armies under Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac conquered the Ecuadorian highlands, and the Kichwa dialect of Quechua they planted began replacing local speech, as among the Otavalo. Spanish forces under Sebastián de Belalcázar took Quito in 1534, and encomienda rule, epidemics and the spread of Spanish drove highland Barbakoan tongues such as Pasto and Cara to extinction, Cara lingering among the Caranqui until the eighteenth century; forest peoples such as the Tsáchila, Chachi and Awa kept their languages alive in their isolated homelands.
zh: 巴巴科安语（又译巴尔巴科安语）是一个分布在哥伦比亚西南部与厄瓜多尔北部多雨的太平洋低地及邻近安第斯山区的语系。1337年前后，它的各方言服务于一连串族群：高原边镇伊皮亚莱斯与图尔坎一带的帕斯托人，基多以北湖区的卡拉人（卡兰基人），太平洋坡地密林中的阿瓦人，埃斯梅拉达斯和圣多明各沿海丛林中的察奇拉人与查奇人，以及波帕扬附近的关比亚诺人和普本人，厄瓜多尔海岸则有哈马科阿克人。15世纪末至16世纪初，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基与瓦伊纳·卡帕克率领印加军队征服厄瓜多尔高原，他们带来的克丘亚语方言基奇瓦语开始取代当地语言，奥塔瓦洛人便是在这时改说基奇瓦语的。1534年塞巴斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔率西班牙军队攻占基多，委托监护制、疫病和西班牙语的扩张把帕斯托语、卡拉语等高原支系推向消亡，其中卡拉语在卡兰基人中一直残存到18世纪；而察奇拉人、查奇人和阿瓦人等森林族群则在闭塞的家园里保住了自己的语言。

en: Barawana, or Baré, is the Arawakan language of the Baré people, also called Hanera, who lived along the upper Rio Negro from the site of present-day Manaus upstream to the Casiquiare canal, on the borderland of Brazil and Venezuela. It was divided into two dialects, Ihini and Arihini, and formed a small cluster with the now extinct Guinau, Mandawaca and Marawá tongues, Mandawaca being close enough to be mutually intelligible. Through the eighteenth century Baré was among the dominant languages of the upper Rio Negro, and from the early 1800s its name was used as a blanket term for all the Indigenous peoples of the river. Its decline followed the spread of Nheengatu, the Tupi-based Amazonian general language that was the official tongue of the colony of Grão-Pará and Maranhão from 1689 to 1727 and was carried up the Rio Negro by Carmelite missionaries; the Baré gradually adopted it, together with Spanish and Portuguese, in place of their own speech.
zh: 巴拉瓦纳语又称巴雷语，是巴雷人（亦称哈内拉人）的阿拉瓦克语言；巴雷人沿内格罗河上游而居，从今马瑙斯一带上溯至卡西基亚雷运河，地处巴西与委内瑞拉交界。它分伊希尼和阿里希尼两种方言，与现已消亡的吉瑙语、曼达瓦卡语、马拉瓦语组成一个小语群，其中曼达瓦卡语与它接近到可以互通。整个18世纪，巴雷语都是内格罗河上游最通行的语言之一，从19世纪初起，“巴雷”一名更被用来统称该河流域的所有原住民。它的衰落伴随涅恩加图语的扩张：这种以图皮语为基础的亚马孙通用语在1689—1727年间是格劳—帕拉和马拉尼昂殖民地的官方语言，由加尔默罗会教士带到内格罗河上游；巴雷人逐渐改用涅恩加图语以及西班牙语和葡萄牙语，本族语言随之弃用。

en: The Barito languages are a group of some twenty Malayo-Polynesian tongues named after the Barito River of South Kalimantan and divided into West Barito, East Barito and Mahakam branches, though some linguists treat them as a contact area rather than a single lineage. Their speakers are Dayak peoples of the central and southern Borneo interior, among them the Ngaju of the Ngaju and Kahayan river basins, whose West Barito speech shares the region with Banjarese Malay as a lingua franca, and the Ma'anyan of the East Barito regencies. The Ma'anyan preserve the memory of Nansarunai, a polity that had arisen before the twelfth century and was destroyed by Majapahit expeditions by 1389, a disaster their oral tradition calls the Javanese destruction and which scattered their sub-groups upriver. Most striking of all, the Southeast Barito speech was carried across the Indian Ocean: Ma'anyan is the closest relative of Malagasy, the language of Madagascar, taken there by traders and migrants between the seventh and thirteenth centuries and layered with Malay and Javanese loanwords.
zh: 巴里托语是以南加里曼丹巴里托河命名的一群马来—波利尼西亚语言，约有二十种，分为西巴里托、东巴里托和马哈坎三支，但部分语言学家认为它更像一个语言接触圈而非单一谱系。使用者是婆罗洲中南部内陆的达雅人，包括恩加朱河与卡哈扬河流域的恩加朱人，他们说西巴里托语，同时以班查马来语为通用语；还有东巴里托各县的马安延人。马安延人保存着南萨鲁奈的记忆：这个12世纪以前兴起的政权在1389年被满者伯夷的远征所灭，马安延人的口述传统称之为爪哇之祸，残部由此四散溯河而居。最引人注目的是，东南巴里托语还跨越了印度洋：马安延语是马达加斯加岛马达加斯加语最近的亲属，后者由7至13世纪间的商人和移民带到那里，并叠加了大量马来语和爪哇语借词。

en: Basque, whose speakers call it Euskara, is the language of the Basque Country on the western Pyrenees, straddling northern Spain and southwestern France, and is Europe's only living language isolate, with no proven link to any other tongue; most scholars regard it as the survivor of a language spoken before the Indo-European languages reached the region. Its grammar sets it apart from its Romance neighbours, with agglutinative word-building and an ergative-absolutive case system, even though centuries of contact have filled its vocabulary with Latin and later Spanish and French loanwords. The oldest coherent Basque sentences survive in the San Millán glosses of about 950, but a written literature began only in the sixteenth century: the Mexico bishop Juan de Zumárraga wrote the earliest surviving prose in 1537, Bernard Etxepare printed the first Basque book, Linguæ Vasconum Primitiæ, in 1545, and the Protestant priest Joanes Leizarraga published a Basque New Testament in 1571 at the request of Jeanne d'Albret, queen of Navarre. Its five historic dialects, Biscayan, Gipuzkoan, Upper Navarrese, Navarrese-Lapurdian and Souletin, mirror the old Basque provinces on both sides of the mountains.
zh: 巴斯克语在母语者口中称埃乌斯卡拉语，通行于比利牛斯山西段、地跨西班牙北部和法国西南部的巴斯克地区，是欧洲现存唯一的孤立语言，与任何已知语言都没有可证实的亲缘关系；多数学者认为它是印欧语言进入该地区之前当地语言的孑遗。它的语法与周围的罗曼语截然不同，采用黏着构词和作格-通格格位体系，但长期接触也使它的词汇里充满拉丁语以及后来西班牙语、法语的借词。现存最早成句的巴斯克语见于约950年的圣米良批注，而书面文学到16世纪才发端：1537年，墨西哥主教胡安·德·苏马拉加写下了存世最早的巴斯克语散文；1545年，贝尔纳特·埃切帕雷印出第一本巴斯克语图书《巴斯克语初果》；1571年，新教牧师霍阿内斯·莱萨拉加应纳瓦拉女王让娜·德·阿尔布雷之命出版了巴斯克语《新约》。它历史上的五大方言——比斯开、吉普斯夸、上纳瓦拉、纳瓦拉-拉布尔丁和苏莱方言，正对应着山脉两侧的旧巴斯克诸省。

en: Bassa, more fully Basaa, is a Bantu language of coastal Cameroon, spoken by the Bassa people of the lower Sanaga valley and the Wouri estuary, in the country's Centre and Littoral regions, in dialects such as Kogo, Yabasi and Dibuum. Its speakers belong to the Bantu farming peoples who settled the Atlantic coast of central Africa in the last centuries before Christ. Bassa oral tradition remembers a long migration through the interior to the rock sanctuary of Ngog Lituba, and by about 1400 its clans had spread from there to the lower Sanaga and the banks of the Wouri, where they lived by subsistence farming and fishing. Like other Bantu tongues the language is built on a system of noun classes, and its coastal dialects were shaped by the trade of the Cameroon estuary, where the neighbouring Duala rose as merchant middlemen in the centuries before the colonial era.
zh: 巴萨语是喀麦隆沿海的一支班图语言，由萨纳加河下游和武里河口一带的巴萨人使用，分布在喀麦隆中央区和滨海区，下分科戈、亚巴西、迪布姆等方言。操巴萨语的人群属于公元前最后几个世纪定居中非大西洋沿岸的班图农民。巴萨人的口传传统保存了一段穿越内陆的漫长迁徙记忆，最终落脚于名为恩戈格利图巴的岩石圣地；约1400年，各部族又从那里扩散到萨纳加河下游和武里河两岸，以自给农业和捕鱼为生。与其他班图语言一样，巴萨语以名词分类体系为骨架；其沿海方言深受喀麦隆河口贸易的影响，在殖民时代之前的几个世纪里，邻近的杜阿拉人正是在这一带崛起为经商的中介族群。

en: Batak denotes a cluster of Malayo-Polynesian languages of northern Sumatra and the Barrier Islands. On the Sumatran mainland around Lake Toba, the Batak languages proper divide into a northern branch of Karo, Pakpak-Dairi and Alas-Kluet and a southern branch of Toba, Angkola, Mandailing and Simalungun; the same wider group also takes in Gayo and the island languages of Nias, Mentawai and the divergent Enggano. Far from isolated, Batak highlanders traded camphor, benzoin and pepper through ports such as Barus, where a Tamil inscription of 1088 survives, and Chinese and Portuguese sources describe a Batak land under Srivijayan and later Acehnese influence. The languages were written in the Surat Batak script, derived from Pallava and Kawi models, which datu priests used mainly for divinatory and magical texts, while love laments kept the craft alive among ordinary speakers. From the sixteenth century the pepper trade of Aceh drew the Batak highlands into closer commerce with the Muslim sultanates on their coasts.
zh: 巴塔克语是苏门答腊北部及屏障群岛一群马来—波利尼西亚语言的统称。在苏门答腊本岛的多巴湖一带，狭义的巴塔克语分为北支的卡罗语、代里—帕克帕克语、阿拉斯—克鲁特语，以及南支的托巴语、昂科拉语、曼代林语和西马隆贡语；更广义的语群还包括加约语以及尼亚斯语、明打威语和差异很大的恩加诺语等岛屿语言。巴塔克高地人并非与世隔绝，他们经巴鲁斯等港口贩运樟脑、安息香和胡椒，当地留存有1088年的泰米尔碑文；中国和葡萄牙文献都记载过一块受室利佛逝、后受亚齐影响的巴塔克之地。这些语言使用苏腊巴塔克文，它源自帕拉瓦文和卡威文，主要由达图祭司用于占卜与巫术文本，而爱情哀歌则使书写在普通人中流传。16世纪起，亚齐的胡椒贸易把巴塔克高地与沿海穆斯林苏丹国更紧密地连在一起。

en: Baure is a Southern Arawakan language of the Llanos de Mojos, the seasonally flooded savanna of the Beni in eastern Bolivia, and the southern branch of the family to which it belongs also includes the Moxo and Terena tongues. It is closest to the Trinitario and Ignaciano Moxo varieties, differing from them chiefly by dropping word-final vowels, and itself comprises Baure proper, Carmelito and Joaquiniano. Jesuit priests moving out from Santa Cruz de la Sierra began evangelizing the region in the 1670s, founding Loreto and then, in 1686, the principal mission of Trinidad on the Mamoré River. In these reductions Moxo served as the general indigenous lingua franca, while Baure was used alongside it among the Baure people, who kept their language alive in greetings, folktales, ritual speech and the festival Song of the Baures.
zh: 巴乌雷语是南支阿拉瓦克语言，通行于玻利维亚东部贝尼省季节泛滥的莫霍斯平原；它所属的南部语支还包括莫霍语和特雷纳语。它与莫霍语的特里尼塔里奥、伊格纳西阿诺两种方言最接近，主要区别是巴乌雷语丢失了词尾元音；其内部又分巴乌雷本语、卡梅利托和华基尼亚诺三种方言。17世纪70年代，耶稣会教士从圣克鲁斯—德拉谢拉出发到该地区传教，先建洛雷托传教站，又于1686年在马莫雷河畔建立主要传教站特立尼达。在这些归化村里，莫霍语是原住民的通用语，巴乌雷语则在巴乌雷人中间并行使用，存留在问候、民间故事、仪式谈话以及节庆时唱的《巴乌雷之歌》中。

en: Beja, called Bidhaawyeet by its speakers, is the sole member of the Northern Cushitic branch of the Afroasiatic family, spoken by the pastoral Beja nomads of the Eastern Desert between the Nile and the Red Sea, from south-eastern Egypt through eastern Sudan into north-western Eritrea. The Beja descend from the Medjay and later the Blemmyes of ancient texts, and potsherd ostraca from Egyptian desert sites and monasteries of the 200s to the 500s preserve fragments of an Old Beja, including a translation of a psalm found at Saqqara. The kingdom of Aksum subdued the Beja and made them vassals in the 200s; the Arab writer al-Ya'qubi counted five Muslim Beja kingdoms in the 800s, while al-Maqdisi still described the Beja as Christians in the 900s. From the 800s migrating Arab tribes intermarried with them and spread Arabic and Islam, which prevailed among the Beja by the 1400s, and when Beja was committed to writing it used the Arabic alphabet.
zh: 贝贾语的使用者自称比达维耶特语，是亚非语系库希特语族北支唯一的语言，通行于尼罗河与红海之间的东部沙漠，由东南埃及经苏丹东部延伸到厄立特里亚西北部，使用者是以游牧为生的贝贾人。贝贾人是古文献中麦德杰伊人、后来的布莱米斯人的后裔；3世纪埃及沙漠遗址和修道院出土的陶片上保留着古贝贾语的残篇，塞加拉发现的一篇《诗篇》译文便是其中之一。阿克苏姆王国于3世纪征服并臣服了贝贾人；阿拉伯作家雅库比在9世纪记载了五个穆斯林贝贾王国，而穆卡达西在10世纪仍称贝贾人为基督徒。9世纪起迁入的阿拉伯部落与贝贾人通婚，带来阿拉伯语和伊斯兰教，到15世纪伊斯兰信仰已在贝贾人中占据上风；贝贾语落于文字时使用阿拉伯字母。

en: Bel is the name given to a group of closely related Austronesian languages of the Malayo-Polynesian branch, spoken along Astrolabe Bay and the nearby coast of Madang Province in northern Papua New Guinea. Its members include Takia on the southern half of Karkar Island and on Bagabag, Marik on the Gogol River, Gedaged in the coastal villages around Madang, which is itself sometimes called Bel, and a row of smaller tongues such as Bilibil, Matukar, Mindiri, Wab and Awad Bing. Long contact with neighbouring Papuan languages has reshaped their grammar: where most Austronesian languages place the verb before its object, the Bel languages have shifted to subject–object–verb order, copying the speech habits of their inland neighbours. These coasts were unknown to Europeans until 1827, when the French explorer Jules Dumont d'Urville sailed into the bay and named it Astrolabe Bay after his corvette.
zh: 比利奥语是对一批关系密切的南岛语系马来—波利尼西亚语支语言的称呼，通行于巴布亚新几内亚北部马当省的阿斯特罗莱布湾及附近海岸。其成员包括卡尔卡尔岛南半部和巴加巴格岛上的塔基亚语、戈戈尔河畔的马里克语、马当周边沿海村落使用的格达格德语（该语言本身有时也被称作比利奥语），以及比利比勒语、马图卡尔语、明迪里语、瓦布语、阿瓦德宾语等一批较小的语言。与邻近巴布亚语言的长期接触改变了它们的语法：多数南岛语言把动词放在宾语之前，比利奥诸语却改从内陆邻语的习惯，采用主语—宾语—动词的语序。欧洲人直到1827年才来到这片海岸，法国探险家儒勒·迪蒙·迪维尔驶入海湾，并以自己的护卫舰星盘号将其命名为阿斯特罗莱布湾。

en: Palauan, called tekoi er a Belau by its speakers, is a Malayo-Polynesian language of the Austronesian family, native to the Palau archipelago at the western end of the Caroline Islands. It occupies an unusual place in Micronesian linguistics: together with Chamorro it is one of only two indigenous languages of the region that fall outside the Oceanic sub-branch, and its exact relatives remain disputed. Its vocabulary nevertheless records centuries of sea-borne contact, including Oceanic words absorbed through Yapese and influences from Philippine and Samalic languages, while the name Belau itself goes back to the Palauan word for village. The islands were settled by Austronesian migrants from the direction of the Philippines or Indonesia in the third or second millennium before Christ. The Magellan expedition sighted the outlying island of Sonsorol as early as 1521, and in 1696 Palauan sailors shipwrecked on Samar enabled the missionary Paul Klein to draw the first European map of the islands. Through all this time Palauan remained an oral language, with no Latin-letter orthography until the later colonial period.
zh: 帕劳语的使用者自称其为“特科伊·埃尔·阿贝劳”，是南岛语系马来—波利尼西亚语族的语言，本土位于加罗林群岛西端的帕劳群岛（又译帛琉）。它在密克罗尼西亚语言中位置特殊：与查莫罗语一样，它是当地仅有的两种不属于大洋洲语族的本土语言之一，其确切亲属关系仍有争议。尽管如此，它的词汇记录了数百年的海上往来，既有经雅浦语吸收的大洋洲语言成分，也有菲律宾诸语言和萨马尔语的影响；“贝劳”这个名字本身就来自帕劳语里意为村庄的词。公元前第三至第二个千年纪，来自菲律宾或印度尼西亚方向的南岛语移民定居于此。早在1521年，麦哲伦的船队就望见了偏远的松索罗尔岛；1696年，遇险漂流到萨马岛的帕劳水手帮助传教士保罗·克莱因绘制出欧洲第一幅帕劳群岛地图。在整个这一时期，帕劳语始终是口头语言，拉丁字母拼写要到后来的殖民时代才出现。

en: Bengali, or Bangla, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan language spoken across the Bengal region, chiefly in Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal, with dialects reaching Assam and Tripura. It descends from the eastern Magadhi Prakrit through the Abahatta stage, and was already distinct in the eighth century, when a Chinese-Sanskrit dictionary of 782 recorded more than fifty Bengali words. The Buddhist Charyapada verses of the eighth to twelfth centuries are its earliest literature, and the ancestor of Bengali was the court language of the Pala and Sena rulers. Middle Bengali, from about 1400, absorbed Arabic and Persian words under the Bengal sultans, who patronised it instead of Persian; Shah Muhammad Sagir's Yusuf-Zulekha and the Chandidas poets' Srikrishna Kirtana are its landmarks. Its Brahmic alphabet took its own course around the year 1000, and Portuguese missionaries printed Romanised Bengali grammars in Lisbon by 1743. The standard language rests on the west-central Rarhi dialect of Nadia and Kushtia, while eastern dialects such as Sylheti and Chittagonian diverge sharply.
zh: 孟加拉语自称班格拉语，是东印度—雅利安语的一支，通行于孟加拉地区，主要在孟加拉国和印度西孟加拉邦，相近方言还延伸到阿萨姆和特里普拉。它由东部摩揭陀俗语经阿巴哈特阶段演变而来，8世纪已形成独立语言——782年编纂的一部汉梵词典记录了五十多个孟加拉语词。8至12世纪佛教徒的《恰利耶帕达》偈颂是其最早的文学，孟加拉语的祖先曾是波罗和犀那王朝的宫廷语言。约1400年起的中孟加拉语时期，它在孟加拉苏丹扶持下取代波斯语获得宫廷地位，并吸收阿拉伯语和波斯语词汇；沙阿·穆罕默德·萨吉尔的《优素福与祖莱哈》以及昌迪达斯诗人们的《室利黑天颂》是这一时期的里程碑。其婆罗米系字母约在1000年走上独立发展道路，葡萄牙传教士早在1743年就在里斯本印行了罗马字孟加拉语语法。标准语以纳迪亚和库什提亚一带的中西部拉尔希方言为基础，锡尔赫特、吉大港等东部方言则与它差异显著。

en: Besiro, better known as Chiquitano, is the language of the Chiquitania savanna in the Bolivian department of Santa Cruz, with its speakers also reaching into the Mato Grosso country of Brazil; the people call themselves Monkox and their speech Besiro, while the Spanish named them Chiquitos. Its wider family is disputed, being treated either as an isolate or as a branch of Macro-Je. At the coming of the Jesuits four varieties were in use, Tao, Pinoco, Manasi and Penoqui, of which Manasi is known only from a manuscript of 1706 and Penoqui was so different that the missionary Felipe Suarez compiled a separate catechism and dictionary for it. The Chiquitos had held out against the Spanish since the founding of Santa Cruz de la Sierra in 1559, until Jesuits opened the first reduction at San Javier de los Pinocas in 1692 and built a ring of mission towns in which Besiro became the common tongue of nearly fifty gathered tribes, numbering some fifty thousand people. When the Jesuits were expelled from the Spanish empire in 1767, the mission network dissolved: some villagers fell into unfree ranch labour, while others withdrew into the forest, carrying their language with them.
zh: 贝西罗语更常用的名字是奇基塔诺语，通行于玻利维亚圣克鲁斯省的奇基塔尼亚热带草原，使用者也分布到巴西马托格罗索一带；该族群自称蒙科什人，称自己的语言为贝西罗语，“奇基托斯”则是西班牙人给他们的名字。它的语系归属有争议，或被视为孤立语，或被归入大热语系。耶稣会士到来时，这种语言有陶、皮尼奥科、马纳西和佩诺基四种变体，其中马纳西语仅见于1706年的一份手稿，而佩诺基语差异之大，使传教士费利佩·苏亚雷斯不得不为它单独编写教理问答和词典。自1559年圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉建立以来，奇基塔诺人抵抗西班牙人近两百年，直到1692年耶稣会在皮尼奥卡人的圣哈维尔建立第一个归化传教镇，随后建起一圈传教城镇；贝西罗语在那里成为近五十个被聚拢部落的共同语，信徒总数约五万人，奇基塔诺族群也由此形成。1767年耶稣会被逐出西班牙帝国，传教网随之瓦解：一部分村民沦为牧场的不自由劳工，另一些人带着语言退入森林。

en: Bhili is a Western Indo-Aryan language of the Bhil group, closely related to Gujarati and Rajasthani and spoken across the hills and forests of west-central India, above all in Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra. Its roots lie in the same Old Gujarati continuum that served as a literary language from the twelfth century and had taken a fairly standardised written shape by about 1300. The Bhils are one of India's largest and most dispersed tribal peoples, and their name may come from a Dravidian word for the bow that was their characteristic weapon; their older aboriginal speech has been completely replaced by this Indo-Aryan tongue. Bhili exists mainly as an oral language and splits into as many as three dozen local varieties, shading into Rajasthani in the north-west and Marathi in the south-east. It is written in the Devanagari script but holds no official status, and many Bhils also use the dominant language of the region around them.
zh: 比尔语是比尔语群的一支西印度—雅利安语言，与古吉拉特语和拉贾斯坦语亲缘密切，通行于印度中西部的山林地带，尤以中央邦、古吉拉特邦、拉贾斯坦邦和马哈拉施特拉邦为多。它的根源可追溯至古吉拉特古语这一方言连续体；该语体12世纪起已用于书面文学，到1300年前后形成相当规范的书面形态。比尔人是印度人数最多、分布最广的部族群体之一，其名称可能源自达罗毗荼语中意为“弓”的词，弓箭正是他们标志性的武器；他们更早的土著语言已完全被这支印度—雅利安语言取代。比尔语主要以口头形式存在，分化出多达三十余种地方变体，在西北渐次融入拉贾斯坦语，在东南渐次融入马拉地语。它以天城文书写，但没有官方地位，许多比尔人还兼用当地的主流语言。

en: Biak, called wós Vyak by its speakers, is an Austronesian language of the South Halmahera-West New Guinea branch, spoken on Biak, Supiori and Numfor and the smaller Schouten Islands in Cenderawasih Bay, off the northern coast of New Guinea in present-day eastern Indonesia. Its name derives from that of Biak island, and its dialects, of which Biak-Numfoor is the best known, differ only in minor sound changes. The Biak were skilled seafarers: oral tradition recalls the war leader Gurabesi and ties with the Sultanate of Tidore in the fifteenth or sixteenth century, and the Portuguese navigator Jorge de Menezes reached the islands in 1526. From the early eighteenth century Biak settlers founded coastal villages along the Bird's Head Peninsula, and their language left its mark on the map, giving such place names as Manokwari, Doberai and Bomberai. Biak traders carried the language across the trade routes of Cenderawasih Bay as intermediaries between inland Papuans and Moluccan and other merchants.
zh: 比亚克语的使用者自称其为 wós Vyak，属于南岛语系南哈马黑拉—西新几内亚语支，通行于今印度尼西亚东部新几内亚岛北岸外、极乐鸟湾中的比亚克岛、苏皮奥里岛、农福尔岛及斯考滕群岛的小岛。语言之名得自比亚克岛，各方言中以比亚克—农福尔方言最知名，彼此只有细微的语音差异。比亚克人善于航海：口传史提到15或16世纪的战争领袖古拉贝西以及他们与蒂多雷苏丹国的联系，葡萄牙航海家豪尔赫·德·梅内塞斯于1526年抵达这些岛屿。18世纪初起，比亚克移民在鸟头半岛沿海建立村落，他们的语言也留在了地图上，马诺夸里、多贝拉伊、邦巴赖等地名都出自比亚克语。作为内陆巴布亚人与摩鹿加等地商人之间的中介，比亚克商人把这种语言带到了极乐鸟湾的各条商路上。

en: Bihari is a group of Eastern Indo-Aryan languages descended from the ancient Magadhi Prakrit, spoken across Bihar, Jharkhand, adjoining parts of Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, and the Nepalese Terai. Its chief members are Bhojpuri in the west, Magahi in the old Magadhan heartland and Maithili in Mithila to the east, with Angika and Bajjika. Buddhist Siddha poets composed the twilight-language Charyapada verses here between the eighth and thirteenth centuries, the group's earliest literary trace. Maithili became a court language under Mithila's Karnata dynasty: Jyotirishwar Thakur's early-fourteenth-century Varna Ratnakara, in the Tirhuta script, is the first prose work in any modern Indian language, and Vidyapati, active from about 1360 to 1450, wrote more than a thousand Radha and Krishna songs that shaped Vaishnava poetry as far as Bengal. Bhojpuri meanwhile gathered folk epics such as the Lorikayan between the eleventh and fourteenth centuries, first written in Kaithi but later generally in Devanagari.
zh: 比哈尔语是东印度—雅利安语一组语言的统称，均由古代摩揭陀俗语演化而来，通行于比哈尔、贾坎德、北方邦与西孟加拉邦毗邻地区以及尼泊尔特莱平原。主要成员包括西部的博杰普尔语、古摩揭陀核心地带的摩加希语、东部弥提罗地区的迈蒂利语，以及昂吉卡语和巴吉卡语。8至13世纪，佛教成就者诗人在这一带用“黄昏语”创作《恰利耶帕达》偈颂，是该语组最早的文学痕迹。迈蒂利语在弥提罗的卡尔纳特王朝成为宫廷语言：14世纪初乔蒂里什瓦尔·塔库尔以提尔胡塔字母写成的《瓦尔纳·拉特纳卡拉》，是所有近代印度语言中第一部散文作品；约1360至1450年在世的维迪亚帕蒂创作了千余首罗陀与黑天之歌，影响远及孟加拉的毗湿奴派诗歌。博杰普尔语则在11至14世纪积累了《洛里卡耶纳》等民间史诗，过去用凯提字母书写，后来一般改用天城体。

en: The Bikol languages are a group of Central Philippine Austronesian languages, closely related to Tagalog and the Visayan tongues, spoken on the Bicol Peninsula of southeastern Luzon and on the neighboring islands of Catanduanes and Burias. They form a fragmented continuum whose varieties are often mutually unintelligible, divided into Coastal Bikol, Inland Bikol such as Rinconada and the Albay group, and Pandan Bikol; Central Bikol, the speech of Naga and Legazpi, serves as the regional literary and urban standard. Before Spanish rule Bikol was written in a local baybayin syllabary. A Spanish expedition under Juan de Salcedo reached Naga in 1573 and Franciscan missionaries began converting the region in 1578, after which the Latin alphabet and a thick layer of Spanish loanwords took hold, alongside older Sanskrit loans from earlier maritime contacts. The Franciscan Marcos de Lisboa compiled the first Bikol vocabulary between 1602 and 1611, though it was printed only in 1754, and Andres de San Agustin's grammar of Bikol appeared in 1647. The languages are also unusual in preserving a special angry register, a coded vocabulary reserved for forceful speech.
zh: 比科尔语是南岛语系菲律宾语支中部语群的一组语言，与他加禄语和米沙鄢诸语关系密切，通行于吕宋岛东南部的比科尔半岛以及邻近的卡坦端内斯岛和布里亚斯岛。它内部高度分化，各变体往往互不相通，分为沿海比科尔语、林科纳达和阿尔拜语群等内陆比科尔语，以及潘丹比科尔语；其中那加和黎牙实比一带的中比科尔语是地区文学和城市通用的标准变体。西班牙统治之前，比科尔语用当地的贝贝因音节文字书写。1573年胡安·德·萨尔塞多率领的西班牙远征队抵达那加，方济各会传教士于1578年开始在当地传教，此后拉丁字母和大量西班牙语借词扎根，更古老的梵语借词则见证了更早的海上交往。方济各会士里斯本的马可仕在1602至1611年间编成第一部比科尔语词汇表，但直到1754年才印行；圣奥古斯丁的安德肋的比科尔语语法书则于1647年问世。比科尔语还有一个罕见特征：保留着一套专门用于激烈言辞的“愤怒语域”暗语词汇。

en: Binanderean is the Papuan language family of the northeast coast of New Guinea's Bird's Tail peninsula, spread across Oro Province and the adjoining edge of Morobe. Its many closely related tongues include Binandere itself, Suena and Zia in the north, the Orokaiva group with Aeka and Hunjara, the coastal Korafe, Notu and Baruga, and the divergent Guhu-Samane. Long classed within Trans–New Guinea, the family is grouped by some scholars with the Goilalan languages and the Purari isolate, also called Namau, of the Purari Delta. Contact with Austronesian newcomers ran deep: Oceanic-speaking villages along the coast were absorbed into Binanderean communities, the Papuan Tip languages took on a subject–object–verb word order under their influence, and Maisin became a mixed Oceanic language heavy with Binanderean material. The Orokaiva, the family's largest people, were renowned warriors organized into river, coastal and inland groups. When the French expedition of Bruni d'Entrecasteaux charted the nearby islands in 1793, the inland valleys of the Bird's Tail still lay entirely beyond European knowledge.
zh: 比南德雷语是新几内亚鸟尾半岛东北海岸的巴布亚语族，分布在奥罗省及莫罗贝省的邻近地带。它有许多亲缘密切的语言，包括比南德雷语本体、北部的苏埃纳语和齐亚语、以奥罗凯瓦语为主并含埃卡语、洪贾拉语的奥罗凯瓦语群，沿海的科拉费语、诺图语和巴鲁加语，以及分歧较大的古胡-萨马内语。它长期被划入跨新几内亚语系，后来有学者把它与戈伊拉拉语族、普拉里三角洲上的孤立语普拉里语（又称纳马乌语）归在一起。它与南岛语新来者的接触很深：沿海说大洋语的村落被吸纳入比南德雷语社群，巴布亚尖端诸语在其影响下采用了主宾谓语序，迈辛语则变成带有大量比南德雷语成分的混合大洋语。该语族最大的群体奥罗凯瓦人是出名的战士，分为河畔、沿海和内陆三支。1793年布吕尼·当特尔卡斯托的法国探险队测绘附近群岛时，鸟尾半岛的内陆河谷仍完全在欧洲人的认知之外。

en: The Bomberai grouping unites the West Bomberai family of Papuan languages, now usually placed within Trans-New Guinea. On the Bomberai Peninsula of western New Guinea it comprises Baham and its close relative Iha, together with the more distant Kalamang; its third branch is Timor-Alor-Pantar, which carries the many tongues of the Alor and Pantar islands, the Bunak speech of the central Timor mountains, and the East Timorese languages Makasae and Fataluku, the latter most closely related to Oirata of Kisar. These are the westernmost Papuan languages to survive, probably brought from New Guinea by a migration shortly before the Austronesian arrival, and all of them carry heavy Austronesian loan layers; Fataluku has also taken in Sanskrit and Arabic words through Malay and later Portuguese ones. Trade in birds-of-paradise feathers linked the peninsula with Srivijaya in the 600s, and the Javanese Nagarakretagama of the 1300s names Wwanin and Sran, likely the Onin and Kowiai lands, as Majapahit tributaries, the earliest record of native names for Papuan regions. The Spanish expedition of Luis Vaz de Torres first sighted the coast for Europeans in 1606, after which Tidore, expanding under the leader Gurabesi, drew the peninsula into its tributary sphere, while Alor and Solor paid tribute to the Sultanate of Bima. The Dutch built Fort Du Bus on Triton Bay in 1828 to anchor the Tidore protectorate, but abandoned it in 1835.
zh: 邦贝拉伊语这一划分整合了巴布亚语系的西邦贝拉伊语族，通常归入跨新几内亚语系。在新几内亚西部的邦贝拉伊半岛上，它包括巴哈姆语及其近亲伊哈语，还有关系较远的卡拉芒语；第三个分支是帝汶—阿洛—潘塔尔语支，涵盖阿洛、潘塔尔群岛的众多语言，帝汶岛中部山区的布纳克语，以及东帝汶的马克萨伊语和法塔卢库语——后者与基萨尔岛的奥伊拉塔语关系最近。这些是现存最靠西的巴布亚语言，很可能是南岛语人群到来前不久从新几内亚迁徙而来，因而都带有深厚的南岛语借词层；法塔卢库语还经马来语吸收了梵语、阿拉伯语词汇，后来又借入葡萄牙语词。极乐鸟羽毛贸易在7世纪已把半岛与室利佛逝联系起来；14世纪爪哇的《爪哇史颂》提到“瓦南宁”和“斯兰”，通常比定为奥宁和科维艾地区，是满者伯夷的朝贡地，也是巴布亚地区本土名称最早的记录。1606年，路易斯·巴埃斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙远征队让欧洲人第一次望见这片海岸；此后蒂多雷在首领古拉贝西率领下扩张，把半岛纳入朝贡圈，而阿洛和索洛则向比马苏丹国纳贡。1828年，荷兰人在特里顿湾修建杜比斯堡以维系蒂多雷保护地，却在1835年将其放弃。

en: Bora-Huitoto is the name given to the proposed grouping of two closely situated language families of the western Amazon rainforest, Boran and Witotoan, spoken in the jungle lowlands between the Napo, Putumayo and Caquetá rivers, chiefly in the Colombian Amazonas department and across the border in Peru and Brazil. The Bora, whose Miraña kin form a closely related people of the same family, lived by slash-and-burn farming, hunting and river fishing, while the Witoto or Huitoto were once a loose nation of many villages grouped into the Murui, Muinane and Meneca peoples, sharing long communal maloca houses and summoning one another across the forest with great maguare drums during coca rituals. Whether the two families truly share a common ancestor remains debated among linguists, some also adding the Andoque language to the proposal. Shielded by forest and swamp from the Andean empires, these peoples had no recorded contact with Europeans until the early 1600s, and even then outsiders rarely penetrated their territory, so the languages passed through the following centuries largely untouched by Spanish.
zh: 博拉‑维托托语是对亚马孙雨林西部两个地理位置相近的语族——博拉语族与维托托语族——的合称，通行于纳波河、普图马约河与卡克塔河之间的丛林低地，主要在今哥伦比亚亚马孙省以及秘鲁、巴西一侧的边境地区。博拉人（其亲族米拉尼亚人是同一语族中关系密切的族群）以刀耕火种、狩猎和河渔为生；维托托人曾是由众多村落组成的松散族群，分为穆鲁伊、穆伊纳内和梅内卡等支系，共居在名为“马洛卡”的长屋中，并在嚼古柯的仪式上以巨大的“马瓜雷”鼓穿越丛林互相传讯。这两个语族是否真有共同祖先，语言学家仍有争论，还有人把安多克语也归入这一划分。由于有森林和沼泽作为屏障、远离安第斯诸帝国，这些族群直到17世纪初才有与欧洲人接触的记录，而且外来者此后也很少深入其领地，因此在此后数百年间，这些语言基本没有受到西班牙语的触动。

en: Bornean gathers the indigenous Malayo-Polynesian languages of Borneo that linguists place within the Greater North Borneo group: the Dusunic and Murutic languages of Sabah, among them Dusun, Murut and Tidung, the Kenyah languages of the interior highlands, the Punan languages, and Melanau and the related Kajang tongues of the central Sarawak rivers. They descend from Austronesian settlers who entered Borneo from the Philippines and split into communities along the north-western and eastern coasts. Most of these societies were oral ones, for written records were not a native tradition, and their languages long absorbed loanwords from Malay, the trade lingua franca of the coasts. The Melanau, among the earliest settlers of Sarawak and self-styled river people, appear as Malano in Chinese, Javanese and Western maps, and came under strong Bruneian Malay influence from the thirteenth century. Brunei also ruled and taxed the Dusun farmers of the Sabah interior, whose name means people of the orchards, and a British survey of 1774 already described them as mountain agriculturalists with a dialect of their own, while the Kenyah and Punan kept to longhouse swidden life in the Apo Kayan highlands and the upper Rejang forests.
zh: 文莱语汇集了婆罗洲本土的马来—波利尼西亚语言，语言学家将它们归入大北婆罗洲语群：沙巴的杜顺语支和穆鲁特语支，包括杜顺语、穆鲁特语和蒂东语；内陆高地的肯雅语；普南语；以及沙捞越中部河流地带的梅拉瑙语和相关的卡壤语。它们来自经菲律宾进入婆罗洲的南岛移民，这些移民沿西北海岸和东海岸分流而居。这些社会大多没有本土书写传统，其语言长期吸收马来语借词，而马来语是沿海贸易的通用语。梅拉瑙人是沙捞越最早的定居者之一，自称河上人，在中国、爪哇和西方的地图上以马拉诺之名出现，13世纪起深受文莱马来人影响。文莱还统治沙巴内陆的杜顺农民并向其征税，杜顺一名意为果园之人，1774年的英国考察已记载他们是有自己方言的山区农人；肯雅人和普南人则在阿波卡扬高地与拉让河上游森林里过着长屋游耕生活。

en: Bosavi, also called the Papuan Plateau languages, is a family of closely related Trans–New Guinea languages named after Mount Bosavi, the forested mountain rising from the rainforest plateau east of the Strickland River and southwest of the central highlands of Papua New Guinea. Its members spread across the plateau and the flanks of Mount Sisa, and include Kaluli and Sonia, Aimele, Kasua and Onobasulu, together with Edolo–Beami, the language of the Beami people, while Dibiyaso, once listed with them, is often treated as an isolate. The peoples of the plateau live in small longhouse communities in dense rainforest, drawing their living from sago, garden crops and forest game. When Yñigo Ortiz de Retez gave New Guinea its name in 1545, this inland plateau lay far beyond any European route, and its languages continued to develop untouched by the outside world until the colonial era.
zh: 博萨维语又称巴布亚高原语，是一组亲缘密切的跨新几内亚语系语言，得名于博萨维山；这座林木覆盖的山矗立在斯特里克兰河以东、巴布亚新几内亚中央高地西南边缘的雨林高原上。其成员遍布高原和锡萨山山坡，包括卡卢利语与索尼亚语、艾梅莱语、卡苏阿语、奥诺巴苏鲁语，以及比阿米人使用的埃多洛-比阿米语；曾与它们并列的迪比亚索语则常被视为孤立语。高原上的民族在茂密雨林中组成小型长屋社群，以西谷米、园圃作物和林间猎物为生。1545年伊尼戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·雷特斯为新几内亚命名时，这座内陆高原远在任何欧洲航线之外，其语言在殖民时代之前始终不受外部世界干扰地自行演变。

en: The Sal languages, also called Brahmaputran after the Brahmaputra Valley, are a Sino-Tibetan branch identified by the linguist Robbins Burling and named for the shared root sal meaning sun. They fall into three groups, Bodo–Garo, Konyak and Jingpho–Luish, and are spoken across north-eastern India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and southern China. The Bodo–Garo group alone includes Bodo, Garo, Koch, Rabha, Deori, Dimasa, Tiwa and the Tripuri speech Kokborok. Bodo–Garo speakers settled the Assam lowlands in remote prehistory, perhaps three thousand years ago, and their ancestral tongue is thought to have served as the valley's lingua franca before Assamese spread, leaving a large lexical legacy. The languages are verb-final, prefix classifiers to numerals and have a markedly simplified morphology. By the thirteenth century Bodo–Garo peoples had formed valley polities such as Chutia, Kachari and Tripura, before the Tai-Ahom kingdom began its advance in 1228.
zh: 萨尔语又称布拉马普特拉语，得名于布拉马普特拉河谷，是汉藏语系的一支，由语言学家罗宾斯·伯林划定，以诸语言共有的词根sal（意为太阳）命名。它下分博多—加罗、孔亚克、景颇—侬三个语支，通行于印度东北部、孟加拉国、缅甸和中国南方的交界地带。其中博多—加罗语支包括博多、加罗、科赫、拉巴、德奥里、迪马萨、蒂瓦，以及特里普里人的科克博罗克语。博多—加罗人的先民在上古时代便已定居阿萨姆低地，距今或达三千年；其祖语很可能曾是整个河谷的通用语，后来才让位于阿萨姆语，并为后者留下大量词汇。这些语言动词居句末、数词前加量词，形态明显简化。到13世纪，博多—加罗诸族已在河谷建立乔提耶、卡查尔、特里普拉等邦国，泰人阿洪姆王国则于1228年开始西进。

en: The Brythonic, or Brittonic, languages form the P-Celtic branch of the Insular Celtic family, alongside the Goidelic tongues of Ireland and Scotland. They descend from Common Brittonic, spoken across most of Roman Britain; after the Roman withdrawal the Anglo-Saxon advance drove the Britons westward and northward, and the Battle of Dyrham in 577 cut the south-western Britons off from the Welsh. From the fifth and sixth centuries refugees also carried the language across the Channel to Brittany, where it became Breton. The old common language then split into Welsh, Cornish and Breton, together with the now extinct Cumbric of the Old North and perhaps Pictish. In the later Middle Ages English pressed steadily west: Cumbric had disappeared by the twelfth century, and Cornish was confined to the far west of Cornwall, where it ceased to be a living community language by the late eighteenth century. Welsh held its ground in Wales, though the Laws in Wales Acts of 1536 and 1542 made English the language of law and administration; William Morgan's Welsh Bible of 1588, followed by Welsh-Latin and Welsh-English dictionaries in 1632 and from 1770 to 1794, fixed a literary standard that carried the language through the eighteenth century.
zh: 布立吞语（又称布里索尼语）是海岛凯尔特语族中的 P 凯尔特分支，与爱尔兰和苏格兰的戈伊德尔语并列。它们源自通行于罗马不列颠大部地区的共同布立吞语；罗马撤离后，盎格鲁—撒克逊人的进逼把不列颠人赶往西部和北部，577年的迪勒姆战役又使西南的不列颠人与威尔士人失去陆路联系。从5世纪到6世纪，难民还把这种语言带过海峡传到布列塔尼，在那里演变为布列塔尼语。古老的共同语随后分化为威尔士语、康沃尔语和布列塔尼语，此外还有早已消亡的古北坎布里克语，皮克特语或许也属此类。中世纪后期英语不断西扩：坎布里克语在12世纪前消失，康沃尔语被压缩到康沃尔半岛最西端，到18世纪后期已不再是活的社区语言。威尔士语则在威尔士站稳脚跟，尽管1536年和1542年的《威尔士联合法令》规定英语为法律和行政语言；1588年威廉·摩根的威尔士语圣经，以及1632年和1770—1794年间问世的词典，确立了书面标准，支撑这种语言走过18世纪。

en: Bua is a small group of Niger–Congo languages of southern Chad, spoken between the Chari River and the Guéra Massif. It includes Bua itself, Niellim, Tunia and the Gula languages, among them Gula Iro spoken around Lake Iro, and its tongues have been heavily shaped by contact with neighbouring Chadic languages.
zh: 布阿语是乍得南部的一组尼日尔—刚果语系小语言，通行于沙里河与盖拉山地之间，包括布阿语本支、涅利姆语、图尼亚语和古拉诸语，其中就有伊罗湖一带使用的古拉伊罗语；这些语言深受邻近乍得语族语言接触的影响。

en: Buginese, called Basa Ugi by its speakers, is the language of the Bugis people of the river and lake lowlands of south-western Sulawesi. It belongs to the South Sulawesi subgroup of Malayo-Polynesian, alongside Makassarese, Mandarese and the Toraja languages, all of which were traditionally written in the Lontara script, a Brahmic system derived from the old Kawi script and incised on palm-leaf manuscripts. Austronesian farmers had reached the region by about 2500 BC, and iron smelted in the Bugis-led trading polity of Luwu, already listed among the three powers of the peninsula in the Javanese epic Desawarnana of about 1365, fed an agricultural transformation after 1200. The creation epic La Galigo preserves the oldest layer of the language, while rival kingdoms arose at Bone, Wajo and Soppeng; Bone first appears in the fifteenth century and in 1582 joined its neighbours in the alliance of the Three Summits against the Makassarese sultanate of Gowa. The Bugis accepted Islam in 1605, and Bone was brought to the faith when Gowa conquered it in 1611. In the Makassar War of 1666 to 1669 the Bone prince Arung Palakka allied with the Dutch East India Company to overthrow Gowa, and the Treaty of Bungaya left Bone the leading power of South Sulawesi. The long wars then scattered Bugis traders and settlers across the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Borneo, and Bone itself fought Dutch expeditions in 1824; the dialects of Buginese still follow the boundaries of the old pre-colonial states.
zh: 布吉语自称巴萨乌吉，是布吉人的语言，通行于苏拉威西岛西南部的河湖低地。它属马来—波利尼西亚语系的南苏拉威西语支，与望加锡语、曼达尔语和托拉查诸语同支，传统上都用源出古老卡威文的婆罗米系隆塔拉文写在棕榈叶上。南岛农民约在公元前2500年抵达此地；1200年以后，以布吉人为首的贸易政权鲁乌出产的铁器推动了农业变革，约1365年的爪哇史诗《爪哇史颂》已把鲁乌列为该半岛三大势力之一。创世史诗《拉加利戈》保存了布吉语最古老的层面，波尼、瓦乔和索彭等王国随后兴起：波尼最早见于15世纪，1582年与邻国结成三峰同盟，对抗望加锡人的戈瓦苏丹国。布吉人于1605年皈依伊斯兰教，波尼则在1611年被戈瓦征服后改宗。1666至1669年的望加锡战争中，波尼王子阿隆·帕拉卡联合荷兰东印度公司推翻戈瓦，《邦加亚条约》使波尼成为南苏拉威西的霸主。长期战乱又促使布吉商人和移民扩散到马来半岛、苏门答腊和婆罗洲，波尼本土还在1824年与荷兰远征军交战；布吉语的各方言大致沿着旧日诸邦的边界划分。

en: Bukawa is an Oceanic language of the Austronesian family, spoken in a chain of coastal villages along the Huon Gulf in north-eastern Papua New Guinea, from Cape Arkona to the outskirts of Lae, with the large village of Busama among its southern settlements. It belongs to the North Huon Gulf group together with Yabem and Kela; like Yabem it has developed phonemic tone, as old inherited words were worn down to short roots whose meaning rests on pitch as well as sound. Its name is not native but comes from Yabem, drawn from the village of Bugawac on Cape Arkona, and the language itself splits into four regional dialects. Traditional Bukawa counting runs over the fingers of both hands and then the feet, so that twenty is expressed as one person, and families use a fixed set of birth-order names in which the seventh son is simply called No Name. The gulf these villages face was unknown to Europeans until the 1790s, when the French expedition of d'Entrecasteaux, searching for the lost explorer Lapérouse, charted these coasts and named the gulf after its officer Huon de Kermadec.
zh: 布卡瓦语是南岛语系的一种泛太平洋语言，通行于巴布亚新几内亚东北部休恩湾沿岸的一连串村落，北起阿尔科纳角，南至莱城近郊，南岸的布萨马是其较大的聚落之一。它与亚本语、凯拉语同属北休恩湾语组；和亚本语一样，布卡瓦语发展出了音位声调——古老的传承词逐渐磨损成短词根，词义要靠音高和发音共同区别。它的名称并非本族语词，而是借自亚本语，源于阿尔科纳角的布加瓦克村；语言本身分为四个地域方言。布卡瓦人传统上依双手十指再数双脚脚趾计数，因此二十被称作一个人；家庭还沿用一套固定的排行名，第七个儿子干脆被叫作无名。这些村落面对的海湾在1790年代以前不为欧洲人所知，当特尔卡斯托率领的法国探险队为寻找失踪探险家拉彼鲁兹而测绘这一带海岸，并以随队军官于翁·德·凯尔马代克之名将海湾命名为休恩湾。

en: Bulgarian is an Eastern South Slavic language of the eastern Balkans, descended from Slavs who settled there in the sixth century. It was the first Slavic language committed to writing: in the 860s Saints Cyril and Methodius translated Greek liturgy into the Slavic tongue of the region, and in 886 the Bulgarian Empire adopted their Glagolitic alphabet, which the Preslav Literary School soon replaced with Cyrillic. This literary norm, called Old Church Slavonic or Old Bulgarian, gave way between the twelfth and fifteenth centuries to Middle Bulgarian, the administrative language of the Second Bulgarian Empire and later of Walachia and Moldavia; in this period Bulgarian shed its noun cases and developed a suffixed definite article, setting it apart from the other Slavic languages. Under Ottoman rule it took in many Turkish words, while the vernacular damaskin texts bridged the gap to modern Bulgarian. During the nineteenth-century national revival, scholars such as Neofit Rilski and Ivan Bogorov drafted competing grammars and orthographies, and from 1835 proposals for a standard language multiplied.
zh: 保加利亚语是东巴尔干的东部南斯拉夫语言，源自6世纪迁居当地的斯拉夫人的口语。它是第一种见诸文字的斯拉夫语言：9世纪60年代，圣西里尔和美多德把希腊语礼拜典籍译成当地斯拉夫语，886年保加利亚帝国采用了他们创制的格拉哥里字母，普雷斯拉夫文学学派很快又改用西里尔字母。这一书面规范被称为古教会斯拉夫语或古保加利亚语，12至15世纪让位于中古保加利亚语——它是第二保加利亚帝国以及后来瓦拉几亚、摩尔达维亚的行政语言；这一时期保加利亚语失去了名词变格，发展出后缀式定冠词，与其他斯拉夫语言分道扬镳。奥斯曼统治时期它吸收了大量土耳其语借词，口语化的“达马斯金”文本则承上启下，通向近代保加利亚语。19世纪民族复兴期间，内奥菲特·里尔斯基、伊万·博戈罗夫等学者竞相编写语法和正字法，从1835年起，规范标准语的方案层出不穷。

en: Burmese is a Tibeto-Burman language of the Sino-Tibetan family, the native speech of the Bamar people of the upper Irrawaddy valley and the lingua franca of the Burmese kingdoms; its dialects, including Rakhine and Danu, are also carried by neighbouring peoples. It is a tonal, pitch-register language with subject–object–verb order and a heavy load of Pali vocabulary, much of it borrowed through the earlier Pyu speech of the Pagan kingdom. The Burmese alphabet, a Brahmic abugida ultimately of Kadamba or Pallava origin and adapted from the Mon script, first appears in eleventh-century Pagan inscriptions, the oldest evidence dating to 1035. Old Burmese gave way to Middle Burmese in the sixteenth century amid sound mergers and rising lay literacy, when square letterforms became the rounded circular script of palm-leaf manuscripts. Modern Burmese emerged in the mid-eighteenth century, spread through the villages by Buddhist monastery schools, and the Konbaung conquest of the Mon kingdom of Pegu in 1757 carried it into the Irrawaddy delta, which by 1830 had largely shifted from Mon to Burmese.
zh: 缅甸语是汉藏语系藏缅语族的语言，是伊洛瓦底江上游缅人的母语，也是缅甸诸王国的通用语；若开语、达努语等方言也由邻近民族使用。它是带声调的音区语言，语序为主宾动，并含有大量巴利语词汇，其中不少是经蒲甘王国时代更早的骠语借入。缅文字母是源出卡丹巴或帕拉瓦、并由孟文改造而来的婆罗米系元音附标文字，最早见于11世纪的蒲甘碑铭，现存最早证据可追溯到1035年。16世纪古缅甸语过渡为中古缅甸语，语音发生合并，俗人文书识字率上升，方块字形也变成贝叶经上圆润的圆形字体。近代缅甸语在18世纪中叶形成，靠村落里的佛教寺院学校传播；1757年贡榜王朝征服勃固的孟人王国，把缅甸语带入伊洛瓦底江三角洲，到1830年，该地区已大体从孟语改用缅甸语。

en: Bwaidoga, recorded in some sources as Bwaidoka, is an Oceanic language of the Papuan Tip cluster, spoken on Goodenough Island, also called Nidula, the westernmost of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands off the eastern tip of New Guinea. It heads a small linkage of closely related speech forms on the island, among them Diodio, Iduna and Iamalele, and serves as a local lingua franca beyond its home villages. The island's people, related to the Papuans of the mainland, have inhabited its steep volcanic slopes for several thousand years, farming the narrow coastal plains while the mountainous interior remained almost untouched. Europeans first sighted the archipelago in 1792, when the French navigator Bruni d'Entrecasteaux sailed through the Solomon Sea in search of the lost expedition of La Perouse.
zh: 布瓦多加语在部分资料中记作布瓦多卡语，是泛太平洋语系巴布亚尖端语群的一支大洋语，通行于新几内亚东端外海当特尔卡斯托群岛最西端的古迪纳夫岛，该岛土名尼杜拉。它统领着岛上一组关系密切的方言，包括迪奥迪奥语、伊杜纳语和亚马莱莱语等，并在母语村落之外充当地区通用语。岛上居民与新几内亚大陆的巴布亚人有亲缘关系，数千年来在陡峭的火山坡上生息，耕种狭窄的沿海平原，而多山的内陆几乎无人涉足。欧洲人最早在1792年望见这组群岛，当时法国航海家布吕尼·当特尔卡斯托为寻找失踪的拉佩鲁兹探险队，乘船穿过了所罗门海。

en: Cacán, also recorded as Kakán, Calchaquí or Diaguita, was the language of the Diaguita peoples of the Argentine northwest, from Catamarca and La Rioja into Salta, San Juan, Tucumán and Santiago del Estero, with some authors placing it also in the Atacama and Coquimbo districts of northern Chile. Its speakers were split into many subtribes, among them the Calchaquí, Pazioca, Capayán, Hualfín, Pular and Quilmes, and their dialects diverged enough that Capayana needed interpreters for the Spaniards; even the name Diaguita comes from a Cacán word meaning village inhabitant. The language has no proven relatives, although links with Kunza and the little-known Humahuaca tongue have been proposed. The Jesuit Alonso de Bárcena compiled a grammar of Cacán, but the manuscript is lost, leaving only short glosses and place names. In the Calchaquí Wars of 1560 to 1667 the Diaguita confederation fought the Spanish Empire; defeat brought mass deportations and the depopulation of the Calchaquí valley, and the Quilmes were resettled near Buenos Aires. Cacán ceased to be spoken around the middle of the eighteenth century, living on chiefly in toponyms such as Animaná, which means sky place.
zh: 卡坎语又称卡坎、卡尔查基语或迪亚吉塔语，是阿根廷西北部迪亚吉塔诸族的语言，分布在卡塔马卡、拉里奥哈，并延伸到萨尔塔、圣胡安、图库曼和圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗诸省，也有学者认为它还通行于智利北部的阿塔卡马和科金博地区。使用者分成许多支系，包括卡尔查基、帕西奥卡、卡帕扬、瓦尔芬、普拉尔和基尔梅斯等，各方言差异很大，西班牙人听卡帕亚纳方言甚至需要译员；就连“迪亚吉塔”这个名字也来自卡坎语，意为“村落居民”。这种语言没有已证实的亲属语言，只有学者推测它与昆萨语及记录极少的乌马瓦卡语有关。耶稣会士巴尔塞纳曾编写一部卡坎语语法，但手稿已经失传，存世的只有简短词汇和地名。1560年至1667年的卡尔查基战争中，迪亚吉塔联盟与西班牙帝国交战，战败后各部族遭到流放，卡尔查基河谷人口一空，例如基尔梅斯人就被迁到布宜诺斯艾利斯附近。卡坎语约在18世纪中叶不再使用，主要借意为“天空之地”的阿尼马纳等地名留存下来。

en: The Caddo languages form a small family of the North American Great Plains, stretching from present-day North Dakota south to Oklahoma and Texas. Its five members fall into a southern branch, Caddo proper, spoken across northeastern Texas and the adjoining parts of Oklahoma, Arkansas and Louisiana, and a northern branch of Wichita, Kitsai, Pawnee and Arikara; the Pawnee lived along the Platte River in Nebraska and the Arikara on the upper Missouri. Linguistic comparison suggests Proto-Caddoan split into these two branches more than three thousand years ago. The Caddo-speaking peoples were maize farmers and temple mound builders of the Caddoan Mississippian culture, which flourished from about 800 and raised great earthworks such as the Spiro Mounds, until a long drought between 1276 and 1299 disrupted many of their villages. All five languages were unwritten and sustained by oral tradition.
zh: 卡多诸语言是北美大平原上的一个小语系，分布范围从今天的北达科他向南延伸到俄克拉荷马与得克萨斯。它的五种语言分为两支：南支即卡多语本支，通行于得克萨斯东北部及俄克拉荷马、阿肯色、路易斯安那三州毗邻地带；北支包括威奇托语、基蔡语、波尼语和阿里卡拉语，其中波尼人生活在内布拉斯加的普拉特河畔，阿里卡拉人活动于密苏里河上游。语言比较显示，原始卡多语早在三千多年前就已分成这两支。说卡多语的各族是种植玉米的农人，也是卡多安密西西比文化的神庙土丘建造者；该文化约自800年起兴盛，修筑了斯皮罗土丘等大型土工建筑，1276—1299年的长期大旱又使许多村落衰落解体。这五种语言都没有本族文字，全靠口耳相传。

en: Cahita is a branch of the Uto-Aztecan family of the Gulf of California coast, whose surviving members are Yaqui, or Yoem Noki, of the Rio Yaqui valley in Sonora, and the closely related Mayo language of the Mayo river country; the early Jesuits recorded the name Cahita for the Hiaki, Mayo and Tehueco together, and perhaps ten mutually intelligible varieties once covered much of Sonora and Sinaloa, among them the poorly attested Acaxee, Tahue and Mocorito. The Yaqui first met Spaniards in 1533, when Diego de Guzman's expedition was fought to a standstill, and Francisco de Ibarra failed to found a settlement in 1565. In 1608 the Yaqui and their Mayo allies defeated Spanish forces in two battles, and after the peace of 1610 they themselves invited the Jesuits in 1617. For roughly 120 years the mission relationship let the Yaqui keep their lands and settle into eight towns while taking wheat, cattle and horses into their economy. Silver finds in the Rio Yaqui valley from 1684 drew settlers, and in 1740 the Yaqui, Mayo, Opata and Pima rose together and cleared the colonists out by 1742; the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 then ended the mission order. After independence a new tax law of 1825 provoked the rising of Juan Banderas, who united Yaqui, Mayo and Opata fighters until his capture at Soyopa and execution in 1833.
zh: 卡希塔语是加利福尼亚湾沿岸犹他-阿兹特克语系的一个语支，现存两支：索诺拉亚基河谷的雅基语（自称约姆诺基），以及马约河流域与它极为接近的马约语。早期耶稣会士把希亚基、马约和特韦科统称为卡希塔；历史上约有十种互通的变体遍布索诺拉和锡那罗亚大部，其中包括记载贫乏的阿卡谢、塔韦和莫科里托。1533年雅基人首次遭遇西班牙人，迭戈·德·古斯曼的远征被打得停滞不前，1565年弗朗西斯科·德·伊瓦拉也未能建立定居点。1608年，雅基人联合马约人在两场战斗中击败西班牙军队，1610年议和后，他们于1617年主动邀请耶稣会士入境。在此后约120年的传教关系中，雅基人保住了土地，被组织进八个城镇，并把小麦、牛和马纳入自己的经济。1684年起亚基河谷发现银矿，定居者涌入，1740年雅基、马约、奥帕塔和皮马人联合起义，到1742年把殖民者驱逐出去；1767年耶稣会被驱逐，传教秩序告终。独立后，1825年的新税法激起胡安·班德拉斯起义，他联合雅基、马约和奥帕塔战士作战，直至1833年在索约帕战败被俘并处决。

en: Calima is the name scholars give to the unattested speech of the pre-Columbian societies of the Calima River valley, in the Western Cordillera of what is now the Colombian department of Valle del Cauca. A long archaeological sequence unfolded there: the farming Ilama chiefdoms arose around 1500 BCE, the expansionist Yotoco culture flourished from the first century CE and gave way after the sixth century to the more centralized Sonso chiefdoms, which still occupied the valley in 1337 and lasted into the 1500s, while the related Malagana tradition produced fine burnished ceramics and goldwork on the floodplains. No word of the valley's languages was ever written down, so their classification is unknown; colonial-era accounts, followed by some Spanish-language sources, link the region's peoples to the Cariban-speaking Panche of the Magdalena slope, but this rests on chronicler report rather than linguistic evidence. Spanish conquest of the Cauca valley in the sixteenth century dissolved the Sonso chiefdoms, and the old tongues disappeared under the spread of Spanish.
zh: 卡利马语是学者对今哥伦比亚考卡山谷省西部山脉卡利马河流域诸史前社会语言的统称，这些语言没有留下任何文字记录。当地考古序列漫长：务农的伊拉马酋邦约兴起于公元前1500年，扩张性的约托科文化从1世纪起繁荣，6世纪后让位于权力更集中的松索酋邦——1337年时占据谷地的正是松索人，其社会一直延续到16世纪；相关的马拉加纳传统则在河漫滩上留下了精美的磨光陶器和金器。由于没有记下任何词汇，这些语言的归属已无从考证；殖民时期的记述以及后世一些西语文献把当地人与马格达莱纳坡地、使用加勒比语的潘切人联系起来，但这只是编年史家的说法，并无语言学证据。16世纪西班牙人征服考卡河谷，松索酋邦瓦解，当地的古老语言也随西班牙语的扩散而消失。

en: The Cariban languages form a family of about three dozen closely related tongues Indigenous to north-eastern South America, spoken from the mouth of the Amazon across the Guiana Highlands to the Colombian Andes, with smaller groups in central Brazil. They descend from a reconstructed Proto-Cariban, whose homeland probably lay in the lower Amazon basin; from there Cariban-speaking peoples spread into the Guianas, while some branches moved south into the upper Xingu. When Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492, the Kalina, or Caribs, of the Guiana coast gave the region its name, the Spanish calling them Caribes. The Island Caribs of the Lesser Antilles, although they mainly spoke an Arawakan tongue, used a Cariban pidgin kept alive above all by men. In the following centuries missionaries learned Cariban languages for their missions, where a Carib-based lengua general served as a common tongue.
zh: 加勒比语族是南美洲东北部原住民的一组语言，约有三十余种，彼此亲缘较近；通行范围从亚马孙河口经圭亚那高原直到哥伦比亚的安第斯山区，在巴西中部也有小块分布。它们由学者构拟的原始加勒比语演化而来，其故地可能在亚马孙河下游；加勒比语民族由此扩散到圭亚那地区，也有支系南迁至上欣古河流域。1492年哥伦布抵达加勒比海时，圭亚那沿海的加勒比人（自称卡里纳人）使这一地区得名，西班牙人称他们为卡利贝人。小安的列斯群岛的岛民加勒比人虽主要使用一种阿拉瓦克语，却同时通行一种以加勒比语为基础的混合语，且主要由男性传承。此后几个世纪里，传教士为传教活动学习加勒比诸语，各传教区还以一种加勒比语通用语作为共同语言。

en: Cayubaba is the language of the Cayubaba people of the Bolivian Amazon, who live west of the Mamoré River in the Beni lowlands, within the floodplain country historically known as Moxos. No genetic relationship to any other language has been established, so it is classed as an isolate. The first European to reach them was the Jesuit Agustín Zapata in 1693, who found seven large villages in their territory; early in the eighteenth century another Jesuit, Antonio Garriga, founded the Exaltación mission among them, followed by the missions of San Carlos, Concepción and Peñas.
zh: 卡尤巴巴语是玻利维亚亚马逊地区卡尤巴巴人的语言，他们住在贝尼低地马莫雷河以西，即历史上称作莫霍斯的泛滥平原地带。该语言与其他语言尚无确立的亲缘关系，被归为孤立语言。1693年，耶稣会士阿古斯丁·萨帕塔最先来到他们中间，在其地界上见到七座大村庄；18世纪初，另一位耶稣会士安东尼奥·加里加在他们当中建立了埃克萨尔塔西翁传教站，其后又建起圣卡洛斯、康塞普西翁和佩尼亚斯等传教站。

en: The Celebic languages form a primary branch of the Malayo-Polynesian subgroup of Austronesian, spread across the island of Sulawesi, formerly called Celebes. They account for almost every language of Central and Southeast Sulawesi, with a few outliers such as Wotu and Bonerate in the south, and make up the island's largest language group by number of tongues. Their main divisions are the Kaili-Pamona and Tomini-Tolitoli groups of the center and Tomini Bay, and the Eastern Celebic cluster of Saluan-Banggai, Bungku-Tolaki and Muna-Buton, which carries the speech of the Kaili, Pamona, Tolaki, Muna and Buton peoples. The coastal sultanates drew these languages into the spice trade: the Sultanate of Buton, founded on the island off Sulawesi's southeast peninsula in the 1300s, became an Islamic tributary center within the sphere of the Sultanate of Ternate during the 1500s. Linguists trace the family to a reconstructed Proto-Celebic ancestor marked by regular sound changes from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian, among them the loss of *h and the merger of *d into *r.
zh: 西里伯斯语是南岛语系马来—波利尼西亚语族的一个主要分支，通行于旧称西里伯斯的苏拉威西岛，几乎涵盖中苏拉威西和东南苏拉威西的全部语言，南苏拉威西也有沃图、博内拉泰等少数分支；按语言数量计，它是苏拉威西岛上最大的语群。其主要分区包括中部及托米尼湾沿岸的凯里—帕莫纳语群和托米尼—托利托利语群，以及由萨卢安—邦盖、邦库—托拉基和穆纳—布顿组成的东西里伯斯语群，凯里人、帕莫纳人、托拉基人、穆纳人和布顿人的语言都在其中。沿海苏丹国把这些语言卷入香料贸易：14世纪兴起于苏拉威西东南半岛外海布顿岛的布顿苏丹国，在16世纪成为特尔纳特苏丹国势力范围内的伊斯兰朝贡贸易中心。学者构拟出共同的原始西里伯斯语，其标志性音变包括词首*h脱落、*d并入*r等。

en: Cèmuhî, also recorded as Camuki, Tyamuhi or the language of Wagap, is a Kanak language of the Northern New Caledonian group within Oceanic Austronesian, spoken on the northeast coast of Grande Terre around Poindimié, Touho and Koné, in the Paici-Camuki customary area of the North Province. Like other Kanak languages it goes back to the Proto-Oceanic speech of the Lapita settlers who reached New Caledonia around 1000 BCE. Cèmuhî is a tonal language, with three pitch registers distinguishing words, a rare trait in Melanesia. North of the Tiwaka valley the language was also known by the name tié.
zh: 塞穆希语又记作卡穆基语、蒂亚穆希语或瓦加普语，是大洋洲语族北新喀里多尼亚语群的卡纳克语言，通行于格朗德特尔岛东北沿海普安迪米耶、图奥和科内一带，属北部省派西-卡穆基传统区。与其他卡纳克语言一样，它源自约公元前1000年抵达新喀里多尼亚的拉皮塔定居者所说的原始大洋洲语。塞穆希语是声调语言，有三个音高寄存器来区别词义，这在美拉尼西亚并不多见。在蒂瓦卡河谷以北，它过去还被称为蒂埃语。

en: Cham is the chief language of the Chamic or Aceh-Chamic branch of the Malayo-Polynesian family, whose speakers settled the coast of central and southern Vietnam from the island world and carried the Sa Huynh culture; its closest kin are Acehnese of northern Sumatra, the highland Jarai and Rade tongues, and Tsat on Hainan. It is the oldest attested Austronesian language, for the Dong Yen Chau inscription of the late fourth century, carved in an Indic-derived script, records Old Cham centuries before the earliest surviving Malay and Khmer texts. Cham served the trading polities of Champa, whose sea routes ran from India to China, and absorbed a large Sanskrit religious vocabulary together with loans from the neighbouring Austroasiatic Bahnaric languages. From the tenth century many Chams turned to Islam, and after the ruling dynasty adopted the faith in the seventeenth century Western Cham came to be written in an Arabic Jawi script alongside the traditional Brahmic Cham letters. The Vietnamese capture of Vijaya in 1471 broke Champa's power and left only the principalities of Kauthara, annexed in 1653, and Panduranga, which Emperor Minh Mang absorbed in 1832. Refugees carried Western Cham into Cambodia, while Eastern Cham held on around Phan Rang, the two varieties growing steadily further apart.
zh: 占语是马来—波利尼西亚语族占语群（又称亚齐—占语群）的主要语言。其先民从海岛地区渡海而来，带着沙黄文化定居在今越南中南部沿海；与它亲缘最近的，是苏门答腊北部的亚齐语、高原上的嘉莱语和埃地语，以及海南岛的回辉话。占语是有文献可考的最古老南岛语：4世纪末的东晏洲碑铭用一种源出印度的文字刻写古占语，比现存最早的马来语和高棉语文献还早数百年。占语曾效力于占婆诸贸易政权，这里的海上商路西通印度、东达中国，语言中因此吸收了大量梵语宗教词汇，也从邻近南亚语系的巴拿语借入不少词语。从10世纪起占人陆续改宗伊斯兰教，17世纪统治家族全面皈依后，西部占语除了传统的婆罗米系占文字母，也开始用阿拉伯字母的爪夷文书写。1471年越南军队攻陷毗阇耶，占婆国势崩解，仅剩古笪罗和宾童龙两个小邦，前者于1653年被吞并，宾童龙也在1832年被明命帝纳入版图。难民把西部占语带到柬埔寨，东部占语则在潘郎一带存续，两种方言渐行渐远。

en: Chamorro is the Austronesian language of the Chamorro people, indigenous to the Mariana Islands, with distinct Guamanian and Rotanese dialects alongside that of the northern islands. Together with Palauan it stands outside the Oceanic group, probably forming its own branch of the Malayo-Polynesian family. The Chamorros are descended from migrants from the Philippines who reached the Marianas around 1500 to 1400 before Christ, the first human settlement in Remote Oceania, with later arrivals from the Caroline Islands and Island Southeast Asia. Their pre-contact society was ordered into matrilineal clans and four ranks, and built its houses on the megalithic latte pillars found nowhere else. Ferdinand Magellan sighted Guam in 1521 and Miguel Lopez de Legazpi claimed the islands for Spain in 1565, after which they served the Manila galleons until 1815. A Jesuit mission under Diego Luis de San Vitores arrived in 1668, bringing the Latin alphabet and the Catholic faith; the Spanish-Chamorro Wars that followed, and the smallpox epidemic of 1688, shattered the old society. From this long contact the language absorbed a vast Spanish vocabulary, turning the old paleo-Chamorro into the neo-Chamorro still used when whalers began calling at Guam in 1823.
zh: 查莫罗语是查莫罗人的南岛语，本土位于马里亚纳群岛，有关岛方言、罗塔方言和北部分言等差别明显的变体。它与帕劳语一样处在大洋洲语族之外，很可能自成马来—波利尼西亚语族下的一个独立分支。查莫罗人的先民是公元前1500年至前1400年前后从菲律宾抵达马里亚纳群岛的移民，这是人类在远大洋洲最早的定居点，此后又有来自加罗林群岛和东南亚岛屿的移民陆续到来。接触欧洲人之前，他们的社会按母系氏族和四个等级组织，房屋建在别处不见的巨石“拉提石”柱上。1521年费迪南德·麦哲伦望见关岛，1565年米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮代表西班牙宣布占有这些岛屿，此后到1815年为止，这里一直为马尼拉大帆船提供补给。1668年，迪亚哥·路易斯·德·圣维托雷斯率领的耶稣会传教团到来，带来了拉丁字母和天主教；随之爆发的西班牙—查莫罗战争以及1688年的天花疫情重创了旧有社会。在长期接触中，查莫罗语吸收了大量西班牙语词汇，古老的古查莫罗语由此演变为新查莫罗语；1823年捕鲸船开始停靠关岛时，人们使用的已经是这种新形式。

en: Charrua is the name given to a small family of poorly documented tongues of the Plata basin, once heard across Uruguay, the Argentine province of Entre Rios and perhaps parts of Paraguay. Its recorded members are Chana, whose speakers called it Lantek, Mbegua, Guenoa and Charrua itself, each carried by semi-nomadic hunter-gatherer peoples who moved with the seasons, fishing the shore in summer and hunting deer and rhea inland with bolas and bows. The Jesuit Pedro Lozano records that these peoples killed the explorer Juan Diaz de Solis during his voyage of 1515 up the Rio de la Plata, and the Charrua and Chana long resisted Spanish settlement. From the eighteenth century cattle ranching enclosed their hunting grounds and turned famine into a way of life, answered by mounted raids known as malones. The languages were never properly written down, and the independent life of their speakers ended in 1831 with the Massacre of Salsipuedes, when the Uruguayan army destroyed the Charrua camps and dispersed the survivors.
zh: 查鲁亚语是拉普拉塔河流域一个记录稀少的小语系的统称，曾通行于乌拉圭、阿根廷恩特雷里奥斯省以及巴拉圭部分地区。有记录的语言包括查纳语（使用者自称兰特克语）、姆贝瓜语、格诺阿语和查鲁亚语本支，使用者都是随季节迁徙的半游牧狩猎采集族群：夏天到岸边捕鱼采贝，冬天带着投石索和弓箭深入内陆猎鹿和美洲鸵。耶稣会士佩德罗·洛萨诺记载，1515年航海者胡安·迪亚斯·德·索利斯溯拉普拉塔河而上时正是死在这些族群手中，此后查鲁亚人和查纳人长期抵抗西班牙人的拓殖。18世纪起，牧牛业圈占了他们的猎场，饥荒成为常态，他们便以骑马突袭的“马龙”还击。这些语言始终没有被认真记录成文，而使用者的独立生活在1831年走到尽头：乌拉圭军队制造萨尔西普埃德斯大屠杀，摧毁查鲁亚人的营地并驱散幸存者，诸语言随之消亡。

en: Cheke Holo, also called Maringe, A'ara, Holo or Kubonitu, is an Oceanic language spoken on Santa Isabel Island in the Solomon Islands. It shares distinctive phonological traits with the other languages of Santa Isabel, including aspirated stops and voiceless sonorants, while its verbs carry no markers of tense or person.
zh: 切克霍洛语又称马林盖语、阿阿拉语、霍洛语或库博尼图语，是所罗门群岛圣伊莎贝尔岛上通行的一种泛太平洋语系语言。它与圣伊莎贝尔岛的其他语言共有送气塞音、清响音等独特语音特征，动词则没有时态和人称标记。

en: Cherokee, self-named Tsalagi, is the only surviving language of the Southern branch of the Iroquoian family; its speakers' ancestors are thought to have moved from the Great Lakes into the southern Appalachians some three thousand years ago. At European contact it had three dialects, Lower, Middle or Kituwah, and Overhill or Otali. A polysynthetic tongue in which a single verb, built from a pronominal prefix, a root and aspect and modal suffixes, can carry a whole sentence, Cherokee remained purely oral until around 1809, when Sequoyah, a Cherokee who knew no writing, began devising a script. After first trying word-pictures, he settled on a syllabary of eighty-six characters, each standing for one syllable, and the Cherokee Nation adopted it in 1825. Within a few years laws, hymns and parts of the Bible appeared in print, literacy among the Cherokees surpassed that of their white neighbours, and from 1828 the bilingual Cherokee Phoenix became the first newspaper published by Native Americans in their own language.
zh: 切罗基语自称察拉吉语，是易洛魁语系南支唯一仍在通行的语言；一般认为，说这种语言的先民约在三千年前从五大湖地区迁入阿巴拉契亚山脉南部。欧洲人到来时，它分为下、中（又称基图瓦）和上山（又称奥塔利）三种方言。切罗基语是多式综合语，一个动词由代词前缀、词根、体后缀和语气后缀构成，本身就能表达整句话的意思。在1809年前后以前它一直没有文字：那一年，不识任何文字的切罗基人塞阔雅开始创制书写系统，他先尝试图画表意，最终设计出一套86个字符的音节文字，每个符号代表一个音节，切罗基民族于1825年正式采用。几年之内，法律、圣诗和《圣经》的部分卷册相继印行，切罗基人的识字率甚至超过了邻近的白人；1828年起，切罗基语与英语双语的《切罗基凤凰报》出版，成为美洲原住民第一份用本族语言发行的报纸。

en: Chibchan is the language family of the Isthmo-Colombian world, reaching from Mosquitia in eastern Central America through Costa Rica and Panama into northern Colombia. Its many members include Guna, Ngabe, Naso, Pech, Rama and the Talamanca tongues, and the family takes its name from Chibcha, also called Muysccubun, the speech of the Muisca of the Colombian highlands. Reconstructed Proto-Chibchan words for manioc, maize, squash and tobacco show that its speakers were horticulturalists who spread across the isthmus in remote prehistory. After the Spanish conquest the Church made Chibcha a vehicle of evangelization: from 1580 schools were ordered to teach in native languages, in 1606 the clergy was instructed to give religious teaching in Chibcha, and friars such as Bernardo de Lugo compiled its grammars. The Muisca language declined during the eighteenth century, and in 1770 Charles III banned its use.
zh: 奇布查语系是地峡—哥伦比亚文化区的原住民语系，范围从中美洲东部的莫斯基蒂亚经哥斯达黎加、巴拿马延伸到哥伦比亚北部，成员众多，包括古纳语、恩加贝语、纳索语、佩奇语、拉马语和塔拉曼卡诸语；语系得名于奇布查语（又称穆伊斯卡语），即哥伦比亚高原穆伊斯卡人的语言。重构出的原始奇布查语词汇中有木薯、玉米、南瓜和烟草，说明其使用者是农人，在远古史前时代便已扩散到整个地峡。西班牙征服后，教会把奇布查语当作传教工具：1580年起下令兴办原住民语言学校，1606年又要求教士用奇布查语讲授教义，贝尔纳多·德·卢戈等修士还编写了语法书。穆伊斯卡语在18世纪走向衰落，1770年卡洛斯三世下令禁止使用该语。

en: Chicham, natively called aent and better known as Jivaroan, is the language of the peoples living along the headwaters of the Marañón River and its tributaries, in northern Peru and the Ecuadorian Oriente. It forms a small family of its own, comprising Shuar, Achuar-Shiwiar, Awajun and Huambisa, while the extinct language of the Palta may also have belonged to it. The name Jivaro probably derives from xivar, the Shuar word for people. In 1527 the Shuar defeated an Inca army sent by Huayna Capac, and in 1599 they drove the Spanish settlers out of their territory, which kept the language alive in the forest through the colonial era; its speakers combined slash-and-burn gardening with hunting by blowgun and curare-tipped darts.
zh: 奇查姆语母语者自称“阿恩特”，更常见的名称是希瓦罗语，通行于秘鲁北部和厄瓜多尔东方地区马拉尼翁河上游及其支流一带。它本身构成一个小语系，包括舒阿尔语、阿丘阿尔-希维阿尔语、阿瓦洪语和万比萨语，已消亡的帕尔塔语可能也属于这一语系。“希瓦罗”一名大概来自舒阿尔语中意为“人”的词“希瓦尔”。1527年，舒阿尔人击败了瓦伊纳·卡帕克派出的印加军队，1599年又把西班牙定居者逐出自己的土地，使这门语言在整个殖民时代得以在丛林中延续；其使用者从事刀耕火种的园圃农业，并用吹箭筒和涂有箭毒的飞镖狩猎。

en: Chickasaw-Choctaw denotes the Western branch of the Muskogean family, whose two chief languages, Choctaw and Chickasaw, are so close that some linguists treat them as dialects of one tongue; the poorly recorded Houma language belongs to the same branch. Both peoples recall descending from a single ancestral group, and before European contact the Chickasaw had moved east of the Mississippi into what is now northeastern Mississippi, while the Choctaw settled across Mississippi, Alabama and Louisiana. These are highly synthetic, agglutinative languages with subject-object-verb order. Around 1700 a simplified pidgin drawn mainly from Choctaw and Chickasaw, Mobilian Jargon, became the lingua franca of the Gulf coast and lower Mississippi, used by the Natchez, Tunica, Caddo, Chitimacha and many other peoples and absorbing words from French, Spanish and English as well. A Roman-based Choctaw orthography was devised under the United States civilization program early in the nineteenth century, and in the 1830s both nations were forced west to Indian Territory, carrying the languages into what is now Oklahoma.
zh: 奇克索—乔克托语指马斯科吉语族的西支，两大语言乔克托语和奇克索语关系极近，部分语言学家把它们视为同一语言的两种方言；记录稀少的霍马语也属于这一支。两个民族都传说是同一祖先群体的后裔：欧洲人到来之前，奇克索人已东渡密西西比河，定居于今密西西比东北部，乔克托人则分布在密西西比、亚拉巴马和路易斯安那一带。这些语言高度综合、以黏构词，语序为主宾动。约1700年前后，一种主要简化自乔克托语和奇克索语的混合语——莫比尔混合语——成为墨西哥湾沿岸和密西西比河下游的通用语，纳奇兹人、图尼卡人、卡多人、奇蒂马查人等许多民族都使用它，其中还吸收了法语、西班牙语和英语词汇。19世纪初，美国的“文明计划”为乔克托语制定了拉丁字母拼写法；19世纪30年代，两个民族都被强制西迁印第安领地，这两种语言也随之进入今俄克拉荷马一带。

en: Chimbu denotes the Chimbu–Wahgi family of the New Guinea highlands, spoken across the fertile Wahgi Valley and the surrounding mountains of what are now Chimbu and Western Highlands provinces. Its best-known members are Kuman, the Chimbu language proper, Wahgi, Nii and Melpa, the tongue of the Kawelka and neighbouring tribes around Mount Hagen. Their placement within the Trans–New Guinea phylum is debated, though their pronouns keep the family's dual and plural endings, and all the languages use contrastive tone alongside rare lateral consonants, including the velar lateral of Melpa; Melpa speakers also count in a binary system and switch to a special pandanus language while gathering karuka nuts in the forests. The densely farmed valleys these languages occupy are among the few places where agriculture arose independently: at Kuk Swamp archaeologists have uncovered drainage ditches and taro plots going back to around 7000 BCE, with banana and sugar-cane cultivation established there by about 4500 BCE, sustaining the highland societies whose descendants still speak Chimbu–Wahgi tongues.
zh: 钦布语指新几内亚高地的钦布—瓦吉语族，通行于肥沃的瓦吉河谷及周边山地，即今天的钦布省和西高地省一带。最主要的成员包括钦布本地的库曼语，以及瓦吉语、尼伊语和梅尔帕语——梅尔帕语是哈根山一带卡维尔卡等部落的语言。它们是否属于跨新几内亚语系尚有争议，但其代词保留了该语系的双数和复数词尾；诸语言都用对立声调，还配有罕见的边音，如梅尔帕语的软腭边音。梅尔帕人采用二进制计数，在林中采集卡鲁卡坚果时还会改用一种专门的露兜树语。这些语言所在的河谷农垦密集，是世界上少数独立发展出农业的地方之一：考古学者在库克沼泽发现了可追溯至约公元前7000年的排水沟渠和芋头田，到约公元前4500年，当地已有香蕉和甘蔗种植，滋养着高地社会，其后裔仍使用钦布—瓦吉诸语。

en: Chitimacha, known to its speakers as Sitimaxa, is a language isolate of the Louisiana bayous, spoken by the Chitimacha people of the Atchafalaya Basin, a vast swampy estuary west of the lower Mississippi. The name Chitimacha is said to mean people of the Grand River. Its speakers were settled agriculturalists who grew corn, beans and squash in riverside villages, traveled in dugout cypress canoes and reckoned descent through the mother's line. They had lived on the Louisiana coast for some two and a half thousand years when French raiders entered their country in the late seventeenth century; the long war that followed ended with peace in 1718, by which time disease and fighting had sharply reduced their numbers. The language had no native script and was handed down orally.
zh: 奇蒂马查语在本族语中称西蒂马克萨，是路易斯安那河网地带的一门孤立语言，使用者是密西西比河下游以西阿查法拉亚盆地广阔沼泽河口区的奇蒂马查人。据说奇蒂马查一名意为大河之民。他们是定居的农耕者，在河畔村落种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，乘柏木挖凿的独木舟出行，按母系计算世系。法国劫掠者在17世纪末侵入他们的土地时，奇蒂马查人已在路易斯安那海岸生活了约两千五百年；随之而来的长期战争直到1718年才议和，此时疫病和征战已使他们的人口锐减。奇蒂马查语没有本族文字，依靠口耳相传。

en: Chiwere, also called Iowa-Otoe-Missouria, is a Siouan-Catawban language of the closely similar Iowa, Otoe and Missouria dialects; its nearest relative is Ho-Chunk, or Winnebago, and the four peoples were once one group in the western Great Lakes, linked to the Oneota culture. From the sixteenth century successive bands broke off and moved south and west, settling as farming and bison-hunting villagers along the Missouri and Platte rivers in earth lodges and tipis. The name Chiwere means to speak the home dialect. The French explorer Jacques Marquette met the Missouria on the Missouri in 1673, but an attack by the Sauk and Meskwaki in 1730 nearly destroyed that tribe, and epidemics left fewer than a hundred by 1829, when the survivors merged with the Otoe. The Otoe were the first people met by the Lewis and Clark expedition at Council Bluff in 1804. Missionaries first recorded it in the 1830s; in 1837 the Iowa were removed to a Kansas-Nebraska reservation, and later treaties gradually pressed its speakers into Indian Territory.
zh: 奇维雷语又称艾奥瓦—奥托—密苏里语，是一门苏—卡托巴语系语言，由艾奥瓦、奥托和密苏里几支高度相近的方言组成，最近的亲属语言是霍昌克语，即温尼贝戈语。这四个民族原是五大湖西部的同一群体，与奥内奥塔文化有关。16世纪起，各支陆续分离，向西南迁徙，在密苏里河与普拉特河沿岸定居，务农兼猎野牛，住土屋和梯皮。奇维雷一名的意思是说家乡方言。1673年，法国探险家雅克·马凯特在密苏里河畔见到密苏里人；但1730年索克人和梅斯克瓦基人的袭击几乎摧毁该族，到1829年只剩不足百人，幸存者并入奥托人。1804年，奥托人是刘易斯与克拉克探险队在康瑟尔布拉夫遇到的第一个民族。19世纪30年代，传教士首次把这种语言记录成文；1837年艾奥瓦人被迁到堪萨斯—内布拉斯加保留地，此后的条约又把其使用者逐步压入印第安领地。

en: Choco, or Chocoan, is the small language family of the rain-soaked Pacific lowlands of western Colombia and eastern Panama, centred on the Atrato and San Juan river basins of the Chocó. In 1337 its two living branches were already taking shape: the Emberá continuum of riverine forest villages, whose name ẽberá simply means person or human being, and Wounaan, also called Waunana or Noanamá, on the lower waterways; extinct highland kin such as Anserma, Caramanta and Arma once reached into the Cauca valley, while Cueva was spoken in the Darién. The family has never been convincingly linked to any other, although past scholars proposed ties to Cariban, Arawakan and Chibchan. Spanish entradas of the 1500s found the flooded, densely forested coast hard to hold, and Emberá groups long kept their autonomy by retreating upriver; from the late 1700s several bands moved north into the Darién, clashing with the Guna and pushing them toward the Caribbean shore. Emberá and Wounaan therefore remained everyday community languages through the colonial centuries rather than being replaced by Spanish.
zh: 乔科语（乔科安语）是哥伦比亚西部与巴拿马东部潮湿太平洋低地的一个小语系，核心区在乔科省的阿特拉托河与圣胡安河流域。1337年时，它现存的两大支系已具雏形：以河畔林间村落为家、方言连续成片的恩贝拉语——ẽberá 这个词本身就是“人”的意思；以及分布在下游水道的沃纳安语，又称瓦乌纳南语或诺阿纳马语。已消亡的安塞尔马语、卡拉曼塔语、阿尔马语等高原亲缘语言曾延伸到考卡河谷，库埃瓦语则通行于达连地区。过去曾有学者推测乔科语系与加勒比语系、阿拉瓦克语系或奇布查语系有亲缘关系，但始终没有得到可靠证明，它仍被视为独立语系。16世纪西班牙人的入侵发现这片水网密布、丛林幽深的海岸难以控制，恩贝拉人群体通过向河流上游退却长期保持自治；18世纪末，又有数支队伍北迁入达连地区，与古纳人冲突，把后者挤向加勒比海岸。因此在整个殖民时代，恩贝拉语和沃纳安语始终是社群的日常语言，并未被西班牙语取代。

en: Chokwe, also called Ciokwe or Tshokwe, is a Bantu language of the borderlands where Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia meet, and it serves as a lingua franca across eastern Angola. Its speakers, the Chokwe, trace their chiefs' ancestry to the Lunda migrations of the 1500s, and they entered history as one of the twelve clans of the Lunda Empire of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. After quarrels over tribute they broke away from the Lunda king, the Mwata Yanvo, and their trade in wax, ivory and other goods made them a prosperous, independent power. Related peoples such as the Mbunda, Luchazi and Luvale speak closely neighbouring languages, and the Chokwe farm, hunt and fish to the rhythm of the rainy and dry seasons.
zh: 绍奎语又称乔奎语或特肖克韦语，是一门班图语，通行于安哥拉、刚果（金）和赞比亚三国交界地带，并在东安哥拉充当通用语。说这种语言的绍奎人，其酋长世系可追溯到16世纪的隆达人迁徙；在17至18世纪，他们是隆达帝国十二个氏族之一。后因贡赋争执，他们脱离隆达国王姆瓦塔·扬沃独立，凭借蜂蜡、象牙等贸易成为富庶的强权。姆本达、卢查齐、卢瓦勒等亲缘族群使用与它相近的语言；绍奎人随雨季和旱季的交替务农、狩猎和捕鱼。

en: Chono was the language of the nomadic canoe people of the Chiloé, Guaitecas and Chonos archipelagos in southern Chile, hunter-gatherers who were the first identifiable inhabitants of those islands and left many shell middens. Francisco de Ulloa's expedition met them in 1553, and after a royal decree of 1608 the Spanish of Chiloé turned their southern voyages into slave raids. Jesuits reaching Chiloé in 1609 compiled a grammar and vocabulary, now lost, and missionized groups settled on Guar Island from 1710. The only surviving text is an eighteenth-century catechism, from which only about twenty words are known with certainty; place names across the fjords still show Chono origins. Its classification is unresolved, with parallels to Kawésqar but an unrelated core, and after the Spanish depopulation of the archipelagos in the 1740s the Chono merged into the Huilliche and mestizo population, the language disappearing by the early nineteenth century.
zh: 乔诺语是智利南部奇洛埃群岛、瓜伊特卡斯群岛和乔诺斯群岛上的游牧独木舟民族使用的语言；这些以渔猎采集为生的人是这些岛屿最早可辨识的居民，留下了大量贝丘。1553年，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚的探险队首次接触到他们；1608年西班牙国王颁布法令后，奇洛埃的西班牙人把南下航行变成了掳奴行动。1609年抵达奇洛埃的耶稣会士编写过语法书和词汇表，后来均告散佚；接受传教的乔诺人从1710年起被安置在瓜尔岛。留存下来的唯一文本是一份18世纪的教理问答，从中能确定的词只有约二十个，而峡湾地区的许多地名仍保留着乔诺语来源。它的谱系没有定论，与卡韦斯卡尔语有相似之处但核心词汇并无亲缘；18世纪40年代西班牙人清空群岛后，乔诺人融入维利切人和混血居民之中，这门语言到19世纪初便不复可闻。

en: Chontal was an extinct, unclassified language spoken in the northern part of what is now the Mexican state of Guerrero during the prehispanic and early colonial periods. In the sixteenth century it was still fairly widely spoken, but Spanish missionaries preached in Nahuatl, the regional lingua franca, and no description of the language survives.
zh: 琼塔尔语是一种已消亡、语系归属不明的语言，前西班牙时代和殖民早期通行于今墨西哥格雷罗州北部。16世纪时仍有相当多的使用者，但西班牙传教士改用当地通用语纳瓦特尔语传教，琼塔尔语没有留下任何语言记录。

en: Chukotko-Kamchatkan is a small language family of the extreme northeast of Siberia, held together by two distant branches. The Chukotkan branch of the tundra and the Chukchi Peninsula comprises Chukchi, Koryak, Alyutor and Kerek, while the Kamchatkan branch survives only in Itelmen on the western coast of Kamchatka, whose basic vocabulary is barely a third cognate with the northern languages; no link to any other family has been proven, and the group is usually classed with the Paleosiberian remnant peoples. Its speakers lived from sea-mammal hunting on the coast and reindeer herding inland, and Chukchi and Koryak share the endonym Luoravetlan, the real people. Russian Cossacks reached the Kolyma in 1643 and the Anadyr in 1649, founding Anadyrsk, and from 1697 Vladimir Atlasov annexed Kamchatka, where Itelmen revolts were met with mass deportations and forced conversion, so that by the early 1800s all Itelmens bore Russian names and a Russian-Itelmen creole called Kamchadal had emerged. On the tundra the Chukchi defeated expedition after expedition between 1701 and the 1750s, killing the commander Pavlutsky in 1747, after which Catherine the Great abandoned Anadyrsk in 1764 and switched to tribute and trade fairs instead. Through all these upheavals the family's languages remained purely oral, carried by epic song and shamanic tradition.
zh: 楚科奇‑堪察加语是西伯利亚极东北角的一个小语系，由两个关系疏远的语支组成。冻土地带和楚科奇半岛上的楚科奇语支包括楚科奇语、科里亚克语、阿留特语和克列克语；堪察加语支则只剩堪察加半岛西海岸的伊捷尔缅语，它的核心词汇与北方诸语言只有约三分之一同源。该语系与其他语系的亲缘关系都没有得到证实，通常被归入古西伯利亚语这一残余类别。操这些语言的族群，沿海的以捕猎海兽为生，内陆的放牧驯鹿；楚科奇人和科里亚克人还共用“卢奥拉韦特兰”这一自称，意为“真正的人”。俄国哥萨克于1643年抵达科雷马河，1649年抵达阿纳德尔河并建立阿纳德尔堡；1697年起，弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫吞并堪察加，伊捷尔缅人的起义遭到大规模驱逐和强制皈依，到19世纪初所有伊捷尔缅人都改用俄语名字，还产生了俄语与伊捷尔缅语混合的“堪察达尔”克里奥尔语。冻原上的楚科奇人则在1701年至18世纪50年代接连击败俄军远征队，1747年击毙俄军指挥官帕夫卢茨基；此后叶卡捷琳娜大帝于1764年放弃阿纳德尔堡，改以贡赋和贸易集市施治。在这整场动荡中，该语系的各种语言始终没有文字，靠史诗歌谣和萨满传统口耳相传。

en: Chumashan is a small language family, with no proven relatives elsewhere, spoken along the central California coast from San Luis Obispo to Malibu, in the nearby Transverse Range valleys and on the northern Channel Islands of San Miguel, Santa Rosa and Santa Cruz. It may be one of the oldest language families established in California, where the region's population shows deep continuity. Six members are recorded, Obispeño, Purisimeño, Ineseño, Barbareño, Ventureño and Island Chumash, joined by a dialect continuum on the mainland; plank canoes called tomol, adopted in the first millennium, linked the island villages to the coast. Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo made the first European contact in 1542, but colonization began only in 1772 with Mission San Luis Obispo, followed by San Buenaventura, Santa Barbara, La Purísima and Santa Inés, after which the languages came to be known by the names of those missions. Forced resettlement and epidemics shattered the Chumash communities, and in 1824 mission Chumash, joined by Yokuts allies, rose in the largest organized revolt of California's Spanish and Mexican period.
zh: 丘马什语是一个较小的语系，在其他语言中没有已证实的亲属，通行于加利福尼亚中部海岸——从圣路易斯奥比斯波到马里布——以及附近横断山脉的谷地和圣米格尔、圣罗莎、圣克鲁斯三座北海峡群岛。它可能是加州最古老的本地语系之一，该地区的人口延续极为久远。已记录的语言有六种：奥维斯佩尼奥语、普里西梅尼奥语、伊内塞尼奥语、巴尔巴雷尼奥语、文图雷尼奥语和岛屿丘马什语，大陆各方言连成一条方言连续体；公元第一个千年里出现的木板独木舟“托莫尔”把岛屿村庄与海岸联系起来。1542年胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略首次与欧洲人接触，但殖民要到1772年圣路易斯奥比斯波传教站建立才开始，随后又有圣布埃纳文图拉、圣巴巴拉、拉普里西马和圣伊内斯等传教站，这些语言后来便以传教站的名字为人所知。强制迁徙和疫病摧毁了丘马什人的社区；1824年，传教站里的丘马什人在约库茨盟友的参与下发动起义，这是加州西班牙和墨西哥统治时期规模最大的有组织反抗。
