It has two branches: the divergent Guhu-Samane of the Waria valley in Morobe Province, also known as Mid-Waria, and the Oro or Binanderean branch proper, spoken across Oro Province and including Binandere, Suena, the Orokaiva dialects and Baruga. The family looks like a comparatively recent expansion from the north, whose inland communities gradually absorbed older Oceanic-speaking settlements on the coast; this contact even imposed subject-object-verb word order on the neighboring Papuan Tip languages. The Orokaiva, divided into river, salt-water and inland groups, were remembered as formidable warriors defending their ridges. In 1545 Yñigo Ortiz de Retez sailed past these northern shores on the voyage that named New Guinea, without entering the mountain valleys behind them.
zh: 古胡奥罗语又称大比南德雷语族，汇集了新几内亚“鸟尾”东南半岛东北海岸的巴布亚诸语言。它分为两支：一支是莫罗贝省瓦里亚河谷中分化最深的古湖—珊曼语，又称中瓦里亚语；另一支是奥罗省全境通行的奥罗语，即比南德雷语本支，包括比南德雷语、苏埃纳语、奥罗凯瓦各方言和巴鲁加语。整个语族看起来是较晚近从北方扩张而来，内陆社群逐渐同化了海岸上更早的南岛语聚落；这种接触甚至把主—宾—谓语序强加给了邻近的巴布亚尖端语言。奥罗凯瓦人分为河畔、咸水和内陆三个群体，以守卫山岭的强悍战士著称。1545年，伊尼戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·雷特斯在为新几内亚命名的航行中驶过这段北部海岸，但没有进入海岸后方的山谷。

en: Gujarati is the Western Indo-Aryan language of the Gujarat coast, descended from the Gurjar Apabhramsha and from Old Gujarati, the tongue of the Gujjar clans who ruled much of western India around 1200. The Jain monk Hemachandra codified its parent grammar under the Chaulukya king Jayasimha Siddharaja of Patan, and by 1300 a fairly standard literary form had emerged; Jain monks composed long Rasa narratives, with surviving examples going back to 1185, and the Balavabodha of 1355 is among the earliest Gujarati prose, while merchants made Ahmedabad and Cambay wealthy trading cities. At this stage Gujarati and Rajasthani were one speech, sometimes called Old Western Rajasthani, and the two only separated during the 1400s. Under the Gujarat sultans, who ruled from 1391 to 1583, the Bhakti poet Narsinh Mehta made the vernacular the vehicle of mystical verse. The Middle Gujarati stage then ran to about 1800, and its script is a cursive relation of Devanagari that has dropped the horizontal head line.
zh: 古吉拉特语是古吉拉特沿海地区的西印度—雅利安语言，由古吉拉特阿帕布拉姆沙语和老古吉拉特语演变而来，后者是约1200年前后统治印度西部大片土地的古吉拉特诸部的语言。耆那教修士金月在帕坦的遮娄其国王阇耶辛诃·悉达罗阇在位时编订了其母语的语法，到1300年前后，相当规范的文学语言已经成形；耆那教修士创作罗萨体长篇叙事诗，现存作品可追溯到1185年，1355年的《巴拉瓦博达》则是最早的古吉拉特语散文之一，商人也把艾哈迈达巴德和坎贝经营成富庶的商埠。这一阶段的古吉拉特语与拉贾斯坦语尚未分家，有时合称古西拉贾斯坦语，两者到15世纪才各自独立。在1391至1583年统治的古吉拉特苏丹们治下，虔诚派诗人纳尔辛·默赫塔以方言写作神秘诗篇。中古吉拉特语阶段延续到1800年前后，其文字是天城文的草书近亲，省去了字母上方的横线。

en: The Gunwinyguan languages form a proposed non-Pama–Nyungan family spread across Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory. Its core, spoken in western Arnhem Land around Gunbalanya, is Kunwinjku, also called Gunwinggu, together with Kunbarlang, Jawoyn, Dalabon, Rembarrnga and Ngalakgan; a wider Arnhem, or Macro-Gunwinyguan, grouping adds eastern tongues such as Nunggubuyu, Ngandi and the Anindilyakwa of Groote Eylandt. Their kinship rests mainly on shared verb morphology, and many of them distinguish fortis and lenis stops. When the first British colony in Australia was founded in 1788, Makassan trepang fishermen from Sulawesi were already sailing to the northern coast; their pidgin became a trade lingua franca and left Makassarese loanwords such as balanda, meaning white person, in the Arnhem languages.
zh: 贡温古诸语是拟议中的一个非帕马—恩永甘语族，分布在北领地阿纳姆地。核心语言是通行于阿纳姆地西部贡巴兰亚一带的昆温朱语，又名贡温古语，此外还有昆巴兰语、贾沃因语、达拉邦语、伦巴伦加语和恩加拉甘语；更宽泛的阿纳姆（大贡温古）划分还纳入东部的农古布尤语、恩甘迪语和格鲁特岛的阿宁迪利亚克瓦语。它们的亲缘关系主要建立在共通的动词形态上，多种语言都有塞音强弱对立。1788年英国在澳大利亚建立第一个殖民地时，来自苏拉威西的望加锡海参渔民已航行到澳大利亚北岸，他们的皮钦语成为贸易通用语，并给阿纳姆诸语留下望加锡语借词，例如意为‘白人’的词汇。

en: Gur, also called Central Gur or Mabia and formerly known as Voltaic after the Volta River, is a Niger–Congo branch spoken across the Sahel and savanna belt, above all in Burkina Faso and the northern parts of Ghana and Togo. Its principal languages include Mòoré, the language of the Mossi, together with Dagbani, Mampruli, Gurunsi and Gurma. The Mossi, the largest Gur people, built horseman kingdoms on the upper Volta from the eleventh century, ruled from Ouagadougou by the Mogho Naaba; their neighbours the Dagomba and Mamprusi founded states in what is now northern Ghana. Diverse farming peoples were absorbed into Mossi identity in about 1500. Gur societies kept their history largely by oral tradition, though the Mossi also used the Arabic-based Ajami script, and the languages remained the speech of independent savanna kingdoms throughout this period.
zh: 古尔语又称中古尔语或马比亚语，旧称沃尔特语，得名于沃尔特河，属于尼日尔—刚果语系，通行于萨赫勒和热带草原地带，以布基纳法索以及加纳、多哥的北部最为集中。主要语言包括莫西人使用的莫雷语，以及达邦语、曼普鲁西语、古伦西语和古尔马语。最大的古尔族群莫西人自11世纪起在沃尔特河上游建立骑马武士的王国，由莫霍·纳巴在瓦加杜古统治；他们的邻人达贡巴人和曼普鲁西人则在今加纳北部建国。约1500年，众多农耕族群被融入莫西人的认同之中。古尔社会主要以口传保存历史，不过莫西人也使用以阿拉伯字母为基础的阿贾米文字；在整个这一时期，这些语言始终是独立草原王国的语言。

en: Haida is the language of the Haida people of the Pacific Northwest coast, spoken on the Haida Gwaii archipelago and the nearby Prince of Wales Island in Alaska. Linguists disagree over its classification: some place it in the Na-Dené family, while others treat it as a language isolate. It falls into a Northern and a Southern dialect group, distinguished mainly by phonology, and its sound system features ejective consonants, phonemic vowel length and tone. At the time of the first European contact, the Spanish voyage of Juan Pérez in 1772, Haida had perhaps fifteen thousand speakers. Epidemics then emptied whole village areas. In the 1830s a Haida-based trade pidgin, Haida Jargon, served Haida, Tsimshian, Heiltsuk and English speakers along the coast.
zh: 海达语是太平洋西北海岸海达人的语言，通行于海达瓜依群岛以及邻近的阿拉斯加威尔士亲王岛。语言学家对它的归属有争议：有人将其划入纳-德内语系，也有人认为它是一门孤立语言。它分为北部和南部两个方言群，主要差别在语音方面，音系拥有挤喉辅音、音位性元音长短对立和声调。1772年西班牙人胡安·佩雷斯的航行首次与欧洲人接触时，说海达语的约有一万五千人。此后的瘟疫使整片村落区域人口断绝。19世纪30年代，一种以海达语为基础的贸易混合语“海达行话”在沿海地区通行，供海达人、钦西安人、海尔楚克人和说英语的人共同使用。

en: Haliti, self-designated Haliti-Paresi and commonly called Paresi, is a Central Arawakan language of the Paresi–Xingu branch, spoken by the Paresi people on the plateaus of Mato Grosso in western Brazil; the little-documented speech of the neighboring Enawene Nawe belongs to the same family. In its number system only the first four quantities have distinct words, everything above four being reckoned on a base of five with fingers, toes and other body parts. The Paresi encountered Portuguese colonists for the first time in 1718, and for more than a century afterward their villages were raided for slaves, the captives set to work as miners in Mato Grosso. The disruption scattered or absorbed several Paresi subgroups, while surviving bands such as the Kozarene kept Haliti alive through traditional beer-brewing, bread-making and other communal customs.
zh: 哈利蒂语使用者自称哈利蒂—帕雷西语，通称帕雷西语，属阿拉瓦克语族中部帕雷西—欣古语支，由巴西西部马托格罗索高原上的帕雷西人使用；邻近的埃纳韦内—纳韦人那种记载很少的语言也属同一语族。它的数词只有前四个数目有独立的词，四以上的数量都以五为基数，借助手指、脚趾等身体部位来计。1718年，帕雷西人第一次遇到葡萄牙殖民者，此后一百多年间他们的村落不断遭到奴隶劫掠，被俘者被送往马托格罗索当矿工。这场动荡使多个帕雷西分支流散或被同化，而科扎雷内等留存下来的群体则通过传统酿酒、制饼等集体习俗维系着哈利蒂语。

en: The Halmaheran grouping corresponds to the Raja Ampat–South Halmahera branch of the South Halmahera–West New Guinea subgroup of Austronesian, straddling the Halmahera Sea from the southeastern coast of Halmahera to the Raja Ampat, or Four Kings, islands off the Bird's Head Peninsula of New Guinea. Its South Halmaheran side takes in Maba, together with Buli, Patani, Taba and Gane; on the Raja Ampat side it carries Ma'ya, with dialects on Waigeo, Salawati, Batanta and Misool, the Maden and other Salawati speeches, and the heavily Papuan-influenced Ambel and Matbat. Long contact with Papuan languages left these tongues with unusual features: Ma'ya has three lexically distinctive tonemes, a rarity among Austronesian languages, and some scholars doubt whether the Raja Ampat languages are Austronesian at all rather than relexified Papuan ones, while the South Halmahera languages carry a thick layer of Ternate loanwords. Pottery-making Austronesian communities reached Raja Ampat about 3,500 to 3,000 years ago. Islam arrived in the fifteenth century through contacts with the Bacan Sultanate, and in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the four local kingdoms of Waigeo, Salawati, Sailolof and Misool, bound to Tidore through the Biak-born war leader Gurabesi, formed the Raja Ampat tributary network. The Portuguese navigator Jorge de Menezes first sighted the islands for Europeans in 1526, William Dampier charted the strait that now bears his name in 1699, and the archipelago later passed into the Dutch colonial sphere together with Tidore's other Papuan dependencies.
zh: 哈马黑拉语这一划分对应南岛语系南哈马黑拉—西新几内亚语群下的拉贾安帕特—南哈马黑拉语支，沿哈马黑拉海两岸分布：一边是哈马黑拉岛东南沿海，另一边是新几内亚岛鸟头半岛西北外海的拉贾安帕特（意为四王）群岛。南哈马黑拉一侧有马巴语，以及布利语、帕塔尼语、塔巴语和加内语；拉贾安帕特一侧则有方言分布在卫吉、萨拉瓦蒂、巴坦塔和米苏尔诸岛的马亚语，马登语等萨拉瓦蒂岛上的语言，以及深受巴布亚语言影响的安贝尔语和马特巴特语。与巴布亚语言的长期接触赋予这些语言罕见特征：马亚语有三个区别词义的声调，在南岛语言中十分少见，部分学者甚至怀疑拉贾安帕特诸语究竟是南岛语，还是换用了南岛词汇的巴布亚语；南哈马黑拉诸语则带有厚厚的特尔纳特语借词层。约3500至3000年前，会制陶的南岛语人群抵达拉贾安帕特。15世纪，伊斯兰教经与巴占苏丹国的往来传入；16至17世纪，卫吉、萨拉瓦蒂、赛洛洛夫和米苏尔四个地方王国经出身比亚克的军事首领古拉贝西与蒂多雷结盟，组成拉贾安帕特朝贡网络。1526年，葡萄牙航海者若热·德·梅内塞斯让欧洲人首次望见这片群岛；1699年，威廉·丹皮尔测绘了后来以他命名的海峡；此后，该群岛与蒂多雷在巴布亚的其他属地一同进入荷兰殖民势力范围。

en: Hatam, also spelled Hattam or Atam, is a divergent Papuan language of the eastern Bird's Head Peninsula in West Papua, spoken in the rugged Arfak Mountains and around the coastal town of Manokwari. Its only close relative is Mansim, or Borai, once listed as a Hatam dialect but now treated as a distinct language; together the two form the tiny Hatam–Mansim family, which Ethnologue and Glottolog classify as an independent family or an isolate, although Malcolm Ross has tentatively assigned it to the West Papuan languages on the strength of pronoun parallels. In Hatam the great mountain overlooking Manokwari is called Indon or Indonga, simply the big mountain, a name that still frames local geography. Hatam shares the Arfak range with the unrelated Meyah and Sougb peoples, whose languages are mutually unintelligible with it, and archaeological evidence shows human settlement in these mountains reaching back some 26,000 years. In the fifteenth or early sixteenth century the Biak war leader Gurabesi, in the service of the Tidore sultan Al-Mansur, drew the Bird's Head into the Sultanate of Tidore's loose tribute network, the first major outside power to reach Hatam country. Luís Vaz de Torres's Spanish expedition sailed the New Guinea coast in 1606, while permanent European administration only arrived much later, leaving the Arfak highlands under indirect Tidore overlordship through the early nineteenth century.
zh: 哈特姆语又拼 Hattam 或 Atam，是西巴布亚鸟头半岛东部一种差异很大的巴布亚语言，通行于崎岖的阿尔法克山脉和海滨城镇马诺夸里一带。它唯一的近亲是曼西姆语（又称博赖语），后者曾被列为哈特姆语方言，后被视为独立语言；二者组成小小的哈特姆-曼西姆语系，主要语言学文献将其归为独立语系或孤立语言，不过马尔科姆·罗斯根据代词上的相似之处，暂时把它划入西巴布亚语系。在哈特姆语里，俯瞰马诺夸里的大山称 Indon 或 Indonga，意为“大山”，这个名字仍然是当地地理观念的基本框架。哈特姆人与语言互不相通的梅亚人和苏格布人共处于阿尔法克山区，考古证据表明人类在这些山地的定居可追溯到约2.6万年前。15世纪或16世纪初，比亚克人的军事首领古拉贝西效力于蒂多雷苏丹阿尔-曼苏尔，把鸟头半岛拉入蒂多雷苏丹国松散的朝贡网络，这是触及哈特姆地区的第一个强大外部势力。1606年，路易斯·瓦斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙探险队沿新几内亚海岸航行；而永久性的欧洲人管理要到很久以后才到来，因此整个19世纪早期，阿尔法克高地仍处在蒂多雷的间接宗主权之下。

en: Haudenosaunee denotes the Northern Iroquoian tongues of the Iroquois Confederacy and its neighbours in the north-eastern woodlands. The five original nations, arrayed from east to west across what is now New York, were the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca; the Tuscarora, moving up from the Carolinas, were admitted as a sixth in 1722. Closely related languages of neighbouring peoples, among them the Susquehannock of Pennsylvania and the Erie south of Lake Erie, belong to the same branch. These are polysynthetic, head-marking languages with almost no labial consonants, carried for centuries by oral tradition, ceremony and the formal oratory of the confederacy's Grand Council. The league itself was forged before European contact under the Great Law of Peace. During the Beaver Wars of the 1600s the Haudenosaunee defeated and absorbed the Huron, Neutral, Erie and most of the Susquehannock, whose poorly recorded speech died with its last speakers in the eighteenth century; a short vocabulary taken down by a Swedish missionary in the 1640s is nearly all that survives of it. Missionaries later gave the surviving confederacy languages Latin-based spellings. The American Revolution split the Six Nations, and many families resettled on the Grand River in Ontario after 1783.
zh: 霍迪诺肖尼语指易洛魁联盟及其东北林地邻族所说的北易洛魁诸语。最初的五个部族自东向西分布在今纽约州，分别是莫霍克人、奥奈达人、奥农达加人、卡尤加人和塞内卡人；从卡罗来纳北迁的塔斯卡洛拉人于1722年被接纳为第六族。宾夕法尼亚的萨斯奎汉纳人、伊利湖以南的伊利人等邻族所说的近亲语言也属于这一支。这些语言属多式综合语，以动词词头承载语法关系，几乎没有唇音，数百年来全凭口头传统、仪式和联盟大议会的正式演说延续。联盟本身在欧洲人到来之前依照《伟大和平法则》结成。1600年代的河狸战争中，易洛魁人击败并同化了休伦人、中立人、伊利人和大部分萨斯奎汉纳人；后者记录稀少的语言随最后的使用者在18世纪消亡，留存下来的几乎只有一位瑞典传教士在1640年代记下的简短词表。后来传教士为留存下来的联盟诸语创制了拉丁字母拼写法。美国独立战争使六族分裂，1783年后许多家庭迁居安大略的格兰德河一带。

en: Hausa is the chief language of the Chadic branch of the Afroasiatic family, tonal in structure, and the native tongue of the Hausa of Hausaland, in what is now northern Nigeria and southern Niger. The Hausa Bakwai city-states, of which Daura is remembered as the oldest, took shape between the seventh and eleventh centuries; the walls of Kano were begun under Sarki Gijimasu in 1095 and completed in the fourteenth century. Islam spread through the trading cities from the fourteenth century, and Kano and Katsina became centres of trans-Saharan commerce in cloth, leather and salt. By the early fifteenth century Hausa was being written in an adapted Arabic script called Ajami, which produced the Kano Chronicle and, in the seventeenth century, Abdullahi Suka's Riwayar Nabi Musa, the earliest known Hausa book. As a merchants' language Hausa also became a lingua franca far beyond its homeland. In the opening years of the nineteenth century the reformer Usman dan Fodio led a jihad that made Sokoto the new centre of Hausa Islamic scholarship.
zh: 豪萨语是亚非语系乍得语族最主要的语言，有声调，是今尼日利亚北部和尼日尔南部豪萨兰地区豪萨人的母语。豪萨七邦等城邦在7至11世纪间形成，其中道拉被视为最古老的城邦；卡诺城墙于1095年在萨尔基·吉吉马苏主持下动工，到14世纪建成。伊斯兰教自14世纪起经由商业城市传播，卡诺和卡齐纳成为布匹、皮革和食盐的跨撒哈拉贸易中心。到15世纪初，豪萨语已使用经改造的阿拉伯字母阿贾米文字书写，留下了《卡诺编年史》，以及17世纪阿卜杜拉希·苏卡所著、已知最早的豪萨语书籍《先知穆萨传》。作为商人的语言，豪萨语还成为远超本土的通用语。19世纪初，改革者乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥发动圣战，使索科托成为豪萨伊斯兰学术的新中心。

en: Hebrew is a Canaanite language of the Northwest Semitic group, spoken in antiquity by the Israelites of the Levant. Its oldest written remains, including the Gezer calendar, date to the tenth century BCE, and the Hebrew Bible was composed in Biblical Hebrew, reaching roughly its present form around the Babylonian captivity of 586 BCE; Jews came to call it the holy tongue. After the failure of the Bar Kokhba revolt in the second century CE it ceased to be a mother tongue, displaced in daily life by Aramaic and Greek, but it never fell silent: it remained the language of Jewish prayer, rabbinic learning such as the Mishnah and Talmud, scholarship, commerce and poetry, and the first dated printed Hebrew book appeared in 1475. The Samaritans kept their own Hebrew dialect and an alphabet descended from the ancient Paleo-Hebrew script for their liturgy. In the nineteenth century a movement of scholars and settlers revived Hebrew into a living spoken language once more.
zh: 希伯来语是闪米特语族西北支的迦南语之一，古时为黎凡特以色列人的语言。现存最古的文字材料（包括基色历）可追溯到公元前10世纪；《希伯来圣经》以圣经希伯来语写成，大约在公元前586年巴比伦之囚时期基本定型，犹太人因而称它为“圣语”。2世纪巴尔·科赫巴起义失败后，希伯来语不再是母语，日常生活中被阿拉米语和希腊语取代，但它并未沉寂：始终用于犹太教祈祷、《密西拿》和《塔木德》等拉比学问、学术、商贸和诗歌，第一本有确切纪年的希伯来语印本书于1475年问世。撒马利亚人则保留了自己的希伯来语方言，并在礼仪中使用源自古代希伯来字母的撒马利亚字母。19世纪，在学者和移民的推动下，希伯来语重新复兴为活的口语。

en: Henia-Kamiare, usually called Comechigon after the people who spoke it, was the language of the Comechigon groups of the Argentine hills in what are now the provinces of Cordoba and San Luis. Its two varieties belonged to the northern Henia and southern Kamiare, each a loose cluster of about a dozen tribes. Poorly attested, with only a handful of words recorded with confidence, it is treated as an isolate, although links to the Huarpean languages, to Cacan and to the Sanaviron tongue have all been proposed. The Comechigon lived in half-buried stone houses and farmed the dry valleys, but by the 1690s most had been killed or displaced by Spanish conquistadores. Colonial administration deliberately promoted Quechua brought from Upper Peru instead of the local speech, which then died out, leaving only petroglyphs and a trace of its vowel-lengthening habit in the Spanish of Cordoba.
zh: 赫尼亚-卡米亚雷语通常随其使用者被称为科梅钦贡语，通行于今阿根廷科尔多瓦省和圣路易斯省一带的山地带。它分两种变体，分属北方的赫尼亚人和南方的卡米亚雷人，两者各由约十几个部落松散组成。这种语言记录极少，只有少量词语可以确认，学界将其视为孤立语，但也有人提出它与瓦尔佩语、卡坎语或萨纳维龙语有亲缘关系。科梅钦贡人住在半地下的石屋中，在干旱的河谷务农；到17世纪90年代，他们大多已被西班牙征服者杀害或驱离。殖民当局有意推广东自上秘鲁移入的克丘亚语，本地语言随之消亡，只留下岩画，以及科尔多瓦西班牙语中元音拉长的一点痕迹。

en: Hindustani, or Hindi-Urdu, is the Indo-Aryan lingua franca of the plain of northern India, from the Ganges-Yamuna Doab around Delhi and Meerut across the Hindi belt. It grew out of the Middle Indo-Aryan Apabhraṃśa vernaculars of the seventh to thirteenth centuries and took shape as a contact language under the Delhi Sultanate, when its Prakrit base absorbed Persian, Arabic and Turkic words. The thirteenth-century poet Amir Khusrau wrote in it and called it Hindavi, the language of Delhi, and Sufi teachers carried it through the subcontinent; in the Deccan it developed a southern branch called Dakhani. Until the eighteenth century the same speech went by names such as Hindvi, Rekhta and Lahori, and the name Urdu came into use only around 1780. It is one pluricentric language with two literary registers: Hindi, written in Devanagari and drawn toward Sanskrit, and Urdu, written in the Persian Nastaliq hand and steeped in Persian vocabulary. A grammar printed by the East India Company scholar John Gilchrist in 1796 codified it for British administration.
zh: 印度斯坦语又称印地—乌尔都语，是印度北部平原的印度—雅利安通用语，通行范围从德里、密拉特一带的恒河—亚穆纳河河间地延伸到整个印地语地带。它由7至13世纪的中古印度—雅利安俗语阿帕布拉姆沙发展而来，在德里苏丹国时期作为各民族接触的语言成型，俗语词根之上吸收了大量波斯语、阿拉伯语和突厥语词汇。13世纪的诗人阿米尔·胡斯劳用它写作，称之为“欣达维”，即德里的语言；苏菲派导师又把它传布到次大陆各地，在德干发展出名为达卡尼的南支。18世纪以前，这种语言还有欣德维、雷克赫塔、拉霍尔等名称，“乌尔都”一名约1780年才出现。它是一种多中心语言，有两个书面语域：用天城体书写、偏向梵语的印地语，以及用波斯纳斯塔里克体书写、充满波斯语词汇的乌尔都语。1796年，英国东印度公司学者吉尔克里斯特出版语法书，为殖民行政用途规范了这一语言。

en: Hinóno'eitíít, the Arapaho language, is a Plains Algonquian tongue of the Algic family; scholars group it with the closely related Gros Ventre speech, Atsina, as dialects of one Arapaho-Atsina language with five historical varieties. Its speakers' ancestors, the Heeteinono'eino', farmed maize in the Red River valley on the western edge of the Great Lakes, in present-day Manitoba and Minnesota, until Ojibwe groups armed by French traders pushed them westward with the early Cheyenne. They entered the Great Plains before 1700, at first using dog-drawn travois, and after acquiring horses in the early 1700s became nomadic bison hunters ranging from the South Saskatchewan to the Arkansas River. A group that split off became the Gros Ventre, the A'aninin or White Clay people, whose speech kept three consonants lost in Arapaho proper. On the plains the Arapaho traded meat and hides for corn with the Mandan and Arikara, and around 1811 allied with the Cheyenne, joining them by 1826 in pushing the Kiowa and Comanche south.
zh: 希诺诺埃语即阿拉帕霍语，是阿尔吉克语系的平原阿尔冈昆语言；学者把它与关系极近的格罗斯文特语（又称阿齐纳语）视为同一“阿拉帕霍—阿齐纳语”的方言，该语言历史上曾有五个分支。操此语者的先民希特伊诺诺埃人本在五大湖西缘的雷德河谷（今加拿大曼尼托巴和美国明尼苏达一带）种植玉米，后来被取得法国枪械的奥吉布瓦人连同早期夏延人一起向西驱赶。他们在1700年以前进入大平原，起初以狗拖橇运物，18世纪初获得马匹后转为游牧的野牛猎人，活动范围北起南萨斯喀彻温河、南抵阿肯色河。分出去的一支成为格罗斯文特人，即自称“白黏土人”的阿尼宁人，其语言保留了阿拉帕霍语已失去的三个辅音。在平原上，阿拉帕霍人用兽肉和兽皮向曼丹人和阿里卡拉人换取玉米，并于约1811年与夏延人结盟，到1826年联手将基奥瓦人和科曼奇人挤向南方。

en: Hlai is the speech of the Li people, the largest minority of Hainan Island, and forms a primary branch of the Kra-Dai family on its own, used in the mountains of the island's central and southern parts in several varieties such as Ha, Qi, Run and the divergent Jiamao, together with the ethnically distinct Cun language. Linguists derive its speakers from migrants who crossed the Hainan Strait from the Leizhou Peninsula in prehistoric times, while Chinese records first call the mainland ancestors of these peoples the Li, or Liliao, and the name Li itself is attested from the Later Tang period of 923 to 937. On the mainland the Li had been united in the sixth century under the hereditary chieftain Lady Xian, but after the eleventh century they disappear from continental records, surviving mainly on Hainan, where imperial rule reached the lowlands under the Song and the whole island only under the Qing, who restored administration by 1700. Confined to the highlands as Han settlers took the farmland, the Hlai rose against incoming merchants in 1766. Their language remained purely spoken, with no writing system of its own.
zh: 黎语是海南岛最大的少数民族黎族的语言，自成壮侗语系下的一个语支，通行于岛中部和南部的山区，分为哈、杞、润等方言，加上差异很大的加茂话，以及族属不同的村语。语言学家认为黎族先民在史前从雷州半岛渡过琼州海峡而来；汉文文献最初把这些人的大陆先民称作俚或俚僚，“黎”这个名称最早见于923至937年的后唐时期。在大陆上，俚人曾于6世纪在世袭首领冼夫人治下联合起来，但11世纪以后便不见于大陆记载，主要留存于海南：中原王朝在宋代才间接治理岛上低地，直到清代才控制全岛，并于1700年重建行政体系。随着汉族移民占去耕地，黎族被挤压到高地，又在1766年起事反抗外来商人。黎语始终只有口语，没有自己的文字。

en: Hmong is the largest group within the Hmongic or Miao languages, which together with the Mienic languages form the Hmong–Mien family. It is a continuum of largely mutually intelligible, tonal and monosyllabic dialects, spoken across the mountains of southern China, chiefly Guizhou, Hunan, Yunnan, Sichuan and Guangxi, and carried by migrants into northern Vietnam, Laos and Thailand from the eighteenth century onward. Chinese records call these peoples Miao: before the Qin unification of 221 BCE the word was a loose label for southern tribes, but from the Tang dynasty of 618 to 907 it referred more clearly to the ancestors of the Hmong. Linguistic evidence suggests Hmong–Mien speakers have lived in this same corner of southern China for some 8,000 years. The language took in many Chinese loanwords but had no traditional script; romanized writing systems were devised by missionaries only in the twentieth century.
zh: 苗语是苗瑶语系苗语支中规模最大的一群，与瑶语支共同构成苗瑶语系。它是一组彼此大致可以互通的有声调单音节方言，通行于中国南方贵州、湖南、云南、四川、广西的山区，并在18世纪以后随移民传入越南北部、老挝和泰国。中国史书把这些人群泛称为“苗”：公元前221年秦统一以前，“苗”是对南方诸部族的宽泛称呼，到618—907年的唐代，才较明确地指称苗语人群的先民。语言学证据显示，说苗瑶语的人群在中国南方这片区域已生活了约八千年。苗语吸收了大量汉语借词，但传统上没有文字，拉丁字母拼写系统到20世纪才由传教士创制。

en: Hokan is a proposed language family linking about a dozen small Native American language groups of California, Arizona and Baja California. Its name draws on the word for “two” recurring across them, such as ha'k in Achumawi. The best-attested branch is Yuman–Cochimí: the Yuman languages of the lower Colorado River, among them Kumeyaay, Yavapai and Hualapai, and Cochimí of central Baja California, recorded in Jesuit documents of the 1700s, which is thought to have split from the Yuman languages around 1000 BC. Other members include the coastal Pomo, Karuk and Shasta near Mount Shasta, Salinan, Washo by Lake Tahoe and the Seri of the Sonora coast. Their scattered distribution suggests they once covered the California Central Valley before being separated by later-arriving peoples. The grouping, proposed by Roland Dixon and Alfred Kroeber and expanded by Edward Sapir, remains debated among linguists.
zh: 霍坎语是一个假想语系，用来归组加利福尼亚、亚利桑那和下加利福尼亚的十余个小型美洲原住民语言群体。它的名称取自这些语言中反复出现的“二”一词，例如阿丘马维语的 ha'k。证据最充分的分支是尤曼－科奇米语族：科罗拉多河下游的尤曼诸语言，包括库梅亚伊语、亚瓦派语和瓦拉派语；以及下加利福尼亚中部的科奇米语，它在18世纪耶稣会的文献中已有记录，据信约在公元前1000年与尤曼诸语言分化。其他成员还有沿海的波莫语、沙斯塔山附近的卡鲁克语和沙斯塔语、萨利南语、塔霍湖畔的瓦肖语，以及索诺拉沿海的塞里语。它们零散的分布说明，在后来者迁入之前，这些语言曾遍布加利福尼亚中央谷地。这一归组由罗兰·狄克逊和阿尔弗雷德·克罗伯提出、爱德华·萨丕尔扩充，在语言学界仍有争议。

en: Hopi, called Hopílavayi by its speakers, is a Uto-Aztecan language of the Hopi, a Pueblo people of northeastern Arizona. The Hopi descend from the Ancestral Pueblo peoples of the Four Corners region, and villages such as Oraibi, founded before 1100, rank among the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in North America. Hopi is split into four mesa dialects, First Mesa, Mishongnovi, Shipaulovi and Third Mesa, and belongs to the Pueblo linguistic area, sharing features with Tanoan, Keresan, Zuni and Navajo. Spaniards first reached the Hopi mesas with the Coronado expedition of the 1540s, and missions were later imposed from New Mexico; the Hopi joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, killed their friars and kept their independence thereafter, moving villages to the mesa tops for defence. In the twentieth century Benjamin Lee Whorf made Hopi famous in linguistics through his studies of its grammar and expression of time, claims later scholars substantially revised.
zh: 霍皮语（使用者自称 Hopílavayi）是亚利桑那东北部普韦布洛人一支霍皮人的语言，属于犹他‑阿兹特克语系。霍皮人是四角落地区古普韦布洛人的后裔，奥赖比等村落建于1100年以前，是北美最古老的持续有人居住的定居点之一。霍皮语分为第一台地、米雄诺维、希波洛维和第三台地四种方言，并属于普韦布洛语言联盟，与塔诺安语、凯雷斯语、祖尼语和纳瓦霍语具有共同特征。西班牙人最早在16世纪40年代随科罗纳多远征队抵达霍皮人的台地，后来新墨西哥方面又强行设立传教站；霍皮人参加了1680年的普韦布洛起义，杀死传教士，此后一直保持独立，并把村庄迁到台地顶部以便防守。20世纪，本杰明·李·沃尔夫对霍皮语语法及其时间表达方式的研究使这种语言在语言学界闻名，不过后来的学者对他的结论做了大幅修正。

en: Huizhou, or Hui, is the Sinitic speech of the Xin'an River basin, centered on the old Huizhou Prefecture of southern Anhui and spilling into northern Zhejiang and northeastern Jiangxi. It grew from the Chinese of Central Plains settlers who moved into these mountains and absorbed the language of the native Shanyue people, and it shares its ancient Jiangdong roots with Wu and Min: its initials lean toward Gan while its vowels resemble southern Wu, so linguists have at various times placed it with Wu, Gan or Jianghuai Mandarin. Its varieties differ from township to township and are often mutually unintelligible. Under the Ming, 1368 to 1644, and the Qing, Jianghuai speakers settled in the region, while Huizhou merchants grew rich across the empire, above all in Yangzhou, and sponsored operas sung in the home dialect. The speech of She County and later Tunxi served as the local standard, and Hui is written in Chinese characters.
zh: 徽语又称徽州话，是新安江流域的汉语方言，以古徽州府为核心，地跨安徽南部，并伸入浙江北部和江西东北部。它由历代中原移民的汉语吸收徽州土著山越的语言而成，与吴语、闽语同源于古代江东方言：声母系统接近赣语，韵母却近于南部吴语，因此学者曾分别把它归入吴语、赣语或江淮官话。徽语内部差异极大，往往隔一个乡就彼此听不懂。明代（1368—1644年）及清代，江淮官话人口迁入徽语区；徽商则在各地致富，尤以扬州为盛，并出资扶持用家乡话演唱的戏曲。旧时以歙县县城话为代表音，后来屯溪话成为徽语的代表，徽语使用汉字书写。

en: Hungarian is the Ugric tongue of the Uralic family, which split from the Mansi and Khanty of western Siberia in the first half of the first millennium BC and drifted west to the Volga-Ural steppe. Contact with Iranian peoples and Oghur Turkic Bulgars between the fifth and ninth centuries gave it many loanwords for livestock, farming and rule, while its Uralic grammar and core vocabulary remained intact. The Magyars entered the Carpathian Basin in 895, and after the founding of the Christian kingdom by Stephen I in 1000 the old runic alphabet gave way to Latin letters. The Tihany charter of 1055 preserves the first Hungarian phrases, the Funeral Sermon of the 1190s is the earliest complete text, and a fuller literature grew after 1300, followed by the Hussite Bible of the 1430s and the first printed Hungarian book in 1533. Slavic and German words kept entering the language, joined by Turkish ones under Ottoman rule after 1541, and by the seventeenth century Hungarian had nearly its settled form.
zh: 匈牙利语是乌拉尔语系乌戈尔语支的语言，在公元前第一个千年上半叶与西伯利亚西部的曼西语、汉特语分离，沿伏尔加河与乌拉尔山之间西迁。它长期接触伊朗民族，5—9世纪又受奥古尔突厥语保加尔人影响，吸收了大量畜牧、农耕和统治方面的借词，但乌拉尔语的语法和核心词汇保留完好。马扎尔人于895年进入喀尔巴阡盆地；1000年伊什特万一世建立基督教王国后，古老的如尼字母让位于拉丁字母。1055年的蒂豪尼修道院特许状保存了最早的匈牙利语词句，12世纪90年代的《葬礼布道与祷文》是现存最早的完整匈牙利语文本；1300年以后文学创作渐丰，15世纪30年代出现胡斯派圣经译本，1533年第一部匈牙利语活字印本书问世。斯拉夫语和德语借词持续涌入，1541年起奥斯曼统治时期又添突厥语借词；到17世纪，匈牙利语已大体定型。

en: Gilbertese, officially te taetae ni Kiribati and also called te taetae n aomata, the language of the people, is an Austronesian language of the Micronesian branch of Oceanic, spoken across the low coral atolls of the Gilbert Islands. It splits into northern and southern dialects, with the islands of Butaritari and Makin keeping a further distinct form. Austronesian seafarers settled the atolls over a long span from around 3000 before Christ, and a wave of Samoan arrivals around 1300 added Polynesian words and clans to the mix; by the fifteenth century the northern islands lived under chiefs called uea while the south was run by councils of elders, the unimwaane. European contact began when Commodore John Byron chanced on Nikunau in 1765, and Captains Thomas Gilbert and John Marshall passed through in 1788, after whom Adam von Krusenstern named the archipelago the Gilbert Islands in 1820. Whalers and traders then frequented the islands from the 1820s, but through the 1830s Gilbertese remained an entirely oral language, its first printed word lists still years away.
zh: 基里巴斯语正式名称为“特泰泰·尼·基里巴斯”，又称“特泰泰·纳奥马塔”，意为人民的语言，属于南岛语系大洋洲语族密克罗尼西亚语支，通行于吉尔伯特群岛的低矮珊瑚环礁。它分为北部和南部方言，布塔里塔里岛和马金岛还保留着另一种差别明显的方言。南岛语航海者从约公元前3000年起的漫长岁月里陆续定居这些环礁，约1300年又有一批萨摩亚人迁入，为语言和氏族添入波利尼西亚成分；到15世纪，北部岛屿由称为“乌埃亚”的酋长统治，南部则由名为“乌尼姆瓦内”的长老议事会管理。欧洲人的接触始于1765年，约翰·拜伦准将偶然抵达尼库瑙；1788年托马斯·吉尔伯特与约翰·马歇尔两位船长航经此地，亚当·冯·克鲁森施滕遂于1820年把这片群岛命名为吉尔伯特群岛。此后从19世纪20年代起，捕鲸船和商人常来常往，但直到19世纪30年代，基里巴斯语仍然完全是口头语言，第一批印刷词汇表还要再过多年才出现。

en: The Ijaw or Ijo languages are a cluster of nine closely related tongues of the Niger Delta, split between Eastern and Western Ijo, with Izon the largest; the varieties are not mutually intelligible. Their subject-object-verb order and lack of noun classes are unusual for Niger-Congo, leading Joseph Greenberg to treat them as an early branch and some linguists to class Ijoid as an independent family. By the fifteenth century the Ijaw were tied into delta sea routes, and eastern clans such as Bonny, Okrika and Kalabari grew into kingdoms ruled by powerful kings. Before 1699 Kalabari had become a center of the Atlantic slave trade, exchanging captives brought from the Igbo interior for European hardware, guns and gunpowder, and under Amachree I, who died around 1800, its trading houses expanded in rivalry with the neighboring delta states.
zh: 伊乔语是尼日尔河三角洲一带九种近亲语言的合称，分东伊乔语和西伊乔语两支，其中伊宗语使用最广，各变体之间彼此不能互通。它采用主宾动语序，也没有名词分类系统，这在尼日尔—刚果语系中很罕见，因此格林伯格将它视为该语系很早分出的一支，也有语言学家主张伊乔语支是独立语系。到15世纪，伊乔人已接入三角洲的海上商路，邦尼、奥克里卡和卡拉巴利等东部氏族发展为由强势国王统治的城邦。1699年以前，卡拉巴利已成为大西洋奴隶贸易的集散地，把来自内陆伊博兰的俘虏换成欧洲的金属器具、火枪和火药；在约1800年去世的阿马奇里一世治下，各大商号继续扩张，与三角洲邻邦争雄。

en: Ilocano is an Austronesian language of the Northern Luzon subgroup, native to the narrow coastal plain of northwest Luzon in the Philippines, the provinces of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur and La Union. Its name comes from the native word iluko, meaning people of the bay, and its speakers once called their tongue Samtoy, our language here. Before the Spanish arrival Ilocanos wrote in baybayin, an Indic-derived syllabary; the Ilocano edition of the Doctrina Cristiana, printed in 1621, was the first Philippine book to mark final consonants with a virama mark. Under Spanish rule the Latin alphabet and Spanish-based spelling took over, and Ilocano spread well beyond its homeland as the lingua franca of northern Luzon, used as a second language by the Cordilleran mountain peoples of the interior. In the nineteenth century Ilocano migrants settled the Cagayan Valley and parts of Mindanao, carrying the language across the archipelago.
zh: 伊洛卡诺语是南岛语系北吕宋语支的语言，故乡在菲律宾吕宋岛西北沿海的狭长平原，即北伊罗戈斯、南伊罗戈斯和拉乌尼翁一带。其名称来自本土词汇伊卢科，意为海湾之人，使用者曾把自己的语言称为萨姆托伊，意即我们这里的话。西班牙人到来之前，伊洛卡诺人使用源自印度文字系统的贝贝因音节文字；1621年印行的伊洛卡诺语版《基督教教义》，是菲律宾第一部用收音符号标记音节尾辅音的书籍。西班牙统治时期，拉丁字母和以西班牙语为基础的拼写法取而代之，伊洛卡诺语也远远走出故乡，成为北吕宋的通用语，是内陆科迪勒拉山区各族的第二语言。19世纪，伊洛卡诺移民迁入卡加延河谷和棉兰老岛部分地区，把这种语言带到菲律宾各地。

en: Inuit is the eastern branch of the Eskaleut family, a chain of closely related dialects stretching from Alaska through northern Canada and Labrador to Greenland, with Yupik its nearest relative and Aleut a more distant one. It is a polysynthetic, ergative language, building long words from roots and chains of suffixes, with subject-object-verb order and eight noun cases. Its early form was carried east by the Thule people, who spread out of Beringia across the Arctic archipelago from the twelfth century and replaced the older Dorset culture; by 1300 they had reached western Greenland, and their descendants arrived in the east as the Norse settlements there disappeared. The first word lists were made in the 1600s, Danish missionaries began grammars and dictionaries after 1700, and Paul Egede published the first Greenlandic dictionary in 1750 and the first grammar in 1760, fixing the Latin-script tradition of the Greenlandic variety.
zh: 因纽特语是爱斯基摩—阿留申语系的东支，是一串关系密切的方言，从阿拉斯加经加拿大北部、拉布拉多一直延伸到格陵兰；最近的亲属是尤皮克语，更远的亲属是阿留申语。它是多式综合的作格语言，把词根和一连串后缀拼合成很长的词，采用主宾谓语序，名词有八个格。其早期形式由图勒人带向东方：他们12世纪起从白令地区扩散到北极群岛，取代了更早的多塞特文化；1300年他们已抵达格陵兰西部，其后裔又在古斯堪的纳维亚聚落消失之际来到格陵兰东部。17世纪出现了最早的词汇记录，1700年后丹麦传教士开始编写语法和词典，保罗·埃格德于1750年出版第一部格陵兰语词典，1760年出版第一部语法书，奠定了格陵兰方言的拉丁字母书写传统。

en: Iresim, also spelled Yerisiam, is an Austronesian language of the shoreline of Cenderawasih Bay in Nabire Regency, Central Papua. It forms a small subgroup with its closest relative Yaur, and with Umar more distantly, within the Cenderawasih Bay branch that descends from the ancient seaborne Austronesian settlement of New Guinea's northern coast.
zh: 伊雷辛语又拼耶雷西亚姆语，是中巴布亚省纳比雷县极乐鸟湾沿岸的一种南岛语。它与关系最近的尧尔语组成一个小分支，与乌马尔语关系较远，同属极乐鸟湾语支——该语支源于古代南岛语族群沿海路定居新几内亚北海岸的迁徙。

en: Iroquoian is the family of polysynthetic, head-marking indigenous languages of eastern North America: its better-attested northern branches include the Six Nations tongues and Huron-Wyandot, while Cherokee forms its distant southern branch. The languages grouped here are the less well-recorded northern branches that stood outside the great confederacies. Along the St. Lawrence, Laurentian was heard in the palisaded villages of Stadacona and Hochelaga when Jacques Cartier visited in 1535 and 1536; the word canada, meaning village, passed from it into the name of the country, but by the time Champlain arrived in 1608 its people had vanished, likely destroyed or driven off by Mohawk warfare. Between lakes Ontario and Erie lived the Neutral, called Attawandaron by the Wendat, with some forty villages of farmers and deer-keepers, until Haudenosaunee attacks dispersed them in 1651. Their small kinsmen the Wenro, east of the Niagara, had already fled to the Wendat in 1638. South of Lake Erie the Erie, whose speech was said to be mutually intelligible with Huron, were broken in the mid-1650s and their people adopted into the Seneca and other nations. These tongues now survive only in fragmentary missionary word lists, above all Cartier's Laurentian vocabularies and the French Jesuit Relations.
zh: 易洛魁语是北美东部原住民的一个多式综合、以动词词头承载语法的语系：记录较多的北支包括六族诸语和休伦—怀恩多特语，切罗基语则构成它偏远的南支。这里归在一处的，是各大联盟之外、记录较少的几个北部分支。在圣劳伦斯河沿岸，雅克·卡蒂亚于1535年和1536年到访时，劳伦斯语还通行于斯塔达科纳和霍赫拉加等设有木栅的村落；意为“村庄”的“加拿大”一词便出自这种语言，后来成了国名，但到1608年尚普兰到来时，这批人已经消失，多半毁于莫霍克人的战事或被逐走。安大略湖与伊利湖之间住着中立人，休伦人称他们为阿塔万达隆人，拥有约四十个农耕和养鹿的村落，1651年在易洛魁联盟的攻击下流散。他们人口不多的近亲温罗人住在尼亚加拉河以东，已于1638年投奔休伦人。伊利湖以南的伊利人所说的话据说与休伦语可以互通，却在1650年代中期被击溃，部众被塞内卡等族收养。这些语言只零散保存在传教士的词表里，主要是卡蒂亚记下的劳伦斯语词汇和法国耶稣会士的报道。

en: Japanese is the principal language of the Japonic family, whose only other living branch is the Ryukyuan group. Its ancestor, Proto-Japonic, was carried to the islands by Yayoi-period settlers from the Korean peninsula around the fourth century BC and displaced the languages of the older Jōmon foragers. Writing arrived from the Korean kingdom of Baekje with Buddhism in the early fifth century; the oldest substantial text, the Kojiki of the early eighth century, recorded the spoken Old Japanese through man'yōgana, Chinese characters used for their sound. During the Heian period, from 794, waves of Chinese loanwords reshaped its vocabulary and phonology, while scribes simplified cursive characters into hiragana and derived katakana from character fragments, giving Japanese its mixed script of kanji and two syllabaries. Late Middle Japanese, between 1185 and 1600, absorbed the first European words, Portuguese terms such as pan for bread and tabako for tobacco, and was described by Jesuit missionaries in grammars such as the Arte da Lingoa de Iapam. From the early seventeenth century the prestige dialect shifted from the Kyoto and Kansai region toward Edo, the future Tokyo, seat of the Tokugawa shoguns; the language kept its elaborate honorifics marking the rank of speaker and listener.
zh: 日语是日琉语族的主要语言，该语族现存的另一支只有琉球语。它的祖先原始日语由弥生时代的定居者在公元前4世纪前后从朝鲜半岛带入列岛，取代了更早的绳文采集者的语言。文字随佛教于5世纪初从百济传入；现存最古老的长篇文献是8世纪初的《古事记》，借助万叶假名，即按读音借用的汉字，记录当时的古日语。794年开始的平安时代，汉语借词大批涌入，改变了日语的词汇和音系；书手又把草书汉字简化为平假名，从汉字偏旁提炼出片假名，日语由此形成汉字与两套假名并用的书写体系。1185至1600年的中世日语后期吸收了最早的欧洲借词，如来自葡萄牙语、表示面包的pan和表示烟草的tabako，耶稣会传教士还编写了《日本大文典》等语法著作加以描述。17世纪初以后，权威方言从京都所在的关西转向德川幕府驻地江户，即后来的东京；日语繁复的敬语体系则始终用以标示说话人与听者的身份高低。

en: Javanese is a Malayo-Polynesian language of the Austronesian family, the native speech of the Javanese people of central and eastern Java, whose closest relatives are Sundanese, Madurese and Balinese. Its earliest attested stage, Old Javanese or Kawi, first appears in the Sukabumi inscription of 804 from the Kediri region, carved in letters derived from the Pallava script of India. From the 700s to the 1400s Kawi served as the literary language of Java's Hindu-Buddhist courts, whose kakawin verse chronicles drew roughly a quarter of their vocabulary from Sanskrit. The founding of Majapahit in 1292 opened its final Kawi phase, which produced the Nagarakretagama of 1365, a eulogy of King Hayam Wuruk later preserved on palm leaves in Bali and Lombok after Kawi ceased to be written in Java in the early 1500s. Modern Javanese emerged later in that century as Islam took hold along the north coast: religious works were translated from Malay and the Arabic-based Pegon script was adopted. The rise of the Mataram Sultanate in the 1600s moved the literary center inland to the Surakarta and Yogyakarta courts, which fixed the written standard and its two speech levels, the everyday ngoko and the honorific krama. Javanese books were printed from the 1830s, at first in the native carakan letters, and newspapers and novels followed from the mid-1800s.
zh: 爪哇语是南岛语系马来—波利尼西亚语族的语言，为爪哇岛中东部爪哇人的母语，最近的亲属语言是巽他语、马都拉语和巴厘语。它有记载的最早阶段是古爪哇语，又称卡维语：现存最早的物证是804年谏义里地区的苏卡布米碑铭，所用文字源出印度的帕拉瓦字母。8至15世纪，卡维语是爪哇印度教—佛教宫廷的文学语言，格卡温体长诗大量借用梵语，诗中约四分之一词汇来自梵文。1292年满者伯夷建国，开启了卡维语的最后阶段，1365年赞颂国王哈奄·武禄的《爪哇史颂》即作于此时；16世纪初卡维语在爪哇本土不再通行，这些典籍靠巴厘岛和龙目岛的贝叶抄本保存下来。16世纪，随着伊斯兰教在爪哇北岸扎根，近代爪哇语兴起，宗教作品多译自马来语，还采用了阿拉伯字母的佩贡体书写。17世纪马打兰苏丹国崛起，文学中心转到内陆的梭罗和日惹宫廷，书面标准由此奠定，并形成日常的恩戈科与庄重的克拉马两种语体。19世纪30年代起，爪哇语书籍开始印行，起初仍用本土的爪哇字母，19世纪中叶以后又出现了报纸和小说。

en: Jin is the Sinitic speech of the Shanxi loess plateau, covering most of Shanxi, central Inner Mongolia and the neighboring edges of Hebei, Henan and Shaanxi, and taking its name from Jin, the ancient Spring and Autumn state of these lands. Yang Xiong's Fangyan, compiled in the Western Han, already records the northwestern dialects of Zhao and Wei in this region, and modern Jin still carries a large stock of words from the old Qin and Jin speech. Scholars trace its phonology to the northwestern pronunciation of the Tang, 618 to 907, and the Five Dynasties, 907 to 960, a link seen in the Tangut-Chinese wordbook of the Western Xia. It is the only major non-Mandarin variety of northern China: unlike the surrounding Mandarin dialects it keeps the entering tone as a distinct glottal-stop category, and builds words with rare prefixes and split-syllable forms. Long treated as a Mandarin branch for its partial mutual intelligibility with them, Jin is written in Chinese characters, with the Taiyuan dialect as its representative.
zh: 晋语是山西黄土高原上的汉语方言，分布于山西大部、内蒙古中部以及河北、河南、陕西邻接山西的边缘地带，名称取自春秋时统治这片土地的古国晋。西汉扬雄的《方言》已记载这一带“赵、魏之西北方言”，后世的晋语仍保留大量上古秦晋语的词汇。学者认为它的音韵直承唐代（618—907年）和五代（907—960年）的西北方音传统，西夏时期编成的夏汉对照词书《番汉合时掌中珠》中也能看到许多与晋语吻合的痕迹。晋语是中国北方唯一的非官话大类：与周边官话不同，它把入声作为独立调类保留，收明显的喉塞音，并有罕见的词头和分音词构词法。因与邻近官话部分相通，晋语长期被归入官话；它以汉字书写，通常以太原话为代表。

en: Jirajaran is the extinct language group of the dry hills and valleys of western Venezuela, in Falcón and Lara, whose documented members are Jirajara itself, Ayomán of the village of Siquisique and Gayón of the upper Tocuyo River, with several scarcely recorded neighbours such as Cuiba near Aricagua. The group is treated as a language isolate, for although a few words resemble the Timotean speech of the high Andes and its type recalls Chibchan, the surviving evidence is too thin to prove any relationship, and contact with neighbouring families such as Sape and Puinave accounts for part of the shared vocabulary. Its speakers were farming villagers who kept fields of maize, cotton and yucca; the Gayones of the Tocuyo valley were living in just such settlements when the Spanish reached them. The colony was planted directly on their lands: Juan de Carvajal founded El Tocuyo on the Tocuyo in 1545, and the town became capital of Venezuela Province from 1546, anchoring Spanish rule and sugar cultivation in the heart of Jirajaran country. Through the colonial centuries the old tongues retreated before Spanish into a shrinking number of villages, recorded by later scholars only in fragmentary word lists rather than connected texts.
zh: 希拉哈拉语是委内瑞拉西部法尔孔和拉腊干旱丘陵河谷地带一个已消亡的语群，有文献记录的成员包括希拉哈拉语本支、锡基西克村的阿约曼语和托库约河上游的加永语，另外还有几种记录极少的邻语，如阿里卡瓜附近的奎瓦语。该语群被视为孤立语群：虽然有少量词语与安第斯高地的蒂莫特语言相近，类型上也让人想到奇布查语，但存世证据太少，无法证实任何亲缘关系，而与萨佩语、普伊纳韦语等邻语的接触也能解释一部分共有词汇。说这些语言的人是务农的村社居民，种植玉米、棉花和木薯；西班牙人到来时，托库约河谷的加永人正生活在这样的村落里。殖民地直接建在他们的土地上：1545年胡安·德·卡瓦哈尔在托库约河畔建立埃尔托库约，这座城镇从1546年起成为委内瑞拉省首府，把西班牙统治和甘蔗种植锚定在希拉哈拉地区的腹地。整个殖民时代，古老的语言在西班牙语面前退守到越来越少的村落里，后来的学者只能从零碎的词表、而不是连贯的文本中记录它们。

en: Jurchen was the Tungusic language of the Jurchen people of eastern Manchuria and the tongue of the Jin dynasty that ruled northern China in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries; it is the direct ancestor of Manchu. After the Jurchen overthrew the Khitan Liao dynasty and founded the Jin in 1115, they at first wrote in the Khitan script. In 1119 the chancellor Wanyan Xiyin, on the orders of Emperor Aguda, devised the Jurchen large script from Khitan and Chinese models, and a second small script, promulgated by Emperor Xizong in 1138, entered official use in 1145. From 1164 the court of Emperor Shizong translated Confucian and Taoist classics and histories into the new writing, though none of those books survives; the clearest extant specimen is the bilingual Jin Victory Memorial Stele erected in 1185. The Mongol destruction of the Jin in 1234 threw the script into decline, but it was not forgotten: the Ming eunuch Yishiha set up a Jurchen inscription on the lower Amur in 1413, and Ming translation bureaus compiled Chinese-Jurchen vocabularies during the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. The spoken language meanwhile evolved in Manchuria into early Manchu, and in 1635 Hong Taiji formally renamed the Jurchen people and their language Manchu.
zh: 女真语是满洲东部女真人的满—通古斯语，也是12至13世纪统治中国北方的金朝的语言，是满语的直系祖先。女真人推翻契丹人的辽朝、于1115年建立金朝之初，仍借用契丹文书写。1119年，丞相完颜希尹奉金太祖阿骨打之命，仿照契丹文和汉字创制女真大字；金熙宗又于1138年颁行女真小字，1145年小字正式用于官方文书。1164年起，金世宗朝廷把儒道经典和史书译成女真文，但这些译本均已散佚；存世最清晰的样本是1185年所立、汉文与女真文对照的《大金得胜陀颂碑》。1234年蒙古灭金后，女真文走向衰落，却并未绝迹：1413年明朝宦官亦失哈在黑龙江下游立下女真文石碑，15至16世纪明朝的译馆还编纂了汉—女真对照词汇。口语则在满洲继续演变为早期满语，1635年皇太极正式将女真族名和语言改称为满洲。

en: Kachinic, or Jingpoish, is a cluster of Tibeto-Burman languages in the Sal branch spoken across the Kachin Hills of northern Myanmar and the adjoining parts of Yunnan in China and northeastern India, where the Assamese variety is called Singpho. Its best-known member is Jingpho, the lingua franca of the Kachin confederation and the standard language of around sixteen Kachinic varieties; another is Kado, also called Kadu, spoken in the Chindwin valley of Sagaing Region. The Kadu were the dominant people of that valley in the early second millennium until Chin and then Shan migrants moved in, while the Jingpho only pushed south of the twenty-eighth parallel in recent centuries, one tradition dating their passage through Putao to the 1600s, as the Shan states weakened. Through the early nineteenth century the Kachinic languages remained unwritten, carried by oral tradition, and highland dealings with the lowlands went on in Shan or Burmese.
zh: 克钦语又称景颇语支，是藏缅语族萨尔语群下的一群语言，通行于缅甸北部的克钦山区，以及中国云南和印度东北部的毗邻地带，在印度阿萨姆的变体称“辛颇”。其中最主要的是景颇语，它是克钦族群联盟的通用语，也是约十六种克钦语变体的标准语；另一支是卡杜语，又称卡都语，通行于实皆省的钦敦江流域。卡杜人在2千纪初期曾是该谷地的主体族群，直到钦人、其后是掸人相继迁入；景颇人则在近几个世纪才向南越过北纬二十八度，一说他们于17世纪经葡萄南下，背景是掸人诸邦的衰落。直到19世纪初，克钦语仍没有文字，靠口耳相传，山民与低地打交道时使用掸语或缅语。

en: Marshallese, self-called Kajin Majōl and sometimes known as Ebon after one of its atolls, is a Micronesian language of the Eastern Oceanic branch of Austronesian, most closely related to Gilbertese, Pohnpeian and the other Micronesian tongues. Austronesian settlers reached these low coral atolls as early as the second millennium BC, bringing coconuts, breadfruit and chickens, and their speech evolved into the language of two parallel island chains, with a western Rālik dialect and an eastern Ratak dialect matching the two chains. Its sound system is distinctive: the consonants of Proto-Micronesian split under the influence of neighbouring vowels into palatalised, velarised and rounded series, producing an unusually rich consonant inventory. The first Europeans to arrive were Spaniards, as Alonso de Salazar reached Taongi in 1526 and Álvaro de Saavedra visited Ujelang and Enewetak in 1528, after which Spanish galleons gave the islands a wide berth. European charts later named the whole group after the British captain John Marshall, who sailed through in 1788.
zh: 马绍尔语自称 Kajin Majōl，有时因埃邦环礁而被称作埃邦语，属于南岛语系东大洋语支的密克罗尼西亚语族，与吉尔伯特语、波纳佩语等密克罗尼西亚语言亲缘最近。早在公元前第二个千年，南岛语移民就抵达了这些低矮的珊瑚环礁，带来椰子、面包果和鸡；他们的语言逐渐演化为两条平行岛链上的语言，西部拉利克链通行拉利克方言，东部拉塔克链通行拉塔克方言。它的语音系统很有特点：原始密克罗尼西亚语的辅音受相邻元音影响发生分化，形成腭化、软腭化和圆唇三套对立，辅音体系格外丰富。最早到来的欧洲人是西班牙人：阿隆索·德·萨拉查于1526年抵达塔翁吉，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉于1528年访问乌杰朗和埃尼威托克，此后西班牙大帆船便绕道而行、避开这片群岛。后来欧洲海图以1788年航行至此的英国船长约翰·马绍尔之名为整个群岛命名。

en: Kalenjin is the principal Southern Nilotic language of the East African highlands, a close chain of dialects, often called Nandi-Markweta or Elgeyo in linguistic works, that includes the speech of the Nandi, Kipsigis, Keiyo, Tugen, Marakwet, Pokot, Sabaot and the hunter-gatherer Ogiek, with the Datooga of Tanzania as its nearest kin. Its speakers trace a migration from the Nile Valley and the Ethiopian highlands, Nilotic movement that gathered pace from the eleventh century as pastoral communities spread through the grasslands of what became Uganda and western Kenya. Long contact with Cushitic peoples left a deep layer of loanwords connected with cattle and social organization, together with the age-set system and circumcision rites that mark Kalenjin society. In the Kenyan Rift Valley these Southern Nilotic herders built the Elmenteitan and then the Sirikwa pastoral traditions, whose fortified homesteads, stone circles and livestock bowls dotted the plateau from Mount Elgon to the Mau forest until the Sirikwa communities were absorbed into the emerging Nandi, Kipsigis and Pokot polities. The late eighteenth century brought crisis: the great Laparanat drought of about 1785 and the long Aoyate dry period that peaked in the 1830s scattered the older Chemwal and Maliri groups, and the ensuing Iloikop wars against the Maasai redrew the pastoral map of the highlands in the years around 1800.
zh: 卡伦津语是东非高原最主要的南尼罗特语言，是一条关系紧密的方言链，语言学著作中常称南迪—马克韦塔语或埃尔盖约语，涵盖南迪人、基普西吉斯人、凯约人、图根人、马拉奎特人、波科特人、萨巴奥特人以及狩猎采集群体奥杰克人的语言，坦桑尼亚的达托加语则是它最近的亲属。其使用者的迁徙可追溯自尼罗河谷和埃塞俄比亚高原：11世纪起尼罗特人的迁徙加快，畜牧群体陆续扩散到后来的乌干达和肯尼亚西部草原。与库希特人的长期接触留下了大量与牲畜和社会组织有关的借词，也带来了塑造卡伦津社会的年龄组制度和割礼习俗。在肯尼亚裂谷地区，这些南尼罗特牧人发展出埃尔门泰塔文化和其后的西里夸畜牧传统，从埃尔贡山到马乌森林的高原上遍布设防家园、石圈和畜栏；西里夸社群后来融入新兴的南迪、基普西吉斯和波科特政体。18世纪末危机降临：约1785年的拉帕拉纳特大旱，以及在19世纪30年代达到顶峰的漫长奥亚泰干旱期，使古老的切姆瓦尔人和马里里人群离散，随后与马赛人之间的伊洛伊科普战争在1800年前后重绘了高原的牧场版图。

en: Kam, the language of the Dong people, gives its name to the Kam-Sui branch of the Kra-Dai family, which also contains Sui, Mulam and Maonan together with several smaller tongues. They are spoken mainly in eastern Guizhou, western Hunan and northern Guangxi, with a few villages across the border in northern Vietnam, and their speakers trace their descent to the Bai Yue and the Rau peoples of ancient southern China, who broke into many small chiefdoms after the Yue kingdom collapsed around the first century. Kam itself splits into a more conservative southern form and a northern form more deeply marked by Chinese; like its relatives it is strongly tonal, and centuries of contact have layered Chinese words over its vocabulary. It had no traditional script of its own, and speakers borrowed Chinese characters to note down Kam sounds when needed. The Dong appear under their present name only in Ming records after 1368, and their mountain valleys saw repeated, unsuccessful risings through the Ming and Qing dynasties, while their history was carried orally in long polyphonic songs sung without instruments.
zh: 侗语是侗族的语言，并以此为名形成壮侗语系下的侗水语支，同支还有水语、仫佬语、毛南语和若干更小的语言。它们主要通行于贵州东部、湖南西部和广西北部，越南北部也有少数村落；其先民可追溯到古代华南的百越和僚人，约在1世纪前后越人的王国解体，当地分裂为众多小酋邦。侗语本部分为保守的南部方言和受汉语影响更深的北部方言；与同支语言一样，它有复杂的声调，长期接触也使汉语借词层层叠加。侗语没有自己的传统文字，需要记录时便借用汉字标注侗语读音。侗族以今天的名称见于史籍是1368年明朝建立以后的事，整个明清两代，他们的山谷里爆发过一次又一次终归失败的起事；本民族的历史则靠无伴奏多声部的长篇大歌口头传唱下来。

en: Kamarupi is the Middle Indo-Aryan speech of ancient Kamarupa, the Brahmaputra valley kingdom whose rulers held western Assam from the fifth to the twelfth century. Indo-Aryan settlers had carried the language up the Brahmaputra by the fourth or fifth century, where it grew among Tibeto-Burman and Austroasiatic neighbours and took on an Austroasiatic substrate; when the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang visited King Bhaskaravarman in the seventh century, he already found a vernacular distinct from that of Bengal. As a Prakrit of the Magadhi group it is traced chiefly through provincial forms in the Sanskrit of Kamarupa's copper-plate inscriptions, above all the merging of ś and ṣ into s. Before 1250 this Kamarupi Prakrit was splitting into proto-Kamta and early Assamese, the parents of the later Assamese and Kamatapuri speeches, while its local alphabet became the ancestor of the medieval Assamese scripts.
zh: 迦摩缕波语是古代迦摩缕波国的中古印度—雅利安语；这个王国以布拉马普特拉河谷为中心，5至12世纪间统治着阿萨姆西部。印度—雅利安移民在4或5世纪已沿布拉马普特拉河把这种语言带到当地，它在藏缅语和南亚语邻居环绕中发展，带上了南亚语底层；7世纪中国高僧玄奘造访国王婆塞羯罗伐摩的朝廷时，已注意到当地俗语与孟加拉一带不同。作为摩揭陀俗语群的一支，它的面貌主要靠迦摩缕波铜版铭文里的梵语俗语特征推知，最显著的是咝音ś和ṣ都并入s。1250年以前，这种迦摩缕波俗语已分化为原始卡姆塔语和早期阿萨姆语，即后世阿萨姆语与卡玛塔普里诸语的前身，而它的本地字母也成为中世纪阿萨姆诸字体的源头。

en: Kambiwa, also called Cambioá, is an extinct unclassified language once spoken by the Kambiwa people of Pernambuco in north-eastern Brazil. Pressured by colonial settlers, they left their early homes around the Serra Negra, which they kept as a sacred territory, and the language is known only from short word lists showing a couple of Tupi borrowings.
zh: 坎比瓦语又称坎比奥阿语，是巴西东北部伯南布哥州坎比瓦人使用过的一种已消亡的未分类语言。在殖民定居者的压力下，他们离开了内格拉山一带的早期家园，但仍将此山视为圣地；该语言只留下简短词表，其中有个别借自图皮语的词。

en: Kanisian is the language of the Canichana people of the Bolivian Amazon, formerly spoken along the Mamoré and Machupo rivers in the lowlands of the Beni department. No link to any other language has been demonstrated, so it is usually treated as a language isolate.
zh: 卡尼西语是玻利维亚亚马逊地区卡尼西人的语言，曾通行于贝尼省低地的马莫雷河与马丘波河一带。它与其他语言没有可证实的亲缘关系，通常被视为孤立语言。

en: Kannada is a South Dravidian language, the principal speech of Karnataka in south-western India. Its history falls into Old Kannada from about 450, Middle Kannada from 1200 and Modern Kannada from 1700. Its earliest records are fifth-century inscriptions such as Halmidi, in the Kadamba script from which the Kannada alphabet descends. It was the court language of a succession of Deccan dynasties: the Kadambas, Western Gangas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Hoysalas. Old Kannada literature, mostly by Jain court poets, opened with the Kavirajamarga of about 850, a treatise on poetics and grammar, and flourished under the Rashtrakutas; Ranna compiled the first Kannada dictionary in 996, and a ninth-century palm-leaf Dhavala survives at Mudbidri. The grammar Shabdamanidarpana of about 1260 fixed Middle Kannada literary norms, used by the thirteenth-century Shaiva poets Harihara and Raghavanka for hagiographies and devotional verse. Influenced by Sanskrit and Prakrit, it splits into southern, northern, central and coastal dialects around a Mysore-Bangalore written standard.
zh: 卡纳达语是达罗毗荼语族南支的语言，是印度西南部卡纳塔克邦的主要语言，其历史分为三个阶段：约450年起的古卡纳达语、1200年起的中卡纳达语和1700年起的近代卡纳达语。现存最早的记录是5世纪的铭文，如哈尔米迪石柱铭文，所用的卡丹巴字母正是今卡纳达文字的源头。它曾是德干高原一连串王朝的宫廷语言，包括卡丹巴、西恒伽、遮娄其、罗湿陀罗拘陀和曷萨拉诸朝。古卡纳达语文学多出自耆那教宫廷诗人之手，开山之作是约850年的诗学与语法著作《诗王之路》，在罗湿陀罗拘陀朝盛极一时；诗人兰纳于996年编成第一部卡纳达语词典，穆德比德里还保存着9世纪耆那教经典《达瓦拉》的贝叶抄本。约1260年的语法书《词语明镜》确立了中卡纳达语书面语的规范，13世纪的湿婆派诗人哈里哈拉和拉加万卡即用这种语言撰写圣徒行传和虔诚诗。卡纳达语深受梵语和俗语影响，分为南、北、中、沿海四种方言，书面标准则以迈索尔和班加罗尔一带的用语为基础。

en: Kapampangan is a Central Luzon language of the Austronesian family, spoken on the central plains of Luzon in the Philippines, chiefly in the province of Pampanga and southern Tarlac; its closest relatives are the Sambalic languages of Zambales, and some Aeta groups speak it as a second language. Its name comes from pampang, meaning riverbank, and its speakers honorifically call it Amanung Sisuan, the nurtured language. Before Spanish colonization it was written in an indigenous syllabic script, and Kapampangan was already current in the wealthy Kingdom of Tondo on Manila Bay, whose rulers bore the title of lakan. Under Spanish rule the Latin alphabet took over, and the Augustinian Diego Bergano published an Arte de la lengua Pampanga in 1729 and a Vocabulario in 1732, fixing the language in print. Long contact with maritime trade and with the Spanish colony left layers of Sanskrit and Spanish loanwords, and the nineteenth century brought a literary flowering around playwrights such as Anselmo Fajardo.
zh: 邦板牙语是南岛语系中吕宋语支的语言，通行于菲律宾吕宋岛中部平原，主要在邦板牙省和打拉省南部；与它亲缘最近的是三描礼士的桑巴尔语族，一些阿埃塔群体也把它当作第二语言。其名称源自意为河岸的邦庞一词，使用者还敬称它为阿马农·西苏安，即哺育之语。西班牙殖民之前，邦板牙语用本土音节文字书写，而且早已通行于马尼拉湾畔富庶的汤都王国，该国的统治者称号为拉坎。西班牙统治时期拉丁字母取而代之，奥古斯丁会士迭戈·贝尔加尼奥于1729年出版《邦板牙语技艺》、1732年出版《邦板牙语词汇》，使这种语言有了定型的印刷文本。长期的海上贸易和殖民统治给它留下了梵语和西班牙语两层借词，19世纪又出现了以剧作家安塞尔莫·法哈多为代表的文学繁荣。

en: Karenic is a tonal branch of the Sino-Tibetan family spoken by the Karen peoples across southern and southeastern Myanmar, from the Irrawaddy delta to the hills of Kayin and Kayah states and southern Shan, with villages also across the border in western Thailand. Its three chief languages are Sgaw, Pwo and Pa'O, while Karenni, also called Kayah or Red Karen, and Kayan, the Padaung tongue, form further branches. Unusually for Sino-Tibetan, Karenic languages put the object after the verb, a subject-verb-object order usually put down to long contact with Mon and Tai speakers. Karen oral tradition traces the people to a migration from a river of sand, likely far to the north, and by the Konbaung era they were settled in the eastern hills and delta under Burmese rule, the lowland Pwo living among the Mon while Sgaw communities kept to the highlands. The languages had no script of their own until the early 1830s, when the Sgaw alphabet was created from Burmese letters as Baptist missionaries, at work among the Karen from 1830, began translating and printing in the language.
zh: 克伦语是汉藏语系下的一支声调语言，由克伦各族使用，通行于缅甸南部和东南部，从伊洛瓦底江三角洲到克伦邦、克耶邦的山地和掸邦南部，泰国西部边境也有分布。它的三大语言是斯高语、波语和巴奥语，克耶语（又称红克伦语）和克延语（巴东人的语言）则构成另外的分支。克伦语在汉藏语系中颇为特殊，采用主语—动词—宾语的语序，一般认为是长期与孟人、傣泰人接触所致。克伦人的口传记忆把祖先追溯为自北方一条“流沙河”迁徙而来；到贡榜时代，他们已定居在缅甸治下的东部山地与三角洲，低地的波人与孟人杂居，斯高人则固守高地。克伦语原本没有自己的文字，直到19世纪30年代初，浸礼会传教士自1830年起在克伦人中传教，仿照缅文创制了斯高克伦字母，开始用克伦语翻译和印行书籍。

en: Karluk is the southeastern branch of the Turkic family, taking its name from the Karluk tribal confederation whose varieties spread across Central Asia from the 5th to the 8th centuries; its chief later descendants are Uzbek and Uyghur. Its first literary form was Karakhanid, the first Islamic Turkic literary language, written in Arabic script from the 1000s in the Kara-Khanid Khanate and exemplified by Yusuf Khass Hajib's Kutadgu Bilig and Mahmud al-Kashgari's Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk, as Arabic and Persian loanwords settled into its Old Turkic stock. From Karakhanid came Khorezmian Turkic, the literary language of the Golden Horde in the 1200s and 1300s, laced with local Oghuz and Kipchak words, and it in turn gave way to Chagatai, the shared Turkic literary tongue of the Chagatai, Timurid and Mughal realms, which carried Karluk speech in administration and letters from Kashgar to the Volga.
zh: 葛逻禄语是突厥语族的东南语支，得名于5至8世纪活跃于中亚的葛逻禄部落联盟，其后来的两大后裔是乌兹别克语和维吾尔语。它最早的文学形式是喀喇汗语，即第一种伊斯兰突厥文学语言，11世纪起在喀喇汗汗国用阿拉伯字母书写，代表作有优素福·哈斯·哈吉甫的《福乐智慧》和马哈茂德·喀什噶里的《突厥语大词典》，阿拉伯语和波斯语借词也由此渗入古突厥语根基。喀喇汗语又演化为花剌子模突厥语，即13至14世纪金帐汗国的文学语言，吸收了当地乌古斯和钦察词汇；花剌子模突厥语随后让位于察合台语，后者成为察合台汗国、帖木儿帝国和莫卧儿帝国通用的突厥文学语言，使葛逻禄语在行政和文书领域从喀什噶尔一直通行到伏尔加河流域。

en: Kashmiri, called Koshur by its speakers, is the chief language of the Kashmir Valley and the largest member of the Dardic group, a geographical cluster of northwestern Indo-Aryan hill languages spread across the Hindu Kush, from the Shina and Kohistani tongues of the Indus gorges to Khowar in Chitral and the Pashayi of eastern Afghanistan. These isolated mountain speeches preserve archaic Old Indo-Aryan features lost elsewhere, such as three sibilants, and the extinct Gandhari language of ancient Gandhara was of the same type; the Nuristani languages, once bundled with them, are now classed as a separate branch. Kashmiri itself took shape as it emerged from Apabhramsha Prakrit, and its first literary monuments are the vakhs, short mystical verses of the Shaivite poet Lal Ded, who lived from about 1320 to 1392. From the 8th century it was written in the Sharada script, but from the 14th century Persian served as the court language under the Muslim sultans, heavily enriching its vocabulary, and the Perso-Arabic script gradually joined Sharada as a literary hand. Unusually for Indo-Aryan, Kashmiri has a verb-second word order.
zh: 克什米尔语的母语者称之为科舒尔语，是克什米尔谷地的主要语言，也是达尔德语支中最大的一支。达尔德诸语是印度—雅利安语支最西北端的山地语言群，按地理而非亲缘划分，沿兴都库什山分布，从印度河峡谷的希纳语、科希斯坦诸语，到奇特拉勒的科瓦尔语和阿富汗东部的帕沙伊语都在其中。这些闭塞的山区语言保留了三咝音等古印度—雅利安语在别处已经消失的古老特征，古代犍陀罗地区已消亡的犍陀罗语也属同一类型；曾被归入其中的努里斯坦诸语则被单列为独立语支。克什米尔语本身在阿帕布拉姆沙俗语的基础上成形，最早的文学作品是湿婆派女诗人拉尔·德德（约1320—1392年）的短篇神秘诗瓦赫。它从8世纪起使用沙拉达字母书写，但14世纪穆斯林苏丹立国后波斯语成为宫廷语言，大量词汇进入克什米尔语，波斯—阿拉伯字体也逐渐与沙拉达字母并行。克什米尔语采用动词第二位语序，这在印度—雅利安诸语中颇为少见。

en: Katuic is a branch of around fifteen Austroasiatic languages straddling the middle Mekong region, spoken in eastern Thailand, southern and central Laos, north-central Cambodia and the Annamite hills of Vietnam. Its western languages, Kuy and Bru, have the most speakers; smaller branches comprise Ta'Oi, Pacoh and the namesake Katu group, judged the most conservative of the family. The Bru, whose name means people of the woods, hold the Annamite highlands and trace ties to the Khmer kingdom of Angkor at its height between the 800s and the 1200s, before the lowland valleys passed to Lao and Siamese principalities. The Kuy are regarded as older inhabitants still of the country between the Mun River and the Dangrek Mountains; their Tai exonym Suay means tribute-payers, and the elephant Kuy of Surin were long famed as catchers and trainers of wild elephants for lowland courts. Within this period the Katuic languages remained unwritten, transmitted orally in swidden-farming villages, while writing and religion reached them through the Lao, Thai or Khmer of the plains.
zh: 戈都语是南亚语系的一支，包含约十五种语言，分布在湄公河中游一带，横跨泰国东部、老挝南部和中部、柬埔寨中北部以及越南的长山山区。西支的归语和布鲁语使用人数最多，其余小支包括塔奥伊语、巴戈语，以及得名来源、也被认为是该语族中最保守的戈都语。布鲁人其名意为“林中之人”，居于长山高地，其先世可追溯到9世纪至13世纪鼎盛时期的吴哥高棉王国，后来低地河谷相继落入老挝和暹罗诸邦之手。归人则被认为是蒙河与扁担山脉之间更古老的居民，傣泰语称他们为“索伊”，意为纳贡者；素林的“象夫归人”自古以捕捉和驯练野象、供应低地宫廷而闻名。在这一时期，戈都语始终没有文字，靠轮垦村落里的口耳相传，文字与信仰则经平原上的老挝语、泰语或高棉语传入。

en: Kaulong, also called Pasismanua, is an Oceanic Austronesian language of the island of New Britain in Papua New Guinea, spoken by swidden farmers in the southwest hinterlands of Kandrian District in West New Britain Province. Within Oceanic it belongs to the Pasismanua linkage of the Ngero–Vitiaz branch, alongside Aigon, Miu, Karore and Sengseng.
zh: 考隆语又名帕西斯马努阿语，是巴布亚新几内亚新不列颠岛的一种泛太平洋语族南岛语，由西新不列颠省坎德里安区西南部内陆的游耕农人使用。在泛太平洋语族中，它与艾贡语、米乌语、卡罗雷语和森森语同属恩杰罗—维亚茨分支下的帕西斯马努阿语链。

en: Kavango denotes the cluster of Bantu languages spoken along the Kavango River on the Namibia-Angola border, together with their close Southwest Bantu kin spread across the dry plains of northern Namibia and southern Angola. The riverine Kavango varieties, Kwangali, Mbunza, Shambyu, Gciriku and Mbukushu, each belong to one of the five matrilineal Kavango kingdoms, with RuKwangali the most widely used. Their relatives to the west and south include the Ovambo dialects, among them Kwanyama and Ndonga, the Herero language of the cattle-keeping Ovaherero, and Nyaneka and Umbundu farther into Angola. Bantu farmers and herders entered this region from the northeast: Ovambo groups began settling near the Angola-Namibia border around the 1300s and pushed farther south during the 1600s. Before the 1800s these peoples kept largely to themselves, untouched by the caravan trade reaching other parts of southern Africa.
zh: 卡万戈语指通行于纳米比亚与安哥拉边境卡万戈河沿岸的一组班图语言，以及它们在纳米比亚北部、安哥拉南部干旱平原上的西南班图近亲。沿河的卡万戈分支有克万加利、姆本扎、尚比乌、格西里库和姆布库舒五种，分别对应五个母系传承的卡万戈王国，其中鲁克万加利语使用最广。它们在西面和南面的亲属语言包括奥万博诸方言，其中有宽亚马语和恩东加语；还有牧牛的赫雷罗人所说的赫雷罗语，以及更深入安哥拉境内的尼亚内卡语和翁本杜语。班图农耕者和牧人从东北方进入这一地区：奥万博诸部在1300年前后开始定居于安哥拉与纳米比亚边境一带，1600年代又继续向南推进。在1800年代以前，这些族群大体与世隔绝，未曾受到波及南部非洲其他地区的商队贸易影响。

en: Kavieng corresponds above all to Tigak, also called Omo, the Oceanic language whose territory takes in the town of Kavieng on Balgai Bay at the northern tip of New Ireland, in the Bismarck Archipelago of present-day Papua New Guinea. Tigak belongs to the Meso-Melanesian linkage of the Oceanic branch of Austronesian, alongside the neighboring Nalik, Kara and Notsi tongues of the same district, while inland the isolate Kuot is the island's only non-Austronesian language. The first Austronesian speakers reached the Bismarcks with the Lapita seafarers roughly three thousand years ago, and their speech gradually developed into the local Oceanic languages. The Dutch navigators Jacob Le Maire and Willem Schouten made the first recorded European landfall on New Ireland in 1616, and William Dampier established that it was a separate island in 1700; from 1799 whaling ships began calling regularly for water and provisions, drawing the northern coast into wider Pacific contacts.
zh: 卡维恩语主要对应蒂加克语（又称奥莫语），这是一种大洋洲语言，通行范围包括今巴布亚新几内亚俾斯麦群岛新爱尔兰岛北端巴尔盖湾畔的卡维恩镇。蒂加克语属于南岛语系大洋洲语族的中美拉尼西亚语链，与同一地区相邻的纳利克语、卡拉语、诺齐语同属一支，而内陆的库奥特语是全岛唯一的非南岛孤立语言。约三千年前，拉皮塔航海者把最早的南岛语带到俾斯麦群岛，这些语言逐渐演化为当地的大洋洲语。1616年，荷兰航海家雅各布·勒梅尔和威廉·斯考滕完成了有记载以来欧洲人对新爱尔兰岛的首次登陆；1700年，威廉·丹皮尔确认它是一座独立岛屿。1799年起，捕鲸船开始定期靠岸补给淡水和给养，北海岸由此被纳入更广阔的太平洋交往网络。

en: Kawesqar, also called Alacaluf, is the language of the Kawesqar, a canoe-nomad people of the fjords and channels of western Patagonia, formerly heard from the Gulf of Penas to the waters south of the Strait of Magellan. It is the chief surviving member of the small Alacalufan family, whose northern and southern varieties were known as Aksana and Hekaine. The language had no writing of its own, and its first recorded vocabulary was compiled in 1698 by the French adventurer Jean de la Guilbaudiere; more than fifteen word lists followed from expeditions along the Chilean coast. From the seventeenth century Jesuits based on Chiloe sailed into the channels to gather the canoe peoples into their missions, and in the 1760s a grammar of the speech of the Calen and Taijataf groups was being written at the Cailin mission, only to be lost when the missionary carrying it drowned on a voyage through the Patagonian channels.
zh: 卡韦斯卡尔语又称阿拉卡卢夫语，是西巴塔哥尼亚峡湾与水道间以独木舟游猎的卡韦斯卡尔人的语言，通行范围曾从佩尼亚斯湾一直延伸到麦哲伦海峡以南海域。它是小小的阿拉卡卢夫语系中留存下来的主要语言，该语系分北方的阿克萨纳和南方的海凯内两支。这种语言没有自己的文字，现存最早的词汇表由法国冒险家让·德·拉·吉博迪埃于1698年记录，此后沿智利海岸的历次考察又留下了十五份以上的词表。17世纪起，驻奇洛埃岛的耶稣会士乘船进入水道，试图把操舟民族迁入传教团；18世纪60年代，凯林传教团曾编写一部卡伦人和塔哈塔费人语言的语法，但携带稿件的传教士在穿行巴塔哥尼亚水道时溺水，书稿也就此遗失。

en: Kayagar is the name given to a small group of closely related Trans–New Guinea languages spoken around the Cook River in what is now South Papua province of Indonesia. Besides Kayagar itself, the group comprises Atohwaim, Tamagario and the Gondu River and Yogo varieties, all recorded only in the twentieth century by missionaries and linguists.
zh: 卡亚加尔语是对一组关系紧密的跨新几内亚语系语言的称呼，通行于今印度尼西亚南巴布亚省库克河一带。除卡亚加尔语本支外，该语群还包括阿托赫瓦伊姆语、塔马加里奥语以及贡杜河语、约戈语等变体，它们都是20世纪才由传教士和语言学者记录下来的。

en: Kayambi was the pre-Inca language of the Kayambi people of the northern Ecuadorian highlands, around the Cayambe volcano north of Quito, who formed a confederation with the neighbouring Caranqui. It is known almost only from place names ending in -bi, and like Caranqui it may have belonged to the Barbacoan family, though the evidence is inconclusive. From about 1500 the confederation, led in war by the Cochasquí ruler Quilago, held out for some twenty years against the armies of Huayna Capac before defeat at the lake of Yawarkucha ended its independence. The Incas then settled Quechua-speaking colonists in the region and the Kayambi adopted Kichwa; their old tongue, like Caranqui, is thought to have died out during the eighteenth century.
zh: 卡扬比语是厄瓜多尔北部高原卡扬比人的前印加语言，分布在基多以北的卡扬贝火山一带；卡扬比人与邻近的卡兰基人结成了联盟。它几乎只留下一批以“比”收尾的地名，和卡兰基语一样可能属于巴尔巴科亚语系，但证据并不充分。约1500年起，这个联盟在科查斯基统治者基拉戈的带领下与瓦伊纳·卡帕克的大军抗衡了约二十年，最终在亚瓦尔库查湖畔战败，丧失独立。印加人随后把讲克丘亚语的殖民者迁入此地，卡扬比人改说基奇瓦语；他们的旧语言与卡兰基语一样，一般认为在18世纪间消亡。

en: Kayanic, more fully the Kayan-Murik languages, is the Malayo-Polynesian group spoken by the upriver Dayak peoples of the Borneo interior: the various Kayan dialects, the closely related Bahau and the Murik. Its speakers trace their homeland to the upper Kayan, middle Kapuas and Mahakam rivers of North Kalimantan, the Apo Kayan plateau country that the Kayan share with the Kenyah; over the centuries they spread into Sarawak, settling the Baram, Bintulu and Rajang river basins as part of the Orang Ulu, or upriver people, where their expansion collided with Iban groups moving in the same period. They lived by shifting upland-rice cultivation, built longhouses, and were feared headhunters whose warriors held feasts of collected heads, while their smiths traded forged swords and their singers preserved history in the sung Tekna' epics. In the 1600s the Kayan sub-group Uma Apan pushed into eastern Borneo, adopted Islam and gave rise to the Bulungan people and their sultanate.
zh: 卡扬语全称卡扬—穆里克语，是婆罗洲内陆上游达雅各族使用的马来—波利尼西亚语，包括多种卡扬方言以及关系密切的巴豪语和穆里克语。使用者把祖地追溯到北加里曼丹的卡扬河上游、卡普阿斯河与马哈坎河中游一带，即卡扬人与肯雅人共居的阿波卡扬高原；几个世纪里他们迁入沙捞越，在峇南河、民都鲁河和拉让江流域定居，成为乌鲁人（上游之人）的一部分，迁徙途中还与同期扩张的伊班人发生冲突。他们经营山地稻游耕、居住长屋，是令人畏惧的猎头者，武士要举行猎头宴，铁匠打造的剑用于贸易，歌者则以歌唱史诗《特纳》传承历史。17世纪，卡扬人的乌马阿潘支系深入婆罗洲东部并改宗伊斯兰教，形成布隆岸人和布隆岸苏丹国。

en: Kei, called Veveu Evav by its speakers, is an Austronesian language of the Kei Islands in the southeastern Moluccas, spoken in more than two hundred villages across Kei Besar, Kei Kecil and their surrounding islets. Within the Central Malayo-Polynesian languages it belongs to the small Kei–Tanimbar group, in the Kei–Fordata branch; the same wider grouping also includes Irarutu on the Bomberai Peninsula of New Guinea. Kei serves as the lingua franca of the archipelago, used alongside Kur on Kur Island and the Banda speech brought by refugees from the Banda Islands after the Dutch conquest of 1621. Every island and village, known locally as an ohoi, has its own dialect, and a speaker's dialect marks their place of origin; the Kei Kecil dialect carries the most prestige. The islands' customary order rests on about two dozen rat, or rajas, and the law code Larvul Ngabal, which local tradition traces to the royal princess Dit Sakmas and to ancestors said to have come from Bali in the fourteenth-century heyday of Majapahit, alongside migrants from Seram, Gorom, Ternate and Jailolo. Kei had no indigenous writing tradition, and it was Dutch Catholic missionaries who first recorded the language in a Roman-based orthography during the colonial period. The name Kei itself is often said to derive from the Portuguese word kayos, stone, after the rocky atolls navigators encountered in the sixteenth century.
zh: 凯语在母语者口中称 Veveu Evav，是摩鹿加东南部卡伊群岛的南岛语，通行于大卡伊岛、小卡伊岛及周边小岛的两百多个村庄。在中马来-波利尼西亚语族内，它属于小小的凯-塔宁巴尔语群的凯-福尔达塔语支；同一更大语群还包括新几内亚邦巴赖半岛的伊拉图图语。凯语是整个群岛的通用语，与库尔岛的库尔语、以及1621年荷兰征服班达群岛后难民带来的班达语并存。每个岛屿和村庄（当地称 ohoi）都有自己的方言，说话者的方言即标明其出身，其中以小卡伊岛方言声望最高。群岛的传统秩序依靠二十多位拉特（即拉者）和习惯法《拉尔武尔·恩加巴尔法》维系；当地传说这部法典出自王族公主蒂特·萨克马斯，而岛民的祖先在14世纪满者伯夷强盛时期自巴厘岛迁来，另有来自斯兰岛、戈龙岛、特尔纳特和贾伊洛洛的移民。凯语没有本土文字传统，殖民时期是荷兰天主教传教士最早用拉丁字母记录了这种语言。“凯”这个名称通常认为源自葡萄牙语 kayos（石头），因16世纪航海者见到的多石环礁而得名。

en: Kejia, or Hakka, is the language of the Hakka people, the guest families whose name records their descent from northern migrants, spread across the hills of northeastern Guangdong, southern Jiangxi and southwestern Fujian, with further communities in Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan and Sichuan. Their ancestors left the Central Plains of Henan and Shaanxi in waves of flight that began with the collapse of the Western Jin around 311, and the speech they carried south keeps archaic features lost in Mandarin, above all the checked finals -p, -t and -k. Linguists place its phonological formation in the Song, 960 to 1279, when Gan-speaking settlers pushed into the She mountains of western Fujian and absorbed much of the native She population; by the middle Ming it had become a distinct branch, the closest sister of Gan, with a possible Hmong-Mien substrate. The Meixian dialect of Guangdong serves as its standard, and Hakka is written in Chinese characters.
zh: 客家话是客家民系的母语，“客家”之名记下了他们北人南迁的来历；它主要分布在广东东北部、江西南部和福建西南部的丘陵山区，在广西、海南、湖南、四川也有聚居点。客家人的祖先原居河南、陕西一带的中原，自311年前后西晋灭亡之际起，几度在战乱中举族南迁，因此客家话保留了官话已经失去的古音，尤其是-p、-t、-k三套入声韵尾。学者认为其音韵体系在宋代（960—1279年）成形：当时讲赣语东支的汉人进入闽西畲人的山区垦殖，大量畲人转而使用这种语言；到明代中叶，客家话已发展为独立的一支，与赣语关系最近，底层中可能含有苗瑶语成分。广东梅县话是客家话的代表方言，客家话使用汉字书写。

en: Keres, or Keresan, is the language of the seven Keres pueblos of New Mexico and is now treated as a language isolate, since earlier attempts to attach it to Hokan–Siouan or other large groupings have not been substantiated. Its dialects fall into an Eastern group at Cochiti, San Felipe, Kewa, Zia and Santa Ana and a Western group at Acoma and Laguna, the two differing enough to be counted as separate languages by some scholars. Biological evidence and Cochiti oral tradition suggest the Keres entered the Rio Grande drainage from the west in the early 1300s, after the El Morro valley was abandoned. Coronado's lieutenant Hernando de Alvarado visited cliff-top Acoma in 1540. When Juan de Oñate colonized New Mexico, Acoma rose against the intruders and in 1599 Spanish troops sacked the pueblo in the Acoma Massacre; missions and saints' names followed, and in 1680 the Keres pueblos joined the Pueblo Revolt.
zh: 凯雷斯语又称凯雷桑语，是新墨西哥七个凯雷斯普韦布洛的语言，已被划为孤立语言——早先把它并入霍坎－苏语等大语系的尝试都未能证实。它的方言分为东、西两组：东部通行于科奇蒂、圣费利佩、凯瓦、齐亚和圣安娜，西部通行于阿科马和拉古纳，两组差别显著，有些学者把它们算作两门独立的语言。体质人类学证据和科奇蒂人的口传都表明，凯雷斯人在14世纪初埃尔莫罗河谷荒废之后，自西边迁入里奥格兰德河流域。1540年，科罗纳多的副将埃尔南多·德·阿尔瓦拉多造访了崖顶之上的阿科马。胡安·德·奥尼亚特征服新墨西哥时，阿科马人奋起反抗，1599年西班牙军队在阿科马大屠杀中洗劫了这座普韦布洛；此后传教站和圣徒地名相继而来，1680年各凯雷斯普韦布洛又投身普韦布洛起义。

en: Khasi is the principal language of the Khasic branch of Austroasiatic, an isolated relative of the Munda tongues rather than one of them, spoken by the Khasi people of the Shillong Plateau in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya, with smaller communities in Assam and Bangladesh. Its sister speeches include Pnar, War and Lyngngam, and together they form an ancient Austroasiatic enclave in north-eastern India, preserved as Indo-Aryan and Sino-Tibetan languages spread around them. Khasi makes wide use of prefixes and infixes, places classifiers between numerals and nouns, and divides its nouns into four genders. The Khasi were organized into small matrilineal hill states and long kept their speech without a script; their polities fought British expansion under the leader Tirot Sing in the war of 1829 to 1833.
zh: 卡西语是南亚语系卡西语支的主要语言，与蒙达诸语是远亲而非同支，由梅加拉亚邦西隆高原卡西丘陵、贾因蒂亚丘陵的卡西人使用，阿萨姆邦和孟加拉国也有小型社群。它的姊妹语言包括普纳尔语、瓦尔语和林甘语，共同构成印度东北部一块古老的南亚语飞地，在印度—雅利安语和汉藏语四向扩张中保留下来。卡西语大量使用前缀和中缀，数词与名词之间加量词，名词分四个性。卡西人组成若干母系传承的山地小邦，长期没有文字；各邦在领袖蒂罗特·辛格率领下，于1829—1833年的战争中抵抗英国扩张。

en: Khmer is the principal Austroasiatic language of mainland Southeast Asia, native to the Cambodian plain and also spoken by the Khmer Krom of the Mekong delta and the Northern Khmer of the Thai Khorat plateau. Unlike its tonal neighbours Thai, Lao and Vietnamese, it is a non-tonal, analytic language with subject-verb-object order, its royal and religious vocabulary steeped in Sanskrit and Pali. It was first written before the seventh century in an abugida derived from the Pallava letters of southern India; the Thai and Lao scripts later grew out of the Khmer system. Pre-Angkorian Old Khmer of 600 to 800 and the Angkorian speech of the ninth to thirteenth centuries carried the inscriptions of Chenla and Angkor across the empire, and the Khmer Ramayana, the Reamker, was already known from a seventh-century inscription, though its surviving poem is sixteenth-century work. After Angkor's fall in the early 1400s, Middle Khmer of the fourteenth to eighteenth centuries absorbed Thai literary loans; Ayutthayan conquests under Naresuan isolated the northern dialects, while in the 1600s a Khmer army retook Stung Treng, whose Khmer Khe speech still keeps archaic features. By the early nineteenth century the language stood on the threshold of its modern standard form.
zh: 高棉语是东南亚大陆最主要的南亚语系语言，本土在柬埔寨平原，湄公河三角洲的下高棉人和泰国呵叻高原的北高棉人也说这种语言。与泰语、老挝语、越南语这些声调语言不同，高棉语无声调，属分析语，采用主语—动词—宾语语序，王室和宗教词汇中有大量梵语和巴利语成分。早在7世纪以前，高棉人便用一种源自南印度帕拉瓦字母的拼音文字刻石立碑，泰文和老挝文后来正是在高棉文字体系的基础上发展而来。600年至800年的前吴哥古高棉语，以及9世纪至13世纪的吴哥时期高棉语，承载了真腊和吴哥帝国的碑铭；高棉版《罗摩衍那》史诗《林给》在7世纪的碑刻中已有记载，现存诗稿则成于16世纪。15世纪初吴哥陷落之后，14至18世纪的中古高棉语吸收了泰语文学借词；纳黎萱麾下阿瑜陀耶的征服使北方方言与本土日渐隔绝，而17世纪高棉军队收复上丁地区，当地的高棉赫方言仍保留着古貌。到19世纪初，高棉语已站在后世标准语成型的前夜。

en: Khmu is the chief language of the Khmuic branch of the Austroasiatic family, spoken mainly across the hills of northern Laos and in adjoining parts of Vietnam, Thailand and present-day Yunnan in China. The Khmuic peoples are thought to descend from one of the first populations to settle northern Indochina; they once held the lowlands of what became Laos and northern Thailand until Mon and Khmer empires and then the incoming Tai peoples absorbed them or drove them into mountain refuges. When Fa Ngum founded the Tai-Lao kingdom of Lan Xang in 1353, the Khmu were already highland swidden farmers known in Lao as the Lao Theung. Khmu has no standard variety: its western dialects contrast breathy and tense registers, in one dialect already turning into tones, while eastern dialects keep a three-way contrast of initial consonants. Long unwritten, the language was carried chiefly by oral story-telling, while dealings with lowland principalities went on in Lao.
zh: 克木语是南亚语系克木语支的代表语言，主要通行于老挝北部山区，以及越南、泰国和中国云南的毗邻地带。克木族群被认为是最早定居印度支那北部的人群之一，曾居住在后来成为老挝和泰国北部的低地，先后被孟人、高棉人的政权和迁入的傣泰人同化或逼入山区。1353年法昂建立傣族人的澜沧王国时，克木人已是从事轮垦农业的山民，在老挝语中被称为“老听人”。克木语没有标准语：西部方言以气声和紧嗓两种音区区别词义，其中一种方言的音区已开始演变为声调；东部方言则保留三套声母对立。克木语长期没有文字，主要靠口述故事传承，与低地城邦打交道时则使用老挝语。

en: Khoe is the largest of the non-Bantu language families native to southern Africa, marked, like its neighbours, by click consonants. It has two branches: Khoekhoe, the speech of the Nama and Damara of Namibia and the Cape, and Tshu–Khwe, spoken by the peoples of the Kalahari in Botswana. Speakers of the ancestral Khoe–Kwadi language entered what is now Botswana from the north-east about two thousand years ago, keeping sheep and cattle; the south-western branch that retained pastoralism became the Khoekhoe, while groups left in the drying Kalahari turned to hunting and gathering. The Nama spread through Namibia from the sixteenth century, absorbing client peoples such as the Damara. Portuguese crews first met Khoekhoe clans at the Cape in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, and in 1510 the !Uriǁ'aekua defeated a Portuguese landing party at the Salt River and killed the viceroy Francisco de Almeida. After the Dutch settlement at the Cape, Cape Khoe speech steadily lost ground to Afrikaans, while in the 1770s clans such as the Orlam Afrikaners began trekking north into Namibia, carrying Nama beyond the Orange River.
zh: 科伊语是南部非洲本土非班图语族中最大的一支，和邻近语言一样以吸气音为特征。它分为两支：纳米比亚和开普地区纳马人、达马拉人使用的科伊科伊语，以及博茨瓦纳卡拉哈里沙漠各族使用的丘—科韦语。约两千年前，说原始科伊—夸迪语的族群从东北方向进入今博茨瓦纳，饲养绵羊和牛；保留游牧生活的西南支成为科伊科伊人，留在日益干旱的卡拉哈里的群体则转向狩猎采集。纳马人自16世纪起在纳米比亚扩张，吸纳了达马拉等依附族群。葡萄牙船员在15至16世纪最早于开普接触科伊科伊诸部，1510年，乌里奎夸人在盐河击败一支葡萄牙登陆队，击杀了总督弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达。荷兰人在开普定居后，开普的科伊语逐渐被南非荷兰语排挤；到18世纪70年代，奥拉姆·阿非利卡等部族开始向北迁徙进入纳米比亚，把纳马语带到奥兰治河以北。

en: Kilivila, also called Kiriwina, is an Oceanic language of the Papuan Tip cluster, spoken by the Trobriand islanders of the Trobriand Islands in the Solomon Sea off the eastern tip of New Guinea. It belongs to the Kilivila–Misima linkage, which also covers the speech of the nearby Marshall Bennett Islands and Misima, and its several dialects correspond to the different tribes of the main island. The language is noted for an elaborate system of noun classification, while its speakers are organized in matrilineal clans that hold land in common and take part in the kula, a far-flung circuit of shell exchange carried out in large seagoing canoes. The islands were unknown to Europeans until 1793, when a French expedition charted them and named the group after its officer Denis de Trobriand.
zh: 基利维拉语又称基里维纳语，是泛太平洋语系巴布亚尖端语群的一支大洋语，由新几内亚东端外海所罗门海中特罗布里恩群岛的岛民使用。它属于基利维拉—米西马语链，邻近的马歇尔贝内特群岛和米西马岛的语言也在这一语链中；其多种方言与主岛上不同的部落相对应。这种语言以繁复的名词分类体系著称，而说它的岛民按母系氏族组织、共同占有土地，并参与库拉圈——一种乘坐大型远洋独木舟、在岛屿之间巡回交换贝壳饰品的贸易网络。欧洲人原本不知道这些岛屿，直到1793年一支法国探险队测绘了此地，并以其军官德·特罗布里昂的名字为群岛命名。

en: The Kipchak or Northwestern Turkic languages descend from the speech of the Kipchak and Cuman nomads who dominated the Pontic-Caspian steppe between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries; their medieval form is recorded in the Codex Cumanicus of 1303. After the Mongol conquest of Cumania the language became the Turkic speech of the Golden Horde, also called the Kipchak Khanate, whose ruler Özbeg Khan adopted Islam during his reign from 1312 to 1341. After Timur's invasion of 1396 the Horde fragmented, and during the fifteenth century its lands passed to successor states including the Crimean Khanate and the Kazakh Khanate and other Turkic khanates of the Volga and the steppe, each with its own Kipchak dialect. The rump Great Horde collapsed in 1502, the literary Cuman of Hungary died out in the early eighteenth century, and the Crimean Khanate was annexed by Russia in 1783. From these forms descend the Tatar, Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Nogai languages spoken across the Volga region, the Caucasus and Central Asia.
zh: 钦察语又称西北突厥语，源自11至13世纪称雄黑海—里海草原的钦察人和库曼游牧民的语言，其中古形态见于1303年的《库曼语汇编》。蒙古征服库曼尼亚后，这门语言成为金帐汗国（又称钦察汗国）的突厥语，月即别汗在1312—1341年在位期间皈依伊斯兰教。1396年帖木儿入侵后，金帐汗国走向瓦解，15世纪时其领土分属克里米亚汗国、哈萨克汗国以及伏尔加河流域和草原上的其他突厥汗国，各有自己的钦察方言。残余的大帐汗国于1502年灭亡，匈牙利的书面库曼语在18世纪初绝迹，克里米亚汗国则于1783年被俄罗斯吞并。鞑靼语、巴什基尔语、哈萨克语、吉尔吉斯语和诺盖语便是由这些形态发展而来，分布在伏尔加河流域、高加索和中亚一带。

en: Kiwaian is a close-knit language family of southern Papua New Guinea, spoken in the mangrove deltas of the Fly and Bamu rivers and along the neighbouring coast of the Gulf of Papua, with Kiwai Island and the trading settlement of Daru at its heart. Its half-dozen members, among them Kiwai, Bamu–Gama, Kerewo–Morigi and Waboda, differ little enough to read as dialects of one another. Although their grammar has diverged sharply from neighbouring Trans–New Guinea speech, notably in pronouns that distinguish singular, dual, trial and plural, a stock of shared basic words leads most classifiers to place Kiwaian within that wider family. The coastal Kiwai were noted seafarers, whose canoes carried their language across the delta and into the Torres Strait, where islanders and Papuan communities had traded for millennia. The first European ships reached those waters in 1606, when the Spanish navigator Luís Vaz de Torres sailed along the southern coast of New Guinea; the strait between New Guinea and Australia was later named after him.
zh: 基万语是巴布亚新几内亚南部一个关系紧密的语族，通行于弗莱河与巴穆河的红树林三角洲及邻近的巴布亚湾沿岸，核心地带是基万岛和贸易聚落达鲁。它包含基万语、巴穆—加马语、克雷沃—莫里吉语、瓦博达语等约六种语言，彼此差异很小，可视作方言。虽然它的语法与邻近的跨新几内亚语言分化明显，代词尤其区分单数、双数、三数和复数，但一批共有的基础词汇使多数分类学者仍把基万语归入跨新几内亚语系这个更大的群体。沿海的基万人以航海著称，独木舟把他们的语言带到三角洲各处和托雷斯海峡，海峡岛民与巴布亚社群之间的贸易已有数千年历史。1606年，西班牙航海家路易斯·瓦斯·德·托雷斯沿新几内亚南海岸航行，欧洲船只首次进入这片水域，新几内亚与澳大利亚之间的海峡后来便以他的名字命名为托雷斯海峡。

en: Koiari, also called Koiali or Grass Koiari, is a Papuan language of southeastern New Guinea, spoken in the hinterland of Port Moresby and along the Hunter and Musgrave rivers. It belongs to the Koiarian family, a small group within the Southeast Papuan branch of the Trans–New Guinea languages, spread across the Bird's Tail peninsula. The family divides into a Koiaric branch, comprising Grass Koiari and the closely related Mountain Koiari and Koitabu, and a Baraic branch on the Managalas Plateau, including Barai, Ese, also called Managalasi, and Ömie. Koiari itself has western and eastern dialect groups that differ only in minor points of phonology and vocabulary, and its speakers live interspersed with Motu and Koita villages near the harbour of Port Moresby.
