en: Shu, or Ba-Shu Chinese, was the Chinese speech of the Sichuan Basin, in what is now Sichuan and Chongqing, from the Han dynasty to the Mongol conquest. It was already noted as a distinct regional language in the Fangyan, the dictionary of dialects compiled in the Western Han, and it represented one of the earliest branches to split from Old Chinese: like Min it did not descend from Middle Chinese, and its divergence was even earlier than that of Min. In 1236 the Mongols sacked Chengdu, and by the final Song defeat of 1279 the basin had been depopulated and the old language's transmission was broken. Under the following Ming and Qing dynasties, settlers from Huguang and other provinces brought the speech that developed into Southwestern Mandarin, and the ancient Shu dialect died out, although the Minjiang dialects of southern Sichuan kept part of its vocabulary and phonology.
zh: 蜀语又称巴蜀语，是汉代至元代通行于巴蜀地区（今中国四川、重庆一带）的汉语分支。早在西汉扬雄所撰的《方言》中，蜀地口语就被记为独特的方言；它是从上古汉语最早分化出的支系之一，与闽语一样不源自中古汉语，且分化时间比闽语更早。1236年蒙古军攻陷成都，到1279年南宋灭亡时，四川盆地人口已大幅减少，蜀语传承遭到重创。此后明清两代，湖广等地移民大量入川，带来的方言演变为西南官话，古蜀方言就此绝迹，只有川西南的岷江话保留了它的部分词汇与音韵特征。

en: Siar, also known as Lak, Lamassa or Likkilikki, is an Oceanic language of the southern tip of New Ireland, whose speakers call their tongue ep warwar anun dat, meaning 'our language'. It belongs to the Patpatar-Tolai group of the Meso-Melanesian linkage, the cluster of closely related Austronesian speech covering southern New Ireland and the nearby islands: Patpatar, also called Gelik, on the east coast, Kandas along the south-western coast, and Tangga on the Tanga and Feni islands, whose varieties are so divergent that their speakers treat them as distinct languages while recalling a common migration. Across Saint George's Channel the same linkage includes Tolai, the major language of the Gazelle Peninsula on New Britain. Siar villagers live by fishing and gardening in a region first settled by Lapita seafarers; European contact began when Dutch explorers charted New Ireland in 1616, and whaling ships were calling along the coast by the 1790s.
zh: 西亚尔语又称拉克语、拉马萨语或利基利基语，是新爱尔兰岛南端的一种大洋洲语言，使用者把自己的语言称作 ep warwar anun dat，意为‘我们的语言’。它属于中美拉尼西亚语链下的帕特帕塔尔—托莱语群，这一亲缘相近的南岛语集群分布在新爱尔兰岛南部及附近岛屿：东海岸的帕特帕塔尔语（又称格利克语）、西南沿海的坎达斯语，以及坦加和费尼群岛上的坦加语——后者各变体差异很大，使用者视其为不同语言，但仍记得共同的迁徙渊源。隔着圣乔治海峡，同一语链还包括新不列颠岛加泽尔半岛上的主要语言托莱语。西亚尔人的村落以捕鱼和园圃为生，所在地区最早由拉皮塔航海者定居；欧洲人的接触始于1616年荷兰探险者测绘新爱尔兰岛，到18世纪90年代已有捕鲸船沿岸停靠。

en: Sie, also called Erromangan or Sye, is the Oceanic language of Erromango, the largest island in the Tafea group of southern Vanuatu, and the principal survivor of the several indigenous languages once spoken there. It belongs to the Southern Vanuatu subgroup, whose languages are marked by complex morphology and an echo-subject construction instead of the serial verbs common elsewhere in Oceanic. Erromango was first settled around three thousand years ago by Lapita voyagers, whose speech evolved in relative isolation into the island's dialects. James Cook made the first European landing there in 1774, and from 1804 whalers and, after 1825, sandalwood traders brought regular outside contact; the sandalwood rush of 1830, which included a Hawaiian attempt to seize the island, disrupted village life. Sie had no traditional writing and remained a purely spoken language throughout this period.
zh: 希耶语又称埃罗芒奥语，是南瓦努阿图塔菲亚地区最大岛屿埃罗芒奥岛的南岛语系大洋洲语言，也是岛上几种本土语言中最主要的一支。它属于南瓦努阿图语支，该语支以复杂的词形变化和回声主语结构为特征，没有大洋洲语言常见的连动结构。约三千年前，拉皮塔航海者最先定居埃罗芒奥岛，他们的语言在相对隔绝中演变为岛上的各方言。1774年，詹姆斯·库克首次在岛上登陆；1804年起捕鲸船、1825年起檀木商人相继带来持续的外来接触，1830年的檀木热潮（其中包括夏威夷人夺取该岛的企图）打乱了村落生活。希耶语没有传统文字，在这一时期始终是纯粹的口语。

en: Sihni, or Itonama, is the language of the Itonama people of the Bolivian Amazon, formerly spoken along the Itonomas River in the Beni lowlands and treated as a language isolate. The Itonama were first reached by Spaniards in the seventeenth century, and its last speakers lived in the town of Magdalena.
zh: 西尼语又称伊托纳马语，是玻利维亚亚马逊地区伊托纳马人的语言，曾通行于贝尼低地的伊托诺马斯河一带，被视为孤立语言。伊托纳马人在17世纪首次与西班牙人接触，该语言最后的使用者住在马格达莱纳镇。

en: Siksiká, also called Niitsí'powahsin, is the Algonquian language of the Niitsitapi, the Blackfoot peoples of the northwestern Great Plains, and forms the Plains Algonquian grouping together with Arapaho, Gros Ventre and Cheyenne. It is among the westernmost and most divergent of Algonquian languages, with a pitch accent, a small set of vowels and consonants, and a polysynthetic grammar in which whole sentences may be folded into a single verb. Its four dialects, Siksiká, Kainai, Northern Piegan and Southern Piegan, belong to the nations of the Blackfoot Confederacy, whose country ran from the North Saskatchewan River to the Yellowstone and from the Rocky Mountains to the Cypress Hills. The Niitsitapi took to horses acquired from other Plains tribes by the early 1700s, and the language was carried across the grasslands by bison-hunting bands that gathered each summer for the Okan, the Sun Dance. European traders reached them only in the later eighteenth century.
zh: 西克西卡语又称尼齐波瓦辛，是北美大平原西北部黑脚人（尼齐塔皮人）的阿尔冈昆语言，与阿拉帕霍语、格罗斯文特语和夏延语同属平原阿尔冈昆群组。它是分布最西、与其他阿尔冈昆语言差异最大的语言之一，有声调重音，元音和辅音数量不多，语法为多式综合语，整句话可以糅进一个动词。它分西克西卡、凯奈、北皮埃甘和南皮埃甘四种方言，分属黑脚联盟的各部族；联盟的疆土北起北萨斯喀彻温河、南至黄石河，西起落基山脉、东到赛普里斯丘陵。黑脚人在18世纪初已从其他平原部族那里获得马匹，操西克西卡语的野牛狩猎队伍驰骋草原，每年夏季聚集举行奥坎仪式，即太阳舞。欧洲商人迟至18世纪后期才与他们接触。

en: Sinaugoro is an Oceanic language of the Central Papuan Tip group, one of the Sinagoro–Keapara languages alongside Hula and Keapara, and a close relative of Motu, the speech of the Port Moresby coast. It is spoken in the coastal villages of the Rigo District in Central Province, along the sheltered waters immediately east of the Motu homeland. The two peoples shared the trading world of the hiri, the traditional voyages in which large seagoing canoes carried Motu clay pots west to the Gulf of Papua and brought back sago, contacts that over the centuries turned a simplified form of Motu into the region's trade tongue. In 1606 the Spanish expedition of Luis Vaez de Torres sailed along this same southern coast of New Guinea, the first Europeans known to have done so.
zh: 西瑙戈罗语是中巴布亚尖端语组的一支大洋语，与胡拉语、凯阿帕拉语同属西瑙戈罗—凯阿帕拉语群，并与莫尔兹比港沿岸的摩图语是近亲。它通行于中央省里戈区的沿海村落，就在摩图人故乡以东的平静水域旁。两个族群共处同一个希里贸易圈：传统航行中，大型远洋独木舟载着摩图陶罐向西运往巴布亚湾，再换回西谷椰；数百年间，这类接触使一种简化的摩图语演变成当地的贸易用语。1606年，西班牙人路易斯·瓦埃斯·德·托雷斯的探险队沿新几内亚这段南部海岸航行，这是已知欧洲人第一次来到这里。

en: Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken along the lower Indus, in the region of Sindh after which it is named; the word itself goes back to the Sanskrit síndhu, the ancient name of the Indus. Like other north Indian languages it descends from Sanskrit through the Prakrits and the later Apabhramsha stage. After the Arab conquest of Sindh in 712 it became the first Indo-Aryan language in sustained contact with Arabic and Persian, absorbing a large stock of loanwords and adopting the Perso-Arabic script. Early written literature was sparse: Isma'ili devotional hymns from the eleventh century used a related idiom, while from the late fifteenth century Sufi poets such as Qazi Qadan composed in Sindhi itself, a tradition crowned in the eighteenth century by the mystic verses of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai. In present-day Pakistan and India it is spoken by more than thirty million people, in both the Perso-Arabic and Devanagari scripts.
zh: 信德语是印度—雅利安语支的语言，通行于印度河下游的信德地区，并因此得名；其名称可追溯至梵语中印度河的古称“信度”。与北印度其他语言一样，它由梵语经俗语和后来的阿帕布拉姆沙阶段演变而来。712年阿拉伯人征服信德后，信德语成为最早长期接触阿拉伯语和波斯语的印度—雅利安语言，吸收了大量借词并采用波斯—阿拉伯字母。早期书面文献不多：11世纪伊斯玛仪派的虔诚赞美诗使用一种与信德语相近的语体；15世纪末起，加齐·卡丹等苏菲派诗人开始直接以信德语创作，这一传统在18世纪沙阿·阿卜杜勒·拉蒂夫·比塔伊的神秘主义诗篇中达到高峰。在今巴基斯坦和印度境内，信德语有超过三千万使用者，兼用波斯—阿拉伯字母和天城文。

en:
Sinhala is the Indo-Aryan language of the Sinhalese, the majority people of Sri Lanka; with Maldivian of the Maldives it forms the Insular Indo-Aryan group, both descending from the ancient Elu Prakrit. The chronicle Mahavamsa traces them to settlers from eastern India's Kalinga and Magadha, and the earliest records are third-century-BCE rock inscriptions in a Prakrit close to Magadhi. Its history runs through four stages: Elu Prakrit until the fourth century CE, Proto-Sinhala until the eighth, medieval Sinhala until the thirteenth, and the modern stage thereafter. Contact with Tamil speakers and the island's Vedda people left a Dravidian and Vedda substrate. Its closest kin Maldivian, attested on twelfth-century copper plates, has used the Thaana script since the sixteenth century.

More than fifteen hundred verses on the mirror wall at Sigiriya, dated to the eighth through tenth centuries, are the only surviving poetry of the Anuradhapura age; the Kotte court that united the island in 1450 patronized the bird-named sandesha messenger poems of its monk-poets. Its Brahmi-derived abugida, akin to the Grantha script, also serves the liturgical Pali, and its literary and spoken registers differ sharply in a classic case of diglossia. Printing came under the Dutch: a Colombo press of 1734 issued Sinhala gospels, and British-era Bible societies produced fresh translations in 1823 and 1833.
zh:
僧伽罗语是斯里兰卡主体民族僧伽罗人的印度—雅利安语言，与马尔代夫的迪维希语同属岛屿印度—雅利安语群，二者都由古老的僧伽罗俗语（又称埃鲁俗语）演化而来。编年史《大史》把僧伽罗人的源头追溯到来自东印度羯陵伽和摩揭陀的移民；现存最早的记录是公元前3世纪的岩石铭文，所用俗语接近摩揭陀俗语。它的历史分为四个阶段：4世纪以前的僧伽罗俗语、4至8世纪的原始僧伽罗语、8至13世纪的中世纪僧伽罗语，以及13世纪以后的阶段。与泰米尔人及岛上维达人的长期接触，使它带有达罗毗荼语和维达语底层。它最近的亲属迪维希语最早见于12世纪的铜版铭文，16世纪起采用它拿字母。

锡吉里耶镜墙上留存着一千五百多首8至10世纪的题诗，是阿努拉德普勒时代唯一存世的诗歌；1450年统一全岛的科特王朝朝廷供养了一批诗僧，写下以鹦鹉、鹩哥等禽鸟命名的信使诗。僧伽罗语使用源出婆罗米文的元音附标文字，与南印度的格兰塔文相近，也用于书写礼仪语言巴利语；其书面语与口语分歧显著，是双层语言现象的典型。印刷术随荷兰人到来：1734年科伦坡的印刷所印出僧伽罗语福音书，英国统治时期的圣经会又于1823年和1833年推出新译本。

en: Sintu, also called siNtu or the Southern Bantu languages, is the broad family of Bantu speech covering the southeastern quarter of Africa, from the Makhuwa coast of northern Mozambique and the Shona lands of the Zimbabwe plateau to the Nguni, Sotho and Tswa-Ronga tongues of South Africa. Its name joins the prefix that marks a language to the common Bantu word for a person, ntu. Proto-Southern Bantu was spoken sometime after 1000 in the borderland where South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe and Mozambique meet, as iron-using farmers spread across the region; Nguni speakers had reached the southeastern coast before the 1500s. Long contact with Khoisan herders and hunters left its mark on the southern languages, above all the click consonants heard in Xhosa and Zulu. These were oral languages until missionaries gave them Roman alphabets: the first printed Xhosa works appeared from the Lovedale press in 1823.
zh: 辛图语又称南班图语支，是班图语之下的一大语群，覆盖非洲东南部的广阔地带：北起莫桑比克北部沿海的马库阿语，经津巴布韦高原的绍纳语，南至南非的恩古尼语、索托语和茨瓦—龙加诸语。它的名字由班图诸语中表示语言的前缀与意为“人”的词根组合而成。原始南班图语在1000年之后通行于今南非、博茨瓦纳、津巴布韦与莫桑比克交界一带，伴随使用铁器的农人扩散开来；1500年代以前，恩古尼人已经抵达东南沿海。与科伊桑牧人、猎人的长期接触在南部诸语中留下印记，最突出的便是科萨语和祖鲁语里的吸气辅音。这些语言长期只有口头传统，直到传教士为它们配上拉丁字母：1823年，洛夫代尔印刷所印出了最早的科萨语读物。

en: Zenu, also called Sinú or Sinúfana, was the language of the Zenú chiefdoms of the Caribbean lowlands of northern South America, spoken across the valleys of the Sinú and San Jorge rivers and the coast around the Gulf of Morrosquillo. It is poorly documented and has no surviving written texts; linguists usually place it among the Chocoan languages, though some have tentatively assigned it to Chibchan. Before the Spanish conquest it was the dominant tongue of Zenú territory, whose farming towns were sustained by more than a thousand years of canals and raised terraces managing the annual floods, and whose goldsmiths placed finely worked gold in the graves of the dead. That funeral gold drew the conquistadors: between 1510 and 1535 the chiefdoms were broken by warfare and epidemic disease, and their tombs were systematically looted. The reduced Zenú population kept its speech within the surviving communities, and in 1773 the Spanish crown set aside the reserve of San Andrés de Sotavento for them, but the language continued to lose ground to Spanish and survived only among a shrinking remnant, ceasing to be a living tongue around the opening of the nineteenth century.
zh: 塞努语又称西努语或西努法纳语，是南美北部加勒比低地塞努酋长国的语言，通行于塞努河、圣豪尔赫河流域以及莫罗斯基约湾沿岸。它的记录非常稀少，也没有流传下来的书面文本；语言学家通常把它归入乔科语系，也有人试探性地把它划入奇布查语系。在西班牙征服之前，它是塞努土地上占主导地位的语言；那里的农耕村镇靠一千多年间修建的水渠和高台梯田治理每年的洪水，金匠还把精工制作的金器随死者下葬。正是这些随葬金器引来了征服者：1510至1535年间，各酋长国被战争和瘟疫摧毁，墓葬遭到有组织的盗掘。人口锐减的塞努人在残存的村社里保留着自己的语言，1773年西班牙王室还为他们划出了索塔文托的圣安德烈斯保留地，但塞努语在西班牙语的挤压下不断萎缩，只在越来越少的遗民中流传，到19世纪初已不再是一种活的语言。

en: Skarureh, better known as Tuscarora, is the Iroquoian language of the Tuscarora people, together with its close Virginian cousin Nottoway; the two form a peripheral branch of Northern Iroquoian, distinct from the five inner languages of the Haudenosaunee. Its name means the hemp people or the long-shirt people, and before European contact its speakers lived in the coastal plain of North Carolina along the Roanoke, Neuse, Tar and Pamlico rivers, farming in matrilineal clans. Defeat in the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1713, fought against British colonists and their native allies, broke their power: most surviving Tuscarora drifted north over several generations into Pennsylvania and New York, where in 1722 the Oneida sponsored their admission as the sixth nation of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy. Their kinsmen the Nottoway remained in Virginia, where their language, also called Cheroenhaka, dwindled to a few remembered speakers; nearly all that was preserved of it comes from a vocabulary taken down in 1820 from an elderly Nottoway woman named Edith Turner, which scholars at once recognised as Iroquoian. Like its relatives Skarureh is a polysynthetic tongue built from long chains of word-parts, written in a Roman alphabet with added diacritics. During the American Revolution the Tuscarora divided, some following the British into Ontario while others kept their lands in New York.
zh: 斯卡鲁雷语即更广为人知的塔斯卡洛拉语，是塔斯卡洛拉人的语言，与它在弗吉尼亚的近亲诺托韦语一起，构成北易洛魁语的一个外围分支，和易洛魁联盟五族的核心语言有别。它的名字意为“麻人”或“穿长衣的人”；在欧洲人到来之前，使用者生活在北卡罗来纳沿海平原的罗阿诺克河、纽斯河、塔尔河和帕姆利科河一带，以母系氏族农耕为生。1711—1713年与英国殖民者及其原住民盟友交战的塔斯卡洛拉战争失败后，他们的势力瓦解：幸存的塔斯卡洛拉人在几代人的时间里陆续北迁，进入宾夕法尼亚和纽约，1722年经奥奈达人引荐，被接纳为易洛魁联盟的第六族。他们的亲族诺托韦人留在弗吉尼亚，其语言又称切罗恩哈卡语，使用者日渐凋零，留存下来的材料几乎全部来自1820年从一位名叫伊迪丝·特纳的诺托韦老妇那里采录的词表，学者一看便认出它属于易洛魁语。与亲属语言一样，斯卡鲁雷语是由长长词缀链构成的多式综合语，用加了附加符号的拉丁字母书写。美国独立战争期间，塔斯卡洛拉人分裂，一部分随英国人迁往安大略，另一部分保住了在纽约的土地。

en: Songhai is the dialect chain of the middle Niger bend, spoken from Gao and Timbuktu downriver to Niamey and the Benin border in varieties such as Koyraboro Senni, Koyra Chiini, Zarma and Dendi; its kinship with the Saharan languages is disputed, some linguists treating it as an independent family. Before the 900s horse-riding Songhay speakers imposed their speech on the fishing Sorko, farming Do and hunting Gao peoples of the river, and a Songhai kingdom at Gao is attested from the 1000s. Conquered by Mali in the late 1200s, Gao broke away as Mali weakened, and under Sonni Ali, who reigned from 1464 to 1492, the Songhai empire seized Timbuktu in 1468 and Djenné in 1475, carrying the language across the Sahel as a trade lingua franca. Askia Muhammad I, who took power in 1493, strengthened Islamic law and scholarship, and Timbuktu became a centre of learning where a few Songhai poems and letters were set down in Arabic script, although Arabic itself remained the language of books. The Moroccan Saadian army of Judar Pasha destroyed the empire at the Battle of Tondibi in 1591 and sacked Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné; the elite withdrew south to the Dendi kingdom, while Songhai lived on as the everyday and market speech of the Niger bend.
zh: 桑海语是尼日尔河中游河曲一带的方言群，从加奥、廷巴克图沿河南下到尼亚美和贝宁边境都有通行，包括科伊拉博罗·塞尼语、科伊拉奇尼语、查尔马语和登迪语等变体；它与撒哈拉语族的亲缘关系尚有争议，部分语言学家把它视为独立语族。10世纪之前，骑马的桑海人把自己的语言强加给河畔以捕鱼为生的索尔科人、务农的多人和狩猎的加奥人，以加奥为中心的桑海王国在11世纪已见记载。13世纪末加奥被马里征服，马里衰落后桑海重新独立；1464至1492年在位的桑尼·阿里率领桑海帝国于1468年夺取廷巴克图、1475年夺取杰内，桑海语随之成为萨赫勒商贸的通用语。1493年即位的阿斯基亚·穆罕默德一世强化伊斯兰教法与学术，廷巴克图成为学术中心，留有少量用阿拉伯字母写成的桑海语诗歌和书信，但典籍语言仍是阿拉伯语。1591年，朱达尔·帕夏率领的摩洛哥萨阿德王朝军队在汤迪比战役中摧毁桑海帝国，洗劫加奥、廷巴克图和杰内；统治精英南撤建立登迪王国，桑海语则作为尼日尔河曲日常与集市的语言延续下来。

en: South Arabic is the game's name for the Modern South Arabian languages, a branch of South Semitic spoken along the southern edge of Arabia, in Yemen and the Omani coast of Dhofar, rather than a dialect of Arabic itself. Its chief members are Mehri of the Mahra region and Soqotri, confined to the island of Socotra, along with Shehri, Harsusi, Bathari and Hobyot. Together with the ancient Sabaean tongue and the languages of Ethiopia they form the South Semitic group. These languages were already spoken in the peninsula before the spread of Arabic with Islam in the 600s, and long bilingualism with Arabic has marked them ever since. They remain mainly spoken languages with a rich oral poetry and almost no literature in writing; when written, an adapted Arabic alphabet is used. The tenth-century geographer al-Hamdani already described Mehri as a speech far removed from classical Arabic.
zh: 南阿拉伯语是游戏对一组南阿拉伯语言的称呼，它们属于南闪米特语支，通行于阿拉伯半岛南缘的也门以及阿曼佐法尔沿海，本身并不是阿拉伯语的方言。其主要成员是迈赫拉地区的迈赫拉语、只在索科特拉岛使用的索科特拉语，以及谢赫里语、哈尔苏西语、巴塔哈里语和霍比奥特语。它们与古代赛伯伊语、埃塞俄比亚诸语言同属南闪米特群体。早在7世纪阿拉伯语随伊斯兰教传播之前，这些语言就已通行于半岛，此后长期处于与阿拉伯语并用的双语环境中。它们长期以口头语言为主，口传诗歌丰富而书面文学极少，需要书写时采用经过改造的阿拉伯字母。10世纪的地理学家哈姆达尼就曾说迈赫拉语是一种与古典阿拉伯语相距甚远的语言。

en: The South Cushitic, or Rift, languages form a branch of the Cushitic family surviving mainly in the Great Rift Valley of northern Tanzania. Their speakers descend from agro-pastoralists whose proto-language was home in south-western Ethiopia; they had reached Lake Turkana by the late fourth millennium BC and entered northern Tanzania early in the second millennium BC, introducing agriculture and cattle-keeping to the lands east of Lake Victoria. Long contact with Khoisan hunter-gatherers left its mark in the click-like ejective consonants of several Rift languages. As Bantu and then Nilotic peoples spread through the region, most South Cushitic communities were absorbed, and some of their tongues are known only from loanwords in the Bantu languages that replaced them; Aasax and Kw'adza died out within recorded memory. The languages that endure include Iraqw, the largest, together with Gorowa, Alagwa and Burunge in the Tanzanian highlands, while the Dahalo of coastal Kenya still speak a related tongue as hunter-gatherers. Iraqw tradition credits its ancestors with the stone-walled irrigation complex at Engaruka, which was abandoned around 1700 to 1750 amid pressure from Datog and Maasai herders, after which the Iraqw withdrew to the intensive farming country of the Mbulu highlands.
zh: 南库希特语又称裂谷语，是库希特语族的一支，主要保存在坦桑尼亚北部的东非大裂谷一带。其使用者是农牧族群的后裔，原始母语的故乡在埃塞俄比亚西南部；他们在公元前第四千纪晚期抵达图尔卡纳湖，公元前第二千纪早期进入坦桑尼亚北部，把农业和畜牧带到了维多利亚湖以东地区。与科伊桑狩猎采集者的长期接触，在几种裂谷语里留下了类似啧音的挤喉辅音。随着班图人、随后是尼罗特人扩散到这一地区，大多数南库希特社群被同化，有些语言只能从取代它们的班图语借词中觅得踪迹；阿萨语和夸扎语在有记录的年代里相继消亡。保存下来的语言包括使用人数最多的伊拉奎语，以及坦桑尼亚高原上的戈罗瓦语、阿拉瓜语和布龙格语，肯尼亚沿海的达哈洛人则仍以狩猎采集为生，使用一门近亲语言。伊拉奎人的口述传统把恩加鲁卡的石砌灌溉遗址归功于自己的祖先；在达托加人和马赛牧民的压力下，该遗址约于1700至1750年间被废弃，伊拉奎人此后退守姆布卢高原的精耕农业区。

en: The Italian group, known to linguists as the Italo-Dalmatian languages, unites the Romance vernaculars of central and southern Italy, Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica, and once of the Dalmatian coast: Tuscan, Neapolitan, Sicilian, Sardinian, Dalmatian and the central dialects of Rome and Umbria. They descend from the Vulgar Latin of the peninsula and its islands, and the earliest surviving Romance vernacular text, the Placiti Cassinesi of 960 to 963, comes from near Benevento. Sicilian, layered with Greek, Arabic and Norman influences, holds the oldest literary tradition: the Sicilian School of 1230 to 1266, led by Giacomo da Lentini at Emperor Frederick II's Palermo court, forged the first Italian literary language and the sonnet. Primacy passed to Florentine Tuscan when Dante, Petrarch and Boccaccio made it their vehicle in the fourteenth century. The Renaissance debate over the questione della lingua ended in favour of Pietro Bembo's Florentine standard, confirmed by the Accademia della Crusca of 1582 and the first Italian dictionary of 1612, while printing carried the language into every court. Neapolitan, bearing an ancient Oscan substrate, flourished with the theatre and song of the Kingdom of Naples. Across the Adriatic, Dalmatian served the merchant republic of Ragusa until the late fifteenth century, then yielded to Venetian and Croatian; by the nineteenth century only the Vegliote speech of Krk survived. Sardinia kept the most Latin-like Romance tongue, used in its medieval judicates before Catalan and Castilian became prestige languages under Aragonese rule.
zh: 这组语言对应学界所称的意大利—达尔马提亚语支，汇集意大利半岛中部和南部、西西里、撒丁、科西嘉的罗曼语族地方语言，还包括一度通行于达尔马提亚海岸的达尔马提亚语，托斯卡纳语、那不勒斯语、西西里语、撒丁语和罗马、翁布里亚一带的中部方言都在其中。它们都源自半岛及岛屿上的通俗拉丁语，现存最早的意大利通俗语文本，就是960—963年在南部贝内文托附近写下的法律文书。西西里语积淀了希腊语、阿拉伯语和诺曼语等多层成分，拥有意大利罗曼语中最古老的文学传统：1230—1266年，在皇帝腓特烈二世的巴勒莫宫廷，以雅各布·达·伦蒂尼为首的西西里诗派锻造出第一种意大利文学语言，并创立了十四行诗体。14世纪，但丁、彼特拉克和薄伽丘以佛罗伦萨方言写成不朽杰作，文学主导权随之转入托斯卡纳。文艺复兴时期的语言问题之争最终采纳了彼得罗·本博主张的佛罗伦萨文学标准，1582年秕糠学会成立、1612年第一部意大利语词典问世，印刷术又把这种语言推向半岛各国的宫廷。那不勒斯语带有古老的奥斯坎语底层，随那不勒斯王国的戏剧和歌曲兴盛一时。在亚得里亚海对岸，达尔马提亚语曾是拉古萨商业共和国的用语，15世纪末以后逐渐被威尼斯语和克罗地亚语排挤，到19世纪只剩克尔克岛上的韦格利亚方言。与世隔绝的撒丁则保存了最接近拉丁语的罗曼语，中世纪曾用于当地执政官政权的公文，阿拉贡统治后，加泰罗尼亚语和卡斯蒂利亚语相继成为岛上的上层通用语。

en: Spanish, also called Castilian after the Kingdom of Castile where it took shape, descends from the Vulgar Latin the Romans brought to the Iberian Peninsula. Its first written traces are the Romance glosses added to Latin manuscripts around the tenth and eleventh centuries, and as the Reconquista pushed south the Castilian dialect spread with it, absorbing many Arabic words from Al-Andalus and features of the Mozarabic speech of Christians under Muslim rule, while the related Judaeo-Spanish of the Sephardic Jews later became known as Ladino. In the thirteenth century Alfonso X the Wise made Castilian the language of his Toledo chancery and of works of history and science, creating the first written standard; Antonio de Nebrija presented the first grammar of the language to Queen Isabella in 1492. Carried across the Atlantic by conquest and settlement, Spanish became the speech of a vast American empire, whose varieties draw mainly on Andalusian and Canarian dialects and borrowed words from indigenous languages. The Royal Spanish Academy was founded in 1713 to regulate the now global language.
zh: 西班牙语又称卡斯蒂利亚语，得名于它的诞生地卡斯蒂利亚王国，源出罗马人带到伊比利亚半岛的通俗拉丁语。现存最早的书面痕迹是10至11世纪间加在拉丁文抄本行间的罗曼语批注。随着收复失地运动向南推进，卡斯蒂利亚方言也传播开来，从安达卢斯吸收了大量阿拉伯语词汇，并受到穆斯林治下基督徒所用莫扎拉布语的影响；与之相近的塞法迪犹太人语言后来被称为拉迪诺语。13世纪，智者阿方索十世把卡斯蒂利亚语用于托莱多的王宫文书以及历史和科学著作，确立了最早的书面规范；1492年，安东尼奥·德·内布里哈向伊莎贝拉女王进呈了第一部西班牙语语法。随着征服与殖民，西班牙语被带到大西洋彼岸，成为幅员辽阔的美洲帝国的语言；美洲各变体主要源自安达卢西亚和加那利方言，并借入了不少原住民语言的词汇。1713年成立的西班牙皇家语言学院负责规范这门已通行全球的语言。

en: Suau, also called Iou, is an Oceanic language of the Papuan Tip cluster, head of the Suauic linkage that also includes Saliba, Buhutu, 'Auhelawa, Wagawaga and Bwanabwana. It is spoken in the coastal villages and small islands of Milne Bay Province at the southeastern tip of New Guinea, and beyond its home villages it serves as a regional lingua franca along the surrounding coasts. The people of these shores live from fishing, sago and garden plots, and were among the first populations of the island's southeast to meet Europeans: in July 1606 the Spanish expedition of Luis Vaez de Torres surveyed Milne Bay while sailing westward through the strait that now bears his name.
zh: 苏奥语又称伊奥乌语，是巴布亚尖端语群的一支大洋语，统领苏奥语链，萨利巴语、布胡图语、奥赫拉瓦语、瓦加瓦加语和布瓦纳布瓦纳语都在这一语链中。它通行于新几内亚东南端米尔恩湾省的沿海村落和小岛，并在母语村落之外充当周围海岸的地区通用语。当地居民以捕鱼、西谷椰和园圃为生，也是新几内亚东南部最早接触欧洲人的族群之一：1606年7月，西班牙人路易斯·瓦埃斯·德·托雷斯的探险队在向西穿过以他的名字命名的海峡时，测绘了米尔恩湾。

en: The Sumba grouping covers the languages once classed together as the Bima-Sumba branch of Central Malayo-Polynesian Austronesian. They stretch across the Lesser Sunda Islands: Nggahi Mbojo, the tongue of Bima and Dompu on eastern Sumbawa; the Manggarai, Lio, Sikka and Lamaholot speeches of Flores and the neighboring Solor and Lembata islands; the Sumba languages, led by Kambera, on Sumba; and Hawu on Savu, which may preserve a non-Austronesian substratum. Later linguists split the old branch into Sumba-Hawu and Sumba-Flores groups and treat Bimanese as a separate line. The Hindu-Buddhist kingdom of Bima on Sumbawa traced its origins to around 709, and the Portuguese apothecary Tome Pires already listed its cloth, horses and slaves among regional exports around 1515. Sumba, whose megalithic burials reach back millennia, was claimed by Majapahit in the 1300s and first visited by the Portuguese in 1522. Bima turned to Islam in 1621 under the influence of the Makassarese kingdom of Gowa, and as a sultanate long drew tribute from Manggarai, Sumba, Sawu and parts of Flores before the Dutch East India Company tightened its hold on the region from the 1600s.
zh: 松巴语这一划分涵盖旧分类中合称“比马—松巴语支”的一组中马来—波利尼西亚南岛语言，分布于小巽他群岛：松巴哇岛东部比马和栋普的恩加希姆博若语，弗洛勒斯岛及邻近索洛、伦巴塔岛上的芒加莱语、利奥语、锡卡语和拉马霍洛特语，松巴岛上以坎贝拉语为代表的松巴诸语，以及萨武岛上的哈武语（可能保留了非南岛语底层）。后世语言学家把旧语支拆成松巴—哈武和松巴—弗洛勒斯两个语群，并把比马语单列为一支。松巴哇岛上印度教—佛教色彩的比马王国起源可追溯到709年前后；1515年前后，葡萄牙药剂师托梅·皮莱资已把当地的布匹、马匹和奴隶列入区域出口货单。松巴岛的巨石墓葬传统延续数千年，14世纪被满者伯夷列为藩属，1522年葡萄牙人首次到访。1621年，比马在望加锡戈瓦王国影响下皈依伊斯兰教，成为苏丹国，长期向芒加莱、松巴、萨武及弗洛勒斯部分地区收取贡赋；17世纪起，荷兰东印度公司逐步加强了对这一地区的控制。

en: Sumuri, also spelled Sumeri and one of two Papuan languages called Tanah Merah, is spoken on the northern coast of the Bomberai Peninsula in western New Guinea, around Tofoi and the other villages of Sumuri District on Bintuni Bay. Its classification is unsettled: Malcolm Ross and Timothy Usher treat it as an independent branch of the Trans–New Guinea family, its pronouns recalling the proto-Trans–New Guinea forms, while other scholars regard it as a language isolate, and it was once linked without proof to the neighbouring Mairasi languages. The Sumuri homeland lies in a coast of marshy lowland rainforest that was drawn into interregional trade early: birds of paradise feathers from the region reached Srivijaya in the seventh century, and the fourteenth-century Javanese poem Nagarakretagama names the nearby Onin and Sran lands as tributaries of Majapahit, the earliest written mention of Papuan places. The Spanish expedition of Luís Vaz de Torres first sighted this coast for Europeans in 1606, and it subsequently fell within the sphere of the Sultanate of Tidore, whose hongi fleets raided it for slaves and tribute. The Dutch built Fort Du Bus on Triton Bay in 1828 to formalise their protectorate over Tidore's Papuan dependencies, but the unhealthy post was abandoned in 1835, leaving Sumuri country under loose indirect rule for decades longer.
zh: 苏穆里语又作苏梅里语，是两种称“塔纳梅拉”（印度尼西亚语意为红土）的巴布亚语言之一，通行于新几内亚西部邦巴赖半岛北海岸、宾图尼湾沿岸苏穆里区的托福伊等村庄。它的分类尚无定论：马尔科姆·罗斯和蒂莫西·厄舍把它列为跨新几内亚语系下独立的一支，其代词与原始跨新几内亚语形式相呼应；另一些学者则视其为孤立语言，过去还有人未经证实就把它与邻近的迈拉西诸语联系在一起。苏穆里人的家园位于沼泽低地雨林海岸，很早就卷入跨区域贸易：7世纪时，当地的极乐鸟羽毛已远销室利佛逝；14世纪的爪哇史诗《爪哇史颂》把附近的奥宁和斯兰地区列为满者伯夷的朝贡地，这是巴布亚地名最早的文字记载。1606年，路易斯·瓦斯·德·托雷斯率领的西班牙探险队让欧洲人首次望见这段海岸；此后它被纳入蒂多雷苏丹国的势力范围，蒂多雷称作洪伊的远征船队常来这里掠夺奴隶和贡物。1828年，荷兰人在特里顿湾修建杜布斯堡，以正式确立对蒂多雷治下巴布亚属地的保护权，但这座疫病流行的据点于1835年废弃，苏穆里地区此后又处于松散的间接统治之下数十年。

en: Sundanese is the Malayo-Polynesian language of the Sundanese people, native to the western third of Java in the region called Tatar Sunda or Pasundan. Although surrounded by Javanese, it is classified with the Malayic languages and with the Land Dayak and Kayan-Murik groups of Borneo, rather than with Javanese itself. From the age of Tarumanagara, whose fifth-century Ciaruteun inscription of King Purnawarman was incised in Pallava script and drew heavily on Sanskrit, it served as the language of the Sundanese courts, among them the Hindu kingdom of Pajajaran, which lasted from 932 to about 1579. Old Sundanese was used for religious and historical manuscripts. It was first written in the Old Sundanese script; after the spread of Islam the Arabic-based Pegon alphabet joined it, and in colonial times the Latin alphabet became dominant. Its dialects include those of Banten and Cirebon, while the Priangan dialect of the Bandung highlands is the most widely spoken and forms the standard. Sundanese remained the everyday speech of western Java through the Mataram conquests and the Dutch colonial period.
zh: 巽他语是巽他人的马来—波利尼西亚语，通行于爪哇岛西部三分之一、称做巽他之地的帕巽丹地区。它虽与爪哇语相邻，分类上却与马来语群以及婆罗洲的陆地达雅、卡扬—穆里克语群相近，而不属于爪哇语。早在多罗磨时代，5世纪普尔纳瓦尔曼王的查鲁顿碑文就以帕拉瓦文刻写，深受梵文影响；此后巽他语长期是巽他宫廷的语言，包括932年至约1579年存在的印度教王国巴查查兰。古巽他语用于撰写宗教与历史手稿，最早以古巽他字母书写，伊斯兰教传入后又出现以阿拉伯字母为基础的佩贡字母，殖民时代拉丁字母成为主流。方言包括万丹、井里汶等支，而万隆高原的勃良安方言使用最广，构成标准语的基础。历经马打兰的征服与荷兰殖民时期，巽他语始终是西爪哇的日常语言。

en: Swahili, or Kiswahili, is a Bantu language of the Sabaki branch, native to the Swahili people of the East African coast and its islands, from southern Somalia through Kenya and Tanzania to northern Mozambique. Its grammar and basic vocabulary are Bantu, but centuries of Indian Ocean trade with Arab and Persian merchants gave it a large Arabic word-stock; the name itself comes from an Arabic word meaning of the coast. It grew into a regional lingua franca in trading city-states such as Kilwa, founded in the 800s, whose sultanate dominated the coast from the thirteenth to the fifteenth century and which the traveller Ibn Battuta praised in 1331. Portuguese fleets sacked Kilwa in 1505 and added their own loanwords, yet Swahili continued to spread along the caravan routes. It was written in the Arabic script, and the epic Utendi wa Tambuka, composed by Bwana Mwengo wa Athman in 1728, is among its earliest surviving literary works.
zh: 斯瓦希里语又称基斯瓦希里语，属班图语的萨巴基语支，母语者为东非沿海及岛屿上的斯瓦希里人，分布从索马里南部经肯尼亚、坦桑尼亚直到莫桑比克北部。它的语法和基础词汇是班图式的，但数百年的印度洋贸易使它从阿拉伯和波斯商人那里吸收了大量阿拉伯语词汇，其名称本身就来自一个意为海岸的阿拉伯词。它在基尔瓦等贸易城邦成长为地区通用语：基尔瓦建于9世纪，其苏丹国在13至15世纪称雄沿海，旅行家伊本·白图泰曾于1331年盛赞这座城市。1505年葡萄牙舰队洗劫基尔瓦，并给斯瓦希里语留下了自己的借词，但该语言仍沿商路继续传播。它以阿拉伯字母书写，诗人布瓦纳·姆文戈·瓦·阿斯曼于1728年创作的史诗《坦布卡的故事》是现存最早的斯瓦希里语文学作品之一。

en: Arawakan, also called Maipurean, is one of the largest and most widely spread language families of the Americas, carried by peoples from the eastern slopes of the Andes in Peru and Bolivia across the Amazon basin to the Guianas, Venezuela and Colombia, and as far north as Central America and the Caribbean. Some 2,500 years ago Arawakan speakers reached the Antilles and the Bahamas, where their Caribbean branch, Ta-Arawak, produced Taíno, the language of Cuba, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico and Jamaica, alongside Lokono, Wayuu and Caquetio on the mainland; inland branches include the Upper Amazon tongues of the Manao and Achagua, the Central Paresí–Xingu group, the Campa languages of the pre-Andean foothills, and the southern Moxo, Baure and Terena. The family was first recognized in 1782, when the Italian priest Filippo Gilii showed that the Maipure of the Orinoco and the Moxos of Bolivia were related; its languages are polysynthetic and head-marking, with elaborate verb morphology built mainly through suffixes.
zh: 阿拉瓦克语又称迈普雷语，是美洲规模最大、分布最广的语族之一：使用者分布于秘鲁和玻利维亚的安第斯山脉东坡，横跨亚马孙盆地，直达圭亚那、委内瑞拉和哥伦比亚，北至中美洲和加勒比海。约2500年前，阿拉瓦克诸语的使用者抵达安的列斯群岛和巴哈马，其加勒比分支塔—阿拉瓦克语衍生出泰诺语，通行于古巴、伊斯帕尼奥拉、波多黎各和牙买加，大陆上则有洛科诺语、瓦尤语和卡克蒂奥语；内陆分支包括马瑙语、阿查瓜语等上亚马孙语言，中部的帕雷西—欣古语群，安第斯山麓的坎帕诸语，以及南部的莫霍语、巴乌雷语和特雷纳语。1782年，意大利教士菲利波·吉利最早确认该语族的亲缘关系，证明奥里诺科河的迈普雷语与玻利维亚的莫霍斯语同出一源；这些语言属多式综合语、以词头标注为主，复杂的动词形态主要靠后缀构成。

en: Tabaristani gathers together the Northwestern Iranian vernaculars of the southern Caspian shore and the Semnan highlands: the Caspian languages proper, chief among them Gilaki and Mazanderani, also called Tabari, together with the Semnani group and its neighbours Sangsari, Lasgerdi and Sorkhei. The name comes from Tabaristan, the medieval term for the mountain kingdom of Mazandaran, known in antiquity as Tapuria. As early as the 900s the geographer al-Muqaddasi noted the distinctive speech of Tabaristan, and under the local rulers who held the region after the Arab invasion Mazanderani carried a written literature from the 900s to the 1400s, including the mirror-for-princes work Marzban Nameh and the verse of Amir Pazevari. These tongues keep archaic Median and Parthian features and share unusual structures with the South Caucasian languages. Their literary and administrative use faded after Mazandaran was drawn into the royal administration in the early 1600s, leaving Persian as the language of writing.
zh: 塔巴里斯坦语是对里海南岸与塞姆南高地诸西北伊朗方言的统称，包括严格意义上的里海诸语言——其中以吉拉基语和又称塔巴里语的马赞德兰语为主——以及塞姆南语群和邻近的桑格萨尔语、拉斯杰尔迪语、索尔赫语。其名来自塔巴里斯坦，即马赞德兰山区政权在中世纪的称呼，上古时称塔普里亚。早在10世纪，地理学家穆卡达西就注意到塔巴里斯坦方言的独特之处；阿拉伯入侵后，当地统治者长期保有半独立地位，马赞德兰语在10至15世纪发展出自己的书面文学，代表作品有王侯镜鉴之书《马尔兹班纳梅》和阿米尔·帕泽瓦里的诗歌。这些语言保留了古老的米底语和帕提亚语特征，还与南高加索语言共有一些特殊结构。17世纪初马赞德兰被纳入王室行政体系后，它们在文学和行政上的使用日渐衰落，书面领域让位于波斯语。

en: Tagalog is a Central Philippine language of the Austronesian family, native to the plains around Manila Bay and Laguna de Bay in southern Luzon; its name may mean river dweller, from taga-ilog. Possible Old Tagalog words survive in the tenth-century Laguna Copperplate Inscription, and before Spanish rule Tagalogs wrote in baybayin, a syllabic script. The first complete printed book in the language, the Doctrina Christiana of 1593, appeared in both baybayin and an early Latin orthography, and Spanish missionaries then gave Tagalog a full scholarly apparatus: Francisco Blancas de San Jose printed its first grammar in 1610, Pedro de San Buenaventura the first dictionary in 1613, and the Jesuit Pablo Clain's materials grew into the Vocabulario de la lengua tagala published in Manila in 1754. Three centuries of Spanish rule added a large Romance vocabulary while the Latin alphabet displaced baybayin. The early nineteenth century produced the poet Francisco Balagtas, whose epic Florante at Laura became the cornerstone of Tagalog literature.
zh: 他加禄语是南岛语系菲律宾语支中部语群的语言，故乡在吕宋岛南部马尼拉湾和拉古纳湾周围的平原，其名称可能源自他加伊洛格，意为河边居民。10世纪的拉古纳铜版铭文里保留了可能属于古他加禄语的词汇；西班牙统治之前，他加禄人使用贝贝因音节文字。1593年印行的《基督教教义》是第一部完整的他加禄语印本书，同时使用贝贝因文字和早期拉丁拼写法，此后西班牙传教士为这种语言建立了完整的学术体系：布兰卡·德·圣何塞于1610年印出第一部语法书，佩德罗·德·圣布埃纳文图拉于1613年编成第一部词典，耶稣会士巴勃罗·克莱因的资料最终汇成1754年在马尼拉出版的《他加禄语词汇》。三个世纪的西班牙统治带来了大量罗曼语词汇，拉丁字母也取代了贝贝因文字。19世纪初出现了诗人弗朗西斯科·巴拉格达斯，他的史诗《弗罗兰特与劳拉》成为他加禄文学的基石。

en: Tai is the name for a close-knit complex of tonal, analytic languages and dialects of the Kra-Dai family, spoken in an arc from Guangxi, Guizhou and Hainan in southern China through Yunnan to Laos, Thailand and the Shan hills of Myanmar. Its best-known members are Siamese, or Thai, Lao, Shan and the Dai varieties such as Tai Lü and Tai Nüa, which shade into one another as a dialect continuum; words are mostly monosyllabic, word order is subject-verb-object, and grammatical relations are shown by particles rather than endings. Southwestern Tai speakers moved out of southern China between the eighth and tenth centuries and founded the chiefdoms and kingdoms of the Mekong and Chao Phraya valleys. They wrote in Brahmi-derived alphabets adapted from Mon and Khmer models, the earliest Thai inscriptions appearing at Sukhothai around 1292, while the Zhuang kept their speech in Chinese-derived Sawndip characters. In the Ayutthaya kingdom of 1351 to 1767, Siamese absorbed a large stock of Khmer words, and Theravada Buddhism carried in Pali and Sanskrit terms shared across the Tai world.
zh: 泰语是壮侗语系下一群关系紧密的声调型分析语言和方言的统称，分布呈弧形，从中国南方的广西、贵州、海南经云南延伸到老挝、泰国和缅甸掸邦山区。最知名的成员有暹罗语（即泰国官方泰语）、老挝语、掸语，以及傣仂、傣那等傣语变体，彼此渐次过渡，构成一条方言连续体；词汇多为单音节，语序为主谓宾，语法关系靠虚词而非词尾变化表达。西南台语人群在8至10世纪间迁出中国南方，在湄公河和湄南河流域建立了诸多酋邦与王国。他们借用源自孟文、高棉文的婆罗米系字母书写，最早的泰文铭文约于1292年出现在素可泰；壮族则长期使用仿照汉字创制的方块壮字。1351至1767年的阿瑜陀耶王国时期，暹罗语吸收了大量高棉语词汇，上座部佛教又带来了遍布整个台语世界的巴利语和梵语借词。

en: Taíno, also called Island Arawak, is the extinct Arawakan language that by the late 1400s was the common speech of the Greater Antilles and the northern Lesser Antilles, heard from the Bahamas and Cuba across Hispaniola and Puerto Rico as far as Guadeloupe. Its Classic dialect, expanding from around 1200, served as the lingua franca of the Indies, while the related Ciboney and Lucayan varieties covered central Cuba and the Bahamas; Columbus noted in 1492 that islanders traveling by canoe could understand one another throughout the archipelago. As Spanish conquest advanced the language gave way to Spanish, English and French, but not before passing into European languages a large cargo of words, among them canoe, hammock, hurricane, maize, cassava, potato, tobacco and savanna. Place names such as Borinquen, the old name of Puerto Rico, come from the language, and its closest living relative is the Wayuu tongue of the Guajira coast.
zh: 泰诺语又称岛屿阿拉瓦克语，是已经消亡的阿拉瓦克语言，到15世纪后期已是大安的列斯群岛和小安的列斯群岛北部的通用语言，通行范围从巴哈马、古巴横跨伊斯帕尼奥拉和波多黎各，远达瓜德罗普。其经典方言约1200年起向外扩展，曾是西印度群岛的贸易通用语；关系相近的西博内方言和卢卡扬方言则分别通行于古巴中部和巴哈马。1492年哥伦布记载，群岛居民驾独木舟往来各处，彼此都能听懂对方的话。随着西班牙征服推进，泰诺语逐渐被西班牙语、英语和法语取代，但它先已给欧洲语言留下一大批借词，如独木舟、吊床、飓风、玉米、木薯、土豆、烟草和热带草原。波多黎各旧称博林肯等地名即出自该语言；与它亲缘最近的现存语言是瓜希拉海岸的瓦尤语。

en: Takic is a proposed grouping of closely related languages in the northern branch of the Uto-Aztecan family, formerly spoken across coastal southern California from the vicinity of Malibu south to Carlsbad, on the Southern Channel Islands, and inland through the Mojave Desert, Coachella Valley and Tehachapi Mountains. Its members included Tongva, also called Gabrielino, Serrano, Kitanemuk, Tataviam, Cahuilla, Cupeño and Luiseño. Archaeologists reconstruct a Takic expansion from a desert homeland in the western Mojave, whose speakers moved south into coastal California thousands of years ago and absorbed or displaced older populations. Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo met coastal Takic speakers in 1542, but sustained contact began only after 1769, when Spanish missions such as San Gabriel and San Juan Capistrano were founded in their lands. Forced resettlement, epidemics and forced labour shattered the mission peoples, who rose in rebellions such as the one led by the prophetess Toypurina in 1785; Mexico's secularization of the missions in the 1830s left most survivors landless.
zh: 塔基克语是犹他‑阿兹特克语系北支下一组关系相近的语言（其归并仍有争议），曾通行于南加州沿海——从马里布附近向南到卡尔斯巴德——以及南海峡群岛，并深入莫哈韦沙漠、科切拉谷地和特哈查比山区，包括通瓦语（又称加夫列利诺语）、塞拉诺语、基塔穆克语、塔塔维亚姆语、卡维拉语、库佩尼奥语和路易塞尼奥语等。考古学家推测，说塔基克语的人群数千年前从莫哈韦西部的沙漠故土向南迁徙，进入加州沿海，吸收或取代了更早的居民，这一过程被称为塔基克扩张。1542年胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略曾遇到沿海的塔基克语使用者，但持续接触要到1769年以后：西班牙人在他们的土地上建起圣加百列、圣胡安·卡皮斯特拉诺等传教站。强制迁徙、疫病和劳役摧毁了传教区的各族群，1785年女先知托伊普里纳领导的起义便是反抗之一；19世纪30年代墨西哥将传教站世俗化后，多数幸存者失去了土地。

en: Tamambo, also called Malo, is an Oceanic language of Vanuatu, spoken on Malo island and neighboring islets off the southern coast of Espiritu Santo. Malo holds the earliest known Lapita culture settlement in Vanuatu, occupied around 1400 BC, and Tamambo is counted among the most conservative of the Southern Oceanic languages, retaining many features inherited from the speech of those first Austronesian settlers. It has two dialects: the western dialect, whose form of the island's name gives the language its name Tamambo, and the eastern dialect called Tamapo, which had nearly died out by the twentieth century. Traditionally an unwritten language with no standard orthography, Tamambo was only systematically recorded by linguists in recent decades.
zh: 塔曼博语又称马洛语，是瓦努阿图的一种大洋洲语，通行于圣埃斯皮里图岛南岸外的马洛岛及附近小岛。马洛岛拥有瓦努阿图已知最早的拉皮塔文化定居点，约公元前1400年便有人类居住；塔曼博语被视为最保守的南大洋洲语言之一，保留了这些最早的南岛定居者语言中的许多特征。它分为两种方言：西部方言对岛名的读法即“塔曼博”一名的由来，东部方言称塔马波，到20世纪已近乎消亡。塔曼博语传统上没有文字，也没有标准拼写法，直到近几十年才有语言学者对它进行系统记录。

en: Tamazight, or the Berber languages, is the North African branch of the Afroasiatic family, spoken by the indigenous Amazigh peoples across a dialect continuum from Morocco and Algeria to the Siwa Oasis of Egypt, with the Tuareg varieties carrying it deep into the Sahara and an extinct form, Guanche, once spoken on the Canary Islands; its internal diversity is comparable to that of the Romance languages. Berber speakers spread westward from the Nile Valley into the Maghreb in the second millennium BC, and their ancestors built the kingdoms of Numidia and Mauretania. From around 600 BC their language was cut into rock and tombstone in the Libyco-Berber alphabet, whose Tuareg descendant, Tifinagh, remained in use among desert nomads. The Arab conquests of the seventh and eighth centuries brought Islam and a long process of Arabization, and scholars also wrote Berber in Arabic letters, yet the language stayed the speech of the mountains and the desert. Between the eleventh and sixteenth centuries Berber dynasties ruled the Maghreb and al-Andalus: the Sanhaja Almoravids, the Masmuda Almohads, and then the Zenata Marinid, Zayyanid and Hafsid houses, the Marinids holding Fez in 1337. After these dynasties fell, Arabic gained ground in the cities while Tuareg confederations kept Tamazight alive along the trans-Saharan trade routes, preserving verb-subject-object word order and the old Tifinagh letters.
zh: 塔马齐格特语即柏柏尔诸语，是亚非语系在北非的一支，由原住民阿马齐格各族使用，形成从摩洛哥、阿尔及利亚延至埃及锡瓦绿洲的方言连续体，图阿雷格各变体更把它带进撒哈拉深处，加那利群岛上已灭绝的关切语也是它的一支；其内部差异之大，堪比罗曼语族诸语。说柏柏尔语的人群在公元前2千纪从尼罗河谷向西扩散进入马格里布，他们的先民建立了努米底亚和毛里塔尼亚等王国。约公元前600年起，这种语言被人以利比亚-柏柏尔字母刻在岩壁和墓碑上，该文字的图阿雷格后裔提非纳文一直为沙漠游牧者所用。7至8世纪的阿拉伯征服带来伊斯兰教和漫长的阿拉伯化进程，学者也用阿拉伯字母书写柏柏尔语，但它仍是山区和沙漠居民的语言。11至16世纪，柏柏尔人王朝统治着马格里布和安达卢斯：桑哈贾人的穆拉比特王朝、马斯穆达人的穆瓦希德王朝，以及其后泽纳塔人的马林、宰扬和哈夫斯三家；1337年马林王朝仍以非斯为都。这些王朝覆灭后，阿拉伯语在城市不断扩张，图阿雷格诸联盟则在跨撒哈拉商路沿线保住了塔马齐格特语，也保存了动主宾语序和古老的提非纳文字。

en: The Upper Tami or Border languages are a small independent family of Papuan languages straddling the border between New Guinea's eastern and western halves, named after the Tami River in the far north of the island. They fall into three branches: Taikat, to which Awyi belongs; Bewani; and Waris, whose languages such as Imonda and Waris itself spread on both sides of the frontier. Unlike their Sepik neighbours, Border languages have no grammatical gender and no dual or plural number on nouns, and their pronouns long made them hard to place in any wider Papuan grouping. The later 1700s brought upheaval: Bewani speakers expanded rapidly out of their hills, setting off chain migrations that split the Kwomtari-speaking country in two, pushed the Fas into the swamps around Utai, and drove other groups down the Pual River until the newcomers were checked by fighting in the Kaure lands. These movements remade the linguistic map of the border country only a few generations before the first colonial patrols reached it.
zh: 上塔米语又称边境语，是巴布亚诸语言中一个独立的小语族，地跨新几内亚东西两部分之间的边境，因岛子极北部的塔米河得名。它分为三支：阿维语所属的塔伊卡特支、贝瓦尼支，以及伊蒙达语、瓦里斯语等分布在边境两侧的瓦里斯支。与邻近的塞皮克诸语言不同，边境诸语言的名词没有语法性别，也没有双数、复数变化，其代词特征长期使学者难以把它归入更大的巴布亚语分类。18世纪后期这一地区剧烈动荡：贝瓦尼语使用者从山地迅速扩张，引发连锁迁徙，把科姆塔里语族群的地盘截成两段，把法斯人赶入乌泰一带的沼泽，又驱使其他族群沿普阿尔河而下，直到入侵者在考雷人土地上的战斗中受阻。这些迁徙重塑了边境地区的语言版图，而距首批殖民巡逻队抵达此地不过几代人的时间。

en: Tamil is a southern Dravidian language, the mother tongue of the Tamil people of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry in south-eastern India and of northern and eastern Sri Lanka. Its Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions go back to about the third century BCE, and the Tolkāppiyam, a treatise on grammar and poetics dating to the late second century BCE, is its earliest surviving long text. The Sangam academies of the first century BCE to the fifth century CE produced 2,381 poems on love, war and kingship. Old Tamil gave way to Middle Tamil by the eighth century, and the Nannūl grammar of the thirteenth century became the norm of the literary register. Written in a script descended from Tamil-Brahmi, Tamil was the lingua franca of South Indian maritime traders, whose inscriptions have been found as far afield as Egypt. Its closest relative is Malayalam, from which it diverged only in the thirteenth or fourteenth century. In 1578 Portuguese missionaries printed a Tamil prayer book, the first printed Indian-language book.
zh: 泰米尔语是达罗毗荼语族南支的语言，是印度东南部泰米尔纳德邦、本地治里以及斯里兰卡北部和东部沿海泰米尔人的母语。泰米尔—婆罗米字母铭文可上溯至公元前3世纪左右，现存最早的长篇典籍是成于公元前2世纪末的语法与诗学著作《托尔卡皮耶姆》。公元前1世纪至公元5世纪，桑伽姆学园留下了2381首吟咏爱情、战争与君王的诗歌。古泰米尔语在8世纪前演变为中泰米尔语，13世纪问世的语法经典《南努尔》奠定了文学语言的规范。泰米尔文由泰米尔—婆罗米字母发展而来，泰米尔语曾是南印度海商的通用语，远在埃及都出土过它的铭文。与它亲缘最近的是马拉雅拉姆语，两者迟至13至14世纪才彻底分化。1578年，葡萄牙传教士印制了泰米尔语祈祷书，这是第一种付印的印度语言书籍。

en: The Tanimbar grouping corresponds to the Kei-Tanimbar languages, a small family of the Central Malayo-Polynesian branch of Austronesian scattered over the Kei and Tanimbar archipelagos in the southeastern Maluku and along the north coast of the Bomberai Peninsula of New Guinea. Its best-known member is Keiese, self-named Veu Evav, which serves as the lingua franca of the Kei islands; the family also takes in Fordata, Yamdena of the main Tanimbar island and Selaru of the southwest, and newer classifications widen it into a Tanimbar-Bomberai group. Every island and village keeps its own dialect, and as the islands had no native writing tradition, Dutch Catholic missionaries were the first to write Keiese in a Roman-letter alphabet. Kei oral history recalls Balinese aristocrats arriving in the Majapahit era, along with migrants from Sumbawa, Buton, Seram, Gorom, Jailolo and Ternate, and the islands are still ruled in custom by twenty-two rat, or raja. Two villages on Kei Besar preserve the Banda language brought by refugees from the nutmeg-producing Banda Islands. Portuguese navigators sighted Tanimbar around 1525 and charted it on maps from the 1560s, after which the islands entered the Dutch colonial sphere, exporting trepang, tortoiseshell and copra.
zh: 塔宁巴尔语这一划分对应南岛语系中马来—波利尼西亚语支的卡伊—塔宁巴尔语群，零散分布在马鲁古东南部的卡伊群岛、塔宁巴尔群岛以及新几内亚邦贝拉伊半岛北岸。其中最主要的是卡伊语，使用者自称韦乌埃瓦夫，是卡伊群岛的通用语；语群还包括福尔达塔语、塔宁巴尔主岛的扬德纳语和西南部的塞拉鲁语，较新的分类又把它扩大为塔宁巴尔—邦贝拉伊语群。每个岛、每个村庄都有自己的方言，而当地没有本土书写传统，最早用罗马字母记录卡伊语的是荷兰天主教传教士。卡伊人的口述史称，满者伯夷时代有巴厘贵族到来，此后又有来自松巴哇、布顿、斯兰、戈龙、贾伊洛洛和特尔纳特的移民，群岛在习俗上仍由二十二位拉查（拉者）治理。卡伊大岛上的两个村庄保留着班达语，那是肉豆蔻产地班达群岛的难民带来的语言。1525年前后，葡萄牙航海者望见塔宁巴尔，16世纪60年代起的地图上已标出该群岛；此后这里进入荷兰殖民势力范围，出口海参、玳瑁和椰干。

en: Tanoan, more fully Kiowa–Tanoan, is the language family of the Pueblo peoples of the Rio Grande valley in New Mexico, together with the Kiowa of the southern plains. Its three Pueblo branches are Tiwa, spoken at Taos and Picuris and around Albuquerque, Tewa and Towa; the related Kiowa, whose ancestors once lived near the northern Rockies, is now used in Oklahoma. Reconstructed vocabulary points to a homeland of hunter-gatherers on the Colorado Plateau, where the speakers gradually took up maize agriculture from the Basketmaker II culture of 50–450. Proto-Tiwa-Tewa split between 725 and 920, after which the Tiwa moved toward the Rio Grande between 920 and 980; the Towa reached the Rio Puerco valley around 1200 and the Tewa came south from Mesa Verde around 1275, settling the apartment-like pueblo towns that Spanish explorers later encountered.
zh: 塔诺语，全称基奥瓦－塔诺语系，是新墨西哥里奥格兰德河谷普韦布洛诸族与南部平原基奥瓦人的语系。它的三个普韦布洛分支是蒂瓦语（通行于陶斯、皮库里斯和阿尔伯克基一带）、特瓦语和托瓦语；与它们同源的基奥瓦语，其先民曾住在落基山脉北段，后来使用于俄克拉荷马。复原的同源词显示，该语系的原乡在科罗拉多高原，先民本是狩猎采集者，在50—450年的篮篮二期文化中逐渐转向玉米农业。原始蒂瓦－特瓦语于725—920年间分化，蒂瓦人随后在920—980年间迁往里奥格兰德河；托瓦人约在1200年进入里奥普埃尔科河谷，特瓦人约在1275年从梅萨维德南下，建起后来西班牙探险家见到的那种集合式普韦布洛城镇。

en: Tarahumaran is a branch of the Uto-Aztecan family of northern Mexico, made up of Tarahumara, the language of the Raramuri of Chihuahua, and Huarijio, spoken in the mountains and river country of Chihuahua and Sonora by people who call themselves Wariho or Macurawe; the little-known Chinipa, Guasapar and Temori varieties are usually listed as extinct members. The Raramuri, probably heirs of the Mogollon culture, once held most of Chihuahua but withdrew into the high sierras and canyons of the Sierra Madre Occidental as Spaniards moved in from the late sixteenth century. Jesuits built the first mission at San Pablo Balleza in the early 1600s, and the Tepehuan Revolt of 1616 cost the life of the missionary Juan Fonte and closed it for years. The opening of the Parral silver mines in 1631 brought slave raids and more missions, prompting Raramuri wars in 1648, when San Francisco de Borja was destroyed, and again from 1696 to 1698; the war leader Teporaca was captured and executed in 1690. Never fully conquered, the highland Raramuri kept their language and identity, while communities in the lower missions merged into the colonial population. The Jesuit expulsion of 1767 handed the declining missions to Franciscans, and the canyon country remained a stronghold of the language.
zh: 塔拉乌马拉语是墨西哥北部犹他-阿兹特克语系的一个语支，包括奇瓦瓦拉拉姆里人的塔拉乌马拉语，以及在奇瓦瓦和索诺拉的山地与河谷地带使用的瓦里希奥语——使用者自称瓦里霍或马库拉韦；记载稀少的奇尼帕、瓜萨帕尔和特莫里变体通常被列为已消亡成员。拉姆里人大概是莫戈永文化的后继者，曾据有奇瓦瓦大部，但在16世纪末西班牙人进入后退守西马德雷山脉的高山与峡谷。耶稣会在17世纪初于圣巴勃罗·巴列萨建立第一个传教区，1616年的特佩华纳起义使传教士胡安·方特丧命，传教区也关闭多年。1631年帕拉尔银矿开采后，奴隶劫掠和传教区进一步增多，引发拉姆里人1648年的战争，圣弗朗西斯科·德博尔哈传教区被毁，1696至1698年战火再起；战事领袖特波拉卡于1690年被俘处死。高地的拉姆里人从未被彻底征服，保住了语言和身份，低地传教区的人群则融入殖民社会。1767年耶稣会被驱逐，日渐衰败的传教区转交方济各会，而峡谷地带始终是这门语言的重镇。

en: Tarairiú, whose speakers called themselves Otxukayana, is the extinct and unclassified language of the Tarairiú nation, once heard between the Assú and Apodi rivers in Rio Grande do Norte and across the dry sertão of north-eastern Brazil. It survives only in a few word lists, and the nation united more than twenty peoples, among them the Janduí, Kanindé, Payakú and Xukurú, under paramount chiefs such as Draruk and his son Kanindé. Dutch visitors in the 1630s, including the painter Albert Eckhout and the Paraíba governor Elias Herckmans, described and portrayed these Tapuia warriors. Allied with the Dutch against Portuguese rule, the Tarairiú fought a century of frontier wars from 1630 to 1730 over the Assú valley, counted among the largest indigenous wars in Brazil. Their seasonal moves followed the floods of the sacred Piranhas-Açu, and they combined hunting and honey gathering with maize and cassava farming.
zh: 塔拉伊留语的使用者自称奥特苏卡亚纳人，这种已消亡的语言分类不明，曾通行于北里奥格兰德州阿苏河与阿波迪河之间，以及巴西东北部干旱的塞尔唐高原。该语言仅存几份词表；塔拉伊留民族联盟统合扬杜伊、卡宁德、帕亚库、舒库鲁等二十余个部族，先后在大酋长德拉鲁克及其子卡宁德领导下活动。17世纪30年代的荷兰访客，包括画家阿尔伯特·埃克豪特和帕拉伊巴长官埃利亚斯·赫克曼斯，都记述并画下过这些塔普亚战士。塔拉伊留人与荷兰结盟对抗葡萄牙统治，从1630年到1730年在阿苏河流域进行了长达一个世纪的边疆战争，被视为巴西规模最大的原住民战争之一。他们随圣河皮拉尼亚斯—阿苏河的涨落季节性迁徙，以狩猎、采蜜配合玉米和木薯种植为生。

en: Tayrona was the Chibchan language of the Arhuacan subgroup spoken by the Tairona chiefdoms of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the coastal massif rising above the Caribbean shore of northern South America. It is almost unattested, surviving in little more than a single recorded word, but its lineage continues in the Arhuacan tongues of the mountain peoples descended from the same chiefdoms. Tairona society took shape from the tenth and eleventh centuries as a network of farming towns on stone terraces linked by paved roads; the greatest of them, Teyuna, later called Ciudad Perdida, was founded around 800 on the Buritaca River with 169 terraces cut into the mountainside and may have held several thousand people. The name Tairona began as that of a single valley chiefdom on the northern slope, and in the surviving Ijka speech its cognate means sons of the jaguar. The first Spaniards were tolerated, but after 1600 open warfare drove much of the population high into the Sierra Nevada; there, beyond easy colonial reach through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, their descendants kept the related Kogi, Damana and Kankuamo speeches alive while Tayrona itself dissolved into them.
zh: 泰罗纳语是奇布查语系阿尔瓦科语支的一种语言，通行于圣玛尔塔雪山的泰罗纳诸酋长国；这座滨海雪山耸立在南美北部的加勒比海岸边。该语言几乎没有留下记录，传世的据报只有一个词，但它的血脉延续在雪山诸民族的阿尔瓦科语支语言中，他们正是这些酋长国的后裔。泰罗纳社会在10至11世纪成形，是一个由石砌梯田农耕城镇组成、以铺路相连的网络；其中最大的城镇特乌纳（后来被称为迷城）约于800年建在布里塔卡河畔，山坡上凿出169级台地，居民可能达数千人。“泰罗纳”最初只是北坡一个河谷酋长国的名字，在存世的伊卡语里，它的同源词意为“美洲豹之子”。最早到来的西班牙人一度被容忍，但1600年以后公开的战争迫使大量人口退入圣玛尔塔雪山高处；在17、18世纪殖民势力难以企及的地方，他们的后裔保住了与泰罗纳语同源的科吉语、达马纳语和坎夸莫语，而泰罗纳语本身则消融在这些语言之中。

en: Tehit, also recorded as Tahit, Tehid, Kaibus or Teminabuan, is a Papuan language of the southwestern Bird's Head Peninsula in Southwest Papua, centred on the country around the present town of Teminabuan. It is spoken in seven dialects, among them Fkar, Imyan, Saifi and Tehit Jit. Tehit belongs to the small West Bird's Head family, whose half-dozen languages occupy the peninsula's western tip and the eastern part of Salawati Island across the strait; on pronoun evidence the family appears related to the North Halmahera languages, and long contact with Austronesian tongues has given it an atypical subject-verb-object order together with borrowed pronouns and numerals. Its closest linguistic neighbours include Moi along the coast and Moraid further inland. These shores and islands were the heart of the maritime network woven from the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries by the Biak war leader Gurabesi and his Tidore patrons, whose sultanate claimed suzerainty over the Raja Ampat islands and the western Vogelkop; Austronesian seafaring terms and trade contacts entered Tehit speech in that era. The Spanish expedition of Luís Vaz de Torres passed the New Guinea coast in 1606, but no European power planted a permanent post among the Tehit in this period, so their dialects and clan life continued under the loose overlordship of Tidore and the Raja Ampat rajas.
zh: 特希特语又记为塔希特语、特希德语、凯布斯语或特米纳布安语，是西南巴布亚鸟头半岛西南部的巴布亚语言，核心区域在今特米纳布安镇一带。它有七种方言，包括弗卡尔、伊米扬、赛菲和特希特吉特等。特希特语属于小小的西鸟头语系，该语系约六种语言分布在半岛西端和海峡对岸萨拉瓦提岛的东部；根据代词证据，它似乎与北哈马黑拉诸语有亲缘关系，而与南岛语言的长期接触又使它采用了非典型的主-谓-宾语序，并借入代词和数词。它最近的语言邻居包括沿海的莫伊语和更靠内陆的莫赖德语。从15至16世纪起，这片海岸和岛屿正处于比亚克军事首领古拉贝西及其蒂多雷宗主所编织的海上网络中心，蒂多雷苏丹国对拉贾安帕群岛和鸟头半岛西部宣称宗主权，南岛语的航海术语和贸易接触也在这一时期进入特希特语。1606年，路易斯·瓦斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙探险队经过新几内亚海岸，但这一时期没有任何欧洲强国在特希特人中间设立永久据点，于是他们的各方言和氏族生活在蒂多雷与拉贾安帕拉者松散的宗主权下延续下来。

en: Telugu is the most widely spoken of the Dravidian languages, native to the Andhra coast and Deccan plateau of south-eastern India, the country watered by the Krishna and Godavari rivers. Linguists estimate that it split from Proto-Dravidian around 1000 BCE, making it the first major branch to become distinct. Telugu words already appear in Prakrit inscriptions of the fourth century BCE, while the first long inscription written entirely in Telugu dates to 575 CE. Its written form descends from a Brahmi-derived script once shared with Kannada, and its literature began in earnest with Nannayya's Telugu Mahabharata of 1022, which fixed a literary idiom enriched by Sanskrit. Telugu served as a court language under the Eastern Chalukyas, Kakatiyas and the Vijayanagara Empire, whose rulers patronised a golden age of Telugu poetry, and it became the prestige language of high culture and Carnatic music across much of southern India.
zh: 泰卢固语是达罗毗荼语族中使用人口最多的语言，故土在印度东南部的安得拉海岸与德干高原，即克里希纳河与戈达瓦里河流域。语言学家估计它在公元前1000年前后从原始达罗毗荼语分化，是最早独立出来的主要分支。公元前4世纪的俗语铭文里已出现泰卢固词语，而第一篇通体用泰卢固语写成的长铭文则出现于575年。它的文字源自婆罗米字母，曾与卡纳达文共用一套书写系统；文学创作以1022年南纳亚的泰卢固语《摩诃婆罗多》为开山之作，确立了大量吸收梵语成分的文学语言。泰卢固语先后充当东遮娄其、卡卡提亚和毗奢耶那伽罗等王朝的宫廷语言，在毗奢耶那伽罗诸王扶持下迎来诗歌黄金时代，并成为南印度广大地区精英文化和卡纳提克音乐的声望语言。

en: Tepiman, also called Piman, is a branch of the Uto-Aztecan family whose languages stretch from southern Arizona southward along the Sierra Madre Occidental to Durango. Linguistic evidence suggests its varieties began to split from one another about a thousand years ago. Its four members are O'odham, the language of the Tohono O'odham and Akimel O'odham of Arizona and northern Sonora; O'ob, spoken by the mountain and lowland Pima; O'otham, the Tepehuan language of Durango and neighboring states; and the poorly documented Tepecano. Tepehuan, a Nahuatl name meaning mountain people, covers three groups who call themselves O'dam, Audam and Odami. Farming peoples of dispersed mountain villages, they stayed neutral in the Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590, and Jesuits opened missions among them from 1596 at Santiago Papasquiaro, Santa Catarina de Tepehuanes and El Zape. Repeated epidemics and forced labor in mines and haciendas fed the great Tepehuan Revolt of 1616, led by the messianic Quautlatas with a broken cross as his symbol; Spanish forces crushed it by 1620 at heavy cost, and the surviving Tepiman speakers remained in mission communities and remote valleys of the northwest.
zh: 特皮曼语又称皮曼语，是犹他-阿兹特克语系的一个语支，各语言从亚利桑那南部沿西马德雷山脉一直延伸到杜兰戈。语言证据显示，它的各变体约在一千年前开始分化。该语支有四名成员：奥奥德姆语，即亚利桑那和索诺拉北部的托霍诺·奥奥德姆人与阿基梅尔·奥奥德姆人（皮马人）的语言；奥奥布语，为山地和低地皮马人使用；奥奥塔姆语，即杜兰戈及邻州特佩华纳人的语言；以及记载稀少的特佩卡诺语。“特佩华纳”是纳瓦特尔语名字，意为山里人，其下三个群体自称奥达姆、奥丹和奥达米。他们是散居山村的农耕民族，在1550至1590年的奇奇梅卡战争中保持中立；耶稣会从1596年起在他们中间传教，在圣地亚哥·帕帕斯基亚罗、圣卡塔琳娜·德特佩瓦内斯和埃尔萨佩建立传教区。接连的瘟疫以及矿山和庄园的劳役催生了1616年的特佩华纳大起义，先知式人物夸乌特拉塔斯以断十字架为标志领导起事；西班牙军队到1620年以惨重代价将其镇压，幸存的特皮曼语使用者此后生活在传教区村镇和西北部偏远山谷中。

en: The Ternate grouping unites the North Halmahera languages, the principal non-Austronesian, or Papuan, language family of the Moluccas, spoken across northern and eastern Halmahera and the surrounding islands. It takes in Ternate on the island of the same name, Tidore on neighboring Tidore, Mare, Moti and Maitara, the Tobelo speeches of Kao Bay and northern Morotai, and Galela of Halmahera's northern tip. Ternate and Tidore are so close that their separation rests mainly on sociopolitical grounds, while Galela and Tobelo form a dialect continuum once termed Northeast Halmaheran. Long contact with Malay and other Austronesian tongues has left all of them with heavy loan layers; Ternate itself also carries Javanese, Portuguese, Dutch and English words. These were the languages of the four North Malukan sultanates of Ternate, Tidore, Jailolo and Bacan, whose clove trade made the region wealthy after Islam reached the elite in the late fifteenth century. Written in the Jawi script from at least that era, they are the region's only Papuan languages with indigenous literary traditions, and Ternate became the lingua franca of North Maluku, lending words as far as Sulawesi and shaping the North Moluccan and Manado varieties of Malay. The Portuguese arrived with Francisco Serrão in 1512 and built a fort in 1522, but were expelled in 1575 under Sultan Baabullah; after decades of Dutch-Spanish rivalry and Spain's withdrawal in 1663, a treaty of 1683 made Ternate a Dutch vassal, though Tidore's Prince Nuku led anti-Dutch revolts after 1780.
zh: 特尔纳特语这一划分整合了北哈马黑拉语系，它是马鲁古最主要的非南岛语（即巴布亚语言）语系，通行于哈马黑拉岛北部和东部及周围岛屿。其中包括同名岛屿上的特尔纳特语，邻近蒂多雷、马雷、莫蒂和迈塔拉岛上的蒂多雷语，卡奥湾和莫罗泰岛北部的托贝洛诸语，以及哈马黑拉岛北端的加莱拉语。特尔纳特语与蒂多雷语极为接近，两者的分立主要出于社会政治原因；加莱拉语和托贝洛语则构成一个方言连续体，旧称东北哈马黑拉语。长期与马来语及其他南岛语言接触，使这些语言都带有厚厚的借词层，特尔纳特语本身还吸收了爪哇语、葡萄牙语、荷兰语和英语词汇。这些语言曾是北马鲁古特尔纳特、蒂多雷、贾伊洛洛、巴占四大苏丹国的语言：15世纪末伊斯兰教传入精英阶层后，丁香贸易让这一地区富庶起来。特尔纳特语和蒂多雷语至迟在那时已有爪夷文书写，是当地仅有的拥有本土书面传统的巴布亚语言；特尔纳特语还成为北马鲁古的通用语，借词远播苏拉威西，并塑造了北马鲁古马来语和万鸦老马来语。1512年葡萄牙人随弗朗西斯科·塞朗到来并于1522年修建城堡，却在1575年被巴布乌拉苏丹治下的当地人驱逐；经过荷兰与西班牙数十年的争夺、1663年西班牙人撤出，1683年的条约使特尔纳特沦为荷兰附庸，而蒂多雷的努库王子在1780年后仍领导反荷起义。

en: Thin Nu Waab, the language of Waab, is the Yapese name for the tongue of the Yap Main Islands, four high islands enclosed by a single reef in the western Carolines. It is an Austronesian language of the Oceanic branch, though its exact subgroup is disputed, and it is distinct from the Chuukic languages, such as Ulithian and Woleaian, spoken on Yap's outlying atolls. Yap was settled by seafarers from the direction of the Malay Peninsula, New Guinea and the Solomons, and around 950 the village of Gatcheper in Gagil built a maritime tribute network, later called the Yapese Empire, that stretched more than 1,300 kilometres east toward Chuuk and carried Yapese speech and customs across the western Carolines. Yapese navigators also sailed to Palau to quarry the great stone disks called rai, towing them home on rafts behind their canoes. Alvaro de Saavedra first sighted Yap in 1528 and Ruy Lopez de Villalobos charted its reefs in 1543, after which Spain counted the islands among its Philippine possessions from the seventeenth century. The language itself remained unwritten, and is notable among the world's languages for its ejective fricatives.
zh: “辛努瓦布”意为瓦布的语言，是雅浦人对雅浦主群岛语言的自称；雅浦主群岛是西加罗林群岛中被同一道礁脉环绕的四座高岛。它属于南岛语系大洋洲语族，但确切的语支归属仍有争议，并且与雅浦外围环礁上通行的乌利西语、沃莱艾语等楚克语支语言截然不同。雅浦最早的定居者是来自马来半岛、新几内亚和所罗门群岛方向的航海者；约950年，加吉尔酋邦的加切佩尔村建立起一张海上朝贡网络，后人称之为雅浦帝国，其势力向东延伸1300多公里直抵楚克，把雅浦语和雅浦风俗带到西加罗林各地。雅浦航海者还远航帕劳开采名为“雷伊”的巨型石盘，用木筏拴在独木舟后面拖回故乡。1528年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨韦德拉首次望见雅浦，1543年鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·比利亚洛沃斯测绘了这里的礁脉，此后从17世纪起，西班牙把这些岛屿算作其菲律宾领地的一部分。雅浦语本身始终没有文字，并以拥有挤喉擦音而在世界语言中引人注目。

en: Tibetan is the Tibeto-Burman language of the Tibetan Plateau and the Himalayas, whose many varieties descend from Old Tibetan, the speech first written down in the seventh century with an Indic-derived script. A reform of 816 under King Sadnalegs fixed the literary standard that became Classical Tibetan, the language of the Buddhist canon translated from Sanskrit and of the Mahavyutpatti lexicon; it bound together the mutually divergent spoken forms of Ü-Tsang, Kham and Amdo and the Himalayan varieties of Ladakh, Bhutan, Sikkim and Baltistan. After the later diffusion of Buddhism from the tenth to twelfth centuries, the Gelug order built the great monasteries of Ganden, Sera and Drepung, and in the seventeenth century the Fifth Dalai Lama, Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso, made Classical Tibetan the language of government, scholarship and liturgy across his realm. The central and Kham dialects developed tones, while the more conservative Amdo and Ladakhi speech kept older features, and the classical written form remained the shared medium of Tibetan Buddhism throughout the period.
zh: 藏语是通行于青藏高原和喜马拉雅山区的藏缅语族语言，众多方言都源自7世纪开始用源自印度的文字书写的古藏语。816年，赞普赤德松赞（赛那累）主持的文字规范确立了书面标准，即古典藏语，也就是从梵文译出的佛教经典和《翻译名义大集》所用的语言；它把卫藏、康区、安多以及拉达克、不丹、锡金、巴尔蒂斯坦等地差异很大的口语联结在一起。10至12世纪佛教后弘期之后，格鲁派建起甘丹寺、色拉寺和哲蚌寺等大寺；17世纪时，五世达赖喇嘛阿旺罗桑嘉措把古典藏语确立为其辖境内行政、学术和宗教仪轨的语言。卫藏和康方言逐渐发展出声调，更为保守的安多和拉达克话则保留了古语特征；在整个这一时期，古典书面藏语始终是藏传佛教共同的媒介。

en: The Timoric languages are a branch of the Central-Eastern Malayo-Polynesian group of Austronesian, spoken on Timor, the neighboring island of Wetar and, in most classifications, the islands of southwest Maluku. They carry the speech of the Atoni of west Timor through Uab Meto, the Tetun and Mambai of the east, the Helong around Kupang, the Rotenese of Roti and the Wetarese across the Wetar Strait. Long contact with the Papuan languages of Timor, Alor and Pantar has left these tongues with unusual phonology and many borrowed words. Timor entered regional trade as a source of sandalwood, noted under the name Ti-wu in the Chinese Zhu Fan Zhi of the 1200s and listed among the realms of Majapahit in the Nagarakretagama of the 1300s. The Portuguese settled in eastern Timor in the late 1500s and the Dutch East India Company took Kupang in the mid-1600s, and their long rivalry over the sandalwood trade made Tetun, spread by coastal commerce and Catholic missions, the island's main lingua franca.
zh: 帝汶语是南岛语系中东部马来—波利尼西亚语群的一支，通行于帝汶岛、邻近的韦塔岛以及多数分类方案中的马鲁古西南部诸岛。其中包括西帝汶阿托尼人说的乌阿布梅托语、东部的德顿语和曼拜语、古邦一带的赫隆语、罗地岛的罗地语以及韦塔海峡对岸的韦塔语。由于长期与帝汶、阿洛和潘塔尔岛上的巴布亚语言接触，这些语言语音独特、借词众多。帝汶以檀香木产地进入区域贸易：13世纪中国的《诸蕃志》以“底勿”之名记载该岛，14世纪的《爪哇史颂》又把它列入满者伯夷的藩属。16世纪末葡萄牙人在东帝汶定居，17世纪中叶荷兰东印度公司夺取古邦；双方围绕檀香木贸易长期争夺，而借助沿海商业和天主教传教活动传播的德顿语，也由此成为岛上最主要的通用语。

en: Timoto was the highland language of the Timote people, the southern branch of the Timoto–Cuica complex of the Venezuelan Andes, spoken through the Motatán and Chama river valleys from the country around Timotes to La Grita, including the Tatuy alluvial plain where the city of Mérida now stands. It is known in several local forms, among them Mucuchí and Marripú, and its name has been traced to ti-motɨ, meaning speakers of Mutú; the word mutú or mukú recurs across the region as a place name and may have meant people, community or village. Together with Cuicas it formed a decimal-counting language with no proven relation to the Arawakan, Cariban or Chibchan families around it, carried by a society of terrace farmers who irrigated stone-faced platforms on the mountainsides, lived in planned stone villages and grew potatoes and maize. Where the Cuicas met the Spaniards peacefully, the Timotes were remembered as warlike: after Mérida was founded on their Tatuy lands in 1558, clashes forced the settlers to move the town within a year. Resistance could not stop the colony, however, and under the rule of Mérida and its estates the Timote villages were slowly absorbed into Spanish-speaking life, the old speech surviving only in highland hamlets and in fragmentary vocabularies collected long after the conquest.
zh: 蒂莫托语是蒂莫特人的高地语言。蒂莫特人是委内瑞拉安第斯山区蒂莫特—奎卡族群的南支，语言通行于莫塔坦河与查马河流域，从蒂莫特斯一带延伸到拉格里塔，也包括后来梅里达城所在的塔图伊冲积平原。它有多种地方变体，其中有穆库奇和马里普；它的名字被追溯为 ti-motɨ，意为“说穆图语的人”，而“穆图”或“穆库”作为地名在该地区反复出现，可能表示人、村社或村庄。它与奎卡斯语共同构成一种采用十进位计数的语言，与周围的阿拉瓦克、加勒比、奇布查诸语系都没有经证实的亲缘关系；承载它的社会是梯田农人，在山坡上修筑石砌灌溉台地，住在规划整齐的石屋村落里，种植马铃薯和玉米。奎卡人平和地迎接西班牙人，蒂莫特人却以好战留在记载中：1558年梅里达在他们的塔图伊土地上建城后，冲突迫使殖民者不到一年就迁移了城址。但抵抗终究挡不住殖民地，在梅里达城及其庄园的统治下，蒂莫特村落慢慢被纳入西班牙语生活，古老的语言只在高地小村和征服很久以后才收集到的零碎词汇中留下痕迹。

en: Timucua is a language isolate once spoken across northern and central Florida and into southern Georgia, where it was the principal native tongue at the time of Spanish colonization. Its nine or ten dialects, recorded among the Mocama, Potano and other Timucua groups, differed only slightly and served mainly to mark tribal boundaries. Nearly everything known of the language comes from Francisco Pareja, a Franciscan missionary who reached St. Augustine in 1595 and spent thirty-one years among the Timucua; he devised a writing system for them, and between 1612 and 1628 printed Spanish-Timucua catechisms together with the first grammar of the language. Only ten primary sources now survive, seven of them his. The speech of the Calusa and Tocobaga on the Gulf coast, by contrast, was almost never written down and remains unclassified. In 1763, when Spain ceded Florida to Britain after the Seven Years' War, the last Timucua speakers left with the Spanish missions for Cuba and the language fell silent.
zh: 蒂穆夸语是一门语言孤立语，曾通行于佛罗里达北部和中部，并延伸到佐治亚南部，是西班牙殖民时期当地最主要的原住民语言。莫卡马、波塔诺等蒂穆夸群体使用的九、十种方言差别很小，主要用来区分部族界限。关于这种语言的知识几乎全部来自方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·帕雷哈：他1595年抵达圣奥古斯丁，在蒂穆夸人中生活了31年，为该语创制了文字，并在1612至1628年间刊行西班牙语—蒂穆夸语教义问答和第一部语法书。存世的一手资料只有十种，其中七种出自他之手。相比之下，墨西哥湾沿岸卡卢萨人和托科巴加人的语言几乎没有文字记录，归属仍无定论。1763年七年战争结束后，西班牙将佛罗里达割让给英国，最后一批蒂穆夸语使用者随西班牙传教团前往古巴，这门语言遂告消亡。

en: Tiri, also recorded as Tinrin, Ciri or Mea, is a Kanak language of the Austronesian family spoken in the west-central part of Grande Terre, the main island of New Caledonia, where it divides into a Tiri dialect and a Mea dialect. It belongs with the extinct Zire tongue to the Zire-Tiri branch of the southern New Caledonian languages, themselves part of the Southern Oceanic group, and makes extensive use of possessive classifiers that mark the kind of ownership between a noun and its possessor. The Kanak languages descend from Lapita voyagers, whose first coastal settlements in New Caledonia appeared around 1100 BC. James Cook sighted Grande Terre in September 1774 and named it New Caledonia; the Comte de Lapérouse reconnoitred the west coast in 1788, and whalers such as William Raven mapped the Loyalty Islands from 1793, yet for decades afterwards contacts with the archipelago remained only sporadic. Tiri remained an unwritten language of oral custom throughout this period.
zh: 蒂里语又记为廷林语、奇里语或梅阿语，是新喀里多尼亚主岛格朗德特尔岛中西部通行的卡纳克语言，属南岛语系，内部又分蒂里、梅阿两种方言。它与已消亡的济雷语共同构成新喀里多尼亚南部语言的济雷-蒂里语支，后者隶属于南大洋洲语群；蒂里语大量使用领属分类词，用以标明名词与领有者之间的占有关系。卡纳克诸语言源自拉皮塔航海者，他们约在公元前1100年开始在新喀里多尼亚沿海建立定居点。1774年9月詹姆斯·库克望见格朗德特尔岛，并将其命名为新喀里多尼亚；1788年拉彼鲁兹伯爵考察了西海岸，1793年起威廉·雷文等捕鲸人测绘了洛亚蒂群岛，但此后数十年间与该群岛的接触仍只是零星发生。在这一时期，蒂里语始终是没有文字的口头习俗语言。

en: Tirio is a small family of Trans-New Guinea languages of the lower Fly River region in Papua New Guinea's Western Province. It comprises Tirio, also called Makayam, Bitur, also known as Mutum, Baramu, Were and the speech of Sumogi Island, whose members share about forty per cent of their vocabulary.
zh: 蒂里奥语是跨新几内亚语系的一个小语族，通行于巴布亚新几内亚西部省弗莱河下游地区，包括蒂里奥语（又称马卡扬语）、比图尔语（又称穆图姆语）、巴拉穆语、韦雷语以及苏莫吉岛上的语言，语族内各语言约有四成词汇相同。

en: Tokelauan is a Polynesian language of the Austronesian family, spoken on the three coral atolls of Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo, and until modern times also on Swains Island, called Olohega in the language itself; the name Tokelau means north-northeast, or north wind. Its speakers descend from settlers who arrived from the direction of Samoa roughly a thousand years ago, and the atolls may have served as a gateway into eastern Polynesia. Although each atoll governed itself separately under chiefly clans and they sometimes fought one another, all three kept a single language with a shared oral tradition centred on the god Tui Tokelau. Tokelauan's closest relative is Tuvaluan, with which it is mutually intelligible; it also closely resembles Samoan, with a degree of mutual intelligibility, and shares marked features with the Niuafo'ou language of Tonga. It had no traditional written form and was transmitted entirely by word of mouth. Europeans first learned of the islands when John Byron sighted Atafu in 1765 and named it Duke of York's Island; Edward Edwards found Nukunonu in 1791, and an American whaler sighted Fakaofo in 1835.
zh: 托克劳语是南岛语系波利尼西亚语族的语言，通行于阿塔富、努库诺努和法考福三个珊瑚环礁，近代以前也通行于本语称作奥洛赫加的斯温斯岛；“托克劳”在本语中意为“北东北”或“北风”。说这种语言的人是约一千年前从萨摩亚方向迁来的定居者后裔，托克劳环礁可能还是通往东波利尼西亚的门户。三个环礁虽各自在氏族首领治下独立行事、彼此间偶有战事，却始终使用同一种语言，共享以神祇图伊托克劳为中心的口传传统。托克劳语最亲近的亲属是图瓦卢语，两者可以互通；它与萨摩亚语也十分接近、保持一定程度的互通，并和汤加的纽阿福欧语有明显的相似之处。托克劳语没有传统文字，完全靠口耳相传。欧洲人最早在1765年得知这些岛屿：约翰·拜伦望见阿塔富并将其命名为约克公爵岛，爱德华·爱德华兹于1791年发现努库诺努，1835年一艘美国捕鲸船又望见了法考福。

en: Tolomako, also called Bigbay after the Big Bay area of northern Espiritu Santo in Vanuatu, is a conservative Oceanic language and a close sister of the much-changed Sakao language spoken farther along the same coast. Its pronunciation and grammar stay close to what scholars reconstruct for Proto-North-Central Vanuatu: it has a simple consonant-vowel syllable structure and isolating syntax, its personal pronouns distinguish singular, dual, trial and plural, and its verbs mark realis and irrealis mood rather than tense. A closely related variety, Tsureviu, is usually treated as its dialect. Big Bay itself entered recorded history in 1606, when the Spanish expedition of Pedro Fernandes de Quiros landed there and briefly claimed the island as a great southern continent.
zh: 托洛马科语又称大湾语，得名于瓦努阿图圣埃斯皮里图岛北部的大湾地区，是一种保守的大洋洲语，与同一海岸更远处变化剧烈的萨卡奥语为近亲姐妹语言。它的语音和语法接近学者构拟的原始中北瓦努阿图语：音节结构简单，为辅音加元音的形式，句法属孤立型；人称代词区分单数、双数、三数和复数，动词不标时态，而标现实与非现实语气。与它极相近的楚雷维乌语一般被视为它的方言。大湾本身在1606年进入有记载的历史：当年佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯的西班牙探险队在此登陆，并一度把该岛当作南方大陆加以宣称。

en: Tongic is the Polynesian subgroup made up of Tongan, the language of the kingdom of Tonga, and Niuean. Its main member, Tongan or lea fakatonga, is a verb–subject–object language whose ancestors Lapita voyagers had carried to Tongatapu by the ninth century BC. By the twelfth century the Tuʻi Tonga chiefs spread Tongan influence across the central Pacific, from Niue and Samoa to Rotuma and Wallis, and Tongan settlers of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries left a deep mark on the language of ʻUvea. Tongan preserves the old Polynesian glottal stop, written with the turned comma called fakauʻa, and keeps the l sound that most sister languages merged with r. Dutch sailors Willem Schouten and Jacob Le Maire made the first word lists in 1616, Abel Tasman called at Tongatapu in 1643, and James Cook visited between 1773 and 1777. Protestant missionaries arrived in 1797 and the Wesleyan minister Walter Lawry in 1822; under their work the language gained its Latin-script missionary alphabet, and the future king George Tāufaʻāhau was baptised in 1831.
zh: 汤加语是波利尼西亚语族汤加语支的主要语言，同支还有纽埃语。拉皮塔文化的航海者在公元前9世纪已把它的祖先带到汤加塔布。到12世纪，图伊汤加酋长把汤加语的影响播及中太平洋，从纽埃、萨摩亚到罗图马和瓦利斯；15至16世纪的汤加移民又在乌韦阿语中留下深深的印记。汤加语保留了古波利尼西亚语的喉塞音，用名为法考阿的倒置逗号书写，并保留了边音，而多数姊妹语言里边音与颤音已经合流。1616年荷兰水手威廉·斯豪滕和雅各布·勒梅尔最早编出词汇表，1643年亚伯·塔斯曼抵达汤加塔布，詹姆斯·库克则在1773至1777年间多次到访。新教传教士于1797年到来，卫斯理宗牧师沃尔特·劳里于1822年到来；在他们的工作下，汤加语有了拉丁字母的传教士拼写体系，未来的国王乔治·陶法阿豪也于1831年受洗。

en: Tonkawa is a language isolate, with no proven relatives, spoken by the Tonkawa people of the southern Great Plains, whose autonym Tickanwatic means the real people. In 1601 the Tonkawa lived in what is now northwestern Oklahoma as a loose set of nomadic bands with some horticulture, and they drifted south into Texas in the late seventeenth century under pressure from the Apache and Wichita; by 1700 they had reached the Red River. In the 1740s some bands settled at the Spanish San Gabriel missions, and in 1758 Tonkawa warriors joined the native coalition that destroyed the mission of Santa Cruz de San Saba. The language had no native script and was carried entirely by oral tradition.
zh: 通卡瓦语是一门没有已知亲属语言的孤立语言，使用者是南部大平原的通卡瓦人；他们的自称蒂坎瓦蒂克意为真正的人。1601年，通卡瓦人还生活在今天的俄克拉荷马西北部，由若干游徙的氏族群体组成，兼营少量种植；17世纪末在阿帕奇人和威奇托人的压力下向南迁入得克萨斯，到1700年已抵达雷德河。1740年代，部分群体定居西班牙人的圣加布里埃尔传教站；1758年，通卡瓦战士又加入原住民联军，摧毁了圣克鲁斯－德圣萨瓦传教站。通卡瓦语没有本族文字，完全靠口耳相传。

en: The Orya–Tor languages are a family of just over a dozen Papuan languages of Western New Guinea, named after the Tor River on the forested coast east of the Mamberamo. Orya is their closest outside relative; Kwesten, Mander and Bonerif belong to the Tor grouping proper, and older links with the Lakes Plain languages have not held up.
zh: 奥里亚—托尔语是印度尼西亚西新几内亚的一个巴布亚语族，含十余种语言，因流经马姆贝拉莫河以东森林沿海平原的托尔河得名。奥里亚语是该语族最亲近的外部亲属，奎斯滕语、曼德尔语、博内里夫语等则构成托尔语群本体；早年把它与湖平原语挂钩的说法未能成立。

en: The Torricelli languages are a family of some fifty Papuan tongues named after the Torricelli Mountains of north-western Papua New Guinea, whose forested ridges run between the Pacific coast and the Sepik River basin; their speakers have held these hills for several millennia, and migrations of Sepik-speaking peoples later split the family into three geographically separated areas. Its most populous branch is Arapesh, which includes Bukiyip or Mountain Arapesh, spoken between Yangoru and Maprik and famed for a complex agreement system with eighteen noun classes, while the Wapei branch contains Olo, spoken around Aitape in the Payi and Wapi dialects. The family has no proven relatives outside itself, though shared pronoun endings, a plural suffix m and dual suffix p, hint at a link with the Sepik languages. Typologically Torricelli speech stands apart from most Papuan families in keeping subject–verb–object order and prepositions, and its nouns take plural endings and even assign gender according to their sound. The first European to trace this northern coast was the Spaniard Yñigo Ortiz de Retez, who named the island New Guinea in 1545, long before the mountain villages were reached by outsiders.
zh: 托里切利诸语是一个约含五十种巴布亚语言的语族，以巴布亚新几内亚西北部的托里切利山脉命名，林木覆盖的山岭横亘在太平洋海岸与塞皮克河盆地之间。说这些语言的人已在山中居住数千年，后来塞皮克语族群的迁徙把该语族分隔成三个地理上互不相连的区域。使用人数最多的分支是阿拉佩什语，其中包括通行于扬戈鲁与马普里克之间的布基伊普语，又称山地阿拉佩什语，以拥有十八个名词类的复杂一致体系著称；瓦佩伊分支则有奥洛语，通行于艾塔佩一带，分帕伊和瓦皮两种方言。该语族在外部没有确证的亲属，不过代词共有的复数后缀m和双数后缀p暗示它可能与塞皮克语族有关。语言类型上，托里切利诸语与多数巴布亚语族不同，保持主语—动词—宾语语序并使用前置词；名词有复数变化，甚至按读音划分性别。最早沿这片北海岸航行的欧洲人是西班牙人伊尼戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·雷特斯，他于1545年将这座岛屿命名为新几内亚，而山中小村被外界触及则是很久以后的事。

en: Totozoquean is a proposed language family of Mesoamerica that joins two well-established groupings: the Totonacan languages of the Gulf coast, spoken across Veracruz, Puebla and Hidalgo, and the Mixe–Zoque languages of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Oaxaca and Chiapas. The grouping rests on comparative reconstructions of a proto-Totozoquean sound system published in the early twenty-first century and remains debated; the Huavean languages of the Oaxaca coast may be its closest relatives. When the Spanish conquest reached the Gulf coast in 1519, Totonacan languages were spoken all along the shore and were occasionally written in the colonial period, while the Mixe–Zoque family reaches far deeper into the past: many scholars hold that the Olmecs, who flourished from roughly 1200 to 400 BCE, spoke a Mixe–Zoque language, and the Isthmian or Epi-Olmec script may record an early Zoquean tongue.
zh: 托托索克语是中美洲一个假说性的语系，把两个已确立的语群联系在一起：一是墨西哥湾沿岸、通行于韦拉克鲁斯、普埃布拉和伊达尔戈的托托纳坎语族，二是瓦哈卡和恰帕斯特万特佩克地峡的米塞-索克语族。这一归类建立在21世纪初对原始托托索克语音系的比较构拟之上，学界仍有争议；瓦哈卡沿海的瓦维语系可能是它最近的亲属。1519年西班牙征服波及墨西哥湾沿岸时，托托纳坎诸语言遍布海岸，殖民时代偶尔有书面记录；米塞-索克语族的历史则更为久远，不少学者认为约公元前1200年至前400年兴盛的奥尔梅克人说的就是一种米塞-索克语言，地峡文字（也称后奥尔梅克文字）记录的可能也是早期的索克语。

en: Truka is the presumed, now extinct language of the Truká people of north-eastern Brazil, whose villages occupy the Ilha da Assunção archipelago on the São Francisco river at Cabrobó in Pernambuco. No word lists or texts were recorded, so the language remains unclassified and is known only from the identity of its speakers.
zh: 特鲁卡语是巴西东北部特鲁卡人推定使用过的已消亡语言；特鲁卡人聚居于伯南布哥州卡布罗博市圣弗朗西斯科河上的阿松桑岛群岛。由于没有留下任何词表或文本，该语言无法分类，今人只能凭借使用者的族群身份知道它的存在。

en: Tsėhesenėstsestotse, the language of the Cheyenne, is a Plains Algonquian tongue of the Algic family, highly polysynthetic and reshaped from Proto-Algonquian by a long chain of vowel and consonant shifts, as when the ancestral word for man became Cheyenne hetane. In the mid-seventeenth century its speakers lived between the Mississippi and Mille Lacs Lake in Minnesota, gathering wild rice and hunting bison, and French visitors met them at Fort Crevecoeur in Illinois. Driven west by the Assiniboine and later the Ojibwe and Lakota, they reached the Missouri River in 1676, learned earth-lodge village life from the Mandan and Arikara, and moved into the Black Hills; around 1730 they passed horses on to the Lakota, and by the later 1700s had themselves become nomadic bison hunters on the high plains. The language has two varieties, those of the Tsétsêhéstâhese and the Só'taeo'o, who traveled together with slightly different speech and separate sacred bundles.
zh: 夏延语是阿尔吉克语系下的平原阿尔冈昆语言，多式综合特征显著，从原始阿尔冈昆语经过一连串元音和辅音演变而来，例如祖语中指“人”的词经音变成为夏延语中的“赫塔内”。17世纪中叶，操此语者居住在密西西比河与明尼苏达的米尔拉克湖之间，以采集野米和狩猎野牛为生，法国人曾在伊利诺伊的克雷夫克尔堡见到他们。他们先后被阿西尼本人、奥吉布瓦人和拉科塔人向西驱赶，1676年抵达密苏里河，向曼丹人和阿里卡拉人学会了土屋村落生活，随后进入布莱克山；约1730年他们把马匹传给拉科塔人，到18世纪后期自己也转为在高平原上游猎野牛的游牧者。夏延语有两个分支，分别属于采采赫斯塔赫塞人和索塔埃奥人，两支同行而口音略异，各奉不同的圣物束。

en: Tshon, more usually called Chonan, is the name given to the language family of the nomadic hunter-gatherers of Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego; the term comes from a word meaning man or person shared by its languages, and the family was first outlined under the label Tshon by Roberto Lehmann Nitsche. Its best-recorded members are Tehuelche, also called Aonikenk, spoken on the mainland steppe north of the Strait of Magellan, and Selk'nam, or Ona, of north-eastern Tierra del Fuego, alongside the closely related Haush speech and the little-recorded Teushen tongue lying between Tehuelche and the peoples of the Pampas. Some scholars extend the family northwards to include Gününa Küne, the language of the Puelche, and perhaps the old Querandí speech of the Buenos Aires hinterland, though these links remain debated. Ferdinand Magellan's men met Tehuelche speakers at San Julián Bay in 1520 and called them Patagones, and the Jesuit Thomas Falkner described the steppe peoples in 1774, but the family has no proven relative outside the region. From the eighteenth century Araucanian influence spread across the Pampas, bringing Mapuche speech, horses and new alliances, while the advancing Spanish and, after independence, Argentine and Chilean frontiers introduced sheep estates and epidemics that steadily broke up the old nomadic world. One by one the Chonan tongues fell silent, leaving Tehuelche and Selk'nam wordlists as their main record.
zh: 聪语常称乔南语系，是巴塔哥尼亚和火地岛游猎采集民族所属的语系；“聪”来自这些语言中共同表示“人”的词，学者莱曼-尼采最早以“聪”为名勾勒出这个语系。记录最充分的成员是麦哲伦海峡以北大陆草原上的特维尔切语，亦称阿奥尼肯克语，以及火地岛东北部的塞尔克南语，又名奥纳语；此外还有与塞尔克南语相近的豪什语，以及夹在特维尔切人与潘帕斯各族之间、记录稀少的特乌申语。部分学者主张把语系范围向北扩展，纳入普埃尔切人的古努纳库内语，或许还包括布宜诺斯艾利斯内陆克兰迪人的古老语言，但这些亲缘关系仍有争议。1520年，麦哲伦的船队在圣胡利安湾遇到说特维尔切语的人，称他们为巴塔哥恩人；1774年，耶稣会士福克纳记述了草原各族，但这个语系始终找不到与地区外语言可靠的亲缘关系。18世纪起，阿劳坎人的影响席卷潘帕斯，带来马普切语、马匹和新的联盟；随后不断推进的西班牙以及独立后的阿根廷、智利边界带来牧羊场和疫病，一步步瓦解了古老的游猎世界。乔南诸语言相继沉寂，主要靠特维尔切语和塞尔克南语的词表留下记录。

en: Tsimshian, called Sm'algya̱x or “the true language” by its speakers, is the principal member of the Tsimshianic family, which most linguists treat as an independent family of North America. Its close relatives are Nisga'a and Gitksan of the upper Skeena and Nass rivers, from whose speech the coastal dialect split after Tsimshian groups moved down the Skeena to the Prince Rupert harbour and the neighbouring islands. It is also spoken at New Metlakatla in Alaska. The language mirrors the ranked, matrilineal society of its speakers, distinguishing some twenty-seven terms for chief. Europeans first reached a Tsimshian village in 1787, and in 1834 the Hudson's Bay Company built its fort at Lax Kw'alaams, drawing nine Tsimshian chiefs to settle around it for the fur trade.
zh: 钦西安语被使用者称为斯马尔基亚克斯，意为“真正的语言”，是钦西安语族最主要的成员；多数语言学家把该语族视为北美一个独立的语系。它的近亲是上游斯基纳河与纳斯河流域的尼斯加语和吉特克桑语：钦西安各部顺斯基纳河而下，迁居鲁珀特王子港及附近岛屿后，沿海方言便从这些亲族语言中分化出来，阿拉斯加的新梅特拉卡特拉也有人使用。这种语言反映了使用者等级分明的母系社会，仅表示“酋长”的词就有约二十七个。欧洲人最早于1787年抵达钦西安人的村落；1834年哈德逊湾公司在拉克斯夸拉姆斯设立商堡，九位钦西安酋长为经营毛皮贸易而率部定居其周围。

en: Tsogo, also called Getsogo, is a Bantu language of the forested highlands of southern-central Gabon, spoken by the Mitsogo people of the Ngounié river country around the town of Mouila. Oral tradition and linguistic comparison with the related Myene speech suggest that the ancestors of the Tsogo split from a wider Bantu group during the Stone Age and had settled these valleys by around 1200 BC, living in small mobile villages by slash-and-burn farming, hunting and fishing. It is also one of the principal languages of the Babongo Pygmies of the Gabonese forest. Tsogo society is organised through matrilineal initiation societies, of which the Bwiti ceremony is the most widely known, and the language carries the hymns, ritual knowledge and oral histories of those societies.
